11100525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100525.value: 基於冷凍微針的IL-10 CAR-T細胞皮內遞送策略：應用於實體腫瘤治療與細胞在皮膚內遷移之雙光子成像分析

11100525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100525.value: Cryomicroneedles (cryoMNs) are the latest generation of microneedle devices designed for intradermal cell delivery. These are made of cell-containing cryogenic media and can be stored for months in a freezer, transported, and subsequently used. The use of cryoMNs circumvents the complex and redundant procedure of conventional therapeutic cell administration (i.e., bolus injection or systematic infusion). We explored its application in one type of cellular immunotherapy (cancer vaccination), wherein cryoMNs intradermally delivered ovalbumin-pulsed dendritic cells into the dermal layer of mouse skin. The delivered cells produced stronger antigen-specific immune responses and protection against melanoma development in mice than did dendritic cell vaccination performed using intravenous and subcutaneous injection methods. This study explores cryoMN’s application in adoptive cellular immunotherapy by intradermally delivering chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells to target and eliminate solid tumors. There are two major challenges. First, conventional CAR T cells exhibit limited infiltration into solid tumors. Second, the cryoMN patch fit for humans is usually no larger than 2 cm × 2 cm with 400 needles (each needle has a height of 750 µm and a base diameter of 300 µm). cryoMNs of this size can only load 0.2–0.5 million cells, whereas conventional CAR T cell therapy requires at least 0.2 million CAR T cells/kg or 10 million cells for a patient weighing 50 kg. Fortunately, our collaborator Prof. TANG Li reported a metabolic reprograming strategy (Nat Immunol, 2021, 22(6):746; Nat Biotechnol, 2024). He engineered CAR T cells to secrete the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, which enhances cell proliferation and effector function and eventually alleviates T cell exhaustion through an autocrine mechanism. These new CAR T cells demonstrated tumor clearance at 1/10th the dosage of traditional CAR T therapy in a mouse melanoma model, with long-term immune memory offering protection against tumor recurrence. These results address two challenges described above. We will develop IL-10-expressing CAR T cells, optimize cryoMN formulations, and fabricate CAR T containing cryoMNs. We will study the tumor treatment efficacy of both conventional and low dosages (1/10th) of CAR T cells, which is benchmarked with subcutaneous administration and intravenous injection. Finally, we will study the survival and migration patterns of intradermally delivered CAR T cells from the skin to other tissues or organs using two-photon imaging, which will reveal the interactions between intradermally delivered T cells and the host. We hope to provide effective, efficient, yet patient-friendly immunotherapy for suffering patients. 冷凍微針（cryomicroneedles, cryoMNs）是一種新型微針裝置，專為細胞的皮內遞送而設計。這種微針由含細胞的低溫保存液製成，可在冷凍條件下儲存數月，便於運輸並應用於臨床。它能夠避免傳統細胞治療方式（如推注或靜脈輸注）中繁瑣且重複的操作流程。我們已在癌症疫苗這一細胞免疫治療策略中應用過冷凍微針，將負載卵白蛋白的樹突細胞遞送至小鼠真皮層。這種遞送方式比起靜脈或皮下注射，能誘導更強的抗原特異性免疫反應，並有效抑制黑色素瘤的生長。 本研究計畫將進一步探討冷凍微針於另一類細胞免疫治療——過繼性細胞療法中的應用，將CAR-T細胞皮內遞送以對抗實體腫瘤。我們面臨兩項主要挑戰：第一，傳統CAR-T細胞難以有效滲入實體腫瘤；第二，適用於人體的冷凍微針貼片尺寸通常不超過2公分×2公分，包含約400支微針（每針高750微米，底徑300微米），最多僅能裝載20至50萬個細胞，而傳統CAR-T療法所需劑量約為每公斤體重20萬個細胞，也就是說一位50公斤病人需至少1千萬個細胞。 我們的合作夥伴唐力教授近期在Nature Immunology（2021）與Nature Biotechnology（2024）中提出一種代謝重編程策略，成功解決上述問題。他設計的CAR-T細胞能分泌抗發炎細胞激素IL-10，透過自分泌機制促進增殖與效應功能，同時減輕細胞耗竭。在小鼠黑色素瘤模型中，這類細胞只需傳統劑量的十分之一就能清除腫瘤，並建立長期免疫記憶，有效防止腫瘤復發。 本計畫將製備表達IL-10的CAR-T細胞，優化冷凍微針的配方，並製作含CAR-T細胞的冷凍微針。我們將比較這些細胞在常規劑量與低劑量（十分之一）條件下的抗腫瘤效果，並與皮下注射與靜脈注射進行對照。最後，我們將透過雙光子顯微鏡觀察CAR-T細胞在皮膚內的存活與遷移，了解它們如何從注射部位向其他組織移動，並進一步揭示皮內遞送後與宿主組織之間的交互作用。最終目標是發展一種有效、安全且對病人更友善的免疫細胞療法。

11101025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11101025.value: 解析皮肌炎中的線粒體細胞外囊泡

11101025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101025.value: Dermatomyositis (DM) is an autoimmune disease marked by chronic inflammation, muscle weakness, and distinctive skin rashes. Our understanding of DM’s pathogenesis remains limited, preventing effective treatments. Recent studies highlight mitochondrial dysfunction and aberrant interferon (IFN) signaling as critical factors in DM progression. However, the precise mechanisms linking these pathways remain unclear. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles that transfer bioactive molecules between cells, influencing various physiological and pathological processes. Our studies and others have shown that mitochondrial components can be released in EVs, termed mitochondrial EVs (MEV), which promote inflammatory signaling in recipient cells. Preliminary data indicate a strong association between MEV and IFN in DM pathogenesis. Specifically, IFN-α treatment of C2C12 myofibroblasts stimulates the generation of MEVs carrying mtDNA, which could activate cGAS-STING and IFN production in naïve C2C12 cells, suggesting a feedforward loop of IFN-MEV signaling in promoting inflammation. At the molecular level, we identified Drp1 GTPase as a key player in IFN-MEV signaling. These cellular findings are supported by observations in DM patient samples and a mouse model of autoimmune myositis. This proposal seeks to define the mechanisms of IFN-MEV signaling in DM, potentially uncovering novel therapeutic targets. Our central hypothesis is that IFN induces Drp1-dependent MEVs that propagate inflammatory responses in myositis. We aim to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of Drp1 and how IFN activates MEVs. Findings will be validated using mouse models and patient samples. The successful completion of this project will aid in developing new biomarkers and therapeutic strategies for DM. It could also have significant implications for other autoimmune diseases characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and dysregulated IFN signaling. 皮肌炎（Dermatomyositis, DM）是一種自身免疫性疾病，其特徵為慢性發炎、肌肉無力以及特有的皮膚疹。我們對DM發病機制的理解仍有限，這也阻礙了有效治療的發展。近期研究指出，線粒體功能障礙與異常的干擾素（IFN）訊號傳導是DM進展的關鍵因素。然而，這些途徑之間的具體連結機制仍不清楚。 細胞外囊泡（Extracellular Vesicles, EVs）是具有膜結構的微粒，能在細胞間傳遞生物活性分子，影響多種生理與病理過程。我們與其他研究發現，線粒體成分可透過EVs釋放，稱為線粒體EVs（Mitochondrial EVs, MEVs），可在受體細胞中促進發炎訊號。初步數據顯示，MEV與IFN在DM發病機制中有密切關聯。在分子層面上，我們鑑定出Drp1 GTP酶是IFN-MEV訊號中的關鍵因子。這些細胞層面的發現也獲得DM病患樣本與自體免疫性肌炎小鼠模型的支持。 本研究計畫旨在釐清IFN-MEV訊號在DM中的機制，可能揭示新的治療靶點。我們的核心假設是：IFN誘導Drp1依賴性的MEVs，進而在肌炎中擴散發炎反應。我們將探討Drp1的分子機制以及IFN如何活化MEVs。研究結果將透過小鼠模型與病患樣本進行驗證。本計畫的成功完成將有助於開發新的生物標記與DM治療策略，並可能對其他以粒線體功能障礙與IFN訊號失調為特徵的自身免疫疾病產生重要影響。

11101525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11101525.value: 開發基於L-RNA的螢光亮起適配體，用於功能性G-四鏈體結構的檢測與成像

11101525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101525.value: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-classical nucleic acid structures that are found across numerous species, including humans. Multiple reports have highlighted the regulatory and functional roles of these intricate structural motifs in different biochemical events. However, there are still gaps in our understanding and study concerning the precise targeting of functionally important G4 structures and monitoring of their formation in cells. To address these issues, inventing original platforms and tools — particularly with the capability to recognize G4 structures over non-G4 structures and even structurally similar G4s, as well as to image the G4s of interest in live cells — are two primary areas for further uncovering novel G4 biology and developing novel methods for G4 targeting and detection. Our laboratory has a strong interest and track record in unraveling the folding and roles of G4 structures using interdisciplinary approaches. Over the last years, we have established new platforms to generate novel L-RNA aptamer tools for the targeting of G4 structures. More recently, we have generated the first non-G4-containing L-RNA aptamer, and this aptamer exhibited promising binding affinity and selectivity to its intended rG4 target of interest. Building on top of our previous successful and exciting works, in this project, we will develop a novel and general L-RNA-based fluorescence light-up aptamer (L-RNA FLAP) platform that enables G-quadruplex structure detection. Moreover, we will study the effect of RNA sequence and structure on L-RNA FLAP tools, and optimize the binding property and sensitivity of the shortlisted candidates for the sensing of G-quadruplexes. Finally, we will investigate the biostability and cell delivery of G-quadruplex-specific L-RNA FLAP tools, and examine the dynamics of functional G-quadruplex structures under different cellular conditions. Our laboratory has the needed equipment and expertise to execute the tasks described in this project. The innovative methodologies and L-RNA FLAP tools developed in this study, including the aptamer sequences and structures, have significant patent potential. Our pilot experiments, using Alzheimer's disease-linked APP rG4 target as an example, have showcased the feasibility of our design on the L-RNA FLAP platform, and the initial data on the newly developed L-RNA FLAP tools are encouraging. Our laboratory will continue to work productively to ensure the completion of this original and timely research program. We are positive that the outputs of this work will contribute significantly to the advancement of rG4 detection and monitoring, as well as expand our knowledge of rG4 function and regulation in biology. G-四鏈體（G4）是非典型的核酸結構，存在於多種生物物種中，包括人類。多項研究報告強調了這些複雜結構模體在不同生化事件中的調控功能和作用。然而，對於精準識別功能性重要的G4結構以及監測其在細胞內形成的過程，相關認知與研究仍有不足。為了解決這些問題，開發具備能夠辨識G4結構與非G4結構，甚至結構相似的G4，並且能夠於活細胞中成像感興趣G4的創新平台與工具，成為進一步揭示新穎G4生物學與推動G4定向與檢測新方法的兩大關鍵方向。 本實驗室長期以跨領域方法致力於解析G4結構的摺疊機制與生物功能。過去幾年，我們建立了新平台以生成嶄新的L-核糖核酸適配體（L-RNA aptamer）工具，用於鎖定G4結構。近期，我們成功設計出首個不含G4結構的L-RNA適配體，且該適配體展現出對目標rG4具良好結合親和力與選擇性。在先前研究成果的基礎上，本計畫將開發一套新型且通用的基於L-RNA的螢光亮化適配體平台（L-RNA FLAP），用於偵測G-四鏈體結構。此外，我們將研究RNA序列與結構對L-RNA FLAP工具的影響，並優化入選適配體候選者的結合特性與靈敏度，以感測G-四鏈體。最後，我們將探討特異性G4 L-RNA FLAP工具的生物穩定性及細胞傳遞效率，並研究功能性G-四鏈體在不同細胞環境下的動態變化。 本實驗室具備執行本計畫所需的設備與專業技術。本研究所開發的創新方法與L-RNA FLAP工具（包括適配體序列與結構）具有重要的專利申請潛力。我們以阿茲海默症相關的APP rG4作為示範靶標進行的初步實驗，證明了L-RNA FLAP平台設計的可行性，且初步數據相當令人振奮。我們實驗室將持續積極努力，確保本原創且即時研究計畫的順利完成。相信本計畫成果將對rG4的檢測與監測技術推進帶來重大貢獻，並豐富我們對rG4在生物學中功能與調控機制的認識。

11101725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11101725.value: 透過有源電極陣列施加硬腦膜外電刺激以緩和失聰性耳鳴

11101725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101725.value: Hearing involves the transduction of air pressure waves into electrical impulses as sounds are processed from the peripheral cochlea to the central auditory cortex. Peripheral damage to cochlear hair cells due to hearing loss generates phantom sound in the central nervous system, which is referred to as hearing loss-induced tinnitus. The auditory cortex plays an essential role in both normal and phantom sound perception. Owing to its accessible location, the auditory cortex has been targeted for neurostimulation to modulate sound perception. We developed an electrocorticography (ECoG) array that is placed on the cortical surface to enable sequential or simultaneous recording and stimulation of the auditory (i.e., tonotopic) region. Our previous work demonstrated that such cortical surface stimulation using a passive ECoG electrode array can alleviate hearing loss-induced tinnitus in rodents. However, the experiments were carried out on the subdural surface after the surgical removal of the dura mater, causing edema, cerebral hemorrhage, and inflammation during and after surgery, which limits the clinical implementation of such stimulation. Therefore, we recently developed a molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)-based active ECoG array for high-resolution recording and stimulation of the epidural surface. In the proposed study, we will test our hypothesis that electrotherapy via the active transistor array can effectively modulate cortical responses and sound perception on the epidural surface. If validated, this approach will offer a less invasive and more biocompatible alternative to existing methods. The adoption of this advanced approach is expected to result in the development of a clinically relevant neural implant that will enable high-resolution recording and stimulation of the epidural surface, providing a foundation for treating various sensorimotor and neuropsychiatric disorders, such as epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, schizophrenia, neuropathic pain, and depression. 聽覺是聲音傳入耳蝸後，氣壓波轉化成電脈衝，並傳送到中樞聽覺皮層所產生的感覺。聽力損失造成的耳蝸毛細胞周邊損傷會致使中樞神經系統產生幻聽，即失聰性耳鳴。聽覺皮層在正常及幻聽的聲音感知中都有關鍵作用。由於聽覺皮層的位置較易觸及並接受電刺激，其已被應用於調控聲音感知中。本研究組研發了一款置於大腦皮層表面的腦皮層電圖（ECoG）陣列，可以對聽覺區域進行腦電波記錄及神經刺激，並容許兩者交替或同步進行。本研究組早前的研究證明，這種皮層表面電刺激能有效減輕嚙齒類動物的失聰性耳鳴。但是上述實驗均在硬腦膜下進行，手術期間及術後容易出現腦水腫、腦出血和發炎，限制了其臨床應用可行性。本研究組近日研發了一款先進的ECoG有源陣列。此項研究將驗證本研究組的假說：透過有源陣列在硬腦膜外表面施行電療，能有效調節皮層反應及聲音感知。若獲證實，此技術將具備更低侵入性與更佳生物相容性的優點。此先進方案有望成為臨床相關的神經植入裝置，實現硬腦膜外表面的高解析度記錄與電刺激，為治療多種感知運動和神經性精神疾病奠定基礎，例如癲癇、柏金遜症、阿茲海默症、思覺失調、神經痛及抑鬱症等等。

11102125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11102125.value: Lis1在骨骼發育及骨折收復的功能研究

11102125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102125.value: The aim of this project is to determine the functional roles of Lis1 in protein trafficking and signaling modulation during bone development and fracture repair, thereby aid a better therapeutic intervention for treating osteoporosis and osteoporotic bone fracture. Osteoporosis is a major health problem in the world. Age-related bone loss is very common but therapeutic strategies that result in a complete cure is currently missing. This is due to ineffective intervention for making new bones. Lis1 is implicated in regulating intracellular protein complex trafficking. Its function in cellular signaling transduction is not fully elucidated. The mechanistic functions of Lis in endochondral bone formation and homeostasis are unknown as genetic deletion of Lis1 in early limb mesenchyme results in a complete loss of chondrogenesis in both forelimbs and hindlimbs in the embryos. Specifically, it is unclear what’s the function of Lis1 during osteoblast differentiation and whether it promotes new bone formation. Our preliminary results demonstrated a high expression of Lis1 in osteoblast differentiation suggesting its requirement in new bone formation. Based on these observations, we propose to study in detail Lis1 functions and dissect its mechanistic actions whether through regulating intracellular protein trafficking and modulating signaling transduction. Our long-term goal is to identify new modulators that promote new bone formation, which can be further developed as effective drugs that will efficiently enhance de novo bone formation in osteoporosis or osteoporotic bone fracture. The central hypothesis is that Lis1 facilitates osteoblast differentiation through modulation of canonical Wnt signaling activity. Based on our preliminary results, the open question is how organelle functions of Lis1 regulate the stability and activity of b-catenin. To address this, we hypothesize that Lis1 targets the destruction complex and alters the availability of b-catenin. Our work will define the mechanistic control of canonical Wnt signaling by Lis1 and shed new insights to the signaling regulation of bone development and fracture repair. The hypothesis will be tested by pursuing the following specific aims: 1) To determine the functional roles of Lis1 in bone development 2) To elucidate the molecular mechanisms of Lis1 during endochondral bone formation 3) To examine the roles of Lis1 during bone fracture repair The proposed research is significant because it is expected to advance the understanding of skeletal biology in regulating the process of new bone formation. The knowledge will aid the development of new drugs that promotes de novo bone formation. 本項目的目標在於確定Lis1蛋白在骨骼發育與骨折修復過程中，對於蛋白質運輸與信號調控的功能性角色，從而為骨質疏鬆症及骨質疏鬆性骨折提供更佳治療方案。骨質疏鬆症是全球重大健康問題，雖年齡相關骨流失現象普遍，但目前仍缺乏能完全治癒的治療策略，此因現有療法難以有效促進新骨形成。已知Lis1參與調控細胞內蛋白複合體運輸，但其在細胞信號傳導中的功能尚未完全闡明。由於在胚胎肢體間質細胞中早期刪除Lis1基因會導致前後肢軟骨生成完全缺失，Lis1在軟骨內成骨與骨穩態中的機製作用仍屬未知。特別是Lis1在成骨細胞分化過程中的具體功能，以及是否具有促進新骨形成的作用尚不明確。我們的初步研究顯示Lis1在成骨細胞分化過程中高度表達，暗示其為新骨形成所需。基於這些發現，我們擬深入研究Lis1功能，並解析其是否通過調控細胞內蛋白運輸與信號傳導來發揮作用機制。我們的長期目標是找出能促進新骨形成的新型調節因子，進一步開發成可有效增強骨質疏鬆症或骨質疏鬆性骨折患者新生骨形成的藥物。 核心假說認為：Lis1通過調節典型Wnt信號通路活性來促進成骨細胞分化。根據初步結果，現存關鍵問題是Lis1的細胞器功能如何調控β-連環蛋白的穩定性與活性。為此我們提出假設：Lis1作用於降解複合體並改變β-連環蛋白的可利用性。本研究將闡明Lis1對典型Wnt信號通路的機製性調控，為骨骼發育與骨折修復的信號調節提供新見解。我們將通過以下具體目標驗證假說： 確定Lis1在骨骼發育中的功能性角色 闡明Lis1在軟骨內成骨過程中的分子機制 檢驗Lis1在骨折修復中的作用 本研究的重大意義在於可望推進對骨骼生物學中新骨形成調控機制的理解，此知識將有助開發促進新生骨形成的新型藥物。

11103025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103025.value: 多巴胺透過初級運動皮質中的星形膠質細胞調控運動學習

11103025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103025.value: Movement is essential to all our behaviors, from manipulating objects with our hands and expressing emotions, to the locomotion needed for defense, seeking food, and finding shelter. Motor learning is the process by which organisms acquire and refine motor skills through practice. It is characterized by progressively more efficient and precise movements over time and faster response and completion times. Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying motor learning is critical, as it plays a key role not only in daily activities but also in rehabilitation for neurological conditions such as stroke, brain injury and neurodegenerative diseases. However, our knowledge of how higher animals acquire motor skills is still rudimentary. Recent research has unveiled important roles of astrocytes in brain functions that were previously underestimated. They are now recognized as active participants in various critical processes in the brain, including neural plasticity. In our preliminary studies, we explored the calcium dynamics of astrocytes in the primary motor cortex, a key area for motor control and learning, and revealed a potential role of astrocytic calcium activity in motor learning. This astrocytic activity is closely correlated with neuronal firing, and is responsive to dopamine release originating from the midbrain ventral tegmental area (VTA). In this proposal, we hypothesize that astrocytes play a crucial role in processing action and outcome of motor action critical for motor learning, which depends on dopaminergic input from VTA. We aim to further our preliminary findings to fully explore the roles of dopamine on astrocytes in motor learning. Specifically, during the learning process, we will 1) elucidate the essential features of astrocytic calcium activity critical for motor learning, 2) characterize dopamine release dynamics in M1 during the process, 3) elaborate the relationship between dopamine signaling and astrocytic calcium activity, and finally 4) establish the causal relationship of astrocytic dopamine signaling with motor learning and neuronal signaling. To achieve these objectives, new generation of highly sensitive dopamine sensor, simultaneous two-photon imaging and astrocyte-specific dopamine receptor knockdown techniques are employed to generate real-time and high spatial resolution imaging results in behaving animals necessary for proving the hypothesis. By studying astrocytes and their role in motor learning, we can unlock new pathways for medical and technological advancements that benefit society at different levels. This research holds the promise of transforming how we understand and enhance motor functions, leading to significant improvements in health and human performance in the long term. 運動對我們所有的行為都是不可或缺的，無論是用手操作物品、表達情感，還是為了防禦、覓食和尋找庇護所需的移動。動作學習是生物透過練習獲得並精進動作技能的過程，其特徵是隨著時間推移，動作變得越來越高效且精準，反應與完成的速度也更快。理解動作學習背後的神經機制至關重要，因為它不僅在日常活動中扮演關鍵角色，也在中風、腦部損傷及神經退化性疾病等神經系統疾病的復健中發揮重要作用。然而，我們對高等動物如何習得動作技能的認識仍然非常初步。 近期研究揭示了星形膠質細胞在大腦功能中扮演的重要角色，這些角色過去常被低估。如今，它們被認為是多項大腦關鍵過程中的積極參與者，包括神經可塑性。在我們的初步研究中，我們探討了初級運動皮質中星形膠質細胞的鈣離子動態，該區域是運動控制與學習的關鍵部位，並揭示了星形膠質細胞鈣活性在運動學習中的潛在作用。這種星形膠質細胞的活性與神經元放電密切相關，並對源自中腦腹側被蓋區（VTA）的多巴胺釋放具有反應性。在本研究提案中，我們假設星形膠質細胞在處理運動行為的動作與結果方面扮演關鍵角色，這對運動學習至關重要，並依賴來自VTA的多巴胺輸入。 我們的目標是進一步拓展初步研究成果，全面探討多巴胺在星形膠質細胞於運動學習中的作用。具體而言，在學習過程中，我們將： 1）闡明星形膠質細胞鈣離子活性對運動學習至關重要的基本特徵； 2）描繪在初級運動皮質（M1）中多巴胺釋放的動態變化； 3）詳述多巴胺訊號與星形膠質細胞鈣活性之間的關係； 4）建立星形膠質細胞多巴胺訊號與運動學習及神經元訊號之間的因果關係。為達成這些研究目標，我們將採用新一代高靈敏度多巴胺感測器、同步雙光子成像技術，以及星形膠質細胞專一性多巴胺受體抑制技術，以在行為動物中獲得即時且高空間解析度的影像結果，以驗證我們的研究假設。 透過研究星形膠質細胞及其在運動學習中的角色，我們能開啟醫療與科技發展的新途徑，造福社會各個層面。此項研究有望徹底改變我們對運動功能的理解與強化方式，從而在長期內促進健康與人類表現的重大提升。

11103225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103225.value: 花青素是丁香假單胞菌調節毒力和生物膜的宿主信號

11103225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103225.value: Pseudomonas syringae is a widespread plant pathogen, causing huge economic losses and presenting a threat to food security worldwide. Like many other Gram-negative pathogens, P. syringae uses its type III secretion system (T3SS) to invade host plants and cause lethal diseases. Although a number of components have been identified to regulate T3SS, how the bacterium senses host signal(s) and further transduces the signal(s) to the known regulatory factors remain largely unknown. We have recently identified a novel host signal, cyanidin, which directly binds and activates the two-component system RhpRS and thus inhibits T3SS as well as biofilm of P. syringae. Pro40 in the N-terminal sensor domain and Pro89 in the HAMP domain of RhpS play essential roles in cyanidin perception. Based on these preliminary results, we propose a novel signaling pathway of cyanidin-RhpRS-T3SS/biofilm, whose verification is the focus of the proposal. Genetic and biochemical characterizations of this novel signaling pathway is the first step toward identifying signals to which the T3SS responds, and toward the development of new strategies for disease control based on T3SS manipulation. Our long-term goal is to leverage the outcomes of the herein proposed studies to develop better therapies against P. syringae infection. 丁香假單胞菌是一種廣泛存在的植物病原菌，造成巨大的經濟損失，並對全球糧食安全構成威脅。與許多其他革蘭氏陰性病原菌一樣，丁香假單胞菌利用其III型分泌繫統（T3SS）入侵宿主植物並引髮緻命疾病。儘管已鑒定出多種調控III型分泌繫統的成分，但該細菌如何感知宿主信號並進一步將信號傳遞給已知的調控因子，目前仍不清楚。我們最近鑒定出一種新的宿主信號花青素，它可以直接結合並激活雙組分繫統RhpRS，從而抑製丁香假單胞菌的III型分泌繫統和生物膜。RhpRS的N端傳感結構域中的Pro40和HAMP結構域中的Pro89在花青素感知中起着至關重要的作用。基於這些初步結果，我們提出了一種新的信號通路：花青素-RhpRS-T3SS/生物膜，其驗証是本研究的重點。對該新信號通路的遺傳和生化表徵是識別T3SS響應信號，以及開髮基於T3SS調控的新型疾病控製策略的第一步。我們的長期目標是利用本研究的成果，開髮更有效的丁香假單胞菌感染治療方法。

11103325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103325.value: 多组学方法研究视网膜色素上皮分泌因子在出生后小鼠眼球大小决定中的作用

11103325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103325.value: Human eye size is determined by genetic factors and modulated by environmental factors. Given the complex structure of the human eye, eye size determination cannot be accomplished by a single ocular tissue; rather, it is a synchronized process that involves cross-tissue signaling. Previous research, including our own study, suggests that the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) plays a crucial role in eye size determination. The RPE is the source of various growth factors and is involved in influencing the sclera, the outer structural layer of the eye globe. However, there is a gap in our knowledge regarding the specific signaling molecules that mediate communications between the RPE and the sclera. In a preliminary study, we conducted an RNA-seq analysis of the RPE in neonatal mice during the first month of postnatal development. This period is significant because it marks a transition from rapid to slower eye growth in size. Our findings revealed that Wnt2, a canonical Wnt ligand, is specifically expressed in the RPE of neonatal mouse eyes and that its expression decreases rapidly from birth to one month of age. Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated Wnt2 overexpression in the RPE led to increased eye size in mice. The enlarged eye was primarily attributed to an expansion of the vitreous chamber, while the retinal structure remained relatively normal. In this proposed study, we will test the hypothesis that RPE-derived Wnt2 acts on the sclera to promote eye growth during normal animal development and in the progression of myopia. To demonstrate that the sclera is the target of Wnt2, we will directly activate downstream signaling pathways of Wnt in the sclera and examine the effects of Wnt2 on the recipient scleral tissue using proteomic analyses. In addition, this proposal will take an unbiased approach to characterize the RPE-to-sclera secretome in mice to identify other eye size-regulating signaling proteins for further investigation. Overall, we believe that this proposed study will provide valuable insights into the role of RPE-derived Wnt2 in determining eye size and help uncover additional signaling proteins involved in regulating eye size. 人類眼球的大小受基因和環境的共同影響。由於眼睛由許多相互關聯的部分組成，其大小的決定並非由單一部分完成，而是需要不同眼部組織之間的協作。在這個過程中，一個重要的參與者是視網膜色素上皮（RPE），它是一層特殊的細胞。RPE會產生一些生長信號，幫助調節鞏膜（眼球外層的堅韌部分）的大小。然而，目前我們還不完全清楚哪些特定的分子幫助RPE與鞏膜溝通來控制眼球大小。在一項早期研究中，我們觀察了新生小鼠在出生後第一個月內的RPE——這一階段眼球的生長快速，然後逐漸減緩。我們發現，RPE在新生小鼠中會產生一種稱為Wnt2的分子，但在出生後一個月內，其水平顯著下降。當我們利用病毒技術在RPE中人工提高Wnt2水平時，小鼠的眼球變大了，主要是因為眼球中間的玻璃體腔擴張，而視網膜結構則基本保持正常。在這項研究中，我們想要驗證RPE產生的Wnt2是否通過向鞏膜發送信號來促進正常發育中的眼球生長，以及是否與近視等疾病相關。我們還計劃直接激活鞏膜中的Wnt相關通路，觀察其反應，並識別可能參與調節眼球大小的其他重要蛋白。最終，這項研究可能讓我們更好地理解RPE在眼球大小決定中的作用，並幫助我們發現其他相關的分子。這些發現有望為近視等眼球生長相關疾病提供更好的管理方法。

11103625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103625.value: 开发融合肿瘤相关巨噬细胞与生物膜动态的微流控模型

11103625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103625.value: The relationship between the human genitourinary tract microbiome and the development of genitourinary cancers presents significant implications for patient care and treatment outcomes. While the gastrointestinal microbiota's role in drug metabolism is well-established, emerging evidence indicates that the microbiome may influence cancer treatment responses (Table 1). Cancer patients frequently experience heightened susceptibility to bacterial infections post-chemotherapy, and inappropriate antibiotic treatments can adversely affect prognosis and survival rates. Bacterial-induced inflammation can promote or inhibit cancer progression, underscoring the complexity of microbiome interactions. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) within the tumor microenvironment are crucial mediators, exhibiting changes that can either enhance or diminish the efficacy of cancer therapies. Despite growing evidence linking bacterial infections to cancer outcomes, effective therapeutic strategies remain underexplored, largely due to unresolved mechanisms governing these interactions. Current in vitro models, primarily relying on 2D cultures of cancer cell lines or bacteria, fail to capture the intricate dynamics between tumors and their microenvironments. Although animal models provide better physiological relevance, they often do not translate well to human patients due to differences in biological pathways. Based on the pioneering microfluidic inflammatory bacteria-tumor model developed, this proposal aims to integrate TAMs to explore how bacterial distribution affects immunomodulation and treatment responses within the tumor microenvironment. Our research will specifically investigate the impact of biofilm-induced inflammation on TAM polarization, shifting from a pro-inflammatory M1-like state to an anti-inflammatory, pro-tumor M2-like state. We have identified a promising combinatorial treatment strategy that pairs photodynamic therapy (PDT) with chemotherapy, which may enhance therapeutic effectiveness for cancer patients with concurrent bacterial infections. Our objectives include clarifying how biofilm-mediated inflammation influences tumor progression and resistance to treatment. This understanding will inform the development of integrated anti-biofilm and immunotherapy approaches for clinical trials. We will rigorously assess drug responses in the inflammatory tumor model for genitourinary malignancies, focusing on critical parameters such as apoptosis susceptibility, cell viability, and the emergence of drug-resistant and metastatic populations. By incorporating machine learning for automated analysis of experimental outcomes, we aim to facilitate the translation of our findings into clinical practice. Our research has the potential to significantly improve point-of-care testing and treatment strategies for cancer patients impacted by bacterial infections. Ultimately, these advancements could lead to more accurate diagnoses, personalized treatment plans, and, most importantly, improved overall survival rates for patients battling genitourinary cancers. 泌尿生殖道微生物组与泌尿生殖系统癌症的发生及治疗反应之间的关系，正日益受到关注，并对患者护理及治疗成效具有深远影响。尽管胃肠道微生物在药物代谢中的作用已广为人知，最新研究显示微生物组亦可能影响癌症治疗的疗效。癌症患者在化疗后常出现细菌感染风险上升，若使用抗生素不当，可能导致预后恶化及生存率下降。细菌诱导的炎症既可促进亦可抑制肿瘤进展，反映微生物组与肿瘤之间的复杂交互作用。 肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAMs）在肿瘤微环境中扮演关键角色，其极化状态可显著影响治疗反应。然而，目前对细菌感染与癌症治疗之间机制的理解仍有限，现有体外模型（如二维细胞培养）无法准确模拟肿瘤与微环境的真实互动，动物模型亦因物种差异而难以完全转化至临床。 本研究拟基于先前开发的微流控炎症性细菌-肿瘤模型，进一步整合TAMs，系统探讨生物膜诱导的炎症如何影响TAM极化及肿瘤治疗反应。研究将重点分析TAMs由促炎性M1样状态向抗炎性、促肿瘤的M2样状态转化的机制，并评估光动力疗法（PDT）联合化疗的治疗潜力，特别针对伴随细菌感染的泌尿生殖系统癌症患者。 研究目标包括：阐明生物膜介导的炎症如何影响肿瘤进展与治疗抗性；评估联合治疗策略在细胞凋亡、细胞活力及耐药性与转移性细胞群方面的疗效；并利用机器学习技术自动分析实验结果，以加快研究成果的临床转化。本研究有望推动个性化治疗策略的发展，提升诊断准确性与治疗成效，从而改善泌尿生殖系统癌症患者的整体生存率。

11103825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103825.value: 血管内皮细胞表达的TGF-β2参与动脉粥样硬化发生发展的机制研究

11103825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11103825.value: Dr He, Lei Dr Wang, Li

11103825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103825.value: The transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) family comprises three isoforms, namely TGF-β1, TGF-β2, and TGF-β3. They play significant roles in inflammation, tissue repair and fibrosis. The involvement of these isoforms in the development of atherosclerosis is fascinatingly complex and context- or cell type-dependent. They can exert either a protective or detrimental effect. The results from existing literature provide clear indication that different isoforms are likely to exert distinct effects. Further investigation of the intricate functions of TGF-β isoforms in the vasculature will undoubtedly provide insights into new therapeutic approaches for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerotic vascular diseases. The endothelial cells lining in the interior of vessels are directly exposed to physical and chemical stimuli. This exposure allows us to comprehend how endothelial cell dysfunction represents the most important initiator of atherosclerosis. In our preliminary study, we conducted a reanalysis of our single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data, which yielded an intriguing observation. Our findings indicate that TGF-β signaling and its associated endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition are significantly enriched in endothelial cells of ApoE-/- mice. Furthermore, we observed elevated TGF-β2 expression in endothelial layers of plaque lesions in human arteries and mouse aortas relative to plaque-free arteries. This suggests that TGF-β2 may be a key player in the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis. Nevertheless, there is still so much to be discovered regarding the precise function of endothelial TGF-β2 activation in conjunction with other proinflammatory cytokines in atherogenesis. The principal objective of this project is to investigate molecular mechanisms through which TGF-β2 activation plays a critical role in endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory responses at the onset and progression of atherosclerosis. To this end, the project will pursue the following three objectives, which are inter-connected and of great interest: (1) To investigate the role of endothelial TGF-β2 in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. (2) To investigate the mechanisms underlying TGF-β2-induced inflammatory responses in endothelial cells (3) To investigate the mechanisms by which shear stress regulates the expression of endothelial TGF-β2 and to screen anti-atherosclerotic TGF-β2 inhibitors As a logical extension of our previous research on atherosclerosis, the new findings from this project will provide invaluable insights into the potential development of TGF-β2-targeted therapeutic strategies against atherosclerotic vascular disease, which could have a significant impact on public health. 轉化生長因子-β（TGF-β）家族包含三個亞型：TGF-β1、TGF-β2 和 TGF-β3。它們在炎症、組織修復和纖維化過程中扮演著重要角色。這些亞型在動脈粥狀硬化發病機制中的作用極為複雜，具有環境或細胞類型依賴性，可能產生保護性或有害效應。現有文獻表明，不同亞型可能發揮不同的作用。深入研究 TGF-β 亞型在血管組織中的複雜功能，無疑將為動脈粥狀硬化性血管疾病的預防和治療提供新的策略。 血管內皮細胞直接暴露於物理和化學刺激之下，這使得內皮細胞功能障礙成為誘導動脈粥狀硬化的關鍵起始因子。我們的初步研究結果顯示，單細胞 RNA 測序和批量 RNA 測序數據均表明，TGF-β 信號通路及其相關的內皮細胞向間質細胞轉化（EndMT）在 ApoE-/- 小鼠的內皮細胞中顯著富集。此外，在患者股動脈和小鼠主動脈的斑塊病變內皮層中，TGF-β2的表達量相較於無斑塊動脈也顯著升高。這表明 TGF-β2可能是動脈粥狀硬化發生和進展的關鍵因素。然而，關於內皮細胞TGF-β2如何被激活，及其與其他促炎細胞因子在動脈粥樣硬化發生中的確切功能，仍存在許多研究空白。 本計畫的首要目標是闡明 TGF-β2水平升高，在動脈粥樣硬化發生和進展的初期及過程中，透過哪些分子機制對內皮功能障礙和炎症反應發揮關鍵作用。為此，本計畫設定了以下三個相互關聯且極具價值的研究目標： (1)探討內皮細胞 TGF-β2在動脈粥樣硬化發病機制中的作用。 (2)闡明TGF-β2誘導內皮細胞炎症反應的機制。 (3)研究剪切應力調節內皮細胞 TGF-β2 表達的機制，並篩選具有抗動脈粥樣硬化潛力的TGF-β2抑制劑。 作為我們先前動脈粥狀硬化研究的邏輯延伸，本計畫的新發現將為開發靶向 TGF-β2 的治療策略提供寶貴見解，並可能對公共衛生產生深遠影響。

11104225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11104225.value: 環境相關條件下微/納塑膠對魚類血液、大腦和肝臟系統的影響

11104225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104225.value: Negotiation for a global treaty on plastic pollution is currently ongoing, and public concerns about microplastics in the environment are escalating, which triggers considerable worries about their impacts on human and environmental health. In the natural environment, plastic pollutants undergo various physical, chemical, and biological processes that lead to plastic fragmentation into micro- or nano-scale particles (known as micro/nanoplastics, MNPs). MNPs have become ubiquitous and have been discovered in numerous environments globally and are also prevalent in our daily lives. They have emerged as significant contaminants, raising critical ecotoxicological concerns. Because the toxicity of MNPs is closely linked to their locations within organisms, it is necessary to develop specific experimental protocols and techniques tailored for MNPs, such as bioimaging technologies. While many studies have shown the impacts of MNPs on gastrointestinal tracts and gills as the first uptake sites, much remains to be examined regarding their impacts on other critical organs, especially when coupled with bioaccumulation. With our recent discoveries of the rapid and efficient transport of MNPs to different organs following blood circulation, this proposal intends to examine the impacts of MNPs on three critical organs in fish: the heart, liver, and brain. Specifically, we will 1) evaluate the significance of blood as a central delivery system and develop fish blood as a biomarker response platform; 2) conduct expansion microscopy (ExM) bioimaging of MNPs impacts on fish organ development at the nanoscale cellular level; and 3) diagnose the impacts of MNPs on fish cardiovascular function, neurobehavior, and liver metabolism and function. The strength of this project will be the application of various cutting-edge technologies under environmentally relevant conditions, as well as directly coupling biokinetics with the identified toxicity, which is now critically needed in our environmental risk assessments of MNPs. One of our goals is to develop a sensitive platform to rapidly assess the impacts of MNPs in fish systems. By developing various sensitive detection methods, this proposal will be able to reveal the critical impacts of MNPs on specific fish organs at the cellular, biochemical, physiological, and behavioral levels following blood transport. It is anticipated that this project will significantly contribute to our understanding and prediction of the risks posed by MNPs in aquatic environments. The results will aid in the formulation of effective strategies to manage plastic input into the environment, providing the public with scientifically sound and reliable information on MNPs risks in the environment. 目前全球塑膠條約的談判正在進行中，公眾對環境中微塑膠的擔憂正在升級，這引發了人們對其對人類和環境健康影響的相當大的擔憂。在自然環境中，塑膠污染物經歷各種物理、化學和生物過程，導致塑膠破碎成微米或納米級顆粒（稱為微/納米塑膠，MNP）。MNP 已變得無處不在，並在全球眾多環境中被發現，在我們的日常生活中也很普遍。它們已成為重要的污染物，引發了嚴重的生態毒理學問題。由於 MNP 的毒性與其在生物體內的位置密切相關，因此有必要開發針對 MNP 量身定製的特定實驗技術，例如生物成像技術。雖然許多研究表明 MNP 對胃腸道和鰓作為第一個攝取部位的影響，但關於它們對其他關鍵器官的影響，特別是當與生物積累相結合時，還有很多待研究。本项目提出研究 MNP 對魚類三個關鍵器官（心臟、肝臟和大腦）的影響。具體來說，我們將 1）評估血液作為中央輸送系統的重要性，並開發魚血作為生物標誌物反應平臺; 2）在納米級細胞水準上對MNPs對魚類器官發育的影響進行扩张顯微鏡（ExM）生物成像; 3）診斷 MNP 對魚類心血管功能、神經行為以及肝臟代謝和功能的影響。 該項目的優勢在於在環境相關條件下應用各種尖端技術，以及將生物動力學與已確定的毒性直接耦合，這是我們對 MNP 的環境風險評估現在迫切需要的。通過開發各種靈敏的檢測方法，本项目將能夠揭示 MNP 在血液運輸后細胞、生化、生理和行為水準上對特定魚類器官的關鍵影響，对我們了解和預測 MNP 在水生環境中帶來的風險做出貢獻。研究結果將有助於制定有效的策略來管理塑膠對環境的輸入，為公眾提供有關 MNP 在環境中的風險的科學可靠資訊。

11104325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11104325.value: 近親繁殖對香港水域瀕危印度太平洋江豚寄生蟲感染負荷造成的影響

11104325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11104325.value: Prof BOWMAN, Dwight Douglas Dr Martelli, Paolo Dr McGowen, Michael R

11104325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104325.value: Indo-Pacific finless porpoise is one of the two resident cetacean species in Hong Kong waters. They have small population size and very low natural rate of population growth, and frequent reports of stranding, in face of various natural and anthropogenic stressors. Previous studies indicated that Indo-Pacific finless porpoises in Hong Kong and Pearl River Estuary water are genetically diverged and isolated from adjacent populations. This raises concerns over their limited genotypic diversity, likely a consequence of inbreeding within a small and isolated population, which can lead to detrimental consequences on their direct and reproductive fitness. Consistent with the hypothesis that reduced genotypic diversity often leads to increased susceptibility to pathogens, previous work by the project team reported that parasites were commonly found in the respiratory and reproductive systems of stranded finless porpoises, with impact on the direct survivorship and reproductive success on these animals. Bioinformatic tools covering genome-wide datasets are now available for revealing single nucleotide polymorphisms that may drive physiological adaptation in wildlife populations. This project aims to investigate the impact of inbreeding and decreased genotypic diversity in relation to susceptibility to parasites in Indo-Pacific finless porpoises in Hong Kong waters. With diverse expertise of the project team, stranded finless porpoise carcasses will be examined by radiological (i.e., virtopsy) and conventional methods (i.e., necropsy and parasitological studies) to assess the prevalence and load of parasitic infection across the years 2014−2028. Genomic data will be extracted and analysed to determine the level of inbreeding and genotypic diversity in each finless porpoise. The association between parasitic load and level of inbreeding will be investigated to evaluate the impact of inbreeding in Indo-Pacific finless porpoises in Hong Kong. Specific genetic background associated with increase susceptibility to parasitic infection will also be explored. This project will fill important knowledge gaps on population genetics and parasitology of finless porpoises, providing valuable insights on the sustainability of the local Indo-Pacific finless porpoise population. Project findings will also contribute essential data for defining the management unit of finless porpoises in Hong Kong and adjacent waters, as well as provide baseline data for long-term monitoring, which are essential for formulating appropriate evidence-based conservation measures to safeguard this endangered species and the wider marine environment. Through various means of knowledge transfer, the results will benefit both the scientific community and the general public. 印度太平洋江豚是香港水域其中一種「原居豚」。牠們的族群規模小，自然增長率極低，且面臨各種自然和人為威脅，擱淺個案時有出現。昔日的研究顯示，香港及珠江口水域的江豚在遺傳學上異於鄰近族群，這令人懷疑孤立族群內近親繁殖的發生，降低族群內的基因多樣性並影響牠們的健康和繁殖。項目團隊以往曾發現，擱淺江豚的呼吸系統和生殖系統中常有寄生蟲，降低牠們的存活率和繁殖率，此與低基因多樣性可能增加動物對病原體易感性的假設吻合。現有的生物資訊學工具，涵蓋全基因組數據集，可揭示江豚的單核苷酸多態性，這些多態性可能驅動野生動物族群適應環境危害的能力。本項目旨在研究香港水域江豚的近親繁殖和基因多樣性降低與寄生蟲易感性的關係。 憑藉多元化的專業知識，項目團隊將透過影像學（影像解剖）和傳統方法（屍體檢驗、寄生蟲學研究）檢查於香港擱淺江豚的屍體，以評估2014年至2028年間寄生蟲感染的流行率和負荷。項目團隊會提取並分析基因組數據，以鑑定每隻江豚的近親繁殖程度和基因多樣性水平。項目團隊將調查近江豚親繁殖水平與寄生蟲負荷的關聯，以評估近親繁殖對江豚的影響，並探索江豚與寄生蟲易感性相關的特定遺傳背景。本項目將填補有關江豚族群遺傳學和寄生蟲學的知識空缺，為本地江豚族群的可持續性提供重要數據。研究將為定義香港及鄰近水域江豚的管理單位提供寶貴見解，並為長期監測提供基礎數據，對制定合適這個瀕危物種及海洋環境的保育措施至關重要。項目成果亦將透過不同知識傳播方式惠及科學界和公眾。

11105025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11105025.value: 動脈粥樣硬化期間CEP250調控巨噬細胞功能的作用

11105025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11105025.value: Prof Yiu, Kai Hang Prof Yu, Huang

11105025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11105025.value: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by lipid accumulation and immune cell infiltration within the arterial wall. Macrophages are the primary immune cells in atherosclerotic plaques, contributing to disease initiation and progression through polarization, infiltration, and lipid uptake, ultimately turning into foam cells, the primary component of atherosclerotic plaques. Despite significant advances, the molecular mechanisms regulating macrophage behavior during atherosclerosis remain poorly understood. Next-generation sequencing of aortas from ApoE-/- mice revealed that centrosomes are involved in the development of atherosclerosis. GWAS further identified a group of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in CEP250, the centrosomal core component, associated with a higher risk of atherosclerosis. Analyzing the publicly available single-cell sequencing data revealed that CEP250 levels are higher in macrophages from atherosclerotic plaques. Immunostaining of clinical atherosclerotic specimens and aorta from the mouse model of atherosclerosis further confirmed that the CEP250 level is higher in macrophages from plaques. Preliminary studies further revealed that CEP250 overexpression enhances macrophage polarization, migration, and lipid uptake, suggesting a central role for CEP250 in promoting macrophage-driven plaque formation. GSEA enrichment of transcriptome profile indicated CEP250 overexpression activates the mTOR1 pathway, a critical signaling cascade involved in macrophage polarization, transendothelial migration, and lipid uptake. Further study revealed that CEP250 bound and stabilized the autophagy adaptor protein p62/SQSTM1, a key regulator of aggresomes and aggresome-like induced structures, which play a role in the ubiquitination of misfolded proteins. TurboID2 proximity labeling revealed that CEP250 binding proteins are closely related to RHO GTPase. This phenomenon was confirmed by the GSEA Biocarta enrichment of RNA sequencing data from RAW cells overexpressing CEP250, indicating that the CEP250-p62-RHO GTPase pathway might contribute to the phenotypic changes in macrophages during atherogenesis. This study highlights the central role of CEP250 in regulating macrophage function during atherogenesis, establishing a link between centrosome dynamics, inflammation, migration, phagocytosis, and protein homeostasis. These findings have potential applications in atherosclerosis risk assessment and the development of personalized therapies for cardiovascular disease. Understanding how CEP250 influences macrophage function could lead to novel strategies to modulate macrophage activity and reduce inflammation in atherosclerotic plaques. Furthermore, identifying CEP250 as a biomarker could enhance early diagnosis and risk assessment, providing a tool for personalized treatment. The modulation of macrophage activity by CEP250 may also be relevant in other inflammatory diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis, cancer, and metabolic disorders, where macrophage-driven inflammation plays a key role. 動脈粥樣硬化是一種慢性發炎性疾病，其特徵是動脈壁內脂質積聚和免疫細胞浸潤。巨噬細胞作為動脈粥樣硬化斑塊中的主要免疫細胞，透過極化、浸潤和脂質攝取等過程推動疾病發生與進展，最終轉化為泡沫細胞——構成動脈粥樣硬化斑塊的核心成分。儘管研究已取得重大進展，調控巨噬細胞在動脈粥樣硬化過程中行為的分子機制仍未被充分理解。 對ApoE-/-小鼠主動脈的新一代定序分析顯示，中心體參與了動脈粥樣硬化的發展。全基因組關聯分析（GWAS）進一步發現，中心體核心組件CEP250中的一組單核苷酸多態性（SNPs）與動脈粥樣硬化風險升高相關。通過分析公開的單細胞定序數據，發現動脈粥樣硬化斑塊中巨噬細胞的CEP250表達水平顯著上升。臨床動脈粥樣硬化標本及小鼠模型主動脈的免疫染色結果進一步證實，斑塊內巨噬細胞的CEP250表達量更高。初步研究還發現，過度表達CEP250會增強巨噬細胞的極化、遷移和脂質攝取能力，表明CEP250在促進巨噬細胞驅動的斑塊形成中扮演關鍵角色。 轉錄組譜的基因集富集分析（GSEA）顯示，CEP250過度表達會激活mTOR1通路——該信號通路在巨噬細胞極化、跨內皮遷移和脂質攝取過程中至關重要。進一步研究發現，CEP250可結合並穩定自噬銜接蛋白p62/SQSTM1（一種聚集體和類聚集體誘導結構的關鍵調控因子，參與錯誤折疊蛋白的泛素化過程）。TurboID2鄰近標記技術揭示，CEP250的結合蛋白與RHO GTP酶密切相關。這一現象經由對過表達CEP250的RAW細胞進行RNA定序數據的GSEA Biocarta富集分析得到證實，表明CEP250-p62-RHO GTP酶通路可能參與動脈粥樣硬化形成過程中巨噬細胞的表型變化。 本研究闡明了CEP250在動脈粥樣硬化形成過程中調控巨噬細胞功能的核心作用，建立了中心體動態變化與發炎反應、細胞遷移、吞噬作用及蛋白質穩態之間的橋樑。這些發現具備應用於動脈粥樣硬化風險評估與心血管疾病個人化治療開發的潛力。理解CEP250調控巨噬細胞功能的機制，或能為調節巨噬細胞活性、減輕斑塊炎症提供新型策略；而將CEP250作為生物標記物，可提升早期診斷與風險評估精準度，為個人化醫療提供工具。此外，CEP250對巨噬細胞活性的調控機制可能延伸至類風濕性關節炎、癌症及代謝性疾病等其他巨噬細胞驅動炎症的疾病領域。

11105125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11105125.value: 運用人工智能引導的行為分類技術研究小鼠模型中腦體細胞突變對圖雷特綜合徵的致病性

11105125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11105125.value: Tourette’s syndrome (TS) is a childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by repetitive and unwanted movements or sounds, called “tics”. TS likely results from disruptions in the cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic-cortical (CBGTC) circuit due to genetic and environmental factors, leading to disinhibition in the motor neural circuits. Although TS has a heritability of approximately 0.77, genome-wide association studies of common mutations have not identified strong signals, indicating a significant role for rare or de novo mutations. In a cohort study, my lab has previously identified a list of somatic mobile element insertions (MEIs) in the brains of TS patients. In comparison to the control individuals, the MEIs identified in TS were enriched in genes associated with post-synaptic membranes. This includes candidates that may be linked to TS, such as three GABAA receptor genes: GABRB3, GABRG3, and GABRA4. Among these, the MEIs in GABRB3 and GABRG3 were widespread somatic mutations that are present in ~1% of brain cells. We will analyze the potential pathogenicity of candidate genes in TS by first developing an AI algorithm to study tic behaviors in mice, and then applying it to investigate the behaviors in mice carrying the specific gene knockdown. We will target the three GABAA receptor genes, and a cilia-associated gene, CFAP47, which also had evidence to be associated with TS. Specifically, we will (1) establish a PTX-induced mouse model with simultaneous recording of behavior, EEG, and EMG signals; (2) design an AI algorithm to distinguish video/audio clips of normal, tic, and seizure behaviors; and (3) utilize CRISPR/Cas9 for in situ gene knockdown of the candidate genes and evaluate mouse behavioral changes. The discovery of a new possible pathway, through somatic disruption of the GABA pathways, could lead to the development of more effective and targeted treatment. In addition, the AI algorithm designed to detect specific TS behaviors can serve as an effective benchmark for evaluating new drug efficacy in future studies. 圖雷特綜合徵（Tourette's syndrome, TS）是一種兒童期發病的神經發育障礙，其特徵表現為重複且不受控制的運動或發聲，稱為「抽動」。該疾病可能源於遺傳與環境因素共同導致的皮層-基底節-丘腦-皮層（CBGTC）神經迴路功能障礙，進而引發運動神經迴路抑制功能缺失。雖然TS的遺傳度約為0.77，但全基因組關聯研究並未在常見突變中發現顯著信號，提示罕見突變或新生突變可能發揮重要作用。 我們實驗室透過隊列研究發現，TS患者大腦中存在一系列體細胞可動元件插入（MEIs）。與對照組相比，TS患者中的MEIs顯著富集於突觸後膜相關基因，包括三個可能與該疾病相關的GABAa受體基因：GABRB3、GABRG3和GABRA4。其中GABRB3和GABRG3基因的MEIs屬於廣泛存在的體細胞突變，約存在於1%的腦細胞中。 我們將透過開發一種人工智能算法研究小鼠抽動行為，進而應用於特定基因敲除小鼠的行為研究，以此分析候選基因在圖雷特綜合徵（TS）中的潛在致病性。研究將聚焦三個GABAA受體基因以及纖毛相關基因CFAP47——該基因已被證實與TS存在關聯。具體研究步驟包括：（1）建立印防己毒素(picrotoxin)誘導的小鼠模型，同步記錄行為學、腦電圖和肌電圖信號；（2）設計人工智能算法以區分正常、抽動和癲癇發作行為的視頻/音頻片段；（3）利用CRISPR/Cas9技術對候選基因進行原位敲除，並評估小鼠行為變化。 透過體細胞突變破壞GABA通路這一新發現的可能路徑，有望推動更高效、更具靶向性的治療方法開發。此外，為檢測特定圖雷特綜合徵行為而設計的人工智能算法，可作為未來研究中評估新藥療效的有效基準工具。

11106125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11106125.value: 鯊魚和魟魚骨骼中的軟骨管： 在獨特且有潛力的組織模型中建立結構-功能關係

11106125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11106125.value: The skeletons of sharks and rays challenge current paradigms in cartilage biology. In these fishes, although the bulk of the skeleton is a cartilage similar to ours, it performs mechanically-similar tasks to bone, provides lifelong skeletal support even in species with lifespans far longer than ours, and has cells that survive even after the matrix mineralizes around them. Moreover, our recent work shows that shark and ray cartilage can be full of blood vessels (unlike adult mammal cartilage) and has ubiquitous growth centers. Together, these distinct aspects of shark and ray cartilage argue it can be a uniquely powerful system for studying cartilage biology. Our limited knowledge of shark and ray cartilage structure and growth, however, has prevented further development of this system towards biomedicine. In this project, we investigate the structure and function of shark and ray cartilage canals, passages that ferry vasculature into the tissue. The presence of these canals in adult animals is, to our knowledge, exceptional in vertebrate animals, suggesting that their persistence could be a key aspect in the resilience and high performance of cartilage in these fishes. The research team is uniquely suited for the work, leveraging the PI’s and collaborators’ extensive experience in shark/ray anatomy and biology, in mammal/avian cartilage canals, and in diverse multi-modal tissue characterization. We will investigate canals from a hierarchical perspective across four research aims: using cutting edge-materials and imaging tools to (1) characterize canal 3D structure from centimeter to nanometer scales and (2) across development of the cartilage, (3) linking structure to function through innovative tissue diffusion studies and (4) investigations of canal variation across shark and ray species. Combined results will provide a novel and integrated understanding of shark and ray cartilage biology, while opening windows into the evolution of skeletal tissues and the health and ecology of ocean keystone species. Further, the physiological perspectives into this extraordinary skeletal tissue will help develop it as a fresh model system for biomedicine, expanding our tissue biology rulebook (e.g. on cartilage lifespan and mechanics), with insights for improving cartilage health (e.g. by inspiring novel implant and scaffold designs). 鯊魚和魟魚的骨骼挑戰了目前的軟骨生物學範式。在這些魚類中，儘管骨架的主要部分是類似我們的軟骨，但它卻能執行類似骨骼的機械任務，即使在壽命比我們長得多的物種中，也能提供終身的骨架支撐，而且即使在周圍的基質礦化後，細胞仍能存活。此外，我們最近的研究顯示，鯊魚和魟魚的軟骨可以充滿血管（不同於成年哺乳類動物的軟骨），並且有無處不在的生長中心。鯊魚和魟魚軟骨的這些獨特之處，使其成為研究軟骨生物學的獨特強大系統。然而，我們對鯊魚與魟魚軟骨結構與生長的有限知識，卻妨礙了這個系統朝向生物醫學的進一步發展。在本專案中，我們研究鯊魚與魟魚軟骨通道的結構與功能，這些通道可將血管帶入組織中。據我們所知，這些軟骨管在成年動物中的存在，在脊椎動物中是獨一無二的，這表明它們的持續存在可能是這些魚類軟骨的彈性和高性能的一個關鍵方面。本研究團隊擁有獨特的優勢，可充分利用首席研究員與合作者在鯊魚/魟魚解剖學與生物學、哺乳類/烏鴉類軟骨管以及多種多模式組織特性分析方面的豐富經驗。我們將從四個研究目標的層次角度來研究軟骨管：使用尖端材料和成像工具來 (1) 描述從厘米到奈米尺度的軟骨管 3D 結構；(2) 跨越軟骨的發展；(3) 透過創新的組織擴散研究將結構與功能連結起來；(4) 研究不同鯊魚和魟魚品種的軟骨管變異。結合這些結果，將可提供對鯊魚和魟魚軟骨生物學的嶄新、完整的了解，同時為骨骼組織的進化以及海洋關鍵物種的健康和生態學，開啟一扇窗戶。此外，從生理學的角度觀察這種非凡的骨骼組織，將有助於將其發展為生物醫學的新模型系統，擴大我們的組織生物學規則（如軟骨壽命和機械學），為改善軟骨健康（如通過啟發新的植入物和支架設計）提供啟示。

11200325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11200325.value: 基於電漿體與數位微流控技術的自動化超高靈敏液體活檢分子分析儀

11200325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200325.value: Cancer is a severe disease with a high mortality rate. For instance, there were 4 million new cases and 2.4 million deaths in 2016 in mainland China; 35,000 new cases and 15,000 deaths in 2019 in Hong Kong. Also, Alzheimer’s disease remains a global health challenge and is among the top 10 causes of death in mainland China. On the other hand, there have been several infectious disease outbreaks in recent years: SARS, H1N1 influenza, MERS, Zika, and COVID. These outbreaks have had significant global impacts, which have been exacerbated by urbanization and population growth. To facilitate early-stage diagnosis and treatment efficacy studies, multiplexed molecular profiling of liquid biopsy is an essential and non-invasive approach that can be applied for longitudinal monitoring. Most commercial systems utilize the 96-well plate platform with costly fluidic pumps and robotic controllers for precise fluidic manipulation, making it difficult to deploy the systems in resource-limited point-of-care (POC) settings or distribute them to a network of labs/clinics/hospitals (less burden on a central lab with faster turnaround time). We need a POC system for multiplexed molecular profiling with high sensitivity, rapid, simple and low cost, enabling widespread dissemination. This proposed project aims to tackle these bottlenecks by employing the synergy of several state-of-the-art technologies (nanoplasmonics, chemifluorescence, immunolabeling, and digital microfluidics) to develop next-generation POC molecular profiler with ultra-high sensitivity, high precision and fast processing time. We will design and fabricate a hybrid nanoplasmonic top plate with localized sensing areas to enhance fluorescence signals based on localized surface plasmonic resonance. Plasmonic resonance and chemifluorescence assay will enhance the sensitivity of molecular profiling. Then, we will integrate the nanoplasmonic top plate into the digital microfluidic device to achieve automation without the need for pumps and robotic arms and fast processing time with a low volume of samples and reagents. Also, we will improve the specificity in immunolabeling and optimize the chemifluorescence assay to reduce background noise and improve precision for molecular profiling in the digital microfluidic device. For case demonstration, we will employ the molecular profiler for multiplexed profiling of cytokines/chemokines and neurology biomarkers, demonstrating an enhanced limit of detection (sub-pg/mL), rapid assay time (< 1 hr) and improved precision (< 10% COV). The platform can also be applied to analyze cells, bacteria, viruses, and extracellular vesicles. Successful completion of the project will establish Hong Kong as a leading hub for biomedical engineering and translational biomedical devices. 癌症是一種嚴重的疾病，具有高死亡率。在2016年，中國大陸新增癌症病例達400萬例，死亡人數達240萬人。在2019年，香港新增病例為35,000例，死亡人數為15,000人。此外，阿茲海默症是全球健康挑戰之一，也是中國大陸十大死因之一。另一方面，近年來出現了多次傳染病爆發，包括SARS、H1N1流感、MERS、ZIKA以及COVID-19。這些疫情對全球造成了重大影響，而城市化與人口增長更進一步加劇了其影響。為了促進疾病早期診斷與治療效果研究，多重分子液體活檢分析是一種重要且非侵入性的方式，可應用於長期監測。目前大多數商業系統採用96孔板平台，並配備昂貴的流體幫浦與機器人控制器以進行精準的流體操作，使得這些系統難以在資源有限的即時診斷環境中部署，或分散至實驗室／診所／醫院網絡中（可減輕中央實驗室負擔並加快結果回報時間）。我們需要一種具備高靈敏度、快速、簡便且低成本的即時診斷系統，用於多重分子分析，以促進廣泛應用。本項目旨在透過多項尖端技術（奈米電漿體、化學螢光、免疫標記與數位微流控技術）的協同作用，開發新一代即時診斷分子分析儀，具備超高靈敏度、高精準度與快速處理能力。我們將設計並製造一種混合奈米電漿體上板，具備局部感測區域，藉由局部表面電漿共振來增強螢光訊號。電漿共振與化學螢光分析將提升分子分析的靈敏度。接著，我們將把奈米電漿體上板整合至數位微流控裝置中，以實現無需幫浦與機械手臂的自動化操作，並以少量樣本與試劑達成快速處理。此外，我們將提升免疫標記的特異性，並優化化學螢光分析，以降低背景雜訊並提升分子分析的精準度。在實例展示中，我們將使用分子分析儀進行細胞激素／趨化因子與神經生物標記的多重分析，展現出增強的檢測極限（低於pg/mL）、快速分析時間（少於1小時）與提升的精準度。此平台亦可應用於細胞、細菌、病毒與細胞外囊泡的分析。若本項目成功完成，將有助於建立香港作為生物醫學工程與轉化醫療設備的領先樞紐地位。

11201325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201325.value: 一種用於自供電機械感測器的壓電離子放大策略

11201325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201325.value: Applications such as environmental monitoring, implantable biosensors, and security are major driving forces for deploying large numbers of interoperating sensors. Often, these sensor nodes are distributed across vast areas or implanted in inaccessible locations, making it crucial for them to operate independently, sustainably, and without maintenance. However, most current sensors require power sources, posing significant challenges. For instance, replacing batteries in devices implanted in the body or located in remote areas can be inconvenient or even prohibitive. Additionally, the chemicals used in batteries are often environmentally unfriendly. Therefore, achieving self-powered operation for sensors is critically important for a wide range of applications from both economic and sustainability perspectives. One straightforward strategy is for the sensor to generate an electrical signal in response to an environmental stimulus. These "generative sensors" can operate without batteries. Piezoionic sensors are emerging as a major class of devices that offer such self-powered pressure-sensing capabilities. Although significant advances have been made in the microstructure, composition, and biocompatibility of piezoionic pressure sensors, no strategy has been proposed to amplify the ionic separation that ultimately leads to a larger piezoionic voltage output. In this project, we propose to enhance the voltage response of piezoionic pressure sensors through piezoionic amplification. This amplification can be achieved by increasing the difference in mobility between anions and cations. A key innovative aspect of this project is the explicit enhancement of pressure-induced ionic separation, which has not been previously reported. To realize this strategy, we propose using crown ether, a ring-shaped molecule specifically selected to diameter-match the ionic carrier (e.g., Na+) to assist in solvation, thereby enhancing ionic mobility. We plan to undertake four main tasks: (1) materials synthesis, (2) piezoionic amplification engineering, (3) device fabrication, and (4) application demonstration. To substantiate feasibility, our research methodology is supported by extensive preliminary results. Preliminary experiments have already shown a 30-fold piezoionic amplification in a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel system due to crown ether grafting, which is highly encouraging and will be further improved in this project. The successful completion of this project will lead to an effective approach for developing mechanical sensors and piezoionic devices that are simultaneously soft and highly sensitive. Most importantly, the ability for sensors to be self-powered will eliminate system complexity, operational overhead, and environmental impacts associated with battery-powered operation. The capabilities achieved will enable advanced designs and new applications in wearable electronics, personal health monitoring, soft robotics, and beyond.

11201525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201525.value: 核反应堆稠密栅燃料棒束模型内多维两相流参数的先进实验和模拟

11201525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201525.value: In 2015 the Paris Agreement established a goal of limiting the global average temperature increase from pre-industrial times to a level well below 2 °C, with an objective of 1.5 °C. The 2023 United Nations Climate Change Conference formally stated the indispensable role of nuclear energy in meeting the goals of the Paris Agreement. As of January 2024, 25 countries had agreed to triple global nuclear power capacity by 2050 compared to 2020. It is foreseeable that nuclear energy will experience rapid growth globally over the next three decades. The key to increasing the amount of nuclear power generation is to increase the power output of existing nuclear reactors as well as to build new reactors. In the fuel assembly of a nuclear reactor, fuel rods are typically arranged in arrays of 8 × 8 (boiling water reactor) or 17 × 17 (pressurized water reactor). If the number of fuel rods per fuel assembly is increased using an advanced fuel rod bundle design with a tight-lattice core, the power output of the fuel assembly will be 5-to-20 % greater than that of a conventional fuel assembly for the same surface heat flux per fuel rod. The increased number of fuel rods per fuel assembly increases the uranium weight per fuel assembly, allowing for more efficient long-term operation cycles. Furthermore, the advanced fuel rod bundle design increases the fuel density of a fuel assembly, resulting in reduced neutron leakage from the reactor core. Thus, nuclear fuel will be burnt efficiently, contributing to nuclear waste reduction by improving the neutron economy. In light water reactors, a steam-water two-phase mixture flowing through a nuclear reactor core plays a critical role in nuclear safety through fuel rod cooling and controlling nuclear chain reactions by moderating neutron energy during normal operations and nuclear accident conditions. Optimized thermal-hydraulic design of the advanced fuel rod bundle requires a robust two-phase flow numerical simulation code well validated by experimental data. However, no systematic highly spatially-resolved two-phase flow database in a tight-lattice core is available. The proposed project aims to measure highly spatially-resolved two-phase flow dynamics in a simulated advanced nuclear fuel rod bundle with a tight-lattice configuration. The established database is used to develop high-fidelity constitutive equations in a numerical simulation code. The developed models and established database will substantially improve the fidelity of numerical simulation codes, which significantly contributes to safe and economical nuclear reactor design. 2015年《巴黎协定》确立把全球平均气温较工业化之前气温的温升控制在2 °C之内，并为把升温控制在1.5 °C之内而努力。在2023年联合国气候变化大会上，正式确认了核能在实现《巴黎协定》目标中的关键作用。截至2024年1月，已有25个国家承诺在2050年前将全球核电装机容量较2020年提升三倍。可以预期，在未来三十年内，全球核能将迎来显著增长。 实现核能发电量持续增长的关键在于提升现有核反应堆的功率输出，并加快新建反应堆的部署。在核反应堆的燃料组件中，燃料棒通常按照8×8（沸水堆）或17×17（压水堆）的阵列排列。若采用稠密栅棒束结构的先进燃料组件设计，可在维持单位燃料棒表面热流密度不变的前提下，将每个燃料组件的功率输出提高5%至20%。燃料棒数量的增加也提升了组件的铀装载量，进而实现更高效的长周期运行。同时，燃料密度的提高有助于降低堆芯中子的泄露率，从而增加核燃料利用率，并通过改善中子经济性减少核废料的生成。 在轻水反应堆中，流经反应堆堆芯的蒸汽-水两相混合物在正常工况和事故工况下通过冷却燃料棒和调节中子能量来控制链式反应，对核安全起着至关重要的作用。先进燃料组件热工水力优化设计需要稳健的两相流数值模拟程序，并且该程序的模拟精度被实验数据充分验证。然而，目前还未有系统的高空间分辨的稠密栅组件内的气液两相流数据库。 本项目拟开展实验研究，测量模拟先进核燃料棒束组件的稠密栅棒束内的气液两相流动特性。实验所产生的数据库将用于开发数值模拟程序中的高保真本构方程。项目所建立的数据库和方程将极大提高数值模拟程序的保真度，对安全经济的核反应堆设计具有重要意义。

11201825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201825.value: 用於面部表情分析的深度特徵聯合聚類

11201825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201825.value: Gabor wavelets and other pre-defined features have been widely used for human facial expression analysis. These features have a high level of redundancy, and several methods can be used to select features for classifier training. The PI’s team has proposed a radically new method for feature selection based on co-clustering, which can detect coherent patterns consisting of subsets of samples and subsets of features. With as low as 0.9% of Gabor wavelet features selected, we were able to obtain a facial expression recognition accuracy even higher than that with the full set of features used. Deep neural networks (DNNs) have superior performance to traditional classifiers that use pre-defined features for facial expression recognition and many other pattern classification tasks. However, a DNN is often viewed as a black box, where we only deal with the input samples and output results, and the features and their properties inside the black box are largely hidden. In this project, we open the black box and analyze the deep features using co-clustering. Our preliminary work shows the middle layers in a DNN produce interesting co-cluster patterns. We will investigate these coherent patterns for facial expressions from images and video data. The co-clusters reveal simultaneous and consistent structures both spatially and temporally. They will be employed for facial expression and micro-expression generation and classification. We will develop techniques to simplify deep neural networks by removing the weights that do not contribute to the selected features. Our method combines the classification power of deep neural networks and feature selection power of co-clustering. In addition to providing effective techniques for facial expression analysis, our work will lead to a deep understanding of the hidden layers in deep neural networks. The co-clusters can reveal the coherent patterns produced inside the black box and can help us build more powerful networks in terms of computational speed and accuracy. Robust facial expression analysis techniques will have many applications to medical diagnosis, human-machine interactions, sports, education and training, video gaming, and entertainment. Although our work focuses on facial expressions in this project, the research results can be employed in a wide range of other applications. Also, our work will help offer explainability of deep neural networks. The black box will no longer be mysterious, and this will open the door for us to develop a new generation of efficient intelligent data analysis systems for many practical applications. 加博爾小波和其他預定義特徵已被廣泛用於人類面部表情分析。這些特徵具有高度冗餘性，並且有多種方法可用於選擇用於分類器訓練的特徵。 我們團隊提出了一種基於聯合聚類的全新特徵選擇方法，可以檢測由樣本子集和特徵子集組成的相關模式。即使只選擇0.9%的加博爾小波特徵，我們也能獲得比使用全集特徵更高的臉部表情辨識準確率。 深度神經網路在臉部表情辨識和許多其他模式分類任務中，其性能優於使用預定義特徵的傳統分類器。然而，深度神經網路通常被視為一個黑盒子，我們只處理輸入樣本和輸出結果，而黑盒子內的特徵及其屬性在很大程度上是隱藏的。 在本項目中，我們打開黑盒子，並使用協同聚類分析深度特徵。我們的初步研究表明，深度神經網路的中間層會產生有趣的聯合聚類模式。我們將從圖像和視訊數據中研究這些面部表情的連貫模式。這些共聚類揭示了空間和時間上同步且一致的結構。它們將用於面部表情和微表情的生成和分類。我們將開發一些技術，透過移除對所選特徵無貢獻的權重來簡化深度神經網路。 我們的方法結合了深度神經網路的分類能力和聯合聚類的特徵選擇能力。除了提供有效的臉部表情分析技術外，我們的工作還將加深對深度神經網路隱藏層的理解。共聚類可以揭示黑盒子內部產生的相關模式，並幫助我們建立在計算速度和準確率方面更強大的網路。強大的面部表情分析技術將在醫療診斷、人機互動、體育、教育培訓、視頻遊戲和娛樂等領域擁有廣泛的應用。 雖然本計畫主要關注面部表情，但研究成果可以廣泛應用於其他領域。此外，我們的工作也將有助於提高深度神經網路的可解釋性。黑箱將不再神秘，這將為我們開發新一代高效的智慧數據分析系統，應用於許多實際應用程式打開大門。

11202325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202325.value: 機器遺忘的誘因機制設計

11202325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202325.value: User data is essential for training artificial intelligence (AI) models, enabling innovations like AI chatbots. However, privacy regulations, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) [1], empower users to request removing their sensitive data, which can adversely affect AI model accuracy. In response, major AI operators are exploring economic solutions to address it [2], raising a critical question: How much should users be compensated for their data contributions? This proposal addresses this question through the lens of machine unlearning (MU) [3, 4], a key technology to enforce users’ “right to be forgotten” under GDPR. Ideally, an MU algorithm should remove the influence of the “forget set” [5] efficiently while maintaining model accuracy. As existing MU research focused on technology aspects, it lacks insight into the economic interactions between operators and clients. This proposal aims to bridge that gap by designing incentive mechanisms for MU, tackling pricing challenges faced by AI operators. The first part explores static incentive mechanisms in MU for privacy protection [4]. Motivated by OpenAI’s “Copyright Shield” scheme [6], we consider a compensation mechanism for data retention. Existing studies on MU incentive mechanisms [7, 8, 9] overlooked the centralized MU setting, where the AI operator manages unlearning and bears model degradation costs. By characterizing unlearning costs through real-world experiments and formulating a three-stage Stackelberg game among regulators, operators, and clients, we aim to derive the optimal pricing strategies for operators. Building on these static setting results, the second part investigates dynamic incentive mechanisms to enhance model adaptability in changing environments [4]. As data properties evolve due to concept drift [10], previously trained models risk becoming obsolete unless outdated data is unlearned and fresh data is incorporated. Thus, AI operators must identify clients with critical outdated data and incentivize fresh data collection. While dynamic MU applications [11] exist, the related academic research (especially on incentive mechanisms) is limited. We propose adopting the age of information (AoI) to quantify data freshness and develop an online pricing algorithm to encourage clients to provide fresh data for model updates. In conclusion, with our preliminary results in static [12, 13] and dynamic [14] incentive mechanism design for MU, this research is highly viable. These efforts will establish a theoretical foundation for data pricing under MU, address real-world AI challenges related to privacy and model adaptability, and open up exciting research directions in MU. 用戶數據對於訓練人工智慧（AI）模型至關重要，促成了如 AI 聊天機器人等創新。然而，隱私法規（例如《一般資料保護規則》（GDPR）[1]）賦予用戶要求移除其敏感資料的權利，這可能會對 AI 模型的準確性產生不利影響。為此，主要的 AI 業者正探索經濟解決方案來應對此問題 [2]，並引發一個關鍵問題：用戶應該因其數據貢獻獲得多少補償？ 本提案從「機器遺忘」（Machine Unlearning, MU）[3, 4] 的角度切入，探討上述問題。MU 是一項關鍵技術，用以實現 GDPR 所保障的「被遺忘權」。理想的 MU 演算法應能有效移除「遺忘集合」（forget set）[5] 的影響，同時維持模型的準確性。現有 MU 研究多聚焦於技術層面，缺乏對業者與用戶之間經濟互動的洞察。本提案旨在填補此空白，設計 MU 的誘因機制，並解決 AI 業者面臨的定價挑戰。 第一部分探討 MU 中的靜態誘因機制以保護隱私 [4]。受到 OpenAI「版權保護」計畫 [6] 的啟發，我們考慮一種針對數據保留的補償機制。現有 MU 誘因機制研究 [7, 8, 9] 忽略了集中式 MU 設定，其中 AI 業者負責執行遺忘並承擔模型退化的成本。我們將透過實驗量化遺忘成本，並構建一個三階段 Stackelberg 博弈模型，涵蓋監管機構、業者與用戶，以推導業者的最適定價策略。 在靜態設定的基礎上，第二部分進一步探討動態誘因機制，以提升模型在變動環境中的適應性 [4]。由於概念漂移（concept drift）[10] ，除非能夠遺忘舊數據並引入新數據，數據特性會隨時間演變，導致先前訓練的模型可能過時。因此，AI 業者需識別持有過時關鍵數據的用戶，並激勵其提供新數據。儘管已有動態 MU 的應用案例 [11]，但相關學術研究（尤其是誘因機制方面）仍相當有限。我們提出以「資訊年齡」（Age of Information, AoI）量化數據新鮮度，並設計一種線上定價演算法，以鼓勵用戶提供新數據以更新模型。 總結而言，基於我們在 MU 靜態 [12, 13] 與動態 [14] 誘因機制設計方面的初步成果，本研究具高度可行性。這些努力將建立 MU 下的數據定價理論基礎，回應 AI 在隱私與模型適應性方面的現實挑戰，並開啟 MU 領域令人振奮的研究方向。

11202725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202725.value: 受紅樹林啟發的變破壞性因素為保護性力的防腐策略

11202725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202725.value: In addressing the grand, pressing challenge of marine metal corrosion, organic anticorrosion coatings stand out due to cost-effectiveness and application breadth. Extensive efforts have primarily focused on hindering the inward diffusing path of corrosive substances and/or influencing the coating-metal interfacial redox reactions. Various methods based on physical barriers and electrochemical mechanisms are combined into one coating, which could yield high performance while at a cost of higher complexity. These coatings generally undergo a depletion of the inherent, finite anticorrosion capacity, because no extra external energy is used for corrosion control. This gets exacerbated substantially in the splash zone which features the highest corrosion rate. Nevertheless, in pursuing to mimic the mangrove’s energy-supported control over ion transport, an intriguing finding was discovered by chance: pure organic piezoelectric coatings show substantially superior anticorrosion performance in wave-simulating conditions than commercial epoxy varnish (corrosion current density 3-4 orders of magnitude lower and impedance modulus ~4 orders of magnitude higher after 30 days immersion in dynamically shaking 3.5% NaCl solutions). Furthermore, unusual anticorrosion behaviors exhibited by the piezoelectric coatings from static to dynamically shaking conditions manifest some fundamentally different, yet unknown, mechanisms from conventional coatings. Thus, this project aims to bring forth a completely new and highly efficient anticorrosion strategy that could transform destructive, corrosion-accelerating impacts into protective, corrosion-decelerating forces by using piezoelectric materials alone. The key for this is hypothesized that the piezoelectricity-induced charged surfaces (a) interact with ions to repel Cl− to promote passivation and prevent pitting corrosion and (b) influence the electrochemical potential of the metal to provide protection. We will endeavor to explore (i) how piezoelectricity variation influences the anticorrosion performance, (ii) how the strain-induced charged surface interacts with corrosive ions at the coating-solution interface, and (iii) whether the piezoelectricity provides a cathodic protection-like anticorrosion to the metal substrate, through fabrication, examination including laboratory and real marine tests, and analyzation and modeling to reveal the novel mechanisms. Upon completion of this project, we will be able to establish such a new, efficient anticorrosion strategy of piezoelectric anticorrosion coatings, which could outperform commercial organic anticorrosion coatings through newly explored mechanisms. An in-depth, systematic analyzing framework will be formulated to uncover the novel relation between strain-induced charged surfaces affecting electrochemical reactions at the microscale and piezoelectricity dominating anticorrosion properties at the macroscale. 在應對海洋金屬腐蝕這一重大而緊迫的挑戰中，有機防腐塗層因其成本效益和應用範圍而脫穎而出。廣泛的研究努力主要集中在阻礙腐蝕物質向內擴散的路徑和/或影響塗層-金屬界面的氧化還原反應。集各種基於物理屏障和電化學機制到一個塗層，雖然可以獲得高性能，但同時也增加了複雜性。由於沒有額外的外部能量用於腐蝕控制，這些塗層通常會耗盡其固有的、有限的防腐能力。在腐蝕速率最高的浪花飛濺區，這種情況會更加嚴重。 然而，在試圖模擬紅樹林能量支持離子輸運控制的過程中，我們偶然發現了一個有趣的結果：單純有機壓電塗層在模擬波浪條件下表現出比商用環氧清漆更優異的防腐性能（在動態震盪的 3.5% NaCl 溶液中浸泡 30 天后，腐蝕電流密度低 3-4 個數量級，阻抗量高約 4 個數量級）。此外，壓電塗層在靜態和動態震盪條件下表現出的不尋常的防腐行為表明了一些與傳統塗層完全不同但尚不清楚的機制。 因此，本項目旨在提出一種全新高效的防腐策略，僅利用壓電材料即可將破壞性的、加速腐蝕的拍擊力轉化為保護性的、減緩腐蝕的力。其關鍵在於：我們假設壓電效應引起的帶電表面 (a) 與離子相互作用，排斥 Cl−，從而促進鈍化並防止點蝕；(b) 影響金屬的電化學勢，從而提供保護。我們將致力於探索：(i) 壓電效應的變化如何影響防腐性能；(ii) 應變誘導的帶電表面如何在塗層 - 溶液界面處與腐蝕性離子相互作用；以及 (iii) 壓電效應是否能為金屬基材提供類似陰極保護的防腐效果。我們將透過製造、檢驗（包括實驗室和實際海洋試驗）以及分析和建模來揭示新的機制。 本項目完成後，我們將能夠建立一種新型、高效的壓電防腐塗層防腐策略，並透過新探索的機制使其性能超越市售有機防腐塗層。我們將建構一個深入、系統性的分析框架，以揭示微觀尺度上應變引發帶電表面影響電化學反應與宏觀尺度上壓電效應主導防腐性能之間的新關係。

11202925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202925.value: 從能量採集到感知：基於動能採集的自維持、無傳感器可穿戴感知框架研究

11202925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202925.value: Continuous context sensing with wearable devices has a wide variety of applications. Current wearable sensing solutions use a variety of specialized sensors, such as accelerometers, gyroscopes, and biosensors, which are built into wearable devices. Unfortunately, operating these sensors requires an external power supply, making context monitoring a power-intensive process for wearable sensors. Power supply has been identified as a major bottleneck to the adoption of wearable devices pervasive enough to meet the vision of ubiquitous computing. Wearables must either be fitted with large batteries or frequently recharged. However, frequent battery replacement and manual recharging is not only a waste of manpower and resources, but also harmful to the environment. Therefore, energy-efficient and continuous wearable sensing remains an unsolved problem. Harvesting energy from ambient sources, such as kinetic motions, has emerged as a promising technology to power the Internet of Things devices. However, the above problem cannot be fully addressed by integrating energy harvesters into wearable devices because the current power output of energy harvesters does not yet meet the requirements of continuous sensor sampling. Motivated by this, the project will innovatively study whether we can make energy harvesting devices sensible by exploiting the harvested signals directly rather than relying on additional sensors. To this end, we will model, design, implement, and extensively evaluate a novel wearable sensing framework: energy harvesting as sensing (EHaS). The proposed EHaS framework aims to infer user and animal contexts directly from harvested energy signals without engaging extra sensors. The project will be divided into three major tasks: (1) towards accurate and fine-grained EHaS framework, (2) towards data-efficient EHaS framework, and (3) towards energy-efficient EHaS framework. The novelty of this research lies in its broader view of energy harvesting technology, looking beyond its basic power supply capability. By exploiting energy harvesters to achieve simultaneous energy harvesting and sensing, the project will open up a new direction for research into wearable sensing and pave the way for the development of self-sustaining, and sensorless wearable devices. 利用可穿戴設備進行連續情境感知擁有廣泛的應用前景。目前的可穿戴感知解決方案依賴內置於設備中的各種專業傳感器，例如加速度計、陀螺儀以及生物傳感器。然而，操作這些傳感器需要外部電源支持，使得情境監測成為一個耗能較高的過程。電力供應已被確定為阻礙可穿戴設備廣泛應用的主要瓶頸，這直接影響了普適計算願景的實現。可穿戴設備要麼需要配備大容量電池，要麼需要頻繁充電。然而，頻繁更換電池和人工充電不僅浪費人力和資源，還對環境造成危害。從環境中收集能量（如動能）已成為解決物聯網設備供電問題的潛在方案。然而，儘管這一領域取得了顯著進展，但目前的能量收集設備由於轉換效率低和環境能量密度有限，其輸出功率仍不足以滿足連續傳感器採樣的需求。 本項目將研究是否可以通過直接利用收集到的信號，而不是依賴額外的傳感器，使能量收集設備具備感知能力。為此，我們將建模、設計、實現並全面評估一種新穎的情境感知框架：能量收集即感知（EHaS）。提出的EHaS框架旨在通過收集的能量信號直接推斷用户和動物的情境，而無需額外傳感器的參與。項目將分為三個主要任務：（1）實現精準且細粒度的EHaS框架；（2）實現數據高效的EHaS框架；（3）實現能量高效的EHaS框架。 本研究的創新之處在於對能量收集技術提出了更廣泛的應用視角，不僅僅將其視為一種電源供應手段。通過利用能量收集設備實現能量收集與感知的同步，本項目將為可穿戴感知研究開闢新的方向，併為開發自我維持的無傳感器可穿戴設備奠定基礎。

11203225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203225.value: 用于 6G 及后6G的太赫兹低噪声放大器

11203225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203225.value: According to Precedence Research, the global 6G market is projected to reach USD6.7 billion in 2024 and surge to USD57.55 billion by 2034, reflecting a compound annual growth rate of 24%. Emerging 6G applications, such as holographic telepresence, 3D video streaming, and immersive mixed reality, demand the ultrawide bandwidth provided by terahertz (THz) frequencies. IEEE 802.15.3d, the first standard for THz wireless communications in the 253-322-GHz band, supports data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s, with service ranges extending from a few centimeters for intra-device links to approximately 100 meters for fronthaul/backhaul. To further extend these service ranges, continuous innovation in high-power THz transmitters and high-sensitivity receivers is essential. Through a Collaborative Research Fund project (C1009-22G) titled “An Enabling Technology for 6G Wireless Communications,” we have developed cutting-edge THz power amplifiers (PAs) and receivers using 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. A notable achievement includes a 180-194 GHz eight-way power amplifier co-designed with an on-chip power-combining antenna array, delivering a saturated radiated power (Psat) of 66 mW. Additionally, we have designed 256-281-GHz 10-stage and 213-255-GHz 7-stage single-way PAs, achieving peak gains of 29.5 dB and 22.1 dB, with gain-bandwidth products (GBWs) of 490 GHz and 531 GHz, respectively. These amplifiers support data transmission rates of 60 Gb/s and 72 Gb/s with error vector magnitudes (EVMs) of -24.9 dB and -28.0 dB for 64-QAM modulation. Their measured Psat values are 1.4 mW and 1 mW, respectively. To date, no literature has reported 65-nm CMOS-based low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) operating above the D-band (110-170 GHz). Existing receivers beyond the D-band predominantly employ a mixer-first architecture. For instance, our 460 GHz receiver, designed with a second-order subharmonic mixer, achieved a measured conversion gain of -2.8 dB and a noise figure (NF) of 26 dB. In this project, we propose the design of the first CMOS-based H-band LNAs for THz receivers to significantly enhance receiver sensitivity and, consequently, extend service range. The designed 10-stage, 29.2-dB-gain PA, without specific NF optimization, predicts an NF of 11.7 dB, with the transistor’s fmax reaching 384 GHz. By optimizing the trade-offs between NF, gain, and 1 dB input power compression point (IP1dB), we are confident that CMOS LNAs operating in the H-band are achievable. This project aligns with the focuses of the National 14th Five-Year Plan and will position the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) as a leading player in the global market of 6G and beyond. 根据Precedence Research的数据，全球6G市场规模预计将从2024年的67亿美元激增至2034年的575.5亿美元，年复合增长率达24%。远程全息互动、3D视频流和沉浸式混合现实等新兴6G应用，都需要利用太赫兹频段提供的超宽频谱资源。IEEE 802.15.3d作为首个覆盖253-322 GHz频段的太赫兹无线通信标准，可支持超过100 Gb/s的数据传输速率，既可满足设备内部几厘米范围的短距通信，也能支持前传/回传链路达100米的远距连接。为了进一步拓展通信距离，推进高功率太赫兹发射机与高灵敏度接收机的技术创新至关重要。 通过"6G无线通信关键技术研究"合作研究基金项目（C1009-22G）的支持，我们采用65 nm CMOS工艺研发了一系列先进的太赫兹功率放大器（PA）和接收机。其中一项突出成果是180-194 GHz的八路PA与片上天线阵列进行功率合成的协同设计，其饱和辐射功率（Psat）高达66 mW。此外，在更高的频段，我们还设计了256-281 GHz的十级PA和213-255 GHz的七级PA，其峰值增益分别为29.5 dB和22.1 dB，增益带宽积分别达到490 GHz和531 GHz。这两款PA在64-QAM调制下分别实现了60 Gb/s和72 Gb/s的数据传输速率，误差矢量幅度分别为-24.9 dB和-28.0 dB，实测Psat值分别为1.4 mW和1 mW。 迄今为止，尚未有文献报道过工作在D波段（110-170 GHz）及以上的基于65 nm CMOS工艺的低噪声放大器（LNA）。现有的D波段以上的接收机主要采用混频器首级架构。例如，我们研发的一款460 GHz接收机采用了二次谐波混频器作为第一级，实测转换增益为-2.8 dB，噪声系数（NF）为26 dB。本项目拟提出首个基于CMOS工艺的H波段LNA，可显著改善太赫兹接收机的灵敏度，从提高通信距离。上述的十级PA具有29.2 dB增益，其晶体管fmax为384 GHz，在未进行NF优化的情况下，预计可实现的NF为11.7 dB。基于该设计，本项目将进一步优化NF、增益和1 dB输入压缩点之间的性能平衡，我们相信实现H波段CMOS LNA的目标是完全可行的。 本项目符合国家"十四五"规划重点发展方向，有望使粤港澳大湾区在全球6G及未来移动通信市场中占据领先地位。

11203625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203625.value: 自然森林超材料中地表諧振器與地震波相互作用的理論、分析、原位實驗研究

11203625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11203625.value: Dr Chen, Zhenyu Prof Erasmo, Carrera Prof REDDY, J.N.

11203625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203625.value: The expanding realm of metamaterials now covers numerous cross-disciplinary and real-life applications from nanoscale to macroscale sizes in optic/electromagnetic, acoustic/elastic, and, more recently, seismic systems. The dynamic properties of seismic metamaterials are investigated as potential shields to protect strategic buildings, historic structures, civil infrastructures, etc. Because it is still at an infancy stage, a detailed investigation involving in-situ soil exploration, ground conditions, and the interaction of seismic waves with surface resonators is necessary.
