There is currently no analytical solution available that accurately predicts seismic wave propagation and interaction with ground resonators. Further, the composite stratified layered saturated/unsaturated porous medium makes the problem highly nonlinear owing to the complex wave mechanism that is largely unknown. Thus, an accurate analytical, computational, and experimental approach for predicting the behavior of seismic wave propagation and interaction with ground resonators is highly desirable. Although there exist some preliminary models for seismic wave propagation in unsaturated and saturated porous media including the Umklapp process, an in-depth understanding of the frequency characteristics and interaction with natural forest still require extensive analysis in theory, numerical analysis and experiment. It will provide physical insights for the effectiveness of forest trees as potential seismic metamaterials, termed meta-forestation. More generally, we wish to establish a new natural anti-seismic meta-forestation subject of study. Our findings may motivate the local and global communities, government organizations, and environmental activists for a more systematic and scientific forestry approach in line with earthquake protection and an effort for effective meta-forestation. There are also great potentials and spin-off applications in other cross-disciplinary areas including ultrasonic inspection, geological investigation, mechanical vibration, and surface acoustic wave devices, to name a few. The proposed project is expected to have the following outcomes in addition to technical papers. It will (i) offer new insights for seismic wave propagation in in-situ composite porous media and for interaction with seismic ground-resonators. An in-depth theoretical and computational investigation assisted by laboratory and practically manageable full-scaled experiments for the Umklapp process will be conducted, and the feasibility of meta-forestation as effective earthquake protection will be explored. (ii) Research students will be trained. The successful completion of this project will (iii) provide a new platform for researchers to further expand the applications of seismic metamaterials for potential earthquake-proof designs and to protect a specific geographical region from seismic hazards. There will be other spin-off research benefits including applications in (iv) ultrasonics, geology, mechanical vibration and acoustics. 題目：自然森林超材料中地表諧振器與地震波相互作用的理論、分析、原位實驗研究 摘要 超材料的研究範圍不斷擴展，現已涵蓋從納米級到宏觀尺寸、橫跨光學/電磁、聲學/彈性以及最近擴展到的地震系統等眾多跨學科及現實生活應用。地震超材料的動態特性被研究作為保護戰略建築、歷史結構、民用基礎設施等的潛在屏障。由於該領域仍處於初期階段，因此需要進行詳細研究，包括原位土壤探勘、地質條件分析，以及地震波與地表諧振器的相互作用等。目前尚無精確預測地震波傳播及其與地表諧振器相互作用的解析解。此外，複合分層飽和/非飽和多孔介質因其複雜且大多未知的波動機制，使得問題呈現高度非線性。因此，亟需建立精確的解析、計算與實驗方法，以預測地震波傳播及其與地表諧振器相互作用的行為。 儘管現在已有一些針對非飽和與飽和多孔介質中地震波傳播（包括翁庫拉普過程）的初步模型，但對於頻率特性及其與自然森林相互作用的深入理解，仍需在理論、數值分析與實驗方面進行廣泛研究。這將為樹木作為潛在地震超材料（稱之為森林超材料）的有效性提供物理支撐。更廣泛而言，本項目期望建立一個新的自然抗震森林超材料研究主題。該研究發現可能促使地方及全球社群、政府機構與環保人士，採納更系統化、科學化的林業種植方案，以結合地震防護並推動有效的森林超材料化。此研究在其他跨學科領域，包括超音波檢測、地質調查、機械振動與表面聲波裝置等，亦具有巨大的潛力與衍生應用價值。 該提案項目預期除技術論文外，還將產生以下成果：（i）為原位複合多孔介質中的地震波傳播及其與地震地表諧振器的相互作用提供新的見解。我們將在實驗室及實際可行的大尺度實驗輔助下，針對翁庫拉普過程進行深入的理論與計算研究，並探討森林超材料作為有效地震防護措施的可行性；（ii）培養研究生；（iii）為研究人員提供一個新平台，以進一步拓展地震超材料在潛在抗震設計中的應用，並保護特定地理區域免受地震災害；（iv）本項目還將產生其他衍生研究效益，包括在超音波學、地質學、機械振動學與聲學中的應用。

11203725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203725.value: 高階複雜網路的同步性能極限與上限

11203725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203725.value: Proposal Summary Complex network research has been rapidly developed in the past three decades, with fruitful results contributing to network science and engineering, and is still fast evolving to an even more advanced level recently. Typical subjects in complex network research carried out by scientific engineers today include, among many others, network synchronization, network control and high-order network topologies. The PI of this proposal is one of the few pioneers in the aforementioned focal research subjects of the fields. The PI and colleagues developed the very first network synchronization criterion and they were the first to characterize the optimal structures of complex networks with the best possible synchronizability; the PI and colleagues were the earliest to develop and study complex network pinning control for synchronization as well as multi-agent systems; the PI and colleagues were among the first ones to investigate higher-order network topologies in the nation. Success notwithstanding, the above research accomplishments were achieved mainly for conventional complex networks using classical graph-theoretic tools. The present proposal continues the PI’s efforts to take a further step forward to carry on the current research to a more advanced level on higher-order complex networks, which requires more powerful tools from algebraic topology theory and methods involving higher-order simplexes, using measures and techniques based on higher-order Laplacian eigen-spectral analysis, to investigate the network synchronizability limits and ceilings. Specifically, this project has two objectives: Objective 1: Developing 2nd-order network synchronizability limits and ceilings Objective 2: Enhancing edge-based pinning-controlled 2nd-order synchronization Based on the PI’s well-developed analytic techniques and computational methods, this project has a solid foundation and is promising, which will significantly contribute to the fields of network science and engineering upon its completion. 複雜網路研究在過去三十年中得到了迅速發展，取得了豐碩的成果，為網路科學與工程做出了重要貢獻，並且近年來仍在快速發展，並不斷向更高水平發展。當今科學工程師所進行的複雜網路研究的典型主題包括網路同步、網路控制和高階網路拓撲等。 本計畫負責人是上述領域重點研究課題的少數先驅之一，開發了第一個網絡同步準則，並首次刻畫了具有最佳同步性的複雜網絡最優結構；最早開發和研究了用於同步以及多智能體系統的複雜網絡釘扎控制；也是國內最早研究高階網絡拓撲的學者之一。 本計畫繼續努力，將目前高階複雜網路的研究提升到更高的水平。這需要代數拓樸理論和涉及高階單純形的方法中更強大的工具，並利用基於高階拉普拉斯特徵譜分析的測度和技術，來研究網路同步性的極限和上限。 具體而言，本計畫有兩個目標： 目標1：發展二階網路同步性的極限與上限 目標2：增強基於邊的牽制控制二階同步 本專案基於專案負責人成熟的分析技術和計算方法，基礎紮實，前景廣闊，完成後將對網路科學與工程領域做出重大貢獻。

11204125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204125.value: 氣候變化下極端城市風環境的多尺度模拟

11204125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11204125.value: Dr Chan, Pai-Wai Dr He, Junyi Dr Zhang, Yuxin

11204125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204125.value: Many coastal cities, such as Hong Kong, have high population densities and numerous buildings and are located in tropical cyclone (TC)-prone areas. Current standards and codes generally provide design wind speeds based on typical terrain categories for an entire city. However, urban wind conditions during TC events are significantly influenced by complex urban landscapes so that high-resolution estimation of the urban wind environment is desired. To date, fine-scale modeling of extreme urban wind fields remains challenging due to high computational costs and uncertainties associated with atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) conditions. Additionally, the impact of climate change on extreme urban wind conditions is not well understood and related research is limited. To this end, this proposed project will be aimed at developing a novel multi-scale modeling framework to assess the urban wind fields during TCs under various climate change scenarios. The proposed study will integrate the advanced Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to capture complex interactions between large-scale atmospheric processes and fine-scale urban features. The WRF module will provide real ABL conditions for the CFD module. This framework will allow for detailed estimates of urban wind environments, such as the wind velocity distribution on a specific street or region and the wind effects on large-scale buildings or infrastructures. To investigate the influence of climate change on extreme urban wind conditions, a new machine learning-based TC detection and tracking model will be developed based on historical reanalysis datasets. Subsequently, the model will be applied to find out all TC events in a multi-model ensemble consisting of multiple Global Climate Models (GCMs) with various Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) provided by the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6). And all TC events that pose potential threats to Hong Kong will be identified and simulated using the proposed WRF-CFD framework. In addition, uncertainties throughout this modeling pipeline will be quantified and analyzed. Finally, this research will establish a high-resolution dataset characterizing urban wind conditions for different return periods. The dataset will provide invaluable information for urban planners, engineers, and policymakers to improve the design of resilient cities and hazard managements, which are particularly relevant for Hong Kong. Additionally, the research findings will contribute to broader scientific understanding of urban meteorology and climate adaptation strategies, offering new perspectives on how cities can better address the threats of TCs and challenges posed by climate changes. 許多沿海城市，例如香港，具有高人口密度和眾多建築物，且位於熱帶氣旋（TC）多發區域。現行的標準和規範通常基於整個城市的典型地形類別來提供設計風速。然而，熱帶氣旋事件期間的城市風況受到複雜城市景觀的顯著影響，因此需要對城市風環境進行高解析度評估。至今，由於高計算成本以及與大氣邊界層（ABL）條件相關的不確定性，極端城市風場的精細尺度模擬仍然具有挑戰性。此外，氣候變化對極端城市風況的影響尚未明確，相關研究也有限。為此，本提案項目旨在開發一種新穎的多尺度模擬框架，以評估不同氣候變化情境下熱帶氣旋期間的城市風場。 該研究將整合先進的天氣研究與預報（WRF）模型和計算流體動力學（CFD）模擬，以捕捉大尺度大氣過程與精細城市特徵之間的複雜相互作用。WRF模塊將為CFD模塊提供真實的大氣邊界層條件。此框架將允許對城市風環境進行詳細評估，例如特定街道或區域的風速分佈，以及風對大型建築或基礎設施的影響。 為研究氣候變化對極端城市風況的影響，將基於歷史再分析資料集開發一種新的機器學習輔助的熱帶氣旋檢測與追踪模型。隨後，該模型將應用於識別多模型集成中的所有熱帶氣旋事件，這些集成包含多個全球氣候模型（GCMs），並採用耦合模型比對計劃第六階段（CMIP6）提供的多種共享社會經濟路徑（SSPs）。所有對香港構成潛在威脅的熱帶氣旋事件將使用提出的WRF-CFD框架進行識別和模擬。此外，整個模擬流程中的不確定性將被量化和分析。 最後，本研究將建立一個高解析度資料集，表徵不同回歸期的城市風況。該資料集將為城市規劃者、工程師和政策制定者提供寶貴信息，以改進韌性城市的設計和災害管理，這對香港尤其重要。此外，研究結果將有助於更廣泛地科學理解城市氣象學和氣候適應策略，為城市如何更好地應對熱帶氣旋的威脅和氣候變化帶來的挑戰提供新的視角。

11204825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204825.value: 微生物組宏基因體學中噬菌體組裝、註釋和宿主識別的創新計算方法

11204825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204825.value: Bacteriophages (phages) are viruses that specifically infect bacterial cells and are ubiquitously found in various environments such as animal gastrointestinal tracts, aquatic systems, and soil. They are the most abundant biological entities in the biosphere, with an estimation of tens of millions species in nature. By facilitating horizontal gene transfers among bacteria in microbial communities, they contribute tremendously to bacterial adaptation, evolution, and the acquisition of new functions. Phages can lyse very specific bacterial hosts and hence be used for precision antibiotic therapy---interests in this function of phages has surged in recent years due to concerns of growing bacterial resistance to conventional antibiotics. However, the effectiveness of phage-based therapy is contingent on the identification of suitable phages since a phage will kill a bacterium only if it matches the specific strain. Due to difficulties in laboratory cultivation of phages, phage genomes are often mined from metagenomic data using next-generation sequencing (NGS). These datasets can be derived from various environments, such as wastewater, soil, and human gut microbiomes. The analysis of metagenomic data requires sophisticated bioinformatics tools to identify and characterize phage sequences. Various algorithms have been developed to identify phages from other genetic material as well as infer their behavior. These methods are based on various principles, for instance, sequence similarity, $k$-mer composition, or machine learning techniques. Despite the advancements in metagenomic approaches, several challenges persist in accurately identifying phage genomes. First, the immense diversity of phages poses a significant challenge for identification. Our knowledge-base of phage proteins is highly incomplete. At present, vast amount of sequenced data remain unlabeled. This is exacerbated by the fact that many phages exhibit high variability in their genomic sequences, making it difficult to match them against existing reference databases. Moreover, both lytic and temperate phages can integrate host genetic material into their genomes, leading to sequence similarities that complicate identification. In this project, we study the Microbiome metagenomics data, leveraging the availability of both phage and host information in such data, to tackle three computational problems in phage discovery: (1) identification and assembly of phage genomes from microbiome data, (2) annotation of phage proteins, and (3) idenfication of phage hosts. We use a mixture of graph-based methods, protein language models (pLMs), and other statistical approaches. 噬菌體（phage）是一種特異性感染細菌細胞的病毒，廣泛存在於各種環境中，例如動物的胃腸道、水生系統和土壤。它們是生物圈中最豐富的生物實體，自然界中估計有數千萬種。透過促進微生物群落中細菌之間的水平基因轉移，它們對細菌的適應、進化和新功能的獲得做出了巨大貢獻。 噬菌體可以裂解非常特定的細菌宿主，因此可用於精準抗生素治療——近年來，由於人們對細菌對傳統抗生素抗藥性日益增長的擔憂，人們對噬菌體這一功能的興趣激增。然而，基於噬菌體療法的有效性取決於合適的噬菌體的識別，因為噬菌體只有與特定菌株匹配才能殺死細菌。 由於實驗室培養噬菌體存在困難，噬菌體基因組通常使用新一代定序 (NGS) 從宏基因組資料中挖掘。這些資料集可能來自各種環境，例如廢水、土壤和人類腸道微生物組。 宏基因組資料的分析需要複雜的生物資訊工具來識別和表徵噬菌體序列。目前已開發出各種演算法來從其他遺傳物質中識別噬菌體並推斷其行為。這些方法基於各種原理，例如序列相似性、$k$ 聚體組成或機器學習技術。 儘管宏基因組方法取得了進展，但在準確識別噬菌體基因組方面仍存在一些挑戰。首先，噬菌體的巨大多樣性對辨識構成了重大挑戰。我們關於噬菌體蛋白質的知識庫非常不完整。目前，大量定序數據仍未標示。 由於許多噬菌體基因組序列高度多變，使其與現有參考資料庫進行配對變得困難，這加劇了這個問題。此外，裂解性噬菌體和溫和性噬菌體均可將宿主遺傳物質整合到其基因組中，導致序列相似性，使鑑定更加複雜。 在本計畫中，我們研究微生物組宏基因組學數據，利用這些數據中噬菌體和宿主信息，解決噬菌體發現中的三個計算問題：(1) 從微生物組數據中識別和組裝噬菌體基因組， (2) 噬菌體蛋白質註釋，以及 (3) 噬菌體宿主鑑定。我們結合使用了基於圖形的方法、蛋白質語言模型 (pLM) 和其他統計方法。

11206325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206325.value: 前沿的 MRI 檢測帕金遜症的水通道蛋白活性和分子變化

11206325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206325.value: This study will develop an advanced MRI(MISL and CEST) to image the aquaporin pathology, protein and specific molecular changes in Parkinson’s disease(PD). PD is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons. Recent studies have implicated key roles of aquaporins in PD pathogenesis, especially its dysfunction could impair glymphatic clearance, aggravate α-synuclein accumulation and dopaminergic neuron loss. However, it is very challenging to image these changes in vivo during disease progression non-invasively and simultaneously, hindering our understanding of its role in early pathology. This proposal aims to address this challenge by imaging aquaporin and related PD pathologies using CEST and MISL. We hypothesize that multiple CEST and MISL contrasts can reveals key molecular events of PD and are sensitive to AQP4-dependent glymphatic function, α-synuclein accumulation and dopaminergic neurons loss and myelin abnormality. We demonstrated that CEST MRI could detect changes in protein, myelin and specific molecules in a sensitive manner, including protein aggregation and glymphatic dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease, altered glucose uptake and utilization during glucose deprivation treatment in brain cancer, demyelination in multiple sclerosis and AQP4 function in rodent brain, using glucose, amine, amide proton transfer(APT) and nuclear Overhauser effect(NOE) CEST and MISL. Collectively, our pilot MRI studies strongly suggested that these advanced MRI contrasts enable the imaging of many key neuropathologies non-invasively and longitudinally, especially those related to PD. In this project, we will develop an advanced MRI imaging platform to assess the molecular changes during the PD development and upon treatment using MISL and multiple CEST contrasts. First, is to develop and optimize these advanced imaging parameters at 3T for imaging PD neuropathology. Second, is to study the multiple CEST contrasts when there are specific molecular changes during PD progression, and correlate with neuropathology in PD mice. Finally, we will assess the changes of AQP4 upon PD treatment and its interplay with other neuropathology via our multiple contrast analysis in specific brain regions, which could inform treatment efficacy. This advanced MRI platform enables the assess of PD neuropathology in a totally non-invasively imaging of PD neuropathology without contrast agents, especially imaging the role of aquaporin in protein accumulation and neuronal loss. This simultaneously imaging of multiple neuropathology could provide valuable information to monitor disease progression, evaluate treatment and to potentially enable early detection of PD. 本研究將開發一種前沿的MRI技術（MISL和CEST），用於帕金森病（PD）中的水通道蛋白病理、蛋白質和特定分子變化的成像。PD是一種複雜的神經退行性疾病，其特徵是多巴胺神經元的逐漸喪失。最近的研究表明，水通道蛋白在PD的發病機制中起著關鍵作用，尤其是其功能障礙可能會損害腦淋巴系統的清除功能，加劇α-突觸核蛋白的積累和多巴胺神經元的喪失。然而，在疾病進展過程中，非侵入性地檢測這些變化是非常具有挑戰性的，現有的成像技術並不能同時對這這些變化成像，阻礙了我們對其在早期病理中的作用的理解。本項目旨在通過使用CEST和MISL成像水通道蛋白及相關的PD病理來解決這一挑戰。 我們開發多種CEST和MISL對比可以揭示PD的關鍵分子事件，並對AQP4依賴的腦淋巴功能、α-突觸核蛋白積累、多巴胺能神經元喪失和髓鞘異常具有敏感性。我們證明，CEST MRI可以敏感地檢測小鼠中蛋白質、髓鞘和特定分子的變化，例如阿爾茨海默病中的蛋白質聚集和腦淋巴功能障礙、腦癌中葡萄糖剝奪治療期間的葡萄糖攝取和利用變化、多發性硬化症中的脫髓鞘以及AQP4功能，使用前沿的MRI對比，包括葡萄糖CEST、胺、醯胺質子轉移（APT）、核Overhauser效應（NOE）和MISL。總體而言，我們的初步MRI研究強烈表明，這些先進的MRI對比可以檢測PD的標誌，並且足夠敏感以非侵入性和縱向地檢測相關分子、蛋白質和AQP4的變化。 在本項目中，我們將開發一個先進的MRI成像平台，以評估神經病理的發展和治療效果，使用MISL和多種CEST對比。首先，是在3T下開發和優化這些先進的成像參數，用於成像PD神經病理。其次，是研究PD進展過程中特定分子變化時的多種CEST對比，並與PD小鼠的神經病理相關聯。最後，我們將通過多重對比分析評估PD治療後AQP4的變化及其與其他神經病理的相互作用。與神經病理相關的MRI對比可以用於研究PD的區域變化，以評估治療效果。這是一種完全非侵入性的PD神經病理成像，無需使用對比劑，特別是成像水通道蛋白在蛋白質積累和神經元喪失中的作用。這種同時成像多種神經病理的方法可以提供有價值的信息，以監測疾病進展、評估治療效果，並有可能實現PD的早期檢測。

11206425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206425.value: 面向邊緣裝置輸入自適應推理的難度感知聯邦學習

11206425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206425.value: Input-adaptive inference is a pivotal technique for the efficient execution of deep models on continuous data streams. A representative of this strategy is early-exit networks (EENs), which permit early termination of processing on simple inputs that yield confident predictions, thereby reducing inference latency without compromising accuracy. This capability is invaluable in mission-critical edge applications such as intelligent traffic analysis, autonomous vehicles, and smart health monitoring, where timely and reliable decision-making is essential. However, the decentralized and data-scarce nature of edge computing poses challenges in effectively training EENs. Federated learning (FL) offers a promising solution by enabling collaborative training across edge devices without the need to exchange raw data. Yet, current FL methods are inadequate because they lack difficulty-aware training mechanisms, which are fundamental for the accuracy of EENs. This project fills this gap with a novel FL framework that effectively incorporates and leverages difficulty-awareness. Three primary challenges need to be addressed: unaligned exits during model aggregation, ignorance of inference-time resource constraints, and static forward passes in local training. We develop holistic algorithms and techniques that facilitate difficulty-aligned model aggregation, memory-elastic local augmentation, and input-adaptive local fine-tuning, enabling effective and efficient federated training of EENs. To our knowledge, this is the first initiative to explore difficulty-aware federated learning on edge devices. It delivers indispensable strategies, algorithms, and system implementations designed to support the emerging trend of runtime-adaptive deep neural networks in edge applications. 輸入自適應推理（Input-adaptive inference）是在連續數據流上高效執行深度模型的關鍵技術。早期退出網絡（Early-exit networks, EENs）是該策略的代表，允許對產生高置信度預測的簡單輸入提前終止處理，從而在不犧牲準確性的前提下降低推理延遲。這種能力在關鍵任務型邊緣應用中極具價值，例如智慧交通分析、自動駕駛和智慧健康監測，這些場景要求決策必須及時且可靠。然而，邊緣計算的分佈式和數據稀缺特性，為有效訓練早期退出網絡帶來挑戰。聯邦學習（Federated learning, FL）提供了一種具前景的解決方案，使得跨邊緣裝置進行協作訓練而無需交換原始數據成為可能。然而，當前的聯邦學習方法存在不足，因其缺乏對早期退出網絡準確性至關重要的難度感知訓練機制。本研究項目旨在填補這一空白，提出一種新穎的聯邦學習框架，能有效融合並利用難度感知能力。需解決三個核心挑戰：模型聚合過程中各退出點未對齊、忽略推理時的資源約束，以及本地訓練中的靜態前向傳播過程。我們將開發全面的算法和技術，以實現難度對齊的模型聚合、記憶體自適應的本地數據增強，以及輸入自適應的本地微調，從而支持早期退出網絡的高效聯邦訓練。據我們所知，此為首個探索在邊緣裝置上進行難度感知聯邦學習的研究。本項目將提供關鍵的策略、算法及系統實現方案，以支援邊緣應用中運行時自適應深度神經網絡的新興趨勢。

11206525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206525.value: 碳量子點改性三元深共熔溶劑實現大濃差及高穩定的旋流強化膜基微通道吸收式熱池

11206525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206525.value: Buildings are responsible for 20–40% of the world’s energy use and 90% of Hong Kong’s electricity consumption. Advances in energy efficiency and low-GWP refrigerant are both essential for building decarbonization. Utilizing renewable/waste energy is promising, but intermittent energy availability causes inefficiency and under-utilization. Thermal batteries play a significant role in low-carbon energy transition by balancing the supply-demand mismatch. Compared to existing thermal batteries, absorption thermal batteries (ATBs) show great advantages in energy storage density, energy storage efficiency, charging temperature, response rate, and flexibility (discharged for cooling/heating/dehumidification). Besides energy decarbonization, ATB also merits refrigerant decarbonization by using zero-GWP natural fluids like H2O. All these advantages facilitate more sustainable utilization of renewable/waste energy for buildings. However, existing ATB technologies face four major challenges preventing wider application: (1) high crystallization risk (low reliability), (2) high material cost (low cost-effectiveness), (3) poor transport property (low efficiency, slow response), and (4) large reactor size (low density). This proposal seeks to address these deficiencies by developing novel ternary deep-eutectic-solvent (DES) tuned by carbon-quantum-dot (CQD) for membrane-mediated microchannel absorption thermal battery (MMATB) with swirling enhancement. Ternary DESs fabricated by inexpensive methods can eliminate crystallization even under high concentration glides while maintaining excellent transport properties. CQDs can stably enhance heat/mass transfer of ternary DESs without deposition risks. The MMATB offers ultra-high compactness via large specific surface area and bidirectional heat/mass transport switching within single reactor. Additionally, groove-induced swirling flow and machine-learning-based geometry optimization further enhance heat/mass transfer with reduced pressure drop, particularly benefiting DES adoption in MMATB. Preliminary studies demonstrate high viability and cost-effectiveness of the MMATB. Numerical and experimental methods will be employed to complete the following objectives: (1) Model and prototype development of MMATB using CQD-tuned ternary DES for large-concentration-glide and highly-stable energy storage; (2) Characterization of thermophysical properties, sorption kinetics, heat/mass transfer and cycling stability of CQD-tuned ternary DES with various compositions; (3) Investigation of transient charging/discharging behaviors and energy storage performance of MMATB under various working conditions; and (4) Machine-learning-based multi-scale absorbent-battery-building co-optimization to maximize overall performance for different application scenarios. This research is significant for developing high-reliability, cost-effective, high-efficiency, fast-response and high-density energy storage, offering promising building decarbonization solutions. The energy savings are estimated to be 50–80% with payback periods of 2–4 years. It will contribute towards healthy indoor environment, carbon neutrality, and sustainable development goals in Hong Kong and around the world. 建築能耗約占全球總能耗的20–40%，占香港電力消耗的90%。提升能源效率與採用低GWP製冷劑是建築脫碳的關鍵途徑。可再生能源和餘熱的利用前景廣闊，但其間歇性導致能效低下、利用率不足。熱池在低碳能源轉型中發揮著重要作用，能夠有效緩解能源供需不匹配問題。與現有熱池相比，吸收式熱池（Absorption Thermal Battery, ATB）在儲能密度、儲能效率、蓄能溫度、響應速率及靈活性（可用於製冷/供熱/除濕）方面具有顯著優勢。除能源脫碳外，ATB 還可通過採用零 GWP 的自然工質（如 H2O）實現製冷劑脫碳。這些優勢均有助於建築中可再生能源和餘熱利用。 然而，現有 ATB 技術仍面臨四大挑戰，限制了其大規模應用：（1）結晶風險高（可靠性不足）；（2）材料成本高（經濟性較差）；（3）輸運性能差（熱質交換效率低、響應慢）；（4）反應器體積大（設備能量密度低）。本研究擬通過研發碳量子點（Carbon Quantum Dot, CQD）改性的三元深共熔溶劑（Ternary Deep-Eutectic Solvent, DES），並結合膜基微通道吸收式熱池（Membrane-Mediated Microchannel Absorption Thermal Battery, MMATB）與旋渦強化技術，以突破上述瓶頸。三元 DES 可通過低成本製備方法獲得，能夠在高濃度梯度下避免結晶，同時保持優良的輸運性能；CQDs 可穩定增強三元 DES 的傳熱/傳質特性且無沉積風險。MMATB 則依靠單一反應器內的高比表面積與雙向傳熱/傳質切換，實現超高緊湊度。此外，槽紋誘導的旋渦流與基於機器學習的結構優化可進一步降低壓降並強化傳熱/傳質，尤其有利於 DES 在 MMATB 中的應用。 前期研究已表明 MMATB 具有高度可行性與成本效益。擬採用數值模擬與實驗方法完成以下研究目標：（1）基於 CQD 改性三元 DES 的 MMATB 建模與樣機研發，實現大濃度差與高穩定儲能；（2）表徵不同組分的 CQD 改性三元 DES 的熱物理性質、吸收動力學、傳熱/傳質特性及循環穩定性；（3）研究 MMATB 在不同工況下的蓄能釋能瞬態特性與儲能性能；（4）開展基於機器學習的多尺度吸收劑–熱池–建築協同優化，以實現不同應用場景下的整體性能最優。本研究對於發展高可靠性、低成本、高效率、快響應及高密度的儲能技術具有重要意義，並可為建築脫碳提供切實可行的解決方案。預計節能潛力可達50–80%，投資回收期為2–4年。該研究將為香港乃至全球的健康室內環境、碳中和及可持續發展目標作出貢獻。

11206625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206625.value: 網路化多動態系統分散式模型預測控制的事件觸發最佳化及其應用

11206625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206625.value: Distributed control of networked multiple dynamical systems has recently attracted considerable attention due to its wide engineering applications such as formation of mobile robots, vehicles coordination of transportation systems, and so on. Networked multiple dynamical systems are often referred to as multi-agent systems. Many theories and methodologies have been developed for distributed control of multi-agent systems in the past years. One popular strategy is the distributed model predictive control as it can simultaneously handle systems constraints, optimize performance and ensure system stability. Most existing approaches to distributed model predictive control are developed for multi-agent systems under decoupled constraints though practical multi-agent systems are often subject to coupled constraints, which makes it much more challenging to solve the optimization problem for distributed model predictive control in a distributed manner. Some recent works have addressed this difficulty of coupled constraints but only achieve sublinear convergence rates. It implies that those optimization algorithms require a relatively large number of iterations to reach optimal solutions, which is undesirable for real-time control of multi-agent systems. It is more desirable to develop optimization algorithms with linear convergence rates as it can significantly reduce the number of iterations for optimization. In addition, it is noted that those algorithms require frequent communication among neighboring agents to solve the concerned optimization problems. This might become a prohibiting issue if communication networks are subject to bandwidth limits which is often the case in practice. Event-triggered strategies are known to be very effective in reducing the number of data transmission between neighboring agents. Motivated by these observations, this project proposes to investigate and develop novel event-triggered optimization algorithms with linear convergence rates for distributed model predictive control of multi-agent systems under coupled constraints. In particular, we will investigate (i) the problem of event-triggered optimization with linear convergence rates for distributed model predictive control of multi-agent systems under coupled constraints over undirected communication graphs, and (ii) the problem of event-triggered optimization with linear convergence rates for distributed model predictive control of multi-agent systems under coupled constraints over directed communication graphs. This project, by addressing these problems, will explore and develop novel event-triggered optimization theories and methodologies for distributed model predictive control of multi-agent systems under coupled constraints over undirected/directed communication graphs. The outcomes of this project are expected to enrich the theoretical foundation and to provide more solid analysis and synthesis tools in distributed model predictive control of multi-agent systems. 網路化多動態系統的分散式協同控制因其廣泛的工程應用（例如無人機或地面車輛編隊、連網多移動機器人、微電網網路間的電力分配等）而備受關注。網路化多動態系統通常被稱為多智能體系統。近年來，許多針對網路化多動態系統或多智能體系統的分散式協同控制的理論、技術和工具已被開發。一種特殊的分散式控制策略是所謂的分散式模型預測控制，它可以同時處理輸入/狀態約束、最佳化效能並確保系統穩定性。大多數現有的分散式模型預測控制方法都是針對解耦限制下的多智能體系統所開發的。然而，工程應用中的多智能體系統通常受到耦合約束的影響。這些耦合約束的存在使得每個智能體難以以分散式方式解決分散式模型預測控制的最佳化問題。一些近期的研究解決了耦合約束帶來的難題，但收斂速度僅達到亞線性。換句話說，這些工作中開發的最佳化演算法需要在每個控制週期進行大量迭代才能獲得相應的模型預測控制器，這對於多智能體系統的即時控制來說是非常不利的。對於分散式模型預測控制，開發具有線性收斂率的新型最佳化演算法更為可取，因為它可以顯著減少最佳化過程中的迭代次數。此外，值得注意的是，這些演算法需要相鄰智能體之間進行頻繁通訊才能解決相關的最佳化問題。如果通訊網路受到頻寬限制（這在實踐中經常發生），這可能會成為一個很難解決的問題。受這些觀察結果的啟發，本項目提出研究開發具有線性收斂率的新型事件觸發最佳化演算法，用於耦合約束下多智能體系統的分散式模型預測控制。具體來說，我們將研究以下三個問題：（i）在無向/有向通信圖上耦合約束條件下，多智能體系統分佈式模型預測控制的事件觸發優化問題（具有線性收斂率）；（ii）在有向通信圖上耦合約束條件下，多智能體系統分佈式模型預測控制的事件和系統優化問題（具有線性收斂率優化）；本項目將透過解決這些問題，探索並發展在無向/有向通訊圖上耦合約束條件下，多智能體系統分散式模型預測控制的事件觸發最佳化新理論和方法。本項目的成果可望豐富耦合約束條件下多智能體系統分散式模型預測控制的理論基礎，並提供更可靠的分析和綜合工具。

11206825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206825.value: 具有延遲和壓縮通訊的分散式多智能體學習/優化

11206825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206825.value: Distributed multi-agent learning through optimization methods in networked cyber-physical systems has been a hot research topic in recent years due to its advantages, such as robustness, modularity, and scalability. It has been recognized that networked cyber-physical systems will become increasingly data-driven. This proposal aims to explore some fundamental research issues that arise at the intersection of these areas. Unlike conventional centralized learning/optimization methods, multi-agents conduct local training steps and exchange information with neighboring agents or a parameter server in the distributed learning/optimization methods. Such a distributed framework reduces centralized schemes' computation and communication burden and preserves owners' data privacy. The necessity of efficient distributed learning algorithms through optimization techniques with good convergence performance and low computational complexity for practical applications is not just a goal but a pressing need that should be addressed urgently. This proposal primarily addresses unbounded communication delays and compression as sources of imperfect communication. In complex networks, the transmitted data may be imperfect due to communication channels' technical or economic constraints. Hence, developing a new approach is necessary to guarantee the convergence of distributed learning/optimization algorithms under such imperfect communication conditions. This proposal primarily addresses unbounded communication delays and compression as sources of imperfect communication. Hence, a two-time-scale approach is introduced to guarantee the convergence of distributed learning algorithms under these challenging conditions. The proposed approach shall provide significant theoretical and practical implications. Furthermore, the proposal also utilizes the two-time-scale approach to design effective time-triggered schemes that balance communication cost and convergence performance of distributed learning algorithms. If successfully implemented, the theoretical advancements in this proposal will serve as a cornerstone for the future of distributed learning /optimization algorithms in practical applications, demonstrating the potential impact of this research on the field. 近年來，基於最佳化方法的網路化資訊物理系統中的分散式多智能體學習因其穩健性、模組化和可擴展性等優勢，已成為研究的熱點。人們已經認識到，網路化資訊物理系統將日益由數據驅動。本提案旨在探討這些領域交叉領域中出現的一些基礎研究問題。 與傳統的集中式學習/最佳化方法不同，在分散式學習/最佳化方法中，多智能體進行本地訓練步驟，並與鄰近智能體或參數伺服器交換資訊。這種分散式框架減少了集中式方案的計算和通訊負擔，並保護了擁有者的資料隱私。對於實際應用而言，透過最佳化技術實現具有良好收斂性能和低計算複雜度的高效分散式學習演算法不僅是一個目標，更是一個亟待解決的迫切需求。 本提案主要解決無界通訊延遲和壓縮作為不完美通訊的根源。在複雜網路中，由於通訊頻道的技術或經濟限制，傳輸的資料可能有缺陷。因此，有必要開發一種新的方法來保證分散式學習/最佳化演算法在這種不完美通訊條件下的收斂性。 本提案主要針對無界通訊延遲和壓縮作為不完美通訊的根源。因此，引入了一種雙時間尺度方法來保證分散式學習演算法在這些具有挑戰性的條件下的收斂性。該方法將具有重要的理論和實踐意義。此外，本提案也利用雙時間尺度方法設計有效的時間觸發方案，以平衡分散式學習演算法的通訊成本和收斂性能。如果成功實施，本提案中的理論進展將成為未來分散式學習/最佳化演算法在實際應用中的基石，並展現出這項研究對該領域的潛在影響。

11207325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11207325.value: 通過選擇性脫合金開發高強度並具有出色吸能能力的塊體納米超結構高熵合金

11207325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11207325.value: Prof Li, Jia Prof Wang, Qing Dr Zhou, Hao

11207325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207325.value: Energy-absorbing materials have garnered significant attention in industries such as aerospace and transportation. Traditionally, these materials were designed around cellular structures. However, a recent trend towards nano-architected materials, manufactured through additive manufacturing like 3D printing, has emerged to address the common strength-plasticity tradeoff found in conventional options. Despite substantial efforts invested in this field, upscaling printed nano-architected materials remains a notable hurdle. This proposal aims to address these challenges by developing bulk nano-architected high-entropy alloys. Our research begins with designing high-entropy spinodal alloys featuring bi-continuous phases as precursor materials by utilizing machine learning. We intend to develop a cost-effective but efficient electrochemical dealloying technique to form nano-architectures within these high-entropy alloy precursors via selective electrochemical dealloying. Our preliminary results suggest that this innovative method can successfully pinpoint high-entropy spinodal alloys within a quinary alloy system. These alloys can then be leveraged to fabricate bulk nano-architected energy-absorbing materials with exceptional strength and plasticity, surpassing current materials in published literature. However, understanding the mechanisms behind these superior properties and assessing the general applicability of this approach remain crucial. If funded, our plan is to broaden our methodology to encompass more intricate multicomponent systems with practical engineering applications. Our primary focus will be on investigating the mechanisms responsible for the high strength, excellent plasticity, and superior fracture resistance demonstrated by bulk nano-architected high-entropy alloys produced through dealloying. This investigation will be carried out through collaborative research efforts combining multi-scale experiments and simulations. 吸能材料在航空航天和交通運輸等領域備受矚目。傳統上，這類材料的設計多圍繞蜂窩結構展開。然而，為了解決傳統材料常見的強度-塑性權衡問題，近年來逐漸興起通過增材製造（如3D打印）製備的纳米架構材料。儘管該領域已投入大量研究，但如何將打印的纳米架構材料規模化生產仍是重大挑戰。本提案旨在通過開發塊體纳米架構高熵合金來應對這些難題。我們的研究將首先運用機器學習技術，設計具有雙連續相的高熵調幅分解合金作為前驅體材料。隨後計劃開發一種低成本、高效率的電化學去合金化技術，通過選擇性電化學腐蝕在這些高熵合金前驅體中形成纳米結構。初步研究結果表明，這項創新方法能成功定位五元合金體系中的高熵調幅分解合金，並可進一步用於製備兼具卓越強度與塑性的塊體纳米架構吸能材料，其性能超越現有文獻報導的材料。然而，理解這些優異性能背後的機理，以及評估該方法的普適性仍至關重要。若獲得資助，我們計劃將研究方法拓展至更複雜的多組分體系，以滿足實際工程應用需求。研究重點將聚焦於探究去合金化製備的塊體纳米架構高熵合金所展現的高強度、優異塑性和卓越抗斷裂性能的內在機制。這項研究將通過結合多尺度實驗與模擬的協作研究方式展開。

11208025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208025.value: 基於模型預測的潛熱儲熱系統充放功率控制技術研發

11208025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11208025.value: Prof XIAO, Fu Prof Xu, Tao

11208025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208025.value: Latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES) systems, which typically use phase-change materials (PCMs) as the storage medium, can absorb a significant amount of thermal energy during the solidifying process, that can later be released through melting and used when needed. LHTES is a key technology for decarbonizing building operations as it enhances energy flexibility with a high potential to save building energy, reduce cost and improve grid stability. However, this potential has not been fully realized due to the lack of power control, which regulate the charging and discharging rates of LHTES to meet building energy management needs. Controlling the charging and discharging rates of LHTES is challenging owing to the variations in PCM thermal properties, such as thermal resistance and capacitance, during phase changes. To date, this issue has not been addressed in the literature or industry. We thus propose to explore this issue by leveraging model predictive control technology, with the goal of developing an efficient method for regulating LHTES charging and discharging rates to maximize the potential of LHTES for enhancing building energy flexibility. Through a series of collaborative and interconnected research tasks, organized around four objectives, we will address two key challenges: the absence of a control-oriented dynamic model that balances accuracy and complexity, and the need for a computationally efficient method to solve the complex online optimization problem associated with the control strategy. In Tasks 1.1 and 1.2, we will develop such a control-oriented dynamic model and validate it through experimental studies (Objective 1). In Tasks 2.1 and 2.2, we will design a model predictive control strategy for LHTES systems and validate it experimentally (Objective 2). In Tasks 3.1 and 3.2, we will create a control toolkit for the proposed model predictive control strategy (Objectives 3) and assess its potential for enhancing building energy flexibility and efficiency by implementing it in various application scenarios (Objectives 4). The assembled research team, with co-investigators selected for their relevant expertise, will collaborate closely to achieve the proposed objectives. The key deliverables of this project—a control-oriented dynamic model and a model predictive control strategy with its toolkit—will serve as valuable resources for researchers and professionals in building energy management and the relevant industry. In the long term, LHTES power control will significantly advance building energy flexibility, contributing to carbon emission reduction, supporting Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050 and worldwide sustainable development. 潛熱儲熱系統（LHTES）是一種利用相變材料（PCM）來儲存和釋放熱量的技術。 這種材料在凝固時會吸收大量熱量，在熔化時又能將這些熱量釋放出來，以供後續使用。 由於它能夠提高能源使用的靈活性、降低建築運行成本並改善電網穩定性，因此被認為是實現建築低碳運行的重要技術。 然而，目前還沒有有效的辦法來精確控制LHTES的充放功率，這使得它的潛力尚未完全發揮。 控制LHTES系統的充放功率並不容易，因為相變材料在凝固和熔化過程中，其熱特性（比如導熱率和熱容）會發生显著變化。 針對這一挑戰，本项目提出了一種新的解決方案，採用模型預測控制技術來調節LHTES的充放功率。我們將重點解決兩個關鍵問題：一是建立一個準確實用的動態模型; 二是开发一種高效的在線優化解決算法。我們還將開發一套相應的控制软件工具包，並將其應用在不同場景中，評估它對提高建築能效和靈活性的實際效果。 本项目的核心成果包括：以控制為導向的動態模型，在線優化解決算法，以及相應的软件工具包。 這些成果不僅為研究人員提供參考，也為行業實踐提供技術支援。長遠來看，這項研究將顯著提升建築能源使用的靈活性，助力減少碳排放，並支援香港實現《2050氣候行動藍圖》的目標，同時也為全球可持續發展貢獻力量。

11208125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208125.value: Neuhash：基於雜湊的高效能神經形態視覺處理架構

11208125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208125.value: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and vision sensors in the Internet of Things (IoT) promises to enable many applications ranging from handphones with visual recognition to smart glasses, smart cameras for drones, etc. The significant challenge for this is the simultaneous requirement of high frame rate and low size, weight, and power (SWaP) for many applications, such as eye tracking or collision avoidance in drones. A high frame rate produces copious data that invariably requires considerable energy and latency for processing. This proposal aims to overcome these challenges using novel architectures, integrated circuits, and neuromorphic vision sensors. Neuromorphic cameras have pixels that produce data asynchronously only if there is sufficient change in temporal contrast, thus compressing data at the source and allowing fast readout of active pixels since the whole frame does not need access. However, this new format of asynchronous, sparse event data requires redesigning algorithms, architectures, and hardware of the following processor. We propose two solutions that exploit the sparsity of event data. In the first architecture for low-level image processing, we propose to use a hashing-bashed bloom filter (BF) method from computer architecture to map the output of the high-dimensional sensor array to a smaller-sized memory, exploiting the sparsity of input data. Conventional BFs suffer from the need to reset the memory to reduce false detections frequently. To this end, we propose to extend the BF to a second dimension with the possibility of a partial reset of the oldest rows. In the second architecture for high-level object recognition, we propose to use spiking neural networks (SNN) with in-memory computing to accelerate its execution. Using analog locally-sensitive hash (LSH) functions, neurons most likely to fire in the following layers can be estimated, and the remaining can be turned off. This leads to energy savings and an increase in throughput since the slow serial operation of neural state update can be reduced in proportion to sparsity. Both methods provide a completely new degree of freedom to study approximation-resource tradeoffs for vision systems. The first method is expected to yield >10X reduction in memory and ~5X reduction in energy for memory access, while the second is estimated to improve energy-efficiency and throughput of SNNs by ~ 4-10X. We expect the outcomes of this project to enable many new revolutionary vision applications in the future. 在互聯網時代(IoT)，人工智能與視覺傳感器的結合提升多種應用的效能，如手機、智能眼鏡、無人機智能攝像頭等。在人眼追蹤或無人機避障這種應用最具挑戰性的需求是高幀率、小尺寸、輕及低功耗(SWaP)。然而，因高幀率生成的大量數據不可避免地需要高能量及處理延遲。此計畫的目標是透過新穎的架構、積體電路及神經形態視覺傳感器解決這些挑戰。神經形態視覺傳感器的像素只有在足夠的時間上的對比才會產生異步資料，從而在源頭壓縮資料量並且快速讀出活躍的像素，而不是整幀。這種新型的異步且稀疏的事件資料需要重新設計處理器的算法、架構及硬體。我們基於事件資料的稀疏性提出兩種方案。第一種是低階圖像處理的架構，使用電腦架構中基於哈希函數的布隆過濾器(BF)，並利用事件的稀疏性來壓縮高維度的傳感器輸出到小內存。傳統的BFs為了解決高錯誤檢測率而頻繁地重製內存。為此，我們提議擴展BF至二維，且只有部分的BF行需要重製。第二種則是高階目標檢測。我們提出結合脈衝神經網路(SNN)及存內計算來加速運算。透過基於模擬信號的局部品感哈希(LSH)函數，可以預測最有可能發射的神經元，並關閉其餘的神經元。此提議可有效的節能並提高吞吐量，因神經元的串型狀態更新可以與稀疏性成比例減少。這兩種方法提供一個全新的研究自由度在視覺系統上的近似資源權衡。第一個提案可望達到近十倍的內存壓縮及五倍的節能在內存訪問，而第二個提案可望提升四至十倍的節能及吞吐量。我們預期此項目的成果在未來可開啟全新且具有革命性的視覺應用。

11208425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208425.value: 基於計算機視覺與機器學習的城市建築能源模型研發

11208425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208425.value: Climate change poses a significant challenge to global sustainable development, necessitating substantial reductions in carbon dioxide emissions and energy consumption. In high-density cities, building stock is typically the largest energy consumer. In Hong Kong, residential buildings accounted for 28% of electricity use in 2022, which highlights their crucial role in climate change. Consequently, by 2050, the Hong Kong government plans to reduce the electricity consumption of residential buildings by 20%–30%, with half of the targets expected to be met by 2035. This ambitious programme faces considerable challenges and relies on assessing and forecasting the building stock’s energy consumption and energy-saving potential. Urban building energy models (UBEMs) have emerged as valuable tools for supporting urban decisions and are typically classified as top-down and bottom-up. Bottom-up models enable the assessment of the specific effects of renovation but suffer from the difficulty in obtaining sufficient detailed data. Given their vast stock and relatively homogeneous functions, residential buildings are particularly advantageous for energy consumption assessment. However, the current UBEM usage in Hong Kong does not support effective urban retrofitting. Most present UBEMs rely on oversimplified prototypes and may therefore incorrectly amplify the energy-saving potential, while ponderous individual architectural considerations lead to high computational costs and thus hinder applications in urban-scale decision-making. Thus, bottom-up UBEMs balancing accuracy and practicality are urgently needed. This project will explore a framework for modelling the energy consumption of urban buildings and optimising retrofit strategies, and will include the following steps. 1) Element and prototype extraction: Computer vision will be used to extract factors influencing building energy consumption and perform cluster analysis to identify building prototypes. 2) Feature analysis and mechanism identification: Performance simulations will be carried out using prototype buildings to identify key factors and mechanisms. 3) Strategy proposal and effect validation: Artificial neural networks will be used to map relationships among existing building data, energy conservation measures, and energy consumption and develop an urban residential building energy model. The maximum energy-saving potential and corresponding retrofit solutions for specific goals will be identified, and actual energy consumption changes before and after retrofitting will be used for model validation. By developing a UBEM, this project will offer smarter retrofitting building choices, better retrofitting measures, and clearer outcome predictions for energy renovations and thus support energy savings, carbon emission reduction, and environmental protection in Hong Kong. 氣候變遷對全球永續發展構成重大挑戰，亟需大幅減少二氧化碳排放與能源消耗。在高密度城市中，建築存量通常是最大的能源消耗來源。在香港，2022年住宅建築佔據了28%的電力使用量，凸顯其在氣候變遷中的關鍵角色。香港政府計劃到2050年將住宅建築的電力消耗量減少20%至30%，其中一半目標預計於2035年前達成。這一雄心勃勃的計劃面臨重大挑戰，依賴於對建築存量能源消耗及其節能潛力的評估與預測。 城市建築能源模型（UBEMs）已成為支持城市決策的寶貴工具，通常分為自上而下（top-down）與自下而上（bottom-up）兩類。自下而上的模型能夠評估改造的具體效果，但面臨獲取足夠詳細數據的困難。由於住宅建築存量龐大且功能相對固定，其在能源消耗評估方面尤具優勢。然而，香港當前使用的UBEMs無法有效支持城市規模的改造工程。現有的大多數UBEMs依賴過於簡化的原型，可能錯誤放大節能潛力，而對個別建築的繁瑣考量則導致高計算成本，從而阻礙其在城市規模決策中的應用。因此，亟需研發兼顧準確性與實用性的自下而上的UBEM。 本項目將探索一個用於模擬城市建築能源消耗及優化改造策略的框架，包括以下步驟： 1. 要素提取與原型構建：利用計算機視覺提取影響建築能源消耗的因素，並進行聚類分析以識別建築原型。 2. 特徵分析與機制識別：使用原型建築進行性能模擬，識別關鍵因素與作用機制。 3. 策略提出與效果驗證：運用人工神經網絡映射現有建築與能源消耗之間的關係，開發城市住宅建築能源模型。 通過開發UBEM，本項目將提供更智能的建築改造選擇以及更清晰的能源改造結果預測，從而支持香港的節能、減碳及環境保護目標。

11208625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208625.value: 形狀記憶高分子在三維微/奈米結構於太赫茲超材料器件的動態調控

11208625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208625.value: Terahertz (THz) technology is rapidly advancing, with significant applications in communication, imaging, and sensing. Its deep penetration capabilities and non-ionizing nature make it safe for health-related applications. By 2023, the global THz technology market was valued at approximately HK$7 billion, with an annual growth rate exceeding 17%. THz metadevices are pivotal in achieving revolutionary capabilities in THz beam focusing and steering. As THz metadevices continue to evolve, there is an increasing demand for dynamic control over their properties to enable on-demand functional switching within a single device, facilitating more sophisticated operations. Mechanical reconfiguration emerges as a promising tuning method due to its ability to reshape individual unit cells of metasurfaces at a fundamental level. However, the micrometer-scale size of THz metastructures poses a challenge in reshaping specific regions of the metadevice independently, often resulting in a focus on altering the overall shape of the device and thereby limiting tuning flexibility. Shape memory polymers (SMPs) are intelligent materials renowned for their shape-memory properties, capable of assuming multiple shapes. Integrating SMPs into THz metadevices offers a solution to the challenge of completely overhauling the designed topography of metasurfaces. A significant hurdle in utilizing SMPs in THz metadevices is achieving precise shape control at the microscopic level and effectively integrating SMPs with other materials optimized for THz wave interactions. In this proposed project, we aim to address these challenges by leveraging imprint and reversal imprint technologies to fabricate and precisely deform SMP micro- and nano-structures on THz metasurfaces. Additionally, we plan to explore the incorporation of SMPs into multiple-layered metasurfaces to enable advanced functionalities. Our objective is to achieve dynamic programming of THz beam focusing and steering with a broad control range using SMP-based THz metadevices, while also allowing the tuning of the operating wavelength.

11209425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11209425.value: 聯邦學習的熱動力學方法：性能極限探討和應用

11209425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209425.value: Federated Learning (FL) is a Machine Learning (ML) technique that enables multiple ML devices (workers) to learn statistical inference without exchanging data across these devices. Although many FL algorithms have been proposed in the literature, it is not clear whether the proposed FL algorithms can actually converge to the centralized version, in which all distributed datasets are placed and used in training in one single server. There have been some studies investigating the performance gap between FL and the centralized version; however, these studies only consider deterministic bounds. Since all FL algorithms belong to the category of statistical ML, only statistical performance bounds should be considered. This project represents the first attempt to explore the statistical fundamental limits of FL. Specifically, we propose to develop a thermodynamics approach and apply the ergodic theory in thermodynamics to the study of the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of statistical convergence bounds. We will study the fundamental limits of FL training performance from three aspects, namely, computation efficiency, communication efficiency, and impact of heterogeneous data. We will analyze the statistical convergence properties of FL from these three key perspectives. First, to improve computation efficiency, we propose to employ a first-order momentum method, Nesterov Accelerate Gradient (NAG) momentum, on both worker and aggregator sides to increase FL convergence speed; furthermore, the interaction between worker and aggregator momenta will be analyzed, forming the basis for optimizing the momentum factors. Second, to improve communication efficiency, we will develop a three-tier hierarchical FL framework. It restrains communication overhead within local networks while leveraging momentum acceleration at all three tiers (worker-edge-cloud). Third, to mitigate the negative effect incurred by heterogeneous data, we will develop contrastive aggregation personalization, contrastive model personalization, and contrastive momentum personalization inspired by contrastive learning and knowledge distillation. The proposed research has the potential to significantly advance the biomedical industry, which is characterized by its sensitivity to diagnosis accuracy, diagnosis time, and patient data privacy. This is because the proposed methodologies address the performance limits of FL from three key aspects (i.e., computation efficiency, communication efficiency, and data heterogeneity), aligning perfectly with the aforementioned characteristics of the biomedical industry. In this project, we will implement a corneal disease classifier trained by FL, as a real-world demonstration of our theoretical results. Digital twin technologies will also be incorporated, providing feedback on the theoretical methodologies to facilitate further improvements. 聯邦學習（FL）使多個機器學習設備（工作節點）能夠在無需跨設備交換數據的前提下開展統計推理學習。儘管文獻中已提出多種聯邦學習算法，但這些算法能否真正收斂至中心化版本的結果——即所有分布式數據集集中於單一服務器進行訓練的情形——目前尚不明确。已有部分研究探討聯邦學習與中心化版本之間的性能差距，然而這類研究僅關注確定性邊界極限。由於所有聯邦學習算法均屬於統計機器學習範疇，因此應僅考慮統計性能邊界極限。本項目首次嘗試探索聯邦學習的統計基本極限，具體而言，我們計劃構建一種熱力學方法，並運用熱力學中的遍歷理論，研究統計收斂邊界存在的必要條件與充分條件。我們將從計算效率、通信效率及異構數據影響三個方面，探究聯邦學習訓練性能的基本極限，並基於這三個關鍵視角分析其統計收斂特性。首先，為提升計算效率，我們提議採用一階動量方法——Nesterov加速梯度（NAG）動量，以加快聯邦學習的收斂速度；此外，我們還將評估工作節點動量與聚合器動量之間的相互作用，為動量因子的優化奠定基礎。其次，為提高通信效率，我們將開發三層次的分層聯邦學習框架。該框架既能約束本地網絡內的通信開銷，又能在工作節點、邊緣節點、雲端這三個層級均實現動量加速。第三，為減緩異構數據帶來的負面影響，我們將借鑒對比學習與知識蒸餾的思路，開發對比聚合個性化、對比模型個性化及對比動量個性化方法。 上述研究有望顯著推動生物醫藥行業的發展，該行業的顯著特點是對診斷準確性、診斷時間及患者數據隱私極度敏感。而本研究提出的方法從計算效率、通信效率、數據異構性這三個關鍵方面解決了聯邦學習的性能極限問題，與生物醫藥行業的上述特點高度契合。在本項目中，我們將研發一個基於聯邦學習訓練的角膜疾病分類器，作為理論成果的真實應用示範；同時還將引入數字孿生技術，為理論方法提供反饋，從而推動其進一步完善。

11210525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11210525.value: 開發具有自我調整限域聚合物網路的纖維液體金屬導體用於可拉伸電子互連

11210525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210525.value: Most issues in stretchable electronics come from the interfacial connections between different parts which frequently undergo stress/strain concentration. In particular, the interface mismatch between stretchable conductors and rigid microelectronics results in irreversible changes in electrical resistance and permanent interface failure. Designing flexible interconnects that can bridge mechanical mismatches and maintain reliable conductive contact is therefore highly desired. Gallium-based liquid metals (LMs) with a unique combination of metallic conductivity, low toxicity, and fluidity at room temperature have emerged as a promising class of materials for the development of stretchable electronics. Considering their high surface energy which may cause depletion from coated substrates, LMs are usually blended and processed with various polymers to form flexible LM-polymer composites for further development of flexible conductors. However, there are critical issues in the development and application of LM-based flexible conductors. (1) They are not inherently conductive due to a thin layer of polymer that forms between the LM particles. (2) Post-treatments using mechanical forces and lasers can assist sintering of the LM particles within the composites, but the performance of the processed samples varies due to the irreversible damages of the polymer network. (3) They show limitations in interconnecting with microelectronics when service in stretchable electronics: encapsulation is typically applied to prevent the leaking of LMs, but this also makes the conductors less functional for soldering and welding. Targeting at these challenges, in this project, we aim to develop an easy-to-use toolbox of fibrous liquid-metal conductors and corresponding processing technologies for the fabrication of stretchable electronic interconnects. Our preliminary studies show that the dynamic confinement derived from a stretchable-yet-adhesive polymer network can effectively stabilize the conductive path of the liquid-metal conductor and offer high adhesion to diverse surfaces, allowing for efficient soldering. Leveraging the dynamic bonding nature and the confinement effect of the polymer network, we propose that fibrous liquid-metal conductors with large surface-volume ratios and high LM loading ratios may potentially overcome the issues facing by bulk composite films, and thus they can be welded and integrated into various patterns and structures for the fabrication of electronic interconnects. The outcome of this project will not only advance our fundamental understanding on the surface science of LM-polymer assemblies, but also provide new insights into the design of flexible condoctors and electronic interconnects which will benefit their potential applications in wearable electronics, IoT devices, and healthcare-related applications. 可拉伸电子器件中的大多数问题来自不同部件之间的界面连接，这些部件经常受到应力/应变集中。特别是，可拉伸导体和刚性微电子之间的界面不匹配会导致电阻的不可逆变化和永久性界面故障。因此，非常需要设计能够弥合机械失配并保持可靠导电接触的柔性互连。 镓基液态金属具有金属导电性、低毒性和室温流动性的独特组合，已成为开发可拉伸电子产品的一类有前途的材料。在本项目中，我们旨在开发一种易于使用的纤维状液态金属导体工具箱和相应的加工技术，用于制造可拉伸电子互连。我们的初步研究表明，可拉伸且具有粘合性的聚合物网络产生的动态约束不仅可以有效地稳定液态金属导体的导电路径，而且还可以对各种表面提供高附着力，从而实现高效焊接。利用动态聚合物网络的动态键合特性，我们提出具有上述特征的纤维状液态金属导体可以焊接并集成到各种图案和结构中，用于制造电子互连。该项目的成果不仅将增进我们对 LM 聚合物组件表面科学的基本理解，而且还将为柔性导体和电子互连的设计提供新的见解，这将有利于它们在可穿戴电子产品、物联网设备和医疗保健相关应用中的潜在应用。

11210825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11210825.value: 兼具快速計算和高空間分辨率的水力混合模型以實現污水管網的數字控制

11210825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210825.value: Combined and sanitary sewer overflows are major contributors to waterway pollution in urban areas with well-established sewer infrastructures. A significant contributing factor is the non-optimal use of the conveyance capacity of a network in wet days. Real-time hydraulic control is an important tool for the reduction of sewage overflows. It operates sewage pumping stations and valves/weirs/gates in real-time prior to, during, and after rainfalls, so that the network’s conveyance capacity is more effectively utilised, and the overflow incidents and/or volumes reduced. Model predictive control is one of the most powerful real-time control method. It finds the optimal control action by testing the performance of an enormous number of control options using an in-built sewer hydraulic model. However, the currently available mechanistic or data-driven sewer hydraulic models are either too slow or too coarse (in terms of accuracy and/or spatial resolution) to support real-time control of large-scale sewer networks. The overall aim of this project is to construct a new sewer network model with a fast computing speed and a high spatial resolution, to enable model predictive control of catchment-scale sewer networks. In the first step, we will develop a novel hybrid approach to solving mechanistic pipe hydraulic models, namely the Saint-Venant equations. By developing a vector-based, data-driven method to solve the discretised Saint-Venant equations, the solving process is expected to be accelerated by 1-2 orders of magnitude, yet with a high-level spatial resolution. In the second step, we will develop a numerical framework that effectively integrates the above-developed hybrid pipe model into a physics-encoded graph neural network, representing the sewer network structure, to form a network-wide hydraulic model. Allowing parallel computing, this framework will accelerate the solving process by a further 1-2 orders of magnitude. These substantial improvements to the efficiency of the sewer network hydraulic models while achieving the accuracy and spatial resolution of the full solutions, enable the application of model predictive control to catchment-scale sewer networks, which will be demonstrated for the first time in this project via both simulation-based and real-life case studies. The key innovation underpinning the proposed efficient hydraulic models is the effective integration of mechanistic knowledge with data-driven modelling. This hybrid approach could potentially benefit other engineering systems facing similar modelling and control challenges. With strong backgrounds in the modelling and control of urban drainage systems, the PI and Co-I are well positioned to lead the project to success. 本項目擬構建一種兼具快速計算速度和高空間分辨率的新型污水管網水動力模型，以實現流域尺度污水管網的模型預測控制。首先我們將開發一種求解单一管道水力機理模型（即聖維南方程組）的新型混合方法。該方法基於向量化的數據驅動方法來求解離散化的聖維南方程組，預計求解過程可在提速1-2個數量級的同時保持較高的空間分辨率。 第二步，我們將開發一個數值计算框架，將上述混合管道模型集成到物理編碼圖神經網路中（該網路可表征污水管網結構），從而形成全網水力模型。該框架支持并行計算，將使求解過程進一步提速1-2個數量級。通過這些方法能夠顯著提升污水管網水力模型的效率，在保證完整求解準度和空間分辨率的前提下支持模型預測控制，使之能夠應用於流域尺度污水管網。本項目將首次通過仿真案例和實際案例研究對此進行驗證。 本研究提出的高效水力模型的核心創新點是將機理知識與數據驅動建模有效融合。這種混合方法有望為其他面臨類似建模和控制挑戰的工程系統提供借鑒。 項目負責人（PI）和合作研究者（Co-I）憑藉在城市排水系統建模與控制領域的深厚背景，具備引領本項目取得成功的充分條件。

11211025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11211025.value: 基於物理的飛機軌跡生成方法用於終端空域設計評估

11211025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211025.value: The terminal airspace surrounding an airport is characterized by high flight density and complex structures. While aircraft are generally assigned standard arrival and departure routes, deviations frequently occur due to factors such as air traffic control directives, pilot decisions, surveillance limitations, and varying flight performance. Accurately capturing these trajectory uncertainties and generating realistic trajectories is pivotal when revising established routes and guiding the design of future terminal airspace. Traditional simulation-based methods often involve complex, time-consuming, scenario-specific setups and lack the ability to consider actual operational factors. AI generative methods offer promise for rapid trajectory generation but face critical limitations. A key challenge is integrating real-world physical factors, such as aircraft dynamics and operational constraints, into generative models. Many current methods oversimplify or omit these essential factors, focusing on replicating historical data patterns without incorporating the real-world dynamics governing aircraft behavior. Additionally, these models often focus on historical distribution modeling, limiting their flexibility to adapt to novel designs or changing operational scenarios. This gap highlights the need for a more comprehensive approach that incorporates physical laws and operational realities, enabling accurate simulations of both current and novel airspace configurations. In this project, we propose developing physics-informed generative methods to generate realistic aircraft trajectories for terminal airspace design evaluation. The investigation will focus on three main areas: (1) Physics-informed neural network modeling, embedding aircraft dynamics and design constraints into the generative process to ensure adherence to real-world physical laws; (2) Data-driven modeling of trajectory uncertainties, capturing flight behaviors and operational factors and replicating historical patterns; and (3) Transferable design-deviated pattern discovery across various airspace designs, ensuring the model can be applied to diverse airport terminal airspace configurations, enhancing flexibility and transferability. By embedding physical constraints into the generative process, our approach bridges the gap between rapid, efficient modeling and the complex realities of real-world operations, offering a robust framework for comprehensive airspace design assessments. This framework will facilitate fast, flexible, and accurate evaluations of airspace redesigns, improving decision-making in airspace management, while enhancing efficiency, reducing delays, and increasing safety across airport operations. 機場周圍的終端空域具有高飛行密度和複雜結構的特徵。雖然飛機通常被指派標準的進場和離場航線，但由於空中交通管制指令、飛行員決策、監視限制以及不同的飛行性能等因素，經常會發生偏離。準確捕捉這些軌跡不確定性並生成真實的軌跡，對於修訂既定航線和指導未來終端空域設計至關重要。傳統的基於模擬的方法通常涉及複雜、耗時、特定場景的設置，且缺乏考慮實際運行因素的能力。 人工智慧生成方法為快速軌跡生成提供了希望，但面臨關鍵限制。一個主要挑戰是將現實世界的物理因素（如飛機動力學和運行約束）整合到生成模型中。許多現有方法過度簡化或忽略了這些重要因素，僅專注於複製歷史數據模式，而沒有納入支配飛機行為的現實世界動力學。此外，這些模型通常專注於歷史分布建模，限制了它們適應新設計或變化運行場景的靈活性。這一差距凸顯了需要一種更全面的方法，該方法納入物理定律和運行現實，能夠準確模擬當前和新型空域配置。 在本專案中，我們提出開發基於物理資訊的生成方法，以生成用於終端空域設計評估的真實飛機軌跡。研究將聚焦於三個主要領域：(1) 基於物理資訊的神經網路建模，將飛機動力學和設計約束嵌入生成過程，以確保遵守現實世界的物理定律；(2) 軌跡不確定性的數據驅動建模，捕捉飛行行為和運行因素並複製歷史模式；以及 (3) 跨各種空域設計的可轉移設計偏離模式發現，確保模型可應用於不同的機場終端空域配置，增強靈活性和可轉移性。 通過將物理約束嵌入生成過程，我們的方法彌合了快速高效建模與現實世界運行複雜現實之間的差距，為全面的空域設計評估提供了穩健的框架。該框架將促進對空域重新設計的快速、靈活和準確評估，改善空域管理決策，同時提高效率、減少延誤，並增強機場運行的安全性。

11211425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11211425.value: 用於觸覺退化的可穿戴自供電感知界面

11211425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211425.value: Diabetes has emerged as a global health crisis, with over 400 million patients affected and numbers projected to rise significantly in the coming decades. Among the complications of diabetes, diabetic foot is particularly alarming, resulting from peripheral neuropathy and vascular disease associated with hyperglycemia. This condition often leads to reduced sensation and chronic wounds, severely impacting patients’ quality of life. Electrical stimulation (ES) has been recognized as a potential treatment for diabetic foot, offering benefits such as improved circulation, wound healing, and nerve regeneration. However, traditional ES devices face notable limitations, including bulkiness, high energy consumption, and a lack of targeted stimulation, which can reduce their effectiveness and convenience for patients. To address the challenges faced by diabetic patients, particularly those suffering from peripheral neuropathy and reduced sensation, we propose the development of a self-powered wearable haptic technology. This technology leverages a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) as its energy source to provide electrotactile feedback, encapsulated within a thin, soft, and comfortable self-powered electrotactile textile haptic system. The system will not only serve as a therapeutic device but also operate seamlessly within the patient’s daily life, promoting sensory recovery and assisting in wound healing through the gentle stimulation of sensory receptors. The innovations of materials, devices and integration strategy for the system will allow it to harvest energy from routine physical activities, such as walking or exercise, making it a practical tool for everyday use. By integrating the TENG technology directly onto the skin, we are aiming at creating a user-friendly solution that empowers diabetic patients to engage actively in their treatment. 糖尿病已成為全球性的健康危機，患者人數超過4億，未來幾十年預計將大幅成長。在糖尿病諸多併發症中，糖尿病足尤為令人擔憂，這是由高血糖引發的周邊神經病變和血管病變所致。此病症常導致患者感覺減退和慢性傷口，嚴重影響生活品質。電刺激（ES）療法因其能改善血液循環、促進傷口癒合和神經再生等優勢，被視為糖尿病足的潛在治療方案。然而傳統電刺激設備存在明顯缺陷，包括體積笨重、能耗較高以及缺乏標靶性刺激，這些因素降低了治療效果和患者使用便利性。 為因應糖尿病患者（尤其是合併週邊神經病變和感覺減退者）所面臨的挑戰，我們提出開發一種自供電穿戴式觸覺技術。此技術以摩擦奈米發電機（TENG）為能量源，透過超薄、柔軟、舒適的自供電電觸覺紡織系統提供電觸覺回饋。該系統不僅能作為治療設備，更能無縫融入患者日常生活——透過溫和刺激感覺受器促進感覺功能恢復並輔助傷口癒合。我們在材料、裝置和系統整合策略方面的創新設計，使其能從行走等日常活動中收集能量，成為切實可用的日常治療工具。透過將TENG技術直接整合於皮膚接觸層，我們致力於打造使用者友善解決方案，幫助糖尿病患者主動參與治療。

11212225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11212225.value: 具有实际约束和不确定性的非完整动态系统协同包围控制

11212225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212225.value: Cooperative control of multiple dynamic systems, also known as multi-agent systems, has been a central topic in control and robotics due to its significant potential in real-world applications, including search and rescue, and environmental monitoring. Cooperative target enclosing control, in particular, has drawn increasing attention for tasks such as spatial mapping, data acquisition, and support and escort operations. The objective of cooperative target enclosing control is to drive a group of mobile agents to track and surround a static or moving target while maintaining a prescribed formation pattern. Various cooperative target enclosing control strategies have been developed for different types of agent dynamics, such as integrator-type and Euler-Lagrange systems in recent years. However, most existing works do not fully consider practical constraints and uncertainties, which are inevitable in real-world applications. For example, practical systems such as fixed-wing drones, differential drive ground robots, and underwater gliders are subject to nonholonomic constraints due to their inherent motion limitations. Practical multi-agent systems are also often subject to distance constraints due to limited interaction ranges and potential collisions between neighboring agents. In addition, mobile robots might be subject to velocity constraints, including saturated heading rates and bounded maximum and minimum velocities, due to physical limitations such as pitch rate limits and thrust limits. All these constraints present significant challenges in cooperative target enclosing control of multi-agent systems. Furthermore, in scenarios such as patrol and escorting, the assumption that target motions are fully known is often invalid, leading to uncertainties about target dynamics. Recent literature reveals that cooperative target enclosing control problems of multi-agent systems under nonholonomic constraints, distance constraints, and velocity constraints, along with uncertainties about target dynamics, have not been adequately addressed. This project will investigate the problems of cooperative target enclosing control for nonholonomic multi-agent systems, focusing on those practical constraints and uncertainties. Specifically, this project will investigate three problems: (i) static target enclosing control for nonholonomic dynamic systems with distance constraints; (ii) moving target enclosing control for nonholonomic dynamic systems with both distance and velocity constraints; and (iii) moving target enclosing control for nonholonomic dynamic systems when there are uncertainties about target dynamics. This project, by addressing these problems and challenges, will develop novel robust and adaptive distributed target enclosing control strategies. The expected outcomes of this project will enhance the safety and performance of multi-agent systems in cooperative target enclosing control tasks, greatly facilitating their practical applications in real-world scenarios. 多智能體系統的協同包圍控制旨在維持預定編隊形態的同時，驅動多個智能體對靜態或動態目標進行追蹤與包圍。此控制策略應用前景廣闊，可應用於智能系統集群的搜救、分佈式環境監測，以及協同支援與護送等多種實際場景，因此在機器人與控制領域中備受關注。近年來，針對簡單動態的智能體系統（如積分型系統與歐拉–拉格朗日系統）在理想環境下的協同包圍控制研究已日趨成熟。然而，多數研究尚未充分考慮實際應用中的複雜系統約束與不確定性。例如，固定翼無人機、差速驅動地面車輛與水下載具等典型實際系統，皆受限於其內禀非完整性動態約束；系統動力限制所引致的速度飽和問題；有限的測量與通訊能力帶來的感知範圍約束；環境干擾與非合作目標的運動資訊不明更加劇了協同任務中的不確定性。上述系統內外部因素所引發的複雜約束與不確定性，使得協同包圍控制方法的設計與實際部署面臨諸多挑戰。本項目將聚焦於非完整性動態多智能體系統的協同包圍控制，深入探討在上述挑戰條件下，針對靜態與動態目標的包圍控制關鍵問題，並開發兼具魯棒性與自適應性的分佈式控制策略，以期有效提升系統的安全性與效能，促進其在真實場景中的實際應用推廣。

11212525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212525.value: Recent advancements in robotics have led to significant progress in autonomous mobile systems. Micro aerial vehicles have found applications in fields ranging from structural assessments to emergency response. However, these aerial platforms face challenges in carrying substantial payloads and maintaining extended flight times, limiting their practical utility. Conversely, ground-based robots excel at load-bearing, but struggle with negotiating complex terrains and reaching elevated positions. To bridge this gap, hybrid platforms combining aerial and terrestrial capabilities have been explored. However, many designs suffer from inefficiencies due to the direct integration of separate locomotion mechanisms. Our team's solution, the Hopcopter, addresses this challenge by incorporating a passive, elastic leg into a quadcopter, leveraging existing propulsion for both flight and hopping. While the Hopcopter has demonstrated impressive vertical hopping agility in laboratory settings, it has yet to achieve rapid horizontal locomotion, a key capability for real-world deployment across diverse terrains. Building upon the Hopcopter's success, this research aims to develop a high-speed hopping robot with terrain versatility in three steps. The first task focuses on enabling fast forward locomotion by incorporating active leg swings into a 400-g hopper. By decoupling the leg's orientation from body attitude, we achieve swift leg protraction and retraction required for hopping at speeds of up to 5 m/s. Second, the challenge of maintaining stability during high-speed hopping is addressed by drawing inspiration from biological systems. We propose a control strategy that leverages leg retraction and attitude feedback to maintain stable gaits without visual or velocity sensing. The final task enhances terrain adaptability from soft soil to hard ground by integrating compliant footpads that self-align on uneven or sloped surfaces, improving traction and stability. Furthermore, we develop a comprehensive model of the robot's interaction with different terrains, accounting for factors such as ground stiffness and energy loss during contact. This model enables the robot to dynamically adjust its behavior, ensuring consistent hop performance across environments. Upon completion, this research will advance hybrid aerial-terrestrial locomotion, contributing to the development of agile and versatile hopping robots. Key contributions include (i) the demonstration of high-speed hopping in a lightweight robot, pushing the boundaries of agile locomotion in small-scale platforms; (ii) the development of a bio-inspired control strategy for fast, stable hopping without velocity sensing; and (iii) the design and realization of a terrain-adaptive footpad system that allows for consistent performance across diverse environments, enhancing real-world applicability. 11213125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11213125.value: 基於光子芯片帶寬拉伸技術的實時寬帶射頻信號處理

11213125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213125.value: Over the past three decades, the ever-faster wireless networks have been a key driver of enhanced connectivity across human society, enabling the routine use of high-resolution video streaming, web conferencing, and smartphone APPs today. With 5G networks recently becoming commercially available, the race for 6G has already commenced, promising not only even higher data rates but also more precise environmental sensing through Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) networks. However, real-time processing of high-frequency, wideband radio-frequency (RF) signals, essential for these future networks, poses a significant challenge for traditional RF technologies due to exacerbated transmission losses at high frequencies and gain-bandwidth trade-offs in analog devices. Microwave photonics offers a compelling solution by shifting signal processing tasks from electronic to optical domain. This leverages the inherent advantages of photonic systems, including large bandwidths, flat frequency responses, and immunity to electromagnetic interference. Recent advancements in bandwidth-stretching technology have further enabled high-resolution microwave photonic signal processing by channelizing and mapping a gigahertz RF signal simultaneously to multiple optical carriers, effectively expanding the spectral bandwidth to several terahertz. However, current bandwidth-stretched microwave photonic processors are all constructed using discrete optoelectronic devices, with significant disadvantages in terms of size, weight, and power consumption (SWaP). Moreover, they lack the ability to process ultrawideband RF signals required for a 6G ISAC scenario due to the bandwidth limitations of discrete electro-optic modulators. To address these pressing challenges, we propose to develop advanced chip-scale thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) photonic circuits that can perform channelized processing and reception of ultrawideband millimeter-wave signals. Our approach involves the large-scale photonic integration of a flat-top electro-optic frequency comb source, a broadband millimeter-wave optic modulator, and a Vernier optical filter, all on the same TFLN chip. This enables compact and low-cost realization of bandwidth-stretched signal processing with broad bandwidths, rapid acquisition speeds, and high resolutions. The technology will be accompanied by proof-of-concept demonstrations of a broadband channelized RF receiver capable of handling 5/6G wireless communications and millimeter-wave radar signals simultaneously, and an ultrafast broadband millimeter-wave spectrum analyzer. The proposed research is supported by the expertise, infrastructure, and preliminary results on TFLN device fabrication and microwave photonic circuit design in PI’s lab. The proposed system aims to deliver performance metrics that significantly surpass current electronic solutions for 6G ISAC applications. The photonic chip design architecture further unlocks new possibilities across diverse industries, including wireless communications, high-end RF instruments, autonomous driving, and elderly care. 無線網絡在過去三十年中不斷提升的傳輸速率已成為人類社會互聯的關鍵推動力，使高清視頻、網絡會議、智能手機的日常應用成為可能。隨著5G網絡的商業化落地，6G的競賽已然揭幕。6G不僅承諾提供更高的數據速率，還將通過通信感知一體化網絡實現更精確的環境感測。然而，這些未來網絡所需的高頻寬帶射頻信號的實時處理，對於傳統射頻技術而言是一個巨大挑戰，因為高頻下電學信號傳輸損耗增大，模擬器件的增益帶寬限制也日趨嚴重。 微波光子技術可望為上述問題提供解決方案。它將信號處理任務從電域轉移到光域，從而利用光子系統固有的帶寬大、頻率響應平坦以及對電磁干擾抗性強的特性。近年來提出的帶寬拉伸技術，通過將GHz帶寬的射頻信號同時映射到THz間距的多個光載波上並進行信道化處理，可進一步實現寬帶射頻信號的精細化處理。然而，目前的帶寬拉伸微波光子處理器主要由分立光電子器件構成，在大小、重量和功耗方面存在顯著局限。同時，由於分立電光調制器的帶寬限制，這些系統也無法滿足6G通感一體化應用場景所需的超寬頻信號處理需求。 為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出開發薄膜鈮酸鋰微波光子芯片，對超寬頻毫米波信號進行信道化處理和接收。通過將平頂電光頻率梳源、寬頻毫米波-光調制器和游標光學濾波器集成於同一鈮酸鋰光子芯片上，以小體積、低成本的方式實現大帶寬、高采集速率和高精度的帶寬拉伸信號處理。我們將展示可同時處理5G/6G無線通信及毫米波雷達信號的寬頻帶信道化接收機，以及高速寬帶毫米波頻譜分析儀。 本項目的目標是為6G 通感一體化應用提供各方面性能超越當前電子解決方案的新型光子芯片架構，並為未來高端儀器、醫學成像、自動駕駛等領域帶來新的機遇。

11213325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11213325.value: 空間智慧支援框架用於數字化和重新配置密閉工作場所和設施的安全性、可靠性和韌性

11213325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213325.value: Efficient, reliable and safe workplaces and facilities are crucial to citizens’ well-being. However, growing complexities and interactions among humans, machines and the environments in confined workplaces in facilities, infrastructure workspaces, laboratories, etc. pose grand challenges to ensure their normal operations, safety, reliability and resilience. Of various emerging technologies, spatial intelligence including digital twin and artificial intelligence are regarded as promising enablers to tackle these challenges. Nevertheless, automating confined workplaces and facilities and improving their operational and spatial intelligence is challenging as it is difficult to digitalize heterogeneous entities; sense and communicate ambient environment changes; process and analyze the data; monitor and infer human behaviors and their interactions with machines and environments, not to mention about making adaptive decisions against disruptions and hazards. A holistic framework that guides stakeholders developing or deploying spatial intelligence technology may open up new ways to achieve better safety, reliability and resilience. This research aims to develop a spatial intelligence enabled framework to improve the total efficiency, safety, reliability and resilience of confined construction workplaces and facilities. The framework consists of a digital twin model for representing confined workplaces as a man-machine-environment system (MMES); a service-oriented mechanism to share and exchange digital twin data; a spatial intelligence enabled model to quantify, predict and infer total safety, reliability and resilience; a scenario-based approach to make automation and reconfiguration plans for employing spatial intelligence and digital twin; and a cloud-native prototype system to illustrate how to use the proposed framework to implement spatial intelligence solutions for confined workplace and facility management. The research begins with a series of interviews, case studies and focus group meetings to unveil the obstacles and requirements of applying spatial intelligence to reconfigure and optimize confined construction workplaces and facilities; along with identifying feasible strategies and roadmaps for stakeholders to digitalize the MMES and embed intelligence into the system for enhancing safety and reliability. A software reference architecture will then be designed to facilitate the implementation of the proposed framework. Finally, case studies will be conducted to validate the framework and the developed prototype system. The novelty of this investigation lies in the integration of spatial intelligence, digital twin middleware as developed by team, and theories and practices in MMES to delineate the problems, capacities and solutions associated with safety, reliability and resilience of confined workplaces. The findings should provide a solid foundation for the development of a smart, safe and reliable society. 高效、可靠和安全的工作場所和設施對公民福祉至關重要。然而，在設施、基礎設施工作區、實驗室等密閉工作場所中，人、機器和環境之間日益複雜的相互作用對確保其正常運作、安全性、可靠性和韌性構成了巨大挑戰。在眾多新興技術中，包括數字孿生和人工智慧在內的空間智慧被認為是應對這些挑戰的希望。 然而，實現密閉工作場所和設施的自動化並提升其營運和空間智慧仍充滿挑戰，因為數字化異質實體、感知和傳達周圍環境變化、處理和分析數據、監測和推斷人類行為及其與機器和環境的交互都十分困難，更何况針對幹擾和危險做出自適應決策。一個指針對有關人士而開發或部署空間智慧技術的整體框架或許能為實現更高的安全性、可靠性和韌性開闢新的途徑。 本研究旨在開發一個支援空間智慧的框架，以提高密閉建築工作場所和設施的整體效率、安全性、可靠性和韌性。該框架包含：一個將密閉工作場所表示為人機環境系統 (MMES) 的數字孿生模型；一個用於共享和交換數字孿生資料的服務導向機制；一個用於量化、預測和推斷總體安全性、可靠性和彈性的空間智能模型；一種基於場景的方法，用於製定應用空間智能和數字。 本研究首先透過一系列訪談、案例研究和焦點小組會議，揭示應用空間智慧重建和優化密閉建築工作場所和設施的障礙和要求；同時，為利益相關者確定可行的策略和路線圖，以實現 MMES 的數字化並將智慧嵌入系統，從而提高安全性和可靠性。隨後，我們將設計一個軟體參考架構，以促進該框架的實施。最後，我們將進行案例研究，以驗證該框架和已開發的原型系統。 本研究的創新之處在於將空間智慧、團隊自主研發的數字孿生中間件以及MMES領域的理論和實踐相結合，以探討與密閉空間工作場所的安全性、可靠性和彈性相關的問題、能力和解決方案。研究結果將為建構智慧、安全、可靠的社會奠定堅實的基礎。

11213425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11213425.value: 面向多晶材料中現實晶粒長大過程的基於機制的模擬研究

11213425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213425.value: Polycrystals are aggregates of polyhedral single-crystalline grains with various crystallographic orientations. Many materials of technical importance are polycrystals, such as metallic and ceramic structural materials, solid-state battery electrolytes, perovskite solar cells, superconducting cavities for accelerators, etc. The interfaces between adjacent grains in a polycrystal, known as grain boundaries (GBs), are defects due to abrupt changes in crystallographic orientation. Hence, polycrystals are metastable and naturally tend to eliminate GBs through GB migration, leading to an increase in mean grain size – a process known as grain growth. Since GBs (as defects) largely influence the mechanical and physical properties of polycrystalline materials, controlling grain growth is a key strategy for material design. Today, grain growth is still understood as curvature flow in most textbooks. The microstructure of a polycrystal is usually described as a network of interconnected GB surfaces. Curvature flow originates from the reduction in the total GB surface area to lower the total energy of the system. However, recent experiments have revealed that in reality, the grain growth (at least) in metallic materials is not curvature flow! To accurately predict and control grain growth in real materials under actual conditions, we propose to develop a new model based on the disconnection mechanism.
