It has been demonstrated that GBs migrate through the nucleation and glide of disconnections – the line defects in GBs possessing both step and dislocation characters. If we consider only the step character of disconnections, the model will align with the classical curvature flow. However, the dislocation character results in the generation of internal stress during GB network evolution, causing deviations from curvature flow. We will examine whether accounting for internal stress evolution enables the new model to reproduce experimental observations. Our preliminary results based on a 2D toy model have already supported the critical role of internal stress. Once the mechanism-based model is developed, we will demonstrate its impact by investigating some practical problems, including the effects of nonequilibrium initial microstructures and nonequilibrium perturbations on grain growth. Extraordinary material properties are always achieved in nonequilibrium microstructures. Structural stability is essential to preserving the extraordinary properties in service; our model will examine this aspect. Additionally, special microstructures can be produced through grain growth under nonequilibrium perturbations, such as oscillating stress and cyclic annealing. We will use our model to determine the thermomechanical processing conditions that produce the desired microstructures. 多晶材料係由眾多晶體取向不同的單晶多面體晶粒組合而成。很多具重要技術價值的材料都係多晶材料，例如金屬同陶瓷結構材料、固態電池電解質、鈣鈦礦太陽能電池、加速器超導腔等。多晶材料中相鄰單晶晶粒之間的界面稱為晶界（GBs）——由於晶體取向于晶界處突然變化，晶界本質上係一種缺陷。多晶材料處於亞穩態，傾向于透過晶界遷移消除晶界以降低體系能量，導致平均晶粒尺寸增大——此過程稱為晶粒長大。鑑於晶界（作為缺陷）對多晶材料的力學同物理性能影響顯著，控制晶粒長大係材料設計的關鍵策略。 現時大多教科書仍將晶粒長大理解為曲率驅動流。多晶材料的微觀結構通常被描述為相互連接的晶界曲面網絡，而曲率驅動流源自于系統透過減少晶界總表面積来降低總能量。然而，最新實驗揭示：現實中（至少）金屬材料中的晶粒長大並非曲率驅動流！ 為精準預測同控制實際條件下真實材料的晶粒長大，本研究提出開發基於階錯（disconnection）機制的新模型。階錯係晶界中同時具備台階（step）同位錯（dislocation）特徵的線缺陷。實證表明，晶界透過階錯的成核同滑移進行遷移。若只考慮階錯的台階特徵，模型會與經典曲率驅動流理論吻合；但位錯特徵會導致晶界網絡演化時產生內應力，造成偏離曲率驅動流。本研究將驗證：納入內應力演化能否使新模型重現實驗觀測結果。基於二維簡化模型的初步結果已證實內應力的關鍵作用。 此基於機理的模型建成後，我們將透過研究實際問題展示其影響力，包括：非平衡初始微觀結構同非平衡擾動對晶粒長大的影響。需強調，優異材料性能往往於非平衡微觀結構中實現，而結構穩定性對維持服役中的優異性能至關重要——本模型將對此進行評估。此外，可透過非平衡擾動（例如振盪應力、循環退火）下的晶粒長大製備特殊微觀結構。我們將運用模型，確定能產出目標微觀結構的熱處理與機械加工條件。

11214625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11214625.value: 液滴工程用於調控駐留與回彈

11214625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214625.value: Droplet impact dynamics are critical to numerous applications, including self-cleaning, spray cooling, anti-icing, anti-fouling, agricultural spraying, and 3D printing technologies. Effective manipulation of droplet-surface interactions is key to enhancing the efficiency and functionality of these applications. However, achieving precise control over droplet impact outcomes—specifically, the on-demand tuning of droplet non-rebound and rebound—remains a significant challenge. Traditionally, these outcomes are considered mutually exclusive: non-rebound relies on high energy dissipation, while rebound requires minimal energy loss. Our preliminary findings reveal a new phenomenon: emulsion droplets, consisting of dispersed droplets within a continuous phase, exhibit a unique rebound-residence-rebound transition on a super-nonwettable surface as the volume fraction of the dispersed phase (Φ) increases. The internal fluid dynamics of these emulsion droplets introduce a new layer of complexity, where droplets bounce off the surface at both low and high Φ while remaining in residence on the surface without bouncing at intermediate Φ. This behavior reveals a novel mechanism for tunable bouncing behavior through droplet engineering, presenting a sharp contrast to conventional approaches that primarily focus on surface engineering. We propose a comprehensive investigation of this remarkable phenomenon using integrated experimental and theoretical approaches. This project aims to deepen our understanding of droplet impact dynamics to achieve tunable bouncing behavior and translate this knowledge into practical applications, such as in regulatable thermal management. The project is structured into four key tasks. First, we will establish a microfluidic platform to generate and engineer emulsion droplets with precise control over their internal structure and composition, facilitating systematic impact studies on super-nonwettable surfaces. Second, we will explore the mechanisms governing the unique bouncing behavior of emulsion droplets, focusing on energy conversion to identify conditions that favor either droplet residence or rebound. Subsequently, we will develop robust predictive models to describe droplet dynamics, including spreading, receding, and contact time. Finally, we will leverage the insights gained to explore potential applications, particularly in regulating heat transfer processes. This research will contribute new knowledge by advancing conventional energy conversion pathways during droplet impact and shedding light on the intricate interactions between emulsion droplets and solid surfaces. The insights obtained will lay the groundwork for developing technologies that require precise control over droplet behavior, paving the way for the development of innovative materials and surfaces for applications in diverse fields such as heat transfer, agriculture, and advanced manufacturing. 液滴衝擊動力學對眾多應用領域至關重要，包括自清潔、噴霧冷卻、防冰、防污、農業噴灑及3D列印技術。有效操控液滴與固體表面的交互作用，是提升這些應用效率與功能的關鍵。然而，如何精確控制液滴衝擊結果——特別是實現按需切換液滴的“非回彈”與“回彈”行為——仍是一項重大挑戰。傳統上，這兩種結果被視為互斥：非回彈依賴高能量耗散，而回彈則需能量損失最小。我們的初步研究揭示了一種全新現象：乳液液滴（由分散相液滴分佈於連續相中）在超疏液表面上隨著分散相體積比（Φ）的增加，呈現出獨特的“回彈–駐留–回彈”轉變。這些乳液液滴的內部流體動力學引入了新的複雜性——在低Φ與高Φ時液滴會彈離表面，而在中間Φ時則駐留於表面而不發生回彈。此行為揭示了一種透過液滴工程實現可調控回彈的新機制，與以往僅專注於表面工程的傳統方法形成鮮明對比。 本項目擬結合實驗與理論方法，全面探討這一引人注目的現象，旨在深化對液滴衝擊動力學的理解，以實現可調控的回彈行為，並將所得知識轉化為實際應用，例如可調控的熱管理。本項目分為四個核心任務。首先，我們將建立微流控平台，以精準控制乳液液滴的內部結構與組成，從而系統性研究其在超疏液表面上的衝擊行為。其次，我們將探索乳液液滴獨特回彈行為的機制，聚焦於能量轉換過程，找出有利於液滴駐留或回彈的條件。接著，我們將發展穩健的預測模型，描述液滴的展開、回縮與接觸時間等動態行為。最後，我們將利用所得洞見，探索其在熱傳遞調控等實際應用中的潛力。本研究將通過推進液滴衝擊過程中的能量轉換機制，並揭示乳液液滴與固體表面間的複雜互動，為科學界貢獻全新知識。這些成果將為開發能精準控制液滴行為的創新材料與表面技術奠定基礎，促進其在熱管理、農業及先進製造等多個領域的應用。

11214825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11214825.value: 利用局部排列不變性質來設計求解兩階段隨機交流最優潮流問題的神經網路方案

11214825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214825.value: *Project Background* Optimal Power Flow (OPF) is a cornerstone of power system operations, essential for maintaining grid reliability and economic efficiency. It determines optimal power generation and transmission decisions to meet fixed, deterministic load while minimizing costs and adhering to physical and operational constraints. However, the rapid integration of renewable generation and demand-side management has introduced significant uncertainties in supply and demand, with variations reaching 20% of installed capacity in the US grid. This uncertainty renders traditional deterministic OPF solutions increasingly inadequate, potentially leading to excessive reserve requirements, higher operational costs, and increased system risks. To address this challenge, grid operators are turning to advanced approach, particularly scenario-based two-stage stochastic AC-OPF. This approach explicitly accounts for future uncertainties by incorporating multiple scenarios of renewable generation and load demand. However, it faces a critical hurdle: *dimensionality explosion*. As the number of scenarios increases, the problem size grows linearly, making conventional iterative methods computationally prohibitive for real-time operations. Similarly, standard NN approaches, while effective for deterministic OPF, suffer from the same dimensionality issues when applied to stochastic problems. *Project Aim and Description* We will develop new NN schemes for solving scenario-based two-stage stochastic AC-OPF problems orders of magnitude faster than iterative solvers, without suffering from the dimensionality explosion issue. Our approach is threefold: 1. We will exploit (i) the partial permutation-invariance property of two-stage stochastic AC-OPF problems and (ii) Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem to design a novel Partial Permutation-Invariance Neural Network (PPNN). This design can learn the load-to-solution mapping effectively without suffering from dimensionality explosion. 2. We will develop efficient training methodologies for PPNN, including data preparation techniques that leverage permutation invariance and training PPNN on smaller-scale problems to handle larger-scale problems effectively. 3. We will conduct extensive experiments using synthetic and real-world data on IEEE test cases and real-world power grid configurations. We will benchmark our PPNN scheme against state-of-the-art iterative solvers and alternative machine learning solutions. Our methodologies can provide generalizable insights and tools for using machine learning to solve a broad range of stochastic optimization problems. *Preliminary Result and Significance of Project* We have developed a preliminary PPNN scheme. The initial results show that it achieves up to 800x speed-up compared to latest iterative solvers with minor optimality loss and similar out-of-sample feasibility performance. The expected outcome helps enable real-time, reliable, and cost-effective grid operation while accounting for renewable/load uncertainties, supporting the integration of renewable generation to fight climate change. 背景: 最優潮流（OPF）是電力系統運行的基石，對維持電網可靠性和經濟效率至關重要。它決定最優的發電和輸電決策，以滿足固定的確定性負載，同時最小化成本並遵守物理和運行約束。然而，可再生能源發電和需求側管理的快速整合為供需帶來了顯著的不確定性，在美國電網中變化可達裝機容量的20%。這種不確定性使得傳統的確定性OPF解決方案日益不足，可能導致過度的備用容量需求、更高的運行成本和增加的系統風險。 為了應對這一挑戰，電網運營商正轉向先進的方法，特別是基於情境的兩階段隨機交流最優潮流。這種方法通過納入可再生能源發電和負載需求的多種情境來明確考慮未來的不確定性。然而，它面臨著一個關鍵障礙：維度爆炸。隨著情境數量的增加，問題規模呈線性增長，使得傳統的迭代方法在實時運行中計算成本過高。同樣，標準的神經網路方法雖然對確定性OPF有效，但當應用於隨機問題時也會遭受相同的維度問題。 目標與描述: 我們旨在開發新的神經網路方案來解決基於情境的兩階段隨機交流最優潮流問題，其速度比迭代求解器快數個數量級，且不會遭受維度爆炸問題。我們的方法有三個方面： 1. 我們將利用（i）兩階段隨機交流最優潮流問題的部分排列不變性質和（ii）Kolmogorov-Arnold表示定理[1]來設計一種新穎的部分排列不變神經網路（PPNN）。這種設計可以有效學習負載到解決方案的映射，而不會遭受維度爆炸。 2. 我們將為PPNN開發有效的訓練方法，包括利用排列不變性的資料準備技術，以及在較小規模問題上訓練PPNN以有效處理較大規模問題。 3. 我們將使用IEEE測試案例和真實世界電網配置的合成和真實世界資料進行廣泛實驗。我們將把我們的PPNN方案與最先進的迭代求解器和替代機器學習解決方案進行基準比較。 我們的方法可以為使用機器學習解決廣泛的隨機優化問題提供可推廣的見解和工具，超越本計畫所研究的問題。 初步結果與重要性: 我們已成功開發了初步的PPNN方案。初步結果顯示，與最先進的迭代求解器相比，它可實現高達800倍的速度提升，同時具有輕微的最優性損失和類似的樣本外可行性表現。預期的結果有助於實現實時、可靠且具成本效益的電網運行，同時考慮可再生能源/負載的不確定性，支持可再生能源發電的整合以對抗氣候變化。

11214925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11214925.value: 自動駕駛之多級遠程駕駛系統架構

11214925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214925.value: Autonomous driving is revolutionizing the future of transportation and has garnered significant attention from sectors beyond academia, including industry and government. Despite substantial progress, there remains a long way to go before autonomous vehicles can operate independently on open roads. According to the 2024 edition of the Code of Practice issued by the Transport Department of Hong Kong, each autonomous vehicle must be equipped with a remote driving system that allows a remote backup operator to take control via a wireless network when the vehicle encounters complex or unforeseen scenarios. Existing solutions for remote driving of autonomous vehicles are sparse and basic, facing several challenges and flaws. First, the vehicle streams videos of its surroundings to the operator, but these videos are often low-definition or stutter due to limited network bandwidth. Second, there is network latency between when the vehicle captures and sends videos to the operator and when it receives the control commands from the operator. Third, remote driving is more demanding than traditional in-vehicle driving, which can quickly lead to operator fatigue. Each of these issues can directly contribute to traffic accidents during remote driving. In this project, we propose the first remote driving framework that employs a three-level strategy, with each level addressing one of the aforementioned flaws to significantly enhance remote driving safety. Level 1 optimizes bandwidth allocation for video streaming, improving video quality. We will develop dynamic mechanisms that allocate higher bandwidth during challenging driving scenarios or when capturing important content. Additionally, we will design adaptive bitrate streaming to determine the optimal bitrate for each video. Level 2 compensates for network delay, enhancing operational accuracy. We will predict the future positions of nearby obstacles, enabling the operator to issue commands in advance. Besides, a buffering mechanism will be implemented to ensure commands are executed on time and at a constant rate, despite network fluctuations. Level 3 mitigates the operator’s workload. We will provide the operator with recommended trajectories and actions, allowing them to follow suggestions rather than always making decisions. Furthermore, we will develop methods to generate explanations for the rationale behind each recommendation, ensuring effective oversight of the vehicle. Our solutions will be tested not only in the lab but also in a real autonomous vehicle operating at the Foxconn Campus (Longhua, Shenzhen), addressing potential gaps between laboratory and real-world settings, thereby enhancing the impact of our research. 自動駕駛技術正在深刻變革未來交通格局，受到學術界、工業界及政府部門的高度重視。儘管在技術上已取得重大進展，但實現開放道路上的完全自主駕駛仍面臨諸多挑戰。根據香港運輸署發布的《自動駕駛車輛測試及先導使用實務守則》（2024版），每輛自動駕駛車輛必須配備遠程駕駛系統，以便在遭遇複雜或突發狀況時，通過無線網絡由遠程操作員接管控制。 現有自動駕駛遠程駕駛方案數量稀少且功能基礎，存在三大核心缺陷：其一，受限於網絡帶寬，車輛回傳至操作員的視頻流常出現畫質模糊或卡頓；其二，從視頻採集傳輸到接收控制指令存在顯著網絡延遲；其三，遠程駕駛對操作員的要求高於傳統車內駕駛，易導致駕駛疲勞。任何一項缺陷都可能直接引發交通事故。 本項目首創三級聯動的遠程駕駛系統架構，針對性解決上述問題。第一級通過視頻流優化技術提升畫質，開發動態帶寬分配機制在複雜場景或關鍵目標出現時優先分配高帶寬資源，並設計自適應碼率算法優化視頻傳輸質量。第二級採用網絡延遲補償技術提升操作精度，通過預測周邊障礙物未來位置使操作員能夠提前發出指令，同時建立緩衝機制確保指令在網絡波動下仍能按時勻速執行。第三級旨在減輕操作員工作負荷，為操作員提供推薦軌跡與建議操作，使其可參考系統建議而非持續自我決策，並通過可解釋性算法闡明推薦邏輯以保障有效監管。 我們的解決方案不僅將通過實驗室驗證，還將在富士康深圳龍華園區進行實車測試，彌合實驗室與真實場景的潛在差距，從而提升研究成果的實際應用價值。

11215025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11215025.value: 全球室內建築環境中細菌與病毒群落的十年縱向研究

11215025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215025.value: Individuals living in metropolitan areas typically spend 90% of their time indoors, including commuting between their homes and workplaces by mass transit. A diverse community of microbes, including bacteria and fungi (the microbiome) as well as viruses (the virome), coexists in the air and on the surfaces within these built environments (BEs). Consequently, indoor environmental quality has significant health implications, including the potential transmission of pathogens and the exacerbation of asthma and allergies. Recent advances in culture-independent sequencing technologies for phylogenetic markers and metagenomes have greatly improved our understanding of the composition and diversity of BE microbiomes and viromes. However, most past studies have assessed specific cities and temporal snapshot samples, leaving a substantial gap in our understanding of the global spatial and temporal variations in indoor microbiomes and viromes. Therefore, comprehensive insights into these variations are essential for developing safer and healthier indoor environments for occupants worldwide. To address this knowledge gap, we propose an investigation of the spatial and temporal variations in microbiomes, viromes, and virus–host interactions in indoor air and on surfaces within mass transit systems across six global cities—Denver, Hong Kong, London, New York City, Oslo, and Stockholm—between 2017 and 2026. These transit systems present an ideal model for examining BEs because of their dynamic human interactions and diverse environmental conditions. We will use state-of-the-art metagenomic sequencing methodologies on archived and newly collected samples to assess the diversity, taxonomy, and metabolic functions of the bacteria, fungi, and viruses. Additionally, we will elucidate the mechanisms and extent of virus–host interactions associated with spatial and temporal variations and environmental conditions. By leveraging time series datasets, we will develop machine learning models to forecast future compositions of microbiomes, viromes, and virus–host interactions. Preliminary data from earlier years across the six global cities support our hypothesis that the taxonomic compositions and metabolic functions of microbiomes and viromes, and their interactions, exhibit significant biogeographic and temporal variations. The significance of this study lies in its unique time series datasets collected from high-occupancy BEs in six global cities, providing valuable spatial and temporal insights into microbiomes and viromes. Ultimately, the study findings will inform recommendations and guidelines for improving indoor space management to enhance the health and well-being of building occupants.

11215125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11215125.value: 以快速時變超表面實現參數放大和大份額頻率轉換

11215125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215125.value: Electromagnetic metamaterials and metasurfaces have emerged as ubiquitous waveform engineering devices of the 21st century. Materials and surfaces can be tailor-made with designer properties, to manipulate electromagnetic waves and fields with extreme flexibility. This greatly enlarges the freedom in engineering electromagnetic waves and reduces and/or planarizes the form factors of traditional devices such as lenses, polarizers and curved reflectors. Metamaterials and metasurfaces have found applications in communication, imaging, display technology and medicine, among other fields. Time-varying materials bring a “4th-dimension” of wave manipulation and have gained immense interest because they unlock a new level of waveform manipulation capability. Much theoretical work has been undertaken and simple demonstrations have taken place for 1D and 2D time-varying materials (i.e. transmission lines and waves on artificial surfaces). However, an extension to 3D will face technological challenges. Waves in free-space can also be reconfigured by 2D metasurfaces. Time-coded metasurfaces have emerged whereby the temporal variations of meta-atoms transform the incident waves, leading to frequency shifts, angular shifts and non-reciprocal behaviour. However, the frequency of the modulation is generally much slower than the frequency of the incident wave, which greatly limits the potential wave manipulation capability. In this proposal, we aim to perform research toward fast-modulation time-varying microwave metasurfaces, which will allow one to fully realize the wave manipulation potential made possible by temporal variation. We first investigate the microwave time-varying meta-atom to understand causes the relevant response delay mechanisms. Then, we use our acquired knowledge to design a meta-atom which minimizes delay and supports fast modulation. Using the fast time-varying meta-atom, we build time-coded metasurfaces to demonstrate (i) parametric amplification and (ii) large fractional frequency conversion of a free-space wave reflected by the metasurface. Our proposed research will directly resolve a major bottleneck and open the door for the full realization of the wave modulation benefits of time-varying metasurfaces. Further, the parametric amplification and large fractional frequency conversion metasurfaces will find wide-ranging applications in wireless communication, imaging and wireless power transfer. This project will be performed at the State Key Laboratory of Terahertz and Millimeter Waves, which contain state-of-the-art simulation and characterization facilities the project requires. Our research team, consisting of experts in metamaterials, metasurfaces and electronic circuit design, has a track record of innovation in reconfigurable time-varying metasurfaces, and has the requisite complementary expertise to succeed in this project. 電磁超材料和超表面已成為21世紀無所不在的波形工程裝置。材料和表面可以根據設計特性進行客製化，從而極其靈活地操控電磁波和電磁場。這大大擴展了調控電磁波的自由度，並縮小和/或平面化了透鏡、偏振片和曲面反射器等傳統裝置的尺寸。超材料和超表面已在通訊、成像、顯示技術和醫學等領域中得到應用。時變材料帶來了「第四維度」的波形操控，並因其開啟了全新水平的波形操控能力而引起了極大興趣。針對一維和二維時變材料（例如傳輸線和人工表面上的電磁波），學者們已經進行了大量理論研究，並進行了簡單的演示。然而，把科研成果擴展到三維仍將面臨各種技術挑戰。自由空間中的電磁波也可以透過二維超表面進行重構。時間編碼超表面已經出現：超原子的時間變化會改變入射波，導致頻率偏移、角度偏移和非互易效應。然而，調製頻率通常遠低於入射波的頻率，這極大地限制了潛在的電磁波操控能力。 在本提案中，我們旨在研究快速調製時變微波超表面，這將使我們能夠充分發揮時間變化所帶來的波操控潛力。我們首先研究微波時變超原子，以了解相關的反應延遲機制。然後，我們將利用已獲得的知識優勢設計一個能夠把時延最小化並支援快速調製的超原子。我們將用此快速時變超原子建構時間編碼反射超表面，從而調控自由空間波來實現(i)參數放大和(ii)大分數頻率轉換。我們提出的研究將直接解決一個主要瓶頸，並為充分體現時變超表面的波束調控優勢清除障礙。此外，參量放大和大分數階頻率轉換超表面將在無線通訊、成像和無線電力傳輸領域中廣泛應用。 我們的項目將在太赫茲和毫米波全國重點實驗室進行，該實驗室擁有該計畫所需的先進模擬和表徵設備。我們的研究團隊由超材料、超表面和電子電路設計領域的專家組成，在可重構時變超表面領域擁有豐富的科創經驗，並具備成功完成該專案所需的互補專業知識。

11215625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11215625.value: 極端高溫核用碳化物增強難熔共晶高熵合金的開發

11215625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215625.value: Clean energy has emerged as one of the strategic leading technologies for global scientific and technological innovation, as well as economic development. Among various clean energy technologies, advanced nuclear power generation systems, such as fourth-generation reactors (Gen-IV) and fusion reactors, are regarded as the most sustainable future energy solutions due to their intrinsic safety features, high efficiency, and low carbon. However, both Gen-IV and fusion reactors are designed to operate under extremely complex conditions characterized by temperatures exceeding 1000 °C, coupled with intense radiation exposure and severe oxidative corrosion challenges. These factors inevitably contribute to substantial microstructure instability in traditional nuclear structural materials along with pronounced radiation-induced swelling issues. Thus, the challenges associated with extreme high temperature nuclear structural materials remains a critical factor limiting the advancement of nuclear energy. This project introduces an innovative design concept centered on multi-principal element alloys, effectively integrating eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), and carbides to develop a novel carbide-reinforced refractory eutectic high entropy alloys (CREHEAs). EHEAs exhibit remarkable plastic deformation compatibility, RHEAs demonstrate outstanding radiation resistance, and carbides possess exceptional thermal stability at elevated temperatures. Consequently, the newly developed CREHEAs amalgamates the advantageous properties of EHEAs, RHEAs, and carbides, positioning it as a potential candidate for operation within nuclear facilities under extreme high-temperature conditions (1600 °C). Specifically, we aim to select refractory elements such as Nb, Mo, W, Ta, V to construct a lamellar composite structure with C element by casting metallurgy. Building on previous research efforts, the CREHEAs exhibiting excellent thermal stability will be identified with the assistance of the CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagrams) simulation. The designed alloys will be irradiated at a temperature of 873~1373 K, and a high irradiation dose up to 100 dpa. Advanced characterization techniques will be employed to systematically investigate irradiation defects, phase stability, and high entropy effects. The mechanism of CREHEAs irradiation behavior will be elucidated to provide effective guidance for the rational design of radiation-resistant materials. Addressing the challenges associated with nuclear materials in extremely high temperature environments not only offers scientific theoretical insights for the development of CREHEAs, but also establishes a robust foundation for studying nuclear materials under more extreme conditions. 清潔能源已成為全球科技創新和經濟發展的戰略先導技術之一。在各種清潔能源技術中，先進的核能發電系統，如第四代反應堆（Gen-Ⅳ）和聚變反應堆，由於其固有的安全、高效、低碳等特點，被認為是最具可持續性的未來能源解決方案。然而，Gen-IV和聚變反應堆都設計在極端複雜的條件下運行，其特征是溫度超過1000 °C，再加上強烈的輻射暴露和嚴重的氧化腐蝕挑戰。這些因素不可避免地導致傳統核結構材料的微觀結構不穩定以及明顯的輻射誘導膨脹問題。因此，與極端高溫核結構材料相關的挑戰仍然是限制核能發展的關鍵因素。 本項目引入以多主元合金為核心的創新設計理念，將共晶高熵合金（EHEAs）、難熔高熵合金（RHEAs）和碳化物有效整合，開發出一種新型碳化物增強難熔共晶高熵合金（CREHEAs）。EHEAs表現出卓越的塑性變形能力，RHEAs表現出出色的抗輻射性能，碳化物在高溫下具有優異的熱穩定性。因此，新開發的CREHEAs融合了EHEAs、RHEAs和碳化物的優點，使其成為核設施在極端高溫條件下運行的潛在候選材料。 具體來說，我們的目標是選擇Nb、Mo、W、Ta、V等難熔元素，通過鑄造冶金技術與C元素構建層狀復合結構材料。基於先前的研究成果，將在相圖計算（CALPHAD）幫助下確定具有優異熱穩定性的CREHEAs。所設計的合金將在873~1373 K的溫度和高達100 dpa的高輻照劑量下輻照。隨後，先進的表征技術將用於系統地研究輻照缺陷、相穩定性和高熵效應，進而闡明CREHEAs輻照行為的機理，為抗輻射材料的合理設計提供有效指導。解決極端高溫環境下核材料的相關挑戰，不僅為CREHEAs的發展提供了科學的理論見解，還將為更極端條件下的核材料研究奠定堅實的基礎。

11216025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11216025.value: 探究典型鎂合金應力時效中的析出與強化機制

11216025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216025.value: Magnesium alloys exhibit substantial promise as lightweight structural materials, poised to replace their aluminum and steel counterparts in various applications, including vehicles, electronics, and aerospace technologies. A significant impediment to the widespread adoption of magnesium lies in its low absolute strength, resulting in inadequate load-bearing capabilities in structural applications. Stress-aging is a promising strategy to leverage the potential of precipitation strengthening to overcome this obstacle. Nonetheless, the fundamental understanding of stress-aging process in magnesium alloys is still far from adequate for applications. This proposed research project seeks to address this gap by comprehending the thermodynamic and kinetic characteristics for stress-aging process and resulting strengthening in magnesium alloys through hypothesis-driven experiment and dedicated analyses. To resolve the underlying reason for the faster formation of denser, more equiaxed precipitate particles in stress aging of magnesium alloys, we will select representative binary magnesium alloys, conduct comparative investigation into stress- and stress-free precipitation processes, and compare their strengthening efficacy. Furthermore, we will evaluate vacancy concentration and migration barrier in magnesium alloy under applied stress to identify their role in precipitation kinetics. We will also assess how applied stress influences the anisotropic diffusion kinetics and anisotropic matrix/precipitate interface energy in magnesium crystal. When translating the precipitate characteristics to strengthening efficacy, we will carefully examine how stress-aged precipitates with different types (prismatic rod, basal lath, and prismatic plate) affect plastic carriers (dislocation and twinning) in deformation. The experimental observations of precipitation evolution during stress-aging are expected to serve as a benchmark for future computational modeling endeavours in the field of phase transformation under external fields. Ultimately, this project aims to provide valuable insights into the mechanistic understanding of stress-aging phenomenon in magnesium anchored to thermodynamic and kinetics perspectives. The scientific knowledge generated by this research will directly inform the advancement of developing high-strength magnesium alloys via precipitation strengthening. 鎂合金作為輕量化結構材料展現巨大應用潛景，有望於車輛、電子設備與航天科技等領域替代鋁合金及鋼材。然其絕對強度偏低導致結構承載能力不足，成為制約廣泛應用的主要障礙。應力時效處理可透過析出強化效應突破此限制，但目前對鎂合金應力時效機制的基础認知仍遠未滿足實際應用需求。 本研究項目旨在透過假設驅動實驗與專項分析，從熱力學與動力學角度解析鎂合金應力時效過程及其強化機制。為探究應力時效中更快速形成高密度等軸析出相的根本原因，我們將選取代表性二元鎂合金，對比研究應力/無應力狀態下的析出過程及其強化效能。進一步地，我們將評估應力作用下鎂合金的空位濃度與遷移勢壘，明確其對析出動力學的影響機制；同時分析外加應力對鎂晶體中各向異性擴散動力學及基體/析出相界面能的調控作用。在建立析出特徵與強化效能關聯時，將重點研究不同形態析出相（稜柱狀桿、基面層片、稜柱狀板）對塑性載體（位錯與孿晶）的影響機制。 本研究對應力時效過程中析出演變的實驗觀測，可望為外場作用下相變領域的計算模擬研究提供基準數據。最終，本项目將立足熱力學與動力學視角，為理解鎂合金應力時效現象提供機理性見解，所獲科學認知將直接指導透過析出強化路徑開發高強度鎂合金的技術進程。

11216225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11216225.value: 從傳輸比特到交流智能：提升 LLM 驅動多智能體系統中的通訊效率

11216225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216225.value: Applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to domain-specific applications greatly benefits real-world problem-solving, underscored as the leading breakthrough in MIT Technology Review’s 10 Breakthrough Technologies of 2024. To further tackle more complex tasks, LLM-based multi-agent systems are proposed to employ multiple intelligent agents with specific roles and collaborate on target tasks. However, this practice has led to significant deployment challenges, including multi-agent organization, communication efficiency, distributed fine-tuning, and dynamic environments. This proposal is dedicated to addressing these multifaceted issues through a stable and fast hierarchical LLM-powered multi-agent system. Our approach encompasses a general framework with diverse communication patterns for fine-tuning and inference, designed to achieve both high performance and efficiency. The proposed tasks are as follows: 1) Designing an LLM-powered multi-agent architecture for solving complex tasks and understanding communications between agents: We propose a hierarchical approach to effectively organize role-based LLMs with diverse expertise. Intelligent agents will be clustered and ensembled to produce sub-task outputs, and the final results will be achieved through collaborations. 2) Designing efficient communication approaches for transmitting various patterns among agents: This work focuses on three types of communication patterns—bits, gradients, and logits—to fit different scenarios. Bit communication enables prompt sharing among agents, using an LLM-based compressor to encode texts and accelerate transmission. Gradient communication supports weight exchange during role-based LLM fine-tuning via stochastic lattice and vector quantizers. While logit communication uses logit ensembling techniques for effective model collaboration. These methods, applicable beyond our framework, improve efficiency in diverse multi-agent environments. 3) Applying and evaluating our proposed framework in complex tasks, like AI for math and world simulation. This practical assessment will demonstrate the real-world impact of the developed strategies and technologies. By combining expertise in information theory, networking, communication, distributed learning, and natural language processing, this project aims to achieve a comprehensive understanding of communications in the LLM-powered multi-agent framework. It encompasses algorithmic design, performance analysis, and proof-of-concept experiments, providing insights to further refine the framework. We anticipate that this project will not only advance our theoretical understanding of the communication efficiency issue in multi-agent systems but will also provide application solutions for small businesses and industries grappling with these challenges. The research outcomes are expected to inspire and benefit the broader research community, contributing to the ongoing evolution of related fields. 大型語言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）於近年迅速發展，並廣泛應用於不同專業領域，在解決現實世界問題方面展現出重大潛力。《麻省理工科技評論》更將 LLM 列為 2024 年十大突破性技術之一。然而，單一 LLM 在應對複雜及多樣化任務時存在一定局限。為此，研究界近年提出 基於 LLM 的多智能體系統（Multi-Agent Systems），透過多個具備特定角色與專業的智能體協作，以完成更具挑戰性的目標任務。 雖然該方向具備潛在價值，但其部署與實踐仍面臨多項挑戰，包括：多智能體的組織與協調、通訊效率、分佈式微調，以及動態環境下的適應性等。 本研究項目旨在提出一個 穩定而高效的分層式 LLM 驅動多智能體框架，並以理論分析及實證實驗全面探索其通訊機制及效能，從而為多智能體系統的設計與應用奠定基礎。 1、多智能體架構設計。探索並設計一種分層式多智能體框架，以角色化 LLM 作為核心，透過層次化組織與協作機制，有效分解並解決複雜任務。研究智能體之間的互動模式，並分析其在協作過程中的通訊需求與效率。 2、高效通訊機制研發。提出多種適用於不同場景的智能體間通訊方法，包括： 比特通訊：利用 LLM 壓縮器編碼文字資訊，加快即時資訊共享； 梯度通訊：透過隨機格點與向量量化器支援權重交換，以實現分佈式微調； logit 通訊：利用 logit 集成技術提升多模型協作效果。 本研究將系統性比較上述方法之效能、延展性與應用性。 3、框架應用與評估 將所提出的多智能體框架應用於 數學智能（AI for Math） 及 世界模擬（World Simulation） 等複雜任務。透過實驗驗證其在任務完成效率、通訊效能及資源利用率方面的優勢，並評估其於實際應用場景中的影響力。 本項目將結合資訊理論、通訊與網絡、分佈式學習及自然語言處理 等領域的研究方法：建立數學模型，分析不同通訊模式下的效能及資源開銷；設計並實現演算法，進行模擬與原型實驗驗證；分析結果以改進框架設計，並形成具體的理論與實證貢獻。 本項目將深化對多智能體系統中通訊效率與組織模式的理論理解，提出具普遍性的框架與方法。為中小企及產業界提供具可行性的多智能體應用方案，提升複雜任務的解決效率。研究成果可推動相關領域（如人工智能應用、雲端運算、智慧工業等）的持續發展，並惠及更廣泛的研究社群。

11216325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11216325.value: 在寬溫度範圍內工作的水性鋅電池

11216325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216325.value: Aqueous zinc batteries (ZBs) are a promising alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries by addressing critical challenges, such as safety concerns and high costs. However, specific practical applications, such as polar, aerospace, deep-sea, and high-altitude exploration, require ZBs to function effectively under extreme temperature conditions. The narrow operational temperature range of aqueous electrolytes poses considerable obstacles: at low temperatures, the liquid-to-solid phase transformation reduces ionic conductivity, whereas at high temperatures, the highly volatile nature of water leads to instability at the electrode/electrolyte interface. These thermal limitations result in performance degradation and pose safety risks, limiting the broader application of aqueous ZBs across a wide temperature range. The freezing of aqueous electrolytes at low temperatures is driven by the formation of additional hydrogen bonds (HBs), whereas the boiling of water breaks these HBs. Therefore, an effective strategy to expand the operational temperature window of aqueous electrolytes involves regulating the HB networks and modifying the solvation sheath structure of zinc ions. Current approaches to electrolyte optimization are based on concentrated electrolytes, additives and cosolvents, or gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs). Concentrated electrolytes effectively lower the freezing point by reducing the number of HBs between water molecules and increase the boiling point by reducing water content. However, this approach is hindered by high cost and increased viscosity. The use of additives and cosolvents and GPEs offer efficient solutions for developing low-temperature electrolytes by disrupting the HBs within water molecules; however, their application in formulating high-temperature electrolytes remains underexplored. In this project, we aim to develop aqueous and hydrogel electrolytes with enhanced stability and conductivity, while also constructing robust solid electrolyte interphase and cathode electrolyte interphase layers. These advancements will address critical challenges in ZBs operated under extreme temperatures, including electrolyte/electrode degradation, ion transport, side reactions, and dendrite formation. Moreover, we will explore the effects of temperature on the Zn anode and elucidate the reaction mechanisms at the electrolyte–electrode interface at extreme temperatures. Finally, we will fabricate highly stable Ah-level ZBs that can be efficiently operated across a wide temperature range from −80°C to 80°C. 水性鋅電池（ZBs）在某些領域，可以成為傳統鋰電池的有前景替代方案，因為它們解決了安全問題和高成本等關鍵挑戰。然而，特定實際應用——如極地、航太、深海和高海拔探險——要求 ZBs 在極端溫度下有效運作。水性電解質的狹窄溫度範圍帶來重大挑戰：在低溫下液態轉固態相變會降低離子導電率，而水的強揮發性會導致高溫下電極/電解質介面的不穩定。這些問題導致效能衰退和安全風險，限制了水性 ZBs 在廣泛溫度範圍內的更廣泛應用。 水性電解質的凍結是由低溫下的額外氫鍵（HBs）驅動，而水的沸騰則會斷裂 HBs。因此，拓寬水性電解質溫度窗口的一種可行方法是調節 HB 網路和鋅離子的溶劑化鞘結構。目前相關的電解質策略可分為三類，包括濃縮電解質、添加劑/共溶劑，以及凝膠聚合物電解質（GPEs）。濃縮電解質可有效降低凍點（透過減少水分子之間的 HBs 數量）並提高沸點（由於減少水含量），但它們受到高成本和高黏度的困擾。添加劑/共溶劑和 GPEs 是開發低溫電解質的有效策略，透過斷裂水分子內的 HBs；然而，它們用於開發高溫電解質的應用鮮少被報導。 在本項目中，我們提出開發水性和水凝膠電解質，以提升穩定性和導電率，同時建構堅固的 SEI/CEI 層，這可進一步解決極端溫度下運作的 ZBs 在電解質/電極降解、離子傳輸、副反應和枝晶形成等方面的關鍵挑戰。此外，探討溫度對 Zn 陽極的影響，並揭示極端溫度下電解質與電極介面之間的反應機制。最後，製造穩定 Ah 級鋅電池，在廣泛溫度範圍內具有高穩定性。

11216725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11216725.value: 帶建造順序的時域設施選址博弈

11216725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216725.value: In this project, we study the facility location games from the time perspective. In the classic setting of facility location games, the government plans to build a public facility based on the agents' reported information so that agents will not gain by reporting false information and certain objective values are approximately optimized. We will first study the facility location games with time dimension incorporated into both facilities and agents. This new model can be used to study event and venue allocation given participants' preferences and time constraints, We divide the timeline into stages and assume that agents are available in some stages while the facilities can only provide services in certain stages. The granularity of the stages guarantee that the travelling time towards the facility is negligible and agents can use the facility as long as their available stages and facilities' service stages overlap. This is a more general model compared to our earlier work on dynamic facility location games where a single facility moves across different stages to serve agents. Next, we will study facility location games with another dimension of time: building sequence of facilities. In most of the scenarios, building facilities takes time. All the previous works assume that the agents' costs are only affected by the distances to the facilities. However, with the building time taken into consideration, it is necessary to consider the cost incurred while the agents are waiting for the facility to be built. In the multiple facility location case, this waiting time becomes a non-trivial component in the cost since one can build the facilities in different orders. There are multiple settings we will consider in this project. In the homogeneous setting, suppose the government wants to build m identical facilities and an agent only needs to go to one of them but he will not be able to go to the closest one until it is built. However, the access cost keeps improving when more facilities are built. In the heterogeneous setting, an agent needs to go to all facilities and he needs to access a default far facility before all his favourite facilities are built. We study both optimization and mechanism design perspective for the above two models. Finally, considering the budget of the government, we study the problem of selecting a certain number of facilities out of all the candidates, achieving certain level of fairness. 在本项目中，我們從時間視角研究著名的設施選址博弈。在最經典的設施選址博弈中，政府計劃在一條街道上建造一個公共設施，該街道上居住著一些持有私人資訊的智能體。政府的目標是使用一種機制，根據收集到的智能體資訊來決定設施的建造位置，以使智能體不會透過報告虛假資訊而獲益，並近似地優化某些目標值。 我們將首先研究將時間維度融入設施和智能體的設施選址博弈。我們將時間軸劃分為多個階段，並假設智能體在某些階段可用，而設施只能在某些階段提供服務。階段的粒度保證了前往設施的行程時間可以忽略不計，並且只要智能體的可用階段與設施的服務階段重疊，智能體就可以使用該設施。與我們先前關於動態設施選址博弈的研究相比，這是一個更具通用性的模型。 接下來，我們將研究具有另一個時間維度的設施選址博弈：設施的建造順序。在大多數情況下，建造設施需要時間。先前的所有研究都假設智能體的成本僅受與設施距離的影響。然而，考慮到建造時間，有必要考慮智能體等待設施建造所產生的成本。在多設施選址的情況下，由於設施建造順序不同，導致不同智能體根據其對設施的偏好而產生不同的等待成本，因此等待時間將成為成本中一個重要的組成部分。在本项目中，我們將考慮多種場景。在同質場景中，假設政府想要建造m個相同的設施，智能體只需要前往其中一個，但由於等待時間的權衡，他不會再選擇最近的設施。在異質場景中，假設一位畫家想要舉辦展覽，但由於展覽的空間和時間有限，他只能在一個地方展出部分作品。因此，他需要在不同地點舉辦m個不同的展覽來展示他所有的作品。一個代理商想要訪問所有設施，他的成本將是時間加權的距離總和。另一種看待建造順序的方式是考慮使用不同設施的移動攤位。假設一個攤位在某個位置停留一段時間，然後帶著全新的設施移動到下一個位置。在這種情況下，建造設施不需要時間，但下一個設施建成後，目前設施就會被拆除。因此，代理的成本是服務時間加權的距離總和。此外，如果在一組可能的設施中只能選擇部分設施進行建造，則需要在真正建造之前進一步決定選擇哪些設施。由此衍生的問題將是首先選擇設施，然後根據代理商對設施的偏好來安排設施的建造順序。在選擇設施方面，我們也將眾所周知的合理代表性擴展到設施选址博弈，以及更普遍的带衝突的多胜者投票。 最後將兩個維度的時間限制整合成一個統一的模型，其中代理和設施都有可用時間，設施可用時間由建築順序決定。

11216925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11216925.value: 探索在GPU核心化平台上的高速與可擴展演化圖處理

11216925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216925.value: Graphs are essential data structures for capturing relationships among interconnected entities. With increasing demands for real-time insights, evolving graph processing (EGP), which analyzes a sequence of snapshots for tracking the graph property evolution, has become critical across fields. While GPUs have become the preferred choice for EGP due to their massive computing power, our initial study reveals inherent limitations in current EGP systems. The misalignment between analytics workflows and GPU architecture, along with the absence of criteria for selecting the optimal analysis approach, greatly constrains the EGP efficiency. Our preliminary analysis shows there is a potential over 10X speedup with applying appropriate analytics designs. When graph sizes exceed GPU memory capacity, existing data layouts and memory management strategies are ill-suited to data access patterns in EGP, further impairing performance. Although modern heterogeneous platforms offer diverse computing resources to enhance EGP, most systems fail to leverage opportunities in asynchronous data preprocessing and workload distribution. Without addressing these issues, GPU-centric EGP systems will continue to experience significant performance bottlenecks, restricting their impact in high-demand applications. In this project, we will conduct a comprehensive investigation of GPU-centric EGP and develop a holistic system to boost its performance. Our plan includes three tasks: (1) Exploring the optimal query evaluation on GPUs. We will review state-of-the-art EGP systems and investigate major limitations hindering superior performance. Our initial studies reveal significant inefficiencies in workflow scheduling and an inability to determine the best analysis approach. Accordingly, we will develop a graph-update-oriented scheduling strategy that reduces redundant computation and enhances data locality. We will also design a runtime mechanism to accurately estimate the performance of various analysis approaches, allowing adaptive switching to the optimal in diverse scenarios. (2) Developing advanced data layout strategies for large-scale graphs. As existing layouts fall short of supporting efficient out-of-GPU-memory EGP, we will design an incremental-analysis-aware graph representation and a data management scheme where data are adaptively allocated between GPU memory and direct-access storage, to optimize data transfer and memory utilization. (3) Designing effective mechanisms for integrating GPU-centric EGP framework to heterogeneous platforms. To fully leverage GPUs and auxiliary compute resources, we will introduce innovative data preprocessing and workload distribution techniques. These include a speculative preprocessing design and a multi-level workload distribution mechanism to ensure optimal utilization of available compute units. We believe our research will overcome inherent limitations of GPU-centric EGP systems and pave the way for transformative advancements in graph-driven insights. 圖是捕捉互聯實體間關係的基本數據結構。隨著即時分析需求的不斷增加，演化圖處理（EGP），即每次分析一系列快照以追蹤圖屬性的演化，已成為各領域的關鍵技術。雖然GPU憑藉其強大運算能力已成為EGP的首選，但我們的初步研究揭示了現有以GPU為基礎的EGP系統存在固有限制。分析工作流程與GPU架構之間的不匹配，以及缺乏選擇最佳分析方法的準則，極大地限制了EGP的效率。我們的初步分析顯示，若能採用合適的分析設計，潛在加速比可超過10倍。當圖的規模超過GPU記憶體容量時，現有的數據布局與記憶體管理策略難以適應EGP的數據存取模式，進一步削弱系統效能。雖然現代異構平台提供多樣化的運算資源來提升EGP，但大多數系統未能利用非同步數據預處理和工作負載分配的機會。若不解決這些問題，以GPU為核心的EGP系統將持續面臨顯著的效能瓶頸，限制其在高需求應用中的影響力。 在本項目中，我們將對以GPU為核心的EGP展開全面研究，並開發一個整體性系統來提升其效能。我們的計畫包括三個任務：（1）探索GPU上的最佳圖分析方案。我們將回顧當前最佳的EGP系統，並研究阻礙其高效能的主要限制。我們的初步研究揭示了工作流程調度中的顯著低效，以及無法確定最佳分析方法的問題。因此，我們將開發一種以圖更新為導向的調度策略，以減少冗餘計算並提升數據區域性。我們還將設計一種實時機制，以準確評估不同分析方法的效能，從而能在多樣化情境下自適應切換至最佳方法。（2）發展大規模圖的數據布局策略。由於現有布局不足以支援高效的GPU記憶體外EGP，我們將設計一種面向增量分析的圖表示方式，以及一種自適應數據管理方案，以最佳化跨記憶體層級的數據傳輸與使用。我們預期新的數據布局能降低冗餘數據移動，同時最大化記憶體效率。（3）將GPU為核心的框架整合至異構平台。為充分利用GPU與輔助運算資源來支援EGP，我們將引入創新的數據預處理與工作負載分配技術，其中包括推測式預處理設計以及多層次的工作負載分配機制，以確保所有可用運算單元的最佳化使用。我們相信，我們的研究將突破GPU為核心的EGP系統的固有限制，並為圖分析開闢變革性創新。

11217125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217125.value: 飛行時間測距中非視距信道欺騙之檢測研究

11217125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217125.value: Wireless ranging estimates the distance between two devices and is a core component of localisation systems. Ranging measurements from multiple reference are combined to estimate an object’s current position, so localisation requires reliable and accurate ranging measurements. Time-of-Flight(ToF) ranging with Ultrawideband(UWB) has received renewed attention due to its growing prevalence, e.g. increased availability of chipsets supporting the IEEE 802.15.4a standard for UWB ranging, and the introduction of UWB in Apple and Android phones to support item tracking, e.g. AirTags, and access control, e.g. keyless entry. However, UWB has long been considered a prominent wireless ranging technology, which has distinguished itself from other wireless ranging approaches with its ability to achieve highly accurate distance estimates. The expected accuracy of UWB ranging, however, is generally achieved in line-of-sight(LOS) conditions, with distance error increasing significantly in non-line-of-sight(NLOS) conditions, i.e. when an obstacle in the ranging path forces the signal to travel around or through it. The impact of these ranging errors can be reduced if we can 1) detect if ranging was done under NLOS conditions (NLOS identification), and 2) correct the ranging distance (NLOS mitigation). Existing methods for NLOS identification and mitigation are built on classification and regression models, respectively, operating with channel impulse response (CIR) data. However, attacks have been demonstrated where adversaries interfere with a LOS ranging transmission so that it appears to occur under NLOS conditions, i.e. spoofing an NLOS CIR. This potentially results in the system over-correcting, e.g. distance estimate reduction, a non-existent NLOS error so the sender appears closer to the receiver than is the case. NLOS identification and mitigation methods are needed to ensure reliable ranging operation in real-world environments, so there is a need for making these methods resistant to NLOS spoofing attacks for UWB ranging to support both reliable and secure localisation. We address this problem by developing methods to distinguish true NLOS channel conditions from spoofed NLOS channel conditions. Specifically, we will study and characterise the features of NLOS CIRs spoofed under both LOS and NLOS conditions and then develop new methods that leverages this knowledge to detect spoofed CIRs. Using CIR characteristics to detect distance spoofing can also be implemented without modifications to current UWB receivers but is an unexplored topic in literature. Our project would therefore improve current UWB ranging systems while also having scientific merit in initiating early formative work on attack-resistant methods for NLOS identification and mitigation. 無線測距用於估計兩設備間的距離，是定位系統的核心組成。透過整合多個參考點的測距數據，可估計目標的當前位置，因此定位系統需依賴可靠且精確的測距數據。基於超寬帶（UWB）的飛行時間（ToF）測距因其日益普及而備受關注，例如支援IEEE 802.15.4a標準的UWB測距晶片組逐漸普及，以及蘋果與安卓手機引入UWB技術用於物品追蹤（如AirTags）及存取控制（如無鑰匙進入）。然而，UWB長期以來被視為一種卓越的無線測距技術，因其能實現高精度距離估計而有別於其他測距方法。 UWB測距的預期精度通常在視距（LOS）條件下實現，而在非視距（NLOS）條件下，即當測距路徑存在障礙物迫使訊號繞行或穿透時，距離誤差顯著增加。若能1）辨識測距是否在NLOS條件下進行（NLOS辨識），以及2）校正測距距離（NLOS緩解），即可減小此類誤差影響。現有NLOS辨識與緩解方法分別基於分類與回歸模型，仰賴信道衝擊響應（CIR）數據進行操作。然而，研究顯示，攻擊者可能干擾LOS測距傳輸，使其看似在NLOS條件下進行，即偽造NLOS CIR。此舉可能導致系統過度校正，例如縮減不存在的NLOS誤差之距離估計，使發送端看似比實際更靠近接收端。為確保在真實環境中可靠的測距操作，需開發對NLOS欺騙攻擊具魯棒性的NLOS辨識與緩解方法，以支援可靠且安全的UWB測距定位。 為此，我們透過開發區分真實NLOS信道條件與偽造NLOS信道條件的方法來解決此問題。具體而言，我們將研究並表徵在LOS及NLOS條件下偽造的NLOS CIR特徵，並開發利用此知識檢測偽造CIR的新方法。利用CIR特徵檢測距離欺騙可在不修改現有UWB接收器的情況下實現，惟此課題在文獻中尚未充分探討。因此，本研究將提升現有UWB測距系統的性能，同時在抗攻擊的NLOS辨識與緩解方法的早期研究中具備科學價值。

11217325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217325.value: 利用大語言模型及單多目標演化計算的自動算法設計方法

11217325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217325.value: Algorithms play a pivotal role in solving computational problems across various domains, including finance, industry, science, and social studies. Algorithm design often demands extensive expert knowledge and involves a labor-intensive trial-and-error development. In the past few decades, much effort has been made to automate the algorithm design process. A commonly used methodology is to model an automated algorithm design (AAD) task as an optimization problem and then solve it. Existing automated algorithm design approaches suffer from two major drawbacks: i) they require hand-crafted algorithmic components with expert knowledge to define an appropriate search space of candidate algorithms, and ii) they need to manually design problem specific search operators to find an optimal algorithm. These drawbacks significantly limit the search space and hinder the usage of automated algorithm design in real-world applications. In this project, we will develop and study a systematic paradigm by integrating evolutionary algorithms (EAs) with large language models (LLMs) to innovate automated algorithm design. We directly work with algorithms at the level of both natural language and code, which significantly enlarges the search space of candidate algorithms. We adopt well-developed EAs as an iterative framework to search in the space of algorithms while leveraging LLMs to generate new diverse and promising candidate algorithms. In this way, novel algorithms can be generated in an automated manner. This project will investigate how and why our proposed approaches work or fail. To this end, we will study how to define appropriate distances in the search space of algorithms and then conduct landscape analysis to understand the behavior of our approaches. These understandings will be used for further improvements. We will investigate how to address multiple design criteria such as final solution qualities and running time, and how to deal with new problems using knowledge and experience obtained for solving other problems. We will apply our proposed approaches for designing heuristic algorithms for vehicle routing problems, which can be found in many real-world applications such as logistics, transportation, and manufacturing. 演算法在金融，工業，科學和社會研究眾多領域發揮關鍵作用。演算法設計通常需要大量的專業知識，並且需要耗費大量的人力進行反覆試驗。在過去的幾十年中，人們為實現演算法設計自動化做出了巨大的努力。常用的方法是將自動演算法設計 任務建模為最佳化問題，然後進行求解。現有的自動演算法設計方法有兩個主要缺點：i) 它們需要利用專家知識手動編寫演算法元件來定義合適的候選演算法搜尋空間；ii) 它們需要手動設計針對特定問題的搜尋算符來找到最優演算法。這些缺點極大地限制了搜尋空間，阻礙了自動演算法設計的實際應用。 在本專案中，我們將演化演算法與大語言模型結合，開發和研究一種系統化自動演算法設計範式。 我們直接在自然語言和程式碼層面上處理演算法，這將顯著擴大候選演算法空間。我們採用演化演算法作為迭代框架在演算法空間進行搜索，同時利用大語言模型產生新的候選演算法。我們將研究本計畫提出方法的工作機制。我們將研究如何在演算法搜尋空間中定義適當的距離，然後進行景觀分析以研究自動演算法設計方法的行為特徵。這些理解將用於進一步的改進自動演算法設計策略。 我們將研究如何滿足最終產生演算法的多項設計準則，以及如何利用解決其他問題所獲得的知識和經驗來處理新問題。我們將應用本專案的方法設計車輛路徑問題的啟發式演算法。

11217825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217825.value: 鋼渣與再生瀝青路面材料協同再生的多尺度表徵研究推進可持續溫拌鋪路解決方案

11217825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11217825.value: Prof Bhasin, Amit Prof Jiang, Jiwang Prof LENG, Zhen Prof Luo, Sang

11217825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217825.value: In response to the escalating generation of solid waste, the recycling of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) into new bituminous mixtures has become a common practice in pavement construction in Hong Kong and many other regions globally. Among various RAP recycling technologies, warm mix recycling (WMR) stands out for maintaining the performance of hot recycled mixtures while increasing the incorporation of RAP materials and being more environmentally friendly than hot recycling technology. Meanwhile, a consensus has been reached that incorporating steel slag (SS) into WMR mixtures (WMRMs) can improve the adhesion properties of blended bitumen and aggregates. It is expected that the collaborative effect of SS and RAP will increase the percentage of RAP incorporated, while ensuring the sufficient durability of WMRMs (SS & RAP-WMRMs). However, the mechanisms by which SS enhances WMRMs, along with issues related to SS’s volumetric stability, leaching, and erosion remain unclear, which potentially limits the application of SS in WMRMs. To address these concerns, this study will systematically investigate the effect of incorporated SS on the evolutionary mechanism of SS & RAP-WMRM performance through multiscale characterization methods and simulations. Firstly, material genome for SS and RAP will be established, and the natural aging evolution of SS will be characterized. Secondly, leaching and erosion mechanisms of SS will be investigated by standard leaching tests and pretreatment methods will be proposed to minimize heavy metal leaching for sustainable paving applications. The physicochemical interactions and failure mechanisms at the interface of blended bitumen and SS/RAP aggregates will be further examined using staged extraction and multiscale methods. Subsequently, both experiments and simulations will be employed to explore the strength formation and failure mechanisms of SS in SS & RAP-WMRM, ultimately aiming to enhance pavement performances and determine the optimal dosage of SS. Additionally, integrated life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) will be conducted to evaluate the overall environmental performance and cost efficiency of SS & RAP-WMRM pavement compared with conventional pavement. Finally, the optimum design and construction procedure of the SS & RAP-WMRM for diverse application scenarios will be recommended. The outcomes of this study are anticipated to significantly enhance the fundamental understanding of the strength formation and failure mechanisms within SS & RAP-WMRM during both curing and service phases. This will promote wider applications of SS & RAP-WMRM as a sustainable road network solution, benefiting both Hong Kong and the global community. 隨著固體廢物產量不斷增加，將再生瀝青路面材料（RAP）回收至新型瀝青混合料中，已成為香港及全球眾多地區道路建設的常見做法。在眾多RAP回收技術中，溫拌再生技術（WMR）因能在保持熱拌再生混合料性能的同時，提升RAP材料的摻入比例，且相較熱拌再生技術更加環保而備受關注。此外，研究普遍認為，在WMR混合料（WMRM）中摻入鋼渣（SS）可顯著改善瀝青與骨料的黏附性能。預期SS與RAP的協同作用能在確保WMRM耐久性的基礎上，進一步提高RAP的使用比例（SS & RAP-WMRM）。然而，有關SS提升WMRM性能的具體機理，以及SS在體積穩定性、淋溶與侵蝕等方面的問題仍未完全解決，這在一定程度上限制了SS於WMRM中的廣泛應用。為了解決上述問題，本研究將基於多尺度表徵方法與模擬，系統研究SS摻入對SS & RAP-WMRM性能演化機制的影響。研究首先建立SS與RAP的材料基因組，並表徵SS的自然老化演化過程；其次，通過標準淋溶測試探討SS的淋溶與侵蝕機理，並提出可減少重金屬淋溶的預處理方法，以促進SS的可持續道路應用；再者，採用階段提取和多尺度方法，深入分析混合瀝青與SS/RAP骨料界面的物理化學相互作用及失效機理。同時，通過實驗與模擬研究SS在SS & RAP-WMRM中的強度形成與失效過程，從而優化路面性能並確定SS的最佳摻量。此外，研究還將進行全生命週期成本分析（LCCA）與生命週期評估（LCA），以全面評估SS & RAP-WMRM路面在環境效益與成本效率上的表現，並針對不同應用場景，提出最優設計與施工方案。本研究預期將顯著加深對SS & RAP-WMRM在養護與服役階段強度形成與失效機制的理解，從而推動其作為可持續道路解決方案的廣泛應用，為香港及全球社會的道路建設提供重要支持。

11217925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217925.value: 一類仿真優化算法的有限時間分析

11217925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217925.value: The ranking and selection (R&S) problem seeks to efficiently select the best simulated system design among a set of alternatives. As a crucial aspect of simulation optimization, R&S is widely applied in diverse domains such as queueing systems, electric power grids, air and land traffic systems, communication networks, manufacturing plants, supply chains, healthcare, etc. This project is focused on fixed-budget R&S, which aims to correctly identify the best system design under a given simulation budget. The predominant approach for this problem has been asymptotic analysis, with most existing research efforts devoted to understanding the asymptotic performance of the R&S algorithms. However, as a more important performance indicator for practitioners and a natural next research question for scholars, the finite-time performance of these algorithms remains largely unknown. The literature currently lacks effective tools to evaluate the gap between the design recommended by these algorithms and the real best one. This gap hinders reliable assessment and improvement of R&S methods for practical, finite-time decision making. This project aims to fill the research gap by developing analytical tools to characterize the finite-time performance of main R&S algorithms and exploring the application of these tools in practical problems. Specifically, the project will be divided into three tasks: (i) Finite-time performance of OCBA. We will utilize our preliminary results on the optimal computing budget allocation (OCBA) algorithm to develop finite-time upper bounds for its probability of false selection and expected opportunity cost. (ii) Extension to other R&S algorithms. We will extend the analysis method in Task 1 to assess the finite-time performance of the other common R&S algorithms, including the knowledge gradient (KG) and expected improvement (EI). (iii) Application to healthcare problems. To further enhance the impact of this project, we will apply the proposed analysis method to two real-world healthcare problems, namely the medical staff assignment in emergency departments and precision medicine. The outputs from the three tasks can further the understanding of the performance of R&S algorithms and provide strong theoretical support for their application. Practitioners will have effective tools to evaluate the quality of their estimated optimal solutions from simulations. More importantly, this project has the potential to shift the research focus of R&S scholars from asymptotic analysis to finite-time analysis, which mirrors the advancements seen in related fields such as multi-armed bandit problems. 排序與選擇（Ranking and Selection, R&S）問題旨在於多個可行方案中，高效選擇出最佳的仿真系統設計。作為仿真優化的重要一環，R&S被廣泛應用於排隊系統、電力網絡、空中與地面交通系統、通訊網絡、製造工廠、供應鏈、醫療保健等多個領域。本項目聚焦於固定預算R&S，即在給定的仿真資源預算下，正確識別出最佳系統設計。針對這一問題，主流方法為漸近分析，主要關注R&S演算法的漸近性能。然而，對於實務工作者而言，更重要的性能指標，是這些演算法的有限時間性能，但目前這方面仍知之甚少。現有文獻缺乏有效工具來評估這些演算法所推薦設計與實際最佳設計之間的差距，這也阻礙了對於R&S方法在有限時間決策下的可靠評估與改進。 本項目旨在通過發展分析工具，彌補這一研究空白，具體描述R&S主流演算法的有限時間性能，並探索這些工具在實際問題中的應用。具體而言，項目分為三個任務： 1. OCBA的有限時間性能。我們將利用已有關於最優計算預算分配（OCBA）演算法的初步成果，提出其錯誤選擇概率與期望機會損失的有限時間上界。 2. 推廣至其他R&S演算法。我們將把第一步中的分析方法推廣到其他常見的R&S演算法，包括知識梯度（KG）和期望改進（EI），以評估其有限時間性能。 3. 應用於醫療保健問題。為進一步提升本項目的實際影響力，我們將把所提出的分析方法應用於兩類現實醫療問題，即急診部門的醫護人員分配與精準醫療。 上述三個任務的成果將深化對R&S演算法性能的理解，並為其應用提供堅實的理論支持。實務人員將有有效工具來評估其仿真所得的最優解質量。更重要的是，本項目有潛力促使R&S領域的研究重心從漸近分析轉向有限時間分析，這與多臂賭博機問題等相關領域的最新發展相呼應。

11218025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11218025.value: 集體細胞手性：研究其特徵、分子結構和機制，以及在指導傷口癒合中的作用

11218025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218025.value: Left-right (LR) asymmetry is an architectural feature commonly seen in many tissue/organs. Chirality of epithelial cells, a mechanical behavior such as tilted cell orientation and junction remodeling during unidirectional migration, has been reported to drive LR asymmetry in tissue-level morphogenesis. Notably, mesenchymal cells, when cultured as single cells on circular islands, can exhibit a chiral swirling pattern of actin filaments, which is believed as the structural mechanism of cell chirality. However, single epithelial cells are unable to exhibit such chirality, which makes the mechanism of epithelial cell chirality uncertain and questionable. Here, we hypothesized that chirality of epithelial cells may be an emergent property shown as synchronized rotation of epithelial cell sheets on a circular confinement, namely, collective cell chirality. (Task 1) We will first develop a method for assessing collective cell chirality. Madin-Darby Canine Kidney (MDCK) cells, the epithelial cell model, will be cultured on micropatterned geometrical confinement to ensure the integrity of epithelial cell sheets. Next, collective chirality will be characterized based on the biased, synchronized rotation of epithelial cell sheets. (Task 2) We will explore the structural asymmetry of actomyosin cytoskeleton underlying the collective cell chirality. Collective movement of epithelial cells is associated with polarization of the cell-motility apparatus, suggesting the possible asymmetry of actomyosin distribution or dynamics during the synchronized rotation. In addition, we will use arrowhead-shaped islands to force cell polarity, which could be the sufficient prerequisite of epithelial cell chirality, for statistically analyzing the structural asymmetry. (Task 3) We will investigate the molecular mechanism governing the collective cell chirality. We will first apply a biophysical model of torque dipole based on the contractile sarcomere-like unit of actomyosin stress fibers, which will be validated by observation of live actin organization and inhibitory assays of actomyosin stress fibers. (Task 4) We will study the role of collective cell chirality in wound healing, particularly on the possible chiral behavior of leader cells in tissue morphogenesis. As a new perspective to investigate the chirality of epithelial cells and the resultant tissue morphology, our project would establish the knowledge foundation for tissue engineering and mechanobiology. 左右（LR）不對稱性是許多組織/器官中常見的結構特徵。上皮細胞的手性，即在單向遷移過程中細胞傾斜方向和結合重塑等機械行為，已被報導為驅動組織層次形態發生中的LR不對稱性。值得注意的是，間質細胞在圓形島上培養為單細胞時，可以表現出肌動蛋白絲的手性旋轉模式，這被認為是細胞手性的結構機制。然而，單個上皮細胞無法表現出這種手性，使得上皮細胞手性的機制不確定且值得懷疑。 在此，我們假設上皮細胞的手性可能是一種表現為上皮細胞群在圓形限制中同步旋轉的突現特性，即集體細胞手性。（任務1）我們將首先開發一種評估集體細胞手性的方法。作為上皮細胞模型的Madin-Darby犬腎細胞（MDCK）將在微圖案化幾何限制中培養，以確保上皮細胞群的完整性。接下來，集體手性將基於上皮細胞群的偏向同步旋轉進行特徵描述。（任務2）我們將探討支撐集體細胞手性的肌動蛋白-肌球蛋白細胞骨架的結構不對稱性。上皮細胞群的集體運動與細胞運動裝置的極化相關，這表明在同步旋轉過程中肌動蛋白-肌球蛋白分佈或動態可能存在不對稱性。此外，我們將使用箭頭形島來強制細胞極性，這可能是上皮細胞手性的充分前提，以統計分析結構不對稱性。（任務3）我們將研究控制集體細胞手性的分子機制。我們將首先應用基於肌動蛋白-肌球蛋白應力纖維收縮肌節樣單元的力偶模型，並通過活體肌動蛋白組織觀察和肌動蛋白-肌球蛋白應力纖維的抑制試驗進行驗證。（任務4）我們將研究集體細胞手性在傷口癒合中的作用，特別是在組織形態發生中領導細胞可能的手性行為。作為研究上皮細胞手性及由此產生的組織形態的新視角，我們的項目將為組織工程和機械生物學建立知識基礎。

11218325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11218325.value: 大語言模型時代的信息檢索：理解、泛化與可信度

11218325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11218325.value: Prof Li, Qing Prof Xu, Jianliang Dr Yin, Dawei

11218325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218325.value: In the digital era, information retrieval (IR) systems are essential for navigating vast information, powering applications like search engines and e-commerce. Over 90% of online experiences begin with search engines like Google, Microsoft, and Baidu, driving billions of daily interactions. Additionally, government programs, including US-FAI, UK-RI and EU-Horizon, fund significantly in IR advancements, underscoring their technical and economic importance. Despite their importance, current IR systems face several major challenges: 1) Insufficient Understanding in Query Rewriting: Traditional methods struggle to accurately understand and refine user queries, leading to inconsistent and suboptimal retrieval outcomes. 2) Inadequate Generalization in Retrieval and Ranking: Existing designs with separate retrievers and rankers limit their generalization ability across tasks, hampering system flexibility and scalability. 3) Limited Trustworthiness in Answer Generation: Conventional solutions grapple with limited access to external knowledge, reducing answer accuracy and trustworthiness. To address these challenges, this proposal aims to revolutionize IR systems with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance retrieval accuracy, consistency, flexibility, and trustworthiness. Leveraging LLMs' advanced capabilities in text understanding, generalization, knowledge integration, and generation, the project proposes four key research tasks: 1) Query Rewriter: Design an LLM-powered query rewriting framework to improve user intent understanding and align downstream retrieval modules, ensuring retrieval effectiveness and consistency. 2) Retriever and Ranker: Integrate retrieval and ranking tasks via LLMs, bridging semantic gaps and simplifying system design and maintenance. 3) Answer Generator: Develop an active retrieval-augmented generation framework to integrate external knowledge iteratively, ensuring accurate, trustworthy answers. 4) Module Unification: Unify above IR modules into a cohesive LLM-driven framework, boosting overall system performance and efficiency. Project Significance and Feasibility: This proposal's key intellectual merit lies in offering the first comprehensive investigation of LLM-based IR systems, bridging traditional IR's limitations with advanced LLMs for improved search quality. To achieve this, we will systematically investigate bottlenecks in key IR modules, leading to four innovative research directions (Tasks 1-4, with validated feasibility), and commercial validation (Task 5). Success will yield 1) next-generation LLM-powered IR systems, and 2) open-source prototypes for broader use. This project's impact extends globally, transforming IR paradigms, enhancing user satisfaction, platform profitability, technological advancements, ultimately benefiting academia, industry, and society. Our interdisciplinary team, with over 3,000 publications, 70,000 citations, and 20 best paper awards, combines expertise in IR, LLMs, and trustworthy AI. Partnerships with Baidu, Tencent, Ant Group, and Amazon, who plan to deploy our outputs, further strengthen the project's practical impact and feasibility. 在數字時代，信息檢索（IR）系統對於導航海量信息、爲搜索引擎和電子商務等應用提供動力至關重要。但當前的IR系統面臨着幾個主要挑戰：1)對查詢重寫的理解不足：傳統方法難以準確理解和精煉用戶查詢，導致檢索結果不一致和次優。2)檢索和排序的泛化不足：現有的單獨檢索器和排序器的設計限制了它們跨任務的泛化能力，阻礙了系統的靈活性和可擴展性。3)答案生成可信度有限：傳統解決方案難以獲得有限的外部知識，降低了答案的準確性和可信度。 爲了應對這些挑戰，本提案旨在用大型語言模型（ LLM）革新IR系統，以提高檢索的準確性、一致性、靈活性和可信度。利用 LLM在文本理解、泛化、知識集成和生成方面的先進能力，該項目提出了四個關鍵研究任務：1)查詢重寫器：設計一個基於 LLM的查詢重寫框架，以提高用戶意圖理解和對齊下游檢索模塊，確保檢索的有效性和一致性。2)檢索器和排序器：通過 LLM集成檢索和排序任務，彌合語義差距，簡化系統設計和維護。3)答案生成器：開發主動檢索增強生成框架，迭代集成外部知識，確保答案准確可信。4)模塊統一：將以上IR模塊統一爲一個內聚的 LLM驅動框架，提升整體系統性能和效率。

11218925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11218925.value: 透過多模態舞蹈品質評估提升以音樂為靈感的舞蹈生成

11218925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218925.value: This research project aims to enhance music-inspired dance generation by incorporating a Multimodal Dance Quality Assessment (DanceQA) framework. Firstly, previous dance quality assessment methods primarily only relied on skeleton features and often neglected the contributions of RGB and audio features while also facing challenges in developing a reliable DanceQA dataset due to the lack of comprehensive annotations for objective DanceQA metrics and music beats across diverse dance styles. To address these limitations, our study plans to adopt a multimodal approach that integrates 3D skeleton data, RGB features, and audio features into a comprehensive DanceQA framework. This framework will be capable of evaluating dance performance holistically by synchronizing the dancer’s movements with musical rhythms and visual aesthetics. Secondly, traditional methods for generating dance from music relied heavily on analyzing aspects such as loudness, rhythm, emotion, style, and beat, requiring significant expertise and posing challenges when adapting to different dance styles. By incorporating the Multimodal Dance Quality Assessment module, the generated dance motion sequences are continuously assessed, ensuring the production of high-quality dance movements and eliminating the need for additional post-processing to align the music with the dance. Thirdly, we plan to propose a system that captures the user’s movements and provides feedback through advanced motion comparison technologies and a choreography generation module that adapts to various skill levels. Our approach includes zero-shot learning to evaluate new, unseen dance sequences, enhancing the flexibility and applicability of the DanceQA. In pursuit of these goals, the project is structured around key research questions on assessing dance quality with a multimodal approach, improving music-driven dance generation quality, and designing adaptive dance training systems. The outcomes are expected to contribute significantly to the fields of automated dance evaluation and generation and interactive dance training, providing a scalable and efficient solution for both dancers and choreographers. 本研究項目旨在透過引入多模態舞蹈品質評估框架，提升以音樂為靈感的舞蹈生成技術。 首先，過往的舞蹈品質評估方法主要依賴骨架特徵，未有採用彩色圖像與音訊特徵，且由於缺乏帶有廣泛註釋並涵蓋多種舞蹈風格的客觀舞蹈品質評估指標與音樂節拍，導致難以建立可靠的舞蹈品質評估數據庫。為解決這些限制，本研究計劃採用多模態方法，整合三維骨架資料、彩色圖像與音訊特徵，構建全面性的舞蹈品質評估框架，此框架將根據舞者動作與音樂節奏及視覺美感的同步，全面評估舞蹈表現。 其次，傳統的音樂生成舞蹈方法高度依賴對音量、節奏、情感、風格與節拍等方面的分析，不僅需要專業知識，亦難以適應不同舞蹈風格。透過引入多模態舞蹈品質評估模組，生成的舞蹈動作序列可持續進行品質評估，確保產出高品質舞蹈動作，並免除額外的後期處理以令音樂與舞蹈互相協調。 第三，我們計劃提出一套系統，能夠捕捉使用者動作，並透過先進的動作比對技術提供回饋，搭配可因應不同技能水平的編舞生成模組。我們的方法亦包含零樣本學習，以評估全新、未見過的舞蹈序列，提升舞蹈品質評估的靈活性與應用性。 為達成上述目標，本項目將圍繞幾個核心研究問題展開，包括：如何以多模態方法評估舞蹈品質、如何提升音樂驅動的舞蹈生成品質，以及如何設計具適應性的舞蹈訓練系統。預期成果將對自動舞蹈評估與生成、互動式舞蹈訓練領域帶來重大貢獻，為舞者與編舞者提供具擴展性與高效率的解決方案。

11219025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11219025.value: 基於多方隨機排列的分佈式差分隱私：系統建模與安全強化

11219025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219025.value: In today's world, data is the backbone of both public institutions and businesses, driving innovation and decision-making. As the need for data collaboration grows, so does the challenge of safeguarding individual privacy. Differential privacy (DP) has aptly emerged as a powerful privacy-preserving tool. Traditional DP implementations are typically divided into two models: the central model, which relies on a trusted curator to aggregate raw data and apply DP algorithms; and the local model, where users independently add DP noise to their data before sharing them. While the local model provides stronger privacy, it often reduces data utility due to excessive noise. The central model, in contrast, ensures higher utility but depends on a fully trusted curator, posing a potential privacy risk if compromised. Shuffle DP has recently been introduced as a promising middle ground between these two models, providing better privacy-utility tradeoffs by introducing an intermediary entity -- ``trusted shuffler'' -- to anonymize user submissions through random shuffling them. Secure shuffling can provably amplify privacy, allowing users to apply less noise while still achieving the same level of privacy guarantees. However, despite the theoretical appeal, shuffle DP still faces a range of challenges, such as trust assumption, inbuilt restriction, processing overhead, and security vulnerability. They all hinder its widespread adoption in real-world applications. In this project, we propose to investigate a new multi-party shuffle DP (MP-SDP) model to overcome these challenges and promote better privacy-preserving practices. Instead of depending on a centralized shuffler, we plan to customize multi-party computation techniques across several non-colluding intermediary servers to collaboratively shuffle and process data. This will effectively preserve distributed trust, improve system performance, enhance service robustness, and broaden the design possibilities. Our project focuses on three main research questions: 1) How can we establish a solid theoretical framework for MP-SDP? 2) How can we generalize MP-SDP to maximize both privacy and flexibility? 3) How can we identify and address security risks in MP-SDP? Beyond theoretical work, we will implement and rigorously test a federated analytics framework based on the MP-SDP model, refining it through experimental validation. Our preliminary results indicate that MP-SDP offers significant advantages over current approaches regarding trust, overhead, privacy, and security. This makes MP-SDP especially valuable for industries like healthcare and finance, where strong privacy protections and accurate data insights are critical. 在當今世界，數據是公共機構和企業的支柱，驅動創新和決策制定。隨著大家越來越需要分享和合作使用數據，保護個人隱私的難題也變得更大。差分隱私（DP）這項技術，正好成為一個強大的工具，能幫助保護隱私。傳統的差分隱私方法，通常分成兩種方式：一種是中心模式，需要一個可信任的管理者來收集大家的原始數據，然後加點隱私保護的演算法；另一種是本地模式，每個人自己在分享數據前，就先加一些隨機干擾（噪聲）進去。本地模式雖然隱私保護更強，但加太多噪聲會讓數據變得不那麼有用。相反，中心模式能讓數據保持更多價值，但如果那個管理者被駭客攻擊，就可能洩露隱私。最近出現的基於隨機排列的差分隱私（Shuffle DP），就像這兩種方式的中間方案，提供更好的隱私和數據價值的平衡。它引入一個中間角色——「可信任的排列器」——來隨機打亂大家提交的數據，讓它變得匿名。這種安全的隨機排列，能證明讓隱私保護變強，所以大家可以加少一點噪聲，卻還能達到同樣的隱私保障。不過，雖然理論上聽起來不錯，這種方法還是有一些問題，比如需要信任那個排列器、有些內在限制、處理起來很花時間，還有安全漏洞，這些都讓它難以在現實生活中廣泛使用。 在本項目裡，我們想研究一種新的基於多方隨機排列的差分隱私（MP-SDP）模式，來解決這些問題，並推廣更好的隱私保護方式。我們不靠單一的中心排列器，而是用安全多方計算技術，讓幾個不會共謀的中間伺服器一起合作來打亂和處理數據。這將有效地維持分散式信任、改善系統效能、增強服務穩健性，並擴大設計可能性。我們主要探討三個問題：如何為MP-SDP建立堅實的理論框架？2) 如何泛化MP-SDP以最大化隱私和靈活性？3) 如何識別並解決MP-SDP中的安全風險？除了理論研究，我們還會實際做出一個基於MP-SDP的聯邦分析系統，嚴格測試它，並用實驗來改進。初步結果顯示，MP-SDP在信任、處理成本、隱私和安全上，比現有方法好很多。這使得MP-SDP特別適合醫療保健和金融等產業，在這些領域中，強大的隱私保護和準確的數據洞察至關重要。

11219225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11219225.value: 移动型神经刺激器： 用于神经刺激的微型机器人集成系统

11219225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219225.value: Micro-/nano energy-harvest elements are of rapidly growing interest for micro-/nanosystems, especially the implantable or in-body application oriented devices. The objective of this project is to investigate the integration of micro-organic photovoltaic (µOPV) batteries as an onboard power supply onto microrobotic carriers for such applications as a mobile electrochemical station or a neurostimulator. A groundbreaking microrobotic neurostimulator prototype initiates with an innovative mechanical design, seamlessly integrating the implicit function expansion (µOPV cells) into explicit locomotion control (ABF) for the first time. The prevailing challenges of physically integrating microdevices into system-level microrobot systems are broken via a self-established batch fabrication process. The diverse configurations of microrobotic neurostimulators achieve a mass yield with Voc close to 0.60 - 0.80 V, and power density of 1.5 mW mm-2 of M-OPV cells with a 100 μm side length under near-infrared light (808 nm wavelength with 2.26-Sun intensity), underscoring the exceptional biocompatibility that robustly meets the demands of biomedical applications. The microrobotic neurostimulator have multi-mode locomotion capability and environmental adaptability. The Voc (over 0.60 V) under the epidermis and dermis during static electrical stimulation, coupled with dynamic electrical stimulation featuring self-rectified pulse Voc modulation, and opto-electromechanical coupling establishment, offers quantitative insights into the electrical stimulation effect. This, in turn, demonstrates the potential application of our design in implantable skin physiology and targeted nerve stimulation. Our microrobotic neurostimulator design portrays an extraordinary implementation strategy for enhancing the functionality of microrobot systems, serving as a targeted implantable miniature instrument for personalized biomedicine.
