We believe the ideas and techniques developed in this project would be helpful for the mathematical theory of the multi-dimensional compressible Euler equations and nonlinear partial differential equations. We have been working on the related problems for several years. We find a mechanism based on non-zero swirl velocity to determine the location of the transonic normal shock in [22], and establish the existence and uniqueness of subsonic contact discontinuity in an infinitely long nozzle with large vorticity in [10]; the stability of supersonic/transonic contact discontinuity in a finitely long nozzle in [25-27]; stability of three-dimensional attached transonic weak shock in [5]; and convexity of self-similar transonic shocks in [9]. In this project, we will mainly focus on further developing the techniques used in the works above, to study the mentioned objectives. 這個項目的目標是通過研究幾個重要問題，發展出嚴謹的機制和數學理論，以確定有限長度管道中高維穩態可壓縮歐拉流的自由邊界的確定問題。特別是，在噴嘴出口給定壓力下亞音速接觸间断的位置、有限長度管道中带燃燒現象下的跨音速激波位置以及其他相關問題。 從[6, 7, 42]中的開創性工作開始，已經有許多關於管道中自由邊界的穩態解的結果，例如管道中的跨音速激波問題[3, 4, 8, 12–15, 20–24, 28–34, 38, 39, 41, 43]或有限長度管道中的接觸间断[25–27]。根據[18]，我們將在管道出口施加壓力條件、在管道壁上施加滑移邊界條件，並根據來流是超音速還是亞音速，在管道入口施加適當的邊界條件。在數學上，這些問題可以化為由非線性方程所支配的自由邊界值問題。關鍵的困難在於，自由邊界可以在均勻流中任意移動。因此，尋找合理的機制來確定直管道中的自由邊界位置是一個長期存在的數學開放問題。最近，針對直管道中的跨音速激波問題，基於管道壁的非平坦性[24]和非零旋轉速度[22]引入了兩種機制。然而，對於這些問題的嚴謹數學分析仍然遠未滿足。我們相信本項目中開發的思想和技術將有助於多維可壓縮歐拉方程和非線性偏微分方程的數學理論。 我們已經在相關問題上工作了幾年。我們在[22]中找到了一種基於非零旋轉速度的機制來確定跨音速法向激波的位置，並在[10]中建立了具有大渦度的無限長管道中亞音速接觸间断的存在性和唯一性；在[25-27]中研究了有限長管道中超音速/跨音速接觸间断的穩定性；在[5]中研究了三維附著跨音速弱激波的穩定性；以及在[9]中研究了自相似跨音速激波的凸性。在本項目中，我們將主要集中於進一步發展上述工作的技術，以研究提到的目標。

11305725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11305725.value: 二维范德华铁电材料中电控自旋轨道耦合的研究

11305725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305725.value: Modern information technology and artificial intelligence demands high density, low energy consumption, high speed and integrated logic/memory devices. Currently, traditional Si-based semiconductor devices, which rely on electron charge for data processing and storage, face serious challenges in thermal management and quantum limitations. This threatens the continuation of Moore's Law, leading to a surge in research on new materials and novel device concepts. Spintronic devices, which use electron spin for data storage and processing, promise to overcome these challenges with greater efficiency. Such devices have gained tremendous interests across academia, industry, and governments, with applications such as magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) already used in aerospace and the Internet of Things. However, existing spintronic devices depend on current to control magnetization, which falls short of the high density and low power consumption needed for next generation technologies. Electric field control of spin offers low energy, fast operation, and better integration with existing Si-based semiconductor devices, sparking interest in multiferroic materials. However, conventional oxide multiferroics, though promising, face issues in device reliability and Si compatibility. For instance, BiFeO3-based devices suffer from defect accumulation causing coupling failures after repeated use. The field seeks robust, efficient, and semiconductor-compatible magnetoelectric coupling mechanisms. This project proposes using spontaneous ferroelectric polarization in two-dimensional van der Waals (2D-vdW) materials to control spin-orbit coupling (SOC), aiming to achieve non-volatile, highly efficient charge current to spin current conversion, paving the way for next generation spintronic technology. The innovation lies in leveraging the quantum confinement effect of 2D-vdW materials to achieve coexistence of switchable spontaneous polarization and high carrier concentration and mobility. The field is still at its infant stage, and much work is needed for clarifying the underlying physics, as well as the design and test of prototype devices. The success of this project will lead Hong Kong’s innovation in the field of spintronics, forging a solid foundation for the development of next generation integrated logic/memory devices. 现代信息技术与人工智能的发展对数据存储处理器件提出了高密度、低能耗、高速运行及存算一体化等严格要求。当前，依赖电子电荷进行数据处理与存储的传统硅基半导体器件，正面临热管理瓶颈和量子极限的双重挑战，这不仅威胁着摩尔定律的延续，更催生了新材料与新器件的研究热潮。利用电子自旋进行数据存储与处理的自旋电子器件，以其突破这些限制的潜力，已引发学术界、产业界和政府部门的高度关注。然而，现有自旋电子器件依赖电流控制磁化方向，难以满足下一代技术对高集成度和低功耗的核心需求。电场控制自旋的方式兼具低能耗、高速和与硅基器件兼容的特性，推动了多铁性材料研究的热潮。但传统氧化物多铁性材料虽前景可观，却受制于器件可靠性及与硅工艺兼容性的问题。该领域亟需寻找稳定高效且与半导体工艺兼容的磁电耦合机制。 本项目提出利用二维范德华材料的自发铁电极化调控自旋轨道耦合，旨在实现非易失性、高效率的电控电荷流-自旋流转换，为下一代自旋电子技术奠定基础。其核心创新点在于利用二维材料的量子限域效应，实现可翻转自发极化与高载流子浓度、高迁移率的共存。该研究方向目前仍处于起步阶段，需深入探索其物理机制并开展原型器件设计与测试。本项目的成功实施将引领香港在自旋电子学领域的创新浪潮，为发展新一代存算一体化器件提供坚实支撑。

11305825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305825.value: The conformal restriction property is the combination of the conformal invariance property and a certain restriction property. It was first outlined by Lawler, Schramm and Werner, as a characterizing property of SLE(8/3) curves. Recall that SLE (Schramm-Loewner evolution) was introduced by Schramm in 1999 as a candidate for the scaling limit of interfaces for a wide class of lattice models in statistical physics. It is interesting to consider measures on self-avoiding loops, due to the symmetry. Werner characterized the SLE(8/3) loop measure as the unique measure on self-avoiding loops which satisfies the conformal restriction property. Soon after, Kontsevich and Suhov postulated the conformal restriction axioms for a family of measures on self-avoiding loops, depending on a central charge c<=1. They hinted the link between such measures with the SLE loop measure, as well as the unitarizing measures of the Virasoro algebra. In a recent joint work with Gordina and Wang, we constructed a representation of the Virasoro algebra using the SLE loop measure, and showed that this measure is indefinite unitary. The SLE is closely related to the Brownian loop soups, which is a random collection of Brownian loops in a planar domain. For example, the conformal loop ensemble (CLE) is a collection of loops which locally look like SLE. They have been shown to have the same distribution as the outer boundaries of the outermost clusters in the Brownian loop soup. In this project, we plan to study a certain loop ensemble, coming from the clusters of the Brownian loop soup. This loop ensemble is closely related to a certain conformally invariant field h that we constructed in a joint work with Jego and Lupu. We aim to understand the relation between this loop ensemble and the SLE loop measures. In addition, we would like to compute some precise quantities about this loop ensemble, as well as the SLE loops, which would also shed light on the field h. 「共形限製性質」是指「共形不變性」和某種「限製性質」的結合。它首先由Lawler, Schramm和Werner指出，用以刻畫SLE(8/3)曲線。SLE曲線由Schramm於1999年引入，對於統計物理中一大類廣泛的格點模型，都潛在地刻畫它們的界面的縮放極限。 不自交圈上的測度，因為對稱性，是有趣的研究對象。Werner將SLE(8/3)圈刻畫為唯一的滿足共形限製性質的不自交圈上的測度。其後，Kontsevich和Suhov對於一組取決於一個中心荷c<=1的不自交圈上的測度，提出了「共形限製公理」。他們暗示了這組測度與SLE圈測度的關系，以及和Virasoro代數的幺正測度的關系。我們在和Gordina和Wang的一個近期工作中，用SLE圈測度建立了一個Virasoro代數的表示，並證明了這個測度是不定值幺正的。 SLE曲線和布朗圈族關系密切。後者是平面區域內的一組隨機的布朗圈。比如，共形圈族(CLE)是一組局部類似SLE曲線的隨機圈，並被證明與布朗圈族的最外層簇的外邊界同分布。 在這一研究計劃中，我們準備研究某種由布朗圈族的聯通簇生成的圈族。這一圈族和某個我們和Jego和Lupu共同構造的共形不變場h密切相關。我們致力於理解這一圈族和SLE圈測度的關系。並且我們希望計算關於這一圈族以及SLE圈的某些精確量，以得到關於場h的更多信息。

11306025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306025.value: 基于钌的抗癌候选药物的靶点鉴定：一种迈向临床应用前沿的无偏倚整合化学生物学方法

11306025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11306025.value: Prof Ang, Wee Han Prof Che, Chi-Ming

11306025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306025.value: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Triple-negative breast cancers (TNBCs), accounting for 15%–20% of breast cancer cases, are particularly challenging to treat owing to their aggressive nature, higher chance of spreading to other organs, and lack of effective targeted therapies. Although chemotherapy remains the standard treatment, it is often associated with severe side effects, and there is a need for new and safer treatment options. The proposed project will advance the development of a promising ruthenium-based anticancer compound, RUTEN3. Early studies have shown that RUTEN3 can effectively stop the growth of TNBC tumors and prevent their spread, and it has fewer side effects than traditional chemotherapy drugs. However, to advance RUTEN3 toward clinical use, it is essential to understand how it works at the molecular level. Specifically, we need to know the proteins it targets and how it interacts with them. The proposed project will explore three key questions: 1. What are the molecular targets of RUTEN3? Using advanced techniques such as the thermal proteome profiling (TPP), we will identify which proteins RUTEN3 binds to within cancer cells. These interactions will be validated to ensure they are accurate and meaningful. 2. Is RUTEN3 stable in biological environments? We will study how RUTEN3 behaves in different biological fluids and whether it undergoes chemical changes, such as breakdown by enzymes in the liver. Stability is crucial for ensuring that the drug remains effective in the body. 3. Does RUTEN3 interact with its targets through reversible or permanent binding? We will investigate whether RUTEN3 forms reversible (non-covalent) or permanent (covalent) bonds with its target proteins. Reversible interactions can reduce the risk of long-term side effects, whereas permanent interactions may offer higher potency but require careful monitoring to avoid toxicity. Our interdisciplinary team, having expertise in bioinorganic chemistry, molecular biology and proteomics, will adopt state-of-the-art mass spectrometry to conduct these studies. The project will lay the groundwork for more effective, low-toxicity treatments for TNBCs. Within the three-year period covered by this proposal, this project will impact the medicinal chemistry community by clarifying the interactions between ruthenium drug candidates and their protein targets, providing valuable insights into their nature. In the long run, understanding the targets of RUTEN3 will help identify which patients can benefit from this drug candidate, predict any possible side effects it might have and guide future clinical trials. 乳腺癌是全球最常见的癌症之一。其中三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）约占所有乳腺癌病例的15%–20%，由于其侵袭性强、转移风险高且缺乏有效的靶向疗法，治疗尤为困难。尽管化疗仍是标准治疗方案，但其常伴随严重的副作用，因此亟需开发新型且更安全的治疗选择。本项目旨在推进一种基于钌的抗癌化合物RUTEN3的研发。早期研究表明，RUTEN3能有效抑制三阴性乳腺癌肿瘤的生长并阻止其转移，且相较于传统化疗药物副作用更小。然而，要推动RUTEN3进入临床应用，必须明确其分子水平的作用机制，特别是其靶向蛋白及相互作用方式。 本项目将重点探索三个关键问题： 1. RUTEN3的分子靶点是什么？ 通过应用热蛋白质组分析（TPP）等先进技术，我们将鉴定RUTEN3在癌细胞中结合的特定蛋白质，并对这些相互作用进行验证以确保其准确性和生物学意义。 2. RUTEN3在生物环境中是否稳定？ 我们将研究RUTEN3在不同生物体液中的行为，以及是否会发生化学变化（如被肝脏酶分解）。稳定性是确保药物在体内保持疗效的关键因素。 3. RUTEN3与靶点的结合是可逆还是永久性的？ 我们将探究RUTEN3与靶蛋白形成的是可逆（非共价）还是永久性（共价）结合。可逆相互作用可降低长期副作用风险，而永久性结合虽可能提高药效，但需谨慎评估以避免毒性。 我们的跨学科团队融合了生物无机化学、分子生物学和蛋白质组学领域的专业知识，将采用最先进的质谱技术开展研究。本项目将为开发高效、低毒的三阴性乳腺癌治疗方案奠定基础。在为期三年的项目周期内，研究成果将通过阐明钌类药物候选物与靶蛋白的相互作用机制，为药物化学领域提供重要参考。长远来看，明确RUTEN3的靶点将有助于筛选适用患者群体、预测潜在副作用，并为未来临床试验提供指导依据。

11306125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306125.value: 連續時間網絡數據的加性強度學習與動態分析

11306125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306125.value: Network data, which appears in fields like sociology, computer science, and biology, captures the continuous interactions between entities known as nodes. These interactions are recorded over time and can include examples such as social ties among individuals, brain connectivity analyzed through functional magnetic resonance imaging, and gene interactions during human embryonic stem cell development. Understanding how these networks change over time is essential. This research aims to develop a comprehensive framework based on an additive-intensity model to tackle three main challenges: variations in connection numbers over time, the influence of shared characteristics among nodes, and the analysis of large, sparse networks. Often, these networks contain numerous pairs of nodes, but only a small percentage exhibit active interactions, and these interactions can vary over time. By creating this framework, the research seeks to provide enhanced tools for analyzing the dynamic structures of networks, ultimately improving our understanding of complex systems across various disciplines. 網絡數據出現在社會學、計算機科學和生物學等領域，捕捉了稱為節點的實體之間的連續交互。這些交互隨時間記錄，可能包括個人之間的社交聯繫、通過功能性磁共振成像分析的大腦連接性，以及人類胚胎幹細胞發育過程中的基因交互。理解這些網絡隨時間的變化至關重要。本研究旨在基於加性強度模型開發一個全面的學習與動態分析框架，以應對三個主要挑戰：隨時間變化的連接數量、節點間共享特徵的影響，以及大型稀疏網絡的分析。通常，這些網絡包含眾多節點對，但只有少數表現出活躍的交互，且這些交互隨時間變化。通過創建此學習框架，本研究致力於提供增強的工具，用於分析網絡的動態結構，最終提升我們對各學科中複雜系統的理解。

11307625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307625.value: 基於原子光子混合干涉儀和零差檢測的精密測量

11307625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307625.value: Enhancements in measurement precision have often paved the way for groundbreaking discoveries and innovations in experimental methodologies. Precision measurements rely heavily on the technique of interferometry that has led to several Nobel Prizes in Physics, such as the Michelson interferometric test of special relativity, gravitational wave detection, and quantum measurement and manipulation of microwave photons. Traditional interferometers involve interference of the same type of wave by splitting and recombining the wave to obtain the phase information that is sensitive to many physical quantities. Recently, a novel quantum SU(1,1) interferometer was realized that is capable of mixing two different types of waves: light waves and atomic waves, providing a sensitive optical interferometric way to probe the atomic states. In this research project, we will use atoms as sensors to experimentally investigate the precise measurement of physical quantities (such as magnetic fields and optical fields) with the hybrid atom-light interferometer. Due to the intrinsic quantum entanglement between atom and photon, this type of quantum interferometer exhibits a sensitivity that surpasses traditional interferometers limited by the shot noise. Compared to traditional atomic magnetometers based on atomic spins, we now have a completely new method for sensing magnetic fields, which is expected to serve as a high-sensitivity magnetometer without the need of spin-squeezed states. In addition, the quantum SU(1,1) interferometer can perform quantum non-destructive measurements of photon numbers based on the influence of the optical field on atomic phases, which is similar to the Nobel prize winning work in microwave by Serge Haroche but is extended to the optical regime. To further enhance interferometer sensitivity, we also propose the use of homodyne detection technology that can enable the observation of interference between light waves and atomic waves even beyond the coherent time. This will overcome the limitation on the sensitivity of quantum interferometers imposed by the coherence time of entangled resources, expanding the range of applications. This type of atom-light interferometer, based on low-cost hot atomic cells, features a simple optical system, higher precision, and ease of integration, making it a commercially viable quantum technology with direct application prospects and contributing to the development of Hong Kong’s quantum industry market. 測量精度的提高往往為突破性發現和實驗方法的創新鋪平了道路。 精密測量在很大程度上依賴於干涉測量技术，該技术已導致多項諾貝爾物理學獎，如狹義相對論的邁克爾遜干涉測試、引力波探測以及微波光子的量子量測和操縱。 傳統干涉儀通過分波與和波來獲得對許多物理量敏感的相位資訊，從而涉及同一類型波的干涉。 最近實現的一種新型的量子SU（1,1）干涉儀能够混合兩種不同類型的波：光波和原子波，並提供了一種靈敏的光學干涉方法來探測原子態。 在這個研究項目中，我們將使用原子作為感測器，通過原子光子混合干涉儀對物理量（如磁場和光場）的精確量測進行實驗研究。 由於原子和光子之間的內在量子糾纏，這種量子干涉儀的靈敏度超過了受散粒噪聲限制的傳統干涉儀。 與基於原子自旋的傳統原子磁力計相比，我們具有一種全新的磁場傳感方法，有望成為一種不依賴於自旋壓縮態的高靈敏度磁強計。 此外，量子SU（1,1）干涉儀可以根據光場對原子相位的影響對光子數進行量子無損量測，這類似於諾貝爾獎獲得者Serge Haroche在微波領域的工作，但擴展到了光學領域。 為了進一步提高干涉儀的靈敏度，我們還提出使用零差檢測科技，即使在相干時間之外，也能觀察到光波和原子波之間的干涉。 這將克服糾纏資源的相干時間對量子干涉儀靈敏度的限制，擴大應用範圍。 這種基於低成本熱原子池的原子光子干涉儀，具有光學系統簡單、精度高、易於集成等特點，是一種具有商業可行性、具有直接應用前景的量子科技，有助於香港量子產業市場的發展。

11307925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307925.value: 在非晶材料上生長半金屬過渡金屬二硫族化合物及其高效析氫研究

11307925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307925.value: Water electrolysis using highly efficient electrocatalysts has been considered a promising strategy for producing green H2. Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) due to their large surface area, and abundant active sites. As a newly emerging strategy, phase engineering of nanomaterials (PEN) enables the precise control of the atomic arrangements of TMDs to tune their catalytic activities. Importantly, semi-metallic 1T′-MoS2 exhibits superior HER performance compared to the semiconducting 2H-MoS2 due to its higher basal-plane activity and greater intrinsic electrical conductivity. Hence, synthesis of semi-metallic TMDs for electrocatalytic HER is of great significance. Crystalline metal substrates/templates have been used for synthesizing high-quality TMDs. Unfortunately, the as-synthesized TMDs normally possess 2H phase, or mixed 2H and 1T′ phases. Additionally, the metastable 1T′ phase could gradually transform into the thermodynamically stable 2H phase, severely hindering the study of intrinsic catalytic activities and phase-dependent HER performances of the semi-metallic TMDs. Recently, our group has published a work in Nature Materials, proposing a facile and general wet-chemical method to grow a series of semi-metallic 1T′-TMD monolayers with high phase purity and stability on 4H-Au nanowires, in which the key role of the crystal phase of metal substrates/templates in the controlled synthesis of TMDs with unconventional phases was emphasized. Besides the crystalline metal substrates/templates, amorphous nanostructures could also be used as ideal substrates/templates to grow secondary materials. In addition, amorphous nanostructures are highly efficient catalysts for HER due to the abundant unsaturated coordination sites compared to their crystalline counterparts. Therefore, it is believed that synthesis of semi-metallic 1T′-TMDs on amorphous templates to construct hybrid nanomaterials could exhibit superior HER performance by virtue of the intrinsic catalytic HER activity of amorphous nanostructures and semi-metallic 1T′-TMDs. In this proposal, we aim to develop facile and general synthetic strategies to grow various semi-metallic 1T′-TMDs on amorphous templates to construct novel amorphous metal/semi-metallic TMD hybrid nanomaterials (denoted as a-M/sm-TMDs). Some key fundamental issues will be addressed in this proposal, including the growth and stabilization mechanism of semi-metallic TMDs on amorphous templates, the synergistic effect between amorphous metal and semi-metallic TMDs on the HER performance, and the structure-performance relationship in a-M/sm-TMD hybrid nanomaterials towards HER. 利用高效催化劑電解水被認為是生產綠氫的一種極具前景的策略。二維 (2D) 過渡金屬二硫族化物 (TMD) 材料因具有大的比表面積和豐富的活性位點，是析氫反應 (HER) 中具有前景的電催化劑。作為一種新興策略，納米材料相工程 (PEN) 可以精確控制TMD材料中的原子排列，從而調節其催化活性。重要的是，半金屬1T′-MoS2由於具有更高的基面活性和更高的本徵電導率，表現出比半導體2H-MoS2更優異的析氫性能。因此，合成用於電催化HER的半金屬TMD材料具有重要的意義。 晶體金屬基底/模板已被用於合成高品質的TMD材料。然而，合成的TMD材料通常具有2H相或2H和1T′相的混合相。此外，亞穩的1T′相可能逐漸轉變為熱力學穩定的2H相，這嚴重阻礙了對半金屬TMD材料本徵催化活性和相依賴HER性能的研究。最近，我們團隊在《自然-材料》雜誌上發表論文，提出了一種簡單、通用的濕化學方法，在4H-Au納米線上生長一系列具有高相純度和穩定性的半金屬1T′-TMD單層材料，並強調了金屬基底/模板的晶相在控制合成具有非常規相的TMD材料中的關鍵作用。除了晶體金屬基底/模板外，非晶納米結構也可用作生長二次材料的理想基底/模板。此外，與晶體相比，非晶納米結構具有豐富的不飽和配位點，是高效的HER催化劑。因此，我們認為，在非晶模板上合成半金屬1T′-TMD材料以建構雜合納米材料，憑藉非晶納米結構和半金屬1T′-TMD材料固有的催化析氫活性，從而展現出優異的HER性能。 在本項目中，我們旨在開發簡單且通用的合成策略，在非晶模板上生長各種半金屬1T′-TMD材料，從而建構新型非晶金屬/半金屬TMD雜合納米材料 (a-M/sm-TMD)。本項目將探討一些關鍵的基礎科學問題，包括半金屬TMD材料在非晶模板上的生長和穩定機制、非晶金屬和半金屬TMD材料對析氫性能的協同效應，以及a-M/sm-TMD雜合納米材料在HER過程中的結構-性能的構效關係。

11308125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308125.value: 單片鈣鈦礦/矽疊層太陽能電池在反向偏壓應力下的降解機製探索與熱斑效應研究

11308125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308125.value: The integration of perovskite and silicon technologies has given rise to perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs), which potentially could replace traditional single-junction silicon solar cells as the mainstream in the photovoltaic market. Despite their promising prospects, PSTSCs face significant challenges under operational conditions, especially concerning the hot spot effects caused by reverse bias (RB) conditions under partial shading stresses. The initial phase of our investigation focuses on a detailed analysis of the dynamics and consequences of hot spots within PSTSCs. Utilizing a combination of finite element analysis (FEA) and coupled thermal-electrical simulations, we aim to model the thermal and mechanical stresses that lead to hot spot formation. This is complemented by advanced characterization techniques including thermographic imaging, electroluminescence (EL), and photoluminescence (PL) imaging to directly observe the formation and impact of hot spots on cell efficiency and stability. Building on the insights gained from these studies, the project progresses to explore and validate mitigation strategies aimed at enhancing the structural and thermal resilience of the cells. One innovative approach includes the regulation of perovskite film growth through seed crystal induction and additive engineering to increase the uniformity of the films and reduce defect densities, which are critical factors in hot spot formation. Additionally, we explore the design and synthesis of functional materials, such as metal-organic compounds, to stabilize the perovskite structure and suppress ion volatilization under thermal stress. In the final phase of the project, we focus on performance optimization through integrated electro-optical characterization and ionic properties analysis. Our goal is to systematically enhance the device efficiency to achieve over 33% for small-area devices and assess the stability of these optimized cells under a range of stress conditions including high temperatures and varying humidity levels. This involves a rigorous testing protocol aligned with international standards to ensure that the mitigation strategies do not compromise the long-term stability and operational viability of the cells. This comprehensive approach not only addresses the immediate challenges posed by hot spots but also contributes to the broader understanding and applicability of PSTSCs in real-world scenarios. Through this project, we aim to advance the field of photovoltaics by developing more reliable and efficient tandem solar cells that are better suited to meet the demands of modern energy systems. 鈣鈦礦與矽技術的融合催生了鈣鈦礦/矽疊層太陽能電池（PSTSCs），它有望取代傳統的單結矽太陽能電池，成為光伏市場的主流。盡管前景廣闊，PSTSCs在運行條件下仍面臨重大挑戰，尤其是在部分遮陰應力引發的反向偏壓（RB）條件下所產生的熱點效應問題。我們研究的初始階段聚焦於深入分析PSTSCs內部熱斑效應的動態過程及其後果。通過結合有限元分析（FEA）和熱電耦合仿真模擬，我們旨在對導致熱斑形成的熱應力和機械應力進行建模。同時，輔以先進表征技術，包括熱成像、電致發光（EL）和光致發光（PL）成像，以直接觀測熱點的形成及其對電池效率和穩定性的影響。基於這些研究獲得的見解，本項目進而探索並驗證旨在增強電池結構穩定性和熱穩定性的緩解策略。其中一項創新方法包括通過籽晶誘導和添加劑工程調控鈣鈦礦薄膜的生長，以提高薄膜均勻性並降低缺陷密度——這些都是影響熱斑形成的關鍵因素。此外，我們探索設計和合成功能性材料（如金屬有機化合物），以穩定鈣鈦礦結構，並在熱應力下抑製離子揮發。在項目的最後階段，我們通過綜合的電學-光學表征和離子特性分析，專註於性能優化。我們的目標是系統性地提升器件效率，使小面積器件效率超過33%，並評估這些優化後的電池在高溫、變濕度等各類應力條件下的穩定性。這涉及遵循國際標準的嚴格測試規程，以確保所采取的緩解策略不會損害電池的長期穩定性和運行可行性。這種綜合性方法不僅解決了熱斑效應帶來的直接挑戰，更有助於深化對PSTSCs在實際應用場景中的理解和適用性。通過本項目，我們旨在通過開發更可靠、更高效的疊層太陽能電池來推動光伏領域的發展，使其更好地滿足現代能源系統的需求。

11308625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308625.value: 用於提高有機/鈣鈦礦太陽能電池效率與穩定性的多金屬氧酸鹽（POM）與自組裝單分子層（SAM）複合材料分子工程

11308625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308625.value: Organic and perovskite solar cells (OSCs and PSCs) are two emerging photovoltaics (PVs) that have potential in energy conversion applications for residential and utility-scale installations. They can provide abundant solar energy to help reduce fossil fuel consumption for realizing carbon neutralization. PVs are estimated to provide ~22% of cumulative power capacity in 2027. However, most of the current PVs are based on high temperature (>1500°C) processed crystalline silicon, which requires significant energy consumption. In contrast, OSCs and PSCs can be solution or vapor processed at relatively low temperatures (<150 °C) with diverse form factors to provide low-cost and scalable solar energy. Although the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) for single-junction OSCs and PSCs have already reached 20% and 26%, respectively, these numbers still lag their theoretical upper-limits (33%). Furthermore, their long-term stability still cannot meet the stringent requirements for commercial operations. Therefore, it is vital to develop effective ways that can further elevate their efficiency and stability. In a typical planar junction solar cell, there are several interfacial layers (ILs) that play critical roles in enhancing charge transport/collection and stability of devices. However, the currently used organic/inorganic ILs cannot provide suitable properties to ensure high device efficiency and stability. Polyoxometalates (POMs) as a class of early transition metals-based polynuclear oxo-anions can potentially fulfill the requirements for IL. Their unique nano-sizes, structures, optoelectronic properties, redox activities, and excellent photo- and thermal-stability have enabled their uses in various electroactive and optoelectronic applications. However, there lacks a systematic study in molecular engineering their structures and properties to enable their use as efficient ILs for PVs. In this proposal, we will develop functional POMs and their composites with self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to serve as effective ILs for improving PV performance. We will develop them based on four interconnecting tasks: 1) Develop suitable POM/SAM pairs for OSCs and PSCs; 2) Develop cation-exchanged POMs to passivate the perovskite defects for enhancing lattice stability; 3) Develop redox active POM mediators to mitigate ion motion-created failure in PSCs; 4) Demonstrate highly efficient and stable OSCs and PSCs through optimized POM/SAM composites. The outcomes from this project will help advance OSCs and PSCs to achieve exceptional efficiency and stability for facilitating their commercialization. It will also provide good opportunities for training students as next generation leaders in printable PVs and positioning Hong Kong as the frontier research hub for affordable and sustainable clean energy. 有機太陽能電池（OSCs）和鈣鈦礦太陽能電池（PSCs）作為兩類新興光伏技術，在住宅及大型公用設施安裝的能源轉換應用中展現出巨大潛力。這類光電元件可透過高效利用太陽能減少化石燃料消耗，為實現碳中和目標提供重要路徑。據預測，至2027年光電發電將佔全球累計發電裝置容量的約22%。然而，目前主流光電技術仍基於高溫（>1500°C）加工製備的晶矽材料，其生產過程能耗顯著。相較之下，OSCs與PSCs可在相對低溫（<150°C）條件下採用溶液法或氣相沉積製備，且具備多樣化元件構型優勢，可實現低成本、可規模化生產的太陽能利用。儘管目前單結OSCs和PSCs的最高能量轉換效率已分別突破20%和26%，但仍顯著低於其理論極限效率（33%）。更關鍵的是，其長期穩定性尚無法滿足商業化營運的嚴苛要求。因此，開發有效的策略來進一步提高這類裝置的效率和穩定性至關重要。在典型的平面異質接面太陽能電池中，多界面層（ILs）對提升元件電荷傳輸/收集效率及穩定性有關鍵作用。然而，現有有機/無機ILs難以同時滿足高效率與高穩定性的要求。 POMs作為一類基於過渡金屬的多核氧陰離子簇化合物，可作為界面層材料。它具有獨特的奈米尺寸效應、可調控結構、優異的光電特性、氧化還原活性以及卓越的光熱穩定性，在電活性與光電裝置領域展現出巨大應用潛力。但目前尚缺乏透過分子工程策略系統調控POMs結構與性能、以開發高效能光伏裝置界面層的深入研究。本計畫將開發功能性POMs及其與SAMs的複合材料體系，透過以下四個相互關聯的研究任務建構高效能光伏裝置界面層：1）篩選適配OSCs與PSCs的POM/SAM分子對；2）設計陽離子交換型POMs用於鈍化鈣鈦礦缺陷並增強晶格穩定性；3）開發氧化還原活性POM介體以抑制PSCs中離子遷移導致的性能衰減；4）透過優化POM/SAM複合材料體系製備高效穩定的OSCs與PSCs。本計畫的成果將推動OSCs和PSC在效率與穩定性方面取得突破性進展，加速其商業化進程。此外，這也將為培養下一代可印刷光伏技術領域的領導者提供良好機遇，並協助香港建設成為面向經濟型、永續清潔能源的前沿研究中心。

11308725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308725.value: 聚偏二氟乙烯基固態電解質設計與優化及其在高電壓鋰金屬電池中的應用

11308725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308725.value: The global battery market, valued at USD 118.20 billion in 2023, is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 16.1% from 2024 to 2030. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) dominate this market, holding 43.02% of the revenue share due to their superior electrochemical performance and versatility. However, the inherent safety risks associated with volatile liquid electrolytes (LEs) and the demand for higher energy densities present significant challenges to the continued dominance of traditional LIB technology. Recent incidents involving battery explosions in electric vehicles (EVs) highlight the urgent need for safer, high-performance alternatives in the rapidly growing energy storage market. To address these challenges, the development of lithium-ion batteries focuses on the research and development of solid-state lithium metal batteries (LMBs) by utilizing Poly(Vinylidene Fluoride) (PVDF) solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). PVDF SPEs replace volatile liquid electrolytes with nonflammable solid counterparts, mitigating the risk of thermal runaway. In addition, solid-state LMBs retain the potential for high energy density and commercial scalability. Although PVDF-based SPEs hold promise for safer and more efficient battery designs, they face challenges that must be addressed to enable their widespread application in high-performance SSLIBs. One of the key drawbacks is the low ionic conductivity (~10-6 S cm-1 at room temperature), primarily due to the semi-crystalline nature of the polymer, and poor dissociation of lithium salts, leading to sluggish lithium-ion transport. Additionally, there are concerns related to interface compatibility, as irreversible side reactions between Li metal anodes and decomposition at the cathode interface. To realize the potential of PVDF-based SPEs at an industrial scale, significant improvements in ionic conductivity and interface compatibility with both cathodes and anodes are still required. This project aims to enhance the energy density and cycling stability of solid-state batteries by optimizing the phase and solvation structure of PVDF-based SPEs. The stable Li/PVDF interface will be achieved by adding lithium salts and additives. On the cathode side, novel lithium salts will be used to form the stable cathode-electrolyte interface, improving performance under high voltage. The mechanism of interface evolution will be explored to further optimize PVDF SPEs. Meanwhile, the mechanical properties of PVDF electrolyte will be enhanced with reduced thickness. Finally, the pouch-type solid-state LMBs utilizing the PVDF-based SPEs will be fabricated and evaluated for their cycling performance and safety performance for potential commercialization. 2023 年全球電池市場規模達 1182 億美元，預計於 2024 至 2030 年期間以 16.1% 的年均複合增長率（CAGR）持續擴張。鋰離子電池（LIBs）憑藉其卓越的電化學性能與廣泛適用性，佔據 43.02% 的市場收入份額。然而，傳統鋰離子電池因揮發性液態電解質（LEs）帶來的潛在安全風險，以及對更高能量密度的需求，正面臨嚴峻挑戰。近年來，電動汽車（EVs）電池爆炸事故頻發，進一步凸顯了在快速增長的能源儲存市場中，開發更安全且高性能替代技術的迫切需求。 為應對上述挑戰，本研究聚焦於利用聚偏二氟乙烯（PVDF）固態聚合物電解質（SPEs）開發固態鋰金屬電池（LMBs）。相較於易燃的液態電解質，PVDF SPEs 具備不可燃特性，能有效降低熱失控風險。同時，固態 LMBs 仍保有高能量密度與商業化潛力。 儘管 PVDF 基 SPEs 展現出實現安全高效電池設計的前景，但其廣泛應用於高性能固態鋰離子電池（SSLIBs）仍面臨多項挑戰。主要缺陷包括室溫下離子電導率偏低（約 10⁻⁶ S cm⁻¹），原因在於聚合物的半結晶性及鋰鹽解離不足，導致鋰離子遷移遲緩。此外，界面相容性亦存隱憂，例如鋰金屬負極上的不可逆副反應，以及正極界面分解現象。要在工業層面推動 PVDF SPEs 的應用，仍需大幅改善其離子電導率與正、負極界面相容性。 本研究計劃旨在透過優化 PVDF 基 SPEs 的相態與溶劑化結構，以提升固態電池的能量密度與循環穩定性。於鋰金屬負極界面，將引入鋰鹽與添加劑以形成穩定的 Li/PVDF 界面；於正極側，則設計新型鋰鹽以構築穩定的正極–電解質界面，並提升其高電壓下的性能。同時，將探討界面演化機制以進一步優化 PVDF SPEs。此外，將藉由減薄電解質厚度來改善其機械性能。最終，研究將製備並評估基於 PVDF SPEs 的軟包型固態 LMBs，其循環性能與安全性能將為未來商業化提供可行性基礎。

11309025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309025.value: 酸性介質中二氧化碳高效電解製備乙烯

11309025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11309025.value: Dr HUNG, Sung-Fu Dr Wang, Ziyun

11309025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309025.value: Carbon dioxide electroreduction reaction (CO2RR) to valuable chemicals provides a promising pathway for intermittent renewable electricity storage. Among reported CO2RR products, ethylene is particularly desirable due to its largest market size and ever-growing demand. Nowadays, ethylene manufacture, a carbon- and energy-intensive process, is responsible for about 13% of the global petrochemical industry’s CO2 emission. Therefore, it is attractive to explore how to produce ethylene efficiently via CO2RR powered by renewables. Most current CO2RR studies have been conducted in alkaline/neutral media, leading to substantial CO2 loss and thus a high energy penalty for CO2 regeneration. CO2RR in acidic media (i.e. acidic CO2RR) is one promising solution to address the CO2 loss issue. However, the acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis system still suffers from challenges including low ethylene selectivity at industrial-level current density due to the kinetically-favored hydrogen evolution reaction in acidic media and high full-cell voltage. In this project, based on our prior research experience in CO2RR-related catalyst design and reaction engineering, to address the challenges aforesaid, we aim to develop an efficient acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis system through uniting catalyst design and system development. Our prior studies (Nature Catalysis, 2022, 5, 564) and preliminary results suggest that metal-doped Cu-based catalysts are promising for promoting ethylene selectivity in acidic CO2RR. Thus, firstly, we aim to develop metal-doped Cu-based catalysts for boosting ethylene selectivity at an industrial-relevant current density (above 100 mA cm-2), CO2 utilization efficiency, and stability simultaneously in the acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis using a flow cell electrolyzer. Secondly, we will establish the structure-property relations of metal-doped Cu-based catalysts towards CO2RR by integrating in situ/operando spectroscopic characterization techniques with theoretical calculations. Finally, based on the high-efficiency catalysts we will develop, we aim to develop an acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis system with low full-cell voltage. In our prior studies (Nature Sustainability, 2024, 7, 931), as a proof-of-concept, when acidic CO2RR-to-CO coupled with allyl alcohol oxidation reaction (AOR) to acrolein, full-cell voltage was lowered by 0.8 volts and we achieved a high acrolein selectivity of 85% at 100 mA cm-2. The encouraging results prompt us to pair acidic CO2-to-ethylene with AOR-to-acrolein to lower full-cell voltage and achieve a high-efficiency acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis system. Successful implementation of this proposal would provide strategies for further design of high-efficiency CO2-to-ethylene catalysts in acidic media and contribute to developing acidic CO2-to-ethylene electrolysis technologies for future potential practical applications and Hong Kong's target of achieving carbon neutrality before 2050.

11309425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309425.value: 二維過渡金屬硫族化物的電化學Li+嵌入和剝離用於相調控和高價值資源回收

11309425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309425.value: Reclaiming resources (freshwater, lithium, copper, etc.) from wastewater represents a promising solution to mitigate resource stress and achieve sustainable circular economy, particularly in regions like Hong Kong. Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), offer an intriguing platform for various environmental applications. Our group has developed an electrochemical Li+ intercalation and exfoliation method for the large-scale production of 2D materials. However, the detailed mechanisms upon Li+ intercalation for driving these phase transitions remain unclear. This project aims to address these scientific questions before applying 2D TMDs in environmental application. First, the phase evolution and detailed mechanisms will be explored through advanced in-situ and ex-situ characterization techniques. In-situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) will be used to track the formation of new phases in MoS2 and TaS2 during lithium intercalation, in real time and under operando conditions. Ex-situ High Angle Angular Dark Field-Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (HAADF-STEM) will be employed to directly observe lithium occupancy and the zigzag-chain atomic configurations in lithium-intercalated TMDs. Second, MoS2 and TaS2 nanosheets will be exfoliated from various intercalation levels of MoS2 (including MoS2, Li0.2, Li0.3MoS2, Li0.4MoS2, Li0.9MoS2, Li1.3MoS2, and Li1.4MoS2) and TaS2 (including TaS2, Li0.1TaS2, Li0.2TaS2, Li0.4TaS2, Li0.5TaS2, Li0.6TaS2, and LiTaS2). Ex-situ multimodal characterizations, including HAADF-STEM, Raman spectroscopy, XRD, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), will then be conducted to assess the phase, electronic structure, and morphology of the exfoliated TMDs nanosheets. By comparing this data with that of the lithium-intercalated TMDs, we aim to uncover the underlying mechanism of the exfoliation process and its influence on the final properties of the exfoliated TMDs. Third, electrodes for recovering high-value resources (e.g., freshwater, lithium, copper, etc.) will be fabricated using exfoliated MoS2 and TaS2 nanosheets with varying phases (2H, 1T, and 1T’) and different amounts of lithium intercalation. The state-of-the-art capacitive deionization (CDI) technique will be employed for resource recovery and enrichment. Subsequently, their CDI performances-such as gravimetric/volumetric adsorption capacity, rate, and recovery ratio-will be evaluated and optimized. Based on these results, we can summarize how the different phases and lithium intercalation levels influence the resource recovery and enrichment efficiency. The outcomes can provide us valuable insights for optimizing the phase and lithium intercalation levels of exfoliated TMD nanosheets, facilitating the development of TMDs-based electrodes for resource reclamation (such as freshwater, lithium, copper, etc.) from wastewater. 1. 發展原位/非原位多模態表徵技術，用於研究電化學嵌鋰製程中MoS2和TaS2的相變。我們計劃利用原位X射線衍射(XRD)技術評估TMDs晶體結構變化的綜合訊息，然後利用原位拉曼光譜技術來探測TMDs的振動模式，並透過能量變化來指示相變。我們也將採用原位液體池透射電子顯微鏡(TEM)技術，利用選區電子繞射(SAED)圖譜中晶格參數的變化來追蹤單一TMDs奈米薄片的相變。基於原位表徵數據，我們將總結不同TMDs在鋰嵌入過程中的嵌入行為差異、影響因素和相變路徑。旨在透過晶體結構、振動模式和晶格參數來探討不同鋰嵌入量下新出現的相，從而闡明TMDs在鋰嵌入過程中相變的內在成因。 2 對剝離的 MoS2 和 TaS2 進行原位多模態表徵，並與僅嵌入鋰的 TMDs 進行比較，以揭示剝離過程如何影響嵌入鋰的 TMDs。目的是優化剝離參數，以製備高品質的 TMDs 奈米片。我們的初步數據表明，對於 MoS2，2H 到 1T 的相變始於 x = 0.3，並在 x = 1.4 時完成；而對於 TaS2，1T 到 6R 和 1T 到 2H 的相變分別始於 x = 0.1 和 x = 0.2，1T 和 2H 的相變分別始於 x = 0.1 和 x = 0.2，1T 和 2H 的相變分別消失時相。這裡，x 定義為嵌入 1.0 mol MS2 中的 Li+ 摩爾數，標記為 LixMS2（M 代表 Mo 或 Ta）。我們計劃對一系列具有不同鋰嵌入量的剝離TMDs奈米片進行全面的非原位多模態表徵，以探測最終TMDs奈米片的相（2H、1T和1T′）、電導率、化學狀態和形貌。然後將這些物理性質與僅嵌入鋰的TMDs進行比較，並闡明剝離過程對最終剝離TMDs的影響。 3 為了開發具有最佳恢復性能的基於MoS2和TaS2的電極，我們將研究相、鋰嵌入量和剝離過程對電容去離子性能的影響。我們的初步數據表明，透過剝離 Li1.4MoS2 製備的 TMDs 電極表現出優異的重量法 CDI 容量。 TMDs 電極的恢復容量對 K+（22.0 mg g-1）最高，其次是 Na+（17.6 mg g-1）、Ca2+（15.1 mg g-1）和 Mg2+（12.6 mg g-1）。 1Tʹ-MoS2 電極的 CDI 速率從 13 mgNaCl g-1 增加，逐漸達到 17.6 mgNaCl g-1 的穩定容量。我們計劃進一步研究使用具有不同相（2H、1T 和 1T'）和不同鋰嵌入量的剝離 TMD 的恢復性能。我們的目標是確定這些因素（以及剝離和重新堆疊過程）如何影響 TMD 的形貌（包括橫向尺寸和厚度）、親水性、負電荷密度和電容去離子性能。最終，我們的目標是製造具有最佳資源回收性能的基於 TMD 的電極，包括最佳重量/體積吸附容量、速率和回收率。

11309525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309525.value: 開發用於活細胞染色質超分辨成像的自閃爍探針

11309525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309525.value: The spatial organization and compaction of chromatin are essential for gene regulation and cellular function, with abnormalities in chromatin structure closely associated with diseases such as cancer. Super-resolution imaging, particularly single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM), offers a powerful tool for visualizing chromatin architecture at nanometer resolution. However, current DNA probes for SMLM face challenges such as poor cell permeability, high laser power requirements, and dependence on complex photoswitching buffers, limiting their application in live-cell imaging. To overcome these limitations, we aim to develop novel self-blinking probes optimized for chromatin imaging in live cells. These probes will provide invaluable insights into the relationship between chromatin structure and disease, advancing our understanding of chromatin biology and disease mechanisms. In the initial phase, we will synthesize a series of rhodamine derivatives and conduct structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies to identify fluorophores with optimal properties for SMLM imaging. Rhodamines, which undergo reversible intramolecular spirocyclization, can switch between a non-fluorescent lactone (closed) form and a fluorescent zwitterion (open) form. This reversible transition enables potential self-blinking behavior, eliminating the need for external photoswitching buffers. Through detailed SAR analysis, we aim to understand how structural modifications influence self-blinking performance, guiding the selection of the most suitable fluorophores for SMLM probes. Building on these findings, we will integrate the optimized fluorophores into DNA probes for super-resolution imaging of chromatin in live cells. These probes will enable high-resolution chromatin imaging without relying on photoswitching buffers. Additionally, time-lapse SMLM imaging will be employed to study dynamic chromatin changes in response to various epigenetic inhibitors, offering insights into drug-induced alterations of chromatin structure. In the final phase of the project, we will develop dual-function probes capable of both super-resolution imaging and proteomic profiling. These probes will utilize proximity photolabeling techniques to capture chromatin-associated proteins, enabling comparative analyses between normal and cancer cells. This approach will uncover how chromatin architecture and its associated protein networks are restructured during tumorigenesis. The dual-function probes will also facilitate biomarker discovery and contribute to the development of chromatin-targeted therapeutic strategies for cancer treatment. Our research team has extensive expertise in fluorescent probe design, chemical proteomics, and super-resolution imaging, and we are confident that this project will advance the fields of bioimaging and chromatin research. 染色質的空間組織與壓縮對於基因調控和細胞功能至關重要，而染色質結構的異常與包括癌症在內的多種疾病密切相關。超分辨成像，尤其是單分子定位顯微術，為以奈米級分辨率可視化染色質結構提供了有力工具。然而，現有用於單分子定位顯微術的脫氧核糖核酸探針仍面臨細胞通透性差、所需激光功率高以及依賴複雜光開關緩衝液等挑戰，限制了其在活細胞成像中的應用。為克服這些限制，我們擬開發用於活細胞染色質成像的新型自發閃爍探針。這些探針將為理解染色質結構與疾病之間的關係提供寶貴見解，推動對染色質生物學與疾病機制的認識。 在項目第一階段，我們將合成一系列羅丹明衍生物並開展構效關係研究，以篩選出最適用於單分子定位顯微術成像的螢光團。羅丹明可發生可逆的分子內螺旋化，在非螢光的內酯（閉合）形式與螢光的兩性離子（開放）形式之間切換。這一可逆轉變賦予其潛在的自發閃爍特性，從而無需外加光開關緩衝液。通過系統的構效關係分析，我們將闡明結構修飾如何影響自發閃爍性能，並據此確定最合適的螢光團。 在此基礎上，我們將把優化後的螢光團整合進脫氧核糖核酸探針，用於活細胞中染色質的超分辨成像，從而在不依賴光開關緩衝液的條件下實現高分辨率觀測。此外，我們將開展時間推移單分子定位顯微成像，研究染色質在各類表觀遺傳抑制劑處理下的動態變化，揭示藥物誘導的染色質結構改變。 在項目最後階段，我們將開發兼具超分辨成像與蛋白質組學分析功能的雙功能探針。該類探針將利用近鄰光標記技術捕獲染色質相關蛋白，進而在正常細胞與癌細胞間開展比較分析，揭示腫瘤發生過程中染色質結構及其相關蛋白網絡的重塑。該策略還有助於生物標誌物的發現，並促進面向染色質的癌症治療策略的開發。 我們的研究團隊在螢光探針設計、化學蛋白質組學與超分辨成像方面具備豐富經驗。我們有信心推動本項目取得實質進展，進一步促進生物成像與染色質研究領域的發展。

11309725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309725.value: 利用刺激響應型自組裝肽實現過渡金屬配合物的受控活化，用於癌症靶向成像與治療

11309725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309725.value: The project aims to leverage stimuli-responsive self-assembling peptides to control the localization and activation of transition metal-based photosensitizers for cancer diagnosis and therapy. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a promising modality for cancer treatment due to its high spatiotemporal precision and minimal invasiveness. More than ten organic-based photosensitizers have been clinically approved for treating various types of cancer. However, these photosensitizers, primarily based on tetrapyrrolic structures such as porphyrins, face limitations such as complex synthesis and purification, poor water solubility, and low photostability, necessitating the development of more effective alternatives. Photofunctional transition metal complexes offer several advantages over conventional organic fluorophores and photosensitizers in bioimaging and PDT applications, including long emission lifetimes, large Stokes’ shifts, high reactive oxygen species (ROS) photosensitization efficiencies, and high photostability. However, most of the complexes developed thus far display low cancer selectivity and inadequate tumor accumulation and retention in vivo, limiting their accuracy and efficacy in cancer diagnosis and therapy. Molecular self-assembly of small molecules provides a powerful approach to fabricate higher-order structures with diverse functional properties. Peptides, in particular, are of great interest due to their high synthetic accessibility, structural diversity, biocompatibility, and biodegradability. Remarkably, the peptide self-assembly process can be manipulated to respond to various tumor-associated stimuli, offering exciting opportunities for biological and biomedical applications such as cancer imaging and therapy, drug delivery, and tissue engineering. We believe that combining the merits of photofunctional transition metal complexes and stimuli-responsive self-assembling peptides will result in a new generation of theranostic agents for precise tumor imaging and PDT. In this project, we will develop photofunctional transition metal–peptide conjugates that undergo supramolecular self-assembly in response to specific tumor-associated stimuli, selectively forming large and stable nanostructures inside tumor cells. This will substantially enhance the accumulation and retention of the appended metal complexes at the tumor site, enabling selective induction of the emission and ROS-photosensitization properties of the complexes in tumor cells for detection and treatment. We are confident that the development of transition metal–peptide conjugates with stimuli-responsive self-assembly behavior will create new opportunities for cancer diagnosis and treatment. The unique properties of photofunctional transition metal complexes and self-assembling peptides are crucial for these innovative theranostic applications. The results obtained from this project will not only lead to the development of more effective theranostic agents, but also inspire new strategies to improve the precision and accuracy of cancer diagnosis and therapy. 本計畫旨在利用刺激響應性自組裝胜肽，控制基於過渡金屬的光敏劑之定位與活化，用於癌症的診斷與治療。光動力治療（PDT）因其高時空精準度與低侵襲性，已成為極具前景的癌症治療方式。迄今已有逾十種有機基光敏劑獲臨床核准用於多種癌症的治療。然而，這些光敏劑多以卟啉等四吡咯結構為基礎，存在合成與純化複雜、水溶性差及光穩定性低等限制，極需開發更有效的替代方案。具光功能的過渡金屬錯合物在生物成像與PDT應用上，較之傳統有機螢光分子與光敏劑具多項優勢，包括長發光壽命、較大的史托克斯位移、產生活性氧（ROS）的高光敏化效率，以及優異的光穩定性。然而，迄今多數此類錯合物對癌細胞的選擇性不足，且在體內於腫瘤的累積與滯留不佳，限制了其在癌症診斷與治療中的準確性與療效。小分子的分子自組裝提供了強而有力的策略，可構築具多樣功能特性的高階結構。其中特別是胜肽，因其易於合成、結構多樣、生物相容性佳且具生物可降解性而備受關注。更重要的是，胜肽的自組裝過程可被調控以響應各種腫瘤相關刺激，為癌症成像與治療、藥物遞送與組織工程等生物與生醫應用帶來嶄新機會。我們相信，結合具光功能之過渡金屬錯合物與刺激響應性自組裝胜肽的優勢，將催生新一代用於精準腫瘤成像與光動力治療的診療一體化劑。在本計畫中，我們將開發具光功能之過渡金屬–胜肽偶聯物，能在特定腫瘤相關刺激下發生超分子自組裝，並於腫瘤細胞內選擇性形成大型且穩定的奈米結構。此舉將大幅提升所連接之金屬錯合物在腫瘤部位的累積與滯留，使得可在腫瘤細胞內選擇性地誘發該等錯合物的發光與ROS光敏化特性，用於檢測與治療。我們有信心，具刺激響應性自組裝行為的過渡金屬–胜肽偶聯物之開發，將為癌症診斷與治療開創新契機。具光功能之過渡金屬錯合物與自組裝胜肽的獨特性質，對這些創新診療一體化應用至關重要。本計畫所得成果，不僅將促成更有效之診療一體化劑的開發，亦將啟發提升癌症診斷與治療之精準度與準確性的全新策略。

11309925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309925.value: 全局图像分割的数学形式化

11309925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309925.value: Mankind daily produces billions of digital images in all areas of society, science, and technology. Their automatic analysis is the only way to gather usable information from them. Image segmentation algorithms that divide an image into meaningful regions are among the most needed and most difficult algorithms. Until recently, image segmentation was performed on each image independently, but the past three years have seen the emergence of global image processing algorithms. These fully empirical global segmentation algorithms such as SAM (Segment Anything Model) have been trained on millions of images. They deliver surprisingly good results but, being trained on "natural" images, their good results and their failures are not explainable. Indeed, contrary to a synthetic dataset, a natural learning dataset has no mathematical and algorithmic specification. In consequence, the properties of the learning dataset cannot be tuned or amended. Another structural difficulty of global segmentation algorithms is that they deliver overlapping local masks associated to prompts, and therefore lack the structured results of previous handcrafted segmentation algorithms, that deliver image partitions. We plan to resolve the three above mentioned major gaps in current global image segmentation. The first gap is that, contrary to single-image segmentation where a full and rich mathematical theory is available, global image segmentation still lacks a general variational theory, that might guide algorithms and a discussion of formal properties of solutions such as existence or regularity. The second above mentioned structural gap is that most current global segmentation algorithms only output masks, highlighting objects one by one through individual prompts. Thus, they deliver a much less structured output than single-image segmentation algorithms, which provide image partitions and even segmentation trees. The third mentioned gap is the lack of explainablity, which can only be solved by using synthetically controlled image datasets. This proposal puts forth formulas resolving the first gap by proposing variational models for global segmentation. It will design energy minimization methods to resolve the second gap and to convert systems of masks into partitions. It will address the last gap by generating a massive abstract images dataset, learning from it an abstract global segmentation algorithm, and comparing its performance to the performance of global empirical segmentation algorithms. This is an ambitious program with moderate cost, thanks to a strong international collaboration that will also help developing medical and biological images applications. A local industrial collaboration will help make this mathematical research immediately useful. 最需要也是最困难的算法之一。直到最近，图像分割都是在每幅图像上独立进行的，但在过去三年里，出现了全局图像处理算法。 这些完全经验性的全局分割算法，如 SAM（Segment Anything Model），已在数百万张图像上进行过训练。这些算法的结果出人意料地好，但由于是在 “自然 ”图像上进行训练，它们的好结果和失败都是无法解释的。事实上，与合成数据集不同，自然学习数据集没有数学和算法规范。因此，学习数据集的属性无法调整或修正。全局分割算法的另一个结构性难题是，它们提供与提示相关的重叠局部遮罩，因此缺乏以往手工分割算法的结构性结果，即提供图像分区。 我们计划解决目前全局图像分割中存在的上述三个主要缺陷。第一个差距是，与已有完整丰富数学理论的单图像分割不同，全局图像分割仍然缺乏一般的变分理论，而这种理论可以指导算法，并讨论解的形式属性，如存在性或正则性。上述第二个结构性缺陷是，目前大多数全局分割算法只输出掩码，通过个别提示逐个突出对象。因此，与提供图像分区甚至分割树的单图像分割算法相比，它们的输出结构性要差得多。第三个差距是缺乏可解释性，这只能通过使用合成控制图像数据集来解决。 本提案通过提出全局分割的变分模型，提出了解决第一个差距的公式。它将设计能量最小化方法来解决第二个差距，并将遮罩系统转换为分区。它将通过生成海量抽象图像数据集，从中学习抽象全局分割算法，并将其性能与全局经验分割算法的性能进行比较，从而解决最后一个差距。这是一个雄心勃勃的计划，成本适中，得益于强大的国际合作，这也将有助于开发医疗和生物图像应用。本地工业合作将有助于使这项数学研究立即发挥作用。

11310125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11310125.value: 中國人為粗顆粒懸浮粒子：對其排放、氣候和大氣化學影響的研究

11310125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11310125.value: While the majority of research has focused on fine particulate matter (PM2.5), it has been observed that coarse PM (particulate matter with a diameter between 2.5 and 10µm) also presents a severe environmental challenge in China. Coarse PM has been found to have adverse health impacts comparable to those of PM2.5, and it can influence the formation of other pollutants by modifying atmospheric chemistry. Furthermore, coarse PM can influence the climate by changing earth’s radiation balance and cloud properties. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s sixth assessment report (IPCC AR6) underscores that current climate assessments may overlook a significant portion of climate effect from coarse PM. Historically, the primary focus of coarse PM research has been on natural desert dust and marine sea salt aerosol. However, recent observations suggest that anthropogenic sources, such as road dust, agricultural activities, and combustion processes, are the predominant components of coarse PM in most regions of China. Due to the lack of accurate national emission inventory, current models used for air quality and climate applications either do not consider anthropogenic coarse PM or substantially underestimate its burden. It thus appears essential to estimate the emissions of anthropogenic coarse PM and understand its role in atmospheric chemistry and the climate system. In this project, we aim to quantify the emissions and impacts of anthropogenic coarse particles in China. This will be achieved by developing an observational-constrained emission inventory using a Bayesian inverse modeling framework. This emission estimation will be incorporated into a chemical transport model and a radiative transfer model. These models will simulate the spatio-temporal variations of anthropogenic coarse PM, estimate its direct climate effect due to aerosol-radiation interaction, indirect climate effect via changing cloud albedo, and explore its impacts on atmospheric chemistry and other pollutants. The findings from this study will improve current understanding of coarse aerosols, enabling more precise air quality and climate assessments, and informing the development of strategies to address air pollution and climate change. It will also provide methodology framework to study anthropogenic coarse PM at other locations around the world. The gridded data of emission inventory created in this project can be used for various applications and input for other models. 懸浮粒子（PM）一直以來都是影響中國空氣質素的重要污染物。現有研究多聚焦於細懸浮粒子（PM2.5），然實證表明直徑介乎2.5至10微米之粗顆粒懸浮粒子同樣構成嚴峻環境挑戰。此類污染物對健康的危害程度與PM2.5相當，且能透過改變大氣化學反應影響其他污染物生成，更可經由擾動地球輻射平衡及雲層特性影響氣候變化。政府間氣候變化專門委員會（IPCC）第六次評估報告（AR6）明確指出，現行氣候評估模型或嚴重低估粗顆粒懸浮粒子對氣候系統的實質影響。 過往粗顆粒懸浮粒子研究主要針對自然源粗顆粒物（如沙漠塵埃與海洋氣溶膠），然而最新觀測證實中國多數區域的粗顆粒物主要源自人為排放，涵蓋道路揚塵、農業活動及工業燃燒過程。因缺乏精準全國排放清單，現行空氣質素與氣候模型往往忽略人為源或嚴重低估其環境負荷。故系統化估算人為粗顆粒懸浮粒子排放量，並釐清其在大氣化學與氣候系統中的作用機制，為當前迫切需求。 本研究旨在量化中國人為粗顆粒懸浮粒子的排放量與多維環境效應，通過建立觀測數據約束的貝葉斯反演排放清單，整合化學傳輸模型與輻射傳輸模型，模擬污染物時空分佈特徵。研究將量化其直接氣候效應（氣溶膠-輻射相互作用）與間接效應（雲反照率改變），同時解析對大氣化學過程及伴生污染物的影響機制。成果不僅能釐清粗顆粒物環境行為、提升氣候模型預測精度，更可為空氣污染治理與氣候政策制訂提供科學基準；所建構的模擬方法框架，配合高解析度網格化排放數據集，將支持多領域模型應用與環境評估。

11310925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11310925.value: 理解銀河系中心過量伽馬射線

11310925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11310925.value: This proposal aims to understand the Galactic center gamma-ray excess (GCE), a robust signal of gamma-ray photons at GeV energies emanating from the center of our galaxy, observed by the Fermi Large Area Telescope over the past fifteen years. The GCE could result from dark matter annihilation or an unresolved population of faint millisecond pulsars (MSPs), each explanation carrying significant implications for astrophysics or particle physics. While the existence of dark matter is well-established, evidence of its interaction with ordinary matter beyond gravity remains elusive. If the GCE originates from dark matter, it would provide the first evidence of such interaction. Alternatively, if MSPs are responsible, it would offer insights into their luminosity functions and distribution in the Galactic center, which are difficult to detect directly. Despite recent progress in GCE research, key characteristics such as its small-scale power and overall angular distribution still need to be addressed. This project aims to thoroughly explore these properties by combining new signal modeling with multiple data analysis methods. On the signal modeling side, we will investigate different dark matter models and MSPs with different luminosity functions by connecting Fermi data with other astrophysical phenomena or probes. These include studying dark matter distributions in dwarf galaxies, interactions between dark matter and the stellar bar and disk, and photon emissions from MSPs in lower energies that future gamma-ray telescopes can observe. On the data analysis side, we will apply template fitting methods and wavelet-based point source detection. Our previous works have laid the foundation by developing analysis pipelines and galactic diffuse background models. One of our main goals is to improve the reliability of the data analysis methods by addressing challenges such as the negative background component in template fitting and sensitivity limits in point source detection. We will systematically test different background models, improve the analysis algorithms, and explore new techniques, such as discrete wavelets. The outcomes will not only deepen our understanding of the GCE by synthesizing multiple observational data and advanced data analysis methods but also offer new insights into the nature of dark matter or the properties of the new MSP population. The refined data analysis techniques can be applied to other types of astrophysical data. Moreover, this project has the potential to bring together researchers in astronomy and particle physics across Hong Kong and beyond, potentially transforming Hong Kong into a global hub for astrophysics research. 本項目旨在研究銀河系中心過量伽馬射線（GCE），即過去十五年間由費米太空望遠鏡在銀河系中心區域持續探測到的GeV能段異常伽馬射線信號。該信號可能源於暗物質粒子的湮滅，或來自大量未被分辨的微弱毫秒脈衝星（MSP）。無論其成因如何，GCE的物理起源對天體物理學和粒子物理學均具有重大意義。若該輻射由暗物質湮滅產生，它將提供暗物質與普通物質之間除引力外發生相互作用的首個觀測證據；若源自毫秒脈衝星群體，則可透過其輻射特徵反推該類天體在銀心區域的空間分佈與光度函數，這些性質難以透過直接觀測獲取。儘管已有諸多研究，GCE在小尺度上的功率譜分佈和整體角分佈等關鍵特徵仍存在不確定性。本項目將整合新型信號建模與多元數據分析策略，系統探究GCE的特性。在建模方面，我們將結合費米數據與其他天體物理數據（如矮星系的暗物質分佈、銀河系棒與盤的結構特性，以及毫秒脈衝星在更低能段的輻射行為），對比多種暗物質模型及毫秒脈衝星群體光度函數。在數據分析方面，我們將採用模板擬合與小波點源檢測方法。目前已初步搭建分析流程並構造銀河彌散輻射背景模型。項目的重點之一是提升GCE特性分析的穩健性，著力解決模板擬閤中背景模板出現負值、點源檢測靈敏度受限等關鍵技術難點。我們將系統評估不同背景模型的影響，優化現有算法，並嘗試引入離散小波變換等新分析方法。預期成果將在整合多種觀測數據與分析手段的基礎上，深化對 GCE 的理解，並為研究暗物質本質或銀心 MSP 群體的性質提供新線索。所發展的數據分析方法亦可推廣至其他天體物理數據分析。此外，本項目將促進香港學術群體在天文學與粒子物理交叉領域的合作，助力香港建設成為國際天體物理研究的重要基地。

11312025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312025.value: 基於中子散射技術對生物系統中蛋白質動力學及相關量子效應的研究

11312025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312025.value: The research objective of this proposal is to investigate quantum effects in biological systems by studying the relationship between the dynamics and enzymatic activities at the molecular level on multiple timescales experimentally and computationally. Neutron scattering, specifically quasi-elastic and inelastic neutron scattering, has exceptional power for studying the dynamics of proteins in real-time at the molecular level, providing a possible way to study the quantum effects in biological systems. The main advantage of neutron scattering is that neutrons are especially sensitive to hydrogen atoms abundant in biomolecules. Moreover, hydrogen and deuterium isotopes have completely different neutron scattering cross-sections. The experimental results will be interpreted and extended through computational modeling and molecular dynamics simulations. The ultimate goal of the research is to obtain a complete picture that quantitatively describes the relationship between the protein dynamics/structures and biological activities and to develop a further understanding of quantum tunneling in enzymatic catalysis. In the proposed research, complementary neutron scattering techniques will be employed to study protein dynamics and corresponding structural changes on different timescales at the molecular level: (1) quasi-elastic neutron scattering (QENS) will be used in studying the mid-time dynamics in ps to ns timescale, which is particularly relevant to biological activity; (2) neutron spin echo (NSE) technique will be used in investigating the protein domain motion in the long-time range from s to ms; (3) inelastic neutron scattering (INS) will be used to study the short-time dynamics, such as phonon-like motions in proteins; (4) small angle neutron scattering (SANS) will be used in monitoring and analyzing the structural change of the enzymes in situ during the study of the dynamics. In the second part of the project, we propose to perform computational modeling and simulations to interpret and give feedback on the scattering data. Specifically, this quantitative approach aims to understand our experimental and simulation results from the scenario of protein energy landscape (EL), one of the most accepted concepts with broad applications in studying protein dynamics and protein folding/unfolding processes. 本項目擬通過實驗和計算手段，從多個時間尺度上研究生物系統中的量子效應，旨在探究分子層面的動力學變化與酶活性之間的關係。中子散射，特別是準彈性中子散射和非彈性中子散射，在實時研究蛋白質在分子層面的動力學方面具有非凡的效力，為研究生物系統中的量子效應提供了可行的實驗途徑。中子散射的主要優勢在於，中子對生物分子中豐富的氫原子特別敏感。此外，氫和它的同位素氘具有完全不同的中子散射截面。實驗結果將通過計算建模和分子動力學模擬進行解釋和擴展。研究的最終目標是獲得一個能夠定量描述蛋白質動力學/結構與生物活性之間關係的完整圖景，並進一步理解酶催化過程中的量子隧穿現象。 在本項目中，將採用多種相互補充的中子散射技術來研究蛋白質在不同時間尺度上的動力學變化及其相應的結構變化：（1）準彈性中子散射（QENS）將用於研究皮秒至納秒時間範圍內的中間時間尺度，這與生物活性密切相關；（2）中子自旋迴波（NSE）技術將用於研究從微秒到納秒範圍內的蛋白質結構域運動；（3）非彈性中子散射（INS）將用於研究極短時間動力學，例如蛋白質中的聲子類似運動；（4）小角度中子散射（SANS）將用於在研究動力學過程中實時監測和分析酶的結構變化。在項目的第二部分，我們將結合計算建模和模擬解釋和反饋散射數據。具體而言，這種定量方法旨在從蛋白質能量景觀（EL）這一概念的視角來理解我們的實驗和模擬結果。蛋白質能量景觀這一概念已被廣泛接受，並在研究蛋白質動態行為以及蛋白質摺疊/解摺疊過程方面有著廣泛應用。

11312325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312325.value: 高斯自由場和隨機遊走圈族的高度集

11312325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312325.value: The Gaussian free field is an ubiquitous object in probability theory and mathematical physics. It plays a central role in many different situations, and we aim to study further its geometric properties. This process is a random two-dimensional surface, arising spontaneously from the stochastic behavior of various systems, to describe their random fluctuations. It turns out to be extremely rough, which makes its geometric features quite challenging to study. Bernoulli percolation is a classical model for random media, which amounts to open or close the vertices of a lattice in an independent fashion. For some parameter p, each vertex is open with probability p, and it is closed with probability 1-p. As one lets the parameter vary, a phase transition can be observed, i.e. a drastic change of behavior, at some critical threshold pc: for ppc, a giant (infinite) connected component of open vertices appears. Percolation theory is widely used in applications, to understand spatial correlations in random systems. We are interested in the percolative properties of two-sided level sets of the Gaussian free field, where the field remains not too large nor too small, that is, between two values -L and L. For this purpose, we want to bring techniques and ideas from percolation theory, and combine them with other tools developed recently for the random walk loop soup. This latter planar process is intimately related to the Gaussian free field, and its Poisson structure, together with elementary properties of random walks, allows for powerful recombination arguments on loops. In particular, in the subcritical random walk loop soup, we plan to study the sharpness of the transition as one lets the threshold L increase, in analogy to Bernoulli percolation. Next we want to study the behavior of the loop soup for supercritical intensities. Finally, we aim to improve our understanding of the critical case, which is the one directly linked to the Gaussian free field, and where geometric considerations seem to be the most subtle. 高斯自由場在概率論和數學物理中隨處可見，並在許多情形中都扮演關鍵角色。我們致力於進一步研究它的幾何性質。它是二維平面上的一個隨機過程，自然產生於各種系統的隨機行為，形容了這些系統中的隨機擾動。它非常粗糙，所以對它幾何性質的研究很有挑戰性。 「伯努利滲流」是隨機媒介的一個經典模型：我們獨立地打開或閉合一個格點上的點或邊。對一個參數p，每個點有概率p為開，概率1-p為閉。當我們改變這個參數，可以觀察到相變，即在某個臨界點pc顯著的行為變化：當ppc，一個巨大（無限）的開格點聯通分支出現了。滲流理論被廣泛應用於隨機系統中的空間關聯性的研究。 我們感興趣的是高斯自由場中「雙向高度集」的滲流性質，這是指場不是很高或很低的那些點，也就是在-L和L之間的點。為此，我們將運用滲流理論中的技術和想法，並和我們最近對隨機遊走圈族發展出的工具相結合。後者是一個二維過程，和高斯自由場密切相關。它的泊松結構和隨機遊走的基本性質，使得我們得到了拆解重連隨機遊走圈的強有力工具。 特別地，對亞臨界隨機遊走圈族，我們計劃研究增加L值時產生的急劇相變，和伯努利滲流類似。接下來，我們準備研究超臨界隨機遊走圈族的行為。最後，我們的目標是改進我們對臨界隨機遊走圈族的理解——這是和高斯自由場直接相關的情形，也是幾何性質最微妙的情形。

11312425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312425.value: 超級連續譜中束縛態的理論和計算

11312425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312425.value: In the last a few years, the so-called super-bound states in the continuum (super-BICs) have attracted significant research interest in the photonics community. A BIC is a special eigenmode of a wave system with the eigenvalue in the continuous spectrum. Around the wavevector of a BIC, there are resonant modes with a complex frequency and satisfying outgoing radiation conditions. Near a super-BIC, the resonant modes have an ultrahigh quality factor which causes extraordinary resonant effects and has important applications in lasing, sensing, nonlinear optics, etc. Existing examples of super-BICs are mostly found by tuning parameters of the structure. We propose to develop a comprehensive theory for super-BICs governed by the Maxwell's equations. The proposed theory will include a mathematical characterization that clarifies the concept of super-BICs and is useful for finding super-BICs numerically. The theory will also reveal how a super-BIC may be preserved under structural perturbations and may turn to regular BICs through different types of bifurcations. Our study on super-BICs will enhance understanding on resonant wave phenomena and help realizing their applications in photonics and other wave systems. 在過去幾年中，所謂的超級連續譜中的束縛態 (super-BIC) 引起了光子學界的重大研究興趣。BIC 是波系統中的一種特殊的特徵模，其特徵值嵌入在連續譜中。靠近一個BIC ，存在滿足向外輻射條件的具有複頻率的共振模。在超級 BIC 附近，共振模具有超高的品質因數，會造成極大的共振效應，並在鐳射、感測、非線性光學等領域具有重要的應用。現有的超級 BIC 的例子大多是透過調整結構的參數而找到的。我們將為超級 BIC 發展一套全面的理論，包括闡明超級 BIC 概念的數學條件，快速求解超級 BIC 的計算方法，超級 BIC 在結構擾動下得以保留的條件，以及超級 BIC 轉換為一般 BIC 的過程。我們對超級 BIC 的研究將可增進對波動現象的理解，並有助於實現其在光子及其他波系統中的應用。

11312825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312825.value: 菱方堆垛多層石墨烯中的分數量子反常霍爾效應

11312825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312825.value: The integer and fractional quantum Hall effects, discovered in the early 1980s, revolutionized our understanding of quantum matter. The integer effect’s remarkably precise quantization of Hall resistance has contributed to the 2019 redefinition of the kilogram in the SI system. In fractional quantum Hall systems, the emergence of exotic quasiparticles called anyons has opened promising pathways for realizing fault-tolerant topological quantum computation. However, the strong magnetic fields required for the quantum Hall effects makes them impractical for many applications. Recently, scientists have discovered a remarkable phenomenon called the fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) effect that can occur without magnetic fields in certain materials. This discovery opens new possibilities for quantum computing and electronic devices. This research project focuses on understanding the FQAH effect in a particular family of materials called rhombohedral n-layer graphene (RnG) --- essentially, specially stacked sheets of carbon atoms encapsulated between two hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) sheets. Recent experiments have shown that these materials can exhibit the FQAH effect, but the theoretical understanding of why and how this happens remains incomplete. This gap between experimental observations and theoretical understanding presents a crucial challenge that this project aims to address. The research is organized into two different parts. The first part investigates how the FQAH effect works in RnG when electrons in the material experience a weak moiré potential from hBN. This includes developing new mathematical tools to better describe the system, exploring how multiple electronic energy levels interact, and understanding why this effect sometimes disappears at very low temperatures. The second part examines the opposite limit, i.e., what happens when electrons in the material experience a strong moiré potential from the encapsulating hBN. Recent experiments have shown that, in these cases, a weak magnetic field is needed to stabilize the FQAH effect, which raises important questions about the fundamental nature of the effect in these materials. This proposal aims to develop new theoretical tools to understand the role of the magnetic field in the FQAH effect. This project will employ a combination of analytical and numerical methods, including advanced computer simulations and mathematical modeling. The research will benefit from collaborations with leading experts in theoretical calculations and numerical studies. By bridging the gap between theory and experiment, this project aims to advance our understanding of quantum materials and potentially contribute to the development of new quantum technologies that can operate without strong magnetic fields. 整數與分數量子霍爾效應於 1980 年代初期被發現，徹底革新了我們對量子物質的理解。整數效應中霍爾電阻的驚人精確量子化，促成了 2019 年國際單位制（SI）中公斤的重新定義。在分數量子霍爾系統中，奇異的任意子（anyons）準粒子的出現，為實現具備容錯能力的拓撲量子計算開啟了新的可能性。然而，量子霍爾效應所需的強磁場使其在許多應用上並不實際。近年來，科學家發現了一種名為分數量子反常霍爾效應（FQAH）的非凡現象，它能在某些材料中於無磁場的情況下出現。這一發現為量子計算與電子器件的發展開闢了新的前景。 本研究計畫聚焦於理解 FQAH 效應在一類名為菱方堆垛 n 層石墨烯（RnG）的材料中的實現機制——這些材料本質上是以一種特定方式堆疊的碳原子薄層，並被兩層氮化硼（hBN）所包覆。近期實驗已顯示這些材料能展現 FQAH 效應，但其背後的理論理解仍不完整。實驗觀測與理論理解之間的落差，正是本計畫所要解決的關鍵挑戰。 研究將分為兩個部分。第一部分探討當 RnG 中的電子受到來自 hBN 的弱莫爾勢時，FQAH 效應的作用機制。這包含發展新的數學工具以更好地描述系統、探索多個電子能階的交互作用，以及理解為何此效應在極低溫下有時會消失。第二部分則探討相反的情況，即當電子受到來自包覆 hBN 的強莫爾勢時會發生什麼。近期實驗指出，在這些情況下需要施加微弱的磁場才能穩定 FQAH 效應，這引發了關於該效應在此類材料中基本本質的重要問題。本計畫旨在發展新的理論工具，以理解磁場在 FQAH 效應中的角色。 本計畫將結合解析與數值方法，包括先進的電腦模擬與數學建模，並與理論計算與數值研究領域的頂尖專家合作。透過縮短理論與實驗之間的差距，本研究期望推進我們對量子材料的理解，並有望促成能在無強磁場下運作的新型量子科技之發展。

11313025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11313025.value: 帶耗散可壓縮歐拉方程式的高維度稀疏波面問題

11313025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11313025.value: In this project, the PI proposes to investigate the problems on the long time existence and large time behavior of solutions to the rarefaction fronts problem for the compressible Euler equations with the frictional damping (as a lower order dissipation) in two spatial dimensions with the discontinuous initial datum which is a small irrotational perturbation of a planar rarefaction wave away from the vacuum state, by identifying the the rarefaction wave region foliated by the characteristic surfaces. The geometric approach for hyperbolic problems pioneered by Christodoulou and Klainerman in the study of the nonlinear stability of Minkowski spacetime for vacuum Einstein equations, and further developed by Christodoulou and Christodoulou-Miao on shock formation, and by Luo-Yu recently in the study of local-in-time stability of multi-D rarefaction waves for compressible Euler equations will be adopted and developed in this project to investigate the problems proposed to study in this project, to obtain long time higher order nonlinear energy estimates which are closely related to the estimates for the inverse density of the foliation by characteristic surfaces (rarefaction fronts) and the mean curvature of rarefaction fronts. Understanding the evolution of the geometry of characteristic surfaces (rarefaction fronts) will be essential. The investigation of the dissipation of damping and the expanding nature of the rarefaction wave for the long time stability will be crucial. The project also contributes to the development of analytic and geometric tools to understand the evolution of the geometry of characteristic surfaces for multi-dimensional hyperbolic balance laws, with the discontinuous initial data. It should be noted that the PI, joint with his collaborators, has adopted and developed the geometric approach introduced by Christodoulou & Lindblad in the study of the free boundary problem for the incompressible Euler equations to some free boundary problems of fluids and MHD equations ([17, 30, 31]) in which the estimates of bounds for some geometric quantities of the free surface are obtained. One may expect these research experiences will provide some insights into developing the geometric approach for the investigation of the problems proposed to study in this project. Moreover, the PI's involvement ([15, 18, 26, 27])in the study of large-time behavior of piecewise smooth solutions to some hyperbolic systems with dissipations in one spatial dimension with discontinuous initial data will be helpful to this project. 本项目拟研究带摩擦阻尼（作为低阶耗散项）的二维可压缩欧拉方程在初始数据为远离真空态的平面稀疏波的无旋间断小扰动时，其稀疏面问题的解长时间存在性与大时间行为。研究将通过识别由特征曲面（稀疏波面）组成的稀疏波区域，采用并发展Christodoulou-Klainerman在研究真空爱因斯坦方程的闵可夫斯基时空非线性稳定性时开创的双曲问题几何方法——该方法后续被Christodoulou、Christodoulou-Miao应用于激波形成研究，并被Luo-Yu近期用于可压缩欧拉方程多维稀疏波的局部时间稳定性分析。本项目将借助该方法获取与特征曲面叶化逆密度及稀疏波面平均曲率估计密切相关的高阶非线性能量估计，理解特征曲面（稀疏波面）几何结构的演化过程具有核心意义，而阻尼耗散效应与稀疏波膨胀特性对长时间稳定性的影响将是关键研究内容。 该项目还将推动发展分析与几何工具，以理解具有间断初始数据的高维双曲平衡律方程特征曲面几何结构的演化。值得注意的是，项目负责人与合作者曾将Christodoulou-Lindblad研究不可压欧拉方程自由边界问题时提出的几何方法拓展应用于流体与磁流体力学方程自由边界问题研究（文献[17,30,31]），获得了自由曲面若干几何量的有界性估计。这些研究经验有望为发展本项目所涉问题的几何方法提供启示。此外，项目负责人参与的一维空间中具耗散项双曲系统间断初始数据分段光滑解大时间行为研究（文献[15,18,26,27]）也将对本项目产生助益。

11313125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11313125.value: 分子陷阱門機制驅動的選擇性氣體進入與吸附：用於通道型多孔晶體固體的氣體分離

11313125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11313125.value: The gas separation industry represents a significant portion of global energy consumption (10-15%). This project aims to develop a new class of adsorbents – channel-type molecular trapdoor adsorbents – that offer exceptional efficiency in molecular separation. This innovative technology has the potential to greatly reduce costs in various gas separation processes, including fuel gas purification, carbon dioxide capture, air separation, and paraffin/olefin separation. Conventional molecular sieving is highly selective for gas separation but struggles to differentiate between small molecules of similar sizes. Fortunately, PI Shang’s discovery of the “molecular trapdoor” effect, a non-size-based sieving mechanism, offers a solution. Molecular trapdoor adsorbents selectively allow target molecules to enter by regulating their interactions with the materials’ pore-keeping groups. This breakthrough has led to the development of a series of trapdoor (-like) adsorbents that exhibit exceptional selectivity for molecular separation. However, these adsorbents often have slow adsorption kinetics and low capacity. This is because they all necessitate a high-density of pore-keeping groups that block multiple pore apertures of every cage of the porous adsorbents to ensure high selectivity. Unfortunately, these pore-keeping groups also hinder gas diffusion and reduce the pore void volume. This project aims to address the inherent limitations of cage-type trapdoor adsorbents by developing a new class of channel-type trapdoor adsorbents. The new concept of “trapdoor in channel-type adsorbents” allows for reducing the density of pore-keeping groups while maintaining high selectivity. Rather than blocking multiple cage openings, we only need to block the limited channel ends, thus significantly reducing the number of pore-keeping groups required for a given pore volume in a porous crystal. To achieve this, we will address key questions, including how to prepare model channel-type zeolites and metal-organic frameworks accommodating various cations or anions as pore-keeping groups, how to adjust the type and density of pore-keeping groups and type of channels to tune gas admission and adsorption properties, how to elucidate the mechanism of gas admission and adsorption through experimental and computational methods, and how to prove the effectiveness (high adsorption selectivity, kinetics, and capacity) of our novel channel-type adsorbents through gas separation tests. The new knowledge on fundamentals of adsorption and new adsorbent materials generated through this research will advance selective adsorption-based gas separation, and have implications in other gas technologies, including storage, detection, and (catalytic) conversion, which will potentially bring considerable economic, social, and environmental benefits. 氣體分離產業佔全球能源消耗的相當比例（約 10–15%）。本項目旨在開發一類全新的吸附劑——通道型分子陷阱門吸附劑，以實現高效的分子分離。此創新技術有望大幅降低多類氣體分離過程的成本，包括燃料氣體純化、二氧化碳捕集、空氣分離以及正烷烴/烯烴分離。 傳統分子篩基於尺寸的篩分效應在氣體分離上具有高度選擇性，但難以區分大小相近的小分子。幸運的是，尚進教授發現的「分子陷阱門」效應——一種非尺寸基礎的篩分機制——為此提供了解決方案。分子陷阱門吸附劑可透過調控分子與材料中「孔口守門基團」的相互作用，選擇性地允許目標分子進入。該突破已推動了一系列陷阱門（或類陷阱門）吸附劑的發展，並在分子分離上展現了卓越的選擇性。然而，這些吸附劑普遍存在吸附動力學遲緩與容量不足的問題。原因在於，為了確保高選擇性，往往需要在多孔吸附劑的每個籠狀孔單元中引入高密度的孔口守門基團以封堵多個孔口。但這些基團同時阻礙了氣體擴散並降低了孔體積。 本項目擬透過開發通道型陷阱門吸附劑，克服籠型陷阱門吸附劑的固有限制。這一新概念的核心在於：僅需在通道末端設置陷阱門，而非在每一個籠狀孔口中佈滿守門基團。如此一來，便能大幅降低在單位孔體積中所需的守門基團密度，同時保持高選擇性。為實現此目標，本研究將聚焦於若干關鍵科學問題，包括：如何合成可容納不同陽/陰離子作為孔口守門基團的模型通道型沸石與金屬有機框架；如何調控孔口守門基團的種類與密度以及通道類型，以調整氣體進入與吸附特性；如何透過實驗與計算方法闡明氣體進入與吸附的機理；以及如何通過氣體分離實驗驗證所設計通道型吸附劑在高選擇性、快速動力學與高容量方面的性能。 本研究將在吸附基本理論及新型吸附劑材料方面產生全新知識，不僅推動基於選擇性吸附的氣體分離技術發展，亦將對儲存、檢測及（催化）轉化等其他氣體技術領域帶來啟示，從而潛在地實現顯著的經濟、社會與環境效益。

11313325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11313325.value: 拓撲化學合成定制非常規過渡金屬氧化物量子材料

11313325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11313325.value: Transition metal oxides represent an important class of quantum materials where multiple valence states and complex lattice structures give rise to exotic electronic properties. The interplay between transition metal orbitals and oxygen networks in these materials can lead to diverse ground states, as demonstrated in high-temperature cuprate superconductors and magnetic pyrochlore iridates. Recent advances in topotactic soft-chemistry approaches have enabled atomic-level manipulation of ionic structures, opening new pathways to synthesize materials with unconventional valence states and coordination environments. This project focuses on developing three key methodologies -- oxygen de-intercalation, lithiation, and fluorination - for both bulk materials and heterostructures. Our primary goals are to discover new high-temperature nickelate superconductors through lithium insertion and fluorination, and to create novel transition metal oxide thin films with unusual crystal field environments. We will combine topotactic transitions, thin-film epitaxy, electrochemical doping, and atomic precision fabrication to achieve kinetic control over the synthesis process, allowing access to meta-stable phases that are otherwise thermodynamically inaccessible. The research leverages recent breakthroughs in soft-chemistry approaches and the discovery of unconventional nickelate superconductors. By integrating materials synthesis, technical innovation, and quantum materials physics, this project aims to establish new pathways for creating and investigating a wide extent of oxide materials with novel quantum behaviours. 過渡金屬氧化物是一類重要的量子材料，其多重價態和複雜晶格結構賦予其獨特的電子性質。過渡金屬軌道與氧原子網絡的耦合可導致多樣化的基態行為，高溫銅氧化物超導體和磁性鈍石型銥氧化物即為典型例證。近年來，拓撲化學（topotactic）軟化學方法的進展，使得對離子結構進行原子級調控成為可能，為合成具有非常規價態和配位環境的材料開闢了新途徑。 本項目將重點發展三種方法——脫氧、鋰摻入和氟化，並分別應用於塊體材料和異質結構。我們的主要目標是：通過鋰插入與氟化探索新的高溫鎳氧化物超導體；以及制備具有非常規晶體場環境的新型過渡金屬氧化物薄膜。我們將結合拓撲化學轉變、薄膜外延生長、電化學摻雜與原子精度製備，實現對合成動力學的有效控制，從而獲得常規熱力學條件下難以穩定存在的亞穩相。 本研究依託於近期在軟化學方法和非常規鎳氧化物超導體研究中的突破，融合材料合成、技術創新與量子材料物理，旨在建立新的研究路徑，推動非常規過渡金屬氧化物量子材料的發展。

11500625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500625.value: 代碼、數據和預訓練模型對於演算法市場成功的影響

11500625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500625.value: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning have become an important component of many business applications. However, firms still face the question of how to acquire the capabilities they need to develop machine learning algorithms. Traditionally, there are two ways to conduct machine learning projects: outsourcing to vendors or developing in-house teams. This project studies a third channel: algorithm markets. Algorithm markets have existed in two forms: seller-oriented and buyer-oriented. In seller-oriented markets, developers post their algorithms/models for customers to adopt. In buyer-oriented markets, customers post their problems and data for developers to tackle. These markets have traditionally been studied within the e-commerce/app store and crowdsourcing literature. However, algorithms are different from traditional commodities or crowdsourced services. They usually need to be customized more than commodities and have more constraints than regular outsourced services. To effectively manage algorithm markets, it is necessary to understand their unique mechanisms. This project plans to investigate three unique aspects of algorithm markets: code, data, and (pre-trained) models. Code and data are basic elements of machine learning solutions, where code determines model structure and data determines model parameters. Pre-trained models are a new form of solution that combines code and data. This project will examine how the code representation will change the behavior of consumers and how datasets will change the behavior of developers. Next, it will explore how pre-trained models will affect the dynamics of both types of stakeholders. In this investigation, this project will employ machine learning and econometric analysis methods. Machine learning will capture the characteristics of code, data, and pre-trained models, which are too complicated for humans to conceptualize and measure. Rigorous econometric methods will be used to provide causal identification of relations between the variables so that the findings can be implemented by market makers. Theoretically, the project will deepen our understanding of algorithm markets and push forward studies on the stakeholders of machine learning projects. Practically, the project could provide insights to the management of algorithm markets.
