A pilot study, already conducted in collaboration with the News/Co Lab at the Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication at Arizona State University, validated the utility of news knowledge to build news literacy and inform journalists how to incorporate elements of media education into their daily coverage and digital products. This proposal focuses on a media literacy intervention program. The project will be conducted with Dr. Erik Bucy of Texas Tech University. Grant funds will be used to first assess the ability of short digital videos about news practices to enhance procedural news knowledge and aid in fake news detection and rejection. Next, the project will evaluate the efficacy of such intervention by testing the Dunning-Kruger effect in the context of digital misinformation, the idea that people with less news knowledge overestimate their ability to detect and deflect misinformation. Topline findings will be released as available in the form of news releases and blog pieces for distribution to media outlets in Hong Kong, and more in-depth reports will be presented at conferences, in the form of white papers, and manuscript submissions to academic journals. 虛假新聞、陰謀論、計算宣傳等各類數位虛假資訊的興起，日益挑戰著當今社會保護公眾免受操縱與迷惑的能力——這一頑疾在選舉、健康疫情及其他易被政治化的議題中尤為顯著。本研究概述了一項多階段計劃，旨在檢驗程序性新聞知識（Amazeen & Bucy, 2019; Tomboer et al., 2023）的效能，並通過媒體素養干預方案幫助受眾建立對誤導性主張的辨識能力（Apuke et al, 2023）。 我們已與亞利桑那州立大學克朗凱特新聞與大眾傳播學院News/Co實驗室合作完成的先導研究證實：新聞知識不僅有助於提升公眾的新聞素養，更能為新聞工作者如何將媒體教育元素融入日常報導及數位產品提供實踐指導。本研究擬進一步開展媒體素養干預項目，與德州理工大學的Erik Bucy博士合作推進。 項目資金將首先用於評估新聞實務短片對提升程序性新聞知識，和輔助虛假新聞識別與抵制的能力；繼而通過檢驗數位虛假資訊語境下的達克效應（即新聞知識不足者往往高估自身識別與抵禦錯誤資訊能力的現象），評估此類干預措施的實際成效。核心研究發現將以新聞稿形式適時向香港媒體機構發布，更深度成果則通過學術會議、白皮書及期刊論文形式呈現。

11603725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11603725.value: 试点跨国生态中的乐龄科技以促进积极老龄化：提升香港和新加坡老龄人群健康科技的数字化包容性

11603725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11603725.value: As populations across Asia continue to age, innovative approaches are essential to support healthy aging. This project, titled "Piloting Gerontechnologies for Active Ageing in a Multinational Ecosystem (G.A.M.E): Advancing Digital Inclusivity in Health Technologies for Older Adults in Hong Kong and Singapore," addresses two critical challenges—data absenteeism and technology chauvinism—that hinder the adoption of gerontechnologies. Data absenteeism refers to the underrepresentation of older adults in gerontechnology research, while technology chauvinism is the mistaken belief that advanced technologies alone can address aging challenges without considering social and cultural contexts. The project aims to pilot the Gerontechnology for Active Ageing in a Multinational Ecosystem (G.A.M.E) in Hong Kong, expanding upon the PI’s successful development of a similar digital health ecosystem in Singapore. The G.A.M.E ecosystem will integrate several digital health tools, including the W.A.L.K health app (which visualizes health data and provides personalized recommendations), wearable gloves, and exergames in both VR and non-VR formats. These technologies will be co-created with older adults, caregivers, and elderly center managers to ensure they are user-friendly and culturally relevant. Additionally, the project will focus on capacity building by training seniors, caregivers, and center staff to effectively use the ecosystem, helping seniors improve their physical activity, mental well-being, and cognitive function. The research will focus on three key initiatives. First, a quantitative survey (n = 1,000 in Hong Kong and n = 1,000 in Singapore) will be conducted to identify external and individual-level factors contributing to data absenteeism and technology chauvinism, identifying barriers to gerontechnology adoption. Second, the project will engage stakeholders (n = 40)—including older adults, social networks, caregivers, and elderly centre staff—in the co-creation of gerontechnologies. This collaborative approach ensures that the tools are designed with input from those who will be using them. Finally, based on the findings from the survey and co-creation workshops, the G.A.M.E ecosystem will be implemented in elderly centres in both Hong Kong and Singapore. Over an 8-week period, 200 older adults will be trained to use the co-created, gamified gerontechnologies collaboratively, focusing on improving physical activity, mental well-being, and cognitive function. The project will culminate in a friendly exergaming competition between participants from Hong Kong and Singapore. By integrating gerontechnologies into elderly centers and fostering collaboration among users, G.A.M.E has the potential to create a sustainable ecosystem that promotes healthy aging in Hong Kong and beyond. 随着亚洲人口持续老龄化，创新方法对支持健康老龄化至关重要。本项目题为"试点跨国生态中的乐龄科技以促进积极老龄化（G.A.M.E）：提升香港和新加坡老龄人群健康科技的数字化包容性"，旨在解决阻碍乐龄科技采用的两个关键挑战——数据缺失和技术至上主义。数据缺失指的是老龄人群在乐龄科技研究中的代表性不足，而技术至上主义则是指错误地认为先进技术本身就能解决老龄化挑战，而无需考虑社会和文化背景。 本项目计划在香港试点"跨国生态中的乐龄科技以促积极跃老龄化（G.A.M.E）"，扩展首席研究员在新加坡成功开发的类似数字健康生态系统。 G.A.M.E生态系统将整合多种数字健康工具，包括W.A.L.K健康应用程序（提供可视化健康数据并提供个性化建议）、可穿戴手套以及VR和非VR形式的体感游戏。这些技术将与老年人、照护者和老年中心管理人员共同创造，以确保其用户友好性和文化相关性。此外，项目将重点开展能力建设，通过培训老年人、照护者和中心工作人员有效使用该生态系统，帮助老年人改善身体活动、心理健康和认知功能。 研究将聚焦三个关键举措。首先，将进行定量调查（香港n=1,000，新加坡n=1,000），以确定导致数据缺失和技术至上主义的外部和个人层面因素，找出乐龄科技采用的障碍。 其次，利益相关者（n=40）——包括老年人、社交网络成员、照护者和老年中心工作人员——参与乐龄技术的共同创造。这种协作方法确保工具的设计考虑了使用者的意见。 最后，基于调查和共同创造研讨会的结果，G.A.M.E生态系统将在香港和新加坡的老年中心实施。在为期8周的时间里，200名老年人将接受培训，学习如何使用这些共同创造的、游戏化的乐龄技术，重点关注改善身体活动、心理健康和认知功能。项目最终阶段将组织香港与新加坡参与者的体感游戏跨地区交流赛。 通过将乐龄技术整合到老年中心并促进用户之间的协作，G.A.M.E有潜力创建一个可持续的生态系统，促进香港及其他地区的健康老龄化。

11603825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11603825.value: 应对人工智能监管：参与式标准制定、企业合规与自我规制研究

11603825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11603825.value: The rapid evolution of AI has outpaced regulatory frameworks, creating a gap between technological progress and regulatory oversight. While AI’s benefits for productivity and innovation are well-documented, concern over ethical issues, misinformation, and security threats are growing. Current literature on responsible AI (RAI) is often segmented, focusing separately on policy and regulatory perspectives or business initiatives, without adequately connecting the two. Despite ongoing government and industry efforts towards RAI, there is limited understanding of how RAI initiatives can be effectively established via institutional cooperation and how businesses adapt to and influence the shifting regulatory landscape. The proposed project addresses these gaps by exploring two core research questions: (1) How do participatory processes and mechanisms differ between technical and responsible AI standards-setting, and how does firm participation affect compliance and management practices towards RAI? (2) How do RAI practices emerge, develop, and diffuse among smaller, less regulated firms? Study 1 will integrate agile regulation and government-business relations literature to examine the microprocesses of participatory AI standard-setting, focusing on the presence and influence of state and non-state actors across different types of standards. We anticipate technical standards-setting will be primarily led by industry and technical experts, while RAI standards-setting will involve more participatory, multi-stakeholder dialogues. Hypotheses will then be tested on how firms’ standard-setting experiences affects their compliance and internal management of RAI. A mixed-methods approach will be used, drawing on archival data of AI standards developed in China since 2017, firm-level practices, and stakeholder interviews. Study 2 shifts the focus to smaller firms, which are traditionally less engaged in regulatory design. Combining theories of self-regulation and institutional logic, this explorative study will investigate how RAI practices mature and converge within smaller platform firms as regulations evolve. The empirical focus will be on China’s web novel platform sector—a dynamic part of the creator economy where generative AI (GenAI) is transforming content creation. Data will include secondary data on platforms’ GenAI policies and practices, semi-structured interviews with managers and users, and direct observations. As one of the first interdisciplinary analyses of these dynamics, this project will contribute to the regulation and government–business relations literature by highlighting the complex regulation–business interactions in the context of disruptive technologies. It will provide timely insights and practical guidance for policymakers and business leaders, with broader implications for navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of emerging technologies. 人工智能的快速发展已远超现有监管体系的适应能力，技术进步与监管治理之间的落差日益凸显。尽管人工智能在提升生产力与推动创新方面的优势已广为认可，公众对其引发的伦理争议、虚假信息传播与安全风险的关注也不断上升。当前关于“负责任人工智能”（Responsible AI, RAI）的研究多为碎片化，常将政策/监管与企业实践分开讨论，缺乏对两者之间互动关系的系统梳理。尽管政府与行业已在推动RAI方面付出努力，但学界对RAI如何通过制度性协作得以有效建立，以及企业如何适应乃至影响这一变动中的监管环境，仍缺乏深入理解。 本研究拟从两个核心问题出发，填补上述研究空白：（1）技术标准与RAI标准的制定过程中，其参与机制有何差异？企业参与标准制定如何影响其在RAI方面的合规与管理实践？（2）在较少受到监管的小型企业中，RAI实践是如何萌芽、发展并扩散的？第一项研究将融合敏捷监管与政企关系的相关理论，深入剖析AI标准制定中的参与式微观过程，关注国家与非国家行为体在不同类型标准中的角色与影响力。我们预期，技术标准更多由行业与技术专家主导，而RAI标准制定则呈现出更强的多方参与与对话特征。基于此，我们将提出并检验企业参与标准制定是否有助于其在RAI方面的制度建设与日常管理。该研究将采用混合研究方法，结合2017年以来AI标准的档案资料、企业层面的实践数据，以及多方访谈。第二项研究将关注传统上较少参与监管设计的小型平台企业。结合自我规制与制度逻辑理论，该探索性研究将分析在监管演变过程中，小型企业内部RAI实践如何走向成熟与趋同。实证聚焦中国线上创作平台——这是创作者经济中一个充满活力的子领域，生成式人工智能正在深刻改变其内容生产方式。数据来源包括平台在生成式内容政策与实践方面的二手资料、平台管理者与用户的半结构式访谈，以及研究者的直接观察。 作为首批系统研究RAI标准制定与企业响应互动的跨学科项目之一，本研究将为科技监管与政企关系研究提供新的理论视角，揭示在颠覆性技术背景下复杂的政企互动机制。研究成果不仅将为政策制定者与企业管理者提供及时的实证参考与实践指引，也有助于社会各界更有效地应对快速演化的新兴技术监管挑战。

11604125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604125.value: 解析科學實驗中多模態意義建構能力：一項針對香港中學生的探索性研究

11604125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11604125.value: Prof Lin, Angel M. Y. Dr Tang, Kok Sing

11604125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604125.value: In Hong Kong, a substantial proportion of English as a Second Language (ESL) students require explicit support in using multiple modalities to communicate their scientific ideas. This issue may be aggravated in English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) contexts where the English language is commonly used to teach almost all academic subjects and for content assessment. This scenario is likely to place ESL students with lower English proficiency at a disadvantage, which may, in turn, hinder their academic performance. There is, therefore, a strong need for EMI students to develop knowledge of representing and constructing content knowledge using multiple semiotic modes. This three-year research project aims to develop a framework to characterize transduction across different modes of representations during practical work, and construct a rubric for measuring the development of students’ multimodal competence. In the realm of science education, practical work is frequently criticized for its limited impact on students’ conceptual development. The PI will use a collaborative case study design that draws on empirical findings to develop theoretical tools that can help teachers enhance the quality of practical work. 100 junior secondary science students and nine science teachers across nine EMI schools will be recruited as focal participants. Furthermore, three control science teachers from another three EMI schools will be recruited to act as a baseline. At the first stage, this project aims to characterize students’ strategies for transducing across different modes of representations by developing an analytical rubric for measuring students’ material-dialogic communication and multimodal scientific reporting. In the second stage, the research team will conduct evidence-driven professional development programs for teachers. The findings of this study can impact science education in Hong Kong and other similar contexts in three key ways: (a) the framework developed may inform pedagogical approaches to teaching practical work, which can in turn lead to improved collaborative meaning-making among students when they engage in practical tasks and compose multimodal scientific reports; (b) the research findings may suggest modifications and refinement to existing curriculum that explicitly incorporate opportunities for ESL students to engage with multimodal representations in science lessons; and (c) the dissemination of all the deliverables and useful empirical findings to a wide community of local science teachers and English teachers may arguably promote a shared pedagogical understanding among them, which in turn may potentially enhance the collaborations between science teachers and English teachers to maximize student outcomes. 在香港，相當多以英語為第二語言（ESL）的學生需要明確支援，以運用多種模態來傳達其科學概念。在英語作為教學語言（EMI）的環境中，幾乎所有學術科目均以英語教授及評核，此情況可能進一步加劇學生在多模態表達上的困難。英語水平較低的ESL學生因而可能處於不利地位，影響其學術表現。因此，EMI學生有迫切需要掌握運用多種符號模態來建構及表達內容知識的能力。 本項為期三年的研究計劃旨在發展一個理論框架，以描述學生在進行科學實驗活動時跨模態轉換（transduction）的特徵，並建構一套評量學生多模態能力發展的評分量表。在科學教育領域，實驗活動經常被批評對學生概念發展的影響有限。為提升實驗教學的質素，本研究採用協作式個案研究設計，結合理論與實證，發展出可協助教師提升實驗教學質量的教學工具。研究將招募來自九所EMI學校的100位初中科學學生及九位科學教師為主要參與者，並招募另外三所EMI學校的三位科學教師作為對照組。 第一階段的目標是描繪學生在不同模態表徵之間進行轉換的策略，並發展一套分析性量表，以評估學生在物質—對話性交流及多模態科學報告方面的表現。第二階段，研究團隊將根據研究證據設計並推行針對教師的專業發展課程。本研究的成果可望從三方面影響香港及其他類似教育語境的科學教育：(a) 所發展的框架可為實驗教學提供理論依據，有助於提升學生於實驗活動及多模態科學報告撰寫中的協作性意義建構；(b) 研究結果或可為現行課程提供修改建議，促使課程更明確地為ESL學生提供接觸多模態表徵的學習機會；(c) 透過向本地科學教師及英語教師廣泛推廣研究成果及實證資源，有望促進彼此在教學法上的共識，從而加強科學與語文教師之間的合作，以最大化學生的學習成效。

11605925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605925.value: 秩序與景觀：中唐道州永州的吏治觀念與山水書寫

11605925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605925.value: 地方官的文士化是中唐政治突出的現象，影響及文學，帶來題材和文體的新變。中唐的文士地方官面對安史亂(755-763)之後秩序重建的迫切需求，欲以其文學參與到地方秩序的建設中。湖南的道州和永州在此歷程中的地位特殊。道州先後由元結(719-772)、陽城(736-805)和呂溫(772-811)等名刺史出守，他們致力於重建地方秩序，承繼並發展漢循吏的傳統，形成新的吏治文化。道州也因此由南荒之地成為中唐政壇與文壇的共同話題。元結等人秉持儒家觀念，以爲理想的秩序包括和諧的社會與自然秩序。元結在道州創作大量的山水記文，即體現出重建地方自然秩序並將之納入天下秩序的意圖。柳宗元(773-819)繼承元結等人的吏治觀念，其山水遊記也是對永州自然秩序的確立。道州與永州成爲中國最早的山水遊記的誕生地。傳統的山水書寫往往寄託文士個人的情懷，抒情性強烈，但在中唐的新吏治觀念下，山水觀游同時被賦予「為政之具」的價值，書寫山水的遊記亦具有調和地方官作爲官員之惠境與作爲文人之自適的功能。 Order and Landscape: New Administrative Ideas and Landscape Writing in Daozhou and Yongzhou during the Mid-Tang China The significant increase in local officials with literary talents was a prominent phenomenon in the politics of the Mid-Tang, which impacted literature and brought about new changes in themes and genres. Literate local officials faced the urgent need to rebuild order after the An Lushan Rebellion. They wanted to participate in reconstructing local order through their literary works. Daozhou and Yongzhou in Hunan Province had a special position in this process. Daozhou was successively governed by famous officials such as Yuan Jie, Yang Cheng, and Lü Wen, who were dedicated to rebuilding local order, inheriting and developing the tradition of Han dynasty officials, and forming a new administrative culture. As a result, Daozhou transformed from a remote area to a common topic in both political and literary circles. Yuan Jie and others held Confucian ideals, believing that an ideal order includes harmonious social and natural order. He wrote a large number of landscape essays in Daozhou, which reflected his intention to rebuild the natural order of the region and incorporate it into the order of the Tang dynasty. Liu Zongyuan, who was demoted to Yongzhou, inherited the administrative ideals of Yuan Jie and others, and his travel essays on landscapes also established the natural order of Yongzhou. Daozhou and Yongzhou thus became the birthplace of China's earliest landscape travel essays. Traditional landscape writing often expressed the personal sentiments of literati. However, under the new administrative ideals, landscape appreciation was also given the value of "governing approaches," and landscape writing served the function of harmonizing the officials' role and their pursuit of personal fulfillment.

11606025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11606025.value: 分享與否--中國在泰國的技術轉移

11606025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606025.value: Increasing technology transfer from China is positioning Thailand in unprecedented opportunities and challenges of technology learning amid the post-pandemic geo-political and market competition. The proposed project will represent the first comprehensive investigation of China’s technology transfer activities in Thailand between 2013 and 2028, focusing on the transition from the first decades of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and the following five years of the updated version. This is a critical topic for Southeast Asia as it is now the epicentre of global geopolitical and market competition. Bringing together research on China’s state capitalism and the theories of technological learning, we will offer a fine-grained analysis of China’s technology transfer activities and Thailand’s technology learning trajectory in three industrial sectors: railway technology, mechanical and construction engineering, and e-commerce. Undertaking a comprehensive, in-depth, and place-based approach to unpack the process of technology localisation and integration of foreign technologies into the local context, this project calls for a meticulous single-country study. Thailand is chosen for three reasons. First, the recent updates to China’s BRI, resulting in more prudent international development projects and investments, have been crucial in shaping Thailand’s technology learning in high-value-added sectors. Second, Thailand has experienced various models of technology learning from foreign countries through technology localisation in multi-national corporations, overseas internship programmes and local education based on university-industrial linkages. The historical shift in seeking the best technology learning model provides rich data for in-depth comparative investigation. Third, investigating the imperatives, implementation and implications of China’s technology transfer activities in Thailand will complete a broader comparative research strategy led by the PI to explain China’s international development cooperation within the changing geopolitics of the Asian region. Based on a mixed-methods approach combining tracing of secondary data, in-depth interviews and fieldwork, we seek to answer three research questions: 1) What are the imperatives of China’s technology transfer activities in Thailand? 2) How has China’s updated BRI affected its technology transfer activities? 3) What are China’s updated BRI and technology transfer implications for the technology-learning country? Such research-based knowledge will advance the theorisation of state capitalism and technology localisation. The research outcome is also essential for policymakers and industrial practitioners in the technology-sending and recipient countries and other stakeholders that wish to facilitate technology transfer and learning projects. 新冠疫情後中國逐漸增加對外技術轉移項目，在新一輪的地緣政治和市場競爭中，泰國面對難得的技術學習機會，同時也遇上不少挑戰。本研究將首次全面調查2013年至2028年間中國在泰國的技術轉移項目，特別關注2013年至2023年中國「一帶一路」倡議(BRI）的最初十年，以及2023年至2028中國對「一帶一路」倡議重新定調後的改變。東南亞現處於全球地緣政治和市場的競爭核心，本研究對相關發展尤其重要。 本研究將結合關於國家資本主義和產業技術學習的理論，詳細分析中國技術轉移及泰國技術學習項目，並聚焦泰國在鐵路技術、機械和建築工程以及電子商務三個產業發展。我們集中研究單一國家—泰國，以更全面深入地解構當地技術本地化的過程。選擇泰國有三個主要原因。首先，中國近年對「一帶一路」倡議的國際發展項目和投資日益謹慎，增加了泰國在高增值產業的技術學習機會。其次，泰國過去一直經三種渠道，包括跨國公司的技術轉移、海外實習項目及透過大學聯繫產業精準陪訓，尋求最佳技術學習模式，並為本研究提供了豐富的歷史數據。第三，研究中泰技術轉移項目的誘因、實踐和結果，讓本研究的首席研究員進一步推展其主導的全球中國發展研究，以全面分析中國在地緣政治變遷中如何發展國際合作項目。 本研究結合文本數據追蹤、深入訪談和實地調研的研究方法，回答三個研究問題：1）中國為何在泰國進行技術轉移項？2）中國對「一帶一路」倡議的新定調如何影響其技術轉移項目？3）中國新一輪的技術轉移項目對接受國有什麼影響？相關的實證分析將有助完善國家資本主義和技術本地化的理論。研究成果對於技術輸出和接收國的政策制定者、相關產業人員、關注促進技術轉移的學者和其他人員具有重要意義。

11607725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11607725.value: 評估We-INtervention在中國HIV血清不一致男性伴侶中的果效：隨機對照試驗

11607725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11607725.value: Prof Darbes, Lynae Prof Falconier, Mariana K.

11607725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607725.value: HIV-serodiscordant male couples, in which one male partner is HIV-seropositive and the other is HIV-seronegative, experience multiple risks in HIV care and prevention. As stigma often hinders such couples’ access to support and services, leveraging their relational resources is crucial for optimizing their outcomes. The proposed study will assess the efficacy of the three-session We-INtervention focusing on their relationship dynamics to enhance Chinese HIV-serodiscordant male couples’ health and well-being. A pilot randomized controlled trial has already demonstrated the feasibility, acceptability, cultural sensitivity, and preliminary efficacy of the We-INtervention in improving the quality of life, psychological well-being, relationship satisfaction, and health behaviors of both partners in HIV-serodiscordant male couples. The proposed randomized controlled trial will extend the pilot study to examine the effects of the We-INtervention on perceived stigma and other HIV-related behavioral outcomes, the mediators that account for the intervention effects, and the conditions under which the intervention is most effective. In addition to the effects observed in the pilot study, we expect (a) the We-INtervention to improve perceived stigma and health behaviors of HIV-serodiscordant male couples; (b) we-disease appraisal, dyadic efficacy, and common dyadic coping to mediate the effects of the We-INtervention on outcomes; and (c) baseline characteristics to moderate the effects of the We-INtervention on outcomes. A total of 160 Chinese HIV-serodiscordant male couples (320 individuals: 160 HIV-seropositive and 160 HIV-seronegative) will be randomized at a 1:1 ratio to either the intervention or control arm. In the intervention arm, the We-INtervention will be delivered to both partners of each couple separately. In the control arm, each couple will receive health information pamphlets. All couples will undergo quantitative assessments on perceived stigma, quality of life, well-being, relationship satisfaction, and behavioral outcomes pre-intervention, post-intervention, and at 1- and 3-month follow-ups. We will test three hypotheses using multilevel models, common fate mediation analysis, and subgroup analysis, respectively. Finally, We-INtervention participants and interventionists will report their experiences and provide feedback via qualitative exit interviews. We will conduct framework analysis and thematic analysis. The proposed study will contribute to multiple sustainable development goals related to reducing inequality, promoting health and well-being, and building global partnerships. Its findings will help inform local and international researchers on the development of couple-centric interventions with high cultural sensitivity. The We-INtervention, if found to be effective, will be a valuable supplement to existing medical care modules. 在HIV血清不一致的男性伴侶中，一方為HIV血清陽性，另一方為HIV血清陰性，這類伴侶在HIV照護和預防方面面臨多重風險。由於他們常受污名的困擾，難以使用服務，動員他們的關係資源對於優化其健康結局至關重要。本研究擬以中國HIV血清不一致男性伴侶為研究對象，以伴侶關係為核心，發展三節的We-INtervention介入方案，並評估伴侶雙方健康與福祉的改善狀況。 我們先前的隨機對照試驗表明，We-INtervention用於HIV血清不一致男性伴侶雙方具備可行性、接受度和文化敏感性，改善了伴侶雙方生活品質、心理健康、關係滿意度及健康行為等。在先導研究的基礎上，本隨機對照試驗將進一步檢驗We-INtervention對感知污名及其他HIV相關行為結果的影響，並探討介入效果的中介機制及調節機制。 除先導研究中觀察到的果效外，我們假設：(a) We-INtervention將改善HIV血清不一致男性伴侶的感知污名和健康行為；(b) 「我們」疾病評估、二元效能及共同二元應對這三個因素將中介We-INtervention對結果的影響；(c) 基線特徵將調節We-INtervention對結果的果效。 本研究將納入160對中國HIV血清不一致男性伴侶（共320人：160名HIV血清陽性，160名HIV血清陰性），以1:1比例隨機分配至介入組及對照組。介入組中，We-INtervention將提供給成對的伴侶，每對分別進行；對照組則將獲得健康資訊冊。所有伴侶將在介入前、介入後1個月和3個月追蹤時，完成感知污名、生活品質、福祉、關係滿意度及行為結果的量化評估。我們將分別採用多層次模型、共同命運中介分析及亞組分析檢驗三項假設。最後，We-INtervention參與者及施介者將參加質性訪談，報告體驗並提供回饋，我們將採用框架分析和主題分析方法進行質性資料分析。 本研究將促進減少不平等、提升健康福祉及建構全球夥伴關係等多項永續發展目標。研究成果將為本地及國際研究人員開發具有高文化敏感度的伴侶介入計畫提供參考。如果We-INtervention有效，將補充現有的醫療照護模式。

11607825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11607825.value: 檢視和減輕央行數位貨幣當前和未來的金融犯罪風險 檢視和減輕央行數位貨幣當前和未來的金融犯罪風險 檢視和減輕央行數位貨幣當前和未來的金融犯罪風險

11607825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11607825.value: Dr Akartuna, Arda Prof Chai, Andreas Prof Johnson, Shane

11607825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607825.value: Almost two-thirds of countries are exploring the introduction of a central bank digital currency (CBDC) – virtual currencies issued by central banks aimed at streamlining global trade and digital payments. Though CBDCs have the potential of positively reshaping the global financial system, they also have financial crime and deception risks. This area of criminal opportunity is relatively unexplored and is of relevance to China and Hong Kong, which are arguably two of the most enhanced pioneers of CBDC technologies. The People’s Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) are in the piloting stages of the e-CNY and e-HKD respectively. Exploring the financial crime risks of CBDCs in the Greater China Region is of particular importance given current year-on-year increases in deception crimes, which include financial fraud. In Hong Kong, 44% of all crimes recorded in the first half of 2024 were deception crimes (a 6.2% rise). Already in China, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology have issued reports and warnings of emerging e-CNY-related scams. Earlier research has focused on why criminals undertake financial crimes using new technologies, but not necessarily how. The how question is central to developing actionable and pre-emptive prevention measures to ensure the safe and secure development of CBDCs. Anticipating future crime risks and implementing early mitigation strategies can assist in ensuring that crime problems do not become mainstream. To develop these measures, this project employs established yet innovative methods to (1) examine the criminogenic features of CBDCs; (2) identify how criminals may exploit these features as CBDCs become more widely available; and (3) develop prevention strategies that relevant stakeholders can pre-emptively take to address emerging CBDC-enabled crimes. Such stakeholders include pioneers of CBDC development (e.g. the HKMA), as well as regulators, law enforcement and businesses that may use CBDCs to conduct payments and trade in the future. This project aims to ensure the safe and sustainable development of CBDCs, through fostering key stakeholder-collaborative prevention strategies. This will protect the capacity of such stakeholders, particularly crime prevention/regulatory institutions such as the Hong Kong Police Force and HKMA, in ensuring that new types of CBDC-enabled crime do not overwhelm public resources. This will set the foundation for the secure adoption of CBDCs, symbiotic with public confidence in their use, thereby cementing the leadership of Hong Kong as a safe global financial and technological hub in this field. 近三分之二的國家正在探索引入央行數位貨幣（CBDC），這是由央行發行的虛擬貨幣，旨在簡化全球貿易和數位支付。儘管 CBDC 具有積極重塑全球金融體系的潛力，但它們也存在金融犯罪和欺騙風險。這個犯罪機會領域相對未被探索，並且與中國和香港相關，這兩個國家可以說是 CBDC 技術最先進的兩個先驅。中國人民銀行和香港金融管理局（金管局）分別處於數字人民幣和數字港元的試點階段。 鑑於目前包括金融欺詐在內的欺騙犯罪同比增加，探索大中華地區 CBDC 的金融犯罪風險尤為重要。香港在二○二四年上半年錄得的罪案中，有44%是欺騙罪案（上升6.2%）。在中國，工業和資訊化部已經發布了有關新興數字人民幣相關詐騙的報告和警告。 早期的研究重點關注犯罪分子為何使用新技術進行金融犯罪，但不一定是如何進行。如何問題對於制定可操作和先發制人的預防措施以確保 CBDC 的安全可靠的發展至關重要。預測未來的犯罪風險並實施早期緩解策略有助於確保犯罪問題不會成為主流。 為了制定這些措施，該項目採用了既定的創新方法來 （1） 檢查 CBDC 的犯罪特徵;（2） 隨著 CBDC 的普及，確定犯罪分子如何利用這些功能;（3） 制定相關利益相關者可以先發制人地採取的預防策略，以應對新興的 CBDC 犯罪。這些利益相關者包括 CBDC 發展的先驅（例如金管局），以及未來可能使用 CBDC 進行支付和交易的監管機構、執法部門和企業。 該計畫旨在透過促進關鍵利害關係人與合作的預防策略，確保 CBDC 的安全和永續發展。這將保護這些利益相關者，特別是香港警務處和金管局等預防犯罪/監管機構的能力，以確保新型的 CBDC 犯罪不會壓垮公共資源。這將為CBDC的安全採用奠定基礎，與公眾對其使用的信心共生，從而鞏固香港作為該領域安全的全球金融和科技中心的領導地位。

11608825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11608825.value: 中華悲觀主義：理解青年消極的文化理論

11608825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11608825.value: Dr de Seta, Gabriele Dr ZHANG, Ge

11608825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11608825.value: The project will study the contemporary manifestations of pessimism as an emotional complex in China—often encapsulated by the now iconoclastic term tangping or ‘lying flat’—and the perceived Chinese youths’ resignation from previously desirable ideals of ‘the good life’ (e.g. having a stable job, owning a property, and having a family). As Chinese society is becoming disenchanted with precarious hopes of personal flourishing and upward mobility, we witness a shift from a future-oriented ascetic culture to a present-oriented youth culture of economic thrift and utilitarian resignation (sometimes this shift is manifested as a generational gap). While enshrouded by the contagious mood of pessimism, I argue that the contemporary resignation is both pragmatic and political (e.g. a negative utilitarianism) articulated in the colloquial discussions on the Chinese-language internet (e.g. forums on Zhihu and Reddit; publications on GitHub; videos on YouTube, Bilibili, Kuaishou, and TikTok/Douyin; semi-closed communities on X, Clubhouse, and Discord). The nomenclature of sino-pessimism is termed via the influence of afropessimism, not to follow its logic of fatality but to rethink pessimism and nihilism outside of high theory, in order to produce a low theory of youth resignation in conjunction/dialogue with grassroots Chinese-language theories of their own diagnoses and pragmatic exit strategies. I coin the term sino-pessimism as the main heading under which a cluster of emic-etic concepts operates at the lower level of goal-oriented concreteness rather than academic neutrality. The project of sino-pessimism aims to map and create a language for this popular knowledge of undercommons found in the forms of memes, long-thread forum discussions, fictional stories, life narratives, video essays, manifestos, and short videos. This cultural theory of youth resignation is also directly responding to the recent pessimist turn in cultural theory—from queer pessimism, ecological pessimism, and reproductive pessimism to afropessimism—that refuses the modernist framework. Moreover, challenging methodological nationalism, youth resignation should not be understood as an affective singularity only corresponding to the ongoing socioeconomic recession in China but seen as relationally to youth resignations and pessimistic moods in other cultural contexts (most notably in Eastern Europe, Japan, and Korea). 本研究計畫旨在探討悲觀主義作為一種情感複合體在當代中國的具體展現——這種現象常以現今具有反對權威色彩的「躺平」一詞來概括——以及中國青年對先前被視為理想的「美好生活」（例如：擁有一份穩定工作、置產、成家）的退卻與消極。隨著中國社會逐漸對個人發展與向上流動的不穩定希望感到幻滅，我們見證了一種文化轉向：從以未來為導向的清苦生活文化，轉向以當下為中心的青年文化，呈現為經濟節制與功利主義式放棄（此一轉向有時亦表現為代際差異）。在籠罩於瀰漫性悲觀氛圍之中，我主張，當代的放棄既是務實的也是政治性的（例如：一種消極功利主義），並透過中文互聯網上的日常討論加以表述（如知乎與 Reddit 等論壇；GitHub 上的出版物；YouTube、Bilibili、快手與抖音等平台上的影片；以及 X、Clubhouse、Discord 等半封閉社群）。「中華悲觀主義」（sino-pessimism）的命名受到「非洲悲觀主義」（afropessimism）的啟發，並非要沿襲其宿命論邏輯，而是意在於高階理論」（high theory）之外重新思考悲觀與虛無主義，從而生成一種「低理論」（low theory）理解如今青年的消極，並與華語基層語境中自行提出的診斷與務實的撤出方案進行對話與結合。我以「中華悲觀主義」作為總體概念標籤，涵蓋一系列兼具內生（emic）與外生（etic）的概念群，基於具體的目標導向，而非學術中立的層次。「中華悲觀主義」的研究計畫旨在描繪並創造一種語言，用以理解此類「下層公域」（undercommons）中的民間知識，這些知識表現於迷因（memes）、論壇討論、虛構故事、生活敘事、影音評論、宣言文本以及短影片等多種形式之中。這一青年消極的文化理論同時回應了當代文化理論中的「悲觀轉向」——從酷兒悲觀、環境悲觀、生育悲觀到非洲悲觀——共同拒斥現代主義的框架。此外，在挑戰方法論民族主義的同時，青年消極不應僅被理解為對中國當前社會經濟衰退的單一情感回應，而應視為一種關係性現象，與其他文化語境中的青年消極與悲觀情緒相互對照（最顯著的案例包括東歐、日本與韓國）。

11609425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11609425.value: 再訪廣東木魚書：唱本、歷史情景、聲音材料的整合性研究

11609425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609425.value: Studying Cantonese “muyushu” (木魚書 wooden-fish book, Cantonese ballad booklets) are nothing new, but the recent publications of two sets of facsimile reprints of muyushu make it more feasible and economical for researchers to make breakthrough in the field. The first is “Suwenxue Congkan” (俗文學叢刊 Folk Literature) published by the Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica in Taiwan between 2002 and 2016; the second is “Guangzhou Dadian: Qulei” (廣州大典：曲類 Guangzhou Great Classical Works: Songs) published in Guangzhou in 2019. Notwithstanding the abundance of the muyushu reprints, how do we know how they are sung (performed)? Or more precisely, how they have been sung (performed) and hence how a certain narrative song art might have evolved over times? Unless we know how the songs are sung, ballad booklets remain silent and their acoustic value would be depreciated. Increasing availability and accessibility of historical audio records available at various collections make it possible to address these questions and adopt an integrative approach to the research question. The PI will start the project by making an extended catalogue of the two sets of facsimile reprints of muyushu. On basis of the catalogue, textual studies of selected items will be conducted. The PI will then look for further source materials to search for answers to questions that might have developed from the first phase of textual analyses. Simultaneously, the PI will listen, notate and analyze historical audio records of Cantonese ballad produced between the 1900s and 1940s in order to trace the evolution of various musical and vocal styles of sung oral narratives. Studies of audio records will be cross-referenced with the textual and contextual analyses of printed texts, contemporary record company catalogues, and newspaper advertisements of the records. Over the past few years, the PI has been experimenting an integrative approach to using textual, contextual, and audio source materials to “re-sound” the silent booklets, i.e., to “read” texts the aural and vocal proficiency she possesses. The PI therefore believes that into the second decade of the 21st century, it is time for us to revisit the old genre and yield new outputs with significant methodological implications applicable not only to Cantonese genre but also to the studies of narrative song arts of other language districts of China. 有關廣東一般統稱為“木魚書”的研究成果，過去大半世紀以來可說是汗牛充棟。然而，近年大規模的說唱文獻出版項目，為此類研究在方法上取得突破提供了極大幫助。2019年廣州出版的《廣州大典：曲類》，連同2002-2016年間在台北出版的《俗文學叢刊》的相關部分，皆以原件複印的形式，收入了廣東木魚書和其他粵語說唱文獻，品種和數量十分龐大，讓研究者有更好的條件對包括木魚書在內的各種粵語說唱文獻重新梳理。本研究進一步探問的問題是：這些歷經數世紀的紙上文獻，到底是如何唱演的？唱演的方式發生了怎樣的變化？本研究主要利用上述兩套說唱文獻，製作詳細目錄，選取適當的曲目作文本分析；同時聽取20世紀初至40年代的唱片錄音，參考當時的唱片目錄、曲譜、報章相關報道等，推敲文本與唱演形式即書寫/印刷文獻與口頭傳統的關係，祈望能為同類型研究提供方法學上的參考。

11610125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11610125.value: 傳播學縱向研究的理論、方法與評估之系統性綜述

11610125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11610125.value: There is almost a consensus among communication scholars that communication is a time-bearing process. It follows that the communication process is best answered by longitudinal studies. However, we do not know how often communication research is based on time-stamped (i.e., longitudinal) data, let alone how time is exactly conceived, measured, and tested as a scientific concept and how much the studies actually contribute to knowledge discovery and theory development of the field. The current study aims to fill this long-standing gap by performing a systematic review of research articles published in SSCI-indexed communication journals over more than 50 years. We plan to focus on the following research questions: What is time with regard to communication processes and effects? Why is it necessary to involve the time dimension of communication? How is time conceived as a scientific concept in communication research? How is the scientific concept of time measured as an operational variable? How is the operational variable of time tested in communication research? Are the existing conceptualizations and operationalizations of time in communication research appropriate, overplayed, or underutilized? What are the possible antecedents, covariates, and consequences of time-bearing research in communication? The above questions call for a systemic framework to guide our data collection, analysis and interpretation. However, to our best knowledge, such a guideline does not exist in the literature on communication. Nor can we find anything of that kind in neighboring social sciences such as psychology, sociology, and political science where longitudinal studies are equally, or even more, frequently conducted. In the absence of relevant benchmarks, we have developed a classification scheme for the role that time plays in empirical research on communication, ranging from a rhetoric claim, a quantity measure, a temporal context, a temporal index, and a temporal parameter. We have conducted a pilot study, using scoping search to identify 2,000+ longitudinal studies published in SSCI-Communication journals from 1976 to 2023. We plan to examine the full text (instead of commonly used abstract) of the articles, which allows us to delve into the details of how time is conceived, measured, and tested, e.g., how time is exactly framed or phrased, and what contextual terms time is entailed or contrasted. We plan to draw a matching sample of non-longitudinal studies from the same source to serve as a control group, to detect the unique characteristics of longitudinal studies in communication.

11610725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11610725.value: 香港法律語境中的人工智能素養：學術界與行業的話語實踐及社會化

11610725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11610725.value: Mr Burke, John Prof HO, Virginia HARPER Prof MCKEOWN, Jamie Mr Rehman, Ubaid

11610725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11610725.value: The widespread availability of artificial intelligence (AI) tools transforms ways of writing across a range of disciplinary contexts. One sector where this transformation is particularly acutely felt is the legal sector because lawyers’ services are so tightly intertwined with the production of various kinds of texts: for example, legal opinions, contracts, client letters, and so on. AI literacy, the ability to critically, ethically, and effectively use AI in the writing process, becomes an essential skill for novice lawyers, who are starting out in the profession. However, little applied linguistic research has examined AI practices in the legal context both in the academy and in the profession. Consequently, we do not know precisely how lawyers make use of AI in the profession, how legal educators and their students make use of it in the academy, and whether academic practices effectively prepare novice lawyers to write effectively with AI in the professional context. This proposed study will investigate the Hong Kong legal academic and professional context in order to describe and explain AI discourse practices, how these practices align, and how these practices are learned. This research will take a mixed-methods approach with a dominant qualitative orientation and sequential explanatory design, utilising multiple data sources to present a rich account of discourse and socialization practices, that is, processes of constructing texts and processes of learning. Data will include: community documents that describe professional and academic positions on AI, for example, position papers by professional bodies; quantitative surveys of legal professionals (120), educators (60), and students (60) in Hong Kong; 60 in-depth narrative interviews with professionals, academics, and students; and 20 observations of simulated writing tasks that demonstrate discourse practices in action. The research will make an original empirical contribution by enhancing our understanding of AI discourse practices in the Hong Kong legal context at three stages: in the academic stage of legal education (e.g. the LLB), the practical stage (e.g. the PCLL), and in legal practice. In terms of a theoretical contribution, the research will furnish a discipline-specific model of AI literacy, that illuminates discourse processes both unique to the legal context and common across disciplines; in addition, the research will have methodological implications for how to study AI literacy in specific disciplinary contexts. Practically, the research will determine whether law graduates are sufficiently prepared for AI practices in the profession, and how their needs could be better met. 人工智能（AI）工具的普及正改變多個學科領域的寫作方式。這種變革在法律行業感受尤爲深刻，因爲律師服務與撰寫各類文本緊密交織，例如法律意見書、合約、客戶函件等。人工智能素養，即在寫作過程中批判地、合乎倫理地以及有效地運用AI的能力，已成為新手律師必備的核心技能。然而，應用語言學領域對法律語境中AI實踐的研究尚顯不足，學術界及行業層面均缺乏深入探討。因此，我們尚未明確律師如何在行業中使用AI、法律教育者與學生在學術環境中如何運用AI，亦未瞭解學術實踐能否有效幫助新手律師爲職業場景中的AI輔助寫作做好準備。本研究將以香港法律學術界及行業爲研究對象，旨在描述並闡釋AI話語實踐，分析這些實踐的關聯性及其習得過程。 本研究將采用質性主導的混合研究方法，使用順序性解釋設計，透過多數據源呈現話語與社會化實踐（即文本建構過程與學習過程）。數據包括：闡述AI專業與學術立場的社群文件（如專業機構發表的建議書）；對香港法律從業者（120人）、教育者（60人）和學生（60人）的定量問卷調查；與從業者、學者及學生的60次深度敘事訪談；20項模擬寫作任務的觀察記錄，以展示實際操作中的話語實踐。本研究將透過以下三個階段的實證分析，拓展對香港法律語境中AI話語實踐的理解：法學教育學術階段（如法學學士）、實務培訓階段（如法學專業證書課程）以及法律執業階段。在理論層面，本研究將構建一個學科專屬的人工智能素養模型，既揭示法律語境特有的話語過程，也探索跨學科的共性規律；此外，本研究將為特定學科語境中人工智能素養的研究提供方法論啓示。在實踐層面，本研究將評估法律畢業生是否已充分具備在行業中的AI實踐能力，並探討如何更有效滿足其需求。

11611525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11611525.value: 未知的協同效應：探索香港與深圳藝術科技生態系統的關係性空間

11611525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11611525.value: Prof GUO, Yingqi Dr Ou, Ying Dr Renaud, Clement Prof Turner, Fred

11611525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11611525.value: Abstract The convergence of artistic creativity and technological innovation is reshaping cultural, economic, and societal landscapes globally. This study focuses on the art-tech ecosystems of Hong Kong and Shenzhen, two cities rapidly emerging as innovation-driven creative hubs within the Greater Bay Area. Although both cities aim to establish themselves as global leaders in art-tech, their distinct political, economic, and technological environments create unique challenges and opportunities for art-tech creatives working in this cross-border area. Art-tech creatives merge artistic modes of production with technological expertise. They are agents of innovation across sectors, and they work as freelance workers, artists or creative technologists in art-tech firms or collectives, tech companies, startups, innovation hubs, design studios, educational institutions, cultural organizations Despite the rapid growth of technologies such as artificial intelligence, augmented reality, and blockchain, little research has explored how art-tech creatives in Hong Kong and Shenzhen are adapting to these advancements and the challenges they present. Moreover, while the Silicon Valley model has been globally dominant in shaping innovative ecosystems, it overlooks the unique socio-political and technocultural contexts of these two cities. Additionally, there is a limited understanding of how art-tech creatives negotiate their circulation across a diversity of space: institutional spaces, grassroots art-tech organizations, artistic, educational, for-profit sectors, and virtual platforms whose modes of algorithmic governance support/constrain project-based innovation models. To address these gaps, this three-year study adopts a concurrent mixed-methods approach, including policy analysis, ethnographic fieldwork, digital ethnography, and spatially-informed social network analysis. By integrating three theoretical frameworks—relational space theory, middleground theory, and hybrid spaces—the research will provide a comprehensive multi-layered analysis of how geopolitical and regulatory factors influence cross-border collaboration (macro-level), how institutional and informal networks mediate access to creative technologies (meso-level), and how creatives maintain agency within hybrid physical-digital spaces (micro-level). Findings from this study will offer both theoretical and practical insights into the cross-border innovation potential of Hong Kong and Shenzhen’s art-tech ecosystems. By illuminating the complex environments in which art-tech creatives operate, this research will contribute to a deeper understanding of how global innovation hubs can drive artistic and technological advancement through cross-sector and cross-border synergies. The study will also yield actionable policy recommendations aimed at improving access to creative technologies, addressing systemic and algorithmic biases, and fostering sustainable cross-border collaboration. These insights will be invaluable to policymakers, practitioners, and academics exploring the intersection of art, technology, and innovation. 藝術創意與科技創新的融合，正深刻地重塑全球的文化、經濟與社會景觀。鑑於香港與深圳正迅速崛起為大灣區內以創新驅動的創意樞紐，本研究聚焦於兩地的藝術與科技生態系統。儘管香港與深圳皆致力於成為全球藝術科技領域的領導者，兩地在政治、經濟與科技環境上的差異，為在此跨境區域工作的創作者帶來獨特的挑戰與機遇。 藝術科技創作者融合藝術生產模式與科技專業知識，作為跨界創新的行動者，活躍於自由工作者、藝術家、創意技術人員等多重角色之中，並分布於藝術科技企業或創作集體、科技公司、新創團隊、創新基地、設計工作室、教育機構及文化組織等多元空間。 儘管人工智能、擴增實境與區塊鏈等數碼技術迅速發展，針對香港與深圳的藝術科技創作者如何回應這些技術進展及其所帶來挑戰的研究仍然有限。此外，雖然矽谷模式在全球創新生態系統中佔據主導地位，卻忽略了香港與深圳所處的獨特社會政治與科技文化脈絡。對於創作者如何在多樣化的空間中進行流動與協商——包括制度性場域、草根藝術科技組織、藝術、教育與營利部門，以及受演算法治理所支持或限制的虛擬平台——目前的理解亦相當不足。 為填補上述研究空白，本研究將於三年期間採用同步混合方法，包括政策分析、民族誌田野調查、數碼民族誌與空間社會網絡分析。研究將整合三種理論視角——關係性空間理論、中介場域理論與混合空間理論——以提供多層次的綜合分析：宏觀層面探討地緣政治與監管因素如何影響跨境協作；中觀層面分析正式與非正式網絡如何形塑創意科技的可及性；微觀層面則聚焦創作者如何在混合的實體與數碼空間中展現行動能動性。 本研究成果將為香港與深圳藝術科技生態系統的跨境創新潛力提供理論與實務上的洞見。透過揭示創作者所處的複雜環境，研究將深化對全球創新樞紐如何透過跨界與跨境協同推動藝術與科技進展的理解。此外，研究亦將提出具體可行的政策建議，以改善創意科技的可及性、回應系統性與演算法偏誤，並促進可持續的跨境協作。此一洞見對於探討藝術、科技與創新交匯的政策制定者、實務工作者與學者而言，將具高度參考價值。

11611825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11611825.value: 韧性城市设计：基于证据的框架，以提升城市在危机情境下的适应力。

11611825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11611825.value: Prof Alan , Morris Prof Nakapan, Walaiporn

11611825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11611825.value: Urban environments face complex challenges due to rapid population growth, climate change, and public health crises, highlighted by recent events like the Covid-19 pandemic and natural disasters. This research proposal aims to investigate the intersection of urban design and resilience, focusing on the long-term impacts of simultaneous health and environmental emergencies on urban dynamics. A significant gap in the literature exists regarding frameworks that can assess design solutions from the perspective of resilience potential and performance. The research has three main objectives: first, to analyze the long-term impacts of pandemics and natural disasters on urban dynamics; second, to develop innovative design frameworks that address the spatial challenges posed by these crises; and third, to assess the effectiveness of these frameworks in promoting resilience and adaptability. To achieve these objectives, a mixed-methods approach will be employed, incorporating geospatial analysis, social media tracking, interactive surveys, and stakeholder engagement workshops. By triangulating findings from these diverse methods, the study will provide comprehensive insights into the unique vulnerabilities and resilience strategies in emerging urban contexts, which are often characterized by rapid urbanization, high population density, and inadequate infrastructure. Case studies in Thailand and the Philippines will illustrate these dynamics, identifying key patterns of behavior, accessibility, and social engagement in response to health and environmental emergencies. This investigation aims to reveal how urban spaces can be designed to foster community resilience, ensuring they are adaptable to immediate challenges and equipped to withstand future crises. The significance of this research lies in its potential to generate new knowledge that informs urban planning practices and policies. Developing evidence-based frameworks is essential for evaluating design solutions regarding urban resilience, allowing for broader applicability beyond the specific needs of emerging cities. Furthermore, this research will advance theoretical understandings of urban resilience by elucidating the interplay between health crises and environmental risks. By integrating various academic perspectives, the study will contribute to a cohesive body of knowledge that emphasizes the importance of adaptive urban design. Ultimately, this research seeks to enhance understanding of urban resilience, providing actionable strategies that improve community adaptability and promote sustainable urban development. The methodological rigor will ensure that insights gained can inform best practices in urban design, facilitating the creation of resilient urban spaces capable of withstanding future challenges. 由于人口快速增长、气候变化与公共卫生危机，城市环境正面临复杂挑战，近期的新冠肺炎（COVID-19）疫情和各类自然灾害进一步凸显了这一点。本研究计划旨在探究城市设计与韧性的交汇点，重点关注健康与环境紧急事件并发对城市系统动态的长期影响。在相关文献中，关于能够从韧性潜力与绩效角度评估设计方案的框架仍存在显著空白。本研究有三个主要目标：其一，分析疫情与自然灾害对城市系统动态的长期影响；其二，开发能够应对这些危机所带来空间挑战的创新设计框架；其三，评估上述框架在促进韧性与适应力方面的有效性。为实现上述目标，研究将采用混合方法，融合地理空间分析、社交媒体监测、互动式问卷以及利益相关方参与工作坊。通过对多种方法所得结果进行三角互证，研究将为新兴城市情境中的独特脆弱性与韧性策略提供全面洞见。这些情境通常具有快速城市化、高人口密度与基础设施不足等特征。泰国与菲律宾的案例研究将展示相关动态，识别在健康与环境紧急状态下的行为、可达性与社会参与等关键模式。本研究旨在揭示如何通过城市空间设计培育社区韧性，确保其既能适应即时挑战，又具备抵御未来危机的能力。其重要性在于有望生成指导城市规划实践与政策的新知识。构建基于证据的评估框架对于评估与城市韧性相关的设计方案至关重要，并使其具有超越新兴城市特定需求的更广泛适用性。此外，研究还将通过阐明健康危机与环境风险之间的相互作用，推进对城市韧性的理论认识。通过整合多元学术视角，本研究将构建更为连贯的知识体系，强调适应性城市设计的重要性。最终，本研究旨在深化对城市韧性的理解，提出可操作的策略，以提升社区的适应能力并促进可持续的城市发展。方法论的严谨性将确保所得洞见能够指导城市设计实践，推动构建能够经受未来挑战的韧性城市空间。

11611925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11611925.value: 公民對於在財政壓力下公共組織的責任感和可信度的看法：一項實驗研究

11611925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11611925.value: This project will use a randomized controlled trial to test how citizens assign responsibility for service cutbacks in the public sector, given different levels of information about causal responsibility (whose actions led to a particular outcome), latent transparency (the general level of public availability of information), and manifest transparency (specific information about a particular service or event). It will address two research questions: Does clarity of causal responsibility map onto citizens’ responsibility assignment? And does latent transparency provide a buffer against negative effects of manifest transparency on citizen assessments of public service provider trustworthiness? The project will extend and generalize published research co-authored by the principal investigator. Governments in many jurisdictions increasingly seek to provide detailed accounts to citizens about how public services are funded and delivered. At the same time, citizens’ assessment of the trustworthiness of public organizations are low or declining, which has implications for the viability of complex public policies. Two active literatures address how citizens’ respond to transparency overall and how citizens’ assign responsibility for public service problems. There is strong evidence in the former literature that transparency has mixed effects on citizens’ assessments of public organizations and services, clearly showing that more openness per se is no panacea. The latter literature shows a variety of citizen responses to information about who is formally and who is factually responsible for problems, showing that blame is not always placed toward those causally responsible for a problem. At the intersection of these two literatures emerges a set of questions about which types and levels of information about public services maximize accurate responsibility attribution by citizens and underpin their assessments of the trustworthiness of public organizations and services. The proposed project aims to answer these questions. The project proceeds in two phases. First, vignettes about the fiscal conditions of a highly salient public service will be developed and pilot tested to achieve both a high degree of salience to study participants and a valid and reliable representation of the key theoretical concepts. Second, a between-subjects randomized controlled trial will be conducted in two community halls in different public housing estates. The data will be collected under controlled, distraction-free conditions to estimate treatment effects. 本項目將采用隨機對照試驗，測試在瞭解不同程度的因果責任信息（即誰的行為導致了特定結果）、潛在透明度（信息的總體公開程度）和顯性透明度（關於特定服務或事件的具體信息）的情況下，公民如何為公共部門服務削減分配責任。該項目將解決兩個研究問題：因果責任的清晰度是否會反映在公民的責任分配上？潛在透明度是否能緩衝顯性透明度對公民對公共服務提供者的可信度評估的負面影響？該項目將擴展和推廣由首席研究員共同撰寫并已發表的研究成果。 許多司法管轄區的政府越來越多地尋求向公民詳細説明公共服務的資金來源和提供方式。與此同時，公民對公共組織的可信度的評價較低或在不斷下降，這會對複雜公共政策的可行性產生影響。有兩個活躍的文獻流派分別探討公民對透明度的整體回應，以及公民如何為公共服務問題分配責任。前者的文獻有強有力的證據表明，透明度對公民對公共組織和服務的評價具有混合的效用，清楚地表明，增加開放性本身并非萬靈藥。後者的文獻展示了公民對“誰在形式上以及實際上對問題負責”這類信息的各種反應，顯示責任並不總是歸咎於那些對問題負有因果責任的人。在這兩個文獻流派的交叉點上，出現了一系列問題，即探討關於公共服務的哪些類型和層次的信息能最大程度上提高公民對責任的準確歸因，並支撐他們對公共組織和服務的可信度的評價。擬議的項目旨在回答這些問題。 該項目分為兩個階段進行。首先，將開發關於一項極具關注度的公共服務財政狀況的案例描述并進行試點測試，以確保既讓研究參與者高度關注，又能有效且可靠地呈現關鍵理論概念。其次，將在不同公共屋邨的兩個社區會堂進行組間隨機對照試驗。數據將在可控、無干擾的條件下收集，以評估處理效應。

12100125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12100125.value: 用於成骨不全症的下一代口服精準硬骨抑素抑制劑

12100125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12100125.value: Dr Wang, Luyao Prof ZHANG, Ge

12100125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100125.value: Sclerostin represents a promising therapeutic target for bone anabolic therapies. Romosozumab, the first FDA-approved sclerostin inhibitor, blocks sclerostin loop2-LRP5/6 interaction by targeting loop2, which effectively treats osteoporosis. However, increased cardiovascular risks in clinical trials limit its use. Recently, we found that sclerostin could antagonize bone anabolic through sclerostin loop3-LRP4 interaction, and protect the cardiovascular system through sclerostin loop2-LRP8 interaction in macrophages, respectively. We proposed a precise sclerostin inhibition strategy that specifically blocks loop3-LRP4 interaction while maintaining loop2-LRP8 interaction to promote bone formation without elevating cardiovascular concerns. We have identified four key residues within loop3 for loop3-LRP4 interaction used by sclerostin to suppress osteogenic potential in MC3T3-E1 cells (osteoblasts). We then designed a small-molecular inhibitor (PA-Hit B) targeting loop3, which was predicted to bind above four key residues. In vitro, PA-Hit B completely blocked loop3-LRP4 interaction and demonstrated a superior inhibitory potency against sclerostin's suppressive effect on osteogenic potential than romosozumab. As expected, PA-Hit B maintained loop2-LRP8 interaction and did not influence inflammatory cytokines in macrophages, whereas romosozumab did. In osteogenesis imperfecta (OI, Col1a2+/G610C) mice, PA-Hit B promoted bone formation in a dose-dependent manner, outperforming romosozumab. To be noted, PA-Hit B had a long half-life (12h) and high oral bioavailability (62.11%) in healthy rats. Importantly, as a small molecule, PA-Hit B is a promising candidate for developing the next-generation orally administered precise sclerostin inhibitor. Thus, we hypothesized that PA-Hit B could exert bone anabolic potential without elevating cardiovascular risk in OI mice via specifically blocking loop3-LRP4 interaction. Our in vitro mechanistic studies showed that PA-Hit B promoted osteogenic potential in MC3T3-E1 cells via specifically blocking loop3-LRP4 interaction. Consistently, in vivo data from a small sample size of OI mice indicated that PA-Hit B promoted bone formation via the same mechanism. Four objectives will be achieved to further test the hypothesis. In Objectives 1 & 2, we will evaluate, in a larger sample size of OI mice, whether PA-Hit B exerts its bone anabolic potential via specifically blocking loop3-LRP4 interaction. This will be evaluated through pretreatment with blocking peptide designed based on key residues within loop3, and by replacing PA-Hit B with its variant, respectively. In Objective 3, we will assess whether PA-Hit B increases cardiovascular concerns in hSOSTTg.Col1a2+/G610C.ApoE-/- mice. In Objective 4, we will investigate its long-term safety profile in normal rats.
