The circulation of global and regional media flows and cultural influences of popular culture facilitate new understandings of gender identities. This study proposes to explore trans and non-binary experiences on social media among Hong Kong, Singapore and Taiwan youth. Yet at the same time, trans and non-binary youth face disproportionately higher-incidence of violence in daily life and seek community support online more frequently than other populations in the queer spectrum. Studies have often mentioned the positive support transgender people receive online. But online spaces are not always safe for trans people. Sharing daily life experiences and sensitive personal information can expose transgender persons to technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) including bullying, doxing and hateful comments, among others. In Asia-Pacific region, online violence against women sits at a prevalence rate of 88%. Research on TFGBV tends to focus more on cis-gender women and girls. There is emerging recognition that transgender, non-binary and gender-nonconforming persons are at risk of TFGBV and in need of further research. Instead of focusing on only TFGBV prevalence, we aim to examine wider online experiences of trans and non-binary youth in order to understand those who live and negotiate with TFGBV. We propose a sequential mixed-methods approach to collecting data on the use of digital technologies and the prevalence of TFGBV among trans and non-binary youth. We will conduct 90 (30 from each research site) in-depth interviews and 9 focus groups (3 each site) with trans and non-binary youth, service providers and stakeholders. We will also conduct a survey across three sites. The proposed project will: (1) analyse social and cultural meanings of being trans and non-binary; (2) broaden the scope of technology-facilitated gender-based violence by including trans and non-binary youth experiences in Asia; (3) engage multiple stakeholders on social media platform accountability and transparency measures for supporting trans and non-binary youth. 跨性別者一直在社交媒體平台上尋求資訊、支持和建立社區。近年來，跨性別和非二元性別者更積極表達自己的性別認同並尋找有關資訊。跨性別和非二元性別青年在日常生活中面對許多歧視和暴力對待，導致他們更頻繁在社交媒體平台上尋求支持。分享日常生活經歷和敏感個人信息可能使跨性別者暴露於數位/網路性別暴力（TFGBV），包括跟蹤、曝光私人信息、騷擾和網路霸凌。本研究目標旨在理解香港、新加坡、台灣跨性別和非二元性別青年在線經歷，以便更了解TFGBV現象。 我們提出混合方法研究來收集有關跨性別和非二元性別青年使用數位/網路包括社交媒體平台和TFGBV盛行率的數據。我們將與跨性別和非二元性別青年和社區服務提供者進行深入訪談和焦點小組討論。此項目將：（1）分析跨性別和非二元性別身份的社會和文化意義；（2）通過納入亞洲跨性別和非二元性別青年的經歷，理解數位/網路促成的性別暴力範圍；（3）與多方利益相關者合作，就數位/網路平台責任和透明度措施進行交流。

13610225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13610225.value: 為何個體之間觀察面孔方式不盡相同

13610225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13610225.value: Prof Hsiao, Janet Hui-wen Dr Schwarzkopf, Sam

13610225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13610225.value: One of the core tasks of the human perception system is to encode information about other people’s faces, in order to recognize them, speak to them, empathise with them, understand their intentions, and classify them as being from our own group or a different group. Curiously, for such a key cognitive skill, there is no single way in which we scan a face, but rather, we use idiosyncratic patterns that can provide differential access to visual information. In this project, we seek the first systematic study of the nature of these fixation differences, and how they map on to other individual differences in cognition, perception, and social anxiety. We will use cutting-edge computational methods to classify the fixation patterns of different observers, and then will test an array of experimental methods to examine associations with the idiosyncratic fixation patterns. First, we will examine how individual differences in eye-movements relate to known group differences, due to cultural factors, psychopathology, and face recognition ability. Second, we will study how differences in fixation patterns for faces may be related to idiosyncratic differences in more fundamental aspects of spatial processing. Third, we will determine the sensitivity of idiosyncratic fixation patterns to the studied information about a face and body, and their relationship with measures of holistic face processing. Taken together, the experiments in this proposal will give us a deep understanding of the nature of idiosyncratic fixation patterns in viewing faces, and how such differences are related to other cognitive and perceptual functions.

13611425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13611425.value: 數碼說故事融入英語課堂：促進學生全人發展

13611425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13611425.value: Prof CHEN, Sylvia Xiaohua Prof Chiu, Ming Ming Prof Gao, Xuesong Andy Dr Hafner, Christoph Prof HAYWARD, William Prof King, Ronnel Bornasal Dr Kwong, Theresa Prof Lai, Chun

13611425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13611425.value: Hong Kong students often grapple with stress, anxiety, and isolation due to complex social factors, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Recognising the critical role of fostering positive values and attitudes in education, the Curriculum Development Council (CDC) (2022) in Hong Kong has mandated the integration of value education across all subjects, including English. Despite the proliferation of research in technology-enhanced language teaching and learning, a significant gap remains in understanding the intersection of technology integration and its potential to influence value education within English language classrooms. This study aims to bridge this gap by exploring how technology can enhance both second language acquisition (SLA) and the holistic development of primary school students in Hong Kong. Situated within the theoretical framework of Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST) (Larsen-Freeman, 2006), this research will investigate the multifaceted ways in which technology can be leveraged to foster both SLA and the development of core values among learners. The focus will be on the holistic development of primary school students in Hong Kong, encompassing positive psychology (character strengths and well-being), SLA (L2 enjoyment and L2 anxiety), and student learning (active learning and critical thinking). A mixed-methods design involving a controlled experiment with statistical matching and qualitative interviews will be employed. The study will be conducted in four public schools, involving 400 native Chinese-speaking Primary 4-5 students. The intervention will include teaching stories through digital storytelling (DST), enriched with technology-enhanced language teaching and learning, alongside traditional methods. Quantitative data on holistic development will be collected using validated scales before and after the intervention. Qualitative data will be gathered through interviews with students, teachers, and principals. This research will introduce an innovative, replicable, and research-worthy analytical framework (Ecosystem Learning Model) and practice (DST as a multimodal approach). This study will provide meaningful insights into how value education can be infused into English language curricula, offering new directions for curriculum development in the digital era. The findings will generate theoretical principles regarding the application of DST as an innovative pedagogy and provide insightful recommendations for school teachers, principals, and policymakers. By addressing the gap in literature and demonstrating the synergistic effects of technology on both SLA and student well-being, this research will contribute significantly to the field of education. It will offer practical solutions for integrating value education into English language teaching, ultimately enhancing the holistic development of students in Hong Kong. 香港學生常因複雜的社會因素而面臨壓力、焦慮與孤立感，而這些情況在新冠疫情期間更加惡化。香港課程發展議會（CDC）（2022）認識到在教育中培養正面價值觀與態度的重要性，因此已規定在所有科目中（包括英文科）融入價值教育。儘管科技輔助語言教學的研究日益增多，學界對「科技整合」與「英語課堂價值教育」的交叉研究仍存明顯空白。本研究旨在填補此空白，探索科技如何同時促進第二語言習得（SLA）及香港小學生的全人發展。 本研究基於Larsen-Freeman（2006）提出的「複雜動態系統理論」（CDST）框架，探究運用科技協同發展第二語言能力與核心價值觀的多維路徑。研究聚焦香港小學生的全人發展，涵蓋三大範疇：正向心理學（性格優勢與幸福感）、二語習得（學習愉悅感與焦慮感）、以及學習效能（主動學習與批判性思考）。 本研究採用混合研究方法設計，結合統計配對的控制實驗與質性訪談。研究將在四所公立學校進行，對象為400名以中文為母語的小四至小五學生。教學介入將透過「數碼說故事」（Digital Storytelling, DST）進行，結合科技輔助語言教學與傳統教學方法。量化數據將透過驗證量表在介入前後收集學生的全人發展情況；質性數據則透過訪談學生、教師與校長取得。 本研究將提出一個創新、可複製且具研究價值的分析框架（生態系統學習模型）與實踐方法（DST作為多模態教學方式）。研究結果能為價值教育融入英語課程提供實證依據，開拓數位時代課程發展新方向。研究結果建立DST創新教學法的理論原則，並為教師、校長及政策制定者提供實踐建議。通過揭示科技對語言習得與學生福祉的協同效應，填補文獻空白。本研究將為教育領域作出重要貢獻，提供英語教學融合價值教育的實踐方案，最終促進香港學生的全人發展。

14100225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14100225.value: Vangl 在內質網自噬中的作用

14100225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14100225.value: Prof DUAN, Liting Prof Ti, Shih Chieh

14100225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100225.value: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is the largest membrane-bound organelle in eukaryotic cells, responsible for many fundamental cellular functions such as protein/lipid synthesis, protein quality control, and ion homeostasis. To maintain its integrity and functionality, the ER undergoes constant turnover and modulation. ER-phagy, a process that selectively recognizes and degrades ER compartments in response to physiological or pathological stress, is essential for ER homeostasis. This ER-specific autophagy is mediated by ER-phagy receptors that bind both ER regions and LC3/GABARAP family members on autophagosomal membranes. Our current understanding of ER-phagy regulation and its molecular mechanisms remains limited. Vangl1 and Vangl2 are core components of planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling that governs a diverse array of polarized cell behaviors during embryonic development and adult tissue homeostasis. The disruption and aberrant activation of Vangl have been strongly implicated in a variety of developmental defects and cancers. Vangl are tetraspan membrane proteins that mainly localize on the plasma membrane of planar polarized cells. Unexpectedly, we found that a large portion of endogenous Vangl2 localized in the ER in multiple cell types, prompting us to investigate what function Vangl2 is serving in the ER. Our proteomic analysis of Vangl2 identified many ER-resident proteins that may interact with Vangl2, including ER-phagy receptors such as TEX264. Our preliminary data suggest that Vangl may inhibit ER-phagy, potentially through direct binding to LC3C via conserved LIR/CLIR motifs, leading to our hypothesis that Vangl plays an important role in regulating ER-phagy. To address this hypothesis, we will first validate the subcellular localization of Vangl and define its role and specificity in regulating ER-phagy. We will then elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, examining whether the effect of Vangl on ER-phagy is mediated by ER-phagy receptors, the Vangl-LC3C interaction, or both. Lastly, we will assess the functional significance of Vangl-mediated ER-phagy in ER remodeling and breast cancer progression. This study will reveal a novel function of Vangl in the ER, providing new insights into the regulatory mechanism of ER-phagy. 內質網是真核細胞中最大型的膜性細胞器，承擔蛋白質和脂質合成、蛋白質質量控制以及離子穩態維持等關鍵生命活動。為確保其結構完整性與功能狀態，內質網需進行持續的更新與重塑。內質網自噬（ER-phagy）是一種在生理或病理應激條件下選擇性識別並降解特定內質網區域的過程，是維持內質網穩態的重要機制。該過程由特異性的 ER-phagy 受體介導，這些受體可同時結合內質網及自噬體膜上的 LC3/GABARAP 蛋白家族成員。然而，當前對於 ER-phagy 的調控機制及其分子基礎的認識仍然有限。 Vangl1 和 Vangl2 是平面細胞極性（planar cell polarity, PCP）信號通路的核心組分，在胚胎髮育及成體組織穩態中調控多種極化細胞行為。Vangl 功能缺失或異常激活分別與多種發育缺陷及腫瘤發生密切相關。作為四跨膜蛋白，Vangl 蛋白通常位於平面極化細胞的質膜。然而，我們意外發現，在多種細胞類型中，大量內源性 Vangl2 蛋白定位於內質網，這提示其在內質網中可能發揮重要功能。通過蛋白質組學分析，我們鑒定到多種可能與 Vangl2 相互作用的內質網駐留蛋白，包括 ER-phagy 受體 TEX264。初步研究結果顯示，Vangl 可能通過其保守的 LIR/CLIR 基序直接結合 LC3C，從而抑制 ER-phagy。據此，我們提出假設：Vangl 在 ER-phagy 調控中發揮重要作用。 本研究擬首先驗證 Vangl 的亞細胞定位，並系統解析其在 ER-phagy 調控中的作用及特異性；隨後探討其分子機制，包括其作用是否通過 ER-phagy 受體、Vangl-LC3C 相互作用或二者共同介導；最後評估 Vangl 介導的 ER-phagy 在內質網重塑及乳腺癌進展中的功能意義。本研究將揭示 Vangl 在內質網中的新功能，深化對 ER-phagy 調控機制的理解，並為相關疾病機制研究提供新的理論基礎。

14101125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14101125.value: 運用新型不均勻磁化轉移成像技術無創評估腎臟纖維化

14101125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14101125.value: Dr Chang, Hing Chiu Charles Dr Ni, Yunbi Prof Szeto, Cheuk-Chun

14101125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101125.value: Aim To design an advanced inhomogeneous magnetization transfer (ihMT) MR sequence dedicated to kidney, and to apply the proposed renal ihMT to measure collagen content for non-invasive assessment of renal fibrosis. Background Inhomogeneous magnetization transfer (ihMT), as a refinement of magnetization transfer (MT), enables to isolate dipolar order effects within motion-restricted molecules, weighted by the dipolar relaxation time (T1D). Tissue-intrinsic T1D relaxation can provide quantitative information of molecular dynamics and organization, and is more sensitive to the slow motional processes inaccessible to standard T1 and T2 relaxation. Neither external device nor contrast agent injection is required for ihMT. Investigation of long-T1D components elicits enormous enthusiasm, primarily focused on depicting myelin deficit. In contrast, ex-vivo imaging data concerning equally important short-T1D components remain scarce, let alone in-vivo data. Thus far, a widespread use of ihMT is still not on the horizon, and organ-specific applications of ihMT have not yet been extended to human kidney. The key pathological hallmark of fibrosis is excessive accumulation of collagen, intrinsically showing strong MT effect. The majority of existing MRI sequences lacks sufficient specificity for renal fibrosis. So, hope is pinned on the molecular imaging with higher specificity. Vigorous evidence implies that there is a possibility of harnessing ihMT to non-invasively probe into collagen level. Methodology In total, 230 subjects will be prospectively recruited, consisting of 30 healthy volunteers, 100 patients undergoing renal biopsy, 100 patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Firstly, reliability of renal ihMT will be determined on volunteers. Secondly, diagnostic performance for renal fibrosis will be compared across MR sequences (ihMT, ultrashort echo time, macromolecular proton fraction), taking renal biopsy as gold standard. Kidney specimen will undergo morphometric analysis for collagen quantification. Thirdly, the relationship between ihMT measurements and deterioration in renal hemodynamic will be investigated. Fourthly, ihMT measurements will be correlated with CKD severity, progression, and regression. Project Significance The most significant and beneficial impact lies in the first utilization of ihMT imaging for evaluating collagen content change in highly vascularized kidney on MR images, which paves the way for translating ihMT metric to a new clinically applicable biomarker of renal fibrosis.

14101725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14101725.value: 揭示ADAT2介導的RNA A-to-I修飾在結直腸腫瘤發生和抗藥性中的作用

14101725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14101725.value: Dr Chen, Huarong Prof Yu, Jun

14101725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101725.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common cancers in Hong Kong. Although genetic and epigenetic alterations of CRC are well-characterized, post-transcriptional mechanisms involved in colorectal tumorigenesis remains elusive. Transfer RNA (tRNA) is an integral part of the protein translation machinery in cells, and their activity is tightly modulated by a myriad of chemical modifications. Here, our systematic survey of tRNA modifications demonstrated that A-to-I modification as being most significantly induced in CRC tumors. Correspondingly, adenosine deaminase tRNA specific 2 (ADAT2), a deaminase catalyzing A-to-I conversion of tRNAs at position 34, is overexpressed in CRC and correlates with patient prognosis in multiple CRC cohorts. Preliminary studies in CRC cells revealed that ADAT2 overexpression promotes cell proliferation and colony formation in vitro, and tumorigenicity in vivo, whereas ADAT2 knockout exerts opposite functions, suggesting an oncogenic role of ADAT2 in CRC. In line with this notion, whole-body ADAT2 knockout in mice impaired chemically-induced colorectal tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, domain-focused CRISPR/Cas9 screening identified that pro- proliferative effect of ADAT2 is dependent on its deaminase domain, inferring ADAT2-driven tRNA A-to-I conversion underlies its oncogenic function. We thus performed integrated tRNA-sequencing, RNA-sequencing and Ribosome-sequencing in ADAT2-overexpressing/knockout CRC cells to probe the ADAT2-associated translatome. This revealed that ADAT2 profoundly impacts three tRNA anticodons, encoding for the translation of Ser (TCC), Leu (CTC), and Arg (CGC) codons on mRNAs. Next, pathway enrichment analysis showed that ADAT2 boosts oncogenic translation involved in WNT/β-catenin signaling, and overlapping of gene candidates with elevated translation efficiency by ADAT2 together with a high abundance of A-to-I-dependent codons uncovered HDAC7 as an ADAT2 target. Pilot studies showed that HDAC7 functions downstream of ADAT2 to promote cell proliferation and WNT/β-catenin signaling. In terms of translational value, we demonstrated that targeting ADAT2 improves chemosensitivity in CRC cells. These results led us to hypothesize that ADAT2-mediated tRNA A-to-I modification plays an essential role in CRC development and chemoresistance. To address this, we propose four objectives: 1) To determine the function of ADAT2 in CRC in colon-specific Adat2 knockin and knockout mice; 2) To decipher the molecular mechanisms of ADAT2 in CRC through tRNA A-to-I modification; 3) To evaluate ADAT2 as a therapeutic target in CRC; and 4) To investigate the clinical significance of ADAT2 in CRC. These studies will offer insights into the role of tRNA A-to-I modification in colorectal tumorigenesis and its translational impact as a therapeutic target and biomarker in CRC. 大腸直腸癌 (CRC) 是香港最常見的癌症之一。轉移 RNA (tRNA) 是細胞蛋白質翻譯機制的重要組成部分，其活性受到多種化學修飾的嚴格調控。本研究對 tRNA 修飾進行了系統性研究，結果顯示A-to-I 的修飾在 CRC 腫瘤中最為顯著。Adenosine Deaminase TRNA Specific 2 (ADAT2)，一種催化 34 位 tRNA A 到 I 轉化的脫氨酶，在 CRC 中高表達，並與CRC 患者群體的預後相關。初步研究表明，ADAT2促進細胞增殖，集落形成和腫瘤發生髮展，而ADAT2敲除則發揮相反的作用，提示ADAT2在CRC中具有致癌作用。我們在ADAT2過度表現/敲除的CRC細胞中進行了tRNA定序、RNA定序和核醣體定序，以探討ADAT2對翻譯的影響。這顯示 ADAT2 對三種 tRNA 反密碼子有顯著影響。路徑富集分析顯示 ADAT2 促進參與 WNT/β-catenin 訊號傳導的翻譯，並且提高HDAC7的翻譯效率。初步研究顯示 HDAC7 在 ADAT2 下游發揮作用，促進細胞增殖和 WNT/β-catenin 訊號傳導。另外，我們證明靶向 ADAT2 可提高 CRC 細胞對化療的敏感性。這些結果使我們假設 ADAT2 介導的 tRNA A-to-I 修飾在 CRC 發展和化療抗藥性中起著至關重要的作用。為此，我們提出了三個研究目標：1)構建結腸Adat2 敲入和敲除小鼠，確定 ADAT2 在結直腸癌中的功能；2) 闡明 ADAT2 透過 tRNA A-to-I修飾在結直腸癌中的分子機制；3) 評估 ADAT2 作為結直腸癌治療靶點的可能性；4) 探究 ADAT2在大腸直腸癌中的臨床意義。這些研究將有助於深入了解 tRNA A-to-I 修飾在結直腸腫瘤發生中的作用，以及其作為結直腸癌治療標靶和生物標記的臨床意義。

14101925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14101925.value: DNA損傷反應與阿黴素誘導的心臟毒性之間的關係

14101925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14101925.value: Dr Ni, Yunbi Dr Vong, Si Long Joaquim Dr Wong, Ka Lam, Michael Prof Yan, Bryan

14101925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101925.value: DNA damage caused by doxorubicin (DOX), a widely used anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent, contributes to degenerative cardiotoxicity. DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DCT) is mostly attributed to DNA damage-mediated cell death during and shortly after DOX treatment. To date, research has focused mainly on the acute phases of DOX injury, to identify prophylactic strategies that prevent cell death. However, DCT often manifests years after DOX treatment. Very few studies have focused on the long-term sequalae of DCT or possible therapeutic interventions to ameliorate DCT in patients. Upon DNA damage, cells can initiate the DNA damage response (DDR), which comprises the activation of mediators such as ataxia-telangiectasia mutated kinase (ATM) to repair DNA lesions. While transient DDR activation is critical to maintain genomic stability, persistent DDR can promote apoptosis and cellular senescence, and it has been implicated in many cardiovascular disorders. Using cardiomyocytes (CMs) differentiated from patient-derived, DOX-sensitive human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), we discovered that DOX can induce persistent DDR, and this is associated with a transcriptomic and cellular phenotype indicative of cardiac dysfunction. Pharmaceutical inhibition of ATM after DOX treatment reduced DDR protein expression and improved mitochondrial function and sarcomere disarray. In line with these in vitro results, pilot in vivo mouse experiments showed that transient ATM inhibition applied weeks after DOX treatment led to the sustained improvement of cardiac function. We hypothesise that persistent activation of the DDR contributes to the long-term sequelae of DCT and is a therapeutic target for DCT. In this proposal, we will conduct gain/loss of function experiments in hiPSC-CMs and mice to confirm that ATM promotes the sequalae of DCT in vitro and in vivo, and conduct spatial transcriptomic analysis of patient cardiac samples to reveal the association between DDR dysregulation and DCT-heart failure. Ours is the first study on the role of the DDR on the long-term sequalae DCT. Once completed, our study will fill critical knowledge gaps surrounding the cellular and molecular events that occur after DOX exposure and provide important proof of principle data that DCT can be specifically and therapeutically targeted post DOX treatment. 阿黴素（Doxorubicin, DOX）是一種廣泛使用的蒽環類化療藥物，但可能損害 DNA 並引起心臟毒性。DOX起的心臟毒性（Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity, DCT）主要歸因於DNA損傷所引發的細胞死亡。迄今為止，研究主要集中在預防細胞死亡的預防性策略。然而，DCT常常在DOX治療多年後才顯現。針對DCT的長期後遺症或可能的治療干預措施，目前研究仍然非常有限。 當DNA受損時，細胞會啟動DNA損傷反應（DNA Damage Response, DDR），其中包括激活Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated kinase (ATM)以修復DNA損傷。雖然短暫的DDR活化對維持基因組穩定性至關重要，但持續的DDR可能促進細胞凋亡與細胞衰老，並與多種心血管疾病有關。使用人類多能幹細胞衍生的心肌細胞模型(hiPSC-CMs)，我們發現DOX能誘導持續性的DDR，並影響細胞功能。抑制ATM的藥物可降低DDR蛋白表達，並改善粒線體功能。初步的小鼠實驗顯示，在DOX治療數週後短暫抑制ATM，可改善心臟功能。 在這個提案中，我們使用hiPSC-CMs與小鼠確認ATM對DCT的影響，以揭示DDR失調與DCT心衰之間的關聯。一旦完成，我們的研究將提供重要的原理驗證數據，證明DCT可在DOX治療後進行特定且具療效的干預。

14103525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14103525.value: 雙相情感障礙患者子女黑視素介導瞳孔反應與晝夜節律紊亂的研究

14103525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14103525.value: Dr Chan, Ngan Yin Dr Chong, Kam Lung Kelvin Dr Li, Man-ho Dr Li , Shirley Xin Dr Or, Brian Parr-Ning Prof Roecklein, Kathryn Ariel Dr Shea, Caroline Ka-sin Prof Wing, Yun Kwok

14103525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103525.value: Objective: To investigate if the post-illumination pupillary response (PIPR) is altered among adolescent offspring of patients with bipolar disorder (BD) and its association with circadian disturbance, sleep and emotional-behavioural symptoms. Background: Light signal is transmitted through the intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cell (ipRGCs), which project to brain areas that regulate melatonin secretion, sleep and emotion. ipRGC are particularly sensitive to blue light, leading to a sustained pupillary constriction known as the PIPR, a non-invasive marker of the retinal light responsivity. Research indicates that patients with BD exhibit supersensitivity to light, and a stronger PIPR response was associated with emotional-behavior traits of BD among healthy young subjects. Our study further revealed greater sleep and circadian disturbances along with lower nocturnal melatonin levels among unaffected bipolar offspring (O-BD), which are compatible with the observation of a greater light sensitivity in BD. The present proposal aims to measure retinal sensitivity to light using established pupillometry methods in unmedicated O-BD and control offspring (O-HC). Hypothesis: 1) PIPR will be stronger in O-BD than in O-HC. 2) Stronger PIPR will be associated with later dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) and reduced salivary melatonin area under the curve. Secondary hypotheses: Stronger PIPR will correlate with later chronotype, delayed actigraphic sleep pattern, increased emotional and behavioural problems. Participants: Fifty unmedicated and unaffected (those never been diagnosed with mood or psychotic disorder) O-BD aged–12–18 years old and 50 age-gender matched healthy O-HC. Methods: This case control study will assess eligible family participants by structural clinical interviews to ascertain presence of BD and other psychiatric disorders. O-BD are offspring having at least one biological parent meeting a lifetime or current diagnosis of BD in the structured clinical interview. Eligible offspring will be invited to complete questionnaires on sleep, chronotype, emotional and behavioral problems. They will wear actiwatch for seven days and maintain a sleep diary. PIPR will be conducted on Day 6 and saliva samples for DLMO will be collected at home on the evening of Day 7. Group differences will be examined by Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) models. Anticipated results and impact: We expect PIPR to be more pronounced in O-BD and associates with sleep and circadian disturbances. This research will illuminate the role of retinal light sensitivity in the pathophysiology of BD, and to establish a biomarker of sleep and circadian disturbances, facilitating early identification, prevention and intervention in this high-risk population. 研究目標 調查患有雙相情感障礙（BD）患者的青少年子女，其光照後瞳孔反應（PIPR）有否發生變化，並探討其與晝夜節律紊亂、睡眠和情緒行為症狀的關係。 背景 光信號通過內源性光敏視網膜神經節細胞（ipRGCs）傳遞，ipRGCs與大腦調控褪黑素分泌、睡眠及情緒的區域相連。ipRGCs對藍光特別敏感，會引發一種持續的瞳孔收縮反應，即光照後瞳孔反應（PIPR），可作為評估視網膜光敏性的非侵入性生物標誌。研究顯示，BD患者對光特別敏感，而在健康年輕人中，更強的PIPR與BD的情緒行為特徵有所關聯。我們的研究發現，未表現出BD症狀的患者子女（O-BD）存在更嚴重的睡眠和晝夜節律紊亂，以及較低的夜間褪黑素水平，這與BD患者更高的光敏感性一致。本研究擬採用瞳孔測量方法，在未服藥的O-BD和健康對照子女（O-HC）中測量視網膜對光的敏感性。 假設 1. O-BD的PIPR強度高於O-HC。 2. 更強的PIPR與更晚的暗光褪黑素起始（DLMO）及較低的唾液褪黑素總量相關。 次要假設： 1. 更強的PIPR與更晚的時型、延遲的活動睡眠模式、以及更多的情緒和行為問題相關。 參與者 • O-BD組：50名年齡在12–18歲之間、未服藥、未被診斷為情感或精神障礙的雙相情感障礙患者子女。 • O-HC組：50名與O-BD組年齡、性別匹配的健康對照子女。 方法 本研究首先以結構化臨床訪談評估家庭中是否存在雙相情感障礙（BD）或其他精神疾病，O-BD定義為至少有一名生物父母經臨床診斷為BD的子女。接著，透過問卷調查蒐集受試者的睡眠習慣、時型以及其情緒與行為問題等相關數據。所有參與者需連續七天配戴活動記錄儀（actiwatch），並同步填寫睡眠日誌；第六天進行光照後瞳孔反應（PIPR）評估，第七晚則於家中收集唾液標本，以測量暗時褪黑素開始分泌（DLMO）時點及褪黑素濃度。最後，資料分析部分則採用廣義估計方程（GEE）模型來比較組間差異。 預期結果與影響 我們預計O-BD的PIPR更強，並與睡眠和晝夜節律紊亂相關。該研究將揭示視網膜光敏感性在BD發病機制中的作用，有望成為睡眠和晝夜節律紊亂的生物標誌，幫助早期識別、預防和干預高風險群體。

14103825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14103825.value: 植物細胞去黃化過程中光激活的脂滴快速利用

14103825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103825.value: Lipid droplets are organelles that store lipids in eukaryotic cells, contributing to energy metabolism regulation. In plants, particularly oilseed species, these droplets provide essential fats that support seedling growth during darkness when photosynthesis is not possible. Lipid droplets consist of hydrophobic lipids surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer and surface proteins, mostly oleosins in plants. During germination, these droplets release fatty acids, which are then metabolized in peroxisomes to generate energy and building blocks for growth. Autophagy is an intracellular process that manages the turnover of cellular components. It includes various mechanisms, such as macroautophagy, characterized by autophagosomes that selectively engulf substrates, and microautophagy, which directly incorporates cytoplasmic material into lysosomes or vacuoles. ATG8 and autophagy receptors are key factors for recognizing and targeting specific substrates for degradation. NBR1 is a soluble selective autophagy receptor that connects ubiquitinated proteins to ATG8 when autophagy is activated. The protein is conserved among eukaryotes and play roles in selective autophagy in plant cells. Lipophagy refers to the selective autophagic degradation of lipid droplets. It is crucial for supply of energy and carbon skeletons for cell homeostasis and stress responses during energy-demanding phases. Molecular mechanisms of lipophagy in plants are still not well understood, underscoring a gap in current research. Our preliminary data indicate that NBR1 and GFP-ATG8e colocalized with lipid droplets in etiolated seedling cells within an hour of illumination. Electron microscopy showed that lipid droplets are engulfed by the vacuole, indicating their elimination via microautophagy. A lipid droplet protein, oleosin2 remains stable in darkness but rapidly disappears after exposure to light. Lipid droplet digestion is delayed in nbr1 and atg8 mutant seedlings. Furthermore, nbr1 and a V-type ATPase mutant showed similar defects in lipid droplet removal, suggesting they are involved in the same pathway. We hypothesize that light-induced ubiquitination of oleosins and lipidation of ATG8 are required for micro-lipophagy in de-etiolating seedling cells. Furthermore, we speculate that NBR1 and V-ATPase facilitate the protein modifications required for the process. We will test the hypothesis with biochemical and genetic approaches together with high resolution microscopy imaging. Outputs from our study will shed novel lights on molecular players mediating recycling of nutrient reserves in seeds and how plant cells reorganize their internal constituents. This knowledge can lead to the development of improved crop varieties with optimized oil content and stress responses. Additionally, insights gained can foster sustainable agricultural practices and environmental conservation. 脂滴是廣泛存在於真核細胞中的能量儲存細胞器，主要功能在於儲存中性脂類並參與細胞能量代謝的調控。在植物中，尤其是油料作物，脂滴作為幼苗在黑暗條件下（光合作用尚未啟動）生長所必需的能量和碳源，具有至關重要的作用。脂滴由疏水性脂類構成，其外層包裹一層磷脂單分子層，並結合特異性表面蛋白質，在植物中主要為油體蛋白（oleosins）。在種子萌發過程中，脂滴水解產生的脂肪酸經由過氧化物酶體代謝，為細胞提供能量及合成代謝的前體分子。 自噬是維持細胞穩態的重要降解與循環利用途徑，涵蓋多種機制。其中，巨自噬（macroautophagy）透過自噬體選擇性包裹特定底物，而微自噬（microautophagy）則通過液泡或溶酶體直接內吞胞質組分實現降解。在此過程中，ATG8 及自噬受體蛋白是識別並靶向特定底物的關鍵因子。NBR1 作為一種進化上保守的選擇性自噬受體，能夠在自噬啟動時結合泛素化底物並與 ATG8 特異性相互作用，在植物細胞選擇性自噬中具有核心功能。 脂質自噬（lipophagy）是指脂滴透過自噬途徑選擇性降解的過程，對於能量與碳骨架的供應至關重要，尤其在高能量需求及逆境響應階段，脂質自噬有助於維持細胞代謝穩態。然而，植物中脂質自噬的分子機制尚未得到系統闡明，存在顯著的研究空白。 我們的初步研究表明，在黑暗條件下萌發的幼苗接受光照後 1 小時內，NBR1 與 GFP-ATG8e 在細胞中與脂滴發生共定位；電子顯微鏡進一步觀察到脂滴被液泡直接吞噬，提示其主要透過微自噬途徑降解。與此同時，脂滴結構蛋白 oleosin2 在黑暗環境中保持穩定，但在光照誘導下迅速消失。在 nbr1 與 atg8 突變體中，脂滴降解過程顯著延遲。此外，nbr1 與 V 型 ATP 酶突變體均表現出類似的脂滴清除缺陷，提示二者可能協同參與同一降解途徑。 基於此，我們提出以下假設：在葉綠體脫黃化的幼苗細胞中，光誘導的 oleosin 蛋白泛素化修飾以及 ATG8 脂化修飾是脂滴微自噬發生的關鍵分子事件；同時，NBR1 及 V-ATPase 的協同作用可能促進該過程中所需的蛋白修飾與膜動態重塑。我們計劃結合生化、遺傳學以及高解析度顯微成像等多學科手段，系統解析脂滴微自噬的分子調控網絡。 本研究將揭示調控種子營養儲備降解與循環利用的關鍵因子，回答植物細胞在發育過程中如何透過自噬重塑細胞器組成的核心科學問題。這一系列新的發現不僅將深化對植物自噬多樣性與特異性機制的理解，亦為培育高油脂積累與高抗逆性的優質作物品種提供理論基礎，並對推動永續農業與環境保護具有重要意義。

14103925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14103925.value: 探討血管平滑肌細胞中的整合壓力反應及其在主動脈瘤中的作用

14103925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103925.value: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is characterized by the dilation of the aortic wall, which can lead to sudden rupture and life-threatening intra-abdominal hemorrhage, resulting in high mortality rates. AA can manifest as either abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) or thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. AAA often develops asymptomatically and rapidly, making it challenging with very limited treatment options. A critical factor in AAA pathology is the dysfunction and loss of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), accompanied by extracellular matrix degradation, and declined contractile function. Currently, the molecular mechanisms underlying VSMC dysfunction in AAA remain incompletely understood. Recent studies have linked AAA to mitochondrial dysfunction. Other also showed that defects in mitochondrial respiration can activate DELE1, which is cleaved and released to activate HRI, thereby triggering the integrated stress response (ISR) through eIF2α in skeletal myocytes and cardiomyocytes. However, the role of this mitochondrial stress-induced DELE1-HRI and ISR signaling in VSMCs within the context of AAA is still unexplored. Preliminary experiments indicate that DELE1-HRI and downstream ISR signaling may be upregulated in both mouse and human AAA, with inhibition of DELE1 or HRI exacerbating AAA pathology in mice. Additionally, we observed increased ferroptosis in VSMCs, with ISR activation potentially inducing ATF4 to protect against ferroptosis, possibly via GPX4. We hypothesize that mitochondrial disturbances leading to DELE1-HRI and ISR activation is protective against AAA progression through the activation of ATF4 and GPX4 in VSMCs. To test this hypothesis, we will employ HRI knockout mice and SMC-selective Dele1 knockout mice to determine whether deletion of HRI or DELE1 exacerbates AAA progression in AAA models induced by angiotensin II or elastase. Furthermore, we will use primary human VSMCs to investigate how DELE1 and HRI contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction-induced VSMC phenotype loss and cell death by a comprehensive analysis of mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, we will probe the regulatory role of ATF4 on VSMC ferroptosis, focusing on GPX4 using loss or gain of function and small molecule drugs. Small molecules or supplements targeting HRI and GPX4 will be tested for their effects on ferroptosis and AAA progression in vivo. Through these experiments, we aim to elucidate the roles of mitochondrial DELE1, HRI, and ISR signaling in VSMCs and their protective effects against AAA via ferroptosis inhibition. With these plans, we aim to uncover previously unknown mechanism of VSMC dysfunction in AAA and identify new therapeutic targets as well as pharmacological tools for potential AAA intervention. 主動脈瘤（Aortic aneurysm, AA）是指主動脈壁擴張的病理現象，可能導致突然破裂及危及生命的腹腔內出血，造成高死亡率。AA可表現為腹主動脈瘤或胸主動脈瘤及主動脈剝離。AAA常在無症狀的情況下迅速發展，治療選項非常有限。AAA病理的一個關鍵因素是血管平滑肌細胞（Vascular smooth muscle cells, VSMCs）的功能障礙與喪失，伴隨細胞外基質的降解及收縮功能的下降。 目前，AAA中VSMC功能障礙的分子機制仍未完全明瞭。近期研究將AAA與線粒體功能障礙聯繫起來。其他研究也顯示，線粒體呼吸缺陷可活化HRI，進而透過eIF2α在骨骼肌細胞與心肌細胞中啟動整合壓力反應（Integrated Stress Response, ISR）。然而，在AAA背景下，線粒體壓力誘導的DELE1-HRI與ISR訊號在VSMCs中的角色尚未被探索。 我們假設，線粒體功能紊亂導致的HRI與ISR活化，透過在VSMCs中活化ATF4與GPX4，對AAA進展具有保護作用。 為了驗證此假設，我們將使用基因敲除小鼠來判斷在由血管收縮素II或彈性酶誘導的AAA模型中，HRI缺失是否會加劇AAA進展。此外，我們將使用人類原代VSMCs，透過全面分析線粒體功能，探討HRI如何促進線粒體功能障礙所引起的VSMC表型喪失與細胞死亡。在機制方面，我們將探討ATF4對VSMC鐵死亡的調控角色，並使用功能喪失或增益實驗及小分子藥物進行研究。針對HRI與GPX4的小分子或補充劑將在體內測試其對鐵凋亡與AAA進展的影響。 透過這些實驗，我們旨在闡明HRI與ISR訊號在VSMCs中的作用及其透過抑制鐵凋亡對AAA的保護效應。藉由這些研究計畫，我們希望揭示AAA中VSMC功能障礙的未知機制，並找出新的治療靶點及潛在的藥物干預工具。

14104325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14104325.value: 脂肪肝與慢性乙型肝炎的複雜交互作用對肝臟相關臨床結果的影響

14104325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14104325.value: Prof Hsu, Yao Chun Prof Lee, Hye Won Prof Wong, Grace Lai-hung Prof Wong, Vincent Wai-Sun Prof Yuen, Pong Chi

14104325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104325.value: Background Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a critical public health problem affecting 258 million people globally. The population afflicted by CHB is ageing, coupled with a rising prevalence of metabolic syndrome, with around 30% of patients presenting with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This condition engenders a multifaceted interrelation between CHB, MASLD, and long-term clinical outcomes. Though MASLD can cause chronic liver inflammation leading to cirrhosis development, it is also, paradoxically, correlated with lower viral activity and more hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance, i.e., functional cure of CHB. Furthermore, MASLD is closely linked to diabetes, a known risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhotic complications. Diabetes also undermines the accuracy of existing HCC risk prediction scores. Method We will identify three territory-wide cohorts of untreated adult CHB patients from 2000-2025, first-line oral antiviral-treated adult CHB patients from 2005-2025, and adult CHB patients who achieved HBsAg seroclearance from 2000-2025. All patients who visited primary, secondary, and tertiary public medical centres in Hong Kong will be identified through the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System managed by the Hospital Authority, which anonymously captures patients’ demographics, diagnoses, procedures, laboratory tests, and medication use, covering 80% of the population. The study aims to evaluate the impact of hepatic steatosis on the development of HCC, cirrhotic complications, and HBsAg seroclearance in CHB patients under different viral activity, HBsAg seroclearance status, and extent of coexisting metabolic risk factors. Two novel artificial intelligence (AI) models will be developed and validated to predict HCC and cirrhotic complications respectively with enhanced precision, and compared to the performance of existing HCC risk scores and serum fibrosis scores. Validity of study findings and AI models will be further assessed with cohorts of prospectively recruited CHB patients from a local hospital and two hospitals from South Korea and Taiwan, and another external cohort of patients post-HBsAg seroclearance from South Korea. Clinical impact The study will yield crucial real-world insights into the relationship between hepatic steatosis, coexisting metabolic risk factors, HCC, cirrhotic complications, and HBsAg seroclearance in CHB patients with different viral activity and HBsAg seroclearance status. AI models can be integrated into the computer system for daily clinical practice to enhance clinical workflows, enabling timely assessment and management of MASLD and metabolic risk factors, and facilitating vigilant monitoring of patients at risk. Patients will benefit from risk-based management, minimising the likelihood of progression to HCC and cirrhotic complications. 背景 慢性乙型肝炎（CHB）是重要的全球公共衛生問題，影響約2.58億人。隨著CHB患者人口老化，加上代謝症候群盛行率上升，約30%的患者同時患有代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病（MASLD）。此情況導致CHB、MASLD與長期臨床結果之間形成多面向的交互關係。雖然MASLD可能引發慢性肝臟炎症，進而導致肝硬化，但矛盾的是，它亦與較低的病毒活性及更高的乙型肝炎表面抗原（HBsAg）血清清除率（即CHB的功能性治癒）相關。此外，MASLD與糖尿病密切相關，而糖尿病是肝細胞癌（HCC）和肝硬化併發症的已知風險因素，同時也會降低現有HCC風險預測評分的準確性。 方法 我們將從2000-2025年間確立三個全港性隊列：未接受治療的成年CHB患者、2005-2025年間接受一線口服抗病毒治療的成年CHB患者，以及2000-2025年間達成HBsAg血清清除的成年CHB患者。所有曾於香港公營基層、第二及第三層醫療機構就診的患者，將透過醫院管理局管理的「臨床數據分析與報告系統」（CDARS）識別。該系統匿名記錄患者人口統計資料、診斷、治療程序、實驗室檢測及藥物使用情況，涵蓋全港80%人口。 本研究旨在評估脂肪性肝病對CHB患者在不同病毒活性、HBsAg血清清除狀態及代謝風險因素共存程度下，發生HCC、肝硬化併發症及HBsAg血清清除的影響。我們將開發並驗證兩種新型人工智能（AI）模型，分別用於更精準預測HCC及肝硬化併發症，並與現有HCC風險評分及血清纖維化評分進行效能比較。研究結果及AI模型的有效性將進一步透過本地醫院、韓國與台灣兩家醫院的前瞻性CHB患者隊列，以及韓國另一組HBsAg血清清除後患者的外部隊列進行驗證。 臨床意義 本研究將提供關鍵的真實世界數據，闡明脂肪性肝病、共存代謝風險因素、HCC、肝硬化併發症及HBsAg血清清除在CHB患者（不同病毒活性與HBsAg狀態）間的關係。AI模型可整合至臨床電腦系統中，優化日常醫療流程，及時評估與管理MASLD及代謝風險因素，並加強對高風險患者的監測。患者將受益於風險導向的個體化管理，降低進展為HCC及肝硬化併發症的可能性。

14104625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14104625.value: 血液單細胞類型表達譜研究和使用於發燒患者的分類

14104625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14104625.value: Prof Lam, Hugh Simon Hung San Dr Lui, Chung Yan Grace
rows: Prof Lam, Hugh Simon Hung San

14104625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104625.value: Febrile illness is a common condition, particularly among young patients and it is crucial to have biomarkers that enable early triage of patients to various etiologies to allow appropriate treatment. Currently, the majority of diagnostic tests are targeted towards the detection of pathogens while other assays of inflammatory biomarkers are mostly directed to serum proteins. Only recently, blood transcriptome (assays of transcript abundance (TA) in leukocytes as a representation of host response) has been explored to differentiate bacterial and viral infections. However, these gene signature panels involved too many genes for use in a routine clinical laboratory. We pioneered the bioinformatics and laboratory assays to estimate gene expression of a single leukocyte cell-type directly in a whole blood (WB) sample without prior isolation of the specified cell-type [Tang 2011, Huang et al 2023]. Prior bioinformatic analysis using public datasets identified pairs of genes that are used to formulate as ratio-based biomarkers (RBBs) to represent gene expression in specified single cell-types in cell- mixture samples such as WB and PBMC. This technology is also applicable to determine monocytes cell-type specific gene expression in WB to triage febrile patients into major categories of diseases: (1) viral, (2) bacterial, (3) active tuberculosis. Here, we propose to validate and further develop into a rapid triage test based on the host responses using TA of monocytes and also further extend it to TA of granulocytes. The research question and workflow are: (A) We will establish 2 prospective cohorts of febrile patients: (1) pediatric and (2) adult patients. Already identified RBB for monocyte gene expression in PBMC will be validated using these cohorts for their triage performance. (B) Development of granulocyte RBBs by performing sc-RNAseq on the prospective cohort. The impact of the results would be far reaching as host response diagnostics is an emerging area of development in biomarker research. The ability to directly determine TA of a single specified cell-type in blood will be useful in other diseases and clinical scenarios in the future. In this revised proposal, we implemented all comments made by reviewers. We also worked out a list of new RBBs for granulocytes by CODA analysis of bulk data (pending publication). They will be readily validated in the patient cohort going to established with the funding. 發燒性疾病是一種常見疾病，尤其在年輕患者。根據不同病因對患者進行早期分類，以便進行適當的治療至關重要。大多數診斷檢測旨在檢測病原體，而其他檢測則主要與血清蛋白相關。血球轉錄組已被用於區分細菌和病毒感染。在此，我們建議開發一種快速檢測方法，利用宿主對週邊白血球（單核細胞和粒細胞）單細胞群基因表現的反應來區分細菌、病毒和結核病三大類感染.

14104825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14104825.value: 沿陸海梯度紅樹林植食性蟹類飲食生態位分化的比較基因組分析

14104825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14104825.value: Prof Ma, Kayan Dr Thibodeau, Benoit

14104825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104825.value: Mangrove forests are one of the most productive ecosystems globally and the healthy functioning of mangal habitats is tightly linked to the herbivorous activities of Sesarmidae crabs. Herbivory within this group is thought to drive speciation, while the partitioning of dietary niches is anticipated to further enhance species coexistence and specialization. However, the lack of empirical data on the dietary breadth and composition of mangrove crabs at the species level has led to broad categorizations that could lead potentially misleading the ecological roles and evolutionary adaptations of individual species. Moreover, the genetic mechanisms underpinning herbivory, particularly molecular basis to their preferred host plant, remain poorly understood among mangrove macrofauna, including herbivorous sesarmid crabs. In the proposed study, we attempt to dissect the dietary niche partitioning and the corresponding genetic mechanism of lignocellulose degradation and detoxification in mangrove herbivorous crab species based on an integrated ecological and multi-omics approach consisting of three major components: 1/ dietary breadth and composition characterization, 2/ comparative genomic analyses on molecular evolution and 3/ transcriptomic analyses on differential gene expression profile. We aim to test TWO major hypotheses: 1/ mangrove herbivorous sesarmid crab species exhibit dietary niche partitioning mirroring their zonation along the land-sea gradient to facilitate coexistence of species; and 2/ the niche partitioning drive genomic adaptations in response to dietary shift and breadth, which in turn promote divergence and ultimately speciation in mangrove sesarmid crabs. The project will therefore reveal the ecological function among crab species and the genetic mechanism(s) facilitating the utilization of plant materials as food source and plant-crab interaction in adaptive radiation of sesarmid crabs. The study can also illuminate the nutrient and carbon transfer dynamic between terrestrial and marine habitats across the land-sea gradient in mangrove forest. In addition, the comparative genomic analyses can uncover insights into broader biological processes, such evolution in osmoregulation and terrestrialization in marine crustaceans. 紅樹林是全球最具生產力的生態系統之一，其健康運作與相手蟹科蟹類的植食活動有密切相關。相手蟹科的植食性被認為是驅動物種形成的關鍵因素，而飲食生態位的分化能進一步促進不同物種共存與專化。然而，由於缺乏紅樹林蟹類的食物種類廣度與組成之實證數據，導致我們未能充分了解個別物種的生態角色與演化適應。此外，在紅樹林大型動物群中，包括植食性相手蟹科蟹類，其植食性的遺傳機制，尤其是對其偏好攝食的植物適應的分子基礎，仍未被充分理解。本研究擬透過整合生態學與多組學方法，剖析紅樹林植食性蟹類的飲食生態位分化，以及相應的木質纖維素降解與解毒遺傳機制演化。此研究包含三個主要組成部分：1/ 飲食廣度與組成之研究；2/蟹類比較基因組分析分子演化；以及3/ 轉錄組分析以找出基因表現譜之差異。我們旨在檢驗兩個主要假說：1/ 紅樹林植食性相手蟹科蟹類展現出與其沿陸海梯度分區相呼應的飲食生態位分化，以促進不同物種共存；以及2/ 此食性生態位分化促進基因組適應演化，從而促進紅樹林相手蟹科蟹類的分歧並最終導致新物種形成。本計畫因而將揭示蟹類物種的生態功能，以及利用不同植物作為食物來源利用之遺傳機制在相手蟹科蟹類的適應輻射中發揮的作用。此外，比較基因組分析可揭示更廣泛的生物演化適應過程，例如海洋甲殼類的滲透調節與陸地性演化。

14105125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14105125.value: 連續血糖監測對年長2型糖尿病患者的影響之隨機對照研究

14105125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14105125.value: Prof AUYEUNG, Tung Wai Dr Choi, Kai-chow Dr Chow, Edith Wing Kar Prof Chow, Yee Kwan Elaine Prof KWOK, Timothy Chi-yui Dr Lee, Jenny Shun Wah

14105125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105125.value: Abstract: While there is a wealth of data supporting the use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) among young adults with type 1 diabetes, evidence from randomized controlled trial (RCT) exploring the impact of the use of CGM focused on older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) is lacking. Using a cohesive team of endocrinologists, geriatricians and researchers experienced in conducting clinical trials, we propose to conduct a 24-week, multicentre, parallel-group, assessor-blinded, RCT using intermittent real-time CGM (intervention group, n=167) versus conventional capillary blood glucose (CBG) monitoring (control group, n=167) in Hong Kong Chinese older adults aged ≥65 years with T2D to investigate the effect of intermittent real-time CGM use on glycemic control, psychosocial and behavioral changes, cognitive function, frailty, hospitalizations and other clinical outcomes. After enrolment, all participants will complete a 14-day blind run-in phase using masked CGM. After that, eligible participants will be randomized to receive either real-time CGM (at baseline, week-12 and week-24) or usual care with CBG monitoring using fingerstick testing. Participants from both intervention and control group will receive detailed clinical and biochemical evaluations at baseline, week-12 and week-24. Coprimary outcome measures will be changes in glycated hemoglobin and time in range between the 2 groups from randomization to the end of study. Secondary outcomes include changes in other CGM metrics including time below range (level 1 and 2), time above range (level 1 and 2), glycemic variability; hypoglycemic episodes; cognitive function measured by neuropsychological test battery; psychological and behavioral parameters measured by questionnaires including Diabetes Distress Scale, Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale, Diabetes Empowerment Scale, Summary of Diabetes Self Care Activities, as well as quality of life (QoL) assessment by EuroQol Group EQ-5D health questionnaire; frailty; hospitalizations and mortality. Given older people with diabetes are heterogeneous with unique clinical needs and deserve specific treatment approach, the results of this first RCT in the region focused on older adults with T2D in Hong Kong Chinese will provide scientific evidence and practical insights for broader application of intermittent real-time CGM use in the geriatric population. 儘管有大量數據支持在年輕1型糖尿病患者中使用連續血糖監測的好處，但對於年長2型糖尿病患者使用連續血糖監測的影響仍然缺乏隨機對照研究的證據。 結合内分泌科醫生，老年科醫生，及具臨床試驗經驗的研究人員所組成研究團隊，我們建議進行一項爲期24週，多中心，平行組別，評估者單盲的隨機對照研究比較於65歲或以上的中國香港年長2型糖尿病患者中使用間歇性實時連續血糖監測（干預組，n = 167）及指尖點刺測試毛細血管血糖監測（對照組，n = 167）以評估間接性實時連續血糖監測之使用對血糖控制，社會心理及行爲改變，認知功能，衰弱評估，住院以及其他臨床結果的效果。在參加研究後，所有參加者將會使用隱蔽連續血糖監測裝置完成一個爲期14天的盲磨合期。然後，合資格的參加者將會被隨機分組至使用實時連續血糖監測的干預組（於基綫，第12週及第24週時使用）或僅使用指尖點刺測試毛細血管血糖的對照組。干預組及對照組的參加者都將會於基綫，第12週及第24週時接受詳細的臨床及生物化學評估。共同主要結果將會是兩組從隨機分組到研究結束期間的糖化血紅素和目標範圍時間之改變。次要結果包括其他連續血糖監測數據的改變（包括低於目標範圍時間（一級和二級），高於目標範圍時間（一級和二級），血糖變化性）低血糖事件，通過神經心理測試評估認知功能，通過問卷評估社會心理及行爲參數（包括糖尿病困擾量表，抑鬱焦慮和壓力量表，糖尿病能力量表，糖尿病自我護理活動摘要），通過EQ-5D問卷評估的生活質素，衰弱，住院，和死亡。 鑒於年長糖尿病患者個別差異較大，臨床需求各異及需要針對性的治療方法，這項作爲首個針對中國香港年長2型糖尿病患者的隨機對照研究的結果將會為老年人口使用間歇性實時連續血糖監測廣泛的應用提供科學證據及實際見解。

14105725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14105725.value: 糞桿菌增強大腸直腸癌化療反應：分子機制與轉化意義

14105725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105725.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major public problem in Hong Kong causing significant mortality. Altered gut microbiota is casually linked to the development of CRC. Our recent studies have shown that the replenishment of CRC-depleted probiotics could arrest CRC development and potentiate immunotherapy efficacy (Cancer Cell, 2023; Gastroenterology, 2021; Gut, 2022; 2023a, 2023b, 2024), but whether gut bacteria might modulate chemotherapy response remains unclear. To this end, we analyzed the fecal microbiomes of two pilot cohorts of CRC patients who received chemotherapy, and identified a second-generation probiotic, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, that is highly enriched in the responders. Consistent with this, fecal F. prausnitzii levels predict favorable survival in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients. Preliminary functional investigations showed that both pasteurized F. prausnitzii or F. prausnitzii-secreted metabolites synergize with chemotherapy (5-FU: Fluorouracil & Oxaliplatin) to induce proliferative arrest and apoptosis in CRC cells, primary CRC organoids, and CRC xenografts in mice. Moreover, F. prausnitzii overcomes chemoresistance in 5-FU/Oxaliplatin-resistance CRC cells, indicating F. prausnitzii as a promising probiotic for boosting CRC chemotherapy efficacy. Mechanistic studies revealed that the chemotherapy boosting effect of F. prausnitzii involved two pivotal parts. First, the F. prausnitzii surface protein D-galactose/methyl-galactose binding periplasmic protein (MgIB) interacts with Enolase-1 (ENO1) receptor expressed on CRC cells, leading to the down-regulation of ENO1 onco-protein and downstream PI3K-Akt signaling. Second, F. prausnitzii secreted metabolite butyrate binds to and activates G-protein coupled receptor 43 (GPR43), which in turn inhibits MAPK signaling. Supplementation with recombinant MgIB or butyrate recapitulates the chemotherapy boosting effects of pasteurized F. prausnitzii or its secreted metabolites, respectively, offering compelling evidence that they are the components through which F. prausnitzii promotes CRC chemosensitivity. Based on these observations, we hypothesize that F. prausnitzii, a second-generation probiotic, could be utilized to boost chemotherapy efficacy in CRC, and that fecal F. prausnitzii could be a non-invasive biomarker for predicting chemotherapy response in CRC patients. To address these hypotheses, we propose the following 3 objectives: 1) To comprehensively investigate the function of F. prausnitzii in potentiating chemotherapy response in CRC; 2) To dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying F. prausnitzii-mediated chemotherapy response in CRC; and 3) To determine the clinical value of F. prausnitzii as a biomarker for CRC prognostication. We will utilize a multidisciplinary approach to define the functional, mechanistic and clinical significance of F. prausnitzii in CRC chemotherapy, and pave the way for rational development of probiotics for improving treatment response of CRC patients. 結直腸癌（CRC）是香港重要公共衛生挑戰，其高死亡率造成社會沉重負擔。研究表明，腸道菌群失調與結直腸癌的發生發展密切相關。我們團隊前期證實，補充腸癌缺失的益生菌可抑制腫瘤進展並增强免疫治療效果(Cancer Cell, 2023; Gastroenterology, 2021; Gut, 2022; 2023a, 2023b, 2024)，但腸道菌群能否調控腸癌患者化療效應尚未明確。 爲此，我們分析了兩組接受化療的腸癌患者糞便微生物組成，成功鑒定出在化療響應患者中特異性富集的二代益生菌——普拉梭菌（F. prausnitzii）。其糞便豐度可獨立預測患者的生存獲益。功能實驗顯示，巴氏滅活普拉梭菌及其代謝物產物可協同增强化療藥物(氟尿嘧啶和奧沙利鉑)的抗腫瘤效應，在腸癌細胞系、原代腸癌類器官及腸癌異位移植瘤小鼠模型中顯著誘導細胞增殖停滯與凋亡。同時，該細菌能夠有效逆轉腸癌細胞化療耐藥性。上述證據表明普拉梭菌具備作爲化療增敏劑的臨床轉化潛力。分子機制研究證實，普拉梭菌的化療增敏作用通過雙通路實現。首先，該細菌表面蛋白D-半乳糖/甲基半乳糖結合周質蛋白（MglB）與腫瘤細胞受體烯醇化酶1（ENO1）結合，抑制ENO1及下游PI3K-Akt信號軸。其次，普拉梭菌通過產生代謝物丁酸鹽，結合並激活G蛋白偶聯受體43，阻斷MAPK信號轉導。外源補充重組MglB蛋白或丁酸鹽均可恢復巴氏滅活普拉梭菌或其代謝物的化療增敏效應，進一步證實該細菌在化療增敏中的作用。 基於上述發現，我們推測普拉梭菌作爲二代益生菌具有臨床化療增敏價值，并且其糞便豐度可作爲腸癌化療響應性的非侵入性預測指標。由此，我們提出以下三個研究目標：1）系統解析普拉梭菌在促進腸癌化療療效中的作用；2）闡明普拉梭菌介導腸癌對化療反應的分子機制；3）明確糞便普拉梭菌作爲非侵入性化療響應預測指標的臨床意義。綜上所述，我們將採用多學科整合策略，全面剖析普拉梭菌在腸癌化療中的功能機制與轉化應用，為開發基於微生態製劑用於改善腸癌患者化療效應的輔助療法提供理論基石。

14105925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14105925.value: 對猴痘病毒高風險基因位點的分析及疫苗對新型基因變異株保護效力的評估

14105925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14105925.value: Prof Chen, Zigui Dr Lv, Ziquan

14105925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105925.value: The multi-country outbreak of the mpox (previously monkeypox) disease in 2022 led to the WHO declaration of it as a public health emergency of international concern. The pathogen mpox virus, which is in the same genus as the variola virus, has generated multiple new lineages and showed fast human-to-human transmission during this outbreak. Nevertheless, due to its genome's complexity, the mpox virus's evolutionary rate remains unclear. Knowledge of this is important to summarize and understand the evolutionary status of the virus. Detailed genetic characterization of the mpox virus is also needed to identify genomic regions under strong selective pressure and rich in epitopes. Furthermore, although vaccines for mpox are available, the vaccine effectiveness (VE) has a wide range of 35 – 89%. We hypothesize that genetic variations are responsible for the VE variations and propose to use a computational model to capture their relationships and predict the VE of mpox vaccines when new variants appear. The objectives of this project are three-fold: 1) To estimate the evolutionary rate of the mpox virus in the recent outbreak by a novel computational model that handles complex mutation patterns and to comprehensively profile the high-risk genomic regions. 2) To identify key genomic regions associated with mpox disease outcomes through the analysis of combined genome and clinical data of mpox cases. 3) To establish a computational prediction model for mpox VE and evaluate the risk of vaccine breakthrough. Pilot studies demonstrated promising results for all of the objectives. The project team comprises experienced investigators specializing in virus evolution modeling, bioinformatics, and clinical microbiology. Overall, this project will offer both new methods for genome interpretation of viruses and timely characterization of the evolution of the mpox virus and vaccine effects. The findings of this project will facilitate public health agencies for policy-making on epidemic control and disease preparedness. 2022年多國爆發的mpox（原猴痘）疫情促使世界衛生組織宣佈其構成"國際關注的突發公共衛生事件"。作為天花病毒的同屬病原體，mpox病毒在此次疫情中已演化出多個新譜系，並表現出快速的人際傳播特性。然而由於其基因組複雜性，該病毒的進化速率至今尚未明確——這一關鍵資訊對於總結和理解病毒進化態勢至關重要。同時，對mpox病毒進行精細的遺傳特徵分析可以明確處於強選擇壓力下的基因組區域及富含抗原表位的片段。目前的mpox疫苗有效性存在35%-89%的大範圍波動，而基因變異可能是導致疫苗有效性差異的主因之一。我們提出用計算模型來捕捉病毒基因變異與疫苗有效性閒的內在關聯，從而預測新變異株出現時的疫苗有效性。本項目有三個主要目標：1）通過能處理複雜突變模式的新型計算模型估算近期疫情中mpox病毒的進化速率，並繪製高風險基因組區域圖譜；2）結合mpox病例的基因組與臨床信息，找到影響疾病表型的關鍵基因組區域；3）建立mpox疫苗有效性的計算預測模型，評估疫苗突破的風險。我們的前期研究已在這些目標方向上取得積極進展。本項目將提出病毒基因組解讀的新方法，以及對mpox病毒進化與疫苗效應進行即時評估，研究結果將為公共衛生機構制定疫情防控策略提供科學依據。

14106125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14106125.value: 甲氨蝶呤（Methotrexate）對比腫瘤壞死因子抑制劑（TNF inhibition）在預防早期銀屑病關節炎的結構損傷：一項使用高解析度外周定量電腦斷層掃描（HR-pQCT）的隨機臨床試驗（MeTEPsA 試驗）

14106125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14106125.value: Dr Chan, Ka Man Dr Cheng, Tsz Ho Dr Ciang, Chu Oi Natalia Prof Griffith, James Francis Dr Ho, Carmen Tze Kwan Dr Ho, Ling Yin Yvonne Ms Hung, Wing-Yin Vivian Dr Lai, Tin Lok Prof Lai, Yu Hin Chester Dr Lao, Weng Nga Virginia Dr Lee, Jack Jock Wai Dr Lee, Ka Lai Violet Prof Qin, Ling Dr So, Ho Dr To, Chi Hung Dr Wan, Man Choi Prof Wong, Ronald Man Yeung Dr Young, Kit Yu

14106125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106125.value: Background Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) are crucial for effective management. In treatment-naive patients with polyarticular disease (> 4 swollen joints), the choice between using a tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) or methotrexate (MTX) as first-line treatment remains a topic of debate. A lack of data on the efficacy of medications in treating oligoarticular (≤4 swollen joints) PsA further complicating treatment decisions. Moreover, subcutaneous (SC) MTX has been proven to be more efficacious than the oral from at the same dosage in early rheumatoid arthritis, whether this is also true in early PsA has never been studied. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computer tomography (HR-pQCT) is a novel technique for the detailed assessment of bony erosions and enthesiophytes in the metacarpophalangeal joint (MCPJ) 2-4. Using HR-pQCT, a preliminary analysis from a study conducted by our group in early PsA (symptom onset <2 years) revealed a numerically greater reduction in total erosion volume in the TNFi group compared to the MTX group. These findings would certainly require confirmation in a larger-scale randomized trial. Project description We hypothesize that TNFi is superior then SC MTX in preventing structural damage in early, treatment naive PsA, assessed using HR-pQCT. This study aimed to ascertain the effect of SC MTX and TNFi (adalimumab biosimilar) on erosion and enthesiophyte progression in early PsA by HR-pQCT. In this is one-year, open-label, multicentre, randomized trial, patients with ≥ 1 tender and swollen joint, ≥ 1 poor prognostic factor (polyarthritis, structural damage on HR-pQCT or radiography, elevated acute phase reactants, dactylitis, nail involvement and health assessment questionnaire-disability index >1), and symptom onset ≤ 2 years will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to either the SC MTX or TNFi group. HR-pQCT of the MCPJ 2-4 will be performed at baseline, week 24 and 1-year. The primary outcome is to compare the change in erosion volume over MCPJ 2-4 over a period of 48 weeks, between the SC MTX (group 1) and the TNFi group (group 2), assessed by HR-pQCT. Significance Treatment recommendations for PsA suggest early intensive therapy but there are no studies that have previously used efficacy to prevent structural damage to guide therapy. If early use of TNFi is shown to be superior to SC MTX in halting the progression of structural changes, this would provide crucial direction to clinicians when deciding whether to initiate TNFi or SC MTX as first-line therapy.

14106425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14106425.value: 「獨處於孤獨之中」：探索社區獨居長者孤獨感的整合研究

14106425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14106425.value: Prof Dong, Dong Prof Woo, Jean

14106425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106425.value: Background: Loneliness is a growing public health concern among older adults, especially for those living alone in the community. A significant body of evidence has demonstrated its adverse impact on the physical and mental health of older adults, including cognitive decline and mortality. However, a critical gap exists in understanding loneliness from the perspective of older adults in Asian contexts like Hong Kong, where social, cultural and environmental factors influence the experience of loneliness. Interventions aimed at alleviating loneliness have demonstrated limited or short-term success, potentially due to an incomplete understanding of loneliness as a construct within Hong Kong and the lack of culturally appropriate instruments to assess loneliness in this population. These gaps highlight the need for a deeper theoretical understanding of loneliness, as well as a culturally sensitive instrument for assessing loneliness among older adults in Hong Kong. Aims: The proposed project aims to develop 1) a theoretical framework to understand the underlying experiences and processes of loneliness among older adults living alone in the community and 2) a theory-based, context-specific instrument to measure and evaluate loneliness in this population, within the sociocultural and environmental context of Hong Kong. Methods: A three-phase, exploratory sequential mixed methods design will be employed. In Phase I, using the grounded theory approach, interviews will be conducted with older adults to develop a theoretical framework that uncovers the experiences of loneliness in older adults living alone in the community. In Phase II, an instrument will be developed based on key concepts of the theoretical framework, then evaluated for content validity and pilot tested. In Phase III, psychometric testing will be conducted to assess the instrument’s validity (i.e., construct validity, concurrent validity) and reliability (i.e., test-retest reliability, internal consistency) with a broader sample of older adults living alone in the community in Hong Kong. Significance: This project will provide invaluable insights into the unique experiences of loneliness among older adults living alone in the community and facilitate the development of a valid and reliable instrument for measuring and evaluating loneliness in this population. These findings will provide a strong foundation for more effective and sustainable loneliness interventions that address the needs of older adults to support their psychological and mental well-being. Furthermore, knowledge gained from this project will inform improvements in health care, social services, and government policies for aging populations in Hong Kong. 背景 孤獨感正成為長者中日益嚴重的公共衞生問題，對於社區獨居長者的影響尤為顯著。大量實證研究顯示，孤獨感會對長者身心健康造成不良影響，包括認知能力衰退及死亡風險上升。然而，在亞洲社會（如香港），孤獨感的形成深受社會、文化及環境因素影響，但從長者自身視角出發的孤獨感研究仍相當不足。現有針對減輕孤獨感的介入措施大多成效有限或僅具短期效果，這可能源於對本地長者孤獨感的理解仍不夠全面，以及缺乏適合本地文化的孤獨感評估工具。上述缺口突顯我們迫切需要深入理解孤獨感的理論基礎，並開發具文化適切性的孤獨感評估工具。 研究目標 本研究旨在：(1) 建構一套理論框架，以理解社區獨居長者孤獨感的深層體驗及形成過程；(2) 以上述理論框架為基礎，研發一套切合香港社會文化背景的孤獨感評估工具，用於測量及評估本地獨居長者的孤獨感。 研究方法 本研究採用三階段「探索性序列混合方法」設計。 第一階段將運用紮根理論，透過訪談社區獨居長者，建構一個理論框架，揭示其主觀體驗與孤獨感形成過程；第二階段將根據理論框架的核心概念研發評估工具，並進行內容效度評估及初步測試；第三階段將針對更大規模的社區獨居長者樣本群，進行心理計量測試，以評估所研發工具的效度（包括結構效度與同時效度）及信度（包括重測信度與內部一致性）。 研究意義 本研究將深入揭示香港社區獨居長者孤獨感的獨特經歷，並提供一套兼具效度及信度的評估工具，促進孤獨感的量化及評估。研究成果將為制定更有效且可持續的孤獨感介入措施奠定理論及實證基礎，從而切實回應長者心理與精神健康的需要。此外，本研究所得的知識亦將有助於改善香港醫療服務、社會支援及長者政策，以應對人口老化所帶來的挑戰。

14106525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14106525.value: 解析RNA修飾組合體：特定修飾在基因調控中的協同作用

14106525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106525.value: A facet of RNA’s regulatory abilities stems from its diverse chemical composition, consisting of four canonical ribonucleotides (adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine) and more than 170 modified ribonucleotides. These RNA modifications, collectively referred to as the epitranscriptome, considerably affect gene expression, RNA stability, and protein synthesis. Despite their significance, much of the current research focuses on isolating individual RNA modification types for analysis, with functional studies often narrowing their scope to single modification loci. Although this approach is valuable, it overlooks the complex and combinatorial nature of RNA modifications, limiting our understanding of regulatory mechanisms orchestrated by the epitranscriptome. Our preliminary findings revealed that multiple RNA modification loci within the same transcripts are co-modified in a statistically significant manner. Thus, we hypothesize that these nonrandom combinations of RNA modifications are not mere biological noise but key modulators of cellular processes. Building on our expertise in transcriptomic analysis and method development (Li et al., Brief Bioinform, 2024; Zhang et al. Adv Sci, 2023; Chen et al., Nat Commun, 2022; Dumetz et al., Nucleic Acids Res, 2021), we integrated nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS, a technology capable of capturing all RNA modifications) with BALEEN (an innovative algorithm designed to identify RNA modifications at the single-transcript level) to establish the epitranscriptomic landscape in human cell models and explore the dynamics of combinatory modification events. Recognizing the critical role of RNA modifications in posttranscriptional regulation, we hypothesize that the co-occurrence of RNA modifications provides more nuanced control over RNA metabolism, affecting RNA structure and translation dynamics. To test this hypothesis, we developed a comprehensive analytical framework that incorporates structural information and quantitative proteomic data to investigate the potential synergistic effects of these modifications on RNA behavior. Specifically, we focus on m6A-solos, instances where m6A modifications occur dependently, and m6A–m5C-duets, representing co-modified events involving both m6A and m5C. Through this framework, we identified several combinatorial events strongly correlated with transcript expression and protein abundance. In this proposed project, we will explore the full spectrum of combinatorial RNA modifications that have remained elusive in past research. We envision that this framework can be applied to other biological contexts, revealing new dimensions of epitranscriptomic regulation and providing novel insights into both normal and disease-causing cellular states. RNA的調控能力部分源於其化學多樣性：除四種標準核糖核苷酸（腺嘌呤、尿嘧啶、胞嘧啶和鳥嘌呤）外，還存在170餘種核苷酸修飾形式。這些RNA修飾（統稱「表觀轉錄組」）顯著影響基因表達、RNA穩定性及蛋白質合成。儘管意義重大，當前研究多聚焦於單一修飾類型的獨立分析，功能研究也常局限於單一修飾位點。該策略雖具價值，卻忽視了RNA修飾固有的協同組合特性，制約了我們對表觀轉錄組協同調控機制的理解。 我們前期的研究發現：同一轉錄本中多個RNA修飾位點存在統計學顯著的協同修飾現象。據此提出假說：這些非隨機的RNA修飾組合並非生物噪音，而是細胞內的關鍵調控元件。基於我們在轉錄組學分析以及方法開發方面的專長，本研究整合納米孔直接RNA測序技術（DRS，可捕獲全RNA修飾譜）與自主開發的BALEEN算法（在單轉錄本水平鑑定RNA修飾的工具），構建人細胞模型的表觀轉錄組全景圖，系統性探究組合修飾事件的動態規律。 鑒於RNA修飾在轉錄後調控的核心作用，我們進一步假說：RNA修飾的共出現通過精細調控RNA代謝過程，影響RNA結構與翻譯。為驗證該假說，我們建立了一個完善的分析框架，整合RNA結構信息與蛋白質組學數據，旨在解析修飾組合對RNA行為的協同調控機制。本研究重點關注兩類事件：m6A-m6A組合修飾事件（m6A-solos）及m6A-m5C組合修飾事件（m6A–m5C-duets）。通過該框架，我們已發現多組與轉錄本表達量及蛋白質豐度顯著相關的組合事件。 本研究將系統解析既往研究中難以捕捉的RNA組合修飾圖譜。該框架亦可拓展至其他生物學場景，揭示表觀轉錄組調控新維度，為生理及病理狀態的細胞機制提供創新見解。

14107125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14107125.value: 研究細胞間隙連接蛋白 Claudin1作為鼻咽癌的新治療標靶

14107125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14107125.value: Prof Lo, Kwok-wai Prof Tao, Qian

14107125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107125.value: Despite the availability of modern drug therapies, over 80,000 people died worldwide from recurrent/ metastatic nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC). Our multidisciplinary team has dedicated decades of research into unravelling the genomic landscape of NPC and identifying novel therapeutic targets. Recently, therapeutic targeting of the claudin family of proteins that regular cellular tight junctions have gained intensive interest in cancer drug development because of the successful approval of zolbetuximab - a first-in-class monoclonal antibody against claudin18.2 proteins, when combined with chemotherapy in the treatment of gastroesophageal cancer. Tight junctions (TJ) proteins are part of the normal cell cytoskeleton that act as ‘sealants’ for maintaining cell to cell connections in the normal epithelium. In cancers, abnormal claudin activity causes disruption of TJ and thus other processes that enhance the ability of cancer cells to invade nearby tissues – namely, epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT), cell migration and stemness. This proposal is designed to provide the first proof-of-concept for targeting another important member of the claudin family known as claudin1 (CLDN1) in NPC. The CLDN1 protein is vulnerable to antibody treatment because it is partially exposed outside the normal TJs in cancers – known as the ‘non-junctional’ (NJ)-CLDN1. Antibody targeting of NJ-CLDN1 is cancer-specific because it will not bind to the TJ-CLDN1 found in normal epithelium. A first-in-class antibody against NJ-CLDN1 is already in a phase 1 clinical trial for solid tumors and we hope to provide scientific evidence to support evaluation in patients with NPC. Our groundwork has unraveled strong translational data which supports NJ-CLDN1 as a promising drug target for NPC. We found that NJ-CLDN1 is expressed in over 80% of NPC tumors and preclinical models. Antibody targeting NJ-CLDN1 can inhibit cell growth and enhance the effect of chemotherapy depending on the CLDN1 expression level, possibly by inhibiting EMT. Interestingly we found that the CLDN1 gene is switched off in 15% of NPC tumors and understanding of the underlying reasons may help to improve response to this treatment. The objectives of this proposal are: 1) to evaluate the prognostic significance of NJ-CLDN1 expression in NPC tumors; 2) to determine the anti-tumor activity of a NJ-CLDN1 antibody and in combination with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenesis agents in NPC models; 3) to elucidate the molecular mechanisms that underlie the anti-tumor growth effect of NJ-CLDN1 antibody in NPC; 4) to investigate the regulatory mechanism of CLND1 gene expression in NPC. 該研究計劃旨在利用單株抗體針對鼻咽癌的claudin1蛋白。我們的基礎工作已經揭示了強有力的轉化數據，支持claudin1作為鼻咽癌的新藥物標靶。 該提案的目的是：1）評估claudin1蛋白在鼻咽癌的臨床意義； 2) 研究claudin1抗體在鼻咽癌的抗腫瘤活性； 3) 研究claudin1抗體在鼻咽癌中抗腫瘤生長作用的分子機轉； 4) 探討claudin1基因在鼻咽癌中表現的調控機制。

14107625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14107625.value: 追蹤具潛力珊瑚益生菌的族群動態與宿主多樣性

14107625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14107625.value: Dr CHUI, Apple Pui-Yi Dr Falkenberg, Laura J

14107625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107625.value: Coral reefs house approximately 30% of the world's marine biodiversity and sustain the livelihoods of one billion people by providing goods and services. They are threatened by global changes (e.g., warming and ocean acidification) and local stressors (e.g., eutrophication and overfishing). Worldwide, half of the coral reefs have been lost since the 1950s, and in the future 70-90% will disappear under the most optimistic 1.5 ℃ warming scenario. Corals engage in symbioses with eukaryotic and prokaryotic microorganisms. The most notable coral symbiont is Symbiodiniaceae, photosynthetic dinoflagellates that live inside coral cells and fuel their metabolism. When corals face unfavorable environmental changes (e.g., heat stress), Symbiodiniaceae are expelled, leading to the loss of pigmentation and thus coral bleaching. Severe and prolonged bleaching can lead to coral mortality. For example, in a mass bleaching event from 2014-2017, coral mortality occurred in nearly 35% of reefs globally. A new mass bleaching event is happening this year, and corals in Hong Kong are being heavily affected. Microbial therapies are emerging as a promising option for coral conservation. The efficacy of probiotics in promoting coral health and preventing mortality under thermal stress has been demonstrated in laboratory trials. However, a major limitation of current coral probiotics is their poor retention in coral host, requiring repeated and continuous inoculations. The PI recently proposed a practical framework that allows for the selection of coral endosymbiotic beneficial bacteria that carry genomic hallmarks of evolutionarily young endosymbionts. Such endosymbionts identify coral tissues as their optimal habitats, which facilitates their retention in tissue, therefore enhancing their efficacy and minimizing the need and cost for reapplication. We have successfully cultured such endosymbiotic probiotics, specifically Ruegeria, and have demonstrated their superior efficacy in enhancing coral stress tolerance in both laboratory and field trials. Using amplicon sequencing of a population-resolved gene, our initial data show that endosymbiotic Ruegeria isolated from corals are also present in other marine invertebrates. This finding highlights the need for a comprehensive survey of their presence and abundance across marine hosts to fully explore their host spectrum. Furthermore, this dataset will allow the identification of true coral-specific Ruegeria populations. We will establish a simplified benthic community in mesocosm to test the affinity and impact of the select Ruegeria isolates on coral and non-coral hosts. This project aims to evaluate the potential non-target effects of powerful coral probiotics, a key step toward their field applications. 珊瑚礁蘊育全球近30%的海洋生物多樣性，並透過生態服務維持十億人口的生計。然而在氣候暖化、海洋酸化等全球性威脅，以及優養化、過度捕撈等區域壓力下，全球珊瑚礁自1950年代起已消失半數。即便樂觀估計升溫控制在1.5℃內，未來仍有70-90%珊瑚礁面臨滅絕危機。 珊瑚與真核、原核微生物形成共生網絡，其中「蟲黃藻」（Symbiodiniaceae）最為關鍵——這類棲息於珊瑚細胞內的光合甲藻為宿主提供能量。當環境惡化（如熱壓力）時，珊瑚會排出共生藻導致白化現象，嚴重時將造成大規模死亡。例如2014-2017年的全球白化事件就摧毀35%珊瑚礁，而2024年香港海域的珊瑚也正經歷新一輪嚴重白化。 微生物療法近年成為珊瑚保育新方向。實驗室研究證實，益生菌能提升珊瑚耐熱性並降低死亡率，但現有技術面臨重大瓶頸：益生菌難以在珊瑚體內長期定殖，需反覆施用增加成本。本研究團隊近期提出創新框架，透過篩選帶有「演化時間尺度上年輕共生菌進化印記」的珊瑚內生菌（如 Ruegeria 菌株），利用其基因組特徵（如核心代謝基因退化）強化其組織駐留能力，大幅降低重複施用需求。 我們已成功培養此類 Ruegeria 益生菌，並在實驗室與實地驗證其提升珊瑚抗壓力的卓越效果。透過基因標記追蹤技術，初步發現珊瑚源 Ruegeria 亦存在於其他海洋生物。本研究將全面調查其宿主多樣性，釐清專屬珊瑚的菌株族群，並在人工生態池中測試益生菌對珊瑚與非目標生物的親和性及影響，為未來大規模珊瑚復育應用奠定安全基礎。

14108225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14108225.value: JunB在骨骼肌再生中的功能-肌肉幹細胞與微環境互作的研究

14108225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14108225.value: Prof CHEN, Xiaona Prof Sun, Hao

14108225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108225.value: Skeletal muscle has a remarkable ability to regenerate after injury thus provides an excellent model to study tissue regeneration. Muscle regeneration relies on its resident muscle stem cells (MuSCs, also called satellite cells) which normally lie quiescently beneath muscle fiber. MuSCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of MuSCs undergoes self-renewal and returns to quiescence to replenish MuSC pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulations may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia. Here we propose to investigate the functional and mechanistic roles of AP-1 transcription factor (TF) JunB in MuSCs. We found JunB is rapidly induced upon MuSC activation; inducible knockout of JunB in MuSCs hampers cell activation and proliferation thus delays acute injury induced regeneration. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, by combined multiomics analysis, we found JunB binds and suppresses the transcription of factors mediating the extrinsic MuSC-niche crosstalk; JunB ablation leads to increased expression of niche factors and alters niche cell composition and cell crosstalk. Meanwhile, JunB also binds and activates MyoD expression in MuSCs to intrinsically promotes MuSC activation/proliferation. Further mechanistic dissection showed that JunB orchestrates gene transcription by regulating regulate enhancer (E)-promoter (P) looping. Based on the preliminary findings, we hypothesize that JunB acts as a versatile regulator of MuSC activity and muscle regeneration through its multifaceted transcriptional regulatory functions/mechanisms; and MuSC expressing JunB plays dual roles in modulating both intrinsic MuSC activities and extrinsic MuSC-niche crosstalk. Three objectives are thus proposed (1) To investigate how JunB promotes MuSC activation/proliferation during muscle regeneration. (2) To elucidate how JunB modulates MuSC-niche crosstalk. (3) To dissect how JunB regulates the transcription of niche interacting factors. Once completed, this study will be the first to uncover JunB as a critical regulator of MuSC function and muscle regeneration; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. 骨骼肌在損傷後具有卓越的再生能力，因此為研究組織再生提供了一個絕佳的模型。肌肉再生依賴其肌肉幹細胞（MuSC，也稱為衛星細胞）。這些細胞通常位於肌纖維下方處於靜息狀態， 但在損傷後可以快速活化並增殖，然後分化並融合成肌纖維；同時，一部分MuSC進行自我更新並恢復到靜息狀態以補充MuSC儲備。成肌譜系進展的每個狀態都由複雜的內在和外在因素/機制調控網絡所協調。這些調控機制的破壞可能導致其喪失再生能力，從而導致肌肉萎縮症、惡病質和肌少症等肌肉萎縮性疾病。本研究旨在研究AP-1轉錄因子（TF）JunB在MuSC中的調控功能與機製。我們發現JunB在MuSC活化後會被快速誘導； MuSC 中 JunB 的誘導敲除會阻礙細胞活化和增殖，從而延緩急性損傷引起的再生。為了闡明其潛在機制，我們透過多組學分析發現，JunB 結合併抑制介MuSC-微環境互作的多個因子的轉錄；JunB 的缺失導致微環境因子表達增加，並改變微環境細胞組成和細胞互作。同時，JunB 也結合並活化 MuSC 中的 MyoD 表達，促進 MuSC 的活化/增殖。進一步的機制分析表明，JunB 透過調控增強子 (E)-啟動子 (P) 環化來調控基因轉錄。基於如上初步研究結果，我們假設 JunB 透過其多方面的轉錄調控功能/機制，成為 MuSC 活性和肌肉再生的多功能調控因子；JunB在調節內在 MuSC 活性和外源性 MuSC-微環境互作方面發揮雙重作用。因此，我們提出了三個研究目標：(1) 研究 JunB 如何在肌肉再生過程中促進 MuSC 的活化/增殖。 (2) 闡明 JunB 如何調控肌肉細胞-微環境互作。 (3) 深入研究 JunB 如何調控微環境互作因子的轉錄。本研究完成後，將首次揭示 JunB 作為肌肉細胞功能和肌肉再生的關鍵調控因子；從而增強我們對骨骼肌再生調控機制的認知，為未來治療肌肉損傷和疾病的療法開發奠定基礎。

14108525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14108525.value: FOCUS：針對患有發音及／或語言障礙的粵語兒童及青少年，評估介入治療對內在與遠端成效之溝通參與的臨床評估工具

14108525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14108525.value: Prof Chan, Jason Ying Kuen Prof Cunningham, Barbara Jane Ms Kan, Peggy Ms Lam, Yuk Chau Emily Prof Lee, Kathy Yuet-Sheung Dr Ng, Iris Mr YU, Wilson Shing

14108525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108525.value: Speech Sound and/or Language Disorder(s) (SSLDs) can have negative effects on a child’s academic achievements and health-related quality of life including communicative participation. Communicative participation is defined as the child’s communication and interaction in real word contexts. Poor or limited communicative participation skills potentially result in long-term health outcomes including mental health issues, personality disorder, and poorer employment. SSLDs are therefore considered a real public health issue. Intervention by the Speech Therapist (ST) is fundamental, reflected in the establishment of the school-based ST service by the Education Bureau. Measurement of ST intervention outcomes is key to improving clinical practice for the child and family. There has been a dynamic shift from external/proximal outcomes (impairment-based), towards internal/distal outcomes i.e., communicative participation, that addresses Activities and Participation of the WHO’s ICF framework (2002). At present, the Focus on Communication Outcomes of Children Under Six (FOCUS, CanChild) is the only measurement instrument that directly evaluates the impact (and outcome) of speech and/or language intervention on the child’s communicative participation. As such, the PI and Co-I (KL) recently supervised an MPhil project (Wang, 2024) which has since been completed. This project undertook a comprehensive translation and adaptation process of the FOCUS, culminating in the FOCUS-Traditional Chinese (TC), Hong Kong version, which was in close collaboration with Co-I, BC, a member of the FOCUS and CanChild teams. For any measurement outcome instrument to have clinical (and research) utility, the range of measurement properties laid out by the COSMIN Taxonomy of Measurement Properties, must be evaluated and established. The study by Wang (2024) serves as a pilot study having established initial Reliability (test-retest, intra-rater for parents), internal consistency, and Validity (content, face, structural and construct). However, for the FOCUS-TC, HK to be used as an outcome measurement instrument and be clinically useful, we need to establish its Responsiveness (ability of the instrument to detect clinically significant change post-intervention), and Interpretability (the degree to which parent/ST can assign qualitative and clinical meaning to change in scores, as well as Reliability (of STs). The research team is committed to establishing these clinically relevant and very important measurement properties of the FOCUS-TC, HK, such that the instrument can have both clinical and research utility for STs in Hong Kong, Macau and elsewhere and benefit children and their families. 發音障礙及／或語言障礙有機會對兒童的學業表現和與健康相關的生活質素產生負面影響，其中包括「溝通參與」，即兒童在現實情境中的溝通和互動。缺乏溝通參與技巧可能導致長期的健康問題，包括心理健康問題、人格障礙和就業困難。因此，發音障礙及語言障礙被視為一個確實的公共健康問題。教育局建立校本言語治療服務，反映了言語治療的重要性。對言語治療成效的評估對改善兒童和家庭的臨床實踐至關重要。 過往臨床評估多集中於以障礙為基礎的外在與近端成效，近年則開始關注內在與遠端成效，特別是溝通參與。這亦在世界衛生組織「國際健康功能、身心障礙和健康分類」框架（WHO, 2002）中的「活動與參與」的維度相呼應。目前，《the Focus on Communication Outcomes of Children Under Six (FOCUS, CanChild) 》是唯一直接評估發音及/或語言介入治療對兒童溝通參與影響的測量工具。 有見及此，首席研究員和共同研究員（KL）早前指導了一個為FOCUS進行完善的翻譯及適應過程的碩士研究項目（Wang, 2024），並已完成。該項研究與FOCUS及CanChild團隊成員（BC）合作，正式推出FOCUS繁體中文版（香港版本）。任何測量工具若要具備臨床及研究實用性，均應根據COSMIN測量特性分類法所列範疇進行評估與確立。Wang（2024）的試點研究已確立此版本的FOCUS的初步信度（再測信度、家長的評分者內信度）、內部一致度和有效度（內容效度、表面效度、結構效度和建構效度）。 然而，若要令此版本FOCUS成為可供臨床使用的成效測量工具，尚需進一步確立其敏感度（檢測介入治療後是否有臨床顯著變化的能力）可解釋度（即有多大程度能對分數轉變賦予質性的描述和臨床的解釋），以及言語治療師的評分信度。本研究團隊致力於全面建立此版本FOCUS的臨床相關測量特性，使其具備臨床與研究實用性，期能惠及香港、澳門及其他地區的言語治療師，從而造福兒童及其家庭。

14109025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14109025.value: 研究突觸前蛋白SNAP25的功能和分子特徵以作為神經內分泌前列腺癌藥物重定位的潛在靶點

14109025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14109025.value: Prof Wang, Yuliang Prof Wu, Dinglan

14109025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109025.value: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most diagnosed male malignancy worldwide. Rapid acquisition of resistance to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is inevitable, and up to 20% of CRPC may acquire an ‘‘AR-indifferent’’ neuroendocrine (NE) lineage phenotype, termed as neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) or CRPC-NE.
