NEPC is characterized by a pathological feature of small-cell morphology, high expression of NE lineage biomarkers and attenuated AR signalling. Therapeutic options for NEPC are limited, and the exact molecular mechanisms underlying the NE transdifferentiation remain elusive. Emerging evidence suggests targeting extensive parasympathetic nerve infiltration and neurotransmitters in CRPC may represent a potential therapeutic strategy. In the present proposal, we identified SNAP25, the target molecule of Botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A), as a potential regulator in NE transdifferentiation of PCa, as evidenced by its increased expression in NEPC clinical samples and various in vitro and in vivo models of NEPC by single-cell sequencing (SC-seq) analysis and IHC validation of NEPC clinical tissue. SNAP25 knockout or BTX-A treatment significantly suppressed cell proliferation and NE biomarker expression in NEPC cells, while SNAP25 overexpression conferred an NE phenotype to adenocarcinoma prostate cancer cells. While targeting SNAP25 can disrupt acetylcholine (ACh) autocrine/paracrine growth loops. This, in turn, induces dysregulation of the p-AKT/N-Myc axis in prostate cancer, thereby disrupting the NE phenotype. Lastly, SNAP25 expression could be repressed by AR signaling, and we confirmed SNAP25 and CHRM5 are predominantly expressed in NE cells, while CHRM3 is highly expressed in adenocarcinoma cells. Based on these preliminary data, we hypothesize that the high expression of SNAP25 in NE cells, driven by AR loss, plays a crucial role in NEPC progression. This is achieved by regulating ACh autocrine/paracrine signalling from NE cells, promoting the differentiation of adenocarcinoma prostate cancer cells into NE and contributing to the aggressive phenotype of NE cells. Targeting SNAP25 by reducing its expression, potentially through FDA-approved BTX-A, could serve as an effective intraprostatic therapeutic strategy for NEPC patients. Additionally, using ACh antagonists that target CHRM3 and CHRM5 may enhance NEPC treatment systemically by disrupting parasympathetic nerve regulation in NEPC tumours. We strongly believe that this proposed study will not only deepen our understanding of SNAP25's regulatory role in the acquisition and maintenance of the NE phenotype but also provide novel insights into repurposing BTX-A and ACh receptor antagonists as therapeutic agents for treatment-resistant NEPC， potentially impacting clinical practice. 前列腺癌（PCa）是全球最常見的男性惡性腫瘤。絕大多數 PCa 以雄性激素依賴性腺癌的形式出現，這構成了雄性激素阻斷療法 (ADT) 治療晚期 PCa 的基礎。然而，儘管初期療效確切，但該疾病最終會透過雄激素受體 (AR) 信號傳導恢復而復發，並進展至非激素依賴性階段（稱為去勢抵抗性前列腺癌/CRPC）。此階段通常保留腺癌表型，可透過下一代 AR 訊號抑制劑（例如恩雜魯胺）治療。不幸的是，這些藥物的快速抗藥性仍然不可避免，高達 20% 的 CRPC 可能獲得「AR 無關」的神經內分泌 (NE) 譜系表型，稱為神經內分泌前列腺癌 (NEPC) 或 CRPC-NE。 NEPC 的病理特徵為小細胞形態、NE 譜系生物標記高表達以及 AR 訊號傳導減弱。近十年來，治療性 NEPC (t-NEPC) 的盛行率不斷上升，這主要歸因於強效 AR 路徑抑制劑的廣泛使用。 NEPC 的治療選擇有限，NE 轉分化背後的確切分子機制仍不清楚。 在本計劃中，我們透過藥物再利用篩選，確定了 SNAP25（FDA 批准的 A 型肉毒桿菌毒素 (BTX-A) 的目標分子）是前列腺癌 (PCa) NE 轉分化的潛在調節因子，其在臨床樣本以及各種 NEPC 體內外模型中的表達均有所增加。 我們初步的功能研究表明，SNAP25基因敲落 或 BTX-A 治療可顯著抑制 NEPC 細胞的增殖和 NE 生物標記的表達，而過度表達 SNAP25 則可使腺癌 PCa 細胞具有 NE 表型。後續機制研究表明，靶向 SNAP25 可破壞膽鹼能自分泌/旁分泌生長環，進而誘導 PCa 中 p-AKT/N-Myc 軸失調，從而擾亂 NE 表型。最後，AR 訊號傳導可抑制 SNAP25 的表達。 基於此，我們假設在 ADT 期間 AR 抑制所驅動的 SNAP25 上調可透過活化膽鹼能自分泌/旁分泌迴路來促進 PCa 的 NE 轉分化。這可能觸發多個下游級聯反應，促進NE表型的獲得，包括p-AKT/N-Myc訊號路徑。 我們堅信，這項擬議的研究不僅有助於更好地理解SNAP25在NE表型獲得和維持中的調控作用，還能為FDA批准的BTX-A作為難治性NEPC的治療藥物提供新的見解，並可能對臨床實踐產生直接影響。

14109825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14109825.value: 預測快速眼動睡眠行為障礙患者腦退化轉化亞型的新型腸道微生物特徵

14109825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14109825.value: Dr Chan, Joey Wing-yan Dr Chan, Yin Yan Anne Prof Chen, Zigui Dr Ma, Ka Yan Karen Prof Wing, Yun Kwok

14109825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109825.value: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is an early and prodromal marker of various α-synucleinopathies, including Parkinson’s disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) and multiple system atrophy (MSA). Although under the same umbrella of α-synucleinopathy, PD, DLB and MSA share both similarities and disparities in terms of predisposing factors, clinical profiles and pathomechanisms. As the most specific prodrome of α-synucleinopathy, iRBD provides a unique time window for early prevention and intervention before substantial neurodegeneration occurs. In this case, identifying specific conversion types at an early stage of iRBD is essential, not only to facilitate the current understanding of etiology or causes of α-synucleinopathy, but also for future patient-centered intervention trials targeting prodromal neurodegeneration. However, precision prediction of conversion types in patients with iRBD remains challenging. While there are several available markers that may predict overall conversion and/or differentiate between MSA and PD/DLB converters, they are not as effective in distinguishing between PD and DLB. Core neurodegenerative features, especially cognitive decline, remain the most robust and sensitive markers for DLB (dementia-first) vs. PD (parkinsonism-first) conversions, while its predictive validity at an early stage of iRBD is still uncertain. On the other hand, distinct changes in gut microbiota were found in both iRBD patients and multiple α-synucleinopathies. Of note, gut microbiota disturbances associated with PD and DLB have already emerged in patients with iRBD. For example, iRBD had a similar enrichment of Collinsella as in DLB patients and also showed extensive depletion of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria consistent with PD patients. Additionally, data from our cohort showed that patients with iRBD had greater heterogeneity in gut microbial community than that of controls, and pilot prospective analyses further suggested the differential gut microbial patterns between iRBD patients who developed PD and DLB at clinical follow-up. In this regard, we propose to thoroughly analyze the relationship between gut microbiota and neurodegenerative outcomes from our Hong Kong Chinese iRBD cohort with prospectively collected stool specimens, to 1) identify microbiome signatures predictive of parkinsonism- versus dementia-first conversions, 2) translate the signatures into practical quantitative PCR-based assays and test its predictive validity in enriched iRBD patients (i.e., with a higher risk of conversion), and finally 3) estimate the intra-individual reproducibility of the developed assays. We expect that the novel and practical qPCR-based assays, with further external validation, would facilitate future early and individualized interventions for α-synucleinopathies.

14109925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14109925.value: 基於微生物組的中國嬰兒早發性濕疹預防策略的隨機、雙盲和安慰劑對照臨床試驗

14109925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14109925.value: Dr Chan, Oi-man Dr Luk, David Chi-kong Prof Tsui, Stephen Kwok-wing

14109925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109925.value: Eczema affects two-fifths of infants and a quarter of preschool children in Hong Kong. The large majority of childhood eczema first present during infancy when the affected families suffer substantial physical morbidity, social stigmatisation, impaired life quality and psychological stresses. Defective skin barrier seen in eczema allows the penetration of inhalant and food allergens to sensitise and initiate the allergic cascade in the body. This phenomenon of "atopic march" takes place during the preschool years. The identification of predictive biomarkers from early-life exposome or clinical factors would offer an opportunity to design different strategies to improve eczema control or even to prevent eczema development and halt this atopic march. Over the past decade, next-generation sequencing revealed characteristic gut microbial signals for childhood eczema. Such findings resulted in an explosion of microbiome-based therapies such as probiotics and synbiotics, but the evidence for such therapies are conflicting and inconclusive. In recent years, it has become apparent that microbes on the skin are also important determinant for eczema development. Based on 16S rRNA sequencing, birth cohorts from our team over the past decade consistently identified dysbiosis of skin microbiome to be found in early-onset eczema. The two key research questions include the clinical impact of skin microbial biomarkers for predicting infantile eczema and the usefulness of "topical anti-inflammatory controller" combining topical corticosteroid and emollient in preventing early-onset eczema. Based on our recent Skin Cohort with 166 Chinese infants that identified Shannon diversity index (SDI) cut-off 0.687 for skin microbiome over left antecubital fossa at 3 months to be a good biomarker for predicting eczema, this grant proposal adopts the microbiome-based approach to stratify infants using this biomarker into "standard-risk" or "high-risk" groups for eczema development. Depending on such risk stratification, healthy term infants will be randomly allocated 8-week treatment with either of two different active interventions with different degree of immunosuppression by topical corticosteroid (0.1% mometasone furoate or 1% hydrocortisone) in combination with emollient or emollient-only placebo. All subjects will then be followed until the end of infancy for occurrence of eczema, atopy and food allergy as well as subjects' safety. Paired flocked skin swabs will be tested for alterations in microbiomes. Overall, this randomised, double-blind and placebo-controlled clinical trial will generate solid evidence about the scientific merit and clinical value of skin microbiome analysis in facilitating preventive strategy for infantile eczema. 濕疹影響香港五分之二的嬰兒和四分之一的學齡前兒童。大多數兒童濕疹在嬰兒期首次出現，受影響的家庭承受著嚴重的身體疾病、社會歧視、生活品質下降和心理壓力。濕疹患者皮膚屏障缺陷使吸入和食物過敏原能夠滲透，從而引起過敏反應，並引發體內的過敏級聯反應。這種「過敏性行進」現象發生在學齡前。從早期暴露組或臨床因素中識別出可預測的生物標記物，將有助於設計不同的策略來改善濕疹控制，甚至預防濕疹發展並阻止這種過敏性行進。在過去十年中，新一代定序揭示了兒童濕疹的特徵性腸道微生物訊號。這些發現促使益生菌和合生元等以微生物組為基礎的療法蓬勃發展，但這些療法的證據卻相互矛盾且尚無定論。近年來，皮膚微生物也逐漸成為濕疹發展的重要決定因素。基於16S rRNA定序，我們團隊過去十年的出生隊列研究一致發現，早發性濕疹有皮膚微生物群失調。兩個關鍵研究問題包括：皮膚微生物標記對預測嬰兒濕疹的臨床影響，以及結合外用皮質類固醇和潤膚劑的「外用抗炎控製劑」在預防早發性濕疹的有效性。基於我們近期進行的一項針對一百六十六名中國嬰兒的皮膚隊列研究，該研究確定三個月齡嬰兒左肘前窩皮膚微生物組的香農多樣性指數截斷值為0.687，是預測濕疹的良好生物標記。本資助提案採用以微生物組為基礎的方法，將使用此生物標記的嬰兒分為濕疹發展的「標準風險」組或「高風險」組。根據風險分層，健康足月嬰兒將被隨機分配接受為期八週的治療，接受兩種不同免疫抑製程度的積極幹預措施之一：局部皮質類固醇（0.1%糠酸莫米鬆或1%氫化可的松）聯合潤膚劑或僅含潤膚劑的安慰劑。所有受試者將被追蹤至嬰兒期結束，以觀察濕疹和食物過敏的發生，受試者的安全性以及皮膚微生物組的變化。總而言之，這項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的臨床試驗將提供確切的證據，證明皮膚微生物組分析在促進嬰兒濕疹預防策略方面的科學和臨床價值。

14110025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14110025.value: 為何澱粉-表沒食子兒茶素-3-沒食子酸酯（EGCG）複合物（五型抗性澱粉）在緩解非酒精性脂肪肝疾病方面表現優於單獨使用EGCG？

14110025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14110025.value: Prof Chen, Zhen-Yu Prof Cheung, Chi Keung Peter

14110025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110025.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has emerged as a global health concern, affecting 38 % of the population, yet specific therapeutic strategies remain lacking. While a healthy diet is fundamental for managing NAFLD, the exact functional ingredients and their individual or combined effects on alleviating the disease remain poorly understood, a question with significant public health implications as it could help people with NAFLD optimize their dietary choices for therapeutic benefit. Starch is the primary carbohydrate in our diet, providing about 40 % of our daily energy, while epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) is a major polyphenolic catechin found in green tea, a widely consumed beverage worldwide. Notably, EGCG has shown potential biological activities in preventing and treating NAFLD; however, its clinical efficacy is severely limited by poor bioavailability. Our preliminary results demonstrated for the first time that the maize starch-EGCG complex significantly outperformed EGCG alone in alleviating NAFLD symptoms, including an approximately 40 % reduction in visceral fat. However, it remains unclear whether other starch-EGCG complexes could further alleviate NAFLD and what mechanisms are involved. Since the starch-EGCG complex has been recognized as a type 5 resistant starch, it may provide health benefits by reaching the colon and interacting with the gut microbiota, depending on its structural characteristics. We thus hypothesize that starch-EGCG complexes derived from starches with diverse structural properties will exhibit varying efficiencies in managing NAFLD through their unique interactions with gut microbiota, as supported by our preliminary study. In this project, we will first synthesize and evaluate a series of starch-EGCG complexes in a NAFLD mouse model to identify the optimal configurations for therapeutic outcomes. The best-performing starch-EGCG complex will then be examined for its effects on gut microbiota through metagenomic sequencing. Additionally, metabolomic profiling will be conducted to identify key microbial metabolites that mediate the complex’s anti-inflammatory and lipid-regulating effects. Based on the multi-omics sequencing results, we will assess the impacts of targeted bacteria and metabolites on hepatic lipogenesis, lipid oxidation, and inflammation through fecal microbiota transplantation, aiming to elucidate how the reshaped gut microbiota contributes to NAFLD alleviation. The findings will help future clinical research on the starch-EGCG complex as a potential scalable, food-based alternative therapy for NAFLD and related metabolic disorders. 非酒精性脂肪肝疾病（NAFLD）已成為全球健康問題，影響約 38% 的人口，但目前仍缺乏具體的治療策略。儘管健康飲食是管理 NAFLD 的基礎，但確切的功能性成分及其單獨或協同緩解疾病的效果仍未完全明瞭。這個問題具有重要的公共衛生意義，因為它可能幫助 NAFLD 患者優化飲食選擇以獲得治療效益。 澱粉是我們飲食中的主要碳水化合物，提供約 40% 的日常能量；而表沒食子兒茶素-3-沒食子酸酯（EGCG）是綠茶中的主要多酚類兒茶素，綠茶是全球廣泛飲用的飲品。值得注意的是，EGCG 在預防和治療 NAFLD 方面已顯示潛在的生物活性，但其臨床效果因生物利用度低而嚴重受限。我們的初步研究首次證明，玉米澱粉-EGCG 複合物在緩解 NAFLD 症狀（包括內臟脂肪減少約 40%）方面顯著優於單獨使用 EGCG。然而，其他澱粉-EGCG 複合物是否能進一步緩解 NAFLD，以及涉及的機制為何，目前仍不清楚。 由於澱粉-EGCG 複合物已被認定為第五型抗性澱粉，它可能通過到達結腸並與腸道微生物群相互作用而提供健康益處，具體效果取決於其結構特性。因此，我們假設：不同結構特性的澱粉所形成的澱粉-EGCG 複合物，將通過與腸道菌群的獨特互動，在管理 NAFLD 方面表現出不同效率（初步研究支持此觀點）。本項目將首先在 NAFLD 小鼠模型中合成並評估一系列澱粉-EGCG 複合物，以確定最佳治療效果的結構配置。隨後，我們將通過宏基因組測序分析表現最佳的複合物對腸道菌群的影響，並進行代謝組學分析以鑑定關鍵的微生物代謝物——這些代謝物可能介導複合物的抗炎和調脂作用。基於多組學測序結果，我們將通過糞便微生物群移植（FMT）評估目標細菌及代謝物對肝臟脂肪生成、脂質氧化和炎症的影響，旨在闡明重塑後的腸道菌群如何促進 NAFLD 的緩解。 研究結果將為未來有關澱粉-EGCG 複合物作為潛在可擴展的、以食物為基礎的替代療法應用於治療 NAFLD 及相關代謝疾病的臨床研究奠定基礎。

14110125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14110125.value: 對於有中度心血管風險的患者，在接受結腸鏡檢查和/或息肉切除術時繼續或中斷阿司匹林;安慰劑對照試驗

14110125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110125.value: One in 4 adults between 50 and 80 reports taking regular aspirin. The prevalence of aspirin use increases with age as well as co-morbid vascular diseases. Patients with cardiovascular diseases are at risk of developing colorectal neoplasms. In patients undergoing screening colonoscopy, interruption of aspirin is believed to be associated with increased cardiovascular events. Continuation of aspirin can however be associated with an increased risk of post-polypectomy bleeding. International guidelines on peri-endoscopy management recommend the continuation of aspirin based on evidence from cohort studies, mostly retrospective, suggesting that the rate of bleeding is low. Cardiovascular complications from aspirin interruption can lead to disabilities and occasional deaths. The cardiovascular risks following aspirin continuation or interruption in endoscopy have not been well studied. There has been no randomized study to compare either strategy. Endoscopists are divided on their opinion on whether to stop or to continue aspirin. The proposed large randomized controlled trial (RCT) is powered to detect small differences in both outcomes. Findings from this RCT will address this important question and inform our clinical practice. 每4名50至80歲的成年人中就有一人定期服用阿司匹林， 阿司匹林的使用隨著年齡的增長以及合併血管疾病的增加而增加。 心血管疾病患者患結直腸腫瘤的風險較高。他們在接受結腸鏡篩查時，阿司匹林中斷增加心血管事件風險。然而，繼續服用阿司匹林可能與息肉切除術後出血的風險增加。內鏡檢查國際指南建議繼續服用阿司匹林，基於隊列研究的證據。 隊列研究大多爲回顧性研究，表明出血率較低。阿司匹林中斷却引起的心血管併發症可能導致殘疾和偶爾死亡。阿司匹林持續或中斷後的心血管風險內窺鏡檢查尚未通過隨機對照試驗進行研究。 內窺鏡醫生對是否停止或繼續服用阿司匹林意見不一。擬議的大型隨機對照試驗有助於檢測兩種結果的微小差異。本隨機對照試驗的結果將解决這一個重要的問題，爲我們的臨床實踐提供了信息。

14110625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14110625.value: 研究cohesin complex及染色質空間構像在惡性B細胞中的作用

14110625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14110625.value: Prof Dalton, Stephen Prof TSE, Gary Man-Kit

14110625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110625.value: The aim of this project is to investigate the role of cohesin complex regulators in B cell malignancy and discover potential therapeutic strategies. Lymphomas are among the top 10 most common cancers in Hong Kong and Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most frequent subtype. Lymphomas commonly derived from B-cells transiting the germinal center (GC) reaction. B cells within the GCs undergo rapid cell division and simultaneous somatic hypermutation to generate a high affinity B-cell receptors (BCRs). Once proliferating GC B-cells called centroblasts exhaust their resources, they become post-replicative centrocytes and compete for interaction with GC T-cells. Only those centrocytes with high affinity BCRs receive strong T-cell help and can either undergo further proliferative bursts or exit the GC as memory or plasma cells. Proper 3D organization of the genome into territories where sets of genes are coregulated together, as well as long range enhance promoter looping are critical for differentiation and maintaining cell lineage identity. This process is controlled by the cohesin complex. The unloading of cohesion requires specific regulatory factors including WAPL, PDS5A and PDS5B. We discovered that PDS5B is the most commonly mutated architectural protein in DLBCLs. We previously showed that cohesin complex is required for B-cells differentiation in GC. Our pilot studies indicate that PDS5B mutation/deletion reduces germinal center reaction; controls MYC and immune synapse gene IFNRs involved in GC phenotypic transitions and facilitates lymphomagenesis. Mechanistically speaking, Hi-C of GC cells from PDS5B mutated mice exhibited that a ‘TAD merging’ genomic architecture phenotype. In addition, mutant form of PDS5B in DLBCL patients possess a different interactive capacity to cohesin complex to affect cohesin distribution and loop extrusion. Therefore, our hypothesis is that PDS5B is required for T-cell dependent immune synapse epigenetic programming in GC centrocytes, by reprograming of cohesin activity and hence coordinated expression of genes that regulates B cell recycling or exit the GC. As a consequence, B-cells become architecturally “locked” into the proliferative centroblast phenotype which leads to malignant transformation. To test the above hypothesis, we have the following three specific aims: (1) to elucidate the mechanism of PDS5B mutation regulated MYC and IFNR changes; (2) to validate the PDS5B effect in DLBCL patients; (3) to develop potential small molecules treating DLBCL patients bearing cohesin related mutations. Therefore, we expect this project will provide potential novel therapeutic strategies based targeting the novel mechanisms of 3D genome in DLBCL. 本項目的目的是研究cohesin complex調節因子在B細胞惡性腫瘤中的作用，並發掘潛在的治療策略。 淋巴瘤是香港十大常見癌症之一，而瀰漫性大B細胞淋巴瘤（DLBCL）是最常見的亞型。淋巴瘤通常來自經過生殖中心（GC）反應的 B 細胞。GC 內的 B 細胞會進行快速的細胞分裂，同時發生體質超突變，以產生高親和性的 B 細胞受體 (BCR)。一旦增殖的 GC B 細胞（稱為中心細胞）耗盡其資源，就會變成複製後的中心細胞，並與 GC T 細胞競爭互動。只有那些具有高親和性 BCR 的中心細胞才能獲得 T 細胞的強力幫助，並進一步增殖突發或以記憶細胞或等離子細胞的形式離開 GC。 基因組產生適當的 3D構象從而使得相關基因群配製在同一區域，以及長距離增強啟動子相互作用，對於細胞分化和維持細胞特性至關重要。此過程受cohesin complex控制。Cohesin的卸載需要特定的調控因子，包括 WAPL、PDS5A 和 PDS5B。我們發現 PDS5B 是 DLBCLs 中最常突變的結構蛋白。 我們之前的研究顯示，GC 中的 B 細胞分化需要 cohesin 複合物。我們的前期試驗研究顯示，PDS5B突變/缺失會降低生殖中心反應；控制參與GC表型轉換的MYC和免疫突觸基因IFNRs，並促進淋巴瘤的形成。從機制上來說，PDS5B突變小鼠的GC細胞Hi-C表現出「TAD合併」的基因組架構表型。此外，DLBCL 患者的突變型 PDS5B 擁有與 cohesin 複合物不同的互作能力，以影響 cohesin 分佈和環擠出。 因此，我們的假設是，PDS5B 是 GC 中心細胞中依賴 T 細胞的免疫突觸表觀遺傳編程所必需的，透過重新編程凝聚素活性，進而協調調控 B 細胞回收或退出 GC 的基因表達。結果，B 細胞在結構上被「鎖定」為增殖性中心細胞表型，導致惡性轉變。 為了驗證上述假說，我們有以下三個具體目標：（1）闡明 PDS5B 基因突變誘發 MYC 和 IFNR 基因改變的機制；（2）在 DLBCL 患者數據中驗證 PDS5B 突變的致癌作用；（3）開發潛在的小分子藥物治療帶有cohesin相關突變的 DLBCL 患者。因此，我們期望本專案能針對 DLBCL 的 3D 基因組新機制，提供潛在的新型治療策略。

14111925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14111925.value: 闡明抗精神病藥物誘發代謝副作用的罕見及非SNP遺傳基礎：風險預測與個人化干預的全方位策略

14111925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14111925.value: Dr Lui, Sai Yu Simon Prof Sham, Pak-Chung Prof TSUI, Kwok Wing Stephen

14111925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111925.value: Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) are widely used to treat SCZ and psychotic disorders, but they are known to induce metabolic side effects, such as dyslipidemia and obesity, posing significant clinical challenges. While genetic factors are believed to contribute to the variability of these side effects, there are only few pharmacogenomic studies to date, mostly in Caucasians and the majority focused on weight gain only. Also, existing studies only covered common single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), yet rare and other non-SNP variations might also contribute to metabolic side-effects (s/e). Besides, dosage information has not been considered in genomic studies, and previous studies are usually of short duration. Here we will reveal the genetic basis of SGA-related metabolic abnormalities via whole-genome sequencing (WGS). To our knowledge, this is the first WGS study and the first to identify non-SNP genetic variants underlying SGA-induced metabolic s/e. The study will be primarily based on a large naturalistic cohort of psychosis patients from Hong Kong with a median follow-up of >5 years. We will unravel rare variants (RVs) and other genetic variations (e.g. copy number variations[CNV], structural variations[SV], tandem repeats[TR]) associated with metabolic side-effects of SGAs. We also plan to test how drug dosage interacts with genetic factors in affecting metabolic outcomes. Threshold and non-linear effects of SGA dosage will also be investigated. Next, we will study whether statins/metformin may mitigate SGA-induced metabolic s/e, which has not been investigated in real-world studies of a sufficiently long follow-up. We will then evaluate how genetic variations affect the effectiveness of these drugs, which has not been studied before. Finally, we will build prediction models for metabolic abnormalities, integrating both clinical and genomic risk factors. We will consider the whole spectrum of genetic variations, including both common and rare variants, polygenic scores, and clinical risk factors simultaneously. We will also explore state-of-the-art machine learning approaches, such as deep learning with attention mechanisms, which also capture non-linear relationships and interactions. We believe our model will potentially be useful in delineating high-risk patients, fostering early and targeted interventions. 第二代抗精神病藥物（SGAs）廣泛用於治療思覺失調症及其他精神病症，但已知其會引發血脂異常和肥胖等代謝副作用，為臨床帶來重大挑戰。儘管遺傳因素被認為是導致這些副作用個體差異的原因之一，但至今相關的藥物基因體學研究甚少，且多數以高加索人種為對象，並僅僅關注體重增加的議題。此外，現有研究僅涵蓋常見的單一核苷酸多態性（SNPs），然而罕見及其他非SNP變異也可能導致代謝副作用。再者，過去的基因體學研究並未考慮藥物劑量，且研究的持續時間通常較短。 在本研究中，我們將透過全基因組定序（WGS）來揭示SGA相關代謝異常的遺傳基礎。就我們所知，此為首項利用WGS的研究，也是首次鑑定與SGA引發的代謝副作用相關的非SNP遺傳變異。本研究將主要基於一個來自香港、針對精神病患者的大型自然世代研究隊列，其中位追蹤期超過五年。我們將探究與SGA代謝副作用相關的罕見變異（RVs）及其他遺傳變異（例如：拷貝數變異[CNV]、結構變異[SV]、串聯重複序列[TR]）。我們亦計劃檢視藥物劑量如何與遺傳因素交互作用，從而影響代謝結果。SGA藥物劑量的閾值效應與非線性效應也將一併探討。 接著，我們將研究斯他汀類藥物或二甲雙胍是否能減輕SGA引發的代謝副作用，這一點在過去具有足夠長追蹤期的真實世界研究中尚未被探討過。我們將進一步評估遺傳變異如何影響這些藥物的療效，此前從未有研究探討過此議題。 最後，我們將整合臨床與基因體風險因子，建立代謝異常的預測模型。我們將同時考量整個遺傳變異譜系，包括常見與罕見變異、多基因風險評分，以及臨床風險因子。我們也將探索最先進的機器學習方法，例如帶有注意力機制的深度學習，這類方法亦能捕捉非線性關係與交互作用。我們相信，我們的模型將有潛力協助識別高風險患者，從而促進早期及目標性干預。

14112025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14112025.value: 研究 Mrg15 在調控幼年心臟再生中的功能機制

14112025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112025.value: Over the past three decades, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. The mammalian adult heart is notorious for its inability to regenerate; however, the neonatal one can transiently yet functionally regenerate after severe injuries within the first week after birth in mice. Understanding how the neonatal heart regenerates may shed new light on therapeutic development for adult cardiac repair. Neonatal cardiomyocytes (CMs) are more immature and can re-enter the cell cycle for cell division after injury. In contrast, the loss of adult myocardium is not replaced by proliferation of pre-existing CMs but fibrotic scar that partly contributes to functional decline. The molecular mechanisms controlling cell cycle progression and division of neonatal CMs remain unclear. In this study, we found that Mrg15 is highly expressed in the neonatal heart within the first week after birth but gradually downregulated upon heart development. Mrg15 depletion in Isl1+ heart progenitor or CM results in a significant reduction in heart growth and regeneration. Importantly, we found that Mrg15 is responsible for regulating neonatal CM proliferation. Mechanistically, we show that Mrg15 interacts with Tip60, an acetyltransferase, and RNA pol II, potentially regulating gene transcription via chromatin remodeling. Tip60 depletion in CM also leads to reduced CM proliferation, heart growth and regeneration. In this proposal, we will dissect how Mrg15 expression is regulated during neonatal heart development and regeneration (Aim 1), the action mechanism by which Mrg15/Tip60 regulates gene expression related to CM proliferation and neonatal heart regeneration (Aim 2), and whether we can promote adult heart repair by re-activating Mrg15 in the adult heart after injuries. Our proposal will give clinically relevant insights into adult heart repair and regeneration by recapitulating regenerative mechanisms of the neonatal heart into the adult counterpart. 過去三十年來，心血管疾病仍然是全球死亡的主要原因。成年哺乳動物的心臟因其無法再生的特性而聞名；然而，幼年心臟在出生後的第一週內，能夠在嚴重受傷後暫時且功能性地再生。理解幼年心臟的再生機制可能為成人心臟修復的治療開發提供新的啟示。幼年心肌細胞相對較不成熟，且在受傷後能重新進入細胞週期進行細胞分裂。相比之下，成人心肌的損失並非由現有心肌細胞的增殖來替代，而是由纖維化疤痕替代，這在一定程度上導致功能下降。控制幼年心肌細胞細胞週期進程和分裂的分子機制仍不清楚。 在本研究中，我們發現 Mrg15 在出生後的第一週內在幼年心臟中表現高度活躍，但隨著心臟發育逐漸下調。在 Isl1+ 心臟組先細胞或心肌細胞中缺失 Mrg15 會顯著減少心臟的生長和再生能力。重要的是，我們發現 Mrg15 負責調控幼年心肌細胞的增殖。在機制上，我們顯示 Mrg15 與乙酰轉移酶 Tip60 以及 RNA 聚合酶 II 互作，可能通過染色質重塑來調控基因轉錄。心肌細胞中缺失 Tip60 同樣會導致心肌細胞增殖減少，以及心臟的生長與再生能力下降。 在本提案中，我們將探討以下目標： 1. Mrg15 在幼年心臟發育和再生過程中的表達如何被調控。 2. Mrg15/Tip60 通過何種機制調控與心肌細胞增殖與幼年心臟再生相關的基因表達。 3. 是否可以通過在受傷後重新激活成年心臟中的 Mrg15 來促進成年心臟的修復。 本提案旨在通過將幼年心臟的再生機制應用於成年心臟，為成人心臟修復與再生提供臨床相關的重要見解。

14112125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14112125.value: 探究 MED27 基因突變導致神經發育障礙遺傳病的致病機理

14112125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14112125.value: Prof Chan, Edwin Ho Yin Prof WANG, Huating

14112125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112125.value: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) encompass a range of conditions affecting brain function and development, with approximately 90% of them lacking approved treatments. Understanding their pathogenicity (i.e., how they cause disease) is essential to develop precision gene therapies. Recently, we identified an autosomal recessive NDD associated with the Mediator complex subunit 27 (MED27) gene. Mediator (MED) is a highly conserved complex that initiates transcription by bridging transcription factors bound at enhancers to RNA polymerase II transcription machinery at promoters. Studies on individual MED subunits revealed that each influences specific cellular or developmental processes. All patients with MED27 variants exhibited cerebellar hypoplasia or atrophy, indicating the vulnerability of the cerebellum to MED27 alterations. Our hypothesis posits that disease-causing MED27 variants induce conformational change of MED, perturbing its DNA binding and chromatin interactions. This results in dysregulated transcription of genes critical for cerebellum development. To investigate this, we generated human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) harboring patient-specific MED27 mutations. Molecular analysis revealed altered promoter binding and chromatin looping with target genes’ expression changes in mutant hESCs-derived neuronal progenitor cells. Concurrently, we established mouse models carrying patient-specific mutations in Med27 and complete loss-of-function (LoF) of Med27, respectively. Mice with central nervous system LoF Med27 exhibited cerebellar agenesis, while those with cerebellum-specific LoF Med27 displayed progressive cerebellar atrophy, suggesting that Med27 is essential for cerebellar development. Based on these results, we aim to elucidate the pathogenicity mechanism of our newly identified NDD characterized by cerebellar atrophy, utilizing the preclinical models we have generated. To assess potential defects in cerebellar development, we will mimic the developing cerebellum through differentiating human cerebellar organoids from hESCs. We will examine how patient-specific MED27 mutations disrupt DNA binding and chromatin organization and seek target genes that are directly affected by mutant MED27 and might cause impaired cerebellar development. Furthermore, we will evaluate whether mice harboring patient-specific Med27 mutations recapitulate patients’ phenotypes, including potential motor and cognitive deficits, and progressive cerebellar atrophy. We will also identify dysregulated genes in mutant mice through single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomic analysis. By comparing these results with our previous data, we will determine whether the patient-specific MED27 mutations resemble partial LoF effects or instead result in gain of novel functions, each of which would require a distinct therapeutic approach. Our findings will not only establish valuable preclinical models and guide the development of therapeutics, but also shed light on NDDs caused by other MED subunits. 神經發育障礙 (Neurodevelopmental disorders, NDDs) 涵蓋一系列影響大腦功能與發育的疾病，其中約 90% 缺乏治療方法, 而了解其致病機制對於開發精準基因療法至關重要。最近，我們鑑定出一種與 Mediator 複合體亞基 27 (MED27) 基因相關的神經發育障礙遺傳病。Mediator (MED) 是一種高度保守的複合體，通過它可以將結合於增強子上的轉錄因子與啟動子上的 RNA 聚合酶 II 轉錄機制連接起來，從而啟動基因表達。研究顯示，每個 MED 亞基均影響特定的細胞或發育過程。所有攜帶 MED27 突變的患者均表現出小腦發育不全或萎縮，顯示小腦對 MED27 變異高度敏感。 我們假設 MED27 突變會導致 MED 結構發生改變，干擾其與 DNA 的結合及染色質的相互作用，最終導致小腦發育關鍵基因的異常轉錄。為了證實此假設，我們生成了攜帶患者特定 MED27 突變的人類胚胎幹細胞 (hESCs)。前期實驗顯示，在突變型 hESCs 分化而成的神經祖細胞中，下游基因的啟動子結合與染色質環化發生改變，並伴隨基因表達異常。同時，我們建立了攜帶患者特定 Med27 突變和 Med27功能缺失 (LoF) 的小鼠模型。中樞神經系統 Med27 功能缺失的小鼠表現出小腦發育缺失，而小腦特異性 Med27 功能缺失的小鼠則出現進行性小腦萎縮，表明 Med27 對於小腦發育至關重要。 基於這些結果，我們將利用已建立的的臨床前模型闡明這種以小腦萎縮為特徵的新型 NDD 的致病機制。為了評估小腦發育中的潛在缺陷，我們將通過分化hESCs產生人類小腦類器官來模擬小腦發育，並研究 MED27 突變如何破壞 DNA 結合與染色質結構。我們將尋找直接受突變型 MED27 影響的目標基因，並探討其是否導致小腦發育缺陷。此外，我們將評估攜帶患者特定 Med27 突變的小鼠是否重現患者的表型，包括可能的運動和認知缺陷以及進行性小腦萎縮。我們還將通過單細胞分辨率的空間轉錄組學分析確定突變小鼠的基因表達異常情況。通過將這些結果與我們之前的數據進行比較，我們將確定患者特定的 MED27 突變是否造成功能缺失效應，或是產生了新的有害功能，從而推論相應的治療策略。我們的研究結果不僅將建立有價值的臨床前模型並指導基因療法開發，還將為其他由 MED 亞基引起的神經發育障礙遺傳病提供新的見解。

14112225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14112225.value: 精神障礙與快速眼動睡眠行為障礙共病患者的7年隨訪研究：診斷穩定性與α-突觸核蛋白神經退化前驅標記物的進展

14112225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14112225.value: Dr Chan, Joey Wing-yan Dr Huang, Bei Prof Mok, Vincent Chung-tong Ms Yang, Yuhua

14112225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112225.value: REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia characterized by recurrent dream enactment behaviors and REM sleep without atonia (RSWA). Idiopathic RBD (iRBD) has been suggested as the most specific marker of α-synucleinopathy, including Parkinson’s Disease (PD) and Dementia of Lewy Body (DLB). The prevalence of RBD in patients with psychiatric disorders (psy-RBD) was estimated almost ten-time higher than that of the general population. While psy-RBD was conventionally postulated to be antidepressant-induced RSWA, our previous studies showed that psy-RBD had reduced striatal dopamine transmission, prominent prodromal markers (i.e., colour vision and olfaction dysfunction), a higher probability for prodromal PD than psychiatric control without RBD, and a familial aggregation of RBD, PD and dementia. Collectively, it suggests that psy-RBD is more than a simply drug-induced condition, but is likely reflecting an underlying α-synucleinopathy, which needs close monitoring for symptomatic progression and neurodegenerative risk. Despite these insights, the complex relationship among psychiatric disease, RBD and neurodegeneration will require further delineation. In particular, it remains unclear on the differentiation of antidepressant-related RBD from those underlying predisposed neurodegeneration that would be uncovered by antidepressant. Moreover, definitive proof of conversion to neurodegenerative diseases among psy-RBD patients remains unclear, albeit their neurodegenerative risk is increased. Long-term prospective follow-up is essential to capture the full disease trajectory of RBD and prodromal markers in psy-RBD. In the past years, we have established a spectrum of psy-RBD cohort, including 77 psychiatric patients with video-polysomnography (v-PSG) confirmed (psy-RBD), 72 with probable RBD with subthreshold RSWA (psy-pRBD), 82 psychiatric control and 132 healthy controls. This project aims to conduct a prospective study among these groups to delineate the trajectory of neurodegeneration and stability of RBD features in psychiatric population. In addition to clinical features and prodromal markers, we will utilize ambulatory home v-PSG to document REM-related behaviors and EMG activity to capture the evolvement and stability of RBD features. This project will enrich the limited scientific literature on the natural course of RBD in the context of psychiatric disorders, deepen our understanding of prognosis of psy-RBD and clarify the complex relationship among psychiatric disorders (especially depression), RBD and neurodegeneration. From psychiatric perspective, the study will provide insight towards the heterogeneity of depression by identifying subtypes of depressed subjects who will be predisposed to future neurodegeneration. This study could provide prospective evidence that can guide future research and intervention on the intersection of psychiatric disorders, RBD, and neurodegeneration. 快速動眼期睡眠行為障礙（RBD）是一種異睡症，其特徵為反覆出現夢境演繹行為以及缺少正常的快速動眼期肌張力喪失（RSWA）。特發性RBD被認為是α-突觸核蛋白病的最具特異性標誌，包括帕金森氏症（PD）和路易體癡呆（DLB）。 在精神疾病患者中，RBD的發病率（psy-RBD）大約是一般人群的十倍。儘管傳統上認為是由抗憂鬱藥物引起的，近期研究顯示，psy-RBD患者具有早期腦退化相關跡象，包括下丘腦多巴胺傳導減少、前驅標誌如色覺與嗅覺障礙、更高的帕金森氏症風險，家族聚集RBD以及腦退化疾病。這些結果顯示，psy-RBD不僅僅是藥物誘發的現象，更可能反映潛在的α-突觸核蛋白病變，需密切監測其症狀進展與神經退化風險。 儘管已有初步發現，精神疾病、RBD與腦退化之間的複雜關係仍需進一步釐清。尤其是如何區分患者單純由抗憂鬱劑引起抑或有潛在神經退化風險。此外，儘管psy-RBD患者的神經退化風險升高，但其轉化為神經退化性疾病的確鑿證據仍不明確。因此，進行長期前瞻性追蹤研究，有助於完整了解psy-RBD的疾病進程及前驅標誌的演變情況。 我們已建立了psy-RBD的研究隊列，包括77位經由視頻多導睡眠檢查（v-PSG）確認的psy-RBD患者、72位具有臨界RSWA的可能RBD患者（psy-pRBD）、82位精神疾病對照患者及132位健康對照組。本研究旨在進行前瞻性研究，以描繪精神疾病患者中RBD特徵的變化情況與神經退化的演變軌跡。除了臨床特徵與前驅標誌之外，我們亦將使用居家型v-PSG來記錄睡眠行為及肌電活動，以捕捉RBD特徵的演變與穩定性。 本研究將加深對精神疾病背景下RBD自然病程和預後的瞭解，並釐清精神疾病、RBD與神經退化之間的複雜關聯。從精神醫學的角度來看，本研究將有助於解析憂鬱症的異質性，藉此辨識出未來有較高神經退化傾向的亞型。此研究亦可能提供前瞻性的實證，為未來精神疾病、RBD與神經退化的交叉研究與介入提供依據。

14112525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14112525.value: 解析脂質相關巨噬細胞在肝細胞癌免疫治療抗性中的調控機制與功能

14112525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14112525.value: Prof CHENG, Alfred Sze-Lok Prof Yu, Jun

14112525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112525.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a significant global health concern, ranking as the sixth leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized cancer treatment, its effectiveness is limited by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and the diverse etiologies of HCC, resulting in response rates below 30%. Using preclinical models, our recent proof-of-concept studies have demonstrated key transcriptional and epigenetic regulation underlying ICB resistance, in particular through immune exclusion and myeloid-mediated immunosuppression (Gut 2018, 2020, 2023, Sci Transl Med 2021). Identifying the central nodes of TME landscapes from ICB-resistant patients would be instrumental for developing precise immunotherapy strategies and improving clinical outcomes. In the preliminary study of this proposal, we have performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-cell Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) and spatial transcriptomics using two cohorts of HCC patients treated with ICBs (NCT03419481 and NCT05873244) and treatment-naïve patients as controls. Our multi-omics analysis revealed metabolic reprogramming in HCC cells of the ICB non-responders with significant enrichment in fatty acid metabolism-related genes when compared to the responders and treatment naïve-patients. This was accompanied by an induction of a subcluster of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) that expresses high levels of lipid-associated genes and locates in close proximity with tumor cells displaying fatty acid oxidation gene signature. In our syngeneic and orthotopic ICB-resistant mouse models that recapitulate human immune-excluded HCCs, we found that the tumor cells exhibited increased fatty acid dependency, while a subset of lipid-associated macrophages (LAMs) is enriched in concordance with the clinical findings. Bioinformatics analysis of the open chromatin regions uncovered significant enrichment of phagocytotic genes in TAM, which may be controlled at least partially by a myeloid-specific transcription factor PU.1 (encoded by the SPI1 gene) activated in ICB-resistant but not treatment-naïve tumors. Chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing further showed that PU.1 occupies target genes for phagocytosis in a monocytic cell line. In corroboration of these findings, lipid tracing experiments indicated that macrophage phagocytosis facilitates lipid transfer to tumor cells, leading to our hypothesis that PU.1 may drive lipid phagocytosis in LAMs to promote ICB resistance in a fatty acid-dependent manner. As we also found significant correlation between SPI1 and LAM gene signature with prognosis of HCC patients, our study may not only provide valuable insights into the molecular dysregulation of TAM in the immunosuppressive myeloid landscape, but also the basis for developing new strategies against the immunometabolic axis to avert ICB resistance. 肝細胞癌（HCC）是全球重要的健康問題，位居全球癌症相關死亡原因的第六位。儘管免疫檢查點阻斷（ICB）療法已徹底改變癌症治療方式，但其療效受到免疫抑制性腫瘤微環境（TME）以及HCC病因多樣性的限制，導致反應率低於30%。我們最近的臨床前模型揭示了ICB抗性背後的關鍵轉錄和表觀遺傳調控機制，特別是透過免疫排斥和髓系介導的免疫抑制（參見《Gut》2018、2020、2023，《Sci Transl Med》2021）。識別來自ICB抗性患者的TME景觀中的核心節點，對於開發精準免疫治療策略並改善臨床結果至關重要。 我們對接受ICB治療的兩組隊列的HCC患者（NCT03419481和NCT05873244）以及未接受治療的患者作為對照，進行了單細胞RNA測序（scRNA-seq）、單細胞染色質可及性測序（scATAC-seq）和空間轉錄組學分析。我們的多組學分析初步發現，在ICB無反應者的HCC細胞中，脂肪酸代謝相關基因顯著富集，顯示出代謝重編程現象，與有反應者及未治療患者相比差異明顯。這一現象伴隨著一群表達高水平脂質相關基因的腫瘤相關巨噬細胞（TAMs）亞群的出现，這些細胞與表現脂肪酸氧化基因特徵的腫瘤細胞空間上緊密相鄰。在我們建立的能夠重現人類免疫排斥型HCC的同系和原位ICB抗性小鼠模型中，我們發現腫瘤細胞對脂肪酸的依賴性增加，同時與臨床結果一致地富集了一群脂質相關巨噬細胞（LAMs）。對開放染色質區域的生物信息學分析顯示，TAM中吞噬作用相關基因顯著富集，這可能至少部分由髓系特異性轉錄因子PU.1（由SPI1基因編碼）所調控，結果顯示該因子在ICB抗性腫瘤病人中被激活，而在未治療腫瘤中未被激活。染色質免疫沉澱測序進一步顯示，PU.1 在單核細胞系中主要結合於吞噬作用相關的靶基因。與這些發現相呼應的是，脂質追蹤實驗表明巨噬細胞吞噬作用促進脂質向腫瘤細胞的轉移。進而我們提出假設：PU.1可能驅動LAM中的脂質吞噬作用，以脂肪酸依賴的方式促進ICB抗性。由於我們還發現SPI1與LAM基因特徵以及HCC患者預後之間存在顯著相關性，我們的研究不僅提供了對免疫抑制性髓系景觀中TAM分子失調的寶貴見解，也為開發針對免疫代謝軸的新策略以避免ICB抗性奠定了基礎。

14113025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14113025.value: 木香烴內酯透過抑制FAM198B表達克服胰臟癌的吉西他濱耐藥

14113025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113025.value: Human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly malignant and lethal digestive tumor, with more than 510,000 new cases and 467,409 mortalities reported in 2022 (https://gco.iarc.fr/). PDAC is the fourth leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 12%. Gemcitabine (GEM) is the standard first-line treatment for advanced PDAC; however, many PDAC patients are prone to develop GEM resistance. A large-scale dataset analysis using GEPIA (http://gepia.cancer-pku.cn) found that the mRNA level of the human family with sequence similarity 198, member B (FAM198B) is markedly higher in PDAC than in the normal tissues, and higher FAM198B expression was closely associated with higher recurrence and poorer overall survival in patients with PDAC. Importantly, we measured the protein expression of FAM198B and found it was markedly increased in the GEM resistant PDAC tumor tissues than in the GEM sensitive PDAC tumor tissues. Consistently, we also observed that protein and mRNA expressions of FAM198B are significantly higher in the acquired GEM-resistant MiaPaCa-2 (MiaPaCa-2-GR) and Capan-2 (Capan-2-GR) cells than that in their parental MiaPaCa-2 and Capan-2 cells. Interestingly, we found that costunolide (COS), a major bioactive component of Aucklandiae Radix (Bai-Zhu in Chinese), markedly enhanced the chemosensitivity of the GEM-resistant PDAC cell lines MiaPaCa-2-GR and Capan-2-GR, as shown by their apoptosis induction in vitro and tumor regression in vivo under GEM treatment. COS could also inhibit the protein expression of FAM198B in MiaPaCa-2-GR and Capan-2-GR cells in dose-and time-dependent manners. Moreover, FAM198B knockdown enhanced the effects of COS on overcoming GEM resistance in PDAC cell, as demonstrated by their reduction of viability, colony formation, invasion and migration, but increase in cellular apoptosis. Based on these novel findings, we hypothesized that FAM198B is an effective therapeutic target for overcoming GEM resistance in PDAC. To test this hypothesis, we will investigate the following 3 objectives: (1) To determine the regulatory role of FAM198B and effects of COS on overcoming GEM resistance on cancer progression in an orthotopic and metastatic PDAC mouse model; (2) To identify the underlying molecular mechanism of FAM198B on cancer progression and metastasis; and (3) To explore the role of FAM198B in mediating the effects of COS on overcoming GEM resistance in PDAC. The findings from this project will achieve in identifying the novel function of FAM198B in the GEM resistance in PDAC, and provide proof-of-concept evidence of targeting FAM198B in the treatment of GEM-resistant PDAC. 胰臟導管腺癌 (PDAC) 是一種高度惡性且致命的消化道腫瘤，2022 年報告的新病例超過 510,000 例，死亡病例超過 467,409 例。 PDAC 是全球第四大癌症死亡原因，5 年存活率不到 12%。吉西他濱 (GEM) 是晚期 PDAC 的標準一線治療方案。然而，許多 PDAC 患者易對GEM產生耐藥。使用GEPIA進行的大規模資料集分析發現，具有序列相似性198的人類家族成員B (FAM198B) 的mRNA水平在PDAC中明顯高於在正常組織中，並且FAM198B的高表達與PDAC患者的高復發率和較差的總生存率密切相關。更重要的是，我們發現FAM198B的蛋白表達在GEM耐藥的PDAC腫瘤組織中明顯高GEM敏感的PDAC腫瘤組織。此外，在獲得性GEM耐藥的MiaPaCa-2 (MiaPaCa-2-GR) 和Capan-2 (Capan-2-GR) 細胞中FAM198B的蛋白和mRNA表達量明顯高於其親本MiaPaCa-2和Capan-2細胞。有趣的是，我們發現木香烴內酯 (COS)顯著增強了GEM耐藥的PDAC細胞MiaPaCa-2-GR和Capan-2-GR的对GEM的化學敏感性，主要表現在誘導腫瘤細胞凋亡和抑制體內腫瘤生長。 COS也能以劑量和時間依賴的方式抑制MiaPaCa-2-GR和Capan-2-GR細胞中FAM198B的蛋白質表達。此外，敲低FAM198B可增強COS克服PDAC細胞對GEM耐藥的效果，表現抑制GEM耐藥的PDAC細胞的增值、克隆、侵襲和遷移的能力，但增加GEM耐藥的PDAC細胞的凋亡。 基於這些新發現，我們假設FAM198B是對抗PDAC對GEM耐藥的有效治療標靶。為了驗證這個假設，我們將進行以下三個研究目標：（1）在原位和轉移性PDAC小鼠模型中，明確FAM198B的調控作用以及COS在對抗GEM耐藥過程中對癌症進展的影響；（2）明確FAM198B影響癌症進展和轉移的潛在分子機制；（3）探討FAM198B在介導COS對抗PDAC 對GEM耐藥的作用。本計劃的研究結果將有助於明確FAM198B在PDAC 對GEM產生耐藥的作用，並為靶向FAM198B治療GEM耐藥PDAC提供概念驗證證據。

14113425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14113425.value: 用於蝦過敏治療的「即插即用」納米疫苗研究

14113425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14113425.value: Prof Leung, Sai-Cheong Patrick Prof Leung, Ting Fan

14113425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113425.value: Crustacean (shrimp) allergy is the leading cause of food allergy in Hong Kong and globally. It is also the most common cause of food-induced anaphylaxis in the Asia-Pacific region. Tropomyosin has been identified as one of the major shrimp allergens associated to shrimp-induced anaphylaxis and is a pan-allergen among crustaceans that largely explain clinical cross-reactivity. The current standard of care for shrimp allergy remains as dietary avoidance and emergency medication that a disease-modifying treatment, such as allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT), is largely in need. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) for food allergy has been shown successful to achieve desensitization for selected food allergen sources, but its long treatment duration, associated side effects and limited efficacy to achieve longer term disease remission limit its success. AIT vaccines that can reduce side effects and number of required injections while being effective to induce fast-acting IgG and preferably memory B cells to confer tolerance are highly favourable. In this application, we submit that combining tropomyosin-derived polypeptides with Hepatitis B virus core protein (HBcAg) virus-like particle (VLP) is a safe and effective vaccine for treating shrimp allergy via the induction of specific IgG to inhibit IgE binding. Polypeptides containing IgE-binding epitopes induce specific blocking IgG antibody but do not trigger IgE-mediated degranulation, while HBcAg is a nano-carrier inducing strong memory humoral and cellular immune responses. Our group constructed a plug-and-display HBcAg carrier based on the SpyTag/SpyCatcher technology to conveniently decorate the tropomyosin-polypeptides on HBcAg. We also demonstrated the four HBcAg-polypeptide vaccine candidates induced blocking IgG antibodies and protected against shrimp allergy in BALB/c mouse model of shrimp allergy. In this research proposal, we are going to delineate the therapeutic effects, safety and mechanism of our HBcAg VLP-polypeptide vaccines based on both in vivo and in vitro analysis from animal model and human samples. This proof-of-concept study will provide sufficient pre-clinical data and thus the translational feasibility of the vaccines for shrimp allergy treatment. This study will also provide essential information for HBcAg-SpyTag/SpyCatcher vaccine as a versatile modular vaccine platform for personalized vaccine to achieve precision medicine. 甲殼類過敏如蝦過敏是香港及全球食物過敏的主要原因，也是亞太地區食物誘發的過敏性休克最常見的原因。目前治療方法主要採用食物避免或服藥減輕症狀進行被動管理。研究報告過敏原特異性免疫治療(AIT)能夠快速誘導免疫球蛋白G反應及記憶B細胞從而建立耐受性，但其在蝦過敏的治療效果、安全性和作用機制方面尚不清楚。本研究組擬透過病毒樣顆粒疫苗技術對蝦過敏特異性免疫治療進行探究。研究顯示原肌球蛋白是蝦過敏相關的主要致敏原，含有IgE結合表位的原肌球蛋白多肽衍生物可誘導特異性阻斷性IgG抗體產生；在疫苗製備方面，乙型肝炎病毒核心蛋白(HBcAg)作為一種納米載體被廣泛應用，它能夠強烈誘導記憶性細胞免疫反應。本研究擬建構一種基於SpyTag/SpyCatcher技術的「即插即用」乙型肝炎病毒核心蛋白載體，連接SpyTag結合的原肌球蛋白多肽衍生物，進而產生納米疫苗，並在蝦過敏小鼠模型中進行治療效果、安全性及作用機制的驗證，及收集人體細胞樣本進行體外分析以探究此疫苗的調節機制，為蝦過敏特異性疫苗治療方法提供臨床前研究和促進個體化疫苗的精準醫學開發。

14114425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14114425.value: 揭示線粒體納米隧道在介導線粒體間通訊以控制心臟缺血再灌注期間細胞命運中的作用。

14114425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14114425.value: Prof DUAN, Liting Prof Yang, Zhu

14114425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114425.value: Background: Myocardial infarction, commonly known as heart attack, occurs upon restriction of blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart, thereby causing the heart muscle cells to die. While re-introduction of blood flow back to the myocardium via thrombolytic-therapy or primary-percutaneous-coronary-intervention (PCI) is crucial to reduce cell death (infarct), the acute restoration of blood flow paradoxically exacerbates myocardial tissue damage – a phenomenon known as ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI). IRI-induced injury/death has been discovered to converge on the mitochondria – the energy-providing organelle in the cell, whereby preserving optimal function of the mitochondria sustains ‘beating’ of the heart and reduces susceptibility to IRI. In this regard, mitochondrial function is intertwined with dynamics (morphology) to govern cardiac cell fate. During IR, the cardiac mitochondria undergo a phase-dependent shift in morphology, oscillating between the fused and fragmented state. Nonetheless, how the mitochondria communicate with each other to change shapes as a population and regulate cell fate is unknown. In recent years, the phenomenon of nanotunneling has emerged as a unique characteristic of the mitochondria, speculated to be involved in intermitochondrial-signaling, yet the exact function remains elusive. As such, elucidating the role of mitochondrial nanotunneling in mediating intermitochondrial communication will be crucial to regulate cellular fate during myocardial IR. Hypothesis: Mitochondrial nanotunneling regulates intermitochondrial communication to govern cardiac cell fate during IR. Aims: 1. To profile mitochondrial nanotunneling and define its association with mitochondrial dynamics and function during cardiac IR. 2. To identify the contents of the cardiac mitochondrial nanotunnels and determine its role in mediating intermitochondrial communication. 3. To manipulate cardiac mitochondrial nanotunnels and intermitochondrial communication to regulate cardiac cell fate following IR. Methodologies: We will assess, verify, and compare the extent of mitochondrial nanotunneling during the different phases of IR using the cardiac cell line, isolated adult murine cardiomyocytes, isolated human cardiomyocytes, and the C57/BL6 mice. To gauge the role of the mitochondrial nanotunnels in mediating intermitochondrial communication, the contents (mitochondrial-related proteins, mtDNA or pro-survival/death signals) of the mitochondrial nanotunnels formed will be determined. The mitochondrial nanotunnels will be modulated genetically and pharmacologically to regulate cardiac cell fate following IR. Main Outcomes: Elucidating the role of mitochondrial nanotunnels in mediating intermitochondrial communication will provide insights into mitochondrial adaptation (survival) or dysfunction (death) following IR. The ability to modulate mitochondrial nanotunnels within specific mitochondrial subpopulations in the myocyte may serve as a novel therapeutic target against ischemic-related heart disorders. 背景： 心肌梗塞，俗稱心臟病發作，是由於心臟血流和氧氣供應受限而導致心肌細胞死亡。雖然透過血栓溶解療法或直接經皮冠狀動脈介入治療 (PCI) 將血流重新引入心肌對於減少細胞死亡（梗塞）至關重要，但急性血流恢復反而會加劇心肌組織損傷——這種現像被稱為缺血-再灌注損傷 (IRI)。研究發現，IRI 引起的損傷/死亡主要集中在細胞內供能的細胞器——線粒體上，因此，維持線粒體的最佳功能可以維持心臟的“跳動”，並降低對 IRI 的易感性。線粒體功能與動力學（形態）交織以共同決定心臟細胞的命運。在心肌缺血再灌注 (IR) 期間，心肌線粒體的形態會發生相位依賴性轉變，在融合和碎裂狀態之間振盪。然而，線粒體如何相互通訊以改變整體形態並調控細胞命運尚未清楚。近年來，納米隧道現像作為線粒體的獨特特徵，被推測參與了線粒體間訊號傳導，但其確切功能仍未闡明。因此，闡明線粒體納米隧道米隧道在介導線粒體間通訊中的作用對於調控心肌缺血再灌注期間的細胞命運至關重要。 假設： 線粒體納米隧道調節線粒體間通訊，從而控制心肌缺血再灌注 (IR) 期間的心肌細胞命運。 目的： 1. 概述線粒體納米隧道，並明確其與心肌缺血再灌注 (IR) 期間線粒體動力學和功能的關聯。 2. 鑑定心肌線粒體納米隧道的內容，並確定其在介導線粒體間通訊中的作用。 3. 調控心肌線粒體納米隧道和線粒體間通訊，進而調控心肌缺血再灌注 (IR) 後的心肌細胞命運。 方法： 我們將使用心臟細胞系、分離的人類心肌細胞、分離的小鼠心肌細胞和C57/BL6小鼠，評估、驗證和比較IR不同階段線粒體納米隧道的程度。以評估粒線體納米隧道在介導粒線體間通訊中的作用，我們將測定所形成的粒線體納米隧道的成分（我們粒線體相關蛋白、粒線體訊DNA或促進死亡/死亡號）。將利用基因和藥理學方法調節粒線體納米隧道，以調節IR後心臟促進細胞的命運。 主要成果： 闡明線粒體納米通道在介導線粒體間通訊中的作用，將有助於深入了解缺血再灌注 (IR) 後線粒體的適應（存活）或功能障礙（死亡）。調節心肌細胞中特定線粒體亞群內線粒體納米通道的能力，可能成為治療缺血性心臟病的新標靶。

14114525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14114525.value: 以機器學習研發的全新風險評分和長期趨勢分析來預測糞腸球和 鏈球菌敗血症患者感染性心內膜炎風險的前瞻性驗證研究

14114525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14114525.value: Prof Lee, Alex Pui-wai Dr Lui, Chung Yan Grace Dr Yip, Cheuk Fung Terry

14114525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114525.value: Objective: to improve the management of streptococcal and enterococcal Infective Endocarditis (IE) through prospective validation of machine learning-derived prediction scores, bacterial genomic characterization, and secular trend analysis. Hypothesis: We hypothesize the machine learning-derived risk scores our team developed, the StrepIER and the MEFIER scores can predict risk of IE in patients with streptococcal and enterococcal bacteremia. Design and Subjects: The study is performed in three parts. Part 1 is a prospective observational study, to evaluate the performance of StrepIER and MEFIER scores in five major acute hospitals in Hong Kong. We aim to recruit 295 patients with medium IE risk streptococcal bacteremia, and 100 patients with Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia. Case will be identified in the microbiology laboratory of five tertiary care acute hospitals in Hong Kong. Patient information will be collected from electronic database including demographic data, past medical history, and laboratory results for StrepIER and MEFIER scores. Electronic and physical case notes review of calculation of other risk scores and for the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria based on clinical and pathological parameters. Patients will be followed up for at least 90 days after discharge. Patients will be categorized as a high or low risk for infective endocarditis. The definitive diagnosis of IE will be decided by an infective endocarditis expert panel of three blinded to the risk score results. In Part 2, the bacterial genome of E. faecalis and S. gallolyticus subsp. pasteurianus from 325 unique patients of will be analysis using genome-wide association studies to identify specific pathogenic and virulence factors for the development of IE. Part 3 is a secular trend analysis of streptococcal and Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia and infective endocarditis in Hong Kong from 2000 to 2024. Main outcome measure: Primary endpoint is the performance characteristics of the StrepIER in terms of AUC-ROC, sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values. Secondary endpoint is the performance characteristics of MEFIER score, specific bacterial virulence and pathogenic factors for the development of IE will be identified. Seculars trends of incidence and clinical characteristics of streptococcal and enterococcal bacteremia and IE in terms of trend over 25 years will be known. Expected results: Performance characteristics of StrepIER and MEFIER when used singly or in combination with other scores will be known. Together with the secular trend analysis allow effective and accurate application the risk scores in real world settings. Pathogenic and virulence factors for IE will be identified.

14115025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14115025.value: 靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究：一項隨機對照試驗

14115025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14115025.value: Prof Lam, Chiu Wa Linda Prof Mok, Chris Ka Pun Prof Tun, Hein Min Dr Yip, Benjamin Hon Kei Dr Zhang, Daisy Dexing

14115025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115025.value: Recent evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can influence the brain, impacting mood and behaviour through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Although this pathway is recognised, limited studies exist on psychological intervention effects on mental health outcomes via changes in microbiota. Mindfulness-based interventions, group interventions that effectively improve mental well-being, has demonstrated potential effectiveness in changing adults’ gut microbiome. No study has examined their direct effects on microbiota in a randomised controlled trial (RCT) comparing to an active control. We will perform a two-arm RCT to evaluate the efficacy of a mindfulness program for older adults (MBOA), in improving gut microbiota diversity and beneficial microbiome species among older adults with chronic stress. One hundred and thirty-eight Chinese older adults will be recruited from the community and randomly assigned to MBOA or health education control (HEC) groups. Gut microbiota will be measured at baseline, 2-month (immediately after intervention), and 5-month (3-month post-intervention) post-randomisation. We hypothesised that MBOA would improve gut microbiota diversity and beneficial microbiome species at 2 and 5 months post-randomisation when compared to the control. Our findings will demonstrate the potential effects of psychological interventions on the gut microbiome of older adults, providing important information for the first RCT examining mindfulness-based training for improving gut microbiota in older adults with chronic stress. 最新的證據表明，腸道微生物群可以通過微生物-腸-腦軸影響大腦，從而影響情緒和行為。儘管這一途徑已經被認可，但關於心理干預對心理健康結果通過微生物群變化的影響的研究仍然有限。 以靜觀為基礎的干預措施是一種有效改善心理健康的團體干預，並已顯示出在改變成年人腸道微生物組的潛在效果。然而，目前尚無研究在隨機對照試驗中比較其對微生物群的直接影響。 我們將進行一項雙臂隨機對照試驗，以評估針對老年人的靜觀課程（MBOA）在改善腸道微生物多樣性和有益微生物物種方面的有效性，研究對象為經歷慢性壓力的老年人。我們將在社區招募的138名中國籍老年人隨機分組到MBOA組或健康教育對照組（HEC），並在隨機分組的基線、隨機分組後2個月（干預結束時）和5個月（干預後3個月）測量參加者的腸道微生物群。我們假設，與對照組相比，MBOA將在隨機分組後2個月和5個月改善腸道微生物多樣性和有益微生物物種。 我們的研究結果將驗證心理干預對經歷慢性壓力的老年人腸道微生物群的潛在影響，為首個研究靜觀訓練改善老年人腸道微生物群的隨機對照試驗提供重要的信息。

14115125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14115125.value: 探討來自不同 COVID-19 疫苗接種策略所誘導之針對 SARS-CoV-2 各類變異株的 S2 次單元特異性抗體

14115125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115125.value: The emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants has challenged the efficacy of existing COVID-19 vaccines due to mutations in the spike protein which enable these variants to evade immune responses. Moreover, the continuing threat of other zoonotic coronaviruses including SARS-CoV-1, MERS-CoV and other bat origin viruses highlight the urgent need for a broadly protective vaccine. This proposal aims to investigate the mechanisms by which S2 subunit-specific antibodies are induced, as well as to examine their protective roles and cross-reactivity against various coronaviruses, as a potential strategy for universal vaccine development. We will utilize a comprehensive biobank of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from over 1,000 individuals with diverse vaccination histories to analyze plasma samples for the immunogenicity and durability of S2 antibodies following vaccination with different SARS-CoV-2 antigens. We will explore the clonal lineages of S2-specific B cells from these individuals to understand how the S2-specific B cells evolved. Targeting the conserved S2 subunit is anticipated to yield antibodies with enhanced neutralization capabilities against a broad range of coronaviruses, providing critical insights for public health policies and vaccination strategies. Finally, we will evaluate how pre-existing immunity from past infections or vaccination influences responses to S2-targeted vaccines using SARS-CoV-1/MERS-CoV suspectable mouse models. Our models simulate varying immune backgrounds, facilitating the assessment of S2 subunit vaccine efficacy against both SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV. By integrating findings from both human and animal studies, this research aims to advance the understanding of S2-specific immune responses and inform the design of next-generation vaccines that provide enduring protection against emerging coronaviruses, ultimately enhancing vaccination strategies and public health outcomes. 新型 SARS-CoV-2 變異株由於刺突蛋白的突變使其能逃避免疫反應，此現象對現有 COVID-19 疫苗的效力構成挑戰。此外，來自動物的其他冠狀病毒（包括 SARS-CoV-1、MERS-CoV 以及其他源自蝙蝠的病毒）所帶來的持續威脅，凸顯了發展廣泛保護性疫苗的迫切需求。本研究計劃旨在探討誘導 S2 次單元特異性抗體的機制，並評估這些抗體在對抗各類冠狀病毒中的保護作用及交叉反應性，作為發展普遍性疫苗的潛在策略。 我們將利用一個涵蓋逾 1,000 名具有多樣疫苗接種背景的志願者所建立的外周血單核細胞（PBMC）生物樣本庫，分析血漿樣本中於接種不同 SARS-CoV-2 抗原後所誘導的 S2 抗體的免疫原性與持久性。我們亦將探索這些個體中 S2 特異性 B 細胞的克隆譜系，以了解其演化過程。最後，我們將使用對冠狀病毒易感的小鼠模型，評估既往感染或疫苗接種所建立的免疫記憶，如何影響對 S2 靶向疫苗的免疫反應。我們的模型模擬不同的免疫背景，以利於全面評估 S2 次單元疫苗的效果。我們的研究計劃針對保守性的 S2 次單元預期可產生具廣泛中和能力的抗體，對於公共衛生政策與疫苗接種策略提供關鍵見解。

14115325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14115325.value: 擬南芥中free1抑制子DRIF1/2的結構與功能研究

14115325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115325.value: The regulation of membrane protein homeostasis through selective vacuolar degradation in plants relies on the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) machinery, which plays a pivotal role in plant development, defense, and various physiological processes. A plant-unique ESCRT component, FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting1 (FREE1), performs essential functions in multiple aspects of plant biology, including the multivesicular body (MVB)/vacuole biogenesis, membrane cargo sorting and degradation, as well as the autophagic degradation in plants. To delve into the underlying mechanisms of FREE1's multiple functions in plants, we have developed a forward genetic screen approach to identify mutants capable of suppressing the seedling lethal phenotype in FREE1-RNAi transgenic plants. This screening has led to the discovery and characterization of three novel suppressors of free1 (referred to as sof) in the model plant Arabidopsis: BRo1-domain protein As FREE1 suppressor (BRAF), RESURRECTION1 (RST1) and DEAH and RING domain-containing protein as FREE1 suppressor 1 (DRIF1), along with its close homolog, DRIF2. In this proposal, we focus on the study of DRIF1/2, which are plant-unique proteins with elusive functions and mechanisms related to the regulation of FREE1’s function in plants. DRIF1/2 are large proteins with a predicted molecular weight of about 200 kDa, consisting of multiple domains with elusive functions. Notably, no direct interaction between DRIF1 and FREE1 was observed, suggesting elusive components that interact with DRIF1 may be involved in the regulation. Our preliminary results have shown that DRIF1 can interact and colocalize with the retromer component SNX1 (sorting nexin 1). The interaction between DRIF1 and SNX1 is suggested to be engaged in membrane protein recycling and FREE1-related membrane protein degradation. Also, the presence of the intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) at the N-terminal region of DRIF1 suggests that this protein might engage in liquid-liquid phase separation, which may facilitate biochemical reactions. To further illustrate the function of DRIF1/2 and the molecular mechanisms in regulating FREE1-mediated membrane trafficking and organelle biogenesis in plants, here we aim to 1) identify and characterize the interacting partners of DRIF1/2; 2) conduct function-structure studies of Drif1/2 with their interacting partners; and 3) Investigate the mechanism by which DRIF1/2 Regulate FREE1 in Arabidopsis. 在植物中，膜蛋白穩態的調控依賴於選擇性液泡降解機制，而此過程由內體分選複合體（ESCRT）系統所介導。ESCRT 在植物的發育、免疫防禦及多種生理過程中扮演關鍵角色。其中，植物特有的 ESCRT 組件—FYVE 結構域蛋白 FREE1（FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting 1）在多泡體（MVB）／液泡的形成、膜蛋白的分選與降解，以及自噬途徑中均具有核心功能。為深入探討 FREE1 在植物中多重功能的分子機制，我們建立了一套正向遺傳篩選系統，用以鑑定能夠緩解 FREE1-RNAi 轉基因植物中幼苗致死表型的抑制性突變體。透過此篩選，我們於模式植物擬南芥中鑑定出三個新的 free1 抑制子（suppressors of free1，簡稱 sof）：BRo1-domain protein As FREE1 suppressor (BRAF)，RESURRECTION1 (RST1) 和 DEAH and RING domain-containing protein as FREE1 suppressor 1 (DRIF1) ，以及其同源蛋白 DRIF2。本研究將聚焦於 DRIF1／2 的功能解析。DRIF1／2 為植物特有的大蛋白，預測分子量約為 200 kDa，包含多個功能尚未明確的結構域。值得注意的是，DRIF1 與 FREE1 之間未偵測到直接相互作用，暗示可能存在其他介導 DRIF1 調控 FREE1 功能的未知因子。我們的初步研究顯示，DRIF1 可與網格蛋白回收複合體的關鍵組件 SNX1（Sorting Nexin 1）發生相互作用並於細胞中共定位。此相互作用可能參與膜蛋白的回收過程，並與 FREE1 所介導的膜蛋白降解途徑相關聯。此外，DRIF1 N 端的內在無序區（Intrinsically Disordered Regions, IDRs）提示其可能參與液-液相分離（Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation），從而於細胞內形成功能性微環境以促進生化反應的進行。為進一步闡明 DRIF1／2 在調控 FREE1 所介導之膜運輸及細胞器生物生成中的作用機制，本研究擬展開以下三個方向的工作： 1. 鑑定並功能解析 DRIF1／2 的相互作用蛋白； 2. 對DRIF1／2 以及其相互作用蛋白進行結構與功能研究； 3. 探討 DRIF1／2 在擬南芥中調控 FREE1 功能的分子機制。

14116225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14116225.value: 可注射水凝膠載有尋找損傷的AP1122蛋白 - 一種創新的針對退行性肌腱病的解決方案

14116225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14116225.value: Dr Lau, Chun Man Lawrence Prof Ling, Samuel Ka-kin Prof Qin, Ling Prof Wong, Chi-Ming

14116225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116225.value: Tendinopathy is an unmet clinical challenge, causing tendon pain and functional disability. This study explores the therapeutic potential of Trefoil Factor 2 (TFF2), a protective and healing factor of gut mucosa, in tendinopathy. Our pilot data showed that TFF2 is upregulated in human tendinopathy tissue and inflammatory tendon-derived stem/progenitor cells (TDSCs). Besides, TFF2 suppressed inflammation and enhanced inflammatory TDSCs’ functions, while rescuing the survival, proliferation, and tenogenesis of degenerative TDSCs isolated from a collagenase-induced tendon injury model (CI model). Moreover, TFF2 injection facilitated early tendon healing and reduced inflammation in this model. Building upon these discoveries, we engineered AP1122, a recombinant human TFF2 (AP9578) conjugated with a damage-seeking peptide to precisely target the damaged tendon. To maximize efficacy while reducing injection frequency and drug dosage, we developed an injectable AP1122-loaded GelMA hydrogel, which demonstrated superior tendon repair histologically compared to AP9578 in a pilot animal study. Notably, AP1122 demonstrated prolonged retention in damaged tendons and enhanced TDSCs’ function compared to AP9578. We aim to -investigate TFF2 expression in clinical tendon samples and its relationship with inflammation, histopathology, pain, and disability in degenerative tendinopathy; -evaluate the effects of damage-seeking AP1122 on inflammatory responses and functions of TDSCs; and -explore the effects and mechanisms of damage-seeking AP1122-loaded hydrogel on degenerative tendon repair. We will assess the tendon’s TFF2 level, correlating it with inflammatory cytokines, histopathology, and disease severity of tendinopathy patients. Moreover, we will compare the effects of AP1122 and AP9578 on inflammatory TDSCs’ growth, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, tenogenesis, and matrix remodeling. RNA sequencing will unravel novel genes and pathways, notably the EGFR/MAPK/PI3K pathways, mediating their effects. Finally, we will inject AP1122-loaded or AP9578-loaded GelMA hydrogel into the CI-model, evaluating tendon pain, histopathology, ectopic bone formation, and biomechanical properties. Immunohistochemistry/qRT-PCR will measure inflammation, matrix remodeling, tenogenesis, oxidation, and apoptosis. Additionally, we will examine the potential toxic effects of AP1122 and AP9578. Moreover, RNA sequencing will elucidate the differential expressed genes and pathways. Furthermore, we will compare the retention and biodistribution of AP1122 and AP9578 through imaging of fluorescent-labeled constructs post-injection in injured tendons using in-vivo fluorescence imaging and immunohistochemistry of 6x-His tag. In summary, identifying TFF2 as a treatment target, engineering a damage-seeking peptide in AP1122, and using a localized delivery system add novelty to our approach. By understanding novel targets and mechanisms, we aspire to improve outcomes and quality of life of tendinopathy patients.

14116525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14116525.value: 牽張成骨中骨骼內感知迴路解析

14116525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14116525.value: Prof JIANG, Xiaohua Prof Ling, Samuel Ka-kin Prof Xu, Jiankun

14116525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116525.value: Ilizarov technology, rooted in the principle of distraction osteogenesis (DO), has gained widespread application in orthopaedic and dental surgeries for managing complex bone disorders. Despite its significant advantages, challenges such as prolonged consolidation periods persist, necessitating innovative strategies to enhance bone healing outcome and shorten the treatment duration. Our research team has explored various approaches, including the application of stem cells and biomaterials, yet efficient methods to shorten the consolidation phase remain elusive. Crucial questions about the mechanisms underlying DO remain unanswered, particularly regarding how the neural system senses, integrates, and responds to the DO procedure. Our preliminary studies indicate that the parasubthalamic nucleus (PSTN), a central component of the interoceptive network, receives signals from the bone lengthening site in a DO model, rather than in a fracture model, as demonstrated through retrograde tracing assays. Our findings suggest that manipulating PSTN significantly influences bone regeneration outcomes in the context of DO. Notably, excitation of the PSTN appears to accelerate bone regeneration and enhance movement function in animal models, while inhibition of PSTN prolongs the healing process and impairs mobility. These compelling results propose that the PSTN may serve as a central hub for skeletal interoception during the DO process. Based on our preliminary data and existing literature, we hypothesize that the PSTN acts as a skeletal interoception-related brain nucleus that specifically responds to the mechanical stimuli associated with DO. We propose that sensory nerves transmit signals from tension forces to the PSTN, where they are processed. This neural information could then be relayed through sympathetic nerves to regulate local bone healing process. To investigate this hypothesis, we propose three specific aims: 1) to validate the functional role of the PSTN in DO and to map the anatomical circuits involved in skeletal interoception; 2) to determine the role of the sensory nerve-PSTN (ascending) pathway in the fracture and DO models; 3) to determine the role of PSTN-sympathetic nerve (descending) pathway in the fracture and DO models. The outcomes of this research will enhance our understanding of the skeletal interoception circuits involved in DO, potentially revealing a critical link between the central nervous system and mechanoresponsive bone regeneration. This study may also pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting neural pathways to accelerate bone regeneration, with implications that extend beyond DO to address a wide range of challenging bone diseases and disorders in clinical practice. 植基於牽張成骨（DO）原理的Ilizarov技術，已廣泛應用於骨科與牙科手術中以治療複雜骨病變。儘管該技術具有顯著優勢，但仍面臨骨癒合期過長等挑戰，極需創新策略以改善癒合效果並縮短療程。本團隊已探索包括幹細胞與生物材料應用等多種方法，然能有效縮短骨癒合期的方案仍屬空白。關於DO核心機制的關鍵問題尚未解答，特別是神經系統如何感知、整合並響應DO過程。 初步研究顯示，在DO模型（而非骨折模型）中，內感受神經網絡的核心元件——丘腦旁下核（PSTN）會接收來自骨延長部位的訊號，此現象已通過逆行追蹤實驗證實。我們發現調控PSTN能顯著影響DO過程中的骨再生效果：在動物模型中，激活PSTN可加速骨再生並改善運動功能，抑制PSTN則會延緩癒合並損害行動能力。這些重要結果提示PSTN可能是DO過程中骨骼內感知的中樞樞紐。 基於現有證據與文獻，我們提出假說：PSTN作為骨骼內感知相關腦核，會特異性響應DO相關的機械刺激。我們推測感覺神經將張力訊號傳遞至PSTN進行整合，該神經訊息可能再經交感神經下傳以調控局部骨癒合。為驗證此假說，擬開展三項研究目標：1) 驗證PSTN在DO中的功能角色並繪製骨骼內感知的神經迴路圖譜；2) 釐清感覺神經-PSTN（上行）通路在骨折與DO模型中的作用；3) 解析PSTN-交感神經（下行）通路在骨折與DO模型中的功能。 本研究將深化對DO中骨骼內感知迴路的理解，可能揭示中樞神經系統與機械響應性骨再生間的關鍵連結。研究成果不僅有望發展出針對神經通路的新型骨再生加速策略，其應用價值更可超越DO領域，為臨床多種難治性骨病提供創新治療思路。

14116825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14116825.value: 研究韋納症候群中脂肪細胞重塑過程的脂質穩態

14116825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14116825.value: Prof Hui, Hannah Xiaoyan Prof LIU, Xingguo Prof Wang, Wuming

14116825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116825.value: Werner syndrome (WS) is a disease of premature ageing and has systemic symptoms that parallel normal ageing, such as alopecia, diabetes, cancer, thin and wrinkled skin, and osteoporosis. One of the hallmarks of WS is the accelerated manifestation of metabolic disorders, especially dyslipidaemia, lipodystrophy, and insulin resistance. Previous studies have focused on the role of WRN in cellular senescence and chronic inflammation of adipose tissues; however, its roles in adipocyte development and lipid homeostasis remain unclear. Recently, our team investigated adipocyte development in WS, but we have yet to determine the regulatory mechanisms underlying premature aging in this condition. In the proposed project, we will unveil the roles of WRN in adipocyte remodelling and lipid homeostasis, as well as the pathology associated with WS, using our established stem cell and zebrafish models. Given that both senescent adipocytes and cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) can promote cancer development, we will also clarify the relationship between senescent adipocytes and CAAs in WS. Transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing, RNA sequencing, chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing technique, and bioinformatics database analysis will be performed to identify the downstream lipid metabolic regulators of WRN in remodelling adipocytes. Thereafter, we will validate the function of the candidate regulators in maintaining lipid homeostasis in both stem cell and zebrafish models. Furthermore, we will decipher the metabolic regulatory mechanism that governs lipid homeostasis during adipocyte remodelling in WS. Moreover, given the similarity in lipid dysregulation and metabolic disorders between WS and normal ageing, we will validate our findings in WS using data from public databases to determine their applicability to normal ageing and other genetic disease settings. This project aims to enhance our understanding of the pathology of premature ageing in WS through adipocyte remodelling, and it may also identify potential new therapeutic targets related to lipid metabolites for anti-ageing research. 韋納氏症候群（Werner綜合徵，WS）是一種早衰性疾病，表現出與正常老化相似的全身症狀，如脫髮、糖尿病、癌症、皮膚變薄且起皺以及骨質疏鬆。 WS的一個顯著特徵是代謝紊亂的加速表現，尤其是血脂異常、脂肪營養不良和胰島素抗性。過去的研究主要集中在WRN蛋白在細胞老化和脂肪組織慢性發炎中的作用，但在脂肪細胞發育和脂質穩態中的作用尚不清楚。近期，我們團隊對WS中的脂肪細胞發育進行了研究，這項發現為WS患者觀察到的代謝功能障礙提供了新的視角。我們先前已證明染色質重塑基因SNARCA5促進了WS中過早的脂肪細胞分化，但尚未明確成熟脂肪細胞標記消失的機制。在本計畫中，我們將利用已建立的幹細胞和斑馬魚模型來揭示WRN在脂肪細胞重塑和脂質穩態中的作用及其與WS病理的關係。我們將採用ATAC-seq、RNA定序、染色質免疫共沉澱定序（ChIP-seq）和生物資訊資料庫分析，篩選WRN在脂肪細胞重塑中下游的脂質代謝調控因子。隨後，我們將在幹細胞和斑馬魚模型中驗證候選調控因子在維持脂質穩態的功能。此外，我們將解析調控WS脂肪細胞重塑過程中脂質穩態的代謝調節機制。鑑於WS和正常老化在脂質代謝失調和代謝疾病上的相似性，我們還將利用公共資料庫中的WS數據驗證我們的發現，以評估其在正常老化及其他遺傳疾病中的適用性。本計畫將加深我們對WS早衰病理機制中脂肪細胞重塑的理解，並可能為抗衰老研究提供與脂質代謝物相關的新型潛在治療靶標。

14117125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14117125.value: 腎損傷過程中腎小管YAP激活抑製線粒體氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）功能的研究

14117125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117125.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are major health problems. AKI affects up to 20% of all hospitalized patients. CKD affects around 11% of the population worldwide. Despite the differences between acute and chronic kidney diseases regarding the causes and symptoms, AKI and CKD share common mechanisms including tubular cell death and renal inflammation. Renal tubular epithelial cells (TECs) constitute >90% of the kidney mass and play a key role in orchestrating renal inflammation and fibrosis. Renal TECs, especially the epithelial cells of proximal tubules and collecting ducts, have high energy demands. TECs depend on fatty acid oxidation (FAO) as the fuel source and generate energy via mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Previous studies reveal that decreased tubular OXPHOS plays an important role in the development of kidney disease; however, it is not well understood how OXPHOS is regulated in TECs. The Hippo/YAP pathway regulates organ size and tissue homeostasis. YAP is negatively regulated by Hippo signaling, and functions as a co-transcription factor. Our recent studies have revealed that tubular YAP activation promotes tubular injury and renal inflammation and fibrosis; however, the underlying mechanisms are unclear. We now have RNA-seq results showing that OXPHOS but not FAO in the kidney was enriched in tubular Yap knockout mice compared to wild-type mice at 6 hours of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). Multiple nuclear DNA-encoded OXPHOS genes in the kidney were up-regulated by tubular Yap knockout after UUO or cisplatin injection. Expression of multiple OXPHOS genes was also increased in Yap knockout IMCD3 cells. PGC-1alpha is a key regulator of energy metabolism and promotes the expression of OXPHOS genes. Of note, PGC-1alpha was up-regulated by Yap reduction in IMCD3 and HK-2 cells and in injured kidneys. Therefore, we hypothesize that tubular YAP suppresses OXPHOS during kidney injury, thereby aggravating tubular dysfunction and renal inflammation and fibrosis. To test this hypothesis, we will 1) explore the role of YAP in oxygen consumption rate, ATP levels, mitochondrial ultrastructure and cell apoptosis in renal tubular cells in vitro; 2) study the mechanisms used by YAP to regulate the expression of PGC-1alpha and OXPHOS components; and 3) investigate whether OXPHOS mediates the renal phenotypes observed in tubular Yap knockout mice. The results we obtain would be important in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis of kidney disease and may be useful in the development of novel therapeutic treatments for kidney disease. 急性腎損傷（AKI）與慢性腎臟病（CKD）是重大健康問題。AKI影響高達20%的住院患者，而全球約11%的人口受CKD困擾。盡管急慢性腎臟病在病因和癥狀上存在差異，但AKI與CKD具有共同的病理機製，包括腎小管細胞死亡和腎臟炎癥反應。腎小管上皮細胞（TECs）占腎臟質量的90%以上，在協調腎臟炎癥和纖維化過程中起關鍵作用。尤其是近端小管和集合管的上皮細胞具有極高的能量需求，主要依賴脂肪酸氧化（FAO）供能，並通過線粒體氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）產生能量。 既往研究表明，腎小管OXPHOS功能下降在腎臟疾病發展中起重要作用，但TECs中OXPHOS的調控機製尚未明確。Hippo/YAP通路是調控器官大小和組織穩態的關鍵通路，其中YAP作為轉錄輔助因子受Hippo信號負向調控。我們最新研究發現，腎小管YAP激活會加劇小管損傷、腎臟炎癥及纖維化，但其分子機製尚不清晰。我們現在有RNA-seq數據顯示：在單側輸尿管梗阻（UUO）6小時後，與野生型小鼠相比，腎小管特異性Yap基因敲除小鼠腎臟中OXPHOS（而非FAO）通路顯著富集。在UUO或順鉑註射模型中，Yap敲除使腎臟多個核DNA編碼的OXPHOS基因上調，Yap敲除的IMCD3細胞中也觀察到多個OXPHOS基因表達增加。值得註意的是，能量代謝關鍵調控因子PGC-1α（可促進OXPHOS基因表達）在Yap下調的IMCD3細胞及損傷腎臟中表達升高。 這些結果提示，腎損傷過程中腎小管中激活的YAP通過抑製OXPHOS加劇小管功能障礙及腎臟炎癥纖維化。為驗證該假說，我們將：1）在體外實驗中探究YAP對腎小管細胞耗氧率、ATP水平、線粒體超微結構及細胞雕亡的影響；2）解析YAP調控PGC-1α及OXPHOS組分表達的分子機製；3）驗證OXPHOS是否介導了腎小管Yap敲除小鼠的腎臟表型。本研究結果將深化對腎臟疾病發病機製的理解，並為開發新型腎臟病治療策略提供理論依據。

14118025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118025.value: CTNNB1突變在非酒精性脂肪性肝病肝細胞癌（NAFLD-HCC）免疫代謝重塑中的功能研究

14118025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14118025.value: Prof Ding, XiaoFan Prof Wong, Nathalie

14118025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118025.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer related deaths worldwide. Despite current advances in immunotherapy, only a subpopulation can benefit. So far, we and others have reported that driver mutation CTNNB1mut confers resistance to immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) via immune evasion, which is further exacerbated under non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) (Wong et al., Journal of Hepatology 2022). Unfortunately, there are still no FDA-approved targeted treatment options available against mutated CTNNB1 despite its discovery over a decade ago. Indeed, the safety profile for Wnt inhibitors remain an important issue due to its ubiquitous nature and broad effect across malignant and nonmalignant cells. Recent large-scale multi-omics studies reported by us and others have also shown that Wnt activation by different mutations such as AXIN1 loss had distinct mutation patterns and immune subclass as CTNNB1. The means of Wnt activation is likely more nuanced and the knowledge gap in CTNNB1mut-mediated resistance to ICI remains. Recent studies have shed light into the immunometabolic interplay involved in cancer and response to immunotherapy, which could lead to valuable insights as to how we can better target CTNNB1mut HCC. Indeed, targeting CTNNB1mut tumor specific events that confer both tumor-intrinsic fitness (e.g. metabolic adaptation) and -extrinsic advantage (e.g. immune evasion) would be a more effective strategy for overcoming ICI resistance. Our preliminary findings suggest that CTNNB1mut patient-derived organoids (PDTOs) and transgenic mouse models expressing liver-specific CTNNB1 top hotspot mutation S45P can adapt to NAFLD-induced metabolic stress through ketogenesis. CTNNB1mut NAFLD HCC tumors show upregulated ketogenesis at the transcriptome level, indicating a physiologically relevant discovery. Notably, the ketone body beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) has anti-inflammatory effects on neighbouring cells, potentially explaining the immune evasive phenotype in CTNNB1mut HCC. Through CTNNB1/βCatenin chIP-seq analysis, SP5 emerged as a direct CTNNB1mut target promoting elevated BHB levels. Significant enrichment of SP5 motifs across regulatory sites indicate of a feed forward loop to target genes associated with ketogenesis, such as CTRP3. The tumor specificity of this axis is reinforced by primary HCC spatial transcriptome and single cell RNA sequencing data. Interestingly, this is also true for BHB transporter MCT1, which may be a potential avenue of treatment based on the promising phase I clinical trials results of MCT1 inhibitor AZD3965 in solid cancer. Since MCT1 can also transport other immunomodulating metabolites such as lactate, it is important to delineate the immunometabolic rewiring governed by CTNNB1mut HCC to assess its therapeutic potential. 肝細胞癌 (HCC) 是全球癌症相關死亡的主要原因。儘管免疫療法目前取得了進展，但只有一小部分人群能夠從中受益。迄今為止，我們和其他研究人員已報道，驅動突變 CTNNB1mut 透過免疫逃脫機制對免疫檢查點抑制 (ICI) 產生抵抗性，而這種抵抗性在非酒精性脂肪性肝病 (NAFLD) 患者中更為嚴重 (Wong et al., Journal of Hepatology 2022)。遺憾的是，儘管 CTNNB1 突變已發現十多年，但至今仍未有 FDA 批准的針對該突變的標靶治療方案。事實上，由於 Wnt 抑制劑的普遍性和在惡性和非惡性細胞中的廣泛作用，其安全性仍然是一個重要問題。我們和其他研究人員最近報告的大規模多組學研究也表明，由不同突變，例如 AXIN1 缺失引起的 Wnt 活化與 CTNNB1具有不同的突變模式和免疫亞類。Wnt 活化的方式可能更加微妙， CTNNB1mut 介導的免疫檢查點抑制 (ICI) 抗性方面的仍然存在知識空白。 最近的研究揭示了癌症和免疫治療反應中涉及的免疫代謝相互作用，這可能為我們如何更好地靶向CTNNB1mut肝細胞癌提供寶貴的見解。事實上，針對CTNNB1mut腫瘤特異性事件既能賦予腫瘤內在適應性（例如代謝適應），又能賦予腫瘤外在優勢（例如免疫逃脫），將是克服免疫檢查點抑制（ICI）抗性的更有效策略。 我們的初步研究結果表明，CTNNB1mut 患者來源的類器官 (PDTO) 和表達肝臟特異性 CTNNB1 熱點突變 S45P 的轉基因小鼠模型能夠透過生酮作用適應 NAFLD 誘導的代謝壓力。 CTNNB1mut NAFLD 肝癌腫瘤表現出生酮在轉錄組層級的上調，提示這是一個與生理學相關的發現。值得注意的是，酮體 β-羥基丁酸 (BHB) 對鄰近細胞具有抗發炎作用，這可能解釋了 CTNNB1mut 肝癌的免疫逃脫表型。透過 CTNNB1/βCatenin 晶片免疫沉澱定序分析，SP5 成為促進 BHB 水平升高的直接 CTNNB1mut 標靶。 SP5 基序在調控位點上的顯著富集表明存在一個前饋迴路，靶向與生酮作用相關的基因，例如 CTRP3。原代肝癌空間轉錄組和單細胞 RNA 定序數據進一步證實了該軸的腫瘤特異性。有趣的是，BHB轉運蛋白MCT1也存在同樣的情況。鑑於MCT1抑制劑AZD3965在實體腫瘤I期臨床試驗中取得的良好結果，MCT1可能成為潛在的治療途徑。由於MCT1也能轉運其他免疫調節代謝物，例如乳酸，因此闡明CTNNB1mut HCC調控的免疫代謝通路，對於評估其治療潛力至關重要。

14118725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118725.value: 開發基於混合模型的分子定年方法及其對宿主-微生物共演化的影響

14118725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14118725.value: Prof Chen, Youhua Prof Meade, Andrew
