14118725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118725.value: The vast diversity of microorganisms stems from an evolutionary history of over four billion years. Consequently, determining the timeline of their evolution is of considerable interest. Scientists have developed the “molecular clock” methodology, which integrates temporal data from both fossils and molecular sequences. However, estimating the divergence times and substitution rates for microbes presents significant challenges: while previous research [Wang & Luo Nat. Commun. 12, 3324 (2021)] mainly focused on exploring alternative time constraints, the use of inappropriate substitution model has frequently been neglected [Moody et al., Nat Ecol. Evol. 8, 1654–1666 (2024)]. Many studies highlight the advantages of mixture models like C60 over traditional homogeneous models in analyzing microbial evolution, often characterized by deep phylogenies, rapid changes, and compositional heterogeneity. However, their rare use in molecular clock analyses, mainly due to a lack of support from most molecular clock software, can result in inaccurate estimates of divergence times and substitution rates, and further affect any interpretation of the correlation of these timings with other biological events. Here, we propose to address this challenge by developing a new software, phyloHessian, to integrate various mixture models into molecular dating of the the widely used molecular clock software PAML-MCMCtree. This will be based on the calculation of the phylogenetic Hessian matrix using finite difference method and a series of other approximation methods under mixture substitution models. Further, we will conduct a comprehensive comparison of the effects of simple and mixture substitution models on molecular dating, assessing situations where mixture models surpass homogeneous models, particularly in the presence of large sequence divergence and compositional heterogeneity, using both simulated and empirical data. Building on more accurate estimates of divergence times, we will develop a method for ancestral state reconstruction that considers these timings. This method will be applied, in combination with machine learning approaches, to explore the host transition history and genomic changes associated with such transitions in symbiotic bacteria, particularly those that have adapted to a diverse range of eukaryotic hosts. The proposed project integrates the development of methodologies with fundamental biological questions. Despite its focus on (symbiotic) microbes, the methods will be broadly applicable to studying the evolution of other organisms. It also aligns with the “One Health” concept and contributes to understanding the evolution of emerging pathogens from the environment. 微生物有超過四十億年的演化歷史。因此，確定其演化時間具有相當大的意義。科學家們開發了一種稱為「分子鐘」的方法，透過整合來自化石和分子序列的數據以推算物種的分化時間和演化速度。然而，這絕非易事。先前的研究 [Wang & Luo Nat. Commun. 12, 3324 (2021)] 主要集中在探索新的時間校准點，而往往忽略了氨基酸替代模型的影響 [Moody et al., Nat Ecol. Evol. 8, 1654--1666 (2024)]。 許多早前的研究發現了混合模型（如 C60）在分析微生物深時演化方面的優勢，這一優勢在深時系統發育、快速序列變化以及高氨基酸組成異質性時表現得尤為明顯。然而，由於大多數分子鐘軟件缺乏對此的支持，混合替代模型在分子鐘分析中很少應用，這可能導致對分化時間和替換速率的不準確估計，並進一步造成對這些時間與其他生物事件之間關聯的誤解。 在此，我們建議透過開發一種新的軟件 phyloHessian 來應對這一挑戰，該軟件將各種混合模型整合到廣泛使用的分子鐘軟件 PAML-MCMCtree 的分子定年中。這將基於使用有限差分法計算系統發育 黑塞（Hessian） 矩陣，以及在混合替換模型下的一系列其他近似方法。此外，我們將透過模擬和真實數據，對簡單和混合替換模型對分子定年的影響進行系統比較，評估混合模型較傳統替代模型的優勢所在，特別在存在較大序列差異和氨基酸組成異質性的情況下。 在更準確的分化時間估計的基礎上，我們將開發一種考慮這些時間的祖先狀態重構方法。該方法將與機器學習方法相結合，用於探索共生細菌的宿主轉變歷史以及與真核宿主多樣性適應相關的基因組變化。 擬議的項目整合了方法學的開發與基礎生物學問題。儘管它側重於（共生）微生物，但該方法將廣泛適用於研究其他生物的演化。它也符合「同一健康」的理念，並有助於理解環境中新興病原體的演化。

14118825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118825.value: 擬南芥小配子發生過程中成膜體和細胞板形成分子的分子機制

14118825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118825.value: The cell plate and phragmoplast play important roles in plant cell cytokinesis. The phragmoplast, composed of microtubules and actin filaments, guides the formation and expansion of the cell plate. In most cell types, the cell plate initially forms at the center and expands outward. However, in microsporocytes during post-meiotic cytokinesis, the cell plate matures in a centripetal pattern while less is known about microspore cytokinesis in pollen mitosis. Cytokinesis is primarily regulated by SEC (Subunit of Exocyst Complex) proteins, which are components of the exocyst complex. This complex plays crucial roles in membrane trafficking and cell division, however, the function of SEC1 family in pollen cytokinesis is largely unknown. Built on our previous studies on vacuole formation in both Arabidopsis cortical root cells and stomatal lineage cells, we have recently performed whole-cell 3D electron tomography (3D-ET) on Arabidopsis pollens from released microspore to mature pollen with five developmental stages. Our preliminary data derived from this excellent single-cell system show that 1) vacuoles are developmentally regulated and their morphology at the Pollen Mitosis I (PMI) stage is featured by fragmentation and tubulation; 2) cell plate undergo ultrastructural changes at the PMI stage, suggesting the breakdown of the large central vacuole; and 3) cell plate formation and positioning were impaired in sec11 sec1b pollen grains. Our motivation for this project is based on 3D-ET observation of the uniform cell plate formation and changes during PMI. Here we hypothesize that the cell plate formation during PMI in sec11 sec1b pollen grains is abnormal, in consequence, GC (Generative Cell) is aberrantly migrated. We will employ whole-cell ET technology in combination with cellular, molecular, and genetic approaches, to identify and characterize candidate regulators in mediating cell plate/phragmoplast formation with three specific objectives: 1. To generate whole-cell ET model of cell plate formation and associated transport vesicles in PMI pollens. 2. To identify and characterize the roles of selective Kinesin motor proteins in regulating phragmoplast formation. 3. To investigate the roles and mechanisms of SEC proteins in regulating cell plate formation. Kinesin motor proteins and the syntaxin protein SEC are involved in the phragmoplast formation. However, the precise identification of other motor proteins and SEC-interacting proteins involved in phragmoplast/cell plate formation is pending further investigation. Given the crucial role of PMI and the following development of the GC in pollen tube germination and fertilization, our work will provide novel insights into plant reproduction. 細胞板和成膜體在植物細胞有絲分裂中發揮重要作用。成膜體由微管和肌動蛋白絲組成，介導細胞板的形成和擴張。在大多數細胞類型中，細胞板最初在中心形成並向外擴展。然而，在減數分裂後微孢子細胞的細胞分裂過程中，細胞板以向心模式成熟，而關於花粉有絲分裂中小孢子的細胞分裂機制尚不明確。細胞分裂主要由SEC（外囊體複合體亞單位）蛋白調控，這些蛋白是外囊體複合體的組成部分。該複合體在膜運輸和細胞分裂中發揮關鍵作用，然而SEC1家族在花粉細胞分裂中的功能尚不清楚。 基於我們之前對擬南芥皮層根細胞和氣孔譜系細胞中液泡形成的研究所得出的結論，我們最近對擬南芥花粉進行了全細胞3D電子斷層掃描（3D-ET），從釋放的小孢子到成熟花粉，涵蓋了五個發育階段。我們從這一優秀的單細胞系統中獲得的初步數據表明：1) 液泡的形成受發育調控，其在花粉第一次有絲分裂（PMI）階段的形態特徵為碎裂和管狀結構；2) 細胞板在PMI階段發生超微結構變化，暗示中央大液泡的破裂；3)細胞板形成和定位受損sec11 sec1b突變體花粉粒中受損。 我們開展此項目的動機基於對PMI期間細胞板均勻形成及變化的3D-ET觀察。在此，我們假設sec11 sec1b花粉粒在PMI期間的細胞板形成異常，因此生殖細胞（GC）發生異常遷移。我們將採用全細胞ET技術結合細胞、分子和遺傳學方法，以識別和表徵參與細胞板/細胞板膜形成的候選調控因子，並設定三個具體目標： 1. 構建PMI花粉中細胞板形成及相關運輸小泡的全細胞電子顯微鏡模型。 2. 鑑定並表徵經過篩選的動力蛋白在調節細胞板形成中的作用。 3. 探討SEC蛋白在調節細胞板發育在PMI時期的作用及機制。 動力蛋白和syntaxin蛋白SEC參與成膜體的形成。然而，其他參與細胞板/細胞板形成的動力蛋白和SEC相互作用蛋白的精確鑑定尚待進一步研究。鑑於PMI和隨後GC在花粉管發芽和受精中的關鍵作用，我們的工作將為植物生殖提供新的見解。

14119125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119125.value: Roseburia intestinalis 活化腦部 GLP-1R 訊號調控慢性痛誘發抑鬱共病的腸腦軸機制

14119125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119125.value: Patients with chronic pain are at a higher risk of developing psychiatric comorbidities, such as depression. Recent studies emphasize the critical role of gut-brain communication in the development and treatment of neurological disorders. Our recent work identified Roseburia intestinalis (R. intestinalis) as a depleted bacterium in patients with neuropathic pain, and supplementation with R. intestinalis reduced pain hypersensitivity in animal models by modulating the gut-vagal nerve-nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS)-amygdala circuit. R. intestinalis has been shown to exert antidepressant effects in various animal models of depression, and its reduced abundance has been linked to depression in humans. However, it remains unclear whether R. intestinalis affects depressive-like behaviours through the gut-brain axis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists have attached growing interest for their neurological effects. Recent clinical studies demonstrated GLP-1R agonists may reduce depressive symptoms in patients. Our preliminary findings indicate that in a neuropathic pain model, R. intestinalis activates GLP-1+ neurons in the NTS and GLP-1R+ neurons in the lateral septum (LS), which exhibits reduced functional connectivity to the lateral habenula (LHb), a key region involved in depression. We hypothesize that R. intestinalis can enhance endogenous GLP-1 signalling to restore inhibitory outputs from the LS and reduce hyperexcitability in the LHb, thereby alleviating depressive-like behaviours in the context of chronic pain. In this study, using functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI), electrophysiology, chemogenetic manipulations, and conditional knockout models, we aim to: investigate whether endogenous GLP-1R agonism contributes to the antidepressant effects of R. intestinalis (Objective 1); map the GLP-1R-dependent cellular and neural circuit mechanisms by which R. intestinalis modulates the LS, focusing on its interactions with the LHb in mood regulation (Objective 2); and identify the specific metabolites produced by R. intestinalis that mediate gut-brain communication via the gut-nodose ganglion-NTS-LS pathway (Objective 3). Our study may reveal potential gut-brain mechanisms underlying the antidepressant effects of R. intestinalis and highlight the novel gut-brain axis approach to stimulate endogenous GLP-1R signalling for the treatment of neurological disorders. These findings could pave the way for developing microbiome-based therapies to manage chronic pain-associated psychiatric comorbidities. 慢性疼痛患者更容易罹患精神類共病，如抑鬱症。近期研究強調腸腦通訊在神經系統疾病的發展與治療中的關鍵作用。我們的最新研究發現，在神經病理性疼痛患者中，Roseburia intestinalis（R. intestinalis）明顯減少；在動物模型中補充 R. intestinalis 可透過調節腸道–迷走神經–孤束核（NTS）–杏仁核的神經迴路，減輕痛覺過敏。已有研究證實 R. intestinalis 在多種抑鬱動物模型中具抗抑鬱作用，且其在人體中豐度降低與抑鬱症相關。然而，目前尚不清楚 R. intestinalis 是否透過腸腦軸影響抑鬱樣行為。胰高血糖素樣肽-1 受體（GLP-1R）激動劑因其神經保護作用而受到越來越多關注。近期臨床研究顯示，GLP-1R 激動劑可減輕患者的抑鬱症狀。我們的初步發現指出，在神經病理性疼痛模型中，R. intestinalis 可活化孤束核中的 GLP-1 陽性神經元，以及外側隔核（LS）中的 GLP-1R 陽性神經元；後者與外側縫核（LHb，與抑鬱密切相關的關鍵腦區）之間的功能連結有所下降。我們推測，R. intestinalis 能促進內源性 GLP-1 訊號傳導，恢復 LS 對 LHb 的抑制性輸出，從而降低 LHb 的過度興奮性，緩解慢性痛背景下的抑鬱樣行為。在本研究中，我們將結合功能性超聲影像（fUSI）、電生理學、化學遺傳學操控和條件性基因剔除模型，具體目標如下：探討內源性 GLP-1R 活化是否參與 R. intestinalis 所產生的抗抑鬱效應（目標一）；解析 R. intestinalis 調節 LS 的 GLP-1R 依賴性細胞與神經迴路機制，特別是其與 LHb 在情緒調控中的交互作用（目標二）；鑑定由 R. intestinalis 產生、經腸道–結節神經節–NTS–LS 路徑介導腸腦通訊的具體代謝物（目標三）。本研究有望揭示 R. intestinalis 抗抑鬱作用背後的潛在腸腦機制，並提出透過促進內源性 GLP-1R 訊號來治療神經精神疾病的新策略。相關成果亦可為開發微生物組為基礎的治療手段，以應對慢性痛相關的精神共病提供理論依據與實踐方向。

14119925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119925.value: 含捲曲螺旋結構域蛋白141在心臟發育過程中功能的機制研究

14119925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119925.value: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common types of birth defects. The intricate process of heart development demands significant migration and differentiation of cardiac precursor cells, orchestrated by signaling pathways like Wnt and SHH. Despite the increasing research into heart development and regeneration, many aspects of these processes are not fully understood. The Coiled-Coil Domain Containing protein 141 (CCDC141) was previously suggested to be associated with regulating heart rate. Moreover, it was implicated in radial migration in neurons by regulating the centrosome. CCDC141 can interact with Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), subsequently attenuating its ⍺-tubulin deacetylase activity at the centrosome. We found that ccdc141 is expressed in the heart primordia during the heart development of zebrafish and Xenopus embryos. Knockdown of ccdc141 in zebrafish embryos caused heart edema, accompanied by diminished expression of heart marker genes such as cmlc2 and myh6. Additionally, heart looping was notably impaired after the knockdown of Ccdc141. We induced CCDC141 knockout human embryonic stem cells to differentiate into cardiomyocytes. Gene expression profiling assay for the induced cardiomyocytes showed downregulation of mitochondrial genes and those associated with oxidative phosphorylation. Furthermore, the expression patterns of genes related to actin filament and cardio-structural myosins were significantly altered following the loss of CCDC141. These findings highlight the indispensable role of Ccdc141 in heart development. However, the mechanisms underpinning these effects remain to be clarified. Based on the above findings, we, therefore, hypothesized that Ccdc141 is essential for heart development by interaction with Hdac6 to maintain the homeostasis of mitochondria. To test our hypothesis, we propose the following study: 1) to characterize the impact of ccdc141 deletion on heart structure and function in zebrafish and mouse models, 2) to investigate the interaction of Ccdc141 and Hadc6 during heart development, and 3) to investigate the mitochondrial function mediated by Ccdc141 during heart development. By illuminating the role of Ccdc141 in heart development, we aim to provide deeper insights into this sophisticated process. A greater understanding of these mechanisms will facilitate the development of new therapeutic strategies for CHD, potentially bridging existing gaps in our understanding of heart development. 先天性心臟病是最常見的出生缺陷之一。 心臟發育是一個複雜過程，涉及心臟前體細胞的大量遷移和分化，這一過程需要由Wnt和SHH等信號通路精密調控。 儘管心臟發育與再生的研究不斷深入，這些過程中的許多環節仍是盲點。 Coiled-Coil Domain Containing protein 141（CCDC141）曾被認為與心率調節相關，有研究報導稱它可通過調控中心體影響神經元的放射狀遷移。 CCDC141能夠與組蛋白去乙醯化酶6（HDAC6）相互作用，進而減弱其在中心體處對α-微管蛋白的去乙醯化活性。 我們發現，在斑馬魚和爪蛙胚胎心臟發育過程中，ccdc141在心臟原基中表達。 在斑馬魚胚胎中敲低ccdc141會導致心臟水腫，並伴隨心臟標誌基因cmlc2和myh6的表達降低。 此外，ccdc141敲低后心臟環化明顯受損。 我們誘導CCDC141敲除的人類胚胎幹細胞分化為心肌細胞，基因表達譜分析顯示線粒體基因及與氧化磷酸化相關基因表達下調，且肌動蛋白絲和心臟結構肌球蛋白相關基因的表達模式在CCDC141缺失后顯著改變。 這些研究結果突顯了Ccdc141在心臟發育中的不可或缺作用，但其背後的機制尚待闡明。 基於上述結果，我們提出假設：Ccdc141通過與Hdac6相互作用維持線粒體穩態，從而對心臟發育至關重要。 為驗證該假設，我們擬開展以下研究：1）利用斑馬魚和小鼠模型明確ccdc141缺失對心臟結構和功能的影響; 2）探究心臟發育過程中Ccdc141與Hdac6的相互作用; 3）闡明Ccdc141在心臟發育中介導的線粒體功能。 通過揭示Ccdc141在心臟發育中的作用，旨在深化對這一精密過程的理解，併為建立先天性心臟病新治療策略的開發奠定基礎，填補當前我們對心臟發育認識的空白。

14121925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14121925.value: 18F-PSMA PET 在可疑 MRI 前列腺癌診斷中的作用：一項多中心隨機對照試驗

14121925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14121925.value: Prof Ng, Chi-fai Dr Wu, Kwan Kit

14121925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121925.value: Background: The incidence of Prostate cancer (PCa) is rapidly rising in Asia. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) of the prostate improves detection of clinically significant PCa (csPCa), but equivocal mpMRI prostate is common (40% in real-life) and pose challenges in biopsy decisions. 68Ga-PSMA PET-CT has shown potential in improving csPCa diagnosis in single-arm studies. PET-CT using 18F-PSMA radiotracer has gained popularity in the region due to more favourable costs and availability, but the additional value of pelvis-only 18F-PSMA over mpMRI in improving csPCa diagnosis and changing clinical management is unknown. Methods: This is a phase III multi-center randomised controlled trial to evaluate the detection of csPCa by MRI-guided biopsy approach (MRI arm) versus MRI + pelvis-only 18F-PSMA PET-CT approach (COMBINED arm). csPCa is defined as ISUP (International Society of Urological Pathology) Grade group ≥ 2 PCa. Patients with equivocal suspicion of prostate cancer on MRI with PI-RADS score 2 with red flag (PSAdensity >0.2 OR Prostate health index, PHI>35), PI-RADS 3, or PI-RADS 4 (PSAdensity <0.1 OR PHI<35) will be randomised in a 1:1 manner to MRI arm or COMBINED arm. Targeted and systematic prostate biopsy is performed in all patients in the study. The primary outcome includes csPCa diagnosis AND/OR any change in clinical management (determined by an independent panel) from additional csPCa in PET targets. Aims and Hypothesis: For the primary outcome, we hypothesize that COMBINED arm is superior to MRI arm in detecting csPCa AND/OR any change in clinical management from PET-target detected csPCa. Sample size calculation: The sample size was estimated based on the primary outcome: 15% in MRI arm versus 30% in COMBINED arm, with data from the published PRIMARY trial and local Asian data. For the primary outcome, a total of 236 men (118 in each group) are required to achieve 80% power and 5% Type 1 error (two-sided). By estimating a withdrawal rate of 5%, a total of 250 men (125 in each group) are required to be recruited. Timeline and feasibility: Four urology centres in Hong Kong agreed to participate. Each centre performs about 150-250 MRI-guided prostate biopsies each year, among which 40% are equivocal MRI. Assuming 50% of men agree recruitment, the recruitment and whole study should be completed in 24 and 30 months, respectively. Practice-changing potential: If additional clinical value is shown by adding 18F-PSMA PET to equivocal MRI, then this should be the new standard of care. 背景：前列腺癌 (PCa) 在亞洲的發生率正在迅速上升。前列腺多參數磁振造影 (mpMRI) 可提高對臨床顯著前列腺癌 (csPCa) 的檢出率，但 mpMRI 前列腺診斷結果不明確的現像很常見（實際發生率為 40%），這給活檢決策帶來了挑戰。 68Ga-PSMA PET-CT 已在單組研究中顯示出改善 csPCa 診斷的潛力。使用18F-PSMA 放射性追蹤劑的 PET-CT 由於成本更低且易於獲取，越來越受歡迎，但僅針對骨盆的 18F-PSMA 相較於 mpMRI 在改善 csPCa 診斷和改變臨床治療方面是否具有額外的價值尚不清楚。 方法：本研究為III期多中心隨機對照試驗，旨在評估MRI引導下切片方法（MRI組）與MRI+PSMA PET-CT（PET組）對csPCa的檢測效果。 csPCa定義為ISUP（國際泌尿病理學會）≥2級的前列腺癌。 MRI檢查提示可疑前列腺癌，且PI-RADS評分為2級（PSA密度>0.2或前列腺健康指數，PHI>35）、PI-RADS評分為3或PI-RADS評分為4級（PSA密度<0.1或PHI<35）的患者，將按1:1的比例隨機分配至MRI組或PET組。所有患者均接受標靶及系統性攝護腺切片檢查。主要結果包括csPCa診斷和/或PET標靶中新增csPCa導致的臨床管理變化（由獨立專家小組確定）。 目的與假設：對於主要結果，我們假設聯合組在檢測csPCa和/或PET標靶中新增csPCa導致的臨床管理變化方面優於MRI組。 樣本量計算：樣本量是根據主要結果估算的：MRI組為15%，聯合組為30%，數據來自已發表的PRIMARY試驗和亞洲本地數據。對於主要結果，需要總共236名男性（每組118名）才能達到80%的檢驗效力和5%的1型錯誤率（雙側）。根據估計退出率為5%，共需要招募250名男性（每組125名）。 時間表和可行性：香港有四家泌尿外科中心同意參與。每家中心每年進行約150-250例MRI引導下攝護腺切片，其中40%為可疑MRI檢查。假設50%的男性同意招募，則招募和整個研究應分別在24個月和30個月內完成。 實踐變革潛力：如果在可疑MRI檢查中添加18F-PSMA PET檢查能夠顯示額外的臨床價值，那麼這應該成為新的治療標準。

14122625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14122625.value: 一種新型鋅指結構域腫瘤抑制因子在食管鱗癌發病過程中作爲細胞信號傳導的核內主調控因子

14122625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122625.value: Esophageal cancer is common worldwide. In China/HK, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is the main type, characterized by its rapid progression. ESCC is a major cause of cancer deaths in China/HK, with high rate of metastasis/recurrence and low 5-y survival rate, as current treatments for ESCC have only limited efficacy. Tumor metastasis originates from deregulation of cell properties (stemness, epithelial-mesenchymal transition-EMT), caused by disrupted cell signaling derived from inactivation/activation of signaling genes. While ESCC has limited scattered gene mutations, epigenetic inactivation of cancer genes by promoter methylation is frequently involved, even in its early stage. Molecular epigenetic studies of ESCC pathogenesis to elucidate cancer genes related to stemness and metastasis will benefit ESCC patients. I previously profiled the genome-wide CpG methylomes of ESCC and identified multiple methylated cancer genes. Among them is a novel zinc finger protein ZFP447, a nuclear factor. Pilot work showed that ZFP447 is frequently downregulated in ESCC, with its low expression correlated with patient poor survival. ZFP447 has not been studied properly for its functions in human carcinogenesis so far. I found that ZFP447 functions as a candidate tumor suppressor inhibiting ESCC cell proliferation, migration and invasion. ZFP447 regulates the expression of EMT/stemness factors and multiple signaling pathways, indicating that it is a critical regulator of stemness/EMT features and cell signaling in ESCC cells. Thus, I propose to further study in-depth its abnormalities, functions and mechanisms in ESCC. I will examine its epigenetic/genetic alterations in ESCC cell lines (>20) and primary tumors (60 pairs). Its cancer biological functions on ESCC cell proliferation, apoptosis, clonogenicity, invasion and metastasis will be assessed in vitro (especially in ESCC cell lines with more % of stem cells like KYSE180 and KYSE220) and in vivo, through lentiviral inducible expression, shRNA knock-down and nude mice model. I will further investigate its effects on ESCC stemness/EMT features, and decipher its regulated cell signaling pathways (STAT/MAPK, WNT, p53). Moreover, I will determine its transcription regulation role through profiling its target genes genome-wide by ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq, and its regulatory complexes through MASS spectrometry. Finally, I will evaluate the relationship of ZFP447 methylation with ESCC clinical features for its biomarker value. Through this study, I will define its alterations, functions and molecular mechanisms to ESCC metastasis, and its biomarker value. The study will benefit the management of all ESCC patients. 食管癌在全球範圍內高發。中國（包括香港地區）以食管鱗狀細胞癌（ESCC）爲主要病理類型，該亞型病程進展迅速。由於現有治療手段療效有限，ESCC已成爲我國癌症相關死亡的主要誘因，其轉移/複發率高且五年生存率低。腫瘤轉移源於細胞特性（乾性、上皮-間質轉化）的失調，而該失調由信號傳導基因失活/激活引發的細胞信號通路紊亂所致。儘管ESCC的基因突變呈散在分佈，但啓動子甲基化導致的癌基因表觀遺傳失活常參與發病過程，甚至在早期階段即可出現。通過分子表觀遺傳學研究闡明ESCC發病中乾性與轉移相關的癌基因，將爲患者診療提供重要依據。 前期研究通過全基因組CpG甲基化譜分析，鑑定出多個ESCC甲基化癌基因。其中新型鋅指蛋白ZFP447作爲核因子，初步研究表明其在ESCC中頻繁下調，且低表達與患者不良預後顯著相關。目前ZFP447在人類腫瘤發生中的功能尚未明確。本研究發現ZFP447通過抑制ESCC細胞增殖、遷移與侵襲發揮候選腫瘤抑制因子功能。該因子可調控EMT/乾性因子及多條信號通路表達，提示其是ESCC細胞乾性/EMT特徵與信號傳導的關鍵調控樞紐。 據此，本研究擬深入探究ZFP447在ESCC中的異常機制、功能及作用機理：首先檢測20餘株ESCC細胞系及60對原發腫瘤組織中該基因的表觀遺傳/遺傳學改變；通過慢病毒誘導表達系統、shRNA敲降技術及裸鼠模型，在體外（重點使用KYSE180、KYSE220等高幹細胞比例細胞系）及體內評估其對ESCC細胞增殖、凋亡、克隆形成、侵襲及轉移的腫瘤生物學功能；進而解釋其對ESCC乾性/EMT特徵的影響，並闡明其調控的STAT/MAPK、WNT、p53等信號通路；採用ATAC-seq與ChIP-seq在全基因組範圍繪製其靶基因譜，結合質譜分析鑑定其調控複合物組成；最終評估ZFP447甲基化水平與ESCC臨牀特徵的相關性以確立其生物標誌物價值。本研究將系統揭示ZFP447在ESCC轉移中的異常改變、功能作用及分子機制，並確立其臨牀轉化價值，爲ESCC患者的綜合診療管理提供理論依據。

14122725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14122725.value: Wnt2b+腫瘤相關成纖維細胞在胃癌發生過程中的活化及功能研究

14122725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14122725.value: Prof Tian, Xiaoyu Prof To, Ka-fai Prof ZHANG, Ge

14122725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122725.value: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fifth most common malignancy worldwide, with a high prevalence in Eastern Asia, including Hong Kong. Cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) has been reported to play a promoting role, and our previous studies have delineated several oncogenic signaling transduction patterns between CAFs and cancer cells. However, the role of CAFs in GC angiogenesis and rendering resistance to anti-angiogenic therapies has not been investigated. In our preliminary studies, a subgroup of GC CAFs behaves with progenitor-like properties and abnormal upregulation of the Wnt signaling pathway. Then WNT2B was identified as the predominantly abundant Wnt ligand in this CAF population and was closely correlated with the proliferation-promoting and aggressiveness acquirement capacities. High Wnt2b expression predicts poorer prognosis and drives self-renewal and aggressiveness maintenance of CAFs. On the contrary, Wnt2b depletion dramatically impaired the supportive role of CAFs, leading to retarded GC progression with less angiogenesis, confirmed by Col1a2-Wnt2b-/- transgenic mice. Mechanically, ZEB1 serves as a transcriptional regulator of Wnt2b, and its abundance in CAFs served as an independent prognostic marker to indicate unfavorable outcomes. Meanwhile, FZD1 was revealed as the Wnt2b receptor on the CAF surface, which is indispensable for the promoting effects of Wnt2b on CAFs. While in endothelial cells, FZD4 was identified as the predominant Wnt2b receptor, promoting angiogenesis (confirmed by Tie2-Fzd4tg/+ mice) by mainly activating Hippo-YAP1 signaling as a G protein-coupled receptor. Taken together, we hypothesized that the ZEB1-activated Wnt2b+ CAFs play a crucial role in CAF self-renewal and aggressiveness acquaintance and accelerate angiogenesis through the Wnt2b-FZD4-YAP1 axis to promote GC progression. To test the hypothesis, we propose three specific aims: 1) To decipher the role of H. pylori infection in shaping the accumulation and activation of Wnt2b+ CAFs; 2) To delineate the HIF-1α-mediated upregulation of FZD4 and the molecular mechanisms of Wnt2b-FZD4 in angiogenesis by activating the G-protein-YAP1 signaling; 3) To develop FZD4-targeted aptamer-PROTAC conjugate and siRNA-containing lipid nanoparticles to tackle the resistance to anti-VEGF/VEGFR therapies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study aiming to unravel the molecular mechanisms of Wnt2b+ CAFs in GC microenvironment, mainly through Wnt2b-FZD1 in CAFs and Wnt2b-FZD4-G-protein-YAP1 in endothelial cells. This research will play a pivotal role in expanding our understanding by uncovering the intricate relationship between Wnt2b+ CAFs and GC development. Notably, it will provide novel insight and cutting-edge strategies to overcome resistance to VEGF/VEGFR inhibitors and effectively inhibit GC development to benefit patients. 胃癌（GC）是全球第五大常見惡性腫瘤，在包括香港在內的東亞地區發病率較高。據報導，腫瘤相關成纖維細胞（CAF）在其中發揮促進作用，我們先前的研究已闡明瞭幾種CAF與癌細胞之間的致癌信號轉導模式。然而，CAF在胃癌血管生成及導致抗血管生成治療耐藥中的作用尚未被研究。在我們的初步研究中，發現一個胃癌CAF亞群表現出祖細胞樣特性和Wnt信號通路的異常上調。隨後，WNT2B被確定為該CAF群體中主要富集的Wnt配體，並與促增殖和獲得侵襲性的能力密切相關。高表達的Wnt2b預示著較差的預後，並能驅動CAF的自我更新和侵襲性維持。相反，敲除Wnt2b會顯著削弱CAF的支持作用，導致胃癌進展減緩且血管生成減少，這一點在Col1a2-Wnt2b-/-轉基因小鼠模型中得到證實。在機制上，ZEB1作為Wnt2b的轉錄調節蛋白，其在CAF中的表達可作為獨立的預後標誌物，揭示不良預後。同時，研究發現FZD1是CAF表面的Wnt2b受體，對於Wnt2b對CAF的促進作用不可或缺。而在內皮細胞中，FZD4被確定為主要的Wnt2b受體，主要通過作為G蛋白偶聯受體啟動Hippo-YAP1信號通路來促進血管生成。綜上所述，我們提出假說：ZEB1啟動的Wnt2b+ CAF在CAF自我更新和侵襲性獲得中起關鍵作用，並通過Wnt2b-FZD4-YAP1軸加速血管生成，從而促進胃癌進展。為驗證該假說，我們提出以下三個具體研究目標：1）解析幽門螺桿菌（H. pylori）感染在塑造Wnt2b+ CAF積累和活化中的作用；2）闡明HIF-1α介導的FZD4上調以及Wnt2b-FZD4通過啟動G蛋白-YAP1信號通路促進血管生成的分子機制；3）開發靶向FZD4的適配體-PROTAC偶聯物和含siRNA的脂質納米顆粒，以解決對抗VEGF/VEGFR治療的耐藥性問題。據我們所知，這是首個旨在揭示Wnt2b+ CAF在胃癌微環境中分子機制的研究，重點聚焦於CAF內的Wnt2b-FZD1通路以及內皮細胞中的Wnt2b-FZD4-G蛋白-YAP1通路。本研究將通過揭示Wnt2b+ CAF與胃癌發展之間複雜的相互作用關係，拓展我們的認知。尤為重要的是，該研究將為克服VEGF/VEGFR抑制劑耐藥性、有效抑制胃癌發展以造福患者提供新穎的見解和前沿策略。

14123425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14123425.value: 人工智能在主動脈瓣返流中的應用：多中心隨機對照試驗

14123425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14123425.value: Prof Wong, Kenneth Kwan-Yee Ms ZHAO, CHENXU

14123425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14123425.value: Aortic regurgitation (AR) is a common heart valve disease where the aortic valve fails to close properly, causing blood to flow backward into the heart. This condition can lead to heart failure if not diagnosed and treated promptly. However, diagnosing AR is challenging because current methods rely heavily on the skills of the operator, leading to variability and potential misdiagnosis, especially in settings with limited resources or non-specialist clinicians. This research project aims to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) tool that can automatically detect and measure AR using echocardiography (ultrasound of the heart). The AI system will analyze key heart imaging parameters, such as the size of the valve opening and the amount of blood leaking back into the heart, to provide a consistent and accurate diagnosis. By automating this process, the tool will reduce human error and variability, which are common in current diagnostic methods. The system will also be user-friendly, making it accessible to clinicians with limited experience in echocardiography, thus improving diagnosis in resource-limited environments. The project involves two main phases. In the first phase, the AI system will be developed and tested using echocardiographic images from five international hospitals. These images will be used to train the AI to recognize different levels of AR severity. The system’s accuracy will be validated by comparing the AI's measurements with those made by expert cardiologists and using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), the gold standard for heart volume measurements. In the second phase, a randomized controlled trial (RCT) will be conducted to compare the AI-assisted diagnosis with traditional manual methods in clinical settings. The trial will measure how much time the AI saves, how accurate it is compared to manual assessments, and how it impacts treatment decisions. The study will also track patient outcomes over one year to determine if the AI tool improves long-term health. This research aims to standardize AR diagnosis, making it faster, more accurate, and accessible across different healthcare settings. Ultimately, the AI tool could help clinicians make earlier and more accurate treatment decisions, improving patient outcomes and reducing the burden of heart disease globally. 項目摘要（面向非專業人士） 主動脈瓣返流（AR）是一種常見的心臟瓣膜疾病，由於主動脈瓣關閉不全導致血液迴流心臟，若診斷和治療不及時，可能引發心力衰竭。目前，AR的診斷高度依賴操作者的技術經驗，存在較大主觀性和誤診風險，尤其在醫療資源有限或非專業醫生環境中，此問題更為突出。 本項目旨在開發一種基於人工智能（AI），可於經胸超聲心動圖上自動檢測與定量分析AR的輔助工具。該AI系統將分析指南要求的關鍵心臟超聲指標，如瓣口大小及反流量等，以實現標準化和精準診斷，降低人為誤差和操作差異，並具備良好的用戶體驗，使非專業人員也能輕鬆操作，提高資源有限環境下的診斷水準。 項目分為兩個階段：第一階段利用來自五家國際醫院的超聲心動圖影像開發並訓練AI系統，評估其對不同AR嚴重程度的識別能力，並通過心內科專家判讀，以及以心臟磁共振（CMR）驗證系統準確性。第二階段將開展臨床隨機對照試驗（RCT），比較AI輔助和傳統人工診斷之效率、準確性，以及對臨床決策的影響，並隨訪患者一年，評估其對長期預後的改善作用。本研究致力於標準化AR診斷流程，提高效率和準確性，推廣至不同醫療環境，幫助臨床醫生實現更早和更準確的治療決策，從而改善患者結局，降低全球心臟病負擔。

14124525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14124525.value: 齧齒動物模型中不同多巴胺通路在助人行為中的作用

14124525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14124525.value: Targeted helping behavior refers to the phenomenon where individuals assist others based on specific needs or circumstances. This form of prosocial behavior is crucial not only for the mental health of individuals but also for the cohesion of society as a whole. Understanding the neural underpinnings of helping behavior is essential for grasping the functioning of the social brain and has significant implications for addressing disorders related to social behavior. However, the restricted level of control in human studies due to ethical constraints and the complexity of human social interaction, along with the limitation of contemporary brain imaging technologies, have prevented in-depth investigation on the neural mechanism underlying helping behavior. Rodents are shown to exhibit complex social behaviors, including helping behaviors, making them a valuable model to interrogate the neural mechanism of this form of prosocial behavior. Our preliminary studies, based on a rescue from water soaking paradigm, provide compelling evidence to confirm that rats can perform targeted helping behavior toward conspecifics in distress. At the same time, this paradigm allows real-time monitoring of neuronal activities from the brain and their intervention. Our findings suggest that this behavior involves dopaminergic projections from the midbrain’s ventral tegmental area (VTA) to the nucleus accumbens within the limbic system as well as to the prefrontal cortex. In this proposal, we hypothesize that the mesolimbic dopaminergic pathway mediates distinct emotional components that reinforce helping behavior, while the mesocortical dopaminergic pathway regulates the decision-making process. To test our hypothesis, we will 1) conduct a comprehensive characterization of the targeted helping behavior to fully validate its utility; 2) investigate the role of the mesolimbic pathway in mediating motivation to help, reward and the encoding of stress and its relief; 3) explore the potential role of the mesocortical pathway in processing dopaminergic input from VTA that in turn regulates the decision-making process. A variety of cutting-edge research techniques, including optogenetic manipulations, in vivo microendoscopic imaging, fibre photometry, chemogenetics and machine-learning tools will be applied to address our questions. The results of this project will substantially advance our understanding of the neural circuit and mechanisms of the different phases underlying helping behavior, especially the multifaceted functions of dopamine. Ultimately, insights gained from the animal models can inform therapeutic strategies for social behavioral disorders in humans, bridging the gap between basic research and clinical applications. 助人行為是指個體根據他人的特定需求或情境給予幫助的現象。這種親社會行為不僅對個體的心理健康至關重要，也對整個社會的凝聚力發揮著重要作用。理解助人行為的神經機制對於掌握社會大腦的功能具有重要意義，並且對解決與社會行為相關的障礙具有深遠影響。研究表明，齧齒動物表現出包括助人行為在內的複雜社會行為，因此是探究此類親社會行為神經機制的寶貴模型。我們基於水救範式的初步研究證明大鼠能夠對處於困境的同類實施助人行為。同時，該範式還可實現對腦區神經活動的即時監測與干預 。這種行為涉及中腦腹側被蓋區 向邊緣系統伏隔核以及前額葉皮層的多巴胺能投射。 在本研究計畫中，我們假設中腦－邊緣系統多巴胺通路（介導了強化助人行為的不同情緒成分，而中腦－皮質多巴胺通路則調節助人決策過程。為驗證這一假設，我們將對 1)充分驗證助人行為該範式的有效性；2) 探討中腦－邊緣系統通路在調節助人動機、獎賞，以及壓力緩解的編碼中的作用；3)探索中腦－皮質通路調控決策過程中的潛在作用。本研究將結合多種前沿技術，包括光遺傳學操作、在體微型內窺鏡成像、光纖光度法、化學遺傳學以及機器學習工具，以回答上述科學問題。本計畫的成果將顯著推動我們對助人行為不同階段所依託的神經迴路和機制的理解，尤其是多巴胺的多重功能。最終，從動物模型獲得的見解可為人類社會行為障礙的治療策略提供參考，促進基礎研究與臨床應用之間的銜接。

14124925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14124925.value: 雄性激素受體激動劑作為抑制因子標靶治療AR陽性鼻咽癌中的c-myc/cyclin D1訊號軸

14124925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14124925.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a male-dominant cancer. However, whether the androgen receptor (AR) pathway has any contribution to pathogenesis and disease progression is unclear. Non-targeting chemotherapy remains as the major treatment modality in NPC, as less than 7% patients present with druggable oncogenic mutations. Therefore, alternative and biomarker-driven treatment which can benefit substantial portion of NPC patients with high efficacy and low toxicity is urgently needed. In search for the impact of AR signaling in NPC, we found that a subset of NPC cell lines & xenografts as well as around 60% of patients were detected with prominent AR expression. Interestingly, AR antagonist or depletion of AR by PROTAC degrader did not suppress viability or colony formation of the AR-positive NPC cells. On the other hand, activation of AR by selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM), endosarm, could repress tumor growth and promote differentiation in AR-positive NPC cancer cells. Our data also demonstrated that enodosarm could effectively suppress c-myc/cyclin D1 axis. This might coincide with the phenomenon observed in castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), where supraphysiological androgen (SPA) promote the tumor suppressive activity of AR through c-myc repression as well as maintenance at quiescence (G0). NPC is also an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated cancer. As c-myc being a central oncogenic mediator and viral latency gate-keeper in NPC, the repression of c-myc by enodosarm not only led to anti-proliferation but also lytic-reactivation in EBV-infected NPC cells. Our pilot in vivo study also showed enodosarm could suppress the tumorigenicity of NPC via AR signaling activation, downregulation of c-myc & cyclin D1, as well as expression of differentiation marker. In this study, we will (1) investigate the underlying mechanism in transcriptional modulation by AR signaling using ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq and RNA-seq, (2) consolidate the importance of c-myc/cyclinD1 axis in mediating the anti-tumor and lytic-reactivation effects of enodosarm, (3) comprehensively evaluate the in vivo efficacy and transcription dynamics imposed by enodosarm using single-cell RNA sequencing, and (4) demonstrate the potential synergistic effect of combined treatment of enodosarm and CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib) in AR+ NPC models. Our ultimate goal is to provide comprehensive preclinical data to position enodosarm as a promising drug for AR-positive NPC patients in biomarker-selected clinical trials and the development of strategies to augment responses. These regimes may be adminstrated as adjuvant therapy alongside conventional chemotherapy, particularly in patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC for better clinical outcomes. 鼻咽癌是一種男性高發生率的癌症。然而，雄激素受體（AR）訊號通路是否在其發病機制和疾病進展中發揮作用尚不清楚。目前，非標靶化療仍是鼻咽癌的主要治療方式，因為只有不到7%的患者攜帶可成藥的致癌突變。因此，迫切需要一種替代性的、由生物標記驅動的治療方案，以高效低毒性的方式惠及廣大鼻咽癌患者。 為探究AR訊號在鼻咽癌中的作用，我們發現一部分鼻咽癌細胞系、異種移植瘤以及約60%的患者檢測到顯著的AR表現。有趣的是，AR拮抗劑或使用PROTAC降解劑耗竭AR，並未抑制AR陽性鼻咽癌細胞的活力或集落形成能力。另一方面，使用選擇性雄性激素受體調節劑（SARM）恩多索胺（enobosarm）活化AR，可抑制AR陽性鼻咽癌癌細胞的腫瘤生長並促進其分化。我們的數據還表明，恩多索胺能有效抑制c-myc/cyclin D1訊號軸。這可能與去勢抵抗性前列腺癌（CRPC）中觀察到的現像一致，即超生理劑量雄激素（SPA）透過抑制c-myc以及維持細胞靜止期（G0）來促進AR的腫瘤抑制活性。 鼻咽癌也是一種與愛潑斯坦-巴爾病毒（EBV）相關的癌症。鑑於c-myc在鼻咽癌中既是關鍵的致癌介質，也是病毒潛伏期的“守門人”，恩多索胺對c-myc的抑制不僅導致了抗增殖作用，還在EBV感染的鼻咽癌細胞中引發了裂解再激活（lytic-reactivation）。我們的初步體內研究也表明，恩多索胺可透過活化AR訊號、下調c-myc和cyclin D1、以及促進分化標記物的表達來抑制鼻咽癌的致瘤性。 在本研究中，我們將：(1) 利用ATAC-seq、ChIP-seq和RNA-seq研究AR訊號在轉錄調控中的潛在機制；(2) 確證c-myc/cyclinD1訊號軸在介導恩多索胺抗腫瘤和裂解再活化效應中的重要性；(3)使用單細胞RNA定序（scRNA-seq）全面評估恩多索胺在體內的療效及其誘導的轉錄動態變化；4) 在陽性鼻咽癌模型中，論證恩多索胺與CDK4/6抑制劑（帕博西尼，palbociclib）合併治療的潛在協同效應。 我們的最終目標是為恩多索胺提供全面的臨床前數據，將其定位為AR陽性鼻咽癌患者的一種有前景的藥物，用於在生物標記篩選的臨床試驗中開展研究，並製定增強治療反應的策略。這些方案可作為輔助治療與常規化療聯用，特別是在復發或轉移性鼻咽癌患者中，以期獲得更好的臨床結果。

14200125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200125.value: 以分層分佈式學習和計算加速大規模非線性電力潮流優化

14200125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200125.value: Optimal power flow (OPF) is a fundamental optimization problem, which aims to minimize the operational cost of a power network subject to its physical laws, resource capacities, and safety limits. The physical laws mainly refer to the nonlinear alternating-current (AC) power flow equations, which make the OPF problems nonconvex and thus hard to solve, especially with a large and ever-increasing number of decision variables for the rapidly growing controllable distributed energy resources. In this project, we will develop new algorithms to solve large-scale nonlinear OPF problems faster than existing methods, with guaranteed feasibility and improved optimality of solutions. To realize this goal, the proposed algorithms will perform learning and computing in a spatially hierarchical and distributed structure on power distribution networks. We will firstly develop a hierarchical distributed primal-dual gradient algorithm to accelerate the solution of large-scale linearized OPF problems. Then we will adapt this algorithm with an improved gradient calculation method to compensate for the model linearization errors and thus solve large-scale nonlinear OPF problems more accurately. To further enhance the speed of solving large-scale nonlinear OPF problems while ensuring the quality of solutions, we will learn decentralized neural network models from simulated data to predict the iterative descent directions of decision variables in the hierarchical distributed algorithm. Each of the tasks above will start with a simplified, single-phase, radial (tree) power distribution network model and extend to the more realistic unbalanced three-phase model, with the latter containing power sources, loads, and transformers in mixed wye and delta configurations. We shall verify the solution quality and computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms through software simulation on power distribution network models with up to 100,000 nodes. 最優電力潮流 (OPF) 是一類基本的優化問題，旨在於物理規律、資源容量和安全限制約束之下，最小化電網運行成本。這裡的物理規律主要指非線性交流潮流方程，它們使得 OPF 問題具有非凸性，因而難以求解，尤其是在可控分佈式能源快速增長且決策變量個數不斷增加的情況下。在本項目中，我們將開發新的算法，以比現有方法更快的速度求解大規模非線性 OPF 問題，同時保證解的可行性並提高其最優性。為實現這一目標，所提出的算法將立足於配電網的空間分層分佈式結構進行學習和計算。我們將首先開發一種分層分佈式原-對偶梯度算法，以加速大規模線性化 OPF 問題的求解。然後，我們將採用改進的梯度計算方法對此算法進行調整，以補償模型線性化誤差，從而更準確地求解大規模非線性 OPF 問題。為進一步提高大規模非線性OPF問題的求解速度並確保解的質量，我們將從仿真數據中學習分散式神經網絡模型，以預測分層分佈式算法中決策變量的迭代下降方向。上述每個任務都將從簡化的單相徑向（樹形）配電網模型開始，並擴展到更真實的三相不平衡模型，後者包含混合星形和三角形連接的電源、負載和變壓器。我們將通過對多達 100,000 節點的配電網模型進行軟件仿真，驗證所提算法的求解質量和計算效率。

14200425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200425.value: 用於男性早期膀胱癌冷凍治療的超細智能柔性膀胱鏡機器人

14200425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14200425.value: Prof Ren, Hongliang Dr Teoh, Yuen Chun, Jeremy

14200425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200425.value: Bladder cancer (BC) is a prevalent malignancy, primarily affecting males. Early-stage BC, particularly non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), which constitutes 70-80% of BC cases, generally has a favorable prognosis. However, NMIBC is prone to recurrence, complicating long-term management. Cryotherapy, an emerging treatment for NMIBC, eradicates cancer cells by applying a cryogenic medium directly to the tumor site. This method offers benefits such as shorter hospital stays, reduced tissue swelling and blood loss, and potentially lower recurrence rates. However, current cryotherapies require the use of thick, rigid cryo-probes, leading to invasive procedures that can damage healthy tissues. The insufficient dexterity of these devices fails to cover the whole bladder, and their lack of automation and intelligent control, restricts the applicability of such novel therapy. To address these challenges and drawing on our team’s expertise in robotics and AI, we propose an innovative solution: an ultrathin flexible transurethral cystoscopic robot for NMIBC cryotherapy (CryoFR) that integrates novel mechatronics design, intelligent navigation and control, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal image processing techniques. Our newly designed robotic system will provide new capabilities of localized intravesical cryoablation at deep surgical sites, with a superior bladder coverage rate compared to the existing rigid instrumentation. Despite intuitive teleopeation, the robot can autonomously navigate to the desired site with minimal collision, enabled by real-to-sim multimodal bladder reconstruction, real-time registration, and sim-to-real techniques. AI algorithms will optimize motion planning in confined bladder environments and enhance intraoperative cryogen spraying through tumor tracking, vision dehazing, and visual servoing control. By developing ultrathin intelligent flexible robots, our proposed system aims to enable precise, safe, and efficient cryotherapy. The project’s outcomes in flexible telerobotics, intelligent robot control, and pre-clinical studies are expected to guide the future development of these robots for delicate deep-site operations (e.g., brain, bronchi, uterus). This will create opportunities to transfer extensively researched flexible robots to advanced biomedical applications, leading to significant societal impacts. The beneficiaries of this project are numerous. The novelty of the addressed problems can lead to new case studies in robot modeling and control, fostering original contributions beyond flexible and medical robotics. In the long term, NMIBC patients will benefit from a novel noninvasive treatment via the CryoFR system, improving outcomes and quality of life. Urologist surgeons will gain from AI-assisted navigation and robot control, reducing workload and enhancing efficiency. This robot has the potential to transform early-stage bladder cancer care. 膀胱癌為全球最常見之惡性腫瘤之一。本港膀胱癌發病率尤以年齡介乎五十五至七十歲之男性為高，男女比例約為三比一。雖早期膀胱癌之預後一般良好，惟其復發率偏高，對長期病患管理構成重大挑戰，顯示現行治療方案尚未能全面應對相關臨床需要。非肌肉入侵性膀胱癌（NMIBC）佔所有膀胱癌病例約七至八成，若能於早期階段採取有效介入措施，將有助防止病情惡化為具肌肉入侵性之癌症，進一步侵蝕深層組織並擴散至身體其他部位。因此，亟需發展創新治療技術，以提升整體治療成效及病患生活質素。 冷凍治療為一項新興技術，透過將液態氮等冷凍介質直接輸送至局部病灶位置，進行多次冷凍與解凍循環，以達致殺死癌細胞之療效。相較於雙極電燒或激光消融技術，冷凍治療可有效縮短住院時間，並減少組織腫脹及出血情況。該技術已廣泛應用於食道癌及前列腺癌之治療，近期研究亦支持其作為NMIBC之輔助療法。惟現時大部分冷凍治療仍須依賴剛性冷凍探頭或冷凍針進行，相關裝置易對健康組織（如尿道）造成損傷。此外，該等裝置靈活度有限，未能全面覆蓋整個膀胱內壁，尤其於膀胱頂部及下側壁之位置，限制其臨床應用範圍。再者，現有冷凍治療系統多屬初步階段，尚欠缺對末端執行器及冷凍劑量之自動化及智能化控制。鑑於上述挑戰，本研究擬開發一款專為經尿道進行 NMIBC 冷凍治療而設的超細智能柔性膀胱鏡機器人，以應對上述未被滿足之臨床需求。由於男性泌尿系統結構較女性複雜，膀胱鏡操作難度較高，故本研究將聚焦於男性患者群體。 爰此，本研究課題旨在研發一款具備高度靈活性及精準導航能力之超細智能柔性膀胱鏡機器人，能夠經尿道長距離深入膀胱內部，以輔助執行微創冷凍治療程序。預期研究成果將從以下三個層面提供科學及技術指引：（一）新型柔性機器人學理論及技術；（二）智能機器人控制系統研發；以及（三）臨床前研究驗證。此項技術之發展，將有助推動新一代柔性機器人於精細深部操作領域（如腦部、支氣管及子宮等）的應用，促進相關醫療技術之創新與普及。本研究所針對之技術挑戰，亦普遍存在於其他新興療法領域（如電療、熱療及光療）。因此，本課題旨在促進已具成熟基礎之柔性機器人技術向前沿生物醫學應用之轉化，藉此拓展其臨床應用範疇，並提升整體社會效益與影響力。

14200625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200625.value: 基於被動N路徑濾波器的真帶通Delta-Sigma調變器

14200625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200625.value: Bandpass Delta-Sigma modulators (BP DSMs) are the best choice for digitizing narrow-band radio frequency (RF) signals with a high dynamic range, making them the preferred analog-to-digital converter (ADC) solution for direct RF digitization in Internet-of-things (IoT) devices. However, traditional BP DSMs suffer from poor energy efficiency, large chip size, and limited flexibility in passband frequency. There is a growing demand for new solutions to improve energy efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance the flexibility of BP DSMs. We have recently developed BP DSMs based on passive N-path filters (NPFs), which offer superior energy efficiency and passband frequency flexibility compared to traditional designs. These innovative BP DSMs have also influenced the development of other ADCs utilizing the NPF concept. However, these energy-efficient BP ADCs have been demonstrated only for intermediate frequency (IF) inputs. Furthermore, they exhibit a redundant passband at DC, thus not being true BP ADCs. In this project, we aim to advance the art of BP DSMs by introducing a true BP DSM architecture based on suitable NPF candidates. These include a proposed split-capacitor stacking NTF, a 1:3 impedance-transforming NPF, and a capacitor-reused (CS) NPF. The new architecture will fundamentally improve energy efficiency by eliminating the redundant passband at DC and will be capable of accepting RF inputs by leveraging a time-interleaving scheme and a special amplification strategy. Meanwhile, the new architecture will retain the compact size and passband frequency flexibility of existing NPF-based BP DSMs. Our approach involves establishing a theoretical framework for analyzing and designing these true BP DSMs. We will then implement three IF-input true BP DSM prototypes in a low-cost CMOS process, each utilizing one of the aforementioned NPF candidates. The primary objectives of these prototypes are to showcase the feasibility and benefits of the proposed architecture and to compare the performance of the true BP DSMs built with these different NPF candidates. Next, we will develop an RF-input true BP DSM based on the CS NPF in a more advanced CMOS technology. This BP DSM will be tailored for typical IoT receiver applications in terms of input frequency range and bandwidth. Finally, we will design an IoT receiver frontend comprising a broadband RF low-noise amplifier and a true BP DSM. Overall, this project will showcase a new class of BP DSMs that offer exceptional energy efficiency and passband frequency range. 帶通Delta-Sigma調變器（BPDSM）在實現高動態範圍窄帶射頻（RF）信號數位化方面是最佳選擇，是物聯網（IoT）設備中直接RF數位化的首選模擬-數位轉換器（ADC）方案。然而，傳統BPDSM存在能源效率低下、芯片尺寸過大及通帶頻率調適性受限等缺陷。業界亟需能提升能效、降低成本並增強調適性的新型BPDSM解決方案。 我們近期開發出基於被動N路徑濾波器（NPF）的BPDSM，相較傳統設計展現出卓越的能源效率與通帶頻率調適能力。這些創新BPDSM更推動了採用NPF概念的其他ADC技術發展。但現有高效能BP ADC僅能處理中頻（IF）輸入信號，且存在直流冗餘通帶，故非真正的帶通ADC。 本項目旨在通過引入基於新型NPF架構的真帶通DSM技術，推動BPDSM領域發展。這些NPF架構包括：分離式電容堆疊NTF、1:3阻抗轉換NPF及電容複用（CS）NPF。新架構藉由消除直流冗餘通帶從根本上提升能效，並運用時間交錯技術與特殊放大策略實現RF信號接收能力，同時保持現有NPF基BPDSM的緊湊尺寸與通帶頻率靈活性。 研究內容包含：首先建立真帶通DSM的理論分析與設計框架，隨後採用低成本CMOS製程實現三款中頻輸入原型芯片（分別搭載上述NPF技術），驗證架構可行性並比較不同NPF方案性能；接著基於先進CMOS製程開發CS-NPF型RF輸入真帶通DSM，其輸入頻率範圍與帶寬將針對典型物聯網接收器應用優化；最終設計整合寬頻RF低噪聲放大器與真帶通DSM的物聯網接收器前端。 本項目將開創兼具超高能效與靈活通帶頻率的新型BPDSM技術體系。

14201325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201325.value: 逆重力運動微機器人集群在含生物流體微小迂曲三維腔體中進行主動輸送的研究

14201325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201325.value: Research on robot swarms and collectives across various scales is widely regarded as one of the grand challenges in robotics for the forthcoming decade. This proposed project aims to investigate the anti-gravity motion of magnetic microrobot swarms (microswarms) for active delivery in complex tiny-and-tortuous 3D lumens. Collective behaviors observed in living systems, which arise from the self-organization of individual elements, are ubiquitous in nature. In robotics, robot swarms/collectives formed by simple units are expected to have the advantage of performing complex tasks beyond the ability of individual robot agents. Unlike the macroscopic-robotic agents with on-board power supply, sensors, and actuators, the design and development of reconfigurable robot swarms/collectives at small scales requires different strategies. Among different actuation methods of microswarms, magnetic actuation is promising for in vivo applications because low-strength magnetic fields are considered harmless to biological cells and tissues, and remote actuation of microswarms, including generation, transformation, and locomotion, can be realized in a controllable manner. To date, although extensive research has been conducted on various biomedical applications of magnetic microswarms, substantial challenges persist in endoluminal and endovascular applications, especially in tiny and tortuous 3D-branched lumens. Most microswarms lack the ability to overcome gravity to achieve vertical displacement or cannot be precisely controlled within complex 3D channels. Given that the lumens in the human body inherently possess 3D complex structures, this limitation significantly restricts the in vivo applications of microswarms. Therefore, it is essential to investigate the anti-gravity motion of microswarms to enable precise navigation in 3D lumens. In this project, the overall objective is to investigate the anti-gravity motion of magnetic microswarms from the following aspects: (i) Enhance the motion capability of microswarms through input magnetic field optimization, and investigate the effects of biological environments and magnetic field parameters on the anti-gravity motion of microswarms; (ii) Propose and optimize strategies for real-time imaging-based anti-gravity motion of microswarms in complex 3D-branched channels; (iii) Utilize the developed strategies to improve the efficiency and accuracy of active delivery in tiny-and-tortuous complex 3D lumens. We envision this work as a pioneering step in the development of magnetic microswarms, specifically by endowing microswarms with the capability for anti-gravity motion to achieve precise and controllable active delivery in the ubiquitously present 3D lumens in vivo. The advanced technology and outcomes generated from this project will significantly contribute to Hong Kong, particularly in the emerging technology for medical microrobotics and minimally invasive medicine. 在多個尺度上研究機器人群體與集體行為，被廣泛認為是未來十年機器人領域的重大挑戰之一。本研究計劃旨在探討磁性微型機器人群體（微集群）在複雜、微小且曲折的三維腔道中實現主動輸送的逆重力（抵抗重力）運動機制。 本研究的總體目標是從以下幾個方面研究磁性微集群的逆重力運動能力：（i）透過優化輸入磁場提升微集群的運動能力，並研究生物環境與磁場參數對其逆重力運動的影響；（ii）提出並優化基於實時成像的微集群在複雜三維分支通道中進行逆重力運動的策略；（iii）利用所發展的策略提升微集群在微小且曲折的複雜三維腔道中主動輸送的效率與精度。 我們預期本研究將成為磁性微集群發展的先導工作，賦予其逆重力運動能力，以實現體內廣泛存在的三維腔道中精確可控主動傳遞。本研究所產生的先進技術與成果將為香港在醫療微型機器人與微創醫學等新興科技領域做出重要貢獻。

14201425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201425.value: 智齡感知：老年人家庭情感監測與運動反饋的知識增強感知系統

14201425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201425.value: As the population ages, studies have shown that most seniors prefer to live in homes rather than in institutions or elderly care facilities, a concept known as “Aging in place”. Two essential applications that support and facilitate aging in place are familial emotional relationship between older adults and their family members, and exercise recognition for providing feedback on home-based physical exercise. Effective implementation of these applications requires recognizing human activities and motions within the appropriate context. However, current approaches often rely on sensing devices that lack relevant contextual knowledge or reference general feedback from the literature. This project proposes to develop a system called AgeSense, which utilizes sensing devices for emotional monitoring within families and provides personalized feedback on exercise. AgeSense integrates multi-modal sensor data with expert knowledge to enhance the aging-in-place support and experience for older adults. The research tasks proposed are as follows. (1) Development of a sensing-driven knowledge base framework that integrates sensor data, expert knowledge, and personal records to build multi-source knowledge bases, enhancing the relevance and depth of retrieved information. The framework assesses the unique characteristics of family health applications and determines the knowledge needed for each sensing task. Using vectorization and synchronization methods, it creates an application-specific, personalized knowledge base to support applications like familial emotion monitoring and exercise feedback. (2) Development of a knowledgeenhanced, context-aware familial emotion monitoring system that uses two-dimensional dyadic digital biomarkers to classify expressed emotion from older adults’ interactions with their family members. Our approach uses LLMs with a knowledge base to identify expressed emotion digital biomarkers in a search space and continuously feed classification results back to the LLM to improve the accuracy and granularity of the biomarkers, providing deeper insights into family emotional dynamics. (3) Develop a muscle-aware exercise recognition approach that recognizes actions, motion patterns, and muscle contractions from videos by extracting human skeletal point sequences to train graph networks with a knowledge base and self-supervised learning. Our approach then queries LLMs using recognition results to generate personalized feedback, enhancing exercise outcome. (4) System evaluation through deployment in 60 homes of older adults, including both healthy individuals and patients with aging-related conditions, and large public datasets from on-going projects. 隨著人口老齡化的加劇，研究表明，大多數老年人更傾向於居家生活，而非入住養老機構或護理設施，這壹理念被稱為“居家養老”。支持居家養老的關鍵應用包括老年人與家庭成員之間的情感聯結監測，以及針對居家運動的反饋提供。要有效實現這些應用，需要在適當的情境下識別人體活動和動作。然而，現有方法通常依賴缺乏情境知識的感知設備或基於文獻中的通用反饋，難以滿足個性化需求。本項目提出開發名為智齡感知的系統，利用感知設備進行家庭情感監測，並提供個性化的運動反饋。智齡感知通過整合多模態傳感器數據與專家知識，提升對老年人居家養老的支持與體驗。研究主要包括以下任務：（1）開發基於感知驅動的知識庫框架，將傳感器數據、專家知識和個人記錄整合為多源知識庫，提升信息檢索的相關性和深度。框架將評估家庭健康應用的獨特需求，確定每個感知任務所需的知識類型，並通過矢量化和同步方法構建應用特定的個性化知識庫，以支持家庭情感監測和運動反饋等應用。（2）開發知識增強的情境感知家庭情感監測系統，利用二維交互型數字生物標誌物，對老年人與家人互動中表達的情感進行分類。該方法結合大語言模型與知識庫，在搜索空間中識別情感生物標記，並持續將分類結果反饋至大語言模型，以提高標誌物的準確性和細粒度，從而深入解析家庭情感動態。（3）開發肌肉感知的運動識別方法，通過從視頻中提取人體骨骼點序列，識別動作、運動模式和肌肉收縮情況，並利用圖網絡、知識庫和自監督學習進行訓練。然後基於識別結果查詢大語言模型，生成個性化運動反饋，提升運動效果。（4）通過在60個老年人家庭中部署系統，包括健康人及患有與衰老相關疾病的患者，並結合正在進行項目中的大型公共數據集對系統進行評估。本項目將通過智齡感知系統，利用多模態感知技術與知識增強方法，為老年人提供更加智能化、個性化的居家養老支持，提升其生活質量與養老體驗。

14201725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201725.value: 基於可變形螺旋槳輔助附肢、接觸隱式軌跡優化與多模態路徑規劃的地面機器人敏捷性增強研究

14201725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14201725.value: Prof Au, Kwok Wai Samuel Prof Cho, Kyu-Jin Prof Hutter, Marco

14201725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201725.value: Current terrestrial robots, despite their abilities to run, jump, climb, and perform parkour, still do not match the agility of animals. Animals often use their appendages (e.g., tails, limbs) to achieve remarkable maneuverability with robustness to significant disturbances and show terrestrial adaptability to complex environments. Although recent research has integrated the advantages of appendages into terrestrial robotic systems, most efforts have focused primarily on improving maneuverability using tail-like appendages. These appendages can change body orientation effectively but fundamentally limit the robot's ability to achieve rapid, large, and robust body angle change. This is because their output forces rely on internal movements (e.g., tail swinging) and are often constrained by limited appendage workspace. Moreover, pursuing their multifunctionality for enabling the robot’s multi-modality to adapt to environments further complicates these appendages’ design and control. Overall, most existing appendage designs still lack high output force and multi-functionality. There is no viable, compact solution that allows robots to adjust body orientation rapidly and robustly while adapting to complex environments via appendage-induced multi-modalities. Our goal is to develop innovative solutions to enable highly agile and adaptive robot locomotion based on novel appendages. Specifically, a terrestrial robotic platform with morphable propeller-assisted appendages will be developed and serve as a testbed. The project consists of three innovative components: (1) A morphable, propeller-assisted, and multi-functional mechanism. It comprises a 2-DoF morphable linkage and shrouded propellers, providing high output force due to power-dense propellers and thrust redirection by morphable linkages. The mechanisms can enable multiple modes, such as hopping, spinning, flipping, crouching, walking, rolling, and loco-manipulating, allowing the robots to adapt to complex environments. (2) A contact-implicit trajectory optimization framework based on hybrid multiple-shooting iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR). We formulate the agile locomotion generation as a bi-level contact-implicit optimization problem. To solve this problem with various constraints, a hybrid multiple-shooting iLQR is proposed with strict enforcement of dynamic feasibility with constraints and tolerance of infeasible initial conditions. (3) A multi-modal path planning with learned motion costs. We develop a learned-motion-cost-based probabilistic roadmap that involves terrain topographies and then a sample-based algorithm is used for generating mode-aware waypoints. The proposed system will be the first dynamic terrestrial robotic platform with unique morphable propeller-assisted appendages for enhanced maneuverability and adaptability. The success of this project will facilitate more advanced robotic designs and control solutions, enabling terrestrial movements with agility comparable to biological counterparts in real-world environments. 當前的地面機器人雖然已具備奔跑、跳躍、攀爬及翻越障礙等能力，但在敏捷性方面仍無法與動物匹敵。動物常利用其附肢（如尾巴、四肢）展現出卓越的機動性，能夠在遭遇強烈擾動時保持穩定，並展現出對複雜地形的高度適應能力。儘管近期已有研究將附肢的優勢引入地面機器人系統，但大多數工作主要集中於使用類尾巴附肢來提升機動性。這類附肢雖然能有效改變機體姿態，但在實現快速、大幅度且穩健的姿態變化方面存在根本性限制，因為其輸出力主要來自於內部運動（例如尾巴擺動），且常受到附肢可動範圍的限制。此外，為了使機器人具備多模態能力以適應多變環境，對附肢多功能性的追求也進一步增加了其設計與控制的複雜性。總體而言，目前大多數附肢設計仍缺乏高輸出力與多功能整合的能力，尚未有一套可行且緊湊的解決方案，能夠讓機器人透過附肢驅動的多模態行動，在面對複雜環境時快速且穩健地調整身體姿態。 本研究旨在開發創新解決方案，透過新型附肢設計實現高敏捷性與高適應性的地面機器人運動能力。我們將開發一個搭載可變形螺旋槳輔助附肢的地面機器人平台，作為實驗測試平台。此項目包含三個創新核心：1）可變形螺旋槳輔助多功能機構：該機構由具備兩自由度的可變形連桿與罩式螺旋槳組成。藉由高功率密度的螺旋槳產生大輸出推力，並透過可變形連桿改變推力方向，實現包括跳躍、自旋、翻轉、蹲伏、步行、滾動與運動操控等多種模式，使機器人能適應複雜地形環境。2）基於混合多重射擊 iLQR 的接觸隱式軌跡優化框架：我們將敏捷運動的生成建模為一個雙層的接觸隱式優化問題。為了解決其中的多種約束條件，我們提出了一種混合多段的 iLQR 方法，該方法在保證動態可行性的同時，對不可行初始條件具備容錯能力，能夠穩健地生成高動態的運動軌跡。3）基於學習運動代價的多模態路徑規劃：我們將開發一種融合地形拓撲資訊與學習運動代價的機率路徑圖，並採用基於樣本的方法生成具模式感知的航點，進行多模態動作規劃。 本研究所提出的系統將是首個採用可變形螺旋槳輔助附肢的高動態地面機器人平台，具備獨特的機動性與適應能力。該項目的成功將促進更先進的機器人設計與控制技術的發展，使地面機器人能在真實環境中展現出媲美生物體的敏捷移動能力。

14202125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202125.value: 基於音頻增強的開放世界視頻異常感知

14202125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202125.value: As urban environments grow increasingly complex, perceiving anomalies—such as traffic violations, thefts, and fires—has become crucial for public safety. Traditional surveillance systems, which primarily rely on video data, often struggle to perceive subtle or rare anomalies, especially in dynamic and crowded settings like roadways, shopping centers, and industrial sites. These systems frequently overlook the power of audio, which can provide vital contextual cues for identifying potential threats. This gap in current technology results in blind spots, leading to delayed or inadequate responses. To address this, a multimodal approach integrating video, audio, and text is essential for enhancing anomaly perception in real-world scenarios. We present an innovative audio-enhanced multimodal anomaly perception system designed for open-world environments. This system integrates video, audio, and textual data to enhance perception accuracy and robustness, establishing new standards for real-time event monitoring. To achieve this, we will develop a large annotated dataset combining synthetic and real-world video samples, enriched with audio cues and detailed descriptions. Additionally, we will create an audio-enhanced multimodal large language model capable of perceiving complex events more effectively by utilizing interleaved learning strategies that fuse web-scale data from audio, visual, and text sources. The system will also incorporate a device-cloud collaborative learning framework, enabling lightweight, personalized models to function on edge devices in real-time, adapting to diverse environments such as traffic systems, factories, and laboratories. By advancing this cutting-edge framework, we aim to revolutionize anomaly perception across urban environments, enabling faster and more accurate identification of potential hazards and threats. This work has the potential to significantly enhance public safety, optimize industrial monitoring, and strengthen smart city infrastructure. Through this innovative system, cities and industries will be better equipped to swiftly perceive and respond to critical events, reducing risks and safeguarding communities. 隨著城市環境日益復雜，能夠及時感知交通違法、盜竊、火災等異常情況，對保障公共安全變得愈發重要。傳統的監控系統主要依賴視頻數據，在察覺細微或罕見異常方面往往存在不足，尤其是在道路、購物中心、工業場所等動態且人群密集的環境中更為明顯。此外，它們常常忽視音頻所蘊含的價值, 音頻能夠提供識別潛在威脅所需的重要上下文線索。正是由於這一技術缺口，監控系統存在感知盲區，從而造成響應延遲或不夠及時有效。為解決這一問題，亟需采用融合視頻、音頻與文本的多模態方法，以提升在真實場景中的異常感知能力。 為此，我們提出了一種面向開放世界環境的創新型音頻增強多模態異常感知系統。該系統融合視頻、音頻和文本信息，以提高感知的準確性與魯棒性，並為實時事件監測樹立新標準。為了實現這一目標，我們將構建一個大型標註數據集，結合合成與真實世界的視頻樣本，並輔以音頻線索和詳細描述。同時，我們將研發一個音頻增強的多模態大型語言模型，采用交錯學習策略，將來自音頻、視覺與文本的海量網絡數據進行深度融合，從而更有效地感知複雜事件。在體系架構上，系統還將引入端-雲協同學習框架，使輕量化、個性化模型能夠在邊緣設備上實時運行，並靈活適應交通系統、工廠、實驗室等多種環境。 通過推動這一前沿框架，我們旨在革新城市環境的異常感知方式，實現對潛在危險與威脅的更快速、更精確識別。這項工作有望顯著提升公共安全，優化工業監測，並強化智慧城市基礎設施建設。借助這一創新系統，城市與各行業將更有能力迅速感知並應對關鍵事件，從而降低風險，守護社區安全。

14202225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202225.value: 高解析度三維生化結構磁共振成像技術：整合自動化後處理的膝關節結構與成分同步成像

14202225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14202225.value: Prof Griffith, James Francis Dr Ho, Kevin Ki-wai Prof Ong, Michael Tim-Yun Dr Xiao, Fan

14202225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202225.value: Aim To develop techniques for a comprehensive knee exam based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with automatic postprocessing, providing automated routine clinical anatomy and compositional assessment simultaneously while reducing the knee exam time, while reducing the knee exam time and potentially improving throughput and the cost of knee MRI exams. Background Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a major health concern in ageing populations in Hong Kong and worldwide. While 2D Fast Spin Echo (FSE) MRI scans are standard for diagnosis, 3D FSE imaging offers superior advantages. It provides isotropic resolution, allowing single-scan reformatting to any plane, and enables accurate quantitative analysis of OA biomarkers. T1ρ compositional imaging detects early biochemical changes in cartilage with higher sensitivity than conventional methods. With these two components, the integrated 3D FSE-based T1ρ imaging offers detailed anatomical and biochemical information for enhanced OA detection. However, clinical implementation faces challenges due to lengthy scan times and a lack of efficient post-processing methods, highlighting a critical area for further research and development. Project Description We have conducted extensive research on 3D FSE and T1ρ MRI. This project aims to develop 3D isotropic high-resolution bio-anatomical knee MRI technologies that integrate 3D FSE and T1ρ. Our proposed methods involve FSE acquisition with a 0.5mm 3D isotropic resolution, while simultaneously providing a 3D T1ρ map of knee cartilage. Building upon our successful preliminary work, we will utilise deep learning to accelerate data acquisition, enhance image quality, and calculate T1ρ maps from standard clinical scans. We will develop automatic post-processing with foundation models tailored to our proposed bio-anatomical knee MRI, providing a flexible and reliable quantitative measurement of both the anatomy and compositional features of the knee. We will recruit 60 patients with knee OA and 60 healthy controls to evaluate and validate the proposed approach. Significance of Project This project will provide technologies for a comprehensive knee MRI exam covering both acquisition and postprocessing. The exam encompasses the current clinical routine exams and provides important compositional information for early OA assessment. The output of this project is expected to be practical for routine clinical use and to improve clinical management of knee diseases.

14202425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202425.value: 輸出反饋積分強化學習控制的一般架構及其應用

14202425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202425.value: Reinforcement learning (RL) or adaptive/approximate dynamic programming (ADP) is an effective data-driven approach to approximately solving various optimization problems and optimal control problems. The RL method was originally developed to solve the adaptive optimal control problems of discrete-time systems such as Markov decision problem with unknown transition probabilities and was also called Q-learning. Since 2010, its integral form called integral reinforcement learning (IRL) was further developed to deal with various approximate optimal control problems for unknown continuous-time systems. Nevertheless, the potential of IRL has not yet been fully unlocked due to some specific challenges. First, the control law for IRL was originally in the state-feedback form. Since the state vector of a real system may not be physically measurable, developing output-feedback IRL is not only desirable but also imperative. Recently, the problem of developing the output-feedback IRL has been an active research topic. A promising method involves the construction of a model-free observer. Nevertheless, this method requires some unknown matrix to be of full row rank and needs to solve a sequence of high dimensional linear algebraic equations. These limitations significantly hinder the applicability of this approach. Second, the output-feedback IRL has been proved to be quite effective in solving the optimal stabilization problem, but its capability in dealing with tracking and disturbance rejection problem is limited and relies on some restrictive conditions. Third, nowadays, distributed control of networked multiagent systems has been a focus in control society, but a distributed version of the output-feedback IRL method is yet to be established. For these reasons, the first objective of this project is to remove the rank condition and significantly reduce the dimension of the sequence of linear algebraic equations, thus leading to a full-blown framework for efficiently designing output-feedback IRL control law for unknown systems. Second, we will combine the IRL with the internal model principle to deal with the asymptotic tracking and disturbance rejection problem of unknown systems for a large class of reference inputs and disturbance signals. Finally, we will establish a distributed version of output-feedback IRL for dealing with various cooperative control problems of unknown multi-agent systems culminating in offering the model-free output feedback solution to the adaptive optimal cooperative output regulation problem of unknown linear continuous-time multi-agent systems. Several practical applications of this framework will also be demonstrated. 強化學習 (RL) 或自適應/近似動態規劃 (ADP) 是一種有效的資料驅動方法，用於近似解決各種最佳化問題和最佳控制問題。 RL 方法最初是為了解決離散時間系統的自適應最適控制問題（例如轉移機率未知的馬可夫決策問題）而開發的，也稱為 Q 學習。自 2010 年以來，其積分形式（稱為積分強化學習 (IRL)）已進一步發展，用於處理各種未知連續時間系統的近似最佳控制問題。然而，由於一些特定的挑戰，IRL 的潛力尚未充分釋放。首先，IRL 的控制律最初是狀態反饋形式。由於實際系統的狀態向量可能無法在物理上測量，因此開發輸出反饋 IRL 不僅可取，而且勢在必行。近年來，開發輸出反饋 IRL 一直是個活躍的研究主題。一種有前景的方法是建構一個無模型觀測器。然而，此方法要求某個未知矩陣具有滿行秩，並且需要求解一系列高維線性代數方程式。這些限制嚴重阻礙了該方法的適用性。其次，輸出回饋IRL已被證明在解決最優鎮定問題上非常有效，但其處理追蹤和擾動抑制問題的能力有限並且依賴於一些限制條件。第三，目前，網路化多智能體系統的分布式控制已成為控制界的焦點，但分布式版本的輸出反饋IRL方法尚未建立。為此，本計劃的首要目標是消除秩條件並顯著降低線性代數方程式序列的維數，從而得到一個高能的框架，用於高效地設計未知系統的輸出反饋IRL控制律。其次，我們將IRL與內模原理結合，處理一大類參考輸入和擾動訊號的未知系統的漸近追蹤和擾動抑制問題。最後，我們將建立一個分布式的輸出反饋內部強化學習 (IRL) 模型，用於處理未知多智能體系統的各種協作控制問題，最終為未知線性連續時間多智能體系統的自適應最優協作輸出調節問題提供無模型輸出反饋解決方案。此外，我們還將展示該框架的幾個實際應用。

14202825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202825.value: 探索動態散斑與近紅外二區照明在相干門控衍射層析厚結構成像技術中的應用

14202825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14202825.value: Dr Brelen, Marten Prof Chen, Shih-chi

14202825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202825.value: Three-dimensional (3D) micro- and nano-manufacturing has become crucial for developing multifunctional devices with high-level integrations, but it poses challenges to metrology that relates to device yield and cost. For instance, in two-photon lithography, traditional metrology tools are unsuitable for quality control due to potential invasiveness and limited imaging depth and throughput. Optical diffraction tomography (ODT), as an emerging wide-field noninvasive imaging technique, is promising for 3D metrology by providing diffraction-limited resolution. However, most current ODT systems fall short of meeting future metrology demands on thick structures, due to limited imaging depth and poor depth sectioning capabilities when using transmission-mode angle-scanning geometry that also incurs more absorption and scatterings. Leveraging the coherence-gating effect in a reflection-mode ODT system, PI Zhou has recently extended the imaging depth (>500 µm) far beyond the depth of field. Further improving the imaging depth beyond 1 mm while maintaining high spatial resolution and high depth selectivity is challenged by (i) severe multiple scatterings and absorptions at the visible band; (ii) specimen-induced aberrations in thick structures; and (iii) lack of a comprehensive physical model and corresponding 3D reconstruction algorithm. To address these challenges, we propose to develop a novel vortex-speckle illuminated reflection-mode diffraction tomography (vSRDT) technique. For achieving high spatial resolution (lateral/axial ~ 200/400 nm) with sub-micron depth selectivity, we will explore dynamic vortex speckles that offer ring illumination with phase modulations in a reflection-mode system (Task 1). Specifically, we will investigate how illumination parameters can maximize the 3D spatial frequency coverage and reduce the point spread function. A 405 nm vSRDT system, compatible with second near-infrared (NIR-II) illuminations, will be first designed and constructed to test the resolution enhancement. To simultaneously achieve high imaging depth (>1 mm), an NIR-II source will be integrated into the system for mitigating multi-scattering and absorption (Task 2). A 3D reconstruction algorithm that addresses specimen-induced aberrations will be developed by exploring sample a priori information. Using vSRDT, we will demonstrate two important applications (Task 3): (A) 3D metrology for two-photon lithography; and (B) label-free imaging of thick tissues. Zhou has long focused on advancing ODT as published in Nat. Photon., Adv. Photon., Light: Sci. & Appl., etc. as a leading author and getting recognized in this field through receiving Croucher Innovation Awards, NSFC Excellent Young Scientists Fund, etc. We envision vSRDT may benefit not only advanced manufacturing but also biomedical studies, thus bringing enormous impact to both scientific communities and industries. 三維微納製造是開發高度集成多功能器件的關鍵技術，但其發展對檢測技術提出了重大挑戰，直接關係到器件良率和生產成本。以雙光子光刻為例，傳統檢測工具面臨著潛在的侵入性、成像深度有限和通量不足等問題，因此難以滿足器件質量控制的嚴格要求。光學衍射層析成像技術（Optical Diffraction Tomography：ODT）作為一種新興的無侵入性寬場成像技術，能達到衍射極限分辨率，因此有望成為微納结构三維測量的理想解決方案。然而，目前大多數ODT系統採用透射式角度掃描設計，存在以下問題，包括成像深度不足、分辨率有限、層析能力欠佳，以及樣品對信號光的強烈吸收與散射效應。項目負責人團隊近期利用反射式ODT系統中的相干門控效應，將成像深度擴展至500 µm以上。進一步提升成像深度，並保持高分辨率與高層析能力，仍需面臨以下三大挑戰：（1）激光散斑以及多重散射效應導致的圖像對比度降低；（2）厚樣品引入的像差；（3）缺乏準確描述厚結構中光-物質相互作用的完整物理模型及相應三維重建算法。 針對以上挑戰，本研究擬開發一種新型基於渦旋散斑照明的反射式衍射層析成像技術（vortex-Speckle illuminated Reflection-mode Diffraction Tomography：vSRDT）。為實現亞微米層析精度與高空間分辨率（橫向/軸向約200/400 nm），我們將探索基於環形動態渦旋散斑照明的反射式ODT技術（任務1）；重點研究照明光參數對三維空間頻率覆蓋範圍最大化與點擴散函數優化的作用機制；搭建可見光波段vSRDT系統（兼容 NIR-II波段照明），以驗證分辨率提升效果。為實現毫米級成像深度（任務2），系統將集成NIR-II波段照明光源以抑制多重散射效應；通過融合樣品先驗信息開發三維重建算法以校正樣品引入像差。基於vSRDT技術，我們將開展兩項重要應用驗證（任務3）：（A）雙光子光刻三維檢測；（B）厚生物組織無標記成像。項目負責人長期致力於ODT技術研究，相關主導工作已發表於Nat. Photon., Adv. Photon., Light: Sci. & Appl.等領域頂級期刊，並獲得裘槎前瞻科研大獎、國自然優青等榮譽。我們預期vSRDT技術不僅將推動先進製造領域發展，還可促進生物醫學研究，對科學與工業領域產生深遠影響。

14202925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202925.value: 透過線上量子網路基準測試識別量子網路中的高保真路徑

14202925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202925.value: Many scientists/researchers believe the next wave of technological revolution will be in quantum computing. Many countries are now investing heavily on this line of research. One major hurdle in building quantum computers (QCs) to outperform a classical computer is in scaling up the QCs since more quantum qubits means more susceptibility to quantum/environmental interference. One approach to address such problem is to connect many small/medium scale QCs in a quantum network to do parallel/distributed quantum computations. Hence, there has been a surge of attention on how to design quantum networks or even a quantum Internet[20,22,36,37]. Distributed quantum computation over a network is only possible when one can reliably transmit quantum information across the network. However, such reliable quantum information transfer is challenging since each quantum channel (or path) has different quality (or fidelity) due to various quantum noises. If one transmits quantum information across a low fidelity path, corruption may occur and this will significantly impair the distributed quantum computation. Therefore, identifying the best path (i.e., path with the highest fidelity) between two entangled nodes is extremely important in enabling distributed quantum computation. In this proposal, we consider how one can "learn on-the-fly" and adapt to the quantum/environmental noise so to identify the best path(s) in a quantum network using the "online learning framework". We first explore the path-level feedback model, which the current generation of quantum switches/repeaters support via the end-to-end quantum statistical tests (aka "network benchmarking" in the quantum literature). For the next generation quantum switch/repeater, there will be additional capability to have the "link-layer" feedback and this will provide finer granularity of statistical testing. Our goals are to design both the best-path identification protocols for the current and next generation of quantum networks using the online learning paradigm so that distributed quantum applications can be reliably and efficiently carried out. We will analyze and quantify the quantum resource complexity of our online best-path identification protocols and to show that they can provide high fidelity guarantee with high probability. In this project, we will implement a quantum network simulator using NetSquid[7] so to evaluate the performance of our protocols and their improvement over prominent quantum applications such as quantum key distribution (QKD), i.e., BB84, E92, COW or the latest T12 QKD protocols. Finally, to demonstrate the impact of our research, we will collaborate with the Tencent Quantum Research Lab in enhancing distributed quantum applications over their quantum testbeds. 許多科學家/研究人員認為，下一波技術革命將在量子運算領域展開。許多國家目前正大力投資這項研究方向。建造性能超越傳統電腦的量子電腦（QC）的一個主要障礙是量子電腦的規模化，因為更多的量子位元意味著更容易受到量子/環境幹擾。解決這個問題的一種方法是將許多中小型量子電腦連接到量子網路中，進行平行/分散式量子計算。因此，如何設計量子網路甚至量子網路引起了人們的廣泛關注。 只有能夠可靠地在網路上傳輸量子訊息，才能實現基於網路的分散式量子運算。然而，這種可靠的量子資訊傳輸極具挑戰性，因為各種量子雜訊會導致每個量子通道（或路徑）的品質（或保真度）不同。如果透過低保真度路徑傳輸量子訊息，可能會發生損壞，這將嚴重損害分散式量子計算。因此，在兩個糾纏節點之間確定最佳路徑（即保真度最高的路徑）對於實現分散式量子計算至關重要。 在本提案中，我們探討如何利用「線上學習框架」進行「動態學習」並適應量子/環境噪聲，從而識別量子網路中的最佳路徑。我們首先探索路徑級回饋模型，當前一代量子交換器/中繼器透過端對端量子統計測試（在量子文獻中也稱為「網路基準測試」）支援該模型。下一代量子交換器/中繼器將具備額外的「鏈路層」回饋能力，這將提供更細粒度的統計測試。我們的目標是使用線上學習範式為當前和下一代量子網路設計最佳路徑識別協議，以便可靠且有效率地執行分散式量子應用。我們將分析和量化我們的線上最佳路徑識別協議的量子資源複雜度，並證明它們能夠以高機率提供高保真度保證。

14203225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203225.value: 開發基於液晶彈性體和熱塑性聚氨酯納米纖維的污染水平響應空氣過濾器以提高可持續性

14203225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203225.value: Indoor exposure to airborne particles is associated with various adverse health effects, such as respiratory infection, heart disease, and lung cancer. Traditional high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters can effectively remove particles, but such filters are structurally invariant and continuously operate at a high filtration efficiency, accompanied by a high pressure drop. When air quality is good, maintaining a high particle filtration efficiency is not economical, as the improvement in air quality is limited while energy consumption remains high due to the high pressure drop. Therefore, it is worthwhile to develop advanced air filters that can automatically adjust to varying air pollution levels to reduce energy consumption, extend service life, and improve sustainability. Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are shape-morphing materials that can be used as actuators with thermal stimuli. Meanwhile, thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanofibers fabricated by electrospinning can form elastic filter media. Therefore, we hypothesize that pollution-level-responsive air filters can be developed based on a filter skeleton actuator made from LCEs and elastic filter media made from TPU nanofibers. When the particle concentration is high, the filters will contract to achieve high particle filtration efficiency and thus protect the health of occupants. Conversely, when the particle concentration is low, the filters will stretch to achieve a low pressure drop and thus reduce energy consumption. Moreover, we hypothesize that the elastic air filters will exhibit self-cleaning ability as the shear force from the stretching/contracting processes can remove particle cakes, thereby extending the filter service life. This project will start with the development of elastic air filters that respond to thermal stimuli, based on the LCE filter skeleton actuator and TPU nanofiber filter media. The particle filtration efficiency and pressure drop of the filters under different stretching levels will be characterized to establish the pollution-level-responsive function. The mechanisms by which the stretching/contracting processes influence the removal of particle cakes will be investigated. This project will then develop the necessary hardware and software for pollution-level-responsive air filters, and conduct field tests and life cycle assessment to evaluate the energy saving and extended filter service life in a building ventilation system. The proposed project will enhance our understanding of the mechanisms of particle filtration and particle cake removal by elastic air filters. The development of pollution-level-responsive air filters will reduce energy consumption, extend filter service life, and improve sustainability. The findings will advance the development of this novel filtration technology for efficient indoor particle control. 室內人員暴露於空氣中的顆粒物與各種不良健康影響有關，例如呼吸道感染、心臟病和肺癌。傳統的高效空氣過濾器能有效去除顆粒物，但此類過濾器結構上不可變化，並始終以高過濾效率運行，伴隨著高壓降。當空氣質量良好時，保持高顆粒物過濾效率並不經濟，因為其對空氣質量的改善有限，但由於高壓降，能耗仍然很高。因此，有必要開發能根據不同空氣污染水平自動調整的先進空氣過濾器，以減少能耗、延長使用壽命並提高可持續性。 液晶彈性體（LCEs）是形狀可變化的材料，可用作熱刺激驅動器。同時，由電紡製成的熱塑性聚氨酯（TPU）納米纖維可形成彈性過濾介質。因此，我們假設可以基於由LCEs製成的過濾器骨架驅動器和由TPU納米纖維製成的彈性過濾介質來開發污染水平響應型空氣過濾器。當顆粒物濃度高時，過濾器會收縮以實現高顆粒物過濾效率，從而保護室內人員的健康。相反，當顆粒物濃度低時，過濾器會伸展以實現低壓降，從而降低能耗。此外，我們假設彈性空氣過濾器會表現出自清潔能力，因為伸縮過程中的剪切力可以去除顆粒物堆積，從而延長過濾器的使用壽命。 該項目將從開發對熱刺激有反應的彈性空氣過濾器開始，基於LCE過濾器骨架驅動器和TPU納米纖維過濾介質。將對過濾器在不同伸縮水平下的顆粒物過濾效率和壓降進行表徵，以建立污染水平響應曲線。將研究伸縮過程如何影響顆粒物堆積的去除機制。該項目將隨後開發污染水平響應型空氣過濾器所需的硬件和軟件，並進行現場測試和生命周期評估，以評估建築通風系統中的節能和延長過濾器使用壽命的效果。 本項目將增強我們對彈性空氣過濾器顆粒物過濾機制和顆粒物堆積去除機制的理解。污染水平響應型空氣過濾器的開發將減少能耗、延長過濾器使用壽命並提高可持續性。研究結果將推進這一新型過濾技術的發展，以有效控制室內顆粒物污染。

14203425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203425.value: 雙曲聯邦學習及其在推薦系統中的應用

14203425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203425.value: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a pivotal approach for collaborative machine learning, preserving data privacy in our increasingly data-conscious society. However, conventional FL methods, primarily designed for models in Euclidean spaces, face significant limitations when dealing with complex data structures. First, hierarchical and tree-like datasets, common in recommender systems, graph mining, and language processing, cannot be embedded into finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces without substantial distortion.
