Several JavaScript's language features, e.g., asynchronous and event-driven code execution, present significant challenges for both static and dynamic program analysis and result in high false positive and false negative rates in vulnerability detection. In particular, the widely used static analysis tools often produce a large number of false positives, necessitating further manual validation of almost all potential reported vulnerabilities. However, as there currently lacks a reliable vulnerability validation tool, the overwhelming volume of static vulnerability alerts can overburden security analysts and software developers. Furthermore, existing vulnerability mitigation methods largely rely on humans. They largely require developers to analyze and patch security flaws manually. This manual approach not only makes the remediation process slow but also increases the time window of exposure, leaving applications vulnerable to exploitation for extended periods. While automated program repair has been studied and applied in other application domains like C/C++, no such work exists for Node.js. This gap is primarily due to the complexities inherent in modeling JavaScript's syntax and semantics, which are further complicated by the asynchronous, event-driven features. In this project, we aim to mitigate security threats in both web and desktop applications in the Node.js ecosystem. We will develop advanced program analysis techniques to effectively detect and validate vulnerabilities in these applications by taking a hybrid analysis approach. We will specifically account for the unique language and application features (e.g., asynchronous operations) in the Node.js ecosystem. We will also develop automated vulnerability patching solutions through both program analysis and artificial intelligence approaches. 保障Node.js生態系統的安全至關重要，因為它在互聯網上扮演著重要角色：Node.js被廣泛用於開發網頁應用程式以及跨平台的桌面應用程式。若一個Node.js應用程式存在漏洞，它可能會在未經適當過濾的情況下接受來自外部來源的惡意輸入。這些惡意輸入可能被用來以非預期的方式操控程式的行為。例如，攻擊者可以注入惡意代碼來改變應用程式中的數據庫操作或系統指令，這可能導致資料外洩，甚至執行任意代碼的風險。 儘管Node.js生態系統的安全性至關重要，但許多Node.js應用程式中仍然存在各種漏洞，而現有的解決方案難以有效防止這些漏洞的出現。一大挑戰在於如何有效分析JavaScript這種高度動態且靈活的程式語言。JavaScript的多種語言特性，例如非同步與事件驅動的執行模式，對靜態與動態的程式分析方法都構成了重大挑戰，進而導致漏洞檢測中出現高誤判率與高漏判率。尤其是目前廣泛使用的靜態分析工具經常產生大量誤報，使得幾乎所有潛在漏洞都需要進一步人工驗證。然而，由於目前缺乏可靠的漏洞驗證工具，這些靜態分析產生的大量警報會使安全分析師與軟件開發者疲於應對。 此外，現有的漏洞緩解方法在很大程度上仍依賴人工操作。大多數情況下，開發者需要親自分析並手動修補安全缺陷。這種人工處理方式不僅使修補流程變慢，也增加了程式暴露於安全風險中的時間，使應用程式在長時間內容易遭到攻擊利用。雖然自動化程式修補已在C/C++等其他應用領域中被研究和應用，但目前在Node.js領域尚無相關研究出現。這一落差主要是因為JavaScript的語法與語意建模本身就極具挑戰性，再加上其非同步與事件驅動特性，使程式分析更加複雜。 在本研究項目中，我們旨在降低Node.js生態系統中網頁與桌面應用程式的安全威脅。我們將開發先進的程式分析技術，透過混合分析方法，有效檢測並驗證這些應用中的安全漏洞。我們將特別考量Node.js生態系統中獨特的語言與應用特性（例如非同步操作）。我們也將結合程式分析與人工智能技術，開發自動化的漏洞修補解決方案。

14211425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211425.value: 基於多模態融合定位的永磁操控和剛度調節機器人導管系統

14211425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14211425.value: Dr NG, Yuen Ting Rebecca Prof Wang, Hesheng Prof Yu, Jiangfan

14211425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211425.value: Endovascular coil embolization procedure for intracranial aneurysm is highly challenging due to the difficulty in catheter navigation across the tortuous cerebral artery, complex coil deployment process in the thin-walled, easily rupture aneurysm, and risk of ionizing radiation from X-ray fluoroscopy. In this project, we will develop a next-generation steerable robotic catheter system to address these key challenges in endovascular coil embolization to improve active catheter advancement and steering, maintaining catheter configuration via stiffness variation during coil deployment into the aneurysm, and enabling real-time robot pose tracking through a SLAM-based localization framework without continuous fluoroscopy. Specifically, we will develop a miniature variable stiffness steerable robotic catheter based on the concept of magnetic jamming applied on soft magnetic microparticles, a novel Halbach array-based permanent magnetic actuation system with large magnetic field and gradient consisting of nested Halbach permanent magnet arrays, and a multimodal fusion-based visual SLAM framework integrating inputs from a microangioscopic videos, FBG strain information, and magnetic drive signals and registering with the pre-operative CT images to provide real-time catheter pose in the global patient coordinate. Overall, the proposed robotic system will be the first system that respectively allows active catheter translation and steering across the cerebral artery, stiffness control to optimize the coil deployment stage and minimize risk of aneurysm rupture, and accurate ionizing radiation-free localization approach leveraging the latest development in microangioscopy. The three research initiatives also represent an all-rounded robotics-based solution, covering soft robot design, magnetic system design, and localization algorithm implementation, to address real clinical challenges of endovascular coil embolization for more effective treatment of aneurysm.

14212025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212025.value: 基於飛秒雷射二維投影的多維高速光存儲

14212025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212025.value: This proposal aims to develop a femtosecond laser projection data-writing/readout platform for high-speed multi-dimensional optical data storage. To achieve the goal, a programmable depth-resolved 2D light sheet is generated by temporally focusing a femtosecond laser beam via a digital micromirror device (DMD). As the DMD can be rapidly updated at a speed up to 9.5 kHz, parallel data writing can be realized with a target printing speed of 5.2M voxels/sec with substantially improved data storage dimensions. Ultrafast lasers have been widely used to realize multi-dimensional optical data storage. For example, multiplexing optical data storage was demonstrated by simultaneously exploiting the intensity, polarization and wavelength of light in nanoparticles infused media. In parallel, polarization multiplexed data recording was realized by ultrafast laser imprinted nanogratings in silica glass. However, these processes are limited by the serial scanning procedure, which is inherently slow and expensive. While parallel processing methods have been proposed, they often have compromised resolution or limited performance. Therefore, it is critical to develop high-speed solutions for optical data storage without compromising the storage density and accuracy. To realize multi-dimensional high-speed 3D optical storage, we will first develop a femtosecond projection data-writing/reading platform, where the laser intensity can be precisely controlled on a temporally focused 2D light sheet via a DMD. During data-writing, the DMD rapidly switches the designed patterns at 9.5 kHz and an XYZ stage moves the storage medium continuously in synchronization with the DMD to achieve a parallel 3D writing speed of 5.2M voxels/sec. To optimize and study the femtosecond projection platform, we will (1) investigate the laser writing parameters for controlling a multi-dimensional data voxel; (2) elucidate the physical mechanisms for the formation of the data voxels; (3) develop a metrology module for precisely retrieving the optically recorded data in storage media. Lastly, we will imprint multiplexed data voxels at high speeds in different materials, including different glasses and polymers, to demonstrate the material generality, function and resolution of the femtosecond projection data storage platform. The result of this work will substantially improve the capacity and writing speed of multi-dimensional optical data storage as well as enhance the fundamental understanding of the light-matter interaction at the nanometer scale, which presents tremendous opportunities for 3D optical storage and next-generation cloud data centers. In addition, the femtosecond projection method may find other important applications, such as 3D nanofabrication or two-photon lithography with ultrahigh resolution and throughput. 本提案旨在開發一個用於高速多維光學資料儲存的飛秒雷射投影資料寫入/讀出平台。為了實現該目標，透過數位微鏡裝置 (DMD) 對飛秒雷射光束進行時間聚焦，產生可編程具有深度分辨的二維光片。由於 DMD 可以高達 9.5 kHz 的速度快速更新，因此可以實現平行資料寫入，目標列印速度為 5.2M 像素/秒，顯著提高資料儲存維度。 超快雷射已被廣泛用於實現多維光學資料儲存。例如，透過同時利用奈米粒子注入介質中光的強度、偏振和波長，實現了多路復用光學數據儲存。同時，透過在石英玻璃中以超快雷射蝕刻奈米光柵，實現了偏振復用數據記錄。然而，這些製程受限於串行掃描程序，這本身就速度慢且成本高。雖然已經提出了並行處理方法，但它們通常會降低解析度或限制效能。因此，在不影響儲存密度和精度的前提下，開發高速光學資料儲存解決方案至關重要。 為了實現多維高速三維光存儲，我們將首先開發一個飛秒投影資料寫入/讀取平台，該平台可以透過數位微鏡裝置 (DMD) 精確控制時間聚焦的二維光片上的雷射強度。在資料寫入過程中，DMD 以 9.5 kHz 的頻率快速切換設計圖案，XYZ 平台與 DMD 同步連續移動儲存介質，以實現每秒 5.2 兆像素的平行三維寫入速度。為了優化和研究飛秒投影平台，我們將 (1) 研究用於控制多維資料體素的雷射寫入參數；(2) 闡明資料體素形成的物理機制；(3) 開發一個用於精確檢索儲存媒體中光學記錄資料的計量模組。最後，我們將在不同材料（包括不同的玻璃和聚合物）中高速壓印多路復用資料體素，以展示飛秒投影資料儲存平台的材料通用性、功能和解析度。 這項工作的成果將顯著提高多維光資料儲存的容量和寫入速度，並增強對奈米尺度光與物質相互作用的根本理解，這為三維光儲存和下一代雲端資料中心帶來了巨大的機會。此外，飛秒投影方法還可能找到其他重要的應用，例如具有超高解析度和高通量的三維奈米製造或雙光子光刻。

14212325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212325.value: 利用納米金字塔基底石墨烯傳感器與核酸邏輯電路實現癌症多重 miRNA 的高靈敏檢測

14212325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212325.value: Sensitive and multiplexed detection of nucleic acid biomarkers is crucial for early cancer diagnosis and effective management, particularly given the molecular heterogeneity of tumors and the extremely low abundance of biomarkers like exosomal microRNAs. While polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is the current gold standard for nucleic acid detection, it faces limitations such as fluorescence labeling, photobleaching, and reliance on enzymes, which can affect its effectiveness and complicate multiplexed detection. Graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) have emerged as promising alternatives, offering label-free and enzyme-free detection of nucleic acids with high accuracy and speed. Despite achieving detection limits down to attomolar levels, GFETs face two key challenges before clinical integration: 1) the need for multiplexed detection in complex biological samples, and 2) overcoming the Debye screening effect in high ionic strength environments, which limits the sensing distance due to electric double-layer screening. To address these challenges, we propose engineering nanopyramid substrates for GFETs to mitigate the Debye screening effect, thereby enhancing detection sensitivity in human serum. Additionally, we will develop nucleic acid logic circuits to enable multiplexed detection of clinically relevant miRNA biomarkers associated with breast cancer, including the characterization of their phenotypes such as triple-negative breast cancer. Our hypotheses are: 1) Engineering nanopyramid patterns for GFET substrates can effectively mitigate the Debye screening effect, enhancing the sensing performance of GFETs in complex biological fluids; and 2) Nucleic acid logic circuits will facilitate multiplexed detection of oligonucleotides with high sensitivity and specificity in a one-pot reaction. Our specific aims are: Aim 1 - Validate the extension of the Debye length using nanopyramid substrates and assess their impact on GFET sensitivity; Aim 2 - Verify the effectiveness of the designed Boolean logic circuit for multiplexed detection of breast cancer-associated miRNAs. We will first fabricate nanopyramid substrate-integrated GFET sensors using controlled nanofabrication techniques. Then, we will develop and optimize the nucleic acid logic circuit for multiplexed detection, validating its performance using spiked-in miRNA combinations in human serum. Finally, we will test the system using clinical blood samples to demonstrate its potential for early-stage cancer diagnosis and phenotype characterization. This innovative approach aims to overcome key barriers in nucleic acid detection by combining advanced nanostructured GFETs with nucleic acid logic circuits. Successful completion of this project could significantly advance molecular diagnostics by providing a rapid, accurate, and multiplexed platform for point-of-care detection of cancer and other diseases. 核酸生物標誌物的高靈敏與多重檢測，對於癌症早期診斷及臨床管理至關重要，尤其考慮到腫瘤的分子異質性以及外泌體 microRNA 等標誌物含量極低。雖然聚合酶鏈式反應（PCR）為當前核酸標志物檢測的金標準，但其存在需螢光標記、螢光漂白效應以及對酶的依賴等限制，既影響檢測效能，也增加多重檢測的複雜度。石墨烯場效應晶體管（GFET）作為新興替代技術，可實現無標記、無酶依賴的核酸快速高準確度檢測。儘管 GFET 的檢測限已達阿摩爾（aM）級別，其在臨床轉化前仍面臨兩項關鍵挑戰：1）在複雜生物樣本中實現多重檢測；2）於高離子強度環境下克服德拜屏蔽效應（電雙層屏蔽致使有效感測距離受限）。針對上述問題，本項目擬通過工程化設計納米金字塔基底以配合 GFET，降低德拜屏蔽的影響，從而提升在人血清中的檢測性能；同時我們構建核酸布爾邏輯電路，實現對乳腺癌相關之臨床 miRNA 標誌物的多重檢測，從而達到對三陰性乳腺癌有效診斷的目標。此研究假設1）納米金字基底可有效緩解德拜屏蔽效應，顯著提升 GFET 在複雜生物體液中的傳感性能；2）核酸邏輯電路可在“一鍋法”反應中，以高靈敏度與高特異性實現寡核苷酸的多重檢測。我們的具體目標是： 1）驗證納米金字塔基底對等效德拜長度之延展效應，並系統評估其對 GFET 靈敏度的影響；2） 驗證所設計核酸布爾邏輯電路在多重檢測乳腺癌相關 miRNA 上的有效性。 首先，我們利用可控納米製程製備基於納米金字塔基底的GFET 傳感器；其後，開發並優化核酸邏輯電路以實現多重檢測，並在人血清加標（spike-in）的多重 miRNA 組合中驗證性能；最後，採用臨床血液樣本進行測試，以展示其於癌症早期診斷與表型表徵方面的應用潛力。本研究通過將先進納米結構 GFET 與核酸邏輯電路相結合，力圖突破核酸檢測領域的關鍵瓶頸。預期成果有望顯著推動分子診斷發展，提供一個快速、準確、可多重檢測的現場快速檢測（POCT）平台，服務於癌症及其他疾病的臨床應用。

14212425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212425.value: 自然語言意圖驅動的ACL自動化配置

14212425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212425.value: Network management is crucial for computer networks to ensure they operate efficiently, securely, and reliably. This project examines the configuration of Access Control List, or ACL, one of the most basic and widely used protocols in network management [41, 45]. An ACL is a set of rules used to filter and control traffic. Each rule specifies a set of conditions, such as source or destination IP addresses, ports, protocols, etc., that must be met for the traffic to be allowed or denied [2, 4, 5]. Current practice in ACL configuration heavily relies on manual effort [21, 41]. When there is a new policy to enforce, operators carefully reason about the policy goals in order to break it down into ACL rules, determine which router ports and ACLs these rules should be applied to, analyze their potential impact to the existing rules on these target ACLs, and then configure the new rules on individual devices. This process is labor-intensive and time-consuming, taking about one week for a new policy as reported by Alibaba [41]. Given the scale of network, the variety of policies from different stakeholders, and the speed at which these factors change, manual configuration is quickly becoming the bottleneck for network’s ability to evolve. We therefore propose to enable automatic ACL configuration with natural language intents, taking advantage of powerful large language models (LLMs) [1, 9, 44]. In our vision, operators just need to express their high-level configuration intents in natural language. The system automatically understands and translates them into low-level ACL rules using LLMs, detects and resolves any potential conflicts between new intents and existing rules, and deploys them across the network to implement the intent. As a first step towards our vision, we design a novel system called Xumi that tackles three imminent design questions: (1) intent comprehension, (2) conflict detection and resolution, and (3) deployment optimization. We perform a preliminary study with intents and rules based off production ACL configurations from Microsoft Azure. Initial results show the effectiveness of our initial design using GPT-4o, Llama3-70B, and Mistral-Large-2. Configuration automation is a critical research area with eminent practical value for operators who own large networks for critical applications such as telecommunication, cloud, and AI/ML. We will collaborate with network operators and open source Xumi to maximize its impact and adoption. Our effort represents another stride towards autonomous network that can reason and manage itself. 網路管理中，「存取控制清單」（ACL）是基礎且廣泛使用的流量管控協議。當前ACL配置高度依賴人工操作：運維人員需解析政策目標、拆解為ACL規則、選擇部署位置、分析與現有規則衝突，最後逐台設備配置。此過程耗時費力（如阿里巴巴報告指出單一新政策需耗時一週），在大型網路、多變政策需求下，已成網路演進的瓶頸。 為此，我們提出利用大型語言模型（LLMs）實現自然語言意圖的自動化ACL配置。運維人員僅需以自然語言描述高階配置意圖，系統將自動完成： 1. 意圖解析：透過LLMs轉譯為底層ACL規則 2. 衝突處理：檢測並解決新規則與現有配置的衝突 3. 部署優化：跨網路高效部署規則以實現意圖 作為初步實踐，我們設計Xumi系統，針對三大關鍵問題： 1. 意圖理解（採用GPT-4o、Llama3-70B、Mistral-Large-2等模型） 2. 衝突檢測與化解 3. 部署策略優化 基於微軟Azure生產環境ACL配置的測試顯示，初期設計具備可行性。 ACL自動化配置對電信、雲端、AI/ML等關鍵領域的網路運營商具有重大價值。我們將開源Xumi系統並與業界合作，推動網路向「可自主推理管理」的自治網路邁進。

14212525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212525.value: 反應性多模態導航引導脊柱手術的軟體機器人耦合與傳感技術

14212525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212525.value: Bone drilling and pedicle screw placement are vital for treating spinal conditions like tumors, fractures, and scoliosis, with at least 3.85M cases combined annually. The traditional “freehand” method, while common, poses risks due to reliance on surgeon intuition, leading to high risk of neurological damage at only 4mm of medial violation during screw placement. To enhance precision, computer-assisted navigation systems have emerged, improving accuracy rates significantly but facing challenges with line-of-sight tracking and steep learning curves. Robotic guidance offers further advancements, reducing physical fatigue and improving accuracy, yet remains limited by bulky designs, high costs, and lack of in-situ adaptability. There is a significant need for a compact, handheld robotic device that combines the flexibility of free-hand techniques with haptics-enforced instrument positioning for improved precision in spinal surgeries. Therefore, the overall goal of this project is to develop and validate a compact, lightweight robotic instrument positioner with self-contained haptic rendering for adaptable and precise pedicle screw placement. Our proposed robotic instrument positioner will consist of two major components: i) An ungrounded handheld haptic device synergistically operated with a compact, multimodal sensing instrument positioner for high-fidelity guidance; ii) A specialized learning-based control framework leveraging multimodal sensing to achieve real-time decoding of 6D pose and enable in-situ navigation cues. Robotic closed-loop control and haptic feedback is enabled by fusing data from inertial measurement units (IMUs), fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs), LED-PD arrays, and time-of-flight (ToF) sensors, paired with intermittent infrared (IR) tracking. Instrument alignment of pre-planned pedicle screw trajectories will be flexibly enforced based on the synchronized motion planning and gyroscopic haptics. Validation of the system will be initially undertaken in virtual anatomical simulators for scoliosis treatment, followed by lab-based drilling in artificial CT-visible vertebrae and pre-clinical trials in cadavers at the hospital. The success of this project would present a major step forward towards more effective and ergonomic treatment of patients requiring pedicle screw placements, with several key areas addressed: 1) Enhanced treatment of spinal diseases and abnormalities, facilitating improved treatment planning and reduced likelihood of patient progression to severely reduced quality of life; 2) Development of a compact, lightweight handheld robot with self-contained haptic rendering and 6-DoF instrument pose tracking with minimal line-of-sight limitations; 3) Improved surgical outcomes during pedicle screw placement in the spine due to retainment of flexible and intuitive hands-on techniques while providing responsive in-situ haptic feedback, improving adaptability when operating on the deformable spinal column. 骨鑽操作和椎弓根螺釘置入對於治療脊柱腫瘤、骨折和脊柱側彎等疾病至關重要，每年相關病例合計至少385萬例。傳統的“徒手”方法雖然常見，但因高度依賴外科醫生的直覺而存在風險，在螺釘置入過程中內側壁僅4毫米的穿破就可能導致嚴重的神經損傷。為了提高精確度，計算機輔助導航系統應運而生，顯著提高了準確率；然而，此類系統受限於視線追蹤遮擋問題且學習曲線陡峭。機器人引導進一步減輕醫生體力負擔並提高精度，但仍受限於笨重的設計、高昂的成本以及缺乏原位適應能力。當前極需一種精巧的手持式機器人設備，既保留徒手操作的靈活性，又能通過觸覺強化的器械定位，顯著提升脊柱手術的精準度。 因此，本項目的總體目標是開發並驗證一種精巧、輕量化的機器人器械定位器，該定位器具備自包含的觸覺渲染功能，用於實現適應性強的、精確的椎弓根螺釘置入。我們提出的機器人器械定位器由兩大組件構成：i) 一個非接地式手持觸覺設備，與一個緊湊的多模態傳感器械定位器協同操作，實現高保真度的引導；ii) 一個專門的基於學習的控制框架，利用多模態傳感實現6維位姿（6D pose）的實時解碼，並提供原位導航提示。通過融合慣性測量單元（IMUs）、光纖布拉格光柵（FBGs）、LED-PD陣列和飛行時間（ToF）傳感器的數據，並結合間歇性紅外（IR）追蹤，可實現機器人的閉環控制與觸覺反饋。器械將根據同步的運動規劃和陀螺儀觸覺技術，靈活地強制執行預先規劃的椎弓根螺釘軌跡對準。系統的驗證將首先在用於脊柱側彎治療的虛擬解剖模擬器中進行，隨後在實驗室環境中使用CT可見的人工椎體進行鑽孔實驗，並最終在屍體上開展臨床前試驗。 本項目將為需要進行椎弓根螺釘置入的患者帶來更高效且更符合人體工學的治療，標誌著重要進步，主要體現在以下方面：1) 加強脊柱疾病和畸形的治療，促進治療計劃的改進，降低患者病情進展至嚴重影響生活質量的可能性 2) 開發一種精巧、輕量化的手持式機器人，具備自包含的觸覺渲染和6個自由度（6-DoF）器械位姿跟蹤能力，且視線限制最小；3) 在脊柱椎弓根螺釘置入過程中改善手術效果，既保留靈活直觀的徒手操作技術，又提供響應迅速的原位觸覺反饋，從而在操作可變形脊柱時具備更強的適應性。

14212625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212625.value: 大規模微流體晶片可靠性導向控制合成

14212625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212625.value: Nowadays, the continuous-flow microfluidic large-scale integration (mLSI) chips have become a revolutionary platform for biochemical experiments, enabling the precise operation of fluid samples and reagents in nanoliter volumes. With advancements in manufacturing processes, the feature sizes of such chips keep shrinking, allowing more microvalves to be integrated into a single chip. This makes the corresponding control system more complex and presents many challenges. Initially, to address the many microvalves, more external controllers will be required. However, the number of external controllers cannot be increased without limit as demand grows. Additionally, using more controllers requires more control ports, which take up significant space and hinders the miniaturization of the entire chip. Hence, there is a significant demand to reduce the control systems’ reliance on external controllers, without introducing any operational errors. Furthermore, due to their smaller features and higher density, the control channels are more prone to manufacturing defects. In complex systems, the increase in channel length and density will significantly raise the risk of manufacturing defects. Therefore, it is also essential to improve the reliability of the control systems. In this project, we intend to propose RACS, a Reliability-Aware Control Synthesis framework for mLSI chips. 當今，連續流式微流體大規模整合（microfluidic Large-Scale Integration, mLSI）晶片已成為生化實驗的革命性平台，能夠在奈升（nanoliter）體積下精確操作流體樣本與試劑。隨著製造工藝的不斷進步，這類晶片的特徵尺寸持續縮小，使得更多微閥（microvalve）能整合至單一晶片中。這同時使得相應的控制系統更加複雜，並帶來許多挑戰。 最初，為了控制更多微閥，需要配置更多外部控制器。然而，隨著需求的增長，外部控制器的數量不可能無限制增加。此外，使用更多控制器需要更多控制埠，這將佔據大量空間，阻礙整體晶片的小型化。因此，迫切需要在不引入操作錯誤的情況下，降低控制系統對外部控制器的依賴。 另外，由於特徵尺寸縮小且密度提高，控制通道更容易在製造過程中出現缺陷。在複雜系統中，通道長度與密度的增加會顯著提高製造缺陷的風險。因此，提高控制系統的可靠性同樣至關重要。 在本專案中，我們計劃提出一個針對 mLSI 晶片的 RACS（Reliability-Aware Control Synthesis，可靠性導向控制合成） 框架。

14212925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212925.value: 繩索驅動柔性軟體機器人平面研發

14212925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14212925.value: Prof Tang, Xiaoqiang Prof Xu, Dongyan

14212925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212925.value: Cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) are a type of parallel actuating mechanism that has attractive advantages over traditional mechanisms, such as efficient actuation, inherently lightweight, large potential workspace, and ease to setup and control. These have led to various applications in manipulation, such as single platform CDPRs and multilink finger or arm mechanisms. Particularly for multilink mechanisms, the “backbone” of CDPRs is typically rigid for the ease of modelling and implementation. However, this limits the range of postures (degrees-of-freedom), flexibility of the manipulator and the length-to-weight ratio. To address such limitations, tube-like continuum cable-driven manipulators have been studied in recent years. Despite this, only a limited amount of surface contact could be produced during manipulation, which is required in object manipulation and human-robot interaction. In this project, a new type of cable-actuated flexible soft robotic surfaces (C-SRS) is proposed. C-SRSs consist of two primary components: 1) a flexible material surface end-effector; and 2) a set of cables connected to the end-effector. The uniqueness of the project include: 1) the end-effector allows for a large range of surface shapes to be produced in two dimensions; 2) compared with existing pneumatically actuated SRSs, the use of cables can produce motion with higher accuracy; 3) in addition to fully constrained cable setup, underactuated SRSs using a pre-bent surfaces for biomimetic manipulation like a human palm will also be studied; and 4) a hybrid actuation by combining pneumatics and liquid crystal elastomers with cables to enable both finer and accurate control of the C-SRS. The following major challenges will be addressed in this project: 1) to accurately and efficiently model and solve the coupled kinematics and dynamics (kinodynamic) of the high degree-of-freedom C-SRS; 2) the workspace analysis and mechanism synthesis of the new class of C-SRS; 3) the design of the cable attachments (number and location) and both the material and shape of the flexible end-effector surface; 4) the planning and control of the C-SRS for object manipulation; 5) the design and prototyping of pneumatic and liquid crystal elastomers into C-SRS to achieve hybrid actuation; and finally 6) the validation and demonstration of C-SRS to show the potential for future real-world applications. 繩驅並聯機器人（CDPRs）是一種並聯驅動機構，相較於傳統機構具有顯著優勢，如高驅動效率、輕量化、大潛在工作空間以及易於設置和控制。這些優勢使其在操作領域有多種應用，如單平臺CDPRs和多連杆手指或手臂機構。特別是對於多連杆機構，CDPRs的“骨幹”通常是剛性的，以便於建模和實現。然而，這限制了其姿態範圍（自由度）、操作末端的柔性以及長度-重量比。為解決這些局限，近年來越來越多研究聚焦於繩索驅動的管狀連續體機器人。儘管如此，此類機器人在運行過程中只能與外界產生有限的接觸面積，而大接觸面積在很多物體操作和人機交互任務中是必需的。本專案提出了一種新型繩索驅動柔性軟體機器人表面（C-SRS）。C-SRS由兩個主要元件組成：1）由柔性材料製成的平面狀末端執行器；2）連接到末端執行器的一組繩索。該項目的獨特之處包括：1）末端執行器能夠產生大量的二維形變；2）與現有的氣動驅動SRS相比，繩索驅動能實現更高精度的運動；3）除了完全約束的繩索設置外，還將研究預彎曲平面的欠驅動SRS，以及其對於人類手掌的仿生操作；4）通過結合氣壓、液晶彈性與繩索的混合驅動，實現C-SRS更精細和準確的控制。本項目將解決以下主要挑戰：1）精確且高效地建模和求解高自由度C-SRS的耦合運動學和動力學；2）新型C-SRS的工作空間分析和機構綜合研究；3）繩索（數量和附著點位置）以及柔性平面末端執行器的材料和形狀設計；4）C-SRS用於物體操作的規劃和控制；5）將氣亞驅動和液晶彈性驅動集成到C-SRS中以實現混合驅動的設計和原型製作；6）C-SRS模型驗證和成果展示，以表現其在未來現實世界應用中的潛力。

14213125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213125.value: 適用於曲折狹窄腦動脈之可操控、超高解析度與超高速遙控神經OCT內視鏡系統

14213125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14213125.value: Prof Ren, Hongliang Prof Yan, Bryan Ping-yen

14213125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213125.value: Cerebral aneurysms affect over 160 million people worldwide, posing a significant global health burden. Without intervention, more than 50% of these aneurysms are at risk of rupture, leading to high mortality rates and permanent brain damage. Endovascular interventions have emerged as the preferred method for treating aneurysms and strokes. However, these procedures rely on advanced angiographic imaging, which faces challenges such as the limited spatial resolution and contrast capacities of current technologies. Accurate visualization of arterial pathology and neurovascular implants is crucial for making optimal procedural decisions and improving patient outcomes. Intra-neurovascular optical coherence tomography (OCT) is an emerging technology that enables label-free, volumetric in vivo imaging of cerebral artery diseases and metallic devices at micron-scale resolution. However, this technology has limitations in delineating subtle pathological changes and navigating through complex cerebral arteries owing to the following factors: 1) the limited resolution (~15 µm) of current OCT systems operating at 1300 nm; 2) the need for high-speed, distortion-free imaging within curvilinear and narrow arteries; 3) the absence of robotic perception and maneuverability at the distal tip, limiting precise steering in intricate cerebrovascular networks; and 4) the inability to perform teleoperated manipulation of the endoscope, which could reduce radiation exposure for physicians during procedures. In the proposed project, we will develop a telerobotic NeuOCT technology, integrating an OCT–FBG dual-function system, an imaging–sensing fiber probe, a robotic microcatheter, and a remote-control platform. This system will build on our existing 800-nm OCT and robotic endomicroscopy technologies, enabling teleoperated steering and safe navigation through tortuous and narrow cerebral arteries for ultrahigh-resolution and ultrahigh-speed intra-neurovascular imaging. The 0.2-mm fiber probe will have a 3D glass-printed, aberration-corrected micro-lens on the distal tip, capable of imaging at a resolution of ~3 × 10 µm (in axial and transverse directions) while sensing the probe bending direction and angle. This probe will be strengthened mechanically and immersed in a shear-thinning non-Newtonian fluid to enhance torque transfer efficiency and reduce probe-fluid friction for high-speed (≥200 fps) and distortion-free imaging. The microcatheter will feature a 0.35-mm diameter and a magnetically–hydraulically controlled soft robotic tip, enabling omnidirectional steering and variable stiffness and ensuring smooth navigation through complex cerebrovasculatures. By using a telerobotic manipulation platform, we will further validate the effectiveness of the proposed system using neurovascular phantoms and animal models. The NeuOCT has the potential to enhance the management of cerebrovascular diseases such as aneurysms. 腦動脈瘤影響全球超過1.6億人，構成嚴重的全球健康負擔。若未及時干預，逾50%的動脈瘤有破裂風險，導致高死亡率與永久性腦損傷。血管內介入治療已成為治療動脈瘤與中風的首選方法。然而，這些手術高度依賴先進的血管攝影成像，但現有技術在空間解析度和對比度上存在侷限，難以實現對動脈病變和神經血管植入物的精確可視化，影響臨床決策與病患預後。 神經血管內光學相干斷層掃描（OCT）是一項新興技術，能進行腦動脈疾病及支架的微米級、無標記、三維體內成像。但該技術在識別微小病變和穿越複雜腦動脈時受以下因素限制：1）現有1300 nm OCT系統的解析度有限（約15微米）；2）曲折狹窄動脈中需實現高速、無畸變成像；3）缺乏遠端機器人感知和操作，限制了在複雜腦血管網內的精確導航；4）無法遠端遙控內視鏡，醫師在手術時仍需暴露於輻射之下。 本項目將發展遙操作神經OCT（NeuOCT）系統，整合OCT–FBG雙功能系統、成像–感測光纖探頭、機械手臂微導管及遠端控制平台。該系統將依據我們現有800-nm OCT及機器人內視鏡技術，實現於曲折狹窄腦動脈內以超高解析度和超高速進行遙控安全成像與導航。0.2毫米光纖探頭遠端將安裝三維玻璃列印、修正像差微透鏡，成像解析度達約3×10微米（軸向×橫向），同時可感測探頭彎曲方向與角度。探頭將進行機械強化，並浸於流體中，以提升扭矩傳遞效率並降低探頭與流體間摩擦，實現200幀/秒以上的高速、無畸變成像。微導管直徑為0.35毫米，前端具有磁–液雙控軟體機器手臂，可全方位轉向與可變剛度，確保順利通過複雜腦血管。透過遙控操作平台，我們將以神經血管模型及動物實驗進一步驗證本系統效能。NeuOCT有望提升動脈瘤等腦血管疾病之診療品質。

14213225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213225.value: 實現基於高階擴散加權磁共振成像的高品質腦部生物標記圖譜繪製

14213225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14213225.value: Dr Abrigo, Jill Prof Dou, Qi Dr Hui, Sai Kam

14213225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213225.value: For over two decades, diffusion MRI (dMRI) has been an important non-invasive imaging tool for assessing white matter integrity and different brain diseases with the measurement of conventional dMRI-biomarkers, such as apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and fractional anisotropy (FA). However, conventional dMRI-biomarkers are sometimes not able to accurately describe the complex microstructure and its change in the brain tissues. Therefore, advanced dMRI-biomarkers, such as intravoxel incoherent motion dMRI (IVIM), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and neurite orientation density and dispersion imaging (NODDI), have been proposed to be promising biomarkers for achieving the more effective assessments of cerebrovascular and neurodegenerative diseases. Obtaining advanced dMRI-biomarkers often requires a lengthy data collection time than conventional dMRI-biomarkers, despite the use of fast 2D single-shot dMRI (ss-dMRI) technique. In addition, fast 2D ss-dMRI technique can only provide low image resolution and suffers from several image artifacts such as image distortion. Recent technical advances, such as 2D and 3D multi-shot dMRI techniques, have demonstrated that the higher image resolution and lower image distortion can benefit the applications of conventional dMRI-biomarkers. However, it is challenging to use those advanced acquisition techniques for the data collection of advanced dMRI-biomarkers, mainly because of the unacceptable increase in total scan time. Although the advanced dMRI-biomarkers have been proven as the promising imaging biomarkers for brain applications, the limited attainable data quality due to 2D ss-dMRI acquisition technique may restrict the explorations of their future applications. Therefore, the overall goal of this project is to improve the feasibility of advanced dMRI acquisition technique for mapping advanced dMRI-biomarkers. First, we will develop a novel data sharing scheme (DSS) for 3D multi-shot echo-planar imaging technique to highly accelerate the data collection for advanced dMRI-biomarkers mapping. Second, we will develop a synergistic reconstruction framework based on both conventional and deep-learning reconstruction methods to simultaneously recovery the images and compute the dMRI-biomarkers from the acquired data. Third, we will comprehensively evaluate the performance of developed framework by testing the mapping of different advanced dMRI-biomarkers, and conducting comparison study to conventional full-sampling and acceleration techniques. Successful completion of proposed study will enable an acquisition and reconstruction framework which can be generalized for high-quality mapping of different advanced dMRI-biomarkers from highly under-sampled data. The developed framework will be adaptable for different advanced dMRI models, therefore advancing the investigation of advanced dMRI-biomarkers and potentially expanding the application boundaries. 在過去二十餘年裡，擴散磁共振成像（dMRI）已成為評估白質完整性及各類腦部疾病的重要非侵入式成像工具，其主要依據常規 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜的測量，例如表面擴散係數（ADC）和不等向性指標（FA）。然而，常規 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜有時無法準確描述腦組織中複雜的微結構及其變化。因此，體素內非均向性擴散運動 MRI（IVIM）、擴散峰度成像（DKI）以及神經纖維定向密度與擴散性成像（NODDI）等高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜已被提出，它們被視為更具潛力的指標，可實現對腦血管及神經退化性疾病更有效的評估。 取得高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜往往需要比傳統 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜更長的掃描時間，儘管已採用快速 2D 單次激發 dMRI（ss‑dMRI）技術。此技術雖能縮短掃描時間，但僅能提供較低的圖像解析度，且易產生多種影像假影和失真。近來的技術進展，例如 2D 與 3D 多次激發 dMRI 技術，已證明較高的圖像解析度與較低的失真能顯著提升傳統 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜的應用價值。然而，將這些先進採集技術應用於高階 dMRI 生物標誌物圖譜的採集仍面臨挑戰，主要因為總掃描時間大幅地延長。雖然高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜已被證實為腦部應用的有前景醫學影像指標，但受限於 2D ss‑dMRI 採集方式所能達到的資料品質，可能限制其未來應用的進一步探索。 因此，本計劃的整體目標是提高先進 dMRI 採集技術在高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜方面的可實行性。首先，我們將開發一種新穎的數據共享方法 (DSS)，並運用於 3D 多次激發平面迴波成像技術，透過高度欠採樣大幅加速高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜的原始數據採集。其次，我們將基於傳統方法與深度學習的重建技術，建立一個協同重建框架，從獲取的資料中同時重建影像並計算 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜。第三，我們將通過測試不同先進 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜的繪製效果，並與傳統全採樣及加速技術進行比較，來全面評估所開發技術的性能。完成本研將實現一套資料採集和重建的框架，可通用於從高度欠採樣資料中重建各類高階 dMRI 生物標誌的圖譜。該框架可適用於不同的高階 dMRI 模型，從而推動高階 dMRI 生物標誌圖譜的進一步研究，並有望擴展其應用範圍。

14213525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213525.value: AdaLiDAR：適應自動駕駛的自適應 LiDAR 系統

14213525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213525.value: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) has emerged as a crucial sensor for capturing 3D environments with high efficiency. With its precise range detection and ability to function in varying lighting conditions, LiDAR is playing a vital role in many fields, including autonomous driving, robotics, and smart cities. Despite its growing adoption across various industries, current LiDAR technology struggles to meet a key requirement: the ability to adaptively capture dynamic and complex scenes. For example, autonomous vehicles should prioritize detecting moving pedestrians over static roadside structures. However, today’s LiDAR systems rely on fixed scan patterns, severely limiting their ability to adjust focus and prioritize critical areas. This inefficiency results in reduced perception accuracy, creates blind spots, and can cause significant degradation in downstream task performance. To address this limitation, this project is focused on developing an advanced LiDAR system that enhances scanning efficiency and performance by adaptively optimizing scan focus through an intelligent, software-defined micro-mirror controller. Unlike traditional systems, our system aims to dynamically adjust its scan pattern based on environmental characteristics and application-specific requirements, concentrating sample points on key objects without increasing power consumption or scan time. Specifically, we propose the following major research tasks: 1) An efficient mirror control scheme that enables fine-grained resolution control with minimum control overhead. This scheme can derive different resolutions over different regions to create adaptive scanning and improve application performance. It also considers the physical constraints of mirror rotation and minimizes the distortion. 2) A novel adaptive algorithm that maps dynamic environment and application requirements to the prioritized scan focus. Our algorithm will generate a fine-grained attention map by explicitly modeling the relationship between scan intensity and point cloud characteristics. 3) An efficient algorithm for generating optimal scan patterns from attention maps with carefully designed objective function and constraints. Our algorithm will ensure optimal performance in capturing highly dynamic and complex scenes while meeting the various constraints of the LiDAR system. 4) An adaptive object detection scheme for efficient LiDAR scanning in autonomous driving. We will integrate object detection into our adaptive LiDAR system with an end-to-end pipeline, optimizing the performance of autonomous driving. 5) System implementation and extensive validation. The proposed system will be implemented using commodity devices and be validated through extensive experiments in various settings for smart traffic applications using a real-world test of 20 smart lamppost nodes we deployed on the CUHK campus. 光線偵測與測距 (LiDAR) 已經成為高效率捕捉 3D 環境的重要感測器。憑藉其精確的範圍偵測和在不同光照條件下運作的能力，LiDAR 在自動駕駛、機器人技術和智慧城市等許多領域都扮演著重要的角色。儘管 LiDAR 在各行各業的應用越來越廣泛，但目前的 LiDAR 技術仍難以滿足一個關鍵要求：自適應捕捉動態複雜場景的能力。例如，自動駕駛車輛應優先偵測移動中的行人，而非靜態的路邊結構。然而，現今的 LiDAR 系統依賴於固定的掃描模式，嚴重限制了其調整焦點和優先偵測關鍵區域的能力。這種低效率會導致感知精確度降低、產生盲點，並可能導致下游任務效能大幅降低。 為了解決這個限制，本專案著重於開發先進的 LiDAR 系統，透過智慧型、軟體定義的微鏡控制器，自適應地最佳化掃描焦點，進而提升掃描效率與效能。與傳統系統不同，我們的系統旨在根據環境特性和特定應用需求動態調整其掃描模式，在不增加功耗或掃描時間的情況下將採樣點集中在關鍵物體上。具體而言，我們提出以下主要研究任務： 1) 高效的鏡像控制方案，能以最小的控制開銷實現精細的解析度控制。此方案可在不同區域衍生出不同的解析度，以建立自適應掃描並改善應用效能。它也考慮到鏡頭旋轉的物理限制，並將失真降至最低。2) 嶄新的適應性演算法，可將動態環境與應用需求映射至優先順序的掃描焦點。我們的演算法將透過明確建模掃描強度與點雲特徵之間的關係，產生細粒度的注意力地圖。3) 透過精心設計的目標函數與限制條件，從注意力地圖產生最佳掃描模式的有效演算法。我們的演算法將可確保在捕捉高動態與複雜場景時能達到最佳效能，同時滿足 LiDAR 系統的各種限制條件。4) 自適應物體偵測方案，用於自動駕駛中的高效 LiDAR 掃描。我們將在自適應性 LiDAR 系統中整合物件偵測的端對端管道，以優化自動駕駛的效能。5) 系統實作與廣泛驗證。我們將採用商品化的設備來實現所提出的系統，並通過我們在中大校園內部署的 20 個智能燈柱節點的實際測試，在智能交通應用的各種設置中進行廣泛的實驗驗證。

14300025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300025.value: 關於分數布朗運動的通用隨機控制理論

14300025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300025.value: Fractional Brownian motions (fBMs) represent a family of Gaussian processes characterized by continuous sample paths, indexed by the Hurst parameter in (0, 1), a crucial determinant of the roughness of the trajectory. As a generalization of standard Brownian motions (BMs), fBMs are extensively utilized to model phenomena with both short-term and long-term dependencies across various disciplines, including physics, biology, hydrology, network research, and financial mathematics. Initially defined in [61], significant properties of fBMs were later elaborated in [70]. Among subsequent works, [56] pioneered the statistical analysis associated with these processes, and [69] subsequently employed fBMs to model economic data. Due to the vast amount of techniques from Gaussian process, Markov process and martingale theories, stochastic control against BM has dominated for years; while that against fBM has been barely touched until recently with some partial sufficiency results proposed, yet a general approach for generic problems is still missing in the literature. In the present proposed project, we attempt to fill this gap by considering a general stochastic control problem against fBM with Hurst parameter in the union of (1/2, 1) and (1/3, 1/2). Compared with traditional stochastic control problems, neither the Markov process theory nor martingale one is useful for fBMs in general; we shall mainly rely on the Gaussian process theory with estimates for increments [2, 37, 73], rough path theory with estimates for second-order iterated path integrals [27-29, 39, 40, 65], and Jacobian flows analysis [3-6, 12-21, 24, 32], to tackle the problem. Our proposed theory could be further extended to handle a broad class of Gaussian processes and in the mean-field context. Our overall research goal will be accomplished by addressing the following topics: stochastic control, functional analysis, rough path theory and PDE-free analytical tools related to mean-field theory. Our anticipated results should (i) imply the well-posedness of many general modellings in economics and engineering, henceforth future researchers can concentrate solely on numerical approximation issues; (ii) effectively enrich the applicability of stochastic control theory against fBMs to echo their prevalence over vanilla BMs in real-life data-driven modelling nowadays; and (iii) finally, develop systematic and effective numerical approximation schemes for different induced forward-backward systems via a combination of Fourier-cosine method [30, 31, 52, 62, 63, 75, 76] and machine learning techniques [33, 34, 49]. We do apologize for only including most relevant references due to space limit; other sources and topics may be referred to references therein. 分數布朗運動 (Fractional Brownian motions, fBMs) 代表一類高斯過程，其特徵在於具有連續樣本路徑，並由在 (0, 1) 區間內的赫斯特參數 (Hurst parameter) 作為決定軌跡粗糙度的關鍵參數。作為標準布朗運動 (BMs) 的推廣，分數布朗運動被廣泛應用於模擬跨多個學科（包括物理學、生物學、水文學、網路研究及金融數學）中具有短期和長期依賴性的現象。分數布朗運動最初在文獻 [61] 中定義，其重要性質隨後在文獻 [70] 中被闡述。在後續研究中，文獻 [56] 率先開展了與此類過程相關的統計分析，而文獻 [69] 則隨後應用分數布朗運動來建模經濟數據。由於高斯過程、馬可夫過程及鞅理論中存在大量研究，針對標準布朗運動的隨機控制理論長期以來佔據主導地位；而針對分數布朗運動的隨機控制則鮮少被觸及，直到近期才出現部分充分性結果，但文獻中仍缺乏適用於通用問題的一般方法。 在本項目中，我們試圖通過考慮赫斯特參數在 (1/2, 1) 與 (1/3, 1/2) 之聯集內的分數布朗運動的通用隨機控制問題，來填補這一空白。相較於傳統的隨機控制問題，無論是馬可夫過程理論還是鞅理論，一般而言都無法應用於分數布朗運動；我們將主要依賴於基於增量估計的高斯過程理論 [2,37,73]、基於二階逐次路徑積分估計的粗糙路徑理論 (rough path theory) [27-29,39,40,65]，以及雅可比流分析 (Jacobian flows analysis) [3-6,12-21,24,32] 來解決問題。我們提出的理論可進一步推廣，用於處理一大類高斯過程，及應用於平均場 (mean-field) 情境。 我們的整體研究目標將通過探討以下主題來實現：隨機控制、泛函分析、粗糙路徑理論，以及與平均場理論相關的無偏微分方程 (PDE-free) 分析工具。我們預期的成果應能：(1) 為經濟學和工程學中的許多通用模型提供適定性 (well-posedness) 保證，從而使未來的研究者可以專注於數值近似問題；(2) 有效豐富該理論的適用性，以呼應其在數據驅動建模中相較於標準布朗運動更加普及的現況；以及 (3) 透過結合傅立葉-餘弦方法 (Fourier-cosine method) [30, 31, 52, 62,63,75,76] 和機器學習技術 [33, 34, 49]，針對不同導出的前向-後向系統開發系統性且行之有效的數值近似方案。因篇幅限制，我們在此僅列出最相關的文獻。

14300325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300325.value: 巽他火山弧長期火山熱演化的動力學研究

14300325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300325.value: The study investigates the connection between long-term changes in surface temperature and the eruptions in the Sunda Volcanic Arc, an area with a high risk of volcanic activity. The project meets the urgent need for eruption forecasting and risk mitigation in this densely populated area by focusing on subtle, pre-eruptive thermal signals that traditional monitoring systems miss. The main hypothesis is that a volcano's thermal history, particularly its long-term thermal anomaly evolution, reveals its eruptive potential and magmatic system dynamics. Utilizing the Sunda Arc's distinctive characteristics—such as its active volcanoes and diverse eruption styles—the study explores the relationship between eruption behavior and thermal patterns. “Open” systems generate effusive eruptions because magma moves and releases gases easily, where the thermal anomaly may be more localized to the summit. Explosive eruptions occur in "closed" systems when trapped magma and gases build up pressure, causing a larger-scale thermal anomaly through gas percolation in the edifice. To distinguish between “open” and “closed” behaviors, we will construct a long-term thermal dataset using MODIS and Landsat-8 TIRS to identify minute surface temperature changes before eruptions. Another critical component of the research is to establish a sophisticated numerical model integrating heat transfer, fluid flow, and solid mechanics of volcanic systems. This model will improve the previous modeling by considering changes in fluid phases, carbon dioxide as volcanic gases, and the interplay between hydrothermal processes and magma reservoir dynamics. The proposed research will decipher the causes of the long-term thermal anomalies and how they relate to the eruption potentials by comparing model results with the thermal evolution observations from this research and the published surface deformation data. The modeling of subsurface fluid flow can also benefit geothermal energy research, advancing clean and sustainable energy development. Finally, the project uses the Ensemble Kalman Filter, a data-model fusion framework, to integrate models with data for eruption forecasting. Using previous eruptions as training cases, we will adjust the forecasting framework to find the best model parameters, identify patterns that may indicate future eruptions, and assess our forecasting uncertainty. We will create a robust, nearly real-time forecasting system based on thermal monitoring. This will have a significant impact on assessing risk and reducing hazards in the Sunda Volcanic Arc. 這項研究探討了巽他火山弧中地表溫度長期變化與火山噴發之間的關聯。巽他火山弧是一個火山活動風險極高的地區，且人口稠密，因此預測火山噴發和降低風險的需求尤為迫切。本研究的重點是傳統監測系統無法捕捉到的微弱的火山噴發前熱信號。研究的主要假設是，一座火山的熱歷史，特別是其長期熱異常的演變，可以揭示其噴發潛力以及岩漿系統的動態。 利用巽他火山弧的獨特特徵，如活躍的火山和多樣的噴發類型，研究探討了火山噴發行為與熱模式之間的關係。「開放型」系統中的岩漿和氣體可以輕鬆流動並釋放，導致溫和的溢流式噴發，此時熱異常主要局限於火山頂部區域。而「封閉型」系統中，岩漿和氣體被困住，壓力逐漸增加，最終引發劇烈的爆炸式噴發，並通過氣體滲透在火山結構內部產生更大範圍的熱異常。為了區分這兩種噴發行為，研究將利用 MODIS衛星數據構建一個長期的熱數據集，捕捉噴發前的微小地表溫度變化。 研究的另一個重要部分是建立一個先進的數值模型，結合火山系統中的熱傳輸、流體流動和固體力學。這個模型將改進以往的模擬，考慮流體相變、二氧化碳等火山氣體的作用，以及水熱過程與岩漿庫動態的相互影響。通過將模型結果與本研究的熱演化觀測數據以及已發表的地表變形數據進行比較，研究將揭示長期熱異常的成因及其與噴發潛力的關係。此外，對地下流體流動的模擬還可以為地熱能研究提供幫助，推動清潔和可持續能源的發展。 最後，該項目將使用集成卡爾曼濾波（Ensemble Kalman Filter），一種數據與模型融合的框架，來整合模型和數據進行火山噴發預測。通過使用過去的噴發作為訓練案例，調整預測框架以找到最佳模型參數，識別可能預示未來噴發的模式，並評估預測的不確定性。研究將基於熱監測構建一個穩健的、接近實時的預測系統，對巽他火山弧的風險評估和危害減少具有重大影響。

14300425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300425.value: 針對具資訊性刪除資料之正則化 Copula 生存模型

14300425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300425.value: Survival models such as the proportional hazards (PH) model provide a versatile and flexible tool for relating survival outcomes to potential covariates in biomedical, epidemiological, economic, and social-psychological studies. Conventional survival models typically assume that the censoring mechanism is non-informative, i.e., given covariates, the failure and censoring times are independent. However, the independent censoring assumption may not hold in practical studies; for instance, patients who withdraw from medical studies due to deterioration of their health conditions may be at greater mortality risk or suffer more adverse complications than those who remain. Thus, the reasons for the dropout could be related to the failure time. Disregarding such correlation may yield unreliable results and misleading conclusions. In addition, covariate effects may exhibit sparsity when many covariates are present. Overlooking such sparsity may lead to overfitting and reduced model interpretation. Despite available methods in variable selection or sparse estimation of survival models, existing works mainly focused on complete or non-informatively censored data. When informative censoring occurs, the regularized estimation of covariate effects on survival outcomes becomes highly challenging, and available state-of-the-art approaches are still lacking. This proposal aims to develop a regularized copula-based PH model to analyze survival data subject to informative censoring. The proposed model can reveal an unobservable dependence between the failure and censoring times. A sparse estimation procedure is developed to simultaneously select significant covariates and estimate the baseline hazard functions and regression coefficients. Unlike most existing penalization procedures that inevitably compute the inverse of the Hessian matrix and thus deal with the singularity issue, we aim to develop an efficient algorithm to avoid this problem and considerably save computational costs. Useful extensions include (i) modeling the multi-center competing risks data subject to informative censoring, (ii) extending the current model to high-dimensional settings, and (iii) generalizing the proposed method to broader model frameworks, such as partially linear additive PH, single-index PH, and transformation models, which are the vital variants of the proposed model. As for statistical inference, this project intends to conduct penalized procedures for dimension reduction, develop semiparametric techniques to estimate baseline hazard functions and regression coefficients/functions, uncover the correlation between failure and censoring times, and investigate the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. No existing method is available to accomplish these tasks. We will develop user-friendly computer programs/packages for statistical analysis and apply the methodologies to real problems in Hong Kong and other settings. 在生物醫學、流行病學、經濟學及社會心理學等領域中，生存模型（如比例風險模型）為探討存活結果與潛在共變數之間關係提供了靈活且多樣的分析工具。傳統生存模型通常假設刪除機制為非資訊性，即在給定共變數的情況下，失敗時間與刪除時間相互獨立。然而，在實際研究中，獨立刪除的假設往往不成立。例如，因健康狀況惡化而退出臨床研究的患者，相較於持續參與者可能面臨更高的死亡風險或更嚴重的併發症。因此，退出的原因可能與失敗時間相關。忽略此類相關性可能導致不可靠的結果與誤導性的結論。此外，當共變數數量龐大時，其效應可能呈現稀疏性。若未考慮此稀疏性，可能導致模型過度擬合並降低解釋力。儘管目前已有針對變數選擇或稀疏估計的生存模型方法，現有研究多集中於完整或非資訊性刪除資料。當資料存在資訊性刪除時，對共變數效應進行正則化估計將面臨高度挑戰，而現有尖端方法仍付之闕如。 本研究計畫旨在發展一套正則化的 Copula 基礎比例風險模型，以分析受資訊性刪除影響之存活資料。所提出模型可揭示失敗時間與刪除時間之間不可觀測的依賴結構。我們將建立一套稀疏估計程序，以同時選取顯著共變數並估計基準風險函數與迴歸係數。不同於多數現有的懲罰估計方法需計算Hessian矩陣的逆矩陣並面臨奇異性問題，我們擬發展一套高效演算法以避免此問題並大幅降低計算成本。本計畫之延伸方向包括：(一) 建構可處理多中心競爭風險且受資訊性刪除影響之資料模型；(二) 擴展現有模型至高維度設定；(三) 推廣所提方法至更廣泛的模型架構，如部分線性加法比例風險模型、單指標比例風險模型及轉換模型等，皆為本模型的重要變體。在統計推論方面，本計畫將進行懲罰程序以達成降維，發展半參數技術以估計基準風險函數與迴歸係數／函數，揭示失敗時間與刪除時間之間的相關性，並探討所得估計量之漸近性質。目前尚無現有方法可同時完成上述任務。我們亦將開發便利的統計分析程式，並將所建方法應用於香港及其他地區的實際問題。

14300525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300525.value: 非常規相二維銠納米催化劑用於高效電催化合成氨

14300525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300525.value: Ammonia (NH3) plays key roles in agricultural, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries, directly affecting the balance of ecological nitrogen cycle. Traditional ammonia synthesis heavily relies on the energy-consuming Harbor Bosh process, which requires expensive feedstock and high operating temperature. Electroreduction of nitrate is a “two-birds-with-one-stone” strategy for synthesizing ammonia, which not only realizes low-carbon-emission ammonia production at room temperature, but also consumes hazardous N-containing species from industrial wastes and combustion pollutants, shining light to simultaneous sustainable ammonia synthesis and economical water pollution control. Lack of high-performance catalyst is a bottleneck challenge in promoting electrochemical nitrate-to-ammonia conversion towards practical applications. Rhodium (Rh) has intrinsically high selectivity for ammonia among reported catalysts, but it still suffers from high cost and high overpotential. Designing and modulating catalyst surfaces at nanometer scale can realize kinetics control of catalytic intermediates on catalyst surface at a molecular level, while the catalyst cost is exponentially reduced due to the huge surface-to-volume ratio of nanocatalysts. Particularly, constructing unconventional-phase metal nanocatalysts is recently demonstrated very effective to create intrinsically more active metal surfaces with high-density, built-in active sites. These unique structural advantages can be maximized and stabilized on a two-dimensional (2D) morphology. Therefore, construction of unconventional-phase 2D Rh nanosurfaces holds great promise in advancing next-generation ammonia electrosynthesis. In this project, we aim to develop a series of unreported 2D Rh nanomaterials towards highly efficient and selective nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. First, we first tackle the key obstacle in constructing unconventional-phase Rh nanomaterials via an innovative compound-derived synthetic route. Our preliminary results demonstrated the successful preparation of pure and uniform hexagonal close-packed Rh nanoplates with well-defined new surfaces, which show better selectivity, yield rate, and overpotential in ammonia production compared to conventional-phase Rh. Inspired by this, other unconventional-phase 2D Rh nanocatalysts will be designed and synthesized. Their formation mechanisms will be understood. Second, comprehensive study of their Faradaic efficiency, yield rate, and long-term stability towards ammonia production will be carried out, and the crystal phase-dependent catalytic behaviors of Rh with facet accuracy will be derived. In-depth mechanism investigations will be conducted using in situ spectroscopies and theoretical simulation. Key reaction intermediate and origin of phase dependency will be revealed. Lastly, scale-up fabrication of the Rh nanocatalysts towards large-scale ammonia electrosynthesis will be realized. This project will provide new synthetic routes for novel inorganic nanomaterials and offer fundamental guidelines in developing advanced metal electrocatalysts for simultaneous pollutants removal and green chemical synthesis. 氨（NH3）在農業、化工和製藥工業中發揮著重要作用，直接影響著生態氮循環的平衡。傳統的氨合成嚴重依賴於高耗能的Harbor Bosh工藝，該工藝需要昂貴的原料和較高的操作溫度。硝酸鹽電還原是一種“一箭雙雕”的氨合成方法，不僅可實現室溫下的氨生產，而且還能回收利用工業廢棄物和燃燒污染物中的有害含氮物質，為同時實現可持續的氨合成和水污染控制帶來了希望。目前，缺乏高性能催化劑是推動硝酸鹽電化學轉化為氨走向實際應用的瓶頸之一。在已報導的催化劑中，銠（Rh）催化劑對產氨具有較高的選擇性，但其仍然存在成本高和過電位高等問題。在納米尺度上設計和調控催化劑表面，可以在分子水平實現對催化劑表面催化中間體的動力學控制，同時由於納米催化劑巨大的比表面積，催化劑成本可以成倍降低。最近，構建非常規相金屬納米催化劑被證明能夠非常有效地創建具有高密度本徵活性位點的金屬表面。這些獨特的結構優勢可以在二維（2D）形貌上最大化和穩定化。因此，構建非常規相二維Rh納米表面在推進下一代氨電合成方面具有巨大的潛力。在本項目中，我們旨在開發一系列未報導的二維Rh納米材料，以實現高效、高選擇性的硝酸鹽到氨的轉化。首先，我們通過創新合成路線攻克了構建非常規相Rh納米材料的關鍵障礙。我們的初步結果成功製備了純淨、均勻、具有清晰新表面的六方密堆積Rh納米片。與傳統相Rh相比，其在氨合成中表現出更高的選擇性、產率和過電位。受此啟發，我們將設計並合成其他非常規相二維Rh納米催化劑，並深入探究其形成機理。其次，我們將全面研究氨合成的法拉第效率、產率和長期穩定性，並推導出精確到晶面的Rh催化行爲的晶相依賴性。我們將利用原位光譜和理論模擬進行深入的機理研究，揭示關鍵反應中間體及其相依賴性的起源。最後，我們將實現Rh納米催化劑的規模化製備，以實現大規模氨電合成。本項目將為新型無機納米材料的合成提供新路線，並為開發可同時去除污染物和實現綠色化學合成的先進金屬電催化劑提供基礎指導。

14300925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300925.value: 以計算機建模與模擬探索空泡細胞毒素VacA的結構、動力學和激活機制

14300925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300925.value: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a bacterial pathogen that infects over half of the global population. As a pore-forming toxin (PFT) and a major virulence factor secreted by H. pylori, the vacuolating cytotoxin A (VacA) is known to insert into the plasma as well as intracellular membranes of its target cell to form an anion-selective, hexameric channel. While cryo-electron microscopy studies have uncovered the flower-like structures of VacA oligomers, no atomic model of its transmembrane channel could be directly constructed from these electron density maps due to their limited resolution. In addition, the segment corresponding to the transmembrane channel is also unresolved in VacA structure when the toxin is in its water-soluble state. We have developed a computational protocol that combines exhaustive conformational scan with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the transmembrane channel of VacA. Building upon this preliminary work and joining forces with our experimental collaborator, here, we aim to elucidate the molecular mechanism of VacA's cytotoxicity through systematically exploring its structure, dynamics and activation. Specifically, we plan to (1) model the transition of VacA from its water-soluble to membrane-inserted state, (2) quantify the impact of lipid composition on its membrane association and channel formation, (3) elucidate molecular details of VacA acid and alkaline activation and (4) explore how an extra 12-amino acid N-terminal segment hinders VacA channel formation and alters its oligomeric state. By capturing VacA-induced membrane pore formation in atomic detail, our work will offer a mechanistic understanding of the cytotoxicity presented by this important virulence factor. Molecular details of its action and key residues identified in the membrane association, pore formation and acid/alkaline activation of VacA may further guide the development of new therapeutic strategies targeting H. pylori infection. Finally, the computational protocols developed in the proposed work can be readily employed in the structural and mechanistic investigations of other PFTs. 幽門螺旋桿菌（H. pylori）是一種感染全球過半人口的細菌性病原體。作為該菌分泌的成孔毒素和主要毒力因子，空泡細胞毒素A（VacA）能夠插入目標細胞的質膜及內膜系統，形成具有陰離子選擇性的六聚體通道。儘管冷凍電鏡研究已揭示VacA寡聚體的花狀結構，但由於電子密度圖解析度不足，其跨膜通道的原子模型未能被建構。此外，當VacA處於水溶狀態時，其跨膜通道片段的結構也未能被解析。我們開發了一套結合構象窮舉掃描與分子動力學模擬的計算方案，成功構建了VacA的跨膜通道模型。基於前期工作並與實驗團隊合作，本項目擬通過系統研究VacA的結構、動力學與活化機制來闡明其細胞毒性的分子基礎。具體來說，我們計劃：（1）模擬VacA從水溶態向膜嵌入態的轉變過程；（2）量化脂質組成對其膜結合與通道形成的影響；（3）解析VacA酸/鹼激活的分子細節；（4）探究12個胺基酸的N端延伸片段如何阻礙通道形成並改變寡聚狀態。通過原子尺度再現VacA誘導的膜孔形成機制，本研究將為這一關鍵毒力因子的細胞毒性提供機理闡釋。這一過程中揭示的膜結合、成孔及酸/鹼激活過程中的分子細節與關鍵殘基，則有望為幽門螺旋桿菌感染的新療法開發提供指導。此外，本研究所建立的計算方法可應用於其他成孔毒素的結構與機制研究。

14301225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301225.value: The study of water waves from a purely mathematical viewpoint has blossomed over the past three decades or so. Yet much of this activity has focused on irrotational water waves. Enhancing our understanding of rotational water waves, which are commonplace in nature is important, as various phenomena such as wind forcing, can generate vorticity. In this project, we propose to study solutions to 2D free-boundary Euler equations modeling the motion of water waves with rotational initial data from different directions. On the one hand, we study the stability of 2D water waves by showing the long-time evolution of a certain class of small rotational initial data. On the other hand, we investigate the instability of 2D water waves by showing some vast deformation of the moving boundary driven by certain choices of the initial vorticity. The emphasis is on the role played by the vorticity. 從純數學的角度研究水波，在過去大約三十年間蓬勃發展。然而，這方面的研究大多集中在無旋水波上。增強對自然界中常見的旋轉水波的理解至關重要，因為風力作用等各種現象都可能產生渦度。在本專案中，我們擬從不同方向研究二維自由邊界歐拉方程的解，該方程用於模擬具有旋轉初始數據的水波運動。一方面，我們通過展示一類小型旋轉初始數據的長期演化來研究二維水波的穩定性；另一方面，我們通過展示由特定初始渦度選擇驅動的移動邊界的巨大變形，來探究二維水波的不穩定性。重點在於渦度所扮演的角色。

14301425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301425.value: 少體強相互作用費米子的流體力學與集體激發

14301425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301425.value: Hydrodynamics, traditionally a macroscopic theory, describes fluid dynamics of systems composed of numerous microscopic particles. While hydrodynamics typically requires reaching the thermodynamic limit or coarse-graining over identical cells, this stringent requirement may not apply to quantum systems. Few bosons at low temperature could exhibit a order N occupation of single-particle orbitals, governed by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, which can be reformulated as Euler's equation. Together with the continuity equation, they form the hydrodynamic equations for few bosons. For fermions, the situation is less clear. Recent experiments with strongly interacting fermions in two dimensions have observed elliptic flow in systems with as few as eight particles, a phenomenon typically described by hydrodynamic theory. While the dynamics was hydrodynamic at short time, it become ballistic and cannot be captured by the same hydrodynamic theory. This proposal aims to study hydrodynamics for few-fermion systems. We will explore elliptic flow in this regime by numerically solving for the ground state of strongly interacting few-body fermionic systems using explicitly correlated Gaussian technique. We will then simulate time-dependent expansion dynamics to extract the full dynamics, analyzing both short- and long-time asymptotic behavior to extract corresponding hydrodynamic parameters. Subsequently, we will investigate collective excitations in few-body systems with path integral Monte Carlo in addition, focusing on the breathing and scissors modes. The breathing mode exhibits an anomaly in the few-body limit, while the scissors mode could probe angular momentum and quantum moment of inertia. We expect to uncover an anomaly in the quantum moment of inertia for spin-imbalanced few-fermion systems. Finally, we will investigate the time-dependent Kohn-Sham equation in few-body systems, focusing on the non-Markovian nature of the time-dependent effective potential arising from interactions. While this has been seldomly studied in density functional theories in chemistry due to its complexity, we believe that the simple form of short-range interactions between cold atom is ideal for in-depth analysis. This approach could lead to the development of a hydrodynamic-like formulation for few-particle systems. The effective potential could be crucial in explaining the crossover from initial hydrodynamic behavior to final ballistic expansion in elliptic flow. Moreover, the time-dependent Kohn-Sham equation will not only support our understanding of few-body collective modes but also serve as a valuable cross-check. To summarize, this research aims to bridge the gap between few-body and many-body physics, providing insights into hydrodynamic theory and the emergence of collective phenomena, potentially inspiring new experimental realizations in the near future. 流體力學通常描述大量粒子的宏觀行爲，但其在僅有少數量子粒子組成的系統中的適用性尚不明確。近期實驗發現，少數強相互作用的費米子系統在短時間內表現出流體力學特徵（如橢圓流），但隨後迅速轉變爲無法用該理論描述的彈道式膨脹。 本研究旨在通過大規模數值模擬來解開這一謎題。我們將運用多種前沿計算方法系統地研究少體費米子系統的動力學過程，主要目標如下：1.揭示系統從初始流體力學行爲到最終彈道式膨脹的轉變機制。2.探索系統中的集體激發模式（如呼吸模和剪刀模），並預測新的量子現象。總而言之，該研究期望連接少體與多體物理的鴻溝，深化我們對集體現象如何從微觀層面湧現的理解，併爲未來的冷原子實驗提供重要的理論指導。

14301725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301725.value: 雙層籠目反鐵磁金屬中由平帶產生的近藤效應在壓力與厚度下的調控

14301725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301725.value: An important goal of materials research is to design systems with flat bands in their electronic structure, as flat bands can promote interesting correlated phenomena by quenching kinetic energy. The kagome lattice, formed by corner-sharing triangles, naturally hosts a flat band, Dirac cones and van Hove singularities. When the Fermi energy is close to the flat band, kagome metals become ideal platforms for exploring physics related to the flat band. This project aims to study CsCr6Sb6, an antiferromagnetic metal in which chromium atoms form kagome double nets. Intriguingly, the flat band in CsCr6Sb6 is located very near the Fermi energy, creating the source of local moments that are responsible for Kondo and Ruderman–Kittel–Kasuya–Yosida (RKKY) interactions. Building on our success in synthesizing CsCr6Sb6, we are in the privileged position to collect unique data. We will conduct comprehensive magnetotransport measurements on thin flakes of CsCr6Sb6 under pressure to understanding how various phases can be tuned by sample thickness and hydrostatic pressure. We will focus on the evolution of the Neel temperature to explore a potential magnetic quantum phase transition. A careful search of superconductivity will be conducted near the quantum phase transition. Finally, we will study the metallic state using Shubnikov-de Haas quantum oscillations to understand the effect of the flat band on conduction electrons.

14301825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301825.value: 紐結與圖論：從亞歷山大多項式出發

14301825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301825.value: Knots are more than just tangles in shoelaces - they are a fascinating area of mathematical study. Researchers hope to distinguish different knots, measure their complexity, and reveal their geometric and topological properties. The Alexander polynomial, a cornerstone in knot theory, has profoundly influenced the development of the field. This project aims to extend this fundamental study to spatial graphs, building upon the PI's prior work in developing an Alexander polynomial for graphs. By synthesizing ideas from knot theory and graph theory, we hope to make significant advances in understanding how graphs and other one-dimensional objects can be embedded in three-dimensional space. Our research will explore different ways to calculate and interpret the graph Alexander polynomial, using concepts like spanning trees (imagine the smallest number of branches needed to connect all points in a network) and Seifert surfaces (picture a soap film spanning a wire frame). These approaches promise new insights into the topological and combinatorial properties of embedded graphs. One exciting goal is to use our new tools to tackle a long-standing problem in knot theory known as Fox's trapezoidal conjecture. Solving this could be a major breakthrough in the field. Finally, we will work on developing a more advanced version of our polynomial invariant, called categorification. This is inspired by Heegaard Floer homology, which has revolutionized classical knot invariants. This approach could lead to even more powerful ways of analyzing spatial graphs and strengthening many results and applications, mirroring the impact of Floer homology in knot theory. 紐帶不僅出現在鞋帶上，更是一個引人入勝的數學研究領域。研究者致力於區分不同的結、測量其複雜度，並揭示其幾何和拓樸性質。亞歷山大多項式作為紐結理論的基石，對該領域的發展產生了深遠的影響。本計畫旨在運用專案負責人早先建立的亞歷山大多項式的工作對空間圖進行理論研究。透過綜合結理論和圖論的思想，我們希望能深入理解空間圖和其他一維物體在嵌入三維空間時的性質。 我們將從不同角度探索圖亞歷山大多項式，包括運用生成樹（想像連接網絡中所有點所需的最少分支數）和Seifert曲面（設想張在線框上的肥皂膜）等概念。這些方法有望為嵌入圖的拓樸和組合性質提供新的見解。一個大目標是運用我們的新工具來嘗試紐結理論中長期懸而未決的Fox梯形猜想。解決此問題將為該領域帶來重大突破。 最後，我們將致力於發展此多項式不變量的更高級版本——範疇化。Heegaard Floer同調可視為模板，已徹底革新了經典紐結不變量。我們期待更先進的研究工具能帶來更強大的結果和應用。

14302225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302225.value: 3d mirror symmetry is a powerful, yet mysterious duality between dual symplectic resolutions. By studying functorality of SYZ mirror symmetry for its 2d branes, the PI plans to develop a SYZ type construction and transformation to explain 3d mirror symmetry via geometric means. 三維鏡像對稱性是介於對偶辛解析之間的一種強大而又神秘的對偶性。透過研究SYZ鏡像對稱性在其二維膜上的函數性，PI計畫發展出一種SYZ類型的構造和變換，以幾何方法解釋三維鏡像對稱性。

14302325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302325.value: 四維的 Seiberg-Witten與 Heegaard Floer 理論

14302325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302325.value: The PI proposes to continue her study on the relation between gauge theoretic invariants and Gromov-type invariants under the framework of Taubes’s proof of “Seiberg-Witten equals Gromov''. In a series of papers joint with Taubes and Kutluhan [KLT1-KLT5], the PI proved the equivalence of four corresponding flavors of Seiberg-Witten Floer homologies with Heegaard Floer homologies. According to Atiyah's TQFT (topologial quantum field theory) principle [A1], the natutual next step is to extend these results about 3-manifolds to 4-manifolds and cobordisms, and indeed there are long-standing conjectures on the equivalence (modulo certain ambiguities) of the Seiberg-Witten and Heegaard Floer invariants of cobordisms and closed 4-manifolds [OS2a]. The present proposal aims to prove these conjectures. 本計劃提議證明Seiberg-Witten與 Heegaard Floer 理論中的四維不變量等價。

14302425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302425.value: 上層海洋分層變化如何與間冰期期間北大西洋深水通風不穩定性相關聯？

14302425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302425.value: Ocean circulation, previously popularized as 'the Great Conveyor Belt', plays a crucial role in regulating global climate. For decades, scientists believed this system remained stable during warm periods of Earth’s history, only slowing significantly during major climate transitions. However, recent advances in paleoceanography have challenged this view, revealing that the ocean's Great Conveyor Belt has been more variable than previously thought, even during relatively stable warm periods. This discovery challenges our previous understanding of how stable the ocean's circulation has been during Earth's warmer periods like today. This is a significant discovery as these episodes were triggered by relatively subtle change in surface conditions and not necessary by massive meltwater outburst as previously believed. It suggests that deep-water formation may be disrupted relatively more easily than previously thought. With global warming already causing observable changes in ocean temperature and salinity, this finding raises serious concerns that even the current climate change could potentially disrupt this critical component of Earth's climate system, leading to severe and far-reaching consequences for global climate stability. Therefore, we need to generate new knowledge about how relatively subtle variations in temperature and salinity in surface water have impacted stratification, deep water formation, and circulation in the North Atlantic during previous warm periods. In this study, we will use foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotopes to reconstruct nutrient utilization and upper-ocean stratification during Marine Isotope Stage 11 (MIS11), a period suggested to be slightly warmer than today. By investigating how subtle variations in stratification affected deep water formation in the North Atlantic during this time, we aim to better understand the potential impacts of current global warming on ocean dynamics. Additionally, we will use oxygen isotopes in planktic foraminifera shells to reconstruct temperature and salinity, providing further insights into upper-ocean stratification. Carbon isotopes in benthic foraminifera shells will also be utilized to quantify deep water formation changes. By focusing on core sites with existing chronostratigraphy in the Labrador Sea and the North Atlantic, two sites where we can monitor deep-water ventilation, we will assess the variability of surface and bottom conditions during MIS11. By unraveling how our oceans responded to past climate shifts, this study will provide crucial insights into the far-reaching consequences of human-induced global warming on ocean circulation, helping us better prepare for the challenges that lie ahead in a rapidly changing world. 海洋環流，過去被通俗地稱為「大洋傳送帶」，在調節全球氣候方面發揮著關鍵作用。數十年來，科學家們相信這個系統在地球歷史的溫暖時期保持穩定，只有在重大氣候轉換期間才會顯著減緩。然而，古海洋學的最新進展挑戰了這一觀點，揭示出海洋的大洋傳送帶比先前認為的更加多變，即使是在相對穩定的溫暖時期也是如此。這一發現挑戰了我們對海洋環流在地球溫暖時期（如今日）穩定性的先前理解。這是一個重大發現，因為這些事件是由表面條件相對微妙的變化所觸發的，而非如先前所認為的大規模融水爆發所必需引起的。這表明深水形成可能比先前認為的更容易受到干擾。隨著全球暖化已經在海洋溫度和鹽度方面造成可觀察到的變化，這一發現引起了嚴重擔憂，即使是當前的氣候變化也可能破壞地球氣候系統的這一關鍵組成部分，導致對全球氣候穩定性產生嚴重且深遠的後果。 因此，我們需要產生新的知識，了解表面水溫度和鹽度的相對微妙變化如何在先前的溫暖時期影響了北大西洋的分層、深水形成和環流。在這項研究中，我們將使用有孔蟲結合的氮同位素來重建海洋同位素階段11（MIS11）期間的營養物質利用和上層海洋分層，這一時期被認為比今日稍微溫暖。通過調查分層的微妙變化如何在此期間影響北大西洋的深水形成，我們旨在更好地理解當前全球暖化對海洋動力學的潛在影響。此外，我們將使用浮游有孔蟲殼中的氧同位素來重建溫度和鹽度，為上層海洋分層提供進一步的洞察。底棲有孔蟲殼中的碳同位素也將被用於量化深水形成的變化。通過專注於拉布拉多海和北大西洋現有年代地層學的岩心站點，這兩個我們可以監測深水通風的地點，我們將評估MIS11期間表面和底層條件的變異性。通過揭示我們的海洋如何回應過去的氣候變化，這項研究將為人類引起的全球暖化對海洋環流的深遠後果提供關鍵洞察，幫助我們更好地為在快速變化的世界中即將到來的挑戰做好準備。

14302525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302525.value: 不可壓縮密度依賴型 Navier-Stokes 方程式的 Lions 密度塊問題

14302525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302525.value: In geophysical flows such as oceans or rivers, although the fluid is practically incompressible the density and viscosity cannot be considered as constant quantities, as a consequence of mixture of fluids. The incompressible density-dependent Navier-Stokes equations (DDNS) are a basic model describing the evolution of incompressible viscous fluids with variable density and viscosity. In multi-phase fluid dynamics, density and viscosity discontinuities are common. The density patch problem raised by P.-L. Lions concerns whether or not DDNS preserve the initial regularity of the interface given by a piecewise constant density with vacuum. Compared with the case of constant viscosity, where the regularity of the interface was shown propagated globally-in-time and thus no cusp creates in finite-time, however, for the case that the viscosity is a smooth positive function on density, Lions’ question is widely open. Despite its significance in applications and the theory for fluid mechanics, it remains a challenging problem whether strong solutions with merely non-negative bounded initial density and general viscosity must exist in suitable function spaces, even locally-in-time for any initial data. One of the main difficulties is that the coupling between the viscosity and the velocity caused a nonlinear diffusion term and the viscosity is discontinuous. It appears a loss of derivatives phenomenon when performing direct energy estimates for the velocity equation, which makes it challenging to establish gradient estimates for the velocity. The second major difficulty is that for DDNS evolve in a vacuum, the velocity equation is degenerate such that the natural energy balance does not imply the velocity field is of finite-energy, unlike the non-vacuum case. This situation is more complicated in unbounded domains, due to the lack of Poincaré-type inequalities. The purpose of this project is to establish the existence, regularity and stability of strong solutions for DDNS with general viscosity in the whole-space case, supplemented with piecewise smooth initial density that allowing for arbitrary large jumps and vacuum, and give a partial answer to Lions’ density patch problem with variable viscosity. We propose to study these problems by using a Lagrangian approach and technique of striated regularity, and developing new regularity theory for suitable linearized system that can eventually help to solve the nonlinear problem. These ideas and techniques will lead to resolve some problems in the field, particularly the well-posedness issue in bounded function spaces for hyperbolic-parabolic type equations, that is linked to nonlinear diffusion phenomenon. 在海洋或河流等地球物理流動中，儘管流體幾乎不可壓縮，但由於流體混合，密度和黏度不能被視為常數。不可壓縮密度依賴型納維-斯托克斯方程式 (DDNS) 是描述具有可變密度和黏度的不可壓縮黏性流體演化的基本模型。在多相流體動力學中，密度和黏度的不連續性很常見。 P.-L. Lions 提出的密度塊問題涉及 DDNS 是否保持由分段常數密度與真空給出的界面的初始正則性。在常數黏度的情況下界面的正則性在時間上全局傳播，因此在有限時間內不會產生尖點。但是，對於黏度是密度的光滑正函數的情況，Lions 的問題則懸而未決。儘管其在應用和流體力學理論中具有重要意義，但對於任何初始數據，在合適的函數空間中是否存在僅具有非負有界初始密度和一般粘度的強解，甚至局部時間強解，仍然是一個具有挑戰性的問題。主要困難之一是黏度和速度之間的耦合導致了非線性擴散現象，並且黏度是不連續的。在對速度方程式進行直接能量估計時，會出現導數損失現象，這使得建立速度的梯度估計具有挑戰性。第二個主要困難是，對於在真空中演化的DDNS，速度方程式是退化的，因此先驗的能量平衡並不意味著速度場具有有限能量，這與非真空情況不同。由於缺乏龐加萊型不等式，這種情況在無界域中更為複雜。 本計畫旨在建立具有一般黏性的DDNS強解的存在性、正則性和穩定性，在全空間情況下，輔以允許任意大跳躍和真空的分段光滑初始密度，並給出Lions密度塊問題的部分答案。我們計劃使用拉格朗日方法和切向正則性技術來研究這些問題，並針對合適的線性化系統開發新的正則性理論，最終用於解決非線性問題。這些思想和技術將有助於解決該領域的一些問題，特別是與非線性擴散現象相關的雙曲-拋物型方程式在有界函數空間中的適定性問題。

14302725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302725.value: 拓撲相變和長程相互作用系統

14302725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302725.value: Landau’s theory states that phases are completely defined by their symmetries and phase transitions happen when certain symmetry is spontaneously broken. However, the discovery of topological ordered (TO) states has challenged Landau' s theory, because these states have exactly the same symmetry while belonging to different phases. In fact, topological order is defined by its non-symmetry global properties including ground state degeneracy, fractionalized excitations, edge states, and long-range (LR) entanglement patterns. On the other hand, studies on quantum many body systems have primarily focused on systems with short-range interactions, because in most experimental systems the LR Coulomb interactions between electrons are screened to be short-ranged. However, recent experimental realizations of various LR interaction systems (mostly in power-law form), including dipolar systems and Rydberg atoms, have emphasized the importance of understanding systems with LR interactions. As Landau’s theory fails in describing TO states, there lacks a systematic approach to study the transitions between them. The study on LR interactions faces similar dilemma: previous field theory approaches are mainly based on assumption of locality which is apparently broken in systems with LR interactions. Furthermore, LR interactions can also intersect with topological order which makes the situation more complex. We aim to overcome the dilemma by systematically studying these systems with advanced numerical simulations and have formulated several research avenues: (a) monitoring the behavior of entanglement entropy/spectra to identify topological phase transitions, (b) extending the concept of symmetry to unify topological order within the framework of Landau’s theory, (c) studying the stability of topological properties against LR interactions, and (d) designing experimental schemes to realize topological phase transitions induced by LR interactions. The Principal Investigator(PI) has made significant advancements in the numerical study of the critical and entanglement properties of various quantum spin systems with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The Co-Investigator(Co-I) has accomplished great success in theoretical explorations of topological order and generalized symmetry. Through close collaborations between PI and Co-I, hopefully, at the end of the proposal, we would have addressed the entanglement entropy and entanglement spectra at topological phase transitions, understood better about the generalized symmetry in topological order, obtained the whole phase diagram of a lattice model realizing topological phase transition with LR interactions, and finished the design of an experimental scheme to accomplish such systems. Our study has potential to lead to a major breakthrough in condensed matter physics. 傳統的朗道理論認為，物質相完全由其對稱性所刻畫，而相變發生於這些對稱性自發破缺之時。然而，拓撲有序態的發現對朗道理論提出挑戰，因為此類態雖具有相同的對稱性，卻屬於不同的相位。事實上，拓撲序由其內在的全域性質所定義，包括基態簡併、分數化激發、邊界態，以及長程糾纏態。量子多體系統的研究主要聚焦於短程相互作用的系統，因為在多數實驗體系中，電子之間的長程庫倫作用被屏蔽而呈現短程化。然而，近年對多種長程相互作用（多為冪律形式）系統的實驗實現——包括偶極子系統與里德堡原子——凸顯了研究長程相互作用系統之重要性。 由於朗道理論無法描述拓撲有序態，目前缺乏系統性的方法來研究其間的轉變。對長程相互作用的研究亦面臨相似困境：既有理論多以場論中的局域性假設為基礎，但在具長程相互作用的系統中此假設顯然不成立。此外，長程相互作用亦可能與拓撲序同時出現，使情況更為複雜。我們旨在透過大規模數值模擬對這些系統進行系統性研究，以克服上述困境。我們提出數個研究問題：（a）探測糾纏熵／糾纏譜之行為以辨識拓撲相變；（b）延展對稱性的概念，使拓撲序得以在朗道理論框架內統一描述；（c）研究拓撲性質在長程相互作用下之穩定性；（d）設計實驗方案以實現由長程相互作用所誘發的拓撲相變。 本計畫首席研究員運用最先進的大規模量子蒙特卡羅方法，已在（2+1）維量子臨界性與拓撲有序態之糾纏性質，以及具長程相互作用系統之臨界與糾纏性質方面取得重要進展。共同研究員則在拓撲序與廣義對稱性領域完成多項傑出工作。透過首席研究員與共同研究員的緊密合作，預期於本計畫結束時，我們將：（i）釐清拓撲相變處的糾纏熵與糾纏譜；（ii）更深入理解拓撲序中的廣義對稱性；（iii）獲得一個實現長程相互作用驅動之拓撲相變的晶格模型之完整相圖；並（iv）完成實現此類系統的實驗方案設計。上述研究可望為凝聚態物理帶來重大突破。

14302925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302925.value: 非高斯假設下的非參數圖模型：通用框架與有效估計

14302925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302925.value: Graphical models are fundamental tools for representing the conditional independence structure among random variables. Most existing methods require some specific distributional assumptions, such as Gaussian or copula Gaussian, which largely restrict their applicability in many real applications. This research project proposes a general modeling framework for nonparametric graphical models, which requires no explicit distributional assumption and allows for general dependence structures among variables. The developed framework is motivated by the fact that conditional independence among variables can be fully characterized by the second-order partial derivatives of the log density function. On this ground, the PI will develop efficient learning algorithm for both static and dynamic nonparametric graphical models, by leveraging the properties of various reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The PI will investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed nonparametric graphical models, and establish their asymptotic consistencies in terms of score estimation and exact graph recovery. The proposed models will also be applied to conduct a comparative analysis of the S&P 500 stock dataset before and after the pandemic, so as to elucidate its impact on the relationship between companies. 圖模型是表示隨機變量間條件獨立性結構的基本工具。大多數現有方法需要一些特定的分佈假設，例如高斯分佈或Copula高斯分佈，這在很大程度上限制了它們在許多實際應用中的適用性。本研究項目提出了一個非參數圖模型的通用建模框架，該框架不需要特定的分佈假設，並且允許變量之間存在一般的依賴結構。此框架的發展基於這樣一個事實：變量間的條件獨立性可以用對數密度函數的二階偏導數完全表徵。在此基礎上，專案負責人將利用各種再生核希爾伯特空間的性質，為靜態和動態非參數圖模型開發高效的學習算法。我們將研究所提出的非參數圖模型的理論性質，並建立它們在分數估計和精確圖恢復方面的漸近一致性。所提出的模型也將用於對2020年COVID-19疫情前後的標準普爾500股票資料集進行比較分析，以闡明其對公司間關係的影響。

14303125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303125.value: 關於臨界或超臨界狀態的藤田方程

14303125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303125.value: Fujita equation is one of the fundamental nonlinear parabolic equations. It arise in many applied fields such as chemical reaction, phase transitions, MEMS, etc. In this proposal we plan to use variational method and geometric measure theory to study the blowup mechanism and the associated concentration phenomena for the Fujita equation in the critical or supercritical regime. Through the work of the Giga and Kohn, Merle and Zaag, the blow-up in the subcritical case has almost been completely characterized. In the critical or supercritical case rich and complicated phenomena are discovered and there are less research in the literature due to the lack of good tools and methods.
