Given the opportunity to utilize a multi-centre maternity cohort in the Asian area, our study aims to investigate the temperature-preeclampsia association, identify the critical window time of exposure, and examine the modification effect of SES factors on the temperature-preeclampsia association. A multi-centre retrospective cohort study will be conducted across 20 maternity units in Asia region, including Hong Kong, Mainland China, Taiwan, Singapore, Thailand, The Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Japan. The cohort will consist of women aged 18 and above with viable singleton pregnancies from August 2019 to February 2022. Individual exposure to ambient temperature and other meteorological factors will be assessed using remote sensing data. Socioeconomic factors will be assessed using Geographic Information System (GIS) tools and satellite imagery. A lag-distributed nonlinear model will be employed to analyze the relationship between extreme temperatures and preeclampsia, adjusting for confounding variables such as air pollutants and gestational factors. The findings of this project are helpful to researchers for further understanding the etiology of preeclampsia. In addition, with critical window time and socioeconomic modifiers identified, the findings will help healthcare providers develop the prevention strategy for pregnant women, especially those who are at a high risk of preeclampsia onset. 全球氣候變化背景下，極端高溫事件的持續和加劇對弱勢群體，尤其是孕婦構成越來越大的健康威脅。懷孕期間的生理變化，例如代謝增加和血容量上升，可能削弱身體調節能力。以往研究報告指出環境溫度與子癇前症之間存在顯著關聯，但關聯的強度和方向並不一致。至今尚無研究確定子癇前症發病的非最佳環境溫度暴露的關鍵時段，而這可能有助於理解潛在機制。單中心研究設計限制了氣候類型的多樣性以及缺乏與子癇前症相關的妊娠因素，可能導致結果的不一致。此外，僅有少量研究探討了社會經濟因素對溫度與子癇前症關聯的中介效應。基於利用亞洲地區多中心孕產婦隊列的機會，本研究旨在探討溫度與子癇前症的關聯，確定暴露的關鍵時段，並檢驗社會經濟因素對溫度與子癇前症關聯的修飾效應。本研究將在亞洲地區20個孕產中心進行多中心回顧性隊列研究，包括香港、中國內地、台灣、新加坡、泰國、菲律賓、印尼、馬來西亞、越南和日本。隊列將包括2019年8月至2022年2月期間，年齡18歲及以上且懷有可存活單胎妊娠的女性。個體環境溫度及其他氣象因素的暴露將使用遙感數據進行評估。社會經濟因素將使用地理信息系統（GIS）工具和衛星影像進行評估。研究將採用滯後分布非線性模型分析極端溫度與子癇前症之間的關係，並調整空氣污染物和妊娠因素等混雜變量。本項目結果將幫助研究人員進一步理解子癇前症的病因。此外，通過確定關鍵時段和社會經濟修飾因素，研究結果將幫助醫療提供者為孕婦，特別是子癇前症高風險群體制定預防策略。

14610325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14610325.value: 性別愉悅作為跨性別與多元性別人士的肯定性經驗：概念建構、測量工具發展及其對心理韌性的影響

14610325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14610325.value: Prof Operario, Don Dr Restar, Arjee Javellana

14610325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610325.value: Research on transgender and gender diverse (TGD) populations has historically centered on gender-related distress, which not only highlights negative experiences disproportionately but also reinforces the pathologization and medicalization of transgender identities. Challenging this prevailing deficit-based narrative, gender euphoria, characterized by positive emotions stemming from the affirmation of one’s gender identity or expression, has emerged as a growing focus in research. While discussions around gender euphoria frequently occur within TGD communities, there remains a lack of consensus regarding its precise conceptualization and systematic documentation of its triggers, experiences, and potential benefits. Moreover, there is currently no validated tool specifically designed to operationalize and measure gender euphoria. Grounded in the gender affirmation framework and gender minority stress model, this project adopts an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, integrating quantitative and qualitative approaches to advance the conceptualization and measurement of gender euphoria and examine its implications for psychological resilience through three interconnected studies. Study 1 involves semi-structured interviews with 28 TGD individuals, yielding qualitative data on the experiences, responses, and significance of gender euphoria. The insights from Study 1 will inform the development and validation of a new instrument for measuring gender euphoria triggers and responses in Study 2. Building on the results of both preceding studies, Study 3 employs a two-wave longitudinal survey of 260 TGD individuals to prospectively examine the relationship between gender euphoria and mental health and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Informed by an intersectionality framework, subgroup analysis will explore the heterogeneity in manifestations and effects of gender euphoria among transmasculine, transfeminine, and non-binary individuals. The study represents a paradigm shift toward a strength-based perspective, acknowledging the joy and contentment that TGD individuals can experience. The emergence of gender euphoria validates the notion that TGD individuals possess the capacity not only to survive but also to thrive and flourish. Theoretically, this research will delineate and refine the conceptualization of gender euphoria and contribute to the growing literature on whether, how, and for whom gender euphoria functions as a resilience resource among TGD individuals. Practically, the project will produce a validated instrument for assessing gender euphoria. The findings will offer a solid empirical foundation for advocating protective legislation, enhancing public education, and fostering community action in support of transgender rights and resilience. Furthermore, the project will inform gender-affirming social work and mental health practices for TGD individuals throughout their gender identity development journey.

14610725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14610725.value: 中國地方數字監控之跨區域分析

14610725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610725.value: States worldwide deploy digital surveillance tools such as CCTV cameras, facial recognition, and smartphone tracing to maintain social control and regime stability. Despite a growing literature on how digital surveillance facilitates state control, however, insufficient scholarly attention has been paid to the variations in local states’ usage of digital surveillance tools. Even in China, a global leader in the development of surveillance technologies, local governments display varying levels of willingness and capacity to deploy digital surveillance. This project addresses the gap by examining Chinese local governments’ digital surveillance tactics between 2012-2022. Departing from existing studies that focus on national governments and the repressive effects of surveillance on regime opponents, we conceptualize digital surveillance as a tool of everyday governance by local states, which face divergent policy goals, constraints, and incentives under fragmented authoritarianism. By examining how local governments in China deploy digital surveillance tools and explaining cross-regional variations, this project aims to provide insights into the complexity of authoritarian control and evolving governance practices in the digital era. Using mixed research methods combining computational social science, causal inference analyses, and qualitative research, this project aims to achieve three objectives: 1) Drawing on millions of government procurement records and utilizing Large Language Models, we will construct a comprehensive dataset on the location, time, intensity, forms, functions and users of digital surveillance deployment by Chinese local governments. 2) We will explain the longitudinal and cross-regional variations in local surveillance intensity through statistical analysis of the procurement dataset and other data sources. 3) We will investigate how local states extend digital surveillance to rural peripheries through statistical analysis of the procurement dataset and in-depth field research. This project will generate a valuable dataset on local digital surveillance in China and a series of scholarly articles with both theoretical and empirical contributions. Theoretically, we will advance the understanding of how digital surveillance technologies are integrated into local governance practices, contributing to the fields of governance studies, surveillance studies, and technology adoption in authoritarian contexts. Empirically, the findings can inform digital governance policies worldwide and help guide the regulation of surveillance technologies. 隨著數字技術的快速發展，世界各國廣泛運用數字監控技術來協助社會治理，維護社會穩定。本研究旨在深入解析中國數字監控的地方實踐，揭示不同地區部署數字監控的內在邏輯與差異。 本項目運用前沿的計算社會科學方法，系統梳理2012-2022年間超過500萬條政府採購數據，借助大語言模型技術（LLMs），構建首個中國地方數字監控部署的綜合數據庫。項目採用混合研究方法，結合大數據分析、計量經濟學與田野調查，以實現三個核心目標：一是構建中國數字監控部署的跨年分及市區分布的數據庫；二是解析影響地方部署差異的關鍵因素；三是深入考察數字監控向農村地區拓展的機制與路徑。 在理論層面，本研究將深化對數字監控融入治理實踐的理解，在地方治理、科技治國等領域做出貢獻。在政策層面，本研究將為全球數字治理政策的制定提供重要依據，並為監控技術的規範管理提供經驗指導。

14610825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14610825.value: 評估獨居過渡對老年人後續認知功能的影響—一項跨國隊列研究

14610825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14610825.value: Prof Joska, John Prof Marmot, Michael Prof Woo, Jean

14610825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610825.value: Good social relationships have been identified as an important aspect of successful ageing, and having poor social relationships has been associated with a range of negative health outcomes. Family relationships within the same household could be critical sources of support – it provides the daily instrumental support and the necessary social interactions that maintain cognitive functioning. Although transition to living alone at the old age could be a dramatic change in a person’s life and may represent a sudden loss of instrumental and psychosocial support, there has been a paucity of evidence in understanding whether such transition is detrimental to the subsequent cognitive function. It is also unclear whether certain population groups (e.g. males vs. females, high vs. low socioeconomic status (SES) groups) are more vulnerable to the adverse effect of such transition. Females are more prone to become living alone due to their relative longevity advantage over males, while those with lower SES could have more diminished social network than their higher SES counterparts. This study aims to enrich the literature by using modern causal inference techniques (quasi-experimental methods) to answer the following research questions: 1.) the effect of transition to living alone and subsequent cognitive function (global or specific domains of cognition); 2.) whether the above effect varies across the different settings with different levels of socioeconomic development; 3.) whether the effect in research question 1 varies by SES; and 4.) whether the effect in research question 1 varies between male vs. female. For this proposed study, we will make use of population-representative, cross-nationally harmonised, longitudinal study data respectively from the United States, United Kingdom, China, Mexico and South Africa. Specifically, the datasets were harmonised using standardised protocol known as the Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocols (HCAPs) such that cross-national comparisons of later-life cognitive function and impairment could be facilitated. Cross-national cohort comparison studies could improve understanding on whether it is a universal phenomenon that transition to living alone translates to poorer cognitive outcome in a similar fashion across different populations. Better cognitive outcomes in one setting might provide insights for the country’s social and economic policies and programmes for supporting healthy ageing. This research will also inform policymakers and practitioners grappling with how better to support older people in low SES who might be more socially isolated, and thereby reduce health inequalities at the older age. 研究摘要 良好的社會關係已被視為成功老齡化的重要面向，而缺乏社會連結則與一系列負面健康結果相關。同住家庭關係可能是關鍵的支持來源——它提供日常實質協助與維持認知功能所需的社會互動。儘管老年階段過渡至獨居可能帶來生活劇變，並意味著實質與心理支持的突然喪失，但目前鮮少實證探討此轉變是否會損害後續認知功能。此外，特定群體（如男性與女性、高低社經地位群體）是否更易受此轉變的負面影響，目前仍不明確。女性因預期壽命較長而更可能面臨獨居，而低社經地位者的社交網絡可能較高社經地位者更為匱乏。 本研究旨在運用現代因果推論技術（準實驗方法）深化文獻，探討以下問題：1) 過渡至獨居對後續認知功能（整體或特定領域）的影響；2) 上述影響是否因社經發展水平不同的國家而異；3) 問題1的影響是否因社經地位而異；4) 問題1的影響是否存在性別差異。本研究將採用美國、英國、中國、墨西哥及南非具全國代表性的跨國協調縱貫資料庫，特別運用「協調認知評估協議」（HCAPs）標準化程序整合數據，以促進跨國晚年認知功能與損傷的比較。 跨國世代比較研究有助釐清「獨居導致認知衰退」是否為跨人群的普遍現象。特定國家較佳的認知結果，可為該國支持健康老化的社會經濟政策提供借鑑。本研究亦將為政策制定者與實務工作者提供依據，協助改善低社經地位長者（可能面臨更嚴重社會孤立）的支持體系，從而減少老年階段的健康不平等。

14611325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14611325.value: 將基於規則的聊天機械人與ChatGPT支持的實時問答功能相結合以促進65歲及以上社區居民接種季節性流感疫苗：一項部分盲法隨機對照實驗

14611325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14611325.value: Prof Mo, Phoenix Kit-han Prof Siu, Judy Yuen-man Prof ZHANG, Qingpeng

14611325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611325.value: Seasonal influenza vaccination (SIV) coverage has remained low among Hong Kong residents aged ≥65 years. A meta-analysis revealed that interventions tailored to an individual’s stage of change (SOC) were more effective in increasing vaccination uptake. Our team co-created a Chatbot-delivered SOC-tailored intervention promoting SIV with older adults (the SIV-Chatbot) in a project funded by Health Bureau of HKSAR. A randomized controlled trial (RCT) supported the efficacy of the SIV-Chatbot, but the limited ability to provide real-time, appropriate answers to users’ open-ended questions constrains its usefulness. ChatGPT is an acceptable and preferrable means to address health-related questions among local older adults. The research team trained a ChatGPT to provide real-time question-answer (QA) functions concerning the SIV. The ChatGPT generated correct, clear, and concise answers, and demonstrated good usability and preliminary effectiveness in promoting the SIV among local older adults. A partially blinded (outcome assessor and data analyst) and parallel-group RCT will be conducted to test whether a novel hybrid Chatbot (combining the SIV-Chatbot with ChatGPT-supported real-time QA functions) is superior to the SIV-Chatbot alone in increasing SIV uptake among older adults. We will use a co-creation approach to improve the existing ChatGPT, helping it better understand users’ open-ended questions and generate more appropriate answers. Participants are Hong Kong residents aged ≥65 years who can speak and comprehend Cantonese, have smartphones with internet access, and have not taken the SIV for the approaching flu season. Eligible participants will be randomized evenly into either the intervention group (n=227) or the control group (n=227). The control group can only access the SIV-Chatbot, which, after measuring participants’ SOC regarding SIV uptake, will deliver online interventions tailored to their current SOC every two weeks for four times. The intervention group will also be availed of the SIV-Chatbot, with the same SOC-tailored interventions as those delivered to the control group, but they will also have access to real-time QA functions concerning the SIV provided by the trained ChatGPT during the intervention period. Self-reported SIV uptake (the primary outcome) will be measured six months after completing the interventions. Vaccinated participants will be asked to upload their receipt through WhatsApp to validate their SIV uptake. If the hybrid Chatbot is proven superior to the SIV-Chatbot alone, it can be implemented by governmental and non-governmental organizations to increase SIV coverage, and reduce disease burdens caused by seasonal influenza. 香港65歲或以上居民的季節性流感疫苗接種率一直較低。一項薈萃分析顯示，根據個人變化階段度身定制的干預措施在提高疫苗接種率方面更為有效。我們的團隊在一項受香港特別行政區醫務衛生局資助的項目中，與長者共同開發了一款由聊天機械人提供的針對個人變化階段度身定制的干預措施，用於推廣長者的季節性流感疫苗接種。一項隨機對照實驗支持了這款聊天機械人的有效性。但這款聊天機械人無法實時和適當地回答使用者的開放式問題，這限制了其實用性。ChatGPT是解答本地長者健康相關問題的一種可行方法。研究團隊訓練了一個ChatGPT，使其能夠實時解答與流感疫苗相關的問題。這個 ChatGPT能夠生成正確、清晰及簡潔的答案，並表現出良好的可用性，亦在提高本地長者接種季節性流感疫苗方面初見成效。 我們將進行一項部分盲法平行組隨機對照實驗以測試一種新型混合型聊天機械人（將基於規則的聊天機械人與 ChatGPT 支援的實時問答功能相結合）在提高長者季節性流感疫苗接種率方面是否優於單獨使用基於規則的聊天機械人。參與結果評估和數據分析的人員將不會知曉分組情況。我們將採用共同創造的方式來改進現有的 ChatGPT，使其更好地理解用戶的開放式問題並生成更合適的答案。 參加者為年滿65歲的香港居民，能用粵語交流，擁有可上網的智能手機，且尚未接種流感疫苗以應對即將到來的流感季。符合條件的參加者將被隨機分配到干預組（n=227）或對照組（n=227）。對照組僅可使用基於規則的聊天機械人。該機械人在測量參加者與流感疫苗相關的個人變化階段後，將每兩星期提供一次根據其當前變化階段量身定制的線上干預措施，共四次。干預組也將使用相同的基於規則的聊天機械人，但參加者在干預期間還可以使用經過訓練的ChatGPT支援的有關流感疫苗實時問答功能。在完成干預後的六個月，參加者自行匯報的季節性流感疫苗接種情況將會被記錄（主要結果）。已接種疫苗的參加者將會被要求透過 WhatsApp 上傳接種証明，以核實其季節性流感疫苗接種情況。 若果混合型聊天機械人被證實優於單純的基於規則的聊天機械人，該款混合型聊天機械人可被應用到不同的政府和非政府機構中，從而提高季節性流感疫苗接種率並減輕季節性流感所造成的疾病負擔。

14611625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14611625.value: 香港高中數學與高等教育數學的銜接研究：面向本土和全球的重要性

14611625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14611625.value: Dr Igor', Kontorovich Prof Lau, Wilfred Wing-fat Dr Liang, Biyao Prof Zazkis, Rina

14611625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611625.value: Quality mathematics education in Hong Kong is ever more important due to worldwide emphasis on Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education in order to effectively respond to the changing workforce and skillsets in the twenty-first century. Mathematics, a core subject for compulsory education, is a foundational STEM subject with interdisciplinary applications spanning across engineering, quantitative finance, artificial intelligence (AI), and biotechnology. Therefore, mathematics education across compulsory to tertiary education must be designed and executed to support students’ development to become successful in STEM fields. Despite continued efforts by local government to support quality mathematics learning through curricular reforms, there remains a significant and research-evidenced gap in students’ secondary-tertiary mathematics transition locally, and worldwide. Particularly, university academics in mathematics consistently observe secondary school graduates’ unpreparedness for tertiary mathematics, raising concerns for industries and stakeholders in attracting and fostering STEM talents. Thus, there exist urgent needs to improve the secondary-tertiary mathematics transition in Hong Kong and beyond, which has also implication toward sustainable development of STEM and AI applications in the local, wider Chinese, and global contexts in today's increasingly digital world. This study will examine the secondary-tertiary mathematics transition in Hong Kong by a mixed-method approach. Three kinds of stakeholders, namely secondary and tertiary students of mathematics (n=380), in-service and prospective mathematics teachers (n=210), and university academics will participate in the two-part study. Firstly, this study will develop an instrument and quantitatively assess the participating teachers’ and students’ mathematical competence in the topics of pre-calculus and calculus, which are major domains in both secondary and tertiary education. Second, it will adopt an interview methodology, focusing on generating new understanding about the participant groups’ mathematics teaching and/or learning experiences, the challenges and opportunities faced, and the meanings associated with the experiences, while task-based interviews will reveal the participants’ thinking processes in solving the designed mathematical tasks. The study surveys and informs the curricular learning and instructional practices of upper secondary and tertiary mathematics, drawing upon different methodologies (quantitative/qualitative) and epistemologies (cognitive/sociocultural). Findings will contribute toward refining theoretical understanding about the cognitive processes in studying advanced mathematics. Practically, it will provide evidence-based directions toward coherent and quality mathematics education in Hong Kong. More broadly, this study will make impact toward curricular and policy reforms regarding what, and how, public education may better address, leverage, and respond to the changing landscape and needs for STEM education. 由於全球對科學、技術、工程和數學（STEM）教育的重視，以有效應對21世紀勞動力和技能的變化，香港的優質數學教育愈發重要。數學作爲義務教育階段的核心課程，也是STEM學科的基礎，其跨學科應用於工程製造、量化金融、人工智慧和生物科技等領域。因此，從義務教育到高等教育的數學教育必須圍繞支持學生在STEM領域中的成功發展來設計和實施。 儘管香港政府通過課程改革持續努力地促進高質量的數學學習，但在香港和全球範圍內，學生從高中數學到高等教育數學的銜接上仍然存在顯著且已經被研究證實的不足。尤其是，數學領域的大學學者們不斷發現高中畢業生對大學數學的準備不足，這引起了業界和相關人士在吸引和培養STEM人才方面的擔憂。因此，在香港乃至更廣汎的地區，迫切需要改善高中數學向大學數學的銜接問題，同時在當今日益數字化的世界，這對於香港，中國乃至全世界的STEM持續發展和AI應用也具有影響。 本研究將採用混合研究法來探究香港高中數學和大學數學的銜接問題。三類相關人士，分別是高中和大學數學專業的學生（380名）、在職和准數學教師（210名）、大學學者，將參與兩部分的研究。首先，本研究將開發一種工具來量化評估參與教師和學生在前備微積分和微積分上的數學能力，這些知識是高中和高等教育階段的主要內容。其次，本研究將使用訪談法，聚焦於參與者群體的數學教學和/或學習經歷、面臨到的挑戰和機遇、以及與經驗相關的意義，從而產生對以上問題的新認識，同時基於任務的訪談將揭示參與者在解決數學問題中的思考過程。 該研究利用不同的研究方法（量化/質性）和認識角度（認知/社會文化）調查並揭示了高中數學和高等教育數學的課程學習以及教學實踐。研究發現將有助於完善對高等數學學習中認知過程的理論理解。從實踐角度出發，這個研究將為香港連貫且優質的數學教育提供基於經驗的指導。更廣汎地來講，這項研究將對課程和政策改革產生影響，這些改革涉及公共教育做什麽、以及怎麽做才能夠更好地應對、利用和回應不斷變化的STEM教育格局和需求

14611825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14611825.value: 多模態視角下英文授課大學課堂中的學生策略性聆聽研究

14611825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14611825.value: Prof Ducker, Nathan Thomas Prof Lim, Fei Victor Prof Liyanage, Indika Prof Lo, Yuen Yi

14611825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611825.value: The use of English as a medium of instruction (EMI) has grown in lockstep with the internationalization of higher education globally. However, for students whose first language is not English, listening to academic lectures in a second/foreign language (L2) often impedes their understanding of content. As knowledge building in university classrooms is often multimodal, students may combine multiple semiotic modes such as teachers’ speech, gestures, and visual aids to support comprehension. The successful use of such information would require students’ strategic awareness and competence to guide them in knowing when and how to use different modes for improving comprehension outcomes. This study aims to understand students’ multimodal strategic listening in EMI university lectures, and to explore the predictors and outcomes of their strategy use. Extant multimodal research has focused on how teachers mobilize diverse modes for meaning making, yet students’ perceptions and use of multimodal resources are not readily understood. Years of L2 listening strategy research has also primarily explored how listeners handle aural input without sufficiently addressing the multimodal nature of comprehension that is typical in university classrooms. Hence, drawing on a metacognitive framework of strategic listening, this study conceptualizes learners as agentic meaning makers. It investigates if and how they strategize to improve comprehension of diverse semiotic modes of information in EMI university lectures. The study is guided by a two-stage, mixed-methods research design that triangulates findings from diverse sources of quantitative and qualitative data. Stage 1 explores students’ multimodal listening strategy use and their underlying metacognitive knowledge. It comprises a literature review and data generated by 24 purposively selected students via an innovative real-time idiodynamic method. An EMI multimodal listening strategy questionnaire will be drafted based on the data collected. Stage 2 will validate the questionnaire with two cohorts of students (N = 400, N = 800) based on stratified random sampling. Structural equation modelling will be used to examine if students’ multimodal strategy use is shaped by contextual and/or learner-related factors, and whether it predicts lecture comprehension success. Semi-structured interviews with 18 purposively selected students will further expound on the statistical results. Findings will extend academic knowledge for theorizing multimodal strategic listening, develop new research instruments for its measurement, and inform evidence-based strategy training programs. The study will also inform the ‘bigger picture’ of cultivating students’ multimodal literacy and strategic listening competence in EMI higher education.

14612025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14612025.value: 菲律賓馬尼拉住房社會史，1898-1946

14612025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612025.value: The inquiry probes the evolution of housing in Manila during the American colonial era (1898-1946). Analyzing the political, legal, economic, cultural, and architectural contexts that shaped the development of housing, the study explains the relationship between the physical forms of accommodation and the social life they contain. In December 1898, following the signing of the Treaty of Paris, the United States commenced its colonization of the Philippine Islands. Even though historiography has done much to clarify the nature of transition within local society after 1898, the written history of Manila’s housing has been a neglected topic. Accordingly, the study will expand knowledge of life within the Philippines’ capital city during a time when, first, the American colonizer’s implemented policies to ‘uplift’ and ‘civilize’ the local population, and, second, important political-legal advancements transpired. In 1916 and 1917, for example, Acts were passed to permit Filipinos employed as colonial bureaucrats new opportunity to shape national and municipal governmental operation. By means of surveying the number, location, and supply of residences in Manila, the investigation illuminates the alliance between house provision, housing design, and the evolving Filipino way of life. A principal goal of the inquiry is to know the types of housing in Manila, as well as to measure and evaluate changes in built form over time. To comprehend the determinants of urban form the research will assess matters that include the occurrence of building cycles and their relationship to shifts in patterns of investment, cultural change, e.g. the move to suburban living, and new laws passed to permit subdivisions, regulate public health, improve road and transport infrastructure, and safeguard well-being. The investigation, ultimately, is established to enlarge knowledge of the American Empire in Asia. It shall present original findings re the association between societal transformation, the housing of a rapidly expanding urban population, and the Filipino way of life. The project will be of interest to persons investigating the cultural and environmental impacts of ‘progress’ within Philippine society, and it will be of relevance to those interested in urban culture and modernity within the frame of imperialism in Asia. Evidently, owing to the nature of the inquiry with its focus upon housing, the findings will be of significance to persons studying the connection between built fabrics and culture. The project findings will result in peer-reviewed journal papers, and a monograph. 本研究探討美國殖民時期（1898 - 1946 年）馬尼拉房屋的發展演變。通過分析政治、法律、經濟、文化和建築環境對房屋發展的影響，闡釋居住空間結構與市民社交生活之間的關係。 《巴黎條約》於1898年12月簽署之後，美國開始殖民統治菲律賓群島。儘管歷史學界已對 1898 年後當地社會的轉變做了大量研究，但對菲律賓首都馬尼拉房屋發展的記載卻一直被忽視。本研究可讓我們認識馬尼拉人民的生活情況，特別是在美國殖民政府推行了旨在「提升」和「教化」當地民眾的政策，以及推行了重要的政治法律變革，如在 1916 年和 1917 年通過法案，允許菲律賓人擔任殖民地官員，參與國家管治和市政運作。 通過對馬尼拉住宅數量、位置和供應情況的調查，研究房屋供應、住宅設計和居民生活模式轉變之間的聯繫。本研究的核心為了解馬尼拉的房屋類型、衡量和評估其建築形態的變化。從建築週期、文化變遷（如遷往郊區生活），以及允許分拆土地、規範公共衛生、改善道路及交通基建礎和保障社會福祉等的新法案，了解影響城市設計的關鍵因素。 本研究的目的是加深認識美國在亞洲的殖民統治，展示社會轉型、人口快速增長城市的房屋與菲律賓人生活方式之間的聯繫。本研究成果有助學者了解文化和環境對菲律賓社會變遷的影響、以及亞洲帝國主義框架下的城市文化及現代化，也對研究建築結構及文化兩者之間的關係有重要意義。本計劃的研究成果包括撰寫學術期刊文章及專著。

14612625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14612625.value: 使用者主導程度於個人化數位心理健康介入中的角色：探討心理特質影響初顯期成人使用率及參與度的實地追蹤研究

14612625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612625.value: Abstract Introduction Emerging adults are at a prime time to take care of their mental health as they experience myriad life transitions. Being digital natives, digital mental health interventions can be an effective way for them to develop mental self-care into a habit and improve their mental well-being. Recently, personalized digital mental health interventions emerge and vary on how intervention is selected to encourage uptake and how intervention content is determined to encourage engagement. However, the decision-making process used to achieve personalization, particularly how users are involved, remains understudied. To effectively to maximize uptake and engagement, emerging adults’ relevant psychological attributes need to be accounted for in their involvement in the selection and planning of digital mental health interventions. Project aims This study compares the effectiveness of personalized approaches, varying in the level of user involvement during the decision-making process, on uptake and engagement of digital mental self-care tools among emerging adults. The mediating effects of psychological reactance and cognitive load and the moderating effects of independent-interdependent problem-solving styles and power distance beliefs will be examined. Methods and analysis 531 emerging adults will be randomized into 3 conditions: user-directed, user-AI shared decision making, and AI-prescribed approaches for selecting digital mental self-care tools and making an action plan. One-way ANCOVA will be used to analyze differences in state reactance, intention, and actual uptake across conditions, controlling for trait reactance, attitudes to AI, and mental health literacy. Linear mixed model analysis will be conducted to evaluate the longitudinal effects of these approaches on self-care behaviors and well-being outcomes after 10 and 30 days. Structural equation modeling will be used to test the mediation effects of state reactance and cognitive load towards uptake intention and decision. Moderating effects of independent-interdependent problem solving styles and power distance beliefs will be tested using multi-group structural equation modeling. Significance The present project aims to investigate how personalization that incorporates varying levels of user involvement and how psychological attributes of emerging adults affect uptake and engagement of digital mental health interventions and mental well-being. Our work contributes theoretically to the personalization of digital mental health interventions by accounting for multiple mediators and moderators relevant to emerging adults in promoting mental self-care. Practically, it informs the application of effective approaches to personalize digital mental health interventions according to users’ preferences for involvement. 引言： 處於成人初顯期的年輕人正面臨多重人生轉變，這階段是維護心理健康的關鍵時期。作為數碼原住民，這些年輕人特別適合透過數碼心理健康介入培養心理自我照護的習慣，以提升心理健康。近年來，個人化的數碼心理健康介入逐漸興起，與以往模式比較，個人化方式透過度身訂造的方法選擇及決定介入內容以促進使用率及參與度。然而，如何達至個人化的決策過程，特別是對使用者的主導及參與程度，仍缺乏深入探討。若我們要最大化地提升使用率及參與度，在制定介入方案的過程中必須考慮成人初顯期相關的心理特質。 研究目的： 本研究旨在比較使用者在決策過程中的主導程度，對提升數碼心理自我照顧工具使用率及參與度的效果。我們也將檢視心理抗拒與認知負荷的中介作用。此外，使用者的解決問題風格（獨立型或互依型）、權力距離信念的調節效應亦會被審視。 方法與分析： 本研究將招募 531 名成人初顯期參與者，並隨機分配至三個組別以選擇數碼心理自我照護工具並制定行動計畫，分別是：(1) 使用者主導、(2) 使用者及AI 共同決策、(3) AI 主導。我們將使用單因子共變數分析（ANCOVA）比較三組在控制特質性心理抗拒、對 AI 的態度及心理健康素養後，於情境性心理抗拒、採用意向與實際採用上的差異。線性混合模型分析（Linear mixed model analysis）會被用作評估這些方法在10天及30天後對自我照顧行為和心理健康的縱貫性效果。結構方程模型（Structural equation modeling）會被用作測試情境性心理抗拒和認知負荷對採用意願和決定的中介效應。最後，獨立–互依型解決問題風格與權力距離信念的調節作用則將以多組結構方程模型檢測。 重要性： 本研究旨在探討如何在個人化過程中，考慮使用者主導程度及成人初顯期心理特質，以影響數碼心理健康介入的使用率、參與度及心理健康成效。在理論層面上，通過審視與促進心理自我照顧相關的多重中介與調節變數，此研究對了解個人化數碼心理健康介入有所貢獻。在實用層面，本研究將結果為推行用戶主導的個人化數位心理健康介入提供了有力的實證支持。

14612925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14612925.value: 傳承工藝知識：超越傳統工藝的竹子熱彎應用新方法

14612925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612925.value: Bamboo is a traditional construction material in various Asian countries. The craft of bamboo-working has declined due to industrialisation, representing a loss of intangible cultural heritage in China and elsewhere. Recently, however, architectural interest in bamboo as a strong, sustainable material has grown. This creates an opportunity to address two issues: preserving the traditional practice of bamboo craft while promoting a green transition in architecture. Traditional bamboo-working is an experiential skill that relies on the craftsperson’s implicit knowledge, handed down by previous generations. This makes it challenging to scale up the use of bamboo craft to create architectural components, as traditional techniques cannot be performed by an unskilled person. A scientific understanding is therefore needed to transform the implicit knowledge of a small number of artisans into explicit knowledge that can be widely disseminated and applied in sustainable architecture. A key technique in bamboo craft is heat bending. At high temperatures, bamboo is softened and can be bent into desired shapes for functional objects such as boats, chairs, and baskets. Upon cooling, the bamboo sets through thermal relaxation. Heat bending is an artisanal skill that is poorly understood by researchers. Therefore, the proposed project will rigorously investigate the effect of heating at various temperatures on bamboo’s material properties, and optimise the conditions for heat bending of bamboo. This will allow a quantitative understanding of how this sustainable material can be efficiently shaped while avoiding damage such as cracking or burning. The project will scientifically evaluate the thermal relaxation of dried split bamboo to develop a generalisable method of bending this material. It will also study how to incorporate this method into architectural practice via a more versatile, flexible design of bamboo components. For the first time, it will establish how the conventional weaving technique of heat-bent bamboo strips can be used to create woven structures with sufficient mechanical strength for architectural applications. The results will be incorporated into a digital model to promote the widespread computer-aided design of bamboo structures. The new knowledge generated on the thermomechanical properties of bamboo and the architectural utility of heat-bent bamboo components will have valuable social and environmental impacts. Bamboo-working is intangible cultural heritage, and applying it in modern daily living is the best way to preserve it. Moreover, this strong, versatile natural material has huge potential as a sustainable and economical alternative to environmentally damaging, high-emission materials like concrete. 竹子是亞洲多國的傳統建築材料。由於工業化的發展，竹製工藝日漸式微，這標誌著中國及其他地區非物質文化遺產的流失。然而，近年來，竹子作為一種堅固且可持續材料在建築領域的關注度逐漸提升。這為解決兩個問題創造了契機：既保護傳統的竹製工藝，又推動建築業的綠色轉型。 傳統的竹製工藝是一種經驗性技藝，依賴手工藝人的隱性知識並以代代相傳的方式延續。這使得將竹工藝應用於建築構件的大規模生產極具挑戰性，因為傳統技術無法由非熟練工人執行。因此，需要通過科學的理解，將少數工匠掌握的隱性知識轉化為能夠廣泛傳播並應用於可持續建築的顯性知識。竹製工藝的一項關鍵技術是熱彎曲。在高溫下，竹子會變軟并可彎曲成所需形狀，用於製作船、椅子和籃子等功能性物品。冷卻後，竹子會透過熱弛豫而定型。熱彎是一項手工藝，目前研究人員對其了解有限。因此，本計畫將嚴謹地研究不同溫度下加熱對竹材特性的影響，並優化竹子熱彎的條件。這將有助於定量地理解如何有效地成型這種可持續材料，同時避免開裂或燒焦等損傷。 該計畫將科學地評估乾竹片的熱弛豫特性，開發一種通用的竹材彎曲方法。此外，還將研究如何將該方法通過更具多用途和靈活性的竹材構件設計融入建築實踐。該計畫將首次確立如何利用傳統的熱彎竹條編織技術來製造具有足夠機械強度的編織結構用於建築應用。研究結果將被整合到數碼模型中，以促進竹結構電腦輔助設計的廣泛應用。 本研究在竹子熱機械性能及熱彎竹構件建築應用方面產生的新知識，將帶來寶貴的社會和環境影響。竹製品是非物質文化遺產，將其應用於現代日常生活是保護它的最佳方式。此外，這種堅固且多用途的天然材料具有巨大的潛力，可作為混凝土等環境破壞性及高排放性材料的可持續且經濟的替代品。

14613025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613025.value: 評估中藥隨機對照試驗在註冊、偏倚降低、報告與統計分析方面的表現：一項橫斷面研究

14613025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14613025.value: Dr CHAN, Kam Wa Chris Prof FEI, Yu Tong Dr Ho, Leonard Dr Huang, Junjie Dr LI, Nian Prof LIU, Jian Ping Prof MAO, Chen Prof Wong, Martin Chi Sang Prof Wu, Irene Xin Yin Prof YANG, Ke Hu Dr Yip, Benjamin Hon-kei Prof YUAN, Jin Qiu

14613025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613025.value: Abstract Introduction Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) is one of the major modalities in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with high usage amongst Chinese populations worldwide. Evaluating the efficacy and effectiveness of CHM is essential for establishing the evidence base of TCM practice, of which current policies of the Chinese government support such development direction. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for evaluating CHM, provided they are appropriately designed, conducted, and reported. However, it is unclear whether CHM RCTs published in recent years adhered to best practices in (i) a priori registration, (ii) bias reduction, (iii) full reporting, and (iv) using appropriate statistical analysis. This proposed project will comprehensively assess these four aspects among CHM RCTs published in the past decade. Methods Sampling This will be a cross-sectional study of CHM RCT publications indexed in three internationally recognised databases which have the strongest global impact: MEDLINE, EMBASE and CENTRAL. We will develop search strategies for CHM RCTs for these 3 databases, and two investigators will screen all citations generated independently. Eligible publications should (i) evaluate CHM with at least one component listed in the China Pharmacopeia(2020), (ii) report at least one quantitative outcome, and (iii) publish in English or Chinese from 2014 to 2024. All eligible publications will be added to the sampling frame. Then, a random sample of 749 RCT will be selected for assessment using computerized random sequence generator. Assessment Assessment of performance will adhere to current best practice, appraising whether the RCTs fulfilled: (i) adherence to full registration with protocol and statistical analysis plan; (ii) low risk of bias (RoB) as assessed by the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool 2; (iii) satisfactory reporting quality as appraised by the CONSORT-CHM Formulas 2017; (iv) appropriate statistical analysis of primary outcome with covariate adjustment, sensitivity analysis and missing data handling. Bibliographical characteristics of the trials will also be extracted. Full-text screening, assessment and data extraction will be conducted by two investigators independently using a pre-piloted form, and disagreements will be resolved by consensus between investigators or adjudication by a senior researcher. Statistical analysis Data will be presented using frequencies and percentages for dichotomous data and mean with standard deviation (or median with interquartile range) for continuous data. Multivariate regression analyses will be conducted to explore the association between bibliographical characteristics and the performance in each of the four areas described above. 引言 中藥（Chinese herbal medicine, CHM）是傳統中醫（Traditional Chinese Medicine, TCM）中的主要療法之一，在全球華人社群中使用率極高。評估中藥的療效與安全性，對於建立中醫實踐的實證基礎至關重要，而政府目前的政策也支持此一發展方向。隨機對照試驗（Randomized Controlled Trials, RCTs）是評估中藥療效與安全性的黃金標準，前提是其設計、執行與報告皆符合標準。然而，目前尚不清楚近年來發表的中藥RCT是否遵循最佳實踐，包括：(i) 事前註冊、(ii) 減少偏倚、(iii) 完整報告，以及 (iv) 使用適當的統計分析。本研究計劃全面評估過去十年中藥RCT在上述四個方面的表現。 方法 抽樣 本研究為橫斷面研究，對象為收錄於三個具全球影響力的國際資料庫中的中藥RCT文獻：MEDLINE、EMBASE 和 CENTRAL。我們將為這三個資料庫制定中藥RCT的搜尋策略，並由兩位研究人員獨立篩選所有搜尋結果。符合條件的文獻需：(i) 評估至少一種列於《中國藥典》（2020年版）中的中藥成分，(ii) 報告至少一項量化結果，且 (iii) 發表語言為英文或中文，出版年份介於2014至2024年之間。所有符合條件的文獻將納入抽樣框架，並使用電腦隨機序列產生器隨機抽取749篇RCT進行評估。 評估 評估將依據目前最佳實踐進行，判斷RCT是否符合以下標準：(i) 事前註冊，包括研究計劃與統計分析計劃；(ii) 依據Cochrane偏倚風險工具2（Risk of Bias Tool 2）評估為低偏倚風險；(iii) 根據CONSORT-CHM Formulas 2017報告質量高；(iv) 主要結果統計分析適當，包括混雜因素調整、敏感性分析及缺失資料處理。亦將提取試驗的基礎特徵。全文篩選、評估與資料提取將由兩位研究人員獨立進行，並使用預先試驗過的表格，若有分歧則由研究人員協商或由資深研究者裁定。 統計分析 對於二元資料將以頻率與百分比呈現，連續資料則以平均值與標準差（或中位數與四分位距）呈現。將進行多變量回歸分析，以探討基礎特徵與上述四個評估結果之間的關聯性。 預期結果 本研究將全面評估近年中醫藥RCT在方法學與報告質量上的嚴謹性，並指出其具體的優勢與不足之處。透過識別這些不足，我們可以設計有針對性的教育課程，以提升臨床研究人員的研究能力。我們對基礎特徵與研究表現之間關聯性的分析，將有助於辨識與較差表現相關的因素，進而提供對表現不佳可能原因的深入見解，並釐清應優先進行能力建設的研究人員群體。中期而言，本研究將提升臨床研究人員執行嚴謹中藥RCT的能力；長期而言，則有助於建立中藥的強大實證基礎。

14613125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613125.value: 透過身份認同與時間導向方法減少中風久坐行為（STRIVE計劃）：一項隨機對照試驗

14613125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14613125.value: Prof CHEW, Jocelyn Han-shi Dr Choi, Kai-chow Dr Ho, Ken Hok Man Dr Leung, Ka Man

14613125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613125.value: Stroke is a leading cause of disability worldwide. While physical activity is crucial for recovery and preventing further stroke, many survivors spend too much time being inactive (>10 hours/day). Sedentary behaviour has negative health effects even when individuals exercise regularly. Therefore, reducing sedentary behaviour has become a key focus in stroke care. Sedentary behaviour refers to low-energy waking activities (< 1.5 metabolic equivalents of tasks) performed while sitting, reclining, or lying down. The lack of muscle activity during sedentary time increases the risk of recurrent stroke and even increase the risk of death from other causes. However, a recent Cochrane review found that current interventions aimed at reducing sedentary behaviour have not been effective. Tackling sedentary behaviour requires efforts to (1) increase health-promoting behaviours, such as light-intensity physical activity, and (2) reduce health-risking behaviours, such as prolonged sitting. These changes require self-control and the ability to resist the urge to be sedentary. Yet, these skills are often overlooked in stroke literature. To address this gap, we propose a randomised controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a temporal-oriented, identity-based intervention in reducing sedentary behaviour among stroke survivors. The primary outcome will be the amount of sedentary time, and secondary outcomes will include future perspective thinking, behavioural automaticity, bolus of uninterrupted prolonged sedentary time, amount physical activity, functioning and psychological distress. Additionally, we will explore whether the intervention's effects on amount of sedentary time are mediated by future perspective thinking. A total of 148 stroke survivors from stroke unit of two regional hospital and non-government organizations for stroke patients will be recruited for this study. Participants will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group (IG) or the attention control group (CG). The IG will receive an 8-week temporal-oriented, identity-based intervention, consisting of five 45-minute individual sessions and online support. The CG will receive the same number of sessions, but focused on general stroke education. Outcome measures will be assessed at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and at a 6-month follow-up. This trial is the first of its kind to investigate the effectiveness of a temporal-oriented, identity-based intervention in stroke context. The findings will contribute valuable knowledge on the benefits of temporal perspectives in managing sedentary behaviour and provide evidence-based guidance for therapeutic interventions in the stroke community. By targeting this new therapeutic intervention target, we can potentially improve the health outcomes and quality of life for stroke survivors in the community. 中風是全球主要引致失能原因之一。儘管體能活動在中風復康及預防中至關重要，但許多中風倖存者每天久坐時間過長（>10小時/天）。即使進行定期運動，久坐行為仍對健康產生負面影響。因此，減少久坐行為已成為治療中風及預防再中風的關鍵。 久坐行為的定義是指在清醒狀態下，長時間以坐姿或斜躺姿勢進行能量消耗小於等於1. 5代謝當量（METs）的活動。久坐行為期間缺乏肌肉活動會增加復發性中風及全因死亡的風險。然而，最近的Cochrane系統性文獻回顧指出，當前針對減少久坐行為的干預措施並未有效。解決久坐行為需要（1）增加促進健康的行為，例如輕度體能活動，以及（2）減少有健康風險的行為，例如長時間坐著。這些改變需要自我調節及抑制自動且不費力的反應，這在中風文獻中常被忽略。 因此，我們提出了一項隨機對照試驗，以評估時間導向、身份認同干預對減少中風倖存者久坐行為的有效性。主要指標將是久坐行為的時間，次要指標包括未來思考、行為自動性、久坐行為的連續時間、體能活動量及心理困擾。此外，我們將探索干預對久坐行為的影響是否受到未來思維的影響。本研究將從非政府組織及中風患者護理診所招募148名中風倖存者。參與者將被隨機分配到干預組（IG）或等候對照組（CG）。干預組將接受為期8週以時間導向、身份認同的干預，包括三次45分鐘的小組會面及線上支持。對照組將在數據收集程序完成後接受干預。結果指標將在基線、干預結束後及6個月隨訪時進行評估。 這項試驗是首次嘗試在腦中風背景下探討時間導向、身份認同干預的有效性。其研究結果將有助於闡明時間觀點在管理久坐行為方面的益處，並為中風群體的治療干預提供循證指導。通過針對這一新的治療干預目標，我們有望改善中風倖存者的健康結果及生活質量。

14613225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613225.value: 透過大規模實驗探究視覺搜尋

14613225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613225.value: The comprehensive exploration (CE) approach employed in this project draws inspiration from the significant advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) over the past two decades and several recent large-scale psychological studies (e.g., Peterson et al., 2021; Awad et al., 2018). Specifically, this approach seeks to incorporate two key elements from the AI revolution: “large-scale benchmark datasets,” which provide breadth, and “objective assessment metrics,” which ensure precision. This CE approach has been applied in two recent studies (Huang, 2023, 2024) to examine visual working memory (VWM) for spatial locations and colors, respectively. In each study, to ensure breadth, a vast array of stimulus patterns was pre-generated and tested in a large-scale, rigorously controlled experiment involving tens of millions of responses. To ensure precision, a formal computational model (i.e., the CE model) was developed to optimally account for variations in the collected data. With this combination of breadth and precision, these studies have achieved both effectiveness and parsimony: the CE models explain empirical observations nearly as effectively as large neural networks while remaining interpretable and relatively simple. In the current project, this CE approach will be applied to visual search. A total of 500,000 stimulus displays will be generated and tested across 50,000,000 trials. A formal computational model will be developed to predict visual search performance based on the specifics of the stimulus displays. This computational model will serve as an integrative framework, combining various factors known to influence visual search, including feature-based selection and guidance, saliency, target-nontarget similarity, similarity among nontargets, special stimuli (e.g., animals, human faces, emotion-related stimuli, and characters), sequential effects (such as bottom-up feature priming and top-down shifts in attentional set), contextual cueing, reward-driven attention, and the prevalence effect. Furthermore, the model aims to discover new theoretical insights based on observational clues. 本項目採用的「全面探索法」（Comprehensive Exploration, CE）靈感源自人工智能（AI）領域近二十年的重大進展，以及近期數項大規模心理學研究（如Peterson et al., 2021; Awad et al., 2018）。具體而言，此方法旨在融合AI革命的兩大關鍵要素：提供廣度的「大規模基準數據集」與確保精準度的「客觀評估指標」。該CE方法已於近期兩項研究（Huang，2023，2024）中分別應用於檢視空間位置與顏色的視覺工作記憶（VWM），每項研究為確保廣度，皆預先生成海量刺激圖案，並透過嚴格控制的大規模實驗（涵蓋數千萬次反應）進行測試；為確保精準度，則建立形式化計算模型（即CE模型）以最優化解釋數據變異。憑藉廣度與精準度的結合，這些研究同時達成高效性與簡約性：CE模型對實證數據的解釋力媲美大型神經網絡，同時保持可解釋性與相對簡潔的架構。當前項目將此CE方法延伸至視覺搜尋領域，計劃生成50萬組刺激顯示畫面，並透過5,000萬次試驗進行測試。我們將開發形式化計算模型，根據刺激顯示的具體特徵預測視覺搜尋表現。此計算模型將作為整合框架，涵蓋已知影響視覺搜尋的多重因素，包括基於特徵的選擇與引導、顯著性、目標與非目標的相似度、非目標間的相似性、特殊刺激（如動物、人臉、情緒相關刺激、文字）、序列效應（如自下而上的特徵啟動與自上而下的注意定勢轉移）、情境提示、獎勵驅動的注意力，以及普遍性效應。此外，模型將基於觀測線索進一步挖掘新的理論洞見。

14613525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613525.value: 即時適應性治療對睡眠及作息問題的最佳化與結果評估：微觀隨機試驗與隨機對照試驗

14613525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14613525.value: Dr Chakraborty, Bibhas Dr Chung, Ka-Fai Prof Harvey, Allison Prof Yeung, Wing-Fai

14613525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613525.value: Given the unmet need for evidence-based behavioural sleep medicine, mobile health (mHealth) technologies have emerged as a promising solution due to their convenience and widespread accessibility. Particularly, the integration of advanced mHealth technologies, such as just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs) and wearables, has gained substantial momentum in recent years. These innovative tools facilitate real-time and real-world monitoring, enabling the delivery of personalised and adaptive sleep interventions that can address dynamic individual needs precisely. The proposed project will aim to (1) advance the algorithm and content of a pilot-tested JITAI; (2) conduct a micro-randomised trial (MRT) to optimise the effect of JITAI components (i.e., contextually personalised suggestions, generic messages, or no notifications) in conjunction with wearables and ecological momentary assessments (EMAs); and (3) conduct a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to examine the efficacy of the optimised JITAI on sleep and circadian functions in short- and medium-term. The proposal will involve three phases. Phase I will focus on the technological advancements of the pilot-tested JITAI, GoodShleep. Phase II will entail an MRT involving 77 participants with sleep or circadian problems who will participate in the advanced GoodShleep. The JITAI will dynamically tailor the sleep intervention by adjusting the type and amount of support provided. It will comprise (1) an 8-week, modular-based transdiagnostic intervention for sleep and circadian dysfunction (TranS-C); (2) brief EMA surveys to detect sleep–wake regularity and mood status; and (3) 24-hour real-time wearables assessing sleep and activity levels. Phase III will be an RCT comprising 80 participants with sleep or circadian problems who will be randomised to receive the optimised JITAI GoodShleep+ and care-as-usual (CAU). For the MRT, the proximal outcomes will be sleep–wake regularity, activity levels, and mood status. A pre-post intervention comparison will be performed. The major assessments of the RCT will be at baseline, immediate post-intervention, and 12-week follow-up. These will include both subjective measures (e.g., sleep and circadian function and psychological health symptoms) and objective (i.e., sleep–wake patterns) measures. Mixed-effects models will be used to evaluate the effect of the JITAI on the outcomes. The proposed project will represent a pioneering effort that bridges the current gap in service provision within the field of behavioural sleep medicine. By optimising the state-of-the-art JITAI and evaluating its efficacy, we aim to provide individuals experiencing sleep and circadian problems with a real-time and real-world solution that is accurate, cost-effective, low burden, and easily accessible. 鑑於對以實證為本的行為睡眠治療需求未獲滿足，行動健康技術因其便利性與可及性，已成為極具潛力的解決方案。特別是先進的行動健康技術整合，近年來已獲得顯著關注，例如即時適應性治療與智能手錶。這些創新工具促進了即時且真實的監測，從而能夠提供個人化且能適應個人變化的睡眠治療，精確應對各種個人需求。 本計畫將旨在：(1) 進一步提升已進行先導研究的即時適應性治療之演算法與內容；(2) 進行一項微觀隨機試驗，並結合智能手錶與生態瞬時評估，以最佳化即時適應性治療的元素（即根據情境的個人化建議、一般訊息或不推送通知）的效果；以及(3) 進行一項隨機對照試驗，以檢驗最佳化即時適應性治療對睡眠與作息功能在短期及中期的成效。 本計畫將分三個階段進行。第一階段將聚焦於提升即時適應性治療：「好眠羊」技術的先導研究。第二階段將進行一項共有77名有睡眠或作息問題參與者的微觀隨機試驗，他們將參與最佳化後的「好眠羊」。即時適應性治療將不斷調整治療內容與支援程度，以個人化方式提供睡眠治療。其內容包括：(1) 一套為期八週、模組化的跨診斷睡眠及作息模式功能障礙治療；(2) 簡短生態瞬時評估問卷以偵測作息規律性及情緒狀態；(3) 24小時智能手錶以實時監測睡眠與活動量。第三階段為一項隨機對照試驗，共有80名有睡眠或作息問題之參與者，將被隨機分配至接受最佳化即時適應性治療「好眠羊+」或恆常護理對照組。 於微觀隨機試驗中，近端結果將為作息的規律性、活動量及情緒狀態；並將進行治療前後比較。隨機對照試驗的主要評估時點將為基線、治療結束後即時評估及隨後12週的跟進，評估內容包括主觀（如睡眠與作息功能、心理健康症狀）及客觀（如睡眠與清醒模式）指標。混合效應模型將會被應用於評估即時適應性治療對結果的影響。 本計畫將在行為睡眠醫學領域中，以創新方式彌補現有服務的不足。藉着最佳化最先進的即時適應性治療並驗證其成效，我們期望為有睡眠與作息問題的人提供一套準確、具成本效益、低負擔且容易取得的即時、真實的解決方案。

14613625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613625.value: 評估酷熱天氣對香港外展醫護人員心理健康影響的重複測量研究

14613625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14613625.value: Prof Huss, Anke Miss Li, Beixi Miss Ma, Yuen Ting Julie Dr Wang, Feng

14613625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613625.value: Background The growing aging population and rising disease burden are amplifying the demands for extensive community and home healthcare services, placing significant occupational stress and mental health challenges on outreach healthcare providers (OHPs). The extra strain and discomfort from labor-intensive tasks, such as lifting and moving patients, and carrying heavy toolkits while wearing personal protective equipment, contribute to increased mental and other health problems among OHPs. These challenges are exacerbated during home visits in adverse weather conditions, particularly on very hot days. The current heat stress warning system at work was developed using general population data, and there is a lack of workplace-specific evidence on evaluating the mental and other health impacts arising from hot weather conditions with sensor-based individual-level meteorological measurements among local outdoor workers. Objectives The primary objectives are to 1) measure individual-level meteorological exposures (ambient and personal temperature, sunshine/UV radiation, and relative humidity) among Hong Kong OHPs in summer and winter seasons, and create a novel Standard Effective Temperature (SET) index for more accurate characterizing thermal environments from various scenarios; 2) determine biosensor-monitored physiological momentary stress responses of individuals from diverse scenarios; 3) assess mental health impacts (i.e. depression, anxiety) of hot weather conditions and the mixture effects with other meteorological exposures, while considering the mediating pathways of biosensor-monitored physiological stress responses, sleep, physical activity, greenspaces, and noise. Brief description We plan to randomly recruit 400 OHPs for this 3-year study with repeated measures. We will adopt a standard questionnaire to obtain participants’ epidemiological information, sleep quality, and mental health problems (depression, anxiety). Meteorological features and individual-level environmental exposures (e.g., noise, PM2.5) will be collected using portable kits on 7 consecutive days in summer and winter seasons, along with a biosensor to monitor the physiological stress responses from various scenarios. First spot morning urine samples will be collected to assess the levels of cortisone and cortisol. Stress and mental health impacts of hot weather conditions as well as the mixture effects with other meteorological exposures will be examined using multiple logistic and Bayesian kernel machine regression analysis. Significance This proposed project would contribute new insights to enhance evidence-based policies for mitigating hot weather-related mental and other health problems through precise sensor-based individual-level meteorological measurements. Adopting a novel SET index enables more reliable extrapolation of findings from the OHP population and enhances the comparability of thermal environments with other outdoor workers including those in construction. 背景 隨著人口老化與疾病負擔上升，社區與居家醫療服務的需求日益增加，令外展醫護人員（OHPs）承受顯著的職業壓力與心理健康挑戰。抬移病人、搬運沉重工具包等沉重體力工作，尤其是穿戴個人防護裝備後進行這些工作，會帶來額外負荷與不適，從而增加外展醫護人員的心理與其他健康問題。這些挑戰在惡劣天氣，尤其是酷熱天氣下進行家訪時更為嚴重。現行的“香港暑熱指數”及“工作暑熱警告“是以一般人口資料建立，缺乏以本地戶外工作者為對象並結合感測器所測得的個體層面氣象因素而得出的更精準證據。 研究目標 本研究的主要目標為：1) 於夏季與冬季測量香港外展醫護人員個體層面的氣象暴露（環境與個人溫度、日照／紫外線輻射與相對濕度），並建立一個新穎的標準有效溫度（SET）指數，以更準確代表不同場景下的熱環境水平；2) 測定個體在不同場景下、以生物傳感器監測的即時生理壓力反應；3) 評估酷熱天氣對心理健康（如憂鬱、焦慮）的影響及其與其他氣象暴露的混合效應，同時評估生物感測器監測的生理壓力反應、睡眠、身體活動、綠地與噪音等的中介效應。 研究方法簡介 本項目是為期三年的重複測量研究。擬隨機招募400名外展醫護人員。採用標準問卷收集參與者的流行病學資料、睡眠品質與心理健康問題（憂鬱、焦慮）。於夏季與冬季各連續7天以穿戴式傳感器收集個體層面的氣象特徵與環境暴露（如噪音、PM2.5），並配戴生物感測器以監測不同場景下的生理壓力反應。同時，將收集清晨的首次尿樣用於測定皮質酮與皮質醇濃度。之後將運用多元邏輯斯迴歸與貝葉斯核函數迴歸分析，檢視酷熱天氣對壓力與心理健康的影響，以及與其他氣象暴露的混合效應。 研究意義 本研究使用個體感測器精確測量個體層面的氣象因素，可為制定以實證為基礎的職業健康政策提供依據，以減輕與酷熱天氣相關的心理與其他健康問題。本研究采用新穎的SET指數可以更可靠地推斷戶外熱暴露人群的研究結果，並增强與其他戶外工人（如建造業從業員）熱環境的可比性。

14613725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14613725.value: 邁向循證健康老齡化：一項關於≥75歲人群使用降脂藥物預防心血管疾病的獲益與風險的縱向研究

14613725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14613725.value: Prof Lee, Kam-pui Prof Yang, Zhirong

14613725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613725.value: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death both globally and in Hong Kong. Hyperlipidemia is a major risk factor of CVD. Lipid-lowering drugs are thus commonly prescribed for CVD prevention, particularly in older people. 35%-63% of the primary care patients aged ≥75 years in Hong Kong, the United Kingdom and the United States are taking lipid-lowering drugs for preventing CVD. While the drugs have proven effective in younger populations, the evidence about their efficacy in people aged ≥75 years is scarce, because previous clinical trials, for practical reasons, rarely involved such people, and the few relevant trials reported “negative” results. Furthermore, very old people are in general more susceptible to adverse effects of drug treatment due to frailty and multimorbidity. The risk is particularly high in the presence of polypharmacy (concurrent use of ≥5 drugs) which affects nearly half of the older people in Hong Kong. Major professional associations in the world all acknowledge the uncertainty around the balance of benefits and harms of lipid-lowering drugs in people aged ≥75 years and explicitly call for more studies on this topic. Towards evidence-based chronic disease care, a policy focus area in Hong Kong, this project aims to answer three questions that have not been sufficiently addressed by existing studies: 1) Are lipid-lowering drugs overall effective in reducing CVD morbidity and mortality among people aged ≥75 years? 2) Is the efficacy, if existent, affected by negative factors such as multimorbidity and polypharmacy? 3) What are the adverse events specifically associated with long-term use of lipid-lowering drugs in people aged ≥75 years, and who (with what characteristics) are more susceptible to these harms? It will use three internationally recognized, high-quality, longitudinal datasets that allow for overcoming the limitations of previous studies. The project members have a good track record in the research about hyperlipidemia and CVD prevention. Besides, they have collaborated on multiple papers, including one derived from the abovementioned datasets. These experiences laid a solid foundation for this project. The evidence generated by the project should inform rational, individualized use of lipid-lowering drugs in people aged ≥75 years, which can help reduce CVD morbidity and mortality overall while alleviating medication burden and preventing unnecessary harms among those unlikely to benefit, thereby achieving precise prevention of CVD in older people. This should eventually contribute to healthy aging of local and global populations. 心血管疾病（CVD）是全球及香港的頭號死亡原因。高脂血癥是CVD的主要風險因素，因此降脂藥物被廣泛用於預防CVD，尤其在老年人群中。在香港、英國和美國，35%-63%的≥75歲基層醫療患者正在服用降脂藥物預防CVD。雖然這些藥物在較年輕人群中被證實有效，但關於其對≥75歲人群療效的證據十分有限——由於可行性的限制，既往臨床試驗很少納入該年齡組，而少數相關試驗報告了"陰性"結果。此外，高齡人群通常因衰弱和共病狀態更易受到藥物治療不良反應的影響，這種風險在多重用藥（同時使用≥5種藥物）情況下尤為突出，而香港近半數老年人正面臨這種情況。全球主要專業協會均承認，目前關於≥75歲人群使用降脂藥物的獲益-風險的證據不足，並明確呼籲開展更多相關研究。 本項目旨在解決現有研究未充分解決的三個關鍵問題：1）降脂藥物能否降低≥75歲人群整體的CVD發病率和死亡率？2）若能夠的話，其療效是否會受到共病狀態和多重用藥等因素的影響？3）≥75歲人群長期使用降脂藥物會導致哪些特異性不良反應？什麼人群更易受到這些危害？研究將采用三個國際公認的高質量縱向數據集，以克服既往研究的局限性。項目組成員在高脂血癥與CVD預防研究領域業績突出，並已基於上述數據集合作發表多篇論文（含相關前期成果），為本項目奠定了堅實基礎。項目證據將有助於指導≥75歲人群降脂藥物的合理個體化使用，在降低整體CVD負擔的同時，減輕潛在獲益有限患者的用藥負擔並避免不必要的藥物傷害，從而實現CVD的精準預防，最終助力本地及全球健康老齡化目標的實現。

14614925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14614925.value: 開發和測試一個跨國新聞素養量表和干預措施以辨別網路上的錯誤資訊

14614925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14614925.value: Dr Rossini, Patrícia Dr Yamamoto, Masahiro

14614925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14614925.value: The global information environment has become volatile due to the problem of misinformation, which can polarize societies and undermine democratic norms. Following a review of the literature, the International Panel on the Information Environment (IPIE) proposed that greater “information and media literacy” among citizens would be an effective countermeasure against misinformation. However, its actionable value for policymakers is hindered by the different approaches to media literacy and the lack of cross-national evidence. This project focuses specifically on news literacy as it is directly related to discerning what news is real and misleading online, and it addresses the current research gaps by (a) explicating and validating a theoretically informed news literacy scale across different countries and languages and (b) testing the efficacy of news literacy on individuals’ discernment of news veracity (i.e., what is true and what is false). The goal of this project is to provide cross-national evidence that news literacy can be an effective countermeasure against misinformation. News literacy is a component of media literacy that emphasizes knowledge of the dynamics and processes of news production, which should help citizens discern the veracity of the news they consume. It is highly relevant because misleading information (or more colloquially, “fake news”) is often disseminated under the guise of “news” through social media. However, there is still no standard measure of news literacy, and it is unclear whether news literacy is a unidimensional or multidimensional concept. This project will include two phases. Based on the existing literature and input from experts, the first phase will involve constructing, testing, and validating a multilingual news literacy scale through online surveys. The second part will examine whether the news literacy scale and a news literacy intervention can improve individuals’ discernment of news headlines (i.e., whether they are true or false). The project will be conducted in Hong Kong, the United States, and Brazil, which are suitable societies for comparison because they are politically and socially polarized, and their citizens have expressed substantive concerns about and experienced misleading information online. The results from the project will have significance by providing a theoretically derived multilingual scale that can be adapted to other countries. Practically, the findings will answer the call by IPIE for researchers to pursue strategic approaches to better understand the effectiveness of specific countermeasures to mitigate the belief in and spread of misinformation. 由於錯誤資訊的問題，全球資訊環境變得不穩定，這可能導致社會分裂並削弱民主規範。在檢視相關文獻後，國際資訊環境專家小組（IPIE）建議，提高公民的「資訊與媒體素養」將是對抗錯誤資訊的一項有效對策。然而，媒體素養的不同方法以及缺乏跨國證據，限制了其對政策制定者的實際應用價值。本項目專注於新聞素養，因為它與分辨網路上真實與誤導性新聞直接相關，並通過以下方式填補當前研究的空白：（a）闡明並驗證一個基於理論的跨國及多語言新聞素養量表，以及（b）測試新聞素養在個人判斷新聞真實性（即真假辨別）方面的效能。本項目的目標是提供跨國證據，證明新聞素養可以成為對抗錯誤資訊的有效對策。新聞素養是媒體素養的一個組成部分，強調對新聞製作動態和過程的了解，這應能幫助公民辨別他們所接觸新聞的真實性。這一點尤為重要，因為誤導性資訊（或通俗地稱為「假新聞」）經常以「新聞」的名義透過社交媒體傳播。然而，目前尚未有一個標準化的新聞素養衡量方式，也不清楚新聞素養是一個單維度還是多維度的概念。本項目將分為兩個階段進行。 基於現有文獻和專家意見，第一階段將通過線上調查構建、測試並驗證一個多語言的新聞素養量表。第二階段將探討新聞素養量表以及新聞素養干預是否能提升個人對新聞標題（即判斷其真實或虛假）的辨識能力。本項目將在香港、美國和巴西進行，這些社會適合作為比較對象，因為它們在政治和社會上存在極化，其公民對網路上的誤導性資訊表達了實質性的關注並有相關經歷。本項目的結果將具有重要意義，提供一個基於理論的多語言量表，並可適用於其他國家。在實務上，研究結果將回應國際資訊環境專家小組（IPIE）的呼籲，促使研究人員採取策略性方法，更深入了解特定對策在減少對錯誤資訊的信任及其傳播方面的效能。

14615225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14615225.value: 在大灣區引領跨城市學校網路：以四個教育集團為例

14615225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14615225.value: Prof Greany, Toby Prof Walker, Allan David Prof WANG, XIAOLI

14615225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615225.value: Over the past two decades, school networks and inter-school partnerships have been promoted worldwide as mechanisms for sharing knowledge and expertise, improving student outcomes, addressing equity challenges and securing wider innovations. China has a notable history of forming schools into education groups (jiaoyu jituan). In the GBA alone, there are at least four types of school networks that feature cross-school, cross-city, and even cross-border collaboration. Some of these networks include member schools from Mainland China and Hong Kong. These networks are initiated by various entities, including Mainland education bureaus, universities and Hong Kong charitable organisations. As a result, the GBA stands out as one of the most dynamic and diverse regions for school networking, showcasing innovative approaches to school-to-school collaboration. Given this context, a pressing need exists to study how these different types of networks are structured and led. Most educational leadership research tends to focus on specific roles, such as principals, teachers, or district supervisors, and on specific levels, such as system, school, or department levels. This often results in a disjointed portrayal of educational leadership practice. To overcome this siloed perspective, it is crucial to frame educational leadership as a systemwide phenomenon to understand how leadership practice is co-performed and collaborated by leaders at different levels, especially in expanding school networks. This study will adopt a multilevel distributed perspective to examine the leadership distribution and leadership practices in four selected cross-city school networks in the GBA through a case study design. The focus of the research includes the configuration of the school networks (how each network is configurated and how leadership is distributed across the different levels of leaders), leadership practices enacted by different levels of leaders (how each network is actually led, and how different levels of leaders mobilise and coordinate resources and nurture relationships to initiate and implement network-wide improvement initiatives); and impact of joining networks on school leaders (how school-level and teacher leaders of the member schools perceive the benefits of joining a school network). As such, the research will provide a nuanced discussion about the socio-cultural, political and educational conditions that facilitate or inhibit these network configurations and leadership practices in China. The findings will make theoretical contributions and advance understanding of network configuration and multilevel distributed leadership; identify strategies for enhancing leadership capacities in school networks, and inform policies related to school networking. 在過去二十年裡，學校網絡（school networks）和校際合作關係在全球範圍內得到推廣，成為各地政府在校際間共用知識、資源與專業技能、提升學生成績、應對公平挑戰以及實現更廣泛創新的重要機制。中國在組建教育集團方面有著顯著的歷史。僅在粵港澳大灣區（GBA），就至少存在四種類型的學校網絡，它們以跨校、跨市乃至跨境合作為特徵。其中一些網絡包含來自中國內地和香港的成員學校。這些網絡由不同主體發起，包括內地教育局、大學以及香港的慈善組織。因此，粵港澳大灣區成為學校網絡建設最為活躍和多樣化的地區之一，展現了校際合作的創新模式。在這一背景下，研究這些不同類型網絡的結構和領導方式具有迫切的必要性。 大多數教育領導力研究往往聚焦於特定角色，如校長、教師或教育局領導，以及特定層面，如系統、學校或學科組層面。這常常導致對教育領導力實踐的描述缺乏連貫性。為了克服這種孤立的視角，將教育領導力視為一種全系統現象至關重要，有助於理解（在不斷擴展的學校網絡中）不同層面的領導者如何共同履行和協作開展領導實踐。 本研究將採用多層次分佈式領導力視角，通過案例研究設計，考察粵港澳大灣區四個選定的跨城市學校網絡中的領導力分佈和領導實踐。研究重點包括：學校網路的結構配置（每個跨區域網絡如何配置，以及領導力如何在不同層面的領導者之間分佈）；不同層面領導者所採取的領導實踐（每個網絡實際上是如何被領導的，以及不同層面的領導者如何調動和協調資源、培育關係，以發起和實施全網絡範圍的改進舉措）；以及加入網絡對學校領導者的影響（成員學校的校級領導者和教師領導者如何看待加入學校網絡的益處）。 在案例研究的基礎上，本研究將深入探討那些促進或阻礙此類網絡結構配置與領導實踐的社會文化、政治因素及教育制度條件。研究成果將在學校網路研究以及多層次分佈式領導力的理解方面做出理論貢獻；並為改進學校網路的相關政策的制定提供參考。

14615625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14615625.value: 探討在職幼稚園教師於線上專業學習社群如何提升早期視覺藝術的教學能力

14615625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14615625.value: Dr Hung, Keung Prof Jong, Siu-yung, Morris Prof Yin, Hong-biao

14615625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14615625.value: The aim of this study is to examine how in-service kindergarten teachers can establish a professional learning community where teachers share and acquire their artistic knowledge and skills within a digital commons. Arts-related pedagogical practices in Asian kindergarten settings have traditionally been product-oriented. Previous studies argued that teachers need to strengthen their subject knowledge for improving their visual arts teaching in kindergartens. Inadequate teacher training poses limitations in terms of the knowledge and competencies of teachers of early visual arts, and this issue is particularly relevant in Hong Kong. Developing a professional learning community (PLC) could be one of the approaches for teachers’ professional development. Research has indicated that transitioning conventional PLCs to an online format is an effective approach for facilitating professional communities. In Hong Kong, however, no studies have yet investigated how kindergarten teachers can use a digital commons as an online professional learning community for enhancing visual arts education. This study aims to fill this crucial research gap. Our proposed study (1) investigates how in-service kindergarten teachers develop a professional learning community for early visual arts through a digital commons, (2) demonstrates teachers’ artistic knowledge and skills that they shared and acquired within a digital commons, and (3) examines the effectiveness of using a digital commons to enhance their competencies in early visual arts education. Accordingly, we employ the theoretical framework of PLC (supportive and shared leadership, shared practices, shared values and vision, supportive conditions, and collective learning and application for learning) to conduct this study. We apply a mixed-method approach, through observations, interviews and an online survey, to investigate teachers’ PLC behaviours in an online platform, to explore teachers’ knowledge and skills acquired in early visual arts education by using a digital commons, and to evaluate the development and effectiveness of a digital commons. The theoretical contribution of this study lies in expanding our understanding of how kindergarten teachers learn to establish professional learning communities through an online platform. From a practical standpoint, our findings will inform the design and implementation of an online learning platform for Hong Kong’s kindergarten teacher education programmes to enhance the pedagogical content knowledge of kindergarten teachers. Ultimately, the results could influence future curricular reform, promote the wider adoption of a digital commons in Hong Kong kindergartens, and facilitate the development of online professional learning communities for early visual arts education at the local level. 本研究旨在探討如何為在職幼稚園教師建立線上的專業學習社群。透過此電子化的共享學習平台，教師能夠交流並習得有關幼兒藝術教學的專業知識與技能。在亞洲幼稚園中，藝術相關的教學實踐常以結果為導向。過往研究指出，教師需要加強學科知識，以提升在幼稚園課堂中教授視覺藝術的能力。然而，由於教師培訓不足，他們在早期視覺藝術方面的知識與技能受到限制，此問題在香港尤其顯住。有研究指出，建立專業學習社群可能是提升教師專業發展的一條有效途徑。將傳統的專業學習社群轉變為線上形式，已被證實是一種促進專業交流的有效方式。然而，目前在香港，尚未有相關研究探討幼稚園教師如何利用電子共享平台作為線上專業學習社群，以提升其視覺藝術的教學能力。本研究旨在彌補這一重要的研究缺口。 我們擬議的研究目標包括：（1）探討在職幼稚園教師如何通過電子共享平台發展早期視覺藝術的專業學習社群；（2）展示教師在電子共享平台中分享與習得的藝術知識與技能；（3）評估使用電子共享平台在提升教師早期視覺藝術教育能力的有效性。為實現研究目標，我們採用專業學習社群的理論框架，其涵蓋支持性與共享的領導力、共享實踐、共享價值觀與願景、支持性條件，以及集體學習與應用等核心元素來進行本研究。我們將採用混合研究方法，透過觀察、訪談與線上問卷調查，研究教師在線上平台中的專業學習行為，分析教師透過電子共享平台習得的早期視覺藝術教育的知識與技能，並評估平台的開發與實施效果。 本研究的理論貢獻在於拓展我們對幼稚園教師如何透過線上平台建立專業學習社群的理解。從實踐角度來看，研究結果將為香港幼稚園教師教育項目中線上學習平台的設計與實施提供參考，從而提升教師的教學內容與知識。最終，研究成果可能對未來課程改革產生積極影響，促進電子共享平台在香港幼稚園的廣泛應用，並推動本地早期視覺藝術教育在線上專業學習社群的發展。

14616125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616125.value: 創作粵語現代音樂：挑戰、實踐與機遇

14616125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14616125.value: Prof Yim, Patrick Dr Yuen, Lok Ting Christine

14616125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616125.value: Cantonese, a tonal language that uses six distinct pitch levels to differentiate word meanings, is naturally musical. Ironically, its musical expression is often limited by the pitch contour of its tones. Unless Cantonese lyrics are sung to an optimized melody, they can be misunderstood even by native speakers. This is often seen in Cantonese hymns and school anthems where incorrect matching of tone and melody can cause words like ‘principal’ (haau6 zoeng2) to be mistaken for ‘flirty elephant’ (haau4 zoeng6). To understand what constitutes optimal melodic settings for correct perception of the text, scholars have explored the tone-melody interface in Cantonese operas and the strategies lyricists adopt to compose intelligible texts with pre-existing melodies in Cantonese popular music. However, little research has been done regarding how intelligible melodies can be composed for pre-existing texts, and no one to date has explored how composers navigate the text-setting constraints in contemporary classical music, a genre encompassing vocal and instrumental works composed by living composers. This study aims to bridge this gap by employing empirical methods to investigate the unexamined constraints and creative potentials in Cantonese text-inspired contemporary composition. Our methodology includes empirical perception experiments perception experiments where participants listen to recordings of original and altered musical segments to assess whether the Cantonese text can be correctly perceived. Using the test data, we will perform harmonic, rhythmic, and textual analyses of representative pieces to explore how composers transform linguistic constraints into creative opportunities across various musical elements. Currently unexplored in academic contexts, this repertoire of instrumental works with embedded Cantonese texts provides insights into how composers use text-setting to create musical materials beyond the affordances of the human voice. This project will culminate in a suite of open-access web applications that aid Cantonese creativity, a symposium with exchange concerts between the USA and Hong Kong, academic outputs, and other online resources. By exploring the creative practices of a rapidly growing genre that has served as a conduit between the music and the musicality of Cantonese, I expect to offer new tools for musicians across diverse genres of Cantonese music and initiate scholarly collaborations between music studies, linguistics, and computer science. In a broader context, the project will address the under-representation of Cantonese music in the global classical scene, and challenge the stereotypical perception of Asian musics as the cultural Other. 粵語以六聲起伏音高區分詞義，本身具有音樂性。然而，當粵語入曲，其音樂表達往往受限於聲調的音高輪廓。若粵語歌詞未能與旋律協調，即使是母語人士也可能誤解歌詞內容。譬如在不少本地粵語聖詩與校歌中，聲調與旋律若錯配，「主」（zyu2）或誤為「豬」（zyu1），令人啼笑皆非。為探究如何為粵語歌詞配上最適合的旋律以確保文本被正確理解，學者們已研究了粵劇中的詞樂配合，以及粵語流行音樂中如何為既有旋律創作易於理解的歌詞。然而，關於如何為既有文本創作易於理解的旋律，鮮有研究當代古典音樂（涵蓋在世作曲家的聲樂與器樂作品）中，作曲家如何應對據詞譜曲的限制。 本研究旨在填補這一空白，通過感知實驗，讓參與者聆聽原始與改編的音樂片段，判斷能否正確辨識旋律的粵語聲調。根據實驗數據，我們將分析和聲、節奏和織體，研究作曲家如何將語言限制轉化為音樂創作的機遇。嵌入粵語文本的器樂作品尚未被學界充分研究，這類作品顯示作曲家如何以詞為引，超越人聲之限，創作出新穎的音樂語言。 本項目將產出多項成果：創作輔助軟件、美國與香港的交流音樂會、學術論文和線上資源。通過研究這一新興音樂類型如何把粵語言特色融入音樂，我們期望為粵語音樂家提供新工具，並促進音樂、語言學與計算機科學的跨學科合作。推而廣之，本研究致力提升粵語音樂在全球古典音樂中的地位，改變對亞洲音樂作為「他者」的刻板印象。

14616325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616325.value: 太平洋亞洲跨界：性／別與海洋影像

14616325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616325.value: In recent decades, oceanic themes and underwater scenes have increasingly appeared in film and video works, both globally and in Asia. Corresponding to the rise of blue humanities and critical ocean studies, scholars have dived into the research of aquatic films (Starosielski 2013), underwater filmmaking (Cohen 2022), ocean wildlife documentaries (Ferguson 2006, Mikkola 2018), and ideas such as underwater optics and film and immersivity (D’Aloia 2012). However, most of this work has focused on American, European, and Australian films, and not much has touched upon imagination of the ocean and the underwater world in East Asian or Southeast Asian cinema. On the other hand, although East Asian cinema and Southeast Asian cinema are established academic subfields, not much has been written on the ocean and cinema or has considered the ocean and water as a major theme or framework. These two area cinemas rely on continental models of national cinema, and even fewer works have linked them together or considered them in conjunction. Building upon previous scholarship concerning the oceanic turn and the interconnectedness of the ocean, Transing Pacific Asia seeks to trace how gender, sexuality, and the ocean intersect in Pacific Asian cinema. Combining feminist and queer theory, decolonial Asian studies, and the oceanic turn, Transing Pacific Asia looks at oceanic imagination and calls for a transing and submerged perspective in the study of Pacific Asian media. It defines transing as the questioning of bodily, material, national, and epistemic categories. Investigating what is interconnected within Pacific Asia through the study of oceanic cinema, Transing Pacific Asia will engage with two notions of transing: the transing of the body in transgender studies and in feminist posthuman theorization of transcorporeality, and the transing of national boundaries. Specifically, I will examine three interconnected themes. The first theme focuses on the intersection of (under)water, gender, and desire, specifically, the gendered and sexualized trope of mermaids and merfolk, as well as films that reveal new currents in the representation of gender and sexuality. The second theme encompasses film and video works on coastal and Indigenous communities, highlighting the colonial administration of sexuality and contemporary feminized labor, such as female free divers in Japan and South Korea. The third theme consists of representations of nonhuman animals and the oceanic environment in eco-documentaries. 近年來，海洋主題與水下場景在全球與亞洲的電影與影像作品中越來越常見。隨著「藍色人文學」與「批判性海洋研究」的興起，學者們開始深入探討與水相關的電影領域，包括水域電影（Starosielski 2013）、水下攝影（Cohen 2022）、海洋野生動物紀錄片（Ferguson 2006，Mikkola 2018），以及水下光學、沉浸式影像等概念（D’Aloia 2012）。然而，這些研究大多集中在歐美與澳洲的電影，對東亞或東南亞電影中對海洋與水下世界的想像則著墨甚少。另一方面，儘管東亞與東南亞電影已是成熟的學術領域，但關於海洋與電影的研究仍不多，也很少將海洋與水作為主要主題或分析框架。這兩個地區的電影研究多依循「國族電影」的陸地模式，且更少有作品將兩者連結或並置思考。 「太平洋亞洲跨界」這個研究在既有的海洋轉向基礎上，探索性／別與海洋在太平洋亞洲電影中的交會。結合女性主義與酷兒理論、去殖民的亞洲研究，以及海洋轉向的視角，本書提出一種「跨界」與「沉潛」的觀看方式，重新思考太平洋亞洲的媒體研究。此處的「跨界」（transing）指的是對身體、物質、國族與知識分類的質疑與重構。透過海洋電影的研究，本書將探討太平洋亞洲內部的互聯性，並聚焦於兩種「跨界」概念：一是跨性別研究與女性主義後人類理論中的「跨身體性」（transcorporeality），二是對國族邊界的跨越。本研究將聚焦三個彼此交織的主題：首先，探討水與水下空間如何與性別與慾望交會，特別是美人魚與水族人等性別化的意象，以及呈現性／別新潮流的影像作品；其次，分析描繪海岸與原住民社群的影像作品，關注政府對性別的治理與當代女性勞動的樣貌，例如日本與韓國的海女；最後，探討生態紀錄片中對非人動物與海洋環境的再現，思考人與自然之間的關係與倫理。

14616525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616525.value: 雲端落地：中國城市數據中心選址的結構－技術關聯分析

14616525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14616525.value: Prof Chung, Calvin King Lam Prof LIU, Yan Dr Zhang, Mengzhu

14616525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616525.value: Goal: For this qualitative study, we propose a nuanced conceptualisation to explain the politics of data centre (DC) siting in four Pearl River Delta cities and the new politics following these DCs’ operation. Despite varying conditions and approaches to DC development, these cities have established DCs, making it a critical area of investigation. Instead of viewing DC siting as an optimisation process, we hypothesise that siting decisions are fiercely contested, with actors battling to enact a particular governance structure for DC siting using governmental technologies. This political process generates new power dynamics, influenced by each city’s unique political-economic conditions and resources. We will critically review DC siting policies and interview key actors to verify our hypothesis, with the aid of qualitative analytical methods and large language models. Significance: China’s central government has heavily invested in next-generation information technologies, making DCs a cornerstone of the 14th Five-Year Plan. Local governments have integrated DCs into their digital economy development plans. However, the resource-intensive nature of DCs, with high land and energy demands, challenges China’s goals for food security, ecological civilisation, and carbon neutrality. Some cities impose constraints on DC development due to limited land and energy quotas, while others prioritise it without such restrictions. DC siting has become a critical aspect of China’s digital infrastructure development, evoking both admiration and frustration. These complexities create a unique political landscape influencing China’s urban and regional development. Researching how Chinese cities navigate these complexities is crucial for developing theoretical insights into the politics of digital infrastructure and informing policies to mitigate the negative impacts of DC development. Novelty: Previous studies on the politics of DC siting have primarily focused on the struggles over governance structure, i.e. actors at which governance scale and in which sector can have a greater say. These studies have downplayed how governance structure can be enforced. Another focus is on how governmental technologies are critical to actors’ attempts to shape others to make DC siting decisions in particular ways. Both types of studies have offered insightful, albeit one-sided, explanations of the politics of DC siting. Building on these studies, we propose the concept of ‘structure-technology nexus’ to examine such politics as a process that involves concurrent struggles over the governance structure of DC siting and the governmental technologies deployed to enact such structure. 項目目標：本質性研究旨在提出一個更具細緻性的概念框架，以解釋珠三角四個城市數據中心（DC）選址的政治過程，以及這些數據中心投入運作後所引發的新政治動態。儘管各城市在數據中心發展方面的條件與策略不盡相同，它們均已建成數據中心，使其成為值得深入探討的關鍵議題。本研究假設，數據中心的選址並非單純的優化過程，而是充滿爭議的政治場域。各方行動者透過治理術，爭奪對選址治理架構的主導權。這一政治過程在不同城市的政治經濟條件與資源背景下，產生了新的權力動態。我們將批判性地審視數據中心選址政策，並訪談關鍵行動者，以驗證研究假設。研究將結合質性分析方法與大型語言模型進行輔助分析。 項目意義：中國中央政府大力推動新一代信息技術，數據中心已成為「十四五」規劃中的基礎支柱。地方政府亦將數據中心納入其數字經濟發展藍圖。然而，數據中心對土地與能源的高度依賴，對中國的糧食安全、生態文明與碳中和目標構成挑戰。部分城市因土地與能源配額有限而對數據中心發展設限，另一些城市則優先推進，未設明確限制。數據中心選址已成為中國數字基礎設施發展中的關鍵環節，既引發讚賞，也帶來困惑與爭議。這些複雜性構成了影響中國城市與區域發展的獨特政治景觀。研究中國城市如何應對這些挑戰，對於發展數字基礎設施政治的理論洞見，以及制定減緩數據中心負面影響的政策，具有重要意義。 項目創新性：過去關於數據中心選址政治的研究，主要聚焦於治理架構的爭奪，即哪些治理層級與部門的行動者能擁有更大話語權。這些研究往往忽略了治理架構如何被具體實施與強化。另一研究重點則是治理術如何成為行動者影響他人選址決策的關鍵工具。這兩類研究雖提供了有價值的見解，但仍偏向單一視角。本研究在此基礎上，提出「結構－技術關聯」（structure-technology nexus）概念，以更全面地分析數據中心選址的政治過程。

14616925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616925.value: 生成式人工智能對STEM自主學習中的需求滿足：支持還是阻礙？

14616925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14616925.value: Dr Bond, Melissa Dr Fenyvesi, Kristóf Dr Fung, Chun Lok, Dennis Prof Lavicza, Zsolt

14616925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616925.value: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have the potential to foster student self-regulated learning (SRL) more effectively than non-AI technology. Some argue, however, that over-relying on these technologies may lead to a decrease in human connection and higher-order thinking skills.
