This proposed randomized controlled trial, coupled with a longitudinal process evaluation, aims to: (1) determine the effectiveness of a theory-based SHE program compared to a Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) app and waitlist control in adults with an insomnia disorder, (2) identify facilitators and barriers to participant adherence to the intervention, and (3) explore the impact mechanisms of SHE by evaluating how these and other mediators affect insomnia improvement. We will recruit 264 adults with an insomnia disorder, randomizing subjects to either the theory-based SHE intervention, CBT-I app, or a wait-list control group. Participants in the SHE group will receive two face-to-face, 2-hour SHE sessions in a small group, followed by four weekly individual telephone consultations. Participants in CBT-I app group will receive a CBT-I program consisting of six weekly modules, which are delivered in the Chinese language through a smartphone application proACT-S. Participants in the waitlist control will receive no study intervention. The primary outcome measure is the severity of insomnia symptoms and daytime impairment, assessed by the Insomnia Severity Index at weeks 6, 12, and 24. Secondary outcomes include subjective sleep diary data and objective actigraphy, as well as anxiety and depressive symptoms, and quality of life. We will assess intervention adherence through a daily record logbook. Post-follow-up qualitative focus group interviews will be conducted for in-depth analysis of facilitators, barriers, and mediating factors in a standalone process evaluation. The present proposal will examine a novel, theory-based SHE program that utilizes behavior change techniques to promote participants’ adherence and, hence, effectiveness, addressing the limitations of the traditional SHE, which only provides educational instructions without guidance on habit modification. Our study results will provide robust evidence of the cost-effectiveness of SHE as a standalone therapy and CBT-I app, which will greatly relieve a prevalent and burdensome health problem in the community. 睡眠衛生教育（Sleep Hygiene Education, SHE）是一種可及性高、成本低的失眠干預措施。然而，SHE 以教育為主，較少關注行為改變，導致其療效有限。因此，SHE 尚未被廣泛推薦作為失眠患者的單一治療方法。為解決這一問題，本研究擬探討一種基於理論、以行為改變為核心的 SHE 方法，結合相關理論中的行為改變技術（Behavior Change Techniques），以期充分發揮 SHE 的治療潛力。 本項擬開展的隨機對照試驗結合縱向過程評估，旨在：（1）比較基於理論的 SHE 項目與認知行為治療失眠（Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia, CBT-I）手機應用程式及等待名單對照組在成人失眠障礙患者中的療效；（2）識別影響參與者干預依從性的促進因素與障礙因素；（3）通過評估這些及其他仲介變數對失眠改善的影響機制，探索 SHE 的作用路徑。我們將招募264名失眠障礙成人，隨機分配至基於理論的 SHE 干預組、CBT-I 應用程式組或等待名單對照組。SHE 組參與者將接受兩次每次2小時的小組面對面 SHE 培訓，隨後進行為期四周的每週一次個別電話諮詢。CBT-I 應用程式組參與者將通過智慧手機應用程式 proACT-S 接受為期六周的中文 CBT-I 模組。等待名單對照組參與者則不接受任何研究干預。 主要結局指標為失眠症狀嚴重程度及日間功能損害，採用失眠嚴重程度指數（Insomnia Severity Index）於第6、12、24周評估。次要結局包括主觀睡眠日記資料和客觀活動記錄儀（actigraphy）資料，以及焦慮、抑鬱症狀和生活品質。干預依從性將通過每日記錄日誌進行評估。隨訪後將開展定性焦點小組訪談，對促進因素、障礙因素及仲介因素進行深入過程評估分析。 本研究將評估一種新型、基於理論的 SHE 項目，通過行為改變技術促進參與者依從性和療效，彌補傳統 SHE 僅提供教育指導、缺乏習慣改變指導的局限性。研究結果將為 SHE 及 CBT-I 應用程式作為單一治療手段的成本效益提供有力證據，有望顯著緩解社區中普遍且負擔沉重的健康問題。

15106525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15106525.value: 腸道菌群在視神經脊髓炎譜系疾病相關性視神經炎中的炎症調節作用

15106525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15106525.value: Prof CEN, Ling-Ping Prof Chan, Ho-lung Henry Dr CHAN, Kar-mun, Carmen Prof CHEN, Tingjun Ms HUANG, Yuanchun Dr Lam, Chuen Thomas Prof THAM, Clement Chee-yung Dr ZHOU, Liping

15106525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106525.value: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a severe autoimmune inflammatory disorder of the central nervous system (CNS), with NMOSD-related optic neuritis (NMOSD-ON) being a significant manifestation that primarily targets the optic nerve and often leads to permanent vision loss. Compelling clinical evidence and our previous studies confirm a link between gut microbiota and NMOSD-ON in patients with seropositive aquaporin-4 (AQP4)-IgG (AQP4-ON), with Prevotella copri identified as a notable intestinal bacterium that influences the immune response. Additionally, our proteomic analysis and established antibiotic cocktail treatment (ABX) AQP4-ON mouse model indicate T cell-mediated cytotoxicity and microglial activation during disease development. This leads to the hypothesis that gut microbiota dysbiosis, particularly involving P. copri, plays a regulatory role in neuroinflammation during the development of NMOSD-ON, potentially promoting T cell activation and differentiation in the systemic immune system while activating microglia in the CNS. To validate this hypothesis, we will utilise the ABX AQP4-ON mouse model to explore the effects of colonisation with gut microbiota from AQP4-ON patients and monocolonisation with P. copri. Neural cytotoxicity and inflammation will be assessed through histology and immunofluorescence staining of the retina and optic nerves at multiple time points during disease development. In vivo imaging will monitor the retinal structure and integrity of RGCs, while visual function will be monitored through electrophysiological experiments. T cell phenotypes and microglial activation will be investigated by flow cytometry and reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in the colonised ABX AQP4-ON mice. Quantitatively analyses will evaluate the impact of dysbiosis on neural cytotoxicity, inflammation, T cell activation and differentiation, as well as microglial activation during disease development. Studying the gut microbiota’s role in NMOSD-ON will not only enhance our understanding of the complex interplay between gut microbiota and neuroimmune responses in NMOSD-ON, but also deepen our comprehension of the interactions between the gut and the CNS in autoimmune disorders. Furthermore, it will lay the groundwork for novel therapeutic strategies targeting gut microbiota, potentially leading to breakthroughs in the treatment of NMOSD and related conditions.

15108225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15108225.value: NOPE：一種可調控肝細胞癌可塑性狀態關鍵因子的甲胎蛋白

15108225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15108225.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, with most patients diagnosed at advanced stages when resection or transplantation is ineffective. Sorafenib and lenvatinib, molecularly targeted therapies, have improved survival in advanced HCC, but their benefits may be limited by acquired drug resistance. Tumor cells exploit the embryonic stem cell (ESC) pathway, known as cell plasticity, to evade targeted therapies. Several embryonic proteins that regulate ESC properties and are reactivated in tumors, known as 'oncofetal proteins,’ have been identified as liver tumor-initiating cell (T-IC) markers. Glypican-3 (GPC-3) is a promising HCC therapeutic target; however, the limited identification of functionally significant cell surface oncofetal proteins hinders its clinical application. Identification of novel oncofetal proteins with defined T-IC functions is crucial for developing strategies to combat tumor recurrence and drug resistance in HCC. Analysis of in-house T-ICs OMICS profiling datasets from HCC clinical samples, including comparisons of CD133+ liver T-ICs to CD133- non-T-ICs subsets and CD24+ liver T-ICs to CD24- non-T-IC subsets, along with publicly available datasets using machine-learning-derived stemness scores, revealed 13 cell surface receptors consistently upregulated in liver T-ICs and exhibiting increased expression in TCGA datasets. A human hepatocyte differentiation model was used to identify oncofetal proteins that peaked during the intermediate stages of liver development, absent in mature hepatocytes but upregulated in HCC tumor tissues, leading to the identification of IGDCC1, also known as NOPE, as a potential oncofetal protein indicating liver T-ICs. Enrichment of stem cell signature in NOPE-high-expressing HCC patients further suggests NOPE's role in regulating cell plasticity in HCC. To date, the clinical relevance and functional role of NOPE in HCC remain unclear and the potential regulation of phenotypic plasticity has not been explored. In our pilot study, NOPE was found to regulate the cell state and drug resistance. In HCC patients, elevated NOPE mRNA levels correlated with poor survival. AP-MS and immunoprecipitation confirmed NOPE's direct interaction with PABPC1, thereby regulating the β-catenin signaling pathway. We hypothesize that NOPE and its signaling cascade regulate HCC cell plasticity and have clinical relevance. This study aims to (1) characterize NOPE's role in cell plasticity and drug resistance, (2) elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, and (3) evaluate NOPE's clinical significance and correlation with liver T-IC in HCC. Achieving these goals may reveal NOPE's novel function in regulating plastic cell states and drug resistance, potentially leading to innovative HCC therapies.

15109525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15109525.value: 生化與結構生物學研究解析自噬與溶酶體功能主調控因子TFEB在營養信號調控下的核質穿梭過程

15109525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15109525.value: Autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved cellular “self-eating” process that degrades cytosolic content in a lysosome-dependent manner. Autophagy and lysosomal dysfunction have been implicated in various human diseases including cancer and neurodegeneration. The Transcription Factor EB (TFEB) is a member of the MiT-TFE family of transcription factors with a conserved basic helix-loop-helix-leucine-zipper (bHLH-Zip) domain for DNA binding. TFEB binds to a network of genes containing the Coordinated Lysosomal Expression and Regulation (CLEAR) motif and acts as master regulator of autophagy and lysosomal function. Dysregulated TFEB activity has been linked to obesity and tumorigenesis. TFEB undergoes nutrient-driven nucleocytoplasmic shuttling as regulated by mTOR-related nutrient-sensing pathways. Under nutrient-rich conditions, TFEB is phosphorylated and retained in the cytosol. Nutrient deprivation triggers the dephosphorylation of TFEB and its rapid nuclear import to activate transcription of the CLEAR network of autophagy and lysosomal genes. Following nutrient refeeding, nuclear TFEB is re-phosphorylated and exported back to the cytosol to turn off the transcription activity. The molecular machinery that carries out the nuclear import/export of TFEB and their modulation by mTOR signaling is not fully understood and will be the focus of our study. Additionally, TFEB was recently reported to undergo liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) in the nucleus. The resulting TFEB condensates was shown to be critical for transcription of the CLEAR network. How the LLPS of TFEB affects its nutrient-driven nucleocytoplasmic shuttling is not known and will also be investigated. Guided by our previous studies of the autophagy process and the karyopherin (Kap) proteins that constitutes the nuclear import/export machinery, we hypothesize that the interplay between Kap proteins and the LLPS of TFEB regulates nutrient-driven nucleocytoplasmic shuttling. We propose to conduct biochemical and structural studies to investigate how Kap-α/β molecules responsible for the nuclear import of TFEB recognize the Nuclear Localization Signal (NLS) embedded in the bHLH-Zip domain. We will also study how CRM1, the Kap protein responsible for nuclear export of TFEB, interacts with the Nuclear Export Signal (NES) that is subject to mTOR phosphorylation. Lastly, we will study how Kap-α/β and CRM1 modulate the LLPS of TFEB to facilitate its nuclear import/export. We have obtained extensive preliminary data that demonstrate the feasibility of our research plan and serve as initial validation of our hypothesis. Findings from this study will offer novel insight on nutrient-regulated TFEB activity and how to target TFEB in human physiology and diseases. 自噬是一種進化上高度保守的細胞“自我吞噬”過程，通過溶酶體依賴性機制降解胞質內容物。 自噬及溶酶體功能障礙已被證實與多種人類疾病相關，包括癌症和神經退行性疾病。 轉錄因子EB（TFEB）屬於MiT-TFE家族轉錄因子，具有保守的bHLHZip結構域，能夠結合含有（CLEAR）基序的基因網路協調相關基因的轉錄。 TFEB作為自噬及溶酶體功能的主調控因子，其異常活性已被發現與肥胖和腫瘤發生密切相關。 TFEB在細胞核與細胞質之間的穿梭受mTOR相關的營養感應通路調控，並呈現營養依賴性。 在營養充足條件下，TFEB被磷酸化並滯留於胞質中; 而營養缺乏時，TFEB去磷酸化並迅速轉運入核，啟動CLEAR網路相關自噬及溶酶體基因的轉錄。 營養補充后，核內TFEB再次被磷酸化並輸出至胞質，從而關閉其轉錄活性。 目前，介導TFEB核質穿梭的分子機制及其受mTOR信號調控的具體方式尚未完全闡明，這個問題將成為本研究的重點。 此外，近期研究發現，TFEB在細胞核內可發生液-液相分離（LLPS），形成的TFEB凝聚體對於CLEAR網路基因的轉錄至關重要。 然而，TFEB的LLPS如何影響其營養驅動的核質穿梭尚不清楚，本研究亦將對此進行研究。 基於我們此前對自噬過程及核轉運蛋白（karyopherin， Kap）相關研究的積累，我們假設Kap蛋白與TFEB的LLPS之間的相互作用調控其營養依賴性的核質穿梭。 我們擬開展生化及結構生物學研究，探討負責TFEB核進口的Kap-α/β分子如何識別bHLH-Zip結構域中嵌入的核定位信號（NLS）; 同時研究負責TFEB核輸出的Kap蛋白CRM1如何與受mTOR磷酸化調控的核輸出信號（NES）相互作用。 最後，我們還將研究Kap-α/β和CRM1如何調控TFEB的LLPS，以促進其核質穿梭過程。 我們已積累大量的前期數據，有力支援了本研究方案的可行性，併為我們的科學假設提供了初步驗證。 預計本研究的成果將為營養調控下TFEB活性的分子機制，以及其在人體生理和疾病中的靶向調控策略，提供新的科學參考和依據。

15109925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15109925.value: 重複經顱磁刺激增強中風患者雙重任務鍛鍊益處的效果與機制

15109925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15109925.value: Prof Chau, Ka Hung Bolton Dr Chung, Raymond Chi Keung Dr Yang, Leon Lei

15109925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15109925.value: Functional ambulation requires the ability to walk while simultaneously engaging in an attention-demanding cognitive task (i.e., dual-tasking). However, stroke survivors often present with greater deficits in dual-task walking function than their able-bodied peers. Impaired dual-task walking may hinder successful reintegration into community living and contribute to a greater risk of falling. Structured dual-task exercise training has shown promise in improving function post-stroke. Evidence from imaging studies suggests that the prefrontal cortex is a strong neural correlate of dual-task walking function, making it a potential target for interventions to improve dual-task walking post-stroke. Non-invasive brain stimulation has been shown to have a positive impact on upper-limb motor function and gait after a stroke. It is thought to enhance the effects of exercise training, resulting in improved outcomes compared to exercise alone. Preliminary evidence from previous research suggests that repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) can induce the greatest improvements in dual-task gait in patients with Parkinson’s disease or post-stroke compared with the stimulation of other brain regions. Similarly, our pilot study of 30 stroke patients found that the addition of rTMS to dual-task exercise training induced greater improvements in dual-task walking than dual-task exercise alone. A study with a larger sample size and rigorous design is needed to comprehensively determine the effects of rTMS in this context. Additionally, previous studies have focused primarily on temporal measures of dual-task gait (e.g., speed), but not other important gait parameters that are highly relevant to functional walking (e.g., gait variability and stability), suggesting that a more comprehensive assessment of gait performance following rTMS is warranted. There is also a need to examine the neural mechanisms underlying the improvements seen in dual-task walking following rTMS. Given these considerations, the overall aims of the study will be to examine (1) the effects of rTMS of the DLPFC prior to dual-task exercise on dual-task mobility and cognitive performance, compared to sham rTMS combined with dual-task exercise, and (2) the mediation effect of PFC activity on the impact of this intervention (rTMS + dual-task exercise) on dual-task mobility and cognitive performance. The proposed project is innovative in that it will be the first to study the effects of rTMS in combination with dual-task training. The results generated will inform clinical practice in stroke rehabilitation and provide a greater understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying post-stroke impairment of dual-task walking.

15111225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15111225.value: 阐明细胞质中NFAT5生物分子凝聚体在哺乳动物高渗应激反应中的新功能及调控机制。

15111225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15111225.value: Mammalian cells elicit genetic programs of adaptive cellular activities in response to changes in extracellular tonicity to maintain normal cellular function. Nuclear Factor of Activated T-cells 5 (NFAT5) is a mammalian transcription factor crucial for cell survival and adaptation to hypertonicity via orchestrating the expression of a battery of osmo-protective genes. NFAT5 activity is tightly regulated by nuclear availability. We made novel observations that cytoplasmic NFAT5 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to form biomolecular condensates under isotonic condition. Hypertonic stress induced dissolution of the NFAT5 cytoplasmic biomolecular condensates in an importin-beta-dependent manner that is necessary for NFAT5 nuclear import. We further showed the formation of NFAT5 cytoplasmic biomolecular condensates is regulated by a novel intrinsic disorder regions (IDRs) located at the N-terminal half of the NFAT5 (N-IDRs). Recombinant N-IDRs protein underwent LLPS and demonstrated characteristic features of biomolecular condensates. The propensity of N-IDRs LLPS was inhibited by elevated ionic strength in vitro, concordant with the dissolution of cytoplasmic NFAT5 biomolecular condensates by hypertonic stress in cellulo. We hypothesized that NFAT5 cytoplasmic condensates function as a signaling hub for transducing hypertonic stress signals to NFAT5 functional response. We propose to delineate the mechanism underlying how N-IDRs mediates LLPS under isotonic condition, and how hypertonic stress leads to its dissolution. We will establish a NFAT5-mNeonGreen fusion reporter cell line for real time monitoring of dynamics of NFAT5 biomolecular condensates in native setting. We will also define the minimal amino acid sequence, and thoroughly evaluate the molecular determinants, including charge, charge block, and post-translational modifications, on the sequence that regulates LLPS. Furthermore, we will elucidate how importin-beta regulates NFAT5 biomolecular condensates by evaluating the importin-beta-interacting sequence on N-IDRs. Finally, we will conduct siRNA screen of the kinome to identify potential kinase(s) that regulate N-IDRs and NFAT5 LLPS under hypertonic stress, and characterize the phosphorylation sites of N-IDRs by the candidate kinase(s). A recently published work showed that upon hypertonic stress, nuclear NFAT5 is organized into biomolecular condensates that are important for its transcriptional activity, mediated by a novel IDRs located at the C-terminal half the protein. Therefore, NFAT5 is the only known protein with two distinctive IDRs that show opposite LLPS property in different cellular compartments under the same stimulus. Our proposed studies hold value in unveiling a novel regulatory mechanism for NFAT5 activation, and contribute to our understanding on the emerging concept of cellular regulation through LLPS. 哺乳动物细胞针对细胞外渗透压的变化激发适应性细胞活动的遗传程序，以维持正常的细胞功能。活化T细胞核因子5（NFAT5）是哺乳动物中的一种转录因子，通过调控一系列渗透保护基因的表达，对细胞在高渗透压环境下的生存和适应至关重要。NFAT5的活性受到其核内可用性的严格调控。我们首次观察到，细胞质中的NFAT5在等渗条件下经历液-液相分离（LLPS），形成生物分子凝聚体。高渗透压应激通过依赖于importin-beta的机制诱导NFAT5细胞质生物分子凝聚体的解离，而这一过程对NFAT5的核转运是必需的。进一步研究表明，NFAT5细胞质生物分子凝聚体的形成受位于NFAT5 N端半部分的新型固有无序区（N-IDRs）调控。重组N-IDRs蛋白在体外呈现LLPS特性，并显示出生物分子凝聚体的典型特征。体外高离子强度抑制了N-IDRs的LLPS倾向，这与高渗透压应激在细胞内引起的NFAT5细胞质凝聚体解离现象相一致。我们假设NFAT5细胞质凝聚体作为一个信号枢纽，将高渗透压应激信号传导给NFAT5功能响应。我们计划阐明N-IDRs在等渗条件下介导LLPS的机制，以及高渗透压如何导致其解离。我们将建立一个NFAT5-mNeonGreen融合报告细胞系，用于实时监测NFAT5生物分子凝聚体在本征环境中的动态变化。我们还将确定调控LLPS的最小氨基酸序列，全面评估序列上的分子决定因素，包括电荷、电荷区块和翻译后修饰。此外，我们将通过评估N-IDRs上与importin-beta相互作用的序列，阐明importin-beta如何调控NFAT5生物分子凝聚体。最后，我们将进行激酶组siRNA筛选，以识别可能调控N-IDRs和NFAT5在高渗透压应激下LLPS的激酶，并鉴定候选激酶对N-IDRs的磷酸化位点。一项最新发表的研究显示，高渗透压应激下，核内NFAT5组织形成生物分子凝聚体，这对其转录活性至关重要，该过程由位于蛋白质C端半部分的新型固有无序区介导。NFAT5是目前唯一已知具有两个结构不同、在同一刺激下于不同细胞区室中表现出相反LLPS行为的固有无序区的蛋白质。我们提出的研究对于揭示NFAT5激活的全新调控机制具有重要价值，并将促进对通过LLPS实现细胞调控这一新兴概念的理解。

15111325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15111325.value: 新泛醌合成原核生物細胞器的發現和結構分析

15111325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15111325.value: Ubiquinone (UQ), or commonly known as coenzyme Q in eukaryotes, is a redox-active lipid that has a fundamental role in cellular bioenergetics. In bacteria, UQ is an essential component of the aerobic respiratory chain by serving as a key electron carrier to facilitate ATP synthesis through oxidative phosphorylation and therefore its presence is crucial for energy production and bacterial survival. Additionally, UQ functions as a membrane-soluble antioxidant, protecting bacterial cells from oxidative damage. Its involvement in various metabolic pathways allows bacteria to adapt to diverse environments, making UQ vital for their growth and pathogenicity. Being one of the most hydrophobic molecules exists in nature, most of the reactions involved in the biosynthesis of UQ are paradoxically carried by a number of soluble enzymes that assemble together to form a large 1-MDa multienzyme complex for carrying out the biosynthesis of UQ in the cytosol – a groundbreaking result recently published by Pierrel and colleagues (Chehade M.H. et al, 2019). Exactly why UQ biosynthesis requires the formation of a soluble metabolon and the molecular mechanism underlying UQ production in bacteria are virtually unknown. As a first step towards understanding this fundamental biochemical process, we undertake a structural biology approach. Our laboratory has succeeded in isolating the soluble, endogenous mulitenzyme complex and determined its native structure to high resolution by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). The resulting cryo-EM reconstruction reveals an unexpected quaternary organization of the Ubi enzymes on a lipid vesicle and has led to the discovery of a novel prokaryotic organelle, which we termed as the ubiquinosome. Building upon our novel findings, in this proposal, we will further structurally characterize the fine architecture of the ubiquinosome nanocompartment by combining cryo-EM and mass spectrometry. We will also resolve the structures of the Ubi complex during its catalytic turnover. By determining the first complete structure of an intact UQ biosynthetic complex, we anticipate that the results emerged from this study will provide breakthrough in the field of bioenergetics and paves the way for numerous future follow-up studies. Our proposed work not only provides invaluable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying UQ biosynthesis in bacteria, but also new directions for rational design of novel antibiotics that specifically target the Ubi complex. Ubiquinone (UQ)，在真核生物中通常稱為輔酵素 Q，是一種具有氧化還原活性的脂質，在細胞生物能中扮演重要角色。在細菌中，UQ 是有氧呼吸鏈中重要的元件，透過氧化磷酸化作用，成為促進 ATP合成的關鍵電子載體，因此它的存在對能量的產生和細菌的存活至關重要。此外，UQ 可作為膜溶性抗氧化劑，保護細菌細胞免受氧化損害。它參與各種代謝途徑，使細菌能適應各種環境，因此 UQ 對於細菌的生長和致病性至關重要。 作為自然界中最疏水的分子之一，UQ 的生物合成過程中所涉及的大部分反應 ，卻由許多可溶性酵素，這些酵素組合起來形成一個 1-MDa 的大型多酵素複合物，在細胞體內進行UQ 的生物合成--這是 Pierrel 和同事最近發表的一項突破性成果。究竟為什麼 UQ 的生物合成需要可溶性代謝分子的形成，以及細菌中產生 UQ 的分子機制幾乎是未知的。 我們採用了結構生物學的方法，作為了解這個基本生化過程的第一步。我們的實驗室已成功分離出可溶的內源多酵素複合物，並透過冷凍電子顯微鏡 (cryo-EM) 確定其高解析度的原生結構。所得到的冷凍電子顯微鏡重建結果揭示了在脂質囊泡上的 Ubi 複合酶的四元組織，進而發現了一個我們稱之為泛素體（ubiquinosome）的新原核生物細胞器。在此基礎上，我們將結合冷凍電鏡和質量光譜分析，進一步從結構上描述泛素體納米區的細微結構。我們還將解析 Ubi 複合物在其催化轉換過程中的結構。我們預期這項研究的結果將為生物能學領域帶來突破，並為未來許多後續研究鋪路。我們建議的工作不僅提供了有關 UQ在細菌中生物合成的分子機制的見解，也為專門針對 Ubi 複合物的新型抗生素的合理設計提供了新方向。

15111525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15111525.value: 新型基因簇介導細菌對阿奇霉素抗性的潛在機制

15111525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15111525.value: Azithromycin (AZI) is a widely used broad-spectrum macrolide antibiotic drug, widely employed for combating a spectrum of infections spanning respiratory, skin, gastrointestinal, aural, and sexually transmitted ailments. Despite its efficacy, the relentless surge in clinical resistance to AZI poses a formidable challenge, escalating treatment complexities, costs, and inciting heightened concerns regarding the dissemination of resistance genes and the concomitant infection control hurdles. Building upon our prior investigations into the multifaceted landscape of AZI resistance mechanisms within clinical pathogens, our scrutiny unearthed a groundbreaking revelation: the dynamic interplay between the Mph(A) enzyme and the Mrx efflux pump, ushering in a novel paradigm in our understanding of antimicrobial resistance. This serendipitous discovery spurred us to explore analogous realms of synergistic functional collaboration driving resistance mechanisms. Our focus honed onto the msr(E)-mph(E) gene cluster, a potent duo orchestrating synchronized resistance to AZI. Within this genetic alliance, the mph(E) gene, a scion of the mph gene family, encodes a macrolide phosphotransferase akin to its predecessor, mph(A). Complementing this, the msr(E) gene, a member of the msr gene family within the ABC subfamily F (ABC-F) type efflux pump repertoire, adds another layer of complexity. Despite this, the intricate machinations underpinning their cooperative resistance mechanisms remain shrouded in mystery. In this study, we embark on a quest to unravel the elusive molecular mechanisms underpinning the msr(E)-mph(E) gene cluster's pivotal role in mediating AZI resistance. Our tripartite objectives delineate a roadmap to decode the enigma: unveiling the functions of the mph(E) and msr(E) genes through targeted gene cloning in Objective #1, dissecting the intricate dance of synergy between these genes in mediating AZI resistance in Objective #2, and delving into the origin and evolutionary trajectory of this gene cluster in Objective #3. The culmination of this endeavour promises a profound illumination of the molecular underpinnings driving bacterial resistance to AZI, offering a panoramic view of bacterial evolution strategies in circumventing antibiotic onslaughts. These insights are poised to revolutionize our approach to combatting the emergence and dissemination of AZI-resistant bacterial strains, propelling the development of novel antibacterial agents and fortifying our armoury in the ceaseless battle against antimicrobial resistance. 阿奇霉素（AZI）是一種廣泛使用的廣譜大環內酯抗生素藥物。它主要用於治療呼吸道感染、皮膚和軟組織感染、胃腸道感染、耳部感染以及性傳播感染。然而，臨床對AZI的抗藥性發生率持續上升，增加了治療的複雜性和成本，以及抗藥基因的傳播風險和感染控制挑戰。在以往的研究中，我們調查了臨床病原體中AZI抗藥性的幾種機制，並證明了Mph(A)酶和Mrx外排泵的功能傳遞。這一新機制促使我們發現其他類似的協同功能合作在介導抗微生物抗藥性方面的存在。我們發現mph(E)-msr(E)基因簇也介導對AZI的協同抗藥性。mph(E)基因屬於mph家族，編碼一種大環內酯磷轉移酶，與mph(A)相似。我們發現 mph(E)-msr(E) 基因簇也介導對 AZI 的增效抗性。 mph(E) 基因屬於 mph 家族，並編碼一種與 mph(A) 相似的巨環藥物磷酸轉移酶。 msr(E) 基因屬於 ABC F 亚家族 (ABC-F) 型外排泵。雖然其背後的機制尚不清楚。因此，我們旨在闡明該基因簇在介導 AZI 抗性中的分子機制。提出了三個目標來解決三個研究問題並檢驗假設。將通過第一目標中的相關基因克隆來發現 mph(E) 和 msr(E) 基因的功能。在確認 mph(E) 和 msr(E) 基因在介導 AZI 抗性中的作用後，將在第二目標中研究 mph(E) 和 msr(E) 基因增效作用的機制。最後，將在第三目標中調查 mph(E)-msr(E) 基因簇的起源和進化路徑。這個項目的完成應該能讓我們了解 mph(E)-msr(E) 基因簇的機制，以調節細菌對 AZI 的抗藥性以及細菌在逃避抗生素殺滅中的演變。這些結果將為預防和控制 AZI 抗藥性細菌株的出現和擴散，以及新抗菌藥物的開發提供新的見解。

15201125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201125.value: 3D digital maps are significant spatial infrastructure for constructing digital twins in the era of intelligent surveying. They provide high-precision and realistic city simulations, as well as support for 3D dynamic analysis. However, the production and application of 3D digital maps face several spatial data quality challenges, including data completeness, position accuracy, consistency, and temporal accuracy. These issues directly impact the usability and reliability of 3D digital maps. The primary data utilized in creating 3D digital maps, particularly photo-realistic 3D models, are typically derived from various sources such as aerial imagery, point clouds, and 360-degree panoramic images. Assessing the quality of 3D digital maps requires examining them against these reference data or data from a new period. However, comparing and inspecting 3D digital maps against diverse reference modalities presents a challenge known as multimodal change detection (CD). Within this research gap, two fundamental research issues warrant exploration: i) investigating the relationship between data quality issues and types of changes, and ii) developing AI models that support multimodal CD. The proposed project aims to enhance the data quality of 3D digital maps and streamline map revision by leveraging AI-driven multimodal CD approaches. This can identify inconsistencies between 3D digital maps and their reference data. The project will achieve its objectives through the development of three interconnected deliverables: i) a modality conversion method utilizing depth completion techniques to generate the initial dataset, forming the foundation for AI-based multimodal CD; ii) a CD method focused on spatial data quality of 3D digital maps, employing AI-based spatial registration and 2D/3D joint recognition techniques to identify inconsistencies; and iii) a software plugin for automatic quality inspection of 3D digital maps, integrating the AI-based CD method and providing a user-friendly interface for assessing quality issues. The effectiveness of the proposed approaches will be verified through case studies conducted in two selected regions: Kowloon in Hong Kong and Beijing in mainland China. These regions will serve as real-world testbeds to evaluate the performance and applicability of the developed techniques. The scientific contribution lies in the introduction of multimodal CD techniques for spatial data quality inspection. By incorporating multimodal CD, the research endeavors to significantly enhance the quality of 3D digital maps. As a result, it offers reliable data support for decision-making in areas such as urban planning in smart cities. N/A

15201225.value: 緩解延伸現實電子商務配置中的誘導式設計： 從實證研究邁向計算評估

15201225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201225.value: E-commerce is now a massive business, increasingly driven by rich multimedia experiences. Simultaneously, extended reality (XR) is largely seen as the next major breakthrough to transform multimedia engagement. In XR, dark patterns are a form of interactions that can deceive users into making undesired choices. Thus, they are particularly harmful in e-commerce. Existing research on dark patterns in XR settings is inadequate for multiple reasons: (1) The emerging types of dark patterns in XR e-commerce have not yet been investigated. (2) The effect and extent of unrecognized dark pattern types in XR e-commerce remain unexamined. (3) The lack of countermeasures and auditing tools hinders the widespread use of XR e-commerce applications. This project explores the current state-of-the-art manipulative techniques in XR applications in e-commerce scenarios, followed by the development of an assessment tool to mitigate the negative effects of dark patterns. Thus, the first step is to leverage a speculative design approach by recruiting experts from XR, e-commerce, and deceptive design areas. Second, based on the expert’s opinions, we validate the dark patterns in XR-enabled e-commerce scenarios through user studies. We focus on evaluating user interaction with manipulative design in XR experiences. This will involve a 500-participant empirical study, resulting in a 1500-hour video recording that serves as pioneering data for computationally analyzing dark patterns in e-commerce scenarios. Third, a toolkit leveraging the dataset for auditing dark patterns is proposed accordingly. The toolkit provides AI-assisted examination of potential risks from dark patterns and visualization tools that pinpoint the risks in 3D immersive spaces. Impact-wise, our findings will reinforce the research community’s understanding of design guidelines for XR e-commerce experiences and promote ethical XR applications. Also, education is a highly effective way to countermeasure dark patterns. The project initiative also presents opportunities to enhance user awareness of deceptive encounters by revealing newly detected dark patterns. Also, following open science practice, the toolkit will be released to the research community and practitioners in the industry through suitable open-source licenses, with the ambition of our tools becoming the standard evaluation metric for future research on dark patterns in XR e-commerce scenarios. 電子商務現在已經成為一項規模龐大的業務，並日益受到豐富多媒體體驗的驅動。 與此同時，延伸實境（XR）在很大程度上被視為改變多媒體互動的下一個重大突破。在XR中，誘導式設計是一種互動形式，可以欺騙使用者做出不想要的選擇。 因此，它們在電子商務中尤其有害。基於多種原因，現有關於XR 環境中誘導式設計的研究並不足夠：（1）XR 電子商務中新興的誘導式設計類型尚未被研究。（2）XR電子商務中未被認知的誘導式設計類型的影響和程度仍未被研究。（3）缺乏對策與稽核工具，妨礙了 XR電子商務應用程式的廣泛使用。 本專案探討目前最先進的XR應用在電子商務情境中的操控技術，接著開發評估工具以減緩誘導式設計的負面影響。因此，第一步是透過招募 XR、電子商務和欺騙性設計領域的專家，利用思辨設計方法。其次，基於專家的意見，我們透過使用者研究來驗證XR 啟用的電子商務情境中的誘導式設計。我們著重於評估使用者在XR 體驗中與操控性設計的互動。這將涉及500人參與的實證研究，產生1500小時的視訊記錄，作為電子商務場景中誘導式設計計算分析的開創性資料。第三，相應地提出了一個利用該資料集來審核黑暗模式的工具包。該工具包提供AI輔助檢查誘導式設計的潛在風險，以及在 3D身歷其境空間中指出風險的可視化工具。
