The developed model will adopt a novel functional form that admits zero probability, which is related to user preferences. User-specific choice sets will be accommodated by characterizing heterogeneous preferences with discrete/continuous probabilistic distributions. The choice model will be incorporated into network equilibrium analyses for transportation planning applications. The transformative aspect of the proposed project will lie in the development of (1) a novel discrete choice model that can realistically describe the choice behavior of travelers, (2) novel network equilibrium models to reproduce the aggregate behavioral pattern for transportation planning, and (3) efficient solution algorithms for the application of the developed network equilibrium models. This project will not only have a broad impact on transportation research but also offer new insights into developing effective solutions in other choice contexts. 交通網絡中出行選擇集異質性與內生性的行為交互建模研究 交通系統的智能規劃與運營，需要理解和預測出行選擇行為。這種行為反映了人們如何使用各種出行選項（例如路線）以及他們如何對新型出行服務做出反應。在交通網絡中，出行選擇行為呈現出獨特的特徵和挑戰。由於認知能力有限，用戶（即出行者）通常只考慮交通網絡所包含的大量可用選項中的一小部分。個人用戶實際考慮的選項集合（即「選擇集」）取決於其個人偏好，並且研究者無法直接觀察到。此外，在進行交通網絡層面的分析時，考慮不同人群偏好的多樣性至關重要。隨著新型出行服務和個性化出行指引的出現，這些特徵可能變得更加突出。 出行者的選擇行為主要通過微觀層面的離散選擇模型來描述，並整合到網絡均衡模型中，用於分析存在個體間交互的總量需求模式。然而，現有研究嚴重依賴任意的/啟發式規則來外在地確定選擇集，忽略了選擇集對用戶偏好的依賴性。這種獨立性假設阻礙了對由異質性偏好引起的、用戶特定選擇集的捕捉。由於離散選擇模型的估計和預測對選擇集相當敏感，傳統的建模方法可能導致系統性的出行需求分析偏差，並顯著降低規劃方案的質量。 本項目旨在解決上述挑戰，通過開發一種新的離散選擇模型，該模型能夠同時考慮選擇集的內生性（即選擇集依賴於偏好）和用戶異質性。開發的模型將採用一種新穎的函數形式，允許零概率（即某些選項完全不被考慮），這種零概率與用戶偏好相關。用戶特定的選擇集將通過離散/連續的概率分佈來描述異質性偏好來得以體現。該選擇模型將被整合到用於交通規劃應用的網絡均衡分析中。本項目的變革性在於將開發：(1) 一種能夠更真實描述出行者選擇行為的新型離散選擇模型；(2) 用於再現交通規劃所需總量行為模式的新型網絡均衡模型；(3) 應用所開發網絡均衡模型的高效求解算法。該項目不僅將對交通研究產生廣泛影響，也將為其他選擇情境下開發有效解決方案提供新的見解。

15218825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15218825.value: 带有终端约束的机制依赖的随机控制问题

15218825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218825.value: In this project, we will investigate a class of regime-dependent stochastic control problems with terminal state constraints, motivated by challenges in financial mathematics. While stochastic control problems with either regime switching or terminal state constraints have been extensively studied, the integration of both has received little attention due to the heightened mathematical complexity it introduces. However, this integration is essential for accurately capturing and understanding various financial phenomena. The core difficulty of this project stems from combining terminal state constraints with regime switching. Terminal state constraints result in singular terminal conditions for the backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) that govern the value function and optimal control. Meanwhile, regime switching increases the problem's dimensionality, transforming a one-dimensional BSDE into a system of coupled BSDEs with singular terminal values -- an area yet unexplored in existing literature. Addressing this challenge will require the development of new technical tools and methodologies. Our study will create a synergy between stochastic control problems, systems of BSDEs with singular terminal values, and their financial mathematics motivations. First, solving the coupled BSDEs allows us to verify the solutions to the stochastic control problems. Second, as we explore the well-posedness of these BSDE systems, we will draw upon financial mathematics to guide our intuition and provide critical insights. Finally, our investigation into stochastic control problems will illuminate underlying financial issues, enhancing our understanding of real-world financial dynamics. 在這個項目中，我們將研究具有終端狀態約束的機制依賴型隨機控制問題，這類問題很自然地出現在金融數學問題中。 一方面，帶有機制轉換的隨機控制問題導致耦合倒向隨機微分方程（BSDE）組。另一方面，具有終端狀態約束的隨機控制問題則導致BSDEs具有奇異的終端值。文獻中廣泛研究了具有機制轉換或終端狀態約束的隨機控制問題。然而，由於數學上的複雜性，幾乎沒有關於這兩者結合的研究，即對具有奇異終端值的耦合BSDE系統的研究。 在這個項目中，我們將研究三個由金融數學問題所產生的新型機制依賴隨機控制問題，這些問題都具有終端狀態約束。其難點在於具有奇異終端值的多維BSDEs，這是本項目的主要技術貢獻。本項目中的隨機控制問題、具有奇異終端值的BSDE系統以及金融數學動機彼此相輔相成。首先，通過研究BSDE系統，我們完成了隨機控制問題的驗證。其次，當我們研究BSDE系統的適定性時，我們重新審視金融數學背景以獲得必要的直覺和見解。第三，隨機控制問題的研究為潛在的金融數學問題提供了啟發。

15219125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15219125.value: 用於無監督3D場景分割與生成的多模態物件為中心學習方法

15219125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219125.value: Humans can effortlessly learn mental representations of 3D objects through multiple sensory modalities, such as visual inputs and language descriptions. By leveraging learned object-centric priors, we can recognize similar objects in unseen 3D scenes without additional knowledge and recombine these priors to create new 3D scenes. Endowing machines with such capabilities—3D object-centric learning, scene segmentation, and scene generation—is critical for applications in robotics, embodied AI, and mixed reality. However, current methods often treat these tasks separately, relying heavily on dense human annotations to train independent networks, which is resource-intensive and unappealing for real-world applications. This project seeks to introduce a unified framework of algorithms that can model 3D objects and scenes without needing human annotations of 3D scenes. It will focus on three core objectives: 1) multimodal object-centric prior learning, 2) unsupervised 3D scene segmentation, and 3) 3D scene generation without 3D supervision. Despite the advances made by fully-supervised methods, this project faces significant challenges, particularly in establishing effective object-centric prior learning and addressing the lack of explicit supervision signals. To address these challenges, we propose several key innovations. First, we will learn a novel multimodal 3D object-centric model that integrates both discriminative and generative capabilities. By leveraging pretraining techniques, we aim to learn a view-equivariant diffusion model from large-scale multimodal datasets, enabling the object-centric priors to be both discriminative and generative and therefore performing effectively in downstream tasks. Second, we will introduce an innovative unsupervised 3D scene segmentation technique. Rather than relying on costly human annotations, our method will utilize only pretrained object-centric priors to accurately segment 3D scenes into individual objects. Third, we will pioneer a 3D scene generation approach that, instead of depending on annotated 3D scene datasets, harnesses our pretrained object-centric priors and sparsely annotated 2D images. Overall, this project aims to advance 3D scene modeling by offering a more efficient, unsupervised solution. Preliminary results are very promising, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. Crucially, the multimodal object-centric priors will serve as a foundation for various downstream tasks. This work has the potential to significantly impact emerging fields, including robotics, game design, and training data generation for embodied AI. 人類能夠輕鬆透過多種感官模態（如視覺輸入和語言描述）學習三維物體的表徵。運用已學得的以物體為中心的先驗知識，我們可以在未見過的三維場景中辨識出相似的物體，並重新組合這些先驗知識以創造新的三維場景。賦予機器這種能力——即三維物體導向學習、場景分割與場景生成——對於機器人、具身人工智慧以及混合實境等應用至關重要。然而，現有方法往往將這些任務分開處理，並嚴重依賴大量人工標註來訓練獨立的網路，這不僅資源消耗龐大，也不利於實際應用。 本計畫旨在提出一套統一的算法框架，能夠在無需三維場景人工標註的情況下建模三維物體與場景。研究將聚焦於三個核心目標：1) 多模態物體導向先驗學習，2) 無監督三維場景分割，以及 3) 無三維監督的三維場景生成。儘管全監督方法已取得顯著進展，本計畫仍面臨重大挑戰，特別是在建立有效的物體導向先驗學習及克服缺乏明確監督訊號方面。 為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出了幾項關鍵創新。首先，我們將學習一種新穎的多模態三維物體導向模型，結合判別式與生成式能力。透過預訓練技術，我們目標從大規模多模態資料集中學習一個視角等變的擴散模型，使物體導向先驗同時具備判別與生成能力，並能有效應用於下游任務。其次，我們將提出一種創新的無監督三維場景分割技術。我們的方法不依賴昂貴的人工標註，而是僅利用預訓練的物體導向先驗，準確地將三維場景分割為個別物體。第三，我們將開創一種三維場景生成方法，不再依賴標註過的三維場景資料集，而是利用我們預訓練的物體導向先驗與稀疏標註的二維影像。 總體而言，本計畫旨在推進三維場景建模，提供一種更高效、無監督的解決方案。初步結果顯示此方法具備可行性，且多模態物體導向先驗將成為各種下游任務的基礎。這項工作有望對機器人、遊戲設計以及具身人工智慧訓練資料生成等新興領域產生重大影響。

15219525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15219525.value: 發展一個自動化基準模型以評估大型項目的成功與表現

15219525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15219525.value: Dr Chan, Man Wai Dr Debrah, Caleb Prof SING, Chun-pong

15219525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219525.value: Megaprojects are large-scale, complex undertakings that generally require an investment of US$1 billion or more, take several years to develop and build, involve numerous public and private stakeholders, and are transformative, affecting millions of people. Globally, megaprojects face a pressing performance paradox: they often exceed budget and time constraints while under-delivering promised benefits. Studies reveal that 90% of megaprojects are over budget, with overruns above 50% frequently observed, and Hong Kong (HK) is no exception. Despite these challenges, the HK Government has proposed over HK$376 billion worth of megaprojects in the past three years. Consequently, the need for a more effective assessment of their success and performance is both important and urgent. Megaprojects are a completely different breed of projects in terms of their magnified and unique characteristics, such as their huge size, high degree of complexity, large-scale investment, major risks undertaken, multiple stakeholder involvement, and societal impact, leading to several implementation challenges. The unique nature and characteristics of megaprojects necessitate the development of specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Those used for the more normal projects are not adequate. Traditional approaches to normal-sized projects rely heavily on manual data collection and documentation procedures, which can be both time-consuming and inaccurate. This highlights the practical need for comprehensive database assembly and an automated benchmarking model, making use of the data to assess the performance of megaprojects and improve success rates meaningfully. This project aims to develop an automated composite project success index enabling management to better enhance the performance of megaprojects. The objectives are to: (a) identify the most appropriate megaproject KPIs; (b) develop a composite megaproject success index; (c) automate the benchmarking process; and (d) validate the system developed. To identify necessary KPIs, an extensive literature review, content analysis, the fuzzy Delphi method, face-to-face interviews, and questionnaire surveys will be employed. The core objective of the project is to develop a web-based computer-based software platform that will be used to store, analyse, monitor, and control the megaproject database. Theoretically, this study will advance knowledge of those KPIs that are uniquely applicable to megaproject success. In practice, the system will assist decision-makers in improving megaproject success factors more reliably and enable timely remedial actions. Of additional great potential importance is the fact that the system’s database will offer empirical evidence, enabling decision- and policy-makers to implement legislation that will itself serve to drive megaproject performance improvements.

15221425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15221425.value: 基於相變材料集成冷量分配系統的建築能源柔性提升和優化，實現高效電網互動

15221425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221425.value: Engaging building energy flexibility is recognized as a cost-effective solution to address the growing stress on power balance of power systems due to increasing renewable penetration. By altering their power use patterns, buildings can meet various grid balancing needs while also gaining economic benefits. Enhancing building energy flexibility is therefore essential to maximize benefits for both buildings and power grids. Integrating Phase Change Materials (PCMs) into cooling distribution systems and building structures has demonstrated to be effective for enhancing the energy flexibility of buildings. However, most existing studies have focused on integrating PCMs for load shifting, which typically requires high storage capacity and substantial space for PCM installation. Such applications are impractical for most high-rise buildings in subtropical high-density cities, particularly when retrofitting existing buildings, which are lightweight and have low thermal inertia and significant space constraints. Short-term grid interactions, such as load shedding and urgent load reduction, are increasingly needed for power grids with rising renewable penetration. Adopting PCMs for short-term grid interactions is relatively more practical in lightweight high-rise buildings, as less storage capacity is required. An effective approach is to integrate PCMs with the cooling distribution systems, which allows for higher controllability in applications. But what are the appropriate PCM thermal properties and integration configurations for such applications and how to effectively design and control the PCM-integrated cooling distribution systems remains open questions. This project, therefore, aims to develop PCM-integrated cooling distribution systems for enhancing the energy flexibility of cooling-dominated high-rise buildings, including existing buildings, to enable effective short-term grid-interactions without major modifications to conventional construction, control and energy efficiency. The impacts of PCM integration on the overall effective energy flexibility of buildings adopting PCM-integrated cooling distribution systems will be investigated analytically and experimentally, as well as the preferable PCM properties and integration configurations for typical flexibility services involving short-term grid interactions. A robust control strategy will be developed for the effective charging and discharging of PCM-integrated cooling distribution systems without negative impact on energy efficiency and major modification to regular system operation/control. An effective life-cycle optimization method will be developed to optimize the integration of PCMs with cooling distribution systems, achieving maximum benefits by considering flexibility services provision and energy use across different seasons. The project outcomes will facilitate the energy flexibility enhancement of cooling-dominated high-rise buildings and therefore support high renewable penetration in power systems for achieving carbon neutrality. 建築能源柔性被認為是一種極具成本效益的解決方案，以應對由於可再生能源滲透率不斷提高而導致的電力系統平衡壓力日益加劇的問題。建築通過調整用能模式不僅能夠滿足電網不同平衡需求，還能獲得經濟收益。因此，提升建築能源柔性對於實現建築和電網的利益最大化至關重要。將相變材料集成到冷量分配系統和建築結構中，已被證明能夠有效提升建築能源柔性。然而，現有的大多數研究主要聚焦通過集成相變材料實現負荷轉移，這通常需要較高的儲能容量和大量的相變材料安裝空間。對於亞熱帶高密度城市中的大多數高層建築，尤其是在對現有建築進行改造時，這類應用並不現實，因為這些建築結構較輕、熱慣性低且空間有限。 隨著可再生能源滲透率的不斷提高，電網對短時互動（如削峰和緊急負荷削減）的需求日益增加。在輕型高層建築中，採用相變材料進行短時電網互動相對更為可行，因為所需的儲能容量較小。一種有效的方法是將相變材料與冷量分配系統集成，這能夠在實際應用中實現更高的可控性。然而，對於此類應用，合適的相變材料熱性能參數和集成配置應如何選擇，以及如何有效設計和控制相變材料集成冷量分配系統，仍然是有待解決的問題。 因此，本項目旨在開發相變材料集成冷量分配系統，以提升製冷主導的高層建築（包括既有建築）的能源柔性，在無需對現有建築結構、控制方式和能效進行大量改動的前提下實現高效短時電網互動。項目將通過理論分析和實驗研究，探討相變材料集成對採用相變材料集成冷量分配系統建築整體有效能源柔性的影響，並研究適用于典型短時電網互動柔性服務的最佳相變材料性能參數和集成配置。項目還將開發一種穩健的控制策略，實現相變材料集成冷量分配系統的高效充放能，同時不影響能效，也無需對常規系統運行和控制進行大量改動。此外，項目將提出一種有效的全生命週期優化方法，優化相變材料與冷量分配系統的集成，在考慮不同季節能耗和柔性服務的基礎上，實現最大化效益。項目成果將有助於提升製冷主導的高層建築的能源柔性，從而支持電力系統高比例可再生能源滲透，助力實現碳中和目標。

15221625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15221625.value: 基于视觉感知启发和第一性原理的人工智能生成内容视觉质量评估

15221625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221625.value: Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has seen remarkable advancements in recent years, particularly in image and video generation domains. One important application of AIGC is in the content creation industries, including entertainment, advertising, and design, in which human visual perception is considered the ultimate golden standard. Therefore, AIGC for content creation industries must be accurate, adhere to the intended usage, and maintain high visual quality to achieve the best possible end user’s quality of experience (QoE). Existing image and video quality assessment (IQA/VQA) models focus on fidelity in terms of reconstruction quality against the original visual data. These cannot be applied to the assessment of the quality of generative artifacts, Although the most reliable way to assess the generative artifacts is by conducting true subjective testing through collecting personal opinions, it is laborious and challenging to apply on a large scale in practice. Therefore, we aim to design an objective metric that accommodates generative artifacts highly correlated with subjective QoE. In this project, we focus on developing quality assessment methods for AIGI/AIGV governed and inspired by both the first principle and human visual perception. Specifically, the unique challenges in AIGI/AIGV quality assessment involve two issues: measuring the generative artifacts and integrating human visual perception characteristics. We identify the following objectives for the proposed research: (1) Designing the structural integrity detector to identify object-centric deformation artifacts; (2) Developing a relational integrity detector by constructing a relational graph to identify relation deformation artifacts; (3) Developing a task-driven attention modulator with textual guidance and visual saliency prior; (4) Building a transformer-based quality assessment system equipped with visual foundation model for quality prediction. The proposed research includes both theoretical analysis and experimental verifications. In theoretical analysis, we shall focus on the structural and relational integrity representation to extract the unique generative artifacts and integrate physical law into evaluation. We shall also explore task-driven attention allocation and integrate it to simulate the visual perception. In experimental verifications, we will conduct comprehensive experiments on advanced video generators to verify the theoretical analysis and model effectiveness. The outcome of the proposed research will be disseminated via both publications and patents. Source codes of the algorithms developed in this project will be uploaded to an open-source platform for sharing with the research community. We expect that the impact of this research will reach beyond academia to benefit the deployment of AIGC products

15222025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222025.value: 基於傳感數據和火災圖像智慧預測回燃風險與爆炸災害

15222025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222025.value: The fast urbanization in Asia continues to increase the building and population densities in large cities, causing massive fire risks and challenges in firefighting. Backdraft is the abrupt burning of overheated gasses in a fire. In case of a backdraft, an explosion may happen after firefighters open a door or a window during the firefighting operation. The backdraft often occurs without a clear warning and is one of the most dangerous threats to firefighters’ life. Therefore, it is urgent to understand the causes and dynamics of backdraft deeply and then further forecast its occurrence with high accuracy and efficiency. The backdraft fire phenomena are controlled by many factors, including the oxygen-limited enclosure time, smoke gas composition, fuel distribution, and ventilation conditions like a random window breakage or a door opening; thus, predicting the backdraft onset has been a grand challenge for fire researchers and firefighters. Past studies in well-controlled laboratories have only addressed relatively simple backdraft fire scenarios while rarely looking into the forecast of its occurrence. To date, it is still almost impossible to give an early warning of backdraft in a complex building fire scene. This research aims to investigate the critical fire and building parameters for inducing a backdraft explosion and develop a smart backdraft forecast engine driven by deep-leaning methods. Reduced-scale experiments will be first conducted to investigate the critical fire, ventilation and environmental parameters that trigger a backdraft explosion. Then, we will perform large-scale room fire tests and numerical simulations to reveal the scale effect of backdraft. The obtained backdraft database of sensor data and fire smoke images in multi-scale experiments will be used to train the Fusion-transformer network constrained by physical rules and develop a backdraft forecast system. The proposed backdraft forecast will be verified and optimized by experiments at a multi-story fire test facility. Eventually, a scientific training program will be developed for firefighters to apply the backdraft forecast system and potentially mitigate backdraft hazards and casualties in future firefighting operations. This research will benefit the scientific community and society in the following respects: (1) Advancing scientific understanding of underlying dynamics and critical parameters of the complex backdraft fire phenomena. (2) Pioneering the use of state-of-the-art computer vision and deep learning methods in forecasting backdraft explosion and reducing its occurrence. (3) Providing scientific guidelines for firefighters to use the intelligent model, providing an early warning of backdraft, and achieving safer firefighting operations. 亞洲快速的城市化進程持續增加大城市的建築和人口密度，帶來了巨大的火災風險和消防挑戰。回燃是指火災中過熱氣體的突發快速燃燒。如果發生回燃，消防員在消防救援過程中打開門窗後可能會發生爆炸。回燃通常發生時沒有明顯的預警，是威脅消防員生命的最危險因素之一。因此，深入了解回燃的成因和動態，並進一步準確高效地預測其發生至關重要。回燃火災現象受多種因素控制，包括氧氣封閉時間、煙氣成分、燃料分布以及通風條件（例如窗戶的隨機破損或門的打開）；因此，預測回燃的發生一直是火災研究人員和消防員面臨的巨大挑戰。過去在嚴格控制的實驗室中進行的研究僅涉及相對簡單的回燃場景，而很少對其發生進行預測。迄今為止，在覆雜的建築火災場景中，幾乎不可能對回燃進行早期預警。 本研究旨在探究引發回燃爆炸的關鍵火災和建築參數，並開發一個由深度學習方法驅動的智能回燃預測引擎。我們將首先進行小尺度實驗，以探究引發回燃爆炸的關鍵火災、通風和環境參數。 然後，我們將進行大規模室內火災試驗和數值模擬，以揭示回燃的尺度效應。在多尺度實驗中獲得的傳感器數據和火災煙霧圖像回燃數據庫將用於訓練受物理規則約束的融合擴散網絡，並開發回燃預測系統。提出的回燃預測方法將在多層火災測試設施上通過實驗進行驗證和優化。最終，我們將制定一套科學的培訓方案，幫助消防員應用回燃預測系統，並在未來消防作業中盡可能地減少回燃危害和人員傷亡。 本研究將在以下幾個方面造福科學界和社會： (1) 加深對覆雜回燃火災現象的潛在動力學和關鍵參數的科學理解。 (2) 率先使用最先進的計算機視覺和深度學習方法預測回燃爆炸並減少其發生。 (3) 為消防員使用智能模型提供科學指導，提供火災回燃預警，實現更安全的消防作業。

15222725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222725.value: 基於物理一致性圖神經網絡的高層建築分層熱動態建模方法研究

15222725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222725.value: Large buildings are major electricity consumers, significantly impacting the supply-demand balance and the reliability of power grids. Effective building energy management is crucial for energy conservation, emission reduction, demand response (DR), and improving occupant comfort. A comprehensive understanding and characterizing of building thermal dynamics is fundamental to achieving these goals. Building thermal behaviors vary across spatial and temporal dimensions due to differences in thermal mass at the zone, floor, and building levels. Most existing thermal dynamic models for large buildings treat the entire building as a single, lumped entity, limiting the ability to model thermal dynamics with high spatial granularity. Additionally, the thermal inertial of chilled water is often neglected. Consequently, the optimal control and DR strategies developed using these models are inadequate for floor-level optimization and hardly account for variations in occupancy and equipment use across different floors and the thermal inertial of chilled water in the building’s overall DR potential. This underscores a pressing need for more granular and computationally efficient modeling methods that accurately capture the thermal behaviors of high-rise buildings at both the floor and building levels. This project aims to develop a hierarchical bottom-up thermal dynamic modeling method using a Physically Consistent Graph Neural Network (PCGNN) for high-rise buildings. The complex modeling task is divided into two interrelated sub-tasks: a PCGNN-based method for floor-level thermal dynamic modeling and a model aggregation method for building-level modeling. The graph design is informed by physical knowledge, including building physics and AC system topology, while the neural architecture of the PCGNN is guided by building physics. The thermal inertia of chilled water is captured by adding a global node in the aggregated model. A constrained fine-tuning scheme is developed for parameter identification in model aggregation. Using the developed models, Model Predictive Control (MPC)-based DR strategies for both floor-level and building-level will be developed and tested on a TRNSYS-Python simulation platform and two high-rise commercial buildings, and compared with DR strategies using RC models. The physical knowledge-assisted data-driven modeling method developed will advance existing building thermal modeling techniques. This project will provide new insights into realistic DR in high-rise buildings, by accounting for differences across floors and all passive thermal storage, including the building envelope, internal thermal mass, and chilled water system. The outcomes will support the development of advanced control optimization and DR strategies for high-rise buildings, targeting energy savings, carbon emission reduction, and enhanced demand response. 大型建築是主要的用電大戶，對電力系統的供需平衡及電網的可靠性產生重大影響。有效的建築能源管理對於節能減排、需求響應以及提升居住者舒適度非常重要。全面理解和表徵建築熱動態特性是實現上述目標的基礎。 由於區域、樓層及建築整體的熱容的差異，建築的熱動態特性在空間和時間維度上有顯著不同。目前，大多數針對大型建築的熱動態模擬是將整個建築視為單一的整體，這種方法限制了對熱動態特性進行高空間解析度建模的能力。此外，冷凍水的熱慣性在現有模擬中常被忽略。因此，基於這些模型開發的最優控制和需求響應策略難以實現樓層級別的優化，也難以充分考慮不同樓層的人員活動和設備使用差異，以及冷凍水熱慣性對建築整體需求響應的影響。這凸顯了亟需更具空間細微性且計算高效的建模方法，以準確表徵高層建築在樓層及整體層面的熱動態特性。 本項目旨在針對高層建築，開發一種基於物理一致性圖神經網絡（PCGNN）、自下而上的分層熱動態建模方法。建模任務被分解為兩個相互關聯的子任務：基於PCGNN的樓層級熱動態建模方法，以及用於建築整體熱動態模擬的聚合方法。圖結構的設計融合了建築物理知識和空調系統拓撲結構信息，PCGNN的神經網絡結構亦以建築物理知識為指導。通過在聚合模型中引入全局節點，有效捕捉冷凍水的熱慣性。針對模型聚合中的參數辨識，提出了一種新的帶約束的微調方案。基於所開發的模型，本項目將設計並測試基於模型預測控制（MPC）的樓層級和建築整體需求響應策略，並在TRNSYS-Python模擬平台及一座高層商業建築上進行對比實驗，評估其與傳統RC模型需求響應策略的性能差異。 本項目所提出的物理知識輔助的數據驅動建模方法將促進現有建築熱動態建模技術的發展。通過全面考慮樓層間的差異，及包括建築圍護結構、建築內部和冷凍水系統在內的所有被動熱儲能，本項目將為高層建築的實際需求響應提供新的思路。研究成果將有助於針對高層建築研發先進的控制優化與需求響應策略，助力實現節能降碳和需求響應能力提升的目標。

15222825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222825.value: 基於非均勻變形誘導效應的可自訂梯度成分增材製造高性能功能梯度材料的開發

15222825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222825.value: Metallic gradient materials are composed of different metallic phases or components with gradually continuous variation over the materials’ volume for superior functional and mechanical properties, showing great promise for applications in critical scenarios (biomedicine, aerospace, ballistic engineering, nuclear industry, etc.). In addition to the natural physical and chemical properties of the components, this heterogeneity results in unique and enhanced mechanical properties compared to homogeneous metals, which have uniform composition and structure. This phenomenon is named the heterogeneous deformation-induced (HDI) effect, which is a crucial mechanism for mechanical enhancement in non-homogeneous materials. Additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, such as laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), have been rapidly developed and widely used to fabricate compositional gradient parts and structures. Leveraging AM technologies to produce high-performance functionally gradient materials (FGMs) is expected to be promising in the innovative development of engineering materials. Existing research on non-homogeneous metallic materials is mainly focused on the HDI effect of inhomogeneous grain structures under the same composition, lacking systematic research and theory to support the design and development of compositional gradient materials. The current practice only adjusts grain size or microstructure, which is usually unable to produce high-performance materials used in extreme engineering conditions. On the other hand, compositional gradient materials usually show more robust comprehensive performance than the individual components through the combination of materials with different naturally outstanding physical and chemical properties and deliver promising potential to obtain the needed surface functional properties and overall mechanical properties for extreme condition applications. Even though prior arts have verified the advantages of this effect, there is a lack of systematic research and theoretical knowledge to support the development of metal-based compositional gradient materials. The research on this topic is urgently needed. In tandem with this, this research aims to investigate the mechanisms of performance enhancement in various types of metal-based compositional gradient FGMs through the design and optimization of compositional gradients in different metal-based material systems (BCC, FCC, HCP, and medium/high-entropy systems) prepared by LPBF technology. The project will focus on the following tasks: (1) Development of optimal process parameters for specific single components using LPBF technology; (2) Development of high-performance FGMs through customizing the gradient combinations of single components; (3) Investigation of heterogeneous deformation-induced effects and gradient design guidelines based on the identified deformation mechanisms with strong applicability; (4) Development of high-performance compositional and structural dual-gradient lattice components based on the developed compositional gradient design guidelines. 金屬梯度材料由不同的金屬相或組成，其成分隨材料體積逐漸連續變化，具有優異的功能和機械性能，在生物醫學、航空航天、彈道工程、核工業等關鍵應用領域顯示出巨大的應用前景。除了組成本身的物理和化學性質外，與成分和結構均勻的均質金屬相比，這種異質性也使其具有獨特且增強的機械性能。這種現象稱為異質變形誘導 (HDI) 效應，是非均質材料機械性質增強的關鍵機制。積層製造 (AM) 技術，例如雷射粉末床熔合 (LPBF)，已迅速發展並廣泛用於製造成分梯度零件和結構。利用 AM 技術生產高性能功能梯度材料 (FGM) 有望在工程材料的創新發展中大有可為。現有非均質金屬材料研究主要集中於相同成分下非均質晶粒結構的HDI效應，缺乏系統性的研究和理論支撐成分梯度材料的設計和開發。目前的做法只是調整晶粒尺寸或微觀結構，通常無法製備出用於極端工程條件的高性能材料。另一方面，成分梯度材料通常透過組合具有不同天然優異物理化學性能的材料，表現出比單一組分數更優異的綜合性能，有望獲得極端條件應用所需的表面功能性能和整體力學性能。儘管現有技術已經證實了該效應的優勢，但目前仍缺乏系統性的研究和理論知識來支撐金屬基成分梯度材料的開發，亟需進行這方面的研究。 同時，本研究旨在透過設計和優化採用LPBF技術製備的不同金屬基材料系統（BCC、FCC、HCP和中/高熵系統）的成分梯度，研究各種類型金屬基成分梯度功能梯度材料性能提升的機制。本計畫將重點介紹以下工作：（1）利用LPBF技術開發特定單一組分的最佳製程參數；（2）透過客製化單一組分的梯度組合開發高性能功能梯度材料；（3）研究非均勻變形引起的效應，並基於已確定的適用性強的變形機制制定梯度設計指南；（4）基於已開發的成分梯度設計指南，開發高性能成分和結構雙梯度組分。

15223025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223025.value: 統一多元機載光達平台配置的真實三維森林重建算法：深入探究2010至2020年間香港森林的變化

15223025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223025.value: Detailing 3D forest structures is critical for managing biodiversity, habitats, and forest resources. Also, serving as an essential input of 3D radiative transfer models (RTM), realistic 3D digital representations (scenes) of forests play an important role in data interpretation and accurate information retrieval from Earth Observation Satellites (EOS). The proposed proposal outlines a comprehensive approach for 3D forest reconstruction from airborne laser scanning (ALS) data, aiming to resolve the inconsistencies of derived plant area density (PAD) distribution generated from various sensor platform configurations adapted by open-access data from various ALS campaigns. The developed unified algorithm will enhance the existing 3D reconstruction models from past research led by the PI (the PVlad model) and co-I (the AMAPVox model). Firstly, we will select a forested test site (Smithsonian Environmental Research Center, SERC) with extensive existing field measurements and two separate ALS campaigns (G-LiHT and NEON) with different sensor platform configurations. Subsequently, we will develop a unified approach so that more consistent 3D reconstruction can be achieved. Furthermore, we will conduct a comprehensive sensitivity analysis using the lidar module of the discrete anisotropic radiative transfer model (DART-lidar, led by the PI) to further enhance the algorithm so that it can be applied to a broad range of ALS sensor platform configurations. Supported by HK CEDD (letter enclosed), the ultimate goal of the proposed project is to provide detailed 3D reconstructions of forest ecosystems in Hong Kong, spanning from 2010 to 2020, using the CEDD's ALS data with different sensor platform configurations. These 3D models will enable the examination of decadal shifts in forest structure, enhancing our understanding of how forests evolve under the influence of both natural events and human activities. The use of high-resolution PAI images will help identify areas of notable forest (including mangrove) expansion and specific areas severely impacted by typhoons and landslides. Additionally, examining the vertical PAD distribution will yield deeper insights into forest growth patterns, ecological roles, and recovery trajectories following such events. The outcomes of this project will deliver essential data that can be utilized in formulating conservation strategies and boosting ecological resilience by providing detailed insights into the temporal and spatial dynamics of Hong Kong’s forest ecosystems. This proposal aims not only to advance the technical use of ALS data in forest analysis but also to contribute to more comprehensive environmental management and planning efforts by offering actionable insights for forest conservation and sustainability. 詳細描繪森林的三維結構，對於生物多樣性、棲地與森林資源的管理至關重要。同時，作為三維輻射傳輸模型（3D-RTM）的關鍵輸入，精準的森林三維數位表徵（場景）在自地球觀測衛星（EOS）進行精準資訊擷取方面亦扮演重要角色。 本提案提出一套以機載雷射掃描（ALS）資料進行森林三維重建的完整方法，旨在解決由不同感測器平台配置（以各類ALS感測器平台之開放資料為基礎）所推導之植被面積密度（PAD）分布不一致的問題。所開發的統一演算法將在既有三維重建模型之上進行強化，包括PI先前開發的PVlad模型與co-I開發的AMAPVox模型。為達成此目標，我們將選定一處具有豐富地面量測資料的森林測試場域（史密森尼環境研究中心，SERC），並採用兩個具不同感測器平台配置的獨立ALS感測器平台（G-LiHT與NEON）。我們將發展一套統一的方法，以獲得更一致的三維重建成果。此外，我們將使用DART輻射傳輸模型的LiDAR模組（DART-lidar，由主持人領導）進行全面的敏感度分析，以進一步優化演算法，使其可適用於更廣泛的ALS感測器平台配置。 本計畫的最終目標，是利用具不同感測器平台配置的香港CEDD資料，為香港在2010年至2020年間的森林生態系提供高精細的三維重建。此類成果可用於分析森林結構在三維空間中的十年期變化，促進對森林在自然與人為影響下動態的更深入理解。運用高解析度的PAI影像，本計畫將評估森林顯著生長的區域，特別是沿海紅樹林，以及受颱風與山體滑坡不利影響之區域。此外，垂直結構的分布可為目標區域的生長、生態功能與事件後的復原型態提供更細緻的評估洞見。 本計畫的成果將為保育策略與生態韌性提升提供關鍵資料，並就香港森林生態系的時空動態提出詳盡的洞察。此提案不僅旨在推進ALS資料於森林分析中的技術應用，也期望透過提供可行的洞見以促進森林保育，進而助益更廣泛的環境管理與規劃工作。

15223425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223425.value: 以提升跑道起降安全及容量之背景風與航空氣象影響下的動態尾流衰減預測方案

15223425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15223425.value: Dr Chan, Pai-Wai Prof Delehaye, Daniel

15223425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223425.value: The statistics from the International Air Transport Association shows that the air traffic demand surged by 70% since 2004. The total number of passengers in 2024 is projected to exceed that of 2019, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. As a result, optimising runway capacity has become a critical focus to increase aircraft traffic movement and improve runway efficiency. Currently, the National Airspace System (NAS) predominantly employs miles-in-trail (MIT) procedures to enforce a minimum distance in miles for aircraft sequencing during the en-route phase. This static separation method, however, operates under the assumption of worst-case wake turbulence scenarios, potentially limiting aircraft movements within a given time frame and causing delays, which can be exacerbated under adverse weather conditions or other uncertainties. These methods include the aircraft recategorisation (RECAT) proposed by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) but remain static separation minima. Dynamic and safety-oriented wake separation strategies, which adapt to varying weather and traffic conditions, have become major research focus globally. To address these issues, we attempt to design and develop time-based dynamic pairwise wake separation considering wind and other meteorological factors. With the accumulation of LiDAR wake data captured from historical actual landing flights, data-driven methods have proven advantageous in analysing wake behaviour and optimising separation to enhance runway efficiency. Therefore, this research proposes an intelligent dynamic wake separation prediction framework utilising LiDAR wake data and ADS-B data at the Hong Kong International Airport. First, we develop a two-step wake vortex region detection and strength estimation model via object detection algorithms based on LiDAR-scanned wake images. Physics-informed techniques are developed to improve prediction reliability in this safety-oriented runway operation problem. The results of wake region detection are used to support the second-stage research of long-term spatiotemporal decay and movement prediction of wake pairs in short scan range, combining the runway entry prediction. Further, another LiDAR in horizontal scan mode facilitates capturing precise 3D wake evolution, with complex wind conditions including headwind and tailwind. Uncertainty modelling are implemented to improve the trustworthiness of the deep learning models. Finally, the dynamic wake separation for pairwise arrival under varying meteorological conditions is determined by analysing wake encounter risk and wake presence in the standard flight approach path. By comparing the dynamic wake separation and traditional separation standards, this research expects to achieve near-time improvement of runway operational capacity and throughput without compromising flight safety. 15223925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223925.value: 用於鋼結構梁-柱連接的鎳鈦形狀記憶合金螺栓在剪切與複合荷載作用下的滯回行為研究

15223925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223925.value: The conventional seismic design methodology for steel structures requires plastic deformations of structural elements to achieve the desired seismic performance. However, it has been perceived that excessive post-earthquake plastic (permanent) deformations can lead to long-term suspensions of structural functionality, and even demolitions of extensively deformed structures. To prevent these consequences, the concept of seismic resilience has been increasingly emphasised in the design of steel structures. Seismic resilient steel structures can recover earthquake-induced structural deformations, thereby enabling rapid restoration of structural functionality following a major earthquake. A promising way of achieving seismic resilience is to use shape memory alloys (SMAs) for critical components in structural connections. The superelasticity of SMA can enable spontaneously recovery of inelastic deformations upon the removal of external loading. Among different types of SMA components, SMA bars are particularly suitable for structural applications considering the balance of availability, cost and performance. However, SMA bars in existing applications are usually designed to carry only tensile loads, and threaded at both ends (forming SMA bolts) to guarantee reliable fixing. Such end threading requires further weakening of the working section to avoid premature thread fracture, hence resulting in a low material utilisation cost-efficiency. To address this issue, a promising strategy is to use SMA bolts in bearing type bolted connections, where the bolts are predominantly subjected to shear, and possibly combined with tension and bending actions. In such conditions, the stresses are mostly concentrated at the shear planes in the working section, with a relatively low risk of thread fracture. Therefore, the weakening of the working section is not required, and the cost-efficiency of utilising SMA can be remarkably enhanced. However, it should be noted that current research and understanding of the behaviour of SMA bolts subject to combined loading is scant. The proposed research, therefore, will investigate the behaviour, design and application of SMA bolts subject to combined shear, tension and bending. The main research objectives include: (1) to experimentally examine the behaviour of SMA bolts under combined loadings; (2) to develop a constitutive model to simulate the cyclic behaviour of SMA in complex stress states; (3) to experimentally and numerically investigate the application of SMA bolts under combined loadings in bolted beam-to-column connections; and (4) develop design recommendations for SMA bolts and connections considering combined loadings of bolts. The research outcomes will underpin viable solutions supporting development of the structural resilience of steel structures subject to seismic events. 傳統鋼結構抗震設計方法要求結構構件透過塑性變形實現預期抗震性能。然而，過大的震後塑性（永久）變形將導致建築功能長期停擺，對於嚴重變形的結構甚至需要拆除。為避免此類後果，抗震韌性設計理念在鋼結構設計中日益受到重視。具備抗震韌性的鋼結構可自發性恢復地震造成的結構變形，進而在強震後快速恢復使用功能。實現結構抗震韌性的有效途徑之一是在關鍵連接部位採用形狀記憶合金（SMA）構件。 SMA的超彈性特性使其能在卸載後自發性恢復非彈性變形。在各類SMA構件中，SMA棒材因兼具易得性、成本與性能優勢，特別適合工程應用。但現有SMA棒材通常僅設計承受拉力，且需兩端車削螺紋（形成SMA螺栓）以確保可靠錨定。此類端部螺紋加工要求削弱工作段截面以避免螺紋過早斷裂，導致材料利用率和成本效益低。針對此問題，可行策略是將SMA螺栓用於承壓型螺栓連接節點。此類連接中螺栓主要承受剪力，並可能同時承受拉彎複合作用。此時，螺栓中的應力集中於工作段的剪切面，而螺紋的斷裂風險顯著降低，故無需削弱工作段截面，從而可以大幅提升SMA的成本效益。但需要指出的是，目前對SMA螺栓在複合荷載作用下的受力行為研究仍相對不足。因此，本研究將系統探究SMA螺栓在剪-拉-彎複合荷載作用下的性能、設計及應用，主要目標包括：(1) 透過試驗研究複合荷載作用下SMA螺栓的力學行為；(2) 建立複雜應力狀態下SMA的循環本構模型；(3) 透過試驗與數值模擬研究SMA螺栓在梁-柱螺栓連接中的複合荷載性能；(4) 提出考慮螺栓複合受力的SMA螺栓及連接設計準則。研究成果將為提升鋼結構的抗震韌性提供可靠的技術支撐。

15224125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224125.value: 自動駕駛統一多模態感知框架

15224125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224125.value: Autonomous driving has significant potential to reduce traffic congestion and improve driving safety. As the "eyes" of autonomous vehicles, perception systems typically use multiple sensors, such as cameras, LiDAR, and radar, to interpret and understand their surroundings. Current perception solutions apply independent feature extractors for each of the sensors and fuse multimodal features only at a later stage, which leads to sub-optimal perception performance. Firstly, even a failure in one of the modalities would cause the whole system to fail. Secondly, all feature extractions require to be synchronized before fusion, leading to extra inference latency. Lastly, this approach struggles to adapt to new sensor configurations, limiting system flexibility and scalability. This project aims to develop a unified framework to enhance the efficiency and practicality of multimodal perception in real-world applications. Unlike using specialized models for unimodal data, processing multimodal data with a unified framework is much more difficult given the heterogeneous nature of such data. For example, images have regular 2D grid structure, while point clouds are sets of points scattered in 3D space, making their spatial arrangement inherently different. Moreover, the quantity of point clouds and voxels varies greatly across different scenes, creating additional difficulty when attempting to fuse them consistently with fixed-length image features. We make the first attempt to tackle this challenge in this project. 1) We first convert multimodal data, such as images, point clouds, and voxels, into a sequence of tokens. These tokens are encoded with spatial embeddings so that their spatial locality can be preserved in the serialized format. Additionally, we introduce contingency tokens, which are adaptively mixed up with the modality tokens, ensuring model remains reliable even if one or more sensors fail. 2) We then develop an efficient model to process these tokens in a unified manner, enabling flexible interactions across modalities and spatial regions. To support real-time applications, a hardware-efficient algorithm is applied to accelerate attention computation. 3) Finally, we will apply this unified approach to various perception tasks such as object detection, scene understanding, and occupancy prediction. This unified perception framework greatly enhances autonomous driving by simplifying sensor data fusion, boosting efficiency, and improving scalability. Preliminary results show clear advantages in using both camera and LiDAR for object detection compared to existing solutions. The research outcomes of this project will exhibit positive impact on traffic congestion reduction, public safety and sustainable transportation. 自動駕駛具有顯著潛力，可減少交通擁堵並提高駕駛安全性。作為自動駕駛車輛的「眼睛」，感知系統通常使用多種感測器（如攝影機、雷射雷達和雷達）來解釋和理解周圍環境。當前的感知解決方案為每種感測器應用獨立的特徵提取器，僅在後期融合多模態特徵，這導致感知性能次優。首先，單一模態的失敗可能導致整個系統失效。其次，所有特徵提取需要在融合前同步，增加了推理延遲。最後，這種方法難以適應新的感測器配置，限制了系統的靈活性和可擴展性。本項目旨在開發一個統一框架，以提升多模態感知在現實世界應用中的效率和實用性。與使用專用模型處理單模態資料不同，使用統一框架處理多模態資料因其異構性而更具挑戰性。例如，圖像具有規則的二維網格結構，而點雲是三維空間中散布的點集，其空間排列本質上不同。此外，不同場景中的點雲和體素數量差異很大，這為將它們與固定長度的圖像特徵一致融合帶來了額外的困難。我們在本項目中首次嘗試解決這一挑戰：1）我們首先將多模態資料（如圖像、點雲和體素）轉換為一系列令牌。這些令牌透過空間嵌入進行編碼，以保留其序列化格式中的空間局部性。此外，我們引入了應急令牌，這些令牌與模態令牌自適應混合，確保即使一個或多個感測器失效，模型仍能保持可靠性。2）我們隨後開發了一個高效模型，以統一方式處理這些令牌，支持跨模態和空間區域的靈活交互。為了支持即時應用，我們應用了一種硬體高效的演算法來加速注意力計算。3）最後，我們將這一統一方法應用於多種感知任務，如目標檢測、場景理解和佔用預測。這一統一感知框架透過簡化感測器資料融合、提升效率和改善可擴展性，極大地增強了自動駕駛能力。

15224525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224525.value: 研發用於加工難加工超合金之微納結構表面的磁振金剛石壓印系統

15224525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15224525.value: Dr SUN, Zhanwen Prof Yip, Wai Sze Lenny

15224525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224525.value: Micro/nano-structured surfaces are widely used in modern industries, including biological, tribological, optical, and antibacterial components. Ultra-precision diamond machining technologies, primarily fast/slow tool servo turning and diamond milling, are regarded as promising methods for machining these surfaces due to their high flexibility and efficiency. However, current diamond machining technologies face challenges including low form accuracy and significant subsurface damage in the machining of difficult-to-machine superalloys, such as Inconel superalloys and Ni-based alloys. To address these issues, a new ultra-precision diamond machining technology for fabricating micro/nano-structured surfaces on difficult-to-machine superalloys with high form accuracy and improved subsurface characteristics is required. Diamond imprinting technology provides significant advantages in machining of micro/nano-structured surfaces, characterized by high efficiency and minimal tool wear, due to its unique non-additive and non-subtractive machining mechanism. Nevertheless, the mutual extrusion between the diamond tool and workpiece can easily lead to subsurface damage, compromising the integrity of machined surfaces. To mitigate this issue, this project proposes an innovative magnetic-vibration diamond imprinting (MVDI) technology. MVDI leverages high-frequency impact from a diamond indenter to produce complex micro/nano-structured surfaces through plastic deformation. This unique machining mechanism allows MVDI to flexibly machine micro/nano-structured surfaces with intricate geometric features of high aspect ratio, high density, and multiple layers. The high-frequency impact accelerates dislocation and dynamic recrystallization of subsurface material, while a tunable magnetic field actively modulates subsurface microstructural evolution in real-time. This results in unique reinforced layers with high-density nanocrystals and twin crystals on the subsurface, significantly enhancing fatigue resistance. A toolpath planning algorithm and surface generation model according to spring back errors of MVDI will be developed to ensure precise fabrication. Additionally, a multiscale coupling model will be proposed to actively control subsurface microstructural evolution, incorporating magneto-plastic effects based on discrete dislocation dynamics, crystal plasticity theory, and finite element modeling. The strengthening mechanisms of different subsurface microstructures will be explored to achieve high form accuracy and optimal subsurface reinforced layers. Finally, the micro/nano-structured surfaces utilized in fields such as optics and fluid dynamics like micro-optics arrays and micro/nano-channels will be machined on Inconel superalloys and Ni-based alloys. This underscores the innovative contributions of MDVI to the field. The unique advantage of MVDI lies in its ability to address both the form accuracy of micro/nano-structured surfaces and the subsurface microstructural modulation during machining. The research aims to break through the inherent limitations of existing ultra-precision diamond machining technologies, particularly in machining micro/nano-structured surfaces on difficult-to-machine superalloys. 微納結構表面於現代工業中應用廣泛，涵蓋生物、摩擦學、光學及抗菌元件等多個領域。超精密金剛石加工技術（主要包括快/慢刀伺服車削與金剛石銑削等）憑藉其高度靈活性與高效率，被視為製造此類表面的極具前景之方法。然而，現有金剛石加工技術在處理難加工超合金（如Inconel鎳基超合金及其他鎳基合金）時，仍面臨形狀精度不足與亞表面損傷嚴重等挑戰。為解決上述問題，亟需發展一種新型超精密金剛石加工技術，以實現在難加工超合金上加工出高面型精度和具有優異亞表面特性的微納結構表面。 金剛石壓印技術憑藉其獨特的非增材、非減材加工機制，在微納結構表面加工中具有顯著優勢，特點為效率高且刀具磨損極小。然而，金剛石刀具與工件之間的相互擠壓容易導致亞表面損傷，影響加工表面的完整性。為緩解此問題，本研究提出創新型的磁振金剛石壓印（Magnetic-Vibration Diamond Imprinting, MVDI）技術。MVDI利用金剛石壓頭施加高頻衝擊，透過塑性變形生成複雜的微納結構表面。該加工機制使MVDI能夠靈活製造具有高深寬比、高密度及多層次等複雜幾何特徵的微結構。高頻衝擊有助於促進亞表面材料的位錯運動與動態再結晶，同時可調磁場可主動即時調控亞表面微觀結構的演變。此過程將於亞表面形成具高密度纳米晶與孿晶的獨特強化層，從而顯著提升抗疲勞性能。 為確保製造精度，將開發基於MVDI回彈誤差的刀具路徑規劃算法與表面生成模型。此外，將建立一種多尺度耦合模型，結合離散位錯動力學、晶體塑性理論及考慮磁塑性效應的有限元建模，以實現對亞表面微觀結構演變的主動控制。本研究將探討不同亞表面微觀結構的強化機制，從而實現高形狀精度與最佳化的亞表面強化層。最終，將應用MVDI技術於Inconel鎳基超合金與鎳基合金上，加工適用於光學、流體動力學等領域之微納結構表面，例如微光學陣列與微/納米通道。此舉凸顯了MVDI技術在該領域的創新貢獻。 MVDI的獨特優勢在於能夠同時改善微納結構表面的形狀精度，並在加工過程中實現對亞表面微觀結構的主動調控。本研究旨在突破現有超精密金剛石加工技術的固有局限，特別是在難加工超合金上製造微納結構表面方面。

15224725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224725.value: 气相原子氧复合过程研究：计算与实验的集成探索

15224725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15224725.value: Prof HAO, Jiaao Dr Hong, Qizhen Dr Wang, Qiu Dr Wang, Yejun Prof WEN, Chih-Yung

15224725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224725.value: Hong Kong SAR and mainland China, along with the rest of the world, have demonstrated a profound commitment to advancing aerospace technology, leading to substantial investments in this field. This presents a unique opportunity for Hong Kong's academic community to engage actively in this endeavor. A pivotal gas-phase reaction within high-enthalpy air flows is the oxygen dissociation/recombination reaction represented as O2 + M ↔ 2O + M. While both the forward and reverse reactions are typically present, the recombination (reverse) reaction predominates under de-excitation (expansion) conditions. The proposed research aims to fill significant gaps in understanding atomic oxygen recombination at low temperatures, which are crucial for hypersonic flight applications. Although extensive studies have focused on nonequilibrium conditions during excitation (post-shock), there is a notable lack of investigation into de-excitation conditions, particularly at translational temperatures below 2000 K. This project uniquely integrates advanced computational techniques with innovative experimental methodologies to obtain accurate values of atomic oxygen recombination rate coefficients. For the first time, this research will employ both quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) and semi-classical (SC) methods to compute atomic oxygen recombination rates in low-temperature regimes, addressing large discrepancies found in existing literature. The project will systematically compare the accuracy and applicability of QCT and SC methods, focusing on their performance at temperatures below 2000 K. A significant aspect of this study is its commitment to generating validation-quality experimental data on recombination across a range of low translational temperatures, which is scarce to nonexistent due to various experimental limitations and complications. This will be achieved through specially designed original experiments that establish controlled low-temperature environments, yielding one-dimensional de-excitations, and employ absorption spectroscopy for accurate O2 density measurements. This dual approach not only aims to produce reliable data for atomic recombination rates but also seeks to elucidate the temperature dependence of global recombination rate coefficients. Moreover, it will investigate errors associated with approximating low-temperature rates from high-temperature dissociation rates via extrapolation and detailed balance. By addressing these critical issues, the research will provide valuable insights into the dynamics of low-temperature atomic recombination processes and answer longstanding questions in the field. Ultimately, this proposal aspires to bridge theoretical computations with empirical measurements, thereby filling a crucial gap in the existing literature on atomic oxygen recombination. The findings will have significant implications for both academic research and practical applications in physical chemistry and aerospace engineering, particularly in enhancing the design and optimization of hypersonic flight vehicles. 香港特别行政区、中国大陆及全球各国均展现出对航空航天技术发展的坚定承诺，推动该领域获得大量投资，这为香港学术界积极参与相关研究提供了独特机遇。高焓气流中的关键气相反应——氧解离/复合反应（O₂ + M ↔ 2O + M）——在弛豫（膨胀）条件下以复合（逆向）反应为主导。本研究旨在填补低温原子氧复合认知的关键空白（该过程对高超声速飞行应用至关重要）：尽管现有研究广泛关注激发态（激波后）非平衡条件，但对平动温度低于2000 K的弛豫条件研究存在显著缺失。本项目创新性地融合先进计算技术与实验方法以获取精确的原子氧复合速率系数——首次联合采用准经典轨迹法（QCT）与半经典法（SC）计算低温区复合速率以解决文献分歧；同时通过精密设计的原创实验在受控低温环境中实现一维弛豫，并采用吸收光谱技术精确测量O₂密度，填补验证级实验数据空白。研究将系统比较QCT与SC方法在<2000 K温区的精度与适用性，阐明全局复合速率系数的温度依赖性，并揭示通过高温解离速率外推估算低温速率的误差机制（基于细致平衡原理）。通过解决这些关键问题，本研究将深化对低温原子复合动力学的理解，回答领域内长期存在的科学问题，构建理论与实验的验证桥梁，最终填补原子氧复合研究的核心知识缺口，为物理化学基础研究及高超声速飞行器设计优化提供重要支撑。

15225325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225325.value: 智慧航道監管：赋能安全与可持续发展的视觉融合数据解决方案

15225325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15225325.value: Prof Li, You Kwong Stephen Prof Weng, Jinxian Prof Wu, Bing Prof YANG, Zaili

15225325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225325.value: Supervising traffic in busy waterways is essential for shipping safety and sustainable development. The current system relies mainly on the Automatic Identification System (AIS), with the Radar Surveillance System (RSS) and Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) serving as backups. However, AIS only facilitates vessel identification and tracking; it does not provide real-time visual data on vessel activities. In Hong Kong waters, vessels involved in prohibited activities, such as illegal fishing or smuggling, often deliberately turn off their AIS, and some are not equipped with it, resulting in safety gaps. It is evident that the AIS-centric approach is insufficient and ineffective for maritime monitoring. This project aims to shift waterway regulation from being AIS-centric to being vision-centric, using vision-centric fused data solutions to better monitor vessel risks and emissions, thereby improving the management of waterway safety and environmental practices. Vision-centric fused data can provide timely and rich real-time situational awareness and vessel monitoring information for restricted waters. The project first performs multi-dimensional sequence feature extraction of vessel entities from multimodal trajectories and visuals across time, space, and directional dimensions. It then uses a graph neural network to match visual semantic features and heterogeneous trajectories deeply, ultimately generating multimodal fused results centered around CCTV. Safety monitoring is the core objective of waterway management. In response to the navigation requirements of intelligent vessels transitioning from open waters to busy waterways, CCTV aids in accurately identifying vessel status. We use vision-centric fused data to map real-world scenarios and, in real-time, model and learn vessel movement behaviors, thereby generating probability distribution of future multi-vessel uncertain trajectories. Based on this trajectory distribution, we combine maritime domain knowledge to conduct adaptive grid-based risk assessments of target waterways, establishing the first vision-centric high-risk scenario database. Vision-centric fused data can also improve vessel emission analysis and monitoring in waterways. We develop a multi-task guided deep network model to extract key parameters, such as vessel draft and trim, using fused data that are often challenging to obtain accurately from AIS. Subsequently, we construct a hybrid energy consumption model that combines vessel hydrodynamic equations with neural networks. This model provides reliable emission monitoring data and supports multi-dimensional statistical analysis of regional vessel emissions based on spatial, temporal, and vessel conditions. The project contributes to developing a series of methods that enhance the monitoring of vessel activities in busy waterways by leveraging vision-centric fused data, representing a significant step forward in smart waterway management. 在繁忙航道中有效監管船舶航行，是確保航運安全與海事可持續發展的關鍵。現行監控體系以自動識別系統（AIS）為主，輔以雷達及閉路電視（CCTV）。AIS僅提供船舶識別與軌跡追蹤，缺乏即時視覺監測能力。在香港水域，部分船舶（如違規捕撈或走私）常惡意關閉AIS，形成監管盲區。現有AIS架構已難以滿足現代海事管理對安全與效率的雙重要求。 本研究通過從AIS主導轉向視覺主導，推動航道監管模式升級。透過多源視覺融合技術整合船舶動態數據，可提升風險預警精度與排放監測效能，實現安全管控與環境治理的雙重優化。此架構能即時生成船舶航行態勢圖像化情報，其高解析度空間感知特性，尤適用於香港這類限制性水域。 首先，我們提取船舶多模態軌跡與視覺數據的時空特徵，透過多層次融合架構捕捉動態行為。基於圖神經網絡深度匹配視覺語義與航行軌跡數據，生成以視覺數據為主的多模態融合感知結果，支援安全風險評估與碳排放監測。 安全監控方面，我們採用視覺主導的多源融合架構，透過時序深度學習模型即時解析船舶運動特徵，建模不確定性以生成概率化軌跡預測。結合國際海事規則與本地慣例，發展動態風險評估模型，並構建首個整合視覺語義的高風險場景數據庫。 排放監測領域，本研究透過多任務深度學習架構，精準提取船舶吃水深度、縱傾角等關鍵參數。基於流體力學與神經網絡的混合建模技術，構建首個融合視覺特徵的能耗分析模型，可生成符合IMO標準的排放數據，並支援航速-油耗分析、排放熱點標定等評估，為本地發展綠色航運提供決策依據。 本研究通過視覺融合數據，提出了一套穩健的方法來優化繁忙航道的船隻活動監控，爲智慧航道管理邁出了重要一步。

15225625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225625.value: 全氟聚醚的熱與機械化學降解：探討已知與未知全氟物質的生成

15225625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15225625.value: Dr Blotevogel, Jens Prof JIN, Ling Nathanael

15225625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225625.value: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a large group of synthetic chemicals characterized by multiple fluorine atoms attached to a carbon backbone, which imparts them exceptional chemical stability. This unique structure has led to extensive industrial and consumer product applications for decades. However, substantial evidence of their resistance to environmental degradation and the toxic properties has resulted in regulatory actions that ban many of these compounds, restricting applications to essential uses. Additionally, PFAS are known to interconvert among different forms, and some unregulated PFAS may degrade into regulated forms. Perfluoropolyethers (PFPEs), a subclass of fluorinated polymers, are widely used in high-temperature and mechanically stressed environments such as aerospace components, automotive parts, vacuum pumps, and even in consumer and personal care products. These PFPEs exist as oily liquids, have molecular weights significantly lower than typical fluoropolymers, and contain ether linkages that may contribute to their lability. While it is known that PFPEs can lose significant mass during use and break down under thermal and mechanical stress, the chemical nature and toxicity of their degradation products remain inadequately investigated. This project aims to elucidate the breakdown processes of representative PFPE products, thoroughly characterize their degradation products, and preliminarily evaluate the toxicity of degradation products. We will conduct experiments to assess the volatile loss and thermal degradation of PFPEs at elevated temperatures that represent normal use conditions, as well as at waste disposal conditions of incineration and open burning. Additionally, we will simulate mechanochemical degradation using a ball milling process, where significant chemical transformations are expected. The parent compounds and their degradation products will undergo in-depth chemical characterization using a variety of analytical techniques, including chromatography, mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance. Both volatile products and residual products soluble in water and polar solvents will be examined. The potential generation of the PFAS being regulated or under consideration for future regulation will be quantitatively assessed. We will utilize highly accurate coupled cluster theory to map reaction pathways for selected chemical structures, determine their decomposition temperatures, and conduct thermodynamic and kinetic analyses of the reactions and the underlying mechanisms. Preliminary toxicity tests using an in vitro model will evaluate the human inhalation risk of thermal degradation products. This project will enhance our understanding of the life cycle of PFPEs, potential environmental and health impacts, and their connection to regulated PFAS. 全氟與多氟烷基物質（PFAS）是一大型合成化學物質族群，其特徵為在碳骨架上連接多個氟原子，賦予其卓越的化學穩定性。憑藉這種獨特結構，PFAS 數十年來被廣泛應用於工業與消費性產品。然而，越來越多證據顯示其具高度環境持久性與毒性，已引發監管行動，禁止其中許多化合物，並將應用限制於「必要用途」。此外，PFAS 可在不同形態間相互轉換，部分未受管制的 PFAS 可能降解為受管制的形式。 全氟聚醚（PFPE）作為含氟聚合物的子類別，廣泛用於高溫與機械應力環境，例如航太元件、汽車零件、真空泵，甚至消費性與個人護理產品。這些 PFPE 多為油狀液體，其分子量顯著低於典型氟聚合物。儘管已知 PFPE 在使用過程中可能出現顯著質量損失，並在熱與機械應力下發生分解，但其降解產物的化學本質與毒性仍缺乏充分研究。 本計畫旨在釐清具代表性的 PFPE 產品之分解過程，全面鑑定其降解產物，並初步評估降解產物的毒性。我們將在代表正常使用條件的較高溫度下，評估 PFPE 的揮發損失與熱降解；同時亦在廢棄處置情境下進行測試。此外，將以球磨過程模擬機械化學降解，預期會發生顯著的化學轉化。母體化合物與其降解產物將透過多種分析技術進行深入化學鑑定，包括色譜、質譜與核磁共振；檢測對象涵蓋揮發性產物，以及可溶於水與極性溶劑的殘留產物。我們也將對可能生成的已受或擬受管制之 PFAS 進行定量評估。在理論層面，將採用高精度的耦合簇理論來描繪選定結構之熱降解反應途徑、確定其分解溫度，並針對反應與其機理進行熱力學與動力學分析。最後，將以體外模型進行初步毒性試驗，評估熱降解產物對人體吸入的風險。本計畫將強化我們對 PFPE 生命週期、其潛在環境與健康影響，以及其與受管制 PFAS 之可能關聯的理解。

15225725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225725.value: 電網互動及節能建築AI賦能的基於供應的供冷管理策略的研發和全尺寸現場驗證

15225725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225725.value: The needs for grid-interactive and energy-efficient operation of buildings are more pressing than ever, due to increasing energy demands and environmental concerns. Central air-conditioning system, as one of the major energy consumers in buildings, has great potential to enable grid-interaction and energy efficiency of buildings. However, conventional cooling management strategies of building air-conditioning systems are detrimental to grid-interactive and energy-efficient building operation. With the rapid development of AI, there has been a significant shift in how building operators manage and control buildings. A number of studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of adopting AI-empowered methods for controls of building air-conditioning systems. However, to meet the needs of grid-interactive and energy-efficient operation and facilitate the practical implementation, several major challenges still need to be addressed. First, the commonly-used feedback controls for air-conditioning systems are actually supply-based controls, which work well only under sufficient cooling supply. Although supply-based feedback control is proposed for managing the cooling distribution under insufficient cooling supply, the practical applicability, such as the deployment in conventional digital controllers and integration with demand-based feedback control and high-level grid-interactive and energy-efficient controls, still needs further investigation. Second, robust strategy to optimize the precooling time and chiller sequence during morning start period considering the effective AI-enabled training of data-driven models under very limited operation data in practical applications is still missing. Third, there are many methods to determine the demand limiting or load reduction target. However, how to control the chiller plants to achieve timely load reduction and to maintain the chiller power at the limiting target robustly is still a challenging question. This project, therefore, aims to develop and validate AI-empowered cooling management strategies for grid-interactive and energy-efficient controls of buildings. We will develop AI-empowered optimal control strategies for large chiller plants at morning start period and for fast demand limiting control to enhance building energy efficiency and flexibility. These strategies will be supported by the reconfigurable feedback control at lower level, integrating supply-based and demand-based feedback controls, to ensure proper cooling distribution and building thermal comfort under limited cooling supply. Full-scale implementation and on-site tests will be conducted to validate practical applicability of proposed strategies and further improve these strategies. The project outcomes will facilitate the practical implementation of cutting-edge cooling management optimization strategies that improve building energy flexibility and efficiency, contributing to enhanced sustainability and carbon neutrality in Hong Kong and high-density cooling-dominated cities. 面對當前不斷增加的能源需求和日益嚴重的環境問題，建築的電網互動及節能運作需求比以往任何時候都更為迫切。中央空調系統作為建築的主要能源消耗者，具有實現建築-電網互動和節能的巨大潛力。然而，傳統的建築空調系統冷量管理策略並不利於建築的電網互動和節能運作。 隨著人工智慧的快速發展，建築運維管理和控制方式發生了重大轉變。許多研究已經證明，採用人工智慧賦能的方法來控制建築空調系統是有效的。然而，為了滿足電網互動和節能運作的需求並促進部署實施，仍有幾個主要挑戰需要解決。首先，空調系統中常用的回饋控制實際上可以看作是基於需求的控制方式，這種控制方式僅在冷量供應充足時才能良好運作。儘管現有研究已經提出了基於供給的反饋控制方法來實現冷量供應不足時的合理分配，但其實際應用性仍需現場驗證，例如在傳統數位控制器中的部署以及與基於需求的反饋控制和電網交互及節能控制的集成。第二，考慮到在大型冷水機組運作資料非常有限的情況下，目前仍缺乏穩健的策略透過利用有效利用人工智慧支援的資料驅動模型的策略來優化早晨啟動期間的預冷時間和冷機開啟序列。第三，目前有許多方法可以確定建築需求限製或負荷減載的目標值。然而，如何控製冷水機組以實現即時負載減載並將冷機功耗維持在限定目標值上仍然是具有挑戰性的問題。 因此，本計畫旨在開發和驗證人工智慧賦能的基於供給的冷量管理策略，以實現建築的電網互動和節能控制。我們將開發一套人工智慧賦能的最佳控制策略，用於早晨啟動期間的空調系統控制和建築需求限制控制，分別提高能源效率和柔性。這些策略將與基於供給的可重構回饋控制相結合，以實現節能和負載限定的目標，並確保在冷量供應有限的情況下，實現合理的冷量分配和室內熱舒適控制。本計畫將全面實施所提出的控制策略並進行現場測試，以驗證和增強所提出策略的實際應用性。該計畫的結果將促進先進冷量管理策略的實際實施，這些策略優化了建築的能源靈活性和效率，有助於提高香港和高密度製冷需求主導城市的可持續性和實現碳中和的目標。

15225825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225825.value: 彎曲管道中爆轟波傳播機制研究

15225825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15225825.value: Dr Shi, Lisong Prof Zhang, Bo

15225825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225825.value: Detonation is a supersonic combustion wave driven by a shock front and supported by significant heat release behind it. This phenomenon is crucial for both industrial safety considerations and recent advances in aeronautical propulsion. For example, the rotating detonation engine (RDEs), featuring no moving parts, relies on one or more rotating detonation waves propagating circumferentially to combust fuel-oxidizer mixtures. One of the most challenging technical difficulties currently involves ensuring detonation stability inside the RDE, which typically contains a co-axial annular combustor. The stability and operational mode of these engines are heavily influenced by fundamental detonation physics. However, research on detonation characteristics in curved channels is limited, such as dynamics of multiheaded detonations, critical conditions for stable propagation, and other mechanisms potentially differing significantly from those in straight channels. Additionally, while most existing studies focus on two-dimensional detonation in straight channels, three-dimensional detonation research remains challenging from both experimental and numerical perspectives. This project aims to explore three-dimensional detonation propagation in continuously curved channels using high-fidelity simulations and specialized experiments. Emphasis will be placed on fully developed three-dimensional wave dynamics, ranging from rectangular/diagonal modes at low initial pressures to complex stochastic distributions at high initial pressures, as well as critical conditions where stable propagation could fail. Furthermore, methods will be proposed to extend the range for stable propagation. The findings of this project are expected to advance understanding of non-ideal detonation, benefiting aerospace propulsion design and industrial safety applications. 爆轟波是一種由前方激波壓縮，並由其後方可燃氣體迅速釋放熱能所維持的超音速燃燒波。這一現象對於工業安全以及近年來航空推進領域的發展具有關鍵意義。例如，旋轉爆轟發動機（RDEs）依賴一個或多個沿圓周方向傳播的旋轉爆轟波來燃燒燃料-氧化劑混合物，具有較高的理論燃燒效率且結構相對簡單。目前，確保RDE內部爆轟波穩定性的一大技術挑戰在於其通常採用同軸環形燃燒室，這些發動機的穩定性和運作模式受到基本爆轟波結構的顯著影響。然而，關於曲管內爆轟波特性，特別是多胞格爆轟波的動力學、穩定傳播的臨界條件，以及與直管道內不同的其他傳播機制，相關研究仍相對有限。此外，儘管現有多數研究集中於直管道中的二維爆轟波，三維爆轟波的實驗與數值研究仍面臨諸多挑戰。本項目旨在通過高精度模擬與專門設計的實驗，探討三維爆轟波在連續彎曲通道中的傳播行為。重點將聚焦於完全發展的三維爆轟波動力學，涵蓋從低初始壓力下的矩形/對角模式到高初始壓力下的複雜隨機分布，以及穩定傳播可能失效的臨界條件。此外，亦將提出擴展穩定傳播範圍的方法。本項目的研究成果預期將促進對非理想爆轟現象的理解，並為航天推進設計及工業安全應用提供重要參考。

15227825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15227825.value: 通过增强的ADS测试和安全评估提升自动驾驶汽车安全性

15227825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15227825.value: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) have evolved significantly over the past decade, transitioning from basic driver-assistance systems to sophisticated self-driving technologies. Their potential to drastically reduce traffic accidents caused by human error, enhance transportation efficiency, and offer mobility options for those unable to drive underscores their promise. However, ensuring the safety and security of AVs is vital, as these systems perform critical functions that directly impact passenger and public safety. Recent incidents have highlighted that faults in autonomous driving systems (ADS) can cause considerable harm, and security vulnerabilities could be exploited for remote control, leading to potentially catastrophic outcomes. Despite numerous proposed methods for testing ADS, effective and efficient testing remains a challenge, with few studies addressing the safety and security of real AVs comprehensively. To bridge these gaps, this project will tackle three pivotal research questions related to AV testing and security assessment: (1) How can we enhance the effectiveness of ADS testing? (2) How can we increase the efficiency of ADS testing? (3) How can we identify security issues in practical autonomous vehicles? In response to the first question, we will develop two innovative frameworks designed to enhance ADS testing efficiency by introducing more diverse scenarios and NPC behaviors. For the second question, we will introduce new strategies to enhance testing efficiency, such as reducing redundant computations and prioritizing highly novel test cases. Addressing the third question, we will employ cutting-edge methods to analyze attack paths, devise novel fuzzing techniques for ECUs, and develop hybrid analysis methods to detect vulnerabilities. This project aims to establish both theoretical foundations and practical systems for ADS testing and security assessments of AVs. The research will deepen our understanding of AV safety and security issues, leading to new methods for uncovering vulnerabilities and offering practical tools and valuable datasets.

15228325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15228325.value: 擴展低比特訓練以高效部署大型模型

15228325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15228325.value: Prof Li, Qing Prof Wong, Ngai

15228325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15228325.value: The rapid development of advanced language models is revolutionizing tasks like automated writing and image analysis. However, these technologies require a lot of power and are expensive to operate. They also face technical challenges, such as needing lots of memory and extensive data sharing between devices, which can slow things down. This project aims to make these models more practical and less costly to run through innovative techniques known as Quantization-Aware Training (QAT). Essentially, QAT makes these models "lighter" by simplifying their calculations without losing their effectiveness. This means they can run faster and cheaper, which is great for wider use in various industries. One key aspect of our project is developing new methods to train these models with even less data precision, like using formats called FP8 and FP4. These methods could significantly reduce how much power these models need. However, these formats come with their own set of challenges, such as instability and inaccuracies because they can only handle a limited range of data. To fix this, we’re creating a smart algorithm that adjusts how precise the model's calculations need to be in real-time, ensuring they remain efficient and accurate. Moreover, we're addressing the gap between fast-moving hardware developments and slower software updates, especially in optimizing these low-bit formats. We’ve broken our approach into three tasks: stabilizing the current training methods, exploring new ways to build these models more efficiently, and developing a comprehensive system that includes a way to check and improve these innovations. For example, in healthcare, this could lead to faster and more affordable AI that helps doctors analyze medical images or monitor patient data. In retail, AI can manage inventory or personalize shopping experiences without heavy investment in traditional computing infrastructure. By making powerful AI tools easier and cheaper to use, we're paving the way for a wide range of industries to benefit from cutting-edge technology, making it a part of everyday solutions. 先進語言模型的快速發展正在革新自動化寫作和圖像分析等任務。然而，這些技術需要大量電力，且運行成本高昂。同時，它們還面臨技術挑戰，例如需要大量記憶體，以及裝置間大量的數據傳輸，這些都可能導致運行速度變慢。本計畫旨在透過創新的「量化感知訓練（Quantization-Aware Training, QAT）」技術，使這些模型更實用且降低運行成本。簡單來說，QAT 讓這些模型在不損失效能的情況下，透過簡化運算過程變得更「輕量」。這代表它們可以運行得更快、更便宜，有助於在各行各業更廣泛地應用。 本計畫的一個重點是開發新的方法，讓這些模型能以更低的數據精度進行訓練，例如使用稱為 FP8 和 FP4 的格式。這些方法有望大幅降低模型所需的電力消耗。然而，這些格式也帶來了新的挑戰，例如因為只能處理有限範圍的數據，可能導致不穩定和不準確。為了解決這個問題，我們正在開發一種智慧演算法，能即時調整模型運算所需的精度，確保其高效且準確。 此外，我們也在解決硬體快速發展與軟體更新較慢之間的落差，特別是在優化這些低位元格式方面。我們將研究分為三個任務：穩定現有的訓練方法、探索更有效率的模型建構方式，以及開發一套完整的系統，包含檢查與改進這些創新技術的方法。 舉例來說，在醫療領域，這可以帶來更快速且更經濟實惠的 AI，協助醫生分析醫學影像或監控病患數據。在零售業，AI 可以管理庫存或個人化購物體驗，而無需大量投資傳統運算基礎設施。透過讓強大的 AI 工具更容易且更便宜地使用，我們正為各行各業鋪路，讓尖端科技成為日常解決方案的一部分。

15228825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15228825.value: 基於人工引雷通道基部電流與遠場電場測量反演回擊通道高空電流特性的新方法

15228825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15228825.value: Lightning return strokes in cloud-to-ground discharges cause damages to various facilities and bring threats to livings on Earth every year. Lightning warning and protection services have practical importance. The quality of such services highly depends on the extent of our knowledge on lightning. The general approach in lightning research is to observe the lightning behavior with specially designed optical and electromagnetic devices, among which the lightning current measurement plays a vital role. However, due to the random property of lightning, direct current measurements exist only at the channel base of lightning strokes to tall structures or rocket-triggered lightning strokes. The current distribution along a lightning return stroke channel still remains unclear. In addition to direct measurements, there are also a number of model-based studies of return strokes in literature. One of the most rigorous model-based studies is that of Willett et al. (2008), who attempted to infer the current behavior aloft from currents measured at channel base and electric fields measured at 5.2 km away for 24 return strokes in rocket-triggered lightning. Mathematically, since the current waveform is generally a function of both time and channel length, whereas the electric field waveform is a function of time alone, such an inverse problem could not be solved. To solve the problem, they defined three channel-height-dependent factors: a current amplitude factor, a current front risetime factor, and a current front velocity factor. A restriction is that while the three factors are physically correlated, they were treated independently in the model. Therefore, in this project, we aim to propose a new approach to inferring the channel current behavior based on channel-base current and far electrical field measurements of return strokes in rocket-triggered lightning. The approach will be based on a more realistic return stroke model that consists of only three physically-independent but channel-height-dependent parameters: resistance (R), inductance (L), and capacitance (C). Mathematically, such a model has a unique solution corresponding to a given set of channel-base current and far electric field measurements of a return stroke. Success in this approach will enable us to get new knowledge on the current distribution and hence the physical process in a lightning return stroke channel. Moreover, this approach, after validation in this project, can be further developed into a new technique for remotely sensing of current waveforms in a lightning return stroke channel based on multi-station far electric field measurements. 雲對地放電的雷電回擊過程每年都會導致大量設備受損，並威脅地球生命安全。雷電預警與防護服務具有重要現實意義，而此類服務的質量高度依賴於我們對雷電的認知程度。雷電研究的一般方法是採用專門設計的光學和電磁設備觀測雷電行為，其中雷電電流測量至關重要。然而，由於雷電的隨機性，目前僅能在高大建築物雷擊或人工引雷的通道基部進行直接電流測量，沿雷電回擊通道的電流分佈仍不清楚。除直接測量外，文獻中還存在大量基於模型的回擊過程研究。最嚴謹的模型研究之一是Willett等（2008）的工作，他們嘗試基於24次人工引雷回擊通道基部電流測量和5.2公里外電場觀測，推斷高空中回擊通道的電流特性。從數學上講，由於電流波形通常是時間和通道長度的函數，而電場波形僅是時間的函數，因此此類反演問題無法求解。為解決該問題，他們定義了三個隨通道高度變化的因子：電流幅值因子、電流前沿上升時間因子和電流前沿傳播速度因子。局限在於，儘管這三個因子在物理上相關，但模型中卻被獨立處理。因此，本項目旨在提出一種基於人工引雷回擊通道基部電流和遠場電場觀測，反演通道電流特性的新方法。該方法將基於更為實際的回擊模型，模型中只包含三個物理上互不相關、但隨通道高度變化的參數：電阻（R）、電感（L）和電容（C）。數學上，該模型對於每一組通道基部電流和遠場電場觀測數據都具有唯一解。此方法的成功將有助於我們獲得關於回擊通道內電流分佈及其物理過程的新認識。此外，經本項目驗證後，該方法還可進一步發展為基於多站遠場電場觀測的雷電回擊通道電流遙感新技術。

15228925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15228925.value: 基於流形學習的自適應降階建模的主動流動控制

15228925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15228925.value: Prof Noack, Bernd Dr Zhang, Hongfu

15228925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15228925.value: Active flow control (AFC) is a type of technologies that modifies fluid flow behavior by locally injecting a small amount of energy, thereby significantly enhancing the performance of a flow system. Implementing AFC usually requires knowledge of the flow, not just in the natural state but also in interaction with actuators. However, obtaining the full flow information in real-time through sophisticated experimental measurements or high-fidelity simulations by solving the full-order Navier-Stokes (N-S) equations is challenging due to the high dimensionality and strong nonlinearity of fluid flows. This complexity hinders AFC’s application in real-world scenarios. To address this issue, low-dimensional or reduced-order models (ROMs) have become a vital solution, enabling fast prediction of dominant behaviors of high-dimensional systems. A ROM can be developed using the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method, which projects the N-S equations onto a subspace spanned by orthogonal basis modes derived from training data. However, these basis modes may deform, emerge or disappear with different parameter settings, causing a ROM to lack robustness when applied to new conditions. To overcome this limitation, we propose a new adaptive ROM framework capable of handling high-dimensional, time-evolving datasets and extract essential low-dimensional features that sufficiently represent complex flow physics. This framework employs the Grassmann-diffusion manifold to approximate the mapping between input parameters and deforming spatial POD modes, and uses Galerkin projection to predict temporal POD coefficients. The combination of these modes and coefficients allows for the prediction of high-dimensional, time-evolving flow dynamics for out-of-sample cases. Additionally, incorporating a physics-augmented neural network-based surrogate in the manifold's decoding process can enhance the prediction accuracy. We will apply this new framework to explore an intriguing AFC concept: a fluidic pinball consisting of three independently rotating cylinders. An adaptive ROM will be developed for the fluidic pinball, enabling fast prediction to study three AFC problems in a computational environment, including hydrodynamic stealth or cloaking in steady and unsteady flows. Given the problem’s strong nonlinearity and high dimensionality, effective control strategies will be learnt through data-driven deep-reinforcement-learning (DRL). Furthermore, we will demonstrate the rich dynamics of the fluidic pinball and the learnt control strategies in an experimental environment. The success of this research will advance the application of ROMs in more complex AFC challenges, thereby propelling AFC technologies towards real-world applications. 主動流動控制（AFC）是通過局部注入少許能量來改變流體流動行為，從而顯著提升系統性能的一種技術。實現AFC不僅需要了解系統的自然流動狀態，還需掌握其與激勵器的相互作用。然而，由於流體流動的高維性和強非線性特性，通過精密實驗測量或求解全階Navier-Stokes（N-S）方程的高保真模擬來實時獲取完整流場資訊極具挑戰性。這一複雜性阻礙了AFC在真實場景中的應用。為此，低維或降階模型（ROMs）成為關鍵解決方案，能夠快速預測高維系統的主要行為特征。ROM可通過本徵正交分解（POD）方法構建，該方法將N-S方程投射到基於由訓練數據導出的正交基模態建立的子空間上。然而，這些基模態可能隨控制參數變化發生形變、出現或消失，導致ROM在主動控制下缺乏魯棒性。針對這一問題，我們提出一種新型自適應ROM框架，能夠處理高維時變數據集，並提取足以表徵複雜流動特性的低維特徵。該框架中，我們採用Grassmann擴散流形逼近輸入參數與形變POD空間模態間的映射關係，並利用Galerkin投影預測POD時間係數。通過模態與係數的組合，可實現對高維、時變、非樣本的流體動力學預測。此外，在流形解碼過程中引入物理增強的神經網路代理模型，可進一步提升預測精度。我們將應用該框架研究一種有趣的AFC概念——由三個獨立旋轉圓柱構成的流體彈珠。首先為流體彈珠構建自適應ROM，並基於其快速預測能力，在計算環境中研究三類AFC問題，包括定常/非定常流中的水動力隱身/欺騙。針對問題的強非線性和高維特性，將通過數據驅動的深度強化學習（DRL）獲取有效控制策略。此外，我們將在實驗環境中展示流體彈珠的豐富動力學特性及習得的控制策略。本研究的成功將推動ROM在更複雜AFC問題中的應用，加速AFC技術邁向工程實際。

15229525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15229525.value: 面向可持續海洋基礎設施的低成本廢舊塑膠衍生閃速石墨烯改性高耐久自感知混凝土

15229525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15229525.value: Dr Deng, Bing Prof Han, Baoguo Prof NI, Yi-Qing

15229525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229525.value: Hong Kong's social and economic development heavily relies on marine infrastructure. To drive growth, the government has invested significantly in projects like the proposed artificial islands near Kau Yi Chau and the Northern Metropolis. However, the extensive construction of marine infrastructure poses significant environmental, economic, and social challenges, particularly due to the resource/energy-intensive nature of concrete production and high carbon emissions, as well as the concrete durability issues (seawater-induced deterioration and steel corrosion) in marine environments.
