Another major issue in Hong Kong is plastic waste management due to high population density and limited landfill space. The absence of effective recycling methods has caused persistent accumulation of plastic waste in the natural environment, posing potential risks to human health and economic growth. Graphene, renowned for its exceptional properties, can enhance concrete durability in marine environments through microstructure optimization and corrosive ions immobilization/blocking, and integrate sensing properties into concrete, facilitating the development of highly durable and self-sensing marine concrete. It is gaining increasing acceptance as a sustainable alternative in the construction industry. However, its high cost and poor dispersibility within concrete limit its large-scale application. Therefore, this project proposes to convert plastic waste into flash graphene (PWFG) using a simple, efficient, and scalable flash Joule heating (FJH) method, which can upcycle any plastic waste into high-quality, high-dispersibility, and value-added PWFG within milliseconds, without the need for extensive pre-processing/post-purification steps. Due to the technical simplicity of FJH, PWFG is around 100-10,000 times cheaper than traditional graphene. The turbostratic PWFG is also more easily dispersible in concrete. Switching to FJH for graphene production will lead to economic savings, carbon reduction, and large-scale waste valorisation simultaneously. The use of PWFG is expected to enable durability improvement and self-monitoring/evaluation of marine concrete structures. PWFG is thus a promising nanofiller for developing highly durable and self-sensing marine concrete, yet its potential remains underexplored. The project will firstly optimise PWFG production through FJH process. Using traditional concrete fabrication methods without additional dispersion, PWFG-modified concrete materials/reinforced-concrete members will be developed. The effects and mechanisms of PWFG on concrete performance will be explored. Then, the durability of the reinforced-concrete members in marine environments and in-situ monitoring/evaluation methods of corrosion-induced cracking will be studied. Finally, the life-cycle benefits of the reinforced-concrete members will be evaluated. This project will offer an innovative solution to carbon reduction and plastic waste valorisation, pivoting towards sustainable, resilient marine infrastructure and promoting a linear-to-circular economic shift. 香港的社會及經濟發展高度依賴海洋基礎設施。為促進城市持續增長，特區政府積極推動包括交椅洲人工島及北部都會區等大型海洋工程項目。然而，這類基礎設施的廣泛建設帶來嚴峻的環境、經濟及社會问题，特別是混凝土生產過程中資源及能源消耗龐大、碳排放量高，以及混凝土於海洋環境下易受海水侵蝕及鋼筋腐蝕等耐久性問題。 同時，香港因人口密度高及堆填區空間有限，塑膠廢棄物管理壓力日益加劇。現有回收技術未能有效處理大量塑膠廢棄物，導致其在自然環境中持續累積，對公共健康及經濟發展構成潛在威脅。 石墨烯具備優異的物理及化學性能，能通過優化混凝土微觀結構及固定／阻隔腐蝕性離子，顯著提升混凝土於海洋環境下的耐久性，並賦予其自感知功能，有助於發展高耐久及智能化的海洋混凝土。儘管石墨烯在建築行業的應用潛力巨大，但其高成本及分散性不足，嚴重限制了其大規模推廣。 本項目創新地提出利用簡單、高效且可規模化的閃速焦耳熱（FJH）技術，將廢舊塑膠快速轉化為高質量、高分散性及高附加值的閃速石墨烯（PWFG），全過程僅需毫秒級時間，無需繁複的預處理或後純化步驟。得益於FJH技術的優勢，PWFG的生產成本較傳統石墨烯低約100至10,000倍，且其渦輪層狀結構有助於在混凝土中均勻分散。應用此技術不僅可實現經濟效益和碳排放減少，亦促進大規模塑膠廢棄物資源化利用。預期PWFG的引入將顯著提升海洋混凝土結構的耐久性，並賦予其自監測能力。 本研究將系統優化PWFG的FJH製備工藝，並結合傳統混凝土製備方法（無需額外分散步驟），開發PWFG改性混凝土材料及鋼筋混凝土構件。項目將深入探討PWFG對混凝土性能的影響及其作用機理，並評估相關構件於海洋環境下的耐久性及腐蝕誘發開裂的原位監測／評估方法，最終進行全生命週期效益分析。 本項目預期將為碳減排及廢舊塑膠資源化利用提供具突破性的解決方案，推動可持續及高韌性的海洋基礎設施建設，並促進香港由線性經濟向循環經濟的轉型。

15229925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15229925.value: 基於AI賦能與語義增強的香港歷史航空照片修復與三維重建

15229925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229925.value: This proposed project will develop innovative AI-empowered and semantic-enhanced methods for restoring and refining historical aerial photographs, as well as advancing 3D surface reconstruction from these images. Historical aerial photographs, such as those of Hong Kong from 100 years ago, offer unique insights into the long-term evolution of landscapes and environments. They are invaluable for historical, humanistic, and scientific research. However, their practical use is often hindered by issues such as defects and noise. Although recent advances in deep learning have improved the restoration of standard old photographs, research on enhancing old aerial photographs remains limited. Additionally, the spatial resolution of historical aerial photographs is significantly lower than modern standards (e.g., 1924 aerial photographs of Hong Kong have a ~1 m/pixel resolution, whereas recent photographs have a resolution of 0.1 m/pixel). Moreover, these photographs were not typically acquired with 3D mapping in mind, and they often lack the necessary overlap (e.g., ≥ 60%) between stereo images for effective 3D mapping. For instance, the 1924 aerial photographs of Hong Kong have an overlap rate of only ~10%, with large areas covered only monocularly. These factors present significant challenges for the practical use of historical aerial photographs. The objectives of the proposed project will be to: 1) Develop novel deep learning models for restoring historical aerial photographs, including colourisation, semantic segmentation to distinguish defects from features, and feature-preserving denoising. 2) Establish a novel deep learning model for super-resolution enhancement of denoised historical aerial photographs by leveraging semantic information and stereo texture consistency within overlapping regions. 3) Develop an innovative approach that integrates photogrammetry and deep learning for semantic-enhanced 3D surface reconstruction from refined historical aerial photographs, leveraging reliable 3D reconstruction from photogrammetry in overlapping regions and enhancing deep learning for 3D reconstruction in non-overlapping regions. We have obtained 1924, 1963, and 2023 aerial photographs of Hong Kong from the Lands Department of the HKSAR government, which will be used for method development and result validation together with open benchmark data. The research results will enable comparative studies of geographic and environmental changes in Hong Kong over the past century, providing insights into its future development. Additionally, the research outputs will have significant potential for technology transfer in domains such as photograph restoration, city modelling, urban planning, deep learning, and 3D street mapping supporting autonomous driving, benefitting not only Hong Kong but also mainland China and the global community. 本項目旨在開發創新的AI賦能與語義增強方法，以修復和優化歷史航空照片的質量，進而利用這些照片進行三維地表重建。歷史航空照片（如一百年前的香港航空照片）提供了對景觀與環境長期演變的獨特記錄，對於歷史、人文及科學研究具有無可取代的價值。然而，這些照片的實際應用常因照片上的缺陷與噪音等問題而受限。儘管近年來深度學習技術已能提升常規舊照片的修復效果，但針對舊航空照片的質量改進研究仍然稀有。此外，歷史航空照片的空間解析度遠低於現代標準（例如，1924年香港航空照片的解析度約為1米/像素，而現代航空照片的解析度則達到0.1米/像素）。更甚者，這些照片當時並非以三維測繪為目的拍攝，通常缺乏有效三維測繪所需的立體影像重疊度（如≥60%）。以1924年香港航空照片為例，其重疊率僅約10%，且大面積區域僅有單視角覆蓋。這些因素對歷史航空照片的實際應用帶來重大挑戰。 本項目的研究目標包括： 1. 開發新型深度學習模型，用於修復歷史航空照片，包括上色、語義分割以區分缺陷與特徵，以及保特徵的去噪音技術。 2. 建立新穎的深度學習模型，利用語義信息及重疊區域的立體圖像紋理一致性，對去除噪音之後的歷史航空照片進行超解析度增強。 3. 開發創新方法，融合攝影測量技術與深度學習，實現語義增強的三維地表重建。該方法將在重疊區域利用攝影測量進行可靠的三維重建，並在非重疊區域融合深度學習模型的三維重建能力。 本項目將利用1924年、1963年及2023年的香港航空照片進行方法開發與成果驗證。研究成果將促進對香港過去一世紀地理與環境變遷的比較研究，為未來發展提供洞見。此外，研究成果在舊照片修復、城市建模、城市規劃、深度學習及支援自動駕駛的三維街景地圖構建等領域有廣泛的技術轉移潛力。

15230025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230025.value: 針對多模態大語言模型的新型中毒和對抗性攻擊

15230025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230025.value: With the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), multimodal large language models (MLLMs), such as Visual ChatGPT, LLAVA, and Claude 3, are increasingly used in various applications since 2023, e.g., autonomous driving, online education, and medical diagnosis. Meanwhile, MLLMs have been found to generate offensive or malicious content easily, bringing remarkable security and safety risks. In Aug 2024, a children’s watch from the company Qihoo 360 was found to generate offensive content due to data contamination or LLM hallucination. A recent Nature paper reveals that only 1% unreal data can easily collapse AI models. There is an urgent need for pioneering security research on MLLM. This project will conduct novel research on the vulnerability analysis and robustness improvement of MLLMs, addressing poisoning and adversarial attacks. Both attacks can severely compromise an MLLM and output incorrect or malicious results. First, we analyze poisoning attacks on MLLMs in the training stage. 1) To poison MLLMs with backdoors, we propose a novel advanced backdoor attack that increases the attack stealthiness and training efficiency without sacrificing the attack success rate, which poses a new challenge for the current defense. 2) We design aggressive data poisoning attacks on MLLMs by employing diffusion models and feature space guidance to improve existing methods that may introduce detectable anomalies or require extensive manual data tampering. 3) We present the first cross-modal prompt poisoning attack for MLLMs that effectively targets both multimodal visible and invisible triggers, creating a more successful and less detectable form of poisoning. Next, we propose novel adversarial attacks on MLLMs in the inference stage. 1) We design a novel single-modal jailbreak attack based on embedding space optimization that has better stealthiness than existing jailbreak attack methods. 2) We present the first cross-modal generative jailbreak attack based on text-to-text and text-to-image generation models to improve transferability on black-box MLLMs. 3) We propose cross-task adversarial attacks for multimodal foundation models that can degrade performance on various downstream tasks or generate targeted harmful content. Finally, we introduce innovative defense strategies tailored to enhance the robustness and security of MLLMs. 1) We present a novel poisoning defense approach to detecting backdoors and implementing adversarial-ensemble countermeasures to defend against poisoning attacks. 2) We present novel defense mechanisms leveraging latent adversarial training and fine-tune-free methods to mitigate adversarial attacks. These defenses can exhibit superior effectiveness and efficiency in countering potential novel poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to current solutions. 隨著人工智慧（AI）的快速發展，自2023年以來，多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs），如 Visual ChatGPT、LLAVA 和 Claude 3，已越來越多地應用於各種領域，例如自動駕駛、線上教育和醫療診斷。與此同時，MLLMs 被發現容易生成冒犯性和暴力內容，帶來顯著的安全與風險問題。2024年8月，奇虎360公司的一款兒童手錶因數據污染或大型語言模型幻覺而被發現生成不當內容。近期一篇《Nature》論文指出，僅有1%的虛假數據就能輕易導致AI模型崩潰。因此，對MLLM的前瞻性安全研究迫在眉睫。本項目將針對MLLM的漏洞分析與魯棒性提升展開創新研究，重點解決中毒攻擊與對抗性攻擊問題。這兩類攻擊都可能嚴重破壞MLLM，導致其輸出錯誤或惡意結果。 首先，我們將分析MLLM在訓練階段遭受的中毒攻擊。1）針對MLLM的後門中毒攻擊，我們提出一種新型高級後門攻擊方法，在不降低攻擊成功率的前提下，提升攻擊的隱蔽性與訓練效率，對現有防禦手段構成新挑戰。2）我們利用擴散模型和特徵空間引導，設計針對MLLM的激進數據中毒攻擊，以改進現有方法可能引入可檢測異常或需大量人工數據篡改的問題。3）我們首次提出針對MLLM的跨模態提示中毒攻擊，有效針對多模態可見與不可見觸發器，實現更成功且更難被檢測的中毒方式。 接著，我們在推理階段提出新型對抗性攻擊。1）我們設計了一種基於嵌入空間優化的單模態越獄攻擊方法，其隱蔽性優於現有越獄攻擊手段。2）我們首次提出基於文本生成與圖像生成模型的跨模態生成式越獄攻擊，以提升對黑箱MLLM的遷移能力。3）我們提出針對多模態基礎模型的跨任務對抗性攻擊，可降低其在多種下游任務上的表現或生成特定有害內容。 最後，我們將介紹針對MLLM魯棒性與安全性提升的創新防禦策略。1）我們提出新型中毒防禦方法，能檢測後門並實施對抗集成防禦措施，以抵禦中毒攻擊。2）我們提出利用潛在對抗訓練與免微調方法的新型防禦機制，以緩解對抗性攻擊。這些防禦措施在應對潛在新型中毒與對抗性攻擊時，能展現出優於現有解決方案的效果與效率。

15230125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230125.value: 面向區塊鏈加密貨幣與匿名憑證的門限簽名研究

15230125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230125.value: Digital signatures are crucial for securing information systems. ECDSA signatures, for instance, are commonly used to authorize transactions in blockchain systems such as Bitcoin and its variants. Meanwhile, BBS+ signatures, another type of digital signature, are used in anonymous credential systems, allowing an issuer to create credentials that securely delegate certain authorities to others. However, the security of these systems relies crucially on the secrecy of the signing key, creating a single point of failure. If the issuer’s signing key is compromised, an attacker can generate a valid ECDSA signature to authorize any transaction, leading to significant financial losses. In anonymous credential systems, if the issuer’s signing key is hacked, the attacker could produce fraudulent credentials. Due to their anonymous nature, these credentials are difficult to revoke, and the consequences of such a compromise can be severe. To address this critical issue, researchers are exploring threshold digital signatures, which distribute the signing key and signing capability across multiple servers. This approach can enhance the security of blockchain systems and reduce the risk of credential forgery, leading to renewed interest in threshold signature schemes. The growing importance of this area is underscored by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), which plans to release a call for standardization through the Multi-Party Threshold Cryptography project. This research project builds on our recent work and preliminary results to advance threshold digital signatures. We focus on developing secure and efficient threshold ECDSA and BBS+ schemes for real-world applications. Specifically, we aim to enhance the protection of cryptocurrency wallets and prevent credential forgery. Additionally, we plan to actively participate in the upcoming standardization process for Multi-Party Threshold Cryptography at NIST. This project aims to yield novel insights and cutting-edge techniques that will significantly impact the theory and practice of threshold digital signatures. By providing secure cryptographic methods to safeguard blockchain-based cryptocurrencies and anonymous credential systems, this research addresses the critical single-point-of-failure problem in cryptography. It will also contribute valuable insights to the ongoing standardization efforts for Multi-Party Threshold Cryptography led by NIST. Successfully completing this project will critically enhance the theory, standardization, and practical implementation of threshold cryptography, reinforcing its effectiveness for future security needs. 電子簽名是現代資訊系統安全的核心技術。ECDSA 電子簽名廣泛應用於比特幣等區塊鏈平台的交易授權，BBS+ 電子簽名則常用於匿名憑證系統，讓發行方可安全地委派特定權限。然而，這些系統均存在單一故障點風險：一旦私鑰外洩，攻擊者便可簽署任何交易或製造偽造憑證，造成嚴重的財務及信任損失。尤其在匿名憑證系統中，憑證的匿名性令偽造憑證難以撤銷，後果更為嚴重。 門限簽名透過將私鑰及簽署能力分散至多部伺服器，有效消除單一故障點，並提升系統韌性。此技術已獲美國國家標準與技術研究院（NIST）關注，並納入其「多方門限密碼學」標準化計劃。本計劃將建基於我們既有的研究成果，研發安全且高效的門限 ECDSA 及 BBS+ 電子簽名方案，以加強加密貨幣錢包的防護及防止憑證偽造，同時積極參與國際標準化進程。 計劃的預期成果包括提出具理論創新及實務可行性的門限簽名協議，徹底解決密碼系統中的單一故障點問題，並推動全球可互通的門限簽名標準落地。透過在理論、標準及應用三方面推動門限密碼學的發展，本計劃將為未來的區塊鏈及憑證基礎設施提供長期而穩固的安全保障。

15230525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230525.value: 一種用於預訓練說話人驗證模型的語言建模方法

15230525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15230525.value: Prof Lee, Kong Aik Prof Mak, Man Wai

15230525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230525.value: Speech has long been the most natural way to interact with computers, and recent advancements in multimodal large language models such as GPT-O have further solidified its role. As the use of voice-driven technologies continues to grow, ensuring secure and personalized interactions has become crucial. Speaker verification plays a key role in this process, enabling systems to accurately verify a speaker's identity and thus safeguard sensitive information while providing tailored services. While speaker verification systems show very high accuracy in languages like English and Mandarin due to the availability of extensive labeled training data, they tend to struggle with less common languages, where labeled data is scarce. This discrepancy highlights a development challenge, as data labeling is expensive despite the vast amounts of unlabeled data available online. A cost-effective and scalable solution is to pre-train the speaker verification model using large quantities of unlabeled data before fine-tuning the model with a smaller labeled dataset. However, pre-training has not yet achieved notable success in speaker verification, with state-of-the-art models predominantly relying on end-to-end supervised learning. We argue that the primary challenge lies in selecting an appropriate pre-training objective. At present, the predominant pre-training objective for speaker verification is segment-level contrastive learning. This approach assumes that speech segments from different utterances are from different speakers, an assumption we find restrictive. Because speech is fundamentally a spoken form of language, language modeling objectives, such as masked prediction and next-token prediction, should serve as better pre-training objectives. We propose a novel language modeling approach tailored for pre-training speaker verification models. Rather than performing masked prediction or next-token prediction on raw or manually crafted speech features, we first disentangle and tokenize the speech signal into discrete semantic tokens and continuous speaker tokens. After tokenization, we employ language modeling objectives, such as masked prediction or next-token prediction, on the speaker tokens conditioned on the semantic tokens. To further facilitate the learning of segment-level speaker representation, we propose a memory-augmented Transformer, which automatically learns to aggregate frame-level features to segment-level speaker representation through backpropagation using read and write memories. Preliminary findings indicate that the proposed method surpasses leading speaker pre-training models on the SUPERB benchmark in speaker identification and speaker verification. By addressing the current limitations of speaker pre-training, this work has the potential to significantly advance speaker verification technology, particularly in low-resource languages, paving the way for more inclusive, secure, and scalable voice-driven systems. 語音長期以來一直是與電腦互動最自然的方式，而近來如 GPT-O 等多模態大型語言模型的進展，更進一步鞏固了語音在其中的角色。隨著語音驅動技術的應用日益普及，確保互動的安全性與個人化變得至關重要。說話人驗證在此過程中扮演關鍵角色，使系統能準確驗證使用者身分，從而保護敏感資訊並提供個性化服務。雖然說話人驗證系統在英語與中文等資源豐富的語言中已達到極高的準確率，但在資料稀缺的低資源語言中仍面臨困難。這種差異凸顯了一項發展挑戰：儘管網路上存在大量未標註的語音資料，標註資料的取得成本仍然高昂。一個具成本效益且具可擴展性的解決方案，是先使用大量未標註語音資料對說話人驗證模型進行預訓練，再以少量標註資料進行微調。 然而，在說話人驗證任務中，預訓練尚未取得顯著成效，當前最先進的模型仍多依賴端到端的監督式學習。我們認為，主要挑戰在於如何選擇合適的預訓練目標。目前說話人驗證的主流預訓練方法是語段層級的對比學習，該方法假設不同語音片段來自不同的說話人，這一假設具有侷限性。我們主張，語音作為語言的聲音表達形式，應該採用語言建模目標（如遮蔽預測和下一詞預測）作為更合適的預訓練目標。 因此，我們提出一種全新的語言建模方法，專為說話人驗證模型的預訓練設計。該方法並非直接在原始或手工設計的語音特徵上執行遮蔽或下一詞預測，而是先將語音訊號解構並分別表示為離散的語意標記與連續的說話人標記。完成標記化後，系統便可在語意標記條件下，對說話人標記進行遮蔽預測或下一詞預測。為進一步學習語段層級的說話人表示，我們提出一種具備記憶增強機制的 Transformer 模型。該模型透過讀寫記憶模組與反向傳播，能自動學會如何將影格層級的特徵聚合為語段層級的說話人表示。初步實驗結果顯示，所提出的方法在 SUPERB 基準測試中的說話人識別與說話人驗證任務上，超越了目前最先進的說話人預訓練模型。本研究透過解決現有預訓練方法的限制，有潛力大幅推進說話人驗證技術，特別是在低資源語言中，從而推動語音驅動系統邁向更加包容、安全與可擴展的未來。

15230825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230825.value: 多功能氣凝膠一體化層間材料用於未來航空級碳纖維增強複合材料的設計與相關機制

15230825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15230825.value: Prof Shen, Xi Prof Zhang, Weizhao

15230825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230825.value: Carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites hold significant promise for aviation and aerospace applications due to their superior strength-to-weight ratio. However, challenges such as delamination and low through-thickness electrical conductivity pose significant concerns for high-requirement aviation applications. Electrically conductive interlaminar interleaves have shown substantial improvements in both interlaminar toughness and through-thickness electrical conductivity of CFRP composites. The presence of porous networks within these interleaves also enhances the impregnation efficiency of carbon fabrics. Nevertheless, the discontinuous nature of interleaves between carbon fabrics results in inconsistent mechanical properties and limited improvement in through-thickness electrical conductivity. To tackle the above challenges, we propose a novel aerogel-based integrated interleave to enhance both interlaminar properties and through-thickness electrical conductivity of multifunctional CFRP composites through multiscale structural mechanisms. At the macroscale, integrated interleaves with continuous vertical pore channels interlock all carbon fabric layers, improving the load distribution across the CFRP composites and enhancing their interlaminar fracture toughness. At the microscale, vertically aligned pore structures create unique paths to facilitate efficient resin flow during composite fabrication, producing high-quality, void-free composite structures. The use of conductive nanofillers in the integrated interleaves also forms a 3D connected conductive network in the CFRP composites, significantly boosting through-thickness electrical conductivity. At the nanoscale, silane functionalization of the integrated interleaves enhances their wettability to resin, further improving the impregnation efficiency of carbon fabrics. The aforementioned multiscale structure of integrated interleave modified carbon fabrics will be fabricated using a facile freeze-casting approach, followed by solvent exchange and ambient pressure drying, which are energy-efficient and scalable. The fundamental freezing dynamics will be studied to determine the relationship between the freezing parameters, such as freezing rate and temperature, and the microstructure of the aerogel-based integrated interleaves. The effects of multiscale mechanisms on improving both mechanical and electrical performance of integrated interleave modified CFRP composites will also be investigated systematically to establish the processing-structure-property relationship, providing valuable insights for designing and fabricating future multifunctional CFRP composites. The PI has solid experience in designing multifunctional CFRP composites and nanocomposites, as well as developing advanced freeze-casting techniques. The successful implementation of this project will not only provide effective strategies for designing future multifunctional composite materials, but also enable the use of alternative out-of-autoclave techniques to enhance the versatility of CFRP composite manufacturing. This will expand their applications across a wider range of industries and offer innovative solutions for the green manufacturing of composites, thereby contributing to carbon neutrality. 碳纖維增強複合材料（CFRP）因其優異的強度重量比，在航空航太領域展現出巨大應用潛力。然而，層間剝離及厚度方向導電性不足，仍為高要求航空應用中的主要挑戰。傳統導電層間材料多為局部性設計，僅於複合材料中間插入單一層導電材料，雖可在一定程度上提升CFRP的層間韌性及厚度方向導電性，其多孔結構亦有助於碳布的樹脂滲透，但由於分布不連續，導致整體機械性能不均，且厚度方向導電性提升有限。因此，如何實現層間材料的連續性分布與多功能整合，成為提升CFRP整體性能的關鍵。 為解決上述問題，本研究提出創新氣凝膠一體化層間材料，藉由多尺度結構機制，全面提升CFRP複合材料的層間性能與厚度方向導電性。在宏觀層面，連續垂直孔道的一體化層間材料可將所有碳布層有效互鎖，優化載荷分布，顯著增強層間斷裂韌性。微觀層面，垂直排列的孔道促進樹脂於製程中的高效流動，實現高品質、無氣孔的複合材料結構。納米尺度上，導電納米填料於層間材料內構建三維導電網絡，大幅提升厚度方向導電性；矽烷官能化則進一步增強層間材料對樹脂的潤濕性，提升碳布的浸潤效率。 本研究將採用簡便的冷凍鑄造法製備多尺度結構的氣凝膠一體化層間材料，並結合溶劑交換及常壓乾燥工藝，兼具節能與可擴展性。將系統性探討冷凍參數（如速率與溫度）對氣凝膠微結構的影響，並深入分析多尺度機制對CFRP複合材料機械與電性能的提升作用，建立「製造工藝 -— 結構 — 性能」的關係，為未來多功能CFRP複合材料的設計與製備提供理論依據。 主持人具備多功能CFRP複合材料與納米複材設計經驗，並精於先進冷凍鑄造技術。本計畫的成功實施，將為多功能複合材料設計提供有效策略，推動替代高壓釜 (Out-of-autoclave)的製程技術，拓展CFRP複合材料於更多產業的應用，並為綠色製造與碳中和目標貢獻創新解決方案。

15231225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15231225.value: 結合空氣除濕、取水與熱能回收之高耐久陶瓷膜組件於炎熱潮濕地區之開發研究

15231225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15231225.value: Prof Wang, Qiuwang Prof Zhang, Shaowei

15231225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15231225.value: Humidity control is crucial for ensuring comfort, protecting health, preserving materials, enhancing energy efficiency, and boosting productivity. In hot and humid regions, moisture removal has a dominant position in processing fresh air process, accounting for 50-70 % of total cooling load. Conventional condensation dehumidification removes moisture by cooling air below the dew point, resulting in significant electricity consumption. As an effective alternative for electricity-free air dehumidification, liquid desiccant dehumidification offers a solution by utilizing renewable or low-grade heat energy instead of electricity, but it faces challenges like severe salt-induced metal corrosion and desiccant droplet carryover. Membrane-based liquid desiccant air dehumidification, using hydrophobic porous membrane to separate liquid desiccant and air, can effectively prevent desiccant droplet carryover. However, existing polymer membranes require frequent replacements due to issues like membrane deformation/deflection from poor mechanical strength and fouling from salt crystallization, making them unsuitable for long-term use. Finding a robust membrane technology for electricity-free air dehumidification is crucial. We have successfully designed and fabricated self-supported, porous, superhydrophobic ceramic membranes with optimal pore sizes for vapor transport to and from desiccants. Additionally, bridging electricity-free air dehumidification with moist air water harvesting is our recent interest, as the moisture in humid air represents a vast natural water source. By utilizing latent heat from water vapor condensation, the synergy of air dehumidification and water harvesting in a closed desiccant loop can also offer the potential for heat recovery and improved thermal energy utilization compared to traditional dehumidification technologies. Therefore, this project aims to develop a novel, versatile, and robust ceramic membrane module for liquid desiccant air dehumidification, water harvesting, and heat recovery. Initially, a molecular dynamics simulation will explore vapor transportation at the atomic level. Based on these insights, a ceramic membrane with optimal pore size distribution and exceptional permeability will be fabricated. Next, a multi-functional, durable, self-supported membrane module will be created using this ceramic membrane to facilitate desiccant concentration, water harvesting, and heat recovery. To understand salt migration and trans-membrane vapor transport, a multi-physics model will be developed to simulate the flow, heat, and mass transfer processes for the desiccant solution and air. A thermodynamic-hydrodynamic-economic model for the ceramic membrane-based liquid desiccant dehumidification system will evaluate the long-term operation, focusing on dehumidification capacity, freshwater production and energy efficiency. We believe our innovative ceramic membrane module will offer new insights into addressing energy-intensive air dehumidification and freshwater scarcity, enhancing the energy-water-air nexus. 濕度控制對於確保舒適性、保護健康、保存材料、提升能源效率以及促進生產力至關重要。在炎熱潮濕的地區，除濕在新風處理過程中佔據主導地位，其負荷占總冷卻負荷的 50–70%。傳統的冷凝除濕方式是通過將空氣冷卻至露點溫度以下來去除水分，這會導致大量的電力消耗。作為一種不依賴電力的有效除濕替代方案，液體乾燥劑除濕技術利用可再生或低品位熱能來取代電力，然而該技術面臨金屬腐蝕與乾燥劑液滴夾帶的嚴重挑戰。基於半透膜的液體乾燥劑除濕系統，利用疏水多孔膜將乾燥劑與空氣隔離，可有效防止乾燥劑液滴夾帶。然而，現有的聚合物膜因機械強度不足導致變形或彎曲，以及鹽分結晶造成汙垢等問題，需頻繁更換，因此不適用於長期使用。 尋找一種堅固耐用的膜技術以實現無電力空氣除濕至關重要。我們已成功設計並製造出自支撐的多孔超疏水陶瓷膜，具有最適孔徑分佈，能有效促進濕空氣與乾燥劑間的蒸汽傳輸。此外，我們近期的研究重點也在於將無電力空氣除濕與濕空氣取水相結合，因為潮濕空氣中的水氣意味著一種龐大的天然水資源。通過利用水蒸氣冷凝的潛熱，將除濕與取水整合於封閉式乾燥劑循環中，有望實現熱能回收並提升熱能利用效率，優於傳統除濕技術。 因此，本研究旨在開發一種新穎、多功能且堅固耐用的陶瓷膜組件，適用於液體乾燥劑除濕、取水與熱能回收。首先，我們將通過分子動力學模擬在原子層級探討水蒸氣的傳輸機制。基於這些科學洞見，我們將製造出具有最佳孔徑分佈與卓越滲透性的陶瓷膜。然後，將利用該陶瓷膜製作出多功能、耐用且自支撐的膜組件，用以促進乾燥劑濃縮、取水與熱能回收。為深入理解鹽分遷移與跨膜水蒸氣傳輸過程，我們將建立一套多物理場模型，以模擬乾燥劑溶液與空氣的流動、傳熱與傳質過程。此外，我們也將建立一套基於熱力學、流體力學與經濟性的模型，對陶瓷膜液體乾燥劑除濕系統進行長期運行評估，重點關注除濕能力、淡水產量與能源效率。 我們相信，這項創新的陶瓷膜組件將為解決高耗能的空氣除濕與淡水短缺問題提供全新見解，進一步促進能源-水-空氣間的協同效益。

15231825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15231825.value: 複雜荷載條件下軟黏土海床桶式基礎的多尺度分析

15231825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15231825.value: Dr CHEN, Qiushi Dr LI, Zheng

15231825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15231825.value: Oceans cover more than 70% of Earth’s surface. Recent decades have seen the rapid development of offshore wind turbines in response to increasing demand for green energy. Currently, such constructions are mainly conducted in near-shore areas, and caisson foundations are commonly used to fix superstructures. Ensuring the stability of caisson foundation in the harsh working environment of the sea has become a major consideration in design. However, the bearing capacity of caissons in soft clay (common sediments around HK) has not been sufficiently studied. In essence, caisson capacity is the sum of the mobilized soil shear strength and pore pressure near the caisson. An accurate estimation of it thus requires the soil behaviors to be realistically described. To date, most existing studies have only considered soils with time-invariant undrained shear strength under monotonic loads, which is far from real conditions in the field. In reality, the complex offshore loads lead the soil near the caisson to undergo repeated and combined effects of time (consolidation+creep), large numbers of cyclic loadings with principal stress rotations, causing intricate evolution of soil shear strength against time. The resulting evolution of caisson capacity, however, is not yet clear. This project aims to develop an integrated computational framework, through an in-depth study progressing from theoretical fundamentals to practical applications, that offers improved predictions of caisson capacities in soft clay. Effects of time, cyclic loading, and principal stress rotations will be clarified through microstructural and micromechanical investigations to explore the fundamental mechanisms and establish constitutive models. The outcomes will be further integrated with a novel adaptive time homogenization method and implemented into an in-house particle finite element method (PFEM) code to realistically model the caisson-clay interaction with high computational efficiency. Based on validation and extensive PFEM simulations, a time-dependent macroelement-based design tool will be finally upscaled for engineering use. This project will be the first systematic multiscale study of the full lifecycle behavior of caissons in soft clay. It will offer not only a series of valuable experimental data to understand the behaviors of soft clay under complex offshore loads, but also a constitutive model and a multiscale PFEM framework to realistically and efficiently reproduce these soil behaviors and soil-caisson interactions. The established macroelement tool is expected to allow for more realistic considerations during the current time-invariant design procedures, contributing to innovations in design concepts, and safeguarding the prosperous ocean economy in HK and beyond. 海洋覆蓋了地球表面70%以上的面積。近幾十年來，隨著綠色能源需求的不斷增長，海上風力發電得到了快速發展。目前，此類建設主要在近岸地區進行，桶式基礎通常用於固定上部結構。確保桶式基礎在惡劣的海上工作環境下的穩定性已成為設計中的重要考慮因素。 然而，軟黏土（香港週邊常見的沉積物）中桶式基礎的承載力尚未被充分研究。桶式基礎承載力本質上是土體剪切強度與基礎附近孔隙壓之和。因此，準確估算承載力需要真實描述土體的特性。迄今為止，大多數現有研究僅考慮了單調荷載作用下具有時間無關不排水剪切強度的土體，這與現場實際情況相差甚遠。實際上，複雜的海上荷載會導致桶式基礎附近的土經歷時間（固結+蠕變）和大量循環荷載作用以及主應力旋轉的複合作用，從而導致土的剪切強度隨時間發生複雜的演變。然而，由此導致的基礎承載力演變尚不明確。 本項目旨在透過從理論基礎到實際應用的深入研究，開發一個整合的計算框架，以更好地預測軟黏土中桶式基礎的承載力。本項目將首先通過微觀結構和微觀力學研究，闡明時間、循環荷載和主應力旋轉的影響，從而探索其基本機制並建立土的本構模型。研究結果將進一步與一種新穎的自適應時間均質化方法相結合，並應用於粒子有限元法 (PFEM) 程序，以高效地模擬基礎結構-黏土相互作用。基於驗證和大量的 PFEM 模擬，最終將開發一個基於時宏單元的設計工具，並將其應用於工程實踐。 本項目將首次系統性地進行桶式基礎在軟黏土中全生命週期行為的多尺度研究。它不僅將提供一系列寶貴的實驗數據，以了解軟粘土在複雜海上荷載下的行為，還將構建一個本構模型和多尺度有限元框架，以真實高效地再現這些土體行為以及土體-基礎相互作用。預計成熟的宏單元工具將在當前的設計程序中提供更切合實際的考慮，從而促進設計理念的創新，並維護香港及週邊地區海洋經濟的繁榮發展。

15231925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15231925.value: 基於3D打印可固化液體波導的人工複眼相機

15231925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15231925.value: Traditional imaging devices face challenges such as narrow field of view (FOV), distortion, and slow response. Artificial compound eyes (ACEs) mimic natural compound eyes (NCEs) and could overcome these limitations by utilizing an array of ommatidia distributed across a curved surface as imaging units. However, most existing compound eye cameras still rely on flat microlens arrays or combinations of multiple traditional cameras, resulting in a limited FOV (<100 deg) and large size (~20 cm). Curved microlens arrays have also been proposed, but they have difficulties in high-resolution imaging and dynamic perception. It remains a significant challenge for the ACEs to mimic the anatomic structure of NCEs to transfer light from a curved surface to a planar imaging sensor chip while maintaining the spatial relationships without distortion. This project aims to utilize curable liquid waveguides as artificial ommatidia, filling them into the through-holes of a 3D-printed dome to form an artificial compound eyes camera (ACEcam). One end of each through-hole is positioned on the hemispherical surface of dome to receive light from a 180-deg FOV, while the other end is packed in the flat base of dome, projecting light onto a planar imaging sensor. To reduce the acceptance angle (i.e., the angular resolution) of individual ommatidia (from ~51 to 1.15 deg), a curved diaphragm with pinholes will be used to as the apertures of ommatidia. This project is innovative in the following aspects: (1) the use of complete liquid waveguides for ACEs; (2) the formation of numerous curable liquid waveguides using 3D-printed through-holes; and (3) the design of an aperture diaphragm to limit the acceptance angle of ommatidia. The project will be divided into three tasks: (i) design and analysis, (ii) fabrication and characterization, and (iii) system integration and prototyping. In pilot studies, we have used optical fibers to represent the liquid waveguides to build up an ACEcam with 272 ommatidia and have demonstrated the functions of static imaging and dynamic detection. We have also verified the enhanced light transmission via the liquid core (NOA61, n = 1.56) by covering the layered texture of 3D printing with a UV-curable liquid cladding (PTFE, n = 1.37). In this project, the liquid-waveguide ACEcam aims at 10,001 ommatidia, 180-deg FOV, 1.15-deg angular resolution and dynamic perception >10 kHz with a diameter ~14 mm. These superior performances make the ACEcam highly potential for emerging applications such as drones, machine vision, autonomous driving and virtual reality. 傳統成像設備面臨視場（FOV）窄、失真和響應慢等挑戰。人工復眼 （ACE） 模仿天然復眼（NCE），利用分佈在曲面上的一系列單眼作為成像單元來克服這些限制。然而，現有的復眼相機多數仍然依賴平面型微透鏡陣列或多個傳統相機的組合，導致視場有限（<100度）和大尺寸（~20 厘米）。彎曲型微透鏡陣列也有被提及，但在高解析度成像和動態感知方面存在困難。 對於ACE來說，模仿NCE的解剖結構，將光從曲面轉移到平面成像傳感器，同時還能保持不同部分光線的空間關係不變，目前仍然有難度。 本項目的人工復眼相機 （ACEcam）將可固化的液體光膠填充到3D打印圓頂的一系列通孔中，經固化後形成很多光導。每個光導一端位於圓頂的半球形表面上，以接收來自180度視場的光，另一端坐落在圓頂的平坦底部，將光投射到平面成像傳感器上。為了降低單眼的接受角（即角解析度）（從約51度降到到1.15度），ACEcam使用帶有圓孔陣列的彎曲隔膜作為光導單眼的孔徑光欄。本項目的創新性主要在以下幾個方面：（1）ACEcam採用液體光導；（2）使用3D打印的通孔形成許多可固化的液體波導；（3）使用彎曲隔膜上的圓孔陣列來限制單眼的接受角。 本項目包括三項任務：設計和分析、製造和表徵、以及系統集成和原型製作。在前期初步研究中，我們使用光纖代替液體波導，已成功構建具有272個單眼的ACEcam，實現了靜態成像和動態檢測的功能。我們還用紫外線固化的液體包層（PTFE，折射率1.37）來覆蓋3D打印導致的分層紋理結構，驗證了液體固化後的芯層（NOA61，折射率1.56）可高效傳導光線。本項目的液體波導ACEcam預計最終直徑僅為約1.4厘米，將獲得10,001個單眼、180度視場角、1.15度的角解析度和>10 kHz的動態響應速度。ACEcam的優異性能使其可廣泛應用於無人機、機器視覺、自動駕駛和虛擬實境等新興應用。

15234025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234025.value: 論高超聲速鈍體流動的轉捩反轉現象

15234025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15234025.value: Dr GUO, Peixu Dr Li, Xin Prof WEN, Chih-Yung

15234025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234025.value: Understanding and predicting laminar‒turbulent transition in hypersonic flow is crucial for developing future high-speed transportation systems. In practical engineering, the leading edge of a hypersonic vehicle is usually blunted to mitigate aerodynamic heating. Leading-edge bluntness initially delays transition and then promotes it, a phenomenon known as transition reversal. This phenomenon was discovered more than 40 years ago but remains poorly understood. Our preliminary study suggests that transition reversal may result from the breakdown of streamwise streaks originating from the receptivity to freestream disturbances. Therefore, this project proposes to systematically investigate this plausible explanation using linear stability analysis, high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics, and wind tunnel experiments. The outcomes of this project are expected to reveal the physical mechanism of transition reversal for the first time and provide a better understanding of hypersonic boundary-layer transition. 理解和預測高超聲速流動中的層流-湍流轉捩現象，對未來高速運輸系統的研發至關重要。 在實際工程中，高超聲速飛行器前緣通常採用鈍化設計以緩解氣動加熱，而前緣鈍度會先延遲轉捩而後促進轉捩，這一現象被稱為“轉捩反轉”。 儘管該現象早在40多年前已被發現，但其機理至今尚未得到充分闡釋。 我們的前期研究表明，轉捩反轉可能源於自由流擾動感受性誘發的流向條帶結構破裂。 基於此，本專案擬通過線性穩定性分析、高精度計算流體力學及風洞實驗系統驗證這一解釋機制。 研究成果有望首次揭示轉捩反轉的物理本質，併為高超聲速邊界層轉捩機理提供更深入的理論認知。

15234425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234425.value: 發展老化住宅建築群狀況評估的數據驅動預測模型

15234425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15234425.value: Prof Chan, Albert Ping Chuen Dr Chan, Man Wai Prof LAI, Joseph Hung-kit

15234425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234425.value: Urban decay presents a significant challenge for many developed cities worldwide as aging residential building stock continues to expand. In Hong Kong, by the end of 2024, over 28,000 private residential buildings will have reached 30 years or older, representing approximately 64% of total building stock. These aging buildings often suffer from decades of inadequate maintenance, a problem compounded by socio-economic barriers that prevent residents from affording the necessary condition assessment and repairs. To mitigate further deterioration, there is an urgent need for a predictive condition assessment model that facilitates timely maintenance intervention. While modern, data-driven methodologies such as Bayesian Network (BN) algorithms and Graph Neural Networks have been increasingly applied to assess civil engineering infrastructure like ports and building energy systems, their application to aging residential buildings remains underexplored. This research proposes the development of a data-driven prediction model using a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN), leveraging the unique strength of BN to integrate historical data and expert knowledge. This proposal differentiates itself from those prior civil engineering infrastructure studies by utilising the rich database of real-life building inspection reports maintained by Hong Kong Buildings Department, in combination with expert insights and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based panoramic image recognition algorithm for defect detection. This comprehensive dataset facilitate a practical and precise approach for assessing and predicting building conditions over time, enabling timely maintenance interventions and long-term planning. The DBN framework provides a robust and adaptive method for capturing the complex, interconnected nature of building deterioration features, offering improved predictive accuracy compared to traditional deterministic models. This proposed model will present a fresh perspective for both academics and industry practitioners, demonstrating how the condition assessment of aging residential buildings can be transformed through the integration of advanced probabilistic models and emerging technologies. Its capacity to continuously update with new inspection and image data over time enables policymakers and stakeholders to simulate intervention strategies and evaluate their long-term effects on urban resilience. The model is particularly well-suited for large inventories of aging residential buildings, its adaptability extends to other urban contexts facing similar challenges. The global applicability of this approach positions it as a scalable and efficient solution for managing aging residential stock in cities worldwide, bridging a critical gap in the research conducted to date. 城市衰敗對全球許多已發展城市構成嚴峻挑戰，隨著老化住宅建築存量持續增加，此問題愈加突出。以香港為例，截至2024年底，超過28,000幢私人物業住宅樓齡已達30年或以上，約佔全港建築總量的64%。這些老化建築往往因長年缺乏適當維修而逐漸惡化，而居民因經濟條件限制無法負擔必要的檢測與維修，更令問題雪上加霜。為減緩進一步惡化，亟需建立一套能夠進行預測性狀況評估的模型，以便及時進行維護與干預。儘管近年來，數據驅動的方法論，例如貝葉斯網絡（Bayesian Network, BN）演算法與圖神經網絡（Graph Neural Networks）已逐漸應用於港口或建築能源系統等土木基礎設施的狀況評估，但針對老化住宅建築的研究仍相當有限。本研究提出利用動態貝葉斯網絡（Dynamic Bayesian Network, DBN）開發數據驅動的預測模型，充分發揮BN整合歷史數據與專家知識的優勢。與以往針對土木基礎設施的研究不同，本計畫將結合香港屋宇署保存的真實建築檢驗報告資料庫、專家判斷，以及基於卷積神經網絡（Convolutional Neural Network, CNN）的全景影像辨識演算法進行缺陷檢測。透過這個綜合資料集，可實現兼具實務性與精準度的建築狀況評估與預測，有助於及時維修干預及長期規劃。DBN框架可強韌且動態地捕捉建築劣化特徵間的複雜關聯性，相較於傳統確定性模型，具備更高的預測準確度。本研究所提出的模型，將為學術界與業界提供全新視角，展示如何透過先進機率模型與新興技術的結合，革新老化住宅建築的狀況評估方式。該模型具備隨時間持續更新新檢測數據與影像資料的能力，使決策者與相關持份者能夠模擬不同維修干預策略，並評估其對城市韌性的長期影響。此模型尤其適用於龐大的老化住宅建築群，其適應性亦可延伸至面臨類似問題的其他城市情境。由於具備全球適用性，此方法為管理城市老化住宅存量提供了一套可擴展且高效的解決方案，填補了當前研究的重大缺口。

15235625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15235625.value: 老年群體熱健康感知與風險研究：從城市暴露到生理建模

15235625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15235625.value: Dr Huang, Yu Prof NIU, Jian-lei Prof TAN, Qitao

15235625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15235625.value: In recent years, extreme heat events have become more frequent and severe due to global warming, posing significant threats to public health worldwide. This issue is particularly pressing in cities like Hong Kong, which faces an impending aging population crisis. Many senior residents, driven by limited living space and the need for social interaction, frequently use public open spaces. However, older adults are among the most vulnerable groups in the face of climate change due to their diminished ability to regulate body temperature and reduced awareness of heat stress. Personal awareness of heat risks and the ability to take preventive actions are critical to avoiding heat-related health problems. Despite the urgency of this issue, there is still a limited understanding of how older adults perceive and respond to heat risks, making it difficult for authorities to develop effective public health strategies. This research aims to explore the relationship between outdoor heat exposure, heat-health perceptions, and physiological responses across different age groups, with a focus on older adults. The study is divided into three main tasks. First, we will analyse a city-scale, real-time mobile signal dataset from Guangzhou to assess outdoor heat exposure patterns of different age groups and investigate the relationship between heat exposure and hospital visits. By examining their duration of outdoor activity under different heat stress levels, we aim to gain insights into attenuated heat-health perception in older adults and its impact on the healthcare system. Second, we will conduct outdoor field experiments to assess how young and older adults perceive heat and heat-health-related symptoms, and how their bodies respond to heat stress. We will monitor physiological parameters such as heart rate, core body temperature, whole-body water loss, and blood pressure to understand age-related differences in heat-health perception in real-world outdoor environments. Finally, through experiments in a controlled climate chamber, we will develop mathematical models linking heat-health perceptions to physiological responses under neutral to hot conditions. These models will help predict how different age groups perceive their thermal environment and health status, as well as quantify the degree and trend of perceptual attenuation in physiological responses among older adults. By combining real-world data with experimental findings, this research will provide a comprehensive understanding of the risks posed by extreme heat, especially to older adults. The results will inform public health strategies and urban planning efforts to reduce heat-related health risks, ultimately protecting vulnerable populations as global temperatures rise. 近年來，受全球變暖影響，極端高溫事件日益頻繁且強度增強，給全球公共健康帶來了嚴峻挑戰。對於諸如香港這樣的亞熱帶高密度城市而言，這一問題尤為緊迫，因為其正面臨日益嚴峻的人口老齡化趨勢。許多老年居民由於居住空間有限以及社交需求，經常在戶外公共空間活動。然而，老年人由於其體溫調節能力減弱以及對熱應激感知能力下降，成為氣候變化下最為脆弱的群體之一。個體對高溫風險的感知以及主動採取防護措施的能力，是預防高溫相關健康問題的關鍵。儘管這一問題日趨緊迫，目前對於老年人如何感知並應對高溫風險的理解仍然有限，阻礙了公共衛生政策的有效制定。 本研究旨在探討戶外熱暴露、熱健康感知與生理響應之間的關係，特別聚焦於老年群體。研究將分為三個主要工作任務。首先，我們將分析廣州地區的城市尺度實時移動信號數據，以評估不同年齡群體的戶外熱暴露模式，並進一步探討熱暴露與醫院就診之間的關係。通過分析不同熱應激等級下的戶外活動時長，我們期望揭示老年人熱健康感知能力減弱的現象及其對醫療系統的潛在影響。其次，我們將開展戶外實地實驗，比較年輕人和老年人在實際熱環境中的熱感知、熱健康症狀及其生理響應。通過監測心率、核心體溫、全身水分流失量和血壓等生理指標，深入理解不同年齡群體在真實戶外環境下的熱健康感知差異。最後，我們將在可控環境艙中開展實驗，構建從中性至高溫環境下熱健康感知與生理響應之間的數學模型，用以預測不同年齡群體對熱環境與健康狀態的感知能力，量化老年人生理響應中感知衰減的程度與趨勢。 本研究將結合真實世界的大數據分析與實驗研究成果，系統揭示極端高溫對老年群體的健康風險機制，為制定更具針對性的公共衛生策略與城市規劃措施提供科學依據，在全球氣溫持續上升的背景下更好地保護脆弱人群。

15236125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15236125.value: 研究與開發基於GNSS干涉反射測量技術的多路徑效應位置相關特徵以用於城市峽谷定位

15236125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15236125.value: Prof HSU, Li-Ta Prof XU, Bing

15236125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15236125.value: Accurate position information is essential to various location-based applications, which is usually obtained by GNSS, as it can achieve sufficient accuracy at an economical cost. However, its accuracy is significantly degraded in urban areas, where signal propagations can easily be perturbed by the reflections from environmental objects like buildings, introducing multipath effects and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) receptions. With extensive research, NLOS errors have been effectively mitigated or used as features to aid positioning. Due to the complex interaction between direct and reflected signals, the multipath effects can only be mitigated rather than being used as features for positioning. However, for dense urban areas with a limited satellite number, the available measurements and NLOS features are insufficient to perform accurate positioning. Even worse, the poor measurement geometry may amplify the degradation from multipath errors, making it the last bottleneck for accurate urban positioning. It is vital to explore features from the multipath effect to aid positioning in dense urban areas. Meanwhile, multipath effects have been widely used for geometry monitoring in remote sensing via GNSS interferometry reflectometry (GNSS-IR), which has the potential to provide positioning constraints in urban areas. Thus, this project is proposed with four objectives to investigate the feasibility and practicability of using GNSS-IR to obtain location-dependent features from multipath effect, and to develop a corresponding positioning algorithm for accurate positioning in dense urban areas. First, the feasibility of applying GNSS-IR on multipath signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) measurements in urban areas to estimate building facade distance will be investigated, in terms of signal propagation and processing principles. Second, the GNSS-IR will be extended for low Earth orbit satellite signals, by developing a software-defined receiver (SDR) will be developed to evaluate the performances and limitations of different low Earth orbit constellations. Third, the GNSS-IR will be extended for dynamic receivers, where positioning constraints will be derived based on the movement pattern and dynamic criteria. Finally, the location dependency of the multipath constraints from GNSS-IR will be analysed in terms of large-scale and small-scale, which are used to develop a sophisticated 3D mapping aided GNSS positioning algorithm complementarily integrating NLOS features. Upon the completion of these four objectives, the theoretical feasibility of applying GNSS-IR in urban areas, for instant solutions, and for dynamic receivers will be comprehensively studied, which facilitates the development of a practical positioning algorithm that makes use of the multipath effect to improve positioning accuracy in dense urban areas. 準確的定位資訊對各種基於位置的應用至關重要，而這通常透過全球導航衛星系統（GNSS）獲得，因為它可以以經濟的成本達到足夠的精度。然而，其精度在城市環境中會顯著下降，因為信號傳播容易被建築物等環境物體的反射干擾，引入多路徑效應和非視距接收。經過廣泛的研究，非視距接收誤差已被有效減輕或作爲特徵用以輔助定位。由於直射信號與反射信號之間複雜的相互作用，多路徑效應目前只能被減輕，而不能用作定位特徵。然而，對於衛星數量有限的深度城市環境，可用的觀測量與非視距接收特徵不足以實現精確定位。更嚴重的是，劣化的觀測量幾何分佈可能放大多路徑誤差帶來的影響，這也是城市環境準確定位的最後瓶頸。因此，探索在深度城市環境的多路徑效應特徵以輔助定位非常重要。與此同時，多路徑效應已被廣泛地透過GNSS干涉反射測量技術（GNSS-IR）在遙感中用於幾何參數監測，有潛力在城市環境轉化爲定位約束。因此，本項目提出四個目標，以研究使用GNSS-IR從多路徑效應獲取位置相關特徵的可行性與實用性，並為深度城市環境開發相應的精準定位算法。 第一步，將從信號傳播和處理原理的角度，研究在城市環境對多路徑信號的信噪比觀測量應用GNSS-IR估算建築外牆距離的可行性。第二步，將開發一個軟件定義接收器（SDR）把GNSS-IR擴展應用到近地軌道衛星信號，並評估不同近地軌道星座的性能與限制。第三步，將GNSS-IR擴展到動態接收器，基於運動模式和動態指標推導定位約束。最後，將從廣範區域和局部區域的角度分析GNSS-IR多路徑約束的位置相關性，並用於開發一個完善的三維地圖輔助GNSS定位算法，與非視距接收特徵進行互補融合。通過完成這四個目標，將全面研究在城市環境應用GNSS-IR於動態接收器並及時獲取位置約束的理論可行性，從而促進基於多路徑效應改善深度城市環境定位精度的實用定位算法開發。

15236225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15236225.value: 劇烈塑性變形結合熱衝擊處理高熵奈米金屬玻璃實現優異軟磁與機械性質

15236225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15236225.value: Although various types of metallic glasses have surfaced as commercial products, particularly for use as soft magnetic materials with ultra-low coercivity and magnetization loss, large permeability and ultra-high mechanical strength, their intrinsic characteristics of size limitation and brittleness have prevented them from widespread applications. The past decade has witnessed the emergence of metallic nano-glasses (MNGs) that are promising in solving the longstanding issues of size limitation and brittleness of conventional metallic glasses, exhibiting enhanced ferromagnetic properties and tensile ductility. However, there still exist the tradeoff between their mechanical strength and ductility, and that between their soft-magnetic and mechanical properties in MNGs. To date, MNGs with a coexistence of ultrasoft magnetic properties, high mechanical strength and decent tensile ductility are still missing, which are in great demand in industries. This research project aims to investigate the soft magnetic and mechanical properties of (Fe, Co, Ni)-(Si, B, C, P) high entropy metallic nano-glasses (HE-MNGs) where transition-metal elements have nearly equiatomic ratios. For the first time, the soft magnetic property dependence on the sizes of glassy grains in HE-MNGs and its underlying mechanisms are quantitatively determined, making it possible for engineering HE-MNGs with superior soft-magnetic and mechanical properties. The HE-MNGs are processed via a mechanochemical route combining severe plastic deformation and thermal shock, which involves the modulations on the phase structures of their generic glass-glass interfaces and shear-banding regions as induced by severe plastic deformation. The effects of mechanochemical processing route on HE-MNGs are simulated by deep potential-molecular dynamics with machine learning-based potential energy surface, precisely determining the phase structures in the interfacial regions where elemental segregation occurs. Furthermore, the atomistic modeling on soft magnetic and mechanical properties of HE-MNGs are compared with experimental results. This research project validates the robust, cost-effective and high-throughput mechanochemical processing route for HE-MNGs with superior soft-magnetic and mechanical properties. More importantly, the fundamental scientific issues of structural and chemical heterogeneity in the interfacial regions between different glass phases are resolved, facilitating the design of HE-MNGs where the desired phases with superior soft magnetic properties could be formed and are thermodynamically stable in the interfacial regions. Consequently, the HE-MNGs with large dimensions and a coexistence of superior soft-magnetic and mechanical properties can be developed, which are auspicious substitutes for soft magnetic materials currently used in transformer magnetic cores, power conversion electronics, highly sensitive magnetometers and medical imaging devices. 儘管各種類型的金屬玻璃已作為商業產品出現，特別是用作具有超低矯頑力和磁化損耗、高磁導率和超高機械強度的軟磁材料，但其固有的尺寸限制和脆性特性阻礙了其廣泛應用。過去十年，金屬奈米玻璃（MNG）的出現有望解決傳統金屬玻璃長期以來的尺寸限制和脆性問題，並表現出增強的鐵磁性和拉伸延展性。然而，在金屬奈米玻璃（MNG）中，其機械強度與延展性之間，以及軟磁性能與機械性能之間仍存在著權衡。迄今為止，仍缺乏兼具超軟磁性、高機械強度和良好拉伸延展性的MNG，而這些性能在工業領域有著巨大的需求。本研究計畫旨在探討過渡金屬元素原子比接近等原子比的(Fe, Co, Ni)-(Si, B, C, P)高熵金屬奈米玻璃（HE-MNG）的軟磁性和機械性質。HE-MNG 採用機械化學方法加工而成，該方法結合了劇烈塑性變形和熱衝擊，從而改變了其固有的玻璃-玻璃界面和剪切帶區域的相結構，這是由劇烈塑性變形引起的。利用基於機器學習的勢能面深度分子動力學模擬了機械化學加工方法對 HE-MNG 的影響，從而精確地確定了發生元素偏析的界面區域的相結構。因此，可以開發出具有大尺寸和優良軟磁性能和機械性能共存的HE-MNG，它們是目前用於變壓器磁芯、功率轉換電子設備、高靈敏度磁力儀和醫學成像設備中的軟磁材料的良好替代品。

15237125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15237125.value: 香港街区低温氢气燃爆预测模型研究

15237125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15237125.value: Prof Chen, Zheng Dr SHI, Jihao Dr Zhang, Haoran

15237125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15237125.value: Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are essential for HK's commitment to achieving carbon neutrality. Hydrogen, therefore, will be present more frequently in populated areas, such as refueling stations, and office/residential buildings etc. The rapid expansion of hydrogen energy applications is likely to result in hydrogen being stored and transported in liquid form, specifically as cryogenic liquid hydrogen (CryoLH2). Its high density renders large-scale storage economically favourable. However, the accidental release of CryoLH2 raises additional safety concerns, as it evaporates with a volume expansion of 1:848, resulting in a large, highly flammable vapor cloud, the ignition of which can lead to severe vapor cloud explosions (VCEs). The cryogenic temperature enhances flame instabilities, inducing the rapid flame acceleration with potential for deflagration to detonation (DDT) as shown by theoretical analysis. The presence of congested buildings leads to even greater magnitudes of overpressure, catastrophic for both structures and people around. There is limited understanding about CryoLH2 VCEs and their characteristics in the presence of congested buildings in support of public safety guidelines in HK. Obtaining such an insight experimentally would be prohibitively costly. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models, which can be validated experimentally, is a viable approach. However, developing predictive tool is challenging since the traditional physics-based closure approaches often fail to capture the effects of intrinsic flame associated with cryogenic conditions. This project aims to develop and validate a predictive tool, ML_VCEFoam, for CryoLH2 VCEs in HK urban environments. The development will follow a novel strategy employing machine learnings (ML) to enhance the sub-grid turbulent combustion closure model. The Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) approach will be applied to advance the understanding of flame dynamics in CryoLH2 VCE at lab scale. A reliable DNS database capturing the effects of cryogenic temperatures will be constructed to support the ML-based sub-grid closure model development. This ML-based closure model will be integrated with the in-house OpenFOAM solvers to form the predictive tool ML_VCEFoam. Validation of ML_VCEFoam will be conducted by using public tests and previous explosions that happened in HK. Different VCE scenarios from CryoLH2 releases in a variety of representative urban blocks considering local meteorological data will be simulated. The evolution of overpressure in realistic HK environments will be characterized and the critical conditions for DDT in CryoLH2 VCE will be determined. Recommendations for safety distance and prevention measurements around LH2 installations will be formulated to inform Regulations, Codes and Standards for HK. 构建实验室规模的DNS模拟，以表征低温对氢气蒸气云爆炸（CryoLH2 VCE）的影响。主要的子任务或挑战包括：[1] 将现有的基于DNS的求解器扩展到广泛的低温范围；[2] 在毫米级的物理域中进行DNS模拟，以表征自加速机制及低温的影响；[3] 构建可靠的数据集，包括用于机器学习（ML）基于子网闭合模型的训练和测试的两个数据集组。 开发和验证ML_VCEfoam，通过将基于机器学习的子网湍流燃烧闭合模型与CryoLH2 VCE模拟相结合，应用于香港环境。主要的子任务或挑战包括：[1] 训练和测试基于机器学习的子网湍流燃烧闭合模型；[2] 将基于机器学习的子网闭合模型整合到内部的OpenFOAM求解器中，以形成ML_VCEfoam；[3] 通过使用公开的实验测量数据和香港发生的先前爆炸事件对ML_VCEfoam进行验证。 在香港环境中表征超压演变，并确定CryoLH2 VCE中从慢燃（deflagration）到爆轰（detonation，DDT）的临界条件。主要的子任务包括：[1] 参考香港GIS数据选择一系列具有代表性的城市街区；[2] 使用ML_VCEfoam对代表性城市街区进行VCE模拟；[3] 通过表征超压演变并确定在拥挤建筑中CryoLH2 VCE的DDT临界条件，评估不同城市街区的安全距离。 为香港的LH2设施制定安全距离和预防措施的建议，以便为相关法规、规范和标准提供参考。主要的子任务包括：[1] 提供在香港不同类型城市街区周围LH2设施的预测安全距离建议；[2] 提供预防措施建议，以防止在拥挤建筑中CryoLH2 VCE事故的升级；[3] 与香港消防处进行沟通，该部门负责制定相关的规范和标准，以验证和应用这些建议；[4] 讨论研究结果的不确定性，并提供与现有标准的比较。

15237225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15237225.value: 利用超彈性形狀記憶合金屈曲約束構件實現自復位預製裝配式混凝土橋柱

15237225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15237225.value: Prof Alam, M. Shahria Dr CHEN, Zhipeng

15237225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15237225.value: Devastating earthquakes inflict significant damage on infrastructure worldwide, highlighting the urgent need to enhance the seismic resilience of critical structures (like bridges). Conventional seismic-resistant bridge design relies upon structural plastic deformation to dissipate energy and prevent structural collapse during earthquakes. However, those traditional design approaches face new challenges when the goals shift towards more resilient structures after earthquakes. Particularly, minimizing permanent structural deformation and damage becomes a key objective of resilience-based design. Precast segmental concrete piers (PSCPs) are at the forefront of accelerated bridge construction, enabling the rapid assembly of prefabricated segments on-site. Unbonded post-tensioned (PT) components have gained prominence in emerging PSCPs due to their effectiveness in connecting separate segments, mitigating damage, and reducing residual deformations. When supplemented with additional energy-dissipation devices, PT-based self-centering (SC) PSCPs demonstrate favorable seismic resilience. However, this technology often necessitates the use of extremely long PT tendons and complex anchorages, introducing additional design and construction challenges. This project aims to develop an innovative type of SC-PSCPs that eliminates the need for PT components by utilizing novel superelastic shape memory alloy (SMA) buckling-restrained elements (BREs). The large-dimensional SMA-BREs, recently proposed by the applicants, can activate superelasticity under both tension and compression, providing sufficient strength to meet full-scale structural demands. Consequently, the novel SMA-SC-PSCP will exhibit several salient features: (1) Minimizing permanent deformation through controlled rocking behavior; (2) Mitigating damage to concrete piers by concentrating inelastic damage into replaceable fuse elements; (3) Utilizing SMA-BREs as core components capable of withstanding fatigue and corrosion; and (4) Simplifying design and construction compared to conventional SC systems by eliminating the need for long PT tendons and complex anchorages. The integration of these features will reduce repair costs and downtime following earthquakes. To the best of our knowledge, the novel SMA-SC-PSCP systems have not yet been explored by other researchers. The applicants’ pilot study has demonstrated the feasibility and potential advantages of using large-dimensional SMA-BREs as essential SC elements. However, numerous questions regarding the seismic performance of SMA-SC-PSCPs remain unanswered. This project seeks to address these knowledge gaps through synergetic analytical and experimental research. It will systematically investigate the design, modeling, testing, and performance evaluation of multiple SMA-SC-PSCPs. The objective is to develop a high-performance seismic-resistant system suitable for critical bridges, where rapid construction, continuous operation, and swift post-earthquake recovery are crucial. The research outcomes will provide comprehensive insights into the application of these innovative SMA-SC-PSCPs in multi-span bridges. 地震常常對基礎設施造成嚴重破壞，凸顯了提升關鍵基礎設施（如橋樑）抗震韌性的緊迫需求。傳統的橋樑抗震設計理念過度依賴於結構塑性變形進行耗能，當我們將設計目標從預防倒塌逐漸轉向抗震韌性時，這些傳統設計理念和結構體系正面臨許多新的挑戰。作為一種新興的結構體系，預製裝配式混泥土橋柱（PSCP）不僅能實現現場的安裝施工，而且能通過後張預應力構件有效實現自復位和損傷控制能力，從而展現出良好的抗震韌性。然而，該項技術需要使用極長的預應力鋼絞線和複雜錨具，也帶來了額外的設計和施工困難。本項目旨在通過利用超彈性記憶合金屈曲約束構件（SMA-BRE），開發一種新型的具有自復位功能的預製裝配式混凝土橋柱（SC-PSCP）。通過利用SMA-BRE的多個顯著優點，所提出的SC-PSCP不僅可以簡化施工，而且有助於降低震後修復成本和停運時間，顯著提升抗震韌性。基於申請人的前期研究，本項目將結合分析與試驗，針對SMA-SC-PSCP的設計、模擬、試驗與性能評估進行系統性的研究，驗證該新型結構體系的抗震韌性和實用性。

15238025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15238025.value: 面向高容量短距光互連的基於光纖集成非交錯超表面的緊湊型光纖接收機

15238025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238025.value: The rapid emergence of new applications such as artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and the metaverse has significantly increased Internet traffic. This surge has exerted tremendous pressure on the expansion of optical fiber communication systems. According to Cisco's network white paper, global IP traffic is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 30% from 2018 to 2023. It is estimated that by 2024, global IP traffic will reach 720.7 exabytes (1 EB = 10^9 GB) per month. For global IP traffic, the data flowing in and out of data centers (DCs) and access networks constitutes a substantial portion approximate to 67%. The continuously growing and diversified traffic is putting tremendous pressure on cost-sensitive short-reach transmission networks represented by data center networks (DCNs). Next-generation intra- and inter-data center interconnects will require interface rates of 800G (and potentially 1.6 Tb/s) for Ethernet optical networks beyond 2023. However, due to constraints such as dispersion-induced power fading and link budget, intensity-modulation direct-detection (IM-DD) systems struggle to meet the upcoming high-capacity requirements. Superior to IM-DD systems, self-homodyne coherent detection (SHCD) has been proposed to balance transceiver capacity and cost. The main concept of the SHCD system is that the modulated signal and the remote local oscillator (LO) originate from the same laser. In SHCD systems, Stokes-vector receivers (SVRs) are among the most promising candidates. By transmitting signal and remote on orthogonal polarziations, SVR can eliminate the impact of phase noise and frequency offset, permitting a remarkable tolerance to laser linewidth. In this project, we propose an ultra-compact SVR based on a non-interleaved metasurface. Metasurface are ultra-thin artificial structures that can manipulate various light properties. We design a metasurface based on novel chiral units, capable of detecting complete polarization information using a single metasurface, which enhances the power budget of the receiver. The proposed SVR is designed to directly fabricate on the fiber tip, enhancing its compatibility with existing telecommunications infrastructure. Additionally, it can be extended to achieve high-capacity parallel optical communication applications by utilizing multi-mode fibers or multi-mode fibers. This development is essential for supporting the rising global IP traffic and the expansion of data within DCNs. As a result, it can contribute to the improvement of 5G networks, digital finance, Smart Cities, AI, and other burgeoning sectors in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the project holds promise for fostering cross-disciplinary research in metasurface, optical communication, and the development of photonic integrated devices. 人工智能（AI）、雲計算及元宇宙等新興應用的迅速湧現導致互聯網流量激增，對光纖通信系統的擴容構成巨大壓力。 根據思科網路白皮書預測，2018至2023年全球IP流量將以30%的年復合增長率（CAGR）持續攀升，預計至2024年將達到每月720.7艾位字節（1 EB = 10^9 GB）。 數據中心（DC）與接入網間的數據流約佔全球IP流量的67%。 持續增長且多樣化的流量對以數據中心網路（DCN）為代表的成本敏感型短距傳輸網路提出了嚴峻挑戰。 面向2023年後的新一代數據中心內/間互連，乙太網光網路將需要800G（未來可能達1.6 Tb/s）的介面速率。 然而受限於色散引起的功率衰落及鏈路預算等因素，強度調製直接檢測（IM-DD）系統難以滿足即將到來的高容量需求。 作為IM-DD系統的優化方案，自零差相幹檢測（SHCD）技術因其在收發器容量與成本間的平衡優勢被提出。 該系統的核心原理在於：調製信號與遠端本振（LO）源自同一激光源。 在SHCD系統中，斯托克斯向量接收器（SVR）是最具發展前景的技術路線之一。 通過正交偏振態傳輸信號與遠端本振，SVR可消除相位雜訊與頻偏影響，對激光器線寬具有卓越的容忍度。 本專案提出一種基於非交錯超表面的微型化SVR。 超表面作為可操控多維度光場的超薄人工結構，本研究基於新型手性單元設計出單層結構即可獲取完整偏振資訊的超表面，有效提升接收端功率預算。 所提出的SVR可直接集成於光纖端面製備，顯著增強與現有電信基礎設施的相容性，並可通過多模光纖拓展實現大容量並行光通信應用。 該技術對支撐全球IP流量增長及DCN內部數據擴張至關重要，有望推動香港5G網路、數位金融、智慧城市、人工智慧等新興領域發展。 此外，本項目還將促進超表面、光通信與光子集成器件研發的跨學科融合研究。

15238425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15238425.value: 量子突破到電力行業：面向大規模電力系統組合優化問題的安全高效解決方案

15238425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15238425.value: Ms Chen, Binbin Prof Morstyn, Thomas Dr Zhu, Linghua

15238425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238425.value: Combinatorial Optimization in Power Systems (COPS) include unit commitment during steady-state conditions, as well as reconfiguration, restoration, and emergency resource dispatch under extreme weather and natural disasters. Solving large-scale COPS has been a challenge for both academia and industry for decades. Even today, existing optimization algorithms and industrial solvers struggle significantly, resulting in optimal scheduling and restoration plans often relying on power engineers' empirical decisions. This not only leads to substantial economic losses but also undermines system resilience and reliability. The rapid development of quantum computing has made it a revolutionary tool for tackling large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. Leveraging quantum states' superposition and entanglement, quantum computing enables highly efficient exploration of solution spaces and has been widely applied in industries like financial investments and biopharmaceuticals, achieving performance far superior than traditional optimization solvers. However, practical application of quantum computing to power industry remains extremely difficult. Firstly, the scale of COPS far exceeds the computational capabilities of existing quantum computers. Secondly, quantum bits (qubits) are highly sensitive to noise that leads to calculation errors, which is particularly problematic when quantum computing-derived decisions violate power system operational constraints, posing significant safety risks. Moreover, power engineers generally lack expertise in quantum computing, making it difficult for them to assess the impact of quantum computational errors on power system operational safety, or improve quantum algorithms to mitigate these safety risks. This project will be the first to explore, from the perspective of power engineering applications, how quantum computing can be practically applied to large-scale power systems that require stringent operational safety and reliability, given the current computational limitations and potential errors of quantum hardware. Upon completing this project, we will be able to answer the following key questions: 1) How to use minimal quantum computing resources to solve the largest possible COPS problems? 2) How to estimate the probability of power system operation constraint violations due to quantum-algorithm-induced errors? 3) How to optimize quantum circuit and algorithm design to maximize advantages of quantum computing, while minimizing risks to power system operation security? We have formed an inter-disciplinary team including power system researchers, engineers, and quantum computing experts. Our project will not only facilitate efficient operation of global power system with easy-accessible quantum resources, but also provide valuable datasets and technical pathways for quantum computing researchers, promoting the development of quantum computers and their applications in other safety-sensitive industries. 電力系統中的組合優化問題（Combinatorial Optimization in Power Systems，COPS）涵蓋穩態條件下的機組組合決策，以及極端天氣和自然災害下的電網重構、系統恢復與應急資源調度。數十年來，大規模 COPS 一直是學術界和工業界的難題。即使在今天，現有優化算法和工業求解器在應對大規模 COPS 時仍面臨巨大挑戰，實際運行中最優調度與恢復方案往往依賴電力工程師的經驗判斷。這不僅造成顯著的經濟損失，也削弱了系統的韌性與可靠性。 量子計算的快速發展為解決大規模組合優化問題提供了革命性的新工具。借助量子態的疊加與糾纏特性，量子計算能夠高效探索龐大的解空間，並已在金融投資、生物製藥等領域展現出遠超傳統優化求解器的性能。然而，將量子計算實際應用于電力行業依然非常困難：首先，COPS 的規模遠超當前量子計算機的算力極限；其次，量子比特（qubit）對雜訊高度敏感，易產生計算誤差，而這些誤差若導致量子計算生成的方案違反電力系統運行約束，將帶來嚴重的安全風險。此外，大多數電力工程師缺乏量子計算背景，難以評估量子計算誤差對系統運行安全的影響，更難以改進量子算法以降低此類風險。 本項目將首次從電力工程應用的角度，系統探索在現有量子計算機算力有限、且存在潛在計算誤差的條件下，如何將量子計算實際應用于對運行安全與可靠性要求極高的大規模電力系統。項目完成後，我們將回答以下關鍵問題：1）如何在量子計算資源最小化的條件下，求解盡可能大規模的 COPS 問題？2）如何評估量子算法計算誤差導致電力系統運行約束被違反的概率？3）如何優化量子電路與算法設計，以最大化量子計算優勢，同時將運行安全風險降至最低？ 我們已組建由電力系統研究人員、工程師和量子計算專家組成的跨學科團隊。項目成果不僅將推動全球電力系統利用可及性高的量子計算資源實現高效運行，還將為量子計算研究者提供寶貴的資料集與技術路徑，促進量子計算機及其在其他安全敏感行業的應用發展。

15238925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15238925.value: 數據與物理模型雙驅動的行人時空軌跡不確定性建模方法

15238925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15238925.value: Prof CHEN, Ruizhi Prof Shi, Wen-zhong

15238925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238925.value: With the continuous development of urban navigation and GeoAI technologies, the field of uncertainty modeling based on spatial-temporal human trajectory data has entered a new stage, particularly with the application of crowd-sourced geospatial data and merging AI models. This has turned data-driven methods for estimating the uncertainty of spatial-temporal data into a hotpot. However, methods involving deep learning and data-driven models present issues such as poor generalization and robustness. Although physical uncertainty models have broader applicability, they suffer from problems like inadequate precision and the inability to account for error propagation characteristics from different sensing and positioning sources. This project focuses on the domain of movement uncertainty estimation in human mobility, developing the physical and data dual-driven uncertainty modeling method for human spatial-temporal trajectories, thus resolving the existing theoretical difficulties in this field. The project proposes a three-stage research strategy to address existing problems. Initially, we extract common features of sampling and measurement errors and use the concept of human motion-assisted error ellipse to construct the physical uncertainty model for discontinuous spatial-temporal human trajectory, to accommodate the common error propagation characteristics of different sensing and positioning sources, while preserving detailed parameter definitions for unique error sources. Subsequently, to address the time-varying sampling and measurement errors with location sources not solved by the physical uncertainty model, we use a multi-task multi-modal data-driven model to provide a comprehensive representation of unique features of different sensing and positioning sources and establish a precise mapping relationship between uncertainty parameters and features of specific sensing and positioning sources. Finally, we establish a physical and data dual-driven structure for uncertainty modeling of spatial-temporal human trajectory, covering more complex indoor and outdoor sensing and positioning sources and corresponding time-varying sampling and measurement errors, using the data-driven approach to drive parameters of the physical model, thereby accommodating the comprehensive impact and interrelationships of various spatial-temporal trajectories contained heterogeneous sources. Through this three-stage research, we will provide substantial support to theoretical research in the field of uncertainty modeling for spatial-temporal human trajectory data. Simultaneously, we will develop a practical software platform for uncertainty modeling of spatial-temporal human trajectories, thus enhancing the precision and generalization ability of error estimation in civilian applications, and can also benefit the government, enterprise, and the public. 隨著城市導航與地理人工智能（GeoAI）技術的持續發展，基於行人時空軌跡不確定性建模研究已進入新階段，特別是在公眾衆包時空軌跡挖掘與新型人工智能模型的推動下。這促使以數據驅動為核心的時空軌跡不確定性估算方法成為地理資訊科學領域的研究熱點。然而，現有的深度學習與數據驅動模型在實際應用過程中普遍面臨泛化能力不足與魯棒性較差等挑戰。相較之下，物理機制驅動的不確定性模型具備更廣泛的適用性，但是在精度以及對多源感測與定位誤差傳播特性建模方面仍存在不足。本項目聚焦於人類移動軌跡的時空不確定性估算，旨在構建融合物理機制與數據驅動的時空軌跡不確定性建模方法，從而突破現有理論瓶頸。項目設計了三個階段的研究策略以系統性解決現有研究問題。第一階段，針對多源時空軌跡的采樣與測量誤差，提取其共有特徵，並引入運動特徵輔助下的誤差橢圓構建理論，建立適用於非連續時空軌跡的不確定性物理模型，既能統一描述多種感測與定位源的誤差傳播規律，又保留對特定誤差來源的細緻參數化建模。第二階段，針對物理模型難以處理的定位源時變采樣與測量誤差，構建多任務多模態數據驅動下的AI模型，全面表徵不同感測與定位源的異質特徵，並建立不確定性參數與特定感測來源特徵之間的精確映射關係。第三階段，融合物理機制與數據驅動模型的優勢，構建面向複雜室內外多源感測與定位場景的時空軌跡不確定性雙驅動模型框架，通過數據驅動算法來優化物理模型參數，實現對異質時空軌跡中的多源誤差傳播效應與相互作用的統一建模。通過上述三階段的研究，本項目將為行人時空軌跡不確定性建模理論體系提供堅實支撐。同時，將開發一套面向行人時空軌跡不確定性建模的專業軟體平台，顯著提升地理資訊應用中軌跡誤差估算精度與泛化能力，並為政府、企業及公眾帶來廣泛效益。

15239225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239225.value: 開發一種新型的往復走絲超疏水微線電極電化學放電加工非導電材料技術

15239225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15239225.value: Prof Liu, Jiangwen Dr Wang, Yukui

15239225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239225.value: With the rapid development of technology, many new products incorporate microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) components that are hard, brittle and non-conductive. Manufacturing of these MEMS components, especially machining narrow groove features with high aspect ratios through microfabrication processes presents significant challenges. The primary micro-cutting methods currently employed include laser processing, mechanical processing and micro wire electrochemical discharge machining (WECDM). However, laser machining can create a heat-affected zone, leading to thermal deformation of the material and impacting the dimensional accuracy of the final product. While mechanical processing can achieve high-quality surface roughness, it is slow for narrow grooves with high aspect ratios and is susceptible to tool wear and deformation. In contrast, WECDM shows great promise for micromachining non-conductive hard and brittle materials. However, achieving a stable thin gas film through the conventional electrolytic process in the WECDM process remains challenging, as it significantly affects the accuracy, quality and efficiency of the process, limiting its industrial applications. In the proposed work, we aim to address the above issue by developing a new regenerative self-forming stable gas film in WECDM. This will be accomplished by (1) forming a superhydrophobic surface coating on the reciprocating travelling wire electrode, (2) supplying hydrogen bubbles through the electrolytic process to cover any damaged areas of the gas film during operation, and (3) incorporating an additional in-process coating module to dynamically repair and construct the superhydrophobic surface coating on the wire electrode through its reciprocating motion. The preliminary results from our project team are very promising, demonstrating the superhydrophobic surface can spontaneously self-form a much thinner and more table gas film during WECDM, effectively overcoming the challenges of traditional WECDM. Based on these preliminary results and the team's research experience, we aim to develop a highly efficient, accurate, and quality WECDM process for micro cutting of non-conductive materials with high aspect ratios. We will also study the mechanisms involved in dynamically constructing superhydrophobic surfaces for maintaining the continuity and stability of the gas film during processing, and the discharge behavior, tool electrode wear and material removal mechanisms during processing. This research is expected to lead to a breakthrough technology that addresses the bottleneck of high aspect ratio narrow groove fabrication and expands applications in the microfabrication of hard and brittle non-conductive materials. 隨着科技的快速發展，許多新產品採用微機電系統(MEMS)組件，這些組件具有硬度高、脆性強且不導電的特性。加工這些MEMS組件，尤其是通過微加工工藝加工高長寬比的窄槽結構，面臨着嚴重挑戰。目前主要採用的微加工方法包括激光加工、機械加工和微線電極電化學放電加工（WECDM）等。然而，激光加工會產生熱影響區，導致材料熱變形並影響最終產品的尺寸精度。機械加工雖能實現高表面質量，但對高長寬比的窄槽加工效率低，且易受刀具損耗和變形影響。相比之下，WECDM在微加工非導電硬質脆性材料方面展現出巨大潛力。然而，通過傳統電解過程在WECDM工藝中構建穩定且薄的氣層仍面臨挑戰，因而顯著影響傳統WECDM的加工精度、質量和效率，限制了其實際工業應用。 在本項目中，我們通過在WECDM中開發一種全新的自發形成穩定氣層的方法來解決上述問題。其主要通過以下關鍵步驟實現：（1）在往復移動的線電極上製備超疏水錶面塗層；（2）通過電解過程產生氫氣氣泡，以覆蓋氣層在加工過程中受損的區域；（3）集成一個額外的在線塗層製備模塊並通過線電極的往復運動，實現動態修復超疏水塗層。我們團隊的初步研究結果極具前景，並研究發現超疏水線電極表面可在WECDM過程中自發形成薄且穩定的氣層，克服了傳統WECDM中所面臨的挑戰。基於這些初步結果和團隊研究基礎，我們旨在開發一種高效、高精度且高質量的WECDM新工藝，用於高長寬比非導電材料的微加工。此外，我們還將研究動態構建超疏水錶面以維持加工過程中氣層連續性和穩定性的機制，以及加工過程中的放電行爲、線電極損耗機理和材料去除機制等。本項目的開展有望突破非導電材料高長寬比窄槽製造的瓶頸，並拓展在硬脆性非導電材料微加工中的應用。

15239525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239525.value: 利用探地雷達和瞬時頻率分析測繪大比例水管洩漏

15239525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239525.value: This proposal investigates a major city underground problem by large-scale and nondestructive mapping of watermains leakage by multi-channel ground penetrating radar (MCGPR) towed by vehicle. Not knowing the locations of these leakages has been a problem troubling major city causing accidents and recording leakage rate as high as 40% in some cities. In Hong Kong, this rate is about 14.4%, or daily about 200 Olympic swimming pools of water. For speedy repair and rehabilitation, quick, nondestructive, contact-less and accurate mapping approaches are crucial to the identification of leakage points but the required scientific and practical methods are far from being well-established. MCGPR is proposed because of (1) the established mechanism that free water in soil absorb high-frequency electromagnetic wave; (2) its efficient 3D image slicing of the underground conditions; (3) highway-speed scanning, and (4) cm-scale fine resolution. The first systematic workflow for intensity-based GPR slicing of underground and watermains leakage have been established by the PI’s research team in small scale and single-channel GPR (Luo et al., 2019; 2023; Zhou et al., 2023). But when this approach is upscaled to MCGPR and large-scale mapping, investigations are required in a systematic way to address various failure modes of watermains and overlaid materials, together with considerations of multiple GPR channels and their E-field polarizations. So, a GPR database of common leakage-failure patterns/modes of watermains will be established with three approaches. The first is numerical simulation of 48 combinations of failure modes, 16 GPR experiments in a 25,000 sq.ft full-scale test site (Q-Leak), and extraction of GPR spectral instantaneous frequency (IF) at the controlled zones of leakage/no-leakage. The second approach is to upscale the works to road survey by MCGPR, in which a hybrid geo-referencing strategy for positioning and navigating the GPR antenna array will also be established. Third, sensitivity and specificity of leakage mapping will be evaluated in two Sites of Interests (SoIs) with suspected leakage. The deliverables of these project will form a critical basis for mapping invisible leakage for avoiding accidence, saving water resources and better municipal management of watermains. It also leads to the development of tech-based strategy of regular health track of city’s underground utilities. 本提案旨在調查一個主要城市的地下問題，利用車輛牽引的多通道探地雷達 (MCGPR) 對水管外洩進行大規模無損測繪。無法確定這些洩漏的位置一直是困擾主要城市的一大難題，導致事故頻繁，部分城市的洩漏率高達 40%。在香港，這一比例約為 14.4%，相當於每天約 200 個奧運游泳池的水量。為了快速修復和恢復，快速、無損、非接觸且準確的測繪方法對於識別洩漏點至關重要，但所需的科學性和實用性方法尚未完善。 提出利用 MCGPR 的原因是：(1) 土壤中水分吸收高頻電磁波的機制；(2) 能夠有效率地對地下狀況進行 3D 影像切片；(3) 可在高速公路上掃描；(4) 具有公分級的高解析度。研究小組負責人的研究團隊已在小尺度單通道 GPR 中建立了首個基於強度的地下水管和水管洩漏 GPR 切片系統工作流程 。但是，當將此方法擴展到 MCGPR 和大尺度測繪時，需要有系統地進行調查，以解決水管材料的各種失效模式，同時還需要考慮多個 GPR 通道及其電場極化對測繪的影響。 因此，我們將透過三種方法建立一個包含常見水管洩漏故障模式的 GPR 資料庫。第一種方法是對 48 種故障模式組合進行數值模擬，在 25,000 平方英尺的全尺寸測試場（Q-Leak）進行 16 次 GPR 實驗，並在洩漏/無洩漏的受控區域提取 GPR 頻譜瞬時頻率 (IF)。第二種方法是透過 MCGPR 將工程升級到道路勘測，其中還將建立一種用於定位和導航 GPR 天線陣列的混合空間對位的策略。第三種方法是在兩個疑似洩漏點 (SoI) 中評估洩漏測繪的敏感度和特異性。這些計畫的成果將為繪製隱藏洩漏圖奠定重要基礎，以避免事故發生、節省水資源和改善市政水管管理。這也將促進制定基於MCGPR的定期城市地下設施健康追蹤策略。

15239625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239625.value: 提高智慧倉庫的物品揀選效率-實現工作站間箱體移動的新設計

15239625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239625.value: Robotic mobile fulfillment systems (RMFS) are widely used by e-tailers and e-commerce centers (e.g., Amazon) in their intelligent warehouses to handle the huge variety of small products and massive orders with small item quantities coming from online sales nowadays. An order-picking process starts with AMRs moving the required pods from the storage zone to workstations for item-picking. As orders usually require multiple-items, multiple-pods are usually required to consolidate an order in the same workstation which is commonly configured with bins (one-bin for one-order) and conveyors along the two sides. The existing shortcomings of RMFS is the incapability of moving bins between workstations. Theoretically, orders containing the same item types can be allocated to the same workstation to increase the number of item-pickings from pods. However, these types of “same orders” are in fact rare. Thus, in reality, lots of orders without common item types will end up staying in the same workstation (until completion) as bins cannot move between workstations in the current RMFS design. This results in low item-picking efficiency (system efficiency), and frequent pod movements (and hence high carbon emissions). To overcome this shortcoming, we propose a novel optimal design, called inter-workstation bin movement RMFS (IWBM-RMFS), to enable bin movement between workstations by using AMRs. Moreover, we will develop a decision-support tool to support the decision-making for this new design regarding the assignment of orders-to-workstations and the scheduling of pods for item-picking, with the aim of minimizing the order completion time and maximizing the item-picking efficiency. As prior RMFS optimization approaches cannot handle the new challenges induced by inter-workstation bin movement (IWBM), a novel customized efficient algorithm will be developed. With the support of a pioneer AMRs developer from China and a leading e-commerce center from Hong Kong, we will conduct numerical experiments by using real and semi-real data to evaluate the proposed decision-support tool and explore the importance of IWBM to RMFS efficiency.
