Go-along interviews allow both researchers and participants engaging in place-informed discussion in the physical socio-spatial environment of interest, providing opportunities for researcher to delve into participants’ routine and experiences. And participatory design model-making is an activity that encourages non-designer participants to give concrete inputs about a topic through tools like models and sticky notes. We plan to apply a maximum variation sampling strategy and recruit approximately 40 participants, comprising 20 stroke survivor–caregiver dyads, with stroke survivors having low-to-slight levels of disability and at least a moderate level of disability. Researchers will conduct go-along interviews with stroke survivor-caregiver dyads in public parks to understand their long-term self-managed rehabilitation experiences. To identify elements of outdoor exercise equipment and exercise space design in parks that could enhance stroke survivors’ and their caregivers’ experiences in parks, the researcher will conduct participatory design model-making focus group interviews with the dyads. Both data collection and analysis will be underpinned by an explorative–descriptive qualitative theoretical approach with the aim to provide pragmatic insights to healthcare and design discipline. This project initiates the critical first step to investigate the phenomenon of how the biggest disability group and their caregivers negotiate with the outdoor exercise facilities in parks for self-managed rehabilitation and what could be done to support them in healthcare and park design in the future. 在香港，中風是導致長期殘疾的主要原因。然而，中風後一年以上，公立醫療系統通常不再提供專業復康服務，迫使中風康復者必須依賴自身及其非正式照顧者進行長期復康訓練。值得注意的是，我們觀察到香港部份中風康復者及其照顧者會利用公園戶外健身設施來自主管理長期復康訓練。 由於公園的戶外健身設施及運動空間最初並非為復康目的而設計，目前各界對其用於中風後自主復康的研究仍屬空白。關於中風康復者及其照顧者如何利用這些戶外設施進行復康訓練與健康維護，以及公園健身設施與運動空間設計中的哪些輔助元素能為他們提供更好支持，這些都是有待探索的領域。 本計劃透過多元質性研究方法彌補此知識缺口。我們將採用「隨行訪談法」與「參與式設計模型製作焦點小組」作為研究方法。隨行訪談能讓研究者和參與者在實際的社會空間環境中進行場景導向的對話，使研究者得以深入理解中風康復者與照顧者的行為與經驗；而參與式設計模型製作則能夠透過模型、便利貼等工具，引導非設計專業參加者對研究主題提出具體反饋的一項研究活動。 我們計劃採用最大變異抽樣策略，招募約40名參與者（20組中風康復者及其照顧者），其中中風康復者需涵蓋輕度至中度殘疾與至少中度以上殘疾的程度。研究者將在公園對這些研究參加者進行隨行訪談，並錄取影像記錄其運動行為。為辨識公園健身設施與空間設計中能提升使用者體驗的關鍵元素，研究者將組織參與式設計模型製作焦點小組訪談。整個資料收集與分析過程將以探索性-描述性質性理論為基礎，旨在為醫療保健與設計領域提供實用見解。 本計畫將邁出關鍵的第一步，探究這個最大殘疾群組及其照顧者如何運用公園戶外設施進行自主復康訓練，以及未來醫療系統與公園設計應如何支緩這個群組。這項開創性研究將為相關領域奠定重要基礎。

15604125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15604125.value: 将服务机器人重新定位为就业创造者而非取代者：探索促进顾客对由行动障碍员工远程操控的服务机器人持积极态度的策略

15604125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15604125.value: Prof Buhalis, Dimitrios Dr Fan, Alei

15604125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604125.value: Despite the availability of various government subsidies—including in Hong Kong—even socially conscious hospitality entrepreneurs find it challenging to create job opportunities for disabled individuals, as service jobs often involve physically demanding tasks such as carrying heavy items and prolonged standing. In response, service robots remotely operated by workers with mobility impairments (hereafter SRs-ROB-WMIs) were developed to enable individuals with severe physical limitations to work remotely. Examples include Dawn Café in Tokyo and Dignity Kitchen in Hong Kong. Given a severe lack of job opportunities, even a moderate increase in employment options could have a meaningful impact on the disabled community. With this in mind, this project does not aim for the unrealistic goal of making SRs-ROB-WMIs the dominant service model but instead seeks to encourage more socially conscious hospitality entrepreneurs to create job opportunities for individuals with disabilities. Despite the noble intentions behind employing SRs-ROB-WMIs, the hospitality industry is, at its core, a business focused on satisfying customers. Thus, ensuring the successful adoption of SRs-ROB-WMIs requires strategies that foster customers’ positive attitudes toward these services. To accomplish this goal, the present study takes the strength-based approach by first (1) identifying the inherent advantages that SRs-ROB-WMIs have over the most common fully automated service robots (Study 1), and then (2) exploring various conditions to maximize these advantages (Studies 2-4). Although each of the four studies is grounded in its own theoretical foundation, the overarching framework that guides all the studies is grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) theory, which emphasizes understanding how stimuli (service robots) evoke psychological responses within individuals, ultimately leading to their final attitudes toward these robots. Study 1 draws on Expectation-Confirmation Theory and Warm-Glow Theory to examine whether psychological factors—such as customers' perceived human touch and societal value—leads to more positive attitudes toward SRs-ROB-WMIs, compared to the most common fully automated service robots. In addition, through Studies 2 to 4, the current project explores various conditions—such as robot-human identity design, degree of individuating information about disabled workers, recruitment distance of disabled workers, and physical task intensity performed by service robots—that can influence customers’ perceived human touch and societal value. This project ultimately aims to position SRs-ROB-WMIs not only as a tool to support the employment of workers with mobility impairments but also as a means to enhance customers’ attitudes toward these services. 尽管包括香港在内的多地政府提供了多种补贴，具有社会责任感的酒店与餐饮业创业者在为残障人士创造就业机会方面仍面临挑战，因为服务类工作通常涉及搬运重物、长时间站立等对体力要求较高的任务。对此，研发了由行动障碍人士远程操控的服务机器人（以下简称 SRs-ROB-WMIs），使严重肢体受限的人士能够远程从事相关工作。例如，东京的 Dawn Café 和香港的 Dignity Kitchen 就是此类案例。由于残障群体的就业机会极为匮乏，即使就业选择的增加幅度有限，也可能带来显著影响。基于此，本项目并不以让 SRs-ROB-WMIs 成为主流服务模式这一不切实际的目标为追求，而是旨在鼓励更多具有社会责任感的酒店与餐饮业创业者为残障人士创造就业机会。 然而，尽管雇用 SRs-ROB-WMIs 的初衷高尚，酒店与餐饮业的核心仍是满足顾客需求的商业行为。因此，确保 SRs-ROB-WMIs 成功被市场采纳，需要制定能够促进顾客对这些服务持积极态度的策略。为达成这一目标，本研究采用优势导向（strength-based）方法，首先（1）识别 SRs-ROB-WMIs 相较于目前最常见的全自动服务机器人所固有的优势（研究 1），其次（2）探索在不同条件下如何最大化这些优势（研究 2-4）。尽管四项研究各自有独立的理论基础，但整体研究框架均以刺激-有机体-反应（SOR）理论为指导，该理论强调理解刺激（服务机器人）如何引发个体的心理反应，并最终影响其对机器人的态度。 研究 1 基于期望-确认理论（Expectation-Confirmation Theory）与温暖光晕理论（Warm-Glow Theory），考察心理因素（如顾客感知到的人情味和社会价值）是否会使他们相比全自动服务机器人，对 SRs-ROB-WMIs 持更积极的态度。此外，通过研究 2 至 4，本项目将探讨多种影响顾客感知人情味和社会价值的条件，包括：机器人与人类的身份设计、关于残障员工的个性化信息披露程度、残障员工的招聘距离，以及服务机器人所执行任务的体力强度。本项目的最终目标是将 SRs-ROB-WMIs 定位为不仅支持行动障碍人士就业的工具，更是提升顾客对这些服务正面态度的有效途径。

15604425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15604425.value: 自閉症與正常发展兒童粵語焦點標記中手勢與語音韻律兩種模態的整合

15604425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15604425.value: Dr Bosker, Hans Dr Chan, Angel Wing-Shan Prof Chen, Zhuoming Dr Ge, Haoyan Prof Li, Bin Prof Sheng, Li Miss Tang, Tempo Po-yi Dr Wayland, Ratree

15604425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604425.value: Abnormal speech prosody and weak quality in manual gesture production have been widely reported in autistic individuals. However, in addition to the deficits found in separate modalities, autistic individuals may have difficulties in integrating gesture and speech prosody. Due to this potential deficit, intervention plans targeting at separate modalities may not be enough. A better understanding of the relationship between gesture and speech prosody may lead to an intervention plan that improves the integration and employs the effects of gesture to boost the use of speech prosody. It is thus high time that we study 1) the temporal relationship between speech prosody and gesture in Cantonese focus marking by typical and autistic populations. It is hypothesized that synchronization is planned between gesture and speech prosody for typical population, but autistic children may show difficulties in the temporal alignment between the two as the Weak Central Coherence theory posits that autistic children focus on uni-sensory information at the expense of multisensory perception; 2) the effects of gesture on the acoustic realization of speech prosody by typical and autistic populations. It is hypothesized that gesture may boost prosodic prominence in focus marking by typical population. However, autistic children may show reduced boosting effects due to difficulties in the integration across modes. Thirty-six autistic children, 36 typical developing children aged from 10 to 12 and 36 adults will complete three experiments eliciting focus marking in speech prosody with and without gesture. Acoustic cues will be extracted using Praat and annotation of gesture that accompanies the focal word in each utterance will be performed in ELAN. Four measurements will be carried out to measure the temporal relationship. Statistical modelling will be further applied to all the extracted data. This project will be among the first to investigate the potential deficits in the integration of the visual and auditory modalities in focus marking especially among autistic children. It enhances our understanding of the temporal relationship between speech prosody and gesture, as well as how gesture may affect the acoustic realization of speech prosody in both typical and autistic populations. Therefore, the project may provide potentially valuable information for the diagnosis of autism and the design of intervention plans. Based on the findings of this study, the intervention plan will be more comprehensive as it addresses the temporal alignment of two modes and gesture may be employed to improve acoustic realization of focus marking in speech. 自閉症患者普遍存在言語韻律異常和手勢使用不當的現象。除了在單一模態中發現的缺陷外，自閉症患者還可能難以整合手勢和語言節奏。由於這種潛在的缺陷，僅針對單一模態的干預計畫可能有所局限。因此、更好地理解手勢和言語韻律之間的關係有助於制定訓練計劃，改善這兩個模態的整合，並有可能利用手勢來促進言語韻律的使用。此計畫我們將研究：1）正常發展兒童和自閉症兒童粵語焦點標記中言語韻律和手勢之間的關係。我們假設正常發展兒童的手勢和言語韻律是同步的，而自閉症兒童的手勢和言語韻律可能難以同步，因為中心連貫薄弱論認為自閉症兒童會關注單感官訊息而忽略多感官的感知； 2) 手勢對言語韻律聲學實現的影響。我們假設手勢可以增強正常發展兒童在焦點標記中的韻律使用。然而，自閉症兒童由於有跨模態整合困難，其增強效果可能減弱。此計畫將招募36名自閉症兒童、36名10至12歲正常發展兒童和36名成年人將完成三項實驗。我們會對所有提取的數據進行統計分析。本計畫將是首批研究自閉症兒童視覺和聽覺模態在焦點標記整合的項目之一。此計畫增強了我們對言語韻律和手勢之間關係的理解，以及手勢如何影響典型人群和自閉症人群中言語韻律的聲學實現。因此，本計畫可能為自閉症的診斷和訓練計劃提供潛在的寶貴資訊。基於本研究的結果而研發的訓練計畫將更加全面，因為它將解決兩種模態的關聯問題，並且可以運用手勢來改善言語中焦點標記的聲學實現。

15604725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15604725.value: 以中國傳統紗羅為靈感：創新自動化柔性可穿戴電子紡織品織造系統

15604725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604725.value: Wearable electronics have gained significant traction in the consumer market, yet they are primarily confined to accessories like smartwatches and fitness trackers. True integration of electronics into clothing remains limited, largely due to challenges in balancing comfort, flexibility, and conductivity. Current techniques for producing conductive yarn circuits often suffer from issues related to scalability and durability, preventing widespread adoption in apparel. In order to overcome these obstacles, this research introduces a novel strategy that draws inspiration from lost traditional Chinese non-fixed leno weaving technology. By incorporating a novel winding loom reed, the study aims to enhance the flexibility and durability of conductive yarn circuits in textiles, addressing the limitations of both modern and traditional weaving techniques. The methodology of this study is threefold: (1) design and modeling of a novel winding reed with coordinated horizontal movement system; (2) development of an automation system of the winding reed; and (3) production of reliable circuits on woven fabrics using conductive yarns with optimal parameters, alongside evaluation and stimulation of the electrical resistance. The winding loom reed enables the creation of non-rigid, flexible warp yarn configurations, significantly reducing mechanical stress on the circuits and allowing for more intricate designs. This novel technique represents a significant breakthrough in the field of textile-based electronics by freeing warp yarns from traditional fixed configurations, resulting in enhanced circuit flexibility and durability. It also addresses the limitations of current weaving technologies, which often produce circuits that are too rigid or prone to mechanical failure over time. The combination of traditional Chinese weaving methods with cutting-edge technology not only advances the field of functional and electronic textiles but also promotes cultural sustainability by reviving and updating ancient weaving practices for modern applications. Ultimately, this study provides a sustainable solution for the future of weaving and wearable electronic textile production, merging cultural heritage with technological innovation. The proposed technique offers a practical and scalable method for producing reliable, flexible, and durable conductive yarn circuits, paving the way for the next generation of truly wearable electronic apparel. 可穿戴電子產品近年來在消費市場上備受矚目，但其應用多侷限於智慧手錶、健身追蹤器等配件，真正能與服裝深度融合的電子產品仍然稀少。這主要歸因於其在舒適性、靈活性與導電性之間難以取得平衡。目前導電紗線電路的製造技術普遍面臨可擴展性與耐用性不足的挑戰，限制了其在服裝領域的廣泛應用。為突破這些瓶頸，本研究提出一項創新策略，靈感源自瀕臨失傳的中國傳統非固定組織紗羅織造技術。透過設計新型盤曲織機筘，本研究旨在提升紡織品中導電紗線電路的靈活性與耐用性，突破現有織造技術的限制。 本研究方法涵蓋三個層面：(1) 設計並建模具備協調水平運動系統的新型盤曲織機筘；(2) 開發盤曲織機筘的自動化系統；(3) 利用優化參數的導電紗線，在機織織物中製作電路，並評估和模擬其電阻性能。新型盤曲織機筘能創造非剛性、柔性的經紗結構，顯著減少電路的機械應力，並實現更複雜的設計。 本技術代表紡織電子領域的重大突破，打破了經紗傳統固定結構的限制，顯著提升電路的靈活性與耐用性。該技術有效克服現有編織技術導致電路剛性過高或隨時間易損壞的問題。藉由融合中國傳統編織工藝與現代技術，不僅推動功能性與電子紡織品的發展，也促進了文化遺產的創新應用與永續發展。最終，本研究為未來編織與穿戴式電子紡織品的生產提供了一種可持續解決方案，將文化傳承與技術創新完美結合。所提出的技術將實現可靠、靈活且耐用的導電紗線電路，為下一代真正可穿戴的電子服裝奠定基礎。

15604825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15604825.value: 生成式人工智能赋能的用户旅程图：促进人本设计的用户研究

15604825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15604825.value: Prof Wei, Huaxin Prof YU, Junnan

15604825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604825.value: Generative AI (GenAI) has greatly advanced in generating textual and visual content for diverse purposes. Leveraging its strength in generative capabilities and context awareness, researchers started to introduce GenAI into human-centered design (HCD). The Journey map (JM) is a user research tool that represents actions users take when experiencing products, thereby informing designs centered on human needs. Given its widespread usage and rigid structure, JM serves as an ideal initial context to explore the role of GenAI in amplifying user research tools. The inherent rigidity of traditional JM often fails to capture dynamic, large-scale user data effectively, limiting insight generation. Although GenAI has proven effective in enhancing design productivity and holds the potential to support JM creation, a significant knowledge gap still remains in understanding the multifaceted impact of GenAI on augmenting user research tools. Additionally, it is imperative to propose effective strategies that maximize GenAI to facilitate user research in HCD. Based on the work done by the PI, this project will deploy a GenAI-empowered tool for creating Journey Map (GeneyMAP), which can automatically distill JM templates, map user data, and explore opportunities, as the probe for the two-phase research. Phase I: We will employ the mixed-methods research design to conduct a within-subject investigation to compare GeneyMAP and the traditional JM tool. We will collect the quantitative questionnaire results and qualitative interview data to assess how the incorporation of GenAI influences the JM process and outputs, as well as how designers perceive the GenAI. Phase II: We will build a GenAI-aided framework that focuses on effective GenAI functions and interaction strategies, initially based on empirical findings from Phase I. Subsequently, we will generalize and extend the framework through a longitudinal field study. Finally, we will apply the extended framework to update GeneyMAP, followed by a comparative evaluation to verify its effectiveness. Our research will contribute to the design field with several outcomes: 1)The empirical insights into the advantages and limitations of incorporating GenAI functions in the JM creation, which advance our understanding of GenAI’s role in HCD. 2) The GenAI-aided design framework provides actionable strategies for designers to effectively collaborate and communicate with GenAI to maximize its functions, inspiring the development of various GenAI-empowered tools that facilitate the HCD. 3) The updated GeneyMAP streamlines the user research process with GenAI, serving both as a future research probe and a reference for further design studies on leveraging GenAI. 生成式人工智能（GenAI）在生成文本和视觉内容等方面取得了巨大进展。凭借其强大的生成能力和上下文感知能力，GenAI正逐渐被引入以人为本的设计（Human-centered Design，人本设计）。用户旅程图（Journey Map，JM）是一种用户研究工具，用于呈现用户在体验产品时的行为，从而为人本设计提供信息。鉴于其广泛的应用和固定的结构，JM是探索GenAI如何增强用户研究工具的理想切入点。然而，传统JM局限于其僵化结构，往往难以有效捕捉动态且大规模的用户数据，从而限制了设计洞察的生成。尽管GenAI已被证明能够提升设计生产力，并具有支持JM创建的潜力，但在理解GenAI对用户研究工具的复杂影响方面，仍存在显著的知识空白。此外，提出有效策略以充分利用GenAI来促进人本设计中的用户研究也势在必行。 基于项目负责人的前期工作，本项目将部署一个由GenAI赋能的用户旅程图创建工具（GeneyMAP），该工具能够自动提炼JM模板、映射用户数据并探索机会，并作为以下两阶段研究的探索媒介。第一阶段：我们将采用混合研究方法，进行被试内对比实验，比较GeneyMAP与传统JM工具。我们将收集定量问卷结果和定性访谈数据，以评估GenAI的引入将如何影响JM的创建过程和结果，了解设计师如何看待GenAI。第二阶段：基于第一阶段的实证研究结论，我们将构建一个GenAI辅助用户研究的框架，重点关注高效的GenAI功能和人机交互策略。随后，我们将通过实地的纵向研究对框架进行凝练和扩展。最终，我们将利用扩展的框架更新GeneyMAP工具，并通过对比评估验证其有效性。 我们的研究将为设计领域带来以下贡献：1.提供实证洞察，阐明在JM创建过程中整合GenAI的优势与局限性，深入理解GenAI在人本设计中的作用。2.创建GenAI辅助设计的框架，为设计师提供可操作的策略以有效地与GenAI协作和沟通，从而充分发挥其功能，并指导各类GenAI赋能工具的开发以促进人本设计。3.更新后的GeneyMAP将通过GenAI简化用户研究过程，既可作为未来研究的探索媒介，也可为进一步利用GenAI的设计研究提供参考。

15604925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15604925.value: 輸入異質性與學習者個體差異在人造量詞學習中的作用

15604925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604925.value: Young children are adept at learning new words, especially nouns, often requiring only a few exposures to acquire new vocabulary. Children also acquire gender markings, a noun classification system, quite rapidly. Numeral classifiers, mandatory for quantification of nouns in many Asian languages, present an intriguing case, as these words are notoriously difficult for typical learners and highly vulnerable in individuals with language learning deficits. Though semantic complexity, input, and cognitive ability are proposed to drive classifier acquisition, there are inherent difficulties in defining semantic complexity and measuring classifier input. Moreover, the impact of cognitive ability on classifier learning has not been directly investigated. These issues have stalled the development of effective teaching methods. To systematically investigate various influential factors, we designed a novel implicit learning paradigm to teach invented classifiers that encode shape features of novel objects. This paradigm allows us to examine how the quantity and quality of input affect learning and generalization of classifiers in comprehension and production modalities. Our pilot work identified a token and type frequency dosage combination that resulted in good learning, and revealed a large comprehension-production asymmetry in children’s but not adults’ learning outcomes. Moreover, there are non-responders (i.e., individuals who showed limited learning despite that the training was effective for others) among both child and adult groups. The current project will move the needle by identifying conditions that can further improve learning. Aim 1 examines the role of four learner variables: age (4-6 years, 7-9 years, 10-12 years), language background (Mandarin and Cantonese, which differ in classifier frequency in the input and children’s acquisition rate), memory capacity, and visuospatial reasoning abilities. Age and language background will serve as proxies for cumulative language experience that may modulate the comprehension-production asymmetry, while memory and reasoning abilities will help differentiate good learners from non-responders. Aim 2 examines if increasing the heterogeneity of input in the visual field during training will enable greater discovery of the referential meaning of the invented classifiers and enhance learning. This study will lay the groundwork for future research on other learning conditions and disordered populations (e.g., developmental language disorder). Moreover, it will generate insights into the nature of learning a complex class of words in natural languages, enrich theories of learning and generalization, and lead to evidence-based, optimized instruction for teaching real classifiers to diverse learners. 兒童擅長學習新詞彙，尤其是名詞，通常只需少量接觸便能掌握新詞。兒童也能快速習得性別標記這類名詞分類系統。量詞（在許多亞洲語言中不可或缺的名詞量化單位）則呈現出特殊案例——這類詞彙不僅令典型學習者倍感困難，更在語言學習障礙者身上表現出高度脆弱性。雖然語義複雜度、輸入量與認知能力被認為是驅動量詞習得的關鍵因素，但界定語義複雜度與測量量詞輸入存在本質困難，且認知能力對量詞學習的影響尚未被直接研究，這些問題阻礙了有效教學法的發展。 為系統性探究各項影響因素，我們設計了嶄新的內隱學習範式，用以教授基於新異物體形狀特徵的人造量詞。此範式能檢視輸入量與質如何影響理解與產出雙模態下的量詞學習與泛化。我們團隊的先導研究發現了一種特定的詞頻與類頻的組合能促成良好學習效果，並揭示了兒童存在顯著的理解-產出不對稱現象，而成人則無不對稱現象。更值得注意的是，儘管訓練對多數人有效，兒童與成人組別中均存在「無反應者」——學習成效有限者。本計畫將突破現狀，探尋能進一步提升學習的條件。 目標一檢驗四項學習者變量：年齡（4-6歲、7-9歲、10-12歲）、語言背景（量詞輸入頻率與兒童習得速度各異的普通話與粵語）、記憶容量及視覺空間推理能力。年齡與語言背景將作為累積語言經驗的代理變量，用以調節理解-產出不對稱現象；記憶與推理能力則有助區分優質學習者與無反應者。目標二探討訓練時增加視覺場輸入的異質性，是否能促進對人造量詞指涉意義的發現並強化學習。 本研究將為未來探究其他學習條件與特殊群體（如發展性語言障礙）奠定基礎，更將深化對自然語言中複雜詞類學習本質的理解，豐富學習與泛化理論，最終為不同學習者提供基於實證的優化量詞教學方案。

15605325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605325.value: 心理意象結合自我調節對柏金遜症患者日常活動的影響

15605325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15605325.value: Ms Chau, Ching Man Rachel Dr Chung, Raymond Chi Keung Dr Li, Ling Dr TANG, Michael Prof Zhang, Jack Jiaqi Ms Zhang, Yue

15605325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605325.value: People with Parkinson’s disease (PwPD) experience motor (e.g., tremors, stiffness) and non-motor symptoms (e.g., fatigue, depression), which cause restrictions in daily activities. Their reliance on slow action is attributed to an impairment in choosing what they pay attention to and ignore (the supervisory attentional system). An increasing number of people have been newly diagnosed with PD worldwide. As an early intervention, rehabilitation is important to complement medical interventions and also when medication no longer works. Conventional rehabilitation using exercise addresses motor symptoms and produces short-term benefits but only focuses on gait and walking. Currently, no rehabilitation strategy addresses the limitations in daily activities among PwPD. Cueing, an updated rehabilitation strategy, can improve walking pace and rigidity but relies on an external cue/device, which is unrealistic in daily life. Cueing also has limited generalisation to daily activities. Mental imagery (imagining oneself performing a task without acting) is a recent rehabilitation strategy used to improve function in PwPD. However, our systematic review suggested that the effectiveness of mental imagery relies on adding extra components to the intervention protocol, including (1) breaking tasks into steps, (2) engaging participants in self-awareness of their problems, and/or (3) drawing attention towards activity performance during imagery. These components may come from another strategy called self-regulation, which is postulated to enhance attention to learning movement strategies. Our prior research in people with stroke has demonstrated the effective use of mental imagery with self-regulation in improving daily activities, attention, and cognitive control required for completing daily activities (the role of the supervisory attentional system). Because supervisory attentional system impairment affects mental flexibility and attention to movements in PwPD, it is reasonable to hypothesise that mental imagery with self-regulation could address PwPD’s reliance on slow actions, which impacts their daily activities. To test this hypothesis, we developed a 6-week mental imagery with self-regulation programme with input from consumers and stakeholders and assessed its feasibility, acceptability, and potential effectiveness in a pilot study involving 11 patients with mild-to-moderate PD. We propose to conduct a fully powered clinical trial to (a) test the effects of mental imagery with self-regulation on improving daily activities (primary outcome) and overall, cognitive, and motor functions (secondary outcomes) in PwPD and (b) compare its effects with those of conventional learning and exercise. The proposed study will improve the rehabilitation outcomes of PwPD, particularly via early intervention in the neglected area of daily activities. 柏金遜症患者會出現運動症狀（如：震顫、僵硬）和非運動症狀（如：疲勞、抑鬱），這些症狀會導致他們在日常活動中受到限制。他們對緩慢動作的依賴歸因於在選擇注意和忽略事物（即監督性注意系統 supervisory attentional system）方面的障礙。全球新確診柏金遜症的人數不斷增加。作為早期介入，康復治療不僅可以配合藥物治療，也在藥物失效時發揮重要作用。傳統康復治療主要通過運動改善運動症狀，雖然有短期效果，但只關注步態和步行。目前，還沒有康復策略針對帕金森症患者在日常活動中的局限。提示法（cueing）是一種更新的康復策略，可以改善步行速度和僵硬，但提示法依賴外部提示或設備，在日常生活中並不現實，而且對日常活動的推廣性有限。 心理意象 (mental imagery)（即想像自己執行某項任務而不實際行動）是近年來用於改善柏金遜症患者功能的康復策略。然而，我們的系統性綜述 (systematic review) 顯示，心理意象的有效性依賴於在介入方案中加入額外的組成部分，包括：（1）將任務分解為步驟，（2）讓參與者自我覺察問題，以及（3）在意象過程中將注意力集中在活動表現上。這些組成部分可能來自另一種策略—自我調節 (self-regulation)，自我調節被認為可以增強學習動作策略時需要的注意力。 我們在中風患者中的過往研究已證明，心理意象結合自我調節能有效改善日常活動、注意力以及完成日常活動所需的認知控制（即監督性注意系統supervisory attentional system的作用）。由於柏金遜症患者的監督性注意系統受損會影響心理靈活性 (mental flexibility) 和對動作的注意力 (attention to movement)，因此合理推測，心理意象結合自我調節有助於解決他們對緩慢動作的依賴，從而改善日常活動表現。 為驗證這一假設，我們設計了一個為期六週的心理意象結合自我調節課程，並徵求了患者和相關利益方的意見，在一項涉及11名輕至中度柏金遜症患者的初步研究中評估了其可行性、接受度和潛在效果。我們計劃開展一項全面的臨床試驗，以（a）測試心理意象結合自我調節對改善柏金遜症患者日常活動（主要結果）以及整體、認知和運動功能（次要結果）的效果，並（b）與傳統學習和運動進行比較。 這項研究將有助於提升柏金遜症患者的康復效果，特別是在對日常活動這一被忽視的範疇的早期介入。

15605825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605825.value: 為長期醫療保健做出更好的決策－從民眾的角度概念化財務健康素養並制定工具

15605825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15605825.value: Mr Chow, Dicky Dr HO, Grace Wing Ka Prof JIN, Yong Dr Leung, Doris Yin-ping Prof WATSON, Bernadette Maria Mr Wong, Toby

15605825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605825.value: Background. Ageing societies, including Hong Kong’s, face the serious challenges of rising long-term care (LTC) demands and limited government financial subsidies. It is not uncommon for individuals to pay LTC expenses out of their own pocket. Financial health literacy (FHL), the ability to understand and utilize financial information and available resources to make sound healthcare and treatment choices, may contribute to decision-making on LTC. Aims. This study aims to investigate laypeople’s views about FHL in LTC decision-making and develop an instrument for FHL. Methods. A Q-methodology, a systematic mix of qualitative and quantitative methods, is adopted to reconstitute all existing conceptualizations of FHL within the local context. This method uncovers laypeople’s perceptions by allowing research participants (not researchers) to create their own meanings bearing on their individual frames of reference. Participants will be Chinese adults living in Hong Kong, aged 50 or above, who are cognitively intact, have at least two types of chronic illnesses, and are able to communicate in Cantonese. The research instrument is a set of opinion statements called a Q-sample. A pilot test of the Q-sorting procedure will be conducted with 40 middle-aged/older adults, who will be asked to comment on the process of Q-sorting. The Q-sample will be ranked and ordered by 60 participants to form ‘Q-sorts’. A by-person factor analysis with varimax rotation will be carried out to identify the optimal solution for the Q-sort data showing how many factors best represent FHL. Plurality of ideas is accepted. Distinguishing and salient statements identified in the composite Q-sorts will be used to develop an instrument for measuring FHL. The internal consistency of the resulting instrument will be assessed using Cronbach’s alpha (with 360 participants) and the 2-week test-retest stability by the intraclass correlation coefficient. The concurrent validity will be examined with health literacy related to chronic illnesses, financial status, and multimorbidity; while the predictive validity will be examined in relation to depressive symptoms and loneliness. Significance of the study. The findings will shed light on the concept of FHL and provide a tool for measuring FHL, to support future planning in LTC policies and practices.

15606525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15606525.value: 輕度認知障礙個體的層次網絡切換與認知靈活性的變化：一項縱貫研究

15606525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15606525.value: Prof Chau, Ka Hung Bolton Prof HSU, Chun Liang Dr Hui, Edward Sai Kam Dr Mak, Ka Fung Henry Prof Shum, Ho Keung David

15606525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606525.value: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is an intermediary stage of cognitive dysfunction lying between the cognitive decline observed in normal aging and the more serious decline associated with dementia. A common and important impairment in MCI is the decline in cognitive flexibility—the ability to adaptively shift between various cognitive processes. Impairments in cognitive flexibility can lead to decreased processing capacity, diminished creativity, and lowered efficiency in storing necessary information, ultimately affecting overall cognitive function and quality of life. Multilayer brain network analysis is an innovative computational model designed to simultaneously characterize multi-model, multi-scale, spatiotemporal neuroimaging data. Incorporating this model into understanding neuroscientific constructs such as cognitive flexibility is crucial, as it has the potential to reveal hidden features of brain networks that are not detectable with more traditional methods. This could be particularly beneficial for monitoring transitions of brain states across time between networks, which will improve our understanding of structural and functional relationships of the brain and enable more accurate tracking in disease progression. In this longitudinal study, we aim to test the hypothesis that changes in multilayer network switching capabilities will predict subsequent changes in cognitive flexibility in MCI individuals. To evaluate this hypothesis, two groups of individuals will be recruited: a group of older adults with MCI and a second group of healthy age-matched controls. The study participants will complete a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation and will participate in neuroimaging sessions, which include structural, task-switching fMRI and resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI), both at the start of the study and after 1 year. Cognitive flexibility will be assessed through a task designed to probe task-switching capabilities. Multilayer network analysis will be employed on rs-fMRI and task-based fMRI, conceptualizing the brain's functional architecture as a complex, dynamic multi-layered network that subserves cognitive flexibility. We hypothesize that the behavioral associations of this measurement could serve as a valuable clinical marker for cognitive deficits. Our study will expand current knowledge in the field by combining insights from neuroscience, psychology, and network theory to explore how our brains support complex cognitive functions. This longitudinal study will establish causal relationship between multilayer network switching and changes in cognitive flexibility, highlighting the brain's adaptability and efficiency. Our findings will illuminate the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying MCI associated with cognitive flexibility deficits. This, in turn, will pave the way for the development of more effective diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies, potentially preventing progression of MCI to dementia. 輕度認知障礙（Mild Cognitive Impairment, MCI）是介於正常老化認知衰退與失智症嚴重退化之間的認知功能異常過渡階段。此症常見且關鍵的損傷在於認知靈活性下降——即個體適應性轉換不同認知過程的能力受損。認知靈活性障礙可能導致信息處理能力減弱、創造力衰退、必要記憶儲存效率降低，最終影響整體認知功能與生活品質。 多層次腦網絡分析是一種創新計算模型，專為同步表徵多模式、多尺度的時空神經影像數據而設計。將此模型應用於理解認知靈活性等神經科學構念至關重要，因其能揭露傳統方法無法檢測的腦網絡隱藏特徵。這對於監測腦網絡狀態隨時間的轉變尤其有益，不僅能深化我們對大腦結構與功能關係的理解，更能精準追蹤疾病進展。 本縱向研究旨在驗證以下假設：多層網絡切換能力的變化可預測MCI患者後續認知靈活性的改變。為驗證此假說，我們將招募兩組受試者：MCI老年患者組與健康同年齡對照組。研究對象需接受完整神經心理學評估，並參與基線與一年後的兩次神經影像檢測，包括結構性磁振造影、任務轉換功能性磁振造影（fMRI）及靜息態fMRI（rs-fMRI）。認知靈活性將透過特定任務轉換測驗評估，而rs-fMRI與任務型fMRI數據將採用多層網絡分析法，將大腦功能架構概念化為支持認知靈活性的複雜動態多層網絡。 我們推測，此測量方法的行為關聯可作為認知缺陷的臨床標記。本研究將整合神經科學、心理學與網絡理論的見解，拓展當前領域知識，探索大腦如何支持複雜認知功能。此縱向設計將確立多層網絡切換與認知靈活性變化間的因果關係，凸顯大腦的適應性與效率機制。研究成果將闡明MCI患者認知靈活性缺損的病理生理機制，為開發更有效的診斷工具與治療策略鋪路，甚至可能阻斷MCI惡化為失智症的進程。

15606825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15606825.value: 中文閱讀與面孔識別中的視覺-正字法機制：透過行為實驗與神經影像分析探究認知神經異同

15606825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606825.value: In recent decades, research has established the critical role of phonological skills in the development of alphabetic reading, yet a similar consensus is lacking for the logographic Chinese system. Reading and writing have long been considered closely connected in Chinese. Hand-copying characters has been an effective exercise in schools to help children learn stroke assembly rules and memorize the intricate graphic forms of characters. This logographic system has been regarded as difficult to learn due to the visual complexity of its basic graphic symbols (characters), the lack of consistent print-sound mappings, the large number of characters to learn, and the tedious and laborious copying exercises involved in the learning process. These features of the logographic system have led to a general belief that visual-orthographic skills should play a crucial role in Chinese reading development but, surprisingly, empirical evidence supporting this notion is scarce. This lack of evidence regarding their importance could be attributed to the multifaceted nature of visual-orthographic skills, which are measured by various tasks assessing distinct aspects. The proposed study intends to comprehensively examine the role of visual-orthographic skills in learning to read Chinese among children aged 5-12 in Hong Kong. Interestingly, neuroimaging studies have revealed that Chinese writing activates a broader visuospatial network compared to alphabetic languages, involving brain regions such as the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left superior parietal lobule and bilateral middle occipital gyri (MOG). Activation of the right MOG, including the fusiform gyrus and the fusiform face area (FFA), during Chinese reading suggests its role in processing the holistic and pictorial nature of Chinese characters, contrasting with the left-lateralized network typical for linear alphabetic scripts. While the FFA is traditionally associated with domain-specific functions such as face perception, its recruitment during Chinese reading implies a potential domain-general role related to the square, two-dimensional structure common to Chinese characters and faces. Thus, studying FFA involvement in Chinese reading will shed light on essential visual skills for mastering this writing system and addressing the specificity of FFA function. By investigating cognitive and cortical processing differences between character recognition and face perception, the project aims to determine whether FFA serves domain-specific or domain-general functions and if face perception can serve as an early predictor for reading proficiency. These findings will help identify the types of visual-orthographic skills crucial for Chinese reading and develop early predictors of Chinese reading proficiency through behavioral and neuroimaging analyses. 過去數十年的認知神經科學研究已確立語音加工能力在拼音文字閱讀發展中的核心作用。然而，該結論是否適用於漢字這類類表意文字系統，至今仍存在理論分歧。中文書寫系統的獨特性主要體現在三個維度：在視覺結構方面，每個漢字都是具有精確空間配置的複雜圖形；在形音對應方面，缺乏系統性的拼讀規則；在記憶負荷方面，需要掌握數千個獨立字符。這些特性使得視覺字形分析能力（即正字法技能）被認為是中文閱讀發展的關鍵因素，但現有實證研究結果存在不一致性，這可能源於該能力本身的多維性以及測量工具的異質性。 近年的腦成像研究揭示，與拼音文字主要激活左腦語言區的線性加工模式不同，中文閱讀展現出獨特的神經表徵模式：不僅涉及左側背外側前額葉（工作記憶）和頂上小葉（空間處理），更顯著激活雙側枕葉皮質（視覺處理），特別是右側梭狀回面孔區（Fusiform Face Area, FFA）。這一發現提示漢字加工可能依賴與人臉識別相似的神經機制，即對二維結構的整體性分析。雖然FFA傳統上被視為專門處理人臉的特異性（domain-specific）腦區，但其在中文閱讀中的激活程度挑戰了腦功能「模組化」的傳統觀點，表明可能存在更為靈活的「功能可塑性」機制。 本研究將以5-12歲香港兒童為研究對象，採用多模態神經影像技術結合行為實驗，系統考察三個核心科學問題：第一，FFA在處理漢字和人臉時是否表現出相似的神經表徵模式？第二，這種神經表徵的個體差異能否預測兒童中文閱讀能力的發展軌跡？第三，成功的中文閱讀習得需要發展哪些特定的視覺正字法技能？研究成果將在理論層面闡明腦功能特異性與可塑性的辯證關係，在應用層面則可為中文閱讀障礙的篩查提供早期預警指標，並為不同文字系統的閱讀教學方法差異提供神經科學依據。

15607425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15607425.value: 動員土藥：中國共產黨早期的醫藥、革命與環境（1937–1947）

15607425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607425.value: This project explores the complex ways in which science, revolution, and the environment intersected in early Communist China by examining the roles of native pharmacy, known as tuyao 土藥, during the War of Resistance against Japan (1937–1945) and the civil war against Chiang Kai-shek’s Nationalist Party (1945–1949). Grown, sourced, harvested, and produced in the Yan’an-centered Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, the wartime headquarters of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), these native medicines were used for both medical and economic purposes. However, they soon acquired significant political and ideological dimensions as the Communists leveraged them to address revolutionary, public health, and environmental goals. In this context, native pharmacy emerged as both a natural product and an artificial construct, embedded within the larger context of Communist revolution and mobilization. This research demonstrates how the Chinese Communists deliberately crafted a native pharmacopeia to wage war and foment revolution, using it to generate wealth and power, advance mass health initiatives, and deepen understanding of local environments. Drawing on heretofore underexamined historical archives and artifacts, newspapers, local gazetteers, memoirs, and popular and literary works, this project appeals to the analytic conception of “boundary work” in science studies. According to this framework, tuyao is seen as a consciously constructed field of medical science, representing a powerful rhetorical and ideological tool for the CCP to set a boundary between a unified, scientific medicine and non-scientific traditional medical practices. The Communists strategically distinguished tuyao from the generic category of traditional Chinese herbs by designating native medicines as primitive, raw materials bounded by their natural sites rather than artificial objects produced by Chinese doctors’ socio-technical network. Tuyao emerged as a new composite knowledge of pharmacy, intricately linked to the local environments of Shaan-Gan-Ning, which were open to investigations by both Western and Chinese medicine. Through this invented “boundary work,” the CCP coordinated multiple actors across various socio-political domains and knowledge systems—practitioners of Chinese and Western medicine, Communist policymakers and the masses, local knowledge and metropolitan science, and human imperatives and the environment. This project reveals that the CCP’s strategy towards Chinese medicine in the Yan’an period, shaped by revolutionary politics, practical needs, and environmental considerations, had a profound impact on, and yet represented a departure from, the self-reliant science and radical attitudes towards nature in Socialist-era China. 本研究通過考察抗日戰爭（1937–1945）及國共內戰（1945–1949）時期本土藥物（土藥）的作用，探究早期共產主義中國語境下科學、革命與環境的多維互動。這些生長、採集並生產於中共中央戰時駐地陝甘寧邊區的本土藥材，最初兼具醫療與經濟功能，但很快被中國共產黨賦予顯著的政治與意識形態維度，成為實現革命目標、公共衛生訴求與環境治理的綜合載體。在此過程中，土藥既作為自然產物，亦作為革命動員背景下的人為建構，深度嵌入共產主義革命脈絡。本研究試圖揭示，中共通過系統性構建本土藥物體系服務戰爭與革命，藉此積累財富與權力、推進群眾衛生工作，並深化對地方環境的認知。 基於對稀見檔案、實物、報刊、方志、回憶錄及通俗文藝作品的跨學科分析，本研究引入科學史領域的「劃界工作」（boundary work）理論框架。土藥被視為中共精心建構的醫學科學場域，其本質是劃分「統一科學醫學」與「非科學傳統醫療」的修辭工具與意識形態裝置。共產黨人通過將土藥定性為「受自然地域限制的原始生藥」（而非中醫社會技術網絡加工的人工產物），使其脫離傳統中藥範疇，最終形成根植於陝甘寧生態環境的新型複合藥學知識體系——該體系同時向中西醫開放研究。通過這種人為的邊界建構，中共協調了跨社會政治領域與知識系統的多元行動者（中西醫從業者、政策制定者與群眾、地方知識與主流科學范式、人類需求與環境資源）。 本研究指出，延安時期中共的中醫藥策略受革命政治、現實需求與環境因素共同形塑，既深刻影響了社會主義時期自力更生科學模式及激進自然觀，又與之存在本質性斷裂。

15607725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607725.value: This project will study and interpret two newly published Warring States manuscripts (c. late 4th c. BCE) held by Tsinghua University. The manuscripts contain sequences of terminology based on the five tones of the pentatonic scale, gong 宮, shang 商, jue 角, zhi 徵, and yu 羽. According to some preliminary accounts, one of these manuscripts contains musical notation, which would make it the earliest music score in Chinese history, predating transmitted zither tablatures by some eight or nine centuries. The other manuscript contains a diagram with five projecting spokes of pentatonic terminology, and may be a tool for instrument tuning, a theoretical reference chart, or some other type of text. Both texts are relevant not only to the history of notation, but also to a longstanding historical debate about the early history of music, and whether an allegedly lost corpus of texts, or Classic of Music, could ever have existed in preimperial times. Some preliminary studies of the manuscripts assume they are theoretical in nature, whereas others consider them to have a more practical use. Although their terminology consists primarily of the five tone terms, these tones often come enmeshed in webs of correlative associations that are prominent in philosophical texts found in the same manuscript cache. Thus, in addition to considering early Chinese musical practice, instrumentation, and sound technologies, the project must interpret the new manuscripts in light of early musical aesthetics, ritual, and models of cosmo-political order. Because the manuscripts demand specialized study from multiple perspectives, the project seeks travel funding to convene experts for a small interdisciplinary workshop. It also requests funding to support one conference trip, a part-time research assistant, and open-access publication fees. 本項目將研究並詮釋兩份新近發表、現藏於清華大學的戰國時期（約西元前四世紀末）竹書。這些竹書包含以五聲音階——宮、商、角、徵、羽——為基礎的術語序列。根據初步報告，其中一份簡牘包含音樂記譜，這將使其成為中國歷史上最早的樂譜，早於現存的琴譜約八、九百年。另一份竹書則包含一個以五個突出輻射為特徵的五聲術語圖示，可能是一種樂器定音工具、理論參考圖表，或其他類型的文本。這兩份文本不僅與記譜史相關，也關涉到關於音樂早期歷史及所謂失傳的《樂經》是否曾於先秦時期存在的長期學術爭論。部分初步研究認為這些竹書屬於理論性質，另有學者則認為其具有更實用的用途。雖然其術語主要由五聲名稱構成，但這些音階常與同一批竹書中出現的哲學文本中的各種對應關聯網絡交織在一起。因此，除了考察早期中國的音樂實踐、樂器製作與聲音技術外，本項目亦須結合早期音樂美學、禮儀以及宇宙—政治秩序模式，對這些新簡牘進行詮釋。

15608125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15608125.value: 決策過程中雜訊傳播的神經計算研究

15608125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15608125.value: Prof KRANZ, Georg Dr Law, Chun-Kit

15608125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608125.value: The human brain contains noisy neural signals that can lead to noisy decisions (i.e. inconsistencies in choices). Decision noise is apparent even in critical contexts like legal and medical settings. While neuroscience theories have primarily focused on modelling expected choices, they offer limited explanation about the mechanisms of how noisy decisions emerge. Our project aims to employ a neurocomputational approach to investigate how noise propagates within the human brain and leads to noisy decisions. Such knowledge will contribute to identifying specific aspects of decision-making impairments in psychiatric disorders and developing way to mitigate noise in decision making. Our project will consist of three studies. Study 1 will utilise functional magnetic resonance imaging to identify how neural noise propagates across brain regions involved in early and late stages of decision making. Healthy human participants will be recruited to perform a decision-making task designed to experimentally-induce varying levels of early noise and late noise. Our preliminary findings established that early-perceptual regions (e.g., V5) are susceptible to experimentally-induced early noise, whereas late-integration regions (e.g., the ventromedial prefrontal cortex) are susceptible to experimentally-induced late noise. We will further analyse how neural noise propagates propagates from early-perceptual to late-integration brain regions using psychophysiological interaction analysis. Study 2 will examine whether individual variations in decision-making strategies are associated with distinct patterns of decision noise. We have already performed computational modelling to simulate and characterise decision noise. Our preliminary findings suggest that when the model employs an additive strategy, the decision noise is more influenced by early neural noise. In contrast, when the model employs a multiplicative strategy, the decision noise is more influenced by late neural noise. Here, we propose to empirically test these predictions in healthy individuals. We will identify individuals’ decision-making strategies and asses the effects of experimentally-induced early and late noise on their decision making. Study 3 will apply our computational models to capture the specific deficits in individuals with known decision-making impairments. This will be achieved by testing individuals with major depressive disorder who typically display heightened decision noise. We hypothesise that their decision making is best described by the additive strategy model, which is prone to early noise. This is also supported by our preliminary findings. Overall, this research will not only enhance our understanding of the impact of neural noise propagation on behaviour, but also offer clinical insights by into understanding the atypical decision-making processes in individuals with depression. 人腦中的神經訊號存在雜訊，這些訊號可能導致決策雜訊，即選擇的不一致。即使在法律和醫療等關鍵環境中，決策雜訊也顯而易見。雖然神經科學理論主要著重於對預期選擇進行建模，但它們對決策雜訊產生機制的解釋有限。我們的研究旨在採用神經計算方法，研究雜訊如何在人腦中傳播並導致決策雜訊。這些知識將有助於識別精神疾病中決策障礙的具體方面，並發展減輕決策雜訊的方法。我們的項目將包含兩項研究。 研究1將利用功能性磁振造影來識別神經雜訊如何在參與決策早期和晚期階段的大腦區域之間傳播。我們將招募健康的參與者執行一項決策任務，該任務旨在透過實驗誘導不同程度的早期雜訊和晚期雜訊。我們的初步研究結果表明，早期感知區域（例如V5）易受實驗誘導的早期雜訊影響，而晚期整合區域（例如腹內側前額葉皮質）則易受實驗誘導的晚期雜訊影響。我們將進一步運用psychophysiological interaction分析，分析神經雜訊如何從早期感知腦區傳播到晚期整合腦區。 研究2將探討決策策略的個體差異是否與不同的決策雜訊模式相關。我們已經進行了計算建模來模擬決策雜訊。我們的初步研究結果表明，當模型採用加法策略時，決策雜訊受早期神經雜訊的影響更大。相反，當模型採用乘法策略時，決策雜訊受晚期神經雜訊的影響較大。我們計劃對這些預測進行實證檢驗。我們將識別個體的決策策略，並評估實驗誘導的早期和晚期雜訊對其決策的影響。這項研究將增進我們對神經雜訊傳播對行為的影響的理解。

15608625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15608625.value: 分類和主題語義系統中的跨語言和跨文化差異

15608625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15608625.value: Prof Li, Ping Dr Nastase, Sam

15608625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608625.value: In today’s globalized society, where intercultural communication and collaboration are more prevalent than ever, understanding how linguistic and cultural experiences shape our perception of the world becomes essential. Investigating cross-linguistic and cross-cultural differences in the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying semantic knowledge can help us address significant challenges in cognitive science, education, and artificial intelligence within an increasingly interconnected research landscape. This project examines whether and how these experiences induce systematic differences in the organization of conceptual knowledge. We will focus on two distinct organizations of conceptual knowledge: based on shared features (taxonomic relations: e.g., dog-cat) or co-occurrence in common scenes and scenarios (thematic relations: e.g., dog-bone). We aim to determine whether these organizational principles are prioritized differently among participants with varying linguistic and cultural backgrounds. For instance, the semantic radicals of Chinese characters, which often reflect object taxonomies, may promote a taxonomic organization of concepts. Conversely, the collectivist values prevalent in Eastern cultures may place greater emphasis on the relationships between objects and their surrounding environment, leading to a preference for thematic organization. Using a multivariate decoding method called representational similarity analysis (RSA), we will examine how representational structure of concepts reflect biases toward taxonomic or thematic organization. Participants from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds will perform taxonomic and thematic judgment tasks, allowing us to compare their behavioral and neural responses towards the same set of concepts. We will explore cross-linguistic/cultural differences in engaging with these types of semantic knowledge and how these differences interact with the flexibility in accessing these two types of conceptual knowledge. Additionally, by evaluating the performance of computational models on diverse language corpora, we aim to determine whether state-of-art large language models can replicate the effects observed in behavioural and neural data. Through RSA, we will establish connections between human judgment, brain activity, and computational models, shedding light on the influence of linguistic and cultural experiences on the representational structure underlying semantic knowledge. This research will not only advance our understanding of conceptual representations but also contribute to a more comprehensive theory of semantic cognition. Furthermore, it holds practical implications for pedagogical design in learning and communicating conceptual knowledge, as well as for the development of artificial intelligence tools—such as search engines, social chatbots, and virtual assistant—that can effectively adapt to various languages and cultures, which is particularly significant in multilingual and multicultural environments like Hong Kong. 在當今全球化社會中，跨文化交流與合作比以往任何時候都更加普遍，理解語言和文化經歷如何塑造我們對世界的認知變得至關重要。研究語義知識背後神經認知機制的跨語言和跨文化差異，可以幫助我們在日益相互關聯的環境中應對認知科學、教育和人工智慧領域的重大挑戰。本項目旨在研究這些經歷是否以及如何在概念知識的組織中引起系統性差異。我們將重點關注組織概念知識的兩種不同方式：基於共同特徵的分類關係（如：狗-貓）或在常見場景中共同出現的主題關係（如：狗-骨頭）。我們的目標是確定不同語言和文化背景的參與者是否會對這些組織原則有不同的優先選擇。例如，漢字的語義部首通常反映物體的分類法，可能會促進概念的分類組織。相反，東方文化中普遍存在的集體主義價值觀可能更加強調物體與其周圍環境之間的關係，從而傾向於主題組織。 我們將使用一種稱為表徵相似性分析（RSA）的多變量解碼方法，來研究概念的表徵結構如何反映對分類或主題組織的偏好。來自不同語言和文化背景的參與者將執行分類和主題判斷任務，使我們能夠比較他們對同一組概念的行為和神經反應。我們將探索在處理這些類型的語義知識時的跨語言/文化差異，以及這些差異如何與獲取這兩種概念知識的靈活性相互作用。此外，通過評估計算模型在不同語言語料庫上的表現，我們旨在確定最先進的大型語言模型是否能夠複製在行為和神經數據中觀察到的效應。通過RSA，我們將建立人類判斷、大腦活動和計算模型之間的聯繫，揭示語言和文化經歷對語義知識背後表徵結構的影響。 這項研究不僅將推進我們對概念表徵的理解，還將有助於建立更全面的語義認知理論。此外，它對學習和傳達概念知識的教學設計具有實際意義，也對開發能夠有效適應各種語言和文化的人工智慧工具——如搜尋引擎、社交聊天機器人和虛擬助手——具有重要價值，這在像香港這樣的多語言和多文化環境中尤為重要。

15608725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15608725.value: 理解香港政府的社交媒体传播：一项电脑辅助的多模態話語分析

15608725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15608725.value: Prof HUAN, Changpeng Prof KRZYZANOWSKI, Michal Wladyslaw Prof O’HALLORAN, Kay Prof Tay, Dennis Zhiming

15608725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608725.value: In the digital age, social media has become an increasingly important tool for government communication, providing new channels for improving transparency and enhancing public trust. Meanwhile, it has also provided an unprecedented opportunity for the public to participate in the policymaking process through expressing their support/opposition, giving suggestions, etc. In Hong Kong, the government has recognised the potential of social media and has been utilising various platforms to communicate with the public, especially amid the crisis of "governability" and political distrust after the social unrests in 2019. However, we still lack a systematic understanding of how social media has been used for coping with the crisis and restoring public trust. Previous research has discussed the lack of democratic engagement in the Hong Kong government's digital communication, but there has been no empirical analysis of the government's actual social media behaviour and discourse, nor of the nature and content of netizens' comments, to support such claims. Against this background, this project seeks to provide a comprehensive analysis of the Hong Kong government's social media communications and netizens' comments using multimodal discourse-analytical methods. The data for this project comprises posts of key government departments in Hong Kong as well as public comments on the posts on three social media platforms, namely, Facebook, Instagram, and X, from 2019 to 2025. To analyse the large amount of multimodal data, we adopt a multi-method approach, including interactivity analysis, topic modelling, optimised semantic-based sentiment analysis, as well as manual and automated multimodal attitude analysis based on large language models. The application and development of cutting-edge technologies provide a novel solution to the long-discussed trade-off between qualitative and quantitative analysis. Generative AI can solve this dilemma by enabling nuanced "qualitative" analysis of large-scale datasets, which has far-reaching implications for discourse-based research. As the first comprehensive analysis of the Hong Kong government's social media communication, the research will provide new insights into the dynamics of social media interactions and recent socio-political changes. It fills a critical gap by highlighting the government's discursive practice as a key component of governance and a new site of power struggle in the digital age. Prognostically, the findings will provide policymakers with an explicit understanding of the strategies of and challenges to their digital discursive practice. Beyond Hong Kong, as social media is reshaping government communication globally, the findings will also provide valuable reference information for discursive governance in other socio-political contexts. 在數碼時代，社交媒體已成為政府溝通日益重要的工具，為提升透明度和增強公眾信任開闢了新渠道。同時，它也為公眾通過表達支持/反對、提出建議等方式參與政策制定過程提供了前所未有的機遇。在香港，尤其在2019年社會動盪後出現"管治危機"與政治信任受損的背景下，政府已意識到社交媒體的潛力，並利用包括 Facebook 在內的平臺與公眾溝通。然而，我們仍缺乏對社交媒體如何被用於應對危機、重建公眾信任的系統性認知。既往研究雖討論過香港政府數碼溝通中民主參與的缺失，但尚未對政府實際社交媒體行為與話語、以及市民評論的性質與內容進行實證分析。在此背景下，本研究採用前沿的多模態分析方法，對香港政府社交媒體傳播及网民評論進行綜合研究。 研究資料涵蓋2019至2025年間香港主要政府部門在Facebook、Instagram和X（原Twitter）三大平臺的發帖及公眾評論。為處理海量多模態数据，我們採用混合研究方法：包括互動性分析、主題建模、基於語義優化的情感分析，以及依託大語言模型的人工與自動化多模態態度分析。前沿技術的應用與發展為長期存在的"質化與量化分析難以兼顧"困境提供了創新解決方案。生成式人工智慧能夠在大規模資料集上開展細緻的“質性”分析，從而有望化解這一兩難，對基於話語的研究方法產生深遠影響。 作為首個針對香港政府社交媒體溝通的全面分析，本研究將為社交媒體互動動態及近期社會政治變遷提供新見解。它通過凸顯政府的話語實踐作為治理的重要組成部分與數碼時代權力互動的新場域，填補了關鍵研究空白。長遠而言，研究結果可以幫助政策制定者更清晰地理解其媒體話語實踐的策略與所面臨的挑戰。隨著社交媒體在全球範圍內重塑政府的溝通模式，本研究成果也將為其他社會政治語境下的話語治理提供寶貴參考。

15609125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15609125.value: 動態商業環境中的設計管理：香港及大灣區科技初創企業設計管理能力模型研究

15609125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609125.value: The importance of design in the context of start-ups has been widely acknowledged in both industry and academic research. However, unlike established ventures (existing companies), start-ups face challenges in acquiring design resources and expertise due to their limited investments. This challenge is particularly critical for start-ups in the incubation stage, where resource constraints are prevalent. Incorporating design activities into their business development is considered a crucial element for achieving success, particularly for tech start-ups focused on delivering consumer products. In the academic, this is the problem solved by design management with a capability-based view. Despite the recognized importance of design, many start-ups lack the knowledge and experience to effectively integrate, apply, and manage design. Although the design management capability in the stable business context has been well-studied and there is good design awareness in entrepreneurial practice, the research on design management in entrepreneurship is limited and the design management capability in entrepreneurship is rarely studied. This is our defined research gap. To achieve this aim, we target to develop the existing capability model of design management into an updated version for the turbulent business context through the exploration of new capabilities. Through a mixed-method strategy, the new capabilities will be first explored with expert interviews. Then, a questionnaire survey will be conducted to identify the key capabilities and build the model. Finally, the guidelines for applying and building the capabilities in entrepreneurial practice will be illustrated via cases. This study aims to achieve four main findings. Firstly, a comprehensive list of the key design activities for start-ups will be identified. Secondly, the goals and outcomes associated with each design activity will be elucidated. Thirdly, the loops encompassing the design activities within the new product development process will be uncovered. Finally, patterns leading to start-up success through the effective implementation of design activities will be identified. In addition to theoretical contributions to the field of design management and entrepreneurial capability, our findings also hold practical value for multiple stakeholders. Start-up founders can benefit from our research by gaining guidance on common capabilities of managing design. Professional designers and design consultancies can develop their capabilities and identify potential clients for capability matching. Incubators and incubation platforms can provide appropriate support for start-ups’ capability building. Policymakers can leverage our findings to develop more effective mechanisms for encouraging the integration of design and start-ups.

15609725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15609725.value: 邁向可信人工智慧：生物醫學大語言模型幻覺現象之深入剖析與對策研究

15609725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15609725.value: Prof Huang, Chu-ren Dr Wang, Benyou Prof ZHANG, Caicai Prof ZHAO, Yan Prof Zhou, Guodong

15609725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609725.value: Abstract In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has undergone monumental advancements, especially in Natural Language Generation (NLG). A landmark development in this field is the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs). These sophisticated LLMs, with their capacity to process intricate data patterns and respond to nuanced instructions, have redefined machine-driven text generation, producing content that closely mirrors human expressions. Their versatility spans a wide range of academic and commercial applications, marking a significant shift in technological advancement. However, the advancement of LLMs is not without challenges. A critical issue is the occurrence of "hallucinations"—outputs that may seem plausible but are factually inaccurate. While such hallucinations may be inconsequential in casual contexts, they pose serious risks in biomedical applications. For instance, if an LLM suggests an incorrect drug dosage or recommends a contraindicated treatment, the consequences could range from clinical misunderstandings to life-threatening outcomes. Addressing these hallucinations in biomedical contexts is, therefore, imperative. Current research primarily approaches hallucination detection at a coarse-grained level (e.g., sentence, passage, or document level), which is insufficient for capturing fine-grained signals or precisely pinpointing hallucination locations. This limitation restricts our understanding of LLMs’ detailed knowledge comprehension and reasoning abilities. Additionally, most existing research is conducted solely in English, leaving significant gaps in non-English languages, such as Chinese and Cantonese, particularly within biomedical contexts. Systematic investigation into the conditions and mechanisms that give rise to hallucinations across multiple abilities, tasks, domains, and languages remains largely absent, making the study of fine-grained biomedical LLM hallucinations an urgent and underexplored area. This research project is dedicated to addressing this gap. We aim to explore the intricacies of fine-grained LLM hallucinations in biomedical contexts, focusing on understanding their origins, defining their characteristics, and developing effective mitigation strategies. Specifically, we aim to answer the following research questions: (1) How do hallucinations manifest at a fine-grained level within LLMs across different tasks, domains, and languages? (2) Can LLMs recognize their own hallucinations and correct them independently? (3) How can external knowledge be effectively integrated to help LLMs reduce hallucinations? By advancing a comprehensive understanding of biomedical LLMs alongside targeted strategies for hallucination mitigation, this research seeks to improve the reliability and integrity of biomedical LLM applications. Ultimately, this project stands at the intersection of technology and public health, advocating a safety-centered evolution of AI in fields where accuracy is not merely beneficial but essential for safety and well-being. 近年來，人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence, AI）技術迅猛發展，尤以自然語言生成（Natural Language Generation, NLG）領域的突破最為顯著。其中，大型語言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）的出現可謂劃時代創舉。這些先進的模型具備處理複雜數據模式及理解細膩指令的能力，徹底重塑了機器自動文本生成的樣貌，且其輸出內容與人類語言表達極為相似。LLMs 的多元應用涵蓋學術、商業與醫療等諸多領域，標誌著科技創新的重大進展。 然而，LLMs 的發展同時伴隨著挑戰，其中一項關鍵問題即為模型的“幻覺”現象——即模型生成內容表面上合理但實則錯誤。雖然此類幻覺問題在日常應用中可能無傷大雅，然而對於醫療健康領域，其風險則極高。例如，若模型錯誤建議藥物劑量或錯誤制定療程方案，則可能導致嚴重臨床誤判，甚至危及患者生命。因此，在生物醫學場景中準確識別並處理此類幻覺問題至關重要。 現有幻覺研究大多聚焦於粗粒度層級（如句子、段落或全文）的幻覺檢測方法，此類方法難以捕獲細粒度幻覺訊號，亦難以準確定位錯誤出現的位置，限制了我們對LLMs知識理解與推理能力的深入了解。此外，現有研究大多聚焦於英文語料，對於諸如中文、粵語等非英語語言在生物醫學場景下的幻覺研究仍嚴重不足。針對不同語言、任務及應用場景，探討幻覺生成的條件與機制，目前仍缺乏系統性研究。 本研究計劃旨在填補此一研究空白，系統化探討LLMs於生物醫學語境中細粒度幻覺的生成模式與特徵，並研發有效的幻覺消解策略。核心研究問題包括：（1）細粒度幻覺是如何在不同任務、領域及語言中呈現的？（2）LLMs 是否具備辨識及自我修正幻覺的能力？（3）如何有效整合外部知識，以協助模型減少幻覺產生？ 本計劃透過建立完善的理論框架與應用工具，促進對生物醫學領域LLMs 的全面理解，並開發針對性的幻覺消解方案。最終目標是提升LLMs 在醫療健康領域的可靠性與可信度，推動人工智慧應用朝著安全可靠的方向發展，以確保科技成果能實際造福社會大眾與公共健康。

15609825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15609825.value: 不发表就出局时代下博士生的情感体验与身份构建：以香港为例

15609825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15609825.value: Prof Hu, Guangwei Prof OCCHIPINTI, Stefano

15609825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609825.value: Neoliberalism and globalization have directly impacted on doctoral students and they are now under pressure to publish in internationally-indexed journals during their studies. However, this task is extremely challenging for them since they are already heavily involved in researching and writing their thesis. While some studies have investigated academic publishing pressure among academics in Hong Kong, fewer have examined the publishing pressure faced by doctoral students. More importantly, little attention has been paid to the emotional experiences of doctoral students attempting to publish, despite the fact that doctoral learning journeys have been recognized as emotional rollercoasters. Therefore, a large-scale study into the emotional experiences of doctoral students that are influenced by the publishing imperative is crucial, as research suggests that emotions substantially influence attrition, motivation, and identity. To address the gap, this mixed-method study will examine the emotional experiences of doctoral students in Hong Kong across four disciplines, as disciplines play an important role in emotional experiences of doctoral students. Specifically, the project aims to: (1) assess the emotional exhaustion of doctoral students in Hong Kong and the social support they receive and (2) study emotional vulnerability and identity construction experienced by these students with regard to academic publishing. The study comprises two main phases. In phase 1, a survey will be administered to 220 doctoral students from four disciplines. The survey will collect data related to their experiences of emotional exhaustion and the social support they receive. Phase 2 will involve narrative frames collected from 30 students from each discipline followed by in-depth semi-structured interviews with 10 students from each discipline. These narrative frames and interviews will investigate emotional vulnerability in academic publishing and its impact on students' identity construction. The proposed project aims to advance our understanding of doctoral students, the new blood of the academic world, by investigating how the publish or perish culture may impact on their emotional experiences and influence their academic identity formation. The project will also study the types and amounts of social support doctoral students receive. Identifying the sources of emotional vulnerability in doctoral students can offer insights that can inform the development of effective policies and practices for promoting their emotional well-being. The findings of this study will also help policy makers and doctoral supervisors understand the emotional struggles of these students and provide implications for university management on how to create a supportive and sustainable publishing culture in tertiary education. 新自由主义和全球化直接影响了博士生，使得他们在学业期间面临着在国际期刊发表论文的巨大压力。尽管他们已深度参与到论文的研究与写作中，但这项任务对博士生仍极具挑战性。虽然已有研究关注了香港学者的学术发表压力，但针对博士生所承受的发表压力的研究却相对较少。更重要的是，尽管博士学习之旅常被认为是情感上的过山车，但博士生在尝试发表论文过程中所经历的情感体验却鲜有关注。鉴于情感在学生流失、学习动机和身份构建过程中起着重要作用，因此有必要开展一项大规模研究，深入探讨发表压力对博士生产生的情感影响。 为填补这一空白，本研究采用混合方法，考察香港四个学科领域博士生的情感体验，因为学科差异在博士生的情感体验中起着重要角色。本项目主要目标包括：（1）评估香港博士生的情感耗竭及其获得的社会支持；（2）研究博士生在学术发表过程中经历的情感脆弱性及其对身份建构的影响。研究分为两个主要阶段：第一阶段，通过问卷调查收集220名博士生的情感耗竭和社会支持数据；第二阶段，将从每个学科各选取30名学生收集其叙事框架，并对每个学科的10名学生进行深入的半结构式访谈。这些叙事框架和访谈将探讨博士生在学术发表过程中的情感脆弱性及其对身份建构的影响。 本项目旨在探讨“不发表就出局”文化如何影响博士生的情感体验及其学术身份的形成，深化我们对博士生这一学术界新鲜血液的理解。同时，项目还将考察博士生获得社会支持的类型和数量，识别博士生情感脆弱性的来源，有助于为制定促进其情感健康的有效政策和实践提供参考。本研究结果还将帮助政策制定者和博士生导师更好地理解博士生的情感困境，并为高校管理层如何营造支持性、可持续的学术发表文化提供启示。

15610825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15610825.value: 探索程序公義與社會共融：華人和少數族裔青少年與警務人員的定性比較研究

15610825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15610825.value: Dr Ho, Shi King Prof LI, Enshen Dr Lo, Kai Chung Prof Wu, Yuning

15610825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610825.value: Democratic policing faces a significant challenge: maintaining legitimacy in the eyes of the public. Historically, the relationship between the police and ethnic minorities (EMs) has been fraught with tension in many societies, and Hong Kong is no exception. Although the Racial Discrimination Ordinance makes it unlawful to discriminate against, harass, or victimise others based on their race, EM groups in Hong Kong report experiencing ‘over-policing’. As the EM population and the number of EM police officers in Hong Kong increase, the legitimacy of the police as perceived by EM groups in this Chinese society warrants urgent attention. However, no empirical or theoretical research addresses the linked issues of police legitimacy and social inclusion in Hong Kong. It is unclear whether the findings of studies of police–EM encounters in Western contexts apply to the context of Hong Kong, whose main EM groups are South Asians. Furthermore, studies of police legitimacy and social identity in Hong Kong and elsewhere fail to take a comparative view by considering the perspectives of both Chinese and EM police officers and citizen. To help fill these critical gaps, the proposed study will pioneer diverse qualitative methods to explore police–youth interactions in Hong Kong, particularly those involving EMs. It will combine semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and vignettes to obtain information from 24 Chinese and South Asian arrested youths, 24 Chinese and South Asian police officers, and 25 appropriate adults and community stakeholders in three phases over 24 months. Recognising those police–citizen encounters can be particularly complicated when different ethnicities are involved, the study will also use AI-generated images depicting police–youth encounters involving various combinations of ethnicities to facilitate discussion of scenarios that cannot be easily recreated in reality. This study will be the first in Hong Kong to use vignette scenarios – including the ‘story completion’ technique to overcome language barriers and address power imbalances – to qualitatively compare perspectives on police procedural justice held by police, youths, and guardians, incorporating the views of both Chinese and EM groups. This innovative methodology will contribute constructively to discussions of police procedural justice and social inclusion within Hong Kong’s context. The study will also serve as a valuable resource for policymakers and practitioners seeking to enhance police-community relations, promote social inclusion, and mitigate ethnic disparities in law enforcement.

15611325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15611325.value: 突破沉默：同志親密伴侶暴力與求助經驗

15611325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15611325.value: Prof Chan, Randolph Chun Ho Dr Chau, Ruby Chui-man Prof Kong, Travis Shiu-ki Dr Tang , Denise Tse-shang Prof Yan, Elsie Chau Wai

15611325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15611325.value: This study will examine intimate partner violence (IPV) among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) individuals in Hong Kong. It will investigate how gender and sexual identities intersect with relational ties and wider socio-cultural and structural conditions in shaping IPV experiences and help-seeking. Significant knowledge gaps remain in understanding LGBTQ+ IPV. Existing IPV literature has predominantly focused on heterosexual relationships, especially heterosexual women, while research examining IPV within LGBTQ+ relationships is limited. Additionally, most IPV research has been quantitative and conducted in Western contexts, largely ignoring the processes through which LGBTQ+ people recognise their intimate relationships as ‘violent’ and react, particularly in non-Western contexts. Considering the dual challenge of navigating a stigmatised LGBTQ+ identity and experiencing IPV, this study is crucial for identifying key junctures at which LGBTQ+ individuals may experience further marginalisation and/or support and (re-)build relational ties in the face of IPV, thereby informing interventions that are sensitive to their needs, strengths, and vulnerabilities. The study will adopt a mixed qualitative design, including: (1)narrative interviews with 30-40 LGBTQ+ individuals to capture personal stories of navigating IPV in relation to their gender and sexual identities; (2)visual timeline methods to map significant life events and transitions shaping IPV experiences and coping strategies; (3)photo elicitation techniques to explore how participants envision better relationship models, and (4)three focus groups with service providers to investigate their perceptions of and responses to LGBTQ+ IPV. The analysis will link personal experiences to relational ties and broader social contexts, including cultural emphasis on family ‘harmony’, associated taboos on IPV, and socio-cultural expectations around gender and sexuality. This study will draw on theorisations of dialectical social imaginaries, intersectionality, and social scripts to elucidate how LGBTQ+ people navigate tensions arising from navigating relational ties between themselves and others and negotiating traditional and new social scripts during their journeys of recognising violence in their relationships and (re-)building relational ties in response to IPV. Conceptualising this process as dialectical and non-linear, this study moves beyond a risk-focused paradigm to examine both the vulnerabilities and strengths of individuals when negotiating the tensions between stigma and help-seeking in the Chinese context. This pioneering study will contribute to gender and sexuality studies and research on IPV. Collaboration with local LGBTQ+ organisations, mental health professionals, and community advocates will inform culturally sensitive interventions aimed at supporting LGBTQ+ victims/survivors, enhance targeted prevention strategies, and raise public awareness of IPV. 本研究旨在探討香港LGBTQ+群體（包括同志、跨性別及酷兒）中的親密伴侶暴力，分析性別與性取向如何與關係、社會文化與結構性條件交織而影響LGBTQ+群體的親密伴侶暴力經歷及其求助方式。目前在理解LGBTQ+ 親密伴侶暴力方面仍存在顯著的知識缺口。現有文獻主要聚焦於異性戀關係，尤其聚焦於異性戀女性，但對LGBTQ+關係中的親密伴侶暴力的研究仍然有限。此外，大多數有關親密伴侶暴力的研究採用定量方法，且集中於西方，對LGBTQ+群體如何在非西方背景下將其親密關係認知為「暴力」並作出回應的過程關注不足。鑑於經歷親密伴侶暴力的LGBTQ+人士需同時面對污名化身份與暴力的雙重挑戰，本研究將分析他們如何在此過程中被邊緣化、獲得支持或重建關係網絡，從而為制定更符合其需求的介入措施提供依據。 本研究採用混合質性研究設計，包括：（1）對30至40位LGBTQ+人士進行敘事式訪談，收集其應對親密伴侶暴力的個人故事；（2）運用視覺時間線方法，分析親密伴侶暴力的經歷與應對策略的重要事件與轉折點；（3）借助照片，探索參與者對更理想的親密關係模式的想像；（4）開展三場與服務提供者的焦點小組，探討其對LGBTQ+ 親密伴侶暴力的認知與回應。研究將分析個人經驗、關係及社會環境，包括分析重視家庭和諧的文化、與親密伴侶暴力相關的禁忌及圍繞性別與性取向的社會文化期待等。 本研究將借鑑多元社會想象、交叉性與社會腳本等理論，分析LGBTQ+人士如何在認知親密關係中的暴力及應對暴力的過程中，處理自我與他人之間的關係張力，並在傳統與新興社會腳本之間作出決定。本研究將此過程視為非線性，突破過往以風險為中心的研究模式，探討個體在華人語境下於污名與求助之間的張力中所展現的脆弱性與力量。 作為一項開創性研究，本研究將對性別研究及親密伴侶暴力研究作出貢獻。透過與本地LGBTQ+機構、心理健康專業人士及社區倡導者的合作，研究成果將有助於制定具文化敏感性的介入措施，以支持曾經歷親密伴侶暴力的LGBTQ+人士，並提升針對性預防策略，提高公眾對親密伴侶暴力的認知。

15612325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15612325.value: 數碼創意經濟中的代際動態：香港家庭如何應對平台職涯的機遇與挑戰

15612325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15612325.value: More and more tech-savvy youths are choosing platform careers in the new (sub)sectors of content creation and influencer marketing, e-sports and competitive gaming, and livestream shopping and e-commerce. This new career trend has brought changes and challenges to conventional family-cultural expectations, norms and arrangements. However, despite the large body of literature on platform(ed) work documenting workers’ job insecurity, algorithmic control and work–life imbalances, little is known about the consequences of this type of non-standard work for intergenerational relations and family life and, in turn, their impact on youth's platform-career pathways. This limited research is particularly notable in Chinese societies, where strong intergenerational bonds prevail. Drawing on in-depth interviews with both young adults who pursue(d) platform careers in Hong Kong and with their parents, the proposed study will be among the first to examine how families grapple with the promise and pitfalls of the digital creative economy. The study will explore how parents perceive and respond to digital possibilities and dilemmas concerning their adult children’s futures. It will also examine the ways in which tech-savvy adult children communicate and negotiate with parents about their digital aspirations. In doing so, the study will reveal how intergenerational relationships, family-cultural obligations and parental authority are (re)constructed and/or rearticulated in a new digital context. Connecting sociology of work, family studies and research on digital technologies, the study will offer new insights into the interplay of unfolding intergenerational dynamics and the digital creative economy. First, by shifting focus from individuals/individual workers to the larger family networks in which they are embedded, the study will unpack how new family tensions, ambivalence and/or solidarity emerge in response to today’s increasingly platformatised economy and labour market. Second, it will contribute to ongoing debate on the impact of changing socio-economic conditions on Confucian ideals of family life in the context of digitisation. Third, it will address the imbalance in previous research, which has focused on the unidirectional influence of parents on (adult) children’s occupational aspirations, by investigating whether and how knowledge of digital technologies and self-entrepreneurial capacities may stimulate younger generations’ sense of agency and transform their relationships and interactions with older generations in the family. Practically, this research will inform policy to promote the new creative sectors, contribute to the work–life enrichment of digital workers, and advance relevant public knowledge and debates in Hong Kong and beyond. 愈來愈多精通科技的年輕人，選擇投身於數碼平台經濟中新興的（次）領域，內容創作與網絡影響力行銷、電子競技與對戰型遊戲，以及直播購物與電子商貿。這股新興職涯趨勢，對傳統家庭文化中的期望、規範與安排帶來了深刻的轉變與挑戰。儘管現有關於平台化工作的研究文獻頗豐，既有文獻較集中探討勞動者面對的工作不穩定、演算法控制及工作與生活失衡等議題，然而對於這類非標準工作型態對代際關係及家庭生活之影響，以及這些影響如何進一步塑造青年之平台職涯路徑，目前的實證研究仍極為有限。這種研究落差在以強調代際連結為特徵的華人社會中尤其顯著。本研究擬透過深入訪談，在香港訪問正在或曾經從事平台職涯的年輕成年人及其父母，從而成為首批系統性探討家庭如何面對數碼創意經濟中種種機遇與矛盾的研究之一。研究將聚焦父母對於子女未來投身數碼職涯的觀感與回應，亦會探討具科技素養之成年子女如何與父母溝通與協商其數碼志向。藉此，研究將揭示在新的數碼情境下，代際關係、家庭文化責任與父母權威如何被（重新）建構及／或再詮釋。結合工作社會學、家庭研究與數碼科技研究三大領域，旨在提供對當代代際動態與數碼創意經濟互動機制的嶄新理解。首先，透過由個人/個體勞動者視角轉向其所嵌入的家庭網絡，研究將分析在平台化經濟與勞動市場背景下，家庭內部如何產生新的關係張力、情感游移與/或成員凝聚。其次，研究將貢獻於有關數碼轉型下社會經濟條件變遷對儒家家庭理想之衝擊的持續討論。第三，研究亦將回應現行文獻長期聚焦父母對（成年）子女職業選擇單向影響的偏頗，探討數碼科技知識與自我創業能力是否及如何激發年輕世代的行動主體性，並進一步改變其與家庭中年長一代之間的關係與互動模式。在實務層面，本研究將有助於政策界理解並推動創意產業的發展，促進數碼勞動者的工作與生活質素，並擴展香港及其他地區相關公共知識與社會討論。

15612525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15612525.value: 打造公平競爭環境：線上教學平台（OTPs）中的語言與性別

15612525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15612525.value: Prof Ahrens, Kathleen Prof Galperin, Hernan

15612525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15612525.value: Gendered differences in communication are recognized across a range of industries and usage domains (Holmes, 2013). In particular, research indicates that women self-promote less than men (Rudman, 1998; Rudman & Glick, 2021). Further, women who self-promote are perceived more negatively than men who self-promote (Lindeman et al., 2019). In the context of many online labor platforms, avoiding self-promotion is essentially impossible due to platforms’ reliance on self-written profiles (Blyth et al., 2024). This is also true on online tutoring platforms (OTPs). Crucially, gendered differences in self-promotional language may be a contributing factor to women’s lower-than-expected prices on these platforms. To date, however, little research has examined differences between men’s and women’s self-promotional language in the context of digital labor platforms. To fill this gap and thereby contribute to theorizing the impacts of gendered communication, this study examines the types of self-promotional discourse that are most effective on OTPs and whether their effectiveness varies depending on the tutor’s or student’s gender, as well as the student’s goals. Factors likely contribute to women earning less than men on OTPs include customers’ gender stereotypes as well as gender-based differences in self-promotion. Success in online markets requires workers to self-promote via self-written descriptions of their skills and services. In the context of OTPs, these self-written profiles play a major role in determining students’ choice of tutor, and this may contribute to the gender wage gap. The proposed project will examine both the self-written profiles and their effects on students via two interrelated studies. The first study investigates the differences between men’s and women’s self-written profiles via an analysis of existing profiles (n = 200) of English tutors from Hong Kong and Mainland China, complemented by an in-depth analysis of the linguistic features of 40 select profiles. The second study uses a survey experiment (n = 1,600) to assess how different tutor profiles (varied by gender and language) influence students’ preferences for tutors, as well as how students’ gender and learning goals influence students’ preferences. The proposed research will contribute to an under-explored aspect of gendered communication by identifying language-based differences in men’s and women’s self-promotion on digital labor platforms. The findings will also address linguistic aspects of the gender pay gap and contribute to stereotype communication scholarship. 在眾多產業與使用情境中，性別化的溝通差異已廣為人知（Holmes, 2013）。研究指出，女性在自我推銷方面的表現通常不如男性積極（Rudman, 1998；Rudman & Glick, 2021），而當女性採取自我推銷策略時，所受到的社會評價往往也比男性更為負面（Lindeman et al., 2019）。在多數線上勞動平台中，自我推銷幾乎無法避免，因為平台運作普遍仰賴用戶自行撰寫個人簡介（Blyth et al., 2024）。線上教學平台（online tutoring platforms, OTPs）亦是如此。重要的是，性別化的自我推銷語言差異，可能是造成女性教師在此類平台上收費偏低的潛在原因之一。儘管如此，關於男女在這類平台上的自我推銷語言差異，目前的研究仍相當有限。為填補這一研究空白，並拓展對性別語言影響的理論理解，本研究旨在探討在線上教學平台上，哪些類型的自我推銷語言最為有效，以及其有效性是否會因教師性別、學生性別或學生學習目標而有所不同。 造成女性在此類平台上收入較低的原因，可能包括顧客對性別的刻板印象，以及性別化的自我推銷方式差異。要在這些線上市場中取得成功，教學者必須透過自撰簡介來展現自身的技能與服務。就線上教學平台，這些自我介紹對學生的選擇具有決定性影響，也可能影響性別薪資差距。本研究將透過兩項相互關聯的子研究，全面檢視教師簡介及其對學生選擇的影響。第一項研究將分析來自香港與中國大陸的200份英語教師的自我簡介，並選取其中40份進行語言特徵的深入剖析，以比較男性與女性在自我推銷語言上的異同。第二項研究則採用問卷實驗法（樣本數1,600），評估不同性別與語言風格的教師簡介如何影響學生對教師的偏好，同時探討學生自身的性別與學習目標對其選擇的傾向。 本研究將為性別化語言在數位勞動平台中的作用提供新見解，揭示男女在自我推銷策略上的語言差異。研究結果亦將進一步說明語言因素如何影響性別薪資差異，並對刻板印象與溝通的研究領域做出實質貢獻。

15613825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15613825.value: 虛擬現實（VR）催眠對改善中國兒童癌症康復者睡眠障礙的有效性：混合方法隨機對照試驗

15613825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15613825.value: Dr Cheng , Wai Tsoi Frankie Prof LAM, Ka Wai Katherine Dr Li , Shirley Xin Dr Poon, Connie Ms Qi, LIU Dr Tyrovolas, Stefanos Dr Wassing, Rick Dr Wong, King Ho Carlos Prof Yeung, Wing-Fai Prof Yorke, Janelle

15613825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15613825.value: Background: Poor sleep is commonly reported by Hong Kong Chinese childhood cancer survivors (CCSs). Combining virtual reality (VR) with hypnosis is a feasible treatment option. However, its effectiveness on sleep outcomes has yet to be investigated. Objective: The objectives are to examine the effectiveness of VR hypnosis on subjective sleep quality and objective sleep parameters among Hong Kong CCSs; explore the change in brain electrophysiological activities during sleep among the survivors who have received VR hypnosis; determine the cost-effectiveness of VR hypnosis; and explore technological challenges of VR hypnosis. Study design: A mixed method randomised controlled trial will be employed.
