A sample of 186 CCSs aged 12 to 18 years will be recruited and randomized into: (1) VR hypnosis group (n=62), who will wear a VR headset to individually receive 30-minute hypnosis one time a week for six weeks, (2) VR relaxation group (n=62), who will individually receive a VR relaxation but without hypnosis component (time and attention will be the same as for the VR hypnosis), and (3) CBT-I group (n=62), who will receive a six 30-minute sessions of CBT-I. Participants will complete questionnaires and wear an Actiwatch to assess their subjective and objective sleep parameters and quality of life at baseline, on completion of the intervention, and at 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-up. The VR hypnosis group will also undergo electroencephalogram (EEG) to assess change in the brain electrophysiological activities before and after the completion of the intervention and at 6 months and complete a validated questionnaire for perceived usefulness and ease of use at 6 months. The primary outcome is subjective sleep quality at 6 months. The secondary outcomes include objective sleep variables at 6 months, change in brain electrophysiological activities on the completion of the intervention and at 6 months, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of VR hypnosis at 6 months, and perceived usefulness and ease of use of VR at 6 months. The effectiveness of VR hypnosis on subjective sleep quality and objective sleep parameters will be determined by analysis of covariance. The changes in EEG measures from baseline to post-intervention and 6 months will be analysed using linear mixed models. Cost-effectiveness analysis and cost-utility analysis will be used to calculate ICER between groups at 6 months. The mean scores of perceived usefulness and ease of use for VR hypnosis will be calculated and compared with the norms of a popular technology. 背景：香港華人兒童癌症康復者（CCSs）普遍報告有睡眠質素欠佳的問題。結合虛擬現實（VR）與催眠是一個可行的治療選擇。然而，其對睡眠結果的有效性尚未被研究。 目的：本研究旨在探討VR催眠對香港兒童癌症康復者主觀睡眠質素及客觀睡眠參數的成效；探索接受VR催眠後康復者在睡眠期間腦部電生理活動的變化；評估VR催眠的成本效益；以及探討VR催眠的技術挑戰。 研究設計：本研究將採用混合方法隨機對照試驗。將招募186名年齡介乎12至18歲的兒童癌症康復者，並隨機分為三組：(1) VR催眠組（n=62），參加者每週一次、每次30分鐘，佩戴VR頭盔進行個人催眠，為期六週；(2) VR放鬆組（n=62），參加者同樣每週一次、每次30分鐘，接受VR放鬆但不包括催眠成分（時間及關注度與VR催眠組相同）；(3) CBT-I組（n=62），參加者接受六次、每次30分鐘的CBT-I治療。所有參加者將於基線、干預結束時，以及1、3及6個月的隨訪時，完成問卷並佩戴Actiwatch以評估其主觀及客觀睡眠參數及生活質素。VR催眠組亦會於干預前後及6個月時進行腦電圖（EEG）檢查，以評估腦部電生理活動的變化，並於6個月時完成一份已驗證的問卷，以評估其對VR催眠的有用性及易用性的感受。 主要結果指標為6個月時的主觀睡眠質素。次要結果指標包括6個月時的客觀睡眠參數、干預結束及6個月時腦部電生理活動的變化、6個月時VR催眠的增量成本效益比（ICER），以及6個月時對VR催眠的有用性及易用性的感受。 VR催眠對主觀睡眠質素及客觀睡眠參數的成效將以協方差分析（ANCOVA）進行評估。EEG指標由基線至干預後及6個月的變化將以線性混合模型分析。成本效益分析及成本效用分析將用於計算各組於6個月時的ICER。VR催眠的有用性及易用性平均分數將計算並與主流科技的標準進行比較。

15614425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15614425.value: 表達紡織藝術與時尚介入對抑鬱發作患者情緒功能及生活質量的影響：隨機對照試驗

15614425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15614425.value: Prof Cheung, Mei-chun Prof Chui, Eric Wing Hong

15614425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15614425.value: In recent years, numerous studies have explored the effect of the arts on health and well-being in various social contexts to counter inequalities and increase engagement. Participation in the arts and access to a range of arts opportunities can dramatically improve health outcomes and increase well-being (Aylett, 2012). Textile arts intervention provides early tactile experience to shape and characterize the emotional, relational, cognitive and neural functioning of participants (Hass-Cohen, Kim, & Mangassarian, 2015). However, limited studies have demonstrated therapeutic effects and the relationships between depression, clothing and self-concept. This study makes the first attempt to conduct a scientific evidence-based evaluation of the beneficial effects on emotional function and quality of life of people with depressive episode through a mixed-methods randomized controlled trail (RCT). A randomized, controlled and single-blind pilot study with a pre-test and post-test design was conducted among 16 people with depressive episode from two local NGOs. A total of 16 consenting participants who were diagnosed with mild to moderate depression as defined by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) (score: >5–14) at baseline measurement met the proposed inclusion criteria. The experimental group (EG; n=7) attended ten 1-hour twice weekly sessions expressive textile arts and fashion-based (ETAFB) intervention over 5 weeks. The control group (CG; n=7) was not subjected to any intervention. All the participants were subjected to a preintervention test and 5-week postintervention test by using the Profile of Mood States (POMS) and World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF). In the preliminary findings, ETAFB intervention was associated with a significant improvement of emotional functioning in the anger, confusion, vigor, and total mood subscales of the POMS, and the enhancement of quality of life particularly in the psychological and social relationships domains of the WHOQOL-BREF. This study aims to investigate the benefits of ETAFB intervention as a treatment for individuals with depression in community settings. The primary outcomes include measures of emotional mood states using POMS. The secondary outcomes are the measures of depression severity using PHQ-9 and the improvement of quality of life, which will be measured by WHOQOL-BREF. A structured ETAFB intervention program framework integrated with the theory of expressive therapies continuum and a co-design model was developed for facilitating scientific evidence-based evaluation. It is hypothesized that participants will show improved emotional functioning, psychosocial outcomes and quality of life after the 5-week intervention.

15615525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15615525.value: 提升對普通話與粵語雙語兒童發展性語言障礙的識別：建立參考標準與嶄新評估方法

15615525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15615525.value: Prof Chen, Si Prof Chiat, Shula Prof Mak, Man Wai Dr Ng, Wing-Yee, Cymie Dr Polišenská, Kamila Dr Yang, Wenchun

15615525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15615525.value: Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) is a specific language learning disability that impacts academic outcomes, mental health, and career development. Despite these negative impacts, when identified and provided with appropriate language intervention, DLD has been shown to be responsive to treatment. Affecting about 2 children in every class of 30, DLD is more prevalent than Autism. Accurate identification of DLD in bilingual Chinese-speaking children is a long-standing global challenge, particularly for Mandarin-Cantonese bilingual children in Hong Kong. This project, an extension of our research team's work and expertise, aims to address a critical barrier in diagnosing DLD in these children: the lack of a reference standard, without which there is no basis to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of new assessment measures. This absence of a reference standard also hinders research progress on understanding DLD among bilingual Chinese-speaking children, creating a cyclical problem. The project has two objectives: (i) develop a reference standard for identifying DLD in Mandarin-Cantonese bilingual children; and (ii) evaluate the diagnostic accuracies of novel assessment measures alone and in combination using this reference standard. The recently published Bilingual Multidimensional Ability Scale (B-MAS) framework (Wang et al., 2024) will be adapted, incorporating newly developed bilingual screening tools and European COST Action Language Impairment Testing in Multilingual Settings (LITMUS) tools adapted for Mandarin and Cantonese. Indirect measures of children's language-related functional abilities will be included, aligning with the UK CATALISE criteria recently adopted by the Hong Kong Association of Speech Therapists. The project will screen 300 first-graders from Hong Kong primary schools, followed by comprehensive bilingual testing of 90 children who score below the 30th percentile in the bilingual screening. The B-MAS rating tool will be adapted for Mandarin and Cantonese, and three expert raters will independently rate each case profile. This project is uniquely positioned to advance our understanding of DLD in Chinese bilingual children, a population underrepresented in research despite the global prevalence of Chinese speakers. The outcomes will include an evidence-based reference standard and novel assessment measures that will change how clinicians and researchers assess and identify DLD in this population. This project will bring Chinese DLD research in line with current international trends and standards. The new dataset generated lays the groundwork for leveraging technological advancements, such as fine-tuning Automatic Speech Recognition Models, developing automatic scoring systems, and creating machine learning models for TD/DLD classification, to improve the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of future assessment practices. 發展性語言障礙（DLD）是一種特定的語言學習障礙，對兒童的學業表現、精神健康及長遠的職業發展均會構成負面影響。儘管如此，研究證實，若能及早識別並提供適切的語言治療，此症對治療有良好反應。此症的普遍程度比自閉症更高，在每班約30名學童中，便有2名兒童受其影響。要準確識別華語雙語兒童的發展性語言障礙，一直是全球面對的長期挑戰，對香港的普通話與粵語雙語兒童而言，這個問題尤其突出。本項目建基於我們研究團隊的現有成果與專業知識，旨在處理診斷這類兒童時所面對的一項關鍵障礙：缺乏一套參考標準。沒有這套標準，我們便無從判斷新評估工具的診斷準確度。同時，參考標準的缺失亦窒礙了學界對華語雙語兒童發展性語言障礙的理解和研究進展，形成惡性循環。 本項目有兩大目標：(i) 為識別普通話與粵語雙語兒童的「發展性語言障礙」，建立一套參考標準；(ii) 利用此標準，檢驗各項嶄新評估工具在獨立及組合使用時的診斷準確度。項目將改編近期發表的「雙語多維能力量表」（Bilingual Multidimensional Ability Scale, B-MAS）框架（Wang et al., 2024），並納入新開發的雙語篩查工具，以及針對普通話和粵語改編的「歐洲科學技術合作行動 （COST ACTION ）：多語社會中的語言障礙：語言模式與評估之路（LITMUS）」系列工具。項目亦會納入兒童語言相關功能表現的間接評估方法，與英國近期獲香港言語治療師協會採納的「語言障礙的標準與術語應用：綜合實證研究」（CATALISE）準則接軌。本項目將於香港小學篩選300名一年級學童，並對當中在雙語篩查中得分低於第30百分位數的90名兒童，進行全面的雙語評估。「雙語多維能力量表」將為普通話及粵語進行改編，並由三位專家評分員獨立為每個案進行評分。 本項目具備獨特條件，能增進學界對華語雙語兒童發展性語言障礙的理解。儘管華語雙語使用者遍佈全球，這一人群在相關研究中卻長期缺乏足夠代表性。項目成果將包括一套具實證基礎的參考標準及多項嶄新評估工具，為臨床人員及研究學者日後評估與識別此症的方式帶來革新。此外，本項目將推動本地的華語發展性語言障礙研究與當前的國際趨勢及標準接軌。項目產生的新數據庫，將為善用各項先進科技奠定基礎，例如微調自動語音識別模型、開發自動評分系統，以及建立用於區分正常發展與發展性語言障礙案例的機器學習模型等，從而提升未來評估工作的效率、信度及可擴展性。

15615825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15615825.value: 以應用語言學方法探討外傭培訓與招聘中的語言學及社會實踐

15615825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15615825.value: While migrant domestic workers’ (MDWs) life stories in the diaspora are relatively well described, there is little research that looks at their migratory journey before and after migration. We know little about what has impacted their life before they migrate, and in order to understand why so many especially Indonesian MDWs struggle while working overseas, we need to examine more closely their migratory journey in its entirety. This project will explore how Indonesian MDWs are recruited and trained before they are sent to Hong Kong. The pre-departure training of Indonesian MDWs will document how future MDWs are prepared for work in Hong Kong. In 2019 alone, 16 Indonesian MDWs committed suicide while working in Hong Kong, and this suggests that the pre-departure training they receive is insufficient in terms of preparing them for the hardships they endure in the city. Previous research concludes that Indonesian MDWs find their pre-departure training demeaning and humiliating (Ladegaard, 2024), and the current project will further explore these issues. It will collect evidence about how they are taught Cantonese, how they are marketed to recruiters from Hong Kong, and what they are taught about Hong Kong ‘culture’, and what advise they receive about the relationship they should have with their new employers. The expected outcomes of the project have the potential to explain why Indonesian MDWs are more severely exploited and abused than Filipino migrant workers, and why they are more likely to put up with mistreatment. The project also has potential for social impact by instigating change in DMWs’ training in Indonesia. 描述外傭海外生活故事的記錄相對較多，卻鮮有研究關注她們移居前後的歷程。我們不甚了解外傭移居前的生活受到何種因素影響。大量外傭赴外工作時都會經歷困境，尤以印傭為甚，要了解箇中原因，我們需要更深入地探究她們的整個移居歷程。本研究將探討印尼外傭在被派遣到香港之前的招募及培訓過程。印傭出發前的培訓，記載了她們為赴港工作所做的準備。單是2019年，就有16名印傭在香港工作期間自殺，顯示她們在赴港前接受的培訓 並不足以協助她們應付在香港面臨的困境。之前的研究總結出，印傭認為其出國前的培訓帶有貶低及羞辱成分（Ladegaard, 2024），本研究將會進一步探討這些問題。本研究將收集證據，了解她們如何學習廣東話、香港的招聘人員如何推銷她們、她們被灌輸了哪些香港「文化」，以及她們在與新僱主關係方面得到了甚麼建議。本研究之預期成果或可解釋為何印傭遭受的剝削和虐待較菲傭嚴重，以及為何她們忍受虐待的機會較大。本研究亦有望為印傭培訓帶來改變，產生社會影響。

15615925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15615925.value: 鄉學與理學 以宋代福建莆陽為例

15615925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15615925.value: While established studies have illustrated how Neo-Confucianism successfully penetrated various regions in the Southern Song, this project examines how some local literati resisted its spread or at best accepted it in a limited manner. Pursued from the perspective of local history, my study views Neo-Confucianism as a coercive external force, aiming to properly restore agency to the local literati who nonetheless had to confront the growth and dissemination of the Neo-Confucian ideas and teachings. It will be shown that the local men of learning were by no means passive recipients of Neo-Confucianism, their encounter with which was a continuous process of adaptation, acculturation, and even subversion in various scholarly contexts and traditions. Puyang (莆陽) in Fujian is a case in point. During the Northern Song, Puyang produced over four hundred jinshi in the imperial examination, ranking fourth nationwide. The noteworthy fact here is that Puyang had a strong local literati community, a well-established mature intellectual tradition, and a powerful political network that supported and patronized local scholarship. While the expansion of Neo-Confucianism in the Southern Song met with less counteraction in regions with less entrenched academic traditions, scholars from Puyang, with their deep-rooted traditions, put up significant resistance. I will examine how the gradually flourishing Neo-Confucianism in the mid-Southern Song infiltrated Puyang, highlighting the contestations as local scholars negotiated between native traditions and external Neo-Confucianism. In a nuanced fashion, my research reveals the many ways in which they acculturated their local scholarship to the new intellectual world of Neo-Confucian predominance, ultimately securing a historiographic place within the highly influential Qing era compilation of the Song Yuan xue'an 宋元學案. This study, in some significant ways, is also a reexamination and reinterpretation of the composition of the Song Yuan xue'an, which has long furnished the foundation for the modern understanding of Song-Yuan scholarship. A careful analysis of its compilation and contents reveals that many of the academic lineages are regionalized, featuring leaders and their respective disciples and followers from the same regions. This indicates that after the Southern Song, the well-known historical phenomenon of localization involved local scholarship. Various local academic traditions, especially that of the intellectual renowned Puyang, competed for prominence as they continuously interacted with Neo-Confucianism both in terms of absorption and resistance, ultimately earning their inclusion as distinctly identifiable schools or lineages in the Song-Yuan xue'an. 既有研究指出，程朱理學在南宋成功滲透到各個地區，但本計畫則考察一些地方士子如何抗拒其傳播，或最多以有限的方式接受它。從地方史的視角出發，我的研究將程朱之學視為一種外來的壓迫力量，旨在恰當地重塑地方士子原有的自主性，因為他們仍不得不面對理學思想與教義的擴展與傳播。研究將顯示，地方學人絕非被動接受新儒學，他們與之的接觸是一個持續的適應、文化融合甚至顛覆的過程，體現在各種學術背景與傳統中。 以福建的莆陽為例。在北宋時期，莆陽在科舉考試中共產生超過四百名進士，位居全國第四。莆陽擁有強大的地方士子社群、成熟的知識傳統以及支援和資助地方學術的強大政治網絡。南宋理學的擴展在學術傳統較不根深蒂固的地區遇到較少反抗，但具有深厚傳統的莆陽學者則展現出較大的抵抗。我將探討南宋中晚期理學逐漸興盛時期，如何滲透到莆陽，並突顯地方學者在本土傳統與外來新儒學之間的抗衡與協商。在細膩的分析中，研究揭示他們是如何將本土學術與新儒學的主導思想融合，最終在具有影響力的清代《宋元學案》中，佔據醒目的一席之地。

15616225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15616225.value: 第二階段調節式中介分析的優化方法

15616225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15616225.value: Dr Chan, Wai Dr Kwan, Lok Yin Joyce

15616225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15616225.value: Moderated mediation analysis examines how mediating mechanisms vary across specific conditions and has experienced significant growth in applied research. From 240 publications in 2013-2014, the number rose to 699 in 2017-2018, and 1,770 in 2021-2023. This project will focus on second stage moderated mediation analysis, which has been utilized in nearly half of the moderated mediation papers published in 2023. Despite the extensive use of second stage moderated mediation analysis, two critical observations warrant attention. First, the specification of the second stage moderated mediation model overlaps with some alternative models (e.g., a direct moderation model). This implies that researchers are unable to statistically determine whether the claims of a moderated mediation effect or a direct moderation effect are more valid. Second, this specification fails to represent the index of moderated mediation through two connected pathways, conflicting with the traditional understanding of product coefficients (e.g., as in indirect effects). This renders it difficult for researchers to grasp the conceptual meaning of this index. Overall, these observations suggest that the conventional specification for the second stage moderated mediation model is incomplete. To fill this gap, this project aims to revisit the conventional specification of this model for both manifest and latent variables. In this research proposal, we will identify problems in the conventional specification and propose a refined specification in Part I (Manifest Second Stage Moderated Mediation Analysis). We will also extend the testing of the refined specification with latent variables in Part II (Latent Second Stage Moderated Mediation Analysis). This project aims to comprehensively develop and evaluate the proposed methods through three distinct phases. Phase 1 (Simulation Studies) will involve conducting two simulation studies to assess the performance of these methods under various data-analytic conditions (e.g., sample size, effect size). Despite being theoretically sound, the empirical performance of the proposed methods remains uncertain. The outcomes of Phase 1 will identify optimal data-analytic conditions to guide researchers in their application. Phase 2 (Real Data Validation) will apply these methods to real data sets, validating moderated mediation findings from existing studies. The results will inform researchers about the appropriate contexts for using these methods and the robustness of existing findings. In Phase 3 (Method Implementation), we will develop two statistical tools: a syntax-based R package and a graphics-based Shiny web app. These tools aim to reduce the burden of executing the methods, facilitating easier implementation for researchers.

15616625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15616625.value: 香港庇護工場的參與式設計

15616625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15616625.value: Prof Hou, Jeffrey Prof Lian, Fei Prof Zou, Guangtian

15616625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15616625.value: Sheltered workshops, designed to provide employment opportunities for persons with disabilities (PWD), have played a central role in rehabilitation services for over a century. In Hong Kong, the number of sheltered workshops has grown significantly since their inception in 1949, particularly following key policy developments in the 1970s and 1980s. Today, the city’s sheltered workshops serve more than 5,000 people with disabilities, offering tailored workplaces to nurture users’ vocational skills and self-identity and ultimately empower them to contribute actively to society. In practice, however, sheltered workshops face persistent challenges, particularly in achieving their original goal of helping PWD transition to mainstream employment and society. Critics argue that sheltered workshops isolate PWD and hinder their social integration due to outdated facilities, a lack of community engagement and systemic barriers to their involvement in decision-making. Yet few studies to date have asked how the design of these environments can foster greater inclusivity, breaking down the metaphorical ‘walls’ that isolate PWD from participation in society. Improving the environmental design of sheltered workshops and engaging PWD in the design process could help sheltered workshops achieve their mission of promoting social integration. The proposed project will take an evidence-based qualitative approach, combining multiple methods, to identify optimal environmental designs for sheltered workshops that promote inclusivity for users (known as ‘trainees’), especially those with mild intellectual disabilities. The researchers will conduct on-site research of sheltered workshops in the US, Germany and Japan (with further reference to mainland China and Singapore), which have developed unique models and best practices for supporting PWD. By comparing these models and practices, the team will identify strategies for the environmental design of sheltered workshops that can be adapted to Hong Kong. They will gather and analyse the perspectives of key stakeholders, including trainees, government representatives and workshop staff, ensuring that participants’ voices shape the decision-making and design outcomes. Through a series of reviews, design thinking workshops, semi-structured interviews and participatory action research workshops, the project will generate actionable recommendations for improving the spatial layout and functionality of sheltered workshops in Hong Kong and beyond. As well as filling important gaps in design research and social studies, the project’s findings will provide policymakers and practitioners with guidance on designing, renovating and managing sheltered workshops to equip trainees to actively participate in the community, thus building a more inclusive society. 庇護工場旨在為殘疾人士提供就業機會，並在過去一個多世紀中於康復服務中扮演著核心角色。在香港，自1949年首間庇護工場成立以來，其數量顯著增加，特別是在1970及1980年代重要政策發展之後。現時，香港的庇護工場為超過5,000名殘疾人士提供服務，透過度身訂造的工作環境，培養使用者的職業技能和自我認同，最終賦權他們積極貢獻社會。然而，在實踐中，庇護工場面臨持續的挑戰，尤其是在協助殘疾人士過渡到主流就業及融入社會方面未能完全達到原有目標。批評者認為，庇護工場因設施落後、缺乏社區參與及制度性障礙，導致殘疾人士被孤立，阻礙其社會融合。儘管如此，至今鮮有研究探討這些環境的設計如何促進更大的包容性，打破將殘疾人士與社會參與隔離的「隱形高牆」。改善庇護工場的環境設計，並讓殘疾人士參與設計過程，有助於庇護工場實現促進社會融合的使命。本研究計劃將採用循證的質性方法，結合多種研究方式，找出能促進包容性的庇護工場環境設計。研究團隊將實地考察不同地方的庇護工場，這些地區已發展出獨特的模式及最佳實踐以支援殘疾人士。通過比較這些模式和實踐，團隊將找出可供香港借鑑的庇護工場環境設計策略。團隊將收集及分析主要持份者的意見，包括學員、政府代表及工場職員，確保參與者的聲音能夠影響決策及設計成果。透過文獻回顧、設計思維工作坊、半結構式訪談及參與式行動研究工作坊，計劃將提出可行的建議，以改善香港及其他地區庇護工場的空間佈局及功能。除了填補設計研究及社會研究的重要空白外，計劃成果亦將為政策制定者及實踐者提供指引，協助他們設計、翻新及管理庇護工場，使學員能夠積極參與社區，從而建立更具包容性的社會。

15617125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15617125.value: 住房與香港低收入兒童的健康發展：一項前瞻性縱向隊列研究

15617125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15617125.value: Dr Han, Yaeeun Prof Lau, Yi Hung Eva

15617125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15617125.value: Housing provides an important physical and social environment for children's development, social-emotional functioning, and academic performance. In particular, children at early ages grow and develop exponentially and spend considerable time at home every day. Therefore, the role of housing in shaping early childhood development is considered crucial. While the linkage between housing and child outcomes has been well-documented in the literature, how this relationship operates in Hong Kong has been poorly understood. Given the socioeconomic disparities in children's health outcomes and pressing housing difficulties among disadvantaged groups in Hong Kong, more cross-sectoral efforts have been urged for Hong Kong children's health and well-being, particularly among those from low-income families. In response, we propose a prospective longitudinal study to examine the effects of housing on the healthy development of low-income young children in Hong Kong. Utilising the PI's prior study (2023-2024) as baseline data (Wave 1), we will track the health and development of low-income children aged two to seven in relation to their housing conditions in two follow-up surveys (Wave 2 in Year 1, Wave 3 in Year 3). Drawing on the bioecological model of human development, the proposed research will be guided by four research questions. First, we will investigate which housing factors have more salient effects on child development than others and whether these relationships differ across different child, family, and neighbourhood attributes. Second, we will identify which domains of child development and developmental stages are susceptible to inadequate housing conditions, and how the effects of housing on child development change over time. Third, we will attempt to explain why and how housing influences child development, focusing on the mediating roles of the residents' subjective housing experience and parents' psychological well-being. Finally, we will evaluate if Hong Kong's housing assistance or improvement programs can mitigate the adverse effects of housing on low-income children's development. This research will provide empirical evidence on the importance of housing in healthy child development and inform housing interventions that can contribute to making a child-friendly city. This study will also serve as the baseline data for future longer-term studies tracking low-income children from their early childhood to adolescence and adulthood. 住房為兒童的身心發展、社會情緒功能和學業表現提供了重要的物質和社會環境。尤其值得一提的是，幼兒時期的兒童成長發育呈指數級增長，每天在家中度過大量時間。因此，住房在塑造兒童早期發展中的作用至關重要。雖然住房與兒童發展結果之間的關聯已在文獻中得到充分證實，但這種關係在香港的具體運作機制尚不清楚。鑑於香港兒童健康狀況的社會經濟差異以及弱勢群體面臨的緊迫住房困難，人們呼籲加強跨領域、多方協作，以保障香港兒童，尤其是來自低收入家庭的兒童的健康和福祉。為此，我們提出一項前瞻性縱向研究，以探討住房對香港低收入幼兒健康發展的影響。我們將利用首席研究員（PI）於2023–2024年的研究作為基線數據（第一輪），透過兩次後續調查（第一年第二輪，第三年第三輪）追蹤兩至七歲低收入兒童的健康和發展與其住房條件的關係。借鑒人類發展的生物生態模型，本研究將圍繞著四個研究問題。首先，我們將探討哪些住屋因素對兒童發展的影響比其他因素更為顯著，以及這些關係是否因兒童、家庭和鄰裡因素的不同而有所差異。其次，我們將確定哪些兒童發展的領域和發展階段容易受到住房條件不足的影響，以及住房對兒童發展的影響如何隨時間變化。第三，我們將嘗試解釋住房影響兒童發展的原因和方式，特別關注居民的主觀住房體驗和父母心理健康的中介作用。最後，我們將評估香港的住房援助或改善計畫能否減輕住房對低收入兒童發展的負面影響。本研究將提供實證證據，闡明住房對兒童健康發展的重要性，並為有助於建設兒童友善城市的住房干預措施提供參考。本研究也將為未來追蹤低收入兒童從幼兒期到青少年期及成年期的長期研究提供基線數據。

15617225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15617225.value: 香港中文字體設計的傳承與發展：1950至2000年代的歷史軌跡、本土美學與協作影響

15617225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15617225.value: This research project thoroughly investigates the history and cultural dimensions of type design in Hong Kong from 1950s to 2020s, addressing the lack of scholarly attention to this topic. It recognizes the significant influence of Japanese culture on Hong Kong's design landscape, particularly in the development of Chinese type design. By examining collaborations between Hong Kong and Japanese type designers, the research aims to uncover motivations and implications driving these partnerships and their impact on the evolution of Chinese type design in Hong Kong. Additionally, the project explores the unique characteristics and aesthetic foundations of typography in Hong Kong through a comparative analysis of Japanese and Chinese type design within the local context. It highlights the influence of Japanese aesthetics on Hong Kong's typographic landscape and identifies distinct elements in Chinese type design. The study traces the historical trajectory of Hong Kong type design to provide a comprehensive understanding of its evolution. By examining the cultural, historical, and design-related factors that have shaped Hong Kong's typographic landscape, this research contributes to the existing knowledge base. It reveals how diverse cultural influences, including Chinese and Japanese, have influenced type design in Hong Kong. The project also investigates the impact of sociopolitical shifts and technological advancements on Chinese type design in the city. This research sheds light on the dynamic nature and progression of typography in Hong Kong by exploring collaborations and influences between Hong Kong and Japanese type designers. It examines their role in shaping Chinese type design, contributing to its distinct identity and cultural significance. The study further explores innovative design strategies employed by Hong Kong designers to bridge traditional Chinese characters with contemporary aesthetics. Ultimately, this research project provides valuable insights into the historical legacies, vernacular aesthetics, and collaborative influences that have shaped Chinese type design in Hong Kong. It enhances our understanding of the relationship between Japanese and Hong Kong type design, offering a comprehensive overview of unique typographic traditions within the city. These insights can inform future design practices, cultural preservation efforts, and educational initiatives aimed at celebrating and promoting the rich heritage of Chinese type design in Hong Kong. The study contributes to the preservation, recognition, and continued evolution of Chinese type design in Hong Kong's dynamic design landscape. 本研究項目全面探討自1950年代至2020年代香港中文字體設計的歷史與文化面向，回應學術界對此議題關注不足的現象。研究指出日本文化對香港設計界，尤其在中文字體設計發展方面，具有深遠影響。透過分析香港與日本字體設計師之間的合作，本研究旨在揭示這些合作背後的動機與意義，以及其對香港中文字體設計演變所產生的影響。 此外，研究通過比較日本與中國字體設計在香港本地語境下的異同，深入探討香港字體設計的獨特特徵及美學基礎。研究強調日本美學對香港字體設計的影響，同時辨識出中文字體設計中的獨特元素。研究亦梳理香港字體設計的歷史脈絡，提供其演變過程的全面理解。 本研究從文化、歷史及設計等多重角度，分析塑造香港字體設計景觀的各種因素，豐富現有學術知識。研究揭示多元文化，包括中日文化，如何影響香港的字體設計發展。項目亦探討社會政治變遷及科技進步對香港中文字體設計的影響。 透過深入分析香港與日本字體設計師的合作及相互影響，本研究展現香港字體設計的動態發展，並探討其在塑造本地中文字體設計獨特身份及文化意義上的角色。研究亦進一步探討香港設計師如何運用創新設計策略，將傳統漢字與當代美學融合。 最終，本研究項目為香港中文字體設計的歷史傳承、本土美學及協作影響提供寶貴見解，深化對日本與香港字體設計關係的理解，並全面呈現本地獨特的字體設計傳統。這些洞見有助於未來設計實踐、文化保育及教育推廣，促進香港中文字體設計豐富傳承的發展。研究亦有助於香港動態設計界中中文字體設計的保存、認同及持續演化。

15617425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15617425.value: 香港粵語孤獨症兒童的聲調感知：基於行為和腦電圖指標的年齡差異研究

15617425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15617425.value: Prof CHEN, Fei Dr RONG, Yicheng

15617425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15617425.value: Autistic individuals are frequently reported to exhibit atypical neural processing of pitch, which may impact their social and communicative activities, especially among those speaking tone languages where the pitch is an essential suprasegmental element in contrasting lexical meanings (i.e., lexical tone). There is evidence from typically developing (TD) children speaking tone languages that lexical tone processing progresses with their accumulative native tone language experience. However, little is known whether such experience can improve lexical tone processing in tone-language-speaking children with autism following the same way as in TD peers. To investigate age-related differences in lexical tone perception in autistic speakers of a tone language, we will conduct behavioral and EEG experiments on Cantonese-speaking autistic children aged between six and ten in Hong Kong (HK), with an even distribution of participants across this age range. Their performance will be compared with age- matched TD children. Using the EEG measurements, we will investigate how native language experience shapes the neural processing of naturally produced lexical tones at two levels: pre-attentive and attentive levels. Moreover, whether the neural mechanisms responsible for processing pitch height and pitch slope develop with a synchronous rate is also of interest in the current project. We also seek to explore the role of age in fine-grained lexical tone perception in HK Cantonese-speaking autistic children. Whether the finding based on Mandarin-speaking children can be carried over to Cantonese-speaking children remains unclear, since Cantonese differs from Mandarin in tone system and autism is subject to the influence of culture and language. In order to gain a comprehensive comprehension of the connection between lexical tone perception and autism spectrum disorders (ASD), we will investigate how the varying characteristics within this population affect the processing of lexical tones, both at the level of behavior and neural activity. Specifically, we will assess autistic symptom severity, language ability, and executive functions to examine their relationships with different aspects of lexical tone perception. One novelty of the current project is investigating age-related differences in lexical tone processing in autistic children speaking a tone language, using both behavioral and neural measures. This project will contribute new insights into the cognitive theories of sensory processing abnormalities in ASD, which have primarily been based on research conducted in non-tonal languages. In addition, it will uncover the roles of language experience, executive function, symptom severity in pitch processing. 孤獨症個體常被報道在音高處理的神經機制上表現出非典型特徵，這可能影響其社交和溝通活動，尤其是在使用聲調語言的群體中，因為音高作為一種超音段信息，是區分詞意的重要特徵（即詞彙聲調或聲調）。研究表明，在聲調語言背景的典型發展（TD）兒童中，隨着母語聲調語言經驗的積累，其聲調處理能力會逐步提升。然而，目前尚不清楚，這種語言經驗積累是否能夠以與TD兒童相同的方式，促進聲調語言背景孤獨症兒童的聲調處理能力。為研究聲調語言背景孤獨症兒童在聲調感知中的年齡相關差異，我們計劃對香港（HK）6至10歲的粵語背景孤獨症兒童進行行為和腦電圖（EEG）實驗，並將其表現與同齡的TD兒童進行比較。通過EEG數據，我們將探討母語經驗如何在兩個層次上塑造聲調的神經處理：前注意階段和注意階段。此外，本研究還將探討處理音高高度和音高斜度的神經機制是否以同步發展。我們還計劃進一步探索年齡在香港粵語背景孤獨症兒童精細化聲調感知中的作用。基於普通話背景兒童的研究結果是否適用於粵語背景兒童仍不明確，因為粵語的聲調系統與普通話存在顯著差異，而孤獨症的表現也受到文化和語言的共同影響。 為全面理解聲調感知與孤獨症譜系障礙（ASD）之間的關係，研究將進一步探討該群體內部的不同特徵如何影響聲調的處理，包括行為層面和神經活動層面。具體而言，我們將評估孤獨症癥狀的嚴重程度、語言能力及執行功能，並分析這些因素與聲調感知不同方面之間的關係。本研究的一大創新之處在於，首次結合行為和神經測量方法，系統探討聲調語言背景孤獨症兒童在聲調處理中的年齡相關差異。本研究將為ASD中感官處理異常的認知理論提供新見解，這些理論此前主要基於非聲調語言背景群體的研究。此外，本研究還將揭示語言經驗、執行功能以及癥狀嚴重程度在音高處理中的作用。

15618125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15618125.value: 中國農村兒童問題性互聯網使用：基於多群體視角的縱向混合研究

15618125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15618125.value: Prof Shek, Daniel, Tan Lei Prof Yu, Lu Dr Yu, Yanping Dr Zhou, Jianhua Dr Zhou, Zheng

15618125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15618125.value: Problematic internet use (PIU) among children and adolescents is a global concern and can lead to adverse developmental outcomes, such as physical and mental health disorders, and low well-being. Nevertheless, few studies have examined PIU among rural Chinese children, even though they are relatively vulnerable to poor family functioning and inadequate educational resources caused by urban-rural dual differentiation and unequal development in China. Guided by a comprehensive social-cognitive-ecological model, this study will investigate the developmental mechanisms of PIU by exploring how family functioning affects children’s internet use, and how children’s self-regulation processes (self-efficacy, self-control) and school ecology (school climate, extracurricular activities, digital literacy) affect that link. Specifically, we will address the following four research questions: 1) How does family functioning predict rural children’s PIU over time? 2) How does family functioning shape rural children’s PIU through the mediating effects of self-efficacy and self-control? 3) How does school ecology moderate the relationship between family functioning and PIU in rural children? 4) How do different stakeholders (i.e., children, parents, and educators) view the development and prevention of PIU based on their own narratives? An explanatory mixed methods design with two phases (quantitative and qualitative studies) will be conducted. In Phase I, we will conduct a three-wave longitudinal quantitative panel study with a one-year time interval between successive waves, surveying 1,182 children and their parents from 10 primary schools in the rural areas of five provinces in China. This survey will investigate the longitudinal relationships between rural children’s family functioning, self-efficacy, self-control, school ecology, and different types of PIU. In Phase II, we will invite 40 child-parent pairs who have completed the three-wave survey to participate in a qualitative study through theoretical sampling, which will entail in-depth interviews with both children and their parents. In addition, 35 schoolteachers, principals, and local education officials will be invited to join focus group discussions. Multiple informants, including children themselves, parents, and educators, will comment on the survey findings from Phase I and provide additional insights into the developmental and prevention mechanisms of PIU. These research findings will provide insights on PIU prevention and intervention strategies that engage children, parents, and schools, thus contributing to the implementation of extracurricular activities and digital literacy training. The findings will inform policies aimed at families and school education and thus promote the well-being and welfare of children in rural China. 兒童和青少年的問題性互聯網使用是一個全球性議題，可導致不良發展結果，例如：兒童身心發展障礙及低幸福感。由於中國城鄉二元分化以及區域發展不平衡，農村兒童更容易面臨家庭功能失調及教育資源不充分的問題。然而，關於中國農村兒童問題性互聯網使用的相關研究相當有限。 本研究基於社會認知生態綜合模型，通過探究家庭功能如何影響兒童互聯網使用，以及兒童的自我調節過程（自我效能感，自我控制）和學校生態（學校氛圍、課外活動、數碼素養）如何影響這種聯繫，去探究問題性互聯網使用的發展機制。具體而言，我們將解決以下四個研究問題：（1）隨著時間變化，家庭功能如何縱向預測兒童的問題性互聯網使用？（2）家庭功能如何透過自我效能感和自我控制的中介作用去影響兒童的問題性互聯網使用？（3）學校生態如何調節家庭功能與兒童問題性互聯網使用之間的關係？（4）不同群體（兒童、家長和教育工作者）如何看待問題性互聯網使用的形成及預防機制？ 本研究將採用兩階段混合研究設計（包括定量和定性研究）。階段一，我們將在中國五個省份農村地區的10所小學中，對1,182名中國農村兒童及其父母進行三波段（每年一次）的縱向追蹤調查，以探究家庭功能、自我效能感、自我控制、學校生態以及不同類型的問題性互聯網使用之間的縱向關係。階段二，在完整參與了三波段追蹤調查的樣本中，我們將通過理論抽樣法邀請40對親子參與深度訪談，同時組織35名學校教師、校長以及地方教育官員參與焦點小組討論。兒童、父母、教育工作者這三個群體將分別對第一階段的研究結果進行評價，並對問題性互聯網使用的發展及預防機制提出進一步的見解。這些研究結果將為問題性互聯網使用的預防和介入策略提供參考，並能夠推動課外活動及數碼素養培訓項目的實施。此外，本研究還為家庭及學校教育政策的制定提供參考，從而促進中國農村兒童福祉。

15618325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15618325.value: 提升前線同工對院友暴力行為的認知 - 一項隨機對照調查

15618325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15618325.value: Dr Fong, Daniel Prof Lachs, Mark Prof Lai, Wing Leung Daniel Dr Leung, Edward Prof Lou, Weiqun Dr Teresi, Jeanne

15618325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15618325.value: Background Resident-to-resident aggression (RRA) is a public health concern with profound impacts on the well-being and safety of older adults living in residential care facilities (RCFs). There is an urgent need for effective training programmes tailored to frontline workers in residential care settings. Objectives To develop and evaluate a staff training intervention programme for personal care workers (PCWs) with a focus on the understanding, detection, management, and reporting of RRA in Hong Kong. Hypotheses Compared to the matched control group, the intervention group who have completed the training programme would show: (a) a higher level of knowledge in RRA; (b) a greater likelihood of detecting and reporting RRA incidents; and (c) better resident outcomes (e.g., reduced likelihood of injuries/accidents/falls, depression and anxiety, utilisation of urgent or non-routine healthcare services, improved quality of life, etc.). Design and participants A wait-list clustered randomised controlled trial (RCT) will be conducted with a target sample of 174 PCWs and 370 residents. All full-time PCWs who deliver direct care to older residents and all eligible older residents from the sampled RCT units will be included in the proposed study. Data will be derived from PCW surveys, resident/proxy surveys, and PCW on-going record of RRA. The former two surveys will be conducted at three time points: baseline, post-intervention, and 12-month follow-up. Intervention The proposed intervention will be an on-site training programme, with three sessions covering (a) basic knowledge of RRA, (b) appropriate management of RRA incidents, and (c) reporting of RRA and related best practices. Main outcomes Primary outcome is improved knowledge of RRA among staff members. Secondary outcomes include improved detection / reporting of RRA, residents’ exposure to RRA at the 12-month follow-up period, as well as resident physical and psychological health outcomes, including a reduced likelihood of injuries/accidents/falls, improvements in health-related quality of life, reduction in instances of depression, anxiety, and the utilisation of urgent or non-routine healthcare services, and improved performance in daily activities. Contribution of the project The proposed project will provide reliable empirical evidence to support the formulation of the first staff training programme specifically addressing RRA in the Hong Kong context. The intervention facilitated by the project is expected to enhance the ability of staff members to handle RRA incidents, reduce future instances of RRA through early detection and proper management, and enhance the health and well-being of older residents at the RCFs. 護老院的院友之間發生暴力行為是一項重要的公共衛生問題, 直接影響院友的身心健康和個人安全. 我們有急切需要提供有效的訓練課程與院舍的前線同工. 這項研究的目的是開發及評估一個適用於個人護理員的訓練課. 只在提供員工的對院友暴力行為的理解, 發現, 處理, 和報告. 我們推測成功參與訓練的參加者將會對於院友暴力行為有較高的認識, 比較容易發現和舉報這些個案, 院友的情況也較為樂觀 (例如較低受傷或意外風險, 較少抑鬱和焦慮症狀, 較少使用緊急醫療服務, 較高生活質素.) 我們將進行一項隨機對照調查. 招收174名個人護理員及370名院友. 所有參與研究的護理員均在日常照顧院舍長者. 我們將在訓練開展以, 結束後, 及訓練結束12個月後進行調查檢討訓練成效. 訓練包括三節課堂, 概括院友暴力行為的基礎資料, 正確處理手法, 和舉報這些行為的方. 基本研究結果是同工對院友暴力行為的認識, 附加研究結果包括訓練結束後12個月同工發現和舉報院友暴力行為, 院友實際發生的暴力行為, 以及院友的身心健康. 這項研究將有助提升前線同工處理院友暴力行為的能力, 進而減低這些行為在院舍裏發生的比率.

15618625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15618625.value: 從家庭視角探討香港長者精神健康服務中的共同決策：一項混合方法研究

15618625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15618625.value: Prof Bai, Xue Dr Choy, Chak Pui Jacky Dr Tsoh, Mei Yuek Joshua

15618625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15618625.value: Hong Kong's mental health care services are facing increasing strain due to rapid population aging and rising awareness of mental health issues. While accessing mental health services is vital for symptom management and care planning, many individuals, especially older adults, often decline or fail to adhere to recommended treatments. Shared Decision Making (SDM), a collaborative process in which patients, clinicians, and carers jointly decide on treatment, has been shown to improve treatment acceptance, adherence, and patient outcomes. Despite these benefits, older adults in Hong Kong report low levels of involvement in decision-making. Research on SDM in Hong Kong, particularly regarding older adults with mental health conditions, is limited and lacks a comprehensive examination of the family’s role in the process. This study aims to investigate the SDM process in mental health care for older adults from a family perspective, exploring how SDM agreements are reached and how family dynamics influence the process. A explanatory sequential mixed-methods design will be employed. The first phase will involve a quantitative longitudinal study integrated with the 2026 third wave of the Panel Study of Active Ageing and Society (PAAS). This phase will assess how involvement in option discussions leads to SDM agreements, focusing on the roles of control preferences and willingness to compromise in an estimated 300 older adults with experience in mental health SDM. A larger dataset of older adults (estimated N = 1,704) will be used to evaluate how family structure, functioning, and relationships shape the SDM process longitudinally. The second phase will involve qualitative in-depth interviews with 30 older adults, 30 carers, and 15 clinicians experienced in mental health SDM. These interviews will explore participants' perceptions of each other's roles in SDM and the influence of family dynamics on the decision-making process. The findings are expected to refine theoretical models of SDM by identifying key stages and mechanisms, incorporating family perspectives. By uncovering how involvement in SDM, along with individual preferences and flexibility, is shaped by both personal and family characteristics, this study will help define distinct patient/user-family profiles that predict SDM behaviors and inform tailored strategies to meet diverse needs. Findings will the future development of evidence-based practices and policies to optimize SDM in both family and clinical settings, ultimately improving service utilization and adherence outcomes for older adults with mental health concerns and their families.

15619525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15619525.value: 在子女周圍「盤旋」之家長及「躺平」的孩子：探討香港青年之「躺平」傾向及其父母之過度管教之間的關係

15619525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15619525.value: Dr Law, Yee Man, Moon Prof Shek, Daniel, Tan Lei Dr Tam, Hau Lin, Cherry

15619525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15619525.value: Emerging adulthood is an important transition period between adolescence and adulthood during which young people establish their independence, take on responsibilities and explore their adult identity. Recently, the ‘lying flat’ (tang ping, i.e., a state of inactivity and rejection to participate in the competitive rat race) phenomenon has spread among youngsters in mainland China and Hong Kong, and received much attention on social media and from the government. Unfortunately, studies examining the antecedents leading to emerging adults’ lying flat orientation are scarce, particularly regarding the contribution of family socialisation. In the social sciences, over-parenting is considered a developmentally inappropriate parenting style of which parents over-involve and excessively care for their children to ensure their children’s success and happiness. However, researches have shown that over-parenting is associated with negative developmental outcomes among emerging adults. Over-parenting involves a parent–child enmeshment that interferes with emerging adults’ self-differentiation and smooth transition from adolescence to adulthood, extending their dependency on their parents. According to the psychological entitlement model, over-parented emerging adults may perceive that they deserve preferential treatment from their parents (i.e., psychological entitlement), which provides an over-nurturing environment for them to ‘lie flat’. In contrast, the self-determination theory posits that over-parenting restricts emerging adults’ autonomy and jeopardises their competencies, which in turn leads to withdrawal behaviour and inactivity. Moreover, emerging adults’ lying flat orientation may also lead to over-parenting behaviour when their parents become anxious that their children may fail in future. Hence, the proposed study will pursue three objectives: 1) to examine the bi-directional relationships between over-parenting (paternal and maternal) and lying flat orientation over time among Hong Kong Chinese emerging adults; 2) investigate the mediating roles of psychological entitlement, autonomy and self-efficacy in these relationships; and 3) assess the moderating roles of emerging adults' educational level and perceived competitive psychological climate in these associations. The proposed project will be based on a three-wave longitudinal study using social surveys over three years. A sample of 910 emerging adults with diverse educational backgrounds will be recruited as the survey respondents. The results will enrich our understanding of how over-parenting, including its mediating and moderating mechanisms, contribute to lying flat orientation among emerging adults in Chinese contexts. The results will have practical implications for social workers, educators, parents and policymakers in addressing the over-parenting and lying flat phenomena. 青年期是青少年階段與成年階段之間一個重要的過渡時期，年輕人在此階段建立獨立感、承擔責任並探索其成人身份。近年來，「躺平」（即處於不作為、拒絕參與激烈競爭的狀態）現象在中國內地及香港的年輕人中蔓延，並在社交媒體及政府層面引起廣泛關注。不幸的是，探討青年人「躺平」傾向的前因之研究仍然稀少，尤其是有關親職管教對其傾向之影響。在社會科學領域中，過度管教被視為一種不適當的管教方式，父母往往透過過度參與及保護以確保子女的幸福及成就。然而，過往的研究顯示，過度管教為青年帶來負面的心理發展。過度管教有機會導致父母與子女之間出現過度糾纏，干預青年的自我區分能力，妨礙他們從青少年到成年的順利過渡，延長他們對父母的依賴。 根據心理特權模型分析，接受過度管教的青年會認為自己合理地獲得父母之特殊待遇（即心理特權），為他們製造一個過度呵護的環境，有利於「躺平」傾向之形成。相反，自我決定理論認為，過度管教限制了青年的自主性，損害其能力之發展，導致其退縮行為和不作為。此外，青年的「躺平」傾向也會引發父母對子女之未來的憂慮，加劇其過度管教行為。 因此，研究擬訂三個目標：1）檢視香港青年之「躺平」傾向及其父母之過度管教之間的雙向關係隨著時間而產生之變化；2）探討心理特權、自主性及自我效能感在這些關係中產生之中介作用；及3）評估青年之教育程度及其對競爭環境之心理感知在這些關係中之調節作用。本研究將以三年的縱向社會調查為基礎，招募910名不同教育背景之香港青年作為調查對象。研究結果將豐富我們了解過度管教如何影響華人青年之「躺平」傾向（包括其中介與調節機制）。期望研究成果能對社會工作者、教育工作者、家長及政策制定者在應對過度管教與「躺平」現象方面有實際之應用價值。

16100025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100025.value: 研究介導前膠原蛋白從內質網輸出的分子機制

16100025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100025.value: Collagen comprises 17% of our body weight and is essential for building tissues. Defects in collagen production lead to a wide range of disorders, including osteogenesis imperfecta and various forms of fibrosis. Collagen synthesis begins with the formation of procollagen molecules, which assemble into a triple helix within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). These molecules are then transported along the secretory pathway and secreted out of the cell to perform their cellular and physiological functions. Although fundamentally important, the molecular mechanisms mediating collagen secretion remain largely unclear. The coat protein complex II (COPII) is crucial in forming vesicles and packaging cargo at the ER. Collagen, however, poses a unique challenge due to its size, often over 300 nm long, and rigidity, contrasting with the standard 70 nm diameter of COPII vesicles. This poses a critical question: how do ER-derived transport carriers expand to accommodate large procollagen molecules? Using an in vitro vesicle formation assay and various cellular and biochemical approaches, we have identified two key cellular factors, giantin and VAMP Associated Protein A (VAPA), that are enriched in large transport carriers and playing important roles in the packaging and secretion of procollagen I (PC1). Giantin, a large cis-Golgi membrane-associated protein, and VAPA, an ER-resident protein involved in lipid transport, both have unclear roles in ER-to-Golgi cargo trafficking of secretory cargoes. In this study, we will utilize established methodologies, such as the vesicle formation assay, the Retention Using Selective Hooks (RUSH) assay, and transmission electron microscopy analysis, to delve deeper into the functional roles of COPII in creating large ER-derived transport carriers (Aim 1). We will also elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which VAPA influences collagen secretion (Aim 2). Giantin has been shown to be enriched in COPI vesicles and it is also reported to mediate tethering of vesicles to the Golgi apparatus. In Aim 3, we will investigate whether giantin mediates the tethering of incoming large ER-derived transport carriers to the Golgi and test whether the ER retrieval of giantin-enriched COPI vesicles contributes to the formation of ER-derived large transport carriers. Our study will uncover novel insights into the mechanisms responsible for packaging procollagens into transport carriers from the ER, a crucial step for collagen secretion. Given the link between excessive collagen production and fibrotic diseases, the findings from our studies will be instrumental in developing targeted inhibitors to modulate collagen secretion, offering a new strategy for treating fibrotic diseases. 膠原蛋白佔人體重量的17%，是構建組織的重要成分。膠原蛋白生產缺陷會導致多種疾病，包括成骨不全症及不同類型的纖維化病變。膠原蛋白的合成始於前膠原蛋白分子的形成，這些分子在內質網（ER）內組裝成三股螺旋結構，隨後沿分泌途徑運輸並分泌到細胞外，以發揮其細胞及生理功能。儘管這一過程至關重要，但介導膠原蛋白分泌的分子機制至今仍不清楚。 外被蛋白複合物II（COPII）在內質網形成囊泡及包裝貨物過程中起關鍵作用。然而，膠原蛋白因其長度（通常超過300納米）和剛性結構，與COPII囊泡的標準直徑（約70納米）形成鮮明對比，這帶來一個核心問題：內質網衍生的運輸載體如何擴張以容納巨大的前膠原蛋白分子？透過體外囊泡形成實驗及多種細胞與生化方法，我們發現兩個關鍵細胞因子, 巨型蛋白（giantin）和VAMP相關蛋白A（VAPA), 在大型運輸載體中富集，並對前膠原蛋白I（PC1）的包裝與分泌起重要作用。巨型蛋白是一種位於順式高爾基體膜的大型蛋白，而VAPA則是參與脂質運輸的內質網駐留蛋白，兩者在分泌性貨物從內質網到高爾基體的運輸過程中的角色尚不明確。 本研究將運用已建立的方法，如囊泡形成實驗、選擇性掛鉤保留（RUSH）實驗及透射電子顯微鏡分析，深入探討COPII在形成大型內質網衍生運輸載體中的功能（目標1）。我們亦將闡明VAPA影響膠原蛋白分泌的分子機制（目標2）。巨型蛋白已知在COPI囊泡中富集，並被報導可介導囊泡與高爾基體的栓繫作用。在目標3中，我們將研究巨型蛋白是否介導內質網衍生的大型運輸載體與高爾基體的栓繫，並測試富含巨型蛋白的COPI囊泡的內質網回收是否促進大型運輸載體的形成。 本研究將揭示前膠原蛋白從內質網包裝到運輸載體的新機制，這是膠原蛋白分泌的關鍵步驟。由於過量膠原蛋白生產與纖維化疾病密切相關，我們的發現將有助開發針對性抑制劑以調控膠原蛋白分泌，為治療纖維化疾病提供新策略。

16100225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100225.value: 暖化和養分失衡對香港沿海水域偽菱形藻發生和毒素產生影響

16100225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100225.value: A group of marine microalgae, Pseudo-nitzschia (PSN), blooms frequently in coastal waters. Some species produce the toxin domoic acid (DA), which is harmful to marine mammals and can be fatal to humans consuming contaminated shellfish. Although the diversity and the spatial and temporal distribution patterns of PSN have been well studied in the past decade, the mechanisms and environmental driver of DA production in PSNPSN are poorly understood. In our pilot research, we detected a high abundance of PSN in Hong Kong coastal waters. Therefore, the potential ecological and health threats posed by toxic PSN cannot be ignored. In the proposed project, by conducting field surveys, laboratory experiments, and modeling studies and using molecular biological methods, we will 1) investigate the species composition, ecological characteristics, and DA toxin levels of PSN in the coastal waters of Hong Kong; 2) examine the responses of PSN to key environmental stressors, focusing on warming and nutrient imbalances; and 3) elucidate the metabolic pathway involved in DA production and the molecular mechanisms underlying this process in PSN. Our previous research conducted in Hong Kong coastal waters and the Pearl River Estuary revealed continual increases in nutrient concentrations, particularly inorganic nitrogen, leading to an excess of nitrogen relative to phosphorus. This trend in recent decades has been driven by urbanization and rapid economic development in the Greater Bay Area. A high nitrate concentration and high nitrogen-to-phosphorus ratio have led to the increased dominance of diatoms in the phytoplankton community, in which PSN is a major component. Moreover, we recently found that increasing the nutrient supply can raise the optimal growth temperature and the maximal growth rate of some diatom species, including PSN, suggesting that abundant nutrients bolster marine diatoms in coping with warming. Therefore, it is important to study the effects of nutrient availability and imbalances on the thermal responses of PSN, including growth and toxin production. The results of the proposed project will advance this important research topic, provide guidance for marine environmental protection, and increase public awareness of environmental health. 一組海洋矽藻 Pseudo-nitzschia （PSN，偽菱形藻） 經常在沿海水域大量繁殖。其中一些物種會產生毒素軟骨藻酸 （domoic acid），這種毒素對海洋哺乳動物有害，對食用受污染貝類的人類來說可能是致命的。儘管偽菱形藻的多樣性和時空分佈模式在過去數十年中得到了較為廣泛的研究，但人們對它產生毒素的機制和環境驅動因素知之甚少。在我們的先導研究中，我們在香港沿岸水域檢測到大量 PSN。因此，有毒PSN帶來的潛在生態和健康威脅不容忽視。在擬議專案中，我們將通過實地調查、實驗室實驗和建模研究，並使用分子生物學方法，1）調查香港沿岸水域的PSN的物種組成、生態特徵和毒素含量;2）檢查PSN對關鍵環境壓力源的反應，重點關注變暖和養分失衡;3）闡明參與domoic acid產生的代謝途徑以及產毒過程的分子機制。我們之前在香港沿岸水域和珠江口進行的研究顯示，營養物質濃度（尤其是無機氮）持續增加，導致氮相對於磷過量。近幾十年來，大灣區的城市化進程和經濟的快速發展推動了這一趨勢。高硝酸鹽濃度和高氮磷比導致矽藻在浮遊植物群落中的優勢增加，其中 PSN 是其中的主要成分。此外，我們最近發現，增加養分供應可以提高包括PSN在內的一些矽藻物種的最佳生長溫度和最大生長速率，這表明豐富的養分有助於海洋矽藻應對變暖。因此，研究養分濃度和不平衡對 PSN 在升溫環境中的影響（包括生長和毒素產生）非常重要。擬議專案的成果將推進這一重要的研究課題，為海洋環境保護提供指導，並提高公眾的環境健康意識。

16100425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100425.value: 揭示深海化能合成環境中的細胞內營養共生

16100425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100425.value: Many marine invertebrates in deep-sea chemosynthetic ecosystems depend on chemoautotrophic symbionts for nutrients and survival. Giant vesicomyid clams (Archivesica marissinica) are widely distributed across global deep-sea hydrothermal vent and methane seep ecosystems. As a prominent and representative group of large benthic organisms in these ecosystems, clams play a crucial role in the establishment of biological communities and energy cycling. They primarily obtain symbionts through vertical transmission and depend heavily on sulfur-oxidizing bacteria in their gills to acquire the sulfide required for energy and nutrients. However, the key to comprehending this adaptation to harsh environments is the establishment of the mechanisms underlying the animal host’s ability in maintaining the stability of the symbiotic system and host symbiont interactions, which remains largely unknown, especially during environmental changes. In this study, our aim is to test the following two hypotheses: 1) changes in symbiont abundances in response to environmental changes (sulfide supply to the host will be drastically dropped after experimental animals from active seep site are transplanted to inactive seep site) will trigger the changes in the expression level of the host genes involved in the maintenance of the symbiotic system; and 2) changes in the energy metabolism, nutrient biosynthesis of symbionts will trigger the changes in the expression level of the host genes in obtaining nutrients from symbionts. Specifically, combined with environmental background measurement techniques, we will conduct in situ sulfide-blocking experiments on clams in the Haima methane seep. We will collect clams for the experiment, with the control group comprising naturally growing clams, using an in situ RNAlater fixation chamber. Following the experiments, we will apply multiple omics and imaging approaches to quantify changes in symbiotic bacterial abundance and functional changes (i.e., gene expression and protein abundance) in the holobiont. Metabolomics will be applied to validate changes in the nutrient biosynthesis capability. ISH will be used to validate any interesting genes came out from the omics analyses. We will also check for any corelations between symbiont abundances and their activity of nutrient biosynthesis. Through these studies, we aim to systematically reveal the mechanisms underlying symbiotic relationships between invertebrate animals and microorganisms in chemosynthetic deep-sea ecosystems using vesicomyid clams, which are a typical form of invertebrates, as the model organism. The knowledge gained will improve our comprehension of the regulatory processes underlying the response of clams to deep-sea environmental changes. 深海化能合成生態系统中許多海洋的無脊椎動物依賴化能自養共生體獲取營養與生存。巨型囊蛤（Archivesica marissini-ca）廣泛分佈於全球深海熱液噴口和甲烷滲漏生態系统。作為這些生態系统中突出且具代表性的大型底棲生物類群，蛤蜊在生物群落的建立和能量流中發揮著至關重要的作用。它們主要透過垂直傳播來獲取共生體，並嚴重依賴鰓中的硫氧化細菌來獲取能量和營養所需的硫化物。然而，理解這種對惡劣環境適應的關鍵在於了解動物宿主維持共生系統穩定性和宿主共生體相互作用的機制，而這在很大程度上仍不清楚，尤其是在環境變化期間。本研究旨在檢驗兩個主要假設：1）共生體豐度隨環境變化而改變（將來自活躍滲漏點的實驗動物移植到非活躍滲漏點後，宿主的硫化物供應將急劇下降），從而引發參與維持共生系統宿主基因表达水平的變化；2）共生體能量代謝、營養生物合成的變化，引發宿主從共生體獲取營養的基因表达水平的變化。具體來說，我們將結合環境背景測量技術，對海馬甲烷滲漏區的蛤蜊進行原位硫化物阻斷實驗。我們將使用原位RNAlater装置收集實驗用蛤蜊，對照組則由自然生長的蛤蜊組成。實驗結束後，我們將應用多組學和成像方法，量化共生菌豐度的變化和全生物體的功能變化（即基因表达和蛋白質豐度）。代謝組學將用於驗證營養物質生物合成能力的變化。原位雜交（ISH）將用於驗證組學分析中發現的任何有趣基因。我們也將探討共生體豐度與其營養物質生物合成活性之間的相關性。透過這些研究，我們旨在以典型的無脊椎動物－蛤蚌為模式生物，系統地揭示化能合成深海生態系中無脊椎動物與微生物共生關係的潛在機制。這些研究成果將有助於我們更好了解蛤蚌響應深海環境變化背後的調控機制。

16100525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100525.value: 研究突触蛋白Kek2介导的遗忘的分子机制

16100525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100525.value: Synaptic plasticity is fundamental for learning and memory, which are essential for adaptive behavior and cognitive function. Memory dysfunction significantly decreases the quality of life, as in the case of neurodevelopmental disorders and dementia. Conversely, robust memory formation, as observed in post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), also impedes daily life. To develop therapeutic strategies to tackle memory-related disorders, studies providing the mechanistic details of synaptic plasticity are crucial. We recently reported a novel mechanism linking synaptic plasticity and memory forgetting mediated by the synaptic protein Kek2 in Drosophila. We demonstrated that learning induces activation of cGMP pathway via nitric oxide (NO), leading to gene expression of Kek2, a cell-surface protein localized at the presynapse, which is essential for forgetting in the memory center, mushroom body (MB). Activation of the cGMP pathway results in presynaptic changes, suggesting that learning-dependent activation of the NO-cGMP pathway induces synaptic recovery for forgetting via Kek2 expression. Although targeting the NO-cGMP pathway to intervene in forgetting could be effective in treating memory-related disorders, the central question is how general or specific the NO-cGMP-Kek2-dependent synaptic plasticity is across different neuron types which could be involved in other functions than forgetting. In fact, by mapping Kek2 expression in the whole brain, Kek2 exhibited oscillatory expression in the visual circuits, particularly during the morning and evening when flies are active. This Kek2 expression controls responsiveness to light in their activity peak, which is not related to forgetting. In this study, we will aim to characterize the molecular details of Kek2-dependent synaptic plasticity in different neurons to uncover its common and differential mechanisms, with the following objectives: 1) characterize the Kek2-interactome in various neurons, 2) test the behavioral significance of Kek2-interacting proteins, and 3) examine the roles of Kek2-interacting proteins in synaptic plasticity. The long-term goal of this study will be to specifically suppress forgetting for improving memory and to specifically enhance forgetting for erasing fearful memories. Accordingly, identifying Kek2-interacting proteins specific to the memory circuit will facilitate the development of practical therapeutic strategies to intervene in forgetting without concerns regarding secondary effects. Therefore, our proposal is significant for determining the molecular details specifying Kek2-dependent synaptic plasticity in forgetting, which possesses the potential impact to increase our understanding of synaptic plasticity and reveal the underlying molecular mechanisms that could target forgetting. 突触可塑性是学习和记忆的基础，这对于动物的适应行为和认知功能至关重要。记忆功能障碍显著降低生活质量，例如神经发育障碍和痴呆症的情况，而在创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）中观察到的强大记忆形成也会妨碍日常生活。为了解决记忆相关的障碍，关于突触可塑性的研究提供更大的机制细节，对于开发治疗策略至关重要。我们最近报道了一种新机制，揭示了突触可塑性和遗忘之间的联系，该机制由果蝇的突触蛋白Kek2介导。我们证明了通过一氧化氮（NO）诱导的cGMP通路促进Kek2的基因表达，Kek2是一种定位于突触前膜的细胞表面蛋白，对遗忘至关重要。cGMP通路的激活导致突触前的变化，表明学习依赖性激活的NO-cGMP通路通过Kek2的表达诱导突触的恢复以促进遗忘。尽管针对NO-cGMP通路进行干预以影响遗忘可能对治疗记忆相关障碍有效，但核心问题是NO-cGMP-Kek2依赖的突触可塑性在不同脑区或神经元类型中是多么普遍或特异。通过绘制Kek2在整个大脑中的表达，我们发现Kek2在特定神经回路中表现出振荡的突触表达，特别是在果蝇活跃的早晨和晚上。我们发现Kek2的表达控制着该神经回路的特定功能，表明Kek2根据神经元的类型调节不同的功能结果。在本研究中，我们旨在表征不同神经元中Kek2依赖的突触可塑性的分子细节，以揭示其共同和差异机制，具体目标如下：1）确定各种神经元中的Kek2相互作用组，2）测试Kek2相互作用蛋白的行为重要性，3）检查Kek2相互作用蛋白在突触可塑性中的作用。本研究的长期目标是具体抑制遗忘，以改善记忆，并特意增强遗忘以抹去恐惧记忆。因此，识别特定于记忆回路的Kek2相互作用蛋白将有助于开发实用的治疗策略，以干预遗忘而不必担心副作用。因此，我们的提案对于确定指定Kek2依赖的突触可塑性的分子细节具有重要意义，这可能会增加我们对突触可塑性的理解，并揭示可以针对遗忘的潜在分子机制。

16100625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100625.value: 從基因到生態系統：解碼真核浮游植物與細胞核-細胞質大s型DNA病毒的共同演化

16100625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100625.value: The proposed project will aim to investigate the co-evolution of eukaryotic phytoplankton, specifically Mamiellophyceae, and their associated nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs), focusing on prasinoviruses. We will explore the intricate dynamics of host–virus interactions in marine ecosystems, addressing critical gaps in our understanding of viral impacts on algal populations, resistance mechanisms, and the influence of environmental factors on these relationships. Through a comprehensive, multi-faceted approach, we will characterize infection dynamics across various Mamiellophyceae–prasinovirus combinations under different temperature regimes, examining population impacts and recovery rates. We will investigate gene expression changes in both the host and virus during infection cycles, with a focus on temperature-dependent molecular mechanisms. Long-term chemostat experiments will be conducted to observe the co-evolutionary patterns between Mamiellophyceae and prasinoviruses, and the genetic and phenotypic changes over time will be assessed. Finally, we will validate the laboratory findings using metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data from natural environments to confirm the observed genetic changes and their ecological relevance. The proposed research will provide crucial insights into the genetic diversity, resistance evolution, and ecological impacts of NCLDVs in marine microbial ecosystems. By integrating laboratory experiments with environmental data, we will aim to develop a more holistic understanding of alga–virus interactions in marine systems, with potential implications for predicting ecosystem responses to environmental changes, including ocean warming. The project’s findings will contribute significantly to our knowledge of host–NCLDV co-evolution, elucidating the complex interplay between these important marine microorganisms and their viral pathogens. This understanding will be vital for accurately modeling the dynamics of marine ecosystems and predicting their responses to global climate change. 本研究提案旨在探討真核浮游植物，特別是綠藻綱（Mamiellophyceae），與其相關的巨型病毒——草綠藻病毒（prasinoviruses）之間的共同演化。草綠藻病毒屬於細胞核-細胞質大型DNA病毒（NCLDVs）群組。本研究將從分子層面到生態系統層面，探索這些具有重要生態意義的海洋微生物之間的複雜動態關係。通過採用結合實驗室實驗、長期恆化器研究和環境驗證的多元化方法，我們尋求解開宿主抗性、病毒感染力和環境因子（特別是溫度）之間複雜相互作用的謎團。我們的研究將描述各種綠藻綱-草綠藻病毒組合的感染動態特徵，調查宿主-病毒相互作用期間的基因表達變化，進行長期共同演化實驗，並通過來自自然環境的宏基因組學和宏轉錄組學數據驗證實驗室發現。這種綜合性方法將為海洋微生物生態系統中這些宿主-病毒系統的遺傳多樣性、抗性演化和生態影響提供前所未有的見解。通過聚焦於草綠藻病毒——已知最大的病毒之一且為NCLDV群組成員，本研究將有助於我們對巨型病毒生態學和演化的理解。研究結果將闡明這些重要的浮游植物-病毒相互作用如何回應變化中的海洋環境，特別是在氣候變遷的背景下。這些知識對於預測海洋微生物群落的變化及其對全球生物地球化學循環的連鎖效應至關重要。

16100825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16100825.value: 機械敏感的 TMC1/2 通道是否同時兼備脂質翻轉酶的功能？

16100825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100825.value: Phospholipid scramblases (PLSases) are essential for maintaining membrane asymmetry and facilitating lipid movement between membrane leaflets. They play roles in apoptosis, blood coagulation, and signaling. Of the scramblase families—TMEM16s, Xkrs, and ATG-9—Ca2+-activated TMEM16s are the most studied, acting as ion channels and scramblases. The TMEM16 fold is conserved in other families, such as OSCA/TMEM63 and TMC1/2 ion channels, with some members functioning solely as ion channels and others as dual-function proteins. Recent evidence suggests that TMC1/2 channels may also have lipid scrambling capabilities. Studies indicate that inhibiting mTMC1’s channel function or lowering intracellular Ca2+ triggers PS externalization and membrane blebbing in hair cells, proposing TMC1 as a Ca2+-inhibited PLSase. However, TMC2's involvement in lipid scrambling remains debated. Our recent breakthroughs in functional assays of ectopic TMC1/2 suggest that ectopic mTMC1/2, in the presence of mTMIE, exhibit constitutive PLSase activity. We hypothesize that mTMC1/2 function as intrinsic PLSases, requiring mTMIE, and that ions and phospholipids utilize separate passages within TMC1/2. We aim to test these hypotheses through specific objectives: determining the scramblase function of TMC1/2 in expression systems and reconstitution assays, dissecting the regulation by TMIE, characterizing the phospholipid permeation pathway, and evaluating the impact on auditory sensation. Understanding TMC1/2's dual roles could enhance insights into sensorineural hearing loss and identify new therapeutic strategies, including preventing aminoglycoside-associated deafness. Our findings will also illuminate the molecular mechanisms of lipid scrambling within the TMEM16-fold superfamily. 磷脂翻轉酶（PLSases）對於維持膜不對稱性和促進膜小葉之間的脂質運動至關重要。它們在細胞凋亡、凝血和信號傳導中發揮作用。在翻轉酶家族（TMEM16、Xkrs 和 ATG-9）中，Ca2+ 激活的 TMEM16 是研究最多的，同時充當離子通道和翻轉酶。TMEM16 折疊在其他家族中是保守的，例如 OSCA/TMEM63 和 TMC1/2 離子通道，其中一些成員僅作為離子通道發揮作用，而另一些成員則作為雙功能蛋白發揮作用。最近的證據表明，TMC1/2 通道也可能具有脂質翻轉能力。研究表明，抑制 mTMC1 的通道功能或降低細胞內 Ca2+ 會觸發毛細胞中的 PS 外化和膜起泡，因此認為 TMC1 作為 Ca2+ 抑制的 PLSase。然而，TMC2 參與脂質翻轉仍存爭議。我們最近在異位 TMC1/2 功能測定方面的突破表明，異位 mTMC1/2 在 mTMIE 存在下表現出 PLSase 活性。我們假設 mTMC1/2 充當內源性 PLSase，需要 mTMIE，並且離子和磷脂利用 TMC1/2 內的分開通道。我們旨在通過具體目標來檢驗這些假設：確定 TMC1/2 在表達系統和重構測定中的翻轉功能，剖析 TMIE 的調節，描述磷脂滲透途徑，並評估對聽覺的影響。了解 TMC1/2 的雙重作用可以增強對感音神經性聽力損失的深入了解並確定新的治療策略，包括預防氨基糖苷類藥物相關耳聾。我們的發現還將闡明 TMEM16 倍超家族內脂質翻轉的分子機制。

16101225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16101225.value: 利用沉積物環境DNA重建香港海域沿岸生態群落的歷史動態

16101225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101225.value: Biodiversity is key to maintaining the quality and stability of ecosystem services, but it is declining globally due to climate change and human activities. Understanding how to maintain biodiversity is crucial for reversing this trend, necessitating effective methods to collect current and past biodiversity information. Environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis, which involves analyzing DNA directly extracted from environmental samples such as water and soil, is an emerging technique for effective biodiversity monitoring. It enables comprehensive and frequent monitoring of “current” biodiversity, but it can also be used to reconstruct “historical dynamics” of ecological communities, which is necessary for deeper understanding of current ecological patterns. Recently, eDNA analysis has been applied to aquatic sediment samples, where eDNA can be preserved longer than in the water column. This sedimentary eDNA (sedDNA) analysis opens possibilities for reconstructing past ecological dynamics. However, despite its potential, the number of sedDNA studies is still limited and there are a number of technical issues. Hong Kong waters are an area under multiple anthropogenic and environmental pressures, and this area can be an ideal system to understand complex interactions among external forces and ecosystems using sedDNA analysis. Thus, we aim to reconstruct the historical dynamics of ecological communities in Hong Kong waters using sedDNA by focusing on macro-organisms such as fish, crustaceans, and cetaceans. We focus on three aspects in this project: sedDNA method development, application of the developed method, and validation of the sedDNA results. The central questions of this study are what are the historical dynamics of coastal ecological communities in Hong Kong waters, and whether the sedDNA method reconstructs the historical dynamics. We hypothesize that we will extract sufficient information from sediment cores if we use appropriate experimental protocols. Accordingly, the objectives of this study are as follows: 1) To collect and curate historical ecological data in Hong Kong waters (i.e., ground truth data), 2) To determine optimal experimental protocols for sedDNA analysis, and 3) To reconstruct historical ecological communities from Hong Kong sediment cores using sedDNA analysis. The long-term goal of this project is to reconstruct coastal ecosystem dynamics at a large spatial and long-temporal scale. The significance of this study is multi-faceted, as it will develop novel eDNA technologies (technical advances), establish a sedDNA-based biodiversity monitoring network (collaboration network), and provide data on historical ecosystem dynamics, which is currently lacking in many ecosystems (understanding the mechanics of ecosystem dynamics). 生物多樣性是維持生態系統服務質量與穩定性的關鍵，但由於氣候變化與人類活動，其正面臨全球性的衰退。為了扭轉此趨勢，了解如何維持生物多樣性至關重要，這需要有效的方法來收集當前與過去的生物多樣性資訊。環境DNA（eDNA）分析是一項新興技術，透過分析直接從水體或土壤等環境樣本中提取的DNA，可有效進行生物多樣性監測。此技術不僅能全面且頻繁地監測「當前」的生物多樣性，也可用於重建生態群落的「歷史動態」，以深入理解當前的生態模式。近年來，eDNA分析已應用於水域沉積物樣本中，因為沉積物中的DNA保存時間通常比水體中更長。這種沉積物環境DNA（sedDNA）分析開啟了重建過去生態動態的可能性。然而，儘管其潛力巨大，sedDNA研究仍然有限，且存在多項技術挑戰。香港海域受多重人為與環境壓力影響，是一個理想的系統，可利用sedDNA分析來理解外在因素與生態系統之間的複雜互動。因此，本研究旨在利用sedDNA重建香港海域生態群落的歷史動態，聚焦於大型生物如魚類、甲殼類與鯨豚類。本計劃將聚焦於三個面向：sedDNA方法開發、方法應用，以及結果驗證。本研究的核心問題為：香港海域沿岸生態群落的歷史動態為何？sedDNA方法是否能有效重建這些歷史動態？我們假設只要採用適當的實驗流程，便能從沉積岩心中提取足夠的資訊。本研究的具體目標如下：1）收集並整理香港海域的歷史生態資料（即真實資料），2）確定sedDNA分析的最佳實驗流程，3）利用sedDNA分析重建香港沉積岩心中的歷史生態群落。本計劃的長遠目標是重建大尺度與長時間尺度的沿岸生態系統動態。此研究具多重意義：技術層面上將開發新型eDNA技術；合作層面上將建立以sedDNA為基礎的生物多樣性監測網絡；科學層面上將提供目前多數生態系統所缺乏的歷史生態動態資料，進一步促進對生態系統動態機制的理解。

16101825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16101825.value: LRP1 與 HSPG 在 Tau 病理傳播與阿茲海默症中的角色

16101825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101825.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, impacting a growing number of our aging population. Despite recent development in anti-amyloid therapies, their efficacy remains limited. Therefore, there is an urgent need to understand the mechanisms of AD development and progression to identify new therapeutic targets. AD is characterized by two pathological features: amyloid plaques composed of amyloid-β (Aβ) and neurofibrillary tangles containing hyperphosphorylated tau. The latter is more directly linked to neurodegeneration. Recent studies have shown that tau pathology progressively spreads from one brain region to multiple anatomically connected regions, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. To address this knowledge gap, the major goal of this project is to dissect the molecular and cellular pathways that either promote or inhibit tau spreading, with a specific focus on tau receptors LRP1 and heparan sulfate proteoglycan (HSPG). In our previous studies, we have defined the roles of LRP1 and HSPG in Aβ metabolism, establishing the opposing effects of neuronal LRP1 and HSPG in brain Aβ clearance using conditional mouse models. While HSPG has been suggested to promote the pathological propagation of tau, LRP1 has been identified as the primary receptor for tau spread. Importantly, recent studies have suggested, but not proven, that while neuronal LRP1 and HSPG promote tau spread, the same glial receptors in particular LRP1 facilitate tau cellular uptake and degradation. Thus, we hypothesize that neuronal LRP1 and HSPG promote the speed and extent of tau spreading, whereas glial LRP1 and HSPG accelerate tau degradation, thereby inhibiting tau propagation. We propose two specific aims to address our hypothesis. In Aim 1, we will examine how neuronal, astrocytic, and microglial LRP1 and HSPG modulate tau pathological development and propagation in vivo using conditional mouse models where endogenous Lrp1 or Ext1 (encoding an essential enzyme for adding heparan sulfates to HSPG) will be conditionally deleted using the Cre-loxP system. In Aim 2, we will investigate how the presence of amyloid pathology impacts tau pathology and spreading in a neuronal or glial LRP1- or HSPG-dependent manner. Together, these studies should generate critical insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying tau spreading and inform strategies for mechanism-based therapies to combat AD and other neurodegenerative diseases with tauopathies. 阿茲海默症（AD）是失智症的主要原因，影響著日益增長的老年人口。儘管近年來已開發出抗類澱粉蛋白療法，但其療效仍然有限。因此，迫切需要深入了解AD的發展與進程機制，以尋找新的治療標的。AD具有兩大病理特徵：由類澱粉蛋白β（Aβ）組成的類澱粉斑塊，以及含有過度磷酸化tau蛋白的神經纖維糾結（neurofibrillary tangles）。其中，tau蛋白病變與神經退化有更直接的關聯。 近期研究顯示，tau病變會由一個腦區逐漸擴散至多個解剖上相連的腦區，但其背後的機制仍不清楚。為了解決這項知識缺口，本研究的主要目標是解析促進或抑制tau擴散的分子與細胞途徑，特別著重於tau接受體：低密度脂蛋白相關蛋白1（LRP1）與硫酸乙醯肝素蛋白聚醣（HSPG）。在我們先前的研究中，已經界定了LRP1與HSPG在Aβ代謝中的角色，並利用條件性小鼠模型，建立了神經元中LRP1與HSPG對大腦Aβ清除具有相反作用的證據。 雖然有研究指出HSPG可能促進tau病理的傳播，LRP1則被認為是tau擴散的主要受體，但尚未獲得證實。重要的是，最近的研究指出，雖然神經元中的LRP1與HSPG促進tau的擴散，同樣的膠質細胞受體（特別是LRP1）則可能促進tau的細胞攝取與分解。因此，我們假設神經元中的LRP1與HSPG會促進tau擴散的速度與範圍，而膠質細胞中的LRP1與HSPG則會加速tau的降解，從而抑制tau的傳播。 為驗證此一假說，我們提出兩項具體研究目標。第一項目標（Aim 1）是使用條件性小鼠模型，探討神經元與小膠質細胞中的LRP1與HSPG如何調控tau病理的發展與擴散。我們將利用Cre-loxP系統，條件性地刪除內源性Lrp1或Ext1（Ext1編碼一種對於將硫酸乙醣胺添加至HSPG至關重要的酶）。第二項目標（Aim 2）是研究類澱粉病理的存在如何在依賴神經元或小膠質細胞中LRP1或HSPG的情況下，影響tau病變與其擴散。 綜合而言，本研究將提供關於tau蛋白擴散分子機制的關鍵見解，並為開發針對機制的AD及其他tau蛋白病神經退化疾病的治療策略提供理論基礎。

16101925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16101925.value: 顱內生殖細胞腫瘤的轉座因子與免疫微環境：機制與臨床意義

16101925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101925.value: Transposable elements (TEs) play a significant role in the biology of cancers, particularly in enhancing immune responses and generating neoantigens that may improve outcomes for immunotherapy. Despite the increasing recognition of TE activity in intracranial germ cell tumors (IGCTs), the tumor microenvironment (TME) associated with these tumors remains poorly characterized. Understanding the interplay between TEs and the TME is crucial for advancing therapeutic strategies, especially since TE-derived antigens hold potential for targeted immunotherapy. This study aims to investigate the mechanisms underlying TE activity and the immunological landscape in IGCTs, providing insights that could lead to novel therapeutic targets and improved patient outcomes. Our team is well-positioned to conduct this project due to our extensive experience in studying intracranial tumors and our strong collaboration with neurosurgeons, facilitating easy access to patient samples. In our recent study, we analyzed the mutational and transcriptional landscape of GCTs using sequencing data from 227 pediatric GCT patients, including 107 IGCTs. Our findings revealed that chromosome 1p36 loss is enriched in the yolk sac tumor (YST) subtype of GCTs and is correlated with frequent somatic TE insertions. To characterize the TME of IGCTs and further investigate the potential impact of TE activity, we conducted CODEX multi-antibody imaging on two YST samples. Our preliminary data indicate significant immune cell infiltration in these tumors, including the presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS). Notably, tumors with 1p36 loss exhibit a higher density of immune cells, suggesting a complex relationship between genomic alterations and the immune landscape. We hypothesize that the 1p36 loss, correlated with low expression of tumor suppressor gene PRDM2, drives TE activity and genome instability, resulting in an elevated immune response in IGCTs. To test this hypothesis, we plan to perform comprehensive genomic profiling using long-read sequencing to elucidate the role of TEs and associated genomic alterations. We will characterize the TME using advanced techniques such as CODEX and Visium HD to map immune cell interactions and spatial dynamics. Additionally, we aim to collect approximately 10 new patient samples, in conjunction with our existing data, to strengthen our analyses. By integrating these methodologies, we seek to uncover the molecular mechanisms linking PRDM2, TE activity, and immune responses, ultimately informing potential therapeutic strategies for IGCTs. 轉位元素（Transposable elements, TEs）在癌症生物學中扮演著重要角色，特別是在增強免疫反應與產生新抗原（neoantigens）方面，這些抗原可能有助於改善免疫治療的效果。儘管人們對腦內生殖細胞瘤（Intracranial Germ Cell Tumors, IGCTs）中TE活性的認識日益增加，但與這些腫瘤相關的腫瘤微環境（Tumor Microenvironment, TME）仍然知之甚少。了解TE與TME之間的交互作用，對於推進治療策略至關重要，特別是因為TE衍生抗原具有成為靶向免疫治療標的的潛力。本研究旨在探討IGCTs中TE活性機制及其免疫環境，提供可能促成新型治療標的與改善病患預後的洞見。 我們的團隊具備研究腦內腫瘤的豐富經驗，並與神經外科醫師密切合作，能夠順利取得病患樣本，因此非常適合執行本計畫。在我們最近的一項研究中，我們利用來自227位兒童生殖細胞瘤患者（包含107例IGCTs）的定序數據，分析了GCTs的突變與轉錄表現圖譜。我們的研究發現，在GCTs中的卵黃囊瘤（Yolk Sac Tumor, YST）亞型中，染色體1p36缺失現象顯著增加，並與頻繁的體細胞TE插入事件相關聯。 為了描述IGCTs的TME並進一步探討TE活性的潛在影響，我們在兩個YST樣本上進行了CODEX多抗體影像分析。我們的初步數據顯示，這些腫瘤中存在明顯的免疫細胞浸潤，包括三級淋巴結構（Tertiary Lymphoid Structures, TLS）。值得注意的是，具有1p36缺失的腫瘤展現出更高密度的免疫細胞，顯示基因體變異與免疫環境之間存在複雜的關聯。我們的假設是，與腫瘤抑制基因PRDM2低表現相關的1p36缺失驅動TE活性與基因體不穩定性，進而導致IGCTs中增強的免疫反應。 為了驗證此假設，我們計劃利用長讀長定序技術進行全面的基因體分析，以釐清TE與相關基因體變異的角色。我們將使用先進技術如CODEX與Visium HD來描繪免疫細胞的交互作用與空間動態。此外，我們亦計劃收集約10個新的病患樣本，結合現有數據以加強分析結果。透過整合這些方法，我們期望揭示PRDM2、TE活性與免疫反應之間的分子機制，最終為IGCTs的潛在治療策略提供資訊。

16102025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102025.value: 陸生植物透過SPORK2感知溫度的分子機制研究

16102025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102025.value: To survive on Earth, almost all living organisms have adapted to various ecological niches that experience fluctuations in temperature. Temperature has a crucial influence on the function of biological macromolecules, thereby affecting various aspects of metabolism, growth, and development, particularly those that involve thermosensitive proteins. In land plants, environmental temperature changes are perceived and responded to at multiple levels. The outward-rectifying K+ ion channel SPORK2 identified in the motor cell of the plant Samanea saman has been recognized as a temperature-sensitive channel with features similar to thermosensitive transient receptor potential (TRP) channels in animals, despite no homologs from the TRP channel family being found in land plants. The SPORK2 channel, therefore, offers a fresh perspective on understanding plant responses to temperature stress. However, the precise thermosensitive mechanisms of the SPORK2 channel remain largely unknown owing to the lack of atomic-resolution structural information. Our electrophysiology current recordings have confirmed that the SPORK2 channel is sensitive to temperature changes. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we obtained a near-atomic resolution structure for SPORK2 at 2.54 Å. The overall structure exhibits a 2-fold rather than 4-fold symmetry, even though SPORK2 functions as a homo-tetramer. While our preliminary results provide insights into the selectivity filter and gating mechanisms of SPORK2, further investigations are necessary for a comprehensive understanding of this channel. In the proposed project, we will determine the structure of SPORK2 in different functional states, including states triggered by stepwise temperature adjustments.
