We will combine biochemical assays, electrophysiological measurements, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to explore the molecular mechanisms by which the SPORK2 channel perceives and responds to temperature changes.

16102125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102125.value: 透過先進光學顯微鏡診斷原發性纖毛運動障礙症

16102125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16102125.value: Prof Chen, Hao Prof CHEN, Yahong

16102125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102125.value: Our airways are coated with motile cilia, tiny machines that beat to propel invading pathogens. Defects in motile cilia cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a hereditary disease affecting ~ 1 in 7,500 people. Early diagnosis is critical as PCD is life-threatening if left untreated. PCD is an underdiagnosed disease. PCD is genetically heterogeneous and currently two ways are used to confirm a diagnosis: DNA sequencing and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Both approaches have inherent limitations and even when combined together, still ~30% of patients with clinical symptoms do not receive a confirmed diagnosis. We previously reported a super-resolution imaging-based toolbox to aid PCD diagnosis. Here, we propose further integrating fluorescence imaging and high-speed video microscopy(HSVM) for the diagnosis. The method will first be tested using CRISPR knockout multiciliated cells generated in the lab. Next, it will be optimized by adding multiplexing and neural networks. Finally, the method will be combined with HSVM and tested using patient samples. This project addresses the current limitations in PCD diagnosis and will improve its accuracy, sensitivity, and throughput. Once diagnosed, treatment will be followed up. This study benefits the patients and decreases the family/hospital burden caused by the progression of the disease. 我們的呼吸道表面覆蓋著可運動的纖毛，這些微小的纖毛機器通過擺動來驅除入侵的病原體。運動纖毛的缺陷會導致原發性纖毛運動障礙症（PCD），這是一種影響約1/7500人口的遺傳性疾病。PCD及早診斷至關重要，因為如果不加以治療，PCD可能危及生命。 PCD是一種常被低估的疾病。PCD在遺傳上是異質的，目前有兩種方法用於確診PCD：DNA測序和透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）。這兩種方法各有其固有的限制，即使結合使用，仍然約有30%的臨床症狀患者未能獲得確診。 我們之前報告了一種基於超分辨率成像的工具箱來輔助PCD診斷。在此，我們提出進一步整合螢光成像和高速視頻顯微鏡（HSVM）進行診斷。該方法將首先使用CRISPR基因編輯的多纖毛細胞在實驗室中進行測試。接下來，將通過增加多重檢測和神經網絡來優化該方法。最後，該方法將與HSVM結合，並使用患者樣本進行測試。 這個項目旨在解決目前PCD診斷中的限制，並提高其準確性、敏感性和通量。一旦確診，對應的治療將隨之進行。這項研究將使患者受益，並減少由疾病進展造成的家庭和醫院的負擔。

16102825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102825.value: 用於視網膜生物學研究針對神經節細胞、微血管和小膠質細胞的先進活體成像技術

16102825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102825.value: The retina, a delicate tissue in the back of eye, is responsible for detecting light and forming vision. Various pathological conditions can lead to retinal dysfunction and visual impairment. As part of the central nervous system (CNS), the retina uniquely enables non-invasive visualization of its physiology and pathology through optical microscopy. Particularly, high-resolution and non-invasive imaging of the retina in living subjects under physiological conditions can significantly contribute to gaining valuable insights into researching retinal biology and diseases. Given their well-developed genetics and physiological analogies to the human retina, mouse models have been widely used for mechanistic studies of retinal diseases. However, the mouse eye introduces severe aberrations that impede high-resolution visualization of subcellular features. Recently, we developed an adaptive optics (AO) two-photon excitation fluorescence microscope (TPEFM) technology to correct these aberrations and enable microscopic investigations of the mouse retina in vivo. In this proposal, our objective is to make significant advancements in the state-of-the-art AO-TPEFM technology to enhance the study of retinal biology and diseases. Specifically, a laser display system will project intricate patterns onto the mouse retina, facilitating the study of the retina's functional responses to various light stimulations. Additionally, an innovative AO technology will be developed for high-resolution, in vivo imaging of the awake mouse retina. This advancement is crucial due to the potentially substantial variations in retinal biological processes between awake and anesthetized states. In the application study of the proposed new AO-TPEFM technology, we will focus on classifying retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), assessing microvascular integrity, and studying microglia dynamics. RGCs serve as critical and varied neurons linking the retina to the visual cortex, potentially encoding distinct visual information. Our research will address the urgent need for functional classification of RGCs under physiological conditions. In addition, the metabolically highly active retina relies on intricate vascular systems for sustenance, with microvascular irregularities linked to various retinal diseases. Microglia, the resident immune cells within the retina, are critical in maintaining tissue health by responding to disruptions; however, under certain pathological conditions, they could also pose a risk to neurons and tissue integrity. Furthermore, we will explore RGC degeneration, variations in microvascular integrity, and microglial responses during the progression of glaucoma in a mouse model. Finally, it should be emphasized that the retina shares anatomical, functional, and pathological similarities with the brain. 16103525.value: 跨物种分析microRNA前体和shRNA的Dicer切割机制

16103525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103525.value: Dicer, an essential ribonuclease in the RNA interference pathway, plays a pivotal role in processing miRNA precursors (pre-miRNAs) and short-hairpin RNAs (shRNAs) into miRNAs and siRNAs that are crucial for gene silencing. These precursors typically comprise a stem of approximately 20-25 base pairs and a loop of variable lengths. While previous research, including studies from our group, has illuminated the influence of multiple RNA elements within the loop and upper stem on Dicer activity, the impact of elements in the middle and lower stem remains elusive. Additionally, although it is known that Dicer interacts with the 5p- and 3p-ends of these RNA molecules with specific nucleotide preferences at the 5p-end, the preferences at the 3p-end are yet to be delineated. To address these gaps, this project proposes the deployment of massively parallel human Dicer cleavage assays to systematically explore the RNA elements within the middle and lower stems, as well as to define the 3p-end preferences. Our approach includes extending this research to include Dicer from other model organisms such as Drosophila melanogaster and Caenorhabditis elegans thereby providing a comparative insight that could reveal both conserved and unique aspects of Dicer function across species. Preliminary data suggest that several RNA elements in these regions significantly modulate Dicer’s cleavage activity, hinting at a complex regulatory mechanism that could be harnessed to refine miRNA biogenesis and enhance gene silencing strategies. By elucidating how these RNA elements interact with Dicer and contribute to its cleavage specificity, this study aims to advance our understanding of miRNA biology and improve gene-silencing technologies through the design of more effective shRNAs. Dicer作为RNA干扰中的关键核糖核酸酶，在将miRNA前体（pre-miRNA）和短发夹RNA（shRNA）加工成对基因沉默至关重要的miRNA和siRNA过程中发挥着核心作用。miRNA前体通常由约20-25个碱基对的茎部结构和长度可变的环部区域组成。尽管先前研究（包括本课题组已经发表的诸多成果）已阐明环部及茎部上段多个RNA元件对Dicer活性的调控作用，但茎部中段与下段元件的影响仍不明确。此外，虽然已知Dicer与这些RNA分子的5'端和3'端相互作用时对5'端具有特定核苷酸偏好性，但3'端的偏好特征尚待解析。 为填补这些知识空白，本项目拟采用大规模并行化的人源Dicer切割实验系统，全面探究茎部中段与下段的RNA元件特征，并明确其3'端偏好性。我们的研究策略还包括将实验体系拓展至黑腹果蝇（Drosophila melanogaster）和秀丽隐杆线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans）等模式生物，通过跨物种比较揭示Dicer功能在进化过程中的保守性与特异性。 初步数据显示，这些区域的若干RNA元件可显著调节Dicer的切割活性，暗示存在复杂的调控机制。该机制的解析将有助于优化miRNA生物合成过程并提升基因沉默的效果。本研究通过阐明这些RNA元件如何与Dicer相互作用并影响其切割特异性，旨在深化对miRNA生物学的认知，并通过设计更高效的shRNAs来推动基因沉默技术的发展。

16103625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103625.value: 焦虑对斑马鱼视觉运动决策的影响

16103625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103625.value: Anxiety is an evolutionarily ancient emotion characterized by heightened fear of existing or impending threats, which causes an increase in defensive behaviors, such as freezing. Although a number of brain areas have been linked to anxiety, the connection between these areas and the sensorimotor pathways for defensive behaviors remains unclear. We propose to use zebrafish larvae as a model system to investigate how anxiety modulates visual pathways to enhance freezing in response to predator-like visual stimuli. Zebrafish have a relatively simple visual system, and we can take advantage of genetic tools to label and manipulate neurons. In addition, zebrafish larvae are transparent, which facilitates functional imaging in the intact, behaving organism. We previously used large-scale functional imaging to identify the pathways for freezing and hunting responses to visual stimuli. We will use aversive stimuli to induce an anxiety-like state in which larvae freeze in response to normally appetitive or neutral visual stimuli. By imaging before and after this manipulation, we will be able to observe how the onset of anxiety changes functional properties of neurons in the visuomotor pathways. We will also investigate the effect of an anti-anxiety drug on these neurons. These experiments will shed light on how sensory pathways can be modulated by emotional states to produce altered behavior. 焦虑是一种在进化上古老的情绪，其特征是对现实或即将发生的威胁的恐惧增强，从而引发防御性行为（如僵直反应）的增加。尽管已有多个脑区被证明与焦虑有关，但这些脑区与介导防御行为的感觉-运动通路之间的联系仍不清楚。 我们拟以斑马鱼幼体作为模型系统，研究焦虑如何调节视觉通路以增强其对捕食者样视觉刺激的僵直反应。斑马鱼的视觉系统相对简单，我们能够利用遗传工具对神经元进行标记和操控。此外，斑马鱼幼体透明的特性，有助于在完整且处于行为状态的个体中进行功能成像。我们此前已通过大规模功能成像鉴定了介导僵直和捕猎反应的视觉通路。本研究将利用厌恶性刺激诱导幼鱼进入焦虑状态，使其在面对原本具有吸引性或中性的视觉刺激时表现出僵直反应。通过在该操控前后进行成像，我们能够观察焦虑发作如何改变视觉运动通路中神经元的功能特性。我们还将进一步探究抗焦虑药物对这些神经元的作用。这些实验将有助于揭示感觉通路如何在情绪状态的调节下产生行为的改变。

16103725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103725.value: 面向神經元群體活動機制的協方差頻譜理論拓展

16103725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103725.value: Recent advances in simultaneous recordings of large numbers of neurons have sparked significant interest in exploring the multi-dimensional structures of neural population activity beyond simple scalar descriptions. A key question is how these dynamic features arise mechanistically and their relationship to circuit connectivity. In our previous work, we proposed the covariance eigenvalue distribution, or spectrum (not to be confused with the power spectrum), as a robust measure to characterize the shape of neural population activity beyond its dimension. Importantly, we developed an analytical theory to explicitly demonstrate how connectivity statistics, including connectivity motifs, influence the spectrum. This theory made it possible to interpret the covariance spectrum as a result of recurrent connections, rather than simply documenting differences and changes in the spectrum without a mechanistic understanding. Being a curve rather than a number, the model spectrum can be fitted robustly to experimental data to estimate the recurrent connection strength. It has been independently shown to achieve impressive quantitative agreements across diverse data, despite relying on a single parameter. However, this empirical success highlights an intriguing theoretical gap. The neural network model used was kept minimal with linear and homogeneous neurons around a stationary state (related to spontaneous brain activity), and these assumptions may not be well justified in applications. On the other hand, there is encouraging numerical evidence suggesting that the spectrum under more complex models may have an intuitive and unifying form; there are also emerging analytical tools in the field that are well-suited for tackling this theoretical challenge. This project aims to close this gap by generalizing the previous theory by investigating recurrent neuronal circuit models extended with key biological properties such as nonlinear neurons and heterogeneous connectivity, and over diverse dynamical regimes including transient activity, which is important for relating to data when animals are performing tasks. Just as the covariance spectrum describes the population activity beyond an average correlation across neurons, we will also develop an analogous cross-population spectrum to characterize interactions between two populations of neurons beyond scalar measures such as the canonical correlation. Lastly, we will validate the capability of the new theory using published experimental data from zebrafish at the neuronal level and human fMRI data at the brain region level by working closely with our collaborators who have extensive expertise in these experimental contexts. 近年來，隨著同時記錄大量神經元活動技術的進步，人們對於突破簡單標量描述、探索神經元族群活動多維結構的產生了濃厚興趣。一個關鍵問題是，這些動力學特徵是由何種機制產生的，以及它們與神經迴路連接結構的關係。在我們先前的工作中，我們提出以協方差特徵值分佈譜（不同於功率譜）作為一種具有魯棒性的度量，來描述神經元族群活動的型態，而不僅是其維度。更重要的是，我們發展了解析理論來清楚地展示網絡連接統計量（例如連結模體）如何影響該特徵譜。這套理論使我們能夠以循環連接的結構來解釋協方差譜，而不是缺乏機制理解下，僅僅記錄該譜的差異與變化。由於特徵譜是一條曲線而非單一數值，模型預測的譜可以地穩定地擬合實驗數據，以估計循環連接的強度。值得一提的是，儘管只包含一個參數，該譜模型仍被獨立地證實能在各種數據集上取得突出的精準擬合。 然而，這些應用上的成功也凸顯出一個重要的理論缺口。我們所用的神經網路模型極為簡化，例如假設神經元在穩態附近（對應于自發性腦活動）呈線性動力學且同質。而這些假設在實際應用中未必有充分支持。另一方面，有初步數值證據顯示，在更複雜的模型下，特徵譜仍可能具有直觀而統一的形式；同時，領域中近期也出現了適合處理此理論挑戰的新的解析工具。 本研究計畫旨在透過推廣已有理論來彌補上述空白：我們將研究擴充包含了關鍵生物學特性（例如非線性神經元與異質連結）的循環神經元網絡模型，並考慮瞬態活動在內的各種動力學狀態，這對於解析動物認知過程中的實驗數據尤為重要。我們也將發展類似特徵譜的「跨族群譜」，以表徵兩個神經元族群之間的相互作用，突破典型相關性係數等標量描述。最後，我們將與在相關實驗領域具有深厚專長的學者密切合作，利用已發表的斑馬魚（神經元層級）與人類功能核磁（腦區層級）數據，驗證新理論的效能。

16103825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103825.value: 全基因組重複與不對稱著絲粒聚集

16103825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103825.value: Whole-genome duplication (WGD) is a common genomic abnormality in cancer, leading to increased genome instability due to the extra DNA and centrosome burden. Following WGD, while many cells undergo multipolar mitosis due to excess centrosomes, a subset of cells can cluster excess centrosomes to undergo pseudo-bipolar mitosis. Notably, bipolar mitotic spindle formation after WGD can be achieved through either symmetric (2–2) or asymmetric centrosome clustering (1–3). Daughter cells inheriting a single centrosome from asymmetrically clustered bipolar mitoses can persist, contributing to the long-term maintenance of the tetraploid genome. The mechanisms behind asymmetric centrosome clustering and the resulting genome instability remain elusive. In this project, we aim to explore the mechanisms and consequences of asymmetric centrosome clustering following WGD. Approaches including cell cycle synchronization, live-cell imaging, and high-resolution microscopy will be employed to induce WGD and monitor subsequent mitotic events. Our initial findings reveal an uneven distribution of the two types of centrosome clustering within a cell line, as well as substantial inter-cell line variability. Moreover, pseudo-bipolar mitosis arising from asymmetric centrosome clustering displays abnormalities in spindle length, microtubule distribution, and chromosome segregation errors during anaphase. To validate and expand on these observations, we will further explore the impact on kinetochore-microtubule attachments, mitotic fidelity, DNA integrity, and cell fate subsequent to asymmetrically clustered bipolar mitosis. Furthermore, we will investigate potential mechanisms promoting asymmetric centrosome clustering, including the contributions of centrosomal linkers, kinesin motors, and key mitotic processes such as cell rounding. Understanding the extent and mechanisms of asymmetric centrosome clustering will enhance our comprehension of WGD’s role in tumorigenesis. 全基因組重複是癌症中常見的基因組異常，導致由於額外的脫氧核糖核酸和著絲粒負擔而增加的基因組不穩定性。隨著全基因組重複的發生，雖然許多細胞因著絲粒過量而發生多極有絲分裂，但部分細胞能夠聚集過量的著絲粒，從而發生假雙極有絲分裂。值得注意的是，全基因組重複後的雙極有絲分裂紡錘體形成可以通過對稱（2-2）或不對稱（1-3）的著絲粒聚集來實現。從不對稱聚集的雙極有絲分裂中繼承單一著絲粒的子細胞可以持續存在，這有助於四倍體基因組的長期維持。不對稱著絲粒聚集及其導致的基因組不穩定性的機制仍然不明確。在本項目中，我們旨在探索全基因組重複後不對稱著絲粒聚集的機制及其後果。我們將採用包括細胞週期同步、活細胞成像和高解析度顯微鏡在內的方法來誘導全基因組重複並監測後續的有絲分裂事件。我們的初步研究結果揭示了在細胞系內兩種著絲粒聚集類型的分佈不均，以及在不同細胞系之間存在顯著的變異。此外，由不對稱著絲粒聚集引起的假雙極有絲分裂在後期表現出紡錘體長度、微管分佈和染色體分離錯誤的異常。為了驗證並擴展這些觀察結果，我們將進一步探討不對稱聚集的雙極有絲分裂對絲粒-微管連接、有絲分裂保真度、脫氧核糖核酸完整性和細胞命運的影響。此外，我們還將研究促進不對稱著絲粒聚集的潛在機制，包括著絲粒連接子、驅動蛋白馬達以及關鍵的有絲分裂過程（例如細胞變圓）的作用。了解不對稱著絲粒聚集的程度和機制將有助於我們理解全基因組重排在腫瘤發生中的作用。

16103925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103925.value: 海綿動物與古菌共生關係的起源與演化

16103925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103925.value: Marine sponges (phylum Porifera) have existed for more than 500 million years, making them one of the most primitive extant animals. Many sponges host dense and diverse microorganisms and form stable and highly specific relationships with them. Sponges’ unique phylogenetic position, together with their stable associations with complex microorganisms, makes them ideal models for the study of animal-microbe symbiosis that could reveal a wide variety of symbiotic strategies and the core features of all extant symbiosis. Marine sponges are frequently reported to be associated with ammonia-oxidizing archaea and archaeal communities in deep-sea sponges have been found to be orders of magnitude higher than in shallow-water sponges. More importantly, specific archaeal lineages exhibit high degree of host specificity in deep-sea Hexactinellida sponges (hereafter referred to as glass sponges), suggesting a vertical transmission of these symbionts. Despite recent findings with marker gene-based microbiome surveys, archaeal genomes associated with glass sponges remain significantly underrepresented, with only nine available in public databases. This is likely due to predominant distributions of glass sponges in deep sea and limiting a comprehensive understanding of the origin and evolution of archaeal symbiosis in sponges. During a recent cruise to the Northwestern Pacific Ocean, we collected 80 glass sponges, covering at least 18 species, from seamounts at depths ranging from 807 to 5,563 meters. These samples serve as valuable resources to significantly reduce the sample bias related to the underrepresented archaeal symbionts associated with glass sponges. In this project, we hypothesize 1) the symbiosis between archaea and sponges originated at the very dawn of animal evolution; and 2) the extant symbioses are a result of the co-adaptation and coevolution of the archaeal symbionts and the sponge hosts. To test our hypotheses, we will 1) address sample bias of the underrepresented archaeal symbionts from glass sponges by generating high-quality archaeal genomes from the 80 glass sponge samples; 2) reconstruct the evolutionary history of archaeal symbionts, estimate their divergence time and co-relate with the divergence of the hosts; 3) deduce genome content of the symbiont ancestors, reconstruct their metabolic potentials, trace their evolutionary trajectory and investigate their adaptative mechanisms toward host-associated lifestyle. Our research will offer comprehensive insights into the origin and evolution of archaeal symbiosis in sponges, highlight the crucial roles of archaea in supporting sponge functionality, and illuminate how this relationships adapt to environmental changes, which could aid in protecting marine ecosystems under climate change. 海綿動物（Porifera 門）在地球上已存在逾五億年，是現存最原始的動物類群之一。許多海綿與密集且多樣化的微生物共生，並與之形成穩定且高度特異的關係。海綿於系統發育上的獨特地位，加上其與複雜微生物間的長期穩定互動，使其成為研究動物—微生物共生關係的理想模式生物，並有助於揭示現存共生系統的核心特徵。 研究顯示，海綿常與氧化氨古菌（ammonia-oxidizing archaea）共生，且深海海綿中的古菌群落豐度遠高於淺水海綿，差異可達數個數量級。更值得關注的是，特定古菌譜系在深海六放海綿（以下簡稱玻璃海綿）中展現出極高的宿主特異性，顯示這些共生體可能透過垂直傳播方式延續。儘管近年來利用標誌基因的微生物群落研究已有重要發現，但與玻璃海綿共生的古菌基因組在資料庫中依然極為匱乏，目前僅有九個已公開。這或許與玻璃海綿主要分佈於深海環境有關，進而限制了我們對海綿-氧化氨古菌共生關係起源與演化的全面理解。 在最近一次於西北太平洋海域的科考航次中，我們自水深 807 至 5,563 公尺的海山採集了 80 個玻璃海綿樣本，涵蓋至少 18 個海綿物種。這些樣本為緩解與玻璃海綿共生之古菌基因組的採樣偏差，提供了極為寶貴的資源。在本研究中，我們將運用高通量定序技術獲取與深海玻璃海綿共生的高品質古菌基因組，藉此大幅減少玻璃海綿氧化氨古菌共生體的採樣偏差。基於所得之高品質基因組，我們將重建氧化氨古菌共生體的演化歷程，推算其分歧時間，並與宿主的分歧歷史進行對應分析；同時推斷共生體祖先的基因組內容，重建其代謝潛能，追蹤其演化軌跡，並探討其向宿主依附型生活方式的適應機制。本研究將全面揭示氧化氨古菌與海綿共生的起源與演化，突顯氧化氨古菌在維持海綿功能中的關鍵角色，並闡明此關係如何適應環境變化，從而為在氣候變遷背景下保護海洋生態系提供重要科學依據。

16104725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16104725.value: 系統甘油三酯代謝狀態如何調控遠端器官腫瘤生長的機制

16104725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104725.value: The body metabolic state has a profound impact on cancer risk and outcomes. However, the molecular mechanisms that link systemic metabolism and tumorigenesis processes remain largely unclear. Using sophisticated genetic tools available in Drosophila Melenogaster, we performed large-scale genetic screening and identified that modulating triacylglycerol (TAG) metabolism in adipocytes strongly affects tumor growth in distant organs. In this proposal, we will describe our plans to delineate the molecular network that functions upstream and downstream of TAG metabolism in adipocytes to regulate distant tumor growth through a systems biology approach. 系統代謝狀態對癌症風險與預後具有深遠影響，然而，系統性代謝與腫瘤發生過程之間的分子機制仍不清楚。我們利用黑腹果蠅（Drosophila melanogaster）成熟的遺傳工具進行大規模基因篩選，發現調控脂肪細胞中的甘油三酯（TAG）代謝狀態會顯著影響遠端器官的腫瘤生長。在本研究計畫中，我們將透過系統生物學方法，闡明脂肪細胞內 TAG 代謝上下游的分子網絡如何影響遠端腫瘤生長。

16104925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16104925.value: 哺乳動物表觀轉錄組單細胞定量測序，對人類和小鼠胚胎植入前發育中RNA假尿苷修飾的研究

16104925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104925.value: Posttranscriptional RNA modifications are present in nearly all RNA species in mammalian cells. Mammalian messenger RNA (mRNA) contains multiple internal modifications, including N6-methyladenosine (m6A), pseudouridine (Ψ), 2'-O-methylation (Nm), 5-methylcytosine (m5C), etc, etc. Notably, m6A and Ψ are recognized as the two most abundant mRNA modifications in mammals. Ψ modification has been instrumental in the development of effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19, where substituting U sites with Ψ in synthetic mRNA vaccines resulted in reduced immune responses and enhanced protein production. However, despite the abundance of Ψ in mammalian mRNA, the lack of efficient mapping approaches has significantly impeded its functional investigation. In contrast, antibody-based m6A -MeRIP-seq has been widely used to map m6A distribution in mammalian mRNA, facilitating extensive studies on m6A biology. To address the technological challenge associated with sequencing mRNA Ψ, my co-workers and I developed the quantitative sequencing method BID-seq in 2023, which uncovers Ψ modification at single-base resolution. Since then, my lab has been applying this innovative BID-seq technique to conduct functional investigations of Ψ modification, particularly in mammalian development. While m6A modification plays a crucial role in early development, the functions of Ψ in mammalian early development remain largely unexplored and have not been systematically studied. Based on BID-seq, my lab further successfully developed single-cell BID-seq (scBID) for mapping Ψ in an individual oocyte or preimplantation embryo. Our preliminary scBID data indicate a high abundance of Ψ modification in mouse and human oocytes and preimplantation embryos. Moreover, mouse embryos of specific pseudouridine synthase knockout exhibit severe developmental defects, highlighting the critical role of Ψ in regulating mammalian preimplantation embryogenesis. In this proposal, we aim to achieve the following objectives: First, we will utilize scBID to map the comprehensive landscape of Ψ modification throughout mouse and human preimplantation development. Second, we will investigate Ψ functions during maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT) and decipher the observed phenotype following Pus enzyme knockout in mouse preimplantation embryos. Third, we will study the functional role of Ψ in human oocyte maturation, as new biomarkers to assess oocyte quality, infertility, and reproductive aging, thereby establishing the groundwork for clinical and diagnostic application of Ψ modification. In summary, this proposal aims to conduct single-cell quantitative mapping of the mammalian epitranscriptome to study Ψ functions in human and mouse preimplantation development, while also examining Ψ modification in human oocyte quality, infertility, and reproductive aging from a perspective of dynamic RNA epitranscriptome. 轉錄後RNA修飾幾乎存在於所有哺乳動物細胞的RNA物種中。哺乳動物的信使RNA（mRNA）包含多種內部修飾，包括N6-甲基腺苷（m6A）、假尿苷（Ψ）、2'-O-甲基化（Nm）、5-甲基胞嘧啶（m5C）等。值得注意的是，m6A和Ψ被認為是哺乳動物中最豐富的兩種mRNA修飾。Ψ修飾在開發針對COVID-19的mRNA疫苗中發揮了重要作用，其中在合成mRNA疫苗中將U位點替換為Ψ，導致免疫反應減少和蛋白質產量增加。然而，儘管Ψ在哺乳動物mRNA中豐富，但缺乏有效的測序方法顯著阻礙了其功能研究。相比之下，基於抗體的m6A-MeRIP-seq已被廣泛用於測序哺乳動物mRNA中的m6A分佈，促進了對m6A生物學功能的廣泛研究。 為了解決與測序mRNA Ψ相關的技術挑戰，我們於2023年開發了定量測序方法BID-seq，該方法能以單碱基分辨率揭示Ψ修飾。自那時以來，我的實驗室一直在應用這一創新的BID-seq技術進行Ψ修飾的功能研究，特別是在哺乳動物發育中。雖然m6A修飾在早期發育中起著至關重要的作用，但Ψ在哺乳動物早期發育中的功能仍然大部分未被探索，且尚未進行系統性研究。基於BID-seq，我的實驗室進一步成功開發了單細胞BID-seq（scBID），用於測序單個卵子或胚胎中的Ψ。我們的初步scBID數據顯示，鼠和人類的胚胎中存在大量Ψ修飾。 在本提案中，我們旨在實現以下目標：首先，我們將利用scBID繪製鼠和人類胚胎植入前發育中Ψ修飾的全面景觀。其次，我們將研究Ψ修飾在MZT期間的功能。第三，我們將研究Ψ在卵子質量中的功能角色，從而為Ψ修飾的臨床應用奠定基礎。總體而言，本項目旨在對哺乳動物表觀轉錄組進行單細胞定量測序，以研究Ψ在胚胎植入前發育中的功能，同時從動態RNA表觀轉錄組的角度研究Ψ修飾與卵子質量。

16200625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200625.value: 氣候變遷下離岸風力發電機颱風風險評估之物理增強神經參數化框架

16200625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16200625.value: Prof Galasso, Carmine Prof ZHANG, Dongqin

16200625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200625.value: Wind energy serves as a critical, almost carbon-neutral and pollution-free source of electricity, significantly contributing to climate change mitigation. To attain the grand goal of restricting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius, annual wind energy installations must escalate to 335 GW per year, far exceeding current rate of 75 GW per year. Offshore wind possesses superior capacity and reliability over its onshore counterparts. However, in the South China Sea region, the typhoon exposure of Offshore Wind Turbines (OWTs) poses significant risks to their structural integrity and operational stability. In 2024, Super Typhoon Yagi destroyed eight turbines in Hainan Province, China, amidst the alarming prospect that future typhoons might even intensify due to climate change. Thus, it becomes imperative to develop advanced risk assessment methods that can support decisions for the long-term resilience of OWTs in the face of typhoon and climate change considerations. This project aims to deliver a novel physics-enhanced neural-parameterized computational paradigm for assessing typhoon-induced risks to OWTs in the South China Sea region under climate change conditions. The proposal integrates four interconnected tasks. Task I leverages data-driven governing equation discovery to enhance the physics-based typhoon (or tropical cyclone, TC) synthesis models in the Western Northern Pacific basin under changing climates, enabling the generation of more realistic TC scenarios. Task II presents fast Neural Operator based high-resolution modelling of TC-induced wind, waves, and surge over the South China Sea, reducing computation per TC from days to seconds. These two tasks set the foundation for Task III, which accelerates the structural load evaluation of OWTs responding to the TC environments for risk assessment. A neural-parameterized stochastic surrogate model will be developed to emulate the OpenFAST wind turbine structural solver with significant speedup (minutes/hours to sub-seconds). Task IV bridges between the research findings with mitigation/adaptation actions. It will produce OWT failure probability maps, which paves the way for design code recommendations. These scientific insights will enable engineers and policymakers to make informed decisions on OWT design, installation, and maintenance. This proposed project is expected to produce research outcomes that will have a tangible impact on the offshore wind energy industry, from tropical cyclones, to hazard and structure, and thus facilitate offshore wind farm development in Hong Kong and other TC prone regions globally. 風力發電作為零碳排放且無污染的電力來源，對減緩氣候變遷具有重大貢獻。為達成全球暖化限制在攝氏1.5度的目標，年度風力發電裝置容量必須提升至每年335吉瓦，遠超過目前每年75吉瓦水準。相較於陸域，離岸風力發電具有更佳的發電容量與可靠性。然而，在南海地區，離岸風力發電機組暴露於颱風中，構成重大風險。2024年，超強颱風摩羯摧毀中國海南省八座風力發電機組，而未來颱風可能因氣候變遷進一步增強。因此，開發先進的風險評估方法以支援離岸風力發電機組在颱風與氣候變遷考量下的長期韌性決策，已成為當務之急。 本計畫旨在建立創新的物理增強神經參數化計算範式，評估氣候變遷條件下南海地區離岸風力發電機組面臨的颱風誘發風險。本提案整合四個相互關聯的任務。任務一運用資料驅動的統御方程式發現技術，增強西北太平洋海域在氣候變遷下基於物理的颱風合成模式，產生更具真實性的熱帶氣旋情境。任務二提出基於神經算子的高解析度建模，模擬熱帶氣旋在南海地區誘發的風場、波浪及風暴潮，將計算時間從數天縮短至數秒。任務三將開發神經參數化隨機替代模式，模擬OpenFAST風力發電機結構求解器，大幅提升計算速度，從數分鐘縮短至亞秒級，以進行結構載重評估。任務四結合研究發現與減緩調適行動，產生離岸風力發電機組失效機率圖，為設計規範建議鋪路。 本計畫的創新性體現在系統性研究架構，整合先進的機器學習技術與傳統的物理建模方法。從氣候模式到海洋環境建模，再到結構動力學分析，最終到風險評估與決策支援，形成完整的研究鏈條。這種整合性方法能更全面地理解離岸風力發電機組在極端天氣事件下的行為，為產業發展提供可靠的科學基礎。在實務應用方面，本計畫產生的失效機率圖與設計規範建議，將直接服務於離岸風電產業的發展需求，不僅能指導新建風場的選址與設計，也能為既有風場的維護與升級提供科學依據。本計畫預期將產生對離岸風力發電產業具有實質影響的研究成果，促進香港及全球其他易受熱帶氣旋影響地區的離岸風場開發，為離岸風力發電機組的颱風風險評估提供新的解決方案，有望在推動清潔能源發展、應對氣候變遷挑戰方面發揮重要作用。

16201125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16201125.value: 多年冻土区沥青路面光热效应及热辐射调控技术研究

16201125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16201125.value: Prof Wang, Jiwei Dr You, Zhilang Dr Zhang, Jing Prof Zhang, Li Min

16201125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201125.value: The construction of high-grade highways in permafrost regions is a critical global scientific challenge that demands urgent solutions. The key to overcoming this challenge lies in ensuring the stability of permafrost foundations under the impacts of climate change and engineering activities. Compared with the Qinghai–Tibet Highway (~10 m wide), the Qinghai–Tibet Expressway has a wider surface, thicker pavement structures, and darker pavement color and exhibits strong heat-absorbing, heat-gathering, and heat-storing features. Permafrost thawing and settlement of the asphalt pavement induced by these photothermal effects is a core obstacle hindering the successful construction of the Qinghai–Tibet Expressway. In previous research, our team revealed that the heat absorption mechanism is the combination of the strong solar radiation in high-altitude permafrost regions and its efficient absorption by the asphalt surface of roadbeds. Previously, we proposed engineering the asphalt surfaces using high-solar-reflectance coatings to decrease the absorption of radiation and thus control the stability of the underlying permafrost providing a potential solution to this challenge. The proposed project will investigate the photothermal effects and radiation regulation of asphalt pavements in permafrost regions on a pilot section of the Qinghai–Tibet Expressway. The proposed project will be divided into three tasks. In Task 1, we will clarify the impact of high-altitude strong radiation and the high absorptivity of dark asphalt pavement on the temperature field of permafrost subgrade, elucidating the photothermal effects and heat accumulation-induced instability mechanism of asphalt pavements in permafrost regions. In Task 2, we will reveal the influence of functional materials on the photothermal performance of coatings and will develop a dark coating with high near-infrared reflectivity and low thermal conductivity suitable for cold and high-radiation conditions, thereby achieving radiative embankment cooling in permafrost regions. In Task 3, the radiative cooling efficiency of the developed coating pavement structure will be assessed based on laboratory model tests and practical engineering applications, particularly its ability to mitigate the heat accumulation caused by the strong absorption of radiation by asphalt pavements under high-altitude conditions. A significant innovation will be the project's ability to elucidate the photothermal effects and heat accumulation-induced instability mechanism of the asphalt pavement in permafrost regions, as well as develop new cooling method for roadbed structures. This will provide technological guidelines for mitigating the heat accumulation of the high absorptivity of asphalt pavements and thereby facilitate the construction of the Qinghai–Tibet Expressway. 多年冻土区高等级公路修筑技术是亟待解决的世界性科技难题，如何保障气候变化和工程活动双重影响下冻土地基的稳定是解决这一问题的关键。相较于窄幅的青藏公路（宽约10m），青藏高速具有宽幅路基高聚热、厚层路面结构强储热、黑色沥青路面辐射强吸收的“宽、厚、黑”显著聚热特性，沥青路面光热效应诱发的冻土地基融沉问题是制约青藏高速成功修建的核心难题。本研究团队前期揭示了高海拔多年冻土区太阳强辐射和沥青路面辐射强吸收的复合吸热机制，提出采用高太阳光反射率的涂层材料来改变工程表面辐射吸收来控制下部冻土稳定的思路，为解决这一难题提供了可能。 本项目依托青藏高速先导试验段，开展多年冻土区公路沥青路面光热效应与热辐射调控技术研究，为达到研究目标，设置了3项研究任务。在任务1，我们将解析高原强辐射与黑色沥青路面辐射强吸收特性对冻土路基温度场的影响，阐明青藏高原多年冻土区公路工程沥青路面光热效应与聚热失稳机制。在任务2，我们将揭示功能性材料对涂层光热性能的影响，研发适用于高寒、强辐射条件下的近红外高反射率-低导热路面用深色涂层材料，实现青藏高原多年冻土区涂层路基辐射制冷；在任务3，将基于室内试验和现场测试评估所研发近红外热反射-低导热深色涂层路基结构辐射制冷效能，特别是其在缓解高海拔条件下沥青路面辐射强吸收所导致的聚热效应方面的性能。 本研究的创新点在于其将揭示青藏高原多年冻土区公路工程沥青路面光热效应与聚热失稳机制，并提出一种新的冷却路基结构，将为解决/缓解高原强辐射条件下公路工程黑色沥青路面辐射强吸收引发的聚热效应提供科技支撑，助力青藏高速公路建设。

16201625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16201625.value: 高質素邊緣文本到圖像生成

16201625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201625.value: Text-to-image (T2I) generation has emerged a transformative technology to impact different facets of modern life. Central to T2I technology is the diffusion model, which enables the generation of diverse images. However, existing diffusion models demand significant computational resources, limiting their use to cloud platforms consisting of high-end workstations. This cloud-based approach leads to several critical drawbacks, such as high bandwidth, costly maintenance, significant interactive latency, and severe data privacy concerns. To address these limitations, T2I generation on edge devices has been proposed. Despite commendable initial efforts, the prior art suffers from fixed aspect ratios, low resolution (only 512×512 pixels) and long generation times (in seconds), resulting in a user experience and model performance subpar to those associated with cloud services. The proposed project will develop novel, portable and cost-effective T2I models that can run directly on edge devices, delivering performance comparable to cloud services. We will design a cutting-edge on-device foundation model capable of promptly generating high-quality images, i.e., high-resolution images (e.g., 1024x1024 pixels) with flexible aspect ratios, compelling visual appeal and accurate text alignment. To achieve this, we will address two key challenges through advanced network optimization and design: * Limited Memory and Computational Resources on Edge Devices: Current T2I models struggle with out-of-memory (OOM) problem on mobile devices when generating 1024x1024 images. We will enable high-quality on-device image generation by systematically optimizing the diffusion backbone and developing an ultra-fast one-step distillation algorithm. Furthermore, we will enhance the image decoding efficiency from latents by improving the latent space, and design a smaller and faster decoder tailored for edge devices. * Resource-Intensive Training: Training a foundation model from scratch is resource-intensive. To streamline this process, we will develop an efficient multi-stage (low-to-high resolution) training approach. Furthermore, we will design an automated data engine to curate diverse datasets, and comprehensively evaluate our edge model. This proposed project will leverage our extensive expertise in efficient network design and AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things). The outcomes will be disseminated through top-tier academic publications and open-source releases of our optimized models. The proposed work will advance academic research on high-quality edge T2I generation, stimulate wide industrial deployment, democratize its diverse applications due to privacy protection, and reshape how digital media is produced, customized and consumed. 文本到圖像（Text-to-Image，T2I）生成已成為一項變革性技術，對現代生活的不同方面產生了深遠的影響。T2I 技術的核心在於擴散模型（Diffusion Model），這模型使生成多樣化的圖像成為可能。然而，現有的擴散模型需要大量的計算資源，以致其通常在高端工作站雲平台上使用。這種基於雲的方式帶來了數個關鍵缺點，包括高帶寬、昂貴的維護成本、顯著的交互延遲以及嚴重的數據隱私問題。為了解決這些限制，近年來提出在邊緣設備（Edge Devices）上進行 T2I 生成。儘管初步努力值得肯定，但現有技術仍存在固定的長寬比、低解析度（僅 512×512 像素）以及長生成時間（以秒計），導致用戶體驗和模型性能不及雲服務。 本提案項目旨在開發新穎、便攜且具有成本效益的 T2I 模型，使其能夠直接在邊緣設備上運行，並提供與雲服務相當的性能。我們將設計一種尖端的設備內基礎模型（Foundation Model），能夠快速生成高品質圖像，例如高解析度圖像（如 1024×1024 像素），並具有靈活的長寬比、引人注目的視覺吸引力以及準確的文本對齊。為了實現這一目標，我們將通過先進的網絡優化（Network Optimization）和設計來解決兩個關鍵挑戰： * 邊緣設備上的內存和計算資源有限：當生成 1024×1024 像素的圖像時，當前的 T2I 模型在移動設備上面臨內存不足（OOM，Out-of-Memory）問題。我們將通過系統優化擴散骨幹（Diffusion Backbone）以及開發超快速的一步蒸餾算法（One-Step Distillation Algorithm），以實現高品質的設備內圖像生成。此外，我們將通過改善潛在空間（Latent Space）來提高潛在圖像解碼效率，並設計一種更小及更快的解碼器（Decoder），以適應邊緣設備的需求。 * 資源密集型訓練：從頭開始訓練一個基礎模型需要大量資源。為了簡化這過程，我們將開發一種高效的多階段（Multi-Stage）訓練方法（Low-to-High Resolution Training Approach）。此外，我們將設計一個自動化數據引擎（Automated Data Engine），以策劃多樣化的數據集，並對我們的邊緣模型進行全面評估。 本提案項目將利用我們在高效網絡設計（Efficient Network Design）和人工智慧物聯網（AIoT，Artificial Intelligence of Things）方面的廣泛專業知識。結果將通過頂尖的學術出版物和我們優化模型的開源發布進行傳播。擬議的工作將推進高品質邊緣 T2I 生成的學術研究，刺激其在工業領域的廣泛應用，並因其隱私保護的特性，使其多樣化應用民主化，從而重塑數位媒體的生產、定制和消費方式。

16202525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16202525.value: 水溶性有機物受氧化自由基攻擊生成（亞）硝基副產物的前驅物與機制

16202525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16202525.value: Prof HE, Ding Prof Yang, Xin

16202525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202525.value: The substantial presence of synthetic chemicals, resulting from their widespread use, in both natural and engineered water systems impacts human health and the environment, underscoring the importance of micropollutant removal, which is primarily conducted through advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). However, the highly oxidative radicals produced in AOPs, which are intended to destroy micropollutants, often react with dissolved organic matter (DOM) in much larger quantities rather than the micropollutants in trace amounts, leading to reduced process efficiency and the formation of undesirable oxidation byproducts. Nitro(so) byproducts are a group of emerging contaminants that are particularly concerning due to their high toxicity and limited biodegradability; they create risks to aquatic organisms and human health. DOM serves as the primary precursor for these nitro(so) byproducts, as its dissolved organic nitrogen content reacts with the radical species. Additionally, non-nitrogenous components in DOM can react with reactive nitrogen species to form nitro(so) byproducts. The complex interactions within the heterogeneous category of DOM, along with the involvement of various radical species, have limited our understanding of and ability to control the formation of nitro(so) byproducts. Newly developed selective titration assays and refined mass spectrometry techniques are providing innovative tools to explore this complex system down to the moiety and elemental levels. In the proposed project, we will use these techniques, combined with advanced data analysis methods (e.g., machine learning and linkage analysis), to differentiate and identify the main precursors to nitro(so) byproducts in DOM and to identify the formation pathways and mechanisms of these byproducts of the reactions involving the diverse radicals produced in the AOPs that are commonly used for water and wastewater treatment. We will also investigate and confirm the formation pathways of nitro(so) byproducts using model nitrogenous and non-nitrogenous precursor compounds. The proposed project will enhance our fundamental understanding of how nitro(so) byproducts are produced by the interactions between specific DOM precursors and radical species. The established universal and transferable principles will be applicable to the evaluation and selection of AOPs for micropollutant removal in waters where various radical species are generated, transformed (due to radical–matrix interactions), and subsequently consumed by nitrogen-containing components of DOM. The proposed research will also provide a theoretical basis for engineering strategies that can achieve both micropollutant removal and nitro(so) byproduct control in AOPs, contributing to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal 6 (clean water and sanitation) and Goal 14 (life below water). 由於合成化學品的廣泛使用，這些化學物質在自然和工程水系統中的大量存在影響了人類健康和環境，突顯了去除微汙染物的重要性，而這一過程主要通過高級氧化過程實現。然而，在高級氧化過程中產生的用於降解微汙染物的高氧化性自由基往往會與水體中大量存在的水溶性有機物反應，而非與微量存在的微汙染物反應，從而導致高級氧化過程效率降低並產生不良的氧化副產物。（亞）硝基副產物是一類新興汙染物，因其高毒性和有限的生物降解性而備受關注；它們會對水生生物和人類健康構成風險。水溶性有機物是這些（亞）硝基副產物的主要前體，因為其水溶性有機氮組分會與自由基發生反應。 此外，水溶性有機物中的非氮成分也可以與活性氮物種反應，生成（亞）硝基副產物。水溶性有機物中多相組分間的複雜相互作用，以及多種自由基物種的參與，限制了我們對（亞）硝基副產物形成的理解和控制能力。新開發的選擇性滴定分析法和精密的高分辨質譜技術為探索這一複雜系統提供了創新工具，能夠深入到化學基團和元素水平。在擬議的項目中，我們將結合這些技術與先進的數據分析方法（例如，機器學習和關聯性分析），以區分和識別水溶性有機物中（亞）硝基副產物的主要前體，並識別這些副產物在水溶性有機物與水處理常用高級氧化體系產生的多種自由基相互作用過程中的生成路徑和機制。我們還將使用含氮和不含氮的模型化合物作為前體來研究和確認（亞）硝基副產物的形成路徑。該項目將增強我們對特定水溶性有機物前體與不同自由基物種相互作用下（亞）硝基副產物生成機制的基本理解。所建立的通用和可轉移原則將適用於在不同自由基物種生成、轉化（由於自由基-基質相互作用）並隨後被水溶性有機物中含氮成分消耗的水體中評估和選擇用於去除微汙染物的高級氧化過程。該研究還將為實現高級氧化過程中微汙染物去除和（亞）硝基副產物控制的工程策略提供理論基礎，助力聯合國可持續發展目標六（清潔水和衛生）和目標十四（海洋生態）。

16202725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16202725.value: 合作風險緩解的機制設計：準時交付異常情况處理的理論與應用

16202725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202725.value: This proposed research addresses an emerging issue in the rapidly growing online meal delivery business. In this sector, riders (delivery personnel) constantly face the stress of potential lateness. A late delivery means a negative mark in their performance, and often results in penalties. Sometimes the penalty may be too high to bear for the concerned rider as an individual, e.g., when compared with the daily income for the concerned rider. To avoid these penalties, riders may resort to undesirable actions, such as traffic violations or emotional outbursts. While delivery platforms could alleviate this issue by loosening delivery schedules, it is hard to eliminate it entirely due to inherent uncertainties in the delivery process. The essential problem in the above situation is how to handle disruptions in operations of meal delivery, where the main challenge is the inclusion of risk preference, an issue that has not been addressed in disruption management. Specifically, the riders’ tendency of avoiding the penalty is known as loss averse, a form of risk averse. The platform is risk neutral as it handles a large number of meal delivery trips. Given the conflicts of risk preference, some mechanisms are needed to align the platform and riders with conflict of risk preferences. In this project, we propose exploring the concept of loss sharing as a potential solution. The project consists of two phases: developing a theoretical foundation and applying these theories to disruption management in meal delivery. In Phase 1, we will analyze a group of independent, loss-averse newsvendors. In a loss-sharing mechanism, if a newsvendor incurs a negative reward, the loss will be distributed among all newsvendors according to predetermined rules. To ensure riders are willing to participate, we will base our model on cooperative game theory. In Phase 2, we will examine disruption management for on-time delivery, utilizing the theories developed in Phase 1. This phase introduces new complexities in the operations, as each rider may choose to take risky actions during delivery. A mechanism will be developed to dynamically align these actions with the risk-neutral delivery schedule. We have conducted preliminary studies as proof of concept for this proposal and have shared our ideas with one meal delivery company, receiving positive feedback. 本研究關注的是外送餐業務中騎士（配送員）所處的困境。騎士們常常面臨送餐延誤帶來的壓力，尤其是延誤罰款。有時罰款金額對相關騎士個人而言可能過高，一次延誤的 罰款會高於騎士的每日收入。為了避免這些罰款，騎士可能會採取一些違規行為，例如違反交通規則，甚至情緒失控。雖然外送平台可以透過放寬配送時間表來緩解這個問題，但由於配送過程中固有的不確定性，很難完全消除這個問題。 上述問題在本質上屬於營運管理的異常狀況處理。送餐延誤牽涉到了其中尚未解決的一個問題，即風險偏好理論的納入。具體而言，騎士規避罰款的傾向被稱為損失厭惡，是風險規避的一種形式。外帶平台由於處理大量的送餐行程，因此風險中立。風險偏好的衝突，需要一些機制來協調平台和騎士的行為。 在本專案中，我們提出損失分擔的概念作為一個潛在的解決方案。本計畫分為兩個階段：建構理論基礎，並將這些理論應用於送餐異常狀況管理。 在第一階段，我們的研究是基於經典的報童模型。考慮一組獨立的厭惡損失的報童，在損失分擔機制中，如果一個報童的收益為負，其損失將根據預定規則在所有報童之間分攤。為了確保送餐員願意參與，我們將以合作博弈論為基礎來建構模型。 在第二階段，我們將利用第一階段所發展的理論，研究準時送餐的異常狀況管理。此階段為營運帶來了新的複雜性，因為每個送餐員在送餐過程中都可能選擇採取冒險行動。我們將發展一種機制，將這些行動與風險中立的送餐計畫動態地協調起來。 我們已經對該方案進行了初步研究，並且作為概念驗證，與一家送餐公司分享了我們的想法，並獲得了積極的回饋。

16202825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16202825.value: 用于柔性高压直流系统的压接式β-Ga2O3肖特基势垒二极管

16202825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202825.value: In next-generation high-voltage power electronics, ultrawide-bandgap beta-phase Gallium Oxide (β-Ga2O3) devices emerge as strong contenders. With a high critical breakdown electric field (Ecrit) of 6–8 MV/cm and the availability of large-area melt-grown single-crystal substrates, β-Ga2O3 has spurred global interest for high-voltage applications. However, most current research focuses primarily on the electrical and thermal performance of β-Ga2O3 chips, overlooking other challenges encountered in high-voltage applications. In high-voltage power electronics like flexible HVDC systems, the press-pack package is preferred for its high current conduction capability, scalable insulation design, and excellent mechanical stability. There is a notable lack of research addressing the key issues associated with press-pack packages for β-Ga2O3 devices. Specifically, there are no studies on β-Ga2O3's ability to withstand mechanical pressures without fracturing. Furthermore, knowledge about the thermal design considerations for β-Ga2O3 devices with press-pack packages is absent. Lastly, the effects of external mechanical stress on the electrical performance of β-Ga2O3 have little been explored in current research. To demonstrate the feasibility of β-Ga2O3 devices in flexible HVDC systems, this project first aims to develop a β-Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diode (SBD) with breakdown voltage (Vbr) and specific on-resistance (RON,sp) comparable to existing press-pack Si fast recovery diodes. The proposed β-Ga2O3 SBD will employ trench structures with high-k dielectrics in active regions, along with a deep mesa and thick polymer dielectric passivation at the terminal. This design avoids the challenges of p-type doping in β-Ga2O3. Furthermore, this project will investigate key issues caused by press-pack package for β-Ga2O3 SBDs. First, it will explore the critical fracture strength of β-Ga2O3 substrates with various thicknesses. Second, it will optimize the thermal resistance of press-pack β-Ga2O3 SBDs based on a thinned substrate. Lastly, it will examine the effects of external mechanical stress on carrier mobility in β-Ga2O3. The findings from these three studies will also provide valuable insights for the development and application of other types of β-Ga2O3 devices. Press-pack package is a crucial step in advancing β-Ga2O3 devices for high-voltage power electronics applications, underscoring the urgency and significance of this research. This project tackles key technical challenges while providing an application-oriented perspective that will inform future β-Ga2O3 research. By exploring the possibility of press-pack β-Ga2O3 devices, this project aims to pave the way for new developments in next-generation power electronics. 在下一代高压电力电子器件中，超宽带隙β相氧化镓（β-Ga2O3）器件成为强有力的竞争者。β-Ga2O3器件的临界击穿电场（Ecrit）高达6-8 MV/cm，且可利用熔融法生长大面积的单晶衬底，因此在全球范围内引起了人们对其高压应用的兴趣。然而，目前大多数研究主要集中在β-Ga2O3器件的电气和热性能上，而忽略了其在高压应用中可能遇到的其他挑战。在柔性高压直流系统等电力电子应用场景中，压接式封装因其高电流传导能力、可扩展的绝缘设计和出色的机械稳定性而备受青睐。目前，针对β-Ga2O3器件压接式封装的研究明显不足。具体而言，目前尚无关于β-Ga2O3器件的机械应力承受能力的研究。此外，缺少与压接式β-Ga2O3器件的散热设计考量。最后，关于压接式封装中机械应力对β-Ga2O3器件电性能的影响研究也很少。 为了证明β-Ga2O3器件在柔性高压直流系统中应用的可行性，本项目首先会开发一种β-Ga2O3肖特基势垒二极管(SBD)，其击穿电压(Vbr)和比导通电阻(RON,sp)可与现有的压接式硅基快速恢复二极管相媲美。该β-Ga2O3肖特基势垒二极管将在有源区采用沟槽结构与high-k电介质，并在终端区采用深台面和厚聚合物电介质钝化层。这种设计避免了β-Ga2O3中p型掺杂的挑战。此外，本项目还将研究与β-Ga2O3 SBD压接式封装相关的问题，诸如压接式封装中β-Ga2O3器件的机械性能、热阻特性、电学性能等。相关成果也将为其他类型β-Ga2O3器件的开发和应用提供宝贵的参考。 压接式封装技术是推动β-Ga2O3器件在高压电力电子领域应用的关键一步，凸显了本研究的紧迫性和重要性。本项目在攻克关键技术难题的同时，也为未来的β-Ga2O3研究提供了应用导向的视角。该项目旨在通过探索压接式β-Ga2O3器件的可能性，为下一代电力电子技术的新发展铺平道路。

16204025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204025.value: eVTOL飛行器輕質材料非剛性旋翼在實際飛行環境中的氣動聲學特性

16204025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204025.value: The low-altitude economy (LAE) has been developing rapidly. The multirotor electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft is a widely used transportation type in LAE, with sizes ranging from small drones to urban air mobility vehicles. However, it often encounters complex wind conditions that can significantly affect operational safety and noise emission when flying in urban environments. Noise remains a major barrier to public acceptance of eVTOLs, with flow-rotor interaction being the dominant source of noise. While there have been ongoing efforts to understand the noise produced by rigid rotor blades, the widespread use of lightweight materials in eVTOL rotors introduces a substantial research gap regarding the aerodynamics and acoustics of complex blade deformation under realistic flight conditions. The proposed project aims to investigate the aeroacoustics of lightweight non-rigid eVTOL rotors, undergoing flow-induced deformation under realistic flight conditions. A combination of experimental, numerical, and analytical approaches will be employed. In addition, an effective noise reduction method will be developed for low-noise rotors. First, experimental studies on the time-varying blade deformation and the associated noise generation will be conducted in an anechoic wind tunnel. An analytical model for computing the rotor noise with blade deformation consideration will be developed based on the input deformation measurements. Second, experimental and numerical studies will be performed to study blade-vortex interaction (BVI) and the resultant interaction noise when blade deformation occurs under the forward flight condition. The formation and properties of tip vortices and interaction process can be affected by the complex deformation, which will be studied using stereo time-resolved particle image velocimetry. Simultaneous measurements will be conducted using a phased microphone array to capture transient noise sources during BVI. Third, eVTOLs typically operate at lower Reynolds numbers than helicopters, leading to complex boundary layer (BL) physics, which is also influenced by blade motion. A non-intrusive temperature-sensitive paint system will be developed to visualize the BL states on the rotating blade, thereby quantifying the impact of blade deformation on BL states and noise characteristics. Finally, a passive blade motion control method using a flap structure will be used to improve aerodynamics and reduce noise. Proof-of-concept tests have demonstrated promising broadband noise reduction potential of the method. The research results will fill the gaps in our understanding of the effect of time-varying blade deformations on eVTOL rotor noise under realistic flight conditions. Additionally, the findings will contribute to the advancement of low noise eVTOL designs. 近年來，低空經濟發展迅速。其中，多旋翼電垂直起降（eVTOL）飛行器是一種廣泛使用的交通方式，其尺寸從小型無人機到城市空中載人交通工具不等。然而，在城市環境中飛行時，eVTOL飛行器通常會遇到複雜的風場條件，這對操作安全和噪聲排放產生顯著影響。目前，噪聲仍然是公眾接受eVTOL飛行器的主要障礙，其中流動和旋翼相互作用是主要的噪聲來源。儘管目前正在進行不斷的研究以理解剛性旋翼葉片產生的噪聲，但在eVTOL飛行器旋翼中，其廣泛使用的是輕質材料，從而引入了一個重要的研究空白，即關於在真實飛行條件下葉片材料導致的複雜變形對其空氣動力學和聲學特性的影響。因此，該項目旨在研究輕質非剛性eVTOL飛行器旋翼在流動誘導變形影響下的空氣動力學和聲學特性。該研究將同時結合實驗、數值模擬和理論分析的方法。同時，基於槳葉變形特性，開發一種有效的降噪方法。首先，在靜音風洞中進行實驗研究，測量葉片變形和噪聲特性。基於測量獲得的隨時間變化的變形量，開發一個考慮葉片變形的旋翼噪聲的分析模型。其次，在旋翼前飛工況下進行實驗和數值模擬研究，考慮葉片變形時葉片-渦流相互作用及其產生的噪聲的機理。複雜的葉片變形會影響葉間渦的形成和以及與槳葉相互作用的過程，從而改變噪聲產生的機制。這些複雜的流動干擾過程將通過時序粒子圖像速測技術進行研究。同時，使用麥克風陣列進行同步噪聲測量，以捕捉葉片-渦流相互作用時的瞬時噪聲源。第三，eVTOL飛行器通常在較低的雷諾數下飛行，因此導致及其複雜的槳葉表面邊界層物理特性，這些特性也受到葉片變形的影響。該項目將開發一種基於溫敏漆的非侵入式測量系統，用于可視化旋轉葉片上的邊界層狀態，從而量化葉片變形對邊界層狀態和旋翼噪聲特性的影響。最後，該項目將設計一種被動槳葉姿態控制方法來改善空氣動力學並降低噪聲。概念驗證測試已證明該方法在降低寬頻噪聲方面具有潛力。研究結果將填補我們對真實飛行條件下隨時間變化的葉片變形對eVTOL飛行器旋翼噪聲影響的理解空白。此外，研究結果將有助於低噪聲eVTOL飛行器設計的發展。

16204125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204125.value: 用於超高效固態熱泵的大熱彈效應馬氏體合金研發

16204125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204125.value: Solid-state heat-pumping using first-order phase transition of shape memory alloys (SMAs) is a promising green alternative to traditional vapor-compression technology. However, the heat-pumping energy efficiency is limited by the intrinsic large phase-transition hysteresis of SMAs. Thus, it is desired to explore non-phase-transition-based heat-pumping for higher efficiency. One strategic way is to utilize adiabatic temperature change (∆T_ad) from anhysteretic linear elastic deformation. In most materials, this thermoelastic effect (TeE) only generates ∆T_ad of ~0.2 K, but we found that some martensitic alloys are exceptions. Recently, we studied the TeE in [100]-textured polycrystals of low-symmetry martensitic phase in ferroelastic Ti78Nb22 alloy. A ∆T_ad of 4–5K was observed under 700MPa linear-elastic compression at temperatures of 413−473K. This large TeE caused a material-level COP (i.e. energy efficiency) of 87, far exceeding typical values of 4–23 in SMAs. According to theory of thermoelasticity, such a large TeE was attributed to the macroscopic large linear thermal expansion (α_l=10-4/K) of the [100]-textured polycrystals. When stressing the more expensive [100]-oriented monocrystal, the intrinsic giant α_l of 3×10-4/K can bring ∆T_ad to 15K. Even higher ∆T_ad of 21−31K was predicted in [100]-oriented Mn87Cu13 and [001]-oriented Mn80Ga20 martensitic monocrystals. These results are very inspiring and indicate the big potential of cost-effective [100] and [001] textured polycrystals in obtaining large TeE for real-world applications. Nevertheless, producing the desired strong textures in the martensitic polycrystals is challenging; a systematic study is needed to explore the detailed thermomechanical processing paths. This project aims to achieve large TeE in [100] and [001] strongly textured martensitic polycrystals of Ti78Nb22, Mn87Cu13 and Mn80Ga20 for ultrahigh-efficiency solid-state heat-pumping. The desired martensite textures will be produced by three steps: (1) generating <001> strong texture in parent phase via directional solidification, (2) forming martensite (thermally stable up to 480K) at room temperature and (3) controlling martensite texture via reorientation-dominated deformation. Optimal processing schemes will be established based on iterations of alloy fabrication, texture characterization and property measurement. The critical roles of the parent-phase texture, variant reorientation and dislocation slips in martensite texture formation and the resulting macroscopic α_l, ∆T_ad and material COP will be identified. Through systematic efforts, this project will produce textured martensitic polycrystals exhibiting ∆T_ad of 10−15K at temperatures of 380−473K, opening a new approach to high-efficiency heat-pumping for industrial heat supply. 基於形狀記憶合金（SMA）一級相變的固態熱泵技術有潛力取代傳統蒸氣壓縮技術。然而，SMA 固有的相變滯後很大，限制了制熱能效。因此，探索非相變機制的熱泵方法成為提高能效的關鍵方向。其中一種策略是利用無滯後的線性彈性變形所引起的絕熱溫度變化（∆T_ad）。在多數材料中，這種熱彈性效應（TeE）所產生的 ∆T_ad 約僅為 0.2 K，但我們發現某些馬氏體合金是例外。 近期，我們研究了 Ti78Nb22 鐵彈合金低對稱馬氏體相的 [100] 織構多晶體之熱彈效應。在 413−473 K 的環境溫度下，施加 700 MPa 線彈性壓縮，得到的 ∆T_ad 達 4–5 K。產生的材料能效（COP）高達 87，遠超過 SMA 的典型值（4–23）。根據熱彈性理論，這種大熱彈效應歸因於多晶體的大熱膨脹係數（α_l = 10^-4/K）。對於成本更高的 [100] 單晶，其固有的超大 α_l（3×10^-4/K）可使 ∆T_ad 提升至 15 K。[100] 晶向 Mn87Cu13 與 [001] 晶向 Mn80Ga20 馬氏體單晶體的 ∆T_ad 更高達 21−31 K。這些結果極具啟發性，顯示出以低成本製備的 [100] 和 [001] 織構多晶體在實現大熱彈效應並應用於實際熱泵的巨大潛力。然而，在馬氏體多晶體中製備理想的強織構仍面臨挑戰，須系統性地研究具體的熱機加工路徑。 本項目旨在於 [100]/[001] 強織構 Ti78Nb22、Mn87Cu13 與 Mn80Ga20 馬氏體多晶體中實現大熱彈效應，用於超高能效固態熱泵。所需的馬氏體織構將透過三個步驟製備：(1) 通過定向凝固在母相中生成 <001> 強織構，(2) 在室溫下得到可穩定存在至 480 K 的馬氏體相，(3) 利用以重取向機制主導的變形調控馬氏體織構。透過合金製備、織構表徵與性能測量的反覆迭代，建立最適製程方案。本研究將釐清母相織構、變體重定向與位錯滑移在馬氏體織構形成中的關鍵作用，以及其對宏觀 α_l、∆T_ad 和材料 COP 的影響。經系統研究，本計畫將製備出在 380−473 K 溫度範圍內展現 ∆T_ad 達 10−15 K 的馬氏體多晶材料，為高效固態熱泵開創新途徑。

16204225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204225.value: 建築協作機器人自適應主動性設計：提升人機協作中的安全、信任與效率

16204225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204225.value: The construction industry around the globe is riddled with unsatisfactory safety and productivity records. Moreover, the construction industry in Hong Kong has longstanding problems deriving from an ageing workforce, where the average age of the registered workers is 47 years. In such a labour-intensive industry, human-robot collaboration (HRC) is increasingly recognised as a possible solution to alleviating physically demanding tasks, increasing productivity, and enhancing the sustainability of the workforce. For smooth and efficient HRC, a collaborative robot (cobot) must anticipate the collaborative intentions of human workers and take the initiative to assist them before being explicitly asked. Great effort has been invested to achieve such proactiveness, but the varied work environments and unstructured task processes of construction introduce many uncertainties that undermine such collaboration. Without awareness of uncertainty, a cobot’s proactive behaviour could be more of a hindrance or a safety risk than a help. How much should the cobot’s decisions be trusted? Should the cobot still be proactive when not confident of the prediction? These questions are key to ensuring a safe and trustworthy HRC but remain to be investigated in the construction industry. The objective of this research is to propose a novel approach for construction cobots to adjust their proactivity dynamically in response to uncertainty in construction tasks and human risk preferences. Three interconnected challenges will be addressed: (1) modelling and predicting the implicit collaborative intentions of human workers taking into consideration spatio-temporal variance and the dual-agent dynamics of collaborative behaviours in construction tasks; (2) developing a measure of confidence for the predicted collaborative intentions taking uncertainties stemming from both novel task settings and ambiguous task structures into consideration; and (3) designing a strategy to adjust proactiveness with regard to the prediction confidence and dynamic changes of human trust in cobots. Real-world experiments will be conducted with an industrial partner to validate the adaptive proactivity strategy across various construction tasks, comparing it against both reactive and fixed proactive strategies. The research outcome is expected to ensure better worker safety in construction HRC, cultivate trust between human workers and cobots, and enable the wilder application of robots in the construction industry. The findings will advance our comprehension of interactions between intelligent agents (human-human and human-robot) carrying out intricate tasks, refine uncertainty modelling in collaborative decision-making, and inform future human-robot collaboration workflows from a human-cantered viewpoint in the era of construction 5.0. 全球建築業長期面臨安全和生產力挑戰。在香港，隨著勞動力老齡化（註冊工人平均年齡為47歲），此問題將進一步加劇。在勞動密集型行業中，人機協作能減輕體力勞動負擔、提高生產力並確保勞動力可持續。為實現高效人機協作，協作機器人需預測人類工人的協作意圖，並主動提供幫助。 然而，建築任務工作場地多樣、任務流程非標準，為機器人的協作決策帶來巨大挑戰。在缺乏不確定性評價的情況下，協作機器人的主動行為可能成為阻礙，甚至引發安全隱患。關於機器人決策應被信任的程度以及在預測不確定時是否應保持主動性等核心問題，在建築行業中尚未得到充分探討。 本研究旨在提出一種新穎的建築機器人寫作決策框架，使其根據任務不確定性和人類風險偏好動態調整主動性。本研究將解決三個核心挑戰：1）建模與預測人類工人的隱性協作意圖，考慮建築任務中的時空變異性和雙代理動態特性； 2）開發基於預測意圖的不確定性信心度量方法； 3）設計主動性調整策略，綜合考慮預測信心和人類對機器人的動態信任變化。本研究將與建築企業合作，通過多種建築任務的實驗驗證所提出的自適應主動性框架，並與反應式和固定主動性策略進行比較。 研究結果有望提高建築人機協作中的工人安全性，培養人類對機器人的信任，並促進機器人在建築業的廣泛應用。此外，所提出的方法將深化對智能代理（人-人和人-機）在複雜任務中交互的理解，改進協作決策中的不確定性建模，並從以人為中心的視角為建築5.0時代的人機協作工作流程提供指導。

16204325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204325.value: 基於毫米波雷達技術的多模態大語言模型輔助乾眼症評估系統

16204325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204325.value: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent condition that affects tens of millions of individuals worldwide. In Hong Kong, approximately 30% of the population is affected, creating a significant economic burden on the healthcare system. DED is characterized by an unstable, hyperosmolar tear film, which leads to inflammation and damage to the ocular surface and nerves. Regular, long-term monitoring of disease severity is essential for timely and appropriate treatment adjustments. However, managing DED remains challenging because of individual variations, complex underlying causes, patient adherence issues, and fluctuating symptoms, all of which are further exacerbated by limited medical resources. To address these challenges, recent efforts have concentrated on developing home-based DED-screening methods involving multiple modalities. Different from existing solutions, our approach extends beyond screening to focus on disease progression management and monitoring of key indicators in home settings. Specifically, we propose a multimodal large language model (LLM)-assisted DED assessment system based on mmWave radar technology, offering a low-cost and non-invasive solution. The goal of the proposed project is to transform DED management from the traditional hospital-centric model into a home-centric approach. The scope will encompass early screening of high-risk individuals, regular assessments of disease severity, and monitoring of the tear break-up time (TBUT) indicator to evaluate treatment effectiveness and enable timely adjustments to treatment plans. We plan to achieve our objectives in two stages. First, we will develop a DED assessment system that leverages mmWave radar as the sole sensing modality without computational resource constraints. This system will provide highly accurate indicators of disease progression and TBUT, enabling more precise adjustments to treatment plans. The proposed system will focus on four key aspects: i) detecting DED symptoms using antenna-coded mmWave radar; ii) aligning multimodal symptoms between electronic health records (EHRs) with mmWave signals; iii) distilling multimodal features through a specially designed DED-related LLM; and iv) applying multitask learning for DED assessments using mmWave signals alone. Second, we will deploy the DED assessment system on resource-constrained edge devices equipped with mmWave front-end technology. The social impact of the proposed project is expected to be substantial. By developing a low-cost, home-based DED assessment system, we will reduce healthcare expenses for patients with DED and improve their quality of life. The proposed project will accelerate and optimize DED assessment and monitoring, lower the costs associated with related health services, and alleviate the strain on Hong Kong's healthcare system. 乾眼症 （DED） 是一種影響全球數千萬人的疾病。在香港，大約 30% 的人口受到影響，為醫療保健系統帶來重大經濟負擔。DED 的特點是不穩定的高滲淚膜，導致眼部炎症和損害表面神經。定期和長期監測疾病嚴重程度能及時、適當的治療調整。然而，管理 DED 仍然存在由於患者個體差異、複雜的原因、而具有挑戰性、依從性問題和波動的症狀，所有這些都因醫療資源有限因素而進一步加劇。 爲了應對這些挑戰，最近的努力集中在發展以家庭爲基礎的 DED 篩查方法。與現有解決方案不同，我們的方法不僅限於篩查，還專注於疾病進展管理和監控家庭設備中的關鍵指標。具體來說，我們提出了一種基於毫米波雷達技術的多模態大語言模型（LLM）輔助DED評估系統，提供了一種低成本、非侵入性的解決方案。擬議項目的目標是將 DED 管理從傳統的以醫院爲中心的模式轉變爲以家庭爲中心的方法。範圍將包括對高危人羣進行早期篩查、定期評估疾病嚴重程度以及監測淚液破裂時間（TBUT）指標，以評估治療效果並及時調整治療計劃。我們計劃分兩個階段實現我們的目標。 首先，我們將開發一種 DED 評估系統，該系統利用毫米波雷達作爲唯一的感知模態，不受計算資源限制。該系統將提供高度準確的疾病進展和 TBUT 指標，從而能夠更精確地調整治療計劃。擬議的系統將側重於四個關鍵方面：i）使用天線編碼毫米波雷達檢測DED症狀; ii）將電子健康記錄 （EHR） 與毫米波信號之間的多模態症狀對齊; iii）通過專門設計的 DED 相關 LLM 提煉多模態特徵; iv）僅使用毫米波信號，將多任務學習應用於 DED 評估。其次，我們將在配備毫米波前端技術的資源受限的邊緣設備上部署 DED 評估系統。預計擬議項目的社會影響將是巨大的。 通過開發低成本、以家庭爲基礎的 DED 評估系統，我們將減少 DED 患者的醫療費用並提高他們的生活質量。擬議項目將加速和優化 DED 評估和監測，降低相關醫療服務的成本，並減輕香港醫療系統的壓力。

16204525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204525.value: 最小化高像素密度LCoS的边缘场效应，用于扩展C波段的光

16204525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204525.value: In this project, we aim to study and find an efficient way to minimize the fringing field effect for spatial light modulators that can be used for photonic components demanding high pixel density. These components include wavelength-selective switches (for telecommunication and data centers), holograms, AR/VR/MR headsets, Lidars, and many more. The fringing field among the neighboring pixels deteriorates the optical information, reduces efficiency, and loses vital information. Electro-optical modulations in conventional nematic liquid crystals are primarily controlled by dielectric displacement, viscous, and elastic torque. As a result, the fringing field is severe and affects the optical characteristics of the modulated light. This problem becomes even more serious when we try to increase the pixel density, particularly for the large modulation depths and high periodicity. Both amplitude and phase modulation suffer from these artifacts. The pixel edge is very critical for the fringing field. Recently, we found that capping the pixel with the dielectric material or having relative voltage distribution can help to reduce the fringing field effect. In the proposal, we propose to study two approaches to minimize the fringing field effect. First, a variable pretilt angle distribution will be used on the pixel and pixel edge, and second, a specially designed dielectric shield to cover the pixel edge that can screen the fringing field. We have performed a preliminary simulation for the two conditions, and the results are very encouraging, improving the optical features by more than 30%. Here, we propose further studying the two approaches and eventually fabricating an SLM using LCoS with a pixel density of more than 3500 PPI. Furthermore, we also propose to study strategies to curtail the polarization losses. The LCoS uses polarized light that intrinsically induces 50% of light losses. Here, we plan to study two key strategies, including polarization conversion, using efficient diffractive phase elements such as patterned polarization gratings and wave plates. The second approach includes designing polarization-independent blazed grating, which can effectively increase efficiency. Ultimately, we plan to study the diffraction order modulation using the large phase modulation of the fringing field-free LCoS with a fixed grating pitch. The research findings will improve our understanding of feasible methods for making defect-free LCoS SLMs that can be used for advanced wavelength selective switches, display components, and others. 在本项目中，我们旨在研究并找到一种有效的方法来最小化空间光调制器的边缘场效应，该调制器可用于要求高像素密度的光子元件。这些元件包括波长选择开关（用于电信和数据中心）、全息图、AR/VR/MR头戴式设备、激光雷达等等。相邻像素之间的边缘场会损害光学信息，降低效率，并丢失重要信息。传统向列液晶中的电光调制主要受介电位移、粘性和弹性扭矩控制。因此，边缘场非常严重，会影响调制光的光学特性。当我们尝试提高像素密度时，尤其是在调制深度较大和周期性较高的情况下，这个问题会变得更加严重。幅度调制和相位调制都会受到这些伪影的影响。像素边缘对于边缘场至关重要。最近，我们发现用介电材料覆盖像素或设置相对电压分布有助于减少边缘场效应。 在本提案中，我们提出研究两种最小化边缘场效应的方法。首先，在像素和像素边缘采用可变预倾角分布；其次，采用特殊设计的介质屏蔽体覆盖像素边缘，以屏蔽边缘场。我们已经对这两种情况进行了初步模拟，结果非常令人鼓舞，光学特性改善了30%以上。在此，我们建议进一步研究这两种方法，并最终制造出像素密度超过3500 PPI的LCoS空间光调制器（SLM）。此外，我们还建议研究减少偏振损耗的策略。LCoS使用的偏振光本质上会导致50%的光损耗。在此，我们计划研究两种关键策略，包括偏振转换，使用高效的衍射相位元件，例如图案化偏振光栅和波片。第二种方法是设计与偏振无关的闪耀光栅，这可以有效提高效率。最终，我们计划利用固定光栅间距的无边缘场LCoS的大相位调制来研究衍射级次调制。研究成果将加深我们对制造无缺陷LCoS空间光调制器的可行方法的理解，这些器件可用于先进的波长选择开关、显示组件等。

16204725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204725.value: 利用集成4H碳化矽絕緣體量子光子平台產生連續變數簇態

16204725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204725.value: Quantum computing represents a disruptive paradigm across various technological fields, including cryptography, drug discovery, optimization, artificial intelligence, and complex system simulations. Quantum computers leverage the principles of quantum mechanics, such as superposition of quantum states and quantum entanglement, to perform calculations that far exceed the capabilities of classical computers. Among the many potential schemes, continuous-variable quantum systems offer a promising framework for quantum computing tasks by enabling the manipulation and measurement of quantum modes (qumodes) with entanglement in their quadrature components of position and momentum. Unlike conventional quantum bit (qubit)-based systems, which have discrete-valued quantum states in degrees of freedom such as polarization, spatial mode, propagation path, and orbital angular momentum, qumodes possess continuous-valued degrees of freedom. These include the position and momentum of a simple harmonic oscillator, as well as the quadrature amplitude and phase components of light states. In the proposed project, we will generate a single-mode squeezed source. We will establish additional entanglement among the modes from different single-mode squeezed sources to form continuous-variable cluster states. This approach will leverage the advantages of continuous-variable quantum systems, offering a different perspective on existing quantum computing challenges than conventional discrete qubit systems. Additionally, we will seek to advance the preparation of large-scale, high-squeezing, and high-entanglement continuous-variable cluster states for measurement-based quantum computing applications. Specifically, we will achieve preparation of continuous-variable cluster states using photonic integrated circuits on the wide-bandgap quantum photonic platform in 4H-silicon carbide combined with an off-chip fiber-based delay system. We will demonstrate the establishment of entanglement between two separated single-mode squeezed sources using an integrated directional coupler and the off-chip system. Successful attainment of the project objectives will facilitate chip-scale photonic measurement-based quantum computing. 量子運算代表著各種技術領域的顛覆性範式，涵蓋密碼學、藥物研發、最佳化、人工智慧和複雜系統模擬等許多領域。量子電腦利用量子力學原理，例如量子態疊加和量子糾纏，執行遠超傳統電腦能力的計算。 在眾多潛在方案中，連續變數量子系統透過實現對位置和動量正交分量中存在糾纏的量子模式的操控和測量，為量子計算任務提供了一個極具前景的框架。與傳統的基於量子位元的系統不同，傳統的量子位元系統在自由度方面具有離散值的量子態，例如偏振、空間模式、傳播路徑和軌道角動量，而量子模式則具有連續值的自由度。這些自由度包括簡諧振子的位置和動量，以及光態的正交振幅和相位分量。 在本提案中，我們將產生一個單模壓縮源。我們將在來自不同單模壓縮源的模式之間建立額外的糾纏，以形成連續變數簇態。這種方法將充分利用連續變數量子系統的優勢，為應對現有量子運算挑戰提供不同於傳統離散量子位元系統的視角。此外，我們將致力於推進大規模、高壓縮和高糾纏連續變數簇態的製備，以用於基於測量的量子計算應用。 具體而言，我們將利用4H碳化矽寬帶隙量子光子平台上的光子積體電路，結合片外光纖延遲系統，實現連續變數簇態的製備。我們將示範如何使用整合式定向耦合器和片外系統在兩個分離的單模壓縮源之間建立糾纏。項目目標的成功實現將促進基於晶片級光子測量的量子計算。

16205225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205225.value: 機器學習驅動的阻抗激活線粒體分選器

16205225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205225.value: Mitochondria are essential organelles that play a central role in cellular energy production, signaling, and homeostasis. Mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to various diseases, such as metabolic syndromes, neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer. Impairments in mitochondrial function can lead to decreased adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, increased oxidative stress, and disrupted cellular signaling, all of which contribute to the associated disorders. As such, the ability to accurately assess mitochondrial function and heterogeneity is critical for the diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment of mitochondrial-related diseases. Mitochondria within a single cell, let alone across different cell types and tissues, exhibit remarkable functional and structural heterogeneity. Traditional techniques for assessing mitochondrial function, such as respirometry and fluorescence-based assays, provide valuable insights but are often limited to population-averaged measurements. Although flow cytometry has been adopted to study individual mitochondrial characteristics such as membrane potential—a global functional indicator altered in various diseases—it relies on fluorescent probes that can disrupt or interfere with mitochondrial function. The lack of an effective label-free high-throughput method to probe individual mitochondria and identify and purify distinct mitochondrial subtypes presents an obstacle not only to disease diagnosis but also to therapeutic development and our understanding of mitochondrial heterogeneity. Impedance flow cytometry (IFC), an emerging technology, could meet this unmet need. The proposed project will harness IFC technology to develop a high-throughput label-free impedance-activated mitochondria sorter driven by machine learning (ML-driven IAMS). This will be realized in three phases: (1) establishing and validating the experimental setup for IFC measurements of isolated mitochondria; (2) elucidating the relationship between mitochondrial impedimetric measurements and key features such as size, morphology, and membrane potential; and (3) integrating IFC with a sorting module empowered by a machine learning model, followed by a sorting performance assessment. Specifically, we will identify impedimetric parameters that show sensitivity to changes in mitochondrial size, morphology, and membrane potential induced by various mitochondrial agents and metabolic conditions. We will leverage the datasets generated from these experiments to develop machine learning models and then use the models for the real-time sorting of mitochondria based on their characteristics. If successful, the ML-driven IAMS will enable the label-free analysis of mitochondrial membrane potential and further downstream analyses of specific subtypes, a capability that currently does not exist. This development is expected to enhance our understanding of mitochondrial heterogeneity, facilitating the development of targeted therapies and improving diagnosis of mitochondria-related diseases. 線粒體作為關鍵細胞器，在細胞能量生成、信號傳導與穩態維持中居核心地位。其功能失調與代謝綜合症、神經退行性疾病、心血管疾病及癌症等多種病症密切相關。線粒體功能損傷會導致三磷酸腺苷（ATP）生成量下降、氧化應激加劇及細胞信號傳導紊亂，進而誘發相關病變。因此，精準評估線粒體功能與異質性，對診斷、監測及治療線粒體相關疾病至關重要。 單一細胞內的線粒體（更遑論不同細胞類型與組織間）呈現顯著的功能與結構異質性。傳統評估技術（如呼吸測量法與螢光檢測法）雖具參考價值，但多局限於群體平均測量。儘管流式細胞術已用於檢測單個線粒體特性（如膜電位——此全域性功能指標在多種疾病中發生改變），其依賴的螢光探針可能干擾線粒體功能。當前缺乏有效的免標記高通量技術來探測單個線粒體並識別純化特定亞型，此局限不僅阻礙疾病診斷，更制約治療開發及對線粒體異質性的認知。新興的阻抗流式細胞術（IFC）有望解決此技術缺口。 本研究將整合IFC技術，開發基於機器學習驅動的高通量免標記阻抗激活線粒體分選系統（ML-driven IAMS），該系統分三階段實施：（1）建立並驗證已分離出線粒體的IFC測量實驗平台；（2）闡明線粒體阻抗測量值與尺寸、形態及膜電位等關鍵特徵的關聯性；（3）結合IFC與機器學習驅動的分選模組，繼而評估分選效能。具體而言，我們將識別對各類線粒體作用劑及代謝條件所誘導的線粒體尺寸、形態與膜電位變化呈現靈敏度的阻抗參數。運用實驗數據集開發機器學習模型，實現基於特徵的線粒體即時分選。若研發成功，ML-driven IAMS將開創免標記分析線粒體膜電位及特定亞型下游檢測之先河。此項技術有望深化對線粒體異質性的理解，推動標靶療法發展，並提升線粒體相關疾病診斷效能。

16205325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205325.value: 搖擺傾覆 相關性與因果性

16205325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16205325.value: Prof DEJONG, Matthew Prof KOUGIOUMTZOGLOU, Ioannis A.

16205325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205325.value: Rocking motion occurs when structures or objects uplift from their base during earthquakes. Rocking dynamics governs the seismic stability of such systems and is nonlinear, discontinuous, and stochastic. Remarkably, the same mechanisms that occasionally result to failure by overturning, also render rocking systems (such as structures, monuments, critical contents etc.) with an intriguing ability to survive strong earthquakes; a counterintuitive seismic isolation effect. This unique combination of importance and complexity has solidified rocking stability as a landmark challenge in earthquake engineering with more than six decades of systematic research. This proposal aims to advance our understanding of rocking dynamics with fundamental research. Specifically, through a combination of methodologies that have either never been deployed before, or adopt a new perspective, this research will characterize rocking response and predict (or prevent) overturning. The proposed approach involves analytical research, laboratory experiments, and numerical simulations that investigate rocking of rigid single- and multi-body systems at different levels of fidelity. The first objective is to characterize the seismic stability of rocking systems through a three-level theoretical approach. Specifically, we will derive original energy-based analytical stability criteria for rocking systems. We will further introduce advanced stochastic dynamics methodologies to achieve high accuracy with low computational cost when analyzing stochastic rocking response under realistic ground excitations. Moreover, we will examine the overturning of rocking systems with a novel extreme-event theory and tools adapted from the field of financial markets. This methodology is originally devised for different dynamically unstable systems and will allow us to foresee and, at a later stage, even prevent overturning. To complement and validate the theoretical findings, we will conduct extensive experimental shake-table tests on single and multi-block systems. Lastly, we will investigate the ability of machine learning to predict overturning, but also interpret and explain underlying causal relationships. We will also cross-examine machine-learning models with physical simulations to determine their validity. A solid understanding of causality is essential for decision-making, especially in safety-critical applications such as seismic design and retrofit decisions. Upon successful completion, this research will provide fundamental insights and introduce a new paradigm for analyzing and predicting seismic stability of rocking systems by unveiling causal-effect relationships between general classes of ground motions and risk of overturning. Additionally, the proposed analytical methodologies will be applicable to other structural systems with similar nonlinearities, ultimately contributing to the improved seismic resilience of both the built and natural environment and sustainable development. 結構或物體在地震作用下從基底提離便會產生搖擺運動。此類系統的抗震穩定性受搖擺動力學主導，具有非線性、非連續性及隨機性。有趣的是，同一驅動搖擺的力學機制有時會造成傾覆，有時卻能讓搖擺系統——如建築、歷史遺跡與關鍵設備——在強震下展現出優異的隔震能力。這種反直覺的隔震效應讓搖擺穩定性格外重要且複雜，並令它成為地震工程領域六十多年來的經典難題。 本提案旨在透過基礎研究深化對搖擺動力學的理解。具體而言，此研究將採用解析研究、實驗和數值模擬，結合全新的視角和前所未有的方法，表徵單體和多體系統在不同保真度水平的搖擺反應，並預測（或預防）其傾覆。 我們將透過三層理論架構來表徵搖擺系統在地震下的穩定性。首先我們會基於能量原理推導系統穩定性準則，隨後引入隨機動力學方法，以低計算成本實現在地震下的隨機搖擺響應的高精度分析。此外，我們將運用「極端事件理論」與金融市場領域的工具來研究搖擺傾覆。該方法，最初是為其他動態不穩定系統設計，將能預測，甚至阻止傾覆。為驗證理論，我們將對單體與多體搖擺系統進行大量振動台試驗，最後將探討機器學習預測傾覆現象及其解釋潛在因果關係的能力， 並通過實體模擬對機器學習模型進行交叉檢驗以確定其有效性。 深入理解因果關係對決策至關重要，尤其在安全關鍵領域如抗震設計和加固決策的應用。本研究一旦完成，將揭示地震動與傾覆風險之間的因果機制，為搖擺系統的抗震穩定性分析和預測提供基礎性見解和全新的研究典範。此外，本研究提出的分析方法可推廣至其他具有類似非線性特徵的結構體系，最終有助於提升建築和自然環境的整體抗震韌性，為永續發展做出貢獻。

16206925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16206925.value: 利用碳減排電化學膜系統以同時實現污染物去除與高價值產品生成：推動含鹽廢水處理邁向永續發展

16206925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206925.value: Conventional wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) aim to effectively remove harmful contaminants and pathogens, thereby safeguarding the environment and public health. However, several challenges regarding the performance of WWTPs have attracted widespread concern: (i) WWTPs are inefficient at degrading nonbiodegradable contaminants, especially emerging pollutants (EPs); (ii) there is no recovery or generation of high-value products; and (iii) WWTPs result in high carbon emissions due to intensive generation of greenhouse gases (GHGs) and high levels of energy and chemical consumption. In contrast to most regions worldwide, municipal wastewater in Hong Kong contains high levels of Cl- due to the implementation of seawater flushing, which offers an appropriate chemical source for wastewater treatment through advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). Here, we propose an electrochemical membrane system (EMS), specifically a novel low-carbon-emission AOP that can efficiently remove multiple contaminants as well as recover and generate high-value products for saline wastewater treatment to address the abovementioned challenges. Using this EMS, sufficient reactive chlorine species (RCS) will be generated through oxidation-power-driven chloride activation to remove organic pollutants (including EPs) and Escherichia coli (E. coli). Simultaneously, the electric field, assisted with membrane separation, will help recover ammonia, and the reduction power will drive hydroxide and H2 evolution. The proposed EMS is anticipated to adequately address the limitations of WWTPs by (i) efficiently degrading EPs via in-situ chlorine activation; (ii) recovering ammonia and generating H2 and hydroxide as energy and high-value products from wastewater, making wastewater treatment a value-added process; and (iii) mitigating carbon emissions resulting from wastewater treatment because of less GHG generation and offsetting emissions with high-value products. The proposed project will comprehensively study strategies to optimize the performance of a bench-scale EMS in continuous-flow mode, determine the mechanisms required to achieve multifunctions of the EMS, and investigate the feasibility of a large-scale EMS with a novel modularized structure to treat real saline wastewater. The proposed EMS will meet the prospective needs of wastewater treatment because of its improved effluent quality, waste-to-high-value product conversion, and the migration of net zero technology. The proposed project will provide new insights and fundamental theoretical knowledge on EMS to realize multifunctional saline wastewater treatment. To the best of our knowledge, no similar technique has been reported within the global saline wastewater treatment field.
