16215825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215825.value: 用於顯示應用的全真空沉積可擴展製造的高性能頂發射鈣鈦礦發光二極管

16215825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215825.value: The development of new light-emitting materials is the cornerstone of the next- generation light-emitting diode (LED)-based display devices. As one of the most promising light-emitting materials nowadays, metal halide perovskites, hereafter referred to as perovskites, have been demonstrated to have great potential for high- performance optoelectronic devices. For example, the external quantum efficiency (EQE) of perovskite LEDs (PeLEDs) has already exceeded 30% since the first report in 2014, which is comparable to that of organic LEDs (OLEDs). However, most of the current research on PeLEDs still focus on small-area single devices with a bottom-light emitting structure on transparent conductive substrates (such as indium tin oxide (ITO) glass). Most of these devices are prepared by solution methods inside gloveboxes. The unsatisfactory upscalability and reproducibility of these devices are limiting factors for their practical applications. Meanwhile, in contrast to bottom-light-emitting devices, top-emitting PeLEDs are more preferable for active-matrix flat panel displays because they emit light away from the substrate and the backplane circuit, which increases the aperture ratio of the display. However, the EQE of state-of-the-art top-emitting PeLEDs is still below 15 %. Recently, we demonstrated the potential of an all-vacuum deposition method for highly efficient and large-area (3 cm2) PeLEDs, as well as perovskite quantum wire-based top-emitting PeLEDs. Hence, in this project, we propose to use the all-vacuum deposition process to fabricate scalable top-emitting PeLED arrays for display applications. By optimizing the vacuum deposition process, bright perovskite thin film will be obtained with photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) over 90%. The obtained perovskite thin film will be subsequently applied to top-emitting PeLEDs with newly devised transparent top electrodes. We aim to achieve a high EQE of over 20% for top-emitting PeLEDs, luminance (L) over 30,000 cd m−2, and device lifetime (T50) of over 7 days, for a small-area device (<1 cm2). Meanwhile, benefiting from the large-area uniformity of the vacuum deposition process, large-scale top-emitting PeLED arrays (10 cm × 10 cm) will be also fabricated with respectable performance (EQE of over 15%, L of over 5,000 cd m−2) and less than 10% L variation in the whole array area. Finally, after fabricating the PeLED arrays on both the active- and passive-matrix back-driving panels, we will demonstrate a high-resolution proof-of-concept display. The proposed research project will lead to major advancements and promote the future practical applications of PeLEDs in new display and lighting devices. 新型發光材料的開發是下一代基於發光二極體（LED）的顯示器零件的基石。金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦（以下簡稱鈣鈦礦）作為當今最有前景的發光材料之一，已被證明在高性能光電裝置方面具有巨大的潛力。例如，自2014年首次報導以來，鈣鈦礦發光二極體（PeLED）的外量子效率（EQE）已超過30%，與有機發光二極體（OLED）相當。然而，目前對PeLED的研究大多集中在透明導電基底（如氧化銦錫（ITO）玻璃）上具有底部發光結構的小面積單一裝置。這些元件大多採用手套箱內的溶液法製備。這些裝置的可擴展性和可重複性不理想，限制了它們的實際應用。同時，與底部發光裝置相比，頂部發光PeLED更適用於主動矩陣平板顯示器，因為它們的發光方向遠離基板和背板電路，從而提高了顯示器的開口率。然而，目前最先進的頂部發光PeLED的外量子效率(EQE)仍低於15%。最近，我們展示了一種全真空沉積方法，用於高效、大面積（3 cm²）PeLED，以及基於鈣鈦礦量子線的頂部發光PeLED的潛力。因此，在本專案中，我們提出採用全真空沉積製程來製造可擴展的頂部發光PeLED陣列，用於顯示器應用。透過優化真空沉積工藝，我們將獲得光致發光量子產率(PLQY)超過90%的明亮鈣鈦礦薄膜。隨後，我們將把所得的鈣鈦礦薄膜應用於具有新設計的透明頂部電極的頂部發光PeLED。我們的目標是使頂發射 PeLED 的小面積元件（<1 cm2）的 EQE 超過 20%，亮度（L）超過 30,000 cd m−2，裝置壽命（T50）超過 7 天。同時，由於真空沉積製程的大面積均勻性，我們也將製造出性能優異（EQE 超過 15%，L 超過 5,000 cd m−2）且整個陣列區域 L 變化小於 10% 的大規模頂發射 PeLED 陣列。最後，在主動式和被動矩陣反向驅動面板上製造 PeLED 陣列後，我們將展示高解析度概念驗證顯示器。擬議的研究項目將帶來重大進展，並促進 PeLED 在新型顯示器和照明設備中的未來實際應用。

16216725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216725.value: 隐私保护的大型语言模型微调与服务

16216725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216725.value: In recent years, the advent of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized numerous fields. These models, characterized by a vast number of parameters, are designed to achieve superior generalization across diverse tasks. However, the need for intensive computation during fine-tuning and deployment, which are two very common use scenarios in real-world applications, often requires powerful GPUs situated in cloud infrastructures. To leverage cloud computing for efficient LLM fine-tuning and inference, users must transfer their data to cloud service providers and the data is required to be fully visible to the cloud to obtain the services. This raises significant privacy concerns, particularly in sectors like healthcare, education, and finance, where protecting sensitive data is crucial. Some studies have been conducted to enhance privacy protection for LLMs, such as introducing selected noise into query data, employing data encryption techniques, sharing insights from trained models, or implementing split learning to exchange only intermediary results. Yet, such approaches either fall short in comprehensively safeguarding user information or suffer from significant inefficiencies, rendering them impractical for real-world usage. This proposal seeks to introduce a privacy-preserving LLM system, aiming to achieve comprehensive privacy protection for user queries while delivering efficient and precise outputs. In pursuit of this objective, we plan to present three novel methodologies: (1) an exhaustive benchmark suite designed to evaluate the privacy, accuracy, and efficiency of a given LLM; (2) an innovative split learning algorithm aimed at enhancing privacy during LLM fine-tuning and inference, which attempts to ensure input confidentiality and prevent servers from accessing outputs while maintaining the accuracy of LLMs; (3) task scheduling mechanisms that strategically allocate model layers between the client and server for optimizing the time efficiency of fine-tuning and inference. Our goal is to design and develop an efficient and user-centric LLM fine-tuning and serving prototype system that circumvents the need for original user input data. The proposed system will feature user-friendly APIs and can be integrated into existing pre-trained LLMs. Our preliminary studies indicate that: (1) current LLM services are vulnerable to privacy leakage or suffer from significant inefficiencies and (2) user data can remain secure through the exchange of only intermediate results between the client and server. To illustrate the practicality and effectiveness of our proposed optimization methodologies, we will release our framework and evaluation scripts as open-source resources. This initiative will significantly aid the advancement of LLMs within the scientific community.

16216825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216825.value: 跨階段多模態的電路編碼器

16216825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216825.value: Integrated circuit (IC) is the foundation of our modern information society, but the ever-increasing complexity of ICs has led to skyrocketing IC design costs. To improve IC design efficiency, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted electronic design automation (EDA), also known as AI for chip design, demonstrates great potential. However, existing AI-assisted EDA techniques are mostly developed by supervised training on a small carefully crafted labeled dataset for a specific task. This mainstream task-specific paradigm is repetitive and time-consuming. In addition to inefficiency, failing to capture general circuit information implies that existing AI solutions’ understanding of circuits lags far behind general images and languages, indicating huge room for improvement. This project targets essentially generalized AI solutions that better understand circuits. Before scaling up the model size and training dataset, we first re-think circuit from data perspective and identify its special properties: (1) Circuit is a delicately structured implementation of precise functionality. Different from robust data types like images, a minor modification in circuit structure (e.g., flipping one gate) can drastically change the functionality. (2) Circuit is inherently multimodal. Across different design stages, a circuit can be described with hardware description language (HDL) code, a graph of operators, a functionality summary in natural language, and a physical layout. In summary, circuit is a special data type that demands customized solutions. In this project, we propose a powerful pre-trained model named circuit encoder, which converts any given circuit into generalized representations (i.e., embedding vectors) with rich information, based on which lightweight ML models can be fine-tuned to solve various design tasks. This project includes three interrelated milestones: (1) From data perspective, to scale up our training dataset, we propose a new circuit generation technique to generate new circuits from scratch. Viewing circuits as directed cyclic graphs (DCGs), our generation flow starts with DCG-oriented graph diffusion models, followed by refinement with integer linear programming (ILP) and Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS). (2) From model perspective, we will develop the cross-stage and multimodal circuit encoder. The encoder will be pre-trained with multiple novel self-supervised tasks, learning to recognize general logic equivalence rules and structured circuit operators across different stages and modalities. (3) From application perspective, we will apply our general circuit encoder to various circuit design applications, including early design quality evaluation, circuit functionality reasoning, and generative techniques in both HDL code and layout formats. 積體電路（IC）是現代資訊社會的基礎，但隨著IC日益增長的複雜度，IC設計成本也急劇上升。為了提升IC設計效率，人工智慧（AI）輔助電子設計自動化（EDA），亦即所謂的AI晶片設計，展現出極大潛力。然而，目前的AI輔助EDA技術多半是透過針對特定任務，在小規模、精心標註的資料集上進行監督式訓練所開發出來的。這種主流的任務導向模式不僅重複且耗時。除了效率低落之外，未能掌握一般性的電路知識也意味著現有AI對電路的理解遠遠落後於對影像與語言的理解，顯示出巨大的改進空間。總結來說，電路是一種獨特的資料類型，需量身打造的解決方案。在本計畫中，我們提出一個強大的預訓練模型，稱為電路編碼器，能將任意電路轉換為具有豐富資訊的一般化表示，並可進一步以輕量級機器學習模型解決各種設計任務。

16216925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216925.value: 基於滿意度框架的分類模型魯棒性優化

16216925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16216925.value: Prof Long, Daniel Zhuoyu Prof Zhan, Ruohan

16216925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216925.value: Classification is a critical component in many decision-making applications, since it enables the identification of categories based on features of the data. This capability is essential in various fields, including healthcare, finance, and supply chain management, where accurate classification directly influences important decisions. This research emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate performance metrics for classification models. Traditional metrics, including accuracy, precision, the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristics curve (AUC), while widely used, exhibit significant limitations. They often focus solely on classification error rates without adequately addressing the magnitude and risk associated with erroneous predictions. However, neglecting the severity of ranking errors can be crucial in high-stakes applications like medical diagnoses and financial forecasting. To address these shortcomings, we plan to propose novel performance metrics to incorporate both the magnitude of ranking errors and the generalization ability of classifiers when exposed to unseen samples. This new performance metric will be defined through a distributional ambiguity framework, allowing for a robust evaluation of expected ranking errors through the distance metrics that quantify the divergence between the true distribution and the empirical distribution. Furthermore, in contrast to classical distributionally robust optimization approaches, which require to pre-specify the size of uncertainty set, we aim to integrate a target-oriented perspective with robust satisficing scheme. It can facilitate the adjustment of the ambiguity set based on the specific targets. We intend to further explore the properties of the performance metric and examine its computational feasibility with respect to various distance metrics. Additionally, we plan to extend the performance metric to not only evaluate the classifier, but further serve as an optimization criterion for training classification models, enhancing their robustness and adaptability to new data distributions. Model development, reformulation and efficient algorithms will be investigated to ensure that the proposed framework is not only theoretically sound but also practically implementable. Finally, we will conduct various numerical studies based on real data set, e.g., medical diagnosis and credit approval, to identify the advantage and limitations of the performance metric. By developing new performance metrics and integrating it into existing training paradigms, this work can contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of classification performance metrics, ultimately guiding the development of resilient classifiers capable of minimizing prediction errors in dynamic environments. 分類技術在許多決策系統中扮演著關鍵角色，它能自動將數據按照特徵分門別類。這項能力對醫療診斷、金融分析和供應鏈管理等領域至關重要，因為分類結果的準確與否，往往直接影響後續的重大決策。 本項研究重點關注為分類模型選擇合適的評估標準。目前常用的評估標準（例如準確率、精確率和AUC值等）存在不足。這些指標只計算了分類的錯誤次數，卻沒有考慮到不同錯誤可能帶來不同程度的風險。舉例來說，在醫療診斷中把重症誤判為輕症，以及將輕症判為重症，這兩種錯誤的嚴重性天差地別。 為了解決這個問題，我們計劃開發一套全新的評估方法。這套方法會根據錯誤的嚴重程度來加權計算，並且評估分類器處理新數據的能力。我們採用分佈不確定性的理論框架，透過比較實際數據和樣本數據的差異程度，來更全面地穩健地預測可能發生的錯誤。特別的是，我們的方法不需要事先設定參數範圍，而是結合「目標導向」和「穩健滿意度」的智能調整機制，讓系統能根據不同任務需求自動優化評估標準。 接下來的研究重點包括：驗證這套指標的數學特性、測試實際運算的可行性，並將其發展成訓練分類模型的新標準。我們也會開發高效算法，確保這套方法不僅理論嚴謹，更能實際應用。最後會透過真實案例（如癌症診斷和貸款審核）來驗證成效。 這項創新將幫助我們更全面地評估分類系統的性能，最終開發出能適應各種複雜環境、將預測失誤降到最低的智能分類模型。

16217025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217025.value: 從土力學視角剖析微塑膠對土體及植被系統水力-力學特性的影響

16217025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217025.value: Global plastic production is expected to be doubled in 2050. Although plastic provides numerous benefits to human life, microplastic (i.e., size <5mm) can be formed by breakdown of plastic to cause environmental pollution, especially for terrestrial systems. It has been reported that microplastic content in soil can be 4-23 times higher than that in aquatic systems, threatening plant performance which is important for agricultural production and performance of earthen structures. Previous studies mainly focused on the interactions among microplastic, soil microbes and plant growth. However, results are two-fold potentially due to ignorance of soil hydromechanical behaviour, which governs microplastic transport and plant uptake of water and nutrient. This project aims to investigate effects of microplastic on hydromechanical behaviour of soil and also soil-plant systems. The project consists of three parts considering different shapes, concentrations and sizes of microplastic. Polyethylene microplastic, which has been found to be the most prevalent in field soil after a review of over a hundred studies, will be focused. Firstly, element tests will be conducted to determine hydraulic conductivity and shear strength of saturated soil with microplastic by flexible wall permeameters and triaxial testing apparatuses, respectively. Secondly, effects of microplastic on water retention and permeability function of unsaturated soil will be evaluated using pressure plate extractors and soil column tests, respectively. Microplastic transport will be measured in the column tests to examine its relationship with the permeability function. Finally, three native plant species having different adaptability will be grown in columns of microplastic-polluted soil. Plant performance (e.g., biomass, root tensile strength) and behaviour of vegetated soil (e.g., water retention, permeability function, nutrient bioavailability) will be investigated. Principal component analysis will be performed to identify the key parameters governing plant growth under microplastic pollution. In these tests, soil microstructure will be analysed using either mercury intrusion porosimetry or computed tomography scan. This project will first improve the fundamental understanding about microplastic effects on hydromechanical behaviour of soil and soil-plant systems to complement existing studies. New findings will serve as a basis for developing new constitutive models to tackle complex soil-microplastic-plant interactions. Recommendations on enhancing plant performance in microplastic-polluted soil and controlling quality of polluted soil and plants will then be provided. More importantly, the improved understanding achieved by this project will facilitate the development of remediation methods for microplastic-polluted soil. All these contributions are crucial for plant-related disciplines including but not limited to agriculture and geo-environmental engineering. 全球的塑膠生產量預計在2050年將會翻倍。儘管塑膠為人類生活帶來諸多便利，但塑膠的破碎和分解可形成粒徑少於5毫米的微塑膠，造成環境污染，尤其對陸地生態系統影響深遠。研究報道指出，土壤中微塑膠的含量可達水生系統量的4-23倍，影響植物生長，繼而威脅農業生產及地質構造物的穩定性。過往研究主要集中於微塑膠、土壤微生物及植物生長相互作用。然而，由於土體水力-力學行為往往被忽視，相關的研究結論常呈現矛盾。這些行為在微塑膠遷移及植物養料吸收等過程中扮演重要角色。因此，本項目針對微塑膠對土體及植被系統水力-力學特性的影響展開研究。 此研究由三個部分組成，並考慮不同形狀、含量和大小的微塑膠的影響。基於過百個現場調查的結果，土壤中最普遍的聚乙烯微塑膠將會是主要研究對像。首先，本項目通過柔性壁滲透儀和三軸儀的單元試驗測定含微塑膠飽和土壤的滲透系數與抗剪強度。其次，利用壓力板儀法和土柱試驗評估微塑膠對非飽和土壤持水和滲透特性的影響，並在土柱試驗中同步測量微塑膠遷移以釐清其與土壤滲透性的關係。最後，在受微塑膠污染的土柱中種植三種具不同適應力的本土植物，系統地研究植物表現(如生物量、根系強度等)及植被土特性(如持水性、肥力等)，並以統計學方法確定在微塑膠污染下主導植物生長的關鍵因素。另外，在所有試驗中，將采用壓汞法和電腦斷層掃描法分析土體微觀結構。 本項目的研究成果將深化對微塑膠影響土體及植被系統水力-力學特性的科學認知，填補過往研究的不足。所得的新發現將為建立新本構模型奠定基礎，以闡明微塑膠-土體-植被三者複雜的相互作用。在此基礎上，將提出促進在微塑膠影響下植物生長及控制受污染土壤與植物質量的建議，所得的新科學知識甚至幫助推動治理微塑膠污染土的技術開發。這些貢獻對農業、地質環境工程等植物相關學科領域具有關鍵性的價值。

16217225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217225.value: 數字孿生大壩：一種基於多尺度仿真的自適應學習框架用於堆石壩運行期變形預測與控制

16217225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16217225.value: Prof Ma, Gang Dr QU, Tongming

16217225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217225.value: Hydraulic power is the largest renewable energy source worldwide, contributing about one-sixth of global electricity. Rockfill dams are one of the primary infrastructures for hydropower generation. Predicting and controlling the deformation of rockfill dams during their operation has posed a longstanding challenge. Excessive deformation can jeopardize waterproof systems and consequently impair the dam’s functionality. This challenge stems from (1) the intricate mechanical behaviour of rockfill materials and (2) the severe operational environment experienced by rockfill dams. Both factors cause considerable uncertainties when predicting the mechanical responses of rockfill dams using computational methods. In the proposed project, we aim to develop a multiscale simulation-assisted self-learning framework for predicting deformations and making maintenance decisions for rockfill dams. This framework is built on four key pillars: (1) An uncertainty-informed hybrid data and model-driven multiscale simulation strategy will be developed to build a forward simulator of rockfill dams. This simulator will analyze large-scale engineering activities while incorporating rich particle-scale details. (2) Multiscale simulation data will be leveraged to train a computationally efficient and differentiable surrogate model for the temporal-spatial modelling of rockfill dams, which offers a manageable strategy for predicting engineering scenarios with limited on-site data. (3) A gradient-based automatic data assimilation approach will be developed for a self-learning digital twin dam. This approach will enhance the digital model’s capability to mimic the physical dam as more in-situ data become accessible over time. (4) A performance-oriented digital twin-enabled optimisation method will be established to unleash the power of the digital twin in improving the lifecycle management of rockfill dams. This project is expected to deliver a physics-based, AI-empowered, and general-purpose framework for analysing and managing rockfill dam problems. It combines data-rich mechanism-based multiscale simulations with limited, uncontrollable yet precise in-situ data to develop a digital-twin-type predictive model. This entire framework is not only pioneering in the analysis of rockfill dams but also holds immense potential for revolutionizing computational approaches across various geotechnical engineering challenges. 水力能是全球規模最大的可再生能源，貢獻了全球約六分之一的電力。堆石壩是水力發電的主要基礎設施之一。預測及控制堆石壩在運行期間的變形，一直是領域內長期存在的挑戰。堆石壩過度變形可能會破壞防水系統，進而損害大壩服役功能。這一挑戰源於兩大因素：（1）堆石料複雜的力學行為；（2）堆石壩所處的嚴苛運行環境。當透過計算模型預測堆石壩的力學響應時，這兩項因素均會引致顯著的不確定性。 在本研究計劃中，我們旨在開發一套多尺度模擬輔助的自適應學習框架，用於預測堆石壩變形並制定維護決策。此框架的構建基於四大核心支柱：（1）將開發一套融入不確定性的混合數據與模型驅動多尺度模擬策略，構建堆石壩正向模擬器。該模擬器能在分析大規模工程活動的同時，整合豐富的顆粒級細節。（2）將善用多尺度模擬數據，訓練一個計算高效且可微的代理模型，用於堆石壩的時空力學響應建模，為預測現場數據有限的工程場景提供可行策略。（3）將開發一種基於梯度的自動數據同化方法，應用於自適應學習的數字孿生壩。隨著時間推移獲取更多現場數據，此方法將提升數字模型對實體大壩的模擬能力。（4）將建立一套以效能為導向的數字孿生賦能優化方法，釋放數字孿生技術在改善堆石壩全生命週期管理中的潛力。 本計劃預期將交付一個以物理為基礎、人工智能賦能且通用的分析框架，用於處理堆石壩相關問題。它結合了數據豐富的機理導向多尺度模擬，與數量有限卻精準的現場數據，開發出數字孿生預測模型。此整體框架不僅在堆石壩分析領域具有開創性，更有望為各類岩土工程挑戰的計算方法帶來革命性突破。

16218025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218025.value: 面向資源受限環境的邊緣原生智能體AI服務

16218025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218025.value: Recent developments in AI agents have been greatly impacted by advancements in large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-4 and LLaMA. These AI agents utilize the capabilities of LLMs, offering three key benefits: planning, memory, and real-time interaction. By leveraging these advantages, AI agents have the potential to revolutionize various applications, including mobile devices and smart home systems. However, conventional cloud-based AI systems encounter significant challenges when deployed in edge environments, which are typically characterized by limited resources and storage. The high computational demands of LLMs can lead to performance issues, especially in situations where user demands fluctuate and immediate responses are required. This scenario motivates our research to create a new framework that maximizes the strengths of AI agents while overcoming the limitations of traditional cloud-based systems. Deploying AI agents in edge environments presents several challenges, including the need for quick interactions, efficient use of memory, and scalable reasoning capabilities. First, to ensure timely responses and effective decision-making, AI agents must optimize their reasoning speed and resource usage, allowing them to handle complex tasks efficiently. Second, the limited resources in edge environments necessitate a strong focus on memory management to minimize overhead while still maintaining good performance. Lastly, creating scalable reasoning modules introduces challenges in planning and executing tasks dynamically. Addressing these challenges is essential for improving the adaptability and effectiveness of AI agents in edge settings. These insights inform the design of our edge-native agent framework. As a foundational infrastructure for AI services, our approach aims to deliver significant benefits in terms of elastic planning, efficient memory management, and low-latency interactions. This research initiative undertakes a comprehensive exploration of developing a high-performance system for edge-native AI agents, tackling realistic design challenges, offering potential solutions, and identifying promising avenues for future research. Consequently, the proposed framework integrates diverse edge resources, enhancing operational efficiency and expanding the capabilities of AI services in resource-constrained environments. 近年來，AI智能體的發展受到大語言模型（如GPT-4和LLaMA）進步的深刻影響。這些AI智能體利用了大語言模型的三大優勢：規劃能力、記憶功能和即時交互。通過利用這些優勢，AI智能體有潛力徹底革新包括移動設備和智慧家居系統在內的各類應用場景。然而，傳統的基於雲的AI系統在部署到資源受限的邊緣環境中時面臨重大挑戰。邊緣環境通常資源和記憶體有限，而大語言模型的高計算需求可能導致性能問題，尤其是在使用者需求波動且需要即時回應的情況下。這一現實促使我們開展研究，試圖創建一個新框架，在最大化AI智能體優勢的同時克服傳統雲系統的局限性。 在邊緣環境中部署AI智能體面臨多重挑戰，包括快速交互的需求、高效的記憶體使用以及可擴展的推理能力。首先，為確保及時回應和有效決策，AI智能體需要優化推理速度和資源利用率，以高效處理複雜任務。其次，邊緣環境的資源限制要求高度關注記憶體管理，以在減少開銷的同時保持優良性能。最後，構建可擴展的推理引擎需要解決任務動態調度和執行的難題。克服這些挑戰對於提高AI智能體在邊緣環境中的適應能力和效率至關重要。 這些見解指導了我們設計邊緣原生智能體框架的過程。作為AI服務的核心基礎設施，我們的方法旨在提供彈性調度、高效記憶體管理和低延遲交互等顯著優勢。本研究全面探索了面向邊緣原生AI智能體的高性能系統的開發工作，解決現實設計挑戰，提出潛在解決方案，並識別未來研究的有前景方向。因此，所提出的框架整合了多樣化的邊緣資源，提升了運行效率，並擴展了AI服務在資源受限環境中的能力。

16218725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218725.value: 基於遺傳編程的橫向射流控制

16218725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218725.value: A transverse jet is a canonical flow where jet fluid is injected perpendicularly into a crossflow, with diverse applications ranging from fuel injection to film cooling to pollutant dispersion. The interaction between the injected fluid and crossflow generates complex nonlinear dynamics and vortical structures. Depending on its velocity relative to the crossflow, the jet exhibits two distinct instability regimes: (i) convectively unstable, where perturbations grow as they advect downstream, and (ii) globally unstable, characterized by self-excited oscillations and relative insensitivity to extrinsic disturbances. Despite decades of research, controlling these complex dynamics through traditional approaches remains challenging due to the multi-scale nonlinear nature of transverse jets. We propose to use genetic programming (GP) to discover improved control laws that can be interpreted to gain insights into the underlying flow physics, even without access to a system model. Unlike traditional approaches, GP evolves actuation expressions through evolutionary computation, potentially revealing novel strategies for manipulating vortical structures and mixing dynamics while optimizing multiple performance metrics simultaneously. We will implement GP control experimentally on a round equidensity transverse jet flush-injected into a wind tunnel, using velocity and concentration measurements to characterize the jet trajectory, mixing behavior, and shear layer characteristics in both convectively and globally unstable regimes. This research proceeds in three stages: (i) characterizing the baseline jet behavior under conventional time-periodic open-loop control with symmetric (n-fold rotational) and asymmetric (helical, localized, flapping, and dual mode) perturbations; (ii) applying GP open-loop control in both jet instability regimes, benchmarking against the baseline data; and (iii) implementing GP closed-loop control, benchmarking against both the baseline and GP open-loop data. Analysis of the mathematical structure of the evolved GP control laws will provide insights into the underlying flow physics. Expected outcomes include (i) discovery of novel interpretable GP control laws specific to each instability regime, (ii) improved physical understanding of actuator-response relationships, and (iii) improved methodologies for model-free control of transverse jets. The significance of this research extends beyond academic interest, as transverse jets are central to engineering applications ranging from aerospace propulsion to wastewater management. The developed GP methodologies will contribute to data-driven flow control, offering insights applicable to various nonlinear dynamical systems. This work will combine wind tunnel experiments, control theory, and evolutionary computation to advance both our fundamental understanding of transverse jets and our ability to control them effectively. 橫向射流作為經典流動構型，是指射流流體垂直於橫向主來流方向注入的流動現象，在燃料噴射、膜冷卻及污染物擴散等領域具有廣泛應用。射流與橫向主來流的相互作用產生複雜的非線性動力學和渦旋結構。根據其與主來流的相對速度，射流表現出兩種不同的不穩定性狀態：（1）對流不穩定性，即擾動隨著下游對流而增長；（2）全局不穩定性，其特徵是自激振盪和對外部干擾的相對不敏感性。儘管相關研究已持續數十年，但由於橫向射流具有的多尺度非線性特性，傳統控制方法仍難以有效調控其複雜動力學行為。為此，我們提出利用遺傳編程算法發現改進且可解析的控制律，在無需系統模型的前提下揭示流動的深層物理機制。有别於傳統控制策略， 遺傳算法透過進化計算自主生成驅動表達式，能在同步優化多項性能指標的同時，為渦旋結構調控及混合動力學優化提供創新策略。我們將在風洞中對平齊射入的等密度圓形橫向射流進行遺傳算法控制實驗，透過流速場與濃度場量測，系統性表徵對流不穩定與全域不穩定兩種狀態下之射流軌跡、混合特性及剪切層特性。研究分為三個階段遞進開展：（1）在傳統周期性開環控制下，研究對稱性（多重旋轉對稱）與非對稱性（螺旋模態、局部激勵、拍動模態及雙模態）擾動對於基準流場的影響；（2）在兩種不穩定狀態下實施遺傳算法開環控制，並與基準工況進行對比驗證；（3）開展遺傳算法閉環控制實驗，綜合評估其相對於基準工況和遺傳算法開環控制的性能提升。通過對進化所得遺傳算法控制律數學結構的解析，可深入揭示流動控制的物理本質。預期研究成果包括：（1）獲得針對不同不穩定狀態的可解釋性遺傳算法控制律；（2）增進驅動－流動響應之物理機制理解；（3）發展針對橫向射流的無模型控制新方法。本研究的科學價值不僅體現在對橫向射流這一經典問題的學術認識，更彰顯於其工程應用前景——橫向射流在航空發動機燃燒室、廢水處理系統等工程領域均扮演關鍵角色。本研究所發展的遺傳編程控制策略將推動數據驅動流動控制技術的演進，其方法論亦可延伸至其他非線性動力學系統。本研究通過融合風洞實驗、控制理論與進化計算，將在橫向射流的基礎理論認知和實際控制能力兩方面實現突破性進展。

16218825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218825.value: 大型AI模型赋能未来无线通信的边缘智能

16218825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218825.value: As the global telecommunications landscape evolves towards the implementation of 6G networks, the integration of Large AI Models (LAM) into wireless infrastructures promises to redefine the capabilities of the next-generation communication systems. This proposal endeavors to conduct a comprehensive research agenda aimed at harnessing the synergistic potential of edge LAM and wireless technologies to foster ubiquitous, intelligent applications across diverse domains, including smart cities, autonomous driving, and healthcare. Our research will explore the dual paradigms of “wireless for LAM” and “LAM for wireless”, focusing on the deployment of edge LAM to enhance network performance while simultaneously leveraging the unique strengths of 6G networks to facilitate advanced AI-driven applications. We will investigate the complexities of training and inference within wireless edge environments, addressing critical challenges such as data privacy, model scalability, and resource optimization. By developing innovative split learning and parallel computing frameworks for distributed and trustworthy edge LAM training, we aim to create robust systems capable of efficiently processing vast datasets while preserving user privacy. In particular, we will delve into split federated learning approaches that allow for scalable fine-tuning of pre-trained models, ensuring the adaptability of LAMs to diverse wireless environments without compromising communication efficiency. Furthermore, we shall propose a novel microservice architecture for multimodal LAM inference, enabling low-latency, collaborative edge computing that adapts to heterogeneous resource constraints. This architecture will facilitate seamless integration of various functional modules, enhancing the responsiveness and efficiency of intelligent services. Our research will also seek to advance the design of wireless networks through the application of LAMs in channel prediction, beamforming, and resource allocation. By developing federated large language models and graph foundation models tailored for wireless applications, we aim to improve the generalization and performance of current AI- driven network solutions. Through a multidisciplinary approach, our project aspires to establish edge LAM as a transformative technology for 6G, laying the groundwork for an intelligent, interconnected future. By addressing both theoretical and practical challenges, we anticipate significant contributions to the fields of wireless communications and AI, ultimately leading to enhanced societal benefits and economic growth. 随着全球电信格局朝着 6G 网络的实施方向发展，大型人工智能模型 (LAM) 与无线基础设施的集成有望重新定义下一代通信系统的功能。本提案致力于开展一项全面的研究议程，旨在利用边缘 LAM 与无线技术的协同潜力，在智慧城市、自动驾驶和医疗保健等不同领域促进无处不在的智能应用。 我们的研究将探索“无线为 LAM”和“LAM 为无线”的双重范式，重点关注边缘 LAM 的部署以提升网络性能，同时利用 6G 网络的独特优势来促进先进的人工智能驱动应用的发展。我们将研究无线边缘环境中训练和推理的复杂性，以应对数据隐私、模型可扩展性和资源优化等关键挑战。通过开发用于分布式、可信的边缘 LAM 训练的创新型拆分学习和并行计算框架，我们的目标是创建能够高效处理海量数据集并保护用户隐私的强大系统。具体来说，我们将深入研究分体式联邦学习方法，该方法允许对预训练模型进行可扩展的微调，确保LAM能够适应不同的无线环境，同时不影响通信效率。此外，我们将提出一种用于多模态LAM推理的新型微服务架构，实现低延迟、协作式边缘计算，并适应异构资源约束。该架构将促进各种功能模块的无缝集成，从而提升智能服务的响应速度和效率。我们的研究还将致力于通过将LAM应用于信道预测、波束成形和资源分配，来改进无线网络的设计。通过开发针对无线应用的联邦大型语言模型和图基础模型，我们旨在提升当前人工智能驱动的网络解决方案的泛化能力和性能。 通过采用多学科方法，我们的项目致力于将边缘LAM打造为6G的变革性技术，为智能互联的未来奠定基础。通过解决理论和实践挑战，我们期望对无线通信和人工智能领域做出重大贡献，最终提高社会效益并促进经济增长。

16219025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219025.value: 面向进化环境下的高效可控和可编辑的多模态基座模型

16219025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219025.value: Today's large language models (LLMs), with astonishing ability to process textual data, have revolutionized recent AI research and development tendencies. By extending both the input and output of LLMs into other modalities (eg, image, video, and audio), hundreds of Multimodal Foundation Models (MFMs) have been proposed during the past few years. As an "omnipotent'" agent, the ultimate goal is providing satisfactory answers to "any" instructions and questions. Although significant progress has been achieved, there are still several key characteristics have been overlooked: 1. Precisely Controllable: Due to the diverse nature of any open question, there are always multiple reasonable answers. To guide the MFM to generate preferred answers, the current solution is to provide more detailed instructions in the prompt. Unfortunately, the answers for different prompts are unpredictable (ie., there is no controllability). Even worse, pretrained MFM may not understand the prompt with some rare preference types (eg, "answering the question in a Hong Konger style"). 2. Incrementally Evolving: Although almost all MFMs are built on top of pretrained components (eg, LLM, or ViT), the finetuning cost (eg, GPU memory) of MFMs remains very high. On the other side, these pretrained components are continuously updated with new knowledge, advanced training strategies, or better training data. Unfortunately, to benefit from these updated components, current mainstream solutions are retraining the whole MFM from scratch again, which is extremely inefficient and resource-consuming. 3. Efficiently Editable: Usually, for any question, it is not easy for an MFM to generate "perfect" answers directly, especially when the answers are long and complex (eg, paragraphs). For these cases, the answers may need some slightly local refinements (eg, editing a few words). To achieve this goal, the existing solution mainly relies on one more round conversation, which will feed all the conversation history into the MFM again for new answer generation. Thus, these "global answer editing" steps are inefficient. In this proposal, we will explore a series of approaches to equip current MFMs with the three key characteristics. Specifically, we will achieve our goal from three directions: 1) We propose the first explicit preference-aware answer generation method by using reinforcement learning. 2) We develop a memory-efficient transfer learning strategy to update MFMs with incrementally evolving knowledge. 3) We propose an efficient pipeline for locally editing (or refining) multimodal outputs. By equipping MFMs with these overlooked but critical characteristics, we hope to pave the way to building next-generation MFMs. 今天的大型语言模型（LLMs）具有惊人的文本数据处理能力，彻底改变了近期人工智能研究和发展的趋势。在过去几年中，通过将LLMs的输入和输出扩展到其他模态（例如，图像、视频和音频）的方式，学界和业界提出了数百个多模态基座模型（MFMs）。作为一个“全能”的智能体，这些多模态基座模型最终目标是为“任何”指令和问题提供满意的答案。 尽管当前的研究已经取得了显著进展，但仍然有几个关键特性被忽视： 1. 精确可控：由于任何开放问题的多样性，总是存在多个合理的答案。为了引导MFM生成首选答案，目前的解决方案是在提示中提供更详细的指令。不幸的是，不同提示的答案是不可预测的（即，没有可控性）。更糟的是，预训练的MFM可能无法理解某些罕见偏好类型的提示（例如，“以香港人的风格回答问题”）。 2. 逐步演化：尽管几乎所有MFMs都是建立在预训练组件（例如，LLM或ViT）之上的，但MFMs的微调成本（例如，GPU内存）仍然非常高。另一方面，这些预训练组件正在不断更新新知识、先进的训练策略或更好的训练数据。不幸的是，为了利用这些更新的组件，目前主流的解决方案是从头开始重新训练整个MFM，这极其低效且消耗资源。 3. 高效可编辑：通常，对于任何问题，MFM直接生成“完美”答案并不容易，尤其是当答案较长且复杂（例如，段落）时。在这些情况下，答案可能需要一些局部的细微调整（例如，编辑几个单词）。为了实现这一目标，现有的解决方案主要依赖于再进行一次对话，这将把所有对话历史再次输入MFM以生成新答案。因此，这些“全局答案编辑”步骤是低效的。 在本项目申请书中，我们将探索一系列方法，以使当前MFMs具备这三个关键特性。具体而言，我们将从三个相应的方向实现我们的目标：1）我们提出了第一种显式的偏好感知答案生成方法，使用强化学习。2）我们开发了一种内存高效的迁移学习策略，以用逐步演变的知识更新MFMs。3）我们提出了一种高效的管道，用于局部编辑（或精炼）多模态输出。通过为MFMs配备这些被忽视但关键的特性，我们希望为构建下一代MFMs铺平道路。

16219725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219725.value: 高動態性能氧化鎵功率晶體管的設計與開發

16219725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219725.value: Advances in materials and devices open avenues to significantly improve the energy efficiency of power distribution and voltage conversion critical for the proliferation of electrification. To promote sustainable development, traditional silicon-based power transistors are gradually being replaced by wider-bandgap alternatives with superior performance. Beta-phase Gallium Oxide (β-Ga2O3) is a unique ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor whose large breakdown electric field of 6–8 MV/cm and availability of melt-grown single-crystal bulk substrates have triggered worldwide pursuit of β-Ga2O3 power devices for medium/voltage applications such as industrial automation, electrified transportation, and grid integration of renewable energy infrastructures. This project aims at addressing two key scientific questions pertinent to the dynamic performance of β-Ga2O3 power transistors to propel β-Ga2O3 toward a viable wide-bandgap power-switching technology. The first challenge stems from the adoption of high-permittivity dielectric materials for field management, which enhances the average breakdown field strength in transistors but inevitably causes a large reverse transfer capacitance between the gate (input) and the drain (output) terminals. To achieve low-loss switching, such a large capacitive delay will be mitigated by a source-connected field plate that effectively decouples the drain and the gate, thereby enabling fast switching of β-Ga2O3 transistors with integrated high-permittivity dielectrics. Another key obstacle in developing β-Ga2O3 power switches is to resolve the degradation in dynamic ON-resistance due to field-induced electron trapping on the device surface during high-voltage switching operation. A gate-connected p-type surface passivation layer will be employed to shield the underlying device from the trapped surface charges through the injection of mobile holes from an ohmic p-gate junction. This passivation scheme will be realized by direct wafer bonding of p-type diamond to the β-Ga2O3 device, where diamond is chosen in part for its favorable junction properties with β-Ga2O3 that can be harnessed to engineer high-performance β-Ga2O3 devices. The proposed wafer-bonding process not only circumvents the challenges arising from growing diamond on β-Ga2O3 but is also distinct from the mainstream diamond/β-Ga2O3 bonded heterostructures by being readily scalable to large wafers. By designing and engineering β-Ga2O3 power switching transistors for high dynamic performance, this project lays the foundation for low-cost, efficient, and compact power converters. The innovations stemming from this research will generate far-reaching technological, socioeconomic, and educational impacts that advance the frontier of power electronics, accelerate technology transfer to the industry, and educate a new generation of power device engineers.

16219825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219825.value: 基於熱感知架構設計探索與動態任務管理對三維DNN加速器的性能與可靠性進行協同優化

16219825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219825.value: Associated with the rapid growth in the size and complexity of deep neural network (DNN) models, performance demands on DNN accelerators have significantly increased. 2.5D/3D chiplet-based DNN accelerators offer a promising solution to meet these demands. However, they also introduce new challenges in architecture design, temperature, reliability, etc. To handle these challenges, the project aims at developing a framework to co-optimize the performance and reliability of 2.5D/3D chiplet-based DNN accelerators from early-stage architecture design to runtime task management. The project encompasses the following key components. (1) A data-driven thermal model is developed for 2.5D/3D chiplet-based DNN accelerators, using the proper orthogonal decomposition method, which projects the thermal problem from time-consuming physical space onto a function space where the problem can be solved accurately and efficiently. The thermal model is used for thermal estimations of large architecture designs and for providing temperature profiles to support runtime task management during operation. (2) With the thermal model and other analytical models of accelerators, a simulator is designated to 2.5D/3D chiplet-based DNN accelerators, for estimations of performance, power, temperature, etc. (3) Leveraging the simulator, an effective design space exploration (DSE) approach is developed using Bayesian optimization. The DSE approach iteratively explores task mapping and tunes configurations of chiplet-based DNN accelerators, such as the number of chiplet, the number of PE, the on-chip memory capacity, and inter-chiplet space, to identify the optimal architectural configuration and provide an optimal task mapping scheme while meeting performance, thermal constraints. (4) Since 3D accelerators face more severe reliability challenges, thermal-aware architecture optimization alone may not suffice. The project also aims to further improve the reliability of 2.5D/3D chiplet-based DNN accelerators at execution stage through runtime task management. A comprehensive reliability model is therefore proposed, which not only takes thermal stress into account, but also considers thermal fatigue closely tied to runtime task management. To obtain thermal stress efficiently and accurately, a graphic neural network based thermal stress model is trained. (5) Based on the thermal, performance, and reliability models, a runtime task management approach is proposed using the reinforcement learning (RL) method, to enhance the reliability of DNN accelerators at working stage. The RL-based agent dynamically adjusts task mapping and tunes the voltage and frequency settings of individual chiplets, considering the current thermal distribution and timing requirements. The runtime task management effectively reduces peak temperatures, mitigates thermal gradients, and alleviates thermal stress, ultimately enhancing the overall reliability of accelerators. 隨著深度神經網絡（DNN）模型的大小和複雜性迅速增長，對DNN 加速器的性能需求顯著增加。基於 2.5D/3D 晶片的 DNN 加速器提供了一個有前途的解決方案，以滿足這些需求。然而，它們也在架構設計、溫度、可靠性等方面引入了新的挑戰。為了應對這些挑戰，本項目旨在開發一個框架，從早期架構設計到運行時任務管理，共同優化基於 2.5D/3D 晶片的 DNN 加速器的性能和可靠性。該項目涵蓋以下關鍵組件：（1）為基於 2.5D/3D 晶片的 DNN 加速器開發了一個數據驅動的熱模型，使用適當的正交分解方法，將耗時的物理空間中的熱問題投影到可準確高效解決的函數空間中。該熱模型用於大規模架構的熱估算。(2) 利用加速器的熱模型和其他分析模型，為基於 2.5D/3D 晶片集的 DNN 加速器設計了一個模擬器，用於性能、功耗、溫度等參數的估算。 (3) 利用此模擬器，開發了一種基於貝葉斯最佳化的有效設計空間探索 (DSE) 方法。 DSE 方法迭代探索任務映射，並調整基於晶片集的 DNN 加速器的配置，例如晶片集數量、PE 數量、片上記憶體容量和晶片集間空間，以識別最佳架構配置，並在滿足效能和熱限制的同時提供最佳任務映射方案。 (4) 由於 3D 加速器面臨更嚴峻的可靠性挑戰，僅靠熱感知架構優化可能不夠。該項目還旨在透過運行時任務管理，進一步提高基於 2.5D/3D 晶片集的 DNN 加速器在執行階段的可靠性。因此，我們提出了一個全面的可靠性模型，該模型不僅考慮了熱應力，還考慮了與運行時任務管理密切相關的熱疲勞。為了有效率且準確地獲取熱應力，我们訓練了基於圖形神經網路的熱應力模型。（5）基於熱模型、性能模型和可靠性模型，提出了一種基於強化學習（RL）方法的運行時任務管理方法，以提高DNN加速器在工作階段的可靠性。基於RL的代理會根據目前的熱分佈和時序要求，動態調整任務映射並調整各個晶片組的電壓和頻率設定。運行時任務管理有效地降低了峰值溫度，緩解了熱梯度，並減輕了熱應力，最終提高了加速器的整體可靠性。

16221425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16221425.value: 用於高頻寬、高密度 DWDM CMOS 光互連收發器電路

16221425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16221425.value: Explosive increase in data volume created by cutting-edge information technologies such as artificial intelligence and cloud computing is pushing the upgrade of data center interconnects to enable data delivery with high speed, low power consumption, and small latency. Conventional electrical interconnects meet bottlenecks in link speed and communication distance due to limited bandwidth and high loss of copper-based medium. In contrast, optical interconnects utilizing low-loss and high-bandwidth fiber as the medium have become the mainstream choice for communication scenarios with bandwidth–distance product exceeds 100 Gb/s·m. For short-reach optical communications with distances ranging from few meters to hundreds of meters, dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) optical interconnect emerges as a promising solution in recent years. It transmits multiple signals modulated by different optical wavelengths using a single fiber, and hence can provide higher data capacity and better scalability compared with conventional multi-mode fiber-based solutions. With merits of small footprint and low cost, micro-ring modulator (MRM) has been the dominant optical device for electrical-to-optical (E/O) conversion in DWDM optical interconnects. However, the imperfections of MRM, including high temperature sensitivity, nonlinearity in E/O conversion gain, and limited bandwidth, have been obstacles for further developing the link speed. Moreover, for the next generation 800G Ethernet, implementations of DWDM optical interconnects put more emphasis on bandwidth density, to increase the gross communication data rate using the same module volume. One way to increase the bandwidth density is upgrading the modulation scheme from conventional non-return-to-zero (NRZ) signal to 4-pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) signal. Each symbol of PAM-4 signal delivers two-bit information, and hence PAM-4 can double the data rate compared with NRZ using the same system bandwidth. Another method to enhance the bandwidth density is reducing the footprint of optical transceivers, to increase the number of employed wavelength channels. Therefore, compact design methodologies for optical transceivers are demanded. This proposal aims to address the above design challenges by simultaneously adopting novel architecture and circuit techniques in the design of CMOS PAM-4 optical transceiver for DWDM optical interconnects, leveraging our recent success and design experience gained in 48-Gb/s inductor-less optical receiver, 56-Gb/s low-distortion vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) transmitter, and 112-Gb/s large-swing linear Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) transmitter. 人工智能與雲計算等尖端信息技術所產生的數據量呈爆炸性增長，正推動數據中心互聯技術的升級，以實現高速、低功耗與低延遲的數據傳輸。傳統電互聯技術因銅介質帶寬有限與高損耗特性，在鏈路速率與通信距離方面面臨瓶頸。相比之下，採用低損耗、高帶寬光纖介質的光互聯技術，已成為帶寬-距離積超過100 Gb/s·m的通信場景的主流選擇。 針對傳輸距離從數米至數百米的短距光通信場景，密集波分復用（DWDM）光互聯技術近年成為極具前景的解決方案。該技術通過單根光纖傳輸經不同光波長調制的多路信號，相較傳統多模光纖方案具有更高數據容量與更優擴展性。微環調制器（MRM）憑藉小尺寸與低成本優勢，已成為DWDM光互聯中電光轉換（E/O）的主流器件。然而，MRM的高溫敏感性、電光轉換增益非線性及有限帶寬等缺陷，成為進一步提升鏈路速率的障礙。此外，面向下一代800G以太網，DWDM光互聯的實現更強調帶寬密度，需在相同模組體積下提升總通信數據速率。 提升帶寬密度可通過兩種途徑實現：一是將調制方案從傳統不歸零（NRZ）信號升級為4脈衝幅度調制（PAM-4）信號。PAM-4信號每個符號可傳輸兩比特信息，在相同系統帶寬下數據速率可達NRZ的兩倍；二是縮小光收發模組尺寸以增加波長通道數量，因此需採用緊湊型光收發模組設計方法。 本提案旨在通過融合創新架構與電路技術，應對上述設計挑戰，開發用於DWDM光互聯的CMOS PAM-4光收發模組。我們將依托近期在48-Gb/s無電感光接收器、56-Gb/s低失真垂直腔面發射激光器（VCSEL）發射器，以及112-Gb/大擺幅線性馬赫-曾德爾調制器（MZM）發射器等領域取得的技術成果與設計經驗，實現技術突破。

16221525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16221525.value: 土體多次液化的機理研究：實驗、微觀結構演化與本構模型

16221525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16221525.value: Multiple liquefaction is a phenomenon in which the soil liquefies multiple times during a sequence of earthquake shaking. Recent earthquakes in Japan and New Zealand demonstrated that soils under multiple liquefaction behave vastly differently from those during the first liquefaction. Notably, the soil’s resistance can be significantly changed, leading to difficulties in assessing liquefaction hazards. To date, the fundamental mechanism governing multiple liquefaction has not been fully understood due to several significant challenges: (1) Special equipment is needed to conduct the multiple liquefaction test, which involves complicated liquefaction-reconsolidation-reliquefaction of the soil sample multiple times. Therefore, high-quality experimental data on different types of soils are extremely scarce. (2) Soil fabric represents the arrangement of particles and voids in an assemblage. Although the drastic change in multiple liquefaction resistance is often attributed to the evolution of soil fabric, there is a lack of direct observation to support the scientific understanding of the phenomenon; (3) Development of numerical constitutive models is crucial for seismic analysis of structures and foundations on liquefiable soils. To date, no such a constitutive model has been developed, which hinders engineering practice for multiple liquefaction assessment. This project aims at advancing scientific understanding of the fundamental mechanisms of multiple liquefaction through three interrelated tasks. Task 1 develops a comprehensive experimental dataset for multiple liquefaction of clean sand, silty sand and clayey sand by using an innovative stacked ring torsional shear device newly developed at HKUST. The unique, comprehensive data will be used to investigate the effects of fines and to develop various empirical criteria for assessing multiple liquefaction resistance. Task 2 probes the evolution of soil fabric during the multiple liquefaction process by using X-ray tomography and discrete element modelling. Fabric indices measuring particle contact and void distribution will be developed to correlate with soil behaviors. Task 3 develops an innovative constitutive model for multiple liquefaction, linking the macro-behavior (Task 1) and micro-mechanical investigation (Task 2). The model explicitly accounts for coupled shear and volumetric deformation in the resedimentation and reconsolidation process; A new fabric index and its evolution law will be introduced into the constitutive framework, which controls the increase/decrease of multiple liquefaction resistance. The constitutive model will be extensively calibrated using experimental data. Once successful, such a model will become the first of its kind that can be used to evaluate multiple liquefaction hazards and associated engineering problems. 多次液化是指土體在一系列地震過程中多次發生液化的現象。最近的日本和紐西蘭地震表明，多次液化後的土體與第一次液化時的行為截然不同。多次液化後土體的液化抗力能會發生顯著變化，對評估液化風險造成困難。 迄今為止，土體多次液化的科學機理尚不清楚，存在以下重大難題：（1）多次液化試驗涉及土樣多次液化-再固結-再液化的複雜過程，需要特殊試驗設備。當前，針對不同類型土壤的高品質實驗數據極為稀缺。（2）微觀結構代表了土體內顆粒和空隙的排列。雖然多次液化抗力的劇烈變化通常歸因於土體結構的演變，但缺乏直接觀察來支持這種科學認知；（3）數值本構模型對於可液化土體上結構和地基的地震分析至關重要。目前尚未開發出相關的本構模型，阻礙了多次液化評估的工程實踐。 本研究旨在通過三個相互關聯的任務，加深對多次液化機理的科學認知。任務 1 使用香港科技大學開發的新型疊環扭剪裝置對純凈砂、粉質砂和黏質砂進行多次液化試驗。這些獨特而全面的實驗數據將用於研究細粒的影響，並製定評估多次液化抗力的經驗準則。任務2使用X光斷層掃描和離散元模型，探討多次液化過程中土體結構的變化。提出量度顆粒接觸和孔隙分佈的參數，與土體行為相關聯。任務3發展一種創新的多次液化本構模型，將宏觀行為（任務 1）與微觀特性（任務2）結合起來。該本構模型將引入再固結過程中剪切變形和體積變形的耦合、新的土體結構參數及其演化規律，用於控製多次液化抗力的增減。此本構模型將利用實驗數據進行校驗，將成為首個可用於評估多重液化災害及相關工程問題的模型。

16221625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16221625.value: 通過雙梯度析出相微結構實現超強鈦合金的韌化

16221625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16221625.value: Ultrastrong titanium alloys typically suffer from poor fracture toughness, especially when strength exceeds 1.5 GPa, where fracture toughness often drops below 20 MPa·m^0.5. This high strength is achieved through ultrafine nanoscale α precipitates, which unfortunately limit the work-hardening capacity and lead to rapid crack propagation, particularly along coarse grain boundary α due to the absence of significant plastic zones. The challenge of deflecting cracks and enlarging plastic zones in ultrastrong Ti-alloys without sacrificing strength remains unresolved. Recent preliminary work in the PI’s lab has identified three promising strategies to enhance the toughness of Ti-alloys: (1) Intragranular α' size gradients within a 3-dimensional interpenetrated structure, where clusters of α' and β regions interpenetrate, can enhance work-hardening capacity while maintaining high yield strength by enabling new deformation mechanisms, such as phase transitions, dislocations, and complex twinning routes. (2) Globular α (αp) serves as a double-edged sword for toughness: while it can interrupt fast crack propagation along prior β grain boundaries, it also introduces new crack paths along weak and incompatible αp boundaries. (3) Phase-field simulations demonstrate the possibility of refining coarse grain boundary α into finer variants, a feature previously shown in the literature to inhibit fast crack propagation. These findings suggest that a 3-dimensional interpenetrated precipitation microstructure could promote a synergy between strength and toughness by mitigating stress concentration and regulating crack propagation. However, critical questions remain: How can we quantitatively modulate the size, morphology, and spatial gradient of α precipitates? Can these gradient precipitates deform progressively, activating various dislocation slip systems and twinning mechanisms to enhance work-hardening capacity? Can these gradients dissipate strain localization and effectively blunt or deflect cracks, thereby improving toughness? This project aims to fabricate ultrastrong yet tough titanium alloys (e.g., 1.5 GPa strength + 50 MPa·m^0.5 fracture toughness) by developing nested dual-gradient precipitate microstructures using a 3-step heat treatment process. This approach will precisely control the size and morphology of globular αp, grain boundary α, and the intragranular α size/morphology gradient. Multi-scale ex-situ and in-situ experiments will elucidate the deformation mechanisms responsible for both strength and ductility, with particular focus on crack deflection and plastic zone formation at the crack tip. By regulating crack paths and deformation mechanisms, the project aims to deliver enhanced properties through an economically viable process, advancing high-performance titanium alloys for aerospace and engineering applications.

16300325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300325.value: 平帶材料中量子度規之研究

16300325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300325.value: This project is devoted to the study of a length scale defined by the PI called the quantum metric length. The focus of this project is to study the effect of quantum metric length in flat band or nearly flat band materials in which the Fermi velocity of the electrons is zero or nearly zero. Length scales are fundamentally important quantities in physical systems. The sizes of electronic objects, such as the superconducting vortex size, the Andreev bound state size, the Yu Shiba state size etc. are all related to the superconducting coherence length of the superconductor. The Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) theory which predicted that the superconducting coherence length is proportional to the Fermi velocity of the electrons at the Fermi energy. However, in flat band materials, the Fermi velocity goes to zero and the superconducting coherence length should also go to zero according to BCS theory. It was shown by the PI recently that the BCS theory completely failed to describe the superconducting properties (such as the upper critical fields) of magic angle twisted bilayer graphene. Instead, the superconducting coherence length is determined by the quantum metric-defined length scale which can be calculated from the wavefunctions of the (nearly) flat band. Therefore, the sizes of the electronic objects in flat band superconductors are determined by the quantum metric length. In the past decades, many of the well-established theories such as the BCS theory for superconductivity, de Gennes theory of superconducting proximity effects, Friedel’s theory of density oscillations, the theory of RKKY interactions, the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation for excitons etc. rely on the assumption that there are Fermi surfaces for the electrons. These theories cannot be applied to flat band and nearly flat band materials. More recently, the PI demonstrated the importance of quantum metric length both in flat band Josephson junctions and in topological superconductors. However, this direction of study is extremely important, and the study of quantum metric length is only at its initial stage. This proposal is devoted to study the importance of quantum metric length in all the ten topological symmetry classes and how the transport properties are affected by the quantum metric. Another objective is to study how the quantum metric will affect the transport properties of disordered systems. This study is very important for the understanding of moiré materials with large quantum metric and topologically nontrivial bands. 本計畫致力於研究由項目負責人提出的一種長度尺度，稱為「量子度規長度」（quantum metric length）。本計畫的重點在於探討在平帶或近乎平帶、電子費米速度為零或近零的材料中，量子度規長度所造成的效應。 長度尺度是物理系統中的根本量。各種電子相關的物理實體之大小，例如超導渦旋大小、Andreev 束縛態的大小、Yu–Shiba 狀態的大小等，皆與超導體的超導相干長度有關。Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer（BCS）理論預言，超導相干長度與費米能處電子的費米速度成正比。然而，在平帶材料中，費米速度趨近於零，依 BCS 理論超導相干長度也應趨近於零。項目負責人近期指出，BCS 理論完全無法描述魔角扭轉雙層石墨烯的超導性質（例如上臨界場）。相反地，超導相干長度由量子度規所定義的長度尺度決定，而該尺度可由（近）平帶的波函數計算得到。因此，在平帶超導體中，電子物理實體的大小由量子度量長度所決定。 過去數十年來，許多成熟理論——例如超導的 BCS 理論、de Gennes 的超導近接效應理論、Friedel 的密度振盪理論、RKKY 相互作用理論、激子之玻色—愛因斯坦凝聚理論等——皆建立在電子存在費米面的假設上。這些理論無法套用於平帶或近乎平帶的材料。更近期，項目負責人已在平帶約瑟夫森接面與拓撲超導體中展示了量子度規長度的重要性。然而，這一研究方向極為關鍵，而對量子度規長度的探究仍處於初始階段。 本計畫將系統性研究量子度規長度在十種拓撲對稱類別中的重要性，以及量子度規如何影響輸運性質。另一項目標是探討量子度規對無序系統輸運性的影響。此研究對理解具有巨大量子度規與拓撲非平庸能帶的莫爾（moiré）材料至關重要。

16300425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300425.value: 單層共軛金屬有機骨架在TMDC基底上的動態配位組裝

16300425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300425.value: Two-dimensional conjugated metal–organic frameworks (2D cMOFs) are atomically thick layered materials that comprise metal atom nodes and organic molecule linkers articulated via metal–ligand coordination interactions. Theoretical studies have predicted that 2D cMOFs exhibit exciting quantum phases, such as the quantum spin Hall state, quantum anomalous Hall state, and Chern flat bands, making them ideal platforms for exploring quantum phenomena. However, conventional chemical synthesis yields 2D cMOFs only in the form of thin films or multilayer structures, in which the predicted quantum phases are often suppressed by the inter-layer interactions. Therefore, the predicted quantum states have yet to be unambiguously confirmed. The PI has developed a method for synthesizing single-layer (SL) cMOFs on metal surfaces. In the proposed project, we will synthesize SL cMOFs on chemically and electronically inert substrates. The intrinsic quantum properties of SL-cMOFs are expected to be protected on the inert substrates. We will use monolayer or few-layer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) as substrates. TMDCs are semiconducting materials with layered structures held together by weak Van der Waals forces without dangling bonds at the surface. They have a band gap of a few electron volts. The first step in our project will be to grow monolayer or few-layer TMDCs through chemical vapor deposition on a highly ordered pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) surface. The second step will be to grow SL-cMOFs with specific quantum properties, such as flat bands and non-trivial topological gaps, on the TMDC substrates through the on-surface coordination assembly of metals and organic molecules with specific functional groups. We will develop a dynamic on-surface coordination assembly method to achieve our goal. Specifically, metals and organic molecules will be co-deposited at specific fluxes on a hot substrate to form the SL-cMOFs. The deposition fluxes and substrate temperature will be set to disperse the metal atoms as single atoms so that they effectively activate the molecular functional groups and participate in coordination. The third step will be to use low-temperature STM/STS and various spectroscopic techniques including photoluminescence spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy for characterization of the structural, electronic, and optical properties of the SL-cMOFs. We believe that our project will lay the foundation for exploring the quantum properties of SL-cMOFs using techniques such as quantum transport measurements, potentially establishing SL-cMOFs as a new class of quantum materials. 二維共軛金屬有機骨架（2D cMOF）是一種原子級厚度的層狀材料，由金屬原子節點和有機分子連接體構成，並透過金屬-配體配位相互作用連接在一起。理論研究預測2D cMOF將表現出令人興奮的量子相，例如量子自旋霍爾態、量子異常霍爾態和陳平帶，使其成為探索量子現象的理想平台。然而，傳統的化學合成方法只能得到薄膜或多層結構的2D cMOF，而這些結構中預測的量子相通常會受到層間相互作用的抑制。因此，預測的量子態尚未得到明確的證實。 首席研究員 (PI) 開發了一種在金屬表面合成單層 (SL) cMOF 的方法。在本專案中，我們將在化學和電子惰性的基底上合成 SL cMOF。 SL-cMOF 的固有量子特性可望在惰性基底上得到保護。我們將使用單層或少層過渡金屬二硫屬化物 (TMDC) 作為基底。 TMDC 是一種半導體材料，具有層狀結構，由弱范德華力結合在一起，表面沒有懸掛鍵結。它們的帶隙為幾電子伏特。我們專案的第一步是透過化學氣相沉積在高度有序的熱解石墨 (HOPG) 表面上生長單層或少層 TMDC。第二步，我們將透過在表面配位組裝金屬和帶有特定官能基的有機分子，在TMDC基底上生長具有特定量子特性（例如平帶和非平凡拓樸能隙）的SL-cMOF。我們將開發一種動態表面配位組裝方法來實現我們的目標。具體而言，我們將在熱基底上以特定的通量共沉積金屬和有機分子，以形成SL-cMOF。沉積通量和基底溫度將設定為使金屬原子分散為單個原子，從而有效地激活分子功能基團並參與配位。第三步，我們將利用低溫STM/STS以及包括光致發光光譜、拉曼光譜和角分辨光電子能譜在內的各種光譜技術，以表徵SL-cMOF的結構、電子和光學特性。 我們相信，我們的研究計畫將為使用量子傳輸測量等技術來探索 SL-cMOF 的量子特性奠定基礎，並有可能將 SL-cMOF 確立為一種新型量子材料。

16300725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300725.value: 具有多铁性莫尔超晶格的强磁电耦合实验研究

16300725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16300725.value: Prof Meng, Zi Yang Prof YANG, Sen

16300725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300725.value: Multiferroic materials that unite two or more primary ferroic states (e.g., ferroelectricity (FE), ferromagnetism (FM), ferrovalley, ferroelasticity, and ferrotoroidicity) in the same phase offer a rich research landscape. The complex mechanisms behind multiferroic coupling, especially the magnetoelectric effect, provide an exciting opportunity to manipulate spins using electric fields. This capability has vast potential for innovation in the development of advanced multi-stage storage and nonvolatile logic devices. However, the pursuit of room-temperature multiferroics with robust magnetoelectric coupling is a key challenge in this swiftly evolving research domain, owing to the challenges posed by weak coupling in type-I multiferroics and low polarization intensity and a low Curie temperature in type-II variants. Recently, we observed signatures of multiferroic behaviors in moiré superlattices of transition metal chalcogenides through electronic transport measurements in cryogenic conditions. These signatures included Coulomb interaction-induced FE, anomalous Hall signals featuring robust magnetic hysteresis loops, and strong magnetoelectric coupling, demonstrated by charge polarization tunable by a magnetic field and magnetization controllable via an electric field. These behaviors manifest near half-filled insulating states, underscoring the vital role of electron–electron interactions. Furthermore, the persistence of these half-filled insulating states up to near room temperature signals a promising pathway toward realizing room-temperature multiferroics with strong coupling in moiré superlattices. Equally important, the combination of different two-dimensional ferroic building blocks, much like assembling Lego pieces, may lead to the discovery of novel multiferroic phases beyond the prevailing spin-driven FE paradigm. The main objective of the proposed experimental project will be to explore the multiferroic order and magnetoelectric coupling in moiré superlattices based on transition metal chalcogenides. We will investigate the origins of simultaneous ferroic orders, magnetoelectric couplings, and strategies for their enhancement within these moiré structures by studying effects of the Coulomb interaction, spin configuration, interface, and crystal structure. The ultimate goal will be to explore potential device structures with enhanced multiferroic coupling near room temperature. This project will provide critical knowledge and technical information needed to precisely control twisted moiré structures and modulate their electronic properties. A better understanding of the underlying mechanisms governing the coexistence of multiferroic orders will have implications for device design and the technological utilization of room-temperature multiferroics. 多铁性材料将两种或多种主要铁性状态结合在同一相中，从而提供了丰富的研究前景。多铁性耦合背后的复杂机制，尤其是磁电效应，为利用电场操控自旋提供了机会。这种能力在先进多级存储和非易失性逻辑器件的开发中具有巨大的创新潜力。然而，由于I型多铁性材料的弱耦合以及II型多铁性材料的低极化强度和低居里温度带来的挑战，在这种快速发展的研究领域中，寻求具有稳健磁电耦合的室温多铁性材料是一项关键挑战。 最近，我们通过低温条件下的电子输运测量，观察到过渡金属硫族化物莫尔超晶格中多铁性行为的特征。这些特征包括库仑相互作用引起的场致场致发光 (FE)、具有强磁滞回线的异常霍尔信号以及强磁电耦合，后者表现为可通过磁场调节的电荷极化和可通过电场控制的磁化强度。这些行为表现为接近半满绝缘态，凸显了电子间相互作用的重要作用。此外，这些半满绝缘态在接近室温下的持续存在，标志着在莫尔超晶格中实现室温强耦合多铁性材料有望成为一条有效途径。同样重要的是，不同二维铁性构件的组合，就像组装乐高积木一样，可能有助于发现超越当前自旋驱动FE范式的新型多铁性相。 本项目的主要目标是探索基于过渡金属硫族化物的莫尔超晶格中的多铁性序和磁电耦合。我们将通过研究库仑相互作用、自旋组态、界面和晶体结构的影响，探究莫尔结构中同时存在的铁性序和磁电耦合的起源及其增强策略。最终目标是探索室温附近多铁性耦合增强的潜在器件结构。本项目将提供精确控制扭曲莫尔结构及其电子特性所需的关键知识和技术信息。更好地理解控制多铁性序共存的潜在机制，将对器件设计和室温技术应用产生重要影响。

16300825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300825.value: 海洋內波避難所中的熱變異性：於全球海洋生物多樣性中心驗證一個海洋數理模型

16300825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300825.value: Coral ecosystems, and their associated biodiversity and essential ecosystem services, are globally threatened by human-induced climate change, overfishing, and pollution. These pressures are particularly acute in low-income countries within the Coral Triangle (CT), a region that harbours extraordinary coral reef biodiversity crucial for many millions of people. While the vulnerability of shallow-water coral reefs is well documented, deeper habitats remain understudied, despite evidence that they may serve as refuges from shallow-water stressors due to the upwelling of cooler, nutrient-rich (but possibly oxygen-poor) water driven by internal waves. Global numerical ocean simulations indicate that internal-wave cooling may sustain climate refuges in the CT, yet these models require validation through in situ temperature observations. Additionally, biogeochemical processes linked to internal waves – vital for understanding the functionality of these refuges – remain largely unquantified. This study will conduct one of the first comprehensive assessments of environmental dynamics across coral reef depths in the CT, using long-term instrument deployments to quantify internal-wave climates and associated biogeochemical dynamics, including temperature, light, oxygen, and chlorophyll. These data will be used to validate models that predict the location and persistence of coral reef climate refuges, both regionally and globally. This pioneering research will provide critical insights into the environmental processes shaping refuge habitats hidden below the surface, thereby promoting more effective stewardship and sustainable use of coral reefs in the face of accelerating climate change. 人為氣候變遷、過度捕撈和污染正威脅著全球珊瑚生態系統、依存珊瑚生態系統的生物多樣性及它們提供的重要生態系統服務。這些人為環境壓力對於匯聚了豐富珊瑚礁生物多樣性的珊瑚大三角（Coral Triangle, CT）周邊低收入國家的威脅尤其嚴重。過去已對淺水珊瑚礁的脆弱性有廣泛研究，但較深棲地卻仍未得到充分研究。近期研究提供證據表明，由內波驅動的較冷且富含營養鹽的上升流，可能使其成為免受淺水壓力影響的避難所，儘管這些海水可能含氧量較低。全球數理海洋模擬顯示，內波冷卻現象或能於珊瑚大三角海域內形成氣候避難所，但這些模型需要通過現地溫度觀測驗證。本研究將成為少數對珊瑚大三角、珊瑚礁深度範圍的環境動態進行全面評估的研究之一。本團隊將利用長期儀器監測來量化海洋內波氣候。這些數據將被用於驗證預測珊瑚礁氣候避難所位置及持續性的區域或全球範圍模型。這項開創性的研究將提供關於塑造表面下避難所棲地的環境過程的關鍵資料，從而促進在氣候變遷加速的情況下，對珊瑚礁進行更有效的管理和可持續利用。

16301225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301225.value: Adaptive stochastic optimization methods have emerged as powerful tools for training complex models, particularly in high-dimensional and non-convex landscapes. Techniques such as AdaGrad, RMSprop, and Adam have gained widespread popularity due to their ability to dynamically adjust learning rates based on data characteristics, facilitating faster convergence and improved performance across various applications. However, challenges remain in the effective implementation of these adaptive methods. One significant challenge lies in their theoretical analysis, especially when optimizing non-convex objectives, where the correlation between step sizes and both current and past stochastic gradients complicates convergence behavior. Additionally, the reliance on hyperparameter tuning, particularly the global learning rate, can greatly influence the optimization process and outcomes. In this study, we will first explore the theoretical foundations of adaptive optimization and investigate the intricacies of convergence behavior in non-convex settings. Subsequently, we will develop novel adaptive and parameter-free algorithms tailored for momentum-based and adaptive techniques. Our research will focus on three key directions: (1) demonstrating both asymptotic and non-asymptotic convergence results for adaptive gradient methods in non-convex scenarios; (2) developing adaptive global learning rate schedules for AdaGrad and Adam; and (3) proposing an adaptive and parameter-free stochastic optimization method that eliminates the need for manual hyperparameter tuning. We aim to create algorithms that are both user-friendly and efficient, enabling broader adoption across various domains. Through rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation, we aim to contribute to the growing body of knowledge in stochastic optimization, ultimately enhancing the practicality and effectiveness of machine learning methodologies in real-world applications.
