16301625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16301625.value: 對稱性在拓撲光子學譜問題中的應用

16301625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301625.value: The application of symmetry in the study of periodic operators has found particular relevance in topological photonics, which explores the behavior of light in engineered photonic structures with nontrivial topological properties. This project aims to incorporate symmetry into the spectral theory for the partial differential operators that model topological photonics and utilize it to reveal the mechanism of the topological features such as protected interface modes at the interface of two structures with different topological phases. The PI will focus on two-dimensional photonic crystals with specific spatial symmetries, such as the C6 and C4 point groups. The goal is to understand how these symmetries affect the spectrum of the underlying partial differential operators. Key objectives include establishing the existence of spectral degeneracy, examining the breakdown of degeneracy under suitable perturbations that break certain symmetries, proving the existence of eigenvalues corresponding to interface modes, and verifying their stability numerically. The expected results will provide valuable insights into the design and analysis of complex photonic structures that have applications in manipulating and guiding the flow of light. 對稱性在與拓撲光子學相關的週期性算子的研究中有重要的應用。拓撲光子學研究的是光在具有非平凡拓撲性質的人工設計光子材料結構中的行為。本項目旨在將對稱性引入描述拓撲光子學的偏微分算子的譜理論中，並利用對稱性揭示拓撲特徵的機理，例如在具有不同拓撲相的兩種結構交界處出現的受保護界面模態。 本項目將重點研究具有特定空間對稱性（例如 C6 和 C4 點群）的二維光子晶體，目的是理解這些對稱性如何影響底層偏微分算子的譜。主要目標包括：建立譜簡併點（spectral degeneracy point）的存在性、研究在破壞某些對稱性的擾動下簡併點的破壞、證明與界面模態相對應的特徵值的存在性，以及數值驗證其穩定性。 預期的研究成果將為複雜光子結構的設計與分析提供理論指導，並有助於實現對光流的操控與引導。

16302025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302025.value: 探索網絡化蛋白質凝聚體的湧現力學：從網絡形成、臨界生長到老化機制

16302025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302025.value: Multivalent proteins can form membrane-less condensates in living cells through liquid-liquid phase separation, and significant efforts have been made to study their biochemical properties. These protein condensates exhibit emergent mechanical properties that differ from simple Maxwell fluids. The ability of a condensate droplet to resist deformation, maintain structural integrity against entropic mixing, and transport functional proteins in and out of the droplet relies on an interconnected network of filamentous biopolymers and regulatory proteins. In a recent experiment, we employed combined atomic force microscopy-based micro-rheology and quantitative fluorescence measurements to investigate a multivalent networked protein condensate composed of six essential reconstituted postsynaptic proteins (6xPSD), which play a crucial role in neurons responsible for signal transduction. Our findings revealed that 20% of the non-mobile scaffold proteins in 6xPSD form a dynamically cross-linked network, leading to a long-time power-law decay in its time-dependent modulus. Understanding how this percolating network emerges and responds to mechanical signals over both short and long timescales—and how it influences local mechanical properties and dynamic behavior—is essential for elucidating the condensate's organization, physiological functions, and implications in disease states. This proposal will leverage the above experimental breakthroughs to investigate network formation, critical growth, and aging in two well-characterized protein condensates. Our first project aims to determine when and how a percolating network forms from an initially liquid-like protein condensate as the protein-protein interactions increase and become more complex. We will use the PrLD-SAM chimera model, which forms long polymer chains with disordered side chains, mimicking natural functional condensates. By adjusting the number of side chains and introducing single-amino-acid mutations at the binding site, we will map the gelation landscape, explore the percolation mechanism, and study its critical behavior near the gelation point. The second project aims to establish a systematic method with quantitative readouts to characterize the aging process of protein condensates with a percolating network. We will investigate the aging kinetics and mechanisms of the two model condensates, PrLD-SAM and 4xPSD, both of which exhibit aging behavior. By analyzing the time evolution of their mechanical profiles, we will identify key parameters influencing network growth, aging, and eventual fate. Through an interdisciplinary approach that combines quantitative physical methods with biological and biochemical techniques, we seek to enhance our understanding of the multiscale mechanics of protein condensates, including their homeostasis, physiological functions, and connections to diseases, and pave the way for future advancements in the field. 多價蛋白質可透過液-液相分離在活細胞中形成無膜凝聚體。目前學界已對此類凝聚體的生化特性進行廣泛研究。這些蛋白質凝聚體展現出不同於簡單馬克士威流體（Maxwell fluid）的新興力學特性。凝聚體液滴能藉由長鏈生物高分子與調控蛋白組成的互連網絡抵抗形變、維持結構完整性以克服混合熵，並實現功能蛋白在液滴內外的轉運。在最新實驗中，我們結合原子力顯微鏡（AFM）微流變技術與定量螢光檢測技術，研究由六種關鍵突觸後蛋白（6xPSD）重構的多價網絡化蛋白質凝聚體——此類蛋白在神經元信號傳導中扮演關鍵角色。結果顯示，6xPSD中20%的非移動支架蛋白會形成動態交聯網絡，導致其鬆弛模量呈現長時間尺度下的冪律衰減行為。理解此滲流網絡如何在多重時間尺度下形成並響應力學刺激，及其對局部力學特性和動態行為的影響，對闡明凝聚體的結構組織、生理功能與病理關聯具有關鍵意義。 本提案將基於上述研究成果，針對兩種特性明確的蛋白質凝聚體，探討其網絡形成、臨界生長及老化過程。首階段研究將釐清當蛋白質間相互作用增強且趨於複雜時，滲透網絡如何從初始液態蛋白質凝聚體中形成。我們採用PrLD-SAM嵌合體作為模型系統，該蛋白能通過形成具無序側鏈的長聚合物鏈來模擬天然功能性凝聚體。通過調控側鏈數量與結合位點的氨基酸單點突變，我們將建立PrLD-SAM的凝膠化相圖，探討網絡滲流形成機制，並分析其在相變點附近的臨界現象。次階段研究將建立定量化力學表徵方法，用以分析具滲流網絡的蛋白質凝聚體老化過程。我們將以PrLD-SAM和4xPSD兩種模型系統研究老化動力學與分子機制——二者均表現出典型的老化特徵。通過追蹤其力學特性的時序演化，我們將鑑定影響凝聚體網絡生長、老化進程及最終狀態的關鍵控制參數。這項整合定量物理方法與生物化學技術的跨學科研究，將深化對蛋白質凝聚體多尺度力學特性（包括穩態調控、生理功能與疾病關聯）的理解，為此領域的發展奠定重要基礎。

16302425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302425.value: 鈷金屬複合物反應化學與催化機理之DFT計算研究

16302425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302425.value: Cobalt metal complexes have emerged as promising alternatives to traditional precious metal catalysts because they are abundant and cheap. In this proposed study, we plan to employ Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to investigate the reaction chemistry and catalysis of cobalt metal complexes. We aim to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms, reaction pathways, and electronic properties of selected catalytic reactions. The results obtained will deepen our understanding of these reactions and provide valuable guidance for the design of more efficient and sustainable catalytic systems in the future. Recently, we were invited by an experimental group to embark on a collaborative project, concerning the reductive desymmetrization of malononitriles (dinitriles), using cobalt metal complexes as catalysts. This collaborative work has been accepted for publication in Nature Chemistry, 2024 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01592-z), further establishing the foundation of this proposal. In recent decades, significant advances have been made in experimental studies focusing on diverse cobalt-catalyzed reduction reactions, including hydrogenation, hydrosilylation, and hydroboration. Although significant advances have been made on the experimental front, theoretical studies aimed at the comprehensive understanding of these reactions involving cobalt metal complexes are still somewhat limited, particularly given the potential for various oxidation states and spin configurations in the metal center of cobalt complexes. While sporadic DFT calculations associated with experimental findings have been made, a systematic exploration of the catalytic mechanisms involving cobalt metal complexes with various oxidation states and ligands is still lacking. Therefore, the objectives of this proposed research are to clarify the reactions of cobalt complexes in a systematic manner and to obtain a more comprehensive understanding of cobalt chemistry. 鈷金屬複合物 因儲量豐富且成本低廉，有望替代傳統貴金屬催化劑。本研究擬採用密度泛函理論（DFT） 計算，系統探討鈷複合物的反應化學與催化機制，重點解析其電子特性、反應路徑及機理，所得成果將為設計高效、永續的催化系統提供理論基礎。 本研究計畫基於我們與實驗團隊的合作成果：近期我們共同開發了鈷催化腈的還原去對稱化反應，該研究已獲《自然化學》接受（2024年刊出，[DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01592-z]）。 儘管近年來鈷催化還原反應（如氫化、氫矽化、氫硼化）的實驗研究進展顯著，但相關理論研究仍相對匱乏, 尤其針對鈷中心多樣的氧化態與自旋態特性。現有文獻多為零散的DFT計算，缺乏對不同配體環境及氧化態下催化機制的系統性探索。本研究旨在透過計算化學方法，全面闡明鈷複合物的反應特性，補足當前研究的空白。

16302525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302525.value: 在流体-固体界面具有显著滑移的薄膜动力学：建模，分析与模拟

16302525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302525.value: Liquid droplets and films on solid surfaces are ubiquitously found in nature and industrial applications. They exhibit many intriguing properties and phenomena that arise from the coupling of three phases, i.e., liquid, gas, and solid. For decades, continuous research efforts have been made to study various aspects of their dynamics which may involve contact line motion, evaporation, complex mixtures of phases, and non-Newtonian rheology. Taking advantage of the disparity of the length scales displayed in droplets of small contact angles and thin films, an asymptotic approach has been taken to develop a mathematical theory to describe the dynamics of thin films that display a range of interesting phenomena. The asymptotic procedure can reduce the original governing equations (Navier-Stokes equation, incompressibility condition, and boundary conditions) to a simplified, nonlinear thin film evolution equation. It is worth emphasizing that the classical regime of thin film dynamics is based on either the no-slip boundary condition (i.e., zero slip length) or a slip length smaller than or comparable to film thickness. Either condition can be justified for thin films of macroscopic length scales. This proposed project intends to study a new regime of thin film dynamics that is characterized by significant slip at fluid-solid interface. This new regime is theoretically justified if the fluid-solid interface presents a slip length that is large enough compared to film thickness. It can be experimentally reached by thin films that are of micrometer-scale thickness and deposited on engineered superhydrophobic surfaces where the measured slip lengths are in the micrometer range and can approach 200 micrometer. Another case of practical relevance is a lamellipodium of a cell moving on a substrate, where thin film dynamics is exhibited by an active anisotropic fluid with significant slip. The proposed project consists of four interconnected components: (i) a model derivation that is physically intuitive and based on Onsager’s variational principle, (ii) an asymptotic analysis that is mathematically rigorous to put the model on a solid basis, (iii) a finite difference semi-implicit scheme developed for accurate and efficient numerical computation, and (iv) a variety of dynamic phenomena that are to be numerically investigated, including droplet spreading, Landau-Levich problem in film coating, and thin film dynamics of active soft matter, to demonstrate the distinct characteristics of the new regime of thin film dynamics. 固体表面上的液滴和薄膜广泛存在于自然界和工业应用中。它们展现出许多引人注目的特性和现象，这些特性和现象源于液体、气体和固体三相的耦合。几十年来，人们持续致力于研究液滴和薄膜动力学的各个方面，这涉及接触线运动、蒸发、相的复杂混合以及非牛顿流变学。 利用小接触角液滴和薄膜所表现出的长度尺度差异，一种渐近方法被采用来发展数学理论，以描述显示一系列有趣现象的薄膜动力学。渐近过程可以将原始的控制方程（纳维-斯托克斯方程、不可压缩条件和边界条件）简化为一个非线性的薄膜演化方程。值得强调的是，经典的薄膜动力学的基础是无滑移边界条件（即零滑移长度）或滑移长度小于或与薄膜厚度相当的条件。这两种条件都可以由宏观长度尺度的薄膜提供合理的解释。 本项目旨在研究一种新的薄膜动力学范畴，其特征是流体-固体界面具有显著的滑移。如果流体-固体界面的滑移长度相对于薄膜厚度足够大，则可以理论上证明这一新范畴。通过在加工超疏水表面上沉积的微米级厚度的薄膜，可以在实验上达到这一点，测得的滑移长度在微米范围内，甚至可接近200微米。另一个具有实际相关性的情况是细胞在基底上移动的伪足，在这种情况下，活性各向异性流体表现出薄膜动力学，且具有显著的滑移。本项目包括四个相互关联的组成部分：（i）基于昂萨格变分原理的物理直观模型推导；（ii）严格的数学渐近分析，为模型奠定坚实基础；（iii）开发的有限差分半隐式方案，用于准确高效的数值计算；（iv）多种动态现象的数值研究，包括液滴扩散、薄膜涂覆中的朗道-列维奇问题以及活性软物质的薄膜动力学，以展示薄膜动力学的新范畴的独特特征。

16302625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302625.value: 倒置鈣鈦礦太陽能電池之界面奈米溝槽的可擴展工程

16302625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302625.value: This project aims to address the knowledge gap in fundamental understanding and innovative engineering of interfacial nano-grooves (INGs), a material's microstructure type that is proven critical yet rarely exploited for improving power conversion efficiency (PCE), stability, and reliability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). The recent advancement of PSCs has triggered enormous interest in commercialization. The core engineering science lies in the intriguing microstructure-property-performance relationship in perovskites. In this context, while perovskite microstructures such as grain boundaries have been optimized extensively, it is vital to clarify the elusive role of other prominent perovskite microstructures beyond grain boundaries and to open new avenues of thin-film and device engineering. This research will complement previous works, contribute a nontrivial addition to vast existing knowledge, and unleash the full technological potential of perovskites. The PI’s recent research works (Nature Energy 2024, 9, 999; Adv. Mater 2023, 35, 2211155) have revealed that INGs play a vital role in PSCs. The unique geometric morphology and defect chemistry of INGs can influence charge transport, chemical stability, and mechanical reliability in perovskites. This significant development brings immense excitement to gain insight into the microstructural dynamics and property enhancement of INGs. There is a promising opportunity to develop scalable strategies to achieve engineered INGs (E-INGs) with benign or beneficial physiochemical properties for further improved PCE and stability, especially in the inverted p-i-n PSC device setting that currently generates enormous impact in the emerging perovskite industry. The overall approach of this project entails three interrelated tasks: (i) using advanced multimodal characterizations to elucidate the atomic details and structural dynamics of INGs; (ii) implanting a new concept of crystal-solvate pre-seeding toward E-INGs that can lead to perovskite films with benign or even beneficial optoelectronic, chemical, and mechanical properties; and (iii) fabricating stable efficient PSCs and modules to demonstrate the up-scaling potential of E-INGs. The PI is equipped with adequate expertise to perform all these tasks. Based on promising preliminary results, the proposed fundamentals-driven materials engineering is expected to mitigate the INGs-related charge transport, chemical stability, and mechanical reliability issues for PSCs. The outcome of this project will make a direct impact on the PSC development toward commercial applications. Meanwhile, the importance of INGs is generic to all types of thin-film devices, and thus, the theories developed via this project will have overarching impacts on numerous other optoelectronic technologies, including but not limited to, light-emitting devices, memristors, and sensors.

16303025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303025.value: 四元硼杂环的合成及性质研究

16303025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303025.value: Boracycles are important functional scaffolds in catalysts, bioactive molecules, pharmaceuticals, and optoelectronic materials, often exhibiting unique performance compared to their carbon analogs. Furthermore, the use of boracycles as synthons for synthetic reagents or functional molecules is an area of increasing research interest. Current studies predominantly focus on three-, five- and six-membered boracycles, leaving four-membered boracycles largely unexplored. The lack of efficient and versatile synthetic methods limits the investigation into their properties and applications. For example, attributing to the inherent ring strain, four-membered boracycles are expected to serve as valuable synthons with versatile reactivities and functionalities, like other four-membered heterocycles such as azetidine and oxetane. Therefore, exploring the synthesis and reactivity of four-membered boracycles is meaningful and could unlock significant advances in synthetic chemistry. Our preliminary efforts to unlock the boron-carbon diradical (BCDR) chemistry provide a hint to the above research challenge. Employing triplet energy transfer catalysis, intramolecular radical(B)-radical(C) coupling of a BCDR intermediate leads to four-membered benzoboretenes. These benzoboretenes demonstrate stablity against air and chromatography. Meanwhile, they are amenable to ring-opening transformations. Building on this premise, we propose to (1) expand the library of four-membered boracycles using the BCDR protocol, (2) diversify the BCDR chemistry and related synthetic approaches by designing new BCDR members, and (3) explore reactivities of resulting four-membered boracycles with an emphasis on creating structurally novel functional molecules, including isoelectronic analogs of oxaborole pharmacophore, B-/BN-doped aromatics, and 3D bioisosteres of benzene. These newly synthesized boracycles may find valuable applications in medicinal chemistry and optoelectronic materials. Additionally, elucidating the reaction mechanism is also a crucial aspect of this project. The new BC-diradical chemistry is anticipated to result in a diverse array of boracycles previously inaccessible with conventional synthetic methods. Investigations into their reactivities and properties will bring structurally novel functional molecules. This project aims not only to advance the chemistry of boron-containing heterocycles but also to harness their unique properties for innovative applications in various scientific disciplines. 硼杂环是催化剂、药物及光电材料分子中的重要骨架，常表现出独特性能。目前的研究主要集中在三元、五元和六元硼杂环，对四元硼杂环的探索则鲜有报导。缺乏高效、通用的合成方法限制了对其性质与应用的深入研究。因此，发展构筑四元硼杂环的方法具有重要意义，并有望推动合成化学的重大进展。 我们通过解锁硼-碳自由基化学，为上述研究挑战提供了解决方案。利用三重态能量转移催化，实现了分子内硼-碳偶联，成功合成出苯并硼杂丁烯。这些四元硼环表现出良好的空气稳定性，且可通过色谱柱分离纯化。基于这一发现，我们提出以下研究目标：（1）利用硼-碳自由基合成策略扩展四元硼杂环的分子库；（2）探索四元硼杂环的反应性，并通过其制备结构新颖的功能分子；及（3）研究反应机理。 新的硼-碳双自由基化学有望带来一系列传统合成方法难以获得的硼杂环分子。对其反应性和性质的研究将带来结构新颖的功能分子。本项目不仅旨在推进含硼杂环化学的发展，也希望利用其独特性质，在多个科学领域实现创新应用。

16303625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303625.value: IPCC 級全球海洋環流模式中中尺度渦旋和背風波參數化的能量一致耦合

16303625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303625.value: The evolution of the Earth's climate is strongly influenced by the Earth's ocean via the ocean's capacity in transporting and storing heat, carbon and chemicals. The ability to model the ocean's evolution to different forcing scenarios is critically important to understanding how the climate evolves, and informing how to mitigate and adapt to future changes. The basis of such predictions is numerical ocean models, but model responses depend sensitively on the representation of the ocean's dynamical processes. Models with an explicit representation of the dynamical processes are regarded as model truths, but are generally computationally prohibitive and unlikely to be routinely used for the foreseeable future. In practice, models often use parameterization for reasons of computational cost, but these parameterized models do not necessarily reproduce the sensitivities of the analogous model truths. This issue highlights the degree of uncertainty in climate projections that use these numerical models, as synthesized in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports. The proposed project will focus on two classes of dynamical processes and their parameterizations: geostrophic mesoscale eddies and lee waves. Scientific questions of interest in the proposed project are how the two classes of motion interact from a parameterized point of view, how to represent their energetic pathways, and how the above choices affect the possible feedback loops and affect the representation and sensitivities of the modeled ocean state, in the context of an IPCC-class ocean climate model. While there will be dynamical coupling of the parameterizations via the modeled ocean state, we hypothesize that explicit energetic coupling between the parameterizations via the modeled energy pathways is required to recover the key sensitivities in IPCC-class ocean climate models. The proposed work will build on a simple idea of energetic consistency and existing tools to tackle a set of well-defined scientific questions. Answering these questions will improve the understanding of ocean dynamical processes, numerical model development of parameterizations, and contribute results to planned internationally coordinated model intercomparison exercises as part of the upcoming IPCC reports. 地球氣候的演變受到海洋的強烈影響。海洋透過其輸送和儲存熱量、碳和化學物質的能力對地球氣候的演變產生重大影響。能夠模擬不同強迫情境下的海洋演變對於理解氣候如何演變以及如何減緩和適應未來變化至關重要。但海洋數值模型敏感地依賴海洋動力學過程的表徵。能夠明確表徵動力學過程的模型被視為目標，但通常計算成本過高，在可預見的未來不太可能被常規使用。在實踐中，出於計算成本的原因模型通常使用參數化，但這些參數化模型不一定能重現類似目標的敏感度。本期專題凸顯了使用這些數值模型進行的氣候預測的不確定性程度。 本計畫將著重於兩類動力學過程及其參數化：地轉中尺度渦旋和背風波。本計畫關注的科學問題包括：從參數化角度來看，這兩類運動如何相互作用；如何表示它們的能量路徑；以及在IPCC級海洋氣候模型中，上述選擇如何影響可能的反饋迴路，以及如何影響模擬海洋狀態的表徵和敏感性。雖然模擬的海洋狀態會與參數化發生動力學耦合，但我們假設，為了恢復IPCC級海洋氣候模型中的關鍵敏感性，需要透過模擬的能量路徑在參數化之間建立明確的能量耦合。本計畫將基於簡單的能量一致性概念和現有工具，以解決一系列定義明確的科學問題。回答這些問題將增進對海洋動力學過程的理解、參數化的數值模型開發，並為即將發布的 IPCC 報告中計劃進行的國際協調模型比對工作貢獻成果。

16303725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303725.value: 開發基於擾動物理參數集的新式替代模型及其在氣候模型誤差診斷與「新興限制條件」評估中的應用

16303725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303725.value: The Earth's intricate energy balance sustains all life, yet human activities are unsettling this equilibrium. The emission of greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels is propelling global temperatures upwards, causing climate change characterized by severe outcomes like extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and the loss of biodiversity. Accurate climate projections are crucial for devising effective adaptation and mitigation strategies. However, the complexity of the Earth system poses challenges to existing climate models in providing precise future forecasts, hindering in-depth assessments of regional climate impacts. These inaccuracies in projections stem from errors within climate models, arising from inaccuracies in physical parameters and structural deficiencies of the models. Perturbed-physics ensemble (PPE) techniques offer a robust approach to analyze and differentiate between model parameter errors and structural errors, despite the potential high costs associated with conducting PPE experiments. Leveraging novel PPE data from the Community Atmosphere Model version 6 (CAM6), which is the atmospheric component of the Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2), using advanced machine learning methodologies, this study endeavors to develop more accurate emulators compared to the current state-of-the-art Gaussian Process models. These emulators will play a pivotal role in unraveling climate model errors related to physical parameters and model structure, shedding light on the extent to which errors can be mitigated through model tuning and the residual model structural errors that necessitate attention, often through model averaging across diverse models. Furthermore, these emulators will aid in understanding the diversities among CMIP6 models in replicating current climatic conditions. By simulating CMIP6 model current climatology using CESM2-CAM6 emulators, we can estimate the structural disparities of CMIP6 models in comparison to the CESM2 model. These structural disparities in CMIP6 models can be correlated with the diverse future projections of the CMIP6 models, providing insights into how the model's structure influences its future forecasts. Finally, through the utilization of PPE data and emulators, the research endeavors to assess the efficacy of emergent constraints—a contemporary technique for refining climate projections. Despite the limited clarity regarding the physical interpretations of most emergent constraints, the study seeks to validate their reliability using PPE data and emulators, thereby unlocking the potential for dependable applications of emergent constraints in reducing uncertainties in projections of future climate. 地球上生物賴以生存的自然環境靠細緻的能量收支平衡來維持，然而目前人類活動在打破此平衡。大量化石燃料的使用所排放的溫室氣體的溫室效應讓全球不斷升溫，引發氣候變遷，從而導致極端天氣事件更加頻繁、海平面的上升，以及生物多樣性喪失。精確的氣候預測對於制定有效的應對與減緩策略至關重要。但因地球系統太複雜，現有的氣候模型尚未能提供精準的未來預測，對區域氣候影響的深入評估就更為困難。 氣候模型的預測誤差源自模型中的缺陷，其中包括物理參數的不準確性與模型結構的固有缺陷。擾動物理參數集合（PPE）實驗技術可為區分模型參數誤差和結構缺陷的分析提供了強健的數據支撐。但因PPE算力耗費高昂，通常会用少量已有的PPE數據來建一個簡化的替代模型來提高生成PPE的計算效率。本研究利用來自「社區大氣模型第六版」（CAM6，也是「社區地球系統模型第二版」CESM2的大氣組件）的新型PPE數據，結合先進機器學習方法，致力開發比當前最先進高斯過程模型更精準的替代模型。這些替代模型將在釐清氣候模型物理參數誤差與結構缺陷方面發揮關鍵作用，通過模型調參來降低模型誤差，揭示殘餘的結構誤差。模型結構缺陷引起的誤差通常需要透過多模型平均來降低。 此外，這些替代模型有助於理解不同的CMIP6模型在模擬當前氣候條件時的差異。通過將CMIP6模型對照CESM2模型進行解構，我們能估算CMIP6模型相對於CESM2的結構差異。這些結構差異可與CMIP6模型多元的未來預測相互關聯，從而理解模型結構如何影響其氣候預測。 最後，本研究擬運用替代模型來研究現行氣候模型在模擬當前氣候條件時的歧異。「新興限制條件」是一種提高氣候預測精度的新技術，本研究將透過PPE數據與替代模型的應用評估多個常見的「新興限制條件」的有效性。儘管大多數新興限制條件的物理詮釋尚不明確，該研究將嘗試利用PPE數據與替代模型驗證其可靠性，從而開啟「新興限制條件」在氣候科學中可靠應用的潛力。

16303825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303825.value: 随机游走在同质与异质环境中的超量偏差

16303825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303825.value: The principal objective of this project is to investigate fine properties of random walks in homogeneous and heterogeneous environments on the integer lattice in dimension larger or equal to three. Random walks and processes derived from them are among the most fundamental objects in probability theory, serving as important benchmark models for phenomena occurring in physics, chemistry, and biology. A main theme in the investigation of random walks on the integer lattice is to understand the ways in which their paths create interfaces or regions in space of excess presence, and to probe the mechanisms that facilitate such an (atypical) behavior. This naturally leads to the consideration of constrained or 'tilted' random walks, which ought to produce such a behavior at a low entropic cost. Substantial progress has been achieved in this direction in the past two decades due to an improved understanding of the role of the Newtonian (or random walk-)capacity of discrete subsets of the integer lattice, and the emergence of local couplings between the traces or occupation-time fields of (tilted) random walks with the respective quantities in the model of random interlacements. The latter has been introduced by Sznitman in 2010, and can be seen informally as a random infinite connected subset of the integer lattice capturing the local limit of the trace of a random walk on large, discrete tori. One goal of this project is to derive leading-order asymptotics for the probability of excess-type deviations of random walks in non-homogeneous environments, in particular ones with spatial degeneracies (such as the supercritical cluster of Bernoulli bond percolation), and those in which the random walk experiences a spatial drift. Moreover, we aim at developing strong controls on properties of the random walk conditioned on such atypical events. The results from this project will provide a refined insight into the local structure of random walks conditioned on atypical events, and possibly reveal novel second-order effects in the coupling with random interlacements. 本项目的主要目标是研究三维及以上整数格点上随机游走在同质与异质环境中的精细性质。随机游走及其衍生的过程是概率论中最基本的研究对象之一，也是物理学、化学和生物学中的重要基准模型。整数格点上随机游走中的一个核心研究主题，是理解其路径在空间区域中超量出现时形成界面或区域的方式，并探究造成此非典型行为的机理。受限制（constrained）或“倾斜（tilted）”的随机游走能在低熵代价下实现上述行为，因此自然地成为被考虑的对象。该领域在过去二十年间取得了实质性进展。这得益于对整数格点上离散子集的牛顿容度（又称随机游走容度）作用机制更深入的理解，以及（倾斜）随机游走的轨迹或占据时间场与随机交织（random interlacements）中相应量之间局部耦合的发现。随机交织模型由Sznitman于2010年提出，可直观理解为一个被随机游走在大型离散环面上留下的轨迹在局部的极限所刻画，并位于整数格点上的无穷连通子集。本项目的目标之一是确定随机游走在异质环境中发生超量型偏差的概率的主阶渐近行为，尤其针对具有空间退化特征的环境（如超临界伯努利渗流的无穷簇）和导致随机游走出现空间漂移的环境。此外，项目还将致力于建立在上述非典型事件发生的条件下随机游走性质的强控制。本项目的成果将深入揭示非典型事件发生时随机游走的局部结构，并可能揭示其与随机交织耦合时新颖的二阶效应。

16304125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304125.value: 带孤立奇点的蒙日-安培方程解的正则性和稳定性

16304125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304125.value: A wide variety of natural phenomena, such as sound, heat and fluid dynamics, can be well described by partial differential equations (PDEs). They also interact intimately with other branches of mathematics such as geometry and probability, and other scientific fields such as engineering and economics. The Monge-Ampère equations, a class of fully nonlinear partial differential equations involving the determinant of the Hessian matrix of a function, have profound implications across mathematics and its applications. Originating from problems in differential geometry, these equations describe the curvature of surfaces and have become pivotal in optimal transport theory. Their relevance extends to various fields such as meteorology, where they model atmospheric pressure systems, and in economics, where they optimize resource allocation. In computer graphics, Monge-Ampère equations are employed for image processing and 3D modeling, enabling efficient rendering of complex surfaces. The study of these equations not only enriches our understanding of geometric structures but also drives innovation in diverse scientific and engineering disciplines, highlighting their fundamental role in both theoretical and applied mathematics. This proposal aims to investigate the regularity and stability of solutions to some Monge-Ampère equations with isolated singularities. The regularity of solutions to PDEs is a cornerstone of mathematical analysis, reflecting the smoothness and predictability of solutions to complex problems. Regularity results ensure that solutions behave well, avoiding pathological cases that can render equations intractable or meaningless in applications. This aspect is crucial in physics, where PDEs describe fundamental laws. Singularities often represent critical events or transitions. Examining these singularities will allow us to gain further insight into the underlying structure and behavior of solutions. Here, we propose to study the stability of solutions to Monge-Ampère equations with one isolated singularity, the regularity of solutions to Monge-Ampère equations with multiple isolated singularities, and the regularity of the free boundary and the structure of the singularity for a Monge-Ampère obstacle problem. 蒙日-安培方程是一类完全非线性偏微分方程。它涉及函数的二阶导数矩阵的行列式，在数学及其应用领域具有深远的影响。本研究提案旨在探究一些蒙日-安培方程解的正则性和奇点性质。偏微分方程解的正则性是数学分析的基石，反映了复杂问题解的平滑性和可预测性。正则性结果确保解的良好行为，避免可能使方程在应用中变得棘手或无意义的病态情况。这一方面在由偏微分方程描述的基本定律的物理学中尤为重要。奇点通常代表关键事件或转变。研究这些奇点将使我们能够进一步了解解的潜在结构和行为。在此，我们提议研究具有一个孤立奇点的蒙日-安培方程解的稳定性，具有多个孤立奇点的蒙日-安培方程解的正则性，以及蒙日-安培障碍问题的自由边界正则性和奇点结构。

16304225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304225.value: 基於CRISPR/Cas與恆溫放大的核酸感測平台，具有半定量能力，用於靈敏且超快速的居家病毒病原體檢測

16304225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304225.value: In contrast to rapid antigen tests (RATs) developed during the COVID-19 pandemic, nucleic acid-based technologies for at-home testing, despite their notable advantages of high sensitivity and specificity, remain largely underdeveloped. Traditional nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) often necessitate complex equipment and precise temperature control, which restricts their accessibility and practicality. To address these challenges, we propose the development of an innovative NAAT that functions effectively at near-body temperature and delivers semi-quantitative results without the requirement for external equipment. This objective will be achieved through the integration of rationally designed DNA amplification kinetics with a CRISPR/Cas12-based signal amplification system. This approach builds upon our previous research aimed at mitigating aerosol contamination in point-of-care nucleic acid tests, which significantly reduces the likelihood of false positives—a critical enhancement for home testing applications. Concurrently, we will address the specific challenges associated with RNA detection by establishing a CRISPR/Cas13a system enhanced by a positive feedback loop-mediated cascade reaction. This novel strategy aims to markedly improve sensitivity and minimize false positives, thereby overcoming the limitations of existing RNA detection methods hindered by reverse transcription and stringent reaction conditions. By engineering target-independent signal amplification circuits, our system will facilitate rapid and accurate RNA detection under simplified conditions. To ensure the practical utility and effectiveness of these molecular tests, both the equipment-free NAAT and the CRISPR/Cas13a detection methods will be validated using clinical samples from a variety of pathogens, including HPV, Influenza A and B, and SARS-CoV-2, collected by our co-investigator at a teaching hospital. The validation process will incorporate a paper-based colorimetric format to enhance usability and enable semi-quantitative interpretation. Furthermore, a computational tool employing machine learning algorithms will be utilized to refine diagnostic accuracy and interpret results, ensuring that these new technologies are prepared for real-world application and capable of addressing urgent diagnostic needs effectively. 相較於COVID-19大流行期間開發的快速抗原檢測（RATs），基於核酸的居家檢測技術雖具備高靈敏度與高特異性的顯著優勢，然其發展仍相對滯後。傳統核酸擴增檢測(NAATs）通常仰賴複雜儀器及精確溫度控制，從而限制了其可及性與實用性。為克服上述挑戰，本研究提出開發一種創新性NAAT技術，該技術可在近體溫條件下高效運作，並無需外部儀器即可提供半定量結果。此目標將透過整合經理性設計的DNA擴增動力學與基於CRISPR/Cas12的信號放大系統予以實現。本方法奠基於我們先前針對現場核酸檢測氣溶膠污染緩解之研究，從而顯著降低假陽性發生率，此對於居家檢測應用尤為關鍵。 同時，我們將針對RNA檢測之特定挑戰，建構一增強型CRISPR/Cas13a系統，並融入正反饋迴路介導的級聯反應。此新型策略旨在大幅提升靈敏度並抑制假陽性，從而超越現有RNA檢測方法受限於逆轉錄及嚴苛反應條件之侷限。透過工程化之目標獨立信號放大迴路，本系統將於簡化條件下實現迅捷且精準的RNA檢測。 為驗證該等分子檢測方法之實用性與效能，無儀器NAAT及CRISPR/Cas13a檢測系統將運用多種病原體（涵蓋HPV、A型與B型流感病毒、以及SARS-CoV-2）之臨床樣本進行驗證，樣本由本研究合作者於教學醫院蒐集。驗證程序將採用紙基比色格式，以提升使用者友好性並實現半定量分析。此外，將運用整合機器學習演算法之計算工具，精煉診斷準確率並輔助結果解讀，從而確保該等新穎技術適用於真實世界情境，並有效回應迫切診斷需求。

16304325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304325.value: 鋰離子電池超高鎳鋰鎳鈷錳氧化物穩定正極電解質界面的合理設計

16304325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304325.value: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are extensively utilized in portable electronic devices, electric vehicles, and stationary energy storage systems. A significant limitation of current LIB technology is the restricted energy density, primarily due to the low capacity and energy density of cathode materials employed. Ultra-high nickel layered cathode materials, such as LiNixCoyMn1-x-yO2 (NCM) (x ≥ 0.85), exhibit high theoretical capacities (~ 280 mAh g-1), high working voltage (≥ 4.3 V vs Li+/Li) and excellent rate performance. However, the intrinsic physicochemical instability associated with increased Ni contents in NCM results in rapid performance degradation and safety concerns, particularly under extreme conditions such as high voltage and fast charging/discharging cycles. This performance decline can be attributed to micro-cracks formation, irreversible phase transformations, transition metal dissolution, and other issues. Existing strategies, such as doping, surface coating, and electrolyte modification, have not fully addressed these issues. This project aims to design robust cathode electrolyte interfaces (CEIs) on ultra-high Ni NCM cathode materials (Ni90 and Ni85) by strategically incorporating organic components alongside rigid inorganic phases, drawing inspiration from the natural flexible dermal carapace. The innovative CEI structure will be developed through the careful tailoring of electrolyte compositions, modification of separators, and controlled current density during the CEI formation process. The newly developed robust CEIs are expected to mitigate transition metal dissolution, suppress undesirable side reactions, and enhance the structural and thermal stability of ultra-high Ni NCM cathode materials. With the implementation of these protective CEIs, we aim to achieve record-setting long-term cycling performance, with capacity retention exceeding 95% after 500 cycles for Ni85 and 85% after 1000 cycles for Ni90. The outcomes of this project are poised to significantly impact electrolyte design and the application of ultra-high Ni cathodes in the next generation LIBs. 鋰離子電池 (LIB) 廣泛應用於便攜式電子設備、電動車和固定式儲能系統。目前LIB受限於能量密度，這主要是由於所使用正極材料的容量和能量密度較低。超高鎳層狀正極材料，例如 LiNixCoyMn1-x-yO2 (NCM) (x ≥ 0.85)，具有高理論容量（約 280 mAh g-1）、高工作電壓（≥ 4.3 V vs Li+/Li）和優異的倍率性能。然而，NCM 中 Ni 含量增加所帶來的固有物理化學不穩定性會導致性能快速下降並引發安全隱患，尤其是在高壓和快速充放電循環等極端條件下。性能下降的原因可歸因於微裂紋的形成、不可逆相變、過渡金屬溶解等問題。現有的摻雜、表面塗層和電解質改質等策略尚未完全解決這些問題。本項目旨在從天然柔性真皮甲殼中汲取靈感，透過策略性地將有機組分與剛性無機相結合，設計出在超高鎳NCM正極材料（Ni90和Ni85）上堅固的正極電解質界面（CEI）。新開發的CEI有望緩解過渡金屬溶解，抑制不良副反應，並增強超高鎳NCM正極材料的結構和熱穩定性。我們的目標是實現創紀錄的長循環性能，Ni85在500次循環後的容量保持率超過95%，Ni90在1000次循環後的容量保持率超過85%。本項目的成果將對電解液設計和超高鎳正極在下一代鋰離子電池中的應用產生重大影響。

16304625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304625.value: 平方根晶体与格罗腾迪克正性

16304625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304625.value: Crystals in the context of this proposal are special kinds of directed graphs, meaning collections of vertices connected by oriented edges. Each vertex in a crystal has a weight, and adding these weights together gives a polynomial called the character. For certain classes of normal crystals, the character is always a sum of special symmetric polynomials, given by Schur functions in type A and by related functions in other types. Identifying normal crystal structures on sets of discrete objects is a useful tool for proving nontrivial symmetry and positivity properties of generating functions. A theory of normal crystals exists for each finite-dimensional Lie superalgebra. The construction of these crystals is closely related to crystal bases for representations of an associated quantum group. This proposal considers a new family objects called square root crystals, which are related to crystals in the following way. The square of a directed graph is obtained replacing the set of edges with the set of directed paths of length two. A square root crystal, informally, is a directed graph whose square is an ordinary crystal. At present, square root crystals have only been formally defined for the general linear Lie algebra and the queer Lie superalgebra. One objective of this proposal is to explore the open problem of relating these definitions to representation theory and extending them to other types. Just in the cases available, square root crystals are of interest because their characters conjecturally have remarkable positivity properties. As with ordinary crystals, one can identify a special class of normal square root crystals. The characters of these objects appear to always be sums of polynomials called symmetric Grothendieck functions. Another major goal of the proposal is to prove that this phenomenon holds in general. Symmetric Grothendieck functions are well-known in the literature for providing geometric invariants of spaces called Schubert varieties. Our character positivity conjecture would make square root crystals a useful method for establishing Grothendieck positivity of generating functions. Such positivity is often of interest, but frequently can only be derived by nontrivial methods. A third goal of the proposal is to identify natural examples of square root crystals. Our main current examples are limited to certain kinds of set-valued tableaux, but a variety of other constructions are expected to exist. This will lead to new proofs of known Grothendieck positivity results, and to proofs of other still conjectural formulas. 在本提案中，晶体指的是一类特殊的有向图，即由带方向的边连接顶点构成的集合。每个晶体顶点都具有权重，将这些权重相加可得到一个称为特征的多项式。对于某些标准晶体类而言，其特征总是表现为特殊对称多项式之和——在A型中由Schur函数给出，在其他类型中则由相关函数表示。在离散对象集合上识别标准晶体结构，是证明生成函数非平凡对称性与正性性质的重要工具。 每种有限维李超代数都存在相应的标准晶体理论。这些晶体的构造与关联量子群表示的晶体基密切相关。本提案研究了一类称为平方根晶体的新型对象，其与普通晶体的关联方式如下：有向图的平方是通过将所有边替换为长度为二的有向路径得到的；非严格地说，平方根晶体即其平方图构成普通晶体的有向图。 目前，平方根晶体仅在一般线性李代数和奇异李超代数中被正式定义。本提案的目标之一，是探索如何将这些定义与表示理论相联系并推广至其他类型的开放性问题。仅就现有案例而言，平方根晶体的特征多项式据推测具有显著的正性性质，这使其具有重要研究价值。 与普通晶体类似，我们可以识别出一类特殊的标准平方根晶体。这类对象的特征似乎总是表现为对称Grothendieck函数的多项式之和。本提案的另一核心目标，是证明这一现象具有普适性。对称Grothendieck函数因提供Schubert簇空间的几何不变量而闻名学界。我们的特征正性猜想将使平方根晶体成为证明生成函数Grothendieck正性的有效方法——这种正性虽常受关注，却往往需通过复杂手段才能获得。 提案的第三个目标是寻找平方根晶体的自然实例。当前主要例证局限于某些集值表格，但预期存在更多样的构造方式。这将为已知的Grothendieck正性结果提供新证明，并验证其他尚属猜想的公式。

16305025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305025.value: Coccolithophores are unicellular, photosynthetic, and calcifying phytoplankton that are very abundant in the marine environment. They contribute up to 10% of primary production and 50% of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) production in the modern ocean. They also form a major component of Cretaceous limestone deposits, and therefore, they play an important role in the global carbon cycle over earth history. Although different environmental conditions, such as temperature, light, and pH, have been shown to have significant impacts on the growth and calcification processes of Emiliania huxleyi, a ubiquitous coccolithophore, the relative importance of different environmental factors that control the distribution of the diverse community of coccolithophores in the modern ocean remains unclear. Our previous study suggested that copper (Cu) concentrations may play an important role in controlling the distribution of E. huxleyi in the global ocean, but it is not clear whether Cu is crucial for other coccolithophores, which are known to be diverse in their morphology, molecular compliments, and physiology. A mechanistic understanding of the Cu requirements of coccolithophores has not yet been achieved. The impact of Cu on the calcification processes of coccolithophores has never been investigated. Therefore, we propose to investigate the potential roles of Cu in coccolithophores, including its impacts on their growth, photosynthesis, and calcification. Environmental data suggest that Cu is critical and the proposed study will help to determine whether Cu is truly one of the driving mechanisms that control the distribution of coccolithophores in the modern ocean. The results will help to clarify the driving mechanisms that control the production of coccolithophores in the ocean, with major implications for global oceanic CaCO3 production and oceanic carbon-export activity. 顆石藻是單細胞的浮游植物，在海洋環境中分布廣泛。它們對現代海洋的初級生產力貢獻高達10%，對碳酸鈣（CaCO3）生產的貢獻約佔50%。顆石藻也是白堊紀石灰岩沉積物的主要成分，因此在地球歷史上的全球碳循環中扮演著重要角色。雖然不同的環境條件，如溫度、光照和pH值，已被證明對海洋中普遍存在的顆石藻Emiliania huxleyi的生長和礦化過程有顯著影響，但現代海洋中顆石藻種群多樣，各種不同顆石藻分布受何種環境因素的主要調控過程仍不清楚。我們之前的研究表明，銅（Cu）濃度可能在控制E. huxleyi在全球海洋中的分布中扮演重要角色，但尚不清楚銅對其他顆石的影響，這些顆石藻在形態學、分子組成和生理上都具有多樣性。對顆石藻銅需求的機制研究尚不充分。銅對顆石藻礦化過程的影響也從未被研究。因此，我們將研究銅對顆石藻中的潛在影響，包括其對生長、光合作用和礦化的影響。此次研究將有助於確定銅是否是控制現代海洋中顆石藻分布的驅動機制之一。研究結果將有助於澄清控制海洋中顆石藻生產的驅動機制，對全球海洋的CaCO3生產和海洋碳輸出活動具有重要意義。

16305125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305125.value: Gromov-Witten理論和 Landau-Ginzburg模型的數值不變量

16305125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305125.value: Calabi-Yau manifolds X are the geometric objects studied intensively by mathematicians and physicists. The study of numerical invariants on X, such as Gromov-Witten invariants of X, has been one of the most active research activities in the last thirty years. Even though there is a huge amount of research this area, majority of which concentrate on semi-simple case (not the case of CY), or local CY case (not compact), the answers to several key conjectures in GW theory allude mathematicians for a long time until we developed a new method, which solved all these key conjectures. The new method for CY quintic hyper-surface in four dimensional projective space involves several key steps and change of viewpoints. The first step is to reformulate the definition of GW invariants using the P-field theory. The second step is to define the Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten invariants via the P-field theory. With these changes of viewpoints, the setup for GW invariants and that of FJRW can be related by a big master space via a geometric invariant theoretic quotient . P-field theory on this master space provides some moduli spaces. The theory, called mixed-spin-p-fields (MSP for short), was developed by Chang, Guo, J. Li, Liu and the PI. The computations on these moduli spaces are miraculously effective and used by Chang, Guo and J. Li to solve several key conjectures for the CY quintic. It is not straight forward to extend the method to other CY three-folds. Recently, working with collaborators, we found a way to extend the MSP method to complete intersections in GIT. This includes a large class of CY manifolds, which are complete intersections of toric varieties. The success of this method depends upon two things. One is the right geometric setup of some moduli spaces. In our case, it is the MSP moduli space. The other is the computation aspect, which is highly technical. In the study of GW invariants, we take in FJRW invariants in the MSP theory. In fact, our MSP platform can also be used to study FJRW invariants alone. In this project, we will use our newly found setup to study GW invariants of a large classes of CY three-folds. These studies should provide results similar to those famous conjectures on CY quintic three-folds. We will also study FJRW invariants of quintic polynomials which correspond to GW invariants of the CY quintic three-fold under Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg correspondence.

16305425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305425.value: 在未來對撞機上尋找超越標準模型的物理

16305425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305425.value: Despite humanity's remarkable scientific achievements, scientists still grapple with fundamental puzzles surrounding the elementary particles that construct the universe, such as the nature of the Higgs boson and dark matter, the generation of lepton and quark flavor structure, and the origin of neutrino mass. Over the past few decades, a variety of beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) theories of particle physics have emerged to address these profound questions. Many of them predict the widespread existence of light particles such as axion-like particles, dark photons, heavy neutral leptons, etc. Colliders stand as the most powerful instruments available to particle physicists in their quest to unravel these mysteries. Since the inception of the first collider in the 1960s, physicists have made groundbreaking discoveries, including new families of leptons and quarks, the force carriers of strong and weak interactions, and most recently, the so-called ``God Particle'' - the Higgs boson, which greatly extended the boundary of humanity's knowledge. Particle physicists are planning the construction of next-generation colliders in the coming decades. Active research and development efforts are underway for these proposed collider programs. Based on their objectives, these colliders can be broadly categorized into precision machines (e.g., electron-positron colliders) and discovery machines (e.g., high-energy hadron colliders and muon collider). To accommodate their diverse tasks, these colliders are typically designed to operate in multiple modes. The PI proposes to investigate the physical opportunities presented by these new colliders. The primary scientific goal is to develop innovative strategies tailored for these new machines and their operational modes, to search for the light BSM particles. Specifically, the PI would explore the light BSM particles through flavor-violating tau lepton and top quark decays at the Z pole and the top-quark pair threshold of the electron-positron colliders, respectively. Exotic Higgs decays at a muon collider present another avenue for the PI's exploration. These new strategies are expected to capitalize on the high-performance detectors and the clean physics environment of these machines, as well as the different physical signals and event kinematics they offer. The PI has been dedicated to advancing innovative research on physics at future colliders and contributing to the collaborative efforts of the high-energy physics community. With a strong belief in the value of his expertise and experience, the PI is confident in the successful completion of this proposed project. 儘管人類已取得卓越的科學成就，科學家們仍在努力攻克關於構成宇宙基本粒子的根本性難題 —— 例如希格斯玻色子與暗物質的本質、輕子與夸克味結構的生成機制、以及中微子質量的起源。過去數十年來，各種超越標準模型（BSM）的粒子物理理論相繼湧現，試圖解答這些深邃問題。其中許多理論預言了類軸子粒子、暗光子、重中性輕子等輕質量粒子的廣泛存在。 對撞機作為粒子物理學家探索這些謎題的最強大工具，自1960年代首台機器問世以來，已助力科學家取得多項劃時代發現：包括新發現的輕子與夸克家族、強相互作用與弱相互作用的力載體，以及近期被譽為“上帝粒子”的希格斯玻色子——這些突破極大拓展了人類認知的疆界。如今粒子物理學家正規劃在未來數十年內建造新一代對撞機，相關研發工作已如火如荼展開。根據科學目標，這些對撞機主要可分為精密型（如正負電子對撞機）與發現型（如高能強子對撞機和緲子對撞機）兩大類，且通常設計有多重運行模式以適應不同研究需求。 項目負責人擬系統研究這些新型對撞機帶來的物理機遇，核心科學目標是開發針對新型對撞機及其運行模式的創新研究策略，以探尋輕質量BSM粒子。具體而言，負責人將分別通過正負電子對撞機在Z玻色子能區和頂夸克對產生閾值處，基於τ輕子和頂夸克的味破壞衰變來探索輕質量BSM粒子；同時將利用緲子對撞機上希格斯粒子的奇異衰變開闢另一條研究路徑。這些新策略有望充分發揮對撞機高性能探測器與純淨物理環境的優勢，並利用其提供的不同物理信號與運動學特徵。 負責人長期致力於推動未來對撞機物理的前沿創新研究，積極促進高能物理學界的協同合作。基於其深厚的專業積累與研究經驗，負責人對圓滿完成本項目充滿信心。

16305625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305625.value: In this proposed research, the PI and Co-I will study the variational aspects of the Ricci flow in the context of spin geometry. In the resolution of the Poincare Conjecture, Perelman introduced several important functionals whose critical points are self-similar solutions and canonical metrics (such as Einstein and Ricci-flat metrics). These functionals are inspired by Dirac operators in spin geometry. When harmonic spinors exist, some of these Perelman's functionals can be written as the energy integral of the spinor. Inspired by this intriguing relation, some authors such as Baldauf and Ozuch unifies the Perelman's F-functional with the spinorial energy, and proved some monotonicity results along the Ricci flow on asymptotically Euclidean spaces. The PI and Co-I will further introduce a new functional that unifies the spinorial energy, Perelman's W-functional, and Baldauf-Ozuch's functional. We will investigate the monotonicity behavior along the Ricci flow on both compact and non-compact spaces, under either assumption of existence and non-existence of harmonic spinors. We will also study the relation between the existence of some special spinors (such as weighted Killing/parallel spinors), and the restricted imposed on the curvature of the manifold. It is expected that the results will be of interest to mathematicians in the field of differential geometry, and physists in the field of general relativity and string theory. 在這項擬議研究中，主席研究員和協同研究員將在旋量幾何的背景下研究里奇流的變分法方面的特性。在解決龐加萊猜想時，佩雷爾曼引入了幾個重要的泛函，其臨界點是里奇孤立子和愛因斯坦度量等。這些泛函受到旋量幾何中狄拉克算子的啟發。當調和自旋子存在時，佩雷爾曼的一些泛函可以寫成自旋子的能量積分。受這種有趣關係的啟發，一些作者如巴爾道夫和奧祖赫將佩雷爾曼的F泛函與自旋子能量統一起來，並證明了在漸近平坦空間上的一些泛函單調性結果。 主席研究員和協同研究員將進一步引入一個新的泛函，統一自旋子能量、佩雷爾曼的W泛函以及巴爾道夫-奧祖赫泛函。我們將研究在緊緻和非緊緻空間上，分別在假設調和自旋子存在和不存在的情況下，這些泛函沿著里奇流的單調性行為。我們還將研究一些特殊自旋子的存在性與對流形曲率所施加限制之間的關係。 預期這些結果將對微分幾何領域的數學家，以及廣義相對論和弦理論領域的物理學家具有重要意義。

16305925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305925.value: 針對二維過渡金屬硫族化物納米片的活性位點識別與定向工程及其在含硝酸鹽的電化學還原反應中的應用

16305925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305925.value: Renewable electricity–driven nitrate (NO3−)-involving electrochemical reduction reactions offer a sustainable approach for synthesizing various nitrogenous compounds, such as ammonia (NH3), amines, and amides, with applications across diverse sectors. Despite considerable efforts to develop highly efficient catalysts, a critical question remains: “What is the nature of the active site under the working conditions responsible for the observed catalytic activity?” This challenge arises from the structural complexity of catalysts and the difficulties in probing their active sites. It is conventionally believed that metal elements tend to be reduced under negative overpotentials. However, the situation is likely more complex, considering the interactions between the catalyst surface and various physical and chemical factors. The presence of NO3− complicates this further, because it can act as both a coordination ligand to metal ions and an oxidizing agent. Unfortunately, the structural evolution of catalysts during NO3−-involving reduction reactions is extremely underexplored, which limits our understanding of the reaction mechanisms and, more importantly, hinders the rational design of better catalysts. To address these problems, the proposed project will employ two-dimensional (2D) transition metal chalcogenide (TMC) nanosheets as a platform to identify catalytic active sites during alkaline nitrate reduction reaction (NITRR). Ex situ and operando techniques will be utilized to systematically explore the influence of key factors (e.g., metal redox chemistry, cathodic potential, and adsorbents like NO3−, H2O, and OH−) on the changes in the valence state, chemical composition, and coordination environment of TMCs. The mechanisms through which reconstructed structures enhance NITRR will be elucidated through theoretical calculations. Following this, targeted structural engineering will be performed on the active sites to strengthen the factors that improve catalytic activity, based on two strategies: heteroatom metal doping and strain engineering. Finally, a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer that integrates NITRR with an optimized anodic reaction will be developed, and the oxygen evolution reaction will be replaced with organic molecule oxidation reactions while employing TMCs as bifunctional catalysts to enhance the overall efficiency. The success of the proposed project will inspire deeper investigations into the true structure–activity relationships necessary for the targeted design of effective electrocatalysts in different reactions.

16306425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306425.value: 暴胀新物理的自展法研究

16306425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306425.value: What happened at the beginning of everything? The quest to answer this ultimate question may provide important clues about the fundamental laws of nature. Cosmic inflation, the leading paradigm of the early Universe, serves as a natural laboratory with extremely high energy, where new phenomena in the microscopic world can be tested through cosmic-scale observations. With exciting advances in cosmology and theoretical physics, we are now at the point where we can gain a precise understanding of the physics of inflation, and furthermore, have our theories tested with increasingly amount of data from observations. Consequently, this progress relies on interdisciplinary exchanges with other sub-areas of physics. The proposed project will therefore explore intriguing links among primordial cosmology, formal theories of high energy physics, and astronomical observations. On the theory frontier, significant developments have recently been made by incorporating new ideas and techniques of high energy physics into primordial cosmology. One trending topic is the cosmological bootstrap, which directly focuses on observables on the future boundary of inflationary spacetime and seeks to build a “timeless description” for the origin of the Universe. At the practical level, these theoretical advances provide powerful and systematic computational tools for decoding signatures of inflationary new physics in a model-independent way. Ultimately, this will lead to a complete set of predictions on cosmological correlators, serving as important targets of upcoming observations. Furthermore, considering the appreciable volume of new data expected in the near future, we may truly be able to hunt for these relic signals from the very beginning. Centred on the fundamental physics of the primordial Universe, the proposed project will take advantage of cutting-edge developments in both theory and observations. I will apply the bootstrap approach to carve out the theory space of cosmic inflation, and in particular identify detectable effects of various types of new physics. The expected research output will be: 1) a full menu of testable predictions of cosmological correlators with distinctive signatures of new physics; and 2) a comprehensive data analysis of primordial signals in the latest observations and updated forecasts for future surveys. With promising implications for both theory and observations, my results will bridge the gap between the two, and open up new lines of research for further exploration. 一切的开端发生了什么？ 探寻这一终极问题的答案，可能为我们理解自然界的基本规律提供重要线索。作为宇宙起源的主流理论，暴胀（cosmic inflation）本身就是一个能量极高的天然实验室，在此可以通过宇宙尺度的观测来检验微观世界的新现象。随着宇宙学和理论物理学领域激动人心的进展，我们现在已能够精确理解暴胀时期的物理过程，并进一步利用日益增多的观测数据来检验我们的理论。因此，这一进展有赖于物理学其他分支领域的跨学科交流。本项目将由此探索原初宇宙学、高能物理的形式理论以及天文观测之间引人入胜的联系。 在理论前沿，通过将高能物理学的新思想和技术引入原初宇宙学，近期已取得了重大进展。一个前沿热点是宇宙学自展法（cosmological bootstrap），它直接关注暴胀时空未来边界上的可观测量，并试图为宇宙起源构建一种“无时间描述”（timeless description）。在实际层面，这些理论进展为以模型无关的方式解码暴胀新物理的信号，提供了强大而系统的计算工具。最终，这将带来关于宇宙学关联函数（cosmological correlators）的一整套完整预言，成为未来观测的重要目标。此外，考虑到在不久的将来预期会有海量的新数据，我们或许真能捕捉到来自宇宙开端的这些遗迹信号。 本项目以原初宇宙的基本物理为核心，将充分利用理论和观测两方面的前沿进展。我将应用自展法来勾勒宇宙暴胀的理论空间，特别是识别各类新物理的可探测效应。预期的研究成果包括：1）一份完整的、包含新物理显著特征的可检验的宇宙学关联函数预言清单；2）对最新观测中原初信号的全面数据分析，以及对未来巡天观测的更新预测。这些成果对理论和观测均具有深远意义，将弥合两者之间的鸿沟，并为未来的探索开辟新的研究方向。

16306525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306525.value: Cyclic peptides are a relatively new area in which pharmaceutical companies worldwide are increasingly investing, offering an innovative alternative to small-molecule drugs. Cyclic peptides possess unique characteristics not found in small-molecule drugs or linear peptides: (1) Their cyclic structure enhances resistance to degradation by endopeptidases, leading to increased stability and longer half-lives, thus enhancing their pharmaceutical potential. (2) As exemplified by antibiotics like vancomycin and immunosuppressants such as cyclosporin, cyclic peptides often exhibit higher rigidity than linear peptides, resulting in much high receptor affinity and potent activity in small doses. (3) The amino acid residues forming the core structure of cyclic peptides can be freely modified in chemical synthesis to include any desired amino acids, including non-proteinogenic types, allowing for the efficient synthesis of diverse cyclic peptides with various functions from a single core structure. Against this backdrop, this research project aims to develop a synthetic methodology for spirocyclic peptides, a novel type of cyclic peptide that has yet to be chemically synthesized. Using this methodology, we will also devise a practical supply method for microvionin and its related natural products, which are effective against multidrug-resistant MRSA, a pathogen resistant to most conventional antibiotics. However, controlling the topology of cyclic peptides remains a formidable challenge, despite advances in chemistry and the many synthesis methods established for them. Notably, peptides such as spirocyclic and lasso peptides, which feature distinctive three-dimensional topologies not seen in typical cyclic peptides, lack established synthetic methods, and no chemical synthesis examples have been documented. This research seeks to establish general synthetic methodologies for spirocyclic peptides. The plan involves the stereoselective synthesis of labionin derivatives that include the central carbon of a spiro ring, forming the common core of spirocyclic peptides such as microvionin, goadvionins, nocavionin, noursin, and labyrinthopeptin A2. Specifically, we will leverage thiourea-catalyzed aziridine opening followed by electrochemical decarboxylative olefination to stereoselectively synthesize the common framework of spirocyclic peptides, which includes α-tertiary amine and aminovinyl cysteine structures. Subsequently, we will establish a practical supply method for microvionin and its related natural products that are effective against multidrug-resistant MRSA. By doing so, this research endeavors to generalize the previously challenging synthesis methods for spirocyclic peptides, expanding the possibilities for new medium-sized drug modalities. Furthermore, by generalizing the method for synthesizing spirocyclic peptides through topology control, significant applications in the medical field are anticipated. 环状肽是一个相对较新的领域，全球制药公司正日益加大投资力度，将其作为小分子药物的创新替代方案。环状肽具有小分子药物或线性肽所不具备的独特特性：(1) 它们的环状结构增强了对内肽酶降解的抵抗力，从而提高了稳定性和延长了半衰期，增强了其药物潜力。(2) 以抗生素如万古霉素和免疫抑制剂如环孢素为例，环状肽通常比线性肽具有更高的刚性，从而在小剂量下表现出更强的受体亲和力和显著活性。(3) 构成环状肽核心结构的氨基酸残基在化学合成中可以自由修饰，可引入任何所需的氨基酸，包括非蛋白源性类型，使得从单一核心结构高效合成具有多种功能的多样化环状肽成为可能。 在此背景下，本研究项目旨在开发螺环肽的合成方法学，这是一种尚未被化学合成的新型环状肽。通过该方法，我们还将制定一种实用的微维霉素（microvionin）及其相关天然产物的供应方法，这些产物对多重耐药的耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌（MRSA）具有显著疗效，而该病原体对大多数传统抗生素具有抗性。 然而，尽管化学领域取得了诸多进展，并已建立多种合成方法，控制环状肽的拓扑结构仍是一项艰巨挑战。尤其是螺环肽和套索肽等具有独特三维拓扑结构的肽类，在典型环状肽中并不常见，目前尚无成熟的合成方法，也未有化学合成的文献报道。本研究旨在建立螺环肽的通用合成方法学。研究计划包括对包含螺环中心碳原子的labionin衍生物进行立体选择性合成，以构建微维霉素、goadvionins、nocavionin、noursin 和 labyrinthopeptin A2 等螺环肽的共同核心结构。 具体而言，我们将利用硫脲催化的氮杂环丙烷开环反应，随后进行电化学脱羧烯化反应，立体选择性地合成包含α-三级胺和氨基乙烯半胱氨酸结构的螺环肽通用骨架。随后，我们将建立一种实用的微维霉素及其相关天然产物的供应方法，以对抗多重耐药的MRSA。通过这一过程，本研究力图推广此前难以实现的螺环肽合成方法，拓展中等分子量药物的新可能性。此外，通过拓扑结构控制推广螺环肽的合成方法，预计将在医学领域产生重要应用。

16306825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306825.value: 针对参数化及时间依赖辐射输运方程的约化模型强化预优条件子

16306825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306825.value: Radiative transfer equation (RTE) models particles propagating through and interacting with a background medium, with applications in medical imaging, astrophysics, and nuclear engineering. Parametric RTE arises in applications such as sensitivity analysis and optical tomography. In parametric or time-dependent problems, RTE is solved repeatedly, creating a high demand for efficient numerical solvers. Preconditioners are vital in accelerating iterative solvers for RTE. Classical Synthetic Acceleration (SA) methods build preconditioners using low-order approximations of an ideal kinetic correction equation, for example, its diffusion limit in Diffusion Synthetic Acceleration (DSA). Despite their success, their effectiveness relies on the physics assumptions in the underlying low-order approximations. Moreover, they do not exploit low-rank structures across parameters or over time. Recently developed data-driven reduced order models (ROMs) for RTE have shown promise in exploiting low-rank structures associated with parametric problems, offering fast but low-fidelity approximations. However, few studies have exploited these ROMs to accelerate high-fidelity iterative solvers for RTE. To address this gap, our preliminary work enhances SA preconditioners for parametric RTE by using a ROM for the kinetic correction equation, leveraging low-rank structures across parameters. While our method achieves greater acceleration over DSA, it has some limitations. As iterations continue, ROM-based corrections may suffer from efficiency reduction. Though our method mitigates this reduction by switching to DSA, some reduction persists. This issue arises because the preconditioner dependence of the residual trajectory, which the ideal correction equation depends on, is neglected when constructing the ROM. To address this efficiency reduction and further advance ROM-enhanced preconditioners, we propose a project comprising two parts. First, to address the neglected preconditioner dependence of the residual trajectory, we will construct trajectory-aware ROMs to enhance preconditioners for steady-state parametric problems. We will also theoretically establish the relationship between the performance of the proposed preconditioner and the properties of the solution manifold. Additionally, we will improve the efficiency of ROM construction through greedy algorithms, randomization and training-set adaptation. Second, for time-dependent RTE, we will construct ROM-based initial guesses and preconditioners on-the-fly by integrating dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) into our trajectory-aware framework. This integration enables the efficient use of a discrete memory-efficient formulation that traditional projection-based methods cannot efficiently leverage. Furthermore, we will extend our approach to parametric time-dependent problems by utilizing parametric DMD. Upon its success, this research establishes the groundwork for efficient ROM-based accelerations in complex scenarios within medical imaging and applied physics, with the potential for extensions to other equations. 辐射传输方程（RTE）描述了粒子在背景介质中传播并与之相互作用的过程，其应用涵盖医学成像、天体物理和核工程等领域。参数化RTE在敏感性分析和光学CT等应用中尤为重要。在参数化或时间依赖问题中，可能需要反复迭代求解RTE，因此具有对RTE高效数值求解器的迫切需求。 预条件子在加速RTE迭代求解过程中起到核心作用。经典综合加速（SA）方法通过构建理想动力学修正方程的低阶近似（如扩散综合合成加速（DSA）中的扩散极限）来构造预子。虽然这类方法在多个应用中卓有成效，但其有效性依赖于底层低阶近似中的物理假设，且未能充分利用解流形跨参数或跨时间的低秩结构。 近期发展的数据驱动降阶模型（ROM）在挖掘参数化问题低秩结构方面展现出优势，可提供快速但低精度的近似解。然而，利用ROM加速高保真RTE迭代求解器的研究仍属空白。针对这一问题，我们的前期工作利用动理学修正方程的ROM增强了针对参数化RTE的SA预优条件子，这一方法可有效利用跨参数低秩结构。该方法虽较DSA获得显著加速，但仍存在局限性：随着迭代进行，基于ROM的修正效率可能衰减。尽管通过切换至DSA策略可缓解此现象，但效率衰减依然存在——这是因为构建ROM时忽略了理想修正方程所依赖的残差轨迹对预条件子的依赖性。 为攻克效率衰减难题并推进ROM增强型预条件子的发展，我们提出包含两个组成部分的研究计划： 首先，针对残差轨迹的预条件子依赖性被忽视的问题，我们将构建轨迹感知ROM来增强稳态参数化问题的预条件子。理论上将建立所提预条件子性能与解流形性质的关系，并通过贪婪算法、随机化及参数空间自适应等技术进一步提升ROM构建效率。 其次，对于时间依赖RTE问题，我们将动态模态分解（DMD）融入轨迹感知框架，实时构造基于ROM的初始猜测和预条件子。这种融合能高效应用传统投影方法难以利用的一种内存高效表达形式。此外，我们还计划采用参数化DMD将方法拓展至含参数的时间依赖问题。 若本研究可成功完成，将为医学成像和应用物理等复杂场景中基于ROM的高效加速奠定基础，并具备向其他方程拓展的潜力。

16307025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307025.value: 解構紅樹林系統中溶解有機物橫向輸出的命運及其對碳循環的影響

16307025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307025.value: Mangrove forests cover only 0.1% of the Earth's continental surface, but have been identified as some of the most carbon rich forests on Earth, together with other major coastal blue carbon ecosystems (salt marshes and seagrass meadows), accounting for ~ 50% of the total carbon burial in the ocean annually. Using coastal blue carbon ecosystems as carbon sinks to combat global climate change is considered an effective natural solution. Mangrove forests hold a great amount of organic carbon reservoir. While most studies are focused on vertical carbon burial within mangrove sediments, recent findings reveal that the export of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) through tidal-driven porewater exchange surpasses the flux of vertical burial, constituting a vital component of the mangrove carbon budget. This urges a comprehensive understanding both on the quantity and chemical quality of DOC during its lateral transportation. However, our understanding of the migration and transformation of dissolved organic matter (DOM), including DOC and other elements, during porewater exchange processes, along with controlling factors, remains elusive. This limitation has hampered the accurate assessment and prediction of the carbon sequestration potential of mangrove forests and their impact on the marine carbon cycle. Therefore, the study aims to investigate the Mai Po mangrove in Hong Kong as a typical case by collecting samples from sediment porewater, tidal creeks, estuaries, and major endmembers. A range of qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques, such as lignin phenols and dissolved black carbon quantification, optical spectroscopy, microbial community composition, and ultra-high resolution mass spectrometry, will be employed to analyze the composition and spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of porewater DOM. These together will help unveil the enigmatic molecular composition of DOM, as well as its transformation and transportation mechanisms. Elemental mixing models will be constructed to estimate the primary sources of porewater DOM, whereas environmental factors and source variations will be combined to elucidate the factors controlling the DOM molecular composition. Finally, by integrating lab incubation experiments with analyses of DOM composition in tidal creeks and estuaries, a comprehensive assessment of the transformation, migration, and carbon sequestration potential of exported porewater DOM in nearshore water bodies will be made. The findings of this interdisciplinary project will expand and enrich the understanding of blue carbon ecosystem carbon cycling processes and carbon sink functions, carrying significant scientific and societal value. It will also contribute to the training of undergraduate and postgraduate students in chemical oceanography, biogeochemistry, and hydrogeology. 作為地球上生產力最高的生態系統之一，紅樹林具有重要的碳封存與生態服務價值。越來越多研究揭示，經由潮汐驅動的孔隙水交換所輸出的溶解有機碳通量，其實超過其埋藏通量，成為紅樹林碳收支的關鍵組成部分。然而，目前對孔隙水交換過程中溶解有機物（DOM）遷移與轉化的認識，以及其控制因素，仍然相當有限。此一認知缺口阻礙了我們評估與預測紅樹林碳封存潛力及其對鄰近水體（如沿岸與開闊海域）生物地球化學循環的影響。 本計畫擬以香港米埔紅樹林為典型案例，採集沉積物孔隙水、潮溝、河口及主要端元樣本。透過多種定性與定量分析技術（如木質素酚類、溶解黑碳、光譜學與超高解析質譜），解析孔隙水DOM的組成與時空分佈特徵，從分子層面闡明孔隙水交換過程中DOM組成的轉化機制。我們將建立元素混合模型以估算孔隙水DOM的主要來源，並結合環境因子與來源變化，釐清DOM分子組成的控制因素。最後，整合針對性實驗室培養試驗與潮溝、河口的DOM組成，對輸出孔隙水DOM在鄰近水體中的遷移、轉化與碳封存潛力進行初步評估。此跨領域計畫將有助於培養本科生與研究生在化學海洋學、生物地球化學與水文地質學方面的專業能力。

16307325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307325.value: 降低稀疏相位恢復及其相關問題的樣本複雜度

16307325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307325.value: In the realm of science and engineering, a crucial challenge is inferring the state or structure of systems from incomplete and noisy data, particularly when the ambient space is high-dimensional and the available sampled data is limited. Many signals or models, however, exhibit low-dimensional structures, making these problems more tractable. Thus, a primary goal is to utilize low-dimensional structures to recover the underlying signal with as few samples as possible. Despite recent advancements, problems such as sparse phase retrieval still suffer from suboptimal sample complexities. This research aims to reduce sample complexity in sparse phase retrieval and similar problems by employing both convex and nonconvex optimization methods. For convex approaches, we propose reframing sparse phase retrieval using copositive and completely positive programming, and their semidefinite programming approximations. For nonconvex strategies, we intend to develop algorithms with provable guarantees, particularly for sparse principal component analysis, which is pivotal for achieving optimal sample complexity in sparse phase retrieval. We also plan to extend these techniques to tackle related challenges, including sparse principal component analysis and low-rank tensor recovery, where existing methods have not yet achieved optimal sample complexity. Successful reducing sample complexity could significantly impact fields like imaging, machine learning, and signal processing, enabling more efficient data processing and analysis with fewer resources. 在科學與工程領域，一個關鍵挑戰是如何從不完整且充滿雜訊的資料中推斷系統的狀態或結構，尤其是在環境空間高維且可用取樣資料有限的情況下。然而，許多訊號或模型都具有低維結構，這使得這些問題更易於處理。因此，主要目標是利用低維結構以盡可能少的樣本恢復底層訊號。儘管最近取得了一些進展，但諸如稀疏相位恢復之類的問題仍然受到樣本複雜度不足的困擾。本研究旨在透過結合凸和非凸優化方法來降低稀疏相位恢復及類似問題中的樣本複雜度。對於凸方法，我們提出使用共正規劃和完全正規劃及其半定規劃近似來重建稀疏相位恢復。對於非凸策略，我們計劃開發具有可證明保證的演算法，特別是針對稀疏主成分分析，這對於在稀疏相位恢復中實現最優樣本複雜度至關重要。我們也計劃擴展這些技術以應對相關挑戰，包括稀疏主成分分析和低秩張量恢復，這些領域的現有方法尚未實現最佳樣本複雜度。成功降低樣本複雜度將對成像、機器學習和訊號處理等領域產生重大影響，從而能夠以更少的資源實現更有效率的資料處理和分析。

16307525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307525.value: 剪切導致的膠體晶體-晶體相變和熔化相變

16307525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307525.value: Most crystal–crystal (c–c) transitions in metals, ceramics, and the Earth’s mantle are driven by mechanical shear. Increasing the shear force can result in the melting of crystals. However, the kinetic processes involved are challenging to observe experimentally at the microscopic scale and are poorly understood theoretically [1,2]. Colloidal crystals are soft materials, and thus, their behavior under high shear can be easily investigated. Moreover, colloids are outstanding model systems for the study of phase transitions because micrometer-sized colloidal particles can be directly visualized, and their thermal motion can be tracked via optical microscopy, even inside a crystal [3-6]. We previously obtained extensive results for thermal-induced melting and c–c transitions under quasi-equilibrium [7,8]. In the proposed study, we will extend our investigations by examining these phase transitions driven by non-equilibrium shear, as they are poorly understood. Our preliminary experiments revealed novel phenomena that warrant further investigation. We will measure in-situ kinetic transition processes under shear in thin- film colloidal crystals with single-particle resolution, which is difficult to achieve in atomic systems. We will study c–c transitions, melting, and interface migration under various shear strengths, focusing on two types of interfaces that play critical roles in material properties and phase transitions: grain boundaries between the same crystal phase and interfaces between different crystal phases. These experiments will enable us to explore important topics, such as how shear affects nucleation pathways, interfacial morphology and propagation, and whether premelting can be generalized to nonequilibrium conditions under shear. Moreover, the single-particle resolution will enable us to experimentally test novel phenomena predicted by theories or simulations [9,10] for the first time. Diameter-tunable microgel particles, with and without novel tunable long-range attraction, will be used. We will determine the effects of particle interactions, strain, defects, interfacial orientation, shear direction, and shear strength on the above behaviors. In addition, we will perform molecular dynamics simulations to verify our experimental results and quantitatively explore a broader range of parameters, which will provide critical insights into the mechanisms. Overall, this proposed project will deepen our understanding of crystal-phase transitions under shear. The findings will thus be of interest and utility to researchers in condensed-matter physics, materials science of crystals and amorphous solids, metallurgy, and related technologies. 大多數金屬、陶瓷及地幔中的晶體-晶體（c-c）轉變是由機械剪切驅動的。增加剪切力也可導致晶體熔化。然而，這些動力學過程在微觀尺度上難以通過實驗觀察，理論上也更困難[1,2]。膠體晶體作為軟物質材料，易於研究高剪切力下的行為。此外，膠體是研究相變的優秀模型系統，因為微米級的膠體粒子可直接觀測，其熱運動甚至能在晶體內部通過光學顯微鏡追蹤[3-6]。 我們先前已在準平衡狀態下對熔化及晶體-晶體轉變獲得了大量研究成果[7,8]。在本項研究中，我們將延伸探索範圍至由非平衡剪切驅動的相變行為，此領域目前仍缺乏深入理解。初步實驗中已觀察到新穎現象，值得深入研究。我們將在單粒子精度上，對薄膜膠體晶體在剪切力作用下的原位動力學轉變過程進行量測，這在原子體系中難以實現。研究將針對不同剪切強度下的晶體-晶體轉變、熔化及界面遷移現象，包括同種晶疇間的晶界與不同晶體間的界面。這些實驗將有助於探究多項課題，例如：剪切如何影響成核路徑、界面形貌與運動行為？預熔現象能否推廣至剪切下的非平衡條件？此外，單粒子精度將使我們首度能通過實驗驗證理論或模擬預測的新奇現象[9,10]。實驗將採用直徑可調的微膠體粒子（部分具備新型的可調長程吸引力），系統性研究粒子相互作用、應變、缺陷、界面取向、剪切方向與剪切強度對上述行為的影響。我們還將進行分子動力學模擬，除驗證實驗結果外，更可定量探索更廣泛的參數空間，從而為相關機制提供關鍵見解。 總體而言，這項研究計畫將深化我們對剪切作用下晶體相變的理解。相關研究成果不僅對凝聚態物理很有意義，也為晶體與非晶固體材料科學、冶金學及相關技術領域的研究者帶來實用價值與啟發。

16307825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307825.value: 軟物質固體界面的多尺度黏附力學研究

16307825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307825.value: The surface mechanics of soft solids, such as soft polymeric gels, biopolymer-based tissues, and living cells, are critical in numerous biological and industrial processes. In particular, understanding how the surfaces of soft solids respond to adhesive contacts is becoming increasingly important in many emerging engineering fields. However, owing to the compliant and multiscale nature of soft solids, our current knowledge of the adhesion responses at soft interfaces is less developed than that for rigid materials. Traditionally, the mechanical properties of solid surfaces in contact were theoretically modeled through the Johnson–Kendall–Roberts (JKR) framework, which was developed in the 1970s. This classical model successfully predicts the contact profiles by accounting for the balance between adhesion energy and bulk elasticity. However, recent research on the surface mechanics of soft materials suggests that the JKR model likely oversimplifies the adhesion process at soft interfaces, as it neglects the influence of solid capillarity. In a soft gel comprising a crosslinked network and a swelling solvent, various inherent interactions—such as bulk elastic stresses, solid interfacial tension, and internal osmotic pressure—couple across multiple spatiotemporal scales. This complex interplay among various stress factors presents significant challenges for classical contact models in accurately describing adhesion mechanics. Moreover, the resulting multiscale responses introduce experimental difficulties in the in situ characterization of adhesion profiles. To overcome these challenges, we propose an experimental investigation of the adhesion processes on soft polymeric gels. Using a high-precision nano-indenter combined with an advanced laser confocal microscope, we will study the underlying mechanisms that govern the formation and relaxation of adhesion profiles on the surfaces of soft gels. Through systematic variation of intrinsic material parameters of the soft gels, we expect to control adhesion responses across different length and time scales. Our experiments will elucidate underlying physics affecting the multiscale responses to local adhesive contacts. Additionally, we will investigate the emergence and function of contact line instabilities in regulating the mechanics of soft adhesion. Specifically, we will reveal the fundamental relationship between the inherent material length scales and the characteristic sizes of the resulting instability patterns. Overall, the expected outcomes of this project will not only deepen our understanding of the fundamental principles governing soft adhesion but will also inform the design principles of soft functional interfaces for potential engineering applications. 軟物質固體（如聚合物凝膠、生物基組織及活體細胞）的表面力學特性，在工業應用與生命過程中扮演關鍵角色。特別是在新興工程領域，深入理解軟質固體表面的黏附響應機制至關重要。然而，由於這類材料同時具備柔性與多尺度特徵，目前學界對軟界面黏附機制的認識，遠不及對剛性材料界面的理解深入。 傳統上，固體接觸表面的力學行為多以1970年代建立的Johnson-Kendall-Roberts（JKR）理論框架來解釋。此經典模型透過平衡黏附能與彈性能，可有效預測接觸形貌。然而最新研究顯示，由於未考慮固體毛細效應，JKR模型在描述軟界面黏附過程時存在顯著簡化。事實上，由交聯網絡與溶脹溶劑組成的軟凝膠系統中，體彈性應力、界面張力與滲透壓等多種相互作用，會在不同時空尺度上產生耦合效應。這種複雜的多物理機制耦合現象，使得傳統接觸理論難以準確描述軟界面的黏附力學行為，同時也為黏附形貌的原位表徵帶來技術挑戰。 本研究擬採用高精度納米壓痕技術結合先進激光共聚焦顯微鏡，系統性地探究聚合物凝膠的黏附動力學。通過精確調控凝膠的材料參數，我們將在不同時空尺度上解析黏附響應的調控機制，從而揭示其背後的物理本質。特別地，我們將重點研究黏附過程中接觸線失穩現象的產生機制，並建立材料本徵長度尺度與失穩圖案特徵尺寸之間的定量關係。這項研究不僅將深化對軟物質界面黏附機理的認識，更將為功能性軟界面的理性設計提供理論基礎。

16308225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308225.value: 鐵電向列相液晶的結構和響應的計算研究

16308225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308225.value: Liquid crystals (LCs) represent a special class of condensed-matter phases that can flow like a liquid but also exhibits solid-like long-range orientational order. Among these phases, nematic phase is the simplest and has been widely studied owing to its applications in display technology. Nematic phase exhibits apolar symmetry even if the constituent molecules are polar. Only recently, a polar version of the nematic LC, termed ferroelectric nematic LCs (FNLCs), was synthesized and characterized. FNLCs exhibit a macroscopic polarization field with a large dielectric permittivity and strong dielectric anisotropy. Additionally, recent experiments have demonstrated that FNLCs exhibit fast electric-optic response, second harmonic generation, and can generate entangled photon-pairs. Therefore, FNLCs are quickly becoming a promising new material for its applications in electric-optics, sensing, and nonlinear optics. Despite the recent excitement surrounding FNLCs, their emerging applications are currently limited by our poor understanding of the underlying physics. For instance, recent experiments have shown that the ground state of an FNLC made up of achiral molecules is a twisted structure with no preference for handedness. However, our quantitative knowledge about this chiral ground state—such as its pitch length, domain size, and domain wall structure—remains elusive. Additionally, more flexible and precise control over the FNLC structure is constrained by the available boundary conditions. Due to the polarization effect, surfaces typically exhibit strong planar anchoring for FNLCs, while homeotropic and weak-planar anchoring have yet to be realized. Furthermore, our understanding of how an FNLC responds to external fields, including electric fields and flow fluids, lacks both theoretical guidance and experimental data. Therefore, we plan to develop a continuum model to simulate the structure of FNLCs and their response to external fields. Our model will be validated by comparing it to available experimental data. We will further adopt the model to demonstrate control over FNLC structures by confining them with patterned surfaces and by dispersing neutral and charged colloidal particles. Finally, we will develop a hydrodynamic model to account for hydrodynamic effects in FNLCs, aiming to elucidate how to combine electric and flow fields to manipulate FNLCs. All simulation results will be tested in experiments conducted by our collaborator.
