As such, our proposed computational study of FNLCs will advance our quantitative understanding of their structure and response, facilitating the design of new FNLC structures for their emerging applications in photonics, nonlinear and quantum optics, colloids, sensors, and novel functional and responsive materials. 液晶（LCs）是一類特殊的凝聚態物相，它們能像液體一樣流動，同時又表現出類似固體的長程取向有序性。在這些相中，向列相是最簡單的一種，由於其在顯示技術中的應用而得到廣泛研究。即使組成分子具有極性，向列相仍表現出非極性對稱性。直到最近，一種具有極性的向列相液晶，即鐵電向列相液晶（FNLCs），才被合成並表徵。FNLCs表現出宏觀極化場，具有高介電常數和強介電各向異性。此外，最新實驗証實FNLCs具有快速光電響應、二次諧波產生特性，並能生成糾纏光子對。因此，FNLCs正迅速成為在光電學、傳感器和非線性光學等領域極具應用潛力的新型材料。 儘管FNLCs近期備受關注，但我們對其基本物理的理解的不足限制了它的新興應用。例如，最近的實驗表明，由非手性分子組成的FNLCs的基態是一種無手性偏好的螺旋結構。然而，我們對這種手性基態的定量認知，如螺距長度、疇尺寸和疇壁結構，仍不清楚。此外，現有的邊界條件限制了對FNLCs的結構的更靈活精確的控制。由於極化效應，表面通常對FNLCs表現出強平面錨定，而垂直錨定與弱平面錨定尚未實現。更重要的是，我們對FNLCs如何回應外場（包括電場和流場）的理解缺乏理論指導和實驗數據。因此，我們計劃建立連續介質模型來模擬FNLCs的結構及其對外場的響應，並通過與現有實驗數據對比來驗證模型。我們將進一步運用該模型来展示如何通過圖案化表面錨定及摻入中性/帶電膠體粒子來控制FNLCs的結構。最後，我們將開發流體力學模型來研究FNLCs的流場效應，旨在闡明如何結合電場與流場來操控FNLCs。所有模擬結果都將由合作團隊通過實驗驗證。 綜上，本項針對FNLCs的計算研究將推進我們對其結構與響應的定量理解，有助於設計新型FNLCs結構，促進其在光子學、非線性與量子光學、膠體、傳感器以及新型功能響應材料等新興領域的進一步應用。

16308325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308325.value: 基於對稱性破缺π-π堆疊構建高性能鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的抗疲勞界面

16308325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308325.value: Metal halide perovskites have emerged as promising optoelectronic semiconductor materials for the next generation of high-efficiency solar cells owing to their straightforward solution processability, cost-effective fabrication, extensive chemical tunability, broad absorption spectrum, and long carrier transport distances. A key challenge in commercializing perovskite solar cells is their low mechanical stability. In the context of daily temperature fluctuations, discrepancies in thermal expansion coefficients among operational layers of the device can lead to interface delamination, negatively impacting the long-term efficiency of solar cells. This project aims to fabricate and analyze symmetry-breaking π-π packing for fatigue-resistant interfaces, thereby developing perovskite solar cells with extended operational lifetime. Modifying the key interfaces of perovskite light-absorbing layers with specific molecules has proven to be an effective strategy for enhancing solar cell stability. Passivating molecules can significantly improve the durability of interfaces, making them resistant to water, oxygen, and light exposure. Moreover, ensuring the energy level alignment of modified interlayers and the functional layers is crucial to facilitate efficient charge transport. Nonetheless, research on the mechanical properties of perovskite interface passivating molecules remains limited. The geometric principles underlying the packing of these passivating molecules are not yet well understood, which hampers the effective balance between interface stability and charge transport. This project seeks to enhance both the durability and efficiency of perovskite solar cells through the implementation of symmetry-breaking π-π packing. The incorporation of conjugated molecules is anticipated to improve electron transport between layers via electron delocalization. Additionally, the helical arrangement of these molecules is expected to strengthen the mechanical properties of the interface. This interface will be formed by the reaction of chiral organic ammonium salts with benzene rings embedded in charge transport layers in coordination with Pb²⁺ in perovskite precursors. The project will target three key objectives: (i) investigating the influence of interfacial molecular packing geometry on mechanical stability, (ii) quantifying the impact of symmetry breaking π-π interactions on the phonon, electron transport, and chemical stability in solar cells, and (iii) developing chemical design rules to optimize interface stability and solar cell performance. The outcomes of this project will not only contribute to the development of robust, high-performance, cost-effective perovskite solar cells but will also provide valuable insights for researchers and industry experts regarding resilient interlayers in energy devices more generally. This initiative holds the potential for significant economic benefits across industries reliant on energy technologies. 金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦因其便捷的溶液合成方式、廣泛的化學可調性、寬廣的吸收光譜及優異的載流子傳輸距離，近年來備受矚目，成為新一代高效率太陽能電池之理想光電半導體材料。然而，鈣鈦礦太陽能電池在邁向商業化的過程中，仍面臨機械穩定性不足的重大挑戰。在日常溫度變化下，由於器件各功能層間熱膨脹係數不匹配，易導致界面剝離，進而影響其長期穩定性與光電效率。 本項目旨在構建具對稱性破缺的π–π堆疊界面，以實現抗疲勞的材料設計，從而延長鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的運行壽命。透過特定分子修飾鈣鈦礦光吸收層的關鍵界面，已被證實是提升器件穩定性的有效策略。這些鈍化分子能顯著增強界面的耐久性，使其具備對水氣、氧氣與光照引發之降解的抑制能力。此外，修飾層的能帶結構亦需與相鄰功能層良好對齊，以確保電荷高效傳輸。 儘管如此，現階段對鈣鈦礦界面鈍化分子之機械性質的研究仍相當有限，其分子堆疊的幾何原理亦未被充分理解，使得在界面穩定性與電荷傳輸效率之間取得最佳平衡仍具挑戰。本項目將以具對稱性破缺的π–π堆疊策略為核心，期望同時實現鈣鈦礦電池的高穩定性與高效率。共軛分子的引入可透過電子離域效應增強層間電荷傳輸，而其螺旋排列所產生之對稱性破缺結構，亦可進一步強化界面的機械性能。 此種界面將透過手性有機銨鹽與電荷傳輸層中嵌入之苯環，與鈣鈦礦前驅物中的鉛離子（Pb²⁺）進行配位反應來構築。本研究將聚焦以下三大目標：(i) 探討界面分子堆疊幾何對機械穩定性的影響；(ii) 解析π–π作用的化學性質、電子行為與機械效應；(iii) 建立可用於優化界面穩定性與電池性能的化學設計準則。 本項目不僅有望推動高性能且具長期穩定性的鈣鈦礦太陽能電池之發展，亦將為學術與產業界在設計耐久能量元件界面方面提供關鍵見解。此研究對於依賴能源技術的相關產業，亦具潛在且可觀之經濟效益。

16308425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308425.value: 基于模板介导的相工程策略实现新型二维材料与器件的片上合成

16308425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308425.value: Two-dimensional (2D) materials, consisting of atomically thin layers, have emerged as a transformative platform for exploring novel quantum properties and applications. Unlike traditional materials, 2D materials offer exceptional tunability in their electronic, optical, and magnetic properties, opening avenues for applications in next-generation quantum and electronic devices. Recent breakthroughs, such as the discovery of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene and fractional Chern insulators in twisted 2H-MoTe2, exemplify the unique possibilities these materials provide. Remarkably, neither graphene nor monolayer 2H-MoTe2 exhibit superconductivity or ferromagnetism on their own. While substantial progress has been made in synthesizing van der Waals (vdW) layered materials like graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides, a critical challenge remains in extending synthesis techniques to both vdW and non-vdW 2D materials, especially those without bulk analogs. This project seeks to systematically explore a novel, scalable approach for synthesizing 2D materials via on-chip, template-mediated phase engineering. By utilizing monolayer or few-layer templates in combination with transition metals as seed materials, this approach enables the creation of 2D materials at temperatures significantly lower than the bulk melting points of the transition metals. Through this template-based strategy, we aim to synthesize a diverse range of 2D materials exhibiting rich chemical and physical properties, including magnetic, superconducting, and topological states. This methodology provides an unprecedented pathway to synthesize 2D materials unattainable by conventional top-down approaches. A distinctive feature of this technique is the ability to use artificially engineered few-layer stacks with controlled lattice symmetries, opening up new possibilities for symmetry-tuned synthesis. Such precise control is essential for creating 2D materials with exotic magnetic and electronic properties, including skyrmions and unconventional superconductors, which hold significant promise for future spintronic applications. Our research will address fundamental questions about phase stability, tunability, synthesis conditions, and growth mechanisms for these template-synthesized 2D materials, deepening our understanding of both the synthesis process and resulting material properties. Additionally, we will develop lateral and vertical junction-type devices based on the on-chip synthesis approach to explore the interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and topological phases. Through these junction-type devices, we will investigate emergent electronic phenomena relevant to low-dimensional fundamental physics and quantum computing, potentially leading to devices with enhanced functionalities for information storage and logic applications. With expertise spanning materials synthesis, quantum transport, and device fabrication, this interdisciplinary project aspires to advance the understanding and practical development of 2D materials for quantum and electronic applications. 由原子级薄层构成的二维材料已成为探索新奇量子现象和开发前沿应用的变革型平台。相较于传统体材料，二维体系展现出独特的电子关联效应和显著增强的量子调控自由度，为下一代量子与电子器件的应用开辟了新路径。近年来，一系列突破性发现——如扭曲双层石墨烯中出现的关联绝缘态和超导性、以及扭曲2H-MoTe2中观测到的分数量子霍尔绝缘态——充分揭示了二维材料作为量子材料平台的独特优势。这些发现尤为引人注目的是，其母体材料（如本征石墨烯和单层2H-MoTe2）本身并不具备这些奇异量子特性。尽管目前范德华层状材料（如石墨烯和过渡金属二硫族化合物）的合成已取得显著进展，但将现有合成方法拓展至非范德华二维材料体系——特别是缺乏体材料对应物的新型二维晶态材料——仍存在重大科学挑战。 本项目拟开发一种创新的二维材料合成范式：基于模板诱导的相工程策略，实现新型二维材料的可控合成。该方法的突破性在于：（1）可在远低于传统金属熔点的温度下实现高质量二维晶体的生长；（2）通过模板设计调控材料的晶格对称性和堆叠构型，为对材料对称性依赖的量子态的构筑提供全新途径。这种自下而上的合成策略将突破传统机械剥离法的局限，实现传统方法难以获得的非范德华二维材料体系的可控制备。 本研究将系统探究模板介导合成二维材料的相形成机制、结构稳定性调控规律以及物性-结构关联等关键科学问题。通过设计具有特定对称性的模板结构，我们将致力于合成具有铁磁序、超导或拓扑保护边缘态的新型二维材料。基于先进的微纳加工技术，我们将构建横向异质结和垂直堆叠器件，深入研究低维体系中超导性、磁性与拓扑序的耦合效应，推动二维材料在信息存储与逻辑应用器件的发展。 本跨学科项目结合了材料合成、量子输运和器件制备等多方面专业技能手段，旨在建立"材料设计-可控合成-物性调控-器件实现"的全链条研究体系。项目的实施将推动二维量子材料的基础研究，并为下一代信息技术的突破提供创新解决方案。

16308625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308625.value: 现代商业环境中的分类方法

16308625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308625.value: In fields such as social science and finance, the need for effective categorization based on covariates has led to significant advancements in machine learning, particularly in the area of classification. This proposal aims to develop novel classifiers that address the complex challenges faced by businesses today. Our primary goal is to design innovative classifiers that effectively tackle the issues of algorithmic bias and efficiently leverage heterogeneous multiple data sources. More specifically, our first aim centers on the critical balance between maximizing algorithmic efficiency and ensuring fairness in decision-making. We propose a model-based classifier that effectively manages the type I error while incorporating fairness considerations grounded in equal opportunity principles. Additionally, we will provide theoretical insights into the oracle behavior of the type II error, addressing a significant gap in the existing literature and warranting that our approach is both practical and equitable. The second aim explores multi-task learning within a multi-class linear discriminant analysis framework, leveraging knowledge transfer across related tasks to enhance predictive accuracy across diverse contexts. By analyzing relationships among different classes, we aim to derive classifiers that accommodate heterogeneous task similarities. This approach allows us to exploit shared information among tasks, improving overall model performance and robustness. Furthermore, we will investigate the impact of interventions on consumer behavior by studying classifiers developed for pre- and post-intervention phases. This comprehensive approach not only advances theoretical understanding but also equips practitioners with robust tools for effective decision-making and personalized strategies, ultimately fostering improved outcomes in various commercial contexts. 在社会科学和金融等领域，基于协变量的有效分类需求推动了机器学习研究的发展。本课题旨在开发能够应对当今企业所面临复杂挑战的新型分类器。我们的主要目标是设计创新的分类器，有效解决算法公平问题，并高效利用异构多源数据。 具体来说，我们的第一个目标聚焦于在最大化算法效率与确保决策公平性之间取得关键平衡。我们提出一种基于模型的分类器，能够有效控制第一类错误，同时纳入基于“机会均等”原则的公平性考量。此外，我们将从理论上探讨第二类错误的Oracle性质，弥补现有文献中的重要空白，确保我们的方法既切实可行又公平合理。 第二个目标是在多类线性判别分析框架下探索多任务学习，利用相关任务之间的知识迁移，提升不同情境下的预测准确性。通过分析不同类别间的关系，我们旨在构建能够适应异质任务相似性的分类器。这一方法允许利用任务间的共享信息，提升模型整体表现与稳健性。 此外，我们还将通过研究干预前后的分类器，深入探讨干预措施对消费者行为的影响。这一全面的方法不仅推动理论发展，还为实践者提供强有力的工具，助力有效决策和个性化策略制定。

16308825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308825.value: 北極海冰濃度年際變率的年代際變化及其對亞洲冬季極端寒冷事件的影響

16308825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308825.value: In the context of ongoing global warming, frequent extreme cold events during winter in Asia pose significant threats to public health, ecosystems, and the economy. Previous studies indicate that the frequency of Asian winter cold extremes (AWCE) is influenced by interannual anomalies in late autumn Arctic sea ice concentration (SIC) through atmospheric circulation and the associated transport of heat and moisture. Our findings reveal that the interannual variability in late autumn Arctic SIC has become more pronounced since 2000, leading to a stronger influence of Arctic sea ice on the occurrence of AWCE over a broader area. However, a comprehensive understanding of this decadal change is lacking, limiting our predictive capabilities for AWCE. To address this gap, we propose a systematic investigation into the decadal changes in interannual variability of Arctic SIC and its impact on AWCE. This project aims to tackle the following three scientific questions: Q1: What are the major changes in the interannual variability of Arctic SIC and its impact on AWCE before and after 2000, both spatially and temporally? Q2: What are the underlying causes of the decadal changes in interannual variability of Arctic SIC, and how do these changes affect AWCE variability? Q3: How well do climate models reproduce the observed decadal changes in interannual variability of Arctic SIC, and what are the projected changes in Arctic sea ice variability and its influence on AWCE under climate change? To address these questions, we propose an integrated approach utilizing multiple observational datasets, coupled model simulations, and specially designed hypothesis-testing experiments. In Year 1, we will characterize the decadal changes in Arctic sea ice and their impact on AWCE, exploring the physical processes driving these changes by analyzing observational data to address Q1 and formulate hypotheses related to Q2. In Year 2, we will establish causal relationships through hypothesis-testing experiments using the CESM2 model to fully address Q2. In Year 3, we will evaluate climate model simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) in comparison to observations to address Q3. This proposed research aims to enhance our understanding of the physical mechanisms underlying decadal changes in Arctic sea ice interannual variability and its impact on AWCE within the context of a changing climate. The project will contribute to improving seasonal predictive capabilities for AWCE, thereby facilitating better-informed decision-making for climate adaptation and sustainable development. 在全球持續暖化的背景下，亞洲冬季頻繁發生的極端寒冷事件對公共衛生、生態系統和經濟構成重大威脅。先前研究表明，亞洲冬季極寒事件（AWCE）的發生頻率受到晚秋北極海冰濃度（SIC）年際異常的影響，這些異常通過大氣環流及伴隨的熱量與水氣輸送產生作用。我們的研究發現，自2000年以來，晚秋北極海冰濃度的年際變率顯著增強，導致北極海冰對更廣泛區域內AWCE的影響力提升。然而，目前對這一年代際變化的全面認識仍顯不足，限制了我們對AWCE的預測能力。 為填補此知識缺口，本研究擬系統性探究北極海冰年際變率的年代際變化及其對AWCE的影響。本計畫旨在解決以下三個科學問題： Q1：2000年前後，北極海冰年際變率及其對AWCE影響的時空特徵發生了哪些重大變化？ Q2：北極海冰年際變率年代際變化的根本成因為何？這些變化如何影響AWCE的變異性？ Q3：氣候模式對觀測到的北極海冰年際變率年代際變化模擬效果如何？在氣候變遷背景下，北極海冰變率及其對AWCE的影響將如何演變？ 為解答這些問題，我們提出整合多種觀測資料、海氣耦合模式模擬及特製的假設驗證實驗之研究架構。第一年將通過分析觀測數據，量化北極海冰的年代際變化及其對AWCE的影響，探討驅動這些變化的物理過程，以解決Q1並形成與Q2相關的假設。第二年將利用CESM2模式進行假設驗證實驗，建立因果關係以完整解答Q2。第三年將評估第六期氣候模式比對計畫（CMIP6）的模式模擬結果與觀測的吻合度，以解決Q3。 本項研究旨在深化對氣候變遷背景下北極海冰年際變率的年代際變化及其影響AWCE的物理機制的理解。研究成果將有助提升AWCE的季節預測能力，從而為氣候調適與永續發展的決策提供更科學的依據。

16308925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308925.value: 空間轉錄組學研究中表徵細胞類型特異性空間變異基因和共表達基因的統一框架

16308925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308925.value: The rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies presents exciting opportunities to explore organ and tissue architecture. A critical aspect of maximizing these technologies is characterizing spatial expression patterns in a cell type-specific manner, particularly through the identification of cell type-specific spatially variable genes (SVGs) and spatially co-expressed genes (SCOGs). However, existing ST technologies face significant challenges: spatially varying cell type composition complicates the identification of true cell type-specific SVGs and SCOGs, while discrepancies between ST data and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data can lead to misidentification of spatial variations. Furthermore, the spatial patterns of cell type-specific gene expression remain largely unexplored, and effective statistical methods for their analysis are lacking. In this study, we propose a unified framework aimed at characterizing cell type-specific expression patterns. Our novel statistical framework, termed the Mixture of Mixed Models (MMM), excels in identifying cell type-specific SVGs by addressing cell type composition and uncertainties in identification, while also correcting for platform effects between ST and scRNA-seq data. The MMM framework decomposes cell type-specific gene expression in ST data into three components: average gene expression from scRNA-seq, spatial variations, and non-spatial variations. We have developed a robust non-parametric test to assess the statistical significance of spatial variations, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods. Building on our pilot study's success, we aim to generalize the MMM framework to identify cell type-specific SCOGs, framing this as a hypothesis testing problem to control false positives effectively. The novelty of our method lies in its probabilistic model, which adaptively distinguishes between spatial and non-spatial variations. We also address computational challenges through an approximate inference algorithm, ensuring scalability while maintaining well-calibrated type I error rates. Ultimately, our project aims to provide a reliable platform for characterizing cell type-specific spatial expression patterns in ST data, integrating statistical principles with computational insights to enhance our understanding of complex biological systems. 隨著空間轉錄組學（ST）技術的快速發展，研究器官和組織的結構變得更加可行。要充分利用這些技術，必須以細胞類型特異性的方式表徵空間表達模式，重點識別細胞類型特異性的空間變異基因（SVGs）和檢測空間共表達基因（SCOGs）。然而，當前的ST技術在這一表徵過程中面臨諸多挑戰。首先，細胞類型組成的空間變異使得識別真正的細胞類型特異性SVGs和SCOGs變得複雜，因為標記基因可能主導結果。其次，單細胞RNA測序（scRNA-seq）數據常被用作參考，但由於平台差異，ST數據與scRNA-seq之間的差異可能導致空間變異的錯誤識別。最後，細胞類型特異性基因表達的空間模式尚未得到充分探索，並且缺乏有效分析這些模式的強大統計方法。這些挑戰突顯了迫切需要創新的統計和計算方法，以充分發揮ST技術在理解生物過程和疾病機制中的潛力。 本研究提出了一個統一的框架，用於表徵細胞類型特異性表達模式，旨在識別細胞類型特異性的SVGs並檢測細胞類型特異性的SCOGs。在我們的初步研究中，開發了一種名為混合模型的混合模型（MMM）的新統計框架，該框架在識別細胞類型特異性SVGs方面表現出色。MMM框架考慮了細胞類型組成和細胞類型識別的不確定性，同時校正了ST與scRNA-seq數據之間的平台效應。在該框架中，ST數據中的細胞類型特異性基因表達被分解為三個組成部分：來自scRNA-seq數據的同一細胞類型的平均基因表達、空間變異和非空間變異。我們使用一種強健的非參數檢驗來檢驗空間變異的統計顯著性，能夠檢測多種空間模式。初步研究結果顯示，我們的方法在性能上優於現有方法。在此基礎上，我們計劃將MMM框架推廣到識別細胞類型特異性SCOGs，增強對空間表達模式的解釋能力。

16309025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309025.value: 開發一種用於跨尺度熱帶對流模擬的尺度自適應的積雲參數化方案

16309025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309025.value: With advancements in computing power, regional numerical weather prediction (NWP) and climate simulations have increasingly adopted kilometer-scale resolutions. Some modeling centers have also experimented with global atmospheric simulations at these high resolutions. While such enhancements have improved our ability to resolve finer details of weather systems, simulating convective systems at these scales remains challenging. Kilometer-scale resolutions fall within the gray zone of convection parameterization. Traditional cumulus convection parameterization schemes rely on assumptions that fail at these scales; therefore, directly applying them can reduce simulation fidelity. Conversely, simply turning off convection parameterization leads to issues in the initiation, organization, and intensity of simulated convective systems. Efforts have been made to modify conventional cumulus convection parameterizations to make them scale-aware so that as resolution is refined, their effects are gradually diminished. This strategy is beneficial in convection-permitting simulations and variable-resolution simulations that include both coarse and kilometer-scale resolutions. Nevertheless, recent work by Shi and Wang (2022) and Wang et al. (2024) suggests that in the gray zone, combining a mass-flux cumulus scheme with an effective turbulence model for horizontal mixing can enhance the simulation of tropical cyclones at kilometer-scale resolutions. This project aims to build on our previous work by developing a three-dimensional, scale-adaptive convection parameterization for gray-zone and variable-resolution simulations of convective weather systems. It will utilize the new Tiedtke scheme to parameterize mass fluxes in convection and the Reconstruction and Nonlinear Anisotropy (RNA) turbulence model for partially resolved turbulence fluxes in and around convection. Termed 'scale-adaptive,' the new scheme adjusts based not only on the grid spacing in a simulation but also on the life cycle stages of convection. At the same convection-permitting resolution, convection that cannot be fully resolved should be primarily represented with the mass-flux scheme, while mature convection that can be sufficiently resolved requires only the turbulence scheme to model subgrid-scale fluxes. We will design, test, and optimize such a scale-adaptive convection scheme using convection-permitting simulations with the Cloud Model 1 (CM1) for various cases of organized convection. Variable-resolution simulations will also be employed to test the new scheme's capability to enable high-fidelity convection simulations across scales. 隨著運算能力的提升，區域數值天氣預報（NWP）與氣候模擬已逐漸採用公里級解析度，部分模擬中心更開始嘗試在此高解析度下進行全球大氣模擬。儘管解析度的提升增進了天氣系統細部特徵的刻畫能力，但在這些尺度上模擬對流系統仍面臨挑戰——公里級解析度正處於對流參數化的灰色地帶。傳統積雲對流參數化方案依賴的假設在此尺度下失效，直接套用將降低模擬準確性；反之，若直接關閉對流參數化，則會導致模擬對流系統的觸發、組織與強度出現偏差。 近年研究已著手改造傳統積雲對流參數化方案，使其具備尺度自適應能力：當解析度精細化時，參數化作用將逐步衰減。此策略尤其適用於對流可解析模擬（convection-permitting simulations）及涵蓋粗解析度至公里級解析度的可變解析度模擬。值得注意的是，Shi and Wang (2022) 與 Wang et al. (2024) 的最新研究表明，在灰色地帶中，結合質量通量積雲方案與有效的水平混合湍流模型，能顯著提升公里級解析度下熱帶氣旋的模擬表現。 本專案將延續先前研究，開發適用於對流天氣系統灰色地帶及可變解析度模擬的三維尺度自適應對流參數化方案。方案採用新版 Tiedtke 方案參數化對流質量通量，並結合重構與非線性異向性（RNA）湍流模型，以表徵對流區內外部分可解析的湍流通量。此「尺度自適應」新方案不僅依據模擬網格間距調整，更考量對流生命週期階段：在相同對流可解析解析度下，未充分解析的對流主由質量通量方案表徵，而成熟階段可解析的對流僅需湍流方案處理次網格通量。我們將使用雲模型 CM1（Cloud Model 1），針對多類組織化對流個案進行對流可解析模擬，據此設計、測試並優化該尺度自適應對流方案，同時透過可變解析度模擬驗證新方案實現跨尺度高精度對流模擬的能力。

16309225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309225.value: 強場極限下半導體的太赫茲等離激元模式

16309225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309225.value: Plasmons result from collective oscillation of free carriers in conductive materials, for instance, metals and doped semiconductors. Under certain circumstances, they strongly couple with light and subsequently give rise to elementary excitation known as plasmon polaritons, which are present in materials at all dimensionalities. However, owing to restrictions from the dimensionality perspective, only 3D electron systems can accommodate “surface” plasmon polaritons in the most strict definition so as to obtain superb field confinement, a key figure of merit that decides field enhancement factor and the resultant nonlinear optical effects of plasmonic origin. Historically, research of nonlinear plasmonic effects focuses on the metal-based material and has mostly been in the high-frequency spectral range (near-IR and visible). The nonlinear effects at much lower frequencies (mid-IR and THz), in principle, favors semiconductors but have long been shelved, in part, due to the limited access to high-field source in the associated spectral range. The recent advent of high-field THz sources made possible the revival of the venture into the old topic of plasmonic physics in semiconductor with a nonlinear twist. Here we propose to leverage the state-of-the-art nonlinear THz and multi-THz spectroscopy for dynamic investigation and control of plasmonic modes on the way towards the strong-field limit, leading to unexplored nonlinear optical properties. Specifically, plasmonic modes in various forms, e.g., localized surface plasmon polaritons, surface plasmon-phonon polaritons and Brewster mode, will be driven by high-field THz pulses both in the perturbative and non-perturbative regimes. We therefore gain access to study nonlinear effects resulting from high-order field dependence and time dependence of response function to light, respectively. We intend to perform an exhaustive survey of regimes of distinct nonlinearities governed by the celebrated Keldysh criterion. Although focused on the ostensibly well-understood semiconductors, such endeavor will reveal its fundamental physics in the strong-field limit, bearing new opportunities for application of plasmonic-based communication, imaging and sensing devices with enhanced functionality. 等離子體激元源自於導電材料（如金屬和摻雜半導體）中自由載子的集體振盪。在某些條件下，它們與光發生強耦合，從而產生被稱為等離極化激元的元激發模式，並存在於所有維度的材料中。然而受維度限制，嚴格意義上只有三維電子系統才能支持"表面"等離極化激元，從而實現卓越的場局域效應。這一關鍵特性直接決定了場增強因子以及由此產生的基於等離激元的非線性光學效應。傳統上，非線性等離激元效應的研究聚焦於金屬材料，且主要集中在高頻光譜範圍（近紅外線與可見光波段）。相較金屬材料，半導體材料理論上更有利於在低頻波段（中紅外線與太赫茲）實現等離激元的非線性效應，卻因該波段高場強光源的匱乏長期被擱置。隨著新一代高強度太赫茲源的出現，我們得以以非線性交互作用的視角重新檢視半導體中等離激元的經典物理問題。本研究擬採用先進的非線性太赫茲與多頻太赫茲光譜技術，對等離激元模式進行動態研究與調控，以揭示其尚未被探索的非線性光學特性。具體而言，我們將透過高場強太赫茲脈衝在微擾與非微擾區域驅動多種等離激元模式，藉此分別研究由響應函數對光場的高階依賴性和時間依賴性導致的非線性效應。我們將基於著名的Keldysh判據，對各類非線性機制展開系統性研究。 儘管針對的對像是經典的半導體材料，但該研究將在強場極限下揭示其中的新物理，並為未來基於等離激元的通信、成像與感測技術的應用，開闢新機遇。

16309525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309525.value: 高熵合金鈣鈦礦奈米晶體作為量子計算的極化單光子發射器

16309525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309525.value: Quantum computing relies on the functionality of qubits, that make up the singular memory and processing units of the quantum processor. Photons can also be used as qubits, but this scheme requires a predictable emission source, known as a single photon source (SPS), that can produce a single photon without additional photons occurring within a set time period (a few microseconds). Finding materials that can reliably emit “on demand” is challenging and only a few such materials have been identified, including a few examples of colloidal quantum dots. Perovskite quantum dots have long been used for emission applications, however the conventional understanding of quantum dot emission, suggests that only small, highly confined quantum dots should give rise to properties needed for single photon emitters (SPEs). Here we propose to synthesize a new class of “large” colloidal perovskite nanocrystals (~10-20 nm) that can achieve single photon emission, but will show superior resilience to humidity and air that can cause material degradation, improved (electronic) isolation from the surrounding environment, and more precise tuning of the emission wavelength. By using the high-entropy-alloying method of producing emissive perovskite nanoparticles, we can produce superior single photon emitters that will display better overall metrics for generating photonic qubits. High entropy alloying, refers to the method of adding more than five ion types into a single nanocrystal, thus producing a highly entropic (randomly ordered) crystalline material. Furthermore, by understanding and learning how to use the high-entropy-alloying methods to improve single photon emission, we can find a generally applicable method, beyond size tuning, to improve single photon sources across a wide range of shapes and compositions. By focusing on 1D and 2D materials, we expect to produce SPEs with polarized emission, including circularly polarized emission induced by chiral ligands. This project will make use of nanocrystal synthesis and materials characterization, spectroscopy and theoretical modelling to understand the mechanism of strong single photon emission in high entropy perovskite nanocrystals, and to improve and design superior nanocrystals for quantum computing applications. 量子運算依賴量子位元的功能，量子位元構成了量子處理器的單一記憶體和處理單元。光子也可以用作量子位元，但這種方案需要一個可預測的發射源，即單光子源 (SPS)，該源可以在設定的時間段（幾微秒）內產生單一光子，且不會產生額外的光子。尋找能夠可靠地「按需」發射的材料極具挑戰性，目前僅發現了少數此類材料，包括一些膠體量子點的例子。 鈣鈦礦量子點長期以來一直用於發射應用，然而，對量子點發射的傳統理解認為，只有尺寸較小、高度受限的量子點才能產生單光子發射器 (SPE) 所需的特性。本文，我們提出合成一類新型「大型」膠體鈣鈦礦奈米晶體（約 10-20 奈米），它能夠實現單光子發射，同時對可能導致材料降解的濕度和空氣表現出卓越的耐受性，能夠更好地與周圍環境（電子）隔離，並能夠更精確地調節發射波長。透過使用高熵合金化方法製備發射性鈣鈦礦奈米粒子，我們可以製備出性能卓越的單光子發射器，使其在光子量子位元生成方面展現出更佳的整體指標。高熵合金化是指將五種以上離子添加到單一奈米晶體中，從而產生高熵（隨機排列）晶體材料的方法。此外，透過理解和學習如何使用高熵合金化方法來改善單光子發射，我們可以找到一種普遍適用的方法，超越尺寸調節，從而改善各種形狀和成分的單光子源。透過專注於一維和二維材料，我們期望製備具有偏振發射的單光子激發態（SPE），包括由手性配體誘導的圓偏振發射。本計畫將利用奈米晶體合成和材料表徵、光譜學和理論建模來理解高熵鈣鈦礦奈米晶體中強單光子發射的機制，並改進和設計用於量子計算應用的優質奈米晶體。

16309625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309625.value: 含多個雜原子的非標準碳中心之不對稱合成

16309625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309625.value: The development of chiral molecules is crucial for innovative pharmaceuticals and advanced materials. The synthesis of chiral centers with multiple heteroatoms remains challenging despite their significance in functional molecules. This project aims to address this issue by developing new catalytic methods for assembling chiral centers with two or three distinct heteroatoms, thereby expanding the chemical space available for drug discovery and materials science. Our strategy utilizes sulfoxonium ylides as versatile starting points, which differs from traditional diazo compound reactions limited to mono-heteroatom chiral centers. Our preliminary exploration supports the feasibility of this strategy, as we isolated previously underexplored sulfoxonium species containing sulfur, oxygen, or nitrogen atoms. Using these intermediates, we synthesized several diheteroatomic chiral centers with moderate enantioselectivities, and made promising progress in creating chiral centers with three distinct heteroatoms. Further optimization of these reactions could enhance the selectivity to synthetically appealing levels (currently 40-70% ee, aim for >90% ee). The project will focus on designing and synthesizing precursors and intermediates with various heteroatoms and refining the enantioselectivity control for multi-heteroatom chiral centers. We will conduct experimental and theoretical mechanistic investigations to elucidate the kinetics and thermodynamics of key intermediates, aiding in the bioinspired design and modification of chiral catalysts. These noncanonical chiral centers will be integrated into biomolecules to explore their potential applications and facilitate their practical applications in drug development. Our research group has accumulated significant expertise in several fields related to this project, including carbene chemistry (Nat. Commun. 2024, 15, 496; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, e202312793; Nat. Commun. 2022, 13, 6588), proton-shuttling catalysis (Nat. Commun. 2024, 15, 6227; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2023, 145, 12284; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202211408), and the synthesis of niche chiral centers (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024, 63, e202413102; Nat. Chem. 2024, 16, 132; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024, 63, e202409566), positioning us to tackle the challenges of the project. This study aims to contribute significantly to asymmetric catalysis by establishing a general platform for assembling multi-heteroatom chiral centers, offering access to a new chirality pool, and enabling advances across various scientific and industrial fields. 手性分子的開發對創新藥物與先進材料至關重要。含多個雜原子的手性中心雖在功能性分子中極具價值，其合成仍具高度挑戰性。本項目旨在開發新型催化方法，建構含二至三種不同雜原子的手性中心，從而擴展藥物研發與材料科學的化學空間。 我們採用含雜原子硫葉立德作為多功能起始原料，此策略與傳統重氮化合物（僅限單雜原子手性中心）形成顯著區別。我們的初步研究成功分離了含硫、氧或氮原子的硫葉立德物種，驗證了此類核心反應中間體的可行性。利用該體系，我們合成了多種含雙雜原子的手性中心（具中等對映選擇性），並在構建三雜原子手性中心取得實質進展。透過反應優化，選擇性可望提升至具合成應用價值水平（目前40-70% ee，目標＞90% ee）。 本項目重點包括：設計合成具多樣化雜原子的活潑性反應中間體，實現多雜原子手性中心之高對映選擇性控制；透過實驗與理論計算之協同機制研究，闡明關鍵中間體的動力學與熱力學行為，指導手性催化劑的仿生設計與修飾；將此非標準手性中心嵌入生物分子，探索應用潛能並推動藥物開發實用化。 研究團隊具備核心領域的深厚基礎，包括卡賓化學 (Nat. Commun. 2024, 15, 496; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, e202312793; Nat. Commun. 2022, 13, 6588)、質子梭催化 (Nat. Commun. 2024, 15, 6227; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2023, 145, 12284; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202211408) 及特殊手性中心的合成 (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024, 63, e202413102; Nat. Chem. 2024, 16, 132; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024, 63, e202409566)。本研究擬建立多雜原子手性中心通用建構平台，開拓新型手性分子庫，為不對稱催化領域提供變革性解決方案，推動跨領域科學與工業應用發展。

16309725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309725.value: 笼目金属与超导体中的强关联效应研究

16309725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309725.value: The kagome lattice is a fascinating two-dimensional crystal structure known for its unique geometric arrangement and strong magnetic frustration, which inhibits long-range antiferromagnetic order and leads to intriguing band structures. In kagome system, the geometric frustration allows electrons to form destructive interference, quenching their kinetic energy and resulting in the emergence of flat bands. Due to the quenched kinetic energy of the flat band states, even weak Coulomb interactions can become sufficiently strong to induce significant correlation effects. Exotic physical phenomena, such as fractional quantum Hall states, kinetic ferromagnetism, and Kondo physics have been observed in flat-band related kagome systems. In the present proposal, we primarily focus on the strongly correlated physics of flat-band kagome systems. The motivations of our project are twofold: First, recent experimental observations in Fe-doped kagome compounds CoSn, have revealed intriguing phases like nematic order and pseudogaps, while pressure-tuned density-wave orders have been identified in the kagome superconductor CsCr3Sb5. Despite these advancements, the physical nature and microscopic origins of these phases remain unclear. Second, the potential for tunability in kagome systems near flat band filling presents an exciting opportunity to investigate the underlying mechanisms that contribute to these emergent phases. Our research focuses on developing efficient numerical methods that integrate dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and fluctuation exchange approximation (FLEX) to study the strong correlation effects in kagome systems. We aim to explore various order parameters and their physical implications, particularly concerning nematic orders, density-wave orders, and superconducting phases. By DMFT+FLEX calculations on accurate effective low-energy models for kagome metals and superconductors, we will investigate how external pressures, interactions, and filling levels influence the electronic properties. This research will enhance our understanding of unconventional superconductivity and many-body quantum phenomena in kagome systems, ultimately contributing to the broader field of condensed matter physics. 笼目晶格是一种引人入胜的二维晶体结构，其独特的几何排布与强烈的磁阻挫效应会抑制长程反铁磁有序，并产生新奇的能带结构。在笼目体系中，几何挫折允许电子形成相消干涉，从而淬灭其动能，并导致平带的出现。由于平带态的动能被淬灭，即使较弱的库仑相互作用也会变得足够强，从而诱发显著的关联效应。在与平带相关的笼目体系中，人们已经观测到分数量子霍尔态、动力学铁磁性以及近藤物理等奇异物理现象。 在本项目中，我们主要关注平带笼目体系的强关联物理。我们的研究动机主要有两方面：首先，在铁掺杂的笼目化合物 CoSn 中，实验观测到了如向列序和赝能隙等新奇物相；而在笼目超导体 CsCr₃Sb₅ 中则发现了可通过压力调控的密度波序。这些物相的物理性质与微观起源仍不清楚。其次，笼目体系在接近平带填充时表现出显著的可调控性，为探索这些涌现物理背后的机制提供了新的机遇。 我们的研究将着重于开发高效的数值方法，将动力学平均场理论（DMFT）与涨落交换近似（FLEX）相结合，以研究笼目体系中的强关联效应。我们旨在探索笼目体系中的各种序参量及其物理效应，特别是与向列序、密度波序及超导相相关的内容。通过在笼目金属和笼目超导体的精确有效低能模型上进行 DMFT+FLEX 计算，我们将系统研究外加压力、相互作用以及填充水平对其电子性质的影响。本研究将加深我们对非常规超导性和多体量子现象在笼目体系中的理解，从而对凝聚态物理领域的发展产生重要推动作用。

16309825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309825.value: 基於階錯線缺陷結構的晶界動力學三維連續模型

16309825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309825.value: Dynamics of grain boundaries (interfaces between grains of different crystallographic orientations) plays essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors of the crystalline materials. Classical models for grain boundary dynamics are based on the motion by mean curvature. Recent experiments, atomistic simulations, and theoretical predictions have demonstrated that grain boundary dynamics is in general controlled by the underlying structures of line defects of disconnections that have both the characters of Burgers vectors (i.e. dislocations) and steps. The dislocation character leads to motion under the stress field; and as these line defects move along the grain boundaries, the step character changes the grain boundary profile, and the dislocation character generates plastic shear, all of which cannot be modeled by the classical motion by mean curvature models. Previous attempts of continuum grain boundary dynamics models focused on the two-dimensional setting in which all the disconnections are straight lines. While grain boundary networks are intrinsically three dimensional and disconnections are generally curved lines, continuum models that account for these three-dimensional microscopic mechanisms and are suitable for three dimensional simulations of grain boundary networks are still lacking. In fact, unlike in the two-dimensional setting where disconnections are points on the grain boundary curves, in three dimensions, the representation of densities of curved disconnection lines on curved grain boundaries and the associated motion, nucleation and annihilation of the curved disconnections that lead to the evolution of curved grain boundaries present major challenges in the continuum modeling. In this project, we will develop three-dimensional continuum models for grain boundary dynamics based on underlying curved disconnection structure. The density of curved disconnections of the same mode (i.e. with the same Burgers vector and step height) is represented by a dislocation density potential function defined on the curved grain boundary, whose contour lines of integer values give the locations of the curved disconnections; and the grain boundary is defined in terms of the dislocation density potential functions of different modes together with their step heights. The motion, nucleation and annihilation of the curved disconnections and the associated evolution of the curved grain boundary under various driving forces are conveniently given by the evolution of these dislocation density potential functions. Based on this continuum model, grain rotation model in three dimensions will also be developed. The obtained continuum models will provide a basis for large scale simulations of polycrystalline networks. 晶界（不同晶體取向的晶粒之間的界面）動力學在晶體材料的力學和塑性行為中起著至關重要的作用。經典的晶界動力學模型是基於平均曲率運動。最近的實驗、原子模擬和理論預測表明，晶界動力學通常受階錯線缺陷結構線缺陷的控制，這些階錯兼具伯格斯向量（即位錯）和台階的特徵。位錯特徵導致這些線缺陷在應力場下運動；當這些線缺陷沿著晶界移動時，台階特徵會改變晶界形貌，而位錯特徵會產生塑性剪切，所有這些都無法透過經典的平均曲率運動模型進行建模。之前對連續晶界動力學模型的嘗試主要集中在二維環境中，其中所有階錯都是直線。雖然晶界網絡本質上是三維的，階錯通常是曲線，但能夠解釋這些三維微觀機理並適用於晶界網絡三維模擬的連續模型仍然缺乏。 事實上，與二維環境中階錯是晶界曲線上的點不同，在三維空間中，彎曲晶界上彎曲階錯密度的表示，以及導致彎曲晶界演化的彎曲階錯的運動、成核和湮滅，對連續建模提出了重大挑戰。 在本項目中，我們將基於彎曲階錯微觀結構，建立晶界動力學的三維連續模型。用定義在彎曲晶界上的位錯密度勢函數來表示相同模式（即具有相同的柏氏向量和台階高度）的彎曲階錯的密度，其整數值等高線給出了彎曲階錯的位置；晶界則由不同模式的位錯密度勢函數及其台階高度定義。彎曲階錯的運動、成核和湮滅以及彎曲晶界在不同驅動力下的演化，可以透過這些位錯密度勢函數的演化來方便地給出。基於此連續模型，我們還將建立三維晶粒旋轉模型。所獲得的連續模型將為多晶網絡的大規模模擬奠定基礎。

16310125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16310125.value: 观察数据下的潜亚组分析

16310125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310125.value: Latent subgroups refer to the subgroups defined by unobserved latent membership and are intensively studied in the broad areas of data sciences; in particular, educational studies, where treatment effect heterogeneity often arises in the presence of many pre-treatment variables or candidate subgroups deemed latent in nature. How to analyze the latent subgroup with observational data in a valid and efficient way is a challenging question as such analysis typically relies on two inter-connected models, latent class model which relates latent subgroup memberships with item responses and outcome model which evaluates treatment effects in latent subgroups. The classical one-stage framework, which models the joint likelihood of both models simultaneously, may not be feasible with observational data when there are many potential confounders. The two-stage framework, which estimates the latent class model and evaluates subgroup effects with the estimated latent subgroup memberships, can accommodate potential confounders but may suffer from bias issues due to the potential misclassification of the latent subgroup memberships. In this proposal, we focus on the two-stage framework and aim to bridge some gaps in the existing study and application of the two-stage framework with observational data; in particular, (1) derive the maximum misclassification rate that a valid two-stage framework can tolerate; (2) develop a two-stage approach to achieve the desired misclassification rate in (1) and estimate and infer latent subgroup effects consistently and efficiently with the blessing of many/large-scale item responses and (3) correct the misclassification bias of the two-stage framework when necessary. We will consider both estimation and inference under both low-dimensional and high-dimensional setting respectively. The development of the proposed theories and methods relies on intensive study and accurate quantification of the misclassification bias in the two-stage framework, and the proposed methods are expected to have broad applications in educational studies and beyond. The ultimate goal of the proposal is to help better understand the two-stage framework and facilitate latent subgroup analysis with observational data by the development of appropriate statistical theories and methods in the two-stage framework. 潜亚组是指由不可观测的潜变量定义的亚组，这类亚组在与数据科学相关的广泛领域中得到了深入研究，尤其是在教育学中，教育政策效果的异质性往往受到多种变量的影响，或在实践中被认为是由潜变量引起的。如何高效且有效地分析观察数据中的潜亚组是一个具有挑战性的问题，因为这种分析通常依赖于两个相互关联的模型：将潜亚组类别与项目反应相关联的潜类别模型以及评估潜亚组治疗效果的结果模型。经典的一阶段框架同时对这两个模型进行建模并极大化联合似然函数，但这种框架通常不适用于有许多混杂因素的观察数据。两阶段框架则先估计潜类别模型，再利用估计的潜亚组类别评估潜亚组治疗效果，这种框架可以自然地考虑观察数据中的混杂因素，但由于潜亚组类别估计中可能存在的误分类，会面临偏差问题。在本课题中，我们旨在填补现有两阶段框架下潜亚组分析理论和应用中存在的一些空白；具体来说：(1) 推导有效两阶段框架可以容忍的最大误分类率；(2) 开发一种高效的两阶段方法，借助大规模项目反应达到(1)中的要求的误分类率并有效地估计和推断潜亚组治疗效果；(3) 在必要时纠正二阶段框架的误分类偏差。我们将同时考虑低维和高维观察数据下的估计和统计推断。我们所提出的理论和发展的方法依赖于对二阶段框架中误分类偏差的深入研究和精准量化，并将广泛的应用在教育学及其他相关领域。本课题的最终目标是通过在两阶段框架中发展新的统计理论和方法，帮助科研工作者更好地理解该框架，并促进观察数据下更高效有效的潜亚组分析。

16310225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16310225.value: 納米限域條件下C-H-O超臨界流體中化學反應的第一性原理研究

16310225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310225.value: The carbon budget near Earth’s surface is closely linked to sustainable human development, thereby attracting considerable research interest. It is essential to recognize that carbon is not confined to near-surface reservoirs; in fact, Earth's interior contains over 90% of our planet's carbon, which has important implications for carbon cycle processes in the atmosphere and biosphere. C-H-O fluids play a crucial role as carriers, facilitating the transport of substantial quantities of carbon in the deep carbon cycle. This transport significantly influences the carbon budget at Earth’s surface and has profound implications for global climate change over geological time scales. In deep Earth, C-H-O fluids are not only subjected to high pressure (HP) and high temperature (HT) conditions, but are also often confined to nanoscale environments, such as pores, grain boundaries, and fractures within Earth’s minerals. In these settings, the physical and chemical properties of the fluids can differ significantly from those of the bulk phase. However, due to experimental challenges, our understanding of C-H-O supercritical fluids under nanoconfinement is very limited, particularly at the molecular scale. In this proposal, we plan to develop and apply first-principles Markov state models based on ab initio molecular dynamics to study the chemical reactions in C-H-O supercritical fluids. In contrast to many first-principles studies that apply enhanced sampling techniques relying on predefined reaction coordinates or collective variables, this method automatically identifies reaction coordinates and parallel kinetic pathways involving multiple intermediates through unsupervised machine learning approaches, eliminating reliance on human speculation regarding reaction mechanisms. This makes it particularly well-suited for studying C-H-O fluids under extreme conditions and nanoconfinement, where our existing knowledge of chemistry is very limited. We plan to investigate the reaction kinetic network of nanoconfined C-H-O supercritical fluids at pressures of 10–14 GPa and temperatures between 1000 and 1400 K. Our focus will be on both graphene and silicate nanoconfinement. We aim to identify new reaction intermediates, products, and pathways resulting from extreme confinement. Additionally, we will calculate the Raman spectra of these significant intermediates and products to inform future experimental studies. This proposed research will enhance our understanding of carbon speciation in Earth’s interior and contribute to our knowledge of the deep carbon cycle. 地表附近的碳收支與人類可持續發展密切相關，因而備受研究關注。必須認識到碳不僅存在於地表儲層——事實上，地球內部蘊藏著全球90%以上的碳，這對大氣與生物圈的碳循環過程具有重要影響。碳-氫-氧流體作為關鍵的碳載體，在深層碳循環中輸送大量碳元素，顯著影響地表碳收支，並對地質時間尺度下的全球氣候變化產生深遠影響。在地球深處，碳-氫-氧流體不僅處於高壓高溫環境，更常被限制於礦物孔隙、晶界、裂縫等納米尺度空間中。在此類限域環境下，流體的物理化學性質可能與宏觀態存在顯著差異。然而受限於實驗技術，目前對納米限域碳-氫-氧超臨界流體的認知仍非常有限，尤其在分子層面上。 本項目擬發展並應用第一性原理馬可夫狀態模型研究碳-氫-氧超臨界流體的化學反應。有別於多數依賴預設反應坐標或集體變量的增強採樣第一性原理研究，該方法通過無監督機器學習自動識別反應坐標與涉及多重中間體的平行反應路徑，無需人為推測反應機制，特別適用於化學認知極度缺乏的極端條件與納米限域體系。 我們將系統研究10-14 GPa壓力、1000-1400 K溫度下，石墨烯與硅酸鹽雙重納米限域環境中碳氫氧超臨界流體的反應動力學網絡，重點揭示極端限域效應誘導的新反應中間體、產物及路徑，並計算關鍵中間體與產物的拉曼光譜以指導未來實驗觀測。本研究將深化對地球內部含碳分子形成的理解，為深層碳循環研究提供新見解。

16310425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16310425.value: 異質水環境中浮游動物溶解有機物的化學多樣性和產生

16310425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310425.value: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) represents the largest reservoir of organic material in the ocean and plays a crucial role in the global carbon cycle, serving as the primary energy source for microbial heterotrophs. While existing studies have documented significant DOM release by zooplankton through mechanisms such as grazing, excretion, and fecal pellet production, the detailed chemical composition and bioavailability of DOM, as well as the mechanisms influencing its production in heterogeneous environments, remain inadequately explored. This proposed project aims to investigate the relationship between zooplankton-derived DOM chemodiversity, bioavailability, and the underlying physiological responses of zooplankton, utilizing a heterogeneous estuarine-coastal region as the study system alongside controlled laboratory microcosm experiments. We will analyze the optical and molecular characteristics of DOM released by zooplankton in the Pearl River Estuary, employing advanced techniques such as Absorbance Fluorescence Spectroscopy and Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry. This analysis will reveal the chemical diversity and bioavailability of zooplankton-released DOM and its relationship with heterogeneous environmental conditions. Additionally, we will investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms by analyzing gene expression levels in zooplankton and correlating these patterns with the properties of the DOM they produce. This approach will enhance our understanding of how physiological responses in zooplankton shape the characteristics of DOM. Furthermore, we will validate the role of key environmental parameters in influencing zooplankton physiological responses and DOM release through laboratory microcosm experiments. The outcomes of this research will elucidate the complex interplay between biodiversity and physiological processes in shaping DOM chemodiversity and bioavailability within heterogeneous estuarine-coastal ecosystems. By examining how the diversity of zooplankton communities and their metabolic activities influence the composition of DOM, we aim to clarify their relationships with carbon and nutrient cycles. As zooplankton-derived DOM is a vital component of the marine microbial loop, understanding its dynamics is essential for deciphering the intricate interactions governing carbon sequestration and nutrient cycling in oceanic systems. This knowledge will not only advance scientific understanding but also inform broader ecological models, emphasizing the critical role of organismal physiological processes in sustaining ecosystem functions and services, particularly in regulating the carbon cycle in the context of environmental dynamics and predicted climate change. 溶解有機物（DOM）是海洋中有機物質最大的儲存庫，並在全球碳循環中扮演著關鍵角色，作為微生物異營生物的主要能量來源。雖然現有研究已記錄浮游動物通過如攝食、排泄和糞便顆粒產生等機制釋放出顯著的DOM，但其詳細的化學組成和生物可利用性，以及影響其在異質環境中產生的機制，仍然未得到充分探討。本提案旨在研究浮游動物衍生的DOM化學多樣性、生物可利用性與浮游動物的潛在生理反應之間的關係，並利用異質的河口-沿海區域作為研究系統，結合控制的實驗室微生態系統實驗。 我們將分析珠江口浮游動物釋放的DOM的光學和分子特徵，採用先進技術，如吸收螢光光譜法和傅立葉變換離子回旋共振質譜法。這一分析將揭示浮游動物釋放的DOM的化學多樣性和生物可利用性及其與異質環境條件之間的關係。此外，我們將通過分析浮游動物的基因表達水平來研究潛在的分子機制，並將這些模式與它們產生的DOM的特性進行相關性分析。這種方法將增進我們對浮游動物的生理反應如何塑造DOM特徵的理解。 此外，我們將通過實驗室微生態系統實驗驗證關鍵環境參數在影響浮游動物生理反應和DOM釋放中的作用。這項研究的結果將闡明生物多樣性與生理過程在塑造異質河口-沿海生態系統中DOM化學多樣性和生物可利用性之間的複雜相互作用。通過檢視浮游動物群落的多樣性及其代謝活動如何影響DOM的組成，我們旨在澄清它們與碳和養分循環之間的關係。由於浮游動物衍生的DOM是海洋微生物環的關鍵組成部分，理解其動態對於解釋碳封存和養分循環在海洋系統中的錯綜複雜的相互作用至關重要。這一知識不僅將促進科學理解，還將為更廣泛的生態模型提供信息，強調生物體生理過程在維持生態系統功能和服務中的關鍵角色，特別是在環境動態和預測氣候變化背景下調節碳循環的作用。

16310625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16310625.value: 拓撲半金屬的量子糾纏重整化及張量網絡描述

16310625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310625.value: Topological semimetals are examples of the recently discovered class of topological materials which exhibit unique physical properties challenging conventional understanding. In traditional chemistry, covalent and ionic compounds are considered insulating because their electrons are localized in real space—either within atomic orbitals or between atoms, whereas in metallic compounds electrons could move freely throughout the material. Topological semimetals defy these definitions. While they are conductive and cannot be characterized by fully localized electrons, they possess only a limited number of itinerant electrons and exhibit properties that significantly differ from those of conventional metals. Remarkably, the electrons on the surfaces of topological semimetals can move in ways that would be impossible if not for the topological characteristics in the bulk of the material. Quantum entanglement is a key enabler behind the unusual properties of topological materials. Yet, the highly entangled nature of electrons within these materials also complicates the modeling of their physical properties. Unlike their classical counterparts, specifying generically entangled quantum many-body states requires an exponentially large amount of data, rendering the computational resources necessary for this task beyond the capabilities of any classical supercomputer available today. The tensor-network ansatz offers a solution by proposing a specific entanglement structure to simplify the problem. Nevertheless, not all physically significant phases of matter can be adequately described using tensor networks. Topological semimetals, the focus of this study, lie beyond the reach of the current tensor-network paradigm. This project aims to develop better understanding on how to describe topological semimetals from a perspective that would be more amenable to the incorporation of electron-electron interaction. This is achieved by utilizing entanglement renormalization to derive tensor-network representation of topological semimetals. Our approach transforms entanglement from an obstacle into a valuable tool. By using entanglement as the organizing principle, our renormalization scheme systematically removes unimportant degrees of freedom to reveal the system's universal properties, and in the meantime enables a viable tensor-network description. Additionally, the project will explore the relationship between the anomalous surface and the interior of a topological semimetal. 近年新發現的拓撲材料展現出挑戰傳統理解的物理性質，而拓撲半金屬是其中之一。根據一般化學理論，絕緣體內的電子被限制在原子軌道或原子之間的共價鍵中。相對而言，金屬中的電子則可以自由地在材料中移動。然而，拓撲半金屬超越了這些經典定義。儘管它們是導電的，且其中的電子並未被有效地局限在特定位置，但它們僅擁有相對少量的流動電子，並展現出與傳統金屬顯著不同的性質。值得注意的是，拓撲半金屬表面的電子可以以傳統導電材料無法實現的移動。 量子糾纏是促成拓撲材料特殊性質的關鍵因素。然而，這些材料之中電子的高度糾纏特性也使得建立描述其物理性質的模型變得更加複雜。與經典物理系統不同，描述量子糾纏的多體狀態需要指數級的大量數據，使得完成這項任務所需的計算資源超出了當前任何電腦的能力。張量網絡假設提出了一種特定的量子糾纏結構以簡化這一問題。然而，並非所有物理上重要的物質相都能有效利用張量網絡來描述。拓撲半金屬，作為本研究的重點，正是超出當前張量網絡範式的一個重要例子。 本項目旨在通過利用量子糾纏重整化，從一個更有利於納入電子間相互作用的視角來描述拓撲半金屬。我們的方法將量子糾纏從一個障礙轉變為一個工具。通過以量子糾纏作為描述原則，我們的重整化方案系統性地去除不重要的微觀自由度，以揭示在宏觀尺度測量中該系統所呈現的普遍性質，並同時構建以張量網絡去描述拓撲半金屬的框架。此外，本項目還將探索拓撲半金屬的異常表面態與其內部電子態之間的關係。

16310925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310925.value: Tilings appear in many natural structures such as honeycombs, crystals, and molecular structures. This has inspired many man-made engineering structures. Tiling is also an integral part of human civilization. It is, for example, an essential part of Islamic art and is also a recurring theme in the paintings of M. C. Escher. Tiling is also an ancient and fruitful subject of mathematical research, going as far back as the Platonic solids of the antique Greek era. Among the major mathematical achievements are the solution to Hilbert’s 18th problem, the classification of wallpaper groups and crystallographic groups, the classification of isohedral tilings of the plane. More recent notable achievements are the classification of convex pentagons that can tile the plane, and the complete classification of tilings of the sphere by regular polygons. Another major achievement is our just completed classification of edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent polygons, which was first attempted 100 years ago and is the most fundamental problem for spherical tiling. In this project, we will go beyond the past classification work and study more tilings in various contexts. We do not expect to get complete classifications as before. Instead, we only classify tilings for certain families. We identify important families by the hierarchical thinking. This means we organize the conditions on tilings by reduction (usually letting some distinct edges or angles to be equal) and splitting (letting equal edges or angles to become distinct). The classification of the tilings are then done for the whole family, starting from the cases that many edges or angles are equal, and then applying the splitting to get tilings that edges or angles are more distinguished. We apply the hierarchical thinking to three types of tilings: (1) Tiling of the sphere, where the starting point is tilings with not so many tiles, or combinatorial tilings, or tilings with angle combinations for few angles. (2) Tilings of hyperbolic surface of fixed genus, where the number of tilings is actually finite, and we work out the hierarchy for all the tilings. (3) Hexagons that can tile the plane, where the hexagon can be non-convex. The hierarchy is given by the system of edge and angle conditions the hexagon satisfies, the hierarchical information also answers the well known problem of Heesch numbers. 拼圖在自然中廣泛存在，比如蜂巢、晶體、分子結構等，這些自然結構也激發出許多人造的工程結構。拼圖也出現在伊斯蘭藝術和M. C. Escher的畫中，是人類文明不可分割的一部分。 拼圖的數學研究有著古老的歷史，可以追溯到古希臘的柏拉圖立體。關於拼圖的主要數學成就有希爾伯特第十八問題的解決，牆紙群和晶體群的分類，平面的isohedral拼圖的分類。最近的一些研究突破有einstein問題的解決(2023)，週期拼圖猜想的反例 (2022)，可以拼平面的五邊形的分類 (2017), 正規多邊形拼球面的分類 (2023)。另一個突破是我們剛剛完成的由全等多邊形以邊對邊拼球面分類，這個問題有整整100年的歷史，是拼球研究的最基本問題。 在此項目中，我們進一步研究在各種不同設定下的拼圖問題，並特別關注各拼圖間的聯繫。過去的研究主要集中在完全分類，這次我們不做完全分類，而只是對某些相關的拼圖進行分類。這些拼圖之間具有層級關係，即通過簡化（通常是將不同的邊或角認為相同）或繁化（通常是將相同的邊或角認為不同）將一種拼圖變為另一種拼圖。然後的分類研究從最簡化的出發，再不斷繁化，由此可以清晰看出各拼圖中的層級關係，且回答一些有意義的問題，如哪些假設對應哪些拓撲特徵，哪些設對應拼圖的存在性，等等。我們會從如下類別的拼圖開始做層級研究（1）拼球：考慮塊數較少的，或純粹組合的，或只有少量角度的；（2）拼雙曲面：考慮許多邊的多邊形拼固定虧格的曲面，從而只有有限個拼圖，我們希望列出所有拼圖及高清之間的層級關係；（3）六邊型拼平面：這裏的層級關係來自於拼圖中自然得到的邊和角的關係，且層級關係可以用來回答有名的Heesch數問題。

16311125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16311125.value: 狄拉克交錯磁體中非均勻應變導致的奇異性質

16311125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16311125.value: Prof Lei, Shiming Prof SHAO, Qiming

16311125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311125.value: By applying a sufficiently strong magnetic field to two-dimensional (2D) electron gas, one can realize the quantum Hall effect (QHE), where the magnetic field generates Landau levels (LLs) leading to quantized conductance that has great potential in low-dissipation electronic devices. However, the strong external magnetic field imposes great technical limitations, and achieving similar phenomena in much easier approaches is highly desirable. Meanwhile, the discovery of graphene has opened a new era to explore novel physics in two-dimension materials and has greatly advanced the study and understanding of Dirac physics. Due to the Dirac fermions and strong mechanical flexibility and robustness, a non-uniform strain in graphene can induce an extremely high pseudomagnetic field around hundreds of tesla and pseudo-LLs. However, the pseudomagnetic field is fundamentally different from a real one and cannot realize quantized transport as in QHE, because strain cannot break the time-reversal symmetry that forbids QHE. To realize novel properties like quantized transport arising from pseudomagnetic fields, one needs to find a feasible approach to break the time-reversal symmetry and induce Zeeman-like spin splitting. Instead of using an external magnetic field, a natural approach is to search for intrinsic magnetic materials. Based on the PI’s previous work about the C-paired spin-valley locking (CSVL), we realize that CSVL systems, where spin and valley degrees of freedoms are locked to each other due to crystal symmetry instead of the time-reversal symmetry, can fulfill these requirements. In CSVL systems, the antiferromagnetic order will break the time-reversal symmetry and large Zeeman-like spin splitting emerges through the exchange coupling. In this project, we will aim to realize the strain-induced quantized transport in real materials. We will systematically explore the effects of non-uniform strains on CSVL Dirac systems by combining group theory, tight-binding models, k⋅p analysis, first-principles calculations, and Monte Carlo simulations. We will first build realistic k⋅p and tight-binding models for the CSVL Dirac systems under a general strain, where parameters can be extracted from first-principles calculations, and then we will design suitable strains with experimental feasibility that can realize pseudo-LLs. We will also directly calculate the transport property based on realistic tight-binding models using non-equilibrium Green's function methods to verify the strain-induced quantized transport and nontrivial topology. With the successful execution of this project, we expect to understand deeper strain engineering of electronic property of CSVL Dirac systems and provide new material candidates for quantized transport. 通過對二維電子氣施加足夠強的外磁場，可實現量子霍爾效應（QHE）。該效應中磁場誘導的朗道能級（LLs）導致電導量子化，在低耗散電子器件中潛力顯著。然而強外磁場的應用存在重大技術限制，極需開發更簡易途徑實現類似物理現象。 與此同時，石墨烯的發現為二維材料中新奇物理的探索開啟新紀元，極大推進了狄拉克物理的研究認知。因其狄拉克費米子特性及優異機械柔韌性，石墨烯中的非均勻應變可誘導高達數百特斯拉的贗磁場及贗朗道能級。但贗磁場與真實磁場存在本質差異：由於應變無法破壞時間反演對稱性（該對稱性製約QHE產生），贗磁場體系無法實現QHE的量子化輸運。 欲實現贗磁場體系的量子化輸運等新物性，必須尋找可行路徑突破時間反演對稱性限制並誘導類塞曼自旋劈裂。替代外磁場的自然方案是探索本征磁性材料。基於項目負責人前期提出的晶格對稱性配對的自旋-能谷鎖定（CSVL）理論，我們認識到CSVL體系（其中自旋與能谷自由度通過晶體對稱性而非時間反演對稱性相互鎖定）可滿足這些需求——其反鐵磁序將打破時間反演對稱性，並通過交換耦合產生顯著類塞曼自旋劈裂。 本項目旨在真實材料中實現應變誘導量子化輸運。我們將結合群論、緊束縛模型、k⋅p分析、第一性原理計算與蒙特卡洛模擬，系統研究非均勻應變對CSVL狄拉克體系的影響。我們將首先構建普適應變下CSVL狄拉克體系的k⋅p與緊束縛模型（參數源於第一性原理計算），進而設計實驗可行的應變構型以實現贗朗道能級。同時我們將采用非平衡格林函數方法，基於真實緊束縛模型直接計算輸運性質，驗證應變誘導量子化輸運及非平庸拓撲特性。項目預期將深化對CSVL狄拉克體系電子性質應變調控的理解，並為量子化輸運提供新型候選材料。

16311525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16311525.value: 近海沉積物中的多聚磷酸鹽循環

16311525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311525.value: Phosphorus (P) is a common productivity-limiting nutrient in coastal oceans. The release of bioavailable P from sediments is one of the most important P sources. In contrast to the well-studied P release from sediment organic P and iron-bound P (Fe–P), the dynamic cycle of bacterial intracellular polyphosphate (polyP) has never been investigated. PolyP can respond strongly to oxygen variability, but its contribution to sediment P flux remains unquantified. The proposed work will study the sediment polyP cycle in the coastal waters around Hong Kong combining field sampling over multiple seasons with various research approaches, including geochemical analysis, molecular techniques, laboratory experiments (whole-core incubations and sediment bioreactors), and model calculations. We will decipher the fundamental polyP mechanisms, quantify the P fluxes and rates, investigate how the polyP cycle responds to environmental variability, and clarify the contributions of polyP metabolism to sediment P release, especially under seasonal hypoxia (low oxygen conditions). We aim to achieve a fundamental breakthrough in sediment P biogeochemistry and provide practical knowledge that can guide management practices for coastal ocean ecosystems. 磷是近海生態系統中常見的限制性營養元素，而沉積物中生物可利用磷的釋放是最重要的磷來源之一。相較於已充分研究的沉積物有機磷和鐵結合磷釋放機制，細菌細胞內多聚磷酸鹽的動態循環至今尚未被探明。多聚磷酸鹽對氧氣濃度變化具有高度敏感性，但其對沉積物磷通量的貢獻仍未被量化。本研究將結合香港近岸水域的多季節實地採樣與多種研究手段，包括地球化學分析、分子生物技術、實驗室模擬（全柱培養與沉積物生物反應器）及模型計算，系統探究沉積物多聚磷酸鹽循環。我們將揭示多聚磷酸鹽的關鍵作用機制、量化其磷通量與轉化速率，解析該循環如何響應環境變化，並重點闡明多聚磷酸鹽代謝對沉積物磷釋放的貢獻。此研究有望在沉積物磷生物地球化學領域取得突破性進展，並為近海生態系統管理提供科學依據。

16311625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16311625.value: 導出旗簇、層的模空間與幾何表示論

16311625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311625.value: This research proposal aims to significantly advance the PI’s existing theories on derived flag varieties and derived Hecke moduli spaces, focusing on their applications within geometric representation theory and the study of moduli spaces of sheaves. The project is structured into two parts. The first part of the proposal seeks to extend the PI’s previous theoretical frameworks involving derived flag schemes and derived Hecke moduli spaces. This extension will focus on the derived moduli spaces of complex configurations dictated by directed graphs. We will analyze the quasi-smoothness properties of these spaces, establish Serre-type vanishing theorems for forgetful morphisms, and provide detailed descriptions of these spaces within the contexts of Chow groups, K-theory, cohomology, and derived categories. This effort will enrich the mathematical tools available for studying geometric structures and enhance the theoretical underpinnings of derived algebraic geometry (DAG). The second part of the proposal will utilize these theoretical advancements to deepen our understanding of the geometric and algebraic structures underlying moduli spaces of sheaves. Initially, we will expand on the actions of the Heisenberg algebra on moduli spaces, previously studied by Nakajima and Grojnowski and later generalized by Baranovsky and Neguț. Our goal is to remove existing assumptions, extend these results across a broader range of moduli spaces, and elevate these theories to higher categorical levels. Furthermore, we will investigate the symmetries of moduli spaces during wall-crossings, focusing on establishing the representation theory of blowup formulas and extending the studies by Nakajima, Yoshioka, Koseki, and Zhao. By addressing these key areas, the research will deliver significant novel insights into the development and application of derived algebraic geometry, greatly impacting the fields of derived algebraic geometry and representation theory. The outcomes are expected to provide a new understanding of the interconnections between geometry and algebra, potentially influencing further theoretical developments and applications in mathematics and physics. 本研究計畫旨在推進項目負責人對導出旗簇與導出Hecke模空間的理論，並聚焦其於幾何表示論及層的模空間的應用。計畫分為兩部分。 第一部分將擴展現有導出旗簇與導出Hecke模空間的框架，重點研究由有向圖決定之導出模空間的結構。我們將分析其擬光滑性、建立 Serre 型消沒定理，並結合 Chow 群、K 理論、上同調與導出範疇，對這些空間給出更系統性的描述，以豐富導出代數幾何的理論工具。 第二部分將應用上述理論進展，深入探討層的模空間的幾何與代數結構。我們將推廣 Heisenberg 代數在模空間上的作用，消除既有假設，並提升至更高範疇層次。同時，將研究模空間wall-crossing過程中的對稱性，著重建立 blowup 公式的表示論，並擴展 Nakajima、Yoshioka、Koseki 與 Zhao 等人的相關工作。 本計畫預期將為導出代數幾何及表示論領域帶來新的理論視角，促進幾何與代數之間的深入聯繫，並推動相關數學與物理理論的進一步發展。

16312125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16312125.value: 研究氣相錒系金屬和錒系金屬硼團簇的電子結構和化學鍵

16312125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16312125.value: The proposed research focuses on investigating the electronic structure and chemical bonding of cryogenically-cooled actinide and actinide-boride nanoclusters using combined high-resolution photoelectron (PE) imaging and quantum chemistry calculations. Actinide boride materials, such as uranium and thorium combined with boron, are known for their unique structural, electronic, and bonding properties, with potential applications in nuclear technology, catalysis, and advanced materials. Despite their promise, actinide and actinide-boride nanoclusters remain largely unexplored due to the challenges associated with the handling of radioactive elements and the complexity of their electronic structures, particularly involving f-orbitals. This project aims to address these challenges by focusing on three key research areas: (1) Investigating the high-resolution PE spectra of U2⁻ and Th2⁻ molecules to resolve ongoing debates on actinide-actinide bonding, (2) Probing the chemical bonding in diatomic actinide boride clusters (UB⁻ and ThB⁻), (3) Studying the structure and bonding of actinide-doped boride clusters (MBn⁻, n = 3–12) to determine whether actinides behave more like transition-metals or lanthanides in bonding interactions with boron. This research will utilize a custom-built cold-ion trap PE imaging apparatus, capable of capturing high-resolution spectra with minimized thermal broadening, thus allowing for precise characterization of the clusters' electronic states and vibrational structures. Experimental data will be complemented by theoretical calculations in collaboration with experts in the field, including Prof. Zhenyang Lin (HKUST), Prof. Jun Li (Tsinghua University), and Prof. Wan-Lu Li (UCSD). The combined experimental and theoretical approach will allow for detailed analysis and comparison of the electronic structures and bonding patterns, contributing to a deeper understanding of actinide nanocluster chemistry. This study will provide critical insights into actinide bonding mechanisms and the interplay between actinide f- and d-electrons and boron’s electron-deficient bonding, which are key to understanding the chemical properties of actinide boride materials. The expected outcomes of this research will provide foundational knowledge on actinide-boron bonding, potentially leading to the discovery of novel bonding motifs and materials capable of withstanding extreme environments. This work has significant implications for theoretical chemistry, nuclear science, and material design, and could contribute to advancements in catalysis and the development of actinide-based materials for energy-related applications. 本計畫旨在結合高解析光電子成像技術與量子化學計算，研究經低溫冷卻的錒系及錒系-硼化物奈米團簇的電子結構與化學鍵特性。 錒系硼化物材料（如鈾、釷與硼的複合物）因其獨特的結構、電子及鍵結性質而備受關注，在核技術、催化及先進材料領域具有潛在應用。儘管前景廣闊，但由於放射性元素的處理難度及電子結構（尤其是f軌域相關）的複雜性，錒系及錒系-硼化物奈米團簇的研究仍相當有限。 本專案將透過三個核心研究方向解決這些挑戰： （1）研究U₂⁻與Th₂⁻分子的光電子能譜，以解決目前關於錒系-錒系鍵結的爭議； （2）探討雙原子錒系硼化物團簇（UB⁻與ThB⁻）的化學鍵特性； （3）研究錒系摻雜硼化物團簇（MBₙ⁻，n=3–12）的結構與鍵結，判斷錒系元素在與硼的鍵結作用中更接近過渡金屬還是鑭系元素。 本研究將使用自製的冷離子阱光電子成像設備，該設備能捕捉高解析能譜並最小化熱展寬，從而精確表征團簇的電子態與振動結構。實驗數據將與領域內專家的理論計算相輔相成，包括香港科技大學的林振陽教授、清華大學的李軍教授及加州大學聖地亞哥分校的李萬璐教授。這種實驗與理論相結合的方法，有助於詳細分析和比較電子結構與鍵結模式，深化對錒系奈米團簇化學的理解。本研究將揭示錒系鍵結機制，以及錒系f電子、d電子與硼的缺電子鍵結之間的相互作用——這些是理解錒系硼化物材料化學性質的關鍵。 預期研究成果將為錒系-硼鍵結提供基礎知識，可能促成新型鍵結構型與耐極端環境材料的發現。該研究對理論化學、核科學及材料設計具有重要意義，並有望推動催化領域的進步，以及用於能源相關應用的錒系基材料的研發。

16500225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16500225.value: 高端定价与有限供应及购买历史要求

16500225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500225.value: Premium pricing, also known as luxury or prestige pricing, is a strategy used by luxury brands to target high-end markets by consistently charging prices at the upper end of the scale. It is often practiced along with limited supply and purchase history requirements. The primary goal is to cultivate a positive image of quality, exclusivity, and confidence. If executed effectively, this approach can enhance profitability, foster customer loyalty, enhance the perceived value of a product, fortify a business against economic downturns, and heighten entry barriers within its industry. However, such a practice has its own set of risks and disadvantages. By concentrating on a niche market, a brand voluntarily excludes a mass market, potentially losing customers to competitors employing undercutting tactics. Moreover, it can create arbitrage opportunities, leading to the emergence of secondary resale markets that are susceptible to counterfeiting and posing threat to luxury brands. For instance, Patek Philippe was forced to discontinue a highly sought-after model due to its exorbitant price in secondary markets. This bold pricing strategy challenges the traditional competitive pricing norm as it is commonly understood that price significantly influences consumer purchasing decisions, and high prices deter customers (demand is down-ward sloping). The prevailing explanation for premium pricing in the marketing literature is that demand for luxury goods exhibits a backward-bending curve, as introduced by Hawkins (1954). This implies that demand decreases only when prices surpass a certain unspecified threshold because low prices can convey a negative image of a product. Kumcu and McClure (2015) argue that relying solely on demand-side factors is insufficient to explain the strong demand for luxury products as it overlooks supply-side elements. However, they fail to explain the soaring prices of luxury brands and overlook the role that inventory/supply plays in premium pricing practices. Despite the long history of premium pricing, there is a surprisingly limited amount of research on it in economics and marketing, and virtually none in operations management. Our aim is to discern the key factors for successful premium pricing, as well as the influence of inventory decisions and purchase history requirements. Additionally, we intend to investigate the interaction between primary and secondary markets and the impact of secondary markets on luxury brands. Some brands have heavily invested in combating secondary markets, while others have either taken no action or even embraced them by establishing their own platforms for trading second-hand luxury products. 高端定价，也称为奢侈定价或声望定价，是奢侈品牌用来针对高端市场的一种策略，其特点是始终在价格区间的上端收费。它通常与有限供应和购买历史要求相结合。其主要目标是培养产品的质量、独特性和信心的正面形象。如果执行得当，这种方法可以提高盈利能力，促进客户忠诚度，提升产品的感知价值，增强企业抵御经济衰退的能力，并提高行业内的进入壁垒。 然而，这种做法也有其自身的风险和缺点。通过专注于小众市场，品牌自愿排除大众市场，可能会因此失去客户给采用低价策略的竞争对手。此外，这可能会创造套利机会，导致二级转售市场的出现，这些市场容易受到假冒产品的影响，并对奢侈品牌构成威胁。例如，百达翡丽因二级市场的高价而被迫停产一款备受追捧的型号。 这种大胆的定价策略挑战了传统的竞争定价规范，因为通常认为价格对消费者购买决策有显著影响，而高价格则会阻碍客户购买（需求呈下降趋势）。在市场营销文献中，关于高端定价的主要解释是奢侈品的需求呈现出向后弯曲的曲线，正如霍金斯（Hawkins, 1954）所提出的。这意味着，只有当价格超过某个未指定的阈值时，需求才会减少，因为低价格可能会传达出产品的负面形象。库姆库（Kumcu）和麦克卢尔（McClure, 2015）认为，仅依赖需求侧因素不足以解释奢侈产品的强劲需求，因为这忽视了供应侧因素，如产品推广和奢侈品牌的市场力量。然而，他们未能解释奢侈品牌价格飙升的原因，并忽视了库存/供应在高端定价实践中的作用。 尽管高端定价有着悠久的历史，但在经济学和市场营销领域对此的研究却出奇地有限，在运营管理领域几乎没有相关研究。我们的目标是识别成功高端定价的关键因素，以及库存决策和购买历史要求的影响。此外，我们还打算调查主要市场与二级市场之间的互动，以及二级市场对奢侈品牌的影响。一些品牌在打击二级市场方面进行了大量投资，而另一些品牌则没有采取任何行动，甚至通过建立自己的二手奢侈品交易平台来拥抱二级市场。

16500425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500425.value: In economics, researchers often assume that individuals’ preferences satisfy a property called convexity. This means that if an individual is equally happy with two options, then she will weakly prefer any options that lie between those two options to either one of the two options. Convexity implies that as an individual possesses more of something, the extra satisfaction she obtains from each additional unit decreases. Because of this, individuals with convex preferences tend to make balanced choices instead of opting for extremes. Convexity also enables interpreting demand curves clearly and ensures market equilibrium prices exist. Researchers use convex preferences to explain individuals’ behaviors and choices under risk and uncertainty that cannot be explained by standard theories such as the expected utility theory. While economists often assume that individuals have convex preferences and choose the best options based on their preferences, there hasn’t been much research on how to test this assumption. Specifically, if we can observe the choices an individual makes in different situations, can we identify a convex preference such that the observed choices are indeed the best according to the preference? In this project, we aim to answer this question by establishing a condition based on the observed choices made by an individual. This condition will help us determine if we can support the idea of a convex preference for that individual. Our study is important both for theory and practical use. Our findings will allow researchers to analyze real-world data and test whether consumer preferences are indeed convex in various situations. Additionally, our results will provide insights into how closely consumer behavior matches the idea of optimizing some convex preference (i.e., choosing the best options under some convex preference). Ultimately, we hope to improve our understanding of real-world consumer behavior and connect theoretical concepts to practical applications. 在经济学中，研究者通常假设个人偏好满足一种称为凸性的性质。这意味着，如果一个人对两种选项的偏好无差异，那么她对这两种选项之间的任何折衷选项的偏好至少不会弱于原先的任一选项。凸性隐含的意义是：当个体拥有的某种东西越多，她从每新增一单位中获得的额外满足感会递减。因此，具有凸偏好的个体往往会做出平衡的选择，而非走向极端。 凸性还能帮助清晰解读需求曲线，并确保市场均衡价格的存在。研究者利用凸偏好来解释标准理论（如期望效用理论）无法涵盖的个体在风险和不确定性下的行为与选择。尽管经济学家常假设个体具有凸偏好并基于偏好做出最优选择，但关于如何验证这一假设的研究却很少。具体而言，如果我们能观察到个体在不同情境下做出的选择，能否从中识别出一种凸偏好，使得这些观察到的选择确实符合该偏好的最优解？ 本项目旨在通过建立基于个体观察选择的判定条件来回答这一问题。该条件将帮助我们判断能否为个体找到支持凸偏好的证据。我们的研究兼具理论和现实意义：成果将帮助研究者分析实际数据，检验消费者偏好在不同情境下是否确实满足凸性；同时，结论将揭示消费者行为在多大程度上符合“基于某种凸偏好进行优化”的假设。最终，我们希望深化对现实消费者行为的理解，并将理论概念与实际应用联系起来。

16500825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16500825.value: 以少見多：用於低劑量CT修復的基於亨氏單位引導的解剖結構解耦特徵學習方法

16500825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500825.value: Low-dose CT restoration can reduce radiation exposure while maintaining high-quality images that are essential for accurate diagnoses, which are particularly important for enabling doctors to make informed treatment decisions. However, current methods for low-dose CT restoration have shown promising results but are still limited in quality and not yet ready for clinical use due to two fundamental limitations. First, these methods do not fully leverage the rich information in CT images, particularly the differences in tissue types represented by Hounsfield Unit (HU) values. As a result, different anatomical structures are not well distinguished in the features, making effective restoration more challenging. Second, existing methods typically process the entire CT image without adequately focusing on the specific areas that are of interest to clinicians—regions that may contain signs of disease. To address the first limitation, we will introduce an innovative method called HU-Guided Anatomical Decoupled Codebook Learning to extract CT priors from clean images. Specifically, our method will learn prior distributions from the commonly used HU windows in radiology, followed by the development of anatomically decoupled features through HU-guided decoupling and interactive codebook learning. Next, we will propose a novel collective prior alignment method for low-dose CT restoration at three levels: quantized feature-level, anatomical feature-level, and pixel-level. The core innovation of this tri-level alignment facilitates a unified 'degradation-to-clean' transformation process across both feature and image domains, effectively addressing degradation issues in CT restoration. To tackle the second limitation, we note that while traditional diffusion models excel at generating realistic details, they often lack consistency with clean CT images. Therefore, we will propose a novel region-attentive hybrid diffusion model for CT detail enhancement. Finally, we will conduct a comprehensive evaluation that encompasses two key aspects: (i) a large-scale, multi-center abdominal CT assessment covering various degradation scenarios, and (ii) quantitative image quality measurements alongside clinically focused qualitative analyses. Through these efforts, we aim to significantly advance low-dose CT restoration, facilitating accurate diagnoses while minimizing radiation exposure. Our preliminary experiments have already demonstrated the advantages of HU anatomical priors and decoupled codebook learning compared to traditional codebook learning. Our team has extensive research experience in CT-based restoration and has published in high-quality journals and conferences. This project is expected to significantly impact academic research by inspiring follow-up work, including further studies on local detail enhancement for CT restoration, CT to contrast-enhanced CT translation and multi-phase CT registration. 低劑量CT重建技術能夠在降低輻射劑量的同時提供高質量圖像，對於精準診斷尤為重要，這一能力可以有效輔助醫生作出科學的治療決策。然而，目前的低劑量CT重建方法雖然取得了一定進展，但仍然存在質量上的局限，距離實際臨床應用尚有差距。這主要源於以下兩個根本性問題： 首先，現有方法未能充分挖掘CT圖像中蘊含的豐富信息，尤其是亨氏單位（Hounsfield Unit, HU）值所反映的不同組織類型差異。因此，不同的解剖結構在提取的特徵中未得到有效區分，這為重建帶來了額外的挑戰。其次，當前方法大多對整幅CT圖像進行統一處理，而未能有針對性地聚焦於臨床醫生感興趣的特定區域，例如可能包含疾病跡象的部位。 為了解決上述第一個問題，我們提出了一種創新性方法，稱為基於HU引導的解剖結構解耦編碼本學習，用於從高質量圖像中提取CT先驗知識。具體來說，該方法從放射學中常見的HU窗口中學習先驗分佈，並通過HU引導的解耦結合交互式編碼本學習，生成解剖結構解耦特徵。此外，我們還設計了一種新穎的多層次集體先驗對齊方法，專門用於低劑量CT重建。通過在量化特徵層級、解剖特徵層級和像素層級進行對齊，該方法能夠在特徵域和圖像域中實現統一的「退化到清晰」轉換，從而有效應對CT圖像退化問題。 針對第二個問題，我們發現傳統的擴散模型雖然在生成逼真細節方面表現出色，但通常缺乏與高質量CT圖像的一致性。為此，我們提出了一種新穎的區域注意混合擴散模型，用於進一步增強CT圖像細節。最後，我們將對所提出的方法進行全面評估，重點包含以下兩個方面：（1）覆蓋多種低劑量場景的大規模、多中心腹部CT數據集驗證；（2）結合定量圖像質量測量和以臨床任務為導向的定性分析，全面評估實際效果。 通過這些創新，我們旨在顯著提升低劑量CT重建的技術水準，實現降低輻射劑量與精準診斷的雙重目標。初步實驗結果表明，與傳統編碼本學習方法相比，基於HU的解剖先驗與解剖結構解耦編碼本學習在性能上表現出顯著優勢。我們的團隊在CT重建研究領域積累了豐富經驗，並在高水準期刊和會議上發表了相關成果。我們相信，此項目不僅能在學術上產生重要影響，還將激發後續研究，例如CT局部細節增強、CT到對比增強CT的轉換以及多相CT配準等領域的進一步探索。

16500925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16500925.value: 演算法決策中的程式公正：概念擴展與實證證據

16500925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500925.value: Algorithmic decision-making (ADM) is increasingly used in organizations. Management knowledge to date, developed in the context of human decision-making (HDM), may require updating in the realm of ADM. One area of research that necessitates updating is procedural justice—the fairness of the process or procedure for decision-making (Colquitt, 2001; Leventhal, 1980). Existing research in the HDM arena has conceptualized and supported procedural justice as comprising covarying dimensions that reflect one single latent construct (Colquitt, 2001). Challenging this extant conceptualization, we argue that, in the context of ADM, the procedural justice construct follows a multidimensional aggregate model comprising non-covarying dimensions that should be studied separately. Building upon Colquitt’s (2001) concept and measure of procedural justice, we propose that procedural justice within the realm of ADM is composed of non-covarying dimensions, diverging from the idea of covarying dimensions that represent a singular latent construct, as previously put forward. We then proceed to compare the impacts of ADM versus HDM on employees’ perceptions of these different dimensions of procedural justice. Specifically, we hypothesize that, compared to HDM, ADM is associated with higher levels of procedural justice perception in terms of consistency, accuracy, and objectivity, but lower levels of procedural justice perception in terms of voice, influence, and appeal. We further propose objectivity of decision tasks as a moderator for these relationships. We will conduct four studies to test these ideas. In addition, how ADM compares to HDM in the procedural justice dimension of upholding ethical and moral standards is conceptually ambiguous. Accordingly, we will undertake a qualitative effort and analysis to explore specific ethical and moral standards that individuals uphold when evaluating ADM. To conclude, we challenge the extant conceptualization of procedural justice as one latent construct, and will show that procedural justice comprises non-covarying dimensions that should be studied separately in the context of ADM. We will provide a potential explanation for mixed findings concerning ADM and procedural justice by illustrating that ADM has opposite effects on different dimensions of procedural justice. Further, employing procedural justice as an example, we will showcase how investigating a new phenomenon such as ADM can advance current conceptualizations and germane literature.
