17104425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17104425.value: 解析PGC1α介導的粒線體重編程在肝移植術後脂肪變性移植物損傷中的作用機制

17104425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104425.value: Marginal grafts have been increasingly used in liver transplantation due to the shortage of optimal liver grafts. With the high prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease, steatotic graft has become the majority of marginal graft but is associated with more severe graft dysfunction. Thus, understanding the mechanisms of steatotic graft injury will be essential for developing new strategies to minimize graft dysfunction. By combining clinical resources, liver transplant and genetically-modified animal models, we elucidated the compromised AMPKα1 in aggravating steatotic graft injury through PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction (Liu et al., Ann Surg. 2022). Although we illustrated the role of macrophage in graft injury, the association between PGC1α and macrophage polarization remains obscure. Hence, further study investigating the interplay between PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial reprogramming and macrophage within the microenvironment of steatotic graft is essential for new therapeutics development. We preliminarily observed the down-regulated PGC1α as an indicator for graft steatosis in a liver transplant cohort. Moreover, PGC1α-low expression significantly deteriorated long-term graft survival and short-term graft dysfunction. By establishing a rat liver transplantation model, we consolidated the existence of mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming featured by diminished oxidative phosphorylation and enhanced glycolysis. Additionally, the increase of PGC1αlow M1 macrophage was correlated with the down-regulated PGC1α in steatotic graft. Functionally, PGC1α inhibition promoted M1 polarization whereas PGC1α reactivation induced M2. We further demonstrated that PGC1α activation ameliorated graft steatosis, graft dysfunction, cell necrosis and portal inflammation in mouse models. Collectively, these data suggest that PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in macrophage polarization which eventually drives steatotic graft injury. However, further study exploring the molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potentials for PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming is warranted. In this project, we aim to a) investigate the clinical significance of PGC1α and macrophage polarization in steatotic graft outcomes; b) characterize the function of PGC1α in macrophage polarization regarding mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming; c) explore the therapeutic potentials of modulating PGC1α for mitigating steatotic graft injury. The elucidation of PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming for macrophage polarization will lay the ground for a comprehensive understanding steatotic graft injury mechanism. Moreover, PGC1α is a promising biomarker for early allograft dysfunction, as well as a druggable target for developing novel therapeutics against steatotic graft injury through mitochondrial metabolism modulation. 供體短缺問題使得肝移植中越來越多使用邊緣性供肝。由於代謝相關性脂肪性肝病的高發，脂肪變性供肝已成為邊緣性供肝的重要部分，但卻導致更嚴重的移植肝功能障礙。因此，深度挖掘脂肪變性移植肝損傷的機制，將對研發防治肝功能障礙的新策略極為關鍵。本團隊基於豐富的臨床資源、成熟的肝移植動物模型和轉基因模型體系，在前期研究中發現，功能下調的AMPKα1分子通過調控PGC1α介導的線粒體功能障礙，從而加重脂肪變性移植肝損傷（Liu et al., Ann Surg. 2022）。作為肝內炎症微環境的主要細胞，巨噬細胞在移植肝損傷中發揮重要的炎症調控作用，並受線粒體功能的影響。然而，關鍵分子PGC1α與肝內巨噬細胞的相關性尚未明確。因此，本研究將在脂肪變性移植物中探索PGC1α介導的線粒體重編程與巨噬細胞的互作關係及其對移植物損傷微環境的影響與機制，並探索新的治療策略。 本團隊初步數據發現，PGC1α在脂肪變性移植肝中顯著下調，且此下調表型與遠期移植物丟失率及急性期肝損傷嚴重程度呈正相關。通過建立大鼠肝移植模型，我們確證脂肪變性肝移植物微環境中存在線粒體代謝重編程，表現為氧化磷酸化下調而糖酵解增強。此外，脂肪變性移植肝中的巨噬細胞出現特異性極化表型，即移植肝微環境內低PGC1α表達導致PGC1αlow M1巨噬細胞亞群的增多。功能實驗顯示，抑制PGC1α可促進巨噬細胞向M1亞型極化，而再激活PGC1α則誘導其向M2亞型極化。我們進一步證明，外源性激活PGC1α可顯著減輕移植肝脂肪變性，緩解肝功能障礙、細胞壞死及門管區炎症反應。總之，以上數據表明，PGC1α介導的線粒體代謝重編程在巨噬細胞極化中起關鍵調控作用，並可能加重脂肪變性移植肝損傷。因此，深入探究PGC1α介導的線粒體代謝重編程的分子機制及治療策略極具必要性。 在本項目中，我們將：1）探究PGC1α和巨噬細胞極化狀態在脂肪變性移植肝不良預後中的臨床相關性；2）解析PGC1α調控巨噬細胞極化與線粒體代謝重編程的互作機制；3）探索通過調控PGC1α減輕脂肪變性移植肝損傷的治療策略。深度挖掘巨噬細胞極化過程中PGC1α介導的線粒體代謝重編程調控機制，將為全面理解脂肪變性移植肝損傷的多維度機理奠定基礎。此外，PGC1α有望成為早期移植物功能障礙的重要生物標誌物，並極具潛力成為通過線粒體代謝調控對抗脂肪變性移植肝損傷的新治療靶點。

17104625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17104625.value: 煤煙致肺癌的鐵特徵：一項線粒體基因組和鐵調控基因多態性的病例對照研究

17104625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17104625.value: Prof Chan, Michael Chi Wai Prof Cowling, Benjamin John Prof Ho, Kin-fai

17104625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104625.value: Iron is essential for life, yet an excess of iron (Fe) intake may cause cancer. Human population studies have linked iron to an increased susceptibility to colorectal, breast, esophageal, pancreatic, and lung cancers. The lungs are continuously exposed to Fe-containing particulate matter in the air, and in some occupational settings of extreme exposure, pulmonary toxicity can bear an iron signature. The mechanism for asbestos to cause lung cancer and mesothelioma is probably mediated through redox cycling of fiber-bound and bioavailable iron. The lung cancer epidemic due to indoor coal smoke in Xuan Wei, China might also bear an iron signature, supported by the unusual presence of an Fe-rich mineral in coal, coal emissions, and lung cancer tissues. The Fe-rich mineral turned out to be an interstratification of chamosite and berthierine. Berthierine (Fe-Al serpentine) is in the same mineral group with chrysotile (white asbestos). Due to their much higher content of ferrous ion, both chamosite and berthierine could be more biologically active and carcinogenic than chrysotile. Supported by animal study findings, we are tempted to recommend mitochondria-targeted iron chelation (removal) intervention to reduce lung cancer risk in this epidemic region. Yet, improved understanding of mechanisms of this Fe-rich mineral causing lung cancer development in genetically susceptible individuals is required to enhance the evidence base for an intervention experiment that targets iron. In this population-based case-control study, we aim to examine whether genetic polymorphisms in iron regulatory genes can modify the association of this Fe-rich mineral with lung cancer. We also aim to examine whether individual variability in mitochondrial genome profiles can modulate the lung cancer risk in that mitochondria are not only our power plant but also our iron foundry: the main storage and utilization sites for iron in the cell, producing iron-sulfur clusters and heme. Lastly, we aim to examine whether the gene-environment interaction patterns in this setting of coal smoke-induced lung cancer is consistent with those in the setting of lung cancer and mesothelioma caused by asbestos in that the two settings could have one shared iron signature. 家庭燃煤產生的室內排放物被歸類為“對人類致癌（1類）”，相關證據主要基於宣威地區的研究。該地區女性肺癌死亡率居中國之首。現有假設（如多環芳烴、持久性自由基和石英）無法解釋肺癌負擔的上升或地區差異，提示存在其他未被重視的致癌物。 我們的前期研究（2019年資助項目）表明，煙煤中的類石棉礦物磁綠泥石可能通過引發炎症顯著促進宣威肺癌的發生。磁綠泥石屬於蛇紋石族礦物，與公認的人類致癌物温石棉同屬一類。磁綠泥石與温石棉均含鐵元素，而鐵具有潛在致癌性。研究發現，煤中鐵含量與宣威肺癌死亡人數呈高度正相關，並在患者淋巴結組織中觀察到從磁綠泥石中析出的鐵元素。磁綠泥石含量最高的C1煤層（位於煤系最頂層）幾乎僅產自宣威來賓鎮，而此地肺癌死亡率居宣威之首。但關鍵問題是：為何在磁綠泥石暴露水平相似的環境中，部分人羣更易罹患肺癌？ 我們假設單核苷酸多態性（SNP）可調節磁綠泥石與肺癌的關聯，尤其是鐵相關基因。預實驗顯示ALAD基因多態性與宣威肺癌風險顯著相關。本研究擬擴大樣本量並擴展候選基因，旨在回答以下問題：鐵相關基因、線粒體基因、石棉相關基因及其他目標基因的多態性能否影響肺癌風險？其機制可能涉及哪些方面？我們還將重新分析既往研究中置信區間較寬的SNP，驗證其可靠性。為此，我們設計了一項匹配病例對照研究，以來賓村500對肺癌病例和對照為樣本，採用條件Logistic迴歸分析目標SNP，並探討這些SNP能否與煙煤的使用產生交互作用。通過研究這一獨特人羣中磁綠泥石暴露、遺傳變異與肺癌的相互作用，我們期望深化對磁綠泥石致癌機制的理解，併為制定治療和干預策略提供依據。

17106325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106325.value: 外泌體攜帶的STT3寡糖基轉移酶：一種通過糖基化介導化療耐藥性轉移的關鍵因子？

17106325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106325.value: Cytotoxic chemotherapy has served as the only primary therapeutic option for various malignancies, including ovarian cancer, for decades. While many patients initially respond to treatment, approximately 70% ultimately experience recurrence and develop chemoresistance, posing a significant clinical challenge. A critical factor in this treatment failure is the intratumoral heterogeneity among cancer cells, yet the distinct behaviors and interactions of different cancer cell subclones that drive chemoresistance remain poorly understood, primarily hindered by a lack of well-controlled, clinically-relevant models. Moreover, the role of exosomes—crucial mediators of intercellular communication—in chemoresistance remains largely underexplored, with unclear mechanisms regarding how they facilitate chemoresistance among different subclones. By leveraging our unique isogenic model that effectively mimics spontaneous human ovarian cancer metastasis, along with our expertise in exosomal research and glycobiology, we have made four pivotal findings that shed light on the interplay between intratumoral heterogeneity, exosomes, and glycosylation in enhancing chemoresistance. First, highly metastatic (HM) cells can confer chemoresistance to non-metastatic (NM) cells through the transfer of exosomes. Second, proteomic analysis revealed that STT3 oligosaccharyltransferases act as novel exosomal cargo that mediates this process. STT3 enzymes are essential for the initial step of protein N-glycosylation. While aberrant glycosylation is a hallmark of cancer, the roles of glycosylation enzymes in cancer-derived exosomes and their impact on chemoresistance remain largely unexplored, highlighting a new function of exosomes. Third, we demonstrate that exosomal STT3 (exo-STT3) modifies the glycosylation profile of recipient NM cells, significantly enhancing their drug efflux capabilities. Fourth, targeting exo-STT3 in vivo can improve chemosensitivity, particularly in an immunocompetent background. These exciting findings lead us to hypothesize that exo-STT3 from chemoresistant metastatic cells transfers chemoresistant properties to chemosensitive non-metastatic cells by enhancing their glycosylation-dependent drug efflux and promoting immune evasion. To test this hypothesis, we will employ glycomics, glycoproteomics, humanized and syngeneic mouse models, annotated clinical samples, and cutting-edge technology platforms to: (1) Validate the specific functional roles of exo-STT3 in the transfer of chemoresistance; (2) Dissect the regulatory mechanisms by which exo-STT3 influences the glycosylation of drug efflux transporters to mediate chemoresistance; and (3) Unravel the molecular effects of exo-STT3 on the tumor immune microenvironment and its implications for chemoresistance. Taken together, this innovative research aims to chart a new direction for understanding chemoresistance, offering valuable mechanistic insights that could inform the future design of exosome-based predictive biomarkers and therapeutic interventions to enhance chemotherapy efficacy. 細胞毒性化療是卵巢癌的主要治療手段，約70%患者會出現復發及耐藥。腫瘤細胞異質性及外泌體在此中的作用尚未明。 基於我們模擬人卵巢癌自發轉移的同源模型及本團隊在外泌體及糖生物學的研究基礎，我們提出四項核心發現：1. 高轉移性細胞透過外泌體將耐藥性傳遞給非轉移性細胞；2. 蛋白組學鑑定STT3為關鍵外泌體貨物，參與蛋白N-糖基化；3. exo-STT3可重塑NM細胞糖基化譜，顯著增強藥物外排； 4. 體內靶向exo-STT3可提高化療敏感性。 我們假設exo-STT3通過糖基化依賴途徑增強藥物外排並促進免疫逃逸，從而“傳染”耐藥特性。為驗證該假說，將整合糖組學、糖蛋白組學、人源化及同系小鼠模型、帶臨床註釋樣本及前沿技術平台，開展：1. 驗證exo-STT3在耐藥傳遞中的功能；2. 解析其調控藥物外排轉運蛋白糖基化的機制； 3. 揭示exo-STT3對腫瘤免疫微環境的分子影響及其在耐藥形成中的作用。本研究旨在開闢化療耐藥機制新方向，為基於外泌體的預測性生物標誌物及精準干預策略設計提供關鍵機理學依據，以提升化療療效。

17106425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106425.value: 探討IL-18BP作為干擾素驅動免疫治療抗藥性之肝癌關鍵免疫檢查點

17106425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106425.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most prevalent form of primary liver cancer, typically arising in a progressive sequence from inflammation induced by viral and non-viral hepatitis, advancing to cirrhosis and eventually malignant tumors. Detection of HCC often occurs at advanced stages, posing challenges for surgical intervention. Current systemic treatments for HCC primarily consist of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). ICIs have demonstrated more effective outcome and have become one of the major HCC treatments. While ICIs show promise in some HCC patients, majority of patients do not respond or develop resistance. Resistance to ICIs is attributed largely to the negative feedback immunosuppressive mechanisms triggered by T cells and other immune cells. IFNG serves as a double-edged sword in immunotherapy treatment. Following ICI therapy, IFNG is significantly upregulated in the microenvironment, primarily sourced from reinvigorated T cells. Initially, IFNG activates diverse immune subsets; however, extended exposure of IFNG also triggers the expression of immunosuppressive genes as a negative feedback mechanism to prevent immune overactivation. This dual role of IFNG contributes to ICI-mediated adaptive resistance and hinders the effectiveness of immunotherapy. Blockade of IFNG is not optimal as this would suppress the immune cells for both tumor elimination and immune evasion. Therefore, more comprehensive understanding about the specific IFNG-mediated immunosuppressive mechanisms is crucial to the development of new therapeutic strategies to overcome ICI resistance. Interestingly, our preliminary study in murine HCC model demonstrated that IFNG activates the production of a secretory and immunosuppressive protein, IL-18 Binding Protein (IL-18BP). IL-18BP is a decoy receptor which blocks IL-18 signaling through direct binding to IL-18, preventing it from binding to and activating IL-18 receptor (IL-18R) on T (or NK cells). IL-18 is a pro-inflammatory cytokine which plays a major role in stimulating and activating the T and NK cells. We found that IL-18BP is important for anti-PD-1 resistance in HCC. We hope to validate the immunosuppressive function of IL-18BP in HCC and further delve deeper into the IL-18BP-mediated epigenetic changes in immune cells leading to their exhaustion. As proof-of-concept, we will study the effects of IL-18BP antibody in improving the outcome of ICI in HCC. We will also explore whether IL-18BP expression can be employed as diagnostic marker to predict response for ICI treatment. Our work will benefit the understanding of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) resistance mechanisms in HCC. 肝細胞癌（HCC）是最常見的原發性肝癌類型，通常是由於病毒性或非病毒性肝炎引起的炎症，經過多年發展成肝硬化，最後變成惡性腫瘤。HCC往往在晚期才被發現，所以手術治療的機會比較少。目前，HCC的全身治療主要包括兩類藥物：酪胺酸激酶抑制劑（TKI）和免疫檢查點抑制劑（ICI）。其中，ICIs 的治療效果更好，已經成為主要的治療方法之一。不過，雖然有些病人對 ICIs 有反應，但大多數病人效果不理想，甚至會發展出耐藥性。ICIs 耐藥很大程度上與 T 細胞及其他免疫細胞產生的負反饋免疫抑制有關。 在免疫治療中，干擾素γ（IFNG）是一把雙刃劍。ICIs 治療後，IFNG 在腫瘤周圍大量增加，主要來自被活化的 T 細胞。一開始，IFNG 可以活化多種免疫細胞，提高免疫反應，但如果 IFNG 持續存在，也會引發一些免疫抑制基因的表達，從而抑制免疫系統過度活躍。這種雙重作用導致了 ICIs 治療的耐藥性，影響免疫治療的效果。如果單純阻斷 IFNG，又會影響免疫細胞對腫瘤的清除能力以及防止腫瘤逃避免疫系統的能力。因此，我們需要更深入了解 IFNG 具體是如何導致免疫抑制的，這對於開發新療法、克服 ICIs 耐藥非常關鍵。 有意思的是，我們在小鼠肝癌模型的初步研究中發現，IFNG 會促進一種分泌型免疫抑制蛋白 IL-18 結合蛋白（IL-18BP）的產生。IL-18BP 是一種「誘餌」受體，可以直接與 IL-18 結合，阻止 IL-18 與 T 細胞或 NK 細胞表面的受體結合和活化。IL-18 本身是一種促炎因子，能活化 T 細胞和 NK 細胞，增強免疫反應。我們發現，IL-18BP 對於 HCC 中抗 PD-1 治療的耐藥很重要。我們希望進一步驗證 IL-18BP 在 HCC 中的免疫抑制作用，並探索 IL-18BP 如何改變免疫細胞的狀態，導致它們「耗竭」失效。我們會研究 IL-18BP 抗體是否能提升 ICIs 在 HCC 中的治療效果，還會評估 IL-18BP 是否可以作為預測 ICIs 療效的生物標誌物。我們的研究有助於加深對 HCC 中免疫檢查點抑制劑耐藥機制的理解，為今後開發新療法提供依據。

17106525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106525.value: 童年社經環境對長遠健康和教育程度的影響：為期１５年的追蹤研究

17106525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17106525.value: Prof Au Yeung, Shiu Lun Ryan Dr Chan, Sherry Kit-wa Dr Fong, Daniel Prof Rao, Nirmala Dr Tung, Tsz Suen Keith Dr Wong, Rosa Sze Man Prof Yip, Paul Siu Fai
rows: Prof Au Yeung, Shiu Lun Ryan

17106525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106525.value: Background: Historically, there has been a prevailing belief that children from disadvantaged backgrounds have limited opportunities to realise their full potential compared to their wealthier peers. However, as society progresses and provides increased support resources and educational opportunities to foster children’s development regardless of their socioeconomic status (SES), many children from low-income families are able to succeed and reach their goals. Despite this trend, there is a lack of research that follows individuals from early childhood into adulthood. Longitudinal studies are crucial for generating empirical evidence that explores the diverse pathways to adult outcomes from a developmental standpoint. Objectives: The proposed study will examine the predictive power of early-life SES for adult health and educational outcomes. It will also investigate the patterns of leisure activities across childhood and adolescence and their associations with adult outcomes in different SES groups, as well as the potential moderating role of personal psychological resilience. Study Design: The study will constitute the third follow-up of a Chinese kindergarten cohort initially recruited in 2011/12 from 22 kindergartens (age 5-6). The subjects and their families were then reassessed in 2014/15 (age 8-9) and 2018/19 (age 12-13), respectively. The key variables collected in the previous assessments include time spent on various electronic devices (e.g. televisions, game consoles, smartphones), physical activities, family activities, family SES, school readiness, academic ability, and behaviour. The baseline and two follow-up studies were all funded by RGC GRF grants. The proposed study will revisit the cohort in 2026/27 (age 20-21) to examine the longitudinal associations of early SES and engagement in leisure activities with such outcomes as educational attainment, mental wellbeing and emotional problems, and physical health and fitness in young adulthood. Our experience in the previous follow-up suggests that we should be able to recruit at least 70% (n = 688) of the initial cohort. Study Contributions: This proposed cohort study represents a pioneering effort to explore the enduring impact of socioeconomic disparities on health and educational achievement from early childhood through young adulthood. It will offer compelling evidence of the significance of early-life SES and the evolving social dynamics over time in fostering health and developmental outcomes. Emphasis will also be placed on personal attributes such as resilience. The study’s findings are expected to inform policymaking decisions and underscore the significance of cohort studies in advancing our understanding of human development and potential. 背景： 長久以來，人們普遍認為來自弱勢背景的兒童比富裕家庭的同齡人擁有較少機會發揮其潛能。隨著社會進步，社會提供了更多支援資源和教育機會促進兒童的成長和發展。現時，許多低收入家庭的兒童亦能夠取得成功。儘管如此，至今仍缺乏相關的縱向研究。 研究目標： 本研究旨在探討童年社會經濟地位對成年後健康及教育成果的影響。同時，研究將分析兒童至青少年期間休閒活動模式，及其在不同社經地位群體中與成年後健康及教育結果的關聯，並探討個人心理抗逆力的潛在調節作用。 研究設計： 本研究的對象是在2011/12年度從22所幼稚園（幼稚園第3年，5-6歲）招募的華人幼兒及其父母，並分別於2014/15年（8至9歲）及2018/19年（12至13歲）進行了兩次跟進調查。此前評估收集的主要變數包括：使用不同電子設備（如電視、遊戲機、智能手機）的時間、體育活動、家庭活動、家庭社經地位、入學準備、學業能力及行為表現。本研究擬於2026年（20至21歲）對該隊列進行跟進研究，探討童年社經地位及參與休閒活動長遠健康和教育程度的影響。 研究貢獻： 本研究是探索社經環境差異對健康及教育成就從兒童早期至成年持續影響的先驅工作。研究將提供有力證據，展示童年社經地位及其隨時間變化的社會動態對健康及發展成果的重要性，並強調個人特質如抗逆力的角色。研究結果有望為政策制定提供參考，並突顯縱向研究在推動人類發展及潛能認識方面的重要性。

17106625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106625.value: 將結構見解轉化為高準確性和效率基因組編輯工程的基礎

17106625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106625.value: The effectiveness of CRISPR-Cas9 in genome editing applications requires the system to exhibit both high accuracy and efficiency simultaneously. However, achieving higher accuracy often results in lower efficiency in most Cas9 engineering endeavors, and a design strategy to overcome this tradeoff is currently lacking. This research leverages insights gained from cryo-electron microscopy structures of two high-fidelity and active Cas9 variants to guide our innovative design of novel protein mutations. By combining these insights with machine learning-assisted combinatorial mutagenesis to streamline the screening process, there is a new opportunity to develop an ultra-accurate genome editor without compromising its activity. Through unbiased high-throughput assays, we will validate the engineered variants' high on-target and minimal off-target activities across a wide range of target sites in human cells. Furthermore, we will explore the potential applications of these engineered variants in improving the safety of cancer immunotherapies. Our study aims to provide structural evidence and propose a practical approach for creating next-generation, highly accurate CRISPR variants without compromising on-target editing efficiency. CRISPR-Cas9於基因組編輯應用中要求該系統需同時具備高精確性與高效率。然而在眾多Cas9工程研究中，提升精確性往往伴隨效率降低的問題，目前仍缺乏能克服此權衡的設計策略。本研究基於兩種高保真且具功能活性之Cas9變體的冷凍電子顯微鏡結構所獲得的洞見，引導創新性蛋白質突變設計。透過結合此結構洞見與機器學習輔助的組合誘變技術以簡化篩選流程，為開發兼具高精確性且不損及活性的基因組編輯工具開闢新途徑。藉由高通量檢測，我們將驗證工程化變體於人類細胞中針對多樣化靶位點所展現的高靶向活性與低脫靶效應。此外，我們將探索此類工程化變體於提升癌症免疫療法安全性中的潛在應用。本研究旨在提供結構性證據，並提出一種實用方法以創建次世代高精確性CRISPR變體，同時維持其靶向編輯效率。

17107225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107225.value: IFN-λ 在乾燥綜合征發病機制中的作用：功能特徵與治療意義

17107225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107225.value: Primary Sjögren’s syndrome (SS) is an autoimmune disease with high prevalence in Hong Kong. SS is characterized by salivary gland (SG) and lacrimal gland inflammation and damage, leading to dry mouth and dry eyes. Currently, the therapeutic options for SS patients are mainly symptomatic management with applications of immunosuppressive agents, which usually lead to severe side effects. Thus, further studies on the immunopathogenesis and development of novel effective therapies are urgently needed for the treatment of SS. Emerging evidence has shown the implications of enhanced interferon (IFN) responses in the pathogenesis of SS. Most available studies have focused on the roles of type I and type II IFNs whereas much less is known about the involvement of type III IFN (IFN-λ) in SS pathogenesis. Currently, the potential functions of IFN-λ and underlying molecular mechanisms in SG inflammation and tissue damage remain largely unclear. The increased cell death of SG epithelial cells (SGECs) is a major cause of SG glandular hypofunction. Recently, pyroptosis, a new form of inflammatory programmed cell death, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of SS. However, whether and how pyroptosis contributes to SGEC damage and tissue inflammation in SS development needs further investigation. In our pilot studies, we found that increased concentrations of IFN-λ in saliva were positively correlated with disease activities in SS patients. In addition, we detected increased IFN-λ expression in SG-infiltrated myeloid cells and GSDMD activation in SGECs during SS development. Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data revealed increased pyroptosis scores in SG cells from SS-like mice. In culture, IFN-λ treatment directly induced GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis with upregulated IL-1β expression in SGECs. Furthermore, the blockade of local IFN-λ via SG retrograde cannulation markedly ameliorated SG tissue damage during experimental SS (ESS) progression. Thus, our preliminary findings have provided a strong rationale for us to investigate the functions of IFN-λ in driving SGEC pyroptosis and SG tissue inflammatory damage during SS development. In this project, we aim to determine the roles of IFN-λ and underlying molecular mechanisms in inducing SGEC pyroptosis and tissue inflammation during ESS development. Furthermore, we will explore novel IFN-λ-targeted therapies in various ESS mouse models. Together, our proposed translational studies will facilitate the development of new therapeutic strategies by targeting IFN-λ for treating SS, a chronic autoimmune disease with high social relevance in Hong Kong. 原發性乾燥綜合征（SS）是一種自體免疫疾病，其特徵為唾液腺（SG）和淚腺的炎症與損傷，從而導致口乾及眼乾。目前，SS患者的治療以免疫抑制劑為主，但這些方法常帶來嚴重副作用。SS這一慢性疾病在香港的發病率相當高，針對SS的免疫病理機制及新型有效治療方法的研究迫在眉睫。 最新證據顯示，幹擾素（IFN）反應的增強與SS的發病機制有關。現有研究多聚焦於第一型和第二型IFN的作用，而對於第三型IFN（IFN-λ）在SS發病中的作用則知之甚少。目前，IFN-λ在唾液腺炎症及組織損傷中的潛在功能及其分子機制仍不清楚。唾液腺上皮細胞（SGECs）死亡是唾液腺功能低下的主要原因之一。近年來，細胞焦亡（pyroptosis）作為一種新型炎症性細胞死亡形式，被認為與SS的發病有關。然而，細胞焦亡如何促進SGEC損傷及組織炎症仍需進一步研究。 在我們的初步研究中，我們發現SS患者唾液中IFN-λ濃度顯著升高，且與疾病活動度呈正相關。此外，我們在唾液腺浸潤的髓系細胞中檢測到大量IFN-λ表達，並在SS患者及實驗性SS（ESS）小鼠中發現炎症小體組分和GSDMD活化水平均有提高。單細胞RNA測序數據分析提示，SS樣小鼠唾液腺細胞的細胞焦亡評分較正常鼠明顯升高。在體外實驗中，IFN-λ處理直接誘導SGECs發生GSDMD介導的細胞焦亡，並上調IL-1β的表達。此外，通過唾液腺逆行插管技術灌注IFN-λ中和抗體，顯著減輕了ESS小鼠唾液腺組織損傷。因此，我們的初步發現為進一步研究IFN-λ在SS發病過程中誘導SGEC細胞焦亡及唾液腺組織炎症損傷的新功能提供了有力依據。 本研究旨在闡明IFN-λ在SS發病過程中誘導唾液腺上皮細胞損傷及細胞焦亡介導組織炎症的作用及其分子機制。同時，我們將在多種SS小鼠模型中探索靶向IFN-λ的新型治療策略。我們的轉化研究將推動靶向IFN-λ治療SS這一新策略的發展。

17107325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107325.value: 理解「毒素-解毒劑」系統在動物中作為自私基因的作用機制與演化過程

17107325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107325.value: Selfish genes favor their own transmission over the benefit of the host. The toxin-antidote (TA) element is a two-component selfish gene that enhances its transmission by killing noncarriers. The toxin is transmitted through the cytoplasm to cause lethality in individuals that do not carry the antidote gene, which is tightly linked to the toxin. Although TA elements are widely found in prokaryotes, their existence and potential prevalence in eukaryotes have only been discovered recently. In this project, we will map and characterize a newly discovered TA system in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, investigate its toxicity and detoxification mechanism, and analyze its ecological distribution in C. elegans wild populations. By crossing the laboratory strain with a wild strain isolated in Hawaii, we identified a novel TA element in the wild strain which is absent in the laboratory strain. In Specific Aim 1, we use introgression and genomic mapping to narrow down the region that contains the TA and identify the antidote gene using an RNAi-based functional screen and the toxin by testing the toxicity of candidate genes near the antidote. Our preliminary studies have tentatively identified and named the toxin as sept-1 encoding a SEP domain-containing protein and the antidote as zina-1 encoding a zinc finger protein. We will confirm their effects using genetic knockouts, study their expression by creating transcriptional and translational GFP reporters, and characterize their inheritance pattern by visualizing their mRNA and proteins in early embryos. In Specific Aim 2, we will study the toxicity and detoxification mechanisms of the sept-1/zina-1 TA system by identifying the factors required for the toxin-induced lethality through genetic screens and studying the interaction between the toxin and antidote at both protein and RNA levels. Since the antidote is an RNA-binding protein and can form liquid-like droplets in vivo, we will test whether it undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation to form condensates that sequester the toxin mRNA and thus inhibit the toxicity. In Specific Aim 3, we will use a bioinformatic pipeline to map the ecological distribution of the sept-1/zina-1 system among >1000 C. elegans wild isolates and study their coexistence with two other known TA systems. Through population genetics analysis, we aim to understand how the TA elements contribute to intraspecific genomic variation. This project can provide an important example of selfish TA elements in animals, advance our understanding of genomic evolution, and pave the way to develop them into synthetic gene drives. 動物基因組中存在大量的自私基因，它們的遺傳對宿主並無益處。毒素-解毒劑（TA）元件是一種由兩個成分構成的自私基因，通過殺死非攜帶者來增強其傳播。毒素通過細胞質傳遞，對不攜帶解毒劑基因的個體造成致死，而該解毒劑基因與毒素在基因組上緊密連接。儘管TA元件在原核生物中廣泛存在，它們在真核生物中的存在及普遍性，直到最近才被發現。在本項目中，我們將研究在秀麗線蟲 Caenorhabditis elegans 中新發現的TA系統，揭示其毒性及解毒機制，並分析其在 C. elegans 野生群體中的生態分布。 通過將實驗室常用線蟲株與在夏威夷野生株進行雜交，我們在野生株中發現了一個新型的TA元件，該元件在實驗室菌中缺失。在目標一中，我們將利用基因滲入來找出包含TA的區域，並通過RNA干擾（RNAi）篩選來鑑定出編碼解毒劑基因，並通過測試候選基因附近的基因來確定毒素基因。我們的初步研究已識別並命名毒素為sept-1，該基因編碼含有SEP結構域的蛋白質，解毒劑為zina-1，該基因編碼鋅指蛋白。我們將通過基因敲除來確認它們的作用，建立轉錄和翻譯的GFP報告基因來研究它們的表達，並在早期胚胎中觀察它們的mRNA和蛋白質分佈來研究它們的遺傳模式。在目標二中，我們將通過基因篩選來找出導致毒素致死的機制，研究sept-1/zina-1 TA系統的毒性與解毒機制，並分析毒素與解毒劑在蛋白質和RNA層面的相互作用。由於解毒劑是一種RNA結合蛋白，並且可以在體內形成液滴狀結構，我們將測試它是否通過液-液相分離形成濃縮體，以隔離毒素mRNA並抑制其毒性。在目標三中，我們將利用生物信息學流程，繪製出超過1000個 C. elegans 野生分離株中sept-1/zina-1系統的生態分布，並研究它們與另外兩個已知TA系統的共存關係。通過群體遺傳學分析，我們旨在理解TA元素如何促進種內基因組變異。該項目能夠為研究動物中自私TA元素提供重要範例，推動我們對基因組演化的理解，並為將其開發成合成生物學元件提供基礎。

17107725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107725.value: 基於腦出血後用藥評分採用三聯降血壓藥方案研究

17107725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17107725.value: Mr Cheng, Franco WT Dr Fok, Joshua Prof Lau, Gary Kui Kai Prof Leung, Gilberto Ka-kit Dr Lui, Adrian Shing Tsun Prof Wong, Chun Ka Dr Wu, Jerome Hiu Fung

17107725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107725.value: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is the second most common form of stroke, with an estimated 2-3 million cases occurring annually in China. Although it only accounts for around 20-30% of all strokes, ICH is the most severe form of stroke, contributing to 50% of all stroke-related deaths and the greatest stroke-related disability burden. Those who survive their ICH are at high risk of ICH recurrence, subsequent stroke, and cardiovascular events. Hence, reducing these risks after ICH is important to lessen the disease's healthcare and socio-economic burden. Hypertension is the most significant shared risk factor for ICH, stroke, and cardiovascular events. Hence, effectively controlling blood pressure (BP) can reduce the risks of these events. Notably, since these risks are highest within the first year of ICH, promptly achieving BP targets is also crucial. However, around half of ICH survivors have uncontrolled hypertension in real-world data. This is because ICH patients usually have more difficult-to-control hypertension, with many requiring ≥3 antihypertensive medications. Therefore, undertreatment of hypertension is the leading cause of uncontrolled hypertension after ICH. To improve the rates of controlled hypertension, better prescription practices are necessary. One approach to accomplish prompt BP control is to prescribe upfront triple antihypertensive medications (triple pill) shortly after ICH. However, there are concerns regarding overtreating hypertension and excessive BP lowering, which would cause more side effects and have been associated with increased mortality, particularly in older patients. Additionally, the general use of upfront triple pills in all ICH would have healthcare cost implications, as triple pills are more expensive than conventional antihypertensive medications. To facilitate individualized treatment, our team recently developed and validated a predictive score, the TRICH score, to identify patients who require triple pills after ICH. The 9-point TRICH score (1 for age<60, 1 for males, 1 for history of ischemic heart disease, 2 for admission estimated glomerular filtration rate <60mL/min/1.73m2, 2 for admission systolic BP 190-230mmHg, and 4 for >230mmHg) has a c-statistic of 0.79, and a score of ≥3 predicted the need for a triple pill with 0.73 sensitivity and 0.76 specificity. The current TRIACT trial is a 3-year multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded endpoint (PROBE), parallel-group clinical trial that aims to test the clinical application, safety, and efficacy of upfront prescription of triple pills in ICH based on the TRICH score. This approach would enable prompt achievement of BP control after ICH and mitigate the risk of overtreatment. 腦出血是第二大常見的腦中風類型，中國每年約有200-300萬病例。儘管僅佔所有腦中風病患的20-30%，但它卻是最嚴重的腦中風類型，佔所有腦中風相關死亡人數的50%，也是腦中風致殘負擔最重的疾病。腦出血倖存者面臨極高的復發性腦出血、繼發性腦中風及心血管事件風險。因此降低腦出血後的這些風險是對減輕醫療保健系統和社會經濟負擔至關重要。 腦出血主要由高血壓引起，有效控制血壓能顯著降低復發性腦出血、腦中風和心血管事件發生風險。由於這些風險在腦出血後第一年內最高，因此及時達成血壓目標也至關重要。然而，現有數據顯示，約半數腦出血倖存者的高血壓未受控制－因為這類患者的血壓通常較難控制，需要≥3種降血壓藥物合併治療。治療不足是腦出血後血壓失控的主要原因。因此、為提高血壓控制率，改善處方實踐是必須的。達成有效控制血壓的一種方法是在腦出血後早期啟用三重降血壓藥方案。但此舉可能引發過度高血壓治療和血壓降幅過大，導致更多副作用並增加死亡風險，尤其是老年患者。此外，在所有腦出血患者中普遍使用三聯降血壓藥將增加醫療成本，因其價格遠高於常規降血壓藥物。 為實現個人化治療，我們團隊近期開發並驗證了一種預測評分系統（TRICH）評分，用於識別腦出血後需要三聯降血壓藥治療的患者。這個 TRICH 9分量表包括（年齡 <60歲＝1分，男性＝1分，缺血性心臟病史＝1分，入院估算腎功能 GFR <60mL/min/1.73m²=2分，入院收縮壓SBP 190-230mmHg=2分，SBP >230mmHg=4分）。其c統計量為0.79，評分 ≥3預測時三聯藥物需求的敏感性為0.73，特異性為0.76。 因此，本研究為一項為期三年的多中心、前瞻性、隨機分配、開放標記、設盲指標（PROBE）的平行組臨床試驗，旨在基於TRICH評分檢驗三聯藥物在腦出血患者中早期應用的臨床可行性、安全性和有效性。此方法將促進腦出血後快速實現血壓控制，並減輕過度治療的風險。

17108725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17108725.value: RagA-Adora2A-lncRNA TCONS_00004755 信號軸在抑鬱症中的潛在作用：對中藥異黃酮葛根素抗抑鬱機制的啟示

17108725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17108725.value: Prof Feng, Yibin Prof Rong, Jianhui

17108725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108725.value: The increasing prevalence of depression constitutes strong negative impacts on patients’ quality of life, societal harmony and global economy. The first-line antidepressant treatments are predominately targeting serotonin reuptake like citalopram. However, patients are frustrated by limited efficacy and potential side effects on gastrointestinal tract and sexual function. Therefore, it is important to explore the potential of traditional Chinese medicines for effective management of depression. Our previous studies demonstrated that Chinese medicine isoflavone puerarin from Radix Puerariae effectively alleviated depressive-like behaviours and pain responses in mice with spared nerve injury and liposaccharide (LPS) challenge. Transcriptomic profiling of mouse brain using next-generation RNA sequencing revealed the small GTPase RagA as a potential target in depression. RagA senses intracellular amino acids for mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) to regulate p70S6 kinase (p70S6K) and eukaryotic initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 (4EBP1). Indeed, the mTORC1 pathway orchestrates the cell signals to dictate cognitive and neuropsychiatric actions. These results stimulated us to establish the brain-specific RagA knock-in mouse model for the underlying depression mechanism. By employing multi-omics technologies, we discovered that RagA transgenic mice might exhibit depressive-like behaviours via concomitantly activating ADORA2A and LncRNAs like TCONS_00004755. ADORA2A is adenosine A2A receptor and transduces adenosine signal to activate protein kinase A (PKA) and extracellular signal regulated kinase 1 & 2 (ERK1/2) signalling pathways. Convergently, TCONS_00004755 is positively correlated with cell division cycle 20 homolog b (Cdc20b), a key mediator in cell cycle and differentiation. Importantly, ADORA2A and CDC20 may play synergistic roles in the regulation of cell behaviour, life and fate in the context of cognition and psychiatry. Thus, we hypothesize that Chinese medicine isoflavone puerarin may exhibit antidepressant activity via inhibiting RagA-Adora2A-lncRNA TCONS_00004755 axis. Indeed, our pilot experiments support the development of puerarin-based therapy from the following aspects: 1) Puerarin significantly reduced depressive-like behaviours in LPS-challenged mice by suppressing RagA expression; 2) Puerarin derivative WSP01 with better water solubility attenuated depressive-like behaviours in LPS-challenged mice. We will pursue three specific aims: 1) To validate the role of RagA-ADORA2A axis in the onset of depression; 2) To discover the role of lncRNA TCONS_00004755-CDC20b in RagA-induced depression; and 3) To develop soluble puerarin analogues for the treatment of depression. The proposed studies will not only reveal the unexpected roles and the connection of RagA with ADORA2A and lncRNAs in the pathology of depression, but also pave the way to develop puerarin-based antidepressant therapy. 抑鬱症的患病率日益增加，對患者的生活品質、社會和諧及全球經濟造成了嚴重的負面影響。目前的一線抗抑鬱治療主要針對血清素再吸收，例如西酞普蘭。然而，其療效有限，且可能對胃腸道和性功能產生副作用，常令患者感到困擾。因此，探索傳統中藥在抑鬱症有效治療中的潛力至關重要。我們既往研究證實，源自中藥葛根的異黃酮葛根素，能有效緩解神經損傷和脂多糖誘導的小鼠抑鬱樣行為及疼痛反應。利用二代RNA測序技術對小鼠腦部進行的轉錄組分析發現，小GTP酶RagA是抑鬱症的一個潛在作用靶點。RagA可檢測出細胞內氨基酸，進而通過哺乳動物雷帕黴素標靶蛋白複合體1（mTORC1）調控p70S6激酶（p70S6K）和真核起始因子4E結合蛋白1（4EBP1）。而mTORC1信號通路能够協調細胞信號傳導，主導認知和神經精神活動。基於此，我們建立了腦部特異性的RagA基因敲入小鼠模型，以探究抑鬱症的潛在機制。通過多組學技術分析，我們發現RagA轉基因小鼠表現出抑鬱樣行為，其機制可能與同時激活腺苷A2A受體（ADORA2A）和長鏈非編碼RNA（lncRNA，例如TCONS_00004755）有關。ADORA2A作為腺苷A2A受體，負責傳導腺苷信號，以激活蛋白激酶A（PKA）和細胞外信號調節激酶1/2（ERK1/2）信號通路。綜合來看，TCONS_00004755的表達與細胞分裂週期20同源蛋白b（Cdc20b，一種在細胞週期和分化中起關鍵作用的介質）呈正相關。重要的是，在認知和精神疾病中，ADORA2A和CDC20可能在調控細胞行為、生命和命運方面發揮協同作用。因此，我們提出假說：中藥異黃酮葛根素的抗抑鬱活性，可能通過抑制RagA-Adora2A-lncRNA TCONS_00004755信號軸來實現。我們的初步實驗從以下幾個方面為基於葛根素的治療方法的開發提供了支持：（1）葛根素通過抑制RagA的表達，顯著減輕了脂多糖誘導的小鼠抑鬱樣行為；（2）水溶性更佳的葛根素衍生物WSP01，能減輕脂多糖誘導的小鼠抑鬱樣行為。我們後續的研究將聚焦於三個目標：（1）驗證RagA-ADORA2A信號軸在抑鬱症發病中的作用；（2）探究lncRNA TCONS_00004755-CDC20b在RagA誘導的抑鬱症中的作用；（3）開發可溶性葛根素類似物用於抑鬱症治療。這些研究不僅將闡明RagA與ADORA2A及lncRNAs在抑鬱症病理中的作用和關聯，也將為開發基於葛根素的抗抑鬱療法奠定基礎。

17109625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17109625.value: 了解骨骼肌細胞金屬病變的進展以進行治療幹預

17109625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17109625.value: Prof Chan, Danny Dr Ho, Wing Kei, Joshua Dr Su, Zezhuo Prof Xu, Aimin

17109625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109625.value: We previously reported the first case of magnetic controlled growth rods (MCGRs) in The Lancet for spinal curvature treatment in early onset scoliosis. This innovation has revolutionized the surgical treatment of early onset scoliosis; however, MCGR usage is hindered by metallosis, a significant concern also found in patients with other metal implants. Wear metal debris can cause inflammation, pain, tissue damage, and implant failure. Engineering solutions are unlikely to fully eliminate metal ion leakage, necessitating the development of biological solutions. While inflammation and fibrosis are well-recognized responses to metallosis, we aim to explore a new dimension of this response: the impact of metal debris on the metabolism of muscle cells. Our preliminary research leveraging multi-omics profiling from patient samples and harnessing cell line and mouse models, demonstrated that metallosis resulted in ectopic accumulation of triacylglycerol (TG), upregulation of insulin-like growth factor binding proteins (IGFBPs) condign genes, and activation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway in muscle cells. We hypothesize that metal ions interact with IGFBPs, leading to the release of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1). This, in turn, activates the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, which ultimately results in TG accumulation and muscle dysfunction. To test this hypothesis, we will employ titanium ions associated with MCGR, as well as cobalt-chromium-related ions. Additionally, we will explore the crosstalk between muscle cell metabolism and the inflammatory and fibrotic responses. Finally, we will examine the progression and clinical implications of metallosis in skeletal muscle cells using the mouse metallosis model. Our interdisciplinary team, comprising experts in orthopaedics, biology, endocrinology, and bioinformatics, will collaborate to address the complex challenges presented by the dysregulation of metabolism induced by metallosis. Understanding these mechanisms is vital for enhancing the safety of metallic implants, including MCGR, and developing early intervention strategies to prevent metallosis-related complications. 我們之前在《柳葉刀》上報導了第一例用於早發性脊柱側彎治療的磁控生長棒（MCGRs）病例。這項創新徹底改變了早發性脊柱側彎的外科治療方式；然而，MCGR的使用受到金屬中毒（metallosis）的限制，這也是其他金屬植入物患者中常見的嚴重問題。金屬碎屑的磨損可能引起發炎、疼痛、組織損傷以及植入物失效。工程解決方案不太可能完全消除金屬離子的洩漏，因此亟需開發生物學的解決策略。雖然發炎和纖維化是金屬中毒反應中的公認表現，我們希望探索這一反應的新維度：金屬碎屑對肌肉細胞代謝的影響。我們的初步研究利用患者樣本的多組學分析，結合細胞系和小鼠模型，顯示金屬中毒導致三酰甘油（TG）異常積累，胰島素樣生長因子結合蛋白（IGFBPs）表達上調，以及PI3K-AKT-mTOR信號通路在肌肉細胞中的激活。我們假設金屬離子與IGFBPs相互作用，促使胰島素樣生長因子1（IGF1）釋放，從而激活PI3K-AKT-mTOR通路，最終引起TG積累和肌肉功能障礙。為驗證這一假設，我們將使用與MCGR相關的鈦離子以及鈷鉻相關離子。此外，我們還將探討肌肉細胞代謝與發炎和纖維化反應之間的相互作用。最後，我們將利用小鼠金屬中毒模型，研究金屬中毒在骨骼肌細胞中的進展及其臨床意義。我們的跨學科團隊由骨科、生物學、內分泌學和生物資訊學專家組成，將合作應對金屬中毒引起的代謝失調所帶來的複雜挑戰。理解這些機制對於提升金屬植入物（包括MCGR）的安全性、開發早期干預策略以預防金屬中毒相關的併發症具有重要意義。

17111225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111225.value: 揭示牙板退化過程中的單細胞發育圖譜：為全牙再生提供新策略

17111225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17111225.value: Prof Hu, Elaine Mingxin Prof Tucker, Abigail Prof Wang, John Junwen Prof Wen, Ping Dr Wu, Zhaoming Prof Zhu, Xiaofei

17111225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111225.value: Background: Unlike polyphyodont species, such as sharks and alligators, which continuously replace their teeth, diphyodont species, including humans, develop two sets of teeth throughout their lifespan. Understanding the regulatory mechanisms governing tooth replacement could potentially lead to innovative therapies that promote whole-tooth regeneration, allowing humans to naturally replace their missing or damaged teeth. Key Issues: The dental lamina, essential for tooth development, initiates tooth formation but undergoes early regression in diphyodont species. In contrast, most polyphyodont species maintain an intact epithelial dental lamina that continues to proliferate and elongate, enabling continuous tooth replacement. Variations in the longevity of the dental lamina suggest it may play a key role in determining tooth replacement patterns across species. However, current studies have predominantly focused on the mouse, which as a monophyodont does not replace its teeth, leaving the mechanisms of tooth replacement in diphyodont species largely unexplored. Constructing a spatial-temporal atlas that maps the process of regression of the dental lamina in diphyodont species provides a novel avenue for developing regenerative therapies for potential clinical applications in humans. Previous studies have suggested that epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), apoptosis, cell migration, reduced cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and signals from the primary tooth germ and/or surrounding mesenchyme may play a significant role in the regression of the dental lamina. However, the mechanisms of the degradation of the dental lamina in diphyodont species remain poorly understood. Objectives and Methods: This project aims to delineate the spatiotemporal mechanisms involved in the degradation of the dental lamina and explore potential strategies for tooth regeneration. Tissue samples from minipig and human embryos during mid-gestation will be collected and subjected to spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), focusing on the dental lamina and surrounding mesenchyme to map gene expression profiles involved in the degradation of the dental lamina. After elucidating developmental trajectories in the regression of the dental lamina, we will validate these findings in human and minipig embryos using multiplex immunofluorescence, TUNEL assay, and RNA in situ hybridization. Additionally, key signalling will be modulated in minipig explant culture, followed by histological analysis and immunofluorescence to assess whether additional teeth can be regenerated. Significance: This research could pave the way for therapeutic approaches that reactivate tooth regeneration in humans, transforming dental care by enabling humans to naturally replace missing or damaged teeth. Furthermore, the research will contribute to broader fields such as regenerative medicine. 研究背景：與鯊魚、鱷魚等可終生替換牙齒的多牙列動物不同，人類等雙牙列動物一生僅形成兩副牙列。深入闡明牙齒替換的調控機制，將有助於開發促進全牙再生的創新治療手段，為實現人類牙齒再生提供理論基礎。 關鍵科學問題：牙板作為牙齒發育的關鍵結構，在雙牙列動物中於牙齒發育啟動後即出現早期退化，而多牙列動物則能維持牙板的完整性和增殖能力，從而實現牙齒的持續更替。牙板存續時間的顯著差異提示其可能是決定物種間牙齒替換模式的關鍵調控樞紐。然而，現有研究主要集中於單牙列小鼠模型，對於雙牙列動物牙齒替換機制的研究仍存在顯著空白。通過揭示雙牙列動物牙板退化的時空圖譜，將為構建人類牙齒再生治療開闢新途徑。現有研究表明，上皮-間充質轉化、細胞凋亡、細胞遷移、增殖抑制、血管生成以及來自乳牙牙胚及/或周圍間充質的信號分子，均可能參與調控牙板退化。然而，雙牙列動物牙板退化的具體分子機制仍亟待闡明。 研究方案：本研究旨在解析牙板退化的時空調控機制，並探索牙齒再生的潛在策略。通過採集妊娠中期小型豬和人類胚胎的牙板及周圍間充質組織，運用空間轉錄組學和單細胞RNA測序技術，繪製牙板退化過程中的基因表達全景圖譜。在明確牙板退化的發育軌跡後，採用多重免疫熒光、TUNEL細胞凋亡檢測和RNA原位雜交等技術在人類和小型豬胚胎樣本中開展多層次驗證。此外，本研究將進一步通過小型豬離體培養模型調控關鍵信號通路，結合組織學分析和免疫熒光檢測，評估牙齒再生的可行性。 研究意義：本研究有望為人類牙齒再生治療提供全新思路，推動天然牙列替換在臨床口腔醫學中的應用轉化。此外，相關研究成果亦可為再生醫學等相關領域提供理論支持。

17111625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111625.value: 戊型肝炎病毒通用疫苗的研發前景

17111625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111625.value: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an important cause of viral hepatitis. Two antigenically distinct species within the family Hepeviridae cause human infection – Paslahepevirus balayani (bHEV) and Rocahepevirus ratti (rat hepatitis E; rHEV). While bHEV is usually transmitted from person-to-person or as a foodborne zoonosis, rHEV is an ubiquitous rodent pathogen that infects humans via an unknown route. We first discovered that rHEV causes human infections in Hong Kong in 2018; it has since become the most commonly reported rodent-borne zoonosis in the territory. rHEV infections have also been reported in Spain, France, Canada, and mainland China highlighting its importance as an emerging pathogen wherever surveillance is strengthened. The clinical features of rHEV closely mirror bHEV with severe hepatitis, chronic hepatitis and extrahepatic manifestations being reported. Currently, there is only one commercially available hepatitis E vaccine, which is a virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine based on a bHEV truncated capsid protein. We have shown that this vaccine is not completely protective against rHEV infections in experimental animals due to the significant antigenic divergence of rHEV from bHEV. Furthermore, sera from humans vaccinated with the commercial bHEV-based vaccine bind much less effectively to rHEV-derived capsid proteins. Therefore, given the emerging importance of rHEV as a distinct HEV serotype, there is a clear need to incorporate this novel zoonotic pathogen in the next generation of hepatitis E vaccines. We have previously developed a candidate rHEV VLP vaccine, which confers sterilizing immunity against rHEV in an experimental rat model. In this proposal, we will evaluate preclinical immunogenicity and efficacy of a bivalent hepatitis E vaccine candidate incorporating both bHEV and rHEV VLPs. The bivalent vaccine will be compared to monovalent and mock vaccines in rat and gerbil models of hepatitis E. Immunogenicity outcomes will include humoral antibody responses (IgG and IgA enzymatic immunoassays in serum and faeces, VLP cell-binding inhibition assays, and surface plasmon resonance) and cell-mediated immune responses (ELISpot and intracellular cytokine staining). Efficacy outcomes will include protection against rHEV infection in the rat model and protection against bHEV and rHEV infections in the gerbil model. Virus loads will be measured in serum, faeces, and liver tissue. Liver histology and immunohistochemical staining will also be assessed. We have already applied for patents for this bivalent HEV vaccine concept; this pre-clinical study will pave the way to GLP toxicology studies and investigational new drug application in preparation for a human clinical trial. 戊型肝炎病毒是造成病毒性肝炎的主要病原體。戊肝病毒有兩種導致人類疾病的主要基因型：Paslahepevirus balayani (bHEV) 和 Rocahepevirus ratti (rat hepatitis E; rHEV)。bHEV主要通過人与人之間的傳播或作為食源性動物傳染，偶爾會在人類中引起人畜共患病。然而，rHEV普遍存在於啮齒類動物中，其傳染給人的途徑尚不清楚。2018年，我們的研究團隊在接受器官移植的患者中首次發現了rHEV感染。此外，我們發現rHEV已逐漸成為香港地區通過啮齒類動物傳播、引起人畜共患病的常見病原體。隨後，在中國雲南省和海南省，以及西班牙、法國和加拿大等國內外多個國家，也陸續報告了人類感染rHEV的案例，顯示其作為新興病原體的重要性，尤其在加強監測的地區。與bHEV相比，rHEV感染引起的臨床表現相似，包括重症肝炎、慢性肝炎以及肝外表現。 目前，市場上唯一可用的戊肝疫苗是HEV 239疫苗（Hecolin®），這是一種基於bHEV衣殼蛋白設計的病毒樣顆粒（VLP）疫苗，採用大腸桿菌表達技術生產。由於bHEV和rHEV的抗原表位存在顯著差異，我們的研究發現，Hecolin®疫苗不能完全預防實驗動物感染rHEV。此外，從接種了Hecolin® 疫苗的人群中分離的血清抗體與rHEV的衣殼蛋白結合的效率也非常低，表明現有疫苗在應對rHEV方面的保護效果有限。因此，隨著rHEV作為一種新興的病毒型在公共中的傳播日益增加，將其納入下一代疫苗的研發已成為亟需解決的關鍵問題。 在先前的研究中，我們開發了一款基於rHEV衣殼蛋白的病毒顆粒疫苗，並在動物體內實驗中發現，接種該疫苗後，大鼠能夠產生有效的免疫反應。在本研究中，我們將通過動物實驗評估一種雙價戊型肝炎疫苗的免疫原性和有效性，該疫苗融合了bHEV和rHEV病毒樣顆粒（VLPs）。我們將在大鼠和沙鼠的戊型肝炎感染模型中，對雙價疫苗、單價疫苗和空白對照疫苗進行全面比較。免疫原性評估將包括體液抗體反應（血清中的IgG和IgA酶聯免疫吸附測定、VLP細胞結合抑制試驗和表面等離子共振）以及細胞免疫反應（ELISpot和細胞內細胞因子染色）。疫苗有效性評估將包括在大鼠模型中對rHEV感染的保護，以及在沙鼠模型中對bHEV和rHEV感染的保護。病毒載量將在血清、糞便和肝臟組織中進行測定。肝臟組織學和免疫組化染色也將進行評估。我們已為該雙價HEV疫苗的概念申請了專利，此項臨床前研究將為GLP毒理學研究和新藥研究申請奠定理論基礎，為後續的人體臨床試驗做準備。

17111925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111925.value: 脂肪组织来源的S100A4 作为新型食欲抑制激素缓解肥胖和高血糖的临床价值与机制探究

17111925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111925.value: Obesity is a global health crisis affecting hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide, which is a complex metabolic disorder characterized by excessive adiposity. Hyperphagia is a key driver of obesity, which promotes weight gain and results in metabolic disorders. Obesity could significantly increase the risk of developing comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, which have caused heavy healthcare and economic burden all over the world. Therefore, identification of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets for the prediction and treatment of obesity, type 2 diabetes and their related complications are imperative. Appetite regulation plays a critical role in the development of obesity. In this project, we took advantage of our lipodystrophic mouse model with fat transplantation, together with our Olink proteomics platform to identify a novel adipose-derived hormone S100A4 with appetite-suppressing and glucose-lowering effects. S100A4 is a secretory protein belongs to S100 protein family, which can specifically bind to calcium ions and target proteins. Previous studies on S100A4 mainly investigated its role in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and liver fibrosis. However, the specific role of adipose-derived S100A4 and its action mechanisms remain unknown. Our preliminary findings showed a significant increase of S100A4 level in adipose tissues and adipocytes of diet-induced obese mice, together with an obvious upregulation of S100A4 level in adipocyte fractions of subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissues in obese subjects with type 2 diabetes. Therefore, we intend to further investigate whether adipocyte or circulating S100A4 level has clinical correlations with several metabolic parameters using a replication cohort including lean and obese subjects, as well as explore whether the circulating level of S100A4 could predict type 2 diabetes using a prospective cohort. Our preliminary findings also demonstrated that AAV-mediated overexpression of S100A4 in lipodystrophic mice could reduce food intake, body weight and blood glucose level, we thus hypothesize that S100A4 may exert central actions in the hypothalamus to suppress appetite and thus reduce body weight and blood glucose. To test this hypothesis, we will comprehensively characterize the physiological and pharmacological role of S100A4 using adipocyte-specific knockout mouse model and recombinant protein, as well as explore the underlying mechanism by identifying the key receptor and signaling pathways in the hypothalamus that mediates the anorexigenic effect of S100A4 using both hypothesis-driven and omics-driven approaches. This study will provide mechanistic insights for the potential application of S100A4 as a promising biomarker or therapeutic target for hyperphagia-induced obesity and type 2 diabetes. 肥胖是一种影响全球数亿人的健康危机，它是一种以脂肪组织过度堆积为特征的复杂代谢性疾病。食欲过盛是肥胖的关键驱动因素，它会促进体重增长并导致代谢紊乱。肥胖会显著增加罹患2型糖尿病和心血管疾病的风险，这些疾病在全球范围内造成了沉重的医疗和经济负担。因此，发现用于预测和治疗肥胖、2型糖尿病及其相关并发症的新型生物标志物和治疗靶点，已迫在眉睫。 食欲调节在肥胖的发生和发展中起着关键作用。在本项目中，我们利用本实验室的脂肪缺失小鼠模型（配合脂肪移植）通过Olink蛋白质组学平台，鉴定出了一种具有抑制食欲和降低血糖作用的、来源于脂肪组织的新型激素——S100A4。S100A4是隶属于S100蛋白家族的分泌蛋白，它能特异性结合钙离子及其靶蛋白。先前关于S100A4的研究主要聚焦于它在非酒精性脂肪性肝病和肝纤维化中的作用。然而，脂肪组织来源的S100A4的具体作用及其作用机制仍不清楚。 我们的初步发现显示，在高脂饮食诱导的肥胖小鼠的脂肪组织和脂肪细胞中，S100A4的水平均显著升高。同时，在患有2型糖尿病的肥胖受试者的皮下和内脏脂肪细胞中，S100A4的水平也明显上调。因此，我们拟在包含标准体重者和肥胖受试者的重复队列中，进一步探究脂肪细胞中或血清中的S100A4水平是否与多项代谢参数存在临床相关性；并利用前瞻性队列研究探讨循环S100A4水平能否预测2型糖尿病的发生。 我们的初步结果还表明，腺相关病毒（AAV）介导的S100A4过表达，能够降低脂肪缺失小鼠的食物摄入量、体重和血糖水平。因此，我们提出假说：S100A4可能在下丘脑发挥抑制食欲的作用，从而降低体重和血糖。为了验证该假说，我们将利用脂肪细胞特异性S100A4基因敲除小鼠模型和S100A4重组蛋白，全面表征S100A4的生理和药理作用；同时，采用假说驱动和组学驱动相结合的方法，探索介导S100A4在下丘脑中食欲抑制作用的关键受体及信号通路，以阐明其作用机制。本研究将为S100A4作为新型生物标志物或治疗靶点，用于防治食欲过盛诱发的肥胖和2型糖尿病提供新的见解。

17112525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17112525.value: 生成式設計與手動設計的患者專用植入物（PSIs）在正顎手術中的手術精確度比較：一項隨機臨床試驗

17112525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17112525.value: Dr Tsoi, James Kit Hon Dr Yeung, Wai Kan Andy

17112525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112525.value: Patients suffering from dentofacial deformities such as cleft lip and palate, long jaw, and facial asymmetry often experience mastication, speech and breathing dysfunctions, temporomandibular disorder, and poor facial aesthetics. Orthognathic surgery serves as the surgical treatment designed to correct dentofacial deformities and restore oral function along with facial harmony. The success of orthognathic surgery is dependent on the accurate transfer of Virtual Surgical Planning (VSP) to the actual surgery. Patient-Specific Implants (PSIs), which include surgical guides and bone fixation plates, are customized based on individual anatomical features and preoperative surgical plans. This results in greater surgical accuracy compared to the conventional surgical wafer approach. Moreover, the use of PSIs simplifies surgical procedures, subsequently reducing operation time and enhancing patient safety. However, the design of PSIs requires considerable time and expertise in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software, causing many hospitals to outsource the process. This dependence on commercial providers leads to increased costs and extended turnaround times, which restricts the widespread use of PSIs. Additionally, the conventional process for manual-designed (MD) PSIs is prone to errors. This process requires designers to draw each component of a 3D model independently before merging them. Due to the complex geometry of jaw bones, especially the maxilla, this method often results in designs that do not conform adequately to bone structures or present interference, potentially compromising surgical accuracy. As a result, manually designed fixation plates exhibit greater variability in terms of shape fit, which can influence overall surgical precision. To resolve these issues, our team designed a generative-designed (GD) workflow that automates the design of PSIs based on anatomical constraints and biomechanical requirements. As shown in our pilot study, this method not only enhances design efficiency but also yields PSIs that fit bone contours closely while maintaining sufficient strength for clinical use. However, it is still uncertain whether GD PSIs could provide clinically acceptable surgical outcomes for patients. This project aims to evaluate the surgical accuracy and outcomes of GD PSIs compared to MD PSIs in orthognathic surgery through a randomized clinical trial. The results of this project will provide crucial clinical evidence on whether PSIs designed using the GD workflow are superior to MD PSIs. This project may make PSIs more accessible and cost-effective for orthognathic surgery centers and patients, thereby promoting the widespread adoption of PSIs, reducing costs and improving care quality for patients with dentofacial deformities. 患有頜面畸形（如唇腭裂、長顎及面部不對稱）的患者常伴隨咀嚼、語言及呼吸功能障礙、顳顎關節紊亂及面部美觀問題。正顎手術旨在矯正此類畸形，恢復口腔功能與面部協調。手術的成功關鍵在於將虛擬手術計劃（VSP）精準轉化至實際操作中。患者專用植入物（PSIs）—包含手術導板與骨固定板—根據患者解剖特徵及術前規劃量身定制，相較傳統咬合板輔助方式，其能顯著提升手術精準度，同時簡化流程、縮短手術時間並提高安全性。 然而，PSIs的設計需耗費大量時間與電腦輔助設計（CAD）軟體操作專業能力，導致多數醫院選擇外判工序。此依賴商業供應商的模式不僅增加成本與交期，亦限制PSIs的普及。此外，傳統手動設計（MD）PSIs的流程易產生誤差：設計師需獨立繪製3D模型各部件後再進行組裝。由於頜骨（尤其上頜骨）幾何結構複雜，此方法常導致設計與骨結構貼合度不足或產生干涉，可能影響手術精準度。研究顯示，手動設計的固定板在形狀貼合度上變異性較大，進而影響整體手術精度。 為解決上述問題，本團隊開發一套基於解剖限制與生物力學需求的生成式設計（GD）流程，可自動化生成PSIs。初步研究顯示，此方法不僅提升設計效率，更能產出緊密貼合骨輪廓且具臨床適用強度的PSIs。然而，GD PSIs能否提供臨床可接受的手術效果仍待驗證。 本研究擬通過隨機臨床試驗，評估GD PSIs與MD PSIs於正顎手術中的精準度與成效。研究結果將為GD流程設計的PSIs是否優於傳統手動設計提供關鍵臨床證據，有望使PSIs對正顎手術中心及患者更易取得且具成本效益，從而推動其廣泛應用，降低醫療成本並提升牙頜面畸形患者的照護品質。
