With our preliminary data, we hypothesize that hypoblast might contribute to blood development, especially the early erythropoiesis in the yolk sac. Here we propose orthogonal approaches to address this hypothesis. First, we will leverage the expressed molecular barcodes to track the hypoblast fate in human embryoids. This will address whether hypoblast directly differentiates into blood. Second, we will define the epigenomic regulation of hypoblast by multi-modal analyses. This will deepen our understanding of hypoblast fate. This proposal will contribute to fundamental biology and pave the way for cell fate engineering. 人類胚胎中的血液如何發育是發育生物學的基本問題。這種理解將有利於免疫細胞工程針對癌症和自體免疫疾病等各種疾病的努力。最初被認為是短暫實體並在胚胎發育過程中消失的下胚層是否真的有助於血液發育尚不清楚。根據我們的初步數據，我們假設下胚層可能有助於血液發育，尤其是卵黃囊中的早期紅血球生成。在這裡，我們提出正交方法來解決這個假設。首先，我們將利用表達的分子條碼來追蹤人類胚胎中的下胚層命運。這將解決下胚層是否直接分化為血液的問題。其次，我們將透過多模式分析來定義下胚層的表觀基因組調控。這將加深我們對下胚層命運的理解。該提案將為基礎生物學做出貢獻，並為細胞命運工程鋪路。

17116325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17116325.value: 真核生物解旋酶激活的分子機制

17116325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116325.value: To initiate DNA replication, origin DNA must be melted and separated to produce templates for DNA synthesis. In eukaryotes, DNA replication begins from multiple sites distributed along each chromosome. Each initiation event is tightly regulated to ensure that the origin DNA is fired no more once per cell cycle. Mis-regulation of this process can lead to severe consequences, such as cancer and genetic diseases like Meier-Gorlin syndrome. Central to replication initiation is the assembly and activation of replicative helicases at replication origins. During the early G1 phase, Mcm2-7 complexes are loaded into an inactive head-to-head double hexamer (DH) that encircles duplex DNA. When the S phase begins, DDK (Dbf4-dependent kinase) and S-CDKs (S-cyclin dependent kinases) collaborate with Sld3, Sld7, Cdc45, and pre-loading complex (pre-LC) to drive origin firing. Sld3 plays a crucial role in recognising and binding to the DDK phosphorylated MCM-DH, facilitating Cdc45 recruitment with the help of Sld7. Following S-CDK phosphorylation, Sld3 acts as a scaffold to assemble pre-LC at origin DNA, culminating in the formation of two active Cdc45-MCM-GINS (CMG) helicases. Although the framework for helicase activation is becoming clear, the detailed mechanisms regulating this process remain elusive at a molecular level. Our recent cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the MCM-DH in complex with DDK have provided crucial insights into the role of DDK phosphorylation in helicase activation. Building upon this finding, the proposed project aims to investigate how the DDK-phosphorylated MCM-DH is further activated. Our preliminary results indicate that both Dbf4 and Mcm6 facilitate the docking of Sld7 dimer onto the MCM-DH, subsequently enabling a stable recruitment of Cdc45 and Sld3 at origin DNA. In this study, we will delve deeper into the mechanisms regulating helicase activation in both yeast and human. The successful completion of this research will significantly advance our understanding of replication initiation in both yeast and human systems. The information derived from this study will also shed lights on DNA replication related human diseases. 在真核生物DNA複製起始階段，染色體多個複製起點區域的雙股DNA需經歷解旋形成單股模板，此精密調控過程確保每個細胞週期中每個複製起點僅被活化一次。其調控異常與癌症發生及Meier-Gorlin症候群等遺傳性疾病有密切關係。 複製起始的核心事件是複製解旋酶複合體在起始位點的組裝與活化。在G1期早期，Mcm2-7複合物以非活性頭尾對接的雙六聚體（double hexamer, DH）形式裝載於雙股DNA。進入S期後，Dbf4依賴性激酶（DDK）和S期週期蛋白依賴性激酶（S-CDK）透過與Sld3、Sld7、Cdc45及預裝載複合體（pre-LC）的協同作用，啟動複製起點活化程序。其中，Sld3作為關鍵識別因子，在Sld7輔助下介導Cdc45的定向招募，並透過DDK磷酸化的MCM-DH複合體完成初始組裝。經S-CDK磷酸化修飾後，Sld3發揮支架蛋白功能，促進pre-LC複合體在起始DNA區域的結構重排，最後形成兩個具有解旋酶活性的Cdc45-MCM-GINS（CMG）複合體。 儘管解旋酶活化的整體框架已逐步明確，但其分子層面的精細調控網絡仍有待釐清。我們近期透過冷凍電鏡（cryo-EM）技術解析的MCM-DH與DDK複合物高解析度結構，為理解DDK磷酸化在解旋酶活化中的功能提供了關鍵結構基礎。基於此發現，本課題擬重點探討DDK磷酸化修飾的MCM-DH如何透過後續活化步驟形成活性解旋酶複合體。我們的初步研究顯示，Dbf4亞基與Mcm6亞基協同促進Sld7二聚體與MCM-DH的結合，此交互作用顯著增強Cdc45和Sld3在起始DNA區域的穩定性招募。本研究將系統解析酵母及人類系統中解旋酶活化的分子調控機制，透過結構生物學、生物化學及遺傳學多維度驗證，建構從MCM-DH裝載到CMG複合體形成的動態調控模型。研究的完成將深化對真核生物複製起始機制的理解，為DNA複製相關疾病的治療標靶開發提供重要理論基礎。

17117425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117425.value: 解析安老院長者皮膚與腸道微生物組在抗生素耐藥性及病原體動態演化中的作用

17117425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117425.value: Prof Poon, Leo Lit Man Prof Wu, Peng Prof Zhang, Tong

17117425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117425.value: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses an escalating threat among elderly populations, with AMR-related deaths in adults aged 70 and older rising by over 80% between 1990 and 2021. The COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated this issue by increasing antibiotic use and overwhelming healthcare systems globally. Elderly residents in nursing homes, particularly in densely populated areas like Hong Kong, are highly susceptible to infections by antibiotic-resistant bacteria and fungi. Despite increasing interest in gut microbiome research, the role of the skin microbiome in pathogen colonization, transmission and AMR development remains largely underexplored. Emerging evidence indicates that the skin may serve as a significant mediator for the transmission of high-risk pathogens, such as Candida auris, in healthcare settings. This study aims to test the hypothesis that the skin microbiome of elderly nursing home residents serves as a key reservoir for pathogen colonization, AMR development, and transmission, with interactions with healthcare workers further amplifying these risks. Task 1 will comprehensively profile microbial communities across skin and gut sites in elderly residents and healthcare workers in nursing homes, uncovering the ecological distribution of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and pathogens. Task 2 will develop absolute quantification methods to assess whether the skin acts as a critical reservoir for AMR genes and pathogens by mapping the absolute load and uncovering the genetic contexts linking AMR genes to their microbial hosts, in comparison to the gut. Task 3 will employ machine learning to assess whether the skin’s microbial taxa, AMR genes, and pathogen profiles can serve as potential predictors of frailty by identifying microbial markers and specific skin sites most closely linked to it for accurate and timely assessment. Task 4 will target emerging threats from Candida auris and ESKAPEE pathogens, investigating how their colonization and evolution on the skin drive AMR development in nursing homes. Task 5 will leverage high-resolution comparative genomics to track AMR and pathogen transmission among residents and healthcare workers in nursing homes, investigating whether the skin plays a central role in facilitating the spread of these pathogens. Together, these tasks will comprehensively explore the skin’s role in AMR development and pathogen dynamics among elderly residents and healthcare workers in nursing homes, providing critical insights for microbiome-based interventions and infection control strategies that promote healthy aging in Hong Kong's nursing homes and globally. 抗生素耐藥性（AMR）在老年人群中構成日益嚴重的威脅。1990年至2021年間，70歲及以上成人中與AMR相關的死亡人數增加了80%以上。新冠疫情進一步加劇了這一問題，導致抗生素使用增加，並對全球醫療系統造成巨大壓力。安老院中的老年居民，尤其是在香港等人口稠密地區，更易感染耐藥性細菌和真菌。儘管腸道微生物組的研究日益受到關注，但皮膚微生物組在病原體定植、傳播及耐藥性發展中的作用仍然鮮有探討。最新證據表明，皮膚可能是醫療環境下高風險病原體（如耳念珠菌）傳播的重要媒介。 本研究旨在驗證以下假設：安老院老年居民的皮膚微生物組是病原體定植、耐藥性發展及傳播的關鍵儲存庫，並且與醫護人員的互動可能加劇了這些風險。任務1將全面分析安老院老年居民與醫護人員皮膚和腸道不同部位的微生物群落，揭示抗菌藥物耐藥性和病原體的生態分佈。任務2將開發絕對定量方法，通過測定皮膚中AMR基因和病原體的絕對載量，並解析AMR基因與其微生物宿主之間的遺傳背景，與腸道進行對比，以評估皮膚是否為AMR基因和病原體的關鍵儲庫。任務3將利用機器學習，評估皮膚微生物分類群、AMR基因及病原體譜系是否能作為識別衰弱狀態的潛在預測因子，鑑定與衰弱密切相關的微生物標誌物及特定皮膚部位，實現準確及時的評估。任務4將聚焦耳念珠菌及ESKAPEE等致病菌威脅，研究其在皮膚上的定植和進化如何推動安老院中的AMR發展。任務5將利用高解析度比較基因組學，追蹤安老院居民與醫護人員之間AMR及病原體的傳播，探究皮膚在這些病原體傳播中的核心作用。 上述各項任務將全面探索皮膚在安老院老年居民與醫護人員中AMR發展及病原體動態中的作用，為基於微生物組的干預措施和感染防控策略提供關鍵見解，促進香港及全球安老院的健康老齡化。

17117525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117525.value: 基于疫情暴发背景下病毒系统发育树的流行病学参数估计

17117525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117525.value: Prof Cowling, Benjamin John Prof Tsang, Kam Lun Tim Dr Xie, Ruopeng

17117525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117525.value: The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the critical need for rapid, accurate estimation of epidemiological parameters to inform public health responses. This proposal aims to develop an innovative deep learning model, the Birth-Death model with Exposed-Infectious individuals and transmission Heterogeneity (BDEIH), specifically designed to estimate epidemiological parameters for SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern (VOCs). We aim to address the following key knowledge gaps: (1) the challenge of estimating epidemiological parameters when traditional data sources are biased or unavailable, and (2) the need for a comprehensive understanding of how control measures and evolving immune landscapes influence the dynamics of viral transmission. To achieve our objectives, we will conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported SARS-CoV-2 outbreaks and associated variants, supplemented by phylogenetic analysis using genomic sequences from GISAID. Our approach will incorporate factors such as cross-protective immunity and immune history, enabling the model to better reflect the complex interactions between viral strains and host immunity. We will leverage diverse phylogenetic tools and incorporate contact tracing data to enhance estimation reliability and capture transmission heterogeneity, basic reproduction numbers, incubation periods, and infectious periods. The adaptable BDEIH model will offer broad applications beyond SARS-CoV-2, extending to influenza and other respiratory viruses, including those in future pandemics. This research aims to uncover critical insights into the interplay of immune landscapes and control measures, guiding more effective public health interventions. Additionally, this research will engage with stakeholders in infectious disease epidemiology through workshops and collaborative initiatives, ensuring the practical utility of our findings. To enhance accessibility, we will develop documentation and open-source software, allowing for seamless integration of the BDEIH model into public health frameworks. Ultimately, our work will support global pandemic preparedness and help mitigate the societal disruptions caused by infectious disease outbreaks. 新型冠状病毒肺炎（COVID-19）大流行凸显了快速、准确估算流行病学参数对指导公共卫生应对的重要性和紧迫性。本研究拟开发一种新型深度学习模型——基于暴露-感染个体及传播异质性的出生-死亡模型（BDEIH），用于估算SARS-CoV-2关切变异株（VOCs）的关键流行病学参数。 本研究旨在解决两大科学问题：（1）传统数据来源受限时，如何准确估算流行病学参数；（2）如何系统评估防控措施与动态免疫格局对病毒传播动力学的影响。研究将整合已有的SARS-CoV-2疫情数据及相关变异株信息，结合公共数据库（如GISAID）的基因组序列，开展系统综述，荟萃分析，及系统发育分析。模型将纳入交叉免疫保护、免疫史等关键因素，以更精确地刻画病毒株与宿主免疫系统的相互作用机制。 本研究创新性地融合多种系统发育分析工具和接触者追踪数据，提升模型性能，精准量化传播异质性、基本再生数、潜伏期和传染期等核心流行病学参数。BDEIH模型具有广泛的适用性，不仅适用于SARS-CoV-2研究，还可拓展至流感等呼吸道病毒（包括未来大流行病原体）。 通过揭示免疫格局与防控措施的交互机制，本研究将为优化公共卫生干预策略提供科学依据。研究团队将与传染病流行病学领域的相关机构建立合作网络，通过专题研讨会等形式促进成果转化。为提升应用性，我们将开发配套的开源软件和技术文档，推动模型在公共卫生实践中的落地应用。本研究成果将为全球大流行防控准备工作提供技术支撑，助力减轻传染病大流行对社会的影响。

17117825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117825.value: 肝腎綜合徵的解碼：基於腎臟病理學與轉錄組學的啟示

17117825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117825.value: Prof Chan, Albert Chi-Yan Prof Chan, Tak Mao Prof Feng, Sandy Dr Fung, James Prof Seto, Wai Kay Walter Prof YAP, Desmond Yat Hin Prof Yuen, Man Fung

17117825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117825.value: Introduction Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS) is a serious problem for people with advanced liver disease, causing their kidneys to fail quickly. Diagnosing HRS is tough because these patients bleed easily, making it risky to take kidney biopsy. In 2019, the criteria for diagnosing HRS were updated to align with acute kidney injury (AKI) definitions. Our unpublished study showed that 50/54 (92.6%) kidney biopsies from liver transplant (LT) patients showed structural abnormalities, regardless of whether they had HRS AKI or not. Some patients never recover, challenging the idea that HRS AKI is functional and reversible. Knowledge Gaps The exact cause of HRS AKI is unknown. It was thought that LT could completely reverse it as kidneys looked normal in autopsies. There’s no data from living patients to confirm this. Traditional transcriptomic analyses lose spatial context, but single-cell spatial transcriptomics keeps it, providing insights into cellular and molecular signalling during AKI. Kidney cells at proximal tubule are especially vulnerable to AKI, and some might undergo changes that leads to chronic injury. Objectives: The study aims to challenge the beliefs that HRS AKI happens in normal-looking kidneys and is reversible post-transplant. It will explore unique transcriptomic signatures in HRS AKI patients. Clinical Objectives: 1. To disprove that HRS AKI develops in normal-looking kidneys by examining microscopic changes 2. To evaluate if these abnormal changes are reversible with a biopsy 3-month post-LT Mechanistic Objectives: 1. To define the spatial transcriptome pattern in kidney cells and understand their interaction in HKR AKI 2. To compare transcriptomic changes between HRS AKI and non-HRS AKI patients over time Research Method This 3-year study at Queen Mary Hospital will involve LT patients. Kidney biopsies will be taken at LT and 3 months later to observe microscopic and transcriptomic changes. Biomarkers will be monitored to improve diagnostic accuracy. Anticipated results: We anticipate a high percentage of structurally abnormalities in kidneys among LT patients, some microscopic findings will predispose to AKI and will affect the chance of kidney recovery. By studying individual kidney cells with state-of-the-art technology, we aim to find specific molecular patterns in HRS AKI and identify unique markers to improve understanding, diagnose, and treatment. Long-Term Impact: We hope to gain new insights and change what we think HRS AKI affects the kidneys. These findings could change how doctors diagnose and treat HRS AKI. The transcriptomic data could lead to identification of novel biomarkers and druggable target.

17117925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117925.value: 先鋒轉錄因子KLF4的功能解碼與調控機制優化研究

17117925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117925.value: Our body's 200 cell types share the same genetic blueprint. However, each cell type expresses a unique combination of genes, leading to their specialized shapes and functions. Genes not required in a given cell type are turned silent via epigenetic mechanisms that include the compaction of DNA within nucleosomes to reduce accessibility and the deposition of repressive chemical marks such as cytosine methylation. Pioneer transcription factors can read regulatory DNA information within silenced chromatin and switch them on to change cell identity. KLF4 is a crucial pioneer factor that directs cell fate during embryo development. KLF4 can bind nucleosomes as well as methylated DNA with high affinity which triggers demethylation, chromatin opening, and the re-activation of silenced genes. These molecular capabilities underpin its role as a reprogramming factor within defined cocktails of genes that are used to revert differentiated adult cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) which resemble blastocyst-derived embryonic stem cells. KLF4 is also used in direct lineage reprogramming to generate induced neural stem cells without passing through a pluripotent state. Despite its key roles in cell fate control and importance in biotechnological stem cell engineering, how KLF4 engages chromatinised DNA to activate genes remains an enigma. Our team has previously discovered how fellow pioneer factors SOX2 and OCT4 work together to change cell identity and designed engineered SOX and OCT factors that boost iPSC generation and enable technologies for next-generation stem cell models. In this project, we aim to depict how KLF4 binds silenced chromatin and re-engineer this activity. Next, we will disentangle how KLF4 variants pioneer cell fate decisions during somatic cell reprogramming toward iPSCs. Lastly, we will deploy re-designed KLF4 in next-generation epigenetic reprogramming systems aimed at the generation of human stem cells with a higher grade of pluripotency that can also form cells that surround the embryo such as the placenta. A further application of boosted KLF4 will be in the partial reprogramming of cells toward a more youthful state. Our multidisciplinary approach brings together high-resolution cryogenic electron microscopy, protein design, epigenetic profiling, and stem cell engineering. The project team has successfully used these approaches and enhanced other pioneer factors via protein engineering and already discovered candidate KLF4 variants with modified methylation reader functions. Our project seeks to uncover the molecular basis of how a crucial pioneer factor regulates gene activity and find variants that could improve epigenetic engineering and advance stem cell technologies. 人體200餘種細胞類型共享相同的遺傳訊息藍圖，而不同的細胞類型則透過特異性基因表現模式以實現功能特化。表觀遺傳調控機制透過染色質壓縮形成核小體以限制DNA可及性，並施加胞嘧啶甲基化等抑制性修飾，從而沉默特定細胞類型中的非必需基因。先鋒轉錄因子，是一類能夠辨識沉默染色質中調控元件，具有啟動細胞身份轉換的核心功能的轉錄因子。研究發現，KLF4作為關鍵性先鋒因子，在胚胎發育過程中透過高親和力結合核小體及甲基化DNA，觸發DNA去甲基化、染色質開放及基因激活，此分子特性使其成為細胞重編程過程中所需的核心因子：在誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）生成中，KLF4可協同特定基因組合使終末分化細胞逆轉為類囊胚來源的胚胎幹細胞狀態；在直接譜系重編程中，可不經多能態階段直接誘導終末分化細胞生成神經幹細胞。然而，KLF4如何特異性辨識染色質化DNA並活化基因的分子機制仍是未解之謎。本團隊前期已解析SOX2/OCT4先鋒因子協同調控細胞認同轉換的分子機制，並成功設計人工定向進化的SOX/OCT蛋白提升iPSC的生成效率，開發了新一代幹細胞模型建構技術。本計畫擬進行：1）透過冷凍電鏡技術解析KLF4與沉默染色質的動態互作機制，並基於其結構資訊進行功能重構；2）系統解析KLF4變體在體細胞向iPSC重編程過程中引導細胞命運決定的分子路徑；3）將優化設計的KLF4變體整合至新一代表觀遺傳重編程系統，用於製備具有胚胎外組織（如胎盤）分化潛能的高品質多能幹細胞，並探索其透過部分重編程以應用於促進衰老細胞年輕化。本研究將整合冷凍電子顯微鏡結構解析、蛋白質工程理性設計、表觀組學分析及幹細胞工程等跨領域技術。專案團隊已成功運用此技術體系完成多類先鋒因子功能增強，並已篩選獲得具有甲基化閱讀功能修飾的KLF4候選變體。本計畫旨在揭示KLF4調控基因活性的分子基礎，開發可提升表觀遺傳工程效率的功能變體，為幹細胞技術創新提供理論支撐與技術儲備。

17118325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17118325.value: 闡明人類輸卵管精子庫形成的機制與功能

17118325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17118325.value: Dr Lee, Cheuk Lun Dr Leung, Erica T.Y. Dr Li, Hang Wun Raymond

17118325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118325.value: In many mammalian species, including humans, the oviduct functions as a sperm reservoir which is created by the binding of sperm to oviductal epithelial cells (OECs). This interaction is a species-specific event that involves the recognition of defined carbohydrates exposed on the OEC by carbohydrate-binding proteins located on the sperm head. Our previous study demonstrated that sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5), a carbohydrate-binding protein on spermatozoa, is responsible for adhesion to OECs in humans. Sperm reservoir formation in the oviduct serves to ensure a suitable number of fertilization-competent sperm will be available around ovulation. While bound to OECs, sperm are maintained in a quiescent state, prolonging their fertile lifespan. Adhesion to the oviduct also plays a key role in selecting sperm with superior morphology, normal chromatin structure, and superior fertilization ability. This selection process ensures that only high-quality sperm will be able to bind to OECs in preparation for fertilization. Most of our knowledge on the role of the sperm reservoir in fertilization comes from studies in non-human mammals. The functions and mechanism of sperm reservoir formation in humans are unknown, mainly due to the ethical limitations of experimental studies with human oviducts and the lack of a standardized assay to evaluate spermatozoa-OEC interactions. To address these challenges, we established a novel 3D apical-out OEC organoid-binding assay for studying spermatozoa-OEC interactions in humans. We hypothesize that sFUT5-mediated adhesion to OECs plays a vital role in preserving the fertilization potential of human sperm and selecting spermatozoa endowed with superior fertilization competence. This hypothesis will be tested by studying the mechanism and functions of the spermatozoa-OEC interactions and by correlating this with the fertility competence of spermatozoa. The outcome of this project will increase our understanding of the mechanism of oviductal sperm reservoir formation in humans. Clinically, these results indicate the possible use of the spermatozoa-OEC interactions for prolonging/enhancing sperm fertilizing ability in assisted reproduction technology (ART). The findings will also indicate the use of the sperm surface OEC-binding protein level and/or OEC binding ability as a sperm function test for predicting fertilization potential of semen samples. Moreover, the treatment of human subfertility with ART bypasses the natural processes for selecting high-quality spermatozoa in the female genital tract. Therefore, another potential application of this proposal is that it may clarify whether the spermatozoa-OEC interactions can be exploited clinically as natural tool for functional sperm selection. 在包括人類在內的多種哺乳動物中，輸卵管可作為精子儲存庫，其形成機制依賴精子與輸卵管上皮細胞（OEC）的結合。這一相互作用具有物種特異性，涉及精子頭部的碳水化合物結合蛋白識別OEC表面特定的碳水化合物。我們先前的研究發現，精子表面的岩藻糖基轉移酶-5（sFUT5）是一種碳水化合物結合蛋白，負責介導人類精子與OEC的黏附。 精子庫的形成有助於在排卵前後維持足夠數量、具有受精能力的精子。當精子與OEC結合後會保持靜止，進而延長精子的生育壽命。此外，這個結合過程能夠篩選出形態優良、染色質結構正常且受精能力強的精子，為受精做準備。透過這項篩選，只有高品質的精子能夠與OEC結合，進而參與受精。 目前，我們對精子庫在受精過程中的作用主要基於非人類哺乳動物的研究。由於倫理限制和缺乏標準化檢測方法，人類精子庫的功能及形成機制尚不清楚。為解決這些問題，我們建立了一種創新的3D頂端外向OEC類器官結合檢測方法，用於研究人類精子與OEC的相互作用。 我們假設，sFUT5介導的精子與OEC結合對於維持精子的受精能力並篩選出高品質精子具有關鍵作用。我們將透過探索精子—OEC相互作用的機制與功能，並將其與精子的生育能力關聯，來驗證這個假設。 本計畫的研究成果將加深對人類輸卵管精子庫形成機制的理解。在臨床上，這些發現將提示精子—OEC的相互作用有可能用於輔助生殖技術（ART）中，以延長或增強精子的受精能力。此外，精子表面OEC結合蛋白的表達量及其與OEC的結合能力，可望作為評估精子功能和預測受精潛力的指標。由於ART治療繞過了女性生殖道中對高品質精子的自然篩選過程，本研究也將探討精子—OEC交互作用在臨床上作為功能性精子篩選工具的可行性。

17118425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17118425.value: 種植體周圍巨噬細胞透過 PGE2-EP4 信號傳導激活痛覺神經以促進骨整合

17118425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17118425.value: Prof Chow, Billy Kwok Chong Prof Yeung, Kelvin Wai Kwok

17118425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118425.value: Sensory nerves richly innervate the alveolar bone to perceive and respond to noxious stimuli. One of the major recent breakthroughs in bone research is the discovery of the role of sensory nerves in controlling bone homeostasis. Although histological and neurophysiological evidence has confirmed the presence of neurosensory fibers around the dental implants, it remains unclear how they contribute to new bone formation and remodelling in the peri-implant region. Our recent works have demonstrated that the innate immune response triggered by bone injury and biomaterials could modulate the sensory nerves through pain-mediating cytokine prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). Disruption of macrophage-driven innate immune response or peripheral neural sensation result in impaired bone regeneration. We hypothesize that the bone injury caused by surgical procedures for osteotomy preparation and dental implant placement can lead to the release of PGE2 from bone macrophage, which sensitizes peri-implant nociceptive nerves through E-type prostanoid 4 (EP4) receptor to trigger calcium influx through transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1). The activation of this immune-neural axis is critical to bone regeneration and bone mass maintenance around dental implants. Our preliminary data has shown that selective depletion of macrophage or sensory nerve could impair peri-implant new bone formation. Moreover, pharmaceutical manipulation of macrophage-derived PGE2 could regulate peri-implant sensation and bone regeneration outcome. This proposal aims to further test our hypothesis through the following objectives: (1) to confirm the role of PGE2 in mediating peri-implant nociceptive sensation through conditional knockout of its receptor EP4 in sensory nerves; (2) to study the effects of PGE2-induced neuromodulation on peri-implant new bone formation by comparing the influences of sensory neurons with or without EP4 on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis; (3) to investigate the mechanism through which PGE2-activated EP4 interacts with transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) to regulate the neuronal functionality. The significance of the findings arising from this proposal is enormous as it will lead to a paradigm shift in the clinical practice of implant dentistry and will reshape the future design of advanced dental implants. 感覺神經豐富地支配牙槽骨，負責感知並回應有害刺激。近年來，感覺神經在調控骨代謝平衡中的作用已成為骨科研究領域的一項重大突破。儘管組織學和神經生理學證據已確認牙科植體周圍存在感覺神經，但其在新骨形成與重塑中的具體作用仍不甚明了。我們的最新研究表明，骨損傷及生物材料引發的固有免疫反應，能通過疼痛介導的炎症因子前列腺素E2（PGE2）刺激感覺神經。阻斷巨噬細胞介導的固有免疫反應或周邊感覺神經，均會干擾骨的再生過程。因此，我們假設，在準備植牙窩和植入種植體的過程中引發的骨損傷，會促使骨髓巨噬細胞釋放PGE2，後者通過E型前列腺素受體4（EP4）作用于周圍痛覺神經，並激活瞬時受體電位香草醇（TRPV1），導致鈣離子流入。這一免疫-神經軸的激活對於骨再生及植體周圍骨量的維持具有關鍵作用。我們的初步數據顯示，選擇性敲除巨噬細胞或感覺神經，均會顯著影響植體周圍的新骨形成。此外，藥物調控巨噬細胞源性PGE2的作用，也能調節植體周圍的感覺神經反應和骨再生。本研究計劃旨在通過以下幾個目標，進一步驗證我們的假設：(1) 通過條件性敲除感覺神經中的EP4受體，確認PGE2在調節植體周圍痛覺刺激中的作用；(2) 比較EP4在感覺神經對骨形成與破骨作用中的影響，研究PGE2誘導的神經調節對植體周圍新骨形成的影響；(3) 探討PGE2激活的EP4如何與TRPV1互作，從而調控神經元功能。這些研究成果具有重要意義，有望推動臨床種植牙科理念的變革，並指導未來新型牙科植體的設計方向。

17119625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17119625.value: 負性病徵在抗藥性精神分裂症患者中的重要角色：十八個月前瞻性縱向研究

17119625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17119625.value: Prof Chan, Raymond Chor-kiu Prof Chang, Wing Chung Prof SHAM, Pak-Chung Prof SO, Hon-cheong

17119625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119625.value: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) is characterized by persistent psychotic symptoms, functional impairments, and poor response to non-clozapine antipsychotics. Around one-fifth of first-episode schizophrenia patients develop treatment-resistance, usually within five years after onset. Although Kane’s criteria defined TRS based on positive symptoms, the latest TRRIP criteria recognized negative and cognitive symptoms. However, the extant literature on these two important features in TRS patients has limitations. First, although negative symptoms were associated with poor social functioning in TRS patients, previous research was limited by chronic TRS samples and lacked longitudinal evidence. Moreover, previous research found negative symptoms and cognitive deficits in chronic TRS patients, but seldom applied second-generation negative symptom scales to optimize assessments, nor included “hot” (emotion-related) cognitive domains which would be closely related to negative symptoms. Third, negative symptoms emerge early before schizophrenia onset and may exacerbate as the disorder progresses, but it remains unclear whether the early trajectories of negative symptoms would differ between TRS and remitted schizophrenia patients. This prospective cohort study aims to examine the effects of baseline negative symptoms, “hot” and “cool” executive functions on 18-month functional outcomes in recently-emerged TRS patients. We also track the 18-month trajectories of negative symptoms in TRS and remitted schizophrenia patients. We will recruit 80 TRS patients on clozapine and 80 remitted schizophrenia patients with <5 years of illness from a well-established early psychosis intervention programme. To assess negative symptoms, we apply second-generation scales at baseline, sixth, twelfth and eighteenth month. Moreover, we adopt Miyake’s three-factor model of executive functions to assess the inhibition, shifting and updating components, and use six laboratory-based paradigms to measure the corresponding “cool” and “hot” domains of these components at baseline and eighteenth month. Clinical patients’ executive functions will be compared with those of 50 healthy controls to ascertain deficits. We apply clinician-rated and performance-based functional measures at baseline and eighteenth month. Regression models will be used to examine the impacts of baseline negative symptoms and executive function deficits on 18-month functional outcomes in TRS patients. We compare the trajectories of negative symptoms between TRS and remitted schizophrenia patients. Our expected findings will clarify the role of negative symptoms, “hot” and “cool” executive function deficits in recently-emerged TRS patients, and characterize their early trajectory of negative symptoms, paving ways for timely interventions. 當兩種或以上的非氯氮平藥物不能改善思覺失調病徵，患者出現功能障礙，醫生稱之為抗藥性精神分裂症（TRS）。約五分之一的首發精神分裂症患者會在五年左右出現 TRS。雖然過往醫生常以正性病徵來定義 TRS，但最新的 TRRIP 準測亦會考慮負性病徵和認知功能缺損。然而，過去有關 TRS 患者中這兩項重要特徵的研究，存在不少局限。首先，儘管負性病徵與 TRS 患者的社會功能障礙相關，但先前研究大多採用長期的 TRS 患者為樣本，缺乏相關的縱向證據。其次，雖然早前的研究中已經發現長期 TRS 患者有負性病徵和認知功能缺損，但很少採用新一代的負性病徵量表。再者，過往的研究側重‘冷’認知功能，而忽略與負性病徵密切相關的“熱”（情感相關）認知功能。最後，負性病徵會在精神分裂症的早期出現，並隨病情進展而惡化。但過去研究没有解答負性病徵會否在 TRS 患者和對藥物反應良好的精神分裂症患者之間存在差異。有見及此，我們設計了這個前瞻性縱向研究，探討基線負性病徵、“冷”和“熱”執行功能對 TRS 患者十八個月後的功能有何影響。另外，我們會同時追蹤 TRS 患者和對藥物反應良好的精神分裂症患者在十八個月內的負性病徵，比較兩組的軌跡變化。我們將招募80名使用氯氮平的早期 TRS 患者和80名患病時間少於五年，亦對藥物反應良好的精神分裂症患者。我們會使用新一代的負性病徵量表，在基線、六個月、十二個月和十八個月進行評估。此外，我們採用 Miyake 的三因素模型來評估執行功能中的抑制、轉換與更新功能。為了評估相應的“冷”和“熱”範疇，我們使用六個範式去測量其基線和十八個月的執行功能。與此同時，我們亦會評估兩組患者的社會功能。本研究亦會招募50名健康對照者，去比較患者的執行功能是否存在缺損。數據將以迴歸模型進行分析，了解負性病徵和執行功能缺損對 TRS 患者在十八個月後的功能結果的影響。我們亦會以比較模型，分析 TRS 患者與對藥物反應較好的患者之間是否存在負性病徵差異和軌跡變化。研究結果將闡明負性病徵，“冷” 和“熱”執行功能缺損在早期 TRS 患者中的作用，並捕捉其負性病徵的早期軌跡，為及時治療提供理論基礎。

17120225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17120225.value: 膽汁酸代謝物熊去氧膽酸調節胰臟腺癌抗腫瘤免疫的研究

17120225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17120225.value: Prof Feng, Yibin Prof Xian, Yanfang

17120225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120225.value: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is the seventh leading cancer-related death worldwide, with limited treatment options available. The immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TIME) of PAAD, in which infiltration and function of antitumoral CD8+ cytotoxic T cells are compromised, facilitates tumour immune evasion and promotes cancer progression. Recently, gut microbiome was shown to play a role in shaping immunosuppressive TIME in PAAD by regulating the endogenous metabolite profiles. In our preliminary study, we analysed gut microbiota of healthy subjects and PAAD patients. We found that abundance of microbes involved in secondary bile acid metabolism was reduced in PAAD patients. We also observed changes in the bile acid profile in PAAD patients; especially, the levels of gut-derived bile acid metabolite ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) are reduced in PAAD patients. This was corroborated by the observation of lower UDCA production in germ-free mice transplanted with faeces from PAAD patients. Interestingly, immunocompetent mice bearing orthotopic pancreatic tumours presented a reduced tumour size following faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy subjects, indicating an immune-mediated antitumour effect. This effect was not observed in immunodeficient mice following FMT. UDCA treatment of immunocompetent mice led to a reduction in tumour size, which was consistent with the expansion of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, as shown by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis. Metabolites of the faecal microbiome or UDCA had minimal effects on the in vitro proliferation or survival of pancreatic tumour cells. However, we observed direct induction of the CD8+ cell population in vitro, in which UDCA increased the degree of chromatin opening in tcf1 super-enhancer regions and induced the association between TCF1 protein and β-catenin. Based on the literature study and our pilot data, we hypothesise that the gut-derived bile acid metabolite UDCA enhances antitumour immunity in PAAD by maintaining the CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell population and function, thereby reversing tumour progression. This proposal encompasses four specific aims: (i) to systematically evaluate the clinicopathological significance of gut-derived UDCA in PAAD; (ii) to characterise the role of UDCA in boosting antitumour immunity in PAAD by promoting CD8+ CTL re-invigoration; (iii) to explore the mechanism by which UDCA maintains CD8+ CTL persistence; and (iv) to assess the efficacy and safety of UDCA in combination therapy with ICIs. This study may provide a novel therapeutic avenue for PAAD that involves the modulation of the gut microbiome and its metabolic products and may provide insights into the use of UDCA as adjuvant therapy in PAAD management. 胰腺腺癌（PAAD）是全球第七大癌症相關死因，且治療選擇有限。PAAD的免疫抑制性腫瘤微環境（TIME）會削弱抗腫瘤CD8+細胞毒性T細胞的浸潤與功能，促進腫瘤免疫逃逸及癌症進展。近期研究顯示，腸道微生物組可通過調節內源性代謝物譜，在塑造PAAD免疫抑制性TIME中發揮作用。在我們初步研究中，我們分析了健康人群與PAAD患者的腸道菌群，發現PAAD患者體內參與次級膽酸代謝的微生物豐度降低，且其膽酸代謝譜發生改變，尤其是腸道來源的膽酸代謝物熊去氧膽酸（UDCA）水平顯著下降。此結果與無菌小鼠移植PAAD患者糞便後UDCA生成減少的現象一致。值得注意的是，接受健康受試者糞便微生物群移植（FMT）的免疫健全小鼠，其原位胰腺腫瘤體積縮小，顯示出免疫介導的抗腫瘤效應，而此效應在免疫缺陷小鼠中未見。UDCA治療免疫健全小鼠亦能縮小腫瘤，單細胞RNA測序分析顯示此現象與CD8+細胞毒性T細胞擴增相關。體外實驗中，糞便微生物代謝物或UDCA對胰腺腫瘤細胞增殖與存活影響甚微，但我們觀察到UDCA可直接誘導CD8+細胞群體擴增，其機制涉及增加tcf1超級增強子區域的染色質開放程度，並促進TCF1蛋白與β-catenin的結合。基於文獻與初步數據，我們提出假說：腸道來源的膽酸代謝物UDCA通過維持CD8+細胞毒性T細胞的數量與功能，增強PAAD抗腫瘤免疫，從而逆轉腫瘤進展。本計畫包含四大目標：(i) 系統性評估腸道來源UDCA在PAAD中的臨床病理學意義；(ii) 闡明UDCA通過促進CD8+ CTL再活化增強PAAD抗腫瘤免疫的作用；(iii) 探索UDCA維持CD8+ CTL持續存在的分子機制；(iv) 評估UDCA聯合免疫檢查點抑制劑（ICIs）的療效與安全性。此研究或為PAAD開闢調控腸道微生物組及其代謝產物的新型治療途徑，並為UDCA作為PAAD輔助治療提供理論依據。

17121125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17121125.value: 透過超快超聲成像揭示舒張期心肌振動波：對心肌被動彈性的新見解

17121125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121125.value: Myocardial passive stiffness is an intrinsic property of the heart muscle in its non-contracting state. This property is vital for regulating the heart’s electrical and mechanical functions. When impaired, it can lead to serious conditions, e.g., diastolic heart failure. Conventional methods of measuring passive stiffness, like tensile testing and pressure-volume analysis, are destructive or invasive. The emergence of acoustic-radiation-force-based shear wave elastography and natural shear wave imaging offers noninvasive ways to estimate local myocardial stiffness. However, the former raises safety concerns regarding acoustic energy and has a limited ability to interrogate deeper heart wall segments. The latter uses vibrational waves generated during valve closure and atrial contraction phases, which do not correspond to the actual passive state. Safer and more comprehensive methods for assessing myocardial passive stiffness throughout the heart wall are still lacking. Recently, our research team discovered myocardial vibrational waves during the diastasis phase of the cardiac cycle, termed the diastasis wave, in a large elderly cohort. This discovery presents a unique opportunity to evaluate passive stiffness due to the diastasis’ calm and slow heart activity. Our initial findings revealed that the diastasis wave speed is a more sensitive indicator than the clinical E/E’ ratio in distinguishing between hypertensive and normal hearts. Nonetheless, the origin of the natural diastasis wave and its direct relationship with myocardial passive stiffness remains unclear. To further explore the diastasis wave, we propose leveraging our patented ultrafast ultrasound imaging technology, which can seamlessly integrate into standard ultrasound systems. We will first develop a comprehensive framework, including automated segmentation, spatial registration, and frequency-domain analysis, for detecting, analyzing, and understanding the diastasis wave. We will then investigate the origin of the diastasis wave using an ex vivo isolated working rodent heart model, which is a controlled physiological setting and provides an excellent acoustic access to the heart for high-resolution, artifact-free mapping of wave propagation paths in three dimensions. This will provide valuable insights into regional variations of myocardial passive stiffness and offer an imaging tool for pinpointing myocardial abnormality. Lastly, we aim to define a baseline wave speed range in healthy young adults by establishing the relationship between the diastasis wave and myocardial passive stiffness in humans. This research is envisioned to advance our understanding of myocardial passive stiffness of the intact heart in vivo, transform cardiac diagnostics, improve patient outcomes, inform personalized intervention strategies, and progress preventive cardiology. 心肌被動彈性是心臟肌肉在非收縮狀態下的固有特性。此特性對調節心臟的電與力學行為至關重要，一旦受損，可能引發嚴重病症（如舒張性心衰竭）。傳統測量被動彈性的方法（如拉伸測試與壓力-體積分析）具破壞性或侵入性。基於聲輻射力的剪切波彈性成像與自然剪切波成像技術為當前能提供非侵入性評估局部心肌彈性的途徑。然而，前者存在聲波能量安全疑慮且對深層的心壁檢測能力有限，後者則利用瓣膜閉合與心房收縮期產生的振動波，未能反映心肌真實被動狀態。因此，目前尚缺乏可安全評估心肌被動彈性的全面性方法。 近期，本團隊於大型老年族群中發現心動週期舒張間期存在心肌振動波，在此稱其為「舒張間期波」。舒張間期心臟活動平緩，為評估被動彈性提供獨特契機。初步研究顯示，舒張間期波速較臨床E/E’比值更能敏感區分高血壓心臟與正常心臟。然而，此自然舒張間期波的起源及其與心肌被動彈性的直接關聯仍不明確。 為深入探究舒張間期波，本研究擬運用本團隊可無縫接軌標準超聲系統的超快速超聲成像專利技術。首先將建立整合自動分割、空間配準與頻域分析的完整框架，以偵測、解析並解讀舒張間期波；其次採用離體隔離囓齒類心臟模型（具可控環境與優異聲學穿透性），進行高解析、無偽影的三維波傳播路徑成像，釐清舒張間期波起源。此舉將揭示心肌被動彈性的區域異質性，並提供精準定位心肌異常的成像工具。最終透過建立人體舒張間期波與心肌被動剛度關聯，確立健康青壯年基準波速範圍。 本研究成果預期將：深化活體完整心臟心肌被動彈性認知、革新心臟診斷技術、改善患者預後、指引個人化介入策略，並推進預防性心臟醫學發展。

17121325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17121325.value: 靶向胰泌素受體開發抗肥胖藥物

17121325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121325.value: Obesity is a global health crisis, causing comorbidities and increased mortality rates. Current treatments, such as bariatric surgery, are invasive and associated with significant risks, highlighting the pressing need for effective and safe pharmacological interventions. Secretin (SCT), a classical gastrointestinal hormone, has recently emerged as a promising candidate for anti-obesity therapy due to its pleiotropic beneficial effects on energy homeostasis in multiple tissues including promoting lipolysis, suppressing appetite, inducing satiety, and activating brown adipose tissue thermogenesis. Multiple studies collectively indicated that SCT may combat obesity by reducing energy intake and increasing energy expenditure. However, the therapeutic application of SCT peptide is hindered by its very short half-life of only several minutes in circulation. Our laboratory has recently identified a small molecule positive allosteric modulator (PAM) Purmorphamine (Pur) of the secretin receptor (SCTR), which potentiate effects of the SCT but with a much longer half-life (8 hours in mouse). The drug was tested and showed minimal toxicity effects under chronic and sub-chronic treatments at very high doses in mouse (250-500 mg/Kg). In diet-induced obese mice, sub-chronic Pur oral gavage at 10-20 mg/kg reduces body weight, optimizes body composition, improves glucose tolerance, increases energy expenditure when compared to controls. In addition, it potentiates actions of SCT on mitochondrial respiration and lipolysis in fat cells. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that Pur functions as a PAM targeting SCTR to enhance the pleiotropic functions of SCT signaling in various effector organs to combat obesity. The proposed project aims to investigate mechanisms of Pur in promoting weight loss and improving energy balance, in order to develop Pur as a valuable lead compound for anti-obesity treatment. We propose to study its functions in lipolysis, thermogenesis, and nutrient absorption, and to investigate the neural substrate involved. This study will provide critical insights into the potential of targeting SCT/SCTR pathway in weight management, ultimately contribute to the alleviation of the global obesity epidemic and its associated comorbidities. 肥胖已成為全球性健康危機，導致多種併發症並提高死亡率。目前治療方式，如減重手術，具有侵入性且伴隨顯著風險，凸顯出對有效且安全的藥理介入之迫切需求。胰泌素（secretin, SCT）作為首個發現的胃腸激素，近期因其在代謝方面的多重有益作用而成為抗肥胖療法的潛力候補，包括促進脂質分解、抑制食慾、誘導飽足感，以及活化棕色脂肪組織的生熱作用。然而，SCT的治療應用受限於其在體循環中的極短半衰期。本實驗室已突破性地發現胰泌素受體（SCTR）的正向異位調節劑——普爾莫啡胺（purmorphamine, Pur），其可強化SCT的肽效應並具備較佳穩定性，從而克服原生SCT的侷限。初步研究顯示，慢性Pur治療可降低飲食誘導肥胖（DIO）小鼠的體重、優化體組成，並改善葡萄糖穩態。基於這些發現，我們假設Pur可強化SCT訊號在各效應器官的多重功能，從而調控代謝穩態並緩解肥胖。本計畫旨在揭示Pur促進減重及改善能量平衡的未知機制，並將其定位為開發新型抗肥胖藥物的寶貴先導化合物。透過全面評估Pur對代謝的影響、闡明其調控脂解、生熱及營養吸收的分子機制，以及探討其在下丘腦的靶點與神經回路調控，本研究將提供靶向SCT訊號途徑的關鍵洞見，以利於未來減重策略的開發，最終有助於減輕全球肥胖流行及其相關併發症，並深化對能量穩態複雜神經內分泌機制的理解。

17121525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17121525.value: 全球暖化與夜間人造光對亞熱帶飛蛾的複合影響

17121525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121525.value: Urbanization is known to reduce insect abundance and diversity, but it remains unclear how specific traits are filtered and therefore potentially important in rendering species vulnerable to additional global change threats. This is particularly true for subtropical and tropical ecosystems which are home to a high diversity of insect species who may be particularly sensitive to climate change impacts. Meanwhile, the effects of light pollution, or artificial light at night, on tropical insects are also poorly documented. In this study we’ll collect species trait data and community data across environmental gradients for the moths of Hong Kong to test the following hypotheses: H1) urbanization is predicted to lead to a predominance of thermal generalists, and H2) artificial light at night is also predicted to favour thermal generalists, and finally H3) forest sites with denser and more closed canopy are more likely to host unique species and species that are thermally sensitive. We’ll sample moths across an urbanization gradient (H1) that includes near-urban and urban-distant sites and use a combination of light traps and fruit-baited traps to document the associated moth communities. We’ll also collect moths and run experiments to determine thermal traits (e.g., thermal preference, takeoff temperature, and species temperature index). Additionally, we’ll set artificial lights near the distant-urban sites and sample moths at those sites to allow for a comparison of light pollution impacts on moths (H2). Finally, we’ll analyze LiDAR and remote sensing data to determine how vegetation structure and landscape context influences the recorded moths and their traits (H3). Altogether this sampling of moths (and their traits) within this comparative and experimental framework will allow for an important understanding of how urbanization and light pollution affect subtropical insects. The focus on thermal traits will additionally provide a perspective on the sensitivity of these communities to warming, and specifically how multiple global change drivers (artificial light at night, and land-use change/urbanization) may compound one another with adverse implications for tropical insect biodiversity. 城市化已知會降低昆蟲數量和多樣性，但我們不了解城市化是如何篩選物種特徵，進而影響物種應對各種全球變化威脅的能力。在亞熱帶和熱帶生態系統中，昆蟲物種非常多樣，物種對氣候變化可能特別敏感，光害（即夜間人造光）的影響也鮮有紀錄，所以城市化對熱帶昆蟲的潛在影響可能尤為重要。在此研究項目中，我們將在香港橫跨不同環境梯度的地點，收集飛蛾的物種特徵和群落數據，以測試以下假設：一）城市化將有利熱適應泛化種；二）夜間人造光同樣將有利熱適應泛化種；三）茂密的森林將擁有更多獨特的物種和熱適應特化種。我們會分別在接近和遠離城市的地點，以光誘捕燈和果餌誘捕器收集蛾類，以記錄城市化梯度上（假設一）的飛蛾群落，並在收集得來的飛蛾上進行實驗，測定牠們的熱適應特徵（如熱偏好、起飛溫度與物種溫度指數）。此外，我們會在遠離城市的地點設置人造光源，並在這些地點採集蛾類，以探討光害對飛蛾的影響（假設二）。最後，我們會分析光學雷達和其他遙感數據，以研究植被結構和生境對飛蛾群落和其特徵的作用（假設三）。總體而言，此項目將通過對蛾類及其特徵的比較研究和實驗，認識城市化與光害如何影響亞熱帶昆蟲；並透過測定飛蛾的熱適應特徵，了解飛蛾群落在全球暖化下的脆弱性，以及不同全球變化趨勢（如夜間人造光、土地變化和城市化）相互疊加下為熱帶地區昆蟲多樣性帶來的挑戰。

17122025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17122025.value: 早期治療策略與復發對首發性思覺失調長期影響的隨訪研究

17122025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17122025.value: Dr Chan, Sherry Kit-wa Dr Chang, Wing-chung Prof Chen, Yu Hai Eric Dr Lee, Edwin Ho-ming Dr Suen, Yi Nam

17122025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122025.value: Schizophrenia is a chronic illness often requiring long-term antipsychotic treatment, but many patients express concerns about its impact on quality of life and functional outcomes. Understanding how early medication decisions, such as discontinuation and dosage adjustments, influence long-term outcomes is critical for informed clinical decision-making. A randomised controlled trial (RCT) was done between 2003 and 2006, 178 first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients in remission were randomized into maintenance and discontinuation groups, following at least one year of continuous antipsychotic treatment. A 10-year follow-up found that discontinuing medication after two years increased the risk of poor outcomes, leading to recommendations to continue treatment for at least three years. However, studies that examine early medication stratifies show mixed results: some associate early drug reduction with improved long-term recovery, while others link early discontinuation to poorer outcomes, including persistent symptoms and suicide. Longer-term outcomes must be assessed to determine whether these recommendations should be adjusted. Cognitive impairments are a central feature of psychosis, significantly affecting recovery and social functioning. These deficits often persist, with limited understanding of how long-term cognitive trajectories relate to early medication decisions. Recent research highlights the heterogeneity of cognitive functioning in psychosis, suggesting that subgroups of patients experience varying degrees of cognitive change over time. Identifying predictors of cognitive stability or decline, including clinical, demographic, or treatment factors, could help tailor early interventions to prevent cognitive deterioration and improve outcomes. This proposed 20-year follow-up study will examine the longitudinal impact of early medication discontinuation on clinical, cognitive, and psychosocial outcomes in FEP patients. By conducting detailed assessments through interviews and case reviews, we will track outcomes across several points: baseline, 1-year after RCT, 10-year follow-up, and the current 20-year follow-up. The study will evaluate the long-term effects of early medication strategies and antipsychotic medication during the course of illness, providing crucial insights into recovery pathways and informing personalized treatment approaches for psychosis. Meanwhile, we also aim to examine the longitudinal cognitive trajectories of FEP patients, and how they relate to clinical and functional outcomes at 20 years. 思覺失調症是一種精神疾病，往往需要長期抗精神病藥物治療，但許多患者對生活品質和功能的影響表示擔憂。理解早期用藥決策（如停藥與劑量調整）如何影響長期結果，對於臨床知情決策至關重要。2003年至2006年期間進行了一項隨機對照試驗（RCT），將178名處於緩解期和已持續服藥至少一年的首發思覺失調（FEP）患者隨機分配至持續服藥組（89名）與停藥組（89名）。 10年的研究顯示，在治療兩年後停藥會增加不良結果的風險，因此建議至少持續治療三年。然而，關於早期用藥策略的研究結果並不一致：部分研究發現早期減藥與長期康復改善有關（包括減少持續症狀和自殺風險），但也有另一些研究指出早期停藥與較差的結果相關。因此為了判斷現有建議是否需要調整，必須評估更長期的成效。 認知功能障礙是思覺失調病的特徵之一，對康復與社會功能有重大影響。這些損害往往持續存在，但長期認知功能軌跡與早期用藥決策的相關性尚不清楚。近期研究強調了精神病認知功能的多樣性，提示不同患者群體在認知變化上有差異。識別認知功能穩定或惡化的預測因素（包括臨床、人口統計或治療因素），有助於制定早期介入方案，以防止認知惡化並改善成效。 本研究擬進行一項20年隨訪，探討早期停藥對FEP患者臨床、認知功能及社會心理的縱向影響。我們將透過訪談與病歷回顧方式，在多個時間點（基線、RCT後1年、10年追蹤以及當前 20 年追蹤）進行詳細評估。這研究將評估早期用藥策略與疾病過程中抗精神病藥物治療的長期作用，為復康道路提供關鍵見解，並為思覺失調的個人化治療提供參考方法。同時，我們也將檢視FEP患者的長期認知功能變化軌跡，以及其與20年時臨床和功能的關聯。

17122625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17122625.value: 改變口服三氧化二砷用途來治療狼瘡性腎炎

17122625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17122625.value: Prof Chan, Tak Mao Prof Singh Gill, Harry Prof Sun, Hongzhe Prof Tse, Wai Choi Eric Prof Yung, Susan

17122625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122625.value: Lupus nephritis (LN) is an important complication in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and considerable patients show refractory disease or intolerance to standard treatments. Novel therapeutic options that are effective, convenient and affordable are need for treatment individualization in LN. In this context, arsenic trioxide (ATO) is an upfront treatment for acute promyelocytic leukaemia that shows pleotropic actions on immune-reactive cells. The availability of oral ATO in our centre presents a unique opportunity to repurpose the agent for acute and chronic LN management, but animal and in vitro data on its effect in LN and associated B cell response is lacking. The objective of this project is to conduct animal and in vitro studies to provide data to translate oral ATO into clinical application for LN. Our preliminary results suggested that oral ATO treatment in NZB/W F1 mice at the age of 14 weeks prevented/delayed the development of LN, and our in vitro studies further demonstrated that ATO potentially interacts with intracellular MMP-9 to inhibit B cell expansion. In Part I, we shall treat lupus-prone NZB/W F1 mice with established nephritis with: 1) ATO (15 mg/kg body weight) (n=10) or 2) phosphate buffer saline (PBS) (n=10) by oral gavage. The changes in blood cells, kidney function, immunological parameters, renal histology and the sustained effects in surviving animals will be evaluated. In Part II, we shall conduct in vivo and in vitro studies that focus on the effects of ATO on B cell proliferation and MMP-9. Isolated activated B cells from active LN patients will be incubated with 1μM ATO, and the transcript/protein level, half-life and downstream pathways of MMP-9 will be examined. The level and activity of MMP-9 in the culture medium will also be determined. The migration and cell cycle profile of activated B cells after ATO treatment will also be assessed. Furthermore, we shall elucidate the mechanisms of ATO-induced MMP-9 downregulation by assessing: 1) MMP-promoter activity by luciferase reporter assay; 2) MMP-9 ubiquitination; 3) interaction between ATO and MMP-9 protein using an organoarsenic fluorescent probe followed by LC/MS analysis; and 4) reactive oxygen species generation in ATO-mediated MMP-9 expression. The results from this project will help advance the progress of its drug repurposing to become an effective, convenient and more affordable therapeutic option for the acute and chronic management of LN patients.

17123025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123025.value: 翻譯後修飾對組蛋白伴侶FACT活性的調控

17123025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123025.value: Eukaryotes organize their genomic DNA into chromatin with a fundamental structural unit called nucleosome, in which four core histone proteins are tightly wrapped by DNA. As an epigenetic hub, nucleosome retains various epigenetic hallmarks that are crucial for gene expression, cell differentiation and cell state transition. Therefore, maintaining epigenetic homeostasis or stability is crucial for the cell fates! When RNA transcription and DNA replication encounter the nucleosomes, the histones are required to be at least partially removed ahead of polymerases and re-deposited after the passage. During these processes, histone chaperone FACT (Facilitates Chromatin Transcription) plays the quintessential role in promoting both nucleosome disassembly and re-assembly. Through tethering, FACT retains histones on DNA while modulating the nucleosome structures during transcription or replication. It has been reported that the post-translational modifications (PTMs) on FACT, as well as on its substrates, regulate the FACT chaperone activity, while the mechanism remains elusive. In this proposal, we will focus on two important PTMs: the phosphorylation on FACT and the ubiquitination on histone H2B lysine 120 (H2B_K120ub). We hypothesize that the phosphorylation of FACT regulates its conformational plasticity, which is crucial for its chaperone activity. Meanwhile, the H2B_K120ub enhances the interaction between FACT subunit SPT16 and nucleosome substrate. To test these hypotheses, we will integrate the tools in biochemistry, structure biology, and molecular biology. The proposed work will determine the roles these modifications play in regulating FACT activity and elucidate the molecular mechanisms, which is not only fundamental in basic science but also provides new strategies for drug discovery. 真核生物透過核小體的基本結構單元將其基因組DNA組裝成染色質。核小體由四個核心組蛋白組成，並被DNA包裹。作為表觀遺傳樞紐，核小體保留了各種表觀遺傳標記，這些標記對基因表現、細胞分化和細胞狀態轉換至關重要。因此，維持表觀遺傳穩態或穩定性對細胞命運至關重要！ 當RNA轉錄和DNA複製遇到核小體時，組蛋白需要在聚合酶之前至少部分被移除，並在聚合酶通過後重新組裝。在這些過程中，組蛋白伴侶FACT（促進染色質轉錄）在促進核小體的解聚和重新組裝中起著至關重要的作用。FACT將組蛋白保留在DNA上，同時在轉錄或複製過程中調節核小體的結構。據報道，FACT及其底物的翻譯後修飾（PTM）調控FACT的組蛋白伴侶功能，而這些PTM調控FACT功能的機制尚不清楚。 在本提案中，我們將重點研究兩種重要的PTM：FACT的磷酸化和組蛋白H2B賴氨酸120（H2B_K120ub）的泛素化。我們假設FACT的磷酸化調節其構象可塑性，這對其伴侶活性至關重要。而H2B_K120ub則增強了FACT亞基SPT16與核小體底物的相互作用。為了驗證這些假設，我們將整合生物化學、結構生物學和分子生物學的工具，確定這些修飾在調節 FACT 活性中的作用並闡明分子機制。這不僅是基礎科學的基石，而且還為藥物發現提供新的策略。

17123125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123125.value: 包含捲緣螺旋結構域的蛋白質 10作為活化胰臟 beta 細胞的新型藥物靶點：從分子機制到治療潛力

17123125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17123125.value: Prof Hoo, Ruby Lai Chong Dr Wang, Baile Prof Xu, Aimin

17123125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123125.value: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a global health concern characterized by sustained hyperglycemia, which ultimately leads to severe complications. Failure of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells exacerbates T2D progression on top of peripheral insulin resistance. Among the pathogenic factors, mitochondrial dysfunction is a major intracellular event impairing beta cells. While insulin therapy and beta cell-boosting agents effectively control blood glucose, their effects are lost after drugs are withdrawn. Therefore, treatments that restore beta cell function/survival are urgently needed for long-term remission. Coiled-coil-helix-coiled-coil-helix domain-containing protein 10 (Chchd10 or C10) is a nuclear-encoded mitochondrial protein essential in mitochondrial homeostasis. We find that the mRNA and protein levels of C10 are significantly reduced in beta cells under diabetic conditions. Beta cell-specific C10 deficiency impairs insulin secretion in mice. In beta cell line Min6 cells, C10 gene silencing impedes insulin-secreting function; mitochondrial function, as indicated by reduced ATP generation; and the mRNA expression of sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ transporting 2 (SERCA2), the major ER calcium transporter regulating cytosolic calcium recycle/storage in beta cells. Moreover, there is a reduced transcription and protein expression of mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM), a critical factor regulating mtDNA and nuclear genes (e.g. SERCA2) in the mitochondria and nucleus, respectively. In contrast, C10 overexpression promotes cell proliferation and attenuates glucolipotoxicity-induced TFAM reduction, insulin-secreting dysfunction, and apoptotic signaling activation. These findings indicate that C10 is critical for beta cell function and survival. We hypothesize that, under diabetic conditions, C10 loss triggers mitochondrial and ER dysfunction, exacerbating beta cell failure. Mechanistically, C10 loss hinders the TFAM mitochondrial localization by reducing the translocase of inner mitochondrial membrane 44 (TIM44)-mediated mitochondrial import, causing TFAM nuclear accumulation instead. Enhanced nuclear TFAM exerts a negative regulatory effect on its gene transcription. Subsequently, the overall TFAM reduction impairs glucose-induced cytosolic calcium influx mediated by mitochondrial ATP-related KATP-VGCC axis and ER-mediated calcium-induced calcium release. We will validate whether beta cell-selective ablation of C10 spontaneously triggers beta cell failure in mice. Next, we will elucidate the molecular interaction/regulation between C10 and TFAM. Lastly, we will develop beta cell-targeting AAV-C10 gene therapy and evaluate its potential in restoring beta cell function/mass in a diabetic mouse model. This project aims to investigate the pathogenic mechanism elicited by C10 loss and explore the possibility of overexpressing C10 to revitalize beta cells. 17123225.value: Rationale: Existing Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) risk screening tools are primarily based on Western populations and may not accurately predict risk for Asian populations. 17123525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123525.value: 探索TLR4與訓練免疫的關係：從急性腎損傷到慢性腎病的路徑

17123525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17123525.value: Dr Lam, Kong Dr Yiu, Stella Wai Han

17123525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123525.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI)-to-chronic kidney disease (CKD) transition is an increasingly recognized cause of kidney failure with poorly understood mechanisms and thus limited specific therapy other than general CKD care. Trained immunity, or innate immune memory, has been associated with the pathogenesis of numerous chronic inflammatory diseases including atherosclerosis, autoimmune and neurodegenerative diseases with subsequent fibrosis or organ failure, but not yet in kidney disease. Macrophages play an important role in kidney homeostasis by regulating kidney injury and tissue repair, and their heterogeneity has been recognized in murine ischemia reperfusion injury (IRI)-induced AKI-to-CKD transition, in which kidney resident macrophages differentiate into the pro-repair subsets whereas monocyte-derived macrophages contribute to chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Our preliminary single-cell RNA sequencing data show that anti-inflammatory macrophage subsets exhibit not only ablation of innate immune system Toll-like receptor-4 (TLR4) signaling and reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β), but also downregulation of transcription factors Jun and Fos, which are important positive regulators of myeloid differentiation, suggesting that TLR4 signaling may be involved in macrophage metabolic reprogramming and differentiation. To ascertain the phenomenon of trained immunity in AKI-to-CKD transition, we will 1) define the role of TLR4-mediated trained immunity in kidney inflammation and injury in 3 experimental models, namely (i) folic acid-induced, (ii) unilateral IRI-induced and (iii) cisplatin-induced AKI-to-CKD transition in which we expect AKI to induce trained immunity in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), which will be ablated in TLR4 knock out animals, 2) dissect the molecular mechanisms for TLR-4-mediated trained immunity in AKI-to-CKD transition by performing transcriptomic, epigenetic and metabolomic analyses on BMDMs from wild type and myeloid-specific TLR4 KO mice that fully recover from AKI and at the chronic phase of different models of AKI-to-CKD transition, and 3) assess trained immunity in human after AKI in a pilot study of patients with normal baseline kidney function who develop de novo AKI versus healthy subjects: ATAC-seq will be performed on their isolated monocytes for determining chromatin accessibility and it is expected that we will obtain a distinct profile of chromatin remodeling after AKI with increased chromatin accessibility and identify the specific motifs that are associated with hyper-inflammatory responses in monocytes. Findings from our study will therefore unravel a new mechanism of AKI-to-CKD transition in animals and humans, and provide a scientific basis for pursuing trained immunity in interrupting AKI-to-CKD transition.

17123925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123925.value: 生物信息方法開發：基於腫瘤轉錄組的解卷積分析以推斷特定區室的潛在表達譜

17123925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17123925.value: Prof Chan, Karen Kar Loen Prof Ng, Ho-Keung

17123925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123925.value: RNA sequencing technologies for single cells have helped characterize tissue compositions and cell-type-specific transcriptomes in tumours. However, these technologies remain technically challenging to apply across diverse tissues and impractically expensive to scale to thousands of samples. In contrast, bulk tumour RNA-seq has less stringent tissue requirements and provides an inexpensive way to characterize the transcriptomes of tumours at scale. To derive deeper insights from these bulk transcriptomes, many methods have been developed to perform deconvolution with cell-type-specific or single-cell transcriptomic profiles. Transcriptomic deconvolution consists of two related subproblems: estimating the composition of bulk transcriptomic profiles (targets) and de-mixing the bulk targets into cell-type-specific transcriptomic profiles. The vast majority of existing deconvolution methods focus on solving the composition estimation subproblem, treating the cell-type-specific profiles as input references. Reference-free deconvolution models attempt to solve both subproblems simultaneously, but these models are generally non-identifiable and suffer from poor estimation accuracy. Importantly, most benchmarks evaluate deconvolution methods using pseudo-bulk profiles as targets, which overestimates model accuracy for the simple reason that pseudo-bulks do not resemble real bulks. Recent benchmarking on real bulk profiles showed that the composition estimates of state-of-the-art deconvolution methods are often inaccurate. Therefore, transcriptomic deconvolution remains a challenging bioinformatic problem that, if solved, can uncover insights hidden in bulk transcriptome datasets. In this project, we will first establish a rigorous benchmarking framework for transcriptomic deconvolution by creating scenarios that reflect the practical usage of deconvolution methods. We will then develop methods to solve both the composition estimation subproblem and the neglected de-mixing subproblem. By accounting for sampling noise and bias in the reference profiles, our preliminary composition estimation model can significantly outperform existing methods. We will therefore further develop our model to enhance its accuracy under challenging conditions and improve its computational efficiency. For the de-mixing subproblem, our results indicate that our preliminary model infers cancer-specific expression profiles much more accurately than existing methods. Building on this foundation, we will make our de-mixing model more robust by accounting for input uncertainty, and we will extend it to perform cell-type-specific differential expression analysis efficiently. To advance biological knowledge, we will use our deconvolution methods to analyze the transcriptomes of ovarian cancer and germ cell tumours and investigate how the tumour microenvironment contributes to chemoresistance. Our bioinformatic methods, once thoroughly validated, will unlock the potential value in the myriad of bulk tumour transcriptomes that have already been generated, especially for difficult-to-collect tumours. 單細胞RNA定序技術可解析腫瘤組織的細胞組成，並找出特定細胞類型的基因表現特徵。然而，這項技術操作門檻高，難以廣泛應用於各類組織，且成本昂貴，無法大規模分析數千份樣本。相比之下，傳統的整體RNA定序對樣本要求較低，能更經濟地大規模檢測腫瘤的基因表現。為了從這些混合數據中挖掘更深層的資訊，科學家已開發多種「解卷積」方法，試圖從中推算出不同細胞類型的基因活動。 基因表現解卷積包含兩個關鍵步驟：(1) 估算混合樣本中各細胞類型的比例，(2) 將混合數據拆分還原成各細胞類型的獨立基因表現譜。現有方法多聚焦於第一步，需預先提供參考數據才能計算；而無參考的模型雖嘗試同時解決兩問題，卻因數學上的不確定性導致準確度不佳。另外，目前多數評估方式使用人工合成的混合數據進行測試，這會高估模型表現，因為真實腫瘤的複雜度遠超人工數據。近期研究顯示，即使最先進的解卷積方法，其估算結果仍與實際情況有明顯差距。因此，如何精準解讀混合轉錄組數據，仍是生物資訊學的一大挑戰。 本計畫將分階段突破此難題： 1. 建立嚴謹的評估標準：設計更貼近真實場景的測試情境，客觀比較現有方法的優劣。 2. 開發創新演算法： 細胞組成分析：我們的初步模型能有效修正參考數據的偏差與雜訊，表現顯著優於現有工具。後續將進一步提升其準確度與運算效率。 基因表現拆分：現有方法常忽略此步驟，而我們的模型已能更精準推斷癌細胞特異的基因活動。未來將強化模型穩定性，並擴展功能以高效分析細胞類型間的差異表現。 實際應用：我們將運用這些方法分析卵巢癌與生殖細胞瘤，探究腫瘤微環境如何影響化療抗藥性。一旦驗證成熟，這些工具能充分釋放現有海量腫瘤轉錄組數據的潛在價值，尤其對難以採集的稀有腫瘤類型極具意義。

17124625.value: 小分子調節子宮內膜容受性和胚胎植入的機制和功能研究

17124625.label: Co - Investigator(s)

17124625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124625.value: Embryo implantation starts when a blastocyst meets the endometrium. This process required a synchronized development of an embryo and a receptive endometrium. However, the detailed underlying mechanism that regulates this biological process remains obscure. Despite a good quality embryo being transferred, the implantation and even pregnancy rates in IVF treatment remain low. 17125425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125425.value: 新型內質網膜蛋白在血脂紊亂及代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病中的功能與機制研究

17125425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17125425.value: Prof Dewei, Ye Prof Eric, Honoré

17125425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125425.value: The liver is a major metabolic hub of the human body, responsible for glucose production, glycogen storage, biosynthesis of lipids and lipoproteins, fatty acid combustion and detoxification. Dysregulated metabolism in the liver is a primary contributor to a cluster of obesity-related metabolic complications, including type-2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, atherosclerosis and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease (MASLD). These metabolic comorbidities are reaching epidemic proportions globally, posing enormous socioeconomic and healthcare challenges to our rapidly ageing society. To develop more effective pharmacotherapies for these diseases, it is of critical importance to identify cellular components that trigger or instigate obesity-induced metabolic dysregulation in hepatocytes. Transmembrane protein 33 (TMEM33, also known as DB83) is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localised transmembrane with poorly-defined functions. Our preliminary result reveals a progressively increased TMEM33 expression in the liver of obese Chinese with worsening degree of MASLD. In mice with diet-induced MASLD and dyslipidemia, a marked upregulation of TMEM33 occurs predominantly in parenchymal hepatocytes of the liver, whilst TMEM33 knockout mice are refractory to high fat diet-induced dyslipidemia, MASLD and liver injury. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated knockdown of TMEM33 leads to an obvious attenuation of toxic lipids-induced steatosis in both human and mouse hepatocytes. Using RNA-sequencing, we have identified several metabolic pathways altered by TMEM33 deficiency in the mouse liver, including ER stress-responsive chaperones, lipid and sterol metabolism, and immuno-inflammatory responses. Based on these findings, we propose increased hepatic expression of TMEM33 as an important player in initiating and/or perpetuating obesity-induced metabolic complications such as dyslipidemia and MASLD. In this project, we will further evaluate its pathophysiological role in obesity-associated metabolic comorbidities using hepatocyte-specific TMEM33 knockout mice, and will elucidate the molecular mechanism whereby this ER transmembrane protein disrupts metabolic homeostasis by identifying the direct downstream effectors and interaction partners of TMEM33 in hepatocytes. Additionally, we plan to develop TMEM33-siRNA selectively targeting hepatocytes, and conduct a proof-of-concept study to explore the therapeutic potential of this hepatocyte-selective TMEM33 siRNA for the treatment of aforementioned metabolic disorders in mouse models and human liver organoid. The findings from this study are expected to shed new light on molecular pathways linking ER function and lipid metabolism in hepatocytes, and to provide scientific foundation for future development of novel hepatocytes-targeted therapeutics for precision management of obesity-related metabolic complications. 肝臟是人體主要的代謝樞紐，負責葡萄糖生成、糖原儲存、脂質和脂蛋白的生物合成、脂肪酸氧化以及解毒過程。肝臟代謝失調是導致一繫列肥胖相關代謝併發症的主要因素，這些併發症包括2型糖尿病、血脂異常、動脈粥樣硬化以及代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病（MASLD）。這些代謝性共病已逐漸呈現全球流行趨勢，對我們快速老齡化社會造成巨大的社會經濟與醫療負擔。為了開發針對這些疾病更有效的藥物療法，亟需明確驅動肥胖誘導肝細胞代謝紊亂的關鍵細胞組分。 跨膜蛋白33（TMEM33，也稱為DB83）是一種定位於內質網的跨膜蛋白，其功能尚未完全闡明。我們的前期研究發現，肥胖中國人群的肝臟中TMEM33表達隨MASLD病情加重呈進行性升高。在飲食誘導的MASLD和血脂異常小鼠模型中，TMEM33主要在肝臟的實質肝細胞中顯著上調，而敲除TMEM33的小鼠則能抵抗高脂飲食誘導的血脂異常、MASLD和肝損傷。此外，利用siRNA介導的TMEM33敲低可明顯減輕毒性脂質誘導的人和小鼠肝細胞脂肪變性。通過RNA測序分析，我們已在小鼠肝臟中鑒定出多個受TMEM33缺失影響的代謝通路，包括內質網應激響應性分子伴侶、脂質和固醇代謝以及免疫炎症反應。基於上述發現，我們認為肝臟TMEM33表達升高在促進肥胖誘導的代謝併發症（如血脂異常和MASLD）中起到重要作用。 在本項目中，我們將利用肝細胞特異性TMEM33敲除小鼠進一步評估其在肥胖相關代謝共病中的病理生理作用，併通過鑒定TMEM33在肝細胞中的直接下遊效應分子及相互作用蛋白，闡明該內質網跨膜蛋白破壞代謝穩態的分子機制。此外，我們計劃開發選擇性靶向肝細胞的TMEM33-siRNA，併在小鼠模型和人肝臟類器官中探索其對上述代謝性疾病的治療潛力。 本研究預期將闡明肝細胞內連接內質網功能與脂質代謝的新分子通路，為未來開發新型肝細胞靶向療法、實現對肥胖相關代謝併發症的個體化管理提供科學依據。

17125525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125525.value: 重振免疫招募樞紐以恢復癌症免疫療法之療效

17125525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125525.value: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy rejuvenates exhausted CD8+T cells (Tex) and serves as the first-line treatment for many cancer types. Yet, its efficacy is limited, underscoring the urgent need to investigate the mechanisms underlying this treatment deficit. While CD8+T cell exclusion (‘cold’ tumor) is known to impede ICB response, increasing evidence suggests that a substantial number of ICB non-responders (NRs) indeed have adequate CD8+T cells within their tumors, with some even showing signs of Tex rejuvenation. This raises a key question: why do these ‘hot’ tumors remain resistant to ICB? To address this knowledge gap, we employed a multi-pronged approach integrating the analysis from murine models and single-cell transcriptomic patient databases of multiple cancer types. Our analysis revealed that an effective ICB response required both an initial rejuvenation of Tex and a subsequent remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME) orchestrated by CXCL9+Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). This two-stage process resulted in the formation of immune recruitment-hubs, prompting an influx of CD8+T effectors into the TME. This continuous supply of functional CD8+T cells sustained the anti-tumor response, leading to clinical remission. Crucially, we found that in NRs with ‘hot’ tumors, CXCL9+TAM expansion was impaired, despite detectable ICB-induced Tex rejuvenation. This defect led to limited recruitment of CD8+T effectors for effective tumor eradication. To determine the cause of this failed TME remodeling, we analyzed spatial transcriptomic data from tumors of ICB-treated patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) – a deadly cancer with high prevalence in Hong Kong. Our analysis unveiled distinct immune communities between responders and NRs. Of note, we observed an increased interaction between TAMs and tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) in NRs. Ex vivo analysis further revealed that this TAM-TAN interaction underpinned CXCL9+TAM suppression, as TANs isolated from ICB-resistant tumors curtailed CXCL9 production by in vitro-generated TAM-like cells via TGFb. Thus, our preliminary data suggest that the formation of CXCL9+TAM-mediated immune recruitment-hubs is pivotal for continuous CD8+T cell recruitment and effective ICB responses. However, CXCL9+TAM development is regulated by proximal TANs. A failure to expand CXCL9+TAMs explains why some ‘hot’ tumors remain resistant to ICB. In this proposal, we will delineate the molecular basis of CXCL9+TAM development and decipher how TAN-elicited TGFb impedes this process. Finally, we will evaluate strategies to reverse ICB resistance by boosting CXCL9+TAM development. This translatable knowledge will aid the development of combinational immunotherapy with improved response rates and enhanced therapeutic effects. 免疫檢查點阻斷（ICB）療法能夠使耗竭的CD8+T細胞恢復活力，並作為多種癌症類型的一線治療方法。然而，其療效有限，這凸顯了深入研究這種治療缺陷背後機制的迫切性。雖然已知CD8+T細胞排斥（“冷”腫瘤）會阻礙ICB反應，但越來越多的證據表明，相當一部分ICB無返應者（NRs）的腫瘤中實際上存在足夠的CD8+T細胞，其中一些甚至顯示出CD8+T細胞恢復活力的跡象。這引發了一個關鍵問題：為什麼這些“熱”腫瘤仍然對ICB產生抵抗？為了填補這一知識空白，我們採用了一種多管齊下的方法，整合了來自小鼠腫瘤模型和多種癌症類型的單細胞轉錄組患者數據庫的分析。我們的分析揭示，有效的ICB反應既需要耗竭的CD8+T細胞的初步恢復，也需要由CXCL9+腫瘤相關巨噬細胞（TAMs）協調的腫瘤微環境（TME）的後續重塑。這一兩階段過程導致了免疫招募中心的形成，促使效應CD8+T細胞湧入TME。這種功能性CD8+T細胞的持續供應維持了抗腫瘤反應，從而實現了臨床緩解。重要的是，我們發現，在具有“熱”腫瘤的NRs中，儘管可以檢測到ICB誘導的CD8+T細胞恢復，但CXCL9+TAM的擴增受到了阻礙。這一缺陷導致效應CD8+T細胞的招募受限，無法有效清除腫瘤。為了確定這種TME重塑失敗的原因，我們分析了接受ICB治療的肝細胞癌（HCC）患者腫瘤的空間轉錄組數據——HCC是一種在香港高發的致命癌症。我們的分析揭示了應答者和NRs之間不同的免疫群落。值得注意的是，我們觀察到NRs中TAMs與腫瘤相關中性粒細胞（TANs）之間的相互作用增加。體外分析進一步揭示，這種TAM-TAN相互作用是CXCL9+TAM抑制的基礎，因為從ICB耐藥腫瘤中分離出的TANs通過TGFb抑制了體外生成的TAM樣細胞的CXCL9產生。因此，我們的初步數據表明，CXCL9+TAM介導的免疫招募中心的形成對於持續招募CD8+T細胞和有效的ICB反應至關重要。然而，CXCL9+TAM的發育受到鄰近TANs的調控。CXCL9+TAM擴增失敗解釋了為什麼一些“熱”腫瘤仍然對ICB產生抵抗。在本提案中，我們將闡明CXCL9+TAM發育的分子基礎，並解析TAN引發的TGFb如何阻礙這一過程。最後，我們將評估通過促進CXCL9+TAM發育來逆轉ICB耐藥的策略。這一可轉化的知識將有助於開發具有更高應答率和增強治療效果的組合免疫療法。

17125925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125925.value: METTL3透過對ACSM3的m6A甲基化加重糖尿病肥胖導致糖尿病腎病的鐵死亡機制及靶向ACSM3的治療潛力：機制及轉化研究

17125925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17125925.value: Prof Feng, Yibin Prof Meng, Xiao-Ming

17125925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125925.value: Diabesity, the coexistence of diabetes and obesity, presents a significant health challenge globally and is a major risk factor for the development of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Acyl-CoA synthetase medium chain family member 3 (ACSM3) primarily localizes on the outer membrane of mitochondria in liver and kidney, where it plays a role in acyl-CoA metabolic processes and fatty acid biosynthesis. Our RNAseq data analysis of diabetic kidneys from both diabesity mice (db/db mice and high-fat diet mice) indicates a significant reduction in ACSM3 expression in diabetic kidneys. The loss of ACSM3 is associated with a significant increase of ferroptosis (an iron-dependent oxidative form of cell death associated with increased lipid peroxidation) in kidneys of db/db mice. Overexpression of ACSM3 attenuates ferroptosis in HK-2 cells (a human kidney epithelial cell line) treated by high glucose plus oxidized LDL (mimic diabesity conditions). Furthermore, the kidneys of db/db mice exhibit elevated levels of METTL3 and m6A methylation. Knockdown of METTL3 restores ACSM3 loss and alleviates ferroptosis in HK-2 cells under diabesity conditions. These findings suggest that the upregulation of METTL3 and m6A methylation may contribute to ACSM3 loss and exacerbate ferroptosis in DKD. Moreover, a high-throughput screening of compounds in commonly used herbs for DKD by 117 nationally renowned Chinese medicine doctors revealed that Rhapontin, an active compound, binds to ACSM3, which is further confirmed by the Cellular Thermal Shift Assay and Surface Plasmon Resonance experiments. Treatment with Phapontin alleviates the loss of ACSM3 and ferroptosis in HK-2 cells under diabesity, suggesting the therapeutic potential of Rhapontin for DKD. Therefore, we hypothesize that METTL3 mediated loss of ACSM3 significantly contributes to DKD, and restoring ACSM3 can attenuate the diseases, and targeting ACSM3 with Rhapontin may alleviate the diabesity-induced DKD. Three objectives will be investigated: (1). To determine whether ACSM3 loss aggravates DKD via ACSM3/GPX4-mediated ferroptosis under diabesity; (2). To determine whether METTL3-mediated m6A methylation results in ACSM3 loss in DKD under diabesity; (3). To determine whether targeting ACSM3 with Rhapontin attenuates DKD under diabesity. The study will address key questions: What role does ACSM3 play in DKD? how is ACSM3 decreased in DKD? Does targeting ACSM3 with Rhapontin have therapeutic potential? The study may uncover a novel mechanism of DKD and identify therapeutic compounds for DKD under diabesity by specifically targeting ACSM3. 糖尿病肥胖症（Diabesity），即糖尿病與肥胖症的共存疾病，對全球健康構成重大挑戰，且是糖尿病腎臟病（DKD）發生發展的主要危險因素。ACSM3主要位於肝臟和腎臟細胞的線粒體外膜，在脂酰輔酶A代謝過程和脂肪酸生物合成中扮演重要角色。我們對糖尿病肥胖小鼠模型的腎臟進行RNA測序分析顯示，糖尿病腎臟中ACSM3的表達顯著降低，且ACSM3的喪失與腎臟細胞中鐵死亡（ferroptosis）顯著增加有關。過量表達ACSM3可以減緩高糖加氧化LDL刺激HK-2細胞（模擬糖尿病肥胖狀況）條件下的ferroptosis。此外，db/db小鼠腎臟中METTL3和m6A甲基化水平均升高。抑制METTL3可以恢復ACSM3的表達，並減輕在糖尿病肥胖條件下HK-2細胞中的ferroptosis。這些研究結果提示，METTL3及m6A甲基化的上調可能促使ACSM3的喪失，進而加劇DKD中的ferroptosis。 此外，高通量篩選117位國家知名中醫師治療DKD常用中藥內的化合物，並通過細胞熱遷移測試（Cellular Thermal Shift Assay）和表面等離子共振（Surface Plasmon Resonance）實驗發現活性成分Rhapontin可與ACSM3直接結合。細胞實驗發現Rhapontin治療能減少HK-2細胞在糖尿病肥胖條件下的ACSM3喪失及ferroptosis，顯示Rhapontin具有治療DKD的潛力。 因此，我們假設METTL3介導的ACSM3喪失顯著促進DKD的發展，恢復ACSM3可能緩解疾病，並且用Rhapontin靶向ACSM3或可改善糖尿病肥胖引起的DKD。本研究將聚焦於三個研究目標：（1）確定ACSM3的喪失是否通過ACSM3/GPX4介導的ferroptosis加重DKD；（2）確定METTL3介導的m6A甲基化是否導致DKD中ACSM3的喪失；（3）研究用Rhapontin靶向ACSM3是否能緩解糖尿病肥胖相關的DKD。 本研究將回答以下關鍵問題：ACSM3在DKD中扮演什麼角色？為何在DKD中ACSM3會下降？用Rhapontin靶向ACSM3是否具有治療潛力？此研究或能揭示一種新的DKD發病機制，並通過專門針對ACSM3來篩選出潛在的治療化合物。

17126725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17126725.value: 利用序列深度學習模型從單細胞多組學中解碼細胞分化與調控模式

17126725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126725.value: Single-cell multi-omics (scMultiOmics) technology, particularly the paired profiling of transcriptomes (RNA) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC) within individual cells, has recently embraced significant advancements. It is becoming a powerful tool for determining fine-grained cell states, biological processes, and underlying regulatory pathways, with notable applications in embryonic development, tissue differentiation, and tumor-immune interactions. Current scMultiOmics analysis focuses on characterizing cell states by concatenating the two modalities, followed by dimensionality reduction with linear or non-linear methods. These approaches neglect the intrinsic relationships between the epigenetic and transcription layers. However, understanding this coupling is crucial for inferring cell differentiation e.g., by leveraging the transcription regulation and kinetics in an RNA velocity framework. Additionally, routine gene regulatory analyses of scMultiOmics data typically rely on two imperfect steps: 1) TF-to-CRE (transcription factor to cis-regulatory elements) by mapping the DNA sequences of the accessible regions to transcription factors based on their binding motifs annotated in databases (e.g., JASPAR), which are often incomplete, and 2) CRE-to-target by associating regulatory elements with specific cis-genes based on proximity, usually disregarding distal regulations. In this proposal, we aim to address these challenges by introducing a novel computational framework seqMAE (sequence-informed scMultiOmics Auto-Encoder) that learns an effective representation of scMultiOmics data by encoding the DNA sequence around chromatin open regions. Unlike factor analysis or standard auto-encoders, this representation learning utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to parse the discrete DNA sequences into a continuous embedding for regulatory regions. First, we will specifically focus on developing the seqMAE-TF module for transforming chromatin accessibility into specific TF activities, supporting both strong and weak bindings. Briefly, the TF activities will be estimated at a single-cell resolution by gradient-based scores over sequence and TF’s RNAs. Uniquely, the learned sequence embedding of CREs will enhance the use of existing knowledge annotated from binding motifs, ChIP-seq data, and regulon targets. Second, within this framework we will also develop a seqMAE-Velo module to infer cell differentiation by modeling the CRE-to-target dynamical association via regressing CREs’ accessibilities to the transcription rate within a novel RNA velocity framework, potentially reinforced by the sequence-based embeddings. Third, we aim to demonstrate the applicability and robustness of our proposed methods across different protocols, platforms, perturbations, and diverse biological contexts on 11 compiled datasets. Uniquely, we plan to validate our methods using public datasets (e.g., cell type-specific ChIP-seq and TF perturbed scMultiOmics data) and potential experimental validation via close collaborations. 單細胞多組學 (scMultiOmics) 技術，特別是對單一細胞內轉錄組 (RNA) 和染色質可及性 (ATAC) 的配對分析，近年來取得了重大進展。它正成為確定細粒度細胞狀態、生物過程和潛在調控途徑的有力工具，在胚胎發育、組織分化和腫瘤-免疫相互作用中有著顯著的應用。 目前的 scMultiOmics 分析著重於透過串聯兩種模式來表徵細胞狀態，然後使用線性或非線性方法進行降維。這些方法忽略了表觀遺傳層和轉錄層之間的內在連結。然而，理解這種耦合對於推斷細胞分化至關重要，例如，透過利用 RNA 速度框架中的轉錄調控和動力學。此外，scMultiOmics 資料的常規基因調控分析通常依賴於兩個不完整的步驟：1）TF-to-CRE（轉錄因子到順式調控元件），透過基於資料庫（例如 JASPAR）中註釋的結合基序，將可及區域的 DNA 序列映射到轉錄因子，但這些資料庫通常不完整；2）CRE-to-target，透過遠端接近基因的近式元件來調節。 在本提案中，我們旨在透過引入一個全新的計算框架 seqMAE（序列資訊驅動的 scMultiOmics 自動編碼器）來應對這些挑戰，該框架透過對染色質開放區域周圍的 DNA 序列進行編碼，學習 scMultiOmics 數據的有效表示。與因子分析或標準自動編碼器不同，這種表示學習利用卷積神經網路 (CNN) 將離散的 DNA 序列解析為調控區域的連續嵌入。首先，我們將專注於開發 seqMAE-TF 模組，將染色質的可及性轉化為特定的轉錄因子活性，以支持強結合和弱結合。簡而言之，我們將透過對序列和轉錄因子 RNA 進行基於梯度的評分，以單細胞分辨率估算轉錄因子活性。獨特的是，學習到的 CRE 序列嵌入將增強對結合基序、ChIP-seq 資料和調控子標靶註釋的現有知識的利用。其次，在此框架下，我們還將開發一個 seqMAE-Velo 模組，透過在新的 RNA 速度框架內回歸 CRE 對轉錄速率的可及性來建模 CRE 與靶標的動態關聯，並可能透過基於序列的嵌入得到強化，從而推斷細胞分化。第三，我們的目標是在 11 個已編譯的資料集上，證明我們提出的方法在不同協定、平台、擾動和多種生物環境下的適用性和穩健性。獨特的是，我們計劃使用公共數據集（例如，細胞類型特定的 ChIP-seq 和 TF 擾動 scMultiOmics 數據）並透過密切合作進行潛在的實驗驗證來驗證我們的方法。

17127325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17127325.value: 冠状病毒原生双膜囊泡孔复合体介导的RNA转运机制

17127325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127325.value: The continued health and economic threats of coronavirus urge focused efforts to investigate the molecular mechanism of virus replication inside host cells, which is crucial to identifying novel targets for viral inhibition. Coronaviruses significantly remodel the host intracellular membranes to form double-membrane vesicles (DMVs). Together with the viral RNA synthesis machinery, DMVs serve as the replication organelle for viral RNA synthesis, protected from cellular immunity surveillance. After synthesis in the DMV lumen, these viral RNAs are translocated to cytoplasm for viral assembly and viral protein synthesis. Despite the functional significance of DMV in coronavirus life cycle, the mechanism of DMV formation and RNA translocation is poorly understood until recently. Following the discovery of DMV complex by Barcena’s group in 2020, we recently developed a minimal SARS-CoV-2 DMV system to study the mechanism of coronavirus DMV formation and RNA translocation. We uncovered the molecular architecture of the nsp3-4 pore complex at an overall resolution of 4.2 Å, which resolves the long-standing puzzle regarding the stoichiometry and topology of nsp3 and nsp4 within the DMV pore complex, elucidating a potential pathway of membrane zippering and DMV pore formation.
