Our recent work lay a solid foundation to study mechanism of the native functional replication/transcription complex (RTC) which comprises the native DMV pore complex and RNA replication/transcription machinery. However, due to the absence of RNA synthesis machinery in our mini-DMV system, the nsp3-4 complex does not recapitulate the native functional DMV pore complex during virus infection. How viral RNA molecules are translocated from the DMV interior to the cytoplasm through native DMV pore remains unknown. The investigation of DMV complex on the native functional DMVs is required. In this proposal, we will investigate the molecular basis of viral RNA binding and translocation through native coronavirus DMV pore complex. We will combine structural biology and virology approaches to resolve the composition and structure of the native functional coronavirus DMV pore to understand vRNA translocation mechanism. Specifically, we will optimize the structure determination pipeline of DMV pore complex, isolate the native functional RTCs and resolve the structure of native functional DMV pore complex with RNA translocation in action. Perturbing DMV pore formation and viral RNA translocation activity represents a novel approach to viral inhibition. Our study will facilitate the rational design of new antiviral strategies against SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses based on the interference of DMV pore formation and inhibition of DMV pore function. 新冠病毒对健康和经济持续构成威胁，迫切需要深入研究病毒在宿主细胞内复制的分子机制，这对于发现新的抗病毒靶点至关重要。冠状病毒会显著重塑宿主细胞内膜，形成双膜囊泡（DMVs）。这些DMVs与病毒RNA合成机制共同作为病毒RNA复制的场所，并能够躲避细胞免疫系统的监控。在DMV腔内合成的病毒RNA随后被转运到细胞质中，进行病毒组装和病毒蛋白的合成。 尽管DMV在冠状病毒生命周期中具有重要功能，但其形成机制和RNA转运过程直到最近仍知之甚少。继2020年Barcena团队发现DMV复合物后，我们最近开发了一个简化的SARS-CoV-2 DMV系统，用于研究冠状病毒DMV形成和RNA转运的机制。我们解析了nsp3-4孔复合物的分子结构，解决了长期以来DMV孔复合物中化学计量和拓扑结构的谜题，阐明了膜融合和DMV孔形成的分子机制。这些工作为研究冠状病毒功能性复制/转录复合物（RTC）的机制奠定了基础。 在本提案中，我们将研究冠状病毒DMV孔复合物结合和转运病毒RNA的分子基础。我们将结合结构生物学和病毒学方法，解析原生功能性冠状病毒DMV孔的组成和结构，以理解病毒RNA的转运机制。具体而言，我们将优化DMV孔复合物的结构解析流程，分离原生功能性RTCs，并解析在RNA转运过程中的原生功能性DMV孔复合物的结构。我们的研究将有助于基于干扰DMV孔形成和抑制DMV孔功能的原理，通过干扰DMV孔的形成和病毒RNA的转运活性，理性设计针对SARS-CoV-2和其他冠状病毒的新型抗病毒策略。

17127525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17127525.value: 鑑定雙鏈RNA 結合蛋白 PACT 作為 cGAS 輔因子以增強干擾素信號傳導之研究

17127525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127525.value: The cytosolic DNA sensor cGAS serves as a critical sentinel in innate immunity by detecting pathogenic DNA and initiating interferon (IFN) production. Through generation of the second messenger 2’3’-cGAMP and subsequent STING activation, cGAS orchestrates robust antiviral responses. While essential for host defence, aberrant cGAS activation contributes to autoimmune pathology through chronic IFN production. To maintain the right balance, cGAS activity is thus tightly controlled via various mechanisms. We previously demonstrated that the dsRNA-binding protein PACT enhances RNA sensing pathways by activating RIG-I signaling. Recently, our preliminary data revealed an unexpected interaction between PACT and cGAS. However, the mechanistic details and biological significance of this interaction remain unexplored. Furthermore, whether PACT modulates cGAS activity and contributes to dysregulated DNA sensing in autoimmunity is unknown. Our pilot study demonstrates that PACT potently enhances cGAS-dependent IFN responses. We show that PACT physically interacts with cGAS and is essential for optimal cGAS function, as evidenced by reduced IFN and cGAMP production in PACT-deficient cells. These findings reveal PACT as a novel cGAS coactivator and suggest a previously unrecognized regulatory mechanism in DNA sensing pathways, where an RNA-binding protein directly modulates DNA sensor function. Importantly, PACT depletion significantly alleviates the heightened IFN response in a cell model of TREX1 deficiency-associated autoimmunity, indicating that this newly identified regulatory axis may contribute to aberrant DNA sensing in autoimmune disorders. In this proposal, we will first validate PACT-mediated potentiation of cGAS signaling through comprehensive gain-of-function and loss-of-function approaches. We will conduct detailed interaction analysis to map the interfaces mediating cGAS-PACT complex formation. We will then systematically investigate whether PACT modulates cGAS functioning, including its enzymatic activity, DNA binding, oligomerization, and post-translational modifications, thereby influencing downstream signaling. We will also examine the impact of PACT on components of the cGAS signaling pathway, including STING and cGAMP. State-of-the-art biochemical, cell biology and imaging techniques will be employed to gain mechanistic insights. Subcellular localization and novel functional partners of the cGAS-PACT complex will be explored. Finally, we will evaluate the pathological relevance of PACT-mediated cGAS regulation in autoimmunity and explore the therapeutic potential of targeting the cGAS-PACT axis. This research will significantly advance our understanding of cGAS regulation by uncovering PACT as a critical cofactor. Our work will provide new molecular insights into dysregulated DNA sensing in autoimmune diseases and may facilitate development of novel immunotherapies targeting the cGAS-PACT pathway. 胞質 DNA 傳感器cGAS是先天免疫中的關鍵哨兵，能偵測病原體 DNA 並啟動干擾素（IFN）產生。cGAS 透過生成第二信使 2’3’-cGAMP，並隨後激活STING，協調強有力的抗病毒反應。雖然 cGAS 對宿主防禦至關重要，但其異常激活化會導致持續性的干擾素產生，繼而引發自身免疫病理。因此，為了維持適當平衡，cGAS 的活性受到各種機制的嚴格調控。 我們先前證實，雙鏈RNA 結合蛋白 PACT 可透過活化 RIG-I 訊號傳導途徑來增強 RNA 感知。最近，我們的初步數據揭示 PACT 與 cGAS 之間存在意想不到的相互作用；然而，該互作的機制細節及其生物學意義尚未闡明。此外，PACT 是否會調節 cGAS 活性，並與自身免疫中的DNA 感知失調有關，亦有待釐清。 我們的先導研究顯示，PACT 能顯著增強依賴 cGAS 的 IFN 反應。我們證明 PACT 可與 cGAS 發生物理互作，且對cGAS 功能至關重要；在 PACT 缺失的細胞中，IFN 與 cGAMP 的產生均顯著下降。這些發現將 PACT 界定為一種新穎的 cGAS 共活化因子，並提示在 DNA 感知途徑中存在此前未被發現的調控機制——即RNA 結合蛋白可直接調控 DNA 傳感器的功能。重要的是，在與 TREX1 缺陷相關的自身免疫細胞模型中，去除 PACT 可顯著緩解過度的 IFN 反應，說明這一新調控軸可能與自身免疫疾病中的異常 DNA 感知有關。 在本計劃中，我們將首先以全面的功能獲得與功能喪失策略，驗證 PACT 介導的 cGAS 訊號傳導增強效應。我們將進行詳盡的互作分析，以確定介導 cGAS–PACT 複合體形成的結合界面。其後，我們將系統性研究 PACT 是否調節 cGAS 的各項功能，包括其酶活性、DNA 結合、寡聚化及翻譯後修飾，從而影響下游訊號。我們亦會檢視 PACT 對 cGAS 訊號途徑組件（包括 STING 及 cGAMP）的影響，並運用最先進的生化、細胞生物學與成像技術，以獲取機制層面的深入洞見。同時，我們將探索 cGAS–PACT 複合體的亞細胞定位及其新的功能互作夥伴。最後，我們會評估 PACT 介導之 cGAS 調控在自身免疫中的病理相關性，並探索以 cGAS–PACT 軸為靶點的治療潛力。 本研究將透過揭示 PACT 作為關鍵輔因子，顯著推進我們對 cGAS 調控的理解。此工作將為自身免疫疾病中失調的 DNA 感知提供新的分子層次見解，並有望促進針對 cGAS–PACT 通路的創新免疫療法之發展。

17128225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17128225.value: Omnia：⾯向增強式⽣物顯微分析的通⽤多向學習框架

17128225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128225.value: Recent advances in cellular imaging, coupled with deep learning (DL), have enabled detailed analysis of cellular phenotypes, capturing both biophysical and biochemical characteristics. However, significant challenges persist, including fragmented data across increasingly diverse imaging modalities, limited multi-modality imaging capabilities, and the lack of robust methods to combine biophysical and biochemical information. Popular imaging techniques, such as quantitative phase imaging (QPI) and fluorescence microscopy, are powerful but often used separately, limiting our ability to fully understand how structural and molecular data are correlated. To address these challenges, we propose developing Omnia, a unified generative DL framework with two core features: (1) multi-way multimodal contrast conversion, allows Omnia to flexibly convert between multiple imaging contrasts, including biophysical (e.g., QPI, brightfield) and biochemical (e.g., fluorescence, H&E staining) modalities. This ability to perform multi-way conversions goes beyond pairwise conversions typically used in existing models, enabling comprehensive integration of diverse imaging data. By combining information from multiple imaging modalities, Omnia will provide a more complete picture of cellular morphology and function, reducing the need for multiple specialized imaging instruments and improving data consistency across modalities. (2) interpretable disentangled learning, separates and identifies meaningful biological features from the multi-modal imaging data. Disentangled learning allows the model to break down complex cellular data into distinct, interpretable components, such as cell shape, mass distribution, fluorescence signals, and protein localization. This will enable Omnia to learn how biophysical and biochemical characteristics are correlated and complementary, an area that remains poorly understood. The model will provide interpretable outputs, allowing researchers to generate testable hypotheses about cellular processes, which can then be experimentally validated. Built upon our established expertise in advanced imaging and DL image analytics, the project will: (1) develop Omnia, a DL model for multi-modal image contrast conversion; (2) create an integrative bio-imaging pipeline using disentangled learning to extract interpretable cellular features from Omnia; and (3) explore the application of Omnia in investigating how the augmented images and interpretable disentangled morphological extracted from Omnia reveal the processes of ULK4-dependent neurogenesis and human airway organoid morphogenesis, especially uncovering new insights into the relationships between biophysical and biochemical features during key developmental processes. By revealing the intricate connections between the structural and molecular data of cells and tissues, Omnia could transform cell imaging research. This advancement will enable the generation of testable, biologically meaningful hypotheses and drive new discoveries in disease diagnostics and fundamental biological research.

17128325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17128325.value: 設計和開發用於假牙設計的物理資訊神經網絡

17128325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128325.value: Dental prostheses have been appeared for more than 6000 years which are crucial for restoring the function and aesthetics of missing or damaged teeth. The design and fabrication of dental prostheses are critical aspects of restorative dentistry. Traditional methods for designing these prostheses often rely on manual craftsmanship and empirical knowledge, which can be time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies. In fact, even the recent advancement of digital dentistry and computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) and AI technologies has enabled the improvement of field by enhancing accuracy, precision and efficiency, in terms of dental prostheses design, although we can use non-linear finite element analysis to analyse the design and predict the lifetime based on mechanical properties of the personalized prostheses made with different materials, this is not deployable in dental laboratory due to its lengthy process. Data-driven Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) can incorporate physical laws and domain-specific knowledge into the learning process would be developed in order to make a faster, more accurate predictions that align with the underlying mechanics of various dental prostheses. In this study, a dental prostheses design-specific PINN architecture would be built, by learning the design and FEA data, together with the support of inherent materials properties and mechanical fatigue data that formulate the governing partial differential equations (PDE). The PINN will further be validated and check the performance with the validation and test sets of data. Further, PINN will be testified in current digital workflow. To conclude, this would be the first time we can estimate the service life (in mechanical terms) of fixed dental prostheses made with various kinds of materials and different designs at the design stage in a holistic objective way in mechanics. We expect this can be a breakthrough in prostheses design. 假牙在世上已出現超過 6000年，使病人能恢復缺失或受損牙齒的功能和美觀。假牙的設計和製作是修復牙科的關鍵。然而，設計這些假牙的傳統方法通常依賴手工製作和經驗知識，不但耗時，而且還容易出現不一致。事實上，在數位化牙科使用電腦輔助設計與製造 (CAD/CAM) 和人工智能(AI)技術下，製造方面最新的進展已可提高準確性、精確度和效率。但是，在假牙設計方面，雖然我們可以使用非線性有限元來分析設計，並根據不同材料製成的個性化假體的機械性能預測其壽命，但由於其流程冗長，無法在牙科技工實驗室中部署。數據驅動的物理資訊神經網路 (PINN) 可以將物理定律和特定領域知識融入機器學習過程，以便做出更快、更準確的預測各種牙科修復體的基礎力學。本研究將建構一個牙科修復體設計特定的 PINN 架構，透過學習設計和 FEA 數據，結合固有材料特性和機械疲勞數據的支持，形成控制偏微分方程 (PDE)。 另外，為使PINN 進一步得到驗證，除了使用測試資料集檢查其效能，PINN 將在目前的數位工作流程中進行測試。總之，這將是牙科第一次能夠在設計階段以整體客觀的方式從力學角度估計由各種材料和不同設計製成的固定牙科修復體的使用壽命。我們期待這能成為修復體設計的突破。

17128525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17128525.value: 基於pH智能響應銀納米材料的齲齒靶向治療研究

17128525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128525.value: Background Dental caries (tooth decay) is the most widespread non-communicable disease, leading to significant economic burdens. The World Health Organisation (WHO) recommends silver diamine fluoride (SDF) therapy to treat dental caries due to its effectiveness, simplicity, and non-invasive nature. However, SDF causes unaesthetic discolouration of carious lesions, leading to patient dissatisfaction. To address this limitation, we designed a non-discolouring silver nanotherapeutic agent (NSF-MSN-DOPA). NSF-MSN-DOPA specifically targets cariogenic biofilm. It also controls the release of NSF in response to pH change. Our pilot study demonstrated that NSF-MSN-DOPA inhibits Streptococcus mutans, a common cariogenic bacterium. It is non-discolouring and less cytotoxic compared to SDF. Further research is necessary to confirm its anti-caries properties. Objectives To evaluate the antimicrobial, remineralising, and discolouring effects of NSF-MSN-DOPA on carious lesions. Methods We will develop NSF-MSN-DOPA using nano silver fluoride (NSF), mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN), and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA). The morphology, elemental structure, size, crystallinity, and surface characteristics of the NSF-MSN-DOPA nanocomposite will be analysed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), SEM-energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The release kinetics and tooth-binding ability of NSF-MSN-DOPA will be assessed using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). We will prepare human dentine blocks with artificial carious lesions for treatment with NSF-MSN-DOPA. Post-treatment, the blocks will be incubated with a multi-species cariogenic biofilm (Streptococcus mutans, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Candida albicans) for cariogenic challenge in a computerised artificial mouth. SDF and deionised water will serve as positive and negative controls, respectively. To evaluate the antimicrobial effects of NSF-MSN-DOPA against the cariogenic biofilm, we will examine the architecture, viability, and kinetics of the biofilm using SEM, confocal laser scanning microscopy, and colony-forming unit counts. To assess the remineralising effects of NSF-MSN-DOPA on dentine carious lesions, we will analyse the surface morphology, crystal characteristics, and collagen degradation in the dentine blocks using SEM, XRD, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. To evaluate the discolouring effect of NSF-MSN-DOPA on dentine carious lesions, we will measure the colour change of the lesion after NSF-MSN-DOPA application using spectrophotometry. We will repeat the study (except collagen degradation) using human enamel blocks. Possible results and implications We expect that our novel NSF-MSN-DOPA will exhibit biocompatible, non-discolouring antimicrobial and remineralising properties. If successfully developed and translated into clinical practice, NSF-MSN-DOPA will offer a non-invasive, non-aerosol generating, and non-discolouring treatment for dental caries, which affects 2.4 billion people globally. 研究背景 齲齒是全球最常見的非傳染性疾病。世界衛生組織建議使用硝酸氨銀治療齲齒，該治療方法高效、操作簡單且非侵入性。然而，硝酸氨銀會導致齲損部位色素沉著，影響美觀，導致患者對其接受度低。我們設計了一種新型無著色銀奈米治療劑（NSF-MSN-DOPA）。該製劑可特異性靶向致齲生物膜，並響應pH變化精準釋放奈米銀。預實驗證實，NSF-MSN-DOPA能有效抑制主要致齲菌（變形鏈球菌），且相較於硝酸氨銀，NSF-MSN-DOPA具有無著色性和低細胞毒性。但其抗齲效能仍需係統驗證。 研究目標 評估NSF-MSN-DOPA對齲損的抗菌、再礦化及著色效應。 研究方法 以奈米氟化銀、介孔二氧化矽奈米顆粒及3,4-二羥基苯丙胺酸建構NSF-MSN-DOPA複合材料。採用掃描電子顯微鏡（SEM）、SEM-能譜聯用（SEM-EDS）、透射電鏡（TEM）、X射線衍射（XRD）及X射線光電子能譜（XPS）分析其形貌、元素組成、尺寸、結晶度及表面特性。以電感耦合等離子體發射光譜（ICP-OES）測定銀離子釋放動力學及牙體組織結合能力。分別施加NSF-MSN-DOPA處理、SDF及去離子水於齲壞的牙本質塊表面，以多菌種致齲生物膜進行齲蝕測試。透過SEM、共聚焦雷射掃描顯微鏡及菌落計數分析牙本質塊表面生物膜。結合SEM、XRD再礦化情況。使用分光光度計量化齲損區間色度變化。同步進行牙釉質塊實驗。 預期成果與意義 本研究將證實NSF-MSN-DOPA兼俱生物相容性、無著色抗菌及促進再礦化的特性。若成功轉化應用，可望為齲齒患者提供一種非侵入性的創新療法。

17129025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17129025.value: 使用摻鍶生物活性玻璃陶瓷填充的牙科黏著劑治療敏感牙齒：隨機雙盲對照臨床試驗

17129025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129025.value: Dentine hypersensitivity (DH) is a prevalent condition affecting individuals of all ages globally. DH-associated pain is distressing, significantly impacting daily activities and reducing overall quality of life. It hinders routine oral hygiene practices, further compromising patients’ oral health. Non-invasive strategies for DH management are recommended. Clinically, dentine adhesives (DA) demonstrate efficacy in providing immediate pain relief; however, concerns remain regarding the durability of their effects. Current evidence is insufficient to substantiate their effectiveness both immediately after application and beyond a 3-month period. Bioactive glass is compositionally similar to tooth structures and can form chemical bonds with them. It dissolves in aqueous environments and releases calcium and phosphate ions while the glass undergoes mesoporous change to form an apatite-like layer which can occlude and penetrate the dentinal tubules, thereby reducing the dentine permeability with time. A novel strontium-doped bioactive glass-ceramic (SBGC) has been shown to form larger, less soluble and more bioactive crystal particles. Synergistic and complementary effects between DA and SBGC may exist in producing long-term occlusion of patent dentinal tubules. This 6-month randomized double-blind controlled clinical trial aims to compare the effects of an SBGC-filled universal DA in the self-etch mode to that of DA on DH. It is hypothesized that the SBGC-filled DA is more effective in reducing DH and improving the oral health-related quality of life than DA alone. 142 healthy adults (aged 18-69 years) with complaints of DH will be recruited. The most sensitive tooth will be identified and tested with compressed cold air. The participants will give a sensitivity score (SS), which is a VAS from 0 (no pain) to 10 (agonizing), and complete the Dentine Hypersensitivity Experience Questionnaire (DHEQ) at baseline. They will then be randomly and equally divided to receive a single application of 1) SBGC-filled DA (test group) or 2) the same DA without SBGC (control group). After the intervention, they will receive the cold air test and report the SS again. This test will be repeated at 1-month, 3-month and 6-month post-intervention. At 6 months, they will complete the DHEQ again. Post-intervention data will be compared to the baseline data. The results of this study will provide high-quality evidence regarding the efficacy of a novel SBGC-filled DA in DH treatment. This will expand treatment options for DH, reduce the reliance on more invasive and irreversible dental procedures, and enhance the quality of life of the affected individuals.

17129225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17129225.value: CBL0137誘導的從多能性到全能性的分子和功能分析

17129225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129225.value: Totipotency refers to the developmental potential to give rise to all cell lineages in embryogenesis. The zygote and early blastomeres (the mouse early 2-cell embryo) can independently generate a blastocyst for post-implantation development and are thus totipotent. Studying totipotency advances the developmental knowledge, improves reproductive disease treatment and develop better cell therapy products. Major advances have been made recently to establish and culture stem cells (2-cell like cells or 2CLCs) exhibiting totipotency features molecularly and developmentally. This is achieved by using chemicals targeting epigenetic modifiers, signaling pathways, and splicing machinery. However, these new stem cells vary substantially and the underlying mechanisms for totipotency induction are elusive. Importantly, these published mouse 2CLCs have not fully recapitulated totipotent embryos’ salient features particularly transposable element (TE) expression. Furthermore,2CLCs have not been reported to be generated from somatic cells. CBL0137 is a small molecule that binds DNA and functionally inactivates the FAcilitates Chromatin Transcription (FACT) chromatin remodelling complex. It’s being extensively evaluated for cancer treatment. We find that CBL0137 rapidly and efficiently induces totipotency acquisition in both mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), offering a promising cross-lineage approach for investigating totipotency transition. These CBL0137-induced 2CLCs, or Z-cells for their similarities to mouse ZGA embryos, are transcriptomically more similar to mid-late 2C mouse embryos in expression of endogenous retrotransposons and stage-specific genes than the published stem cell models. Experimentally, a single Z-cell can extensively contribute to both extraembryonic and embryonic cell lineages in dpc (days post coitum) 13.5 chimeras. Remarkably, CBL0137 induces “de-differentiation” of the blastocyst to lose lineage gene expression. Mechanistically, CBL0137 binds GC-rich TE genomic regions and activates these TEs and the nearby totipotency genes. In order to dissect totipotency acquisition induced by CBL0137, we propose to use a multi-omic approach including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and Hi-C sequencing to comprehensively interrogate the underlying molecular mechanisms. We will examine and correlate the CBL0137-induced molecular changes to those in mouse normal and cloned embryo development for better understanding totipotency and for improved therapy. Importantly, we will explore CBL0137 in other cellular processes such as reprogramming somatic cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and the trans-differentiation of somatic cells to neural stem cells (NSCs). Finally, we propose to establish and characterize CBL0137-induced human totipotent-like stem cells for fundamental and for translational research. 全能性是指在胚胎发生过程中，具有生成所有细胞系的发育潜能。受精卵和早期胚细胞（如小鼠早期2细胞胚胎）能够独立形成囊胚，进行着床后发育，因此具有全能性。研究全能性有助于推动发育学的认识，改善生殖疾病的治疗，并开发更优质的细胞治疗产品。近年来，全能性研究取得了重大进展，科學家已成功建立和培养表现出全能性特征的干细胞（称为2细胞样细胞或2CLCs），在分子和发育层面都展现出全能性。这一成就主要通过使用针对表观遗传修饰因子、信号通路和剪接机制的化学药物实现。然而，这些新型干细胞差异较大，且全能性诱导的基本机制仍未完全阐明。值得注意的是，目前发表的鼠类2CLCs尚未完全再现全能胚胎的显著特征，尤其是转座元件（TE）的表达。此外，目前尚未报道能由体细胞直接生成2CLCs。 CBL0137是一种小分子药物，能够与DNA结合并使FAcilitates Chromatin Transcription（FACT）染色质重塑复合物失活。该药物正在被广泛评估用于癌症治疗。我们发现，CBL0137能够迅速且高效地诱导小鼠胚胎干细胞（mESCs）和胚胎成纤维细胞（MEFs）获得全能性，为研究全能性转变提供了一种有前景的跨谱系方法。这些由CBL0137诱导的2CLCs，因其与小鼠ZGA（受精后基因激活）胚胎的相似性，被称为Z细胞，在转录组特征上比已发表的干细胞模型更接近中晚期2细胞期的鼠胚胎，特别是在内源性逆转录转座元件和阶段特异性基因的表达方面。实验结果显示，一个Z细胞能够在受精后13.5天的嵌合体中，广泛贡献于胚外和胚胎细胞谱系。令人惊讶的是，CBL0137还能诱导囊胚“去分化”，使其失去谱系基因表达。从机制上看，CBL0137通过结合富含GC的TE基因组区域，激活这些转座元件及其附近的全能性相关基因。 为了深入解析由CBL0137诱导的全能性获得机制，我们拟采用多组学方法，包括单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）、单细胞ATAC测序（scATAC-seq）和Hi-C测序，全面研究其分子机制。我们将比较CBL0137诱导的分子变化与正常和克隆胚胎发育中的变化，以更好理解全能性，并促进其临床应用。此外，我们还将探索CBL0137在其他细胞过程中的潜力，如将体细胞重新编程为诱导多能干细胞（iPSCs）以及体细胞转分化为神经干细胞（NSCs）。最终，我们计划建立并表征由CBL0137诱导的人类类全能干细胞，为基础研究和转化医学提供新工具。

17129925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17129925.value: ELOVL1介導的異常脂質代謝在NAFLD相關肝癌中驅動特異性區域免疫微環境的作用

17129925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129925.value: The role of aberrant lipid metabolism mediated by ELOVL1 driving regional immune microenvironment specialization in NAFLD-related hepatocellular carcinoma Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), also termed metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), is increasingly recognized as a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed liver cancer treatment, the efficacy is inconsistent, particularly in patients with NAFLD-HCC. A key driver of NAFLD progression is dysregulated lipid metabolism, which not only induces lipotoxicity and oncogenic transformation to HCC but also promotes immune evasion within tumor microenvironment (TME). This occurs through the generation of chronic inflammation, which weakens the anti-tumor activity of immune cells, further complicating therapeutic outcomes. Therefore, understanding how aberrant lipid metabolism reshapes the immunosuppressive TME is essential for developing strategies to overcome immunotherapy resistance in NAFLD-related HCC. We focus on understanding the mechanisms behind HCC initiation, progression, and recurrence within the TME. We have identified a correlation between M2 macrophages and poor prognosis in HCC, highlighting their role in tumor growth. We also have demonstrated that disrupted AMPK-PGC1α and GSTA2-ROS signaling contributes to fatty liver injury and HCC recurrence through metabolic dysregulation. To discover the TME-related druggable target for lipid metabolism reprogramming in NAFLD-HCC, we established a CRISPR-dCas9 system to screen the metabolic targets based on different TME features. ELOVL1 was identified as the top candidate driving TME specialization, with its up-regulation linked to poor clinical outcomes. Knockdown of ELOVL1 in induced NAFLD-HCC mouse models confirmed its pro-tumor role. Further single-cell analysis of tumor infiltrating immune cells and preliminary mechanistic exploration in NAFLD-HCC models showed that ELOVL1 promoted a unique metabolic pattern with rich Erucic acid (EA, ω-9), leading to increased infiltration of GPNMB+CD206+ M2-like macrophages and reduced cytotoxic CD8 T cell. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that ELOVL1 overexpression, involved in lipid metabolic reprogramming, may reshape the immunosuppressive TME in NAFLD-related HCC. In current proposal, we aim to (1) demonstrate the role of ELOVL1 in NAFLD-HCC and figure out how it shapes tumor phenotypes to facilitate HCC progression and immune evasion; (2) explore the biological and metabolic mechanism of ELOVL1 and its metabolites within TME; (3) evaluate the synergistic inhibitory effect of ELOVL1 inhibitor and anti-PD1 treatment on NAFLD-HCC growth in pre-clinical models. Our investigation of aberrant lipid reprogramming mediated by ELOVL1 may provide a novel perspective to lay the foundation of clinical translation for the current NAFLD-HCC treatment strategies limitation. 摘要：非酒精性脂肪肝疾病（NAFLD），又稱代謝相關脂肪肝疾病，是一種病程可從單純脂肪肝進展至脂肪性肝炎甚至肝硬化的慢性疾病。NAFLD已被廣泛認為是肝細胞癌（HCC）的主要危險因子之一。儘管免疫檢查點抑制劑已革新肝癌治療，但在NAFLD-HCC患者中的療效仍不穩定。NAFLD進展的關鍵驅動因素之一是脂質代謝失調，這不僅導致脂毒性與癌變，亦促進腫瘤微環境（TME）中的免疫逃逸。慢性炎症削弱免疫細胞的抗腫瘤活性，進一步影響治療成效。因此，深入了解脂質代謝重編程如何重塑免疫抑制性TME，對克服免疫治療抗性至關重要。本團隊致力於探討HCC在TME中的發生、進展與復發機制。我們發現M2樣巨噬細胞與不良預後相關，並揭示其促進腫瘤生長與侵襲性。此外，我們研究了肝臟微環境中的代謝失調，發現AMPK-PGC1α軸的破壞會加劇脂肪肝移植損傷，而GSTA2則透過調控活性氧代謝促進移植後HCC復發，顯示脂質代謝在HCC進程中的重要性。為尋找可針對NAFLD-HCC脂質代謝重編程的TME策略性靶點，我們建立CRISPR-dCas9系統，基於不同TME特徵的代謝靶點體內篩選。結果顯示ELOVL1為驅動TME特化的首要候選基因，并與臨床不良結果相關。於NAFLD-HCC小鼠模型中敲除ELOVL1後，確認其促癌作用。進一步以單細胞分析探討腫瘤浸潤免疫細胞，發現ELOVL1促進一種特殊代謝模式，產生大量油芥酸，導致GPNMB⁺CD206⁺ M2樣巨噬細胞增加，並抑制細胞毒性CD8 T細胞浸潤。我們推測ELOVL1過度表達所引發的脂質代謝重編程，可能重塑NAFLD-HCC中的免疫抑制性TME，進而降低免疫治療反應性。本研究計畫將：(1) 驗證ELOVL1在NAFLD-HCC中的角色，並解析其如何促進腫瘤進展與免疫逃逸；(2) 探討ELOVL1及其代謝物在TME中的生物與代謝功能與機制；(3) 評估靶向ELOVL1的治療效果，以及其與抗PD-1治療的協同抑制作用。本研究對ELOVL1介導的脂質代謝重編程之探討，將為NAFLD-HCC有限的治療策略提供臨床轉譯的新視角。

17130225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17130225.value: 利用功能磁共振成像研究抑制性腦區Zona Incerta在全腦功能連接中的作用

17130225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17130225.value: Zona Incerta (ZI) was first described as a "zone of uncertainty" due to the inability to classify its primary targets or functions. Studies have begun to detail the numerous efferents and afferents of ZI with connections to nearly all major neural centers in central pathways ranging from the spinal cord, brainstem, and thalamus to the cerebral cortex. Recently, ZI has been implicated in diverse functional roles, such as processing sensory information, regulating behaviors, and conveying motivational states. Despite extensive knowledge of incertal projections and functions, we do not yet know where and how zona incerta (ZI) neural activity is distributed in central pathways. Blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) fMRI constitutes a powerful neuroimaging technology that can map brain-wide functions in response to specific sensory or cognitive tasks and during rest (i.e., resting-state functional MRI, rsfMRI). However, investigating the brain-wide functional connectivity of ZI via conventional fMRI approaches is technically challenging. There are presently no stimuli that can be presented to humans or rodents that would exclusively activate the zona incerta. Typically, these sensory or cognitive tasks would also activate numerous other cortical and subcortical regions. Hence, it is challenging to isolate the contribution of ZI neural activity to brain-wide functional connectivity. To address this research gap, it will be imperative to deploy new fMRI approaches. In our preliminary studies, we demonstrated that optogenetic fMRI enabled us to characterize for the first time the effects of manipulated ZI neural activities on rsfMRI connectivity and the brain-wide ZI downstream activation targets upon simple optogenetic stimulation of GABAergic inhibitory neurons. We hypothesize that, by combining fMRI and multi-site optogenetic stimulation, we can systematically (i) examine the role(s) of ZI in brain-wide functional connectivity (ii) characterize the respective downstream activation targets and brain-wide actions of ZI; and (iii) study the association between ZI functional connectivity and their functional effects in a more efficient and robust manner. We intend to examine this hypothesis by using rsfMRI to monitor brain-wide functional connectivity before, during, and after optogenetic stimulation of the ZI. ZI is a largely inhibitory/GABAergic elongated string-like nucleus located between the dorsal thalamus and hypothalamus and can be divided into four major sub-regions, namely the ventral, dorsal, rostral, and causal ZI. ZI is primarily comprised of a heterogeneous group of inhibitory cells, and we will selectively target such inhibitory neurons with specific GABA promoters.

17130325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17130325.value: 結合光遺傳功能性磁共振成像及腦電圖同步技術探究靜息態功能性磁共振成像網絡的神經基礎

17130325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17130325.value: One significant challenge in neuroscience is to comprehensively understand the brain's circuits, particularly the spatiotemporal patterns of neural activities that influence functions and behavior. Extensive efforts are being dedicated to unraveling the complexities of brain circuits and networks, with resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rsfMRI) emerging as a powerful technique to map large-scale brain networks in humans and animals non-invasively. Research indicates that changes in rsfMRI connectivity are closely linked to performance in sensory, memory, and learning tasks, suggesting that brain-wide functional connectivity networks play a crucial role in facilitating and modulating various sensory and cognitive functions. Additionally, advanced neuromodulation technologies like optogenetics and focused ultrasound allow for precise manipulation of brain circuitry, functions, and behavior, showing potential for enhancing and restoring functions in diseased brains. However, current basic brain research often overlooks the readily measurable rsfMRI networks when investigating brain circuits and networks. This is partly due to a lack of complete understanding of how specific rsfMRI networks influence normal brain functions and behaviors, especially at the neural level. Here, we propose to study the neural basis rsfMRI networks through direct neural perturbation of the thalamus and hippocampus with simultaneous electrophysiological measurements. The thalamus and hippocampus are increasingly viewed as the nexus of information processing in the brain, bridging inputs from the brainstem to cortex, to shape brain dynamics and subserve diverse cognitive and behavioral functions. We hypothesize that the optogenetic fMRI approach with simultaneous multi-modal measurements of whole-brain functional connectivity, rsfMRI and multi-site electrophysiological recordings, followed by computational/data-driven analysis of neural activity across temporal and spatial scales will shed light on the functional architecture of brain networks (i.e., dynamics of neural activity propagation/interaction at the whole-brain level). Optogenetic fMRI permits the examination of brain-wide neural activity through spatiotemporally precise manipulations of genetically defined neuronal activity at selected targets. Importantly, our approach to monitoring concurrent rsfMRI networks and underlying neural activity changes upon direct perturbation of specific neurons and/or brain circuits will enable us to further examine how such perturbations affect functions and behaviors.

17200125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200125.value: 將病理基礎模型與臨床知識結合以實現軟組織肉瘤的精準診斷與預後

17200125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17200125.value: Prof Huang, Yuanhua Prof Yeung, Chun Fai Maximus

17200125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200125.value: Soft tissue sarcomas (STS) are cancers of the body's soft tissues, such as muscles and fat. Their incidence is steadily increasing, leading to significant morbidity and mortality, especially among young adults, where certain sarcoma subtypes are among the leading causes of death. Accurate STS subtyping and prognosis (e.g., survival prediction) is crucial for guiding treatment but challenging due to significant morphological heterogeneity with over 50 subtypes. AI-based methods enable direct analysis of whole-slide histopathology images (WSI) for quantitative cancer diagnosis and prognosis. Recent public pathology foundation models (FMs), such as CONCH (Nature Medicine 2024) and Prov-GigaPath (Nature 2024), have advanced this area by extracting complex morphological patterns from histology images, surpassing traditional feature extraction methods based on natural image pre-trained encoders. Although these pathology FMs show promise in diagnosing common cancers, extending them to rare, heterogeneous, and continually evolving cancers like STS presents significant technical challenges: (1) The general-purpose features extracted by FMs may not be optimized for STS. Given the rarity (1% of all cancers) and high heterogeneity of STS, directly training predictors on these features could lead to severe overfitting and poor generalization. (2) STS diagnosis and prognosis increasingly rely on molecular characteristics like genomic mutations. Integrating genomic data into FMs is crucial but technically challenging due to its sparse and noisy nature. (3) As STS diagnostic guidelines evolve and new subtypes emerge, adaptive models incorporating the latest diagnostic findings are essential, but current FMs lack this flexibility. To address these challenges, this project will develop a novel clinical knowledge-informed adaptation framework to adapt pathology FMs for precise STS diagnosis and prognosis. To achieve this, we will incorporate different STS-specific clinical knowledge into FMs: (1) established histopathological features of various subtypes, (2) critical genomic data for diagnosis and prognosis, and (3) evolving diagnostic insights about new subtypes. Our innovations include (i) a novel histopathological factor-guided feature enhancement mechanism to optimize FM features for STS, (ii) the first copula modeling-based approach to integrate genomic data into FMs, (iii) a new Mixture-of-Experts-based dynamic learning paradigm that adapts FMs to evolving diagnostic findings, and (iv) an interactive AI system engaging pathologists to refine model outputs. Preliminary experiments have shown promising results in integrating clinical knowledge into FMs. Collaborating with pathologists from four leading hospitals, this project will pioneer the integration of FMs with clinical knowledge for rare cancer, advancing the global shift towards digital pathology and improving patient outcomes. 軟組織肉瘤（STS）是一類起源於肌肉、脂肪等身體軟組織的癌症，其發病率正持續上升，導致顯著的發病率與死亡率，特別是在年輕人中，某些亞型已成為主要死因之一。準確的STS亞型分類與預後預測（例如存活期預測）對於治療決策至關重要，但由於其形態學高度異質性（超過50種亞型），診斷挑戰極大。基於人工智能的方法能夠直接分析全視野組織切片影像（WSI），用於定量癌症診斷與預後分析。近期公開的病理基礎模型（如 CONCH《Nature Medicine 2024》與 Prov-GigaPath《Nature 2024》）在此領域取得重大進展，能從組織影像中提取複雜形態特徵，超越了以自然影像預訓練模型為基礎的傳統特徵提取方法。 儘管這些病理基礎模型在常見癌症診斷中表現出色，但應用於如STS這類罕見、高異質且不斷演化的癌症仍面臨重大技術挑戰：（1）這些模型提取的通用特徵未必適合STS，STS僅佔所有癌症的1%，直接在這些特徵上訓練預測器可能導致過擬合與泛化能力差；（2）STS的診斷與預後日益依賴於基因突變等分子層級特徵，而基因資料稀疏且雜訊大，整合至模型中技術困難重重；（3）隨著STS診斷指引演進與新亞型出現，模型需具備動態適應能力，而現有基礎模型缺乏此彈性。 為應對上述挑戰，本研究將提出一種嶄新的臨床知識導向調適框架，專為STS的精準診斷與預後而設計的病理基礎模型調適策略。具體來說，我們將引入多種STS特有的臨床知識，包括：（1）各亞型已知的組織學特徵；（2）與診斷和預後高度相關的關鍵基因資料；（3）新亞型相關的最新診斷發現。研究創新包括：(i) 以組織學因素為指引的特徵強化機制，以優化STS任務的模型表徵；(ii) 全球首個基於copula建模的基因資料整合方法；(iii) 一種基於專家混合架構（Mixture-of-Experts）的動態學習策略，能自動適應診斷指引的更新；以及 (iv) 一個與病理醫師互動的AI系統，用於模型輸出的精細調整。 初步實驗已證明將臨床知識整合入病理基礎模型的可行性與潛力。本研究將與來自四所頂尖醫院的病理專家合作，率先推動將病理基礎模型與臨床知識結合應用於罕見癌症領域，促進數字病理的全球發展，最終提升病患的診療結果。

17200425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200425.value: 用於可穿戴生物傳感的可拉伸水凝膠中離子與電子傳輸機制研究

17200425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200425.value: The field of wearable research is advancing rapidly, offering the potential to shift healthcare from a hospital-centric model to a more personal, human-centric approach. At the heart of wearable biosensors are electrodes, which are crucial for determining sensing quality. Yet, when these electrodes are placed near the human body, mismatches occur: the body is organic, soft, and conducts ions, while traditional electrodes are inorganic, rigid, and conduct electrons. These differences can lead to poor signal quality at the body-electrode interface. Hydrogels present an ideal solution for interfacing with the skin, as they can address these mismatches. Traditional hydrogels, however, are often fragile. Recent research has begun to explore stretchable hydrogels, but creating one that is both stretchable and conductive is challenging. This requires combining material properties that are often opposite in nature, such as electrical, mechanical, and electrochemical properties. Moreover, wearable applications demand that these hydrogels endure harsh conditions like strain, temperature changes, and swelling. The effects of these conditions on hydrogels remain largely unexplored. Our team has recently developed a series of double-network stretchable hydrogels using the conducting polymer poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS). These hydrogels are not only stretchable but also have a highly conductive framework, making them promising for wearable biosensing. However, our preliminary findings show that even with similar conductivity, there are notable differences in sensing results among these hydrogels. To understand these discrepancies, it is essential to study and differentiate between ion and electron conductivities. Gaining a comprehensive understanding of these dynamics is crucial for us to optimize hydrogel performance in real-world applications. This project seeks to explore the fundamental behaviors of ion and electron transport in stretchable hydrogels to fill the knowledge gap for wearable applications. We will first synthesize various stretchable PEDOT:PSS hydrogels and examine how their stretchability depends on material composition and processing conditions. We will then use theoretical modeling alongside electrical, mechanical, and electrochemical analyses to study the macroscopic ion-electron transport properties and their relationship with the microscopic structures of the hydrogels. With this knowledge, we aim to control the ionic, electronic, and mechanical properties of hydrogels for practical applications in wearable biosensing. This research will generate new knowledge in materials science. The outcomes will offer timely solutions and valuable references for developing versatile stretchable hydrogel electrodes, critical to advancing medical electronics, wearable health, and digital health applications. 可穿戴設備領域正在快速發展，有望將醫療模式從以醫院為中心轉向更個人化、以人為本的方向。可穿戴生物傳感器的核心是電極，它們對傳感品質至關重要。然而，當這些電極接觸人體時，會出現不匹配現象：人體是有機、柔軟且以離子導電為主，而傳統電極則是無機、剛硬且以電子導電為主。這些差異常導致人體與電極界面的信號品質不佳。 水凝膠因其柔軟、親膚的特性，被認為是解決這種不匹配問題的理想材料。然而，傳統水凝膠通常較為脆弱。近年來，研究人員開始探索可拉伸水凝膠，但要實現同時具備高導電性與高延展性的水凝膠並不容易。這需要在電學、力學和電化學等性能之間取得平衡。而且，可穿戴應用還要求這些水凝膠能耐受拉伸、溫度變化和膨脹等苛刻條件，這些條件對水凝膠的影響仍未被充分研究。 我們團隊最近開發了一系列雙網絡可拉伸水凝膠，基於導電聚合物 PEDOT:PSS（聚(3,4-乙烯二氧噻吩)-聚苯乙烯磺酸鹽）。這些水凝膠不僅具有良好的延展性，還擁有高導電性，展現出在可穿戴生物傳感中的應用潛力。然而，我們的初步研究發現，即使這些水凝膠的導電性相似，其傳感性能仍存在顯著差異。為了解釋這些差異，我們需要深入研究並區分水凝膠中的離子與電子導電性。全面了解這些傳輸機制，對於優化水凝膠在實際應用中的表現至關重要。 本研究旨在探討可拉伸水凝膠中離子與電子傳輸的基本行為，以填補其在可穿戴應用中的知識空白。我們將首先合成不同組成的可拉伸 PEDOT:PSS 水凝膠，並分析其延展性如何受到材料組成和加工條件的影響。接著，我們將結合理論建模與電學、力學和電化學分析，研究水凝膠的宏觀離子-電子傳輸特性與微觀結構之間的關係。通過這些研究，我們希望實現對水凝膠離子、電子和機械性能的精確調控，從而應用於實際的可穿戴生物傳感器中。 這項研究將為材料科學領域帶來新知識，其成果將為開發多功能、可拉伸的水凝膠電極提供及時的解決方案和寶貴參考，助力醫療電子學、可穿戴健康設備和數字健康應用的進步。

17200725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200725.value: 利用立體視頻實現逼真且幾何準確的3D和4D生成

17200725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200725.value: The project proposes to leverage stereo videos for a photorealistic and geometrically correct 3D and 4D generation. While advancements like DALLE and SORA excel in high-resolution image and video generation, they struggle with geometric accuracy and multiview consistency due to focusing on pixel generation rather than 3D geometry representation. Current 3D datasets lack photorealistic textures, and the scale is relatively small compared to image datasets, hindering the generation of photorealistic 3D content. Additionally, research on 4D generation is in its early stages and often has issues with geometric correctness. To address all these issues, we propose to leverage stereo videos for 3D and 4D generation. Stereo videos, like human eyes, provide natural geometric constraints for generating visually consistent content. Specifically, this project mainly focuses on three tasks: 1) Photorealistic and geometrically correct 3D object and scene generation with stereo videos. 2) Generalizable and geometrically correct 4D generation from stereo videos. 3) Geometrically correct and multiview consistent 4D generation. As far as we know, this is the first stereo-video-based 3D and 4D project. Our methods are expected to significantly improve the geometry quality and multiview consistency of the generated 3D and 4D content. We have elaborately designed a trinocular video capture system and gathered 3000 videos of memorable moments in daily life. In the future, we will build a large-scale dataset to facilitate the research along these directions. Such a trinocular video dataset will significantly contribute to the research on 3D/4D reconstruction and generation and video generation. Our stereo-video-based 3D and 4D generation would significantly advance the development of computer vision and computer graphics, providing substantial benefits to the Hong Kong government, Central government, and global communities. In the short term, the outcomes of our project would provide a simulation environment for embodied AI and robotics, streamlining the CAD design in manufacturing, reducing the production costs and timelines in film, and enriching VR gaming experiences. In the long run, these advancements will enhance Hong Kong’s leadership in technology and culture and diversify its economy. To support the project's implementation, we have done some preliminary work in data collection and in verifying the effectiveness of stereo videos for 4D reconstruction. PI has extensive research experience in image and video generation, 3D generation, and 4D generation, which lays the solid foundation for this project. We are confident that we can achieve all project objectives within the specified timeline and budget. 項目旨在利用立體視頻實現可擴展、幾何精確且多視角一致的3D和4D內容生成。儘管近年來高分辨率圖像和視頻生成技術取得了巨大進步（如DALLE、Midjourney和SORA等），但這些方法往往注重像素級生成，而非真實的三維表示，因此在幾何準確性和多視角一致性方面存在不足。此外，現有的3D數據集主要以物體為中心，缺少逼真的紋理，規模也遠小於圖像數據集，這限制了逼真三維場景的生成。在4D生成方面，當前所有方法都需要對每個場景進行單獨優化，耗時較長且難以保證幾何正確性。 為解決上述問題，我們提出利用立體視頻進行3D和4D生成的研究。就像人類的雙眼一樣，立體視頻能夠自然地為場景提供幾何約束，從而促進生成幾何精確、多視角一致的視覺內容。具體來說，本項目將聚焦以下三項任務：1）基於立體視頻的可擴展、幾何精確、多視角一致的3D物體和場景生成；2）基於立體視頻條件實現具備泛化能力和幾何準確性的4D生成；3）給定文本/圖像條件下，實現幾何感知、多視角一致性的4D生成。據我們了解，這將是首個基於立體視頻的3D和4D生成研究項目。本方法的創新性有助於在圖像質量和幾何一致性方面帶來顯著提升。為了推動相關任務的研究和性能評估，我們已設計了三目視頻採集系統，並收集了3000段記錄生活精彩瞬間的視頻。未來，我們還將建設大規模數據集，為該方向的研究提供支持。這將成為首個三目視頻數據集，對現有的圖像和視頻生成技術具有重要推動作用。 基於立體視頻的3D和4D生成技術將極大地促進計算機視覺和計算機圖形學領域的發展，為香港政府、中央政府及全球社會帶來廣泛益處。短期內，本項目成果將為機器人研發提供仿真環境，優化製造業中的CAD設計，降低影視製作成本與周期，豐富虛擬現實遊戲體驗。長期來看，這些技術進步將提升香港在數字故事創作領域的文化影響力，推動經濟多元化，並助力智慧城市建設。 為保障項目順利實施，項目負責人已在數據採集和驗證立體視頻用於4D重建方面做了大量前期工作，並在圖像、視頻、3D和4D生成領域積累了豐富經驗，為本項目奠定了堅實基礎。我們有信心在限定的時間和預算內完成所有項目目標。

17200925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200925.value: 基於憶阻器共位腦訊號處理和加密的高效安全腦機接口

17200925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200925.value: In Hong Kong, over 0.5 million people, constituting more than 7% of the population, live with disabilities. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer these individuals convenience and hope for recovery by directly connecting the brain to the external world. However, contemporary BCIs face two critical challenges. First, processing efficiency is strained by the increasing volume of brain data and complexity of signal processing algorithms, pushing against the limits of current hardware constrained by transistor scaling and von Neumann architectures. Second, BCIs face significant security and privacy concerns since they process sensitive neurological data reflecting brain activity. Wireless transmission exposes this data to risks of theft, interception, and alteration. Meanwhile, unauthorized access could lead to device malfunctions or user harm. Moreover, to comply with ethical and legal standards, BCIs must ensure both the confidentiality and integrity of neurological data. Memristors offer potential solutions through energy-efficient compute-in-memory (CIM) and physically unclonable functions (PUFs) for encryption. This project aims to develop a novel, secure, and energy-efficient BCI system by leveraging memristor technology, specifically through co-located processing and encryption methods. Our preliminary experimental results indicate that such a design can handle common CIM-based processing tasks and simultaneously implement robust PUFs, demonstrating the feasibility of our approach. To achieve this aim, our research objectives are to: 1. Develop multiple memristor-compatible brain signal processing algorithms and accuracy improvement methods. 2. Design co-located methods for memristor-enabled CIM+PUF. 3.Create a memristor chip and circuits with co-located CIM+PUF capability. 4. Implement a secure and energy-efficient BCI using the designed and fabricated memristor chip. Through this research, we will investigate memristor non-idealities, identify key design factors, and determine effective strategies for realizing secure and efficient memristor-based BCIs. The outcomes of this project will contribute to advancing medical and health device applications, potentially improving the quality of life for individuals with disabilities. 在香港，超過50萬人口（佔總人口7%以上）生活在殘障狀態。腦機接口（BCI）透過直接連接大腦與外部世界，為這些人群提供便利和康復希望。然而，當代腦機接口面臨兩個關鍵挑戰。首先，隨著腦部資料量的增加和訊號處理演算法複雜性的提升，處理效率受到衝擊，逼近了受電晶體縮放和馮諾依曼架構限制的當前硬體極限。其次，腦機接口在處理反映大腦活動的敏感神經資料時面臨重大安全和隱私問題。無線傳輸使這些數據面臨被盜、攔截和篡改的風險。同時，未經授權的存取可能導致設備故障或使用者傷害。此外，為了符合倫理和法律標準，腦機接口必須確保神經資料的機密性和完整性。 憶阻器透過高能效的存算一體（CIM）和用於加密的物理不可複製函數（PUF）提供了潛在解決方案。本計畫旨在利用憶阻器技術，特別是透過共位處理和加密方法，開發一種新穎、安全且高能效的腦機接口系統。我們的初步實驗結果表明，這種設計能夠處理常見的基於存算一體的處理任務，同時實現強健的物理不可複製函數，證明了我們方法的可行性。 為實現這一目的，我們的研究目標是：1. 開發多種憶阻器相容的腦訊號處理演算法和精度改進方法。 2. 設計憶阻器驅動的存算一體+物理不可複製函數的共位方法。 3. 創建具有共位存算一體+物理不可複製函數能力的憶阻器晶片和電路。 4. 使用設計和製造的憶阻器晶片實現安全且高能效的腦機接口。 透過這項研究，我們將研究憶阻器的非理想特性，識別關鍵設計因素，並確定實現安全且高效的基於憶阻器腦機接口的有效策略。該計畫的成果將有助於推進醫療和健康設備應用，潛在地改善殘疾人群的生活品質。

17201025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201025.value: 面向長時序通用操作的彈性分層模仿學習

17201025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201025.value: This research aims to develop a resilient manipulation policy for fine-grained bimanual tasks that involve a long sequence of actions, such as assembly tasks summarized in NIST prototype Assembly Task Boards and instrument operation in labs reported by Nature. These tasks challenge robots due to the precise coordination of two arms, contact forces, and timing phases, which conventional model-based manipulation struggles to handle. A recent breakthrough uses end-to-end imitation learning to bypass the complexity of modeling contacts by leveraging the robot's historical motions or sensory channels and to simplify coordination by mimicking an expert’s timing profiles. This approach allows the robot to replicate expert skills in similar situations, showing promising progress in various tasks involving complex contacts and coordination. Despite advancements in imitation learning, current bimanual manipulation policies lack resilience, particularly in adapting to significant covariate shifts between expert demonstrations and actual test situations. They also struggle to respond to and recover from failures effectively. Resilience is crucial for completing long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in industries or businesses where smooth handovers and reliable contact switches are essential. Failure to maintain resilience when approaching task milestones can significantly decrease task success rates. This project proposes achieving a resilient contact-rich manipulation policy by decomposing long-horizon tasks into high-, mid-, and low-level skills and employing hierarchical imitation learning to facilitate adaptation and recovery from failures. The resilient mid-level policy focuses on the recovery behavior of each subtask for short-horizon manipulation. We propose identifying key milestones from expert demonstrations as subgoals to guide the robot in achieving manageable objectives and avoiding premature execution of subsequent subgoals. We also suggest a contrastive learning-based mechanism to utilize both negative demonstrations that fail and precious interactive correction examples from experts. The resilient high-level policy handles switching between different subtasks by mimicking task planning strategies and using a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) mechanism to select optimal mid-level skills. In the event of premature execution of a mid-level skill, the high-level policy will step back until the mode-switch prerequisites are met and then reattempt. The resilience of low-level policies requires robust motor commands despite covariate shifts in kinematics and temporal profiles, which will be addressed through developments characterized by kinematics-awareness and online phase estimation. Our resulting resilient long-horizon manipulation tasks will be tested on extended versions of challenging industrial assembly benchmarks and clinical laboratory benchmarks, where the robot must sequentially complete a series of diverse manipulation tasks. 這項研究旨在針對涉及長序列動作的細緻雙臂操作任務開發具備彈性的操作策略。這些任務因需精確協調雙臂、接觸力以及時序階段，使得傳統的基於模型的操作方法難以應對。近期的突破則是利用端到端的模仿學習，通過利用機器人的歷史動作或感測信號來繞過接觸建模的複雜性，並通過模仿專家時序特徵來簡化協調。這種方法讓機器人在相似情境下能夠複現專家技能，在涉及複雜接觸與協調的各類任務中展現出可喜進展。 儘管模仿學習已有進展，目前的雙臂操作策略在適應專家示範與實際測試情境之間顯著協變偏移時，仍缺乏彈性，且難以有效響應並從失敗中恢復。彈性對於完成工業或商業中需平順交接與可靠接觸切換的長時序、高接觸密度任務至關重要。若在接近任務里程碑時未能保持彈性，將大幅降低任務成功率。 本項目提出，將長時序任務分解為高、中、低三層技能，並採用分層模仿學習以促進適應與失敗恢復，從而實現具彈性的高接觸密度操作策略。彈性的中層策略專注於每個子任務的短時序操作恢復行為。我們建議從專家示範中提取關鍵里程碑作為子目標，引導機器人完成可控的目標，避免過早執行後續子目標。同時，提出一種對比學習機制，充分利用失敗的負面示範及專家的寶貴互動修正範例。 彈性的高層策略則通過模仿任務規劃策略，並採用專家混合（Mixture-of-Experts, MoE）機制來選擇最佳中層技能，以實現不同子任務間的切換。若中層技能被過早執行，高層策略會回退，直至模式切換條件滿足後再重試。低層策略的彈性則要求在運動學與時序特徵發生協變偏移時，依然能發出穩健的運動指令，這將通過具備運動學感知與線上階段估算特徵的開發來解決。 我們最終得到的具彈性的長時序操作策略，將在擴展版本的工業組裝基準與臨床實驗室基準任務中進行測試，機器人需順序完成一系列多樣的操作任務。

17201225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201225.value: 面向用户側表後資源協調的輕量化學習研究

17201225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17201225.value: Prof Cañizares, Claudio Prof Morstyn, Thomas

17201225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201225.value: Nowadays, numerous distributed energy resources (DERs), e.g., rooftop photovoltaics and electric vehicles, have been integrated into houses and buildings, producing and consuming energy behind smart meters. These behind-the-meter (BtM) resources can be coordinated to provide flexibility to power systems. Nonetheless, coordinating BtM resources is challenging due to their spatial distribution and temporal variability. In this context, traditional centralized methods are costly in terms of communication and computation. Thus, lightweight decentralized methods on edge devices are crucial for the scalable coordination of BtM resources. Three specific analyses are needed to coordinate BtM resources, i.e., descriptive analysis for monitoring and modeling of BtM resources, predictive analysis for load forecasting with BtM resources, and prescriptive analysis for the coordination among BtM resources in market environments. In these analyses, edge devices are required to act with low latency and high accuracy, but their computing power is too low to conduct traditional algorithms. Such contradiction hinders the efficient coordination of massive BtM resources. To fill this research gap, this project will work on lightweight learning approaches on edge devices, which can conduct descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analysis, thus realizing the coordination of BtM resources with low costs but high efficiency. First, this project will tailor unsupervised and supervised learning techniques to edge devices, realizing non-intrusive load monitoring and personalized indoor thermal dynamics modeling, respectively. On this basis, a BtM information-embedded load forecasting technique will be investigated, considering the memory constraints of individual edge devices. An accelerated reconciliation method will be further developed to make hierarchical load forecasts consistent at multiple spatial levels. Then, this project will work on efficient energy management schemes for BtM resources under various power markets, taking communication overheads between massive devices into account. Finally, versatile plug-and-play hardware modules will be developed to implement the proposed lightweight algorithms. Validation tests on the hardware will be carried out accordingly on a microgrid platform. This project will constitute a logical extension of the PI’s previous research scope. The novel methods and algorithms developed in the project will enrich the current BtM resources coordination approaches from a practical and novel lightweight angle. In this way, ubiquitous edge devices can be empowered with descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive functions in a lightweight fashion, thereby supporting the flexible coordination of BtM resources and accelerating the transformation of energy systems. 如今，海量分布式能源資源（如屋頂光伏和電動汽車）已接入住宅與建築，表後特性使得智能電表無法直接計量其能源生產與消費。這些表後資源可通過協同調度爲電力系統提供靈活性，但因其空間分布的廣泛性和時變性強等特點，協調難度較大。傳統集中式方法在通信與計算成本方面代價高昂，因此在邊緣設備上部署輕量化的分布式方法對實現表後資源規模化協調至關重要。 表後資源的協調分析包括三個重要方面，即描述性分析（表後資源的監測與建模）、預測性分析（表後資源的負荷預測），以及決策性分析（市場環境下表後資源協調）。然而，邊緣設備雖需滿足低時延、高精度的要求，其有限的計算能力卻難以支撐傳統算法的運行，這一矛盾嚴重制約海量表後資源的高效協調。 爲填補這一研究空白，本項目致力於開發適用於邊緣設備的輕量化學習方法，以低成本、高效率實現表後資源協調。首先，通過提出無監督與有監督學習技術，在邊緣設備上實現非侵入式負荷監測與個性化房屋熱動態建模。在此基礎上，針對單臺邊緣設備的內存限制，提出表後信息嵌入的負荷預測技術，並提出加速協調方法以確保多層級負荷預測的一致性。此外，開發大規模設備間通信開銷可控的高效能能源管理方案，適配多樣化電力市場場景。最後，研制多功能即插即用硬件模塊以集成所提輕量化算法，並在微電網平臺上開展硬件驗證測試。 本項目將作爲項目負責人既往研究範疇的邏輯延伸，以創新方法爲表後資源協調領域注入新動力。項目研發的新型輕量化方法與算法，將從實用性、輕量化雙重維度革新現有表後資源協調範式。通過這一創新路徑，項目將爲邊緣設備部署可擴展的分析能力提供理論支撐與實踐範例，推動能源系統向分布式、智能化方向加速轉型。

17201325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201325.value: 三維點雲中建築開口檢測：一類局部孔洞語意圖及全域設計規則的雙目標優化方法

17201325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17201325.value: Prof Crolla, Kristof Prof YEH, Anthony Gar-On

17201325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201325.value: This project aims to apply bi-objective optimization and graph learning to detect architectural openings, such as 3D hollows and maneuvering clearances installed with windows and doors, from point clouds. Openings admit air and light into buildings and, thus, are essential for any livable architecture. Recent advances in LiDAR technology resulted in affordable 3D point clouds on existing buildings. However, LiDAR points are handicapped in surveying openings’ functional hollows and movable components, leading to missing data (e.g., owing to transparency of glass and air), probabilistic data (e.g., multiple open and closed door states during scanning), and ambiguous data (e.g., hard-to-distinguish voids between space, hallways, and openings). Thus, a dilemma exists between the LiDAR-invisible hollows of openings and LiDAR's limitations. Consequently, the dilemma undermines LiDAR's effectiveness in architectural opening surveying, which is necessary for 3D indoor space networks, visual access to nature, natural lighting 3D maps, local thermal comfort spots, carbon emissions, etc. The dilemma also challenges researchers in other disciplines, e.g., instructing a household robot to open the second drawer or living room window. The major innovation of this project lies in the bi-objective optimization formulation that addresses two objectives, (i) local semantic graphs of openings and (ii) global design regularity of 3D hollows, to resolve the dilemma. First, dense 3D points of functional hollows are added to LiDAR-visible point clouds to create opening and neighboring supervoxel graphs of interest (ONSI). GPU-powered graph learning labels ONSI’s semantics, e.g., door hollow, maneuvering clearance, window, and indoor space. The global design regularities include symmetry, repetition, and collinearity with other openings. Pareto optima indicate candidate architectural openings. The feasibility of this project was partially verified in a small pilot of ONSI graph learning. The project will extend the study scope, incorporate both objectives, and gauge the overall approach to Hong Kong’s and other smart cities’ datasets. This project delivers both academic insights and practical advantages. The findings will expand our understanding of how modern optimization and GPU-powered graph learning can be integrated to process LiDAR data. The explainable local ONSI graphs and global regularity patterns may contribute to a breakthrough in theoretical explanations, regarding how architectural domain knowledge can systematically overcome the limitations in LiDAR data, in the case of openings detection. For professionals, the research outcomes will be integrated into a user-friendly LiDAR processing tool for multiple disciplines and industries, e.g., architecture, construction, engineering, automotive, and robotics. 本項目運用雙目標優化與圖學習技術，從點雲數據中檢測建築開口。LiDAR（激光雷達）技術提供新型建築三維點雲數據，然而，LiDAR在檢測開口存在局限（如透明材質數據缺失、可移動部件的多狀態數據不確定性、及不同類孔洞數據歧義）。本項目的首要創新在於提出一類雙目標優化模型，以解決這一難題。該模型同時考慮兩個目標：（i）開口的局部語義圖，及（ii）三維孔洞的全局規律性。首先，將功能性孔洞的不可見三維點集補充到LiDAR可見的點雲中，生成關注的開口與鄰近超體素圖。基於圖學習技術標注體素圖的語義，例如門洞、操作空間、窗戶和室內空間。全局設計規律性包括對稱性、重複性以及與其他開口的共線性。通過帕雷托最優（Pareto optima）確定候選建築開口。本項目的可行性已在一項小規模的體素圖學習試點中得到部分驗證。項目將進一步擴大研究範圍，整合雙目標，並在香港及其他智慧城市的數據集上評估整體方法。研究成果將深化優化與圖學習技術處理LiDAR數據。可解釋的局部體素圖與全局規律模式可能展示建築領域知識系統性地克服LiDAR技術在特定檢測中的局限，適用於建築、施工、工程、汽車及機器人等多個學科與行業。

17201425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201425.value: 水上復健 AI 治療師

17201425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17201425.value: Dr Lai, Wai-ying Prof Liu, Jun

17201425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201425.value: Aquatic Physical Functional Rehabilitation (APFR) is a viable alternative to traditional land-based rehabilitation, leveraging water’s unique properties like buoyancy and viscosity, making it particularly suitable for individuals with pain or limited mobility. While APFR benefits those with various physical functional deficiencies, concerns remain over timely, proactive, and objective detection and alert of safety risks (e.g., drowning, overexertion, hypothermia, and dehydration) during rehabilitation. This research aims to offer an innovative ‘Technology-Supported Aquatic Rehabilitation Protocol,’ integrating artificial intelligence (AI), low-power wireless sensor technologies, and advanced signal processing and analytics to create a cyber aquatic therapist. This protocol will provide real-time monitoring and analysis of physiological status, along with risk prediction and alerts to enhance APFR safety and effectiveness. The core technological system, the cyber aquatic therapist, will include a low-power wireless sensor network and client applications. The sensor network, equipped with waterproof sensors, will allow continuous collection of physiological and environmental data in real-time to obtain a comprehensive view of physiological status. Data will first be processed locally for immediate monitoring, then transmitted to a cloud server for analysis using advanced AI algorithms. These algorithms will analytically predict abnormal physiological signals and risks. Client applications will manage monitoring and prediction, provide real-time displays of abnormal data and risks, and issue alerts. Assessment of the protocol's accuracy and reliability will follow. Specifically, the precision of physiological monitoring and the accuracy of the AI models will first be assessed within a controlled laboratory framework. Subsequent field tests studying individuals undergoing APFR, carers, and trainers, who will use the protocol in routine training, will occur in real-world settings. Participants will also provide their feedback on the protocol’s usability and overall user experience. Our Technology-Supported Aquatic Rehabilitation Protocol and its cyber aquatic therapist will provide unique monitoring, analytics, and risk alert capabilities, intelligently and significantly improving aquatic rehabilitation safety and effectiveness in ways previously not possible. With this protocol in place, APFR will become more accessible and accepted by individuals in need and their caregivers, contributing to the broader dissemination of advanced rehabilitation practices. Also, with minor adaptations, the protocol can ensure safety in other water-related activities, such as swimming and diving, extending its practical applications beyond APFR and potentially benefiting a broader population. “水中身體功能康復” 是一種可行替代傳統陸地康復的方案，其利用水的特性，如浮力與黏性，使其特別適合有疼痛或行動受限的個體。儘管 “水中身體功能康復” 對多種身體功能缺陷患者具有顯著益處，但在康復過程中，如何及時、主動且客觀地檢測與預警安全風險（如溺水、過度勞累、低體溫和脫水）仍存在不足之處。 本研究旨在提出一種創新的「技術支援的水中康復模型」，結合人工智能（AI）、低功耗無線感測技術，以及先進的信號處理與分析技術，打造一個網路水中治療師。該模型將提供生理狀態的即時監測與分析，並進行風險預測與預警，從而提升水中康復的安全性和有效性。我們的核心技術系統，即網路水中治療師，將包含一個低功耗無線感測器網絡和客戶端應用程式。感測器網絡配備防水感測器，能夠持續即時收集生理與環境數據，全面掌握患者的生理狀態。數據收集後，首先會進行本地即時處理以實現初步監測，隨後傳輸至雲端伺服器，利用先進的人工智能算法進行深度分析。這些算法將預測異常生理信號與潛在風險。客戶端應用程式則負責監測與預測管理，即時顯示異常數據與風險，並發出相應預警。 為確保該康復模型的準確性與可靠性，我們將進行一系列評估。首先，在受控的實驗室環境中，評估生理監測的精確度與人工智能模型的準確性。隨後，進行實地測試，邀請接受“水中身體功能康復”的個體、護理人員及培訓師參與，在實際訓練中使用該模型。參與者亦將提供關於模型可用性與整體用戶體驗的反饋。 我們的技術支援水中康復模型及其網路水中治療師，將提供獨特的監測、分析與風險預警能力，以智能化的方式提升水中康復的安全性和有效性，這是過往無法實現的突破。隨著該模型的開發與應用，“水中身體功能康復” 將更易被有需求的個體及其護理人員接受，從而推動先進康復實踐的廣泛普及。此外，經過適度調整，該模型亦可應用於其他水上活動（如游泳與潛水），確保其安全性，擴展其實際應用範圍，不僅限於 “水中身體功能康復”，並有望惠及更廣泛的人群。

17201525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201525.value: 考慮多車輛類型、多種建築材料、多拓撲機制的創新模塊化建築編隊運輸方法

17201525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17201525.value: Prof Brilakis, Ioannis Prof Li, Jiayang Prof Skibniewski, Mirosław J.

17201525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201525.value: The construction industry is one of the most energy consumption industries since it accounts for 36% of energy usage and 40% of CO2 emissions worldwide. Hong Kong has set out carbon emission target in construction industry to achieve an 11% reduction against business-as-usual in 2023. To this end, the Hong Kong Construction Industry Council (CIC) has been promoting emerging technologies such as MiC for better environmental, social, and economic perspectives compared with the traditional cast-in-place approach. The delivery of MiC components and relevant building materials plays a critical role in construction management. One of the key fundamental research topics is the efficient transport mode for MiC projects with several emerging challenges. Firstly, there are many types of vehicles (e.g., pickup trucks, vans etc) used for transporting the building materials for MiC projects. Currently, each type of vehicle is shared by many projects each of which has a foreman competing for scheduling delivery tasks without considering any collaborative approaches. Secondly, hundreds of building materials (e.g., MiC components, window frames, fit-out materials etc.) will be transported from MiC manufacturers and distribution centers/warehouses. These materials are delivered on a demand basis through phone-call or messages between on-site foremen and shop floor/warehouse managers, resulting in inefficient transport in construction management. Thirdly, the information sharing among different stakeholders within a MiC project is lagged and fragged. This causes a lack of visibility and traceability on building materials delivery. To tackle these challenges, this project aims to address the fundamental research problem by providing a novel approach. A cooperative autonomous electric vehicular platoon framework is firstly designed and developed through considering multi-vehicle types. The framework uses advanced technologies such as Digital Twin, Internet of Things (IoT), etc to share the information to stakeholders so that the platoon could be monitored with real-time statuses. Moreover, an optimization model is proposed to synchronize all required building materials for MiC construction based on the established platoon with multi-vehicle types. This model considers multi-building materials transport with a one-off delivery to improve construction efficiency. Finally, an innovative control method using multi-topology mechanisms is introduced for managing the platoon. The designed and developed framework, models and methods will be validated through simulation studies using the real-life data from industrial collaborators. Key findings and observations from this project will be translated into policies and managerial implications which will be valuable for MiC projects management in the Greater Bay Area. 模塊化建築 (MiC) 對於滿足香港日益增長的住房需求，提高品質和效率至關重要。建築業是能源消耗最高的產業之一，佔全球能源消耗的 36%，二氧化碳排放量的 40%。香港已設定建築業碳排放目標，即 2023 年，建築業碳排放量比常規情況減少 11%。為此，香港建造業議會 (CIC) 一直致力於推廣 MiC 等新興技術，以其與傳統的現澆施工方式相比，在環境、社會和經濟方面取得更佳成效。 高效的運輸模式是 MiC 項目的關鍵基礎研究主題之一，目前面臨許多挑戰。首先，用於運輸 MiC 專案建築材料的車輛類型繁多（例如皮卡車、廂型車等），每種車輛由多個項目共用，每個項目都有一名工頭爭奪運輸任務的調度，缺乏協作機制；其次，數百種建築材料（例如 MiC 組件、窗框、裝修材料等）需要從 MiC 製造商和配送中心/倉庫運輸，這些材料需要透過現場工頭和車間/倉庫經理之間的電話或簡訊按需交付，導致施工管理中的運輸效率低下；第三，MiC 專案內不同利害關係人之間的資訊共享滯後且分散化，導致建築材料交付缺乏可見性和可追溯性。 為了應對這些挑戰，本項目提出考慮多車輛類型、多種建築材料、多拓撲機制的創新模塊化建築編隊運輸方法來應對此基礎研究問題。首先，設計並開發了一個考慮多種車型的自主協作電動汽車車隊框架，該框架運用數位孿生、物聯網 (IoT) 等先進技術，將資訊共享給各利益相關方，以便即時監控車隊狀態；此外，基於已建立的多車型車隊，提出了一個最佳化模型，用於同步組裝式建築 (MiC) 施工所需的所有建築材料，該模型考慮多種建築材料的一次性運輸，以提高施工效率；最後，引入了一種基於多拓撲機制的創新控制方法來管理車隊。 本項目將使用來自產業合作企業的真實數據，透過模擬研究驗證所設計和開發的框架、模型和方法，主要發現和觀察結果將轉化為政策和管理啟示，對粵港澳大灣區的組裝式建築 (MiC) 專案管理具有重要意義。

17202325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17202325.value: 大型圖數據庫的假設檢驗算法

17202325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17202325.value: Prof Amer-Yahia, Sihem Prof Yu, Tao

17202325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202325.value: Hypothesis testing is a statistical analysis method that has been widely used in medical research, social sciences, and business analytics. It is a function provided in many data analytics software such as SPSS and Excel. Traditional hypothesis testing validates assumptions about a population using objects sampled from data represented as tables. However, little is known about its applicability to complex entity relationship information, which is prevalent in large data networks including medical knowledge graphs, bibliographical networks, and social networks. In this proposed project, we will examine the Graph Hypothesis (or GH), which is an assumption about a population using "graph patterns" sampled from a graph database. For example, in a citation network, a graph pattern can be a 3-node path ("university" -- "author" -- "publication venue"), and the corresponding GH is: "The average number of citations of papers published in a VLDB conference by a Stanford University researcher is larger than 300". We plan to study three new classes of GHs, which are the "graph versions" of one-sample, two-sample, and multiple hypothesis testing commonly studied in the literature. Evaluating these hypotheses is computationally intensive because graph patterns have various topologies (e.g., paths and trees), and their instances are abundant (e.g., Wordnet, a 76K-node graph, has 10 billion instances of a 7-node pattern). Moreover, a GH may involve multiple graph patterns. Hence, extracting all graph pattern instances relevant to a GH can incur a huge amount of time and space overhead. To overcome this challenge, we will develop a Hypothesis-Aware SamplEr (HASE), which incorporates GH information to collect samples of relevant graph patterns for hypothesis testing with guaranteed theoretical accuracy and unbiasedness. We will also design algorithms that enable HASE to scale with the number of graph patterns. To allow a user to specify a GH easily, we will develop a system prototype, which adopts a large language model to translate the GH specified in a natural language to a computer-readable format. In terms of research merits, our proposed project will bridge the gap between hypothesis testing, graph analytics, and natural language processing. Graph data have become increasingly prevalent and important in various domains. By 2031, the graph analytics market is expected to reach US$ 808 billion. Our research outcome can potentially be part of graph analytics software. Hence, our project outcomes benefit both research and industry communities. 假設檢定是一種廣泛運用於醫學研究、社會科學及商業的統計分析方法。許多數據分析軟件如 SPSS 和 Excel 都提供此功能。傳統的假設檢定使用資料表中抽取的樣本來驗證假設的真偽。然而，對於複雜的實體關係資訊（如醫療知識圖譜、書目網絡及社交網絡中常見的大型數據網絡）是否適用此方法，目前了解仍有限。本計劃擬探討圖假設（Graph Hypothesis，簡稱 GH），即基於圖數據庫中抽樣的「圖形模式」作假設。例如，在引文網絡中，圖形模式可為三節點路徑（「大學」--「作者」--「發表場合」），相應的 GH 為：「史丹福大學研究者在 VLDB 會議發表的論文平均被引用次數超過 300 次」。 我們計劃研究三種新型的 GH：一樣本、兩樣本及多重假設檢定的「圖形版本」。因為圖形模式拓撲多樣（如路徑、樹狀），且實例豐富（例如 Wordnet，一個含 76,000 節點的圖，7 節點模式的實例達 100 億），計算這些假設可以是非常昂貴的。此外，一個 GH 可能涵蓋多個圖形模式，因而提取所有相關圖形模式實例耗時且佔用大量空間。為克服此挑戰，我們將開發假設感知抽樣器（Hypothesis-Aware SamplEr，HASE），它結合 GH 資訊，理論上保證抽樣精確且無偏，進行假設檢定。我們也會設計可隨圖形模式數量擴展的演算法。為方便使用者定義 GH，將開發具大語言模型的系統原型，將自然語言指定的 GH 轉換成電腦可讀格式。 在研究價值上，本計劃將彌合假設檢定、圖分析與自然語言處理的差距。圖數據已在各領域日益重要，預計至 2031 年，圖分析市場將達 8080 億美元。我們的研究成果可望整合進圖分析軟件，造福學術界與產業界。

17202425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17202425.value: 採用互鎖設計的新型冷彎型鋼拼合截面柱

17202425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202425.value: The construction industry plays an essential role in economic growth and societal development. Recently, Hong Kong government has launched development plans such as the Greater Bay Area, Northern Metropolis and Modular Integrated Construction 2.0 which will create a significant volume of construction opportunities. However, it is important to note that the construction sector also contributes significantly to carbon emissions during the building process, raising concerns about its compatibility with achieving net-zero emissions targets. To align large-scale development with environmental sustainability goals, it is imperative to embrace innovative and eco-friendly construction technologies. In the Hong Kong Chief Executive’s 2024 Policy Address, it highlights the significance of promoting industry transformation through innovation, professionalisation, and revitalisation. In this strategy, it is key important to develop innovative construction forms that outperform traditional ones in terms of structural behaviour, demountability, reusability, economic efficiency and environmental sustainability. Cold-formed steel (CFS) built-up section members have emerged as a promising alternative in modern building systems such as light-gauge steel framing and pre-fabricated buildings due to their superior strength-to-weight ratio, design flexibility, and recyclability. However, conventional assembly methods utilising discrete connectors such as welds, bolts, or screws are labour-intensive and compromise the demountability and reusability of the built-up section members. This project introduces an innovative CFS built-up section column using an interlocking design. The proposed CFS built-up section column can be assembled and disassembled using two CFS channel sections with interlocking parts without the need for traditional connectors. The interlocking design not only serves as an efficient connector but also acts as a stiffener, enhancing structural performance against local buckling. By eliminating traditional connectors, the interlocking design simplifies assembly processes while reducing labour requirements and promoting sustainability through improved disassembly and reuse capabilities. This allows for easy replacement of potentially damaged channel sections, extending material life cycles and promoting resource efficiency for sustainable construction. Comprehensive experimental and numerical investigations will be implemented to investigate the structural performance of the novel CFS built-up section column. Appropriate design rules will be developed to promote its engineering application. Furthermore, a life cycle assessment will be carried out to quantify the potential reductions in carbon emissions associated with the novel interlocking design compared to conventional connection methods. By addressing the challenges of demountability and reusability in structural members, this project aims to facilitate the adoption of innovative construction practices in Hong Kong and beyond, ultimately contributing to a greener built environment. 建築業在經濟增長和社會發展方面發揮著至關重要的作用。近年來，香港政府推出了粵港澳大灣區、北部都會區及第二代「組裝合成」建築法（MiC 2.0）等重大發展計劃，為建築業創造了大量機遇。然而，建築施工過程中產生的高碳排放問題亟待解決，其與實現碳中和目標的協同發展路徑引發廣泛關注。為統籌大規模開發與環境可持續性目標，大力推廣應用創新環保建築技術勢在必行。香港特區行政長官在2024年施政報告中特別強調通過創新驅動、專業提升及產業革新來推動建築業轉型。在此背景下，開發兼具優異結構性能、可拆卸性、可循環利用性、經濟效益及環境可持續性等綜合優勢的新型結構體系具有重要戰略意義。 冷彎型鋼拼合截面構件憑藉其高強輕質、設計靈活性和可回收性，已成為輕鋼框架結構及預製裝配式建築等現代建築體系的優選方案。然而，傳統採用焊接、螺栓或自攻螺釘等連接件的組裝方式存在施工效率低、影響構件可拆卸性與可循環利用性等問題。本項目提出一種採用互鎖設計的新型冷彎型鋼拼合截面柱，通過兩個具有互鎖設計的冷彎型鋼C形截面構件實現無連接件拼合。該互鎖設計兼具連接功能與加勁肋作用，可顯著提升構件抗局部屈曲的結構性能。相較於傳統工藝，該互鎖設計不僅簡化了組裝流程、降低了人力成本，更能通過可拆卸性與可重組性實現材料全生命周期的高效循環利用。 本項目將採用試驗研究與數值模擬相結合的研究方法，系統評估新型冷彎型鋼拼合截面柱的結構性能，並建立相應的設計準則以促進其工程應用。此外，還將開展生命周期評估，量化分析互鎖設計相較於傳統連接方式的碳減排效益。通過突破結構構件可拆卸性與可循環利用的關鍵技術瓶頸，本項目將為香港乃至全球建築業綠色轉型提供創新解決方案，助力可持續城市建設。

17203725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203725.value: 廣義密度分解：推進差分隱私、市場動態與線上分配的統一架構

17203725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203725.value: This project aims to advance the theory of density decomposition and apply it to address key challenges in security, privacy, market dynamics, and online allocation. Density decomposition not only identifies the densest subset in a graph but also reveals the overall structure by breaking the graph into progressively less dense subcomponents. This broader view makes it a valuable tool in fields such as community detection, clustering, and network analysis. By extending density decomposition to accommodate more complex weight functions, this project seeks to uncover deeper structural properties, leading to new and impactful real-world applications. The bipartite graph perspective offers a powerful framework for studying density decomposition, traditionally treating the original nodes as the ground set. However, the PI has recently demonstrated that the roles of both sides are interchangeable, leading to the breakthrough discovery of universally closest distribution refinements. This finding is critical for advancing differential privacy concepts, particularly in tackling complex applications such as interactive time-series mechanisms and enabling concurrent composition with adaptive inputs. While traditional density decompositions with a linearly weighted ground set are well understood, they lack the flexibility to handle more intricate scenarios, such as markets and allocation problems involving generalized weight functions. To address this gap, this project proposes extending the density decomposition framework to incorporate non-linear weight functions such as submodular and supermodular weights. The decomposition serves as a sketch, using current information to determine which decisions require immediate action and which can be postponed. The results will provide a comprehensive framework for analyzing decision-making under uncertainty and solving online optimization where the underlying problems exhibit non-linear constraints. The broader impact of this research extends beyond theoretical contributions, offering practical applications across diverse fields. In addition to developing efficient algorithms for computing generalized density decompositions using advances in minimum-cost and submodular flow techniques, we will design scalable, gradient-based iterative methods that achieve varying levels of approximation. These approaches will incorporate convex programming and market dynamics tailored to handle complex, non-linear weights. The practicality of our methods will be rigorously tested on large-scale datasets. Key test scenarios will include evaluating how the accuracy of iterative decompositions influences decision-making, while also validating theoretical bounds on density approximation. Ultimately, this project introduces cutting-edge methodologies that push the boundaries of density decomposition theory, with the potential to revolutionize areas such as security, privacy, online allocation, and resource optimization, bringing significant advancements to both theory and real-world applications. 本計畫旨在推進密度分解理論，並應用於安全性、隱私保護、市場動態以及線上分配等關鍵挑戰。密度分解不僅可識別圖中最稠密的子集合，亦能透過將圖逐步分解為密度遞減的子組件，揭示整體結構。此一廣義視角使其在社群偵測、分群與網路分析等領域中具有高度價值。透過擴展密度分解以處理更複雜的權重函數，本計畫期望發掘更深層的結構特性，並導出具實質影響力的應用場景。 本計畫採用雙部圖的觀點作為分析密度分解的有力工具，傳統上將原始節點視為基底集合。然而，主持人近期發現雙方角色實際上可以互換，進而突破性地提出「普遍最近分佈精化」的理論。此一發現對推動差分隱私概念極為關鍵，特別是在處理互動式時間序列機制與支援具有適應性輸入的並發組合應用方面。 雖然對於線性權重基底集合的傳統密度分解已有深入理解，但其在處理更複雜場景時，如涉及廣義權重函數的市場與分配問題，顯得力有未逮。為彌補此不足，本計畫提出將密度分解架構擴展至非線性權重函數，包括次模與超模權重。該分解機制可作為一種「摘要」，運用當前資訊判斷哪些決策需立即執行，哪些可延後處理。此研究成果將建立一個完整框架，協助分析不確定性下的決策行為，並解決含非線性約束的線上最佳化問題。 本研究的影響不僅止於理論貢獻，亦涵蓋多領域的實務應用。除了發展高效演算法以利用最小成本與次模流技術計算廣義密度分解外，我們亦將設計可擴展的基於梯度的迭代方法，以達成不同程度的近似精度。這些方法將結合凸規劃與市場動態設計，以處理複雜的非線性權重。我們也將在大規模資料集上嚴格測試方法的實用性，重點測試場景包括評估分解準確度如何影響決策，並驗證密度近似的理論界限。 最終，本計畫將引入前沿方法，突破密度分解理論的既有限制，有望革新安全性、隱私保護、線上分配與資源最佳化等領域，在理論與實務應用上皆帶來重大進展。

17204125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204125.value: 偵測、誤分類和建模誤差下多模態網路流量估計的魯棒感測器位置優化

17204125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204125.value: Effective traffic flow estimation is vital for designing road networks, improving urban mobility, and driving economic growth in a city. It also plays a crucial role in identifying potential areas of danger and implementing safety measures to protect citizens. This research project is motivated by the PI's government project that utilizes thermal imaging cameras to estimate bicycle flows in a community. That project also involves the complexity of distinguishing between various transportation modes when measuring flows. Due to budget constraints, the deployment of thermal cameras is limited to a few locations. Discussions with government officials and transportation experts have revealed that the conventional practice is to place sensing devices on roads with high traffic volumes. Our research aims to conduct a rigorous scientific inquiry into the efficacy of this practice and investigate alternative approaches for achieving more accurate traffic flow estimates. Our preliminary investigations have observed measurement errors, including detection and misclassification errors that may vary among different sensor types and environmental conditions. Therefore, one may consider multiple factors, such as flow volume on each link, sensing quality under the environment in each location, and the strength of inference by the sensor locations to estimate unobserved flows of other locations.
