Given these considerations, our research aims to tackle the joint complexities of detection errors, classification issues, sampling discrepancies, and statistical modeling in estimating traffic flow. The novelty of this proposed research is three-fold. First, it proposes implementing a pre-estimation survey to collect traffic flow samples, providing prior information at a low cost. Second, the study addresses multi-dimensional errors from sensing devices and statistical sampling. A novel estimation quality evaluation model is developed, jointly optimizing measurement and prediction errors based on the available prior information. This evaluation model is formulated as a convex optimization problem, enabling efficient computations. Third, a robust optimization approach leveraging the evaluation framework to identify optimal sensor locations is proposed to account for uncertainties in measurement and estimation processes, enhancing the robustness of sensor location selection. To assess the proposed approach, computational experiments will be conducted using (i) benchmark network instances, (ii) simulated data, and (iii) real traffic flow data. The findings will offer insights into the strategic placement of sensors in networks. Guidelines will be shared with the Government and industrial collaborators. Finally, a key logistics organization in the region will facilitate the transition of the research into practical implementation. 有效的交通流量估計對於道路網絡的規劃、城市交通的改善以及城市經濟增長的推動具有至關重要的意義。此外，其在識別潛在危險區域及實施安全措施以保障市民安全方面亦扮演著關鍵角色。 本研究的動機源自一項政府項目，該項目利用熱成像攝影技術來估算社區中的自行車流量。該項目同時涉及在流量測量過程中區分不同交通模式的複雜性。由於預算限制，熱成像攝影機的部署僅限於少數地點。與政府官員及交通專家的討論顯示，傳統做法是將感測設備設置於交通流量較高的路段。本研究旨在對這一傳統做法的有效性進行嚴謹的科學探討，並進一步研究其他方法，以實現更精確的交通流量估算。 初步研究發現，測量過程中存在檢測誤差及誤分類誤差，這些誤差可能因感測器類型及環境條件的不同而有所差異。因此，需綜合考慮多種因素，例如各路段流量、不同環境下的感測質量，以及感測器位置對其他未觀測路段流量推斷的影響。基於這些考量，本研究旨在解決交通流量估算中的檢測誤差、分類問題、抽樣差異及統計建模等綜合性複雜問題。 本研究的創新之處可歸納為三方面。首先，提出在正式估算前進行交通流量抽樣調查，以低成本獲取先驗信息。其次，研究針對感測設備及統計抽樣所產生的多維誤差，開發了一種新型估算質量評估模型，基於現有先驗信息聯合優化測量及預測誤差。此評估模型被構建為凸優化問題，從而實現高效計算。第三，提出一種基於評估框架的魯棒優化方法，以識別最佳感測器位置，充分考慮測量及估算過程中的不確定性，從而提升感測器位置選擇的穩健性。 為驗證所提出的方法，本研究將進行計算實驗，使用（i）基準網絡實例、（ii）模擬數據及（iii）真實交通流量數據進行分析。研究結果將為網絡中感測器的戰略佈局提供深入見解，並將相關指導方針與政府及產業合作夥伴分享。最後，區域內一家重要的物流機構將協助推動本研究成果的實際應用。

17204525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204525.value: 廣播模式下的電召的士司乘配對策略設計

17204525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17204525.value: Dr Wang, Hai Prof Xiao, Feng Prof Yin, Yafeng

17204525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204525.value: App-based e-hailing taxi services have experienced rapid growth over the past decade. E-hailing platforms typically employ one of two main matching mechanisms—broadcasting or dispatching—to match passengers with drivers. In the dispatching mechanism, the platform directly assigns passenger requests to drivers, who are usually not allowed to reject the assignments. In the broadcasting mechanism, each passenger’s order is broadcast to a group of idle drivers within a certain broadcasting radius, and each driver has the freedom to accept or reject the order. Although the dispatching mechanism has been extensively examined in the literature, the broadcasting mechanism has received much less attention. However, determining critical operational decision variables, such as the broadcasting radius and interval, remains a challenge for e-hailing taxi platforms using the broadcasting mechanism. For example, a larger broadcasting radius can increase the probability of passengers being accepted by drivers, but may increase their expected pickup time by attracting faraway drivers. It is important to develop efficient matching strategies to adjust the key operational decision variables according to real-time supply and demand conditions and trip characteristics. This proposed project will first establish an analytical model to delineate the complex relationships between the key system performance metrics (e.g., passengers’ waiting time and drivers’ earning rate) and the decision variables. On top of this analytical model, we propose a multi-objective optimization model to optimize various system performance metrics that cater to the interests of different stakeholders (drivers, passengers, and platforms). Second, to design more forward-looking matching strategies, we will further develop a dynamic optimization model formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), which can capture dynamic interactions between operational decisions and environmental states, including real-time supply and demand conditions and trip characteristics. We will then develop a tailored reinforcement learning algorithm to solve the MDP for maximizing long-term system efficiency over a long period. Third, we will evaluate the models’ effectiveness through simulations and field experiments. After validation, we will collaborate with our industry partners to implement the most effective matching strategies into their e-hailing taxi apps utilizing the broadcasting mechanism. This project will contribute to both theory and practice, filling the research gap on the operation and management of the broadcasting mechanism for e-hailing taxi markets. It will also bring tangible impacts to the industry and society by helping e-hailing platforms improve their operational efficiency. 基於應用程式的電召的士服務在過去十年中經歷了迅速的成長。電召的士平台通常採用兩種主要的配對模式之一——廣播模式或指派模式——來將乘客與司機配對。在指派模式中，平台會直接將乘客的叫車訂單指派給司機，而司機通常不得拒絕指派。在廣播模式中，每一筆乘客訂單會被廣播給一定廣播半徑內的一群閒置司機，而每位司機可自由選擇是否接單。雖然指派模式在過往文獻中已被廣泛探討，但對於廣播模式的研究卻相對較少。然而，對於採用廣播模式的電召的士平台而言，如何決定關鍵的營運決策變量（如廣播半徑和廣播間隔）仍是一大挑戰。例如，較大的廣播半徑雖然可提高乘客同司機的配對率，但也可能因吸引到較遠的司機而增加乘客的接載時間。因此，提出有效的配對策略，根據即時供需情況和行程特徵動態調整關鍵營運決策變量，具有重要意義。 本項目首先將建立一個數學模型，分析關鍵系統效率指標（如乘客等待時間與司機收益率）與決策變量之間的複雜關係。在此數學模型基礎上，我們將提出一個多目標優化模型，優化多項系統效率指標，以兼顧不同持份者（司機、乘客及平台）的利益。其次，為設計更具前瞻性的配對策略，我們將進一步提出一個動態優化模型，並將其建構為馬可夫決策過程（MDP），以捕捉營運決策與環境狀態（包含即時供需情況及行程特徵）之間的動態互動。我們將針對此MDP開發一套專屬強化學習算法，以優化長期系統效率。第三，我們會透過模擬測試與實地實驗來評估各模型的有效性。驗證後，我們將進一步與業界夥伴合作，將最有效的配對策略應用於其電召的士應用程式中。本項目將對理論與實際應用層面皆有貢獻，彌補電召的士市場廣播模式下的運營與管理相關研究的不足，並協助電召的士平台提升營運效率，為的士業界與社會帶來積極的影響。

17204625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204625.value: 優化大型多模態模型訓練與推理

17204625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204625.value: This project studies distributed training and inference optimization of large multimodal models. Multimodal models are multi-component deep neural networks that learn from multiple input modalities (data types) and may generate output of different modalities (e.g., text, image, video). Multimodal models are driving various applications such as visual question answering and image/video generation. We study key issues to improve distributed training and inference efficiency of multimodal models, focusing on their input dynamism and diverse inter-component routing. Multimodal models are characterized by: (1) Dynamic input shapes: inputs to a multimodal model include data samples of different modalities, whose sizes vary significantly across modalities and samples; (2) Heterogeneous components: separate encoder networks are used to process data inputs of different modalities, alignment modules are often included to align embeddings of different modalities, and different generation modules can be used for different outputs; (3) Large backbone: the current trend is to build a multimodal model on the backbone of a large language model (LLM) and multiple other components (e.g., input encoders and output generation modules), leading to large size and capacity of the model. To address unique challenges brought by these characteristics, optimizing distributed attention computation, dynamic component deployment/serving, and model pruning are the keys. First, distributed computation of the attention mechanism is a main module in state-of-the-art multimodal generative models, and inputs of different modalities incur varying input sizes and may require different attention masks. Optimized distributed attention computation according to input dynamism is crucial for training expedition and maximal resource utilization. Second, a large multimodal model is often built to support various generation tasks/applications, serving miscellaneous requests with diverse combinations of model components. Dynamic resource scaling and effective request scheduling across heterogeneous model components are needed, for timely request serving with optimal resource consumption. Next, large multimodal models demonstrate considerable computational redundancy in the generation process. To handle the irregular redundancy patterns in generative inference of multimodal models, efficient redundancy expression and systematic approaches for model sparsification are desired, that minimize inference time while ensuring model accuracy. We study efficient algorithms and system designs to optimize distributed attention computation in large multimodal model training, enable dynamic resource deployment and high-performance inference of multimodal models in serving diverse applications, and then devise effective model pruning strategies to further expedite multimodal generative serving. We build multimodal model training and inference systems incorporating our designs, and evaluate them on training/serving workloads in real-world AI clouds. 本項目研究大型多模態模型的分佈式訓練和推理優化。多模態模型是多組件深度神經元網絡，能夠從多種輸入模態（數據類型）中學習，並可能產生不同模態（例如文字、圖像、視訊）的輸出。多模態模型正在推動各種應用，例如視覺問答和圖像/視訊生成。我們研究提升多模態模型分佈式訓練和推理效率的關鍵問題，重點在於其輸入動態性和組件間路由的多樣性。 多模態模型的特點是：(1) 動態輸入形狀：多模態模型的輸入包含不同模態的數據樣本，其大小在不同模態和樣本之間差異顯著；(2) 異構組件：不同的編碼器網絡用來處理不同模態的數據輸入，對齊模組來對齊不同模態的編碼，不同的生成模組來產生不同的輸出；(3) 大型主幹網路：當前的趨勢是在大語言模型 (LLM) 主幹網絡和多個其他組件（例如輸入編碼器和輸出生成模組）上建立多模態模型，使得模型規模龐大及能力強大。為了應對這些特性帶來的獨特挑戰，優化分佈式注意力（attention）計算、動態組件部署/服務以及模型剪枝是關鍵。 首先，分佈式注意力計算是當前最先進的多模態生成模型的主要組件，不同模態的輸入會產生不同的輸入大小，可能需要不同的注意力面具（attention mask）。根據輸入的動態性優化分佈式注意力計算對於訓練速度和資源利用率最大化至關重要。 其次，大型多模態模型通常用於支持各種生成式任務和應用，並通過多種模型組件組合來處理各種請求。需要跨異構模型組件進行動態資源擴展和有效的請求調度，以便及時處理請求並實現資源使用的最佳化。 再次，大型多模態模型在生成過程中表現出相當大的計算冗餘。為了處理多模態模型生成推理中不規則的冗餘模式，需要高效的冗餘表達和系統性的模型稀疏化方法，以在確保模型準確性的同時最大限度地縮短推理時間。 我們研究高效的算法和系統設計以優化大型多模態模型訓練中的分佈式attention計算，實現多模態模型的動態資源部署和高效能推理，服務於多樣化的應用；並設計有效的模型剪枝策略，以進一步加速多模態生成服務。我們將構建融合我們設計的多模態模型訓練和推理系統，並在現實世界人工智能雲中進行基於訓練/服務工作負載的評估。

17204725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204725.value: 量化擁擠效應對呼吸道感染的影響

17204725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204725.value: Crowded and poorly ventilated (CPV) settings are hotspots for respiratory infections, such as COVID-19 and influenza. Super-spreading events, as a pandemic drive, mainly occur in CPV environments. Although indoor overcrowding has long been associated with increased rates of acute respiratory infections, the precise mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. Three major physical factors contribute to crowding: size or spaciousness (air space per person), close contacts (distance and duration) and room occupancy (number of people per room). Traditionally, the crowding effect on infection has been studied separately from ventilation (equivalent clean air per person), and the three physical factors have mostly been analysed in isolation. Existing ventilation and space crowding standards do not fully account for their combined effect. The lack of a unified parameter to quantify the effect of crowding factors on infection risk hinders targeted infection control. We have recently developed a generalised short- and long-range Wells–Riley equation for assessing infection risk and identified a dilutional equivalence between spaciousness and equivalent clean air, suggesting a novel concept of spaciousness or size ventilation. In this proposed project, we will evaluate a unified and standardised intake fraction time, considering both short- and long-range inhalation exposure, to study CPV settings and the interrelation between room size, occupant number, close contacts and ventilation. Infection risk will be evaluated using a population quanta generation profile. A two-zone space with a CPV zone and a city of 7 million people with CPV settings will be simulated and analysed to investigate the impact of CPV settings on the spread of influenza and COVID-19. A systematic literature review will be performed to collect datasets on spaciousness and infection in CPV-like settings, such as jails and temporary shelters, and to identify the threshold for air space per person using the new theory. Dilution data will be collected from two crowded classrooms and two nursing homes in Hong Kong, monitored minute by minute over a year, and tested in two air-conditioned small chambers where ventilation supply is controlled through microbe tracer monitoring. The entry and exit times of individuals will be determined using a privacy-proof method. Existing ventilation standards (ASHRAE 62.1 and 241) will be analysed using the newly developed theory for consistency and effectiveness in different occupancy settings, and suggestion for improvement will be provided. Our findings will help establish a new minimum standard for indoor spaciousness to minimise inhalation exposure and infection risk. 擁擠且通風不良（CPV）的環境是呼吸道感染（如COVID-19和流感）的熱點。作為大流行驅動力的超級傳播事件主要發生在CPV環境中。儘管室內過度擁擠長期以來與急性呼吸道感染率增加有關，但這種關聯的確切機制仍不清楚。影響擁擠的三個主要物理因素包括：空間大小（人均空氣空間）、密切接觸（距離和持續時間）以及房間佔用率（每房間人數）。傳統上，擁擠對感染的影響研究與通風（人均等效清潔空氣）分開進行，且這三個物理因素大多被孤立分析。現有的通風和空間擁擠標準未能充分考慮它們的綜合效應。缺乏統一的參數來量化擁擠因素對感染風險的影響，阻礙了有針對性的感染控制。 我們最近開發了一個廣義的短程和長程Wells-Riley方程，用於評估感染風險，並發現了空間大小與等效清潔空氣之間的稀釋等效性，從而提出了一個新概念：空間大小通風。在本提案項目中，我們將評估一個統一且標準化的吸入分數時間，同時考慮短程和長程吸入暴露，以研究CPV環境及房間大小、佔用人數、密切接觸和通風之間的相互關係。感染風險將使用人群量子生成分佈進行評估。我們將模擬和分析一個包含CPV區域的兩區空間以及一個擁有700萬人口且存在CPV環境的城市，以研究CPV環境對流感和COVID-19傳播的影響。我們將進行系統文獻回顧，收集類似CPV環境（如監獄和臨時避難所）中空間大小與感染的數據集，並利用新理論確定人均空氣空間的閾值。稀釋數據將從香港的兩間擁擠教室和兩家養老院收集，進行為期一年的每分鐘監測，並在兩個空調小室中通過微生物示踪監測控制通風供應進行測試。個人的進出時間將使用隱私保護方法確定。我們將使用新開發的理論分析現有通風標準（ASHRAE 62.1和241）在不同佔用環境中的一致性和有效性，並提出改進建議。我們的研究結果將有助於建立新的室內空間最低標準，以最小化吸入暴露和感染風險。

17204825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204825.value: 創新交通監測：運用互聯車輛技術的綜合方案

17204825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204825.value: Effective management of transportation networks demands accurate, network-wide traffic flow monitoring. Despite decades of investment in wired, fixed-sensor systems, their high installation and maintenance costs have significantly restricted their deployment across entire networks. The emergence of connected vehicle (CV) technology offers a promising alternative, potentially enabling wireless traffic flow monitoring on a network-wide scale. However, the transition to full CV adoption is gradual, resulting in a mixed driving environment that consists of both CV and non-CV with varying CV penetration rates across both time and space. Recent research has primarily focused on scaling up traffic flow using CV penetration rates estimated at sensor-free signalized intersections. Many links, however, are connected to unsignalized intersections, leaving network-wide traffic flow monitoring incomplete. This research project will address the critical need for a CV-based full-network traffic flow monitoring system by developing a generalized approach applicable to all three intersection types—signalized intersections, priority junctions, and roundabouts—whether sensor-free or partially equipped with fixed sensors. Phase I will establish the analytical relationship between the population headway distribution and the CV headway distribution using the CV penetration rate. Traffic flow can be indirectly estimated through headway. A CV headway, defined as the time interval between two consecutive CV arrivals, is the sum of all headways within the interval. Thus, the unobservable population headway distribution can be expressed as a function of the observable CV headway distribution and the unknown CV penetration rate. Phase II will develop a generalized method for estimating CV penetration rates and population headway distributions on lanes connected to all three types of sensor-free intersections. The average traffic delay will be analytically derived as a function of CV penetration rates using the Phase I relationship. A mathematical program will estimate CV penetration rates by minimizing the discrepancy between analytical average traffic delay and average CV delay, with the latter serving as an unbiased estimator for actual average traffic delay. Phase III will extend the proposed generalized method to all intersections partially equipped with fixed sensors. The main challenge will be fusing both CV data and reliable direct traffic flow measurements from lanes with fixed sensors into the formulation. The proposed approach will be tested against simulations and using real-world data, advancing network-wide traffic flow monitoring in CV environments, fully utilizing all the available data. 有效管理交通網絡需要準確、覆蓋整個網絡的交通流量監測。儘管數十年來在有線固定傳感器系統上投入大量資源，但其高昂的安裝及維護成本極大地限制了其在整個網絡的鋪設。互聯車輛技術的出現提供了一個極具前景的替代方案，有望實現覆蓋整個網絡的無線交通流量監測。然而，全面採用互聯車輛技術的過程是漸進的，導致形成一個由互聯車輛和非互聯車輛混合組成的駕駛環境，且互聯車輛滲透率在時間和空間上均存在差異。近期研究主要集中於利用在無傳感器燈控路口估算的互聯車輛滲透率來推算整體交通流量。然而，許多路段連接的是非燈控路口，致使覆蓋整個網絡的交通流量監測仍不完整。本研究項目將開發一種通用方法，適用於所有三類路口: 燈控路口、讓路路口及迴旋處，無論其為無傳感器或部分配備固定傳感器，以滿足對基於互聯車輛技術的全網絡交通流量監測系統的迫切需求。第一階段將利用互聯車輛滲透率，建立整體時間車距分佈與互聯車輛時間車距分佈之間的解析關係式。交通流量可通過時間車距間接推算。互聯車輛時間車距定義為連續兩輛互聯車輛到達的時間間隔，其值等於該時間間隔內所有車距之和。因此，無法觀測的整體時間車距分佈可表達為可觀測的互聯車輛時間車距分佈及未知的互聯車輛滲透率的函數。第二階段將開發一種通用方法，用於估算連接至所有三類無傳感器路口之車道的互聯車輛滲透率及整體時間車距分佈。平均交通延誤將基於第一階段的關係式，推導為互聯車輛滲透率的解析函數。通過最小化解析求得的整體平均交通延誤與互聯車輛平均延誤之間的差異，並以互聯車輛平均延誤作為實際平均交通延誤的無偏估計量，將構建一個數學規劃模型來估算互聯車輛滲透率。第三階段將把所提出的通用方法擴展至所有部分配備固定傳感器的路口。主要挑戰在於如何將互聯車輛數據及來自配備固定傳感器車道直接得到的可靠交通流量量測數據融合到該方法的構建中。所提出的方法將通過模擬及使用真實世界數據進行測試，以充分利用所有可用數據，推動互聯車輛環境下覆蓋整個網絡的交通流量監測技術的發展。

17205025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205025.value: 在機器人驅動的設施視覺檢測中實現尺度不變：一種內嵌物理知識的深度學習方法

17205025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17205025.value: Prof Liu, Donghai Prof Lu, Weisheng Wilson Prof Peng, Yifan

17205025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205025.value: Scale is fundamental in scientific discovery. It determines how a physics event unfolds and the way it is perceived. In facility visual inspection, defects of concern (e.g., cracks and spalling) usually appear differently from afar than when they are nearby, forming a typical scale effect. The phenomenon is recently exacerbated by (a) the increasing use of robots that tend to take visual measurements from arbitrary distances (and thus non-unitary scales), and (b) the prevalence of deep learning (DL) — a technique poor in scale-generalization — used to detect defects from the measurements. Existing approaches to scale invariance are either (i) training/energy-intensive for a need to learn from large cross-scale data, or (ii) confined to limited scale ranges due to hand-engineered receptive fields. Inspired by an emerging computational paradigm called physics-AI symbiosis, this project aims to approach scale invariance in defect detection by resorting to (a) fundamental rationales of imaging optics, and (b) statistical defect morphology. The two aspects provide basic physic primitives in articulating the variance of defect appearance when imaged from different scales. It is thus hypothesized that the incorporation of optical and morphological physics with DL will contribute positively to scale generalizability for defect detection. The hypothesis will be examined and tested via: (i) systematic investigation of the scale variation problem by conducting a series of controlled experiments; (ii) formulating a theoretical model to explain scale variation by contrasting empirical observation with optical physics and defect morphology; (iii) development of an optics-informed and morphology-guided DL (OIMG-DL) approach for scale-invariant defect detection; and (iv) evaluating the approach with real-world data. A success of the project will bring about several breakthroughs. Scholarly, it formalizes a descriptive physics-based model to explain scale variance in visual inspection, which has the potential to advance our understanding of DL’s poor scale generalizability. Methodologically, the project provides a novel OIMG-DL approach for visual inspection by complementing data-driven learning with first-principle deterministic physics laws, which distinguishes itself from brute-force training-based methods that are energy-greedy and enumerative design techniques that have limited scalability. Practically, the deliverables include an ensemble of deployable tools for robot-enabled facility inspection, addressing the practical need for scale invariance in defect detection. The project is supported by one research center in building/infrastructure maintenance, one high-tech company in construction robotics, one local society in building inspection, and a veteran professor and educator in inspection and surveying. 尺度是科學發現的基礎要素，它決定了物理事件的呈現方式及其被觀測到的形態。在設施視覺檢測中，裂縫、剝落等缺陷的表觀形態會因觀測距離（尺度）不同而顯著變化，形成典型的尺度效應。當前，機器人檢測（非固定距離成像）和深度學習（尺度泛化能力差）的普及進一步加劇了該問題。現有方法或依賴高能耗的跨尺度數據訓練，或受限於手工設計感受野的窄適用範圍。本項目採用物理-AI協同新範式，通過融合成像光學原理與缺陷形態統計規律，構建尺度不變性缺陷檢測理論模型。具體包括：（1）通過受控實驗系統解析尺度變異機制；（2）結合光學物理與形態學建立理論解釋框架；（3）開發光學-形態學引導的深度學習（OIMG-DL）方法；（4）基於實際數據驗證演算法有效性。本研究將針對視覺檢測場景，首次建立基於物理的尺度變異描述模型，揭示深度學習尺度泛化較差的機理，突破了傳統數據驅動方法的能耗瓶頸與人工設計的局限性，為機器人設施檢測提供一套可部署的工具集。

17205125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205125.value: 不確定先驗分佈信息下的契約與信息設計問題

17205125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205125.value: According to the World Economic Forum, 70% of the newly created global economy in 2020-30 will come from the digital economy (https://intelligence.weforum.org/topics/a1Gb0000001SH21EAG). To address the challenges arising from this landscape, we need to combine Computer Science and Economics. For example, many applications in the digital economy involve large-scale optimization problems in the presence of multiple self-interested parties. The mechanism design literature from Economics offers insights into how to incentivize self-interested agents to align their actions with the mechanism designer's interests. However, we need to reexamine the principles of mechanism design through the computational lens, given the tension between the enormous problem sizes and the limited computational power and information available. An important perspective is the learning aspect of mechanism design, which studies the uncertainty surrounding agents' private information. The classical literature models such uncertainty stochastically, assuming that the agents' private information is drawn from a known prior. However, we never know the prior exactly, but at best have partial information about it through data. Can we learn a near optimal mechanism based on limited information of the prior, and how much information is needed? This question has been studied extensively for auction design, but less so for contract and information design, which are two other research directions in mechanism design that are just as fundamental and relevant. This project aims to fill this research gap and is motivated by two observations. First, the learning aspect of contract and information design is more challenging than that of auction design due to the uncertainty in agents' actions. In auction design, we can eliminate this uncertainty by focusing on incentive-compatible auctions so that agents truthfully report their information no matter what the prior is. In contract and information design, agents' actions unavoidably depend on the prior, for which we only have partial information. This project will design new algorithms to robustify a mechanism to achieve good performance for all nearby priors simultaneously. Second, the existing results on contract and information design all adopt the statistical learning theory approach. By contrast, the latest progress for auctions by the PI and coauthors suggests that one should learn an approximation of the prior; these algorithms give state-of-the-art and often nearly tight sample complexity for almost all auction settings. This project will develop the methodology for approximating the prior in contract and information design and quantify the minimum amount of information needed to design approximately optimal mechanisms. 根據世界經濟論壇的數據，2020至2030年間全球新創造經濟總量中的70%將來自數字經濟。為了應對這一新格局所帶來的挑戰，將計算機科學與經濟學領域相結合至關重要。數字經濟中的許多場景都涉及在多個自利主體的情況下解決大規模優化問題。經濟學中的機制設計文獻提供了如何激勵自利主體使其行為與機制設計者自身利益保持一致的見解。而由於超大問題規模與有限計算能力與信息之間的根本矛盾，我們需要從計算視角重新審視機制設計問題。 設計合適激勵方案的主要困難源於圍繞自利主體私有信息的不確定性。經典文獻通常採用隨機模型來描述這種不確定性，即假設主體的私有信息從一個已知的先驗分布中採樣。然而在現實中我們無法精確獲知先驗分布，充其量只能通過各種數據源獲得關於它的部分信息。因此我們很自然地會問：能否基於對先驗分布的有限信息學習到一個近似最優的機制？需要多少信息（以數據量來衡量）才足以實現近似最優性？ 過去十年間，針對拍賣設計的學習理論問題已被廣泛研究。然而對於契約設計和信息設計這兩個與拍賣設計同等重要和基礎的機制設計問題，其學習理論方面的探索則相對較少。本項目旨在填補這一空白： 1. 契約設計和信息設計的學習方面在概念上比拍賣設計更具挑戰性，這源於主體行為的不確定性。在拍賣設計中，我們可以通過專注於激勵相容拍賣來消除這種不確定性，這類拍賣能確保無論先驗分布如何，主體都會如實報告其信息。而在契約設計和信息設計中，主體的行為不可避免地依賴於先驗分布，我們對其僅有部分信息。為應對這一挑戰，本項目將設計新的算法技術來增強機制的魯棒性，使其能同時對所有鄰近的先驗分布均表現良好。 2. 現有關於契約設計和信息設計學習方面的少數成果均採用了統計學習理論方法。而由項目負責人及合作者提出的最新拍賣設計學習算法表明，直接學習對底層先驗分布的近似更為有效。這些算法為幾乎所有拍賣場景提供了最先進的、且通常是近乎緊的樣本複雜度邊界。本項目將系統地開發通過自然信息獲取通道在契約設計和信息設計中逼近先驗分布的方法論。在此過程中，我們將量化解決這些問題所需的最小信息量，以設計出近似最優的機制。

17205225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205225.value: 面向可變形電子學的單晶全無機鈣鈦礦定量塑性及形變機製研究

17205225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205225.value: Inorganic semiconductors, renowned for their high carrier mobility and superior electrical performance, are highly versatile in a wide range of applications, including optoelectronics, sensors, and energy conversion. However, except for several Van der Waals/layered semiconductors with substantial bulk plasticity and oxide semiconductors with limited plasticity at small-scale, inorganic semiconductors typically exhibit brittle fractures under ambient conditions due to their directional covalent bonds or strong electrostatic interactions among ionic species. The lack of intrinsic plasticity of inorganic semiconductors make them hard to be processed/machined and incompatible for many application scenarios. Dedicated to seeking ductile semiconductors, our team recently found all-inorganic perovskites (CsPbX3, X=Cl, Br and I) can be plastically morphed into distinct morphologies through multislip at room temperature, without affecting their bandgap/functional properties. This finding demonstrates the enormous potential of ductile semiconductors for manufacturing next-generation deformable electronics and energy systems, while a more comprehensive, quantitative study on the plasticity of such all-inorganic perovskites would be deemed necessary. In this project, we will develop and implement our state-of-the-art in situ nanomechanics and electron microscopy techniques, through collaborations with leading experts on materials synthesis, advanced electron microscopy and atomistic simulations, to conduct in-depth nanomechanical investigation on single-crystalline CsPbX3 perovskites based on our preliminary progresses, including: i) By employing sophisticated crystal synthesis and microfabrication, we will quantitatively investigate the orientation-dependent and size-dependent room-temperature plasticity for single crystalline perovskites. ii) We will develop in situ tensile testing in SEM/TEM to investigate the tensile plasticity of perovskites. ⅲ) With the assistance of aberration-corrected transmission electron microscope, we will elaborate on the associated dislocation dynamics and underlying deformation mechanisms responsible for the distinct deformation behaviors, which can provide atomic-resolution microstructural information for further atomistic modeling to uncover the physical origin of plasticity. ⅳ) Leveraging the morphing ability of CsPbX3 perovskites with uncompromised functional properties, along with their intrinsic optoelectronic characteristics, we will explore their potential application in novel deformable electronics/optoelectronics and energy devices. With the successful implementation of this project, more comprehensive and in-depth understanding on the room-temperature plasticity of all-inorganic perovskites will be obtained, which would be of great significance for exploring more ductile inorganic semiconductors, an emerging topic for semiconductor and nanomechanics research nowadays. In addition, this obtained quantitative insights based on CsPbX3 lead halide perovskites will largely expand their applications in developing high-performance and robust micro/nano-electromechanical systems (MEMS/NEMS) and flexible/deformable electronics that can be potentially used in optoelectronics and sustainable energy industries. 無機半導體材料以其高載流子遷移率和優異的電學性能著稱，廣泛應用於光電子學、傳感器和能量轉換等領域。然而，除少數具有顯著宏觀塑性的範德華/層狀半導體以及僅在小尺度下表現出有限塑性的氧化物半導體外，大多數無機半導體由於其共價鍵的方向性或離子間強靜電作用，在常溫下通常表現為脆性斷裂。這種本征塑性的欠缺使得它們難以加工成型，並限制了其在許多應用場景中的適用性。為探索具有塑性的半導體材料，我們團隊近期發現全無機鈣鈦礦（CsPbX3，X=Cl、Br、I）在室溫下可通過多重滑移實現塑性形變，構成不同形貌，同時保持其帶隙和功能特性不變。這一發現揭示了塑性半導體在製造下一代可變形電子器件和能源系統中的巨大潛力，同時也凸顯了對這類全無機鈣鈦礦材料進行更全面定量塑性研究的必要性。 本項目將基於我們在單晶CsPbX3鈣鈦礦力學研究中的初步進展，開發並運用先進的原位納米力學與電子顯微技術，聯合材料合成、先進電子顯微技術和原子模擬等領域的專家，開展系統的納米力學研究。具體包括：1）通過精密的晶體合成與微加工技術，定量表征單晶鈣鈦礦室溫塑性的取向依賴性和尺寸依賴性；2）開發基於掃描/透射電子顯微鏡（SEM/TEM）的原位拉伸測試技術，探究該鈣鈦礦的拉伸塑性；3）借助像差校正TEM，闡明主導其獨特變形行為的位錯動力學與微觀機製，為原子尺度建模提供原子分辨率結構信息，從而揭示塑性的物理起源；4）結合CsPbX3鈣鈦礦形變後功能特性無損的特點及其本征光電性能，探索其在新型可變形電子/光電器件與能源器件中的應用潛力。 本項目的實施將幫助我們更全面、深入地理解全無機鈣鈦礦的室溫塑性，對探索更多具有本征塑性的無機半導體這一當前半導體力學研究的前沿領域具有重要意義。此外，本項目所獲得的定量力學研究見解，將極大拓展CsPbX3鹵化鉛鈣鈦礦在高性能、高可靠的微納機電系統（MEMS/NEMS）以及柔性/可變形電子器件中的應用，有望對光電子學和可持續能源產業發揮重要作用。

17205325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205325.value: 電場輔助離子刷波動強化電驅動膜結晶

17205325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205325.value: Rechargeable metal-ion battery recycling is crucial for both environmental sustainability and economic viability. The challenge lies in efficiently capturing valuable metal ions such as Li+, Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ from leaching solutions derived from the dissolution of spent batteries. Recent advancements in electrodialysis have allowed the development of electro-driven membrane crystallization (e-MC) for separating metal ions and generating crystal products, simultaneously. However, existing polymeric membranes suffer low metal ion throughput, leading to reduced metal ion recovery rate and compromised e-MC rate. Although microporous materials, such as polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs), have enhanced metal ion transport ability, they come at the cost of ion purity, ultimately leading to low e-MC product purity. In addition, mineral scaling on surface or within their structure significantly increases transport resistance. To address these issues, our previous study has explored the feasibility of enhancing the membranes’ selective ion transport through the assembly of ionic monomers/polymers under an electric field, a process we term electric field-assisted 'ion-brush' fluctuation (eF-iBF). Recent studies have provided real-time insights on 'ion-brush' fluctuation kinetics, showcasing its potential for achieving superior crystallization. Nevertheless, there is a lack of comprehensive understanding on how electric fields influence 'ion-brush' fluctuation to construct membranes with enhanced e-MC performance. Therefore, this proposed GRF project aims to pioneer the eF-iBF principle for developing a new class of electro-driven PIMs (e-PIMs) with unprecedented performance of e-MC rate, e-MC product purity, and anti-scaling properties. These e-PIMs are expected to outperform current state-of-the-art electro-driven membranes by at least 1 to 2 orders of magnitude through a combination of interdisciplinary experimental strategies and multi-scale modelling. Specifically, this proposal will (1) reveal the ‘ion-brush’ fluctuation rules under various electric field conditions via mechanistic studies and real-time characterizations; (2) establish the eF-iBF principle for membrane construction to overcome the e-MC rate and product purity trade-offs, and (3) leverage this principle to develop advanced e-PIMs with better e-MC. The major success of this project will be measured by our ability to elucidate eF-iBF mechanisms and establish design guidelines for a new generation of e-PIMs tailored for e-MC. This project aims to deliver a practical and innovative eF-iBF principle for enhanced e-PIMs that not only overcome the e-MC rate and e-MC product purity trade-offs, but also offer superior anti-scaling properties. This proposal will have far-reaching implications for energy, environmental, and economic sustainability, particularly in the realm of metal ion recovery from spent batteries. 可充電金屬離子電池的回收對於環境永續性和經濟可行性都至關重要。其挑戰在於如何有效地從廢棄電池溶解產生的浸出液中捕獲有價值的金屬離子，例如Li+、Ni2+、Co2+和Mn2+。電滲析技術的最新進展使得電驅動膜結晶（e-MC）技術得以發展，該技術可同時分離金屬離子並產生晶體產品。然而，現有的聚合物薄膜存在金屬離子通量低的問題，導致金屬離子回收率降低和e-MC速率受損。雖然微孔材料（例如固有微孔聚合物（PIM））具有增強的金屬離子傳輸能力，但它們是以犧牲離子純度為代價的，最終導致e-MC產品純度低。此外，表面或結構內部的礦物結垢會顯著增加傳輸阻力。 為了解決這些問題，我們先前的研究探索了透過在電場下組裝離子單體/聚合物來增強膜選擇性離子傳輸的可行性，我們將此過程稱為電場輔助「離子刷」波動（eF-iBF）。最近的研究提供了關於「離子刷」波動動力學的即時洞察，展示了其實現卓越結晶的潛力。然而，對於電場如何影響「離子刷」波動以建構具有增強e-MC性能的膜，目前尚缺乏全面的理解。 因此，本計畫旨在開創eF-iBF原理，開發一類新型電驅動離子注入膜（e-PIM），使其在e-MC速率、e-MC產物純度和防垢性能方面擁有前所未有的性能。透過結合跨學科實驗策略和多尺度建模，這些e-PIM預計將比目前最先進的電力驅動膜性能提升至少1到2個數量級。具體而言，本計畫將：(1) 透過機制研究和即時表徵揭示不同電場條件下「離子刷」的波動規律；(2) 建立eF-iBF膜構建原理，以克服e-MC速率和產物純度之間的權衡問題；(3) 利用該原理開發具有更佳e-MC性能的先進e-PIM。本計畫的成功取決於我們能否闡明eF-iBF機理，並為新一代e-MC專用e-PIM制定設計指南。本計畫旨在提供一種實用且創新的eF-iBF原理，用於增強型e-PIM，不僅能克服e-MC速率和e-MC產品純度之間的矛盾，還能提供卓越的防垢性能。該提案將對能源、環境和經濟永續性產生深遠影響，尤其是在廢棄電池金屬離子回收領域。

17205925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205925.value: 融合通訊與計算實現信道自適應的邊緣智能

17205925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205925.value: The development of sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks is accelerating globally to provide fundamental infrastructure for propelling data economies. A distinctive feature of 6G networks is the extensive implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, known as edge intelligence, at network edges. The resultant platform will empower mobile devices and automate Internet-of-Things applications. Compared with traditional cloud computing, edge intelligence offers various benefits, including access to enormous distributed data, delivery of real-time computing services, alleviation of network traffic congestion, and privacy protection. Currently, three primary use cases under 6G standardization consideration – federated edge learning (FEEL), split inference (SPIN), and distributed sensing and inference (DSAI) – require frequent high-dimensional feature/gradient/model transmissions over-the-air. The resulting communication bottlenecks cannot be resolved by merely expanding spectrums or antenna array sizes. To address this challenge, we propose an integrated design approach, Edge Mingled Computing-Communication (EMC2), which adapts computing-communication operations to time-varying wireless channels. This approach involves identifying, quantifying, and optimizing fundamental computing-communication trade-offs in FEEL, SPIN, or DSAI systems. Consequently, we aim to develop a set of channel-adaptive edge-intelligence algorithms that leverage AI's ability to manage channel distortion and dynamically adjust computing/communication operations to prevent bottlenecks. The projected outcome is unprecedented end-to-end (E2E) performance – learning latency, inference accuracy, and sensing accuracy. 1) For FEEL systems, we will design optimal control algorithms to jointly adapt gradient pruning/quantization/descent and modulation-and-coding (AMC) to the channel state, thereby minimizing the E2E learning latency. 2) For SPIN systems, we will devise optimal control algorithms to jointly adapt the flexible AI algorithms with early exiting, AMC scheme, and discriminant-channel estimation to channels to maximize the E2E inference accuracy. 3) For DSAI systems, we plan to devise adaptive sensor-selection strategies that consider both view-and-channel diversity so as to maximum the E2E sensing accuracy. The proposed EMC2 technologies will help to reconcile the high demands of data-intensive edge intelligence with the limitations of 6G air interface. We anticipate that this research will pave the way for numerous innovations and applications in 6G, contributing to the development of transformational technologies. 第六代（6G）流動網絡的發展正在全球範圍內加速，以提供推動數據經濟的基礎設施。6G網絡的一個顯著特徵是在網絡邊緣廣泛部署人工智能（AI）演算法，稱為邊緣智能。由此形成的平台將賦能行動裝置，並自動化物聯網應用。與傳統雲端運算相比，邊緣智能具有多項優勢，包括存取海量分散式數據、提供實時運算服務、緩解網絡流量擁塞，以及保護隱私。目前，6G標準化所考量的三大主要應用場景——聯邦邊緣學習（FEEL）、分裂推理（SPIN）與分散式感知與推理（DSAI）——都需要頻繁進行高維特徵／梯度／模型的空中傳輸。由此帶來的通訊瓶頸，無法僅通過擴大頻譜或增加天線陣列規模來解決。為應對這挑戰，我們提出了一項整合式設計方案——邊緣融合計算－通訊（EMC2），該方案將計算與通訊操作適應於時變的無線信道。此方法包括識別、量化及優化FEEL、SPIN或DSAI系統中的基本計算－通訊權衡。因此，我們旨在開發一套利用AI管理信道失真、動態調整計算／通訊操作的信道自適應邊緣智能算法，以防止瓶頸。預期成果是實現前所未有的端對端（E2E）性能，包括學習延遲、推理精度和感知精度。具體而言：1）針對FEEL系統，我們將設計最佳控制算法，聯合調整梯度剪枝／量化／下降及調制編碼（AMC）以適應信道狀態，從而最小化端對端的學習延遲；2）針對SPIN系統，我們將制定最佳控制算法，聯合調整靈活的AI算法（如提前退出）、AMC方案和判別信道估算，以最大化端對端的推理精度；3）對於DSAI系統，我們計劃設計考量視角和信道多樣性的自適應感測器選擇策略，以最大化端對端的感知精度。所提出的EMC2技術將有助於協調高數據需求的邊緣智能與6G空中接口的限制。我們預期，這項研究將為6G的眾多創新與應用鋪平道路，推動變革性技術的發展。

17206225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17206225.value: 基於高度有序多孔框架的跨材料離子輸運研究

17206225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206225.value: Electrostatic charging derived from charge transfer during friction is commonplace, but understanding the charge species transferred still remains unclear and a debated issue. Electrons are widely believed to be the dominant charge carriers in contact electrification between solids, liquids, and gases. However, polymer-polymer contact electrification is more challenging to understand, as emerging evidence suggests mobile ions can also contribute to the process. This proposal aims to delve into the intricate workings of ionomers and their role in the field of triboelectricity, specifically focusing on the inter-material ion transfer in polymer-ionomer contact electrification. The project is centered around three primary objectives. In the first objective, we will design a series of model ionomers with controlled ion density and ion/electron binding affinity. The challenge lies in managing ion distributions and binding affinity on ionomer surfaces due to the short-range ordering inherent in polymers. To overcome this, we propose to develop synthetic routes for systematically regulating ion density and ion/electron binding affinity, leveraging porous frameworks as platform materials. Two synthetic strategies will be implemented, 1) incorporating various anionic/cationic units into porous frameworks, and 2) modulating the ratio of electron and ion transfer by adjusting the properties of non-ionic components in the ionomer. In the second objective, we will investigate the inter-material ion transfer during contact electrification of ionomers/polymer systems. The model ionomers will be subjected to friction under various ambient conditions. The results will be analyzed to determine the ratio of ionic to electronic contributions. We will then characterize the inter-material ion transfer of ionomers with different ion densities, ion binding affinities, and electron binding affinities. In the third objective, we will establish a new model for inter-material ion transfer during polymer/ionomer contact electrification. This will involve revisiting the water channel model through experimental characterization and computational techniques. We aim to characterize specific locations where ion transfer occurs, the presence of mobile ions on ionomer surfaces, and map the water layer adsorbed on the polymer surface. Computational insights will predict the behavior of mobile cations and anions at the interface. The outcomes of this project are expected to provide valuable insights that will inform the design of new and improved technologies for electrophotography, electrospraying, energy harvesting, and self-powered sensing. Understanding the contact electrification mechanism will assist in defining comprehensive design rules for friction materials, enhancing the performance of inter-material charge transfer. This, in turn, will address the grand challenge of the manufacturing-energy-sensing nexus. 摩擦誘導的電荷轉移所引發的靜電(或稱接觸起電)現象廣泛存在。然而，其過程中具體發生轉移的電荷屬性(如電子或離子)，至今仍存在爭議。傳統觀點普遍認為，電子是固體､液體及氣體等不同物態物質見發生接觸起電時的主要電荷載體。然而近年來研究證據表明，自由移動的離子也可能參與了該過程。這使得接觸起電的機制闡釋變得更加複雜。甚至在均一的同態物質體系中(如聚合物/聚合物這類固體/固體接觸體系)，明晰其實際發生機制也面臨顯著的挑戰。 基於上述問題，本研究旨在深入探究離子聚合物在摩擦電領域的微觀作用機制，重點集中在聚合物/離子聚合物界面處離子跨材料轉移過程。該項目將圍繞以下三個核心目標展開。 目標一：設計並合成具有不同離子濃度及離子/電子親和性的一系列離子聚合物材料。該目標的科學挑戰在於：聚合物固有短程有序特性導致離子聚合物表面離子濃度､分布及離子親和性難以調控。為突破此瓶頸，本項目提出基於多孔框架材料平台，開發系統性調控離子濃度和離子/電子親和性的合成新路徑。本項目將從以下兩種方向出發：1.將陰/陽離子定向引入多孔框架結構中。2. 通過調整離子聚合物中非離子組分的物化性質以實現電子與離子轉移貢獻比例的精準調控。 目標二：聚合物/離子聚合物接觸起電過程中的跨材料離子輸運機理研究。通過在不同環境條件下對模型離子聚合物進行接觸-分離循環測試，系統分析在該體系下電子與離子轉移的貢獻比例，以及探究在不同離子濃度，離子/電子親和性下，體系中離子跨材料轉移的特性和影響規律。 目標三：建立離子聚合物接觸起電中跨材料離子轉移模型。通過實驗表征與計算模擬，本項目將重新審視聚合物/離子聚合物界面處的水通道模型，旨在精準定位離子轉移發生的空間位點，表征離子聚合物表面自由移動離子的分布狀態以及構建聚合物表面吸附水層的高清圖譜。同時，通過計算模擬界面處的陰/陽離子的動態遷移行為，擬解釋界面離子輸運機制。 本項目研究成果預計將為靜電成像､靜電霧化沉積､能量收集及自供電傳感等前沿技術的發展提供新理論指引。同時對接觸起電機制的深度解析，將建立面向摩擦材料的跨材料電荷轉移的普適性設計準則。該研究成果最終致力於破解製造-能源-傳感技術協同發展中的關鍵基礎科學瓶頸。

17207125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207125.value: 自然啟發的漏斗型與負泊松比柔性屏障用於減緩泥石流災害的研究：大型物理模型

17207125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207125.value: The combined stress of human encroachment on hillsides and increase in heavy rainfall, as reported by the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, will increase the threat posed by landslides, which annually cause about US$4 billion in damage and 3,000 deaths globally. Debris flows, mixtures of soil and water surging downslope at high speeds, account for about 50% of the fatalities. In May 2024, a debris flow event buried 2,000 people in Papua New Guinea. Flexible barriers are increasingly used to arrest debris flows. These deform to reduce impact forces, are easy to install, and blend in with the environment. Surprisingly, their designs have not advanced in recent decades, partially owing to their proprietary nature. Research has demonstrated that the key to dissipating debris flow kinetic energy at impact is mobilising internal friction via grain shearing. However, existing barriers are inconsistent with this principle as they are not designed to prolong grain shearing. Guidelines specify that barriers should allow only 10% net deformation of the barrier span and be installed orthogonally to impacts; these result in high impact forces. To advance existing art, it is proposed to leverage nature-inspired concepts, specifically the silk web funnels used by caddisfly larvae to trap food in rivers and the negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) biomechanics of snake skin. Caddisfly funnels prolong the duration of flow inside them to trap food. Meanwhile, whereas most engineering materials have positive Poisson’s ratios, NPR materials expand both in the direction of applied tension and orthogonally to it, resulting in extremely large strains at low stress. The NPR enables snakes to consume large prey without rupturing their bodies. Adopting the aforementioned bio-inspired concepts is expected to significantly reduce the design impact force of flexible barriers and reduce reliance on proprietary knowledge. These improvements will drastically enhance design robustness to safely reduce fatalities and economic losses caused by debris flows. In this project, NPR nets will be alloy-printed. The mechanisms of impact between debris flows and NPR nets, which will be installed at angles to replicate a funnel to prolong shearing, will be revealed using one of the world’s largest flume models. This will yield design guidance. A numerical parametric study will be conducted to investigate parameters not studied in the experiments. The findings will promote the use of bio-inspired flexible barrier designs that are less proprietary and with enhanced performance. 根據聯合國氣候變遷政府間專門委員會（IPCC）報告，人工侵占山坡與降雨量增加將加劇山崩威脅，每年造成約40億美元的損失與3000人死亡。泥石流是主要的災害之一，其高速下沖的土水混合物約佔死亡人數的50%。2024年5月，巴布亞新幾內亞發生的泥石流事件埋沒了2000人。 柔性防護屏障在阻擋泥石流中越來越受到重視，因其能變形降低衝擊力、安裝簡便且與環境融合。然而，近數十年來其設計未有明顯進展，部分原因在於專利限制。研究顯示，釋放泥石流動能的關鍵在於利用顆粒剪切來激發內部摩擦，但現有的屏障並未充分設計來延長顆粒剪切時間。國際指南規定屏障只能允許10%的淨變形，且須垂直於衝擊方向安裝，這造成較高的衝擊力。 為突破現有技術，本文提出借鑒自然界的概念，包括用於河流捕食的毛蟲網漏斗與蛇皮的負泊松比（NPR）生物力學。毛蟲網漏斗能延長內部水流時間以捕獲食物；而大多數工程材料具有正泊松比，NPR材料則在拉伸方向及垂直方向同時擴展，在低應力下產生巨大變形，幫助蛇在不破裂的情況下吞食大型獵物。 採用上述生物啟發的概念，有望大幅降低柔性屏障的設計衝擊力，並減少對專利技術的依賴，從而提升設計的穩健性，安全減少泥石流造成的傷亡與經濟損失。 本研究將利用合金列印製作NPR網格，並利用全球最大規模的水槽模型，模擬泥石流與NPR網的撞擊機制，特別設置成漏斗形狀以延長剪切作用，提供設計指導。同時，進行數值參數分析，探索實驗未涵蓋的參數範圍，以推動具有較低專利壁壘且性能優越的生物啟發柔性屏障設計。

17207225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207225.value: 設計「綠色推動」措施以促進建築廢棄物現場管理：一種基於元宇宙與嚴肅遊戲的機器學習實驗方法

17207225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17207225.value: Prof Chan, Yee Shan Isabelle Prof Chen, Junjie Prof Jiang, Bin Dr Wu, Liupengfei Prof Xue, Fan Dr Yuan, Liang

17207225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207225.value: Nudge theory proposes that subtle changes in choice presentation can have a profound influence on people’s decisions and behaviors. The theory, which was popularized in behavioral sciences and economics, is also widely applied in green initiatives, including The Little Book of Green Nudges for university sustainability, plate/food waste minimization, and the 3Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle) for municipal solid waste management. However, we rarely see such green nudges applied to construction waste management (CWM), although construction waste often comprises 30~40% of all solid waste landfilled. Does nudging have no application in CWM? This research aims to explore various green nudges that can be used to boost onsite CWM. A traditional research methodology would be to design different nudges, conduct physical experiments (e.g., install nudges onsite, observe participants’ behavioral changes), and perform control and treatment group comparisons. However, these physical experiments would be costly and raise ethical concerns. Leveraging modern digital technologies and computing powers, this research adopts an alternative methodology combining metaverse, serious games, and machine learning to investigate how green nudges can boost onsite CWM, as follows: • First, based on a literature review and the views of industrial experts, we will design various ‘green nudges’ for improving onsite CWM; • Second, instead of installing the physical nudges onsite, we will develop them into metaverse serious games using 3D engines and generative artificial intelligence (AI) such as Sora; • Next, we will conduct metaverse serious game experiments to collect participants’ waste management behavior changes, performance, and their biometric data (e.g., electrograms and eye tracking); and • Finally, we will adopt machine learning to interpret the biometric data and explore the relationships between the nudges and behavioral changes, with the aim of finding out which green nudges are more effective than others in improving onsite CWM performance. Although these methods are not new individually, in combination, they form an innovative methodology that is more efficient, less expensive, and poses fewer ethical concerns than exploring green nudges for CWM using traditional methodologies. This research will deliver an improved understanding of what green nudges can improve onsite CWM performance and how they take effect. It will yield a catalogue of deployable nudging measures that stakeholders such as building clients and construction companies can adopt to improve CWM performance onsite. The research will also provide a methodology toolkit that can be replicated to benefit other waste management areas. 助推理論認為，選擇呈現方式的細微變化會對人們的決策和行為產生深遠的影響。該理論在行為科學和經濟學領域廣為流傳，也廣泛應用於綠色倡議，包括聯合國環境規劃署關於永續發展、減少餐盤/食物浪費以及城市固體廢物管理的3R原則（減少、再利用、再循環）的《綠色助推手冊》。然而，儘管建築廢棄物通常佔所有填埋固體廢物的30%至40%，我們卻很少看到這種「綠色助推」應用於建築廢棄物管理。助推在其中是否真的沒有應用前景？ 本研究旨在探討各種可用於促進現場建築廢棄物管理的綠色助推措施。傳統的研究方法旨在設計不同的助推措施，進行物理實驗（例如，在現場安裝助推裝置，觀察參與者的行為變化），並進行對照組和實驗組之間的比較。然而，這些物理實驗成本高昂，並可能引發倫理問題。本研究利用現代數字技術和運算能力，採用結合元宇宙、嚴肅遊戲和機器學習的替代方法，探究綠色助推如何促進現場建築廢棄物管理 。具體方法如下： • 首先，基於文獻綜述和行業專家的意見，我們將設計各種「綠色助推」來改善現場建築廢棄物管理； • 其次，我們將不再在現場安裝實體助推，而是使用 3D 引擎和 Sora 等生成式人工智能將其開發成元宇宙嚴肅遊戲； • 接下來，我們將進行元宇宙嚴肅遊戲實驗，收集參與者的垃圾管理行為變化、績效及其生物特徵資料（例如心電圖和眼動追蹤）； • 最後，我們將採用機器學習來解讀生物特徵數據，並探索助推與行為變化之間的關係，以期找出哪些綠色助推在改善現場建築廢棄物管理績效方面比其他綠色助推更有效。 雖然這些方法單獨來看並不新穎，但結合起來，它們形成了一種創新方法，比使用傳統方法探索現場建築廢棄物管理的綠色助推措施更有效率、更經濟，且倫理問題更少。 本研究將加深對哪些綠色助推措施能夠改善現場建築廢棄物績效及其如何發揮作用的理解。研究將提供一系列可部署的助推措施，供建築客戶、建築公司和環保組織等持份者採用，進而改善績效。本研究也將提供一套可複製的方法工具包，使其他廢棄物管理領域受益。

17207925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207925.value: 用於硬件可追溯模型保護的可控精度模擬存內計算

17207925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207925.value: As the cost of training large language models for generative AI increases exponentially, these models have become valuable assets for technology companies, raising significant concerns to protect their intellectual property. Current security measures often result in substantial hardware overhead, limiting deployment on energy-constrained edge devices. Analog computing in emerging memory devices, offers a promising solution for efficient edge processing. However, these technologies are hindered by unavoidable computing errors due to device defects and variations. The research leverages the inherent fault tolerance of AI algorithms, particularly neural networks, to turn these challenges into opportunities for model protection. The project aims to design fault-tolerant systems that optimize both precision and security by harnessing computing errors to encode hardware-specific information—similar to a watermark—into the model’s output, thereby safeguarding it against unauthorized use. To build the fault-tolerant system, we propose a novel computing architecture to mitigate errors from device defects. This involves decomposing a matrix represented by a crossbar into two submatrices. By adjusting these submatrices to align with defective devices, we can neutralize their negative impact. This technique can be combined with analog slicing, redundancy, and analog error-correcting codes to achieve defect-free analog computing with adjustable precision or stochasticity. The security protocol will leverage controlled computing errors arising from various non-idealities. Device-to-device variation produces unique computing errors as fingerprints that cannot be replicated on different hardware, while cycle-to-cycle variation results in errors that cannot be reproduced after reprogramming the same model on the same hardware. Preliminary simulations indicate that this approach can significantly reduce error rates while embedding additional information about the hardware or deployment instance with minimal hardware overhead. This makes analog computing more feasible for edge applications, particularly those requiring privacy, reliability, and security. The PI brings extensive experience in analog in-memory computing, particularly with RRAM devices, while the Co-I provides expertise in hardware security and private AI on digital hardware. Together, they aim to pioneer innovative strategies in analog computing for model protection. The expected outcomes include optimized techniques for fault-tolerant computing, a comprehensive security protocol for model protection, and a detailed evaluation of the proposed methods’ performance and security, potentially setting new standards for AI model protection with analog hardware. Although the focus is on AI models with RRAM, these techniques can be applied to other edge tasks and are adaptable to other memory technologies, e.g., PCM, FeFETs, STT/SOT-MRAM, and Flash memories. 隨著用於生成式人工智能的大型語言模型訓練成本呈指數級增長，這些模型已成為科技公司的重要資產，由此引發了對其知識產權保護的重大關切。當前的安全措施往往帶來可觀的硬件開銷，限制了其在邊緣設備上的部署。基於新型存儲器件的模擬計算為高效的邊緣處理提供了有前景的解決方案。然而，這些技術受制於器件缺陷與差異所導致的不可避免的計算誤差。 本研究利用人工智能算法固有的容錯性，將這些挑戰轉化為模型保護的機遇。項目旨在通過利用計算誤差，將硬件特定的信息（類似水印）編碼進模型輸出，在優化精度與安全性的同時，保護模型免遭未授權使用。 為構建容錯系統，我們提出一種新型計算架構，以緩解源自器件缺陷的誤差。該方法將交叉陣列（crossbar）所表示的矩陣分解為兩個子矩陣。通過調節這兩個子矩陣使其與存在缺陷的器件對齊，可抵消其負面影響。該技術可與模擬切片、冗余以及模擬糾錯碼相結合，實現具有可調精度或隨機性的等效無缺陷模擬計算。 安全協議將利用由多種非理想性受控引入的計算誤差。器件間差異會產生獨特的計算誤差，形成無法在不同硬件上複製的“指紋”；而編程週期間差異會導致在同一硬件上對同一模型重新編程後也無法復現的誤差。 我們的初步仿真表明，該方法能夠在顯著降低錯誤率的同時，以極小的硬件開銷嵌入關於硬件或部署實例的附加信息。這使得模擬計算更適用於邊緣應用，尤其是那些對隱私、可靠性與安全性有要求的場景。 項目的首席研究員在基於RRAM的模擬存內計算方面具有豐富經驗，而協同研究員則在硬件安全與數字硬件上的隱私人工智能方面具備專長。該團隊將攜手在模擬計算的模型保護方向上開拓創新策略。預期成果包括：面向容錯計算的優化技術、一套用於模型保護的完整安全協議，以及對所提方法的性能與安全性的系統評估，有望為基於模擬硬件的人工智能模型保護樹立新的範式。 儘管研究重點聚焦於搭載 RRAM 的人工智能模型，這些技術同樣適用於其他邊緣任務，並可適配於其他存儲技術，例如相變存儲器（PCM）、鐵電場效應晶體管（FeFET）、矩磁阻存儲器（STT/SOT‑MRAM）以及閃存。

17208425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208425.value: 活性污泥中次級代謝產物的生物合成及其對功能菌群的調控作用研究

17208425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208425.value: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) encode the enzymes to synthesize a wide range of secondary metabolites, which play a crucial role in mediating interactions within the microbial community. Activated sludge (AS) is an engineered microbial system widely used for biological wastewater treatment process, harboring a unique microbiome. While the important roles of secondary metabolites in complex microbial community have got increasing interests of research, there remains a significant gap in the understanding of the diversity of BGCs in AS systems and how their products (secondary metabolites) influence microbial communities. This integrated project aims to comprehensively characterize the profiles of BGCs in AS systems and reveal their dynamics, activities, and influence on functional populations involving in biological wastewater treatment. In this study, the gene abundance, diversity and dynamics of BGCs in AS samples will be revealed by a longitudinal metagenomic sequencing. Genome-centric metagenomic analysis will unveil the profile of novel BGCs, especially those in not-yet-cultured bacteria. Since the abundance of BGCs at gene levels are often inconsistent with the biosynthetic activities, the activities of BGCs will be investigated by time-series metatranscriptomic data to uncover the active and silent BGCs under different environmental conditions. A genome-resolved co-activity network will be developed to predict the interactions between the microbial hosts harboring BGCs and the core functional populations in AS. Metabolic coupling analysis within co-activity communities will infer the candidate BGCs and their products that modulate the functional pathways. To provided direct experimental evidence, the heterogeneous expression of BGCs will be conducted and their secondary metabolite products will be characterized. The roles of BGC-harboring hosts in the microbial interactions will be studies by co-cultured them with other functional populations such as aerobic ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB), which are essential for efficient nitrogen removal of wastewater. Moreover, we will explore novel strategies for introducing BGC hosts as microbial additives in AS to optimize biological wastewater treatment processes. Our study will provide a deep understanding of the production of secondary metabolites in AS system and their roles in complex microbial communities. The findings of this study can also serve as a reference for the development and refinement of microbial communities for a range of biotechnological applications. 生物合成基因簇（BGCs）編碼合成多種次級代謝產物，這些代謝產物在調控微生物互作中起重要作用。活性污泥是工程化的微生物系統，用於污水生物處理。活性污泥蘊含獨特的微生物組。儘管次級代謝產物在複雜微生物群落中的重要作用日益受到關注，但對活性污泥體系中BGCs的多樣性及其產物影響微生物組的機制的認識仍存在空白。本項目旨在綜合地解析活性污泥中的生物合成基因簇的多樣性，揭示他們的動態變化、活性及對污水生物處理中的功能菌群的調控機制。首先採用縱向宏基因組測序揭示活性污泥樣本中BGCs的基因豐度、多樣性及動態變化規律，通過基因組導向的宏基因組分析挖掘未培養細菌中的新型BGCs。結合時序宏轉錄組數據分析不同環境條件下BGCs的激活或沉默狀態，構建基因組導向的共活性網絡，從而預測BGCs宿主菌與活性污泥中核心功能菌群的互作關係。針對共活性網絡中識別出的菌群，通過代謝耦合分析篩選調控關鍵功能途徑的候選BGCs，異源表達BGCs從而表征其產物化學結構。進一步建立BGCs宿主菌與氨氧化菌、亞硝酸鹽氧化菌等核心功能菌群的共培養體系，驗證次級代謝產物對污水脫氮過程的調控作用。研究結果將有助於開發定向調控活性污泥微生物組的新策略。本研究深入闡明活性污泥系統中次級代謝產物的生物合成規律及其群落調控機制，為優化微生物組構建提供參考。

17208725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208725.value: 電泵狄拉克渦旋光子晶體激光器

17208725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17208725.value: Dr Ma, Jingwen Prof Yin, Xiaobo Prof Zhang, Shuang

17208725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208725.value: This proposal aims to develop electrically pumped large-area semiconductor lasers using Dirac-vortex cavities. Since the 1960s, electrically pumped semiconductor lasers have revolutionized many fields including information technology, healthcare, sensors, defense, and industrial manufacturing. Researchers have been improving lasing performance to meet growing demands, focusing on developing large-area lasers that offer both high power and single-mode operation. A key challenge in achieving this goal is the inverse relationship between cavity size (V) and free spectra range (FSR): FSR ~ 1/V. Larger cavities can accommodate more gain medium, allowing for higher output powers, but this reduces the FSR, thereby compromising single-mode performance. This constraint affects most semiconductor lasers, including edge-emitting lasers, vertical cavity surface-emitting lasers, and photonic crystal surface-emitting lasers. The Dirac-vortex state, originally from high-energy theoretical physics, has recently gained increasing interest in photonics as a promising solution. Unlike conventional lasers, Dirac-vortex lasers feature Dirac-cone dispersions, resulting in a fundamentally different relationship: FSR ~ 1/√("V" ). This means their FSR decreases more slowly as cavity size V increases, making them ideal for high-power single-mode operations. Recently, prototypes of Dirac-vortex lasers have been realized, but they either operate under optical pumping or at terahertz wavelengths under cryogenic temperatures, which are impractical for widespread applications. An electrically pumped Dirac-vortex laser that fully showcases the advantages of large-area single-mode operation at optical wavelengths would be a significant milestone, but this remains experimentally elusive. In this proposal, we aim to experimentally create an electrically pumped large-area Dirac-vortex laser. Our preliminary results have demonstrated optically pumped Dirac-vortex lasers and electrically pumped band-edge photonic-crystal lasers. We will design and fabricate a Dirac-vortex cavity on a meticulously engineered semiconductor epitaxy wafer, with a cavity size of 5 mm × 5 mm—100 times larger than existing optically pumped Dirac-vortex lasers. In addition to the photonic design, we will optimize the electrical and thermal aspects to maximize injection current and prevent heat buildup. With electrical current above the threshold, we expect to observe single-mode lasing with a peak power exceeding 1 watt. This project has far-reaching implications for both cutting-edge engineering applications and fundamental scientific research. Technologically, our device will enable practical applications in communication, LiDAR, and manufacturing. Scientifically, Dirac-vortex lasers, as high-dimensional topological models with inherent nonlinearity and non-Hermiticity, can extend existing fermionic topological models established for electronic materials, opening the possibility of novel bosonic topological physics at nanoscales. 自20世紀60年代以來，電泵浦半導體激光器在信息技術、醫療健康、傳感、國防和工業製造等多個領域引發了革命性的變革。為了滿足日益增長的需求，研究人員持續優化激光性能，重點開發能夠同時實現高功率和單模工作的大面陣激光器。實現這一目標的一個關鍵挑戰在於腔體尺寸（V）與自由光譜範圍（FSR）之間存在反比關係：FSR ~ 1/V。較大的腔體可以容納更多的增益介質，從而獲得更高的輸出功率，但這會減小FSR，進而損害單模性能。這一限制影響着大多數半導體激光器，包括邊發射激光器、垂直腔面發射激光器（VCSEL）和光子晶體面發射激光器（PCSEL）。 起源於高能理論物理的狄拉克渦旋態（Dirac-vortex state），近年來在光子學領域作為一項極具前景的解決方案獲得了越來越多的關注。與常規激光器不同，狄拉克渦旋激光器具有狄拉克錐形色散（Dirac-cone dispersions）特性，這導致了一個根本性的不同關係：FSR ~ 1/√V。這意味着當腔體尺寸V增大時，其FSR下降得更慢，使其成為實現高功率單模工作的理想選擇。最近，狄拉克渦旋激光器的原型機已經實現，但它們要麼在光泵浦下工作，要麼是在低溫下工作的太赫茲波長激光器，這些對於廣泛應用來說都不夠實用。能夠充分展現大面陣單模工作優勢、在光學波長下工作的電泵浦狄拉克渦旋激光器將是一個重要的里程碑，但這在實驗上仍未被實現。 在本提案中，我們的目標是實驗性地製造出電泵浦的大面陣狄拉克渦旋激光器。我們的初步研究結果已經成功演示了光泵浦的狄拉克渦旋激光器和電泵浦的帶邊光子晶體激光器。我們將在一個經過精密設計的半導體外延片上，設計和製造一個尺寸為5毫米 × 5毫米的狄拉克渦旋腔——這比現有光泵浦狄拉克渦旋激光器的腔體大100倍。除了光子結構設計，我們還將優化電學和熱學設計，以最大化注入電流並防止熱量累積。當注入電流超過閾值時，我們預期將觀察到峰值功率超過1瓦的單模激光發射。 本項目對前沿工程應用和基礎科學研究都具有深遠的意義。在技術上，我們的器件將為通信、激光雷達（LiDAR）和工業製造等領域的實際應用提供可能。在科學上，狄拉克渦旋激光器作為具有固有非線性和非厄米性（non-Hermiticity）的高維拓撲模型，可以拓展為電子材料建立的現有費米子拓撲模型，為在納米尺度探索新型玻色子拓撲物理開闢道路。

17208825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208825.value: 提高具身智能擴散動作策略的安全性及其在銀髮經濟中的應用

17208825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208825.value: Hong Kong is facing a severe aging population crisis, with over 1.4 million elderly individuals aged 60 and above. As the proportion of elderly residents grows, there is an increasing demand for innovative solutions to support elderly care. In response, the Hong Kong government has significantly invested in embodied AI—intelligent systems physically embodied in robots to perform various caregiving tasks. For instance, the Hong Kong Investment Corporation (HKIC) has invested in companies developing robotic arms and dexterous hands to assist the elderly with daily tasks. A critical component in embodied AI control is the diffusion policy, which allows robots to learn control strategies from a limited amount of expert data and generalize across different scenarios. However, traditional diffusion policy has focused solely on optimizing the robotic arm’s joint configurations to manipulate objects (e.g., utensils, kitchen tools) without considering the safety implications, which are paramount in elderly care. For example, a robotic system must determine whether an object like a kitchen knife is safe for an elderly person to use to prevent potential injuries. This project aims to develop a safety-driven diffusion policy for embodied AI systems, explicitly targeting elderly care applications. The goal is to enable robots to perform tasks effectively and prioritize the safety of the elderly by integrating object safety assessments into their control strategies. This is an open problem. The central challenge lies in extending the traditional diffusion policy—currently optimized for manipulation tasks—to incorporate safety considerations. Elderly care presents unique challenges requiring the robot to assess whether interactions with particular objects (e.g., sharp or heavy items) are safe for the elderly. This introduces a new dimension to the diffusion policy problem: context-aware safety assessment, in which the robot must evaluate an object's suitability before performing a task. This project will profoundly impact the embodied AI industry, elderly care, and government healthcare initiatives. By developing a safety-driven diffusion policy, this research will enable robots to safely assist the elderly in their daily lives, significantly reducing the risks associated with autonomous caregiving systems. Furthermore, the outcomes of this project will contribute to the broader field of embodied AI, particularly in designing intelligent systems that can autonomously balance task efficiency with user safety. 本項目計劃在傳統擴散策略框架基礎上設計一種全新的安全驅動擴散策略（SD-DP）演算法，通過整合安全評估機制與 classifier-free guidance 指導函數，確保所生成的控制策略在優化任務表現的同時滿足老年照護中對物品操作安全的嚴格要求；同時，我們將建置一個名為 SafeCare 的專為老年照護設計的數據集，該數據集計劃從 YouTube 收集高品質真實老年照護情境影片，涵蓋老年人活動、物品互動及照護與輔助裝置的使用，並進行精細標註，以支援 SD-DP 演算法的訓練與評估。研究團隊將基於 SD-DP 演算法訓練並測試控制模型（包括基礎型、結合多模態大型語言模型以及加上安全約束變體），並與標準擴散策略、離線強化學習及模仿學習等現有方法從安全性與任務執行效率兩大面向進行比較評估，利用如「風險降低分數」、「安全違規數」、「任務成功率」及「效率」等指標，預期能在安全性上提升，同時保持或提高任務效率；此外，模型還將在模擬環境中以「餵食協助」作為首要任務進行實驗部署，為未來申請更大規模經費以推動實際機器人部署奠定堅實基礎。

17209225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17209225.value: 藥效動力學驅動的機器學習及其在轉移性前列腺癌自適應藥物組合中的應用

17209225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17209225.value: Prof Chen, Frank Youhua Prof HO, Chin Pang Dr Ho, Isaac Prof Li, Xue

17209225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209225.value: Prostate cancer is prevalent in men, with China experiencing the highest increase in incidence and death rates among all cancers. Treating metastatic prostate cancer (and all cancer types) is challenging due to evolving resistance, causing treatment failure and tumor progression. Integrating evolutionary dynamics into cancer therapy is an emerging field at the interface of data science and cancer research. Cancer resistance evolution and drug therapy represent a strategic interaction between different cancer cell types. Adaptive therapy, which incorporates intratumoral Darwinian dynamics into mathematical modeling, has been validated in simulations and small-scale trials. However, optimizing personalized adaptive therapy for Chinese patients faces four challenges: First, current models rely on predetermined thresholds to discontinue and resume treatment, without a data-driven optimization scheme to identify the best treatment. Second, drug combination is common in clinical practice but there is no systematic approach to identify the best drug combinations for adaptive therapy. Third, mathematical models of adaptive therapy are prone to testing and model errors, leading to unpredictable outcomes. Fourth, adaptive therapy studies are rare in Chinese patients, who have different genotypic and phenotypic features compared with Western patients. To address these fundamental challenges, we propose a pharmacodynamics-driven machine learning approach to determine the optimal adaptive drug combination therapy for individual Chinese prostate cancer patients. The proposed system features a drug combination module and a treatment optimization module. The drug combination module integrates a multi-layer human interactome network and a novel deep learning model to identify synergistic drug combinations based on pharmacodynamics principles. The treatment optimization module incorporates the identified drug combinations into a mathematical model of cancer evolution, as well as the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of drugs and their combinations. A robust reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed to derive the optimal personalized adaptive therapy policy that is robust to testing and model errors. We will train and validate the pharmacodynamics-driven and machine learning-based adaptive therapy through public clinical trial data and our 24-year territory-wide electronic health record data in Hong Kong. Our interdisciplinary team, encompassing medical informatics, robust optimization, and oncology, combined with large-scale real clinical patient data and a pilot trial, gives this project a high likelihood of success. We anticipate it will lead to innovative personalized adaptive drug combination therapies and improved outcomes for many Chinese patients living with prostate cancer, now and in the future. 前列腺癌是男性中常見的癌症，在中國其發病率和死亡率增長最快。治療轉移性前列腺癌面臨巨大挑戰，主要原因是癌細胞會不斷產生耐藥性，導致治療失敗和腫瘤惡化。近年來，將演化動力學理念融入癌症治療，成為結合數據科學與癌症研究的新方向。 癌症耐藥性和藥物治療代表了不同類型癌細胞之間的策略互動。自適應治療方法結合了腫瘤內部的達爾文式演化動態，並用數學模型進行模擬，已在部分研究和小型臨床試驗中得到驗證。但針對華人患者的個性化自適應治療優化還存在四大困難：首先，現有模型依賴預設的治療停止和恢復標準，缺乏數據驅動的優化方法；其次，臨床常用的藥物組合缺少系統性篩選最佳組合的方式；第三，自適應治療的數學模型容易受到測試和模型誤差影響，結果難以預測；第四，針對華人患者的自適應治療研究稀少，而中西患者在基因和表型方面存在差異。 為解決上述問題，我們提出了一套基於藥效動力學的機器學習方法，旨在為華人前列腺癌患者尋找最佳的自適應藥物組合治療。這套系統包括藥物組合模塊和治療優化模塊。藥物組合模塊融合多層次的人體互作網絡和新型深度學習模型，根據藥效動力學原理，篩選出具有協同作用的藥物組合。治療優化模塊則把這些藥物組合納入癌症演化的數學模型，並結合藥物的藥效和藥代特性，利用強化學習算法制定最適合個體患者的自適應治療策略，且能減少測試和模型誤差帶來的影響。我們將通過公開臨床試驗數據及香港24年全境電子健康紀錄，對這套方法進行訓練和驗證。 我們的團隊涵蓋醫學信息學、魯棒優化和腫瘤學專家，結合大規模真實患者數據和先導試驗，有望推動創新型個性化自適應藥物組合治療，為華人前列腺癌患者帶來更好的治療效果，不僅造福現在，更惠及未來。

17210325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210325.value: 城市貨運零排放區的計算性設計

17210325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17210325.value: Prof Wang, Hai Prof Xu, Junshi Prof Yuan, Quan Prof Zhao, Jinhua

17210325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210325.value: With prevalent air pollution and rising freight demand, cities worldwide are searching for policy measures to manage emissions from freight vehicles that disproportionately contribute to harmful pollutants in cities. One increasingly popular approach is zero-emission zones (ZEZs), which restrict non-zero-emission vehicles from entering designated urban areas, leading to air quality improvements and other co-benefits. However, ZEZs can incur significant economic costs for freight carriers relying on conventional fossil fuel trucks, in the forms of forcing vehicle rerouting or imposing vehicle replacements. The rerouted trucks may displace emissions to neighborhoods outside the zone, raising questions about environmental justice and policy effectiveness. Therefore, the spatial design of ZEZs requires carefully evaluating the trade-offs and anticipating carrier reactions, a problem that remains mostly unexplored in the literature. This project proposes the ZEZ design problem (ZEZDP), which aims to generate the optimal ZEZ design that balances the emission reduction for the residents and economic viability for the carriers. In this problem, carriers operate a mix of conventional trucks (CTs) and electric trucks (ETs), and the policymaker makes decisions regarding the zone layout. Given a ZEZ, CTs can no longer access the part of the road network within the zone, while ETs are unaffected. In response, cost-sensitive carriers would adjust their vehicle routing and replacement strategies, thereby affecting emission distribution. This can be represented as a leader-follower or Stackelberg game, where the policymaker serves as the leader and carriers are the followers. To address the ZEZDP, we will adopt a bi-level formulation. The lower-level problem estimates the carriers’ behavior responses regarding the route choice, tour assignment, and vehicle replacement. They will be jointly modeled as a fleet size and mixed vehicle routing problem, and solved by leveraging large-scale truck trajectories for imitation learning. The upper-level problem represents the design decisions of the policymaker, who is concerned with reducing the population exposure to CT emissions. We propose to estimate the exposure as a function of CT flows on the road network, and optimize it by sequentially update the zone layout through a reinforcement learning approach. Furthermore, we will investigate how the ZEZ’s impacts vary across different communities and carriers, and extend the formulation to capture such disparities. The proposed computational framework can be used to generate ZEZ design options under different policy scenarios. We will demonstrate it using real-world data in Shenzhen, and develop a map-based dashboard to support the zone design decisions. 隨著空氣污染日益嚴重及貨運需求持續上升，全球各大城市正積極尋求政策措施，以管理貨運車輛所產生的排放，因為這些車輛在城市中對有害污染物的貢獻尤為顯著。其中一項日益受歡迎的做法是設立零排放區，限制非零排放車輛進入特定的城市區域，藉此改善空氣品質並帶來其他附帶效益。然而，對於依賴傳統燃油貨車的運輸業者來說，零排放區可能帶來顯著的經濟成本，例如被迫繞路或更換車輛。繞路的貨車可能會將排放轉移到零排放區外的社區，從而引發環境正義及政策成效等問題。因此，零排放區的空間設計需謹慎評估各項權衡，並預測運輸業者的反應，而這方面的問題在現有文獻中仍鮮有深入探討。 本項目將提出零排放區設計問題，旨在生成一個在居民減排效益與運輸業者經濟可行性之間取得平衡的最佳零排放區設計。在此問題中，運輸業者同時運營傳統貨車與電動貨車，而政策制定者則負責決定零排放區的布局。一旦設立零排放區，傳統貨車將無法進入區域內的道路網路，而電動貨車則不受影響。作為回應，對成本敏感的運輸業者將會調整其車輛路線與車輛替換策略，進而影響排放的分布。這個過程可被視為一種領導者-追隨者博弈，其中政策制定者為領導者，運輸業者則為追隨者。 為了解決零排放區設計問題，本項目將採用雙層數學規劃架構。下層問題用於預測運輸業者在路線選擇、運輸任務分配以及車輛替換方面的行為反應。這些行為將被共同建模為一個車隊規模與混合車型路線規劃問題，並透過大規模貨車軌跡數據進行模仿學習來求解。上層問題則代表政策制定者的設計決策，其主要關注點在於降低居民對傳統貨車排放的暴露。本項目將暴露量建構為傳統貨車在道路網路上的流量函數，並利用強化學習方法，透過依序調整零排放區的布局來優化暴露量。此外，我們也將探討零排放區對不同社區及運輸業者造成的影響差異，並延伸數學架構以捕捉這些不均現象。本項目提出的計算架構可用於在不同政策情境下生成零排放區設計方案，並將以深圳的真實案例進行示範，開發一個以地圖為基礎的決策輔助平台，以支持零排放區設計決策。

17210525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210525.value: 細水長流：高密度住宅區城市排水系統旱流管理的環境流量解決方案

17210525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210525.value: Dry weather flows (DWF) are non-stormwater runoff in urban drainage systems caused by activities such as street cleaning, car washing, and illicit connections. High-density residential areas are particularly affected by the degraded water quality and health risks associated with DWS, as they generally generate more DWF and face greater exposure. Traditional management methods, such as interceptors, are inadequate given the spatio-temporal variability of DWF and are also ineffective in addressing the issue along drainage channels. Environmental flow refers to the carefully managed amount, timing, and quality of water essential for sustaining healthy ecosystems in waterways. Managing environmental flow in urban drainage channels can potentially address issues caused by DWF. This project aims to develop cost-effective, eco-friendly solutions for DWF management through controlled environmental flows. By releasing freshwater into drainage channels during dry weather, we seek to remove accumulated sediments and pollutants, improving water quality. A key focus is developing a water release scheme to strategically regulate these flows for optimal effectiveness. In the first part of the project, on-site sampling and monitoring will be conducted to analyze the current status of DWF at selected high-density residential sites. This analysis will help characterize the temporal patterns of DWF quantity and quality in these drainage systems. In the second part, the collected data will be used to build predictive models of DWF quantity and quality over time. First, compressed sensing techniques will enhance data quality and reconstruct missing data. Then, deep learning methods will model complex patterns and predict long-term DWF data. Additionally, causal inference-based structural equation models will identify key environmental factors influencing DWF patterns. This integrated approach and long-term predicted data will improve understanding of DWF dynamics and inform the development of effective water release schemes. In the final part, data from the machine learning models will be used with the Water Quality Analysis Simulation Program (WASP) to simulate hydrodynamics and pollutant transport in the drainage system during dry weather. These simulations will be integrated into an optimization framework to develop water release schemes that flush accumulated sediments and pollutants, mitigating DWF impacts while considering limited water resources. In summary, this project will develop a novel environmental flow-based solution for DWF that addresses problems along drainage channels and is more environmentally friendly than conventional methods. This approach is expected to improve people's quality of life and contribute to sustainable development. 在高密度住宅區，街道清潔、洗車或非法渠管接駁等活動會產生旱流（即非雨水的水流）。這些水流往往含有污染物，導致水道水質惡化，對居民健康構成威脅。由於這些地區人口密集，旱流的流量通常較大，居民接觸污染水體的風險也相對較高。傳統的截流設施難以應付旱流在時間和空間上的變化，亦未能有效解決排水渠內的污染問題。 為應對上述挑戰，本項目提出一種成本效益高且環保的創新方案，透過控制「環境流量」來改善水質。我們計劃在乾旱天氣向排水渠注入潔淨淡水，以沖走積聚的沉積物和污染物。所謂環境流量，是指經過科學規劃和調控的水量、釋放時間及水質，目的是維持和保護河道生態系統的健康。 項目分為三個階段進行。首先，於選定的高密度住宅區內的排水渠進行現場水樣採集和監測，分析旱季期間水流的流量與水質隨時間的變化模式。其次，利用收集所得的數據，結合壓縮感知技術提升數據質素並補充缺失資料，再運用深度學習方法預測長期旱流趨勢，並透過因果推斷模型找出影響旱流的主要環境因素。這些分析有助深入了解旱流的動態特性，為制定合適的水流釋放方案提供科學依據。最後，結合機器學習預測結果與水質模擬程式，模擬旱季期間排水渠內的水流及污染物傳輸情況，從而制定更有效的水流釋放策略，在有效清除污染物的同時，亦能善用水資源。 本項目提出的環境流量方案比傳統方法更環保、更有效，能切實改善排水渠的旱流污染問題，提升市民的生活環境質素，促進城市的長遠發展。

17210625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210625.value: 自助服務系統利潤優化：服務可靠性建模及維修方案設計

17210625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210625.value: Advanced automation and IoT technologies have boosted the development of self-service systems (e.g., electric vehicle charging piles and kiosk machines) capable of operating without on-site staff, thereby providing around-the-desk services at low labor costs. As the self-service market booms, projected to reach a market value of $46 billion by 2025, there is an increasing issue with random and repeated failures of self-service systems during operation. These failures interrupt the service process and reduce service level and profit, calling upon effective solutions. This project aims to develop a systematic profit maximization framework for self-service system operators by quantifying the impacts of the systems’ failures on the service level, determining optimal maintenance actions, and including them in the location and sizing decision-making process. To achieve this aim, the following challenges must be tackled. First, self-service systems are subject to multiple failure modes that evolve stochastically with time and environment. These failures interact with the random demand arrival and service processes (usually with non-constant rates) and affect the service level. For example, the service process accelerates some failure modes’ evolvements, and the system failure causes two unique demand-system interactions: failure-induced demand switching (FDS) and failure-associated demand arrival rates. These dynamic and random interactions result in challenges in quantifying the impact of systems’ failures on the service level. Second, maintenance actions also interact with the above-mentioned stochastic processes, and they jointly determine service revenue and maintenance cost (e.g., maintenance prevents failures; however, during maintenance, demands may be rejected, and FDS is restricted), causing the challenge in making maintenance decisions for profit maximization. Third, an operator may install self-service systems in multiple locations. The locations, maintenance policies, demand arrivals, and service reliabilities of these systems exhibit a complex progressive correlation, making it challenging to decide their optimal locations and maintenance actions. To tackle the first challenge, we model the systems’ service reliability by modeling the failure modes’ evolvements and their interactions with the demands, as well as their joint impacts on service reliability. We resolve the second and third challenges by designing a two-dimensional selective maintenance policy and a joint location, sizing, and maintenance policy. This study is among the first attempts at a systematic methodology to maximize self-service system operators' profit. The research findings widely apply to modeling and optimizing the performance of service systems with complex configurations. All stakeholders in the service industry will be the beneficiaries. 自動化與物聯網技術推動了自助系統（如，電動車充電樁和自助終端機）的快速發展，使其能在無需現場人員的情況下自主運行進而以較低的人力成本提供24小時服務。隨著自助服務的迅速普及，預計到2025年，市場規模將達到460億美元。在運營過程中，自助系統被觀測到隨機故障的問題日益突出。這些故障中斷了服務流程，降低了盈利和服務水平，亟需有效的解決方案。本項目旨在為自助系統運營商建立一套系統的利潤最大化框架，通過量化系統故障對服務水平的影響，確定最優維護策略，並將其納入選址與規模決策過程。本項目擬解決以下挑戰。 首先，自助系統受到多種故障模式的影響。通常情況下，故障模式隨時間和環境的變化呈隨機演化，並與需求到達及服務過程相互作用，進而影響服務水平。例如，某些故障模式的演變進程受到服務狀態的影響，而系統故障則引發需求切換（Failure-Induced Demand Switching, FDS）和需求到達率。第二，維護措施也會與上述隨機過程相互作用，共同決定服務收入和維護成本，因此在利潤最大化的目標下制定維護策略面臨較大困難。第三，運營商可能在多個地點部署自助系統，這些系統的地點選擇、維護策略、需求到達和服務可靠性等因素呈現複雜的逐步相關性，增加了優化其最優位置和維護措施的難度。 為應對第一個挑戰，項目通過建模故障模式的演變過程及其與需求的相互作用，以及它們對系統服務可靠性的聯合影響，來刻畫系統的服務可靠性。針對第二和第三個挑戰，項目設計了一種二維選擇性維護策略，以及一體化的選址、規模和維護策略，以實現系統的最優運營與維護。 本項目研究成果在建模與優化具有複雜結構的服務系統性能方面具有廣泛的應用價值。

17211325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211325.value: 情景與主動的偏好魯棒優化

17211325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211325.value: In decision-making under uncertainty, a decision maker's (DM's) preference is often expressed by a choice function such as expected utility or a risk measure, which assigns a numerical value to a risky prospect. Properly identifying the choice function that faithfully represents the DM's true preference is crucial. For example, in portfolio optimization, it is essential for providing a reliable investment plan and achieving a better balance between conservativeness and optimism in return. In practice, such a choice function has to be elicited or given in a subjective manner. Misidentification of the choice function can lead to excessive risk taking under high volatility and may cause extremely high loss for the DM. Preference robust optimization (PRO) is proposed to tackle the above problem where the DM's choice function is ambiguous, and the robust optimal investment plan is found based on the worst-case choice function from a set of plausible ones constructed from available partial information about the DM's true preference. The main limitation of existing PRO works is that a large number of pairwise comparison prospect pairs are required to be labeled by DM, during the preference elicitation, in order to get the worst-case choice function close to the ground truth. PRO could face resistance to adoption in real life applications, due to the heavy cognitive workload imposed on DMs. On the other hand, it also raises the scalability issue of computing the robust optimal solution in practice, especially when the decision-making problem is multi-attribute and choice function describes DM's complex preference behaviors. In this project, we tackle such fundamental limitation by a three-unfolded approach. First, we propose a new framework for PRO where the internal and external side information/features of all historical DMs are recorded during the preference elicitation of each DM.
