We develop a new PRO model: Contextual PRO, where those information can be integrated to construct a contextual uncertainty set, to prescribe robust decisions to the DMs. Second, we build an efficient and scalable end-to-end learning framework to train the contextual uncertainty set by accounting for a proper downstream task loss. Finally, we integrate active learning technique into PRO, which enables sequentially querying the "best" pairwise prospects for the DM to label at a time, and achieves the best contextual uncertainty reduction in an online manner. Our proposed approach is tested on two portfolio optimization problems to verify its superiority towards the state-of-art PRO models and algorithms. 在不確定性決策中，決策者（DM）的偏好通常透過選擇函數（如期望效用或風險測度）來表達，該函數會為風險性前景賦予數值。準確識別能真實反映決策者偏好的選擇函數至關重要。例如在投資組合優化中，此舉對提供可靠投資計劃、實現保守性與樂觀回報間更佳平衡具有關鍵作用。實務中，此類選擇函數須透過主觀方式進行偏好提取或預先設定。若錯誤識別選擇函數，可能導致高波動環境下的過度風險承擔，使決策者蒙受極高損失。 偏好魯棒優化（PRO）即為解決上述問題而提出，其針對決策者選擇函數不明確之情境，基於可行選擇函數集合中的最劣情況函數（該集合利用決策者真實偏好的部分已知資訊建構）來尋求魯棒最優投資計劃。現有PRO研究的主要限制在於：偏好提取過程中需決策者標註大量成對比較前景組合，方能使最劣選擇函數逼近真實偏好。此方法因帶給決策者沉重認知負荷，導致PRO在實際應用中面臨推廣阻力。另一方面，當決策問題具多屬性特徵且選擇函數需描述複雜偏好行為時，現行方法亦引發實際計算魯棒最優解的擴展性問題。 本項目透過三管齊下的策略解決上述根本限制：首先提出一種新型的PRO框架，能夠在每位決策者進行偏好提取時記錄其歷史內外部特徵/資訊。據此發展情境化PRO模型，整合多維資訊建構情境化不確定集合，為決策者提供魯棒決策方案。其次建立高效可擴展的端到端學習框架，透過納入適當下游任務損失函數來訓練情境化不確定集合。最後將主動學習技術整合至PRO系統，實現對"最佳"成對前景組合的動態序列化查詢標註，以在線方式達成最優的情境化不確定性削減。 本項目透過兩個投資組合優化問題進行實證檢驗，來體現本項目所提方法相較前沿PRO模型與算法展現顯著優勢。

17211725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211725.value: 基於白盒神經網絡的可解釋深度學習無線感知

17211725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211725.value: Wireless sensing has emerged as a transformative force in machine perception intelligence, revolutionizing applications in healthcare, eldercare, and homecare. Operating in a non-contact, non-intrusive, and privacy-preserving manner, wireless sensing offers unparalleled capabilities to perceive the physical world, even through occlusions and in the dark, promising machine perception capabilities beyond traditional computer vision. Both academia and industry widely recognize wireless sensing as a major evolution for next-generation wireless technologies. Early approaches to wireless sensing primarily relied on signal processing techniques, which were fundamentally constrained by the limited sensing resolutions of Radio Frequency (RF) signals. Recently, deep learning techniques have been employed to overcome these performance limitations. However, current Deep Wireless Sensing (DWS) models often function as black boxes, lacking interpretability and generalizability. This issue hinders practical performance and raises serious trust concerns, especially in critical applications closely integrated with the physical world like healthcare and eldercare. This project aims to transform DWS by introducing mathematically transparent white-box transformers, a recent breakthrough that constructs interpretable neural architectures through the sparse rate reduction principles. We aspire to advance interpretable DWS by developing a complex-valued white-box transformer model tailored for complex RF data, enhancing interpretability and reliability while addressing the limitations of prior black-box models. We will devise the first complex white-box transformer architecture and present a fully complex implementation that supports complex inputs, parameters, and operators. We will further extend it to multi-modality wireless sensing, incorporating various RF signals like Wi-Fi and millimeter-wave signals. To support comprehensive evaluation and foster future research, we will create and open-source a large-scale multi-modality dataset and a suite of baseline models. The outcomes of this research promise to set new standards for practical, reliable, and interpretable deep wireless sensing, benefiting the research community, industries, and society at large. Despite extensive research on wireless sensing using signal processing or deep learning, interpretable DWS based on white-box architectures has been underexplored, with no known prior studies. The PI's recent work at USENIX NSDI 2023 explored a complex-valued neural network for DWS, demonstrating promising results yet still lacking interpretability. This project will build on these efforts to develop mathematically interpretable complex neural networks for DWS, creating a transformative impact on wireless sensing and inspiring new research directions. Our extensive experience in wireless sensing, coupled with strong industry partnerships (e.g., Origin AI, TCL, Huawei, Bosch, etc.), will facilitate the success of this project and ensure practical, reliable solutions for real-world applications. 無線感知作為一種非接觸、非侵入且保護隱私的技術，能在遮擋或黑暗環境下感知物理世界，正廣泛應用於醫療、長者護理與智慧家居，並被視為下一代無線技術的重要方向。傳統方法依賴訊號處理，受限於射頻訊號解析度；近期的深度無線感知（DWS）雖透過深度學習突破性能瓶頸，但多為黑盒模型，缺乏可解釋性與泛化能力，限制了其在關鍵應用中的可信度。 本計劃將引入數學透明的白盒 Transformer，開發首個針對複數射頻資料的全複數白盒架構，支援複數輸入、參數與運算，並擴展至融合 Wi-Fi 與毫米波訊號的多模態無線感知。我們將建立並開源大規模多模態資料集與基線模型，推動可解釋、可靠且實用的 DWS，為學術界與產業界提供新標準並啟發後續研究。

17212025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17212025.value: 動態無線電能傳輸系統中實現超快速最大效率追蹤與最短充電時間的新型方案

17212025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17212025.value: Prof Hui, Ron Shu-Yuen Dr Li, Sinan

17212025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212025.value: Our research project aims to revolutionize the field of wireless charging technology by focusing on enhancing battery charging in dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems. Traditional approaches to WPT often overlook the complexities of battery charging, leading to inefficiencies and inadequate system responses. To overcome these challenges, our project proposes a comprehensive strategy integrating innovative methodologies such as Temperature-Regulated Current Control (TRCC), Zero Phase Angle Control (ZPAC), and Model-Free Control (MFC) for optimized efficiency and reliability in dynamic WPT systems. Our primary goal is to achieve smooth and high-efficiency power output in dynamic WPT systems with a specific emphasis on battery charging. Through advanced battery modeling and the implementation of TRCC for safe and rapid charging at the receiving end, coupled with ZPAC for maximum efficiency at the transmitting end, we aim to streamline the charging process, minimize charging times, and ensure system stability. Additionally, the incorporation of MFC strategies will enhance interference immunity and overall system performance. Key activities in our project include advancements in TRCC methodology, improvements in ZPAC efficiency through detailed control strategies and experimental validations, and the integration of MFC strategies for dynamic WPT systems. We will develop a scaled-down dynamic WPT system for experimental validation, with plans to upscale the system for real-world applications by increasing charging power levels and mobility speed. By bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and practical implementations, our research aims to set new industry standards for efficiency, convenience, and reliability in wireless charging technology. With a focus on enhancing battery charging capabilities in dynamic WPT systems, our project seeks to contribute to the adoption of sustainable energy solutions, particularly in electric vehicle charging applications, and pave the way for a cleaner and more energy-efficient future. 我們的研究項目致力於透過提升動態無線電能傳輸（WPT）系統中的電池充電性能，推動無線充電技術的革新。傳統的無線電能傳輸方法往往忽視了電池充電過程的複雜性，導致系統效率低下且響應不充分。為克服這些難題，本項目提出了一套綜合策略，融合了溫度調節電流控制（TRCC）、零相位角控制（ZPAC）以及無模型控制（MFC）等創新方法，以實現動態無線電能傳輸系統的效率和可靠性優化。 我們的核心目標是在動態無線電能傳輸系統中實現平穩且高效的功率輸出，特別聚焦於電池充電過程的優化。透過先進的電池建模技術及接收端的溫度調節電流控制（TRCC）實現安全快速充電，結合發射端的零相位角控制（ZPAC）以追求最大效率，我們致力於簡化充電流程、縮短充電時間並保障系統穩定性。此外，採用無模型控制（MFC）策略將提升系統的抗干擾能力及整體性能。我們將構建一個縮小版的動態無線電能傳輸系統進行實驗驗證。透過連結理論創新與實際應用，本研究旨在為無線充電技術樹立效率、便捷性和可靠性的行業新標竿。

17212125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17212125.value: 探究溶原噬菌體與質體可移動基因組在抗生素耐藥細菌噬菌體抗性株間差異中的作用

17212125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212125.value: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria, particularly extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant (ESCR) Escherichia coli (E. coli), pose a significant global health threat due to their resistance to conventional antibiotics. Phage therapy, which employs bacteriophages to target and eliminate bacteria, has re-emerged as a promising alternative. However, its effectiveness is often limited by bacterial strain-specific resistance mechanisms mediated by mobile genetic elements, collectively known as the mobilome. Our preliminary studies suggest that variations in the mobilome among closely related bacterial strains may influence their susceptibility to phages, but the specific genetic factors involved remain unclear. Understanding these factors is crucial for developing effective phage therapies and mitigating antibiotic resistance. This research aims to systematic exploration of mobilome diversity and its impact on phage resistance in clinically relevant ESCR E. coli strains. We propose to combine culture-dependent and culture-independent methods to isolate and characterize a diverse collection of phages capable of targeting ESCR E. coli (Task 1). By constructing a genome-resolved phage-host interaction network, we will identify patterns of susceptibility and resistance across different bacterial strains (Task 2). Subsequent genomic and transcriptomic analyses will pinpoint the genetic determinants responsible for phage resistance, focusing on genes associated with prophages and plasmids (Task 3.1). Finally, we will assess the spread and prevalence of these resistance mechanisms across bacterial populations to understand their potential impact on phage therapy effectiveness (Task 3.2). To achieve these objectives, we will first isolate novel phages from environmental samples and induced prophages using our established collection of antibiotic-resistant E. coli strains. These phages will undergo genome sequencing and annotation to uncover their genetic diversity and infection mechanisms. Host-range assays will be performed to construct the phage-host interaction matrix, providing insights into phage susceptibility patterns. Transcriptomic analyses and advanced bioinformatics tools will be employed to analyze bacterial genomes and identify potential genes conferring phage resistance, which will be further functionally validated through gene knockout or overexpression studies. We will then evaluate the distribution and potential dissemination of these mobilome-mediated resistance mechanisms in broader bacterial populations. The expected outcome will provide deeper understanding of the genetic factors influencing phage resistance, which will inform the development of more effective phage therapies and strategies to combat antibiotic-resistant infections. 抗生素耐藥菌，特別是廣譜頭孢菌素耐藥（ESCR）大腸桿菌，因對常用抗生素具高抗性，已成為全球公共衛生威脅。噬菌體療法因其選擇性殺菌的特點而再度受關注。然而，可移動基因組（如溶原噬菌體和質體）帶來的菌株噬菌體抗性，常限制治療成效。我們早前發現，即使親緣相近菌株，其可移動基因組也會影響對噬菌體的敏感性，但具體遺傳因子尚不清楚。釐清這些因子，有助於開發有效噬菌體療法並抑制細菌抗藥性的擴散。 本研究將以系統性的方式探討 ESCR 大腸桿菌可移動基因組的多樣性及其對噬菌體抗性的影響。首先（任務一），採用培養法與非培養法分離並鑑定可感染 ESCR 大腸桿菌的環境裂解型以及誘導型溶原噬菌體。任務二將建立基因組層級的噬菌體-宿主交互作用網絡，以分析不同菌株間的易感與抗性模式。任務三將透過基因組與轉錄組分析，辨識與噬菌體抗性相關的溶原噬菌體與質體基因；最後評估這些抗性機制在更廣泛細菌族群中的分布及傳播潛能，以了解其可能影響噬菌體療法成效的層面。 具體而言， 我們將從耐藥大腸桿菌菌株庫中獲得新噬菌體，進行全基因體測序、註解與宿主範圍測試，以建立噬菌體和宿主交互矩陣。接著會用轉錄體分析和生物資訊工具篩選抗性基因，並透過基因剔除或過表驗證功能。最後，我們將評估這些抗性機制在資料庫中的分布及其水平傳播潛力。本研究有望促進對噬菌體抗性基因的理解，並為噬菌體療法與抗藥性感染防治提供新策略。

17212725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17212725.value: 一種新穎的區塊鏈智能合約和零知識證明方法，用於準確、安全地存取多利益相關者協作的建築資訊模型

17212725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17212725.value: Prof Lu, Weisheng Wilson Prof Xue, Fan

17212725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212725.value: This project focuses on implementing a novel blockchain smart contract and zero-knowledge proof (BSC-ZKP) model for accurate and secure access to building information models (BIM) for multi-stakeholder collaboration. BIM is a significant industry within architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO), valued at billions of dollars, and mandated in regions like Hong Kong. However, a challenge arises from the disparity between the intricate nature of multi-stakeholder collaboration in BIM and the insecure and simplistic information access methods commonly employed. The conventional federated BIM access approach may not adequately meet the diverse and secure information requirements of collaborating stakeholders. Addressing this issue by refining information access methods tailored to individual project participants’ roles and responsibilities can be intricate and present usability challenges. To tackle this dilemma, the project proposes a novel BSC-ZKP approach. The theoretical innovation of this project lies in the BSC-ZKP model for BIM, where BIM operation records are securely stored in blockchain-based knowledge hubs. This model enables the selection and conversion of historical BIM operation records into knowledge statements, which are further transformed into computational statements and self-executing ZKP logic. By generating proof questions and verifying answers, the BSC-ZKP model facilitates accurate and secure information access to BIM based on project participants’ roles and obligations. A preliminary small-scale pilot study has validated the technological feasibility of the BSC-ZKP model. Researching the BSC is essential for evolving the ZKP model into BSC-ZKP for accurate and secure access to BIM. Leveraging the advanced algorithms of BSC-ZKP offers stakeholders applications such as tailored information access in BIM, user identity verification, and intellectual property protection in multi-stakeholder collaboration. Additionally, seamless interfaces are being developed to integrate BSC-ZKP into mainstream BIM platforms, aiming to apply and assess its effectiveness across various scales and types of construction projects. The primary outcome of this project will be the BSC-ZKP model, a novel, automated, efficient, and cost-effective approach for accurate and secure access to BIM to support multi-stakeholder collaboration. The research results will contribute to expanding the knowledge frontier in accurate and secure information access within the BIM domain. The potential impact of BSC-ZKP extends to enhancing existing BIM practices without disruption, aligning with local government mandates on BIM usage, secure user identity verification, and intellectual property protection. Furthermore, the research outcomes may have implications for engineering informatics, construction management, smart cities, and distributed user management within the evolving landscape of new quality productive forces. 本計畫旨在實施一種新穎的區塊鏈智能合約與零知識證明（BSC-ZKP）模型，以實現精確安全的建築資訊模型（BIM）存取，支持多利益相關方協作。BIM是建築、工程、施工與運營（AECO）領域的重要產業，市值達數十億美元，且在香港等地區已被強制推行。然而，當前BIM多利益相關方協作的複雜性與普遍採用的不安全、過於簡化的資訊存取方法之間存在矛盾。傳統的聯邦式BIM存取方式可能無法充分滿足協作方多樣化且安全的資訊需求。針對此問題，通過精細化調整適應各項目參與者角色與職責的資訊存取方法可能極為複雜，並帶來可用性挑戰。為解決此困境，本計畫提出創新的BSC-ZKP方法。 本計畫的理論創新在於針對BIM設計的BSC-ZKP模型，該模型將BIM操作記錄安全存儲於基於區塊鏈的知識樞紐中。此模型能夠選擇並轉換歷史BIM操作記錄為知識陳述，進一步轉化為計算陳述與自我執行的ZKP邏輯。通過生成驗證問題並核對答案，BSC-ZKP模型能根據項目參與者的角色與義務，實現精確安全的BIM資訊存取。一項初步小規模試驗研究已驗證BSC-ZKP模型的技術可行性。 研究BSC對於將ZKP模型演化為BSC-ZKP以實現精確安全的BIM存取至關重要。利用BSC-ZKP的先進算法，可為利益相關方提供多種應用，包括BIM中的定制化資訊存取、用戶身份驗證及多邊協作中的知識產權保護。此外，本研究正在開發無縫接口，以將BSC-ZKP整合至主流BIM平台，目標是在不同規模與類型的建設項目中應用並評估其效能。 本計畫的主要成果將是BSC-ZKP模型——一種新穎、自動化、高效且具成本效益的方法，用於實現精確安全的BIM存取以支持多利益相關方協作。研究成果將有助拓展BIM領域內精確安全資訊存取的知識邊界。BSC-ZKP的潛在影響包括無縫增強現有BIM實踐、符合地方政府對BIM使用的強制要求、實現安全的用戶身份驗證與知識產權保護。此外，研究成果可能對工程信息學、建設管理、智慧城市及不斷演進的新質生產力背景下的分布式用戶管理產生深遠影響。

17212825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17212825.value: 用微生物組絕對定量方法研究廢水處理過程中硝化菌群的作用

17212825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212825.value: Nitrification process plays a pivotal role in removing nitrogen compounds in biological wastewater treatment systems. Key guilds of nitrifiers, including ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA), and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB), as well as the newly discovered complete ammonia oxidation (comammox) bacteria, are responsible for the oxidation of ammonia to nitrate. Current research on the nitrification process is devoted to several key areas, including the distribution and diversity of nitrifiers and their responses to environmental stresses. Despite these efforts, there remains significant interest among researchers and engineers in determining the abundance, growth rate, and nitrification rate of nitrifiers, particularly their absolute cell numbers, absolute growth rate, cell-level nitrification rate, and contributions in specific ecosystems. The foundation for achieving these goals lies in accurate microbial quantification. Among the currently popular approaches, DNA-based methods, particularly 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic sequencing, are efficient but typically provide only relative abundance, making the determination of absolute cell numbers challenging. Nevertheless, qPCR is recognized as a method capable of achieving absolute quantification. However, it does not consider DNA extraction efficiency, and extracting DNA from complex samples rarely yields complete recovery. The concept of absolute quantification opens new possibilities for microbial analysis. Specifically, the spike-in-based absolute quantification method involves adding control microbes to the sample before DNA extraction, followed by the DNA extraction and sequencing steps. By comparing the ratio of spike-in strains in sequencing data and sample, a scaling factor will be obtained to determine the absolute numbers of target populations in a sample. Additionally, unique molecular identifiers (UMIs), a type of molecular barcoding, help correct amplification biases and increase sequencing accuracy. Combining full-length 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with the spike-in approach allows for absolute quantification while reducing amplification biases and improving resolution. The objectives of this project are: 1) to select and evaluate candidate spike-in microbes, and design and evaluate the UMI-tagged primers; 2) to absolutely quantify the nitrifiers in Hong Kong activated sludge (AS) using spike-in-based metagenomic sequencing and UMI-tagged full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing; 3) to measure the absolute growth rate and nitrification rate of nitrifiers under different conditions in lab-scale reactors, and to determine the contribution of various nitrifiers simultaneously; 4) to conduct a longitudinal exploration of the nitrification rate and transcription correspondence in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs); 5) to advise guidance for treatment process improvement and enhancement of current nitrification process-related models based on the acquired data. 硝化過程在廢水生物處理系統中對去除氮化合物具有核心作用。關鍵的硝化功能菌群，包括氨氧化細菌(AOB)、氨氧化古菌(AOA)、亞硝酸鹽氧化細菌(NOB)，以及新發現的全程氨氧化細菌(comammox)，負責將氨氧化為硝酸鹽。當前硝化過程的研究主要聚焦於以下關鍵領域，包括硝化菌的分布、多樣性及其對環境脅迫的響應。除上述研究外，科研人員和工程師們對精確測定硝化菌的豐度、生長速率和硝化速率仍抱有濃厚興趣，尤其是其在特定生態系統中的絕對細胞數量、絕對生長速率、細胞水平硝化速率及其貢獻。 實現這些目標的基礎在於精確的微生物定量。當前主流方法中，基於DNA的分子定量技術，特別是16S rRNA基因測序和宏基因組測序，雖然高效，但通常僅能提供相對豐度，導致絕對細胞數量的確定面臨挑戰。儘管qPCR被視作一種可實現絕對定量的方法，但該方法未考慮DNA提取效率，且複雜樣品中的DNA提取往往難以實現完全回收。 絕對定量的概念為微生物分析提供了新的可能性。基於摻入內標(spike-in)的絕對定量方法，在DNA提取前向樣品中添加已知數量的內標微生物，隨後進行DNA提取和測序。通過分析測序數據中內標菌株與添加到樣品中內標菌株的數量，獲得校正比例因子，繼而用以確定樣本中目標微生物群的絕對數量。此外，獨特分子標識符(UMIs)作為一種分子條形碼技術，有助於校正擴增偏差並提高測序準確性。將全長16S rRNA基因擴增子測序與內標法相結合，可在減少擴增偏差並提高分辨率的同時，實現絕對定量分析。 該項目的目標是：1）篩選和評估候選的內標微生物，並設計和評估UMI標記引物；2）應用基於內標法的宏基因組測序和UMI標記的全長16S rRNA基因測序技術，實現香港廢水處理廠活性污泥中硝化菌的絕對定量；3）基於實驗室規模反應器，測定不同條件下硝化菌的絕對生長速率和硝化速率，並同步評估各類硝化菌的貢獻；4）探究廢水處理廠中硝化速率與轉錄活性的對應關系; 5） 根據獲取的數據，為處理工藝改進和增強當前硝化工藝相關模型提供指導。

17212925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17212925.value: 模塊化集成施工方法對高層住宅建築運行能耗的影響：多學科研究

17212925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212925.value: Residential buildings are a major category of buildings that significantly contribute to overall global energy consumption. Because of the scarcity of land resources in Hong Kong, many residential buildings are high-rises. Emerging Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) technology is being vigorously promoted due to many benefits in terms of the construction period, cost, sustainability, and beyond, but their potential disparities in operational energy consumption compared with conventional in-situ methods remain unclear. Our preliminary investigations suggest that MiC structures may manifest notable variations in wall thickness, airtightness, and thermal bridging at junctions compared with conventional buildings, potentially resulting in distinct operational energy consumption characteristics. Nevertheless, this conjecture awaits comprehensive validation. In this proposed project, we aim to contribute novel insights into the impact of adopting MiC in high-rise residential buildings on their operational energy performance, compared to conventional in-situ construction methods through a multidisciplinary investigation encompassing the field of structural materials, envelope heat transfer, computational algorithms, and human behaviour studies. The key factors influencing energy consumption in MiC high-rise residential buildings will be identified and quantified. The mechanisms through which modular construction methods impact operational energy consumption will be explored by elucidating the similarities and disparities in energy consumption between MiC and conventional in-situ buildings. To this end, two high-rise residential buildings (one conventional cast-in-situ and one concrete MiC) in Hong Kong will be used as references and one steel MiC high-rise residential building will be used for validation. The proposed project will have three key objectives: 1) identify the key factors that affects the operational energy performance of MiC buildings using a developed systematic framework; 2) quantify the multi-source heterogeneous factors using innovative tailored quantification methods; and 3) provide a hybrid grey operational energy performance prediction model for MiC high-rise residential buildings. The proposed project will unfold over a 36-month period through three interconnected work packages to achieve three objectives. Theoretically, the proposed study will contribute to an enhanced understanding of the operational energy performance of MiC high-rise residential buildings. Practically, it will offer guidance to assess the energy use in MiC residential buildings and lay the foundation for effective energy savings in MiC buildings in the future. The project team, led by two experienced investigators with expertise in building energy assessment and the MiC method, will collaborate with two major clients involved with the target MiC buildings for onsite investigation, and two energy consulting firms for practical technology transfer. 住宅建築是建築的主要類別之一，對全球整體能源消耗具有重大影響。在香港，由於土地資源稀缺，許多住宅建築為高層建築。新興的模塊化集成建築（MiC）技術因其工期、成本、可持續性等多方面的優勢而得到大力推廣，但其與傳統現場施工方法相比在運行能耗方面的潛在差異尚不清楚。我們的初步研究表明，與傳統建築相比，MiC結構在牆體厚度、氣密性和連接處的熱橋接方面可能存在顯著差異，這可能導致其具有獨特的運行能耗特征。然而，這一推測仍有待全面驗證。 在本項目中，我們旨在通過多學科研究，為高層住宅建築採用MiC施工方法相較於傳統現澆施工方法對其運行能源性能的影響提供新見解。該多學科研究包括現場調查、因子分析、圖像處理、機器學習和全面的整棟建築能源模擬，以識別和量化影響模塊化建築高層住宅能耗的關鍵因素。通過闡明模塊化建築與傳統現澆建築在能耗方面的相似性和差異性，我們將探索模塊化施工方法影響運行能耗的機制。為此，我們將香港的兩棟高層住宅建築（一棟傳統現澆建築和一棟混凝土模塊化建築）作為參考。本項目有三個關鍵目標：1）使用開發的系統框架識別影響模塊化建築運行能源性能的關鍵因素；2）使用創新的綜合量化方法量化多源異構因素；3）為模塊化建築高層住宅提供一種混合灰色運行能源性能預測方法。 本項目將在36個月內展開，通過三個相互關聯的工作包逐步推進，以實現上述目標。從理論角度來看，本研究將有助於增進對MiC高層住宅建築運行能源性能的理解。從實踐角度來看，它將為評估MiC住宅建築的能源使用提供指導，並為未來MiC建築的有效節能奠定基礎。項目團隊包括兩名在建築能源評估和MiC方法方面擁有豐富經驗的研究人員。本項目將得到兩個政府機構、一個參與目標MiC建築的主要客戶以及兩家能源諮詢公司的支持。

17213025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17213025.value: 單模氮化鎵微盤雷射的相干性研究

17213025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17213025.value: The microdisk laser is a promising competitor to the current generation of laser diodes, owning to its compact dimensions, high quality lasing and simplicity of manufacturing. Nevertheless, its potentials have been hindered by various stumbling blocks that degrades optical confinement within the cavity or the overlap of modes with the gain region in the laser cavity. In this project, a solution is proposed that deals with all these issues simultaneously, with a envisioned outcome of an electroluminescent microdisk laser with single-mode emission, low lasing threshold and high quality factor. The laser structure adopts the thin-film architecture proposed in our group that ensures that whispering-gallery modes overlap optimally with the gain region, which the integration of a wavelength-selective Bragg reflector that minimizes optical losses for maximal optical confinement of the first-order whispering-gallery mode whilst promoting leakage of high-order modes for single-mode emission. The development of two novel current injection schemes for the thin-film devices enable electroluminescent operation of the lasers. The coherent nature of the laser emission will be verified through coherence length measurements and second-order correlation measurements. The outstanding features of this laser, including compactness, high Q factor, low threshold and wafer-scale fabrication make it an ideal candidate for photonic chip generation and other next-generation photonic integration applications. 微盤雷射因其緊湊的尺寸、高品質的出射雷射以及簡單的製造工藝，有望成為當前雷射二極體的有力競爭者。然而，其潛力一直受到各種技術障礙的限制，導致光腔內的光學限制減弱，以及腔中模式與增益區域的重疊減少。 本計畫提出了一種同時解決上述問題的實驗方案，以實現具有低激射閾值和高Q值的單模微盤雷射。該雷射器採用薄膜結構，確保回音壁模式與增益區域達到最佳重疊；同時整合嵌入了針對激射波長的分佈式布拉格反射鏡，有效地減少光學損耗，最大限度地增強了對一階回音壁模式的光學約束，並促進高階模式的光洩漏，從而實現雷射器單模發射。 我們為此薄膜微盤裝置開發了兩種新型電流注入方案，使雷射器能夠正常實現電致發光。激射雷射的相干特性將透過相干長度測量和二階相關性測量得到驗證。此雷射器的緊湊結構、高Q值、低閾值以及可晶圓級製造等突出優點，使其成為光子晶片製造和下一代整合光子技術發展的重要推動力。

17213325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17213325.value: 基於代謝互作建模深化微生物合成群落研究

17213325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17213325.value: Humans depend on myriads of services offered by complex microbial communities in various applied settings of engineered systems. Maximizing the desired functions of microbial communities involve the engineering practice of identifying optimal operating conditions through extensive experimental assays and the fine-tuning the assembly of microbial synthetic communities (SynComs). This study is proposed to develop the metabolic interaction model-guided SynComs, integrating of genome-scale mathematical modeling, high-throughput experimental assays with microbial strains and machine learning (ML) algorithms. The use of SynComs is to introduce desirable phenotypes by modifying inherent microbial communities, providing a pathway to manage the vast diversity and complex interactions of microbes in engineered ecosystems, ultimately enhancing our control over microbe-mediated systems and their tolerance to various (a)biotic stress factors. Primary challenges in designing SynComs include selecting candidates that mirror the functional characteristics of the target microbiome and rectifying biases in quantifying cell concentrations of SynComs members via the high-throughput sequencing approach. Regarding SynComs application, additionally issues such as addressing cell loss due to inconsistent inoculation efficiencies caused by varying growth rates, and predicting potential interactions that go beyond our current knowledge through modeling, will be encountered. So far, only a few pioneering works have introduced singular desired microorganism for the bioaugmentation or bioremediation purposes in contaminated soil, activated sludge, groundwater, and so on. Moreover, there have been no attempts to work on SynComs with diverse metabolically interactive species, particularly in combination with computational genomic analyses and experimental assays. This project is proposed i) to develop a viability-metagenomics absolute quantification and profile tempospatial variations of functional significance microbes; ii) to predict dynamics and identify "tipping points" as indicators of changes in microbial interactions using the dynamic multispecies metabolic model (DMMM); iii) to compare and generate measured values through experimental assays; iv) to investigate mechanisms of microbial interaction in regulating metabolic pathways by combining chemical analyses with multi-omics approach; v) to formulate a stacked model that integrates our biological knowledge-based model (i.e., DMMM) with a machine learning (ML) algorithms. The deliverables of this project are expected to expedite the use of SynComs as powerful tools in microbial ecology research, and in the fine-tuned control of microbe-mediated technologies. 在眾多工程系統中，微生物群落通過執行多種功能服務於人類。為實現工程系統功能的最大化，需通過大規模實驗分析確定系統最佳運行條件，或通過組裝特定功能微生物構建合成微生物群落，以實現對系統的精細調控。合成微生物群落的核心價值在於通過引入理想微生物表型定向改造系統內微生物群落，進而增強對微生物介導工程系統的控制能力，並提高其對各種（非）生物脅迫因子的耐受性。本研究旨在以微生物代謝互作模型為指導，整合基因組學、數學建模、微生物菌株高通量實驗分析及機器學習算法，推動合成微生物群落的研究及應用。設計與應用合成微生物群落面臨的主要挑戰包括：篩選符合目標微生物組功能特徵的理想菌株，以及矯正採用高通量測序技術對群落微生物細胞濃度進行定量的偏差。此外，在合成群落的應用過程中，還需解決諸如因生長速率差異導致接種效率不一致而引發的細胞損失問題，以及通過數學建模預測超出當前知識範疇的潛在微生物互作等問題。迄今為止，僅有少數先驅性研究在污染土壤、活性污泥、地下水等場景中引入單一目標微生物，用於生物強化或生物修復研究。此外，尚未有研究針對具有多樣代謝互作物種的合成微生物群落展開系統探索，尤其是結合計算基因組學分析與實驗檢測的研究。本項目計劃開展以下工作：（1）開發宏基因組絕對定量方法，並揭示功能相關微生物的時空動態變化特徵；（2）利用動態多物種代謝模型（dynamic multispecies metabolic model, DMMM）預測微生物互作及動態變化規律，並識別標誌微生物互作變化的“臨界點”；（3）通過實驗分析對預測值進行驗證與比較；（4）結合化學分析與多組學方法，探究微生物互作在調控代謝途徑中的機制；（5）構建堆疊模型，研發整合基於生物學知識的模型（DMMM）與機器學習的創新算法。本項目的研究成果將推動合成微生物群落作為強大工具在微生物生態學研究及微生物介導系統中的應用。

17213525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17213525.value: Type inference is crucial in modern programming languages, enabling developers to write code with minimal explicit type annotations while benefiting from strong static typing. Local type inference, as proposed by Pierce and Turner, combines bidirectional typing with local argument synthesis to handle implicit polymorphism. This technique is widely adopted in languages like Java, C#, Scala, and TypeScript. Local type inference is favoured in mainstream languages for its simplicity, ease of error localisation, and scalability to advanced type system features. It allows developers to intuitively understand and predict type behavior, leading to quicker error identification and precise error messages. In contrast, global type inference techniques, such as those based on the Hindley-Milner type system, face challenges with complexity, scalability, and handling features like type overloading, intersection and union types, and subtyping. These challenges often prevent scaling global type inference techniques to languages with advanced type system features. Despite its widespread use, local type inference has seen little development since Pierce and Turner's proposal, unlike the extensively developed Hindley-Milner-based approaches. This stagnation may be due to its relatively complex specification, which lacks the theoretical elegance of Hindley-Milner type systems. Additionally, many implementations must address type system features not covered in the original work, leading to ad-hoc solutions and inconsistencies. Another limitation is its reliance on bidirectional typing, which cannot effectively exploit partially known type information, reducing flexibility and expressiveness. To address these issues, we propose replacing bidirectional typing with contextual typing, a recently proposed generalisation of bidirectional typing. Unlike bidirectional typing, contextual typing can exploit partially known type information during type inference. Contextual typing propagates both type information and other contextual information, such as terms or record labels, during the type-checking process. However, contextual typing, does not yet address polymorphism. The novelty of this proposal lies in integrating contextual typing with implicit polymorphism and local type argument synthesis. This combination forms a new approach called local contextual type inference, providing a powerful, predictable, and scalable technique for polymorphic type inference with subtyping. The project will be divided into three main objectives: (1) explore the combination of contextual typing and local argument synthesis to establish the foundations for local contextual type inference; (2) develop a novel technique for function inference that is local, addressing a key limitation of local type inference; and (3) study the integration of subtyping with local contextual type inference, aiming at handling advanced type features in modern programming languages. 在現代程式語言中，類型推斷至關重要，使開發者能在保有強型別靜態檢查的同時，減少明確類型註解的負擔。Pierce 和 Turner 所提出的局部類型推斷結合了雙向類型檢查與局部參數合成，有效支援隱式多型性。此技術已廣泛應用於 Java、C#、Scala 和 TypeScript 等語言，因其簡潔性、錯誤定位能力強，以及對進階類型系統特性的良好擴展性而備受青睞。 然而，基於 Hindley-Milner 類型系統的全域類型推斷方法在處理複雜類型特性（如類型重載、交集與聯集類型、子型等）時面臨可擴展性與複雜性挑戰，難以適用於現代語言。 儘管局部類型推斷在業界廣泛使用，其理論發展卻相對滯後，部分原因在於其規範較為複雜，缺乏 Hindley-Milner 類型系統的理論優雅性。此外，現有實作常需處理原始規範未涵蓋的類型特性，導致出現不一致的臨時解決方案。雙向類型檢查也存在限制，無法充分利用部分已知的類型資訊，降低了靈活性與表達能力。 為解決上述問題，本文提出以上下文類型檢查（contextual typing）取代雙向類型檢查。上下文類型檢查是一種近期提出的更通用的類型推斷方法，不僅能傳遞類型資訊，還能在類型檢查過程中傳遞術語、記錄標籤等上下文資訊。雖然目前的上下文類型檢查尚未涵蓋多型性，本文創新地將其與隱式多型性及局部類型參數合成結合，形成一種新技術——上下文局部類型推斷（local contextual type inference）。 我們引入「量化類型賦值系統」（Quantitative Type Assignment System, QTAS），以計數器形式追蹤上下文資訊，從而簡化並精確地規範類型推斷過程。此方法避免傳統的統一（unification）機制，改採更易處理的匹配問題，顯著提升了對子型的支援能力。 本研究分為三個主要目標：（1）探索上下文類型檢查與局部參數合成的結合，奠定上下文局部類型推斷的基礎；（2）開發一種新的局部函數推斷技術，解決現有方法的關鍵限制；（3）研究子型與上下文局部類型推斷的整合，構建一種既能處理多型性又能支援進階類型特性的強大推斷機制。

17213825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17213825.value: 具備幾何感知和物理基礎的動態 3D 場景建模、理解與交互

17213825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17213825.value: The emergence of advanced generative AI models like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion marks significant advancements in artificial intelligence. While excelling in text, image, and video generation, these models often fail to adhere to the principles of geometry and physics that govern our three-dimensional world. Humans perceive and interact with their environment based on spatial information, which is integral to our understanding and action. Therefore, accurately mirroring geometric and physical principles from the real world into the virtual one is key to bridging the gaps between reality and virtuality, humans and AI. This project aims to achieve geometry-aware and physics-grounded dynamic 3D scene modeling, understanding, and interaction for spatial intelligence. Our first objective is to achieve geometry-aware and physics-grounded dynamic 3D scene-level modeling. While recent state-of-the-art methods have made strides in object-level modeling, scene-level modeling remains a significant challenge, with the gap between object-level and scene-level modeling substantial. Existing models struggle to adhere to the fundamental principles of geometry and physics. We aim to advance realistic dynamic scene-level modeling to close this gap. Additionally, we aim to develop spatial-aware scene representations suitable for a myriad of downstream tasks. Existing representations for 3D understanding fail to provide a comprehensive understanding of scenes vital for effectively linking with different modalities and foundation models. Our goal is to create spatial-aware representations that encapsulate scene semantics, physical attributes, scene concept graphs, etc., enabling seamless integration with foundation models for versatile applications without retraining. Furthermore, we address the crucial challenge of interaction from two perspectives: (1) user-friendly interactive editing and (2) interactions between entities in the scene. User-friendly interactive scene editing is a core demand for 3D modeling, particularly for practitioners and artists, while existing methods offer limited user control over even object-level editing, let alone scene-level editing. Modeling realistic interactions between entities remains under-explored, which is important for realistic dynamic science modeling. By achieving our three key objectives, we aim to advance spatial intelligence and lay the groundwork for future world models that adhere to classical geometry and physical laws. Ultimately, our goal is to seamlessly connect the virtual and physical worlds, facilitating interactions between humans and the virtual world, and between machines and the physical world, enabling machines to engage not only with each other but also with humans and the dynamic 3D physical environment, fostering a new era of integrated and intuitive interactions across digital and physical spaces. ChatGPT 和 Stable Diffusion 等先進生成式人工智慧模型的出現，標誌著人工智慧領域的重大進步。儘管這些模型在文本、圖像和視頻生成方面表現出色，但它們往往無法遵循支配我們三維世界的幾何和物理原理。人類基於空間信息感知環境並與之交互，而空間信息是我們理解和行動的核心。因此，將現實世界中的幾何和物理原理準確映射到虛擬世界，是彌合現實與虛擬、人類與人工智慧之間差距的關鍵。本項目旨在實現具有幾何感知和物理基礎的動態 3D 場景建模、理解與交互，以發展空間智能。我們的首要目標是實現具備幾何感知和物理基礎的動態 3D 場景級建模。儘管近年來最先進的方法在對象級建模方面取得了進展，但場景級建模仍是一項重大挑戰，對象級與場景級建模之間存在顯著差距。現有模型難以遵循基本的幾何和物理原理。我們致力於推進逼真的動態場景級建模，以縮小這一差距。此外，我們旨在開發適用於多種下游任務的空間感知場景表徵。現有的 3D 理解表徵無法提供對場景的全面理解，而這種全面理解對於有效連接不同模態和基礎模型至關重要。我們的目標是創建包含場景語義、物理屬性、場景概念圖等信息的空間感知表徵，無需重新訓練即可與基礎模型無縫集成，從而實現多用途應用。再者，我們從兩個角度解決交互這一關鍵挑戰：（1）用戶友好的交互式編輯；（2）場景中實體間的交互。用戶友好的交互式場景編輯是 3D 建模的核心需求，尤其是對從業者和藝術家而言，但現有方法即便在對象級編輯中也只能提供有限的用戶控制，更不用說場景級編輯了。對實體間逼真交互的建模仍有待深入探索，而這對於逼真的動態科學建模而言至關重要。通過實現這三個關鍵目標，我們旨在推動空間智能的發展，並為未來遵循經典幾何和物理定律的世界模型奠定基礎。最終，我們的目標是無縫連接虛擬世界與物理世界，促進人類與虛擬世界、機器與物理世界之間的交互，使機器不僅能夠彼此交互，還能與人類及動態 3D 物理環境交互，從而開啟數字空間與物理空間融合且直觀交互的新時代。

17213925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17213925.value: 通過點雲矢量化實現整體四維場景理解

17213925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17213925.value: Nowadays, 3D hardware equipment like Lidar sensors (e.g., Apple Vision Pro and iPhone, Waymo Autonomous Vehicle) and depth devices (e.g., Microsoft Kinect, Meta AR Glass Aria, Intel RealSense) are becoming more affordable and accessible to humans in our daily lives, which generate massive amounts of 3D (point clouds) and 4D (point cloud videos) data every day, resulting in urgent demand for data processing, analyzing, and understanding. Modern scene understanding systems have achieved impressive results on standard benchmarks, which can precisely localize and recognize objects and humans in both images and videos. However, our real world is not 2D and the current vision systems are constrained by their inability to fully capture the vital geometric and dynamic information of the real world, which is intrinsically 4D. 4D scene understanding is quite important as it depicts not only scene semantics and functionalities, but also scene geometries and dynamics, which can provide a more comprehensive and holistic understanding of the surrounding environment. It is underexplored and challenging, due to difficulties in various aspects like irregular scene geometries, diversified scene dynamics, inadequate scene semantics, and unstudied scene functionalities. To tackle these challenges, this project aims to go beyond traditional image and video understanding frameworks and focuses on developing a holistic 4D scene understanding system that can perceive and reason complex entities and adapt to continuously changing environments. This project has the potential to be transformative for various applications in vision, graphics, and robotics, including autonomous driving, intelligent robots, augmented reality, smart healthcare, etc. This project breaks down the task into four tightly connected thrusts. First, we aim to model scene geometries and propose a new point cloud representation named vectorization, which can transform unstructured point clouds into structured vectors for efficient and effective modeling. Second, we target capturing scene dynamics and introduce vectorized cooperative learning, which consists of mutual enhancement and combinatorial optimization strategies. Third, we intend to enhance scene semantics and present vectorized learning on massive heterogeneous data, including vectorized multimodal contrastive learning, self-supervised learning, and generative perception learning. Finally, we focus on exploring scene functionalities and suggest vectorized representation alignment with discriminative and generative modeling and chain-of-thought reasoning. With our solid foundation, strong capability, and encouraging preliminary results, the developed algorithms will be rigorously evaluated on standard benchmarks and in real-world scenarios, and the outcome will advance the frontiers of 4D scene understanding and produce broad impacts in many aspects. 如今，三維硬件設備如激光雷達傳感器（如Apple Vision Pro和iPhone、Waymo自動駕駛汽車）和深度設備（例如Microsoft Kinect、Meta AR Glass Aria和Intel RealSense），在日常生活中變得越來越經濟實惠且觸手可及。這些設備每天產生大量的三維（點雲）和四維（點雲視頻）數據，導致對數據處理、分析和理解的迫切需求。現代場景理解系統在標準基準測試中取得了令人印象深刻的成果，能夠在圖像和視頻中精確定位和識別物體與人類。然而，我們的現實世界並非二維的，現有的視覺系統受到限制，無法完全捕捉現實世界中至關重要的幾何和動態信息，而這些信息本質上是四維的。四維場景理解非常重要，因為它不僅描繪場景的語義和功能，還包括場景的幾何結構和動態變化，從而提供對週圍環境更全面、整體的理解。由於不規則的場景幾何、多樣的場景動態、有限的場景語義以及未研究的場景功能等各種難題，四維場景理解仍然處於探索的初期，具有很大的挑戰性。為應對這些挑戰，本項目旨在超越傳統的圖像和視頻理解框架，開發一個全面的四維場景理解系統，能夠感知和推理複雜的實體，並適應不斷變化的環境。該項目有望在視覺、圖形學和機器人等多個領域實現變革，包括自動駕駛、智能機器人、增強現實、智慧醫療等。本項目將任務細分為四個緊密關聯的方向。首先，我們旨在建模場景幾何結構，提出一種新的點雲表示方法矢量化，它可以將非結構化的點雲轉換為結構化的矢量，從而實現高效且有效的建模。第二，我們目標是捕捉場景動態，引入矢量化協作學習，包括相互增強和組合優化策略。第三，我們希望提升場景語義，提出在大規模異構數據上進行矢量化學習的方法，包括矢量化的多模態對比學習、自監督學習和生成式感知學習。最後，我們專注於場景功能的探索，通過將矢量化表示與判別式和生成式模型以及鏈式推理相結合，以實現功能對齊。憑藉堅實的基礎、強大的能力和初步取得的積極成果，所開發的算法將通過標準基準和實際場景進行嚴格評估，推動四維場景理解的前沿發展，並在多個方面產生廣泛影響。

17214625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17214625.value: 應變、扭曲與對稱性：形變工程的基石

17214625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17214625.value: Deformation engineering DE (including elastic and inelastic strain engineering) employs deformation (includes reversible or permanent strains, such as twisting multilayered layered 2D materials or altering stacking sequences) to tailor material (e.g., mechanical, phononic, thermal, electronic, photonic, piezoelectric, ferroelectric, magnetic, spintronic, superconducting, thermoelectric, catalytic) properties, representing an alternative to conventional methods like alloying, microstructure manipulation, phase engineering, and defect engineering. With the realization of large elastic strains made possible by advances in ultra-strength and/or reduced dimension materials, DE can continuously and reversibly modulate physical properties. Originating from foundational elasticity theories and the observation of piezoelectricity in the early 19th century, DE has evolved through a series of developments including strained silicon for faster transistors, strained-layer superlattices, and the emergence of twistronics/straintronics in 2D materials. Today, DE drives advancements across semiconductors, flexible electronics, superconductivity, energy storage, sensors, and quantum computing, heralding a new era of customizable material properties. At its core, DE exploits the influence of (elastic and inelastic) deformations on atomic bonding and electronic structure. Deformation-induced crystal symmetry alterations modify fundamental material behavior; e.g., symmetry breaking profoundly alters electronic band structure, phonon dispersion, second (and higher) harmonic generation, .... Large macroscopic strains and defects can produce significant non-affine deformations through atomic relaxation, deviating from Cauchy-Born kinematics, especially at the verge of material stability in ultra-strength materials. Non-affine displacements and thermal fluctuations may dominate deformation response. Further, inhomogeneous strains offer an additional dimension to property tuning. The core objective of this project from a theoretical standpoint is to construct a framework that elucidates and reconciles the intricate coupling between internal relaxations, homogeneous/inhomogeneous strain fields, symmetry evolution under applied macroscopic deformation and their implications for physical (including electronic and photonic) properties. This is essential for fully harnessing the potential of DE. On an application level, we will develop a systematic and predictive framework to optimize deformation within the high-dimensional strain/twist/stacking/translation space, limited by material instability and marked by symmetry modification and internal relaxation processes under homogeneous and inhomogeneous deformation to robustly tune bulk, thin film and 2D materials. Our approach builds on group-theoretic methods to investigate crystal symmetry transitions to subgroups under the application of specific deformation. This will be followed by a continuum/statistical mechanics-based analysis of atomic displacements/relaxations due to homogeneous and inhomogeneous macroscopic deformation. Further we employ the principles of material stability to delineate achievable deformations. This deformation response will be correlated with electronic structure and material properties using first-principles methods. 形變工程（Deformation Engineering, DE）（包括彈性和非彈性應變工程）通過施加形變來精確調控材料的性能（例如：力學、聲子、熱學、電子、光子、壓電、鐵電、磁性、自旋電子學、超導、熱電、催化性能），是替代合金化、微觀結構調控、相變工程和缺陷工程等傳統方法的新途徑。隨著高強度材料和低維材料領域的進步，使得實現大彈性應變的施加成為可能，形變工程得以連續、可逆地調控材料的物理性質。形變工程起源於19世紀初的基礎彈性理論和壓電現象的發現，歷經一系列發展並不斷演進，包括用於製造高性能晶體管的矽應變技術、應變超晶格層，以及二維材料中扭曲電子學/應變電子學（twistronics/straintronics）的興起。如今，形變工程正驅動著半導體、柔性電子學、超導、儲能、傳感器和量子計算等領域的進步，預示著材料性能可定制化的新時代。 形變工程的核心在於利用彈性或非彈性形變對材料中原子成鍵行為與電子結構的影響。形變誘導的晶體對稱性改變會調節材料的基本性質；例如，對稱性破缺會深刻改變電子能帶結構、聲子色散關係、二次（及更高次）諧波產生等。大的宏觀應變和缺陷可通過原子弛豫產生顯著的非仿射變形，偏離柯西-波恩運動學假設，尤其是在接近超強材料穩定性極限時；此時，非仿射位移和熱漲落可能主導變形響應。此外，非均勻應變為性能調控提供了額外的維度。 本項目在理論層面的核心目標是構建可闡明並協調以下因素之間的複雜耦合關係的科學框架：內部弛豫、均勻/非均勻應變場、外加宏觀變形下的對稱性演化，以及它們對材料性質（包括電學和光學性質）的影響。這對於充分發掘變形工程的潛力至關重要。 在應用層面，我們將開發一個系統且具預測性的框架，以在高維的應變/扭曲/堆疊/平移空間內優化材料變形。該優化過程考慮材料失穩極限，材料受均勻與非均勻變形下的對稱性修正，和材料變形時的內部弛豫過程，旨在穩健地調控塊體、薄膜及二維材料的性能。 我們的研究方法將基於群論方法，探究在特定變形下晶體對稱群發生的對稱性轉變。隨後，將採用基於連續介質力學/統計力學的方法，分析由均勻與非均勻宏觀形變引起的原子位移/弛豫。進一步，我們將運用材料穩定性原理來界定可實現的變形範圍。最後，將利用第一性原理方法，將這種變形響應與電子結構和材料性質關聯起來。

17215025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17215025.value: 智慧數據賦能智能人工智能：用於訓練領域專家模型的目標視覺數據集自動發現與淨化

17215025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17215025.value: Recent breakthroughs in computer vision are largely driven by data, from task-specific models to vision foundation models like CLIP, DINOv2, Gemini, and GPT-4V. While these foundation models excel in tasks such as semantic analysis and reasoning on general domains, they struggle in specialized domains like medical and autonomous driving and often demand significant computational resources. This calls for developing domain-specific and compact expert foundation models, which requires large amounts of target domain data. The current process of creating such datasets is labor-intensive, prone to bias, and difficult to scale due to its reliance on manual collection and quality control. This project aims to overcome these limitations by automating the discovery of high-quality data from generative models and the open web, significantly expanding data diversity and scale for target domains. The resulting datasets can be used to develop compact expert models or to adapt general foundation models for domain-specific expertise. Despite the abundance of web and generative data (e.g., images), extracting relevant, high-quality samples still requires significant human effort in crafting web queries and prompts. Additionally, these data often include redundant, low-quality (e.g., noisy and harmful) samples, requiring extensive cleaning. To address these challenges, we propose the following major designs for automated data discovery and purification to reduce reliance on human labor and knowledge while enhancing data quality, diversity, and quantity. First, we will develop a concept-driven data discovery method that integrates language models, knowledge graphs (e.g., WordNet), and domain-specific feedback to progressively mine relevant concepts, prune irrelevant ones, and generate targeted queries for data harvesting from the web and generative models, where the combination of two data sources will further maximize the data coverage. Second, we will formulate data cleaning as a quadratic programming problem that optimizes for sample quality, informativeness, and low redundancy, capable of scaling to billions of samples to distill a high-quality, compact visual dataset. Also, we will enhance vision-language pair quality by ensembling assessment scores from multiple models. Finally, the resulting datasets will be used to build expert models, such as specialized versions of CLIP and DINOv2, to solve target domain problems like wild species recognition and autonomous driving, supporting targeted applications. Our preliminary experiments have confirmed the approach's scalability and feasibility. All source codes will be made publicly available on GitHub. The outcomes will advance data-centric AI and extend foundation models into expert domains, shaping AI's evolution from general models to specialized expert systems. 近年來，電腦視覺的重大突破很大程度上得益於數據的推動——從特定任務的模型到通用的視覺基礎模型，如 CLIP、DINOv2、Gemini 和 GPT-4V。儘管這些基礎模型在通用領域的語義分析與推理任務中表現優異，但在醫療、自動駕駛等專業領域仍面臨挑戰，且通常需要大量計算資源。這促使我們亟需研發面向特定領域的緊湊型專家級基礎模型，而這又依賴於大量目標領域的數據。目前構建這類數據集的流程高度依賴人工採集和質量控制，不僅勞動密集、容易產生偏差，而且難以規模化。 本項目旨在通過自動化技術解決上述瓶頸，從生成模型與開放網絡中發現高質量數據，顯著擴展目標領域數據的多樣性與規模。所生成的數據集既可用於訓練緊湊型專家模型，也可用於將通用基礎模型適配為特定領域的專家模型。儘管網絡與生成式數據資源豐富（如圖像），但要提取相關且高質量的數據樣本，仍需大量人工設計檢索關鍵詞和生成提示詞；此外，這些數據中往往還夾雜著冗餘、低質量（如雜訊或有害）的內容，需耗費大量精力清洗。 為此，我們提出以下關鍵設計方案，以自動化地完成數據發現與淨化，從而減少人工勞動與先驗知識的依賴，同時提升數據質量、多樣性與數量。首先，我們將構建基於概念驅動的數據探索方法，融合語言模型、知識圖譜（如 WordNet）與領域回饋，逐步挖掘相關概念、剪枝無關內容，並生成用於從網絡與生成模型中採集數據的目標檢索語句；兩類數據源的結合將最大化數據覆蓋範圍。其次，我們將數據清洗建模為一個二次規劃問題，優化樣本的質量、信息量與低冗餘性，可擴展至數十億樣本以提取高質量、緊湊的視覺數據集；同時，通過融合多模型的評估得分，進一步提升圖文對質量。 最終，這些數據集將用於構建專家模型，例如 CLIP 和 DINOv2 的特定領域版本，用於解決野生物種識別、自動駕駛等任務，支撐下游應用。我們的初步實驗已驗證該方法的可擴展性與可行性。所有原始碼將公開在 GitHub 上。本項目的成果將推動數據驅動人工智能的發展，使基礎模型從通用智能向專家系統演進。

17215125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17215125.value: 基於多尺度方法的泥石流堆積堤形成機理研究與其物理預測模型

17215125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17215125.value: Dr JING, Lu Prof LEUNG, Yat Fai

17215125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17215125.value: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events in Hong Kong due to global warming has significantly raised the risk of landslides and debris flows, which can lead to massive casualties and substantial economic losses. Globally, and especially in Hong Kong, where approximately 70% of debris flow landslides occur on shallow slopes with prominent self-channelization, distinct levees composed of gravels and boulders have been observed along the edges of debris deposits. These levees can confine lateral spreading and enhance the flow mobility, thus substantially extending the runout distance. However, a fundamental understanding of self-channelization and the underlying phase transition between flowing and static debris-fluid mixtures (granular material) is still missing. Moreover, during the formation of levee on slopes and in final deposits, the effects of viscous fluid, poly dispersity, and base roughness on phase transition remain underexplored. Therefore, current landslide mobility models usually lack a constitutive model to describe the flow behaviour during levee formation, which may result in up to 180% overestimation. The proposed research seeks to address this challenge in engineering practice by advancing the understanding of the micro-mechanisms underlying levee formation (static-flow transition) and establishing a theoretical model that defines the criterion for levee formation and quantify its effects on the mobility and runout of debris flows. A systematic experimental approach along with improved numerical tools will be employed to link the microscopic mechanisms of levee formation to its macroscopic impacts on the overall flow behaviour. A multiscale approach will be adopted in the proposed research, integrating experimental, numerical, and theoretical approaches through four interconnected components: (i) laboratory open-slope tests on both dry and fluid-saturated flows, examining steady and transient states to identify the conditions under which levees form; (ii) micromechanical analysis of flow phase transitions and levee formation using an advanced fluid-particle coupling numerical tool, which can efficiently handle highly polydisperse granular-fluid systems; (iii) development of a constitutive model, including a general criteria of levee formation applicable across different length scales and a basal friction formulation for the physical processes during levee formation; and (iv) the implementation of this constitutive model into depth-averaged continuum theories for large-scale case studies. The anticipated outcomes of this research will significantly improve the accuracy of runout and velocity predictions for landslide-related geohazards, thereby informing more effective risk assessment and mitigation strategies. 受全球暖化氣候影響，香港地區極端天氣事件頻發，由此引發的山泥傾瀉與泥石流災害風險顯著加劇，對城市基礎設施和公眾安全構成嚴重威脅。值得注意的是，全球範圍內（特別是香港地區）約70%的泥石流型山泥傾瀉發生在淺層斜坡，並呈現顯著的自組織溝槽化結構特徵。這類山泥傾瀉的流徑邊緣通常沉積有由粗顆粒物質構成的側向堆積堤，該結構通過抑制泥石流的橫向擴散、增強縱向土石和流體的搬運速度，可顯著增加泥石流的最終衝出距離。然而，當前研究對以下關鍵科學問題仍缺乏系統認知：（1）顆粒流中流動相與靜止相之間的動態轉化機制；（2）泥石流中堆積堤自組織形成的內在物理過程；（3）泥石流物理特性（如流體黏度、顆粒分散度及基底粗糙度）對相變行為的調控作用。這些認知空白導致現有的泥石流預測模型普遍缺乏描述堆積堤動形成的本構關係，致使衝出距離預測誤差可能高達180%。 本研究擬通過多尺度研究方法揭示堆積堤形成的微觀力學機制，重點解決靜止-流動相變這一核心物理學問題。研究將建立泥石流自組織溝槽化的耦合微觀機制與宏觀行為的理論框架，具體包含四個相互銜接的研究模塊：（i）進行開放坡面條件下的乾燥/飽和顆粒流實驗，揭示穩態與非穩態條件下堆積堤的觸發閾值；（ii）基於流體-顆粒耦合數值模擬，分析高分散性顆粒系統的相變動力學與堆積堤演化規律；（iii）構建跨尺度動力學本構模型，創新性地引入相變敏感的基底摩擦定律；（iv）將本構關係嵌入深度平均連續介質理論框架，通過工程案例驗證模型預測效能。研究成果將突破現有山泥傾瀉運動預測的理論瓶頸，為地質災害風險評估提供量化工具，對制定科學防災策略具有重要實踐價值。

17215225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17215225.value: 用於集成電路製造中光掩模修復的納米機器人操作任務規劃與控制

17215225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17215225.value: Lithography plays an essential role in semiconductor chips manufacturing. Photomask is a key part of lithography process, that transfers integrated circuit patterns onto silicon wafers. In extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, masks are easily contaminated by carbon and other tiny particles. These contaminants typically adhere to or solidify on the mask surface, resulting in what are known as soft and hard defects. Throughout its service life, a mask is expected to expose 50,000 wafers, and it requires cleaning and inspection after approximately every 100 exposures to ensure its quality. As semiconductor process technology advances to below 7nm, the patterns on the mask become denser and the line widths finer, making even small defects potentially significant in affecting chip quality. Additionally, as the density of the patterns increases, traditional cleaning processes become increasingly inadequate in removing all defects, thus placing higher demands on new technology for mask cleaning and repairing. Traditional mask repair and cleaning primarily utilize focused electron-beam-induced processing (FEBIP); as chip feature size shrinks to below 7nm, this technique exhibits significant disadvantages and limitations. We propose to develop an atomic force microscopy (AFM) based nano robotic manipulator to perform mask cleaning and repair. Due to the limited sensing capability in nano environment, it has been difficult to fully automate robotic cleaning and repairing for masks. The objective of this proposed project is to develop planning and control methods to enable a nano robot to automatically perform mask cleaning and repairing. The specific goals include (1) using large language model (LLM) combining with analytic optimization method to determine the logic relationship of task/action plan and utilizing real-time sensory measurement to enable an embodiment to further determine the temporal/spatial and interactive relationships in the task/action plan; (2) developing video rate atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging method to provide real-time photomask images and enabling image-based motion control to achieve high precision positioning, and interactive force control to ensure reliable and safe cleaning operations; (3) developing multi-functional nano robot end-effectors for photomask cleaning. They are capable of real-time AFM imaging and performing multiple type of cleaning tasks such as nano object removal and deburring defects; (4) experimental implementation, testing and evaluation of the task/action planning and control methods for photomask cleaning to demonstrate the proposed method has the efficiency and effectiveness several folds better than existing technology, and the task/action planning method is capable of self-learning to improve the performance through the operations. 光刻在半導體晶片製造中扮演著關鍵角色。光掩模是光刻工藝的核心部分，用於將積體電路圖案轉移到矽片上。在極紫外（EUV）光刻中，掩模容易受到碳和其他微小顆粒的污染。這些污染物通常會粘附或固化在掩模表面，形成軟缺陷和硬缺陷。在其使用壽命內，掩模預計可以曝光5萬片矽片，每大約曝光100片後需要進行清洗和檢測，以確保其品質。隨著半導體工藝技術向7nm以下發展，掩模上的圖案變得更加密集，線寬更細，即使是微小的缺陷也可能對晶片品質產生重大影響。此外，隨著圖案密度的增加，傳統的清洗工藝越來越難以完全去除所有缺陷，這對掩模的清洗和修復技術提出了更高的要求。 傳統的掩模修復和清洗主要採用聚焦電子束誘導加工（FEBIP）；然而，隨著晶片特徵尺寸縮小到7nm以下，這種技術表現出明顯的不足和局限性。我們計劃開發一種基於原子力顯微鏡（AFM）的納米機器人操作器，用於掩模的清洗和修復。由於納米環境中的感測能力有限，實現掩模的機器人完全自動清洗和修復一直具有挑戰。該專案的目標是開發規劃與控制方法，使納米機器人能夠自動完成掩模的清洗和修復。具體目標包括：（1）結合大型語言模型（LLM）與解析優化方法，確定任務和動作計畫的邏輯關係，並利用即時感測資料進一步明確任務中的時空和交互關係；（2）開發視頻速率的AFM成像技術，提供即時光掩模圖像，並實現基於圖像的運動控制，以實現高精度定位，以及探針-樣品交互力控制，確保清洗操作的可靠性和安全性；（3）開發多功能的納米機器人末端執行器，用於光掩模的清洗，具備即時AFM成像能力，能執行多種清洗任務，如納米異物去除和缺陷去毛刺；（4）進行實驗實現、測試和評估掩模清洗的任務與動作規劃和控制方法，以證明所提出的方法在效率和效果上比現有技術高出數倍，並且任務/動作規劃方法具有自我學習能力，可以通過操作不斷優化性能。

17215525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17215525.value: 酸性電解水制氫用不銹鋼中過渡金屬鈍化機制研究

17215525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17215525.value: The demand for low-cost, corrosion-resistant alloys suitable for water electrolyzers in industrial-scale green hydrogen production is rising due to their substantial impact on system costs. Structural components, such as bipolar plates (BPPs) and porous transport layers (PTLs), constitute an astonishing 60~70% of total stack expenses due to the reliance on precious metal-coated titanium materials. Stainless steels (SSs) are emerging as promising alternatives, given their abundance and established manufacturing techniques. However, their corrosion resistance under high-potential conditions remains a significant challenge, as the Cr(III)-based passive film collapses at potentials exceeding 1000-1200 mV, leading to Cr transpassivity that fails to withstand oxygen evolution reaction (OER) potentials. To address this issue, we propose a strategy to develop potential-resistant stainless steels (PRSSs) for acidic water electrolysis by green energy sources. PRSSs refer to cost-effective, iron-based alloys with superior corrosion resistance across a wide range of passivation regions. Numerous non-noble transition-metal oxides have demonstrated good OER activity and long-term durability in acidic environments. By integrating these passivation-capable transition metals with semiconductive oxides, our alloys aim to achieve wide passivation windows that span from natural potentials to those required for water oxidation, while also minimizing charge transfer resistance during the OER. This strategy builds on the success of previously developed sequential dual-passivation stainless steels and has been validated in another example, Fe-CrCoMo. However, the stability in oxides does not inherently ensure the efficacy of these cost-effective transition metals in passivating alloys, and the comprehensive development of such PRSSs remains a challenge and an underexplored area of research. This project begins by establishing a solid foundation through the systematic investigation on the passivation behavior of selected transition metals in acidic environments commonly used for water electrolysis. These transition metals will be chosen based on criteria such as cost, reported stability of their oxide forms, and their behavior indicated by Pourbaix diagrams. Building on this groundwork, PRSSs will be developed by integrating validated transition metals. The passivation processes, particularly at critical transition points and OER potentials, will be studied to elucidate the mechanisms and diffusion behavior of the dominant elements. Finally, the performance boundaries of the PRSSs will be evaluated, with a special focus on those suitable for proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. 隨著工業級綠氫製備技術的快速發展，水電解槽用低成本耐蝕合金的需求日益迫切，這類材料對系統總成本具有決定性影響。目前雙極板（BPPs）和多孔傳輸層（PTLs）等核心構件因依賴貴金屬鍍層鈦材，佔據電堆總成本的60%~70%。不銹鋼因其資源豐富且工藝成熟，被視為極具潛力的替代材料，但其在高電位工況下的耐蝕性仍是重大挑戰——當電位超過1000-1200 mV時，Cr(III)鈍化膜會發生崩潰，引發鉻的過鈍化現象，難以承受析氧反應（OER）所需的高電位環境。 針對這一難題，本研究提出面向酸性水電解綠氫系統的耐電位不銹鋼（PRSSs）開發策略。這類鐵基合金需在寬電位視窗內保持優異耐蝕性，同時兼顧成本效益。研究發現，多種非貴過渡金屬氧化物在酸性環境中兼具良好OER活性和長期穩定性。通過將這類具有鈍化特性的過渡金屬與半導體氧化物協同整合，我們致力於開發出從自然電位覆蓋至水氧化電位、且OER過程中電荷轉移電阻極低的新型合金。該策略基於前期開發的"連續雙鈍化不銹鋼"，並已在Fe-CrCoMo等合金體系中獲得驗證。但需注意的是，氧化物穩定性並不等同於這些低成本過渡金屬在合金鈍化中的有效性，PRSSs的完整開發仍存在諸多未知領域。 本專案將分三階段推進：首先系統研究水電解典型酸性環境中優選過渡金屬的鈍化行為（篩選標準包括成本、氧化物穩定性及電位-pH圖特徵）；在此基礎上構建PRSSs合金體系；重點解析臨界轉變電位與OER電位下的鈍化機制及主導元素的擴散行為；最終評估該材料在質子交換膜水電解環境中的性能邊界。這項研究將為綠氫裝備的降本增效提供關鍵材料解決方案。

17300225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300225.value: 稳健非参数推断：移动流网络中的动态热点与吸引区域分析 稳健非参数推断：移动流网络中的动态热点与吸引区域分析 稳健非参数推断：移动流网络中的动态热点与吸引区域分析

17300225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300225.value: Analyzing "hotspots" of high population flows in human mobility data provides valuable insights for research and policy across fields including urban planning and epidemiology. Identifying mobility hotspots and the catchment areas from which they attract population flows allows for targeting business or policy interventions, monitoring spatial accessibility, and managing congestion among other applications. Inferential techniques from network science and information theory are designed to reveal structural regularities in noisy complex systems, so these fields enable new powerful tools for understanding hotspot dynamics in human mobility data. To enable statistically robust and efficient inference, methods for identifying hotspots and catchment areas in mobility networks should have three features. (1) Parameter-free model selection for the number and composition of hotspots and associated spatially contiguous catchment areas. This feature learns characteristic spatio-temporal scales from the data itself and reduces constraints from human aesthetic biases. (2) Parameter-free identification of temporal changepoints in hotspot and catchment structure. This feature provides a parsimonious dynamic representation that adapts to changing mobility trends. (3) Scalability to datasets with high spatial/temporal resolution. Existing methods for inferring hotspots or catchment areas in mobility networks fail to meet these criteria. The proposed research addresses the three issues above by building on the PI's recent work to construct and evaluate a novel inference algorithm for extracting dynamic hotspots and catchment areas in human mobility data. First, we use the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle to construct a parameter-free inference objective with built-in regularization for identifying the most parsimonious summary of a human mobility flow dataset as a set of time-varying hotspots and catchment areas. Second, we develop a scalable nested optimization scheme for inferring the hotspot-catchment configuration that minimizes this objective, integrating multiple optimization schemes for MDL-based inference successfully used in the PI's previous work. Next, we evaluate the optimality of the method on test cases with tractable exact solutions and compare with existing algorithms in terms of runtime, changepoint detection, and data compression on synthetic datasets. Finally, we compare our algorithm with existing methods to reveal hotspot and catchment structure in real human mobility datasets representing yearly commuting flows across the US and daily mobility traces within Mexico City. The proposed algorithm provides a methodological advance for statistical network inference and complex systems modelling of human mobility data. It also offers a principled, efficient, easy-to-use method for downstream applications in urban planning and public policy among other fields analyzing mobility patterns. 分析人类移动数据中的"热点"高流量区域，能为城市规划和流行病学等跨领域研究及政策制定提供重要洞见。识别移动热点及其吸引人口流动的辐射区域，有助于精准实施商业或政策干预、监测空间可达性、管理交通拥堵等应用场景。网络科学与信息论中的推断技术专为揭示复杂噪声系统的结构规律而设计，这些领域为理解人类移动数据中的热点动态提供了全新工具。 为实现统计稳健且高效的推断，移动网络热点及辐射区域识别方法需具备三个特征：(1) 对热点数量、构成及空间连续辐射区域进行无参数模型选择。该特性可从数据自身学习时空特征尺度，减少人为审美偏好的干扰。(2) 无参数识别热点与辐射结构的时序变化点。该特性能生成适应移动趋势变化的精简动态表征。(3) 支持高时空分辨率数据集的扩展性。现有移动网络热点推断方法均未能满足这些标准。 本研究基于PI近期工作，通过构建和评估新型推断算法来解决上述三个问题。首先，我们采用最小描述长度(MDL)原则构建无参数推断目标函数，其内置正则化机制可将人类移动流数据精简表征为时变热点与辐射区域的集合。其次，我们开发可扩展的嵌套优化方案，整合PI既往研究中经MDL验证的多种优化方法，以最小化目标函数的方式推断最优热点-辐射配置。接着，我们在可求解测试案例中验证方法的优化性能，并通过合成数据集在运行时间、变点检测和数据压缩等方面与现有算法对比。最后，我们使用美国年度通勤流和墨西哥城日常移动轨迹等真实数据集，将新算法与现有方法进行热点辐射结构识别效果的对比。 该算法为人类移动数据的统计网络推断和复杂系统建模提供了方法论突破，同时为城市规划、公共政策等移动模式分析领域的下游应用提供了原理清晰、高效易用的研究工具。

17300325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300325.value: 求解三維趨化性類型拋物型偏微分方程組的高效相互作用粒子—場方法：算法、分析與應用

17300325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300325.value: Many complex phenomena in science and engineering are modeled by partial differential equations (PDEs) subject to specific boundary and initial conditions. Accurately solving these PDEs is crucial for simulating many real-world phenomena, ranging from fluid flows and biomechanics to population dynamics and tumor growth. However, traditional mesh-based methods, such as finite element methods and finite difference methods, often encounter significant challenges when solving PDEs that exhibit low regularity and high dimensionality. These challenges greatly limit our ability to tackle many complicated real-world problems. In contrast, particle-based numerical methods that bypass the need for traditional mesh generation provide a promising solution to address these challenges. In this project, we aim to develop interacting particle-field (IPF) methods to solve three-dimensional (3D) chemotaxis-type parabolic PDE systems, analyze their convergence, and study the applications of these methods. We will focus on two prototype problems: (1) parabolic-parabolic Keller-Segel (KS) chemotaxis PDE systems; and (2) chemotaxis and haptotaxis PDE systems for cancer cell invasion. We will investigate several important issues. Firstly, we will explore representing low-regularity solutions using particle methods and smooth solutions using mesh-based basis functions, and develop IPF methods to solve these problems efficiently. Secondly, we will explore techniques to improve the accuracy and reduce the computational costs of our methods, such as particle-in-cell methods, model reduction methods, operator-splitting methods, resampling methods, and deep learning methods. We expect that our new methods will not only solve the proposed problems but also solve a wide range of chemotaxis-type PDE systems that pose inherent difficulties for traditional mesh-based methods. Besides developing efficient numerical methods, we will rigorously analyze their convergence and error estimates. These analyses will provide insights into how to further improve the performance of our methods, such as by designing resampling methods and model reduction methods. To expand the impact of this project, we will apply the new methods to solve application problems in biological modeling and cancer cell invasion. Through these numerical results and theoretical findings, we aim to gain a deeper understanding of the mechanisms behind these physical and biological phenomena. The outcomes of the project are expected to result in significant advances in simulating complex phenomena using 3D Chemotaxis-type parabolic PDE systems. With these new methods, we will be able to simulate many real-world problems, particularly biological modeling and cancer cell invasion. Therefore, the proposed project is promising in generating broader impacts in the scientific and engineering communities. 科學與工程中的許多複雜現象可通過受特定邊界條件和初始條件約束的偏微分方程來建模。精確求解這些偏微分方程對於模擬很多實際現象至關重要，包括流體力學、生物力學、種羣動力學及腫瘤生長等領域。然而，傳統的基於網格的數值方法（如有限元方法和有限差分方法）在求解具有低正則性和高維特性的偏微分方程時，往往面臨顯著挑戰。這些挑戰極大地限制了我們處理許多複雜實際問題的能力。相比之下，無需傳統網格生成的基於粒子的數值方法，爲應對這些挑戰提供了一種頗具前景的解決方法。 本項目旨在開發相互作用粒子—場方法，用於求解三維趨化性類型拋物型偏微分方程組，分析其收斂性，並探究這些方法的應用。我們將聚焦於兩個典型問題：（1）拋物—拋物型 Keller-Segel趨化性偏微分方程組；（2）癌細胞侵襲的趨化性與趨觸性偏微分方程組。我們將研究若干重要問題：首先，利用粒子方法表示低正則性解，利用基於網格的基函數表示光滑解，進而開發可高效求解這些問題的粒子—場方法；其次，探索提升方法精度與降低計算成本的技術，如粒子網格法、模型降階方法、算子分裂法、重採樣方法及深度學習方法。我們期望所提出的新方法不僅能求解上述問題，還能適用於一大類傳統網格方法難以處理的趨化性類型偏微分方程組。 除開發高效數值方法外，我們還將嚴格分析其收斂性與誤差估計。這些分析將爲進一步提升方法性能提供啓示，例如通過設計重採樣方法與模型降階方法。爲擴大本項目的影響，我們將把新方法應用於生物建模及癌細胞侵襲中的實際問題。通過這些數值結果與理論成果，我們旨在更深入地理解這些物理與生物現象背後的機制。 本項目的成果有望在利用三維趨化性類型拋物型偏微分方程組模擬複雜現象方面取得重要進展。藉助這些新方法，我們將能夠模擬諸多實際問題，尤其是生物建模相關問題。因此，本項目有望在科學與工程界產生更廣泛的影響。

17300425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300425.value: 採用先進的超快光譜技術來揭示高效有機光伏材料的結構與光物理性質

17300425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300425.value: Organic photovoltaics (OPV) offer the potential for eco-friendly, biocompatible, and low-cost solar cells. Excitingly, the recent development of a new class of electron-accepting material (Y-acceptors) have led to a significant improvement in the solar power conversion efficiency of OPV, now exceeding 20%. However, the precise electron-hole (exciton) separation mechanism and the photophysical properties of the intermediate excited states involved are not fully understood, hindering new material development and performance optimization. This is largely due to the limitation of the common experimental methods being adopted to study the dynamics of the intermediate excited states in OPV materials (such as transient absorption spectroscopy). In this project, we aim to address this knowledge gap using advanced ultrafast optical techniques. First, by monitoring the transient electroabsorption (TEA) spectral signal caused by delocalized intermediate excited states, our research team has developed a new method to probe ultrafast excited state migration from structurally disordered to structurally ordered regions of Y-acceptor films. Importantly, this ultrafast energy migration process is directly correlated with the charge generation efficiency, thus revealing a new structure-property relationship. Our initial results have been recently accepted for publication by Energy & Environmental Science. In this project, we plan to employ this method to study the intermediate excited state properties and ultrafast exciton migration process in state-of-the-art OPV materials with over 19%-20% efficiencies. Furthermore, transient impulsive stimulated Raman spectroscopy (TISR) will be employed to investigate the electron-vibrational decoupling mechanism of the intermediate excited states in Y-acceptors to help explain their exceptionally long lifetimes. Moreover, we aim to understand how the molecular structure of Y-acceptors affects the energy barrier for exciton separation into free charges at the donor-acceptor interface. Previous reports have suggested that Y-acceptors with shorter π-π stacking distance, lower reorganization energy, and higher dielectric constant have lower charge separation energy barrier (thus allowing higher device efficiency), but a quantitative study is lacking. We plan to address this issue by employing time-resolved two-photon photoemission spectroscopy (TR-TPPE), an advanced technique that can accurately measure the interfacial charge separation energy barrier in state-of-the-art OPV systems, as demonstrated in our preliminary work in collaboration with Professor Wai-Lun Chan (Kansas University). Taken together, we anticipate our results will lead to new fundamental understanding of the solar energy conversion process in state-of-the-art OPV materials, providing new insights on how to develop future OPV materials and devices with performance matching crystalline silicon and perovskite PV cells (over 25% efficiency). 有機光伏（OPV）提供了環保、生物相容且低成本的太陽能電池潛力。令人振奮的是，近期新一類電子接受體（Y-接受體）的發展，顯著提升了OPV的太陽能轉換效率，現已超過20%。然而，涉及的電子-空穴（激子）分離機制及中間激發態的光物理性質尚未完全理解，這限制了新材料的開發與性能優化。這在很大程度上是由於現有實驗方法（如瞬態吸收光譜）在研究OPV材料中間激發態動力學方面的局限。 在本專案中，我們旨在利用先進的超快光學技術來填補這一知識空白。首先，通過監測由離域中間激發態引起的瞬態電吸收（TEA）光譜信號，我們的研究團隊開發了一種新方法，用於探測Y-接受體薄膜中由無序結構向有序結構區域的超快激發態遷移。值得注意的是，這一超快的能量遷移過程與電荷產生效率密切相關，從而揭示了一個新的結構-性質關係。我們的初步結果已被《Energy & Environmental Science》雜誌接受發表。在本專案中，我們計劃利用此方法研究效率超過19%-20%的尖端OPV材料中的中間激發態性質與超快激子遷移過程。此外，還將採用瞬態刺激拉曼光譜（TISR）來研究Y-接受體中間激發態的電子-振動耦合機制，以幫助解釋其極長的壽命。 此外，我們還希望理解Y-接受體的分子結構如何影響激子在供體-接受體界面分離成自由電荷的能量障礙。先前的報導指出，具有較短π-π堆積距離、更低重組能以及較高介電常數的Y-接受體，其電荷分離能量障礙較低（因此具有較高的器件效率），但缺乏定量研究。我們計劃採用時間解析雙光子光電子能譜（TR-TPPE）：一種能準確測量尖端OPV系統界面電荷分離能障的先進技術，這在我們與美國堪薩斯大學Wai-Lun Chan教授合作的初步工作中已有證明。 綜合來說，我們預期這些研究結果將有助於深化對尖端OPV材料中太陽能轉換過程的基本理解，並提供新的見解，以促使未來的OPV材料與器件性能達到晶矽與鈣钛礦光伏電池（效率超過25%）的水平。

17300525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300525.value: 費貝爾曼量子表面響應函數的表徵與應用研究

17300525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300525.value: When nanostructures reach the deep nanoscale, their sizes approach the electronic length scales in materials, leading to profound implications such as the emergence of quantum surface optical responses like nonlocality, electronic spillover, and surface-enabled Landau damping. These nonclassical responses have been found to introduce significant discrepancies between classical predictions and experimental results in systems with feature sizes typically below 10 to 20 nanometres. It is imperative to establish a unified electromagnetic framework that incorporates these responses at the interface of granular microscopic and continuous macroscopic regimes. The classical Maxwellian framework was recently amended to include the Feibelman d-parameter, representing the missing electronic length scale, opening up new possibilities for modeling and comprehending nanoscale electromagnetic phenomena. Despite its critical significance and recent advancements, experimental measurement and application of d-parameters remain challenging. This project aims to develop a systematic experimental protocol for measuring and dynamically manipulating d-parameters in pristine metallic and semiconductor thin films and nanostructures. The approach will be rigorously analyzed through variance-based sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations, ensuring compliance with passivity and causality constraints. Utilizing advanced spectroscopic tools like dark-field scattering microscopy, scanning near-field optical spectroscopy, electron energy loss, and cathodoluminescence, waveguide-based and resonator-based methods will be devised to investigate Feibelman d-parameters within the frequency range of technological relevance and study their dynamic behavior under surface adsorption and electrical gating. Subsequently, the project will explore the application of d-parameters in enhancing free electron field emission based on the Bennett mode as their pole in the complex frequency plane. This initiative will advance the understanding of quantum surface responses at the nanoscale and establish a general methodology to facilitate widespread access to d-parameter measurements and their comprehensive cataloguing. These endeavors will also help advance the comprehension of mesoscopic quantum optical effects in condensed matter physics, surface chemistry, vacuum electronics, and nanophotonics. 當奈米結構進入深奈米尺度時，其尺寸接近材料中的電子特徵長度，引發顯著的量子表面光學響應現象，例如非局域性、電子溢出效應與表面誘導的朗道阻尼。這些非经典響應已被證實會在特徵尺寸低於10至20奈米的系統中，造成经典理論預測與實驗結果的顯著差異。亟需一套統一的電磁理論框架，將此類響應納入介於微觀顆粒性與巨觀連續性之間的介面描述。近期经典麦克斯韋理論框架已引入費貝爾曼d-參數（Feibelman d-parameters）作為缺失的電子長度尺度表徵，為奈米尺度電磁現象建模開闢新途徑。儘管其重要性與日俱增且理論進展迅速，d-參數的實驗量測與實際應用仍面臨挑戰。 本計畫旨在建立系統化實驗方案，用於量測並動態操控原始金屬/半導體薄膜及奈米結構中的d-參數。研究將基於變異數的靈敏度分析與蒙地卡羅模擬相結合，嚴格驗證方法學的被動性與因果性約束。透過暗場散射顯微鏡、掃描近場光譜、電子能量損失譜與陰極發光等尖端光譜技術，設計波導型與共振腔型量測手段，研究技術相關頻段內的費貝爾曼d-參數，並探討其於分子吸附與電閘調控下的動態行為。進一步將基於d-參數在複頻率平面上的極點（Bennett模式），探索其於增強自由電子場發射中的應用。此研究將深化對奈米尺度量子表面響應的理解，建立普適性方法論以推動d-參數量測普及化。

17300625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300625.value: 在100Sn核區高精度質量測量和香港大學的MRTOF質譜儀建設

17300625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300625.value: The N=Z=50 100Sn is of particular interest for nuclear structure due to its exotic doubly-magic character and being the heaviest self-conjugate nucleus. It lies on the proton drip-line at the limit of proton stability with its extreme neutron deficiency. Characterizing the magicity of 100Sn offers an important insight into the understanding of nuclear force and assesses various structure models. This flagship nucleus 100Sn and its neighboring nuclei are also playing decisive role for the end-point of the astrophysical rapid proton capture (rp) process nucleosynthesis. Nuclear mass data in the vicinity of 100Sn is therefore essential. However the key nuclei either are inaccessible due to low production yield or have mass values with large ambiguity from indirect measurement via decay endpoint energy. We aim at high-precision direct mass measurement of 100Sn and its neighboring nuclei using multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrograph (MRTOF) placed after Zero-Degree spectrometer at RIBF facility RIKEN. The proposal was submitted to the RIBF-PAC (NP2112-RIBF211: In-beam γ-ray and mass spectroscopy of 100Sn) with PI of this grant application as the experiment spokesperson. This proposal was approved with priority S (highest ranking). The experiment was performed successfully in June 2024. In total 50 different isotopes were measured in which 4 isotopes were measured for the first time, and 21 isotopes were measured with significant improvements of the previously known mass values. Currently, HKU members including three postdoctoral researchers and 1 Ph.D. student are dedicated to the data analysis. The results would provide important benchmark to structure models and advance understanding to the rp-process nucleosynthesis mechanism. For fully addressing the quest of origin of elements, mass data of extremely neutron-rich nuclei in rapid-neutron capture pathway (r-process) are also essential. The High Intensity Heavy-Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF) of IMP in Huizhou China, with construction completed in 2026, allows to reach the “big land” of unexplored neutron-rich isotopes in heavy regions, which is not accessible in any of the facilities in the world. The PI's group is constructing own HKU’s MRTOF for high precision nuclear mass measurement in N~126 and actinoid region. The core mechanical parts of HKU’s MRTOF are already purchased under the PI’s funds (GRF 17312522 and NSFC 12122516). The HKU’s MRTOF is being assembled and will be coupled with IMP’s gas cell for experiments to explore new heavy nuclei via multi-nucleon transfer reaction at HIAF. 100Sn的中子數和質子數皆為50，因其特殊的雙魔特性以及是最重的自交核，因此在核結構研究中具有重要意義。它位於質子滴線上，處於質子穩定性極限，具有極端的中子缺乏性。對100Sn的高精度質量測量，能提供理解核力的重要見解，並幫助評估各種核結構模型。這個核及其鄰近核在核合成中的快速質子（rp）過程終點也扮演著決定性角色。因此，100Sn及其周圍核的核質量數據非常重要，因為它提供了核束縛能的直接資訊，束縛能是所有核子相互作用的綜合結果，並且在核合成的相關計算中扮演關鍵角色。然而，這些關鍵核因產量低或透過衰變端點能量的間接測量而具有較大的不確定性。 我們旨在利用多反射飛行時間質譜儀（ZD-MRTOF-MS）對100Sn及其鄰近核進行高精度直接質量測定，該儀器設於RIBF設施的Zero-Degree光譜儀之後。相關提案已提交給RIBF RIKEN第22屆核子物理委員會（NP-PAC），由本計畫的主要研究者擔任實驗發言人。該提案獲得全額批准，包括10天的束流時間，並被列為優先級S（最高等級）。實驗已於2024年6月成功完成，測量約50個不同的同位素，其中4個為首次測得，約21個的質量數據較之前顯著改進。目前，香港大學的成員，包括三名博士後和一名博士生，正專注於數據分析。這些結果將為各種結構模型提供重要的基準，也有助於理解快速質子捕獲核合成機制。 為了全面解答元素起源的問題，極端富中子核在快速中子捕獲（r過程）中的質量數據也同樣重要。中國科學院近代物理研究所（IMP）正在中國惠州建設高強度重離子加速器（HIAF），將提供前所未有的機會來探索重區域中未被研究的富中子同位素，這在全球任何設施中都無法達成。利用這一前所未有的良機，香港大學的團隊正在建設自己的MRTOF，用於在HIAF的物理實驗中進行高精度核質量測定。HKU的MRTOF核心機械部分已在主要研究者的資金（GRF 17312522 和 NSFC 12122516）支持下完成購置與組裝。隨著完整組裝與測試的完成，HKU的MRTOF將與IMP的氣體捕集器配合，進行多核子轉移反應，以探索新的重核。

17300725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300725.value: 二维莫尔体系中层依赖的电学输运与层间库仑相互作用的实验研究

17300725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300725.value: A successful isolation of graphene—a single atomic plane of graphite—about 20 years ago had led to discoveries of a large family of atomically thin 2D crystals, opening a fast-moving research field to study and understand the physics of these crystals and examine their potentials in device applications. More recently, thanks to the advances in van der Waals (vdW) stacking techniques, these isolated atomic planes have been reassembled into designer heterostructures, revealing new physics. In particular, by precisely aligning the layers, a quasiperiodic moiré structure on a scale much larger than the lattice constants of each layer have been formed. Since the lattice periodicity determines electronic band structures of crystals, these moiré materials possess new states of matter with properties that are absent in their constituents.
