There have been extensive theoretical and experimental studies on such moiré materials, but so far, most of them have focused on investigating their ‘bulk’ properties without distinguishing individual layers or tuning/studying the interlayer coupling. Here, we plan to explore this new research direction by building trilayer moiré heterostructures where only one- or two-atom-thin hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is inserted between the top and bottom layers that form a moiré pattern. By making diverse types of such heterostructures, we aim to examine how the interlayer distance (determined by the hBN thickness) affects Coulomb interactions and moiré potentials between the layers in the system. Furthermore, since the layers are separated by the hBN that is electrically insulating but thin enough to mediate interlayer interactions, we expect to control and study charge transports through individual layers separately while the layers remain coupled by Coulomb interactions. This will allow us to study how their transport properties are changed by interlayer moiré potentials and how different moiré bands can be coupled. We will mainly focus on graphene-hBN-graphene moiré heterostructures as both graphene and hBN, and their moiré structures, had been extensively studied, such that the results obtained can be directly compared with the existing ones, making the analysis straightforward. Graphene layers can also be replaced by other moiré or non-moiré 2D materials, such as magic-angle-twisted bilayer graphene or transition metal dichalcogenides, to investigate the couplings between different types of moiré and/or non-moiré bands. We believe these studies can reveal new moiré physics and provide deeper understandings of interlayer Coulomb interactions in low-dimensional systems. 约二十年前，石墨烯（即单原子层石墨）的首次成功剥离，引领了一系列原子级厚度二维晶体的发现，由此开辟了一个快速发展的研究领域，以研究这些晶体的物理特性并探索其在器件应用中的潜力。近年来，随着范德瓦尔斯堆叠技术的日益精进，这些独立的二维原子平面可被重新组装成人工异质结构，进而表现出新的物理现象。通过精准对齐层间的晶格取向，可以形成以一种周期远大于单层晶格常数的准周期莫尔超晶格结构。晶格周期性决定晶体的电子能带结构，使这些莫尔体系表现出其组成材料所不具备的新奇物质特性。目前已有大量基于这些莫尔体系的理论和实验研究，但大多数工作都集中于研究其"体"性质，并未区分莫尔体系的单层特性或调控/研究层间相互作用。 本研究计划通过构建三层莫尔异质结构来探索这一新方向：在莫尔结构的上下两层之间插入仅1-2个原子厚度的六方氮化硼（hBN）间隔层。通过制备多种此类异质结构，我们将系统研究层间距（由hBN厚度决定）对体系中的库仑相互作用和莫尔势的影响。此外， hBN间隔层具有电绝缘特性且厚度足够薄，使得层间具有库仑耦合的同时，我们可以分别调控和研究各独立层的电学输运行为。这将有助于理解层间莫尔势对输运性质的调控机制，以及不同莫尔能带间的耦合方式。本研究将主要聚焦于石墨烯-hBN-石墨烯莫尔异质结构体系。鉴于石墨烯、hBN及其莫尔结构已有充分研究，与本研究相关的结果可与已有数据直接对比，使分析论证更为明晰。也可将石墨烯层替换为其它莫尔或非莫尔二维材料（如魔角双层石墨烯或过渡金属硫族化合物），以研究不同类型莫尔/非莫尔能带间的耦合效应。该研究将揭示新的莫尔物理现象，并为理解低维体系中的层间库仑相互作用提供更加深刻的见解。

17300925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300925.value: 單層過渡金屬硫族化物與金屬接觸的分子束外延製備

17300925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17300925.value: Dr XIA, Yipu Dr Zhang, Junqiu

17300925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300925.value: The promise of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) for next-generation electronics such as field effect transistors in the sub-10nm regime faces scientific and technical challenges, one of which is the difficulty to achieve good ohmic contact, especially for the p-channel devices, by depositing metals on TMDs. There are ample experimental evidences of Fermi-level pinning (FLP) and so Schottky barriers exist irrespective of the metals deposited, leading to inefficient electron or hole injection. The reason or mechanism of FLP remains under extensive investigations, and it is suggested that defects in TMDs caused by metal deposition can be an important factor. It is therefore imperative to examine systematically and more quantitatively the effect of metal deposition conditions on defect formation and the relative importance of the defects to FLP. Conventionally, metal depositions on semiconductor, including TMDs, for achieving ohmic contacts are done by thermal or e-beam evaporations under medium to high vacuum. By work-function considerations, precious metals are desired for achieving good ohmic contacts with TMDs, which require high temperatures for evaporation. The high-temperature of the sources not only generates high-energy atoms, causing damages to the lattices of TMD films, but also leads to heating of the sample by radiation. The dual effect of the high-temperature sources on defect creation in TMDs can therefore be acute, requiring more quantitative evaluation and remediation. In this project, we will employ molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) operated under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) to fabricate metal-TMD contacts. Besides the UHV environment, MBE also has the advantage of high controllability of deposition parameters, availability of in situ surface characterization tools, such as reflection high-energy electron diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, photoemission spectroscopy, to monitor and analyze the deposition process in real time and interface characteristics in situ. These will facilitate more quantitative studies of contact formation and electronic properties. Lastly, equipped with the knowledge gained from such a study, ways to improve the contacts for better devices may be explored. Hence, the proposed project may not only generate results of fundamental values but also are quite relevant to technological advancements of next generation devices based on 2D materials. 二維過渡金屬硫族化物（TMDs）於次世代電子元件中，如亞10奈米尺度場效晶體管，展現出極具前景的應用潛力。然而，此技術仍面臨諸多科學與工程方面的挑戰，其中之一為於TMDs上沉積金屬以實現良好歐姆接觸的困難，尤其對於p型通道元件而言更為顯著。大量實驗證據表明，費米能級釘扎（Fermi-level pinning, FLP）現象普遍存在，導致無論沉積何種金屬，皆會形成肖特基勢壘，進而降低電子或空穴的注入效率。目前，FLP之成因與機制仍處於研究階段，而金屬沉積所誘發的TMDs缺陷被認為可能為關鍵因素之一。因此，系統且定量地探討金屬沉積條件對缺陷形成之影響，以及缺陷於FLP中所扮演之角色，具有十分重要的意義。 傳統上，為實現歐姆接觸，在半導體（包括TMDs）上澱積金屬多採用中高真空條件下的熱蒸發或電子束蒸發技術。基於功函數考量，貴金屬被視為與TMDs形成良好歐姆接觸的理想選擇，然其蒸發過程需於高溫下進行。高溫源不僅會產生高能原子，導致TMD薄膜晶格受損，亦會透過輻射導致樣品加熱。此雙重效應使得高溫源對TMDs缺陷生成帶來顯著影響，故需進一步進行定量評估與改善。 本項目將採用基於超高真空（UHV）環境的分子束外延（MBE）技術來製備金屬-TMDs接觸。除UHV環境外，MBE亦具備沉積參數高精度可控的優勢，並配備多種原位表面表徵工具，如反射高能電子衍射（RHEED）、掃描隧道顯微鏡（STM）及光電子能譜（PES）等，可即時監控與分析沉積過程及界面特性。此將有助於更為定量地研究接觸形成機制與電子特性。最終，基於此研究的結果和認知，我們希望探索出改善接觸性能以提升器件性能的方法。因此，本計畫不僅具有基礎研究的意義，更為二維材料器件技術的發展提供幫助。

17301125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17301125.value: 利用DNA編碼分子庫發現鄰近誘導小分子和分子膠

17301125.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17301125.value: Prof Chung, Yik Sham Clive Dr Zhai, Yuanliang

17301125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301125.value: Chemical inducers of proximity (CIPs) are powerful tools that enable precise manipulation of cellular processes by bringing molecules into proximity to trigger specific cellular responses. Small molecule inducers of protein-protein interactions (PPIs), also known as molecular glues (MGs), enhance direct contacts between proteins, thereby forming stable ternary complexes and introducing novel biological functions. Despite their potential in exploring fundamental biology and developing therapeutic strategies for challenging drug targets, the development of CIPs and MGs remains largely empirically driven due to the complex nature and structural diversity of proteins. Particularly, innovative screening methods are urgently needed in discovering new MGs beyond existing chemotypes to overcome the challenges posed by their lack of structural modularity, unpredictable binding modes, and diverse binding conformations. This project aims to develop a new method using DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) for selectively identifying "ternary binders" capable of bringing two proteins into proximity. Our focus will be on identifying cooperative PPI inducers as potential MGs. The strategy involves using a protein-fragment complementation approach, where compounds promoting ternary complex formation will restore the activity of a DNA adenine methyltransferase fused to the targets, leading to selective methylation of the DNA tag encoding the compound. Furthermore, potential MGs will be identified by prioritizing compounds that form stable ternary complexes but show weak binary binding. This method is versatile across various protein targets, featuring a "signal-on" design that only enriches ternary complex inducers, ensuring selective selection. Moreover, this approach eliminates the need for protein immobilization and enables selection on the surface of live cells. We will first develop the methodology using two model systems: FKBP12-rapamycin-FRB and DCAF15-indisulam-RBM39, aiming to demonstrate the selective enrichment of ternary binders and discriminate potential MGs from non-cooperative compounds. We will leverage an array of structurally diverse DELs across three types of selections: MG inhibitors and degraders, MGs that correct loss-of-function missense mutations, and MG homo-dimerizers. Furthermore, we will extend the selection method to membrane protein targets on live cells. Upon identifying promising hits, we will characterize their modes of actions and explore their biological activities. The selected MGs will undergo optimization and evaluation as potential drug candidates. Overall, this proposal aims to develop a rapid and unbiased method utilizing DELs to discover novel small molecule inducers of proximity, with a specific focus on MGs. The identified compounds have potential as drug candidates and chemical tools to enhance our understanding of the mechanisms governing induced proximity in biology. 化學誘導鄰近劑（CIPs）是藉由拉近分子距離以觸發特定細胞反應的精準操控工具，能實現對細胞過程的精確調控。小分子蛋白質-蛋白質相互作用（PPIs）誘導劑，亦稱分子膠（MGs），可強化蛋白質間的直接接觸，進而形成穩定的三元複合物並賦予新穎的生物功能。儘管此類技術在探索基礎生物學及開發針對難治性藥物標靶的治療策略上極具潛力，但由於蛋白質結構的複雜性與多樣性，CIPs與MGs的開發目前仍主要依賴經驗驅動。尤其現有化學骨架之外的新型分子膠發現亟需創新篩選方法，以克服其結構模塊性缺失、結合模式不可預測及構象多樣性等挑戰。 本計畫旨在開發基於DNA編碼庫（DELs）的新方法，選擇性識別能拉近兩蛋白質距離的「三元結合劑」。我們將重點鎖定協同型PPI誘導劑作為潛在分子膠，策略採用蛋白質片段互補技術：促進三元複合物形成的化合物將恢復與標靶蛋白融合的DNA腺嘌呤甲基轉移酶活性，進而對編碼該化合物的DNA標籤進行選擇性甲基化。此外，透過優先篩選能形成穩定三元複合物但二元結合能力較弱的化合物，可鑑別潛在分子膠。此方法具廣泛適用性，其"信號開啟式"設計僅富集三元複合物誘導劑，確保選擇特異性，更無需固定化蛋白質並可直接在活細胞表面進行篩選。 我們將以FKBP12-雷帕黴素-FRB及DCAF15-茚磺酰胺-RBM39兩種模型系統開發方法學，驗證三元結合劑的選擇性富集能力，並區分潛在分子膠與非協同化合物。透過三類篩選模式（分子膠抑制劑與降解劑、校正功能缺失型錯義突變的分子膠、同源二聚體誘導劑）運用結構多樣化的DEL庫，並將篩選延伸至活細胞膜蛋白標靶。對潛力化合物進行作用機制解析與生物活性評估後，所選分子膠將作為候選藥物進行優化驗證。 總體而言，本提案致力建立基於DELs的快速無偏見方法，專注於發現新型小分子鄰近誘導劑（尤重分子膠）。所鑑定化合物兼具候選藥物與化學工具雙重潛力，可深化人類對生物學中誘導鄰近機制的理解。

17301525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17301525.value: 基于硒纳米片的二维异质结可编程光电存储器件用于传感器内压缩

17301525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301525.value: The surge in Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated multidimensional visual information processing and increased high-throughput data collection demands, straining conventional signal processing. Efficient data management is essential for edge AI and traditional sensors for capturing multidimensional visual data require complex hardware and extensive storage, posing challenges for multidimensional imaging. Snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) offers a solution by encoding and compressing multidimensional data into a snapshot, therefore reducing storage and bandwidth requirements. However, existing optical modulators add system complexity and latency. The application of two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials promise fast optoelectronic modulation and integrated functionalities. While 2D sensors have reduced processing loads, lossless visual information compression remains unachieved. Then how to design a novel 2D programmable optoelectronic memory device with integrated sensing and processing capabilities becomes the major bottleneck for highly compact SCI system in edge AI. This project aims to tackle the abovementioned bottleneck by designing and fabricating a 2D programmable optoelectronic memory device based on single-crystalline selenium (Se) nanoflakes. The device is capable of encoding, compressing, and storing electrical/optical signals. Se nanoflake has been recognized as a promising 2D semiconductor for novel optoelectronics. However, the feasibility of constructing a high-performance Se nanoflake-based optoelectronic memory device remains to be demonstrated. Here we propose an effective growth strategy for single-crystalline Se nanoflakes and a device architecture for Se-based programmable optoelectronic memory device that could enable a compact SCI system. Our preliminary results have shown that single-crystalline Se nanoflakes can be grown on both silicon dioxide/silicon (SiO2/Si) and sapphire substrates, from which we successfully fabricated a programmable optoelectronic memory device based on a MoS2/h-BN/Se vdW heterostructure on SiO2/Si substrate. The memory device presents unique electro-optical co-stimulus memory behaviors, which is highly wanted in SCI. Following the comprehensive characterization of Se nanoflakes and memory device performance, the working mechanism of the memory device will be systematically explored. Based on the programmable memory herbivores, we expect to employ it in a highly compact SCI system, particularly for video and spectral SCI applications involving multidimensional signals. The successful accomplishment of this project will contribute a high-quality 2D semiconducting nanocrystal to 2D family, benefiting the advanced electronic and optoelectronic communities. Moreover, the demonstration of 2D programmable optoelectronic memory enabled by Se nanoflakes for highly compact SCI could provide groundbreaking inspiration for developing compact and efficient optoelectronic sensors, driving the advancement of edge intelligent vision systems in the future.

17301725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17301725.value: 分数陈绝缘体的量子多体研究

17301725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301725.value: Unlike conventional orders, topological orders, manifested in fractional Chern Insulator (FCI) and fractional quantum Hall states, transcend Landau’s symmetry-breaking paradigm and give rise to unprecedented phenomena, such as anyons, fractional particles, and non-abelian fractional statistics. Traditionally, due to their distinct physical origins, topological and conventional Landau-type orders are perceived as competitors, i.e., establishing one implies demolishing the other. However, there exists the intriguing possibility of them coexisting cooperatively. For many years, such suggested coexisting states predominantly remained a theoretical concept. However, recent advancements in observing FCIs in i). twisted MoTe2 bilayers [Nature 622, 63 (2023), 622, 69 (2023), 622, 74 (2023), PRX 13, 031037 (2023)], and in ii). multilayer graphene [Nature 626, 759 (2024)], have escalated the concept of such coexistence to a new and realistic level. These ground-breaking experimental results provide a unique opportunity to delve into the fascinating interplay between topological and conventional orders. The PI will employ advanced numerical methods in this project to study the emerging phases and phase transitions in FCI lattice models. The numerical toolset we utilized includes not only standard methods like density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and exact diagonalization (ED) but also the reliable and efficient momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) and exponential tensor renormalization group (XTRG) and tangent space tensor renormalization group (tanTRG) methods, which are capable of probing dynamic and finite-temperature properties. Because experimental studies are all conducted at finite temperatures, our methods are essential to address the dynamic and thermodynamic experimentally measurable quantities. With these advanced methods, the PI will investigate: i). The intertwinement of topological order and Landau order and discovers the emergent forms of FCI states. Along this line, we will address the questions of how and why the charge density wave order coexists with the uniform FCI states and how the fractional and integer Hall conductance interchange due to such coexistence, furthermore, we will explore the thermal and quantum phase transitions from such intertwined state to other conventional phases; ii). The collective excitations in both fermionic and bosonic FCIs and their role in tuning FCI transitions. We will understand the fundamental connection between FCI states in the aforementioned recent experiments and the fractional quantum Hall states, and look for the signature of the collective excitations in these states such as magnetoroton, chiral graviton, and their interplay with the quantum metric and experimental setting in moire flat bands and cold bosonic atoms. 与传统的序秩不同，拓扑序在分数量子霍尔（FQH）和分数陈绝缘体（FCI）中表现出来，超越了朗道的对称破缺范式，带来了前所未有的现象，如任意子、分数粒子和非阿贝尔分数量统计。传统上，由于它们的物理起源不同，拓扑序和经典的朗道型序通常被视为竞争关系，即建立其中一种序意味着破坏另一种序。然而，存在一种引人入胜的可能性，即它们可以协同共存。 多年来，这种共存状态大多仍然是理论上的猜想。然而，近年来在观察到FCI的实验进展中，i) 在扭转的MoTe2双层材料中（Nature 622, 63（2023）；622, 69（2023）；622, 74（2023））以及 ii) 在多层石墨烯中（Nature 626, 759（2024）），将这种共存的概念推向了一个新的、更加现实的层面。这些突破性的实验结果为深入研究拓扑序与常规序的相互作用提供了宝贵的机遇。 项目负责人将采用先进的数值方法，研究FCI晶格模型中的新兴相和相变。我们使用的数值工具包括密度矩阵重整化群（DMRG）和精确对角化（ED），以及可靠高效的动量空间量子蒙特卡洛（QMC）、指数张量重整化群（XTRG）和切空间张量重整化群（tanTRG）方法。这些方法能够探测动力学和有限温度性质，特别适合应对实验中在有限温度条件下测量的动态和热力学量。

17301825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17301825.value: 更少標籤的深度學習：算法進展與理論基礎

17301825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301825.value: In recent years, deep learning has revolutionized the field of machine learning through a series of remarkable achievements. After sufficient training on labeled datasets, deep neural networks can achieve high prediction accuracy in various tasks such as natural language processing and image recognition. However, the complexity and large parameter count of modern neural networks often demand a large amount of labeled data, posing challenges as obtaining labeled data can sometimes be costly and labor-intensive. This project aims to explore methods that can mitigate the need for extensive labeled data in deep learning. Many learning tasks involve data across multiple modalities, such as images associated with captions and CT images associated with clinical data. To effectively utilize such multimodal data, the first part of the proposed project will focus on developing efficient active learning methods for deep learning on multimodal data. Novel algorithms combining active learning with multimodal contrastive learning will be proposed to reduce label complexity by jointly utilizing information from different modalities and actively selecting the most informative training examples for labeling. In addition, modern learning tasks frequently involve data associated with graphs; for example, research paper data can directly lead to a citation graph. In the second part of the proposed study, the PI will also develop methods that leverage the inherent graph structures of data to reduce label complexity. Specifically, novel training algorithms for graph attention networks (GATs) will be proposed, with a focus on enhancing the performance of GATs on larger graphs with fewer labeled nodes. All proposed algorithms will be theoretically supported with optimization and learning guarantees and will be evaluated based on real-data experiments. Success in the proposed research will lead to novel neural network training methods that can achieve satisfactory learning performance even when the number of labeled data is limited. The proposed algorithms will also be integrated into packages and software tools with open access, which can potentially be utilized across diverse domains, including image/text classification and genomics analysis. 近年來，深度學習憑藉一系列卓越成就，為機器學習領域帶來了革新。在有標籤數據集上進行充分訓練後，深度神經網絡能在自然語言處理、影像識別等各種任務中達到高準確度。然而，現代神經網絡的複雜性及龐大的參數數量，往往對有標籤的數據有極大的需求，這造成了挑戰，因為獲取標籤數據有時既昂貴又耗費人力。本項目旨在探索能減少深度學習對大量標籤數據需求的方法。 許多學習任務涉及跨多種模態的數據，例如帶有描述的圖片、與臨床數據相關的電腦斷層掃描（CT）影像。為了有效利用這類多模態數據，本項目的第一部分將聚焦於針對多模態數據的深度學習，開發高效的主動式學習方法。我們將提出結合主動式學習與多模態對比學習的新型演算法，透過共同利用不同模態的資訊並主動選擇最具資訊性的訓練樣本進行標註，以降低標籤複雜度。此外，現代學習任務也常常涉及與圖結構相關的數據，例如論文數據可直接形成引用圖。在本項目第二部分，我們亦將開發利用數據內在圖結構來減少標籤複雜度的方法。具體而言，我們將提出針對圖注意力網絡（GATs）的新型訓練演算法，重點提升圖注意力網絡在大型圖且標籤節點較少時的表現。我們將對提出的方法提供最佳化與學習成效的理論保證，並以真實數據上的實驗結果為標準，對本項目提出的方法進行評估。 本研究若能成功，將促成創新的神經網絡訓練方法，即使在標籤數據有限的情況下，亦能取得令人滿意的學習表現。所提出的方法亦將整合於開放存取的軟體套件中，未來可望應用於影像／文本分類及基因組分析等多個領域。

17302025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17302025.value: 間歇性河流系統的碳生物地球化學循環與溫室氣體動態研究

17302025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302025.value: River systems play a crucial role in the global carbon (C) cycle, functioning as significant sources of greenhouse gases (GHGs) for the atmosphere. Total carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) emissions from global river networks are estimated at 1.8-2.3 PgC yr^-1, which is of the same order of magnitude as the global land C sink. Furthermore, river systems are important emitters of nitrous oxide (N2O). Nevertheless, due to the lack of spatially resolved sampling in many river networks worldwide, our current understanding of the biogeochemical processes regulating the riverine C cycle remains limited and the available GHG fluxes are largely uncertain. This is particularly true for intermittent rivers and ephemeral streams (IRES), which comprise over half of global river length. Notably, the prevalence of IRES is increasing in many regions due to global change. Previous studies on riverine C cycling and GHG dynamics have primarily focused on flowing rivers, whereas IRES systems characterized by recurrent flow cessation and complex C cycling processes have been seldom studied. Therefore, we urgently need to investigate GHG emissions from IRES and examine their interactions with hydrological and biogeochemical factors. Understanding the underlying mechanisms that govern their C biogeochemistry and GHG dynamics is critical for refining the estimates of GHG emissions from global river networks. This project will conduct a comparative study of C biogeochemistry and GHG emissions in representative IRES under contrasting settings of climate, hydrology, and human disturbance across the semiarid Heihe River and subtropical Kam Tin River basins in China. We aim to quantitatively investigate the spatiotemporal variability of C biogeochemistry and GHG emissions within IRES systems through a river network-scale approach. Furthermore, we also aim to explore the environmental and anthropogenic controls on biogeochemical C cycling, and examine the taxonomic composition and activity of the microbial community that govern the biogeochemical cycling of C and nitrogen (N) and resulting GHG emissions. The expected results will deepen our mechanistic understanding of C biogeochemistry and GHG emissions in IRES and help unravel the significance of IRES in the global C cycle. This will be one of the first integrated research projects to investigate C biogeochemistry and GHG emissions in IRES under contrasting environmental settings. We will critically analyze C and N cycling processes and GHG dynamics in representative IRES systems and assess their biogeochemical implications. Comparative studies involving contrasting environmental settings will enable us to better comprehend their responses to future global change. 河流系統在全球碳（C）循環中扮演著至關重要的角色，且是大氣系統中溫室氣體（GHGs）的重要來源。全球河流系統的二氧化碳（CO₂）和甲烷（CH₄）排放總量約為18-23億頓碳/年，該排放量在數量級上與全球陸地碳匯通量相當。此外，河流系統還是溫室氣體氧化亞氮（N₂O）的重要排放源。然而，由於缺乏高分辨率的空間采樣數據以及全球河流系統的廣泛分布，目前對河流碳循環生物地球化學過程調控機理的認識仍十分有限。現有的溫室氣體排放通量結果也存在較大誤差，尤其是對於間歇性河流（IRES）而言更是如此。盡管間歇性河流占據全球河流長度的一半以上，但對其水體碳循環的相關研究仍十分缺乏。以往針對河流碳循環和溫室氣體動態的研究主要集中於常流性河流，而間歇性河流系統因其徑流周期性中斷，其碳循環過程更為復雜，目前尚未得到充分研究。這些IRES系統在水文特性上與常流性河流存在顯著差異，通常表現出不同的碳生物地球化學循環特征。因此，迫切需要開展針對IRES系統的溫室氣體排放研究，並分析其與水文及生物地球化學因素的相互作用。理解其碳生物地球化學循環過程和溫室氣體排放的調控機製也對於提高全球河流系統溫室氣體排放通量估算精度具有重要意義。 本課題擬在位於中國半乾旱氣候的黑河流域和亞熱帶氣候的錦田河流域，選取具有不同氣候、水文和人為幹擾條件的代表性IRES系統開展綜合對比研究。通過廣泛的現場實測采樣，我們將定量分析IRES系統中碳生物地球化學循環過程和溫室氣體排放的時空變化。此外，該課題還將探討不同環境因素和人為擾動因素對碳生物地球化學循環過程的控製機理，並分析微生物群落的分類組成，揭示其對有機碳生物地球化學循環及溫室氣體排放的影響。研究結果將深化對IRES系統中碳生物地球化學循環和溫室氣體排放機製的認識，揭示IRES系統在全球碳循環中的重要性。 該研究課題是針對不同環境條件下系統地闡述間歇性河流系統中碳生物地球化學循環和溫室氣體排放的首批綜合研究項目之一。基於該項目的研究結果，我們將全面而深入地分析代表性間歇性河流生態系統的碳循環過程和溫室氣體動態，進而評估其生物地球化學意義。通過對比研究不同環境背景下間歇性河流的碳循環過程，該課題研究結果也將有助於我們更準確地理解間歇性河流生態系統的碳循環過程對未來全球變化的響應。

17302525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17302525.value: 關於反對易晶體對稱性及其保護的拓撲相的理論研究

17302525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302525.value: Symmetry is a core concept in almost all areas of quantum physics, ranging from condensed matter to high-energy physics. For a quantum system, a symmetry usually corresponds to an operator that commutes with the Hamiltonian. However, for one-body systems, it is also possible for symmetry operators to anti-commute with the Hamiltonian. Examples include the particle-hole symmetries of superconductors and the sublattice symmetries of quantum materials. Notably, by incorporating anti-commuting symmetries, Dyson's threefold-way symmetry classes have been extended into the tenfold symmetry classes by Altland and Zirnbauer, with seven of these classes containing anti-commuting symmetries. The importance of anti-commuting symmetries in forming topological matter is evident when considering the fundamental status of the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors, established within the framework of the ten Altland-Zirnbauer symmetry classes (AZ classes). Given the fundamental importance of anti-commuting symmetries in topological phases, the current theory of anti-commuting symmetry is quite limited within the framework of the tenfold AZ classes and is incapable of addressing general cases of anti-commuting symmetries in crystals. The main reason for this limitation is that the anti-commuting symmetries are regarded as internal symmetries and, therefore, cannot capture the intrinsic spatial nature of crystal symmetries. This limitation has been illustrated in our recent work [Nat. Comm. 15, 3787 (2024)], where the spatial nature of sublattice symmetries is revealed, consequently leading to completely different topological classifications. This project is devoted to clarifying anti-commuting symmetries in crystals, or crystalline anti-commuting symmetries, and exploring novel topological phases protected by these unconventional crystalline symmetry classes. Specifically, we plan to address the following points: (i) to provide a general characterization and exhaust all crystalline symmetry classes for both unitary and anti-unitary anti-commuting symmetries within the framework of projective crystal symmetries; (ii) to formulate topological indexes for characterizing stable zero modes protected by crystalline anti-commuting symmetries; (iii) to apply the formulated topological indexes to explore novel topological zero modes in higher-order topological insulators/superconductors and disclinations of crystalline topological insulators/superconductors; and (iv) to address the experimental realization of these novel symmetry classes and to construct models for the discovered novel topological phases. In summary, this project will lay the theoretical foundation for crystalline anti-commuting symmetries, offer practical technical tools for exploring novel topological zero modes protected by them, and pave the way for their physical realizations. We hope that the project will open new avenues for both quantum and metamaterial design and unconventional superconductivity. 對稱性是幾乎所有量子物理領域的核心概念，範圍從凝聚態物理到高能物理。對於一個量子系統來說，對稱性通常對應於與哈密頓量對易的算符。然而，對於單體系統，也可能存在與哈密頓量反對易的對稱算符。例如，超導體的粒子-空洞對稱性以及晶體的亞格子對稱性就是此類例子。值得注意的是，通過引入反對易對稱性，戴森（Dyson）提出的三重分類已被Altland和Zirnbauer擴展為十重分類，其中七類包含反對易對稱性。在形成拓撲物質方面，反對易對稱性的重要性顯而易見，在十重對稱類別框架下建立的拓撲絕緣體和超導體拓撲分類週期表在拓撲物態領域具有基本地位。 鑑於反對易對稱性在拓撲相中的重要性，目前關於反對稱性的理論在十重分類框架下仍相當有限，且無法處理晶體中一般的反對易對稱性情況。造成這一不足的主要原因是，在十重分類中反對稱性被視為內部對稱，因此無法刻劃晶體對稱本征的空間屬性。我們在最新的研究中（Nat. Comm. 15, 3787 (2024)）已經揭示了亞格子對稱性的空間性質，並因此導出完全不同的拓撲分類表。 本項目旨在澄清晶體或晶體中的反對易對稱性以及探索由這些非常規晶體對稱性類別所保護的新型拓撲相。具體而言，我們計畫解決以下幾個問題：(i) 在投影晶體對稱性框架下，對幺正和反幺正的反對易晶體對稱性類別進行一般性描述；(ii) 制定用於表徵由反對易對晶體稱性保護的穩定零模的拓撲指標；(iii) 將所制定的拓撲指標應用於探索高階拓撲絕緣體/超導體中的新型拓撲零模，以及晶體拓撲絕緣體/超導體中的缺陷；(iv) 研究這些新型對稱性類別的實驗實現途徑，並構建相應的模型來描述發現的拓撲新相。 總之，這個項目將奠定反對易晶體對稱性的理論基礎，提供用於探索由其保護的新型拓撲零模的實用技術工具，並為其物理實現鋪平道路。我們希望這個項目能為量子材料或超材料設計以及非常規超導現象開啟新的研究途徑。

17303325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17303325.value: 分子機器中的機械化學耦合作用

17303325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303325.value: Active matter is a captivating field of study characterized by systems that exhibit unique properties distinct from the traditional matter at thermodynamic equilibrium, driven by self-propelling basic units with energy dissipation. The key feature of active matter is that its basic building unit can self-propel with energy dissipation. In this research, we try to answer one fundamental question: can a single molecule swim? In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing synthetic active matter based on micro/nanoparticles. By dissipating energy harvested from the environment, these synthetic active particles, with sizes ranging from 100nm to a few micrometers, can self-propel and interact with surrounding particles non-reciprocally similar to motile bacteria and cells. However, further scaling down the artificial active matter to the molecular scale, while holding fundamental importance and potential for broad applications, has proved challenging. It is highly controversial in physics whether the self-propulsion can be created at the molecular scale. While nature provides excellent examples of molecular-scale active matter, such as motor proteins, it does not show swimming ability. The development of molecular machines, which was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2016, has made remarkable progress. However, the ability to free-swim has not yet been realized. While many hypothetical mechanisms have been proposed, it is still under hot debate in the scientific community whether the chemomechanical coupling may be sufficient to create directional propulsion. A new mechanism that enables chemical energy conversion into mechanical propulsion at the molecular scale with a simple molecular structure and can be universally applicable is still highly desired. This proposed research aims to expand our expertise in micro/nanoparticle-based active matter to explore molecular-scale chemomechanics. Our approach involves reversible photochemical reactions as a model system to develop a general molecular-scale artificial active matter. By studying the spatial fluctuation of fluorescent molecules within the redox-active photochemical system, this research aims to provide a new understanding of how mechanical motion may be generated at the molecular scale. In addition, this research aims to provide a new kind of molecular machine that can generate self-propell via non-reciprocal interactions between reaction centers, which can be further developed into basic building blocks for molecular machines. 活性物質是一個吸引人的全新研究領域，其特徵在於系統展現出與傳統熱力學平衡物質截然不同的獨特性質，這些系統由具有自主推進能力的基本單元驅動，並伴隨能量耗散。此研究深入探討一個根本性問題：單分子是否能夠自主「游動」。 儘管基於微米/奈米顆粒的合成活性物質已引起廣泛關注，但將活性自驅動縮小至分子層級仍面臨挑戰。自然界中雖存在分子尺度活性物質的範例（如馬達蛋白），但實現分子自由游動仍屬未解之謎。本研究旨在透過可逆光化學反應探索分子尺度的化學機械學，以建立一種通用的分子尺度人工活性物質系統。藉由分析氧化還原活性光化學模型中螢光分子的在空間中的擾動，此研究試圖揭示分子尺度下機械運動的生成機制，並透過反應中心間的非互易相互作用開發自推進分子機器。 這項創新研究計畫奠基於現有的微/奈米顆粒活性物質專業知識，開拓分子尺度化學機械學的前沿。以可逆光化學反應作為模型系統，研究將闡明分子層級機械運動生成的基礎機制。對螢光分子在氧化還原活性光化學系統中的隨機擾動的深入分析，將為「透過非互惠相互作用實現自推進分子機器」的設計提供關鍵信息。 最終目標是開發一類新型分子機器，其能以簡單的分子結構將化學能轉化為定向推進力，並在活性物質物理學領域探索其應用潛力，為未來技術革新奠定分子層級的理論與實踐基礎。

17303725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17303725.value: 化学气相沉积合成二维导电金属有机框架及电子器件应用

17303725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303725.value: The modern electronics have big impact on our daily lives, but which have been mainly dominated by silicon electronics and organic electronics. Is there any other material to balance the requirements and the performance meanwhile showing good stability? We highlight that two-dimensional conjugated metal-organic frameworks (2D c-MOFs) shall be rising as promising electroactive materials for electronics due to their intrinsic conductivity, adjustable band gap, and high carrier mobility. The concept is shaped as “MOFtronics”. However, it remains a grant challenge to achieve dimension-controlled MOF films with high charge transport, which thus enables for the reliable integration of electronic device compatible with current complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology. To address this synthetic challenge, this proposal targets to develop conducting 2D c-MOF films via vapor-induced interfacial synthesis under chemical vapor deposition (CVD) conditions. Here, we will employ conjugated planar ligands modified with -OH, -SH and -NH2 functional groups for the construction of 2D c-MOFs via coordination with transition metals. During the CVD synthesis, we will tailor the interactions between ligand vapor and various substrates as well as the ligand-nucleus interactions, thus controlling the diffusion kinetics of the ligands and the subsequent growth kinetics of 2D c-MOF crystals. The critical issue is to achieve ordered 2D pre-organization of the ligands by considering the rational design of ligands and the interfacial assembly strategies. We will establish a deep understanding on relationship between ligand design, on-surface ligand assembly and subsequent ordered 2D coordination polymerization. In this case, we expect to build up a scalable but reliable interfacial synthesis strategy for achieving the dimensional control and the high crystallinity of 2D c-MOF films, thus also pushing the development of interfacial chemistry for advanced functional materials. As contrast, we will also employ Langmuir-Blodgett (LB) assisted synthesis and soft-template assisted interfacial synthesis towards few-layer or monolayer films. Furthermore, the resultant 2D c-MOF film samples will be integrated into model electronic devices for the charge transport studies. A systematic research will be performed to unveil the influence of molecular design, crystallinity, layer stacking and interfacial coupling on charge transport performance and the relevant transport mechanisms. As a consequence, we will establish a reliable structure-property relationship, which will offer the opportunities for the future development and applications of MOF-based electronics. 现代电子技术对我们的日常生活影响深远，其中主要以硅电子技术和有机电子技术为主。是否有其他电子材料能够兼顾柔性、离电协同输运等多样化需求和高输运性能，同时保持优异的稳定性？二维共轭金属有机框架(2D c-MOF)具有本征导电、带隙可调和高载流子迁移率等特性，是二维电子材料领域的新兴热点，有望成为满足上述需求的电子材料。然而，如何制备尺寸可控、高载流子输运的高质量2D c-MOF薄膜，并实现与当前CMOS技术兼容，从而构建高性能电子器件，仍然是一项巨大的挑战。为了应对这一挑战，本项目聚焦化学气相沉积合成2D c-MOF薄膜及其电子器件应用基础研究，将采用-OH、-SH和-NH2官能团修饰的共轭平面配体，通过与过渡金属配位，在CVD条件下构建二维c-MOF。本项目将研究气相前驱体分子在不同衬底表面的传递、吸附和组装行为，揭示前驱体和不同衬底、前驱体和初晶核的界面相互作用，调控MOF晶体生长的动力学过程，明晰前驱体分子设计、衬底表面分子组装与二维有序配位聚合的适配规律，建立气相诱导界面合成2D c-MOF膜的普适性方法；发展Langmuir-Blodgett (LB)辅助预组装与CVD原位聚合的联用策略，建立预组装调控2D c-MOF单层膜构筑的新方法；通过多种界面合成方法的开拓，实现维度可控的高结晶薄膜，推动表界面化学在有序功能材料合成中的应用；构建2D c-MOF薄膜电子器件，阐明前驱体分子设计、拓扑态、堆叠结构、范德华异质结构等对电荷输运性能影响，建立构效关系，为2D c-MOF在电子器件领域的应用提供理论支撑。

17303825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17303825.value: 朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想

17303825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303825.value: A fundamental problem in the theory of network coding is the Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture, which, roughly speaking, states that for a directed strongly reachable multiple unicast network with k pairs of senders and receivers, the transmission rate via network coding is not greater than that via bidirectional routing. Interestingly, this conjecture can be reformulated as a multi-flow problem under the so-called "reachability conditions", as opposed to the "cut conditions" that have been extensively studied in the theory of multi-flows. Over the years, the Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture has been persistently resistant to numerous attacks, making it one of the most challenging problems in the field. To the best of our knowledge, the conjecture has, thus far, been proven to be true only for very special cases. Employing the linearization method we developed over the past several years, we recently showed that the Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture holds true for a strongly reachable k-pair network under the assumption that it has a special form of collapsed backbone. We believe that networks with a collapsed backbone are "elementary and primitive", serving as a basis for studying networks with more general configurations. As such, we plan to further study networks with a collapsed backbone and aim to combine the results to resolve the Langberg and Medard multiple unicast conjecture, which is one of the ultimate objectives of this proposal. The Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture pertains to directed networks. In this proposal, we formulate a counterpart conjecture for undirected networks, which can be regarded as an undirected version of the original Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture. To resolve this undirected version is another ultimate objective of this proposal. Similarly as above, we intend to first study networks with a collapsed backbone to see if the results can be instrumental for general networks. Another strategy that we may adopt is to adapt and improve the linearization method we developed for directed networks to undirected networks. We have dedicated several years to this area of research, resulting in numerous preliminary findings that are promising for further extension and generalization. If successfully executed in the end, this proposal will resolve both the directed and undirected versions of the long standing Langberg-Medard multiple unicast conjecture. By significantly enhancing our understanding of information transmission and commodity flows across networks, this proposal will have far-reaching implications in both theory and practice. 在網路編碼理論中，一個基本問題是 朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想。粗略地說，該猜想指出：對於一個具備強可達性的有向多重單播網路，若有 k 對發送者與接收者，則透過網路編碼的傳輸速率不會高於透過雙向路由的傳輸速率。 有趣的是，這一猜想可以在所謂的「可達性條件」下重新表述為一個多流問題，而非傳統多流理論中廣泛研究的「割條件」。多年來，朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想始終難以攻克，成為該領域最具挑戰性的問題之一。據我們所知，目前僅在極少數特殊情況下證明該猜想成立。 我們在過去幾年中所發展的線性化方法，最近證明了：在具有特殊形式的「塌縮骨幹」結構的強可達 k 對網路中，朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想是成立的。我們認為，具有塌縮骨幹的網路是「基本且原始」的，可作為研究更一般網路結構的基礎。因此，我們計劃進一步研究具有塌縮骨幹的網路，並希望結合研究成果來解決朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想，這也是本提案的最終目標之一。 朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想是針對有向網路提出的。在本提案中，我們也為無向網路提出了一個對應的猜想，可視為原始猜想的無向版本。解決這一無向版本也是本提案的另一個最終目標。同樣地，我們打算首先研究具有塌縮骨幹的網路，以探討其結果是否能對一般網路提供幫助。另一個可能採取的策略是將我們為有向網路所開發的線性化方法加以改進並應用於無向網路。 我們已在此研究領域投入數年時間，並取得了許多具潛力的初步成果，有望進一步擴展與推廣。若本提案最終成功執行，將可解決長期懸而未決的朗伯格－梅達爾多重單播猜想的有向與無向版本。透過大幅提升我們對資訊傳輸與商品流在網路中運作的理解，本提案將在理論與實務層面產生深遠影響。

17303925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17303925.value: 研究有孔蟲環境 DNA 在重建鹽沼和紅樹林環境中晚全新世相對海平面的效用。

17303925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17303925.value: Prof Schunter, Celia Prof Yasuhara, Moriaki

17303925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303925.value: There are open questions regarding the trends and mechanisms of mid to late Holocene relative sea-level (RSL) changes. Although a dense network of high-resolution RSL reconstructions has been generated from salt marsh foraminifera along North Atlantic coastlines, there is a paucity of precise RSL constraints from beyond this region in low- latitude and southern hemisphere locations, which contributes to these knowledge gaps. Foraminiferal tests suffer from poor or selective preservation in tropical and arid environments that dominate low-latitude and southern hemisphere locations, which encompass many regions that are sensitive to ice sheet melt and thus are important for understanding the behavior of ice sheets. This problem in part stems from the traditional methods used to identify and enumerate foraminiferal assemblages where taxonomic assignments are made on the basis of test morphology. Environmental DNA (eDNA) refers to DNA extracted from environmental samples (soil, sediment, air, water) without isolation of target organisms and eDNA applications have been gaining traction in recent years because the approach is able to overcome limitations with traditional monitoring/surveying methods that rely on physical methods of identification. The eDNA method may have advantages over traditional foraminiferal counting techniques because it can reveal greater species diversity (e.g. from soft-walled or 'naked' taxa that do not readily fossilize), and foraminiferal eDNA may be better preserved than their tests (shells), which are necessary for morphological analyses. Here we investigate the utility of a novel approach using environmental DNA to reconstruct past environmental conditions and RSL changes in two settings: (1) salt marshes of the United States Atlantic Coast, an area well-established in the production of high-resolution, foraminiferal-based RSL reconstructions, and (2) mangroves of the South China Sea, the type of area with the greatest potential need for this method due to poor preservation of foraminiferal tests. At each site, we will develop modern foraminiferal training sets using DNA metabarcoding, which will be used to interpret sediment archives and reconstruct past tidal elevation. Results from this novel approach will be compared to those from traditional methods. If effective, this technique may provide a tool to develop improved constraints on the behaviour of RSL from low- latitudes during the mid- to late-Holocene, which will lead to better characterization of the rates, patterns, and mechanisms of pre- and post-industrial sea-level change. 關於中晚全新世相對海平面 (RSL) 變化的趨勢和機制，仍存在一些懸而未決的問題。儘管人們已經從北大西洋沿岸的鹽沼有孔蟲中構建出了一個密集的高分辨率RSL重建網絡，但在低緯度和南半球地區，該地區以外的精確RSL約束仍然匱乏，這加劇了這些知識空白。在低緯度和南半球地區占主導地位的熱帶和乾旱環境中，有孔蟲樣本保存不佳或存在選擇性，而這些地區包含許多對冰蓋融化敏感的區域，因此對於理解冰蓋的行為至關重要。這個問題部分源自於傳統的有孔蟲群落辨識和計數方法，這些方法是基於樣本形態進行分類。環境DNA（eDNA）是指從環境樣本（土壤、沉積物、空氣、水）中提取的DNA，無需分離目標生物。近年來，eDNA的應用越來越受到關注，因為這種方法能夠克服傳統監測/調查方法的局限性，這些方法依賴通常具有侵入性和破壞性的物理識別方法。 本文探討了一種利用環境DNA重建過去環境條件和RSL變化的新方法，該方法在兩種環境下的實用性：(1) 美國大西洋沿岸的鹽沼，該地區在高分辨率有孔蟲RSL重建方面經驗豐富；(2) 南海的紅樹林，由於有孔蟲樣本保存較差，該地區最有可能需要這種方法。在每個地點，我們將使用DNA宏條碼技術開發現代有孔蟲訓練集，用於解釋沉積物檔案並重建過去的潮位高度。我們將把這種新方法的結果與傳統方法的結果進行比較。如果有效，該技術可能成為一種工具，用於改進中晚全新世低緯度地區RSL行為的約束條件，從而更好地表徵工業化前後海平面變化的速率、模式和機制。

17304025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304025.value: 人類世海洋富營養化與缺氧及其對亞洲超大城市鄰近海域底棲生態系統的影響——以東京灣介形蟲微體化石為古生態代用指標的研究

17304025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304025.value: The Anthropocene is a time when human impacts on the planet exceed the ability of the Earth System to recover itself both regionally and globally, with notably negative effects on terrestrial and marine ecosystems. A major factor in the degradation of Anthropocene marine ecosystems is eutrophication and deoxygenation, widely studied in North America and Europe, and now becoming one of the most serious marine problems in eastern and southeastern Asia. A deep understanding of long-term impacts of eutrophication and deoxygenation on marine ecosystems relies on the paleontological and geochemical records in sediment cores in coastal marine areas, in combination with historical records and observational data. Here we attempt to analyze the ecological impact of human development in the Tokyo Bay area, the marine embayment adjacent to the world’s largest metropolitan area. Although there is a detailed history of this region from medieval times to the present, and especially for the period of explosive population growth in the 20th century, Tokyo Bay itself has seldom been studied from a conservation paleobiology perspective, i.e., the use of sediment core and microscopic sized fossil to understand long-term history of marine community and ecosystem under progressive eutrophication and deoxygenation. Here, we plan to collect sediment cores from six sites in Tokyo Bay that will provide a high-resolution record of the past 100 years of environmental impact during the Anthropocene, but that will also sample the previous Holocene record to reconstruct the natural ecosystem baseline, before major human impacts. Paleoecological and geochemical analyses and radiometric dating will be conducted on these cores. Our paleo reconstruction of a deep history of ecological impact of human-induced eutrophication in Tokyo Bay will provide an understanding of the natural biome and early and late-stage human impacts, all of which are essential to understand if the ecosystem and biodiversity of this region is to be protected and restored. Our approach can provide a model for understanding how human impacts on the marine biosphere unfold, useful for management and conservation in Tokyo Bay, and for ecosystem planning in the coastal systems of the entire East and Southeast Asian region, which now contains many of the world’s great coastal megacities, including Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Manila and Jakarta. 人類世是一個人類活動對地球的影響超出區域和全球生態系統自我恢復能力的時代，對陸地和海洋生態系統造成了顯著的負面效應。在人類世海洋生態系統退化過程中，富營養化與脫氧作用作為主要因素，已在北美和歐洲得到廣泛研究，如今正成為東亞與東南亞地區最嚴峻的海洋環境問題之一。深入理解富營養化與脫氧作用對海洋生態系統的長期影響，需要結合海岸帶沈積物巖芯中的古生物學與地球化學記錄、歷史文獻資料及現代觀測數據。本研究擬以全球最大都市圈毗鄰海域東京灣為研究對象，系統分析人類發展對海洋生態的影響。盡管該地區存有中世紀至今（特別是20世紀人口爆炸式增長時期）的詳細歷史記錄，但鮮有從保護古生物學視角（即利用沈積巖芯與微體化石解析漸進式富營養化與脫氧條件下海洋群落及生態系統的長期演變歷史）開展的研究。本研究計劃在東京灣六處點位采集沈積物巖芯，這些巖芯一方面將提供過去100年人類世時期高分辨率的環境影響記錄，另一方面也將鉆取更早的全新世沈積層段，用以重建主要人類活動幹擾發生前的自然生態系統基線。通過對巖芯開展古生態學和地球化學分析及放射性定年，我們將重建東京灣人類活動誘發富營養化的完整生態影響史，揭示自然生物群落特征及不同階段的人類影響機製。這些認知對於該區域生態系統與生物多樣性的保護修復至關重要。本研究構建的方法體系可為解析人類活動對海洋生物圈的影響機製提供範式，既服務於東京灣的生態管理保護實踐，也可為整個東亞與東南亞海岸帶生態系統規劃提供參考——該區域現已成為全球沿海超大城市（包括香港、上海、新加坡、馬尼拉及雅加達等）的密集分布區。

17304225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304225.value: 重尾協方差型隨機矩陣的極值特徵值

17304225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304225.value: In Multivariate Statistics, three fundamental random matrix models—sample covariance matrix, sample correlation matrix, and sample canonical correlation matrix—are used to infer the covariance structure, correlation structure of a random vector, and the cross-correlation structure of two random vectors, respectively. They are well-defined as long as the second moment of the matrix entries exists. The extreme eigenvalues of these matrices are particularly important in Principal Component Analysis and Canonical Correlation Analysis. However, in high-dimensional scenarios, the limiting behavior of these eigenvalues has been understood mainly in the light-tailed regime. Meanwhile, in Random Matrix Theory, important tools have been developed for the spectral statistics of heavy-tailed random matrices recently. Hence, we are at a stage to further extend these tools to establish the limiting behavior of the extreme eigenvalues of the mentioned random matrices in the heavy-tailed regime. 在多元統計學中，三類基礎隨機矩陣模型——樣本協方差矩陣、樣本相關矩陣與樣本典型相關矩陣——分別用於推斷隨機向量的協方差結構、相關結構，以及兩個隨機向量間的交叉相關結構。只要矩陣元素的二階矩存在，這些模型即具明確定義。這些矩陣的最大最小特徵值在主成分分析與典型相關分析中尤為關鍵。然於高維情境下，此類特徵值的極限行為迄今主要於輕尾分佈領域獲得理解。與此同時，隨機矩陣理論近期針對重尾隨機矩陣的譜統計量發展出重要工具。因此，現階段我們得以進一步延伸這些工具，為前述重尾分佈區域的隨機矩陣極端特徵值建立極限行為理論。

17304325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304325.value: 單晶鎳基超合金之高溫動態拉伸行為及微觀結構演化

17304325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17304325.value: Prof Huang, Mingxin Dr Zhang, Jingyu

17304325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304325.value: Single crystal Ni-based superalloys are crucial materials for high-temperature applications, such as turbine blades in aero engines. Their excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures stem from the precipitation of an intermetallic phase γ’ within a solid solution phase matrix γ. During service, turbine blades may encounter impact loads from foreign objects, compromising the safety of aero-engine operations. Therefore, it is essential to study the dynamic behaviour of single crystal Ni-based superalloys at elevated temperatures. Despite this importance, the microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms of these superalloys under such extreme conditions remain unexplored. This lack of knowledge hinders material performance prediction and engineering design. This project aims to address three key scientific issues: (1) the relationship between microstructural evolution and mechanical behaviour in single crystal Ni-based superalloys under dynamic tension at high temperatures; (2) the influence of the interaction between γ and γ' phases on the microstructural evolution; and (3) the development of a microstructure-based model to simulate the mechanical behaviour. Firstly, single crystal Ni-based superalloy DD98M samples and single crystal samples with chemical compositions similar to those of the γ and γ' phases present in DD98M will be prepared. The dynamic response at high temperatures will be assessed using the split Hopkinson tensile bar. To study microstructural evolution, samples will be deformed to various strain levels under dynamic tension using a momentum-trap technique. Secondly, a multi-scale microstructure analysis will be conducted from the micro-meter to atomic levels. Neutron diffraction techniques will be employed to determine dislocation density and configuration. Advanced microscopy techniques will be used to characterise γ/γ' interface, dislocation structures and solute-atom segregation at dislocations to elucidate the dynamic behaviour of DD98M at high temperatures. Finally, a crystal plasticity finite element model will be developed by incorporating the dynamic responses of the γ and γ' phases and dislocation evolution to simulate the DD98M’s dynamic response at high temperatures. The interaction between the γ and γ' phases and its impact on microstructural evolution and overall dynamic behaviour will be unveiled through experimental and simulated findings. The successful completion of this project will lead to a thorough understanding of the dynamic response of single crystal Ni-based superalloys at elevated temperatures. This research is particularly important as the outcomes will facilitate the improved design of high-temperature components and propel the advancement of next-generation superalloys. 單晶鎳基超合金是高溫應用（如航空發動機渦輪葉片）中的關鍵材料。其優異的高溫力學性能主要來自於在固溶體基體γ相中析出的有序間隙化合物γ'相。在服役過程中，渦輪葉片可能會遭遇外來物衝擊載荷，從而影響航空發動機運行的安全性。因此，研究單晶鎳基超合金在高溫下的動態行為具有重要意義。儘管如此，目前在極端條件下這類超合金的微觀結構演化及變形機制尚未明確，這一知識缺口限制了材料性能預測與工程設計的進一步發展。本項目旨在解決三個核心科學問題：（1）單晶鎳基超合金在高溫動態拉伸下微觀結構演化與力學行為之間的關係；（2）γ'與γ兩相互作用對微觀結構演化的影響；（3）建立基於微觀結構的模型以模擬其力學行為。 首先，將制備單晶鎳基超合金DD98M樣品及與DD98M中γ'、γ相化學成分相近的單晶樣品，並利用分體式霍普金森拉伸杆對其高溫動態響應進行測試。為研究微觀結構演化，將使用霍普金森桿中斷技術，使樣品動態拉伸至不同變形量。 其次，將從微米至原子尺度開展多尺度微觀結構分析。運用中子衍射技術測定位錯密度與組態，並結合先進顯微鏡技術，對γ'/γ界面、位錯結構及溶質原子在位錯的偏聚行為進行表徵，深入揭示DD98M在高溫下的動態行為。 最後，將結合γ'、γ兩相的動態響應與位錯演化，建立單晶塑性有限元模型，以模擬DD98M高溫下的動態響應。通過實驗與模擬，揭示γ'與γ相互作用對微觀結構演化及整體動態行為的影響。 本項目的順利完成，將使人們對單晶鎳基超合金在高溫下的動態響應有更深入的認識。這一研究對提升高溫部件設計與推動新一代超合金的發展具有重要意義。

17304425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304425.value: 应用引力透镜于天体物理学：哈勃常数和暗物质性质

17304425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17304425.value: Dr Amruth, Alfred Prof Bartelmann, Matthias Prof Broadhurst, Thomas Mr Chow, Alex Dr Diego, Jose M. Prof Oguri, Masamune

17304425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304425.value: Mass warps spacetime: astronomical observations reveal that light from background galaxies can be focussed by intervening foreground galaxies so as to create multiple images of the same background galaxies in the sky. This phenomenon, known as gravitational lensing, has become an indispensable tool in observational astronomy for addressing key questions in astrophysics as well as fundamental physics. In this proposal, we address: (i) the accuracy at which the Hubble constant (H0, the current expansion rate of the universe) can be thus determined, the value of which provides a crucial test of the ΛCDM model – whereby Dark Energy (DE) is described by the cosmological constant (Λ) – that forms the backbone of modern cosmology; and (ii) the nature of Dark Matter (DM), constituting 85% of all matter in the universe, as revealed through the DM particle mass. The existence of DM is a clear sign that the Standard Model of particle physics is incomplete, making the nature of DM, and that of DE, the most important questions in fundamental physics. The accuracy of inferences from gravitational lensing rests on the accuracy at which lens models capture the mass distributions of foreground lensing objects – here, of galaxies. Lens models are constrained by the positions and magnifications of multiply-lensed images, and must necessarily reproduce the visible properties of lensing galaxies: the universe, however, does not present us a convenient solution for how well lens models truly capture the mass distributions of galaxies, which are dominated by invisible matter. This issue has received scant attention in the literature, and impacts – in a currently unknown manner – the reliability of all inferences made from gravitational lensing. To address this issue, we have developed a novel strategy that involves: (i) making mock multiply-lensed images generated by realistic model foreground galaxies taken from sophisticated cosmological simulations; (ii) constructing lens models from the mock multiply-lensed images in exactly the same manner as from real multiply-lensed images; (iii) thus revealing, by comparing the lens models constructed with the actual mass distributions of simulated lensing galaxies, inaccuracies in lens modelling; and (iv) their impact on the determination of H0, as well as in leaving differences between the predicted and actual positions or magnifications of multiply-lensed images. The latter, known as lensing anomalies, is the focus of intensive tests to determine whether DM comprises ultra-massive particles such as WIMPs or ultra-light particles such as Axions. 质量扭曲时空：天文观测显示，背景星系发出的光线可以通过前景星系的干涉而聚焦，从而在天空中形成同一背景星系的多个图像。这种现象被称为引力透镜效应，已成为观测天文学中解决天体物理学和基础物理学关键问题的不可或缺的工具。在本研究计划中，我们将探讨：（i）通过引力透镜效应确定哈勃常数（H_0,，宇宙当前的膨胀速率）的准确性程度，该精度对于检验Λ-冷暗物质模型至关重要（模型中暗能量由宇宙学常数（Λ）表述），构成了现代宇宙学的基石；（ii）暗物质的性质，暗物质粒子的质量揭示了宇宙中85%的物质由暗物质组成。暗物质的存在明确揭示了粒子物理学的标准模型并不完整，因此暗物质和暗能量的性质成为基础物理学中最重要的问题。 由引力透镜效应做出的推断的准确性取决于透镜模型对前景透镜物体（这里指星系）质量分布的捕捉精度。透镜模型受多重透镜成像的位置和亮度约束，并且必须还原透镜星系的可见特性。然而在宇宙中，我们并没有一种便捷的方法来评估透镜模型是否真正捕捉到了以不可见物质为主的星系的质量分布。这一问题在文献中很少受到关注，并以目前未知的方式影响所有基于引力透镜效应做出的推断的可靠性。为了解决这一问题，我们开发了一种新颖的策略，其中包括：（i）利用从复杂的宇宙学模拟中提取的前景星系真实模型生成模拟的多重透镜图像；（ii）以与实际多重透镜图像完全相同的方式从模拟多重图像搭建透镜模型；（iii）将（ii）中搭建的模型与通过模拟透镜星系的真实质量分布搭建的透镜模型进行比较，揭示透镜模型中的不准确之处；（iv）评估这些不准确之处对于确定哈勃常数的影响，以及对多重透镜成像的位置或亮度的预测值与实际值之间造成的差异。后者被称为透镜异常，是当前研究的焦点，科学家进行了密集的测试旨在确定暗物质是否由超重粒子（如大质量弱相互作用粒子）或超轻粒子（如轴子）组成。

17304525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304525.value: 多面體組合中的整體性與對偶性

17304525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304525.value: Many important combinatorial optimization problems can be naturally formulated as integer linear programs (IP); one approach to these problems is to consider their linear programming (LP) relaxations and explore integrality properties satisfied by the constraints. Let Ax>=b, x>= 0 be a rational linear system and let P denote the polyhedron {x: Ax>= b, x>= 0}. We call P integral if it is the convex hull of all integral vectors contained in P. It is well known that P is integral iff the minimum in the LP-duality equation min{w^T x : Ax>= b, x>=0} = max{y^Tb : y^T A<=w^T, y>=0} has an integral optimal solution, for every integral vector w for which the optimum is finite. If, instead, the maximum in the equation enjoys this property, then the system Ax>= b, x>= 0 is called totally dual integral (TDI). What make these concepts so fundamental are the following facts: If P is integral, then the integer program (IP) min{w^T x : x in P, integral} reduces to its LP-relaxation, thereby is solvable in polynomial time. Edmonds and Giles proved that total dual integrality implies primal integrality: If Ax>= b, x>= 0 is TDI and b is integer-valued, then P is integral. So the model of TDI systems serves as a general framework for establishing combinatorial min-max relations. The study of such integral polyhedra and TDI systems is known as polyhedral combinatorics, which has proved to be a most powerful, coherent, and unifying tool throughout combinatorial optimization. The present project aims to explore the interconnections among primal integrality, dual integrality, and good characterizations by using the structure-driven, polyhedral, and linear programming techniques. To be specific, the PI proposes (i) to investigate Woodall's conjecture, which asserts that in every digraph the maximum number of disjoint dijoins is equal to the minimum size of a dicut; (ii) to characterize all graphs G such that the defining system Ax/2 >= 1, 1>=x>= 0 of the 2-edge connected spanning subgraph polytope is TDI, where A is the cut-edge incidence matrix of G, and 1 (resp. 0) is the all one (resp. zero) vector; and (iii) to characterize all graphs G=(V, E) with two distinguished vertices s and t, such that the maximum size of an odd st-path packing is equal to the minimum total weight of an odd st-path cover in G for any nonnegative integral weight function defined on E. 許多重要的組合最优化問題可以自然地表述為整數線性規劃（IP）；其中一種方法是考慮其線性規劃（LP）鬆弛，並探索其滿足的整體性性質。設 Ax>=b, x>=0 為一個有理數線性系統，令 P 表示多面體 {x: Ax>=b, x>=0}。我們稱 P 為整的（integral），若它是所有包含在 P 中的整數向量的凸包。眾所周知，P 為整當且僅當對每個使得下述方程最優值有限的整數向量 w， 其最小值问题都存在一個整數的最優解。若最大值問題具有此性質，則稱系統 Ax>=b, x>=0 為完全對偶整體（Totally Dual Integral, TDI）。這些概念之所以重要，在於以下事實：若 P 為整體的，則整數規劃（IP）min {wx: x in P, integral} 等价于其 LP 鬆弛，從而在多項式時間內可解。Edmonds 和 Giles 證明了完全對偶整體性（TDI）可导出原始系統的整體性：若 Ax>=b, x>=0 為 TDI 且 b 為整的，則 P 為整的。因此，TDI 系統模型可作為一個建立組合極值-最小值關係的通用框架。正如 Schrijver 所總結的，最小-最大關係不僅能導出優美的數學定理，還能作為相應組合最佳化問題的最優性準則，從而經常導致多項式可解性。對此類整數多面體和 TDI 系統的研究稱為多面體組合理論（Polyhedral Combinatorics），它已被證明是組合優化中最強大、最一致且最具統一性的工具。 多年來，申请人作为該研究領域的主要推動者，成功解決了多個長期存在的重要未解問題，並在理論上作出了重大貢獻。此外，他還與合作者共同發現了一些強大且新穎的組合方法，用於建立上述的整體性性質。在此項目中，他希望進一步探索原始整體性、對偶整體性與良好特徵之間的相互關聯，並運用結構驅動的多面體與線性規劃技術。具體而言，申请人拟研究下述问题： (i) 探討Woodall猜想，即在每個有向圖中，互不相交的Dijoins的最大數量等於最小的Dicut的大小（特別關注具有超源和超匯點的有向圖，以及強平面有向圖的對偶問題）； (ii) 刻画所有滿足定義系統 Ax/2>=1, 1>=x>=0 的2邊連通生成子圖多面體的TDI性，其中 A 為圖的割邊关联矩陣，1為全一向量而 0 為全零向量，並研究這一特徵與旅行推銷員問題的 4/3 猜想之間的關聯； (iii) 刻画所有圖 G=（V，E）和兩個特定頂點 s 与 t, 使得在任何非負整數權重函數下，奇數 st-路徑装填的最大數量等於奇數 st-路徑覆蓋的最小總權重。

17304825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304825.value: 多肽後修飾引入碳硼烷用於硼中子俘獲療法

17304825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304825.value: Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) represents a promising targeted radiation therapy for cancer treatment, distinguished by its precision in destroying tumor cells while minimizing damage to normal tissues. The success of BNCT is contingent on the efficient and selective delivery of boron-10 into tumor cells, a challenge currently limited by existing boron delivery agents such as boronophenylalanine (BPA) and sodium borocaptate (BSH), which suffer from low tumor specificity and boron loading. This project proposes the development of novel peptide-carborane conjugates as boron delivery agents for BNCT. Carboranes, due to their high boron content and unique chemical properties, present a promising solution to enhance boron delivery. We aim to leverage advances in peptide conjugation chemistry to design and synthesize a series of peptide-carborane conjugates, incorporating carborane groups into peptides through a robust synthetic platform using OPA chemistry. The project will focus on developing new enabling methods to synthesis peptide-carborane conjugates, and optimizing the boron content, tumor cell selectivity, and cell membrane permeability of these conjugates. As a proof of concept, we will apply our strategy to introduce carboranes into TH19P01 peptide which is the ligand of Sortilin (SORT1). By targeting the multifunctional protein SORT1, which is overexpressed in various malignant tumors, we will optimize peptide-carborane candidates for effective intracellular boron delivery. The functional performance of these conjugates will be evaluated through biochemical and biological assays, including boron uptake quantification and cytotoxicity tests in cancer cell lines. This research seeks to overcome current limitations in BNCT and pave the way for the development of highly effective boron delivery agents, enhancing the therapeutic potential of BNCT in cancer treatment. 硼中子捕獲治療（BNCT）是一種具有前景的靶向放射療法，用於癌症治療，其特點在於能夠精確破壞腫瘤細胞，同時最大限度地減少對正常組織的損傷。BNCT的成功取決於硼-10高效且選擇性地遞送至腫瘤細胞，而目前這一挑戰受到現有硼遞送劑（如硼苯丙氨酸（BPA）和硼酸鈉（BSH））的限制，這些遞送劑存在腫瘤特異性低和硼負載量不足的問題。本項目提出開發新型肽-碳硼烷偶聯物作為BNCT的硼遞送劑。碳硼烷因其高硼含量和獨特的化學性質，為增強硼遞送提供了一種有前景的解決方案。我們旨在利用肽偶聯化學的進展，設計並合成一系列肽-碳硼烷偶聯物，通過OPA化學的穩健合成平台將碳硼烷基團引入肽中。該項目將重點開發新的合成肽-碳硼烷偶聯物的方法，並優化這些偶聯物的硼含量、腫瘤細胞選擇性和細胞膜滲透性。作為概念驗證，我們將應用該策略將碳硼烷引入TH19P01肽中，該肽是Sortilin（SORT1）的配體。通過靶向在多種惡性腫瘤中過表達的多功能蛋白SORT1，我們將優化肽-碳硼烷候選物，以實現有效的細胞內硼遞送。這些偶聯物的功能性能將通過生化和生物學檢測進行評估，包括在癌細胞系中的硼攝取量化和細胞毒性測試。這項研究旨在克服BNCT目前的局限性，為開發高效的硼遞送劑鋪平道路，從而提升BNCT在癌症治療中的潛力。

17304925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17304925.value: 氧化物半導體和金屬奈米複合材料的獨特三系統集成，為可折疊有機和鈣鈦礦光電器件實現本質上耐用的透明電極

17304925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304925.value: There has been an increasing demand for foldable transparent electrodes (f-TEs) (which can sustain a bending radius <1mm) with high electrical-mechanical-thermal-moisture (i.e., 4-degree) stability in photovoltaic, display, and sensing devices for advancing their emerging applications in foldable smartphones, robotics, and next-generation wearable/healthcare electronics. Among different transparent conductors, silver-nanowire (AgNW)-based nano-nets stand out because of the high conductivity of Ag, high mechanical flexibility, and low cost. However, besides the typical concerns of dislocation, oxidation, and high roughness, AgNWs (diameters <100nm) are limited by their intrinsic charge transport ability which breaks down under high current or voltage bias. Moreover, the strong electric field and massive heat generation will extensively stimulate Ag diffusion, leading to lattice distortion and electrode malfunction, further hindering their device applications. Interestingly, our recent research showed that in the heterogeneous solid-solid system of AgNWs and semiconductor ZnO nanocrystals (ZnONCs), the ZnONCs show a liquid-like wetting behavior on AgNWs with clear crystal lattice connections between Ag and ZnO heterogeneous interfaces. This broadens the charge transport path and enhances the stability of the AgNW-ZnONC heterogeneous interface. Equally important, the homogeneous interfacial interactions in AgNW-AgNW and ZnONC-ZnONC can be strengthened altogether (i.e., tri-system integration) demonstrating excellent optoelectrical properties and the 4-degree durability. The tri-system integration can be achieved through the in-situ solution-processed method (iSPM) initialized by the reaction of reducing agents with AgNWs and ZnONCs to simultaneously trigger the AgNW-AgNW welding, ZnONC-ZnONC coalescence, and ZnONC-AgNW wetting. Nevertheless, there is a lack of deep understanding of the interactions between AgNWs and metal-oxide nanocrystals (MONCs). Meanwhile, extending ZnO to other n-/p-type oxide semiconductors would realize AgNW nanocomposite f-TEs with tunable workfunctions, which are critical for advancing their device applications. In this project, we aim to (1) develop a general iSPM to realize effective f-TEs from the tri-system integration of AgNWs with different MONCs satisfying the demands for emerging optoelectronic applications, (2) identify the interaction behaviors and mechanisms of MONCs on AgNWs, and study the key factors affecting the wetting/interaction, (3) with the understanding in (2), advance/promote the wetting of MONCs by surface modification of AgNWs to obtain high-performance f-TEs, and (4) consolidate the developed f-TEs to demonstrate foldable perovskite/organics optoelectronics devices including solar cells, and light-emitting diodes. The work contributes to generalizing the approach of integrating heterogeneous oxide-metal-nanocomposite systems and establishing a new understanding of oxide-metal nano-adhesion/interaction processes to achieve excellent optical/electrical properties and electrical-mechanical-thermal-moisture stability, and promoting perovskite/organics devices for emerging flexible/foldable optoelectronics. 為了推動可折疊智慧型手機、機器人以及下一代穿戴/醫療電子產品等新興應用的發展，光伏、顯示器和感測設備對可折疊透明電極 (f-TE)（可維持彎曲半徑 < 1 毫米）和高電-機-熱-濕（即 4 度）穩定性的需求日益增長。在各種透明導體中，基於銀奈米線 (AgNW) 的奈米網絡因其銀的高導電性、高機械柔韌性和低成本而脫穎而出。然而，除了位錯、氧化和高粗糙度等常見問題外，直徑 < 100 奈米的銀奈米線 (AgNW) 還受到其固有電荷傳輸能力的限制，在高電流或電壓偏壓下容易失效。此外，強電場和大量發熱會顯著刺激銀擴散，導致晶格畸變和電極失效，進一步阻礙其裝置應用。有趣的是，我們最近的研究表明，在銀奈米線 (AgNW) 和半導體氧化鋅奈米晶體 (ZnONC) 的異質固-固體系中，ZnONC 在銀奈米線 (AgNW) 上表現出類似液體的潤濕行為，Ag 和 ZnO 異質界面之間具有清晰的晶格連接。這拓寬了電荷傳輸路徑，並增強了 AgNW-ZnONC 異質界面的穩定性。同樣重要的是，AgNW-AgNW 和 ZnONC-ZnONC 中的均質界面相互作用可以同時增強（即三體系整合），從而展現出優異的光電性能和 4 度耐久性。三系統整合可透過原位溶液處理法（iSPM）實現，該方法以還原劑與AgNW和ZnONC發生反應為起始，同時觸發AgNW-AgNW焊接、ZnONC-ZnONC融合以及ZnONC-AgNW潤濕。然而，目前對AgNW與金屬氧化物奈米晶體（MONC）之間相互作用的理解尚不足。同時，將ZnO擴展到其他n/p型氧化物半導體，將實現功函數可調的AgNW奈米複合f-TE，這對於推進其裝置應用至關重要。 在本計畫中，我們的目標是: (1)開發一種通用的iSPM，透過AgNW與不同MONC的三系統整合實現有效的f-TE，滿足新興光電應用的需求; (2)確定MONC在AgNW上的相互作用行為和機制，研究影響潤濕/相互作用的關鍵因素; (3)在（2）的基礎上，透過對AgNW進行表面改質來提高MONC的潤濕性，以獲得高性能的f-TE; (4)鞏固已開發的f-TE，展示可折疊鈣鈦礦/有機光電器件，包括太陽能電池和發光二極管。這項工作有助於推廣異質氧化物-金屬-奈米複合系統整合方法，建立對氧化物-金屬奈米黏附/相互作用過程的新認識，以實現優異的光學/電學性能和電-機械-熱-濕穩定性，並促進鈣鈦礦/有機物裝置用於新興的柔性/可折疊光電子學。

17305425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17305425.value: 偏差隨機梯度方法的學習理論

17305425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305425.value: Stochastic gradient methods are widely used in training machine learning models due to their scalability and efficiency. A key ingredient in stochastic gradient methods is the construction of the gradient estimators to relieve the computational burden. While unbiased gradient estimators are natural choices, recent developments show a growing interest in introducing a bias in the learning process. Representative examples include the Zeroth-order stochastic gradient descent (SGD) which uses finite difference to approximate gradients for black-box problems, the Clipped-SGD which applies a clipping operator to gradients to improve the robustness, and the Compressed-SGD which applies a compression operator to decrease the communication cost in distributed learning. The popularity of biased stochastic gradient methods (BSGMs) motivates many recent studies on the convergence analysis to understand their performance on training. As a comparison, there is much less work on generalization analysis to understand how the training behavior generalizes to test examples, which is a concept of central importance in learning theory. This project aims to fill this gap by developing a unifying learning theory for BSGMs. First, we will develop a framework of stability and generalization analysis of BSGMs. We will track how the stability will change within a single update of BSGMs, and build estimates by incorporating the bias into the generalization analysis. Second, we will develop a framework of uniform convergence analysis of BSGMs for nonconvex learning problems. To this aim, we will build tight estimates on the uniform convergence of gradients as well as effective estimates on the complexity of the function space traversed by the BSGMs. For both the stability and the uniform convergence analysis, we will apply our unifying results to specific BSGMs such as the Clipped-SGD, Zeroth-order SGD and Compressed-SGD, towards which we will build tight estimates on the bias. Finally, we will study practical algorithm design based on our theoretical analysis, and justify the efficiency by experimental comparisons on real-world datasets. 隨機梯度方法在訓練機器學習模型中被廣泛使用，原因在於它們的可擴展性和高效性。隨機梯度方法的一個關鍵組成部分是構建梯度估計器，以減輕計算負擔。雖然無偏梯度估計器是自然的選擇，但近期的研究顯示，越來越多的算法通過在學習過程中引入偏差以提升學習效率。具有代表性的例子包括：使用有限差分近似梯度的零階隨機梯度下降（Zeroth-order SGD），通過對梯度施加裁剪操作以提高魯棒性的裁剪式SGD（Clipped-SGD），以及在分佈式學習中應用壓縮操作以降低通訊成本的壓縮式SGD（Compressed-SGD）。 偏差隨機梯度方法（BSGMs）的普及促使了許多關於其收斂性分析的研究，以理解其在訓練過程中的性能。作為對比，關於其泛化能力的研究較少，即理解訓練行為如何泛化到測試樣本的問題，這是學習理論中的核心概念。本專案旨在填補這一空白，開發一種統一的BSGMs學習理論。 首先，我們將建立BSGMs的穩定性和泛化分析框架。我們將追蹤穩定性在一次更新中如何變化，並將偏差納入泛化分析以建立估計。其次，我們將構建針對非凸學習問題BSGMs的一致收斂性分析框架。為此，我們將對梯度的一致收斂性進行緊湊估計，並對BSGMs遍歷函數空間的複雜度進行有效估計。我們將普適結果應用到具體的BSGMs，如裁剪SGD（Clipped-SGD）、零階SGD（Zeroth-SGD）和壓縮SGD（Compressed-SGD），並對相應梯度估計器的偏差進行詳細估計。最後，我們將基於理論分析設計實際算法，並通過在真實數據集上的實驗比較，驗證其效率。

17305625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17305625.value: 極限精度下的含噪量子計量學

17305625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305625.value: Quantum metrology aims to build sensors with superior precision and accuracy by leveraging quantum resources. Its applications span fundamental scientific endeavors, such as detecting gravitational waves, to practical uses, including timing, ranging, navigation, and biomedical imaging. Recent advancements in experimental capabilities have made the preparation and control of many-body quantum systems feasible, enabling their use as powerful and versatile tools in quantum metrology. It is well-known that many-body quantum entanglement is key to boosting estimation performance and achieving the ultimate quantum limit. However, in realistic setups, preparing and maintaining many-body entanglement is challenging, resource-intensive, and sometimes even unfavorable, as highly entangled states are susceptible to inevitable noise such as decoherence and thermalization. Recent progress has shown that suitably designed quantum control applied to the probe state can significantly improve the performance of many-body metrology. For instance, for quantum sensors operating at room temperature, appropriate quantum control is crucial to counterbalance thermal noise and protect the information for sensing. Nevertheless, a framework detailing how the control should be designed and implemented in conjunction with the probe state, and what the ultimate attainable precision in practice is, remains missing. The main target of this project is to establish such a systematic framework for noisy many-body quantum metrology. Crucially, based on our original tools for optimal quantum metrology, we will determine the fundamental limit of noisy many-body quantum metrology, achievable under the practical consideration that control and measurements are performed over small sections of the system. To approach this limit, we will develop computationally efficient methods enhanced by deep learning and tensor networks for optimizing metrological strategies. Our techniques have previously demonstrated great success in mitigating noise in quantum circuits and optimizing long control sequences for quantum metrology. Lastly, we will apply our framework to design self-adaptive and noise-resilient sensing protocols that extend the scope of quantum sensing to new, more complex tasks. This project will explore the fundamental limit of many-body quantum metrology and advance the practical design of many-body quantum sensors, featuring a novel and coherent integration of artificial intelligence into quantum metrology. In the long term, it will contribute to the design of new quantum sensors and sensor networks, extending the influence of quantum metrology to fields such as computer vision and graphics, and leading to a new generation of classical-quantum hybrid intelligent sensors. 量子計量學旨在透過利用量子資源構建具有卓越精確度與準確性的感測器，其應用範圍涵蓋基礎科學研究（如重力波探測）至實用領域（包括計時、測距、導航與生物醫學成像）。 近年實驗技術上的突破使得製備與控制多體量子系統成為可能，這類系統可作為量子計量學中強大且多功能的工具。眾所周知，多體量子糾纏是提升估算效能並達成終極量子極限的關鍵。然而在實際情境中，製備與維持多體糾纏態不僅具挑戰性且耗費資源，有時甚至適得其反——高度糾纏態易受退相干與熱化等不可避免的噪聲影響。最新研究顯示，對探測態施加經過設計的量子控制能顯著提升多體計量學的表現。例如對於室溫下的量子感測器，精準的量子控制對於抵消熱噪聲並保護感測資訊至關重要。然而，目前仍缺乏完整框架來闡明如何結合探測態設計與實施控制方案，以及實際可達到的終極精度極限。 本項目的核心目標正是為噪聲環境下的多體量子計量學建立系統性框架。關鍵在於，我們將基於原創的最優量子計量學工具，在「僅能對系統局部區域實施控制與量測」的實際限制下，確立噪聲多體量子計量學的根本極限。為逼近此極限，我們將開發結合深度學習與張量網絡的高效計算方法，用以優化計量策略。這些技術先前已成功應用於量子電路噪聲抑制與長序列量子控制優化。最終，我們將運用此框架設計具自適應性與噪聲抗性的協議，將量子感測拓展至更複雜的新任務領域。 本項目特色在於將人工智慧與量子計量學進行系統性整合。長期而言，此研究將促進新型量子感測器與感測網絡的開發，將量子計量學的影響力延伸至計算機視覺與圖形學等領域，引領新一代經典-量子混合智能感測器的誕生。

17305825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17305825.value: 大型语言模型的优化视角

17305825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305825.value: Large Language Models (LLMs) have brought about a profound revolution across various sectors, spanning from industry and economy to education and entertainment. While the advancement of LLMs has primarily relied on hardware such as GPUs and engineering technologies, the field is now entering a new phase that necessitates deeper engagement with scientific disciplines. The integration of mathematical and quantitative insights is crucial for driving the next wave of breakthroughs in the realm of LLMs. There is an urgent need to reevaluate the core tasks involved in the lifecycle of LLMs through an optimization lens, with a focus on enhancing the scientific understanding of key phases including pre-training, post-training, fine-tuning, and serving. Specific tasks to be addressed encompass distributed low-bit training, pruning, quantization, and prefill/decode disaggregation architecture. Our research will concentrate on these specific LLM tasks, conducting a systematic exploration from problem identification to algorithmic design, theoretical analysis, fine implementation, and algorithm engineering. Our primary objective is to reduce the computation and memory footprint throughout the lifecycle of LLMs. By offering comprehensive optimization perspectives, we aim to propel the field forward with innovative optimization insights. We aspire to construct a unified and theoretically grounded framework that ensures the cost-effectiveness and scalability of AI solutions, while maintaining high model performance and accuracy. The outcomes of this project are anticipated to enhance LLM technologies, with our original understanding and rigorous analysis of optimization principles poised to make some impacts on both the LLM industry and academia. 大型语言模型（LLMs）在工业、经济、教育和娱乐等多个领域都引发了深刻的变革。虽然LLMs的技术进步主要依赖于GPU等硬件和工程技术，但目前该领域正进入一个新的阶段，需更深入地结合科学的知识。而数学和定量分析的深度融合将对推动LLMs的下一波突破起到至关重要的作用。我们迫切需要从优化的角度重新审视LLMs生命周期中的核心任务，重点提升对预训练、后训练、微调和部署等关键阶段的科学理解。具体任务包括分布式低比特训练、剪枝、量化，以及预填/解码解耦架构等。我们的研究将集中于这些具体任务，进行系统性探索，从问题识别到算法设计、理论分析、细节实现以及算法工程化。 我们的主要目标是减少LLMs在整个生命周期中的内存和计算成本。通过提供全面的优化视角，我们希望推动该领域的创新，提出具有前瞻性的优化策略。我们致力于构建一个统一且具有理论基础的框架，确保AI解决方案的成本效益与可扩展性，同时保持高模型性能和准确性。我们的原创理解和严谨的优化原理分析有望在大模型行业和学术界产生一些积极的影响，预计本项目的成果将有利于LLMs技术的提升。

17306425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17306425.value: 滇中盆地恐龍年代之探究

17306425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17306425.value: Prof Chang, Su-Chin Prof Denyszyn, Steven Dr Pei, Rui Dr Wang, Jun Prof Xu, Xing

17306425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306425.value: In recent decades, the Central Yunnan Basin has yielded numerous well-preserved dinosaur fossils and tracks from the Jurassic period. These findings have significantly advanced our understanding of the evolutionary history of various dinosaur groups and the thriving ecosystem in East Asia during the middle Mesozoic era. Accurately determining the age of the rock formations containing these fossils is crucial to establish robust correlations within and between basins and to establish duration of sedimentation and fossil evolution, yet reliable radiometric age constraints are currently lacking. This project aims to collect and date at least 25 samples from three key outcrops to establish a detailed radiometric age framework, allowing for improved correlation with other rock sequences and a deeper understanding of the rates of dinosaur evolution. The results will play a pivotal role in refining theories about the paleobiogeographic and temporal distribution of basal dinosaurs. 自上世紀以來，大量保存完整的恐龍化石從滇中盆地出土，這些種類繁多、形態各異的化石提供了研究中生代生物演化的重要線索，對了解中生代環境扮演重要關鍵。我們的研究旨在建立恐龍化石層位精確的年代，我們的結果能夠使恐龍研究更加完整、全面性，也為中國西南部恐龍遷移和演化提供關鍵的依據。

17306825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17306825.value: 開殼非交替奈米石墨烯：利用非交替拓撲結構調控多環芳烴的基態特性

17306825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306825.value: Nanographenes with an open-shell character have received tremendous attention due to their highly promising applications in (opto)electronic and magnetic devices. Compared to corresponding benzenoid analogs, nanographenes with nonalternant topologies could exhibit appealing properties due to their unique electronic configuration. Over the past few years, many efforts have been made to design and synthesize graphene molecules with joined pentagonal and heptagonal rings (5-7 pairs), which also have attracted growing interest due to their unique photophysical properties, e.g., abnormal anti-Kasha emission behaviors. However, because of the synthetic challenges and poor stability, examples of nonalternant-containing nanographenes with an open-shell character are rare, limiting the further exploration of their applications. In this project, the PI will establish a new line of research for the synthesis and characterization of open-shell nonalternant nanographenes (Fig. 3), to tailor the ground state of polycyclic hydrocarbons using nonalternant topologies, including singlet diradicals and triplet diradicals. We will systematically study the relationship between their topological structures and physicochemical properties, for instance, their spin multiplicity in the ground state, energy gaps between the singlet and triplet states (ΔES-T), and stability, etc. In addition, multi-radicals with nonalternant topologies will be further developed to study their intrinsic (opto)electronic and magnetic properties, as well as their stability. Moreover, the unique magnetic properties of the resultant nonalternant nanographenes will be investigated by pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, including their spin relaxation time (T1) and spin coherence time (Tm). Through this systematic study, we will try to find some guidelines for designing and synthesizing stable open-shell nonalternant nanographenes. To realize these ambitious goals, this project will take advantage of different chemical approaches including organic chemistry, solid-state physics, and theoretic modeling. 具有開殼特性的奈米石墨烯因其在（光）電子裝置與磁性裝置中的巨大應用前景而備受關注。相較於對應的苯型類似物，具有非交替拓樸結構的奈米石墨烯因其獨特電子組態特性可展現出更優異的性能。近年來，透過建構五元環-七元環對（5-7對）結構設計合成石墨烯分子的研究取得顯著進展，該類材料因反常的反卡莎規則發光等獨特光物理性質引發日益廣泛的關注。然而受限於合成挑戰性與穩定性問題，兼具開殼特性與非交替結構的奈米石墨烯實例稀少，阻礙了其應用探索。本計畫擬建立開殼層非交替奈米石墨烯（圖3）的合成與表徵新體系，透過非交替拓樸結構調控多環芳烴的基態特性（包括單線態雙自由基與三線態雙自由基），系統研究其拓樸結構與物理化學性質（如基態自旋多重、單重態-三重態能隙ΔES-T、穩定性等）的構效關係。進一步發展具有非交替拓樸結構的多自由基體系，深入研究其本徵（光）電磁學性質及穩定性；並藉助脈衝電子順磁共振（EPR）技術探究非交替奈米石墨烯的獨特磁學性質（包括自旋弛豫時間T1與自旋相干時間Tm）。透過系統性研究，為設計合成穩定的開殼非交替奈米石墨烯建立理論指引。為實現上述目標，本計畫將整合有機化學、固態物理學及理論建模等多學科研究方法。

17306925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17306925.value: 馬可夫過程的非參數鞅后验分布

17306925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306925.value: Markov processes are ubiquitous in time series data, which play a key role in fields such as econometrics, finance, healthcare, environmental science and more. Bayesian nonparametric methods are a promising class of models that have strong applications in time series settings due to their flexibility and uncertainty quantification. However, the specification of nonparametric priors is complex, and computation via Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) can be prohibitively time-consuming. The martingale posterior (MP) is a novel approach for Bayesian inference where the elicited statistical model is a sequence of predictive distributions, and posterior sampling is replaced by predictive imputation. In particular, the MP can utilize nonparametric recursive updates, which allow for nonparametric Bayesian inference in a manner which is free of MCMC, thereby greatly improving scalability. Thus far, the focus for MPs has been on settings where the data are independent and identically distributed. This project aims to rigorously extend the MP framework to time series settings, with a particular focus on nonparametric methods. The new framework will enable the introduction of new scalable Bayesian nonparametric methodologies for Markov processes. Desirable theoretical properties and empirical performance will then be demonstrated on challenging data settings. 馬可夫過程在時間序列數據中無處不在，於計量經濟學、金融、醫療保健、環境科學等領域扮演關鍵角色。貝葉斯非參數方法由於其出色的靈活性和不確定性量化能力，在時間序列分析中展現出巨大的應用潛力。然而，非參數先驗的設定較為複雜，且依賴馬可夫鏈蒙特卡羅（MCMC）的計算可能耗時過長。 Martingale posterior（MP）是一種新穎的貝葉斯推論方法，其統計模型由一系列預測分布構成，並以預測插補取代後驗抽樣。尤其，MP可利用非參數遞歸更新，實現無需MCMC的非參數貝葉斯推論，從而大幅提升可擴展性。目前，MP的應用主要集中在數據獨立同分布的情境中。本項目旨在將MP框架嚴謹地擴展至時間序列場景，並重點探討非參數方法。這一新框架將為馬可夫過程引入可擴展的貝葉斯非參數方法，並在具挑戰性的數據場景中驗證其理論性質與實證表現。

17307025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17307025.value: 阿波羅盆地嫦娥六號著陸點岩漿活動歷史及其對月球二分性的指示

17307025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307025.value: For life on Earth, only one face of the Moon is visible, and this side is called nearside. The opposite side of the Moon is called farside but that side was never visible and stayed unknown until 1959 when the first artificial satellite (Luna-3) orbited the Moon and took a picture of it. Scientists suddenly realized that the lunar nearside and farside are significantly distinctive in many perspectives and the Moon is asymmetrical.
