This approach emphasizes the pivotal yet overlooked activities of women, who in their varied capacities as wives, mothers, wealth managers, and political strategists, relentlessly advanced family interests. It also centers the enslaved women who cooked, cleaned, and cared for children in elite households. Starting in the 1650s, the book follows predecessors of Irish and Royalist origin who fled to Surinam, Barbados, Antigua, and Montserrat during the English Civil War and the Cromwellian Conquest of Ireland. Their early participation in plantation slavery and colonial administration yielded significant and enduring results. Between 1650 and 1820, densely interrelated and geographically widespread collectives amassed vast fortunes, estates, and titles. Descendants served as governors of the Leeward Islands, Jamaica, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, and North Carolina. They became MPs, held positions in the royal household, directed the Navy and the Army, and ran the East India Company. During the American Revolution, these largely Loyalist coalitions intensified their interests in the Caribbean, Ireland, and India. 我的第二本專書「Imperial Kin」以「Jamaica Ladies」的發現為基礎，同時也在新的地理、時間和方法學方向上推展我的研究。"Imperial Kin》追蹤了五大洲四代人中的數百個人，展示了某些家族如何迅速地將殖民企業轉變為持久的全球領導。除了微觀歷史和個案研究之外，《帝國親屬》還對殖民統治的親密層面進行了實證性的有力描述，並強調了婚姻、繁衍和養育策略的重要性。這種方法強調婦女關鍵但被忽視的活動，她們以妻子、母親、財富經理人和政治戰略家的各種身份，無情地（ ）推進家庭利益。它也以精英家庭中負責烹飪、清潔和照顧孩子的受奴役婦女為中心。從 1650 年代開始，這本書追蹤了在英國內戰和克羅姆威爾征服愛爾蘭期間逃到蘇里南、巴巴多斯、安提瓜和蒙特塞拉特的愛爾蘭和保皇黨前輩。他們早期參與種植奴役和殖民地管理，產生了重大而持久的成果。在 1650 年至 1820 年間，這些相互關聯且地域廣泛的集體積累了巨額財富、莊園和頭銜。他們的後裔曾擔任背風群島、牙買加、紐約、賓夕法尼亞、南卡羅來納州和北卡羅來納州的總督。他們成為國會議員，在皇室擔任職位，指揮海軍和陸軍並管理東印度公司。在美國革命期間，這些主要是保皇黨的聯盟加強了他們在加勒比海、愛爾蘭和印度的利益。

17610325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610325.value: 童年喪失母親對慢性疾病及醫療服務使用的影響之人口層面研究

17610325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17610325.value: Prof Chan, Linda Prof Lai, Francisco Tsz Tsun Dr Ng, Amy Pui Pui Prof Wan, Yuk Fai Eric Prof Yuen, Jacqueline Kwan Yuk

17610325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610325.value: Losing a parent during childhood is a common event estimated at 4% worldwide. It increases the risk of mental health conditions such as depression and anxiety. Losing a mother in particular can have a profound effect as mothers traditionally serve – although not always – as a child’s main caregiver and often have unique attachments (e.g., through breastfeeding). Given the high prevalence and the profound influence that it can have, studying the population health impacts of maternal bereavement is a largely understudied area of public health importance. Such studies are also of clinical and social importance as they will identify which children (e.g., age at loss, sex, presence of siblings, presence of co-existing medical conditions) are at highest risk of poor health outcomes – thus allowing caregivers and health care practitioners to screen, educate and intervene effectively on the potential impacts of childhood maternal loss and bereavement. However, there are many issues with the current pool of research studies on childhood maternal bereavement. There are many challenges with study design, with small number of participants, and with having short follow-up time. Previous studies have also focused on mental health conditions; none have conducted large population-based studies examining common childhood chronic conditions such as diabetes, eczema, asthma, ADHD, and anemia. Finally, there are limited studies that have identified the characteristics of the child (e.g., sex, age at loss, presence of siblings, pre-existing mental health conditions) and mother (e.g., cause of death) that may put the child at higher risk of poor outcomes after loss. Our studies will fill these gaps, using a novel Hong Kong Hospital Authority database that captures all mothers and the children they delivered between 2020 and 2023. This ‘mom-baby’ database is linked to other Hospital Authority databases such as General Out-Patient Clinic visits, accident and emergency department visits, and hospital admissions. These linkages allow us to follow up, for up to 20 years, the health impacts of losing a mother. Our study has 4 objectives: 1) Describe the public health burden of childhood maternal loss. 2) Evaluate how losing a mother during childhood impacts the risk of developing common childhood chronic conditions. 3) Evaluate the impact of loss on public health care use, including for those who already have a common childhood chronic condition. 4) Identify the characteristics of children who are at high risk for developing the outcomes studied in objectives 2&3.

17610625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610625.value: 有薪產假與侍産假政策對產後健康之影響：基於香港近期政策的準自然實驗研究

17610625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17610625.value: Prof Geldsetzer, Pascal Prof McKee, Martin Dr Ni, Michael Yuxuan Dr Wong, Sau Man Corine

17610625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610625.value: Postpartum mothers are frequently affected by physical health and mental health issues, which have a significant impact on their own future health, family health and wellbeing, and child development, as well as economic and social outcomes. Policies aimed at improving postpartum health are therefore vital and warrant further investigation. Studies on parental leave and postpartum health have primarily concentrated on either expansions in paid leave from already generous levels or sharp changes in benefits, and have largely been conducted in Western countries. There is also a lack of evidence on the causal impact of paternity leave policies on maternal health. Among cities with the longest working hours, Hong Kong recently expanded maternity leave from 10 to 14 weeks on 11 December 2020 and paternity leave from three to five days on 18 January 2019. It provides an opportunity for a natural experiment to investigate the impacts of parental leave policies on maternal postpartum health in a context where the policy changes have been more recent and benefits are limited. The proposed project will utilise data from a territory-wide electronic health record database in Hong Kong. We will deploy a regression discontinuity in time design combined with a difference-in-difference approach to evaluate whether recent expansions have had a positive impact on maternal postpartum health in Hong Kong. We will compare the health outcomes of mothers of children born three months before and after the reforms, relative to the corresponding diﬀerence in the three preceding years. Maternal health outcomes will include inpatient hospital admissions, outpatient hospital visits, visits associated with mental disorders, and prescription drug records. Through the proposed study, we will contribute to the sparse literature that estimates the causal relationship between parental leave policies and maternal health by including a wide range of outcomes and attempting to determine the direction of the association between paternity leave and maternal postpartum health. Our findings will carry significant implications for parental leave policies locally and internationally. If our research reveals that the recent policy adjustments in Hong Kong have yielded favourable effects on maternal health, it will bolster the existing evidence base advocating for and advancing family-friendly employment practices. Our research will not only contribute to the ongoing international debate surrounding family leave policies but also serve as a valuable resource for shaping and improving parental leave policies to generate positive impacts for mothers, children, families, organisations, and society at large. 產後婦女的身心健康狀況往往面臨諸多挑戰，這些狀況不僅深刻影響她們自身的健康，更牽動家庭的健康與福祉、子女的發展，乃至對經濟和社會產生深遠的影響。因此，旨在改善產後健康的政策至關重要，並值得進一步深入研究。目前，關於產假與產後婦女健康的研究，主要集中於從已經相當慷慨的有薪假期基礎上進一步擴展，或探討福利的顯著變化，而且大多數研究在西方國家進行。此外，關於父親侍産假政策對產後婦女健康影響的實證研究仍較為匱乏。作為全球工時最長的城市之一，香港於2020年12月11日將有薪產假從10週延長至14週，並於2019年1月18日將有薪侍産假從3天增加至5天。這些近期政策實施為我們提供了一個自然實驗的機會，在福利相對有限的情況下，深入探討產假與侍産假政策對產後婦女健康的影響。 本研究將利用香港電子健康記錄數據庫的數據，採用時間回歸不連續性設計（Regression Discontinuity in Time, RDiT）結合雙重差分法（Difference-in-Differences, DID），系統評估近期產假與侍産假政策實施是否對香港產後婦女健康有正面影響。我們將比較政策實施前後三個月內生育婦女的健康狀況，並與前三年同期的數據進行對比分析。研究將涵蓋多方面的健康指標，包括住院記錄、門診就診、與精神疾病相關的就診，以及處方藥物紀錄等。通過這項研究，我們將豐富產假政策與產後婦女健康因果關係的文獻，並釐清侍産假政策與產後婦女健康之間的關聯方向。 本研究的成果將對本地及國際產假、侍産假及育兒假政策產生重要影響。若研究結果顯示香港近期的政策實施對產後婦女健康有正面的影響，這將為推動家庭友善就業措施提供強而有力的實證依據。本研究不僅將為國際上關於家庭政策的討論提供重要參考，還將成為制定和改善產假、侍産假及育兒假政策的寶貴資源，從而為母親、兒童、家庭、機構乃至整個社會帶來正面影響。

17610925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610925.value: 針對輕度至中度體弱患者接受心臟手術之脆弱性專屬術前復健方案：一項隨機安慰劑對照試驗

17610925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17610925.value: Dr Chan, Tai Leung Daniel Dr Ho, Ka Lai Cally Prof Wong, Hung-Leung Randolph Miss Wong, Wai Ying Cathy Prof Yu, Sau Fung Doris

17610925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610925.value: Preoperative frailty is well documented as a strong prognostic indicator of poorer health outcomes in cardiac surgical patients. Intervening at the preoperative stage through prehabilitation is gaining increasing research attention. Previous studies have tested single frailty-reversing strategies, either nutritional or exercise, which is inadequate to address patients’ needs. Moreover, the exercise protocols deviated from the principles of exercise prescription suggested for frailty management. Hence, an effective prehabilitation intervention has yet to be developed for frail cardiac surgical patients. We developed a multi-component frailty-specific prehabilitation program for mild to moderately frail cardiac surgical patients and pilot tested among 30 patients. Both quantitative and qualitative data support the feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effects of the program. In this application, we proposed an assessor-blind parallel two-arm randomized controlled trial to examine the full effects and the mediation mechanisms of the prehabilitation program on functional capacity, frailty level, cardiac-related physical functioning, serum albumin, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), psychological outcomes, health-related quality of life, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebral events, and unplanned readmission. This study will recruit 144 patients waiting for elective cardiac surgeries from two university-affiliated hospitals. Adult patients with a Clinical Frailty Scale score between 4 and 6, waiting for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), valve repair/replacement, or combined CABG and valve repair/replacement with at least 5 weeks surgical waiting time and without contraindications for exercise will be recruited. Participants will be randomly allocated to the intervention or control groups to receive the prehabilitation program or a sham exercise intervention, respectively. The prehabilitation program will consist of preoperative education, dietary modification, stress management, and tailored frailty-specific exercise with three 60-minute sessions/week. The exercise training will last at least 4 weeks and will be maintained throughout the preoperative period. The intervention will be a hybrid home-based in-person supervision and remote online supervision to enhance the training effects. The sham control intervention will consist of light intensity stretching exercise that has no effect on frailty reversal. The delivery format and duration will be the same as the prehabilitation for the purpose of neutralizing the attention effects. Intervention outcomes will be evaluated at baseline, 1-day before surgery, 1 and 3 months after the surgery with validated measurement tools. The findings of this study will have the potential to inform the application of a safe and effective intervention to improve the prognosis of frail patients undergoing cardiac surgeries. 術前脆弱性已被廣泛證實為心臟外科患者健康結果較差的重要預後指標。透過術前復健進行介入治療，正逐漸成為研究熱點。先前研究多針對單一脆弱性逆轉策略進行測試，無論是營養或運動，但這些方式不足以滿足患者的整體需求。此外，以往的運動方案偏離了脆弱性管理中運動處方的原則。因此，針對心臟手術中脆弱患者的有效術前復健介入尚未被建立。 我們設計了一套針對輕度至中度脆弱心臟手術患者的多元脆弱專屬術前復健方案，並在30位患者中進行初步試驗。定量與定性資料均支持該方案的可行性、接受度及初步療效。 本申請提出一項評估者盲法的平行雙臂隨機對照試驗，旨在探討該術前復健方案對功能能力、脆弱程度、心臟相關體能、血清白蛋白、高敏感性C反應蛋白（hs-CRP）、心理狀況、健康相關生活品質、大型不良心血管及腦血管事件，以及非計畫性再入院等指標的全面效果與中介機制。 本研究將從兩所大學附設醫院招募144名等待選擇性心臟手術的患者。招募標準為成人患者，臨床脆弱量表（Clinical Frailty Scale）介於4至6分，等待冠狀動脈繞道手術（CABG）、瓣膜修復/置換或合併CABG與瓣膜修復/置換手術，且預計術前等待期至少五週，且無運動禁忌症。參與者將隨機分配至介入組或對照組，分別接受術前復健方案或假運動介入。術前復健方案包括術前教育、飲食調整、壓力管理及針對脆弱性的個別化運動訓練，每週三次，每次60分鐘。運動訓練將持續至少四週，並維持至術前期間。介入方式採混合式，包括居家現場指導結合線上遠端監督，以提升訓練效果。對照組採用輕強度伸展運動，該運動無脆弱性逆轉效果，且交付形式與期間與術前復健相同，藉以抵消對注意力的影響。介入效果將於基線、術前一天、術後1個月及3個月時，使用經驗證的量表進行評估。 本研究結果有望提供安全且有效的介入措施，改善接受心臟手術之脆弱患者的預後。

17611425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17611425.value: 使用個人化經顱磁刺激治療調節與恐懼相關記憶

17611425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17611425.value: Dr LO , Ka-ying Heidi Dr Webler, Ryan

17611425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611425.value: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a common mental health condition associated with substantial emotional and functional impairment. Nearly half of PTSD patients do not respond to current gold-standard treatments, underscoring the need for more effective approaches. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a safe, non-invasive brain stimulation technique that has been shown to reduce PTSD symptoms. However, the optimal TMS protocol for PTSD remains unclear, and some protocols have even been shown to worsen symptoms. The current proposal will apply TMS to a brain circuit recently shown to protect against PTSD. Stimulation will be applied following laboratory (Study 1) or clinical (Study 2) fear memory reminders in line with cross-species evidence that reactivating memories renders them temporarily vulnerable to modification. In Study 1, individualized, neuroimaging guided TMS will be applied to the PTSD-protective circuit to weaken laboratory conditioned fear memories in a large sample of healthy controls. Study 2 extends the clinical application of Study 1 by investigating whether stimulation of the same circuit can weaken trauma memories in individuals with post-traumatic stress symptoms. Taken together, these studies could shed light on the basic neurobiology of fear learning/memory and support the development of a novel, personalized, circuit-based TMS intervention for PTSD. 創傷後壓力症(PTSD) 是一種是一種常見與情緒相關的精神健康疾病。近半數的PTSD患者對目前的黄金標準治療反應並不理想，這凸顯了開發更有效治療方法的迫切需求。腦磁激治療（Transcranial magnetic stimulation）是一項安全、非入侵性的腦部刺激技術，而且已被證明能夠有效地減輕 PTSD 的症狀。然而，針對目前PTSD的最佳TMS治療方案仍不明確。 研究一將對健康控制組的參與者施加透過神經影像引導且個人化的 TMS，針對具備創傷後壓力症保護作用的神經迴路， 以達到削弱恐懼記憶的目的。研究二將伸延研究一的臨床應用，探討刺激上述相同的神經迴路是否能夠削弱創傷後壓力症狀患者的創傷記憶。 綜合而言， 這兩項研究闡明恐懼學習/記憶中的基本神經生物學，並支持以個人化和特定神經迴路的TMS干預的發展。

17611725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17611725.value: 开发一种面向教育的利用大型语言模型分析文本数据的心理测量学方法

17611725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611725.value: Pre-trained large language models (LLMs) offer transformative potential for educational research and practice. Their ability to produce contextual embeddings, which encapsulate semantic relationships and contextual information within text, presents significant potential for textual data analysis. The proposed research aims to develop a psychometric approach for analyzing textual data with LLMs and evaluate its application in STEM educational settings. By treating documents as respondents and words as items, this approach leverages foundational LLMs' ability to produce contextual scores. It also incorporates theoretical strength from partially confirmatory factor analysis (PCFA), enhancing the validity of the process. The modeling process integrates LLMs with exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and PCFA in a two-stage process. In the exploratory stage, foundational LLMs will be identified for contextual scores and initial model structure with EFA. The partially confirmatory stage is designed to develop robust and efficient methods for obtaining model parameters and factor scores, while providing varying levels of theoretical support with PCFA. The research aims to address key technical challenges by evaluating foundational LLMs for their suitability in psychometric analysis, incorporating Bayesian regularization techniques with efficient algorithms like variational approximation to handle large-scale models. The ultimate goal is to provide a flexible and scalable approach that can be applied across diverse settings. To evaluate the proposed approach, a prototype model using STEM educational corpora will be developed, and a qualitative study will be conducted to explore its application across different educational settings. The prototype model provides a solid foundation for exploring the potential applications of the psychometric approach in educational practices. Its development will help identify and address challenges that arise when integrating various techniques and methods in practice. Through qualitative study, we aim to gain a comprehensive understanding of the model's practical utility in STEM education and beyond. By obtaining insights on opportunities and challenges, we seek to refine our approach and develop guidelines for broader implementation. These insights will also inform the ongoing development of the psychometric approach to better meet educators' needs. Although we will focus on STEM corpora, many of the concepts, methods, and procedures extend beyond STEM education and can be similarly applied to any subject matter with rich textual data. The proposed approach offers significant opportunities to transform STEM teaching and learning by enabling knowledge-based, data-driven curriculum design, teaching preparation, and assessment development, fostering a more effective and responsive educational ecosystem. 摘要： 预训练的大型语言模型（LLMs）为教育研究与实践带来了变革性的潜力。其生成语境嵌入（contextual embeddings）的能力，可以捕捉文本中的语义关系和上下文信息，为文本数据分析提供了重要可能性。 本研究拟开发一种基于心理测量的方法，利用LLMs分析文本数据，并评估其在STEM教育环境中的应用。该方法将文档视为应答者、单词视为项目，利用基础LLMs生成语境分数，同时结合部分验证性因子分析（PCFA）的理论优势，以增强分析过程的有效性。 建模过程将LLMs与探索性因子分析（EFA）和PCFA结合，分为两个阶段。在探索阶段，借助基础LLMs获得语境分数，并通过EFA确定初步模型结构。部分验证性阶段旨在开发稳健高效的方法，以获得模型参数和因子分数，并通过PCFA提供不同程度的理论支持。本研究还将通过评估基础LLMs在心理测量分析中的适用性、结合贝叶斯正则化技术以及变分近似等高效算法来应对大规模模型，从而解决关键技术挑战。最终目标是提供一种灵活且可扩展的方法，适用于多样化的应用场景。 为评估所提出方法，将基于STEM教育语料库开发原型模型，并通过定性研究探索其在不同教育环境中的应用。原型模型为探索心理测量方法在教育实践中的潜在应用奠定了坚实基础，其开发将有助于识别并解决实际中整合多种技术与方法时遇到的挑战。通过定性研究，我们希望全面理解该模型在STEM教育及更广泛领域的实际效用。通过获取机遇与挑战的见解，我们将优化方法并制定更广泛应用的指导原则。这些见解也将反哺心理测量方法的持续开发，更好地满足教育工作者的需求。 尽管本研究聚焦于STEM领域语料库，许多理念、方法和流程同样适用于任何拥有丰富文本数据的学科领域。所提方法为STEM教学与学习的转型带来重大机遇，能够实现基于知识和数据驱动的课程设计、教学准备和评估开发，促进更加高效和灵活响应的教育生态系统的形成。

17612125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17612125.value: 在各發展階段中認知技能與數學解難之關係的變化

17612125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612125.value: Mathematical competence, a critical skill for entry into STEM industries, warrants increased attention in educational psychology literature. As individual differences in cognitive factors have been shown to account for up to three-quarters of the variance in mathematical problem-solving (e.g., Geary et al., 2017), having a better understanding of how different cognitive factors are related to mathematical problem-solving would provide educators with important insights concerning the designs of mathematics interventions. However, the hierarchical nature of mathematical problems poses a challenge, with problems becoming more complex as students progress through school levels, and the corresponding cognitive skills required for problem-solving are likely to differ across these developmental stages. Yet, little research has explored these developmental changes in relation to mathematical competence. The proposed study aims to address this important research gap. A large sample of 1,000 participants spanning Grades 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 (n = 200 per grade) will be recruited for the study. Participants will undergo mathematical tests alongside a cognitive assessment battery encompassing working memory, spatial skills, language skills, numerical magnitude, number ordering, arithmetic principles, and problem representation. These constructs have been selected based on their theoretical relevance to mathematical problem-solving, supported by empirical evidence (average r ≥ .30 with mathematical problem-solving). By assessing a comprehensive array of cognitive skills and mathematical problem-solving across diverse grade levels, the study aims to explore the developmental trajectories of these cognitive skills and the evolving relations between these skills and students' mathematical competence. The study’s outcomes hold both theoretical and practical significance. Current theories on mathematical problem-solving primarily focus on identifying important cognitive skills for mathematics learning, overlooking the timing of when these skills become crucial. Understanding the developmental relations between cognitive skills and mathematical problem-solving enriches existing numerical cognition theories with a developmental perspective. Importantly, this knowledge aids educators in targeting interventions effectively by identifying the most suitable cognitive skills to address at specific developmental stages, thus enhancing intervention efficacy. Therefore, the current study has the potential to bolster the STEM workforce in our society by enhancing the effectiveness of mathematical interventions under development. 數學解難能力是進入STEM產業的關鍵技能，應在教育心理學文獻中受到更高的重視。研究顯示，在數學解難的個別差異中，認知因素上的個別差異能解釋的部分多達四分之三（例如，Geary 等人，2017），因此更深入了解不同認知因素與數學解難之間的關係，將有助教育者設計數學課程。隨著學生學習階段的推進，數學問題變得越來越複雜，而解決這些問題所需的認知技能也可能在不同的發展階段有所不同。然而，相關於這些認知技能與數學解難之間關係的發展變化研究尚不多見。本研究計畫旨在填補這一重要的研究空白。 本研究將招募來自小學三年級、小學六年級，以及中學三年級共計600名參與者（每個年級200人）。參與者將接受一系列的測試，內容涵蓋數學解難，以及包含工作記憶、空間技能、語言技能、數值理解、數字排序、算術原理與文字題理解等的認知能力。這些認知能力與數學解難之間的關係均已得到理論及實證的支持（平均相關係數≥.30）。通過評估不同年級的認知技能與數學解難能力，研究旨在探討這些認知技能的發展軌跡，以及這些技能與學生數學解難之間關係隨著發展階段的演變。 本研究的成果具有理論與實務上的重要意義。目前關於數學解難的理論多著重於識別對數學學習重要的認知技能，卻較少關注這些技能何時變得關鍵。理解認知技能與數學解難之間的發展關係，能為現有數學認知理論引入發展性視角。更重要的是，這些研究成果能協助教育者有效地針對特定發展階段，提供適當認知技能訓練，提升這些訓練的效果。因此，藉由提升數學訓練措施的效果，這項研究將有助於促進社會對STEM人才的培育，進而強化社會的科技創新能力。

17613225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17613225.value: 透過香港新興企業化學生住房重新審視學生化現象：運作模式、影響與學生體驗

17613225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613225.value: As Hong Kong strives to become a global higher education hub, non-local student enrolment has more than doubled since 2016, a remarkable trajectory with important housing and urban planning implications. This growth trend is expected to accelerate further, bolstered by the recent ‘Study in Hong Kong’ initiative announced in Policy Address 2024. Against this backdrop, this research investigates Hong Kong’s rapidly expanding and evolving student housing landscape. Noting the currently limited representation of Purpose-Built Student Accommodation (PBSA) and the internationally unusual prevalence of Lease-to-Rent (LtR) models, where corporates lease properties from individual landlords and sublet to students, in Hong Kong, this study focuses on the operations, impacts and student experiences of emergent forms of corporatised student housing. Understanding these issues may reveal new forms/stages of studentification, particularly as these play out in high-density Asian settings. The study addresses four main questions: How has the student housing market in Hong Kong accommodated recently rising demand from non-local students? How is the process of student housing institutionalisation unfolding in Hong Kong as shaped by the local urban and regulatory context? How does the expansion of Hong Kong’s student housing provision contribute to studentification and impact local communities? How do students’ housing experiences in new corporatised accommodation compare to other provision models? This three-year project employs a mixed-methods approach, utilising spatial analysis, questionnaire survey, documentary analysis, field observation, key informant interviews and focus groups to examine the changing landscape of student housing provision in Hong Kong. Engaging with supply-side stakeholders, policy and governance representatives, and local community stakeholders, and students will provide holistic insights on housing development processes and their multifaceted impacts. This research will contribute to the theorisation of student housing expansion and studentification in high-density Asian urban environments. It examines new forms of corporate landlordism, particularly the LtR investment model, and their implications for the management of the urban realm and student housing experiences, thus feeding into the literature primarily focused on Western settings. The findings will have significant policy-informing potential with respect to planning, housing, and education domains. By providing evidence-based insights and identifying good practices for sustainable and non-disruptive student housing development and management, this research aims to enhance cooperation between market actors and universities, mitigate possible negative studentification impacts, improve students’ housing experiences, and offer valuable insights for other high-density Asian cities facing similar challenges in accommodating growing student populations. 隨著香港致力成為全球高等教育樞紐，非本地學生入學人數自2016年以來增長超過一倍，這一顯著發展軌跡對住房和城市規劃產生重要影響。在《2024年施政報告》宣布的「留學香港」倡議推動下，這一增長趨勢預計將進一步加速。在此背景下，本研究探討香港快速擴張和演變的學生住房格局。 鑑於香港專用學生公寓（PBSA）的發展相對有限，以及相對獨特的租賃轉租（Lease-to-Rent）模式在香港的快速發展，本研究聚焦於這些新興企業化/機構化學生住房形式的運作模式、由此產生的影響以及學生體驗。了解這些問題可能揭示學生化（Studentification）現象的新形式或階段及其更廣泛的影響，特別是在高密度亞洲環境中的表現。 本研究探討四個主要問題：香港學生住房市場如何應對非本地學生需求近期的快速增長？在當地城市和監管環境影響下，香港學生住房機構化進程是如何展開的？香港學生住房供應的擴張如何促進學生化現象並影響當地社區？學生在新型企業化住宿中的居住體驗與其他供應模式相比如何？ 這項三年期項目將採用混合方法研究，運用空間分析、問卷調查、文獻分析、實地觀察、深度訪談和焦點小組等方法，考察香港學生住房供應格局的變化。通過與供應方利益相關者、政策和治理代表、當地社區利益相關者以及學生的深度參與，為學生住房發展過程及其多方面影響提供全面見解。 本研究基於高密度亞洲城市環境中學生住房擴張，豐富學生化的理論。通過考察新形式的企業化學生住房，特別是租賃轉租的投資模式，及其對城市領域管理和學生住房體驗的影響，進一步拓展了現有主要基於西方學生住房發展的學生化文獻和理論。 本研究發現將在城市規劃、住房和教育領域具有重要的政策指導潛力。通過提供循證見解並識別可持續和非破壞性學生住房發展和管理的良好實踐，本研究旨在加強市場參與者與大學之間的合作，減輕學生化現象可能產生的負面影響，改善學生的住房體驗，並為面臨類似挑戰的其他高密度亞洲城市在容納不斷增長的學生人口方面提供寶貴參考。

17613325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17613325.value: 中文播客文化：社群、平台與經濟

17613325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17613325.value: Prof Fang, Kecheng Prof McHugh, Siobhan

17613325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613325.value: This project will investigate how different Chinese podcasting cultures are being constructed through the communities, apps and economic transactions made possible by bespoke Chinese podcasting platforms. Despite the rapidly growing popularity of podcasting in China, the limited existing media studies scholarship on podcasting in the region has predominantly focussed on issues of feminist podcasting (and content moderation thereof), meaning we are yet to understand the broader social impact of this novel media technology. We need to map the varied communities emerging from Chinese podcasting, so that we can pioneer an innovative media anthropology approach to understanding the relationships between content creators, audiences, podcast production teams and technology company representatives stemming from novel technoauditory platforms. We need to critically analyse Chinese podcasting apps so that we can open significant new ground in media and communication studies by identifying the cultural meanings and implied users/uses propagated by Chinese podcasting platforms. We need to document the transactional flows that surround Chinese podcasting, so that we can materially advance scientific understanding of the socioeconomics of platform economies. The proposed project will convene an international team of scholars combining expertise in oral history, media studies and media anthropology to construct a comprehensive account of Chinese podcasting cultures to understand the social consequences of this unconventional yet influential ascendent media form. We will perform participant observation as community managers of Chinese podcasting production companies to document the construction of social interactions around podcasts, in order to map the varied communities emerging from Chinese podcasting. We will undertake a critical analysis of Chinese podcast apps, in order to understand the cultural meanings and implied users/uses of Chinese podcasting platforms. We will elicit and interpret narratives surrounding the multiple monetary exchanges enacted through Chinese podcast apps, in order to document the transactional flows that support podcast creation. The benefit of these outcomes will be maximised through academic research outputs, and a programme of public engagement centred around the creation of our own podcast programme, ‘The China Podcast Podcast’, which will bring together podcast creators, platforms and audiences to discuss the influence of this novel media format on Chinese society. 本研究將探討中文播客文化如何透過社群、應用程式以及專屬中文播客平台所促成的經濟交易而被建構。儘管播客在中國的流行程度迅速攀升，現有相關的媒介研究卻十分有限，且多集中於女性主義播客及其內容審查相關議題，因此我們對這一新興媒介技術更廣泛的社會影響仍缺乏深入理解。我們需要描繪中文播客所衍生的多樣化社群版圖，以開創創新的媒介人類學研究途徑，從而理解在這些新興的聽覺技術平台中，內容創作者、聽眾、播客製作團隊與科技公司代表之間的關係。我們需要對中文播客應用程式進行批判性分析，以開闢媒介與傳播研究的新領域，辨識這些中文播客平台所傳遞的文化意涵及其隱含的使用者與使用情境。我們還需要記錄圍繞中文播客產生的各種交易流程，以推進對平台經濟在社會經濟學層面的實質性理解。本研究將組建一支國際學術團隊，結合口述歷史、媒介研究與媒介人類學的專業解讀，構築對中文播客文化的全面性敘述，以理解這一非傳統卻具影響力的新興媒介形式的社會效應。我們將以中文播客製作公司的社群管理者身份開展參與式觀察，記錄播客相關的社會互動建構過程，以描繪中文播客所衍生的多樣化社群版圖。我們將對中文播客應用程式進行批判性分析，以理解中文播客平台的文化意涵及其隱含的使用者與使用方式。我們還將搜集並詮釋由中文播客應用程式所產生的多重金錢交易敘事，以記錄那些推動播客創作的交易流程。該項目研究成果將透過學術出版，以及製作我們自己的公眾參與播客節目——《中文播客播客》（The China Podcast Podcast），連結播客創作者、平台與聽眾三方，共同討論這一新興媒介形式對中國社會所產生的影響，從而實現影響力最大化。

17613425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17613425.value: 高密度城市區域行人空氣污染暴露的分佈模式研究

17613425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613425.value: Air pollution is a critical global health issue, responsible for an estimated 6.7 million premature deaths annually. The problem is particularly pronounced in densely populated urban areas, where emissions from traffic and human activities are concentrated, and urban structures like street canyons hinder the natural dispersion of pollutants. Pedestrians, often exposed to these emissions with limited physical barriers, are especially vulnerable to the harmful health effects. Traditional exposure assessments, however, often focus on broader spatial scales (e.g., regional population-based exposure), overlooking the localized pollution variations experienced by pedestrians. This study aims to bridge this gap by examining pedestrian exposure to air pollution, offering insights to support urban planning and public health initiatives. This research will develop a methodological framework to assess Pedestrian-weighted Exposure to Particulate Matter (PEPM) on urban sidewalks. This study will focus specifically on PM2.5, a pollutant known for its significant risks to public health. To achieve this, a mobile sensing strategy will be deployed to collect high-resolution data on PM2.5 concentrations and pedestrian counts, enabling PEPM measurement with broader spatial coverage and finer granularity than traditional fixed monitoring. A multi-modal feature engineering strategy will integrate diverse urban characteristics, particularly those derived from unstructured data sources (e.g., street canyon characteristics from 3D models, streetscape elements from street view imagery), to comprehensively analyze exposure factors. Additionally, a graph-embedded approach will be developed to model sidewalk exposure, capturing the dynamics of pollutant dispersion and pedestrian flow within urban street networks. A case study in Futian, Shenzhen will be conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. This research will provide a nuanced understanding of pedestrian exposure distribution, potentially revealing patterns distinct from traditional exposure assessments. The insights gained will inform urban planning and policy incentives to mitigate exposure risks. The methodology developed can be adapted to other areas with similar urban environments for air pollution management. Ultimately, this research aims to foster the development of pedestrian-friendly urban spaces that improve air quality and enhance public health outcomes.

17614125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614125.value: 中国硕士毕业生职业发展成果研究

17614125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614125.value: Worldwide, an increasing number of university graduates are enrolled in master’s degree programmes. In China, the expansion of postgraduate education since the 1990s has been accompanied by policy initiatives to improve knowledge and skills for talents in the knowledge economy. The master’s degree also became an alternative pathway for university graduates not immediately transitioning to the labour market, helping them to prepare for job market entry amid intense competition. The traditional value of the master’s degree in Chinese academic master programmes was to deepen disciplinary knowledge and prepare for doctoral study. However, the nature of the master's degree has significantly changed. Many students in China today pursue a master’s degree to improve their employability. Despite this changing nature of master’s degrees, empirical evidence is lacking on whether they indeed improve graduates’ career outcomes. In addition, even if there is a distinction between academic and professional-oriented master’s programmes in China, and students have slightly different expectations of career outcomes across programmes; empirical evidence of comparison about students’ career outcomes is unclear. The proposed project aims to investigate the career outcomes of master’s graduates in normative and subjective terms, compare outcomes across institutional and disciplinary contexts and types of master’s programmes, and conceptualise the social, economic, and cultural value of a master’s degree in the changing labour market. The project draws on the theoretical approach of human capital, credentialism, and job mobility and will be conducted over 36 months using explanatory sequential mixed methods. In the first stage, two secondary data sources will be used for quantitative analysis: publicly accessible education and employment data and national survey data on master’s students. Descriptive and regression analysis will be applied. The second stage will focus on qualitative semi-structured interview data. After the twenty pilot interviews, based on maximum variance sampling considering regions, university tiers, disciplines, and types of master’s programmes, 100 interviewees will be recruited. Content and thematic analysis will be used to analyse the qualitative data. The findings will contribute to theoretical development by defining the master’s degree in economic, sociological, and cultural terms. Practically, the project will offer suggestions for designing and implementing master’s programmes regarding programme goals, curriculum and assessments, allocate resources and foster employability for master’s students. 在全球范围内，攻读硕士学位的高校毕业生数量持续增长。自20世纪90年代以来，中国为适应知识经济发展需求，实施了一系列培养高层次专业人才的政策，推动研究生教育规模不断扩大。与此同时，硕士学位也逐渐成为高校毕业生暂缓进入就业市场、提升就业竞争力的替代选择。传统意义上，中国学术型硕士教育主要致力于深化专业知识和培养科研能力，为博士阶段学习奠定基础。然而当前硕士学位教育的定位已发生显著变化，越来越多的学生攻读硕士主要是为了增强就业竞争力。 尽管硕士学位教育的功能正在发生变化，但关于其是否真正能提升毕业生职业发展质量的实证研究仍然不足。此外，虽然中国的学术型与专业型硕士项目在培养目标上存在差异，学生对不同项目的职业发展预期也有所不同，但关于两类项目毕业生职业发展成果的系统比较研究仍较为缺乏。 本研究拟从客观就业指标和主观职业认知两个维度，探究硕士毕业生的职业发展状况。研究将比较不同高校层级、学科领域和硕士项目类型之间的差异，并基于劳动力市场变革背景下，从社会、经济和文化三个层面重新审视硕士学位的价值。研究采用顺序性解释混合研究方法，以人力资本理论、文凭主义理论和工作流动理论为框架，计划在36个月完成研究。第一阶段将利用公开的教育就业数据和全国硕士生追踪调查数据，运用描述性统计与回归分析方法进行定量研究；第二阶段将聚焦质性研究，先进行20个预访谈，然后按地区、高校层次、学科门类和硕士项目类型进行最大差异抽样，对100名受访者进行半结构化访谈，最后采用内容分析与主题分析法处理质性数据。 研究成果将在理论上从经济学、社会学和文化学角度深化对硕士学位价值的理解。在实践层面，研究将为硕士项目的设计与实施提供具体建议，包括培养目标设定、课程与评估体系优化、资源配置策略以及学生就业能力提升等方面。

17614725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614725.value: 香港人口事件對精神健康的影響：一項為期22年的時間序列分析

17614725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17614725.value: Prof Chang, Wing Chung Dr Ni, Michael Yuxuan Dr Ning, Ke Prof Tian, Linwei

17614725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614725.value: Population events, such as natural disasters, human-made disasters, and conflicts, are known to have negative impacts on mental health. In the past 20 years, several population events have occurred in Hong Kong, including the outbreak of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) in 2003, Occupy Central in 2014, social unrest in 2019, and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Despite increasing evidence that population events are associated with mental disorders such as depression and anxiety, previous studies have been confined to traditional cross-sectional or longitudinal designs and lacked comparisons across population events. In addition, there is limited information on how the population events changed the use of psychotropic medications and mental health services. To address these knowledge gaps, we propose to conduct an interrupted time-series analysis study based on real-time data extracted from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS), a territory-wide electronic health records database in Hong Kong. The study will examine whether there is a link between population events and changes in the incidence of mental disorders, prescriptions for psychotropic drugs, and use of mental health services over 22 years from 2002 to 2024. Mental health impacts will also be compared between two epidemics (SARS and COVID-19), between two major social events (Occupy Central 2014 and Social Unrest 2019), and also between the epidemics and the major social events. All patients aged 16 or above who visited specialist out-patient clinics, general out-patient clinics, accident and emergency departments, and hospital inpatients admitted in Hong Kong from 1 January 2002 to 31 December 2024 will be eligible for inclusion in our study. The primary outcomes will be the incidence of mental disorders, psychotropic medication prescriptions, and mental health service uses. Psychiatric diagnoses and prescriptions will be identified according to the International Classification of Diseases. The first recorded code for the outcomes of each diagnosis, psychotropic medication prescription, and service use within the study period will be classified as an incident diagnosis or event. Weekly incidence numbers of outcome measures before and after each population event will be extracted and fitted regarding the population figures using the autoregressive integrated moving average model with exogenous variable (ARIMAX) for interrupted time-series analysis. The proposed study will shed light on the differential impacts of population events ranging from collective actions to epidemics, which will in turn facilitate policy-making to develop mental health prevention and promotion strategies for enhancing population mental health.

17614825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614825.value: 利用生成式人工智能推动个性化課外学习，賦能香港低收入學校學生的英語學習

17614825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17614825.value: Prof Gu, Ming Yue Michelle Prof Jin, Tan Prof Li, Guofang Prof Tan, Cheng Yong Dr Wang, Qiu

17614825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614825.value: Hong Kong suffers from severe disparities in socioeconomic status (SES). These disparities influence the quality of in-class and out-of-class English learning experiences that students have access to, creating an SES-induced English divide that deprives low-SES individuals of potential upward mobility. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is suggested to have the potential to empower self-directed learning and personalization of learning. This project explores whether helping Hong Kong students at low-SES schools harness PIEL-GenAI (self-directed use of GenAI for personalized English learning beyond the classroom) can enhance their English learning. This 1.5-year project comprises two phases. Phase 1 (0.5 year) adopts an exploratory sequential design. Thematic analyses of interview responses of 45 first-year (Secondary 4 [S4]) students, with varying levels of GenAI use, from three low-SES schools in Hong Kong will be undertaken to reveal the dimensions of PIEL-GenAI, its relationships with English learning (in-class and out-of-class English learning and English proficiency), and its influencing factors. Hierarchical regression analyses and structural equation modeling analyses of subsequent survey responses and English proficiency test scores of 250 S4 students from the three low-SES schools will test the observed relationships and influencing factors. Phase 2 (1 year) adopts a quasi-experimental design to assess the immediate and delayed impact of a PIEL-GenAI intervention (7-week explicit training + 8-week experiential learning) that utilizes a free GenAI app, Poe. The same cohort of students will be assigned to the experimental (receiving the PIEL-GenAI intervention) or control group (self-exploring Poe without any intervention) based on their class, 125 students each. Multi-group latent growth modeling (LGM) analyses on survey responses and English tests collected at three time points will contrast the growth trajectories of PIEL-GenAI, out-of-class English learning, English learning motivation and in-class engagement, and English test scores between the experimental and control groups. Content analyses of class observation data will further reveal variations in in-class learning experience across the two groups. Content analyses of PIEL-GenAI learning portfolios and GenAI conversation logs, and thematic analyses and epistemic network analyses on interview responses collected from 50 experimental group students who exhibit differential PIEL-GenAI gains after the intervention will reveal, contrast, and visualize working mechanisms of the intervention for different students. This study offers insights into the potential role of GenAI in enhancing English learning of students at low-SES schools in Hong Kong. It helps theorize PIEL-GenAI and its relation to English learning, and will generate an empirically tested PIEL-GenAI intervention model. 香港存在嚴重的貧富差距，這些差距影響來自低社會經濟地位（SES）學校的學生在課堂內外的英語學習，造成由SES引發的英語鴻溝，剝奪低SES學生向上流動的潛力。生成式人工智能（GenAI）可以賦能自主學習和個人化學習。本項目探討如何幫助香港低SES學校的學生在課外自主使用GenAI進行個人化英語學習（PIEL-GenAI），以提升他們的英語學習成效。 該項目為期一年半，分為兩個階段。第一階段（半年）通過對來自三所香港低SES學校、GenAI使用程度有差異的30名中四學生進行訪談，挖掘PIEL-GenAI的維度、與英語學習（課內及課外英語學習及英語能力）的關係及其影響因素。接著，對250名來自同三所低SES學校的中四學生進行問卷調查及英語能力測試，採用迴歸分析和結構方程模型檢驗來檢驗相關關係和影響因素。 第二階段（1年）採用準實驗研究設計，評估PIEL-GenAI干預（7週訓練＋8週體驗學習）對英語學習的即時及延遲影響。250名學生按班級分組，隨機分配到實驗組（接受PIEL-GenAI干預）和對照組（自我探索Poe GenAI應用，無任何干預）。在多個時間點收集問卷和英語測試，並用成長模型（LGM）進行分析，對比兩組在PIEL-GenAI、課外英語學習、英語學習動機、課堂參與度及英語成績的成長軌跡。課堂觀察內容分析則進一步揭示兩組在課堂學習體驗上的差異。對實驗組中50名PIEL-GenAI成效差異較大學生的學習檔案和GenAI對話紀錄進行內容分析，並對其訪談資料進行主題及認知網絡分析，以揭示、對比並視覺化干預對不同學生的作用機制。 本研究將提供GenAI在提升香港低SES學校學生英語學習中的作用，並提供一個經實證檢驗的PIEL-GenAI干預模型。

17615125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615125.value: 算法如何重構歷史：文化記憶、中國性與情感空間

17615125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615125.value: The planned study is inspired by a conspicuous phenomenon in contemporary China: the increasing representation of “China” and “Chineseness” as ahistorical, flattened, and monolithic cultural spaces. Within digital entertainment, this trend is particularly evident in subgenres such as time travel and alternate history, which are characterized by deliberate anachronisms, parody, and modern references embedded within historical settings. This phenomenon is part of a global trend of the (dis)appearance of history in popular culture during the algorithmic era, yet it distinctly reflects the ideological and socio-economic conditions of a neoliberalized China. The project aims to explore how these media forms construct an imagined “traditional Chinese society,” often through algorithmic computations that tap into collective fantasies and desires, as well as the social function of these affective spaces. The study will prompt a reexamination of the relationship between modernity and cultural memory in light of Lyotard’s notion of a de-historical era, where grand historical narratives are replaced by fragmented, commercially repurposed histories. In particular, the research will investigate the revival of historical tropes, especially those related to gender, that act as vehicles for contemporary social anxieties and fantasies. By delving into these dynamics, the study seeks to provide a nuanced understanding of how cultural memory and Chineseness are constructed and consumed in the context of technological democratization. Methodologically, the proposed study will combine traditional textual analysis with big data analysis and reader/audience ethnography. The primary texts will include online literature works, TV/web dramas, short videos, and micro-dramas that have emerged in recent years. Due to their large volume, these texts are well-suited for big data analysis. This approach will quantitatively examine stylistic and affective patterns in these texts and investigate the algorithmic processes and perceptions of algorithms that influence content creation and dissemination. Additionally, audience ethnography will be employed to understand how readers and viewers engage with these narratives, revealing how cultural memory and Chineseness are interpreted and emotionally experienced. In short, through an interdisciplinary approach that combines traditional humanities methods with computational techniques, the project aims to fill an important gap by focusing on how technology shapes subjectivities and fosters a commodified and ahistorical sense of Chineseness. By examining the interplay between cultural memory and digital platforms, the study will provide insights into the broader implications of these processes for identity formation and affective politics in contemporary China. 這項研究計劃源於當代中國一個引人注目的現象：「中國」與「中國性」日益被呈現為去歷史化、平面化、同質化的文化空間。 在數碼娛樂領域，這種趨勢在穿越劇、架空歷史等亞類型中尤為顯著——這些作品通過刻意的時代錯置、戲仿手法，以及歷史場景中植入的現代元素，構建出獨特的敘事景觀。 這一現象既是算法時代全球流行文化中歷史消失/再現趨勢的一部分，又折射出新自由主義化中國特有的意識形態與社會經濟狀況。 本研究旨在探討這些媒介形態如何通過算法利用集體幻想與慾望，建構想像中的「傳統中國社會」，並剖析這些情感空間的社會功能。 本研究將基於利奧塔所提出的「去歷史化時代」概念——即宏大歷史敘事被碎片化、商品化的歷史重構所取代——重新審視現代性與文化記憶的關係。 研究將重點聚焦某些傳統母題（特別是與性別相關的母題）在當前網絡文化的重新興起，揭示其如何成為承載社會焦慮與集體想像的載體。 通過深入解析這些動態機制，本研究試圖闡釋技術民主化語境下文化記憶與「中國性」是如何被建構與消費的。 方法論層面，本研究將傳統文本分析、大數據分析與讀者/觀眾訪談相結合。 研究文本則涵蓋近年興起的網絡文學、影視劇、短視頻與微短劇。 由於文本的數量巨大，特別適合大數據分析。 研究將用定量方法分析文本的風格特徵與情感模式，同時揭示影響內容生產與傳播的算法機制與算法認知。 受眾分析則著力揭示受眾如何通過情感參與重構敘事，展現文化記憶與「中國性」的闡釋維度與情感實踐。 簡言之，通過融合傳統人文學科與計算技術的跨學科方法，本研究致力於揭示技術如何形塑主體性、催生商品化與去歷史化的「中國性」認知。 通過解析文化記憶與數碼平台的互動機制，本研究將為理解當代中國身份建構與情感政治提供新的理論視角。

17615425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615425.value: 基於香港20年隊列研究探索抑鬱軌跡與缺血性心臟病之性別特異性關聯與機制

17615425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17615425.value: Dr Chen, Yuntao Prof Kawachi, Ichiro Dr Lam, Wendy Wing Tak Dr Schooling, Catherine Mary Dr Yang, Zhao

17615425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615425.value: Depression often co-occurs with ischemic heart disease (IHD). Understanding the relationship between depression and IHD is crucial, especially in Hong Kong where mental health has become a pressing public health issue. Although depression is recognized as a risk factor for IHD, most previous studies have only measured depression at a single timepoint. As such, whether changes in depression are relevant to the risk of IHD is still unclear. The dynamic nature of depression and its complex interplay with IHD necessitate a longitudinal approach to establish causal relationship and inform interventions. Moreover, depression has an apparent gender disparity, but the gender disparity has not been well considered in previous studies. It is also unclear why depression may lead to higher risk of IHD. To bridge these gaps, we aim to investigate the association of the long-term patterns of depression, i.e., depression trajectory, with the risk of IHD. We will examine the potential differences between men and women in terms of depression trajectories and how depression trajectories may influence the risk of IHD. We will also examine the underlying pathways, including both biological pathways via metabolites and proteins, and behavioral pathways, via smoking, alcohol use, physical activity, social contact and isolation. We will utilize a 20-year cohort study, the Elderly Health Service (EHS) cohort in Hong Kong, that includes repeated measures of depression, comprehensive information on IHD mortality and incidence, and social-behavioral information. In EHS, we will construct depression trajectories using latent class analysis based on repeated measures of depressive symptoms, measured by Geriatric Depression Scale in 116,180 people who have completed at least two measures. We will then use Cox-proportional hazards model to examine their associations with IHD mortality and incidence. To examine the potential gender difference, we will conduct gender-specific analyses. To examine the biological pathways, we will measure metabolomics and proteomics in 700 IHD cases and 700 matched controls from Elderly Biobank established based on EHS cohort. We will identify the biomarkers related to both depression trajectories and IHD, and conduct causal mediation analysis. Similarly, we will examine the pathways via social behavioural factors in EHS. This study will provide valuable information on depression trajectories in elderly people in Hong Kong, and shed light on the link between depression trajectories and IHD, especially the gender difference. By unravelling the underlying pathways, this study holds promise for identifying potential targets for intervention and prevention strategies to mitigate depression-related cardiovascular risk. 抑鬱症常與缺血性心臟病（IHD）共同發生。了解抑鬱症與IHD之間的關係至關重要，尤其是在香港，心理健康已成為一個迫切的公共衛生問題。儘管抑鬱症被認為是IHD的一個風險因素，但大多數先前的研究僅在單一時間點測量抑鬱症。因此，抑鬱症的變化是否與IHD的風險相關仍不清楚。抑鬱症的動態特性及其與IHD的複雜互動，要求採用縱向研究方式，以建立因果關係並提供干預依據。此外，抑鬱症存在明顯的性別差異，但在過去的研究中尚未充分考慮這一點，也不清楚為何抑鬱症會導致較高的IHD風險。為了彌補這些空白，我們旨在研究抑鬱症的長期變化模式，即抑鬱軌跡，與IHD風險之間的關聯。我們將探討男性與女性在抑鬱軌跡方面的潛在差異，以及抑鬱軌跡如何影響IHD的風險。同時，我們也將研究其潛在的途徑，包括通過代謝物和蛋白質的生物學途徑，以及通過行為途徑，例如吸菸、酗酒、運動、社交接觸與隔離。這項研究將利用一個長達20年的隊列研究——香港的長者健康服務（EHS）隊列，該隊列包含多次測量抑鬱症狀、全面的IHD死亡與發病資料，以及社會行為資料。在EHS中，我們將基於多次測量的老年抑鬱量表（Geriatric Depression Scale）運用潛類別分析（latent class analysis）來建立抑鬱軌跡，樣本包括116,180名完成至少兩次測量的受試者。接著，我們會利用Cox比例風險模型，分析這些軌跡與IHD死亡率和發病率之間的關聯。為了研究性別差異，我們還會進行性別特異性分析。為了探討生物學途徑，我們會在基於EHS建立的長者生物庫（Elderly Biobank）中，從700例IHD病例及700名配對的對照中測量代謝組學和蛋白組學，識別與抑鬱軌跡和IHD相關的生物標誌物，並進行因果中介分析。同時，我們也會研究通過社會行為因素的潛在途徑。這項研究將為香港長者的抑鬱軌跡提供寶貴資訊，並闡明抑鬱軌跡與IHD之間的關係，尤其是性別差異。通過揭示潛在的生物學和行為途徑，這項研究有望協助找到潛在的干預和預防策略目標，以減少抑鬱相關的心血管風險。

17615525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615525.value: 探究人际互动与人类与人工智能对话代理（如ChatGPT）互动中共同与差异性的行为与神经机制

17615525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17615525.value: Prof Dean, Mobbs Dr Yao, Yuanwei

17615525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615525.value: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is being integrated into a rapidly growing number of areas of our daily lives. Applications range from algorithms in navigation systems to AI-based conversational agents (AICAs, e.g., ChatGPT). The interactive and conversational approach of AICAs has revolutionized how we interact with technology and renders AICAs promising tools for applications traditionally based on human-human interactions, including personalized assistants, financial advice, or healthcare. However, concerns about AI trustworthiness, influence on public opinion, and inferiority in domains characterized by interpersonal interaction, such as psychotherapy, are increasingly debated. In human-human interactions, humans can utilize a set of social-cognitive functions and brain systems to understand others, learn whom to trust, utilize interpersonal emotion regulation, and identify social influence. While the cognitive and neural processes involved in human-human interaction have been extensively studied, it remains unknown whether humans engage the same cognitive and neural processes in interaction with AICAs. With the rapid integration of AICAs into everyday life, examining whether the underlying cognitive and neural processes resemble those involved in human-human (or non-social) interaction can facilitate estimation of risks and benefits, help design AICAs, and inform AI literacy programs. The present project aims to examine common and distinct cognitive and neural processes that underlie human-AICA interaction in comparison to human-human or non-social interaction. The project intends to focus on domains with both imminent implementation of AICAs and established neurobehavioral models in human-human interaction. The project will focus on the domains of: 1) Mentalizing: inferring triats and intentions of other humans or AICAs, 2) Trust learning: learning to trust other humans or AICAs, 3) Interpersonal emotion regulation: emotion regulation facilitation by a psychotherapist or an AICA, 4) Social influence: impact of diverging aesthetic, moral, or health perception by other humans or AICAs. To precisely examine the underlying cognitive and neural processes, functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) will be implemented in all experiments, and the data will be examined using advanced computational modeling and brain imaging analyses. We hypothesize that interactions between humans and AICAs will engage overlapping cognitive and neural processes as those observed in human-human interactions. However, we additionally hypothesize critical distinctions, such as variations in trust acquisition speed, emotion regulation enhancement, and the involvement of mentalizing or default mode brain systems. Findings can support development of overarching models on human-AICA interaction, determine potential risks (overtrust, social influence) and opportunities (scalable psychotherapy interventions), and contribute to the design of AICAs and AI-literacy programs.

17615625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615625.value: 生成式人工智能輔助嘅多模態創作對弱勢少數族裔英語學習者批判性數字素養嘅影響：一項縱向敘事研究

17615625.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17615625.value: Dr Darvin, Ron Prof GU, Mingyue Michelle Prof Lai, Chun Dr Mirhosseini, Seyedabdolhamid

17615625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615625.value: Critical digital literacies (CDL) refer to social practice of integrating technologies into everyday lives with a critical and reflective stance. CDL learning is increasingly core to academic and future success. The prevalence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) affords opportunities and challenges for CDL learning. Compared to their mainstream counterparts, underprivileged ethnic minority English learners in HK are often disadvantaged in using GenAI for CDL learning because many of them cannot afford the subscription fee for GenAI tools, most of which are not publicly accessible and require purchase in the current educational context of HK. What exacerbates the situation is that GenAI technologies, despite the potential benefits, are often biased towards dominant norms that underrecognize and marginalize ethnic minority learners’ multimodal and multilingual literacy experiences. To capitalize on GenAI for CDL learning, ethnic minority English learners therefore need extra support which, however, is not widely available, risking being further disadvantaged and lagging behind their peers in CDL development. In this context, some secondary schoolteachers offer underprivileged minority students fee-free GenAI-assisted digital multimodal composing (DMC), which refers to new literacy activities that use GenAI to produce texts by interweaving words with images, videos and other modes. Prior research shows that DMC recognizes minority’s multimodal repertoires as assets and DMC with GenAI can help minority students catch up with their studies and enhance English learning motivation. Yet whether GenAI-assisted DMC has made a difference in underprivileged minority students’ CDL development remains underexplored. Given the significance of CDL in determining individual success, this study draws on New Literacies Studies to investigate the impact of GenAI-assisted DMC on underprivileged ethnic minority students’ CDL. Informed by the multimodal turn in literacy research, this study conceptualizes CDL as dynamic and multifaceted, and uses longitudinal narrative inquiry to analyze the potential changes of CDL of 18 underprivileged minority students participating in GenAI-assisted DMC projects. Participants will be recruited through a school implementing such projects. Data will be collected through three rounds of in-depth interviews, supplemented by artifacts, mind-maps, screen recordings, composing logs, lesson observations, and informal conversations with teachers and parents. This study seeks to gather thick descriptions of underprivileged minority students’ GenAI-assisted DMC experiences to generate theoretical understandings of their dynamic CDL development. It will also offer practical advice on how to minimize educational inequalities and how underprivileged ethnic minority students can be better supported in literacy learning in GenAI times. 批判性數字素養（Critical Digital Literacies, CDL）指喺日常生活中以批判性同反思性立場整合技術嘅社會實踐，其學習已日益成為學業成功與未來發展嘅關鍵能力。生成式人工智能（GenAI）嘅普及為批判性數字素養嘅培養帶嚟機遇與挑戰。與主流群體相比，香港嘅弱勢少數族裔英語學習者喺利用 GenAI 進行批判性數字素養學習方面常處於劣勢，因為佢哋大多無力承擔 GenAI 工具嘅訂閱費用。而喺香港當前嘅教育情境中，呢類工具大多不對公眾免費開放且需付費使用。更為嚴峻嘅係，儘管 GenAI 技術具有潛在優勢，但其往往偏向主流規範，忽視甚至邊緣化少數族裔學習者嘅多模態與多語種讀寫經驗。要充分利用 GenAI 促進批判性數字素養學習，少數族裔英語學習者需要額外嘅支持，然而此類支持並不普遍，致使其喺 CDL 發展上存在進一步落後於同儕嘅風險。 喺此背景下，一啲中學教師為弱勢少數族裔學生提供免費嘅 GenAI 輔助數字多模態創作（Digital Multimodal Composing, DMC）機會，即利用 GenAI 融合文字、圖像、影片及其他模態進行文本生產嘅新型讀寫活動。已有研究表明，DMC 能將少數族裔嘅多模態資源視為優勢，而 GenAI 輔助嘅 DMC 有助於其縮小學業差距並提升英語學習動機。然而，GenAI 輔助嘅 DMC 是否真正促進咗弱勢少數族裔學生嘅批判性數字素養發展，仍缺乏深入探究。 鑒於批判性數字素養對個體發展嘅重要性，本研究借鑒新素養研究（New Literacies Studies）嘅視角，探討 GenAI 輔助 DMC 對弱勢少數族裔學生 CDL 嘅影響。基於讀寫研究嘅「多模態轉向」，本研究將 CDL 視為動態且多維嘅概念，並採用縱向敘事研究方法，分析 18 名參與 GenAI 輔助 DMC 項目嘅弱勢少數族裔學生嘅 CDL 變化。研究對象將通過實施此類項目嘅學校招募，數據收集將包括三輪深度訪談，並輔以作品、思維導圖、屏幕錄製、寫作日誌、課堂觀察以及同教師同家長做嘅非正式訪談。 本研究旨在通過詳盡描述弱勢少數族裔學生嘅 GenAI 輔助 DMC 經歷，揭示 CDL 發展嘅動態機制，並提出喺生成式人工智能時代縮小教育不平等、優化弱勢少數族裔讀寫學習支持嘅實踐建議。

17615725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17615725.value: 關係動態中的自我關懷：溝通與心理健康的交互影響

17615725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17615725.value: Dr Choy, Chak Pui Jacky Prof Lum, Terry Yat Sang Dr Wong, Ming Yin Stephanie

17615725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615725.value: There is a growing trend of older couples residing independently in the community. Compared to younger couples, older couples often take on caregiving responsibilities that may shift within the partnership as individual health conditions change. This rotation of caregiving duties can lead to the need for renegotiation of daily routines and responsibilities, potentially adding complexity and stress to the relationship if not effectively managed. Spousal caregivers commonly experience higher levels of care provision, increased depressive symptoms, elevated financial and physical burdens, and decreased psychological well-being. In recent years, self-compassion has emerged as a vital protective factor against psychological distress, characterized by a sensitivity to suffering in oneself and others, along with a commitment to alleviate and prevent it. Research suggests that older people and caregivers who possess self-compassion report lower psychological distress. While there is a growing body of literature on self-compassion in older people and family caregivers, most studies focus on its impact on individual or relational outcomes. Limited research has examined the extent to which one partner’s self-compassion affects each other's psychological well-being, as well as the underlying mediational mechanisms. The individual perspective overlooks the interdependent relationship where psychological well-being of both is affected by their perception of and reactions to each other. Factors such as communication patterns and dyadic behavioral responses to care play a crucial role in shaping the well-being of older couples. Nonviolent communication, also known as compassionate communication, has been identified as a potential mechanism through which self-compassion can impact psychological well-being in dyadic relationships. Drawing on dyadic coping models and the Interdependence Model, the proposed study aims to investigate how self-compassion within older couples influences each other's psychological distress and the role of nonviolent communication as a mediator in this relationship. By employing a longitudinal survey with 150 older couples at three time points, the study will utilize the Actor-Partner Interdependence Mediation Model to explore the interdependent effects of self-compassion on psychological distress within caregiving dyads, with nonviolent communication acting as a mediator. The findings of this study will enhance our understanding of self-compassion within a dyadic context, leading to the development of a framework for self-compassion that considers the dynamics of relationships. Additionally, the study will inform the development of interventions aimed at enhancing self-compassion and nonviolent communication, ultimately improving the mental well-being of older couples and other caregiving dyads. 隨著人口老化趨勢加劇，雙老家庭在社區中的居住比例日益上升。相較於年輕伴侶，年長伴侶在照顧角色的承擔上更容易因個人健康狀況的變化而產生輪替。照顧角色的轉換往往需要重新協商日常生活的安排與責任分工，若未能妥善因應，可能加劇伴侶關係的複雜性與心理壓力。配偶照顧者常面臨較高的照顧負荷、抑鬱症狀增加、財務與身體負擔加重，以及心理健康惡化等挑戰。近年來，自我關懷逐漸被視為抵禦心理困擾的重要保護因子，其核心特質包括對自身與他人痛苦的敏感性，以及致力於減輕與預防痛苦的承諾。研究指出，具備自我關懷特質的長者與照顧者，其心理困擾程度顯著較低。 儘管針對長者與家庭照顧者的自我關懷研究逐漸增加，現有文獻多聚焦於其對個人或關係層面的影響，較少探討一方的自我關懷如何影響另一方的心理健康，以及其中可能的中介機制。以個人為中心的研究視角忽略了心理健康在伴侶間的相互依存性——即彼此的感知與反應會交互影響雙方的心理狀態。在塑造年長伴侶心理健康的過程中，溝通模式與照顧行為的雙人互動反應扮演關鍵角色。其中，非暴力溝通（或慈悲溝通）被認為是自我關懷在伴侶關係中影響心理健康的潛在中介機制之一。 本研究結合對偶因應模型與相互依存模型，旨在探討年長伴侶間自我關懷如何影響彼此的心理健康，以及非暴力溝通在此關係中的中介角色。研究採縱向設計，將於三個時間點收集150對年長伴侶的資料，並運用主客體互倚性中介模型分析自我關懷在照顧關係中對心理困擾的相互影響，並以非暴力溝通作為中介變項。 本研究預期將深化我們對伴侶關係中自我關懷作用的理解，並建立一個納入關係動態的自我關懷理論架構。研究成果亦可為未來設計提升自我關懷與非暴力溝通的介入方案提供實證基礎，以促進年長伴侶及其他照顧雙人關係的心理健康。

17616225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616225.value: 香港和英國的自閉症與非自閉症人士的社交應對策略：跨文化比較

17616225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17616225.value: Prof Lui, Sai Yu Simon Dr Wong, Kathy

17616225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616225.value: Abstract Despite increasing awareness of autism spectrum disorder and improved service provision in recent decades, coping with everyday social situations in the neurotypical world remains a challenge for many autistic people. Recent research based primarily on UK adult reports has identified a number of social coping strategies used to compensate for social difficulties by both autistic and non-autistic people, explaining how autistic people may achieve improvements in social adjustment but often at the expense of compromised mental health. However, there is a lack of research informing us of the extent to which existing findings on social coping strategies are generalisable to cultural contexts beyond the West. The only existing questionnaire measure pertains to fairly shallow forms of strategies that function to camouflage social differences. The aims of the proposed study are to examine the patterns of use and correlates of social coping strategies across cultures, extending the scope of current research beyond Western countries, and to fill a current methodological gap by developing a novel tool for measuring a broader range of such strategies. We will explore the cross-cultural patterns and correlates of social coping strategies across autistic and non-autistic people in Hong Kong and the UK over two phases. We will recruit a balanced ratio of autistic and non-autistic adolescent and adult participants in both sites. We will develop and validate a new questionnaire that covers not only camouflaging behaviours but also cognitive-mediated and proactive strategies (Phase 1). Using the newly developed tool, we will then examine cross-cultural patterns in the use of social coping strategies and their quantitative relationships with autistic traits, executive functions, social functioning, and mental health outcomes (Phase 2). Potential group differences in age, gender, and/or autism diagnosis will also be examined. The findings will provide the first cross-cultural evidence of the patterns of social coping strategies used by autistic people and the wider population, shedding light on the role of sociocultural and individual factors in shaping social coping strategies and the ways in which such strategies promote positive outcomes. The new questionnaire will provide a convenient tool for scalable research and practical use across cultures. 儘管近幾十年來，人們對自閉症譜系障礙的認知不斷提升，相關服務也有所改善，但對許多自閉症人士而言，如何在日常生活中應對社交情境仍然是一項挑戰。近年以英國成人為主要研究對象的報告識別了一系列自閉症人士與非自閉症人士用來彌補社交困難的應對策略，解釋了自閉症人士在社交適應方面的改善方式，但往往以犧牲心理健康為代價。然而，至今尚缺乏關於這些社交應對策略在非西方文化背景下適用程度的研究。目前唯一的測量問卷僅涉及較為淺層的社交應對策略，用於掩飾社會差異。 本研究的目的在於檢視不同文化背景下社交應對策略的使用型式與相關因素，將研究範圍擴展至西方國家以外，並透過開發能夠測量更廣泛社交應對策略的新工具，來彌補現有方法學上的不足。 我們將分兩個階段探討香港與英國的自閉症和非自閉症人士在社交應對策略上的跨文化模式及相關因素。第一階段，我們將在兩地招募比例均衡的自閉症與非自閉症青少年及成人，並發展與驗證一份新的問卷，該問卷除了涵蓋掩飾行為外，還包括認知介導和積極策略。第二階段，我們將運用新開發的工具，分析不同文化背景下社交應對策略的使用模式，並探討其與自閉症特徵、執行功能、社交功能及心理健康之間的關係。同時，我們也將檢視不同年齡、性別及自閉症診斷群體之間的差異。 研究結果將提供有關自閉症人士及一般人群所使用的社交應對策略模式的初步跨文化證據，揭示社會文化和個人因素在塑造這些策略中的作用，以及這些策略如何促進正面的結果。新的問卷將為跨文化研究與實務應用提供便捷的工具。

17616325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616325.value: 城市樹木的智能「觀測」：面向對象的多維度樹木動態與花粉風險監測

17616325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17616325.value: Prof He, Shenjing Prof Wong, Charles Dr Wu, Shengbiao Prof Zhou, Yuyu

17616325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616325.value: Urban trees are integral to the daily life of city dwellers, providing essential ecosystem services, socio-economic-cultural benefits, and promoting human health and well-being. Nevertheless, the adverse effects of urban trees, particularly the allergenic pollen released by certain species, are increasingly recognized as significant risks to public health and the built environment. A comprehensive understanding of the balance between green benefits and pollen-related health risks is critical for effective urban planning and the management of green infrastructure. Monitoring these dual aspects of urban trees remains challenging due to the lack of detailed attributes at the individual tree level, robust estimates of allergenic pollens, and an efficient co-assessment framework. Addressing these knowledge gaps is essential to optimize the ecological and social benefits of urban trees while minimizing allergenic pollen risks, ultimately enhancing data-and-science-driven management for sustainable cities. This research proposes to integrate high-resolution remote sensing observations with advanced deep learning algorithms, time-series analytics, and process-based modeling for intelligent monitoring of urban trees. The primary goal is to measure the dual aspects of green benefits and pollen exposure risks and to investigate variations in these exposures across different spatial, temporal, and population dimensions. First, we will develop an integrated methodological framework that combines high-resolution satellite imagery, LiDAR observations, and cutting-edge deep learning algorithms to identify, segment, and classify urban trees at individual levels. Second, we will create an object-based urban "Treepedia" system to quantify various attributes of individual trees, including biophysical attributes (canopy cover, height, volume, species, greenness) and pollen concentrations. Third, we will incorporate time-series analytics of nano-satellite imagery with process-based models to enable intelligent monitoring of urban trees over time and space, focusing on the dynamics of urban trees and their pollen risks. Fourth, we will conduct a co-assessment of green benefits and pollen exposure risks by linking tree dynamics and pollen risks with population distributions to identify vulnerable hotspots across different space, time, and population dimensions. The research will contribute to the scholarly understanding of the complex interactions between tree species, pollen emissions, and public health. In practice, this research will provide robust data, methodological, and technical support for quantifying multifaceted tree attributes and enabling spatially and temporally explicit evidence for policymakers, urban planners, health sectors, and the general public. This will facilitate the creation of more intelligent, inclusive, and sustainable urban greening policies, optimizing the ecological and social benefits of urban trees while minimizing allergic pollen risks. 城市樹木是城市居民日常生活中重要的組成部分，提供關鍵的生態系統服務以及社會-經濟-文化效益，並促進人類健康與福祉。城市樹木的不利影響，特別是特定物種釋放的過敏性花粉，已日益被視為建成環境與公共衛生的潛在風險。全面理解綠色健康效益與花粉相關健康風險之間的雙重平衡，已成為規劃和管理城市綠化策略的關鍵科學與實務需求。然而，由於缺乏個體尺度城市樹木的多方面屬性、樹木層級過敏性花粉的穩健監測能力，以及有效的共同評估框架，智能監測城市樹木的雙重面向仍面臨困難。因此，這些知識差距需要被填補，以優化城市樹木的生態與社會效益，並限制過敏性花粉風險，最終目標是提升數據科學驅動的管理，以實現永續城市。 本研究提出高解析度遙測觀測與先進深度學習及時間序列演算法的新穎整合，用於城市樹木的智能監測。本研究的主要目的是測量綠色健康效益與花粉暴露風險的雙重面向，並回答關鍵問題：在不同空間、時間與人口維度下，人類的這些雙重暴露存在何種變異？ 首先，我們將開發一個整合的方法論框架，結合高解析度衛星影像、LiDAR觀測，以及最先進的深度學習演算法，以識別、分割並分類個體層級的城市樹木。其次，我們將建立一個基於物件的城市「Treepedia」系統，用於量化個體樹木的多方面屬性，包括結構性（即冠層覆蓋、高度、體量）、光譜性（即綠度），以及組成性（即物種與花粉水平）功能。第三，我們將整合奈米衛星影像的時間序列分析與基於過程的模型，以實現城市樹木在時間與空間上的智能監測，特別聚焦於城市樹木的動態及其花粉風險。第四，我們將透過連結樹木動態、花粉風險與人口分布，進行城市樹木綠色效益與花粉暴露風險的共同評估，以識別不同空間、時間與人口維度下的脆弱熱點。 本研究將提升我們對樹木物種、花粉排放與人類公共衛生之間複雜相互作用的科學理解，從空間與時間角度出發。在實務上，本研究中新開發的多任務方法論框架，用於監測城市樹木，以及新穎的基於物件的城市「Treepedia」系統，將為政府、規劃者、設計師及一般大眾提供強大的技術支持與空間明確的證據，以告知更智能、包容且永續的城市綠化政策。

17616425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616425.value: 基於階梯式元認知干預對管理癌症復發恐懼的效果：序貫多重分配隨機對照試驗

17616425.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17616425.value: Prof Chan, Karen Kar Loen Dr Chan , Wendy Wing Lok Dr Fong, Daniel Yee Tak Dr Foo, Chi Chung Prof Kwong, Ava Prof Ng, Simon Dr Smith, Ben

17616425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616425.value: While a low level of concern about the potential threat of cancer recurrence is a normal, realistic response, a high fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) can be detrimental, affecting individuals’ quality of life and functional capacity. Locally, one in four cancer survivors reported high FCR. Patients with high FCR report excessive intrusive thoughts that often lack identifiable triggers, making them difficult to dismiss. The manifestations of FCR share similar characteristics with those of other emotional disorders, such as anxiety and depression. Therefore, it may be useful to apply a theoretical model to explain the development and maintenance of FCR. The Self-Regulatory Executive Function (S-REF) model adopted a transdiagnostic approach to identify features that cut across different emotional disorders. The S-REF suggests that metacognitive beliefs about negative thinking play an essential role in the development and maintenance of emotional disorders, as these metacognitive beliefs promote intrusive thinking. Our recent work also showed that maladaptive metacognition is associated with high FCR. A theoretically based, manualized intervention, namely ConquerFear, was recently developed and showed its effectiveness in reducing FCR, but this 6-weekly face-to-face therapist-led intervention is time- and resource-consuming, which may have constrained its reach, particularly with limited health budgets. There is a suggestion to use a stepped-care FCR intervention starting with less resource-intensive intervention for patients with sub-clinical FCR and switching patients who do not respond to the less intensive intervention to a more intensive intervention. However, this is yet to be tested. The present study aims to conduct a sequential multiple-assessment randomized controlled trial (SMART) to assess the effect of an adaptive stepped-care ConquerFear intervention in managing fear of cancer recurrence among cancer survivors with subclinical levels of FCR. Eligible patients are Cantonese- or Mandarin-speaking Chinese patients diagnosed with curable cancer who had completed treatment within two years, aged 18 years or above, and with subclinical FCR. A total of 300 eligible patients, identified and recruited from the trial sites, will be randomly allocated to either eConquerFear or eHealthMaintenance as an initial intervention. At one-month post-initial intervention, participants whose FCR scores do not improve at least 10 points based on the FCRI will be re-randomized to supervised, individual, face-to-face ConquerFear intervention or group-delivered ConquerFear. The primary outcome is change in fear of cancer recurrence between baseline and 6-months post-intervention; process outcome is change in scores of metacognition and cognitive attentional syndrome. 雖然對癌症復發潛在威脅的擔憂程度較低是一種正常且現實的反應，但對癌症復發的高度恐懼可能具有不良影響，影響個人的生活質量和功能能力。在本地，有四分之一的癌症倖存者報告有較高的癌症復發恐懼。高癌症復發恐懼患者常表現出過度的侵入性思維，這些思維往往缺乏明確的誘因，令人難以驅除。癌症復發恐懼的表現與其他情緒障礙，如焦慮和抑鬱，具有相似的特徵。因此，運用理論模型來解釋癌症復發恐懼的形成與維持可能具有幫助。自我調節執行功能模型採用跨診斷的方法，旨在識別不同情緒障礙中的共同特徵。該模型認為，對負面思維的後設認知信念在情緒障礙的形成與維持中起著重要作用，因為這些信念促進侵入性思維。我們近期的研究也顯示，適應不良的後設認知與高癌症復發恐懼相關。一種基於理論、結構化的干預措施，即征服恐懼，最近已被開發出來，並證實能有效降低癌症復發恐懼，但這種為期六週、由治療師面對面指導的干預方式耗時耗資，可能限制了其覆蓋範圍，特別是在有限的醫療資源下。有建議使用階梯式照護的癌症復發恐懼干預策略，對於臨床前或輕度癌症復發恐懼的患者先採用資源較少的干預，未見改善的患者再轉換至較為密集的干預。然而，這一策略尚待驗證。本研究旨在進行一項序列多重評估的隨機對照試驗，評估適應性階梯式的征服恐懼干預在管理臨床前癌症復發恐懼的癌症倖存者中的效果。符合條件的患者為講廣東話或普通話的中國患者，診斷為可治癒的癌症，已完成治療兩年內，年齡在十八歲或以上，具有臨床前癌症復發恐懼。將從試點站點招募共三百名符合條件的患者，並隨機分配到電子征服恐懼或電子健康維護作為初步干預。在初次干預後一個月，若癌症復發恐懼得分未改善至少十分，則進行再隨機分配，接受由專人面對面指導的征服恐懼或團體形式的征服恐懼。主要結果為干預前後六個月內癌症復發恐懼的變化，過程性結果則為元認知和認知注意症候群得分的變化。

17616525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616525.value: 重新思考反思寫作：整合人工智能於高等教育評核實踐的循證框架與政策指引

17616525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17616525.value: Dr Lodge, Jason Dr Ng, Davy Tsz Kit

17616525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616525.value: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has garnered significant attention for its potential to revolutionise teaching and learning processes, and with institutions worldwide pledging to embrace generative AI (GenAI) in education, the need for guidelines to ensure effective AI integration in assessment is paramount. However, current educational policies and guidelines from international organisations and individual higher education institutions primarily offer only broad recommendations for allowing educators to adapt assessments in the AI era, lacking specific guidance on how they can or should incorporate AI into different distinct assessments. Assessments are inherently diverse, targeting various learning outcomes, objectives, and skills, such as students’ critical thinking, problem-solving, and subject-specific knowledge, while involving different learning processes. Consequently, the extent to which students are permitted to use AI will depend on the nature of the individual assessment tasks, and it is crucial to carefully consider which stage(s) of a specific assessment task students should be allowed to use AI, as well as which stage(s) they should not. Educators and policymakers must establish clear guidelines regarding the appropriate use of AI in assessments, delineating the boundaries where students should rely on their own cognitive abilities and where AI can be appropriately utilised to support both students’ learning processes and achievement of learning outcomes. Recognising the inadequacy of a one-size-fits-all strategy for AI in assessment policy, the proposed research project aims to address the gap in existing policies by developing a framework to guide the integration of AI specifically into reflective writing assessments. By investigating the impact that AI use across different stages of the reflective writing process has on students’ reflective practices and expression, the framework will provide a concrete, evidence-based protocol that delineates when and how AI can and should be utilised in such tasks, in ways that still support student learning and uphold academic integrity. The findings of this pioneering project will be applicable not only to the higher education context, but also to schools as well, both locally and internationally. It will serve as a valuable resource for educators, students, and institutions alike, serving as a blueprint for the ethical and effective integration of AI into assessment practices. Furthermore, as the first framework of its kind tailored specifically for reflective writing, it will set a crucial precedent for the development of similar frameworks and guidelines for other distinct assessment tasks, paving the way for innovative and impactful educational advancements. 人工智能（AI）的整合，因其有潛力徹底革新教與學的過程，而備受關注。隨着全球各地的院校紛紛承諾在教育中引入生成式人工智能（GenAI），如何制定政策指引以確保AI能有效融入評核，已成為當務之急。 然而，現時由國際組織及各高等教育機構所制定的教育政策與指引，多數僅提供寬泛的建議，讓教育工作者在AI時代調整評核，而缺乏針對不同評核類型的具體指引，說明他們可以或應該如何將AI納入不同的評核任務中。 評核本質上是多樣化的，針對不同的學習成果、目標與技能，例如學生的批判性思維、解難能力及專業知識，同時涉及不同的學習過程。因此，學生可否使用AI的程度，將取決於具體評核任務的性質。必須謹慎考慮學生在特定評核任務的哪個階段可以使用AI，以及在哪個階段不應使用AI。教育工作者與政策制定者必須建立明確的指引，界定AI在評核中的適當用途，清楚劃分學生應依靠自身認知能力的範圍，以及AI可被合理運用以支持學生的學習過程及達成學習成果的範疇。 鑑於「一刀切」的AI評核政策策略並不可行，本研究計劃旨在回應現行政策中的不足，制定一套專為反思寫作評核而設的AI整合框架。透過探討AI在反思寫作過程不同階段的使用對學生反思實踐與表達的影響，該框架將提供一個具體且循證的方案，明確說明在這類任務中AI可以及應該如何被使用，以同時支持學生的學習並維護學術誠信。 這項開創性的研究成果，不僅適用於高等教育環境，亦可延伸至本地及國際的中小學教育。它將成為教育工作者、學生及院校的重要資源，為AI在評核實踐中的合倫理且有效的整合提供藍本。此外，作為首個專為反思寫作設計的框架，它將為日後針對其他不同評核任務而制定的類似框架與政策指引奠定重要先例，推動創新及具影響力的教育發展。

17616925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616925.value: 整合多源数据的亚太地区双边移民人口规模预测

17616925.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17616925.value: Dr Aymerich, Olga Dr Yildiz, Dilek Dr Yu, Anny Yip-Ching

17616925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616925.value: Despite being home to over three-fifths of the global population and some of the largest migration flows that occur globally, the monitoring of international migration in the Asia-Pacific region remains largely unknown. Consequently, relatively little research on international migration in the Asia-Pacific has been developed. The lack of data and resulting research are in large part due to deficiencies in traditional migration data sources, such as census data, population registers, and surveys. Data published from these sources are often outdated and incomplete due to publication delays, inconsistent data collection processes across countries and a lack of harmonisation across countries. This proposal aims to develop a comprehensive, data-integrated approach to predicting migrant population sizes in the Asia Pacific region by combining traditional data sources with novel big data, particularly from social media platforms. Leveraging data from platforms like Facebook’s Advertising API, which provides detailed information on user demographics and mobility patterns, this project will integrate real-time social media data with traditional migration statistics. The resulting model will offer timely estimates of bilateral migrant stocks between Asia-Pacific nations, providing valuable insights into emerging migration trends. The project adapts a Bayesian hierarchical modelling framework, previously applied in the European Union context, to account for the specific challenges of migration data in the Asia-Pacific region, such as underreporting, incomplete data, and differing definitions of migrant populations across countries. By incorporating social media data, the model aims to compensate for gaps in official migration statistics, offering predictive estimates even for countries or corridors where data are missing or delayed. The proposed model will allow for continuous monitoring and now-casting of migrant population sizes, providing policymakers with actionable insights to respond to shifts in migration patterns. This is particularly important in a region where migration is closely linked to labour markets, environmental displacement, and regional political dynamics.
