By critically evaluating the effectiveness and reliability of AI-generated feedback alongside human feedback, the findings will illuminate the role of FO in sculpting student learning experiences and guide the development of educational practices that effectively integrate both human and AI-assisted feedback to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes. 在數位時代，整合 AI 輔助回饋與傳統的教師回饋，將對教育實踐產生潛在的變革性影響。本研究探討一個關鍵問題： 人工智能輔助回饋與人本回饋之間的互動如何影響大學生的自主學習（SDL）？本研究利用以學生為中心的觀點和自我系統過程理論模型，試圖解碼學生在接受回饋時的心理過程。本研究檢視了學生的回饋導向 (FO)，其中包含了他們對回饋使用中的效用、自我效能感、社會意識和責任感的認知。本研究使用結構方程模型(SEM)對香港和深圳的1,100名大學生進行定量分析，旨在闡明教師和人工智能的外部回饋對學生學習參與(LE)和持續發展學習(SDL)的影響。並深入剖析學生對兩類回饋來源「可獲性」與「可信度」的認知，如何塑造回饋環境（FE）、FO、LE及SDL之間的複雜關聯。 本研究認為，LE 代表學生參與其學習活動的過程，而 SDL 則表現為更廣泛的結果，著重於培養學習者自主並有能力管理自己的學習過程。SDL強調自主學習技能在教育與專業場域的成功遷移與應用，以支持持續的個人與職涯發展。此研究旨在提供具時效性的實證數據，延伸現有回饋理論文獻，為教育工作者與研究者提供關鍵見解，助其於AI時代建構有利培育自主學習者的回饋環境。透過嚴謹評估AI生成回饋與人本回饋的效能及信度，研究結果將揭示FO在塑造學生學習經驗中的作用，並指引教育實踐的發展方向，以有效地整合人機協作回饋，從而提高學生的參與度和學習成果。

18611725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18611725.value: 有關中文詞彙判斷的大型行為研究

18611725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18611725.value: Dr Chang, Ya-Ning Prof Chen, Hsuan-Chih Prof Cheung, Him Dr Tsang, Yiu Kei

18611725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611725.value: Due to the characteristics of written Chinese, it is sometimes ambiguous how to segment a sequence of Chinese characters into words (e.g., “一眼” may be considered as two single-character words “一” and “眼”, or a two-character word). The proposed study will investigate how Chinese characters and words are represented in the mental lexicon, by using a large-scale behavioral experiment and computational modeling. Thousands of native Chinese readers across a wide age range (from 16 to above 50 years old) and various education levels (from middle school to graduate school) will complete a lexical decision task online via the WeChat platform. The full set of stimuli includes more than 34,000 Chinese two-character words and a comparable number of nonwords (i.e., arbitrary combinations of two characters). Participants’ response accuracy and reaction time will be submitted to computational modeling, in order to comprehensively explore both item-level and individual-level factors influencing the weightings of combinatorial and holistic processing routes in Chinese visual word recognition. The results of this study will advance our understanding of the nature of Chinese words, from a psycholinguistic perspective. In terms of practical contribution, a large database of Chinese lexical decision will be generated, which will provide recognition difficulty of most Chinese two-character words and can be used by teachers and test developers of Chinese literacy. 由於中文的特性，對一連串中文字進行詞彙切分時常存在歧義（例如『一眼』可作为兩個單字詞『一』和『眼』，或一個雙字詞）。本研究將透過大規模行為實驗與計算模型，探討中文字詞在心理詞典中的表徵方式。數千名母語為中文的參與者（16歲至50歲以上，中學至研究生學歷）將透過微信平臺完成一項線上詞彙判斷任務。實驗材料包含約34,000個中文雙字詞及同等數量的非詞（即任意組合的中文雙字）。參與者的反應正確率與反應時間將導入計算模型，以全面探討影響中文詞彙辨識中組合式加工與整體式加工之路徑權重的材料及個體相關因素。本研究結果將從心理語言學角度深化對中文詞彙本質的理解。同時，研究中建立的大型資料庫將提供多數中文雙字詞的識別難度指標，可供漢語教學者及中文測驗開發者運用。

18612025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18612025.value: 社會排斥對零和信念的影響

18612025.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18612025.value: Dr Jiang, Tonglin Prof Teng, Fei

18612025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612025.value: Zero-sum beliefs refer to the subjective perception that the sum of all the gains and losses of the involved parties in a situation equals zero, wherein one party’s gain inherently offsets another party’s loss. These beliefs are prevalent across contexts, including economic exchanges, workplace dynamics, political negotiations, and daily encounters. Strong zero-sum beliefs often predict undesirable outcomes, such as increased conflicts, decreased relationship satisfaction, and impaired psychological well-being. The profound influence of zero-sum beliefs has aroused strong interest among researchers in understanding the formation of these beliefs. Recent studies have demonstrated how dispositional and situational factors influence zero-sum beliefs. However, it remains unclear whether interpersonal factors may also promote such beliefs. In this research, we examine whether ostracism, a common interpersonal experience in daily life, increases zero-sum beliefs and test the underlying psychological mechanism. We also investigate whether post-ostracism increases in zero-sum beliefs predict unethical behavior and test whether situational interventions weaken the effects of ostracism on zero-sum beliefs and unethical behavior. Ostracism occurs when individuals are excluded and ignored. When individuals are ostracized by others, they may perceive higher stress because they cannot obtain the benefits of positive interpersonal relationships. In such a stressful state, ostracized individuals may mistrust others and perceive resources as scarce, competitive, and zero-sum because doing so provides a simplistic way to navigate complex situations with minimal cognitive effort. Therefore, we predict that ostracism increases zero-sum beliefs through perceived stress. We also examine whether post-ostracism increases in zero-sum beliefs motivate individuals to behave unethically. Zero-sum beliefs entail that one’s and others’ interests are completely opposed, which may motivate ostracized individuals to acquire benefits even at the expense of others. Therefore, we predict that ostracism increases unethical behavior through zero-sum beliefs. When the zero-sum beliefs of ostracized individuals are weakened through awe interventions, their unethical behavior may also be weakened. By adopting a multimethod approach, we examine the effect of ostracism on zero-sum beliefs, reveal the psychological mechanism and behavioral consequence, and identify methods to weaken the relationships among ostracism, zero-sum beliefs, and unethical behavior. As these phenomena are prevalent in daily interactions, it is crucial to test their interrelationships. A comprehensive investigation of the relationships among ostracism, zero-sum beliefs, and unethical behavior can advance existing knowledge and theories. It also facilitates the development of intervention strategies to overcome their negative outcomes and promotes harmonious and cooperative social environments. 零和信念是一種主觀感知，指在特定情境下，所有參與者的得失總和為零，也就是說，一方的得益必然等同於另一方的損失。這種信念廣泛存在於各種社會情境中，包括經濟交易、職場互動、政治談判、以及日常社交。強烈的零和信念往往可以預測負面後果，例如衝突加劇、人際關係滿意度下降以及心理健康受損。由於零和信念對個人與社會具有深遠的影響，研究人員對其形成機制產生了極大的興趣。近期的研究顯示，性格特質和環境因素會影響零和信念的形成，但目前尚不清楚人際關係是否也會促進這種信念的產生。本研究旨在探討日常生活中常見的社會排斥現象是否會增強零和信念，並分析其背後的心理機制。我們還會研究社會排斥後零和信念的增強是否能預測不道德行為的發生，並測試干預措施是否能減弱社會排斥對零和信念和不道德行為的影響。社會排斥是指被他人拒絕和忽視。當人們經歷社會排斥時，可能會感受到更大的壓力，因為他們無法從積極和諧的人際關係中獲取益處。在這種壓力下，被排斥者可能會變得不信任他人，並將資源視為稀缺且具有競爭性的，從而產生零和博弈的思維模式。這種認知傾向有助於被排斥者以較低的認知負擔應對複雜的情境。因此，我們預計社會排斥會透過感知壓力的增加來提升零和信念。我們還會進一步地探討由社會排斥引發的零和信念會否促使被排斥者採取不道德的方法來獲取利益。零和信念意味著個人利益與他人利益完全對立，這可能會導致被排斥者為了自身利益而犧牲他人。因此，我們預計社會排斥會透過增強零和信念來促使人們進行不道德行為。當被排斥後所產生的零和信念被提升敬畏感的干預措施削弱時，被排斥者的不道德行為應會相應減少。我們將採用多種研究方法，系統性地探討社會排斥對零和信念的影響，揭示其心理機制和行為後果，並探索有效的干預措施，以減弱社會排斥、零和信念與不道德行為之間的關係。由於這些現象在日常生活中非常常見，深入理解它們之間的關係至關重要，對理論發展和實際應用均具有重要意義。全面研究社會排斥、零和信念與不道德行為之間的關係，將推進現有的知識和理論，並有助於制定有效的干預措施，以減輕其負面影響，並且促進更和諧、更具合作性的社會環境。

18612325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18612325.value: 利用生成式人工智能實現跨教育階段的自適應反饋以促進真實性語言學習

18612325.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18612325.value: Prof Lan, Yu-ju Prof SONG, Yanjie Prof Xie, Qin

18612325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612325.value: Enabling students to understand vocabulary and use language in authentic contexts is essential for effective language learning. Recently, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies, such as multimodal large language models (MLLMs), have emerged as powerful tools to support this educational paradigm. By integrating the complementary nature of different modalities, such as images, texts, and speeches, MLLMs can provide learners with personalized, interactive learning experiences, like vocabulary learning through pictures and picture-cued writing. However, integrating these AI technologies into educational settings remains controversial. While many researchers and educators advocate for actively embracing AI, a one-size-fits-all approach may not address the diverse needs of all learners. General-purpose MLLMs can generate content that includes uncommon words, which may not be suitable for younger learners. Moreover, recent studies revealed that students may rely too much on AI technologies, ultimately harming their learning outcomes. Therefore, investigating how to effectively leverage the advantages of GenAI tools in enhancing language learning while mitigating potential drawbacks is a pressing concern that warrants further study. This two-year project aims to investigate the effective utilization of generative AI technologies to promote authentic language learning. Specifically, it will focus on supporting students in learning English by independently describing common objects, events, and scenes from their daily lives. Initially, we will fine-tune an MLLM to evaluate students' writing across various educational stages and design strategies to generate real-time formative feedback adaptively to enhance their learning while avoiding over-reliance on AI. Building on this foundation, we will develop a learning support system and recruit over 500 students from various educational stages in primary and secondary schools to participate in experimental research. The research will assess the impact of generative AI on both learning outcomes and learning processes in these activities. We will employ mixed methods research to address our research questions by collecting and analyzing a variety of qualitative and quantitative experimental data, including students' background information, system logs, pre-test and post-test results, questionnaires, and eye-tracking and fNIRS data. This project possesses both theoretical and practical significance. Theoretically, we introduce a novel generative AI-driven language learning approach, outlining its implementation pathway and validating its effectiveness, thereby serving as a model for promoting the integration of generative AI in education. Practically, this learning method will empower students to independently learn English with the assistance of AI in authentic settings, which is particularly beneficial for those who lack opportunities for English language communication outside the classroom. 讓學生理解詞彙並在真實語境中運用語言對於有效的語言學習至關重要。近年來，生成式人工智能 (GenAI) 技術，例如多模態大型語言模型 (MLLM)，已成為支援此教育模式的強大工具。透過整合圖像、文字和語音等不同模態的互補性，MLLM 可以為學習者提供個人化、互動式的學習體驗，例如透過圖片學習詞彙和圖片提示寫作。然而，將這些人工智能技術融入教育環境仍存在爭議。儘管許多研究人員和教育工作者倡導積極擁抱人工智能，但一刀切的方法可能無法滿足所有學習者的多樣化需求。通用的 MLLM 可能會產生包含生僻詞彙的內容，這可能不適合年齡較小的學習者。此外，最近的研究表明，學生可能過度依賴人工智能技術，最終損害他們的學習成果。因此，研究如何有效利用 GenAI 工具的優勢來增強語言學習，同時減少其潛在的弊端，是迫切需要解決的問題，值得進一步研究。 這個為期兩年的項目旨在探索如何有效利用生成式人工智能技術來促進真實的語言學習。具體而言，它將專注於幫助學生透過獨立描述日常生活中常見的物體、事件和場景來學習英語。首先，我們將對MLLM進行微調，以評估學生在不同教育階段的寫作能力，並設計策略以自適應地產生即時形成性回饋，從而提升學生的學習效果，同時避免過度依賴人工智能。在此基礎上，我們將發展一個學習支援系統，並招募500多位來自不同教育階段的中小學學生參與實驗研究。該研究將評估生成式人工智能對這些活動中的學習成果和學習過程的影響。 我們將採用混合方法研究來解答我們的研究問題，收集和分析各種定性和定量的實驗數據，包括學生的背景資料、系統日誌、前測和後測結果、問卷調查以及眼動追蹤和近紅外光譜數據。研究項目具有理論和實踐意義。理論上，我們介紹一種新穎的生成式人工智能驅動的語言學習方法，概述其實施路徑並驗證其有效性，從而為促進生成式人工智能與教育的融合提供了典範。實踐上，這種學習方法將使學生能夠在真實的情境中藉助人工智能自主學習英語，這對於那些缺乏課堂外英語交流機會的學生尤其有益。

18612725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18612725.value: 香港在全球知識體系中的跨境科研合作

18612725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18612725.value: Dr Marini, Giulio Prof Oleksiyenko, Anatoly

18612725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612725.value: In an increasingly interconnected world, cross-border research collaborations are essential for advancing scientific knowledge and enhancing the impact of academic research. Despite this, the unique research system of Hong Kong (HK) remains underexplored within the broader literature on global research systems and collaborations. HK's role as a bridge between East and West, combined with its handover to Mainland China, the world's leading research system by publication volume, provides a distinctive context for examining the evolution of HK's cross-border research collaborations and the factors influencing their citation impact. This project will address the highlighted gap by employing a sequential mixed-methods approach, beginning with a quantitative component followed by a qualitative one. The quantitative component will investigate the evolution of HK's global scientific social capital since 1997, a major shift for HK as it was handed over to Mainland China. The quantitative component will also explore the factors impacting the scientific influence of these collaboratively published research papers. Moreover, the qualitative component will investigate the alignment of the patterns found in the quantitative component of the project with HK's public policy documents guiding research endeavours, especially the very recent policy papers focusing on making HK a higher education hub. The qualitative part will also include interviews with HK-based researchers, who are at the front line of knowledge production. The interviews will provide further explanations about the quantitative findings and explore HK-based researchers' perceptions of HK's research collaborations over the years. The project aims to contribute to knowledge by shedding light on the complexities of cross-border research collaborations in a region characterised by a unique status that includes widespread use of English in a non-Western society and a political landscape with ambitious goals to establish a hub of higher education and knowledge. Additionally, it will provide evidence-based policy recommendations to enhance HK's global research visibility and impact, supporting the strategic objectives in international academic rankings. On a practical level, the research will guide individual researchers and institutional managers in identifying collaboration strategies that most effectively enhance scientific impact. By filling a significant gap in the literature and offering actionable insights, this research will support the development of more effective research policies and practices in HK. The findings are expected to have broader implications for the Greater Bay Area and other regions and institutions aiming to strengthen their cross-border research collaborations and academic impact. 當今世界日益緊密相連，跨境研究合作對促進科學知 識發展及提升學術研究影響力至關重要。然而，香港獨特的研究體系在全球研究系統與合作相關文獻中仍未被充分探討。香港作為東西方之間的橋樑，並於1997年回歸中國（現為全球出版量最大的研究體系），此特殊地位使其成為檢視香港跨境研究合作發展及其引用影響要素的獨特案例。 本研究將採用「先量後質」的混合研究方法來填補上述研究空白。量化部分將探討自1997年以來香港全球科研社會資本的演變，該年份對香港而言意義重大，因其正式移交予中國。此外，量化分析也將深入探討影響這些合作研究論文科學影響力的各項因素。質性部分則針對量化研究所得模式，分析其是否與香港的公共政策文件（尤其是近期聚焦將香港打造為高等教育樞紐的政策文本）相一致。該部分將對香港本地研究人員進行訪談，這些知識生產的直接參與者將為量化研究結果提供補充說明，並深入剖析他們對香港研究合作歷程的觀點。 此項研究旨在提升學術領域的知識，揭示在一個語言以英語為主的非西方社會、政治上又致力打造高等教育與知識樞紐的地區中，跨境研究合作的複雜性。本研究將基於實證數據提出政策建議，旨在提升香港於國際學術排名中的全球研究曝光度與學術影響。 本研究不僅填補重要文獻空白，也提供具可行性的啟示，有助推動香港研究政策及實踐的進一步發展。其研究成果預期將對大灣區及其他致力強化跨境研究合作與學術影響力的地區及機構產生更廣泛的啟發。

18613225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18613225.value: 香港自資授課式研究生課程的質素管理成效——多方持份者的視角

18613225.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18613225.value: Dr Jung, Jisun Prof Oleksiyenko, Anatoly

18613225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613225.value: Self-financed taught postgraduate (TPg) programs have grown rapidly in Hong Kong’s higher education sector over the past few years. These programs cater to both local and international postgraduate students and play a crucial role in the financial sustainability of universities. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, travel restrictions and discriminatory behaviors against Asians have led to an increase in non-local (mostly Mainland Chinese) students enrolling in self-financed TPg programs in Hong Kong. However, with the end of the pandemic, TPg programs must evaluate their quality to maintain their appeal, especially since non-local students may return to traditional Western destinations for their studies. Both research and practical gaps exist in the need to explore customized quality management mechanisms suitable for the market-oriented nature of these self-financed TPg programs, which are now generally following the quality management practices of University Grants Committee (UGC) funded postgraduate programs. Therefore, this study proposes a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of quality management in self-financed TPg programs across the eight UGC-funded universities. Going beyond examining the quality management policies followed by self-financed TPg programs, this proposed study will adopt a pragmatic perspective to explore an in-depth image of the perceptions of and reflections on the program quality from four groups of stakeholders, including students, faculty members, program leaders, and relevant senior administrators. Particularly, the customer-oriented research framework will focus on the learning experiences and reflections of self-financed TPg students, who are the primary stakeholder group. To achieve the research objectives, this proposed study will first conduct a policy review by analyzing institutional policy documents and interviewing relevant administrators to demonstrate the quality management mechanisms of self-financed TPg programs at the institutional level of eight UGC-funded universities. A mixed-methods approach will also be used to survey and interview self-financed TPg students, faculty members, and program leaders to explore their experience and perceptions of the program quality. The proposed study also aims to contribute to the theoretical understanding of students’ self-formation in self-financed TPg programs and to provide empirical evidence to improve self-financed TPg program quality and offer policy recommendations for quality management in Hong Kong’s higher education system. Moreover, it hopes to contribute to the discussion on the impact of neo-liberalism and the widespread adoption of economic rationality in the higher education sector. 近年來，自資授課式研究生課程在香港高等教育領域迅速發展。此類課程主要面向本地及非本地研究生，對大學的財務可持續性具有重要影響。受新冠疫情影響，由於旅行限制及針對亞裔的歧視問題，非本地學生（尤其是中國內地學生）報讀香港自資授課式研究生課程的人數顯著增加。然而，隨著疫情結束，此類課程需進一步評估其質素，以維持競爭力，特別是考慮到非本地學生可能重新選擇傳統的西方留學目的地。目前，自資授課式研究生課程普遍沿用大學教育資助委員會（教資會）資助課程的質素管理機制，但尚未建立符合其市場導向特性的客製化質素管理體系。因此，本研究旨在全面檢視八所教資會資助大學的自資授課式研究生課程的質素管理成效。除探討現行質素管理政策外，本研究亦將基於實用主義視角，深入分析四類持份者（包括學生、教師、課程負責人及高層管理人員）對課程質素的看法與反思。本研究採用消費者導向的研究框架，尤其關注學生群體的學習體驗與意見。為達成研究目標，首先將透過政策文件分析及管理人員訪談，審視八所院校在院校層面的質素管理機制。其次，將運用混合研究方法，對自資授課式學生、教師及課程負責人進行問卷調查與深度訪談，以探討其對課程質素的體驗與評價。本研究期望能深化對香港自資授課式研究生「自我成長」的理論理解，並為提升課程質素提供實證依據，從而為香港高等教育管理提出政策建議。此外，本研究亦希望探討新自由主義及經濟理性對高等教育的廣泛影響。

18613525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18613525.value: 數位時代家長的評估素養及其與學生學習的關聯：工具開發與模型驗證

18613525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18613525.value: Prof Chen, Gaowei Prof CHIU, Ming Ming Dr Lam, Chun Bun Ian Prof Li, Sandy S C Prof Yan, Zi

18613525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613525.value: Parents can affect students’ learning through their involvement in varied assessment processes. However, many non-expert parents lack assessment literacy to deal with students’ assessment-related issues in the digital era (P-ALDE), which can hinder student learning through inappropriate actions (e.g., overhelping, exerting academic pressure, and, even worse, resisting innovative assessment forms such as self- and peer-assessment). Moreover, the rapidly evolving technology, which enables extensive assessment information and requires digital labor, may have fundamentally affected parental involvement in assessment-related issues. While research to date has focused largely on students and teachers, more needs to be known about P-ALDE and its effects on student achievement. However, no published instrument measures P-ALDE. Without such an instrument, we cannot investigate P-ALDE and its influence on student learning, let alone design and test the effectiveness of parent intervention programs. This study seeks to address this issue by (a) developing and validating an instrument to measure knowledge, beliefs, and practices of P-ALDE, (b) investigating the P-ALDE profiles of parents in the local community, and (c) exploring the effect of P-ALDE on students’ academic achievement. Guided by our P-ALDE’s definition and individual interviews with experts and parents, we will develop domains and items of each P-ALDE dimension. Experts will check these items for substantive and content validity. Feedback from interviews with parents will be used to refine the items. The parents or main caregivers of 300 students in Hong Kong will be invited to pilot test and semi-finalize the P-ALDE instrument (pilot study). Based on the responses from another 300 parents, the scale will be examined to determine the dimensionality of the P-ALDE items, each item’s quality, each domain’s reliability, and the scales’ external validity (against actual daily practices) in a Rasch approach (main study). Furthermore, we will investigate P-ALDE profiles and test our theoretical model of P-ALDE and its association with students’ academic achievement with structural equation modeling using data from the main study. Upon completion of the project, the developed P-ALDE instrument can be utilized by scholars to conduct quantitative studies on parents such as the antecedents of P-ALDE. The findings regarding the local P-ALDE profile and its impact on students' academic achievement will provide valuable insights for stakeholders to understand the strengths and weaknesses of P-ALDE in Hong Kong and to aid in the planning of parental intervention programs aimed at enhancing students' learning. 家長可透過參與各種評估過程影響學生的學習。然而，許多非專家家長缺乏在數位時代處理學生評估相關問題的評估素養（P-ALDE），這可能會透過不適當的行為（例如，過度協助、施加學業壓力，更嚴重的是抵制自評、同儕評估等創新型評估形式）阻礙學生學習。此外，快速發展的技術不僅提供了大量評估資訊，還要求家長具備數位勞動能力，這可能從根本上影響了家長在評估相關問題中的參與。儘管迄今為止的研究主要關注學生和教師，但我們仍需更多地了解 P-ALDE 及其對學生學業成就的影響。然而，目前尚無已發表的工具可用於測量 P-ALDE。沒有這類工具，我們就無法探究 P-ALDE 及其對學生學習的影響，更不用說設計和測試家長干預計劃的有效性了。 本研究旨在解決這一問題，具體包括：（a）開發並驗證用於測量 P-ALDE 的知識、信念和實踐這三個維度的工具；（b）探究本地社區家長的 P-ALDE 特徵；（c）探索 P-ALDE 對學生學業成就的影響。基於我們對 P-ALDE 的定義以及與專家和家長的個別訪談，我們將開發每個 P-ALDE 維度的子維度和題項。專家將檢查這些題項的實質效度和內容效度，而來自家長訪談的反饋將用於完善題項。 研究將邀請香港 300 名學生的家長或主要照顧者參與 P-ALDE 工具的預試，並對其進行初步定稿（預試階段）。在主要研究階段，基於另外 300 名家長的回應，研究將採用Rasch模型檢驗該量表，以確定 P-ALDE 題項的維度結構、每個題項的質量、每個子維度的信度以及量表的外部效度（與實際日常行為對比）。此外，我們將利用主要研究的數據，探究 P-ALDE 概況，並通過結構方程模型驗證我們的 P-ALDE 理論模型及其與學生學業成就的關聯。 項目完成後，所開發的 P-ALDE 工具可供學者用於開展有關家長的定量研究（例如 P-ALDE 的影響因素）。有關本地 P-ALDE 概況及其對學生學業成就影響的研究結果，將為利益相關者提供寶貴見解，幫助他們了解香港家長 P-ALDE 的優勢與不足，並協助規劃旨在提升學生學習的家長干預計劃。

18613725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18613725.value: 香港高等教育校園的種族及族裔氛圍：以少數族裔及內地學生為例

18613725.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18613725.value: Prof Kennedy, Kerry John Dr WONG, Koon Lin

18613725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613725.value: Studies indicate that ethnic minority and Mainland Chinese students in Hong Kong (HK) universities experience racism, ethnicism and discrimination. Research elsewhere suggests a significant association between these experiences and students’ well-being. Similar studies, however, are not available in HK despite students’ experiences. Thus, little is known about the way university campuses support these students regarding their policies, curricula, and the day-to-day experiences of these students with their peers, teachers, and other staff. This study seeks to address this issue by investigating students’ experiences of their campus environment and its impact on their wellbeing. Using the concept of campus racial and ethnic climate (CREC), the proposed study will explore how ethnic minority and Mainland Chinese students in HK universities experience CREC, specifically how they perceive CREC, the factors that influence their perceptions, how their wellbeing is affected, what institutional policies and practices support or hinder the development of positive CREC and what policies and practices have potentials to support the development of anti-racist and anti-ethnicist education. The study will draw on critical race theory (CRT) and symbolic interactionism to explore various overt and subtle forms of racism and ethnicism including systemic and institutional as well as stereotypes, prejudice, discrimination, microaggressions and unconscious bias against ethnic minority and Mainland Chinese students. The study will adopt a phenomenological qualitative approach to document the experiences of a group of minority students studying at two public universities in HK. In-depth interviews will be conducted with 40 ethnic minority students of South Asian and South-East Asian heritages, and 40 Mainland Chinese students, totalling 80. Additionally, all documents and webpages related to policies, practices, programmes and support services concerning CREC as well as equity, diversity and inclusion, and some selected relevant curriculum materials of the two universities will be analyzed. Moreover, in-depth interviews with four academic and teaching staff and four administrative staff will be carried out. The project will benefit both minority and majority students, their families, policy makers, university leaders, and academic, teaching and administrative staff. To enhance the impact of the project, stories of participants’ racial and ethnic encounters (anonymously) will be made publicly available on the project website. This will help create pathways towards anti-racist and anti-ethnicist campus and education and will form the basis of similar future initiatives across the government funded universities. The development of anti-racist and anti-ethnicist campus climate represents the longer-term impact of this project. 現有研究已指出香港高等院校中的少數族裔學生與中國內地學生面臨種族主義、族裔歧視及差別待遇的問題。國際上的相關研究亦顯示，此類經驗與學生的身心福祉之間具有顯著關聯。儘管學生在香港亦有類似經歷，然而本地卻缺乏相關研究。關於大學校園如何透過政策設計、課程安排，以及學生與同儕、教師與行政人員之日常互動來支持這些學生，現有研究仍相對較少。因此，本研究計畫透過調查學生們在校園環境中之經歷以及該經歷對他們身心福祉之影響，來回應此一議題。 本研究將運用「校園種族與族裔氛圍」(Campus Racial and Ethnic Climate,簡稱CREC)之概念，探究香港高等院校中的少數族裔與中國內地學生對此校園氛圍的經驗與感知。具體而言，本研究將分析學生如何感知校園種族與族裔氛圍、影響其感知的因素、以及此氛圍如何影響其身心福祉，並進一步探討哪些制度性政策與實踐有助於或阻礙正向校園與族裔氛圍之建構，以及哪些政策與實踐具有推動反種族主義與反族裔歧視教育之潛力。本研究將援引「批判種族理論」（Critical Race Theory,CRT）與「象徵互動論」（Symbolic Interactionism），以探討各種明顯或隱微的種族與族裔歧視形式，包括制度性與結構性層面，以及針對少數族裔與中國內地學生所表現出的刻板印象、偏見、歧視、微侵犯（microaggressions）與無意識偏見等現象。 本研究將採用現象學取向的質性研究方法，記錄就讀於香港兩所公立大學之少數族裔學生。研究將深度訪談共80名學生，包括40位具有南亞或東南亞背景的少數族裔學生，以及40位中國內地學生。此外，本研究將分析兩所大學中與校園種族與族裔氛圍（Campus Racial and Ethnic Climate,CREC）及公平、多樣性與包容性（Equity,Diversity,and Inclusion,EDI）相關之政策、實踐、教育計畫與支援服務的文件與網頁內容，並選取部分相關課程資料進行分析。研究亦將訪談四位教學與研究人員，以及四位行政人員。 本研究成果將惠及少數族裔與主流族群學生及其家庭、政策制定者、大學領導層，以及學術、教學與行政相關人員。為提升本研究之社會影響力，參與者所分享的種族與族裔互動經歷（經匿名處理）將公開發布於本研究網站上。此研究有助於推動建立反種族主義與反族裔歧視的校園文化與教育實踐，並為未來其他政府資助大學推動類似倡議奠定基礎。長遠而言，促進反種族主義與反族裔歧視的校園氛圍之發展，將是本研究之核心影響目標。

18613825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18613825.value: 探索青少年STEM創客情感能量的動態發展：一個基於可穿戴設備的民族志研究

18613825.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18613825.value: Prof Cheng, May Hung May Dr Davis, James Prof English, Lyn D Dr Liu, Duo

18613825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613825.value: Emotional energy refers to human beings’ enduring sense of social cohesion experienced as an outcome of successful social interaction in work, living or learning environments (Bellocchi, 2017). Research into emotional energy is gaining momentum in sociology, psychology, and education, as fostering a lasting sense of social cohesion is vital for effectively addressing complex social, economic, and environmental challenges (UNESCO, 2023). Previous research indicates that the development of emotional energy is dynamic. Yet, little is known about (i) how emotional energy varies in different stages of learning, (ii) how it changes over a chain of learning activities; and (iii) what are the key factors influencing its changes in education contexts. These knowledge gaps have been barriers to systematically designing approaches to enhancing and sustaining the emotional energy of learning groups so as to ensure the long-term efficiency of school curricula. This project will choose to investigate emotional energy in the context of maker-centred STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) learning, due to (i) its unique cross-disciplinary nature and complex learning process and (ii) the role of emotional energy as a prerequisite for unlocking student group creativity in STEM education (Ding et al., 2024). Based on a pilot study of STEM maker groups and the investigators’ previous research of maker-centred STEM learning (e.g., English* & King, 2019; Wan* et al., 2022) and emotional energy (e.g., Davis*, 2021), this project will adopt an ethnographic methodology to investigate the longitudinal change of emotional energy cross in STEM maker activities. To capture the developmental trajectory of emotional energy, the collaborative learning process of 30 pairs of Primary 5 students from 3 schools will be captured by using wearable cameras (as unobtrusive observation devices) for one year over 8 STEM maker activities. Artefact-based retrospective interviews will be conducted to explore the key factors influencing the development of emotional energy of young STEM makers. An innovative aspect of this project is its exploration of the socio-emotional processes in STEM learning. The employment of wearable devices makes it possible to investigate longitudinal changes in the emotional energy of a good number of student groups. Its unique research context will make the investigation into the dynamics of emotional energy more effective and significant. The findings will advance the knowledge frontiers in emotional energy theories by unveiling the variation of emotional energy in different stages of cross-disciplinary learning, outlining its developmental trajectory, and identifying key influencing factors. 情感能量（Emotional energy）是指人類在工作、生活或學習環境中，通過成功的社會互動所產生的對社會凝聚力的持久性感知（Bellocchi, 2017）。隨著人們日益意識到 培養這種持久凝聚力 對人類有效應對日益複雜的社會、經濟和環境問題的重要性（UNESCO, 2023），社會學、心理學及教育領域對情感能量的研究正快速增長。既有研究表明，情感能量的發展具有動態性，但以下問題仍知之甚少：(i) 情感能量在學習不同階段的變化規律；(ii) 其在一系列學習活動中的演變過程；(iii) 教育情境中影響其變化的關鍵因素。這些知識空白阻礙了系統設計能提升並維持學習群體情感能量的方法，所以學校課程的長期效能很難得到保障。本研究選擇以創客為核心的STEM（科學、技術、工程與數學）學習為研究情境，主要是考慮到其獨特的跨學科特性與複雜的學習過程。 基於對小型STEM創客團隊的預實驗研究，以及研究者過往關於創客式STEM學習（如English & King, 2019; Wan等, 2022）與情感能量（如Davis, 2021; Davis & Bellocchi, 2020）的成果，本項目將採用民族誌方法，縱向探究STEM創客活動中情感能量的跨階段變化。為捕捉情感能量的發展軌跡，研究將通過可穿戴相機（作為低干擾式觀察設備），為期一年記錄來自3所學校的30組小五學生在8項STEM創客活動中的協作學習過程，並輔以製成品回溯訪談法，探討影響青少年STEM創客情感能量發展的關鍵因素。 本項目的創新性在於運用可穿戴設備技術，使得對大量學生群體情感能量的縱向追蹤研究成為可能。其獨特的研究情境將使情感能量動態機制的探索更具可行性與實效性。研究成果將揭示跨學科學習不同階段中情感能量的變異規律、長期發展軌跡及影響因素，從而推動情感能量理論的 前沿發展。

18614525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18614525.value: 教師生成式人工智能素養的概念化、評估與發展

18614525.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18614525.value: Dr Chen, Chen Logan Prof Chiu, Kin-fung Thomas Dr Ismail, Celik Prof Lai, Chun Prof Lee, John Chi Kin

18614525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18614525.value: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers tremendous potential for teachers’ professional practice, yet existing studies consistently report significant challenges in teachers’ GenAI integration, such as minimal integration between GenAI and pedagogy and ignoring ethical concerns. These challenges are closely tied to teachers’ GenAI competency, meaning the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to understand and effectively leverage GenAI for teaching and professional development. Despite the growing importance of GenAI in education, there is currently no framework outlining essential GenAI competencies for teachers. Constructing such a framework and developing a targeted professional development program to cultivate these competencies is therefore a matter of urgency. This research project aims to address this gap through a three-phase design. Phase ONE aims to formulate a teachers’ GenAI competency framework. We will comprehensively review and analyze existing global and local research and documents on teachers’ GenAI integration. Experienced Hong Kong teachers will be interviewed to investigate their perspectives and practices regarding GenAI integration. These data will inform the development of a context-relevant teachers’ GenAI competency framework, laying the groundwork for the second phase of the study. Phase TWO seeks to develop an instrument to assess Hong Kong teachers’ GenAI competency. The instrument will be developed through a systematic process, beginning with initial item development based on the framework generated in Phase One. This will be followed by an expert-panel review and a pilot study with at least 300 in-service teachers to ensure the instrument’s validity and reliability. Phase THREE will focus on developing and evaluating a professional development program for teachers’ GenAI competency. Informed by the framework generated in Phase One, the program will employ a flipped professional development model and consist of five modules delivered over 15 weeks. A randomized controlled trial involving 250 teachers will be conducted to assess the program’s effectiveness. Three waves of surveys using the instrument developed in Phase Two, as well as teacher interviews, shared practices, and reflective journals, will be analyzed to evaluate the program’s efficacy. In summary, this project addresses a significant research gap in teachers’ use of AI, outlining a teachers’ GenAI competency framework and providing a solid theoretical foundation for future research. The developed instrument and the professional program can serve as benchmarks for similar initiatives globally.

21200425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21200425.value: 結構信息理論及其在空間轉錄組學時空動力學中的應用

21200425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200425.value: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) have enabled the profiling of multi-omics data, capturing gene expression and spatial positioning of cells on tissue slides, along with tissue histology images. Additionally, protein structures predicted by AlphaFold can provide valuable insights. In biological systems, cells form hierarchical structures, with subpopulations and clubs offering coarse and fine-grained classifications, such as T cell subpopulations and CD8+ T cell clubs. Similarly, genes are organized hierarchically into communities and modules, which define varying levels of functional granularity, such as cell cycle communities and mitosis modules. Cell trajectory analysis tracks transitions like activation, differentiation, and tumor evolution, capturing cellular spatial movement over time. Gene dynamics, in turn, trace changes in key genes along these trajectories as cells evolve in time and space. Understanding these cellular and gene hierarchies and dynamics is essential to unraveling tumorigenesis, metastasis, and immune responses. However, current ST analysis methods face limitations, such as: (1) Producing flat cell clusters without accounting for hierarchical structures. (2) Gene regulation network inference often neglects hierarchical gene structures, spatial context, and protein structures like those predicted by AlphaFold (winner of The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024). (3) Existing ST trajectory methods usually focus on either at cell or subregion level, there is a lack of approaches that capture cell transitions across different levels with auto-selected starting points. (4) Gene dynamics detection focuses primarily on individual genes, overlooking complex gene interactions that drive regulation. In this proposal, we aim to apply structural information theory to ST data analysis to address these limitations. We will develop open-source software to detect cell and gene hierarchies from spatial omics data and model spatiotemporal trajectories and gene dynamics across multiple hierarchical levels. This tool will be applied to ovarian cancer ST omics data from both collaborators and publicly available datasets, with the goal of discovering new biomarkers linked to cellular behavior and gene regulation driving ovarian cancer progression. 空間轉錄組學（ST）的最新進展已能同時定量多組學資料，捕捉組織切片上細胞的基因表達與空間位置，並結合組織病理影像。此外，由 AlphaFold 預測的蛋白質結構也能提供重要見解。在生物系統中，細胞呈階層式組織，子族群與小群可提供粗與細兩種層級的分類，例如 T 細胞子族群與 CD8+ T 細胞小群。類似地，基因亦以階層方式組織成社群與模組，對應不同層級的功能粒度，例如細胞週期社群與有絲分裂模組。細胞軌跡分析可追蹤活化、分化與腫瘤演化等轉變，並捕捉細胞隨時間在空間中的移動。相應地，基因動態則沿著這些軌跡描繪關鍵基因在時空中隨細胞演進的變化。理解這些細胞與基因的階層結構與動態，對於揭示腫瘤發生、轉移與免疫反應至關重要。然而，現有的 ST 分析方法存在以下限制：(1) 產生扁平的細胞分群，未考量階層結構。(2) 基因調控網路推斷往往忽略基因的階層式結構、空間脈絡，以及如 AlphaFold所預測的蛋白質結構。(3) 既有 ST 軌跡方法通常僅聚焦於細胞層級或次區域層級之一，缺乏能跨不同層級捕捉細胞轉變且可自動選擇起始點的方法。(4) 基因動態偵測主要著眼於單一基因，忽視驅動調控的複雜基因互作。在本計畫中，我們擬將結構信息理論應用於 ST數據分析以因應上述限制。我們將開發開源軟體，自空間組學數據中偵測細胞與基因的階層結構，並在多重階層層級上建模時空軌跡與基因動態。該工具將應用於合作方與公開資料庫的卵巢癌 ST 組學資料，目標是發現與細胞行為與基因調控相關、驅動卵巢癌進展的新型生物標記。

21200625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21200625.value: 適用於增材製造難觸及表面的精整加工與原位測量之新型磁驅系統

21200625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200625.value: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) has revolutionised the production of highly complex near-net-shape components that would not be manufacturable with traditional methods. However, the poor quality of as-built surfaces continues to necessitate post-processing for industrial applications. This problem is exacerbated in internal surfaces, such as cavities and holes, which are difficult to access. Moreover, effective measurement methods for such difficult-to-access surfaces are scarce. Existing mechanical and chemical internal surface finishing techniques are typically inefficient and cannot provide appropriate data for surface quality evaluations. Therefore, we propose a novel magnetically driven system that can be used for surface finishing and in situ surface quality measurement of difficult-to-access AM surfaces. The proposed system will be based on the concept of a magnetic field penetrating non-ferromagnetic materials to control the movement of another magnet within the cavity. Surface finishing will be achieved through i) the development of a magnetic finishing tool with electroplated super-abrasives; ii) the design of a tri-coil electromagnet module to facilitate stable material removal from the difficult-to-access surface; and iii) the utilisation of a six-axis robot to provide the feed motion of the electromagnet module for scanning all the internal surfaces of the workpiece. We will simulate the kinetics of the magnetic finishing tool using a finite-element model integrating the magnetic field with multibody dynamics simulations. A material removal and surface generation model will be built considering the surface defect anisotropy and microstructural anisotropy of the AM components, based on the microscale indentation and scratching theory. A magnetically driven system for in situ surface measurement will be achieved by i) replacing the magnetic finishing tool with a smooth magnet tool and ii) constructing a machine learning model to correlate the signals of the tool–workpiece interaction with the surface roughness values. A fuzzy echo state broad learning model will be established for the surface measurement, considering its advantage in capturing dynamic characteristics of time series from complex nonlinear systems. This proposal is groundbreaking due to its uniqueness in i) achieving both surface finishing and roughness measurement of difficult-to-access AM surfaces in a single magnetically driven system, and ii) revealing the surface generation mechanism in abrasive finishing AM components by considering their surface defect anisotropy and microstructural anisotropy. The outcomes may accelerate the implementation of AM components in various manufacturing applications, including automotive, aerospace and medical industries, as well as moulds and dies sectors. 金屬增材製造技術革新了高度複雜近淨成形零件的生產方式，這類零件採用傳統方法很難製造。然而，對於工業應用而言，製成表面的低劣質量仍需後續處理。此問題在具有難觸及內表面的零件上更為嚴重。此外，針對此類難觸及表面的有效測量方法十分匱乏。現有的機械和化學內表面精加工技術通常效率低下，且無法為表面質量評估提供合適的數據。 因此，我們提出一種新型磁驅系統，可用於增材製造難觸及表面之精整加工及原位表面質量測量。所提出的系統將基於磁場可穿透非鐵磁性材料零件以控制其內部另一磁體運動的原理。表面精整加工將透過以下方式實現：i）開發一種帶有電鍍超硬磨料的磁性砂輪，置於零件內表面；ii）設計一個三線圈電磁鐵模組，以促進難觸及表面材料的穩定去除；iii）利用六軸機械人提供電磁鐵模組的進給運動，以掃描工件的整個內表面。我們將使用結合電磁場與多體動力學的有限元模型，來模擬磁性砂輪的運動。基於微觀壓痕和刻劃理論，並考慮增材製造零件的表面缺陷各向異性和微觀組織各向異性，我們將建立材料去除模型及表面創成模型。 用於表面原位測量的磁驅系統將透過以下方式實現：i）將上述磁性砂輪替換為表面光滑的磁性工具；ii）構建一個機器學習模型，將工具和工件相互作用的信號與表面粗糙度值關聯起來。考慮到寬度學習模型在捕捉複雜非線性系統時間序列動態特性方面的優勢，我們將建立一個模糊回聲狀態寬度學習模型測量表面粗糙度。 此提案的獨創性在於：i）在同一個磁驅系統中同時實現對增材製造難觸及表面的精整加工和粗糙度測量；ii）透過考慮增材製造零件的表面缺陷各向異性和微觀組織各向異性，揭示其在基於磨粒的精整加工過程中的表面創成機制。提案成果有望加速增材製造零件在汽車、航空航天、醫療以及模具領域中的應用實施。

21201925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21201925.value: 护航软件衍化安全的终生式混合程序分析框架

21201925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201925.value: As software becomes increasingly integral in varying operating systems and forms a crucial part of modern society, software security is fundamental to guarantee effective and efficient operations of societal functions. However, the rapid evolution of software systems poses significant challenges for traditional vulnerability detection methods to keep pace with the frequent updates. Specifically, existing efforts have to re-examine the whole program when software updates and patches. Since most of the code has not been changed in every update, this large proportion of the code is repeatedly analyzed. Such redundant analysis forces existing practices to sacrifice precision or entirely skip examining code updates, causing significant financial losses and safety hazards. Thus, self-evolving vulnerability detection, being responsible for the whole life cycle of any software, is urgent to exploit. To this end, this proposal presents a novel framework as a lifelong self-evolving program analysis for detecting vulnerabilities in rapidly updating software, aiming to facilitate broader adoption in real-world applications. The proposed detection framework can effectively identify and tackle three fundamental limitations for better generality, durability, and scalability. 1) Lack of generalized representation for preserving diverse program semantics across the software updates to support vulnerability validation. We will design a unified representation to precisely describe program semantics for each module across versions. Such a summary can avoid repeated analysis restarts with each software update due to outdated assumptions. 2) Lack of support for the burst of targets introduced from software updates raises severe deficiency in vulnerability analyses. We will propose a multi-target-driven analysis algorithm consolidating the path exploration with target-related program module connections. The consolidation brings synergy to overcome the inefficiency of existing single-target-driven approaches in simultaneously handling multiple changes in fast-evolving software. 3) Lack of program semantics storage and querying mechanism across software updates for accelerating vulnerability analysis. We will explore the code indexing techniques to support efficient analysis results update and transfer across software versions. This persistent design addresses inadequate mechanisms in reusing analysis results across versions, leading to error accumulation and resource waste. By leveraging these advancements, the proposed framework aims to revolutionize vulnerability detection for evolving software, providing a robust baseline for future research and applications. The project will not only enhance the current literature on vulnerability detection, but also offer a comprehensive framework for securing fast-evolving software systems. Through this work, we mitigate the risks associated with software updates, ultimately contributing to safe and reliable digital infrastructures. 软件作为现代社会基石，其安全对高效运行至关重要。然而，软件系统的快速迭代对传统漏洞检测构成挑战。现有方法在每次更新时需重新分析整个程序，重复检测未变更代码，牺牲精度或跳过更新检查，导致财务损失与安全风险。因此，覆盖软件全生命周期的自我进化漏洞检测亟待开发。 为此，我们提出一种创新的终生自进化程序分析框架，助力漏洞检测适应快速更新的软件，推广其实用性。该框架解决三大局限，提升通用性、持久性与可扩展性：1. 缺乏统一语义表示：设计统一表示法，精确描述各模块跨版本的程序语义，避免因更新而重复分析。2. 多目标分析不足：提出多目标驱动分析算法，整合路径探索与模块关联，克服单一目标方法在处理快速变化时的低效。3. 语义存储与查询缺失：探索代码索引技术，支持跨版本分析结果的高效更新与重用，减少错误累积与资源浪费。通过这些突破，该框架革新漏洞检测，为未来研究与应用奠定坚实基础。它不仅丰富漏洞检测文献，还为快速进化软件系统提供全面安全保障，降低更新风险，助力构建安全可靠的数字基础设施。

21208525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21208525.value: 借助最优化理论改进噪音输入下的大模型训练策略

21208525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21208525.value: Large machine learning models, including large language models and large vision models, have achieved great success but suffer from poor robustness due to their tendency to overfit to meaningless noise in real-life data. This may lead to hallucination and unexpected behaviors, such as inadvertently inciting users to engage in dangerous activities, costing billions of dollars. To address this issue, practitioners often resort to labor-intensive data cleaning, which is accessible primarily to large organizations. Recognizing that such short-term fixes are insufficient, the academic community is moving towards more sustainable practices. This involves mitigating noise during training and even leveraging randomness to improve efficiency. Achieving this requires a deeper understanding of the training process. Instead of relying on traditional statistical theories that depend on strong assumptions, optimization theory emerges as a compelling, versatile alternative. Viewing the optimization landscape as a complex terrain, we aim to chart out paths to optimal solutions, a task complicated by noise-induced obstacles that grow larger and more frequent as model size increases. Our initial findings suggest that certain optimization features can act as a compass, guiding us in the right direction even when detours are unavoidable due to these obstacles. Inspired by this discovery, our project will be conducted in three phases: 1) we will establish precise theories for a specific class of non-convex problems to explain the relationship between model size and robustness. Our early findings suggest that this could be done by focusing on singular values of critical points, a universal optimization feature, enabling this approach to be further generalized. 2) Next, we will adapt existing learning algorithms for large models with these new insights to help find routes with less noise-induced obstacles. For example, we plan to modify the popular ADAM optimizer to iteratively weigh gradients based on the landscape properties we have previously discovered. 3) Finally, we will advance our research on harnessing the power of randomness by studying how large model sizes and noise can together increase training performance. Our preliminary results show that structured noise can eliminate bad solutions in matrix completion tasks, only at the cost of a little accuracy. This project could lead to real-life benefits like improved detection of pedestrians and obstacles by self-driving cars in poor weather conditions or at night. It may also reduce the need for data pre-processing and pave way for a new paradigm that could assure users of guaranteed robustness. 大规模机器学习模型（包括大型语言模型和视觉模型）在实际应用中表现出色，但它们往往容易对真实数据中的噪声过拟合，从而导致鲁棒性下降。这类模型可能生成“幻觉”内容，甚至偶尔会出现误导用户从事危险活动的异常行为，可能带来数十亿美元的损失。目前，为解决这类问题，行业中通常通过大量人力进行数据清洗，但这种方法代价高昂，很少被中小型团队采用。 为了摆脱对事后清洗的依赖，学术界正逐步转向更有前瞻性的解决方案——在训练中主动抑制噪声影响，甚至有目的地利用随机性来提升训练效率。这一思路要求我们深入理解模型训练的过程，而不是依赖传统统计理论中那些对数据分布或独立性做出强假设的方法，这些假设在面对大规模模型和高噪声数据时往往失效。 我们将训练过程比作探索一个复杂的地形：模型参数空间是起伏不定的山地，而噪声则是其中不断出现的陷阱或障碍；模型越大，障碍越多，也越复杂。研究发现，在训练过程中，某些优化特征——尤其是关键点处的奇异值结构——能够像导航仪一样，为训练指引方向，即使在噪声干扰下，训练路径仍然可以大致朝向正确的最优解。 基于这些初步发现，我们的研究将分三个阶段展开。首阶段是建立理论框架，聚焦一类非凸优化问题，揭示模型规模如何影响训练鲁棒性，并分析关键点奇异值结构的作用；第二阶段是将理论应用于优化算法改进，比如在 ADAM 优化器中引入基于地形特征的梯度加权方法，以帮助模型避开恶劣噪声区域；第三阶段则探索如何利用随机性，即在训练中故意引入结构化噪声，已有实验显示，在矩阵补全任务中，这种方式虽然牺牲了一点精度，却能有效避免陷入不良解，提升整体性能。 如果这个项目成功，其成果可能直接应用于现实，比如让自动驾驶系统在雨天或夜间更精准地检测行人和障碍物，也有望减少对数据预处理的依赖，并推动形成一种兼具理论依据与实践效果的新训练范式，从根本上提升大模型训练的效率与鲁棒性。

21210325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21210325.value: 基於機器學習的高分辨、高信噪比生物成像技術

21210325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21210325.value: Optical microscopy is a powerful tool in biological and biomedical research due to its subcellular resolution and non-invasiveness. However, accurately imaging the structures and functions of living organisms in their native state remains challenging. This is because (1) biological tissues and imaging systems can both introduce optical aberrations, degrading imaging resolution; and (2) in vivo imaging requires gentle conditions (i.e., low illumination power), often resulting in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To address these challenges and enable high-fidelity in vivo imaging, we propose two novel machine learning-based microscopy techniques: (1) A machine learning-based adaptive optics approach [XL-ML-AO]: Adaptive optics (AO) corrects aberrations to restore high-resolution imaging performance. However, conventional AO techniques have limitations, including the need for specialized, expensive hardware and a limited effective field of view (FOV). The PI recently developed a machine learning-based AO (ML-AO) method (Nature Machine Intelligence, 2024), which can perform joint wavefront estimation and three-dimensional structural information extraction in a purely computational manner. However, this method cannot be directly applied to large-FOV bioimaging due to Nyquist sampling requirements, limited correction capabilities, and the more pronounced issue of spatially varying aberrations with larger FOVs. To address these limitations, we introduce an image up-sampling strategy, a refined loss function, and an image stack partitioning procedure. These advancements are expected to enable the proposed method, XL-ML-AO (eXtra-Large FOV ML-AO), for high-resolution, large-FOV bioimaging. (2) A machine learning-based denoising technique [SLIDING]: Low laser exposure is needed to minimize photodamage and photobleaching. However, this often results in low-SNR images, preventing high-fidelity interpretation of biological structures and activities. In this research, we propose a Self-supervised Learning enabled Image DenoisING (SLIDING) approach for SNR enhancement. The algorithm is specifically designed for processing images with extremely low-SNR, enabling SLIDING to handle challenging imaging tasks such as volumetric imaging of neuronal activities in the mouse brain in vivo. These techniques address key challenges in bioimaging, aiming to facilitate high-resolution, large-FOV, high-SNR investigations of living organisms. We will systematically assess their robustness and versatility across multiple microscopy modalities, diverse biological samples, and various imaging applications. This work will be supported by collaboration with experts in optical microscopy (Prof. Wei Chen), retinal biology (Prof. Wenjun Xiong), and neurobiology (Prof. Zhitao Hu). Ultimately, this project aims to deliver a versatile computational toolkit for biologists, enabling transformative investigations of living organisms across diverse research fields, including neurobiology, retinal biology, and beyond. 光學顯微成像因其亞細胞解析度與非侵入性，已成為生物學與生物醫學研究中的重要工具。然而，在活體成像中，準確解析生物結構與功能仍具挑戰，主要原因為：(1) 生物組織與成像系統都可能引入光學像差，導致空間分辨率下降；以及 (2) 活體成像需要控制光功率，常造成信噪比（SNR）偏低。為解決這些挑戰並實現高保真活體成像，我們提出兩項基於機器學習的新型顯微成像技術：（1）機器學習自適應光學方法 [XL-ML-AO]：自適應光學（AO）能校正光學像差，恢復高分辨率成像。然而，傳統 AO 造價貴、技術門檻高，同時受限於有限的有效視場（FOV）。我們近期開發了一種基於機器學習的 AO（ML-AO）方法，可通過純計算方式同時進行波前估計與三維結構信息提取。然而，該方法無法直接應用於大視場生物成像，原因包括奈奎斯特取樣需求和有限的像差校正能力，以及在大視場下嚴重的空間變異像差問題。為突破這些限制，我們引入圖像上採樣策略、優化的損失函數，以及影像堆疊分區處理方式。這些改進預期能推動所提出的方法 XL-ML-AO（超大視場機器學習 AO）實現高解析度、大視場的生物成像。（2）機器學習降噪技術 [SLIDING]：為減少光毒性與光漂白，活體成像需要低光功率，但這往往導致低 SNR 影像，限制了對生物結構與活動的準確解析。在本研究中，我們提出一種基於自監督學習的圖像降噪方法（Self-supervised Learning enabled Image DenoisING, SLIDING），專門針對極低 SNR 成像條件設計。此方法可應對高度挑戰性的成像任務，例如活體小鼠腦神經活動的體積成像。這些技術針對生物成像中的核心挑戰，旨在推動活體樣本的高分辨率、大視場與高 SNR 研究。我們將在多種顯微成像模式、多樣生物樣本及不同應用場景下，系統性評估其魯棒性與廣泛適用性。本計畫將與多名光學、生物學專家合作推進。最終，本研究計畫的目標是提供一套多功能的計算工具包，協助生物學家在神經生物學、視網膜生物學及更廣泛領域開展具有變革性的活體研究。

21212025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21212025.value: 面向網絡系統的攻擊魯棒性在線機器學習研究

21212025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21212025.value: Online learning is a widely used framework for decision-making under uncertainty, where a system makes sequential decisions and learns to make better choices that improve performance over time. In critical applications like edge computing, cloud computing, and distributed systems, online learning enables systems to allocate resources, select servers, and adjust configurations based on feedback such as response time, network latency, and user satisfaction. However, as these learning-enabled systems become more integrated into essential services, they also become vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Attackers can manipulate the feedback received by the learning system, leading it toward suboptimal decisions that degrade performance or compromise security. Although existing research has made strides in studying adversarial attacks and defenses in online learning, it primarily focuses on simplified settings like single-agent learning under ideal conditions. These approaches often overlook the complexities of real-world environments, such as multiple learning agents making cooperative decisions, action spaces that grow combinatorially with system complexity, and diverse adversarial strategies. This project aims to develop attack-robust online learning algorithms to secure networked systems operating in adversarial environments. The research is structured to explore both attack strategies and defense mechanisms. First, it will focus on designing adversarial attacks that exploit vulnerabilities in learning algorithms with complex combinatorial action spaces, such as multi-resource allocation in cloud networks or ranking multiple items in online services. Second, the project will extend these attack strategies to multi-agent systems, investigating how attackers can manipulate shared information between agents to disrupt cooperation and degrade overall system performance. For defense, the project will develop robust learning algorithms capable of withstanding these sophisticated attacks. These algorithms will account for practical constraints such as partial observability, limited resources, and adaptive adversarial strategies, ensuring their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. The expected outcomes of this project include both theoretical advancements and practical tools for enhancing the robustness of online learning systems in networked environments. This research will establish design principles to make learning-enabled systems more resilient to adversarial attacks, along with delivering software tools that operators can use to deploy the proposed robust algorithms or assess the resilience of their existing systems. These innovations will enhance the resilience of critical applications like cloud services, edge computing, and autonomous systems to adversarial attacks. Ultimately, the project will contribute to advancing the fields of online learning, distributed systems, and cybersecurity, creating a strong foundation for future research in attack-robust learning. 在線學習是一種廣泛應用於不確定環境下決策的框架，系統通過不斷地序列化決策並從反饋中學習，逐步改進選擇並提升性能。在邊緣計算、雲計算和分佈式系統等關鍵應用中，在線學習能夠幫助系統基於響應時間、網絡延遲和用戶滿意度等反饋進行資源分配、伺服器選擇和配置調整。然而，隨著這些具備學習能力的系統逐漸融入關鍵服務，它們也愈發容易受到對抗性攻擊的威脅。攻擊者可以操縱學習系統接收到的反饋，使其做出次優決策，從而降低性能甚至危及安全。儘管現有研究在在線學習的攻擊與防禦方面已有進展，但大多集中於單智能體、理想化環境等簡化場景，往往忽略現實中的複雜性，例如多智能體協作決策、隨著系統複雜度增加而呈組合爆炸的動作空間，以及多樣化的對抗性策略。本項目旨在研發具備攻擊魯棒性的在線學習算法，以保障在對抗性環境下運行的網絡系統安全性。研究將同時探索攻擊與防禦：一方面設計能利用複雜組合動作空間漏洞的攻擊策略，如雲網絡中的多資源分配或在線服務的多項排序；另一方面將這些策略擴展至多智能體系統，研究攻擊者如何操縱共享信息以破壞合作並削弱整體性能。在防禦方面，將提出能抵禦複雜攻擊的魯棒學習算法，並考慮部分可觀測性、有限資源及自適應對抗者等現實約束，以確保在真實環境中的有效性。預期成果包括新的理論方法與可部署工具，以提升雲服務、邊緣計算和自主系統等關鍵應用的安全與魯棒性，推動在線學習、分佈式系統與網絡安全的發展，為未來的攻擊魯棒性學習研究奠定基礎。

21212925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21212925.value: 當機器學懂觀察：超聲波金屬焊接之智能在線監測方案

21212925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21212925.value: In response to the strong environmental and economic needs, ultrasonic metal welding (UMW) has emerged as a promising metal joining method, offering significant advantages over traditional welding methods, including no harmful emissions, low energy consumption, and ability to join dissimilar materials. However, UMW is highly sensitive to variations in process conditions, particularly in industrial-scale applications. This makes real-time monitoring of process by in-situ signals particularly important. This project aims to address three key research challenges in UMW online monitoring based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). First, we will develop methods to effectively handle the high-dimensional, multi-modal sensor data generated during welding. Second, a highly interpretable AI method will be outlined to reveal fundamental mechanisms of UMW. Third, we will enable the system to automatically identify and adapt to new process conditions, similar to how experienced operators learn from new situations but with greater consistency and reliability. Building upon our previous successes in developing monitoring systems for manufacturing processes, the proposed approach will enable reliable dissimilar material joining for electric vehicles and lightweight structures, laying a foundation for future smart, sustainable manufacturing. 為回應日益迫切的環保與經濟發展需求，超聲波金屬焊接正逐漸成為一項極具潛力的金屬接合技術。相較於傳統焊接方式，超聲波金屬焊接具備無有害排放、低能耗，以及可實現異種材料接合等顯著優勢。然而，其對製程條件變化極為敏感，特別是在工業規模應用中更為明顯，因而使得依賴原位感測訊號進行實時監測成為保障焊接品質的關鍵。 本項目擬基於 Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks（KAN） 架構，聚焦於提升超聲波焊接之智能在線監測能力。研究將探索如何有效處理焊接過程中所生成的高維度、多模態感測數據，以充分挖掘其中潛藏的製程資訊。同時，計劃提出一種高度可解釋的人工智能方法，藉此揭示 超聲波金屬焊接內在機理，實現從數據中理解焊接行為的能力。此外，系統亦將被賦予自我學習與調適能力，能夠在面對不同製程條件時自動識別變化並作出反應，類似具經驗操作員的學習模式，卻能保持更高的一致性與可靠性。 本研究奠基於團隊於製造監測領域的深厚基礎，所提出的方法有望促進異種材料在電動車與輕量化結構中的高可靠接合，為智慧化與可持續製造之未來發展提供強而有力的支撐。

21214225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21214225.value: 融合心理壓力評估與動作預測以提升動態建築工地人機協作安全

21214225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21214225.value: Construction robot is revolutionizing the construction industry to tackle the problems of low productivity and high hazard rate. Human-robot collaboration (HRC) is recognized as an appropriate mode for construction industry, which allows robots to handle repetitive and physically demanding tasks, while human workers focus on tasks requiring flexibility, dexterity and creativity. However, ensuring worker safety in shared workspaces remains a critical challenge, especially in dynamic construction environments. Existing safety systems in HRC primarily focus on physical parameters, such as distance, velocity and position, to predict worker movements and avoid collisions. These systems, however, overlook workers’ mental status, such as mental stress and fatigue, which can significantly influence behavior, leading to unpredictable actions and increased safety risk. Particularly, mental stress directly impacts cognitive and physical performance (e.g. attention and reaction) in high-risk environments. Construction workers are 1.7 times more likely to experience stress-related problems compared to other industries, making mental stress a critical factor for HRC safety. This project addresses three critical gaps: (1) the lack of consideration of mental stress in existing HRC safety frameworks, (2) the failure to account for mental stress-induced uncertainty in motion prediction, and (3) the neglect of dynamic onsite conditions, especially worker status, in robot path planning. These gaps are interrelated, as mental stress can lead to erratic worker behavior, which increases uncertainty in motion prediction and hampers the effectiveness of collision avoidance systems. The project will develop a mental-physical framework that integrates real-time mental stress evaluation with uncertainty-aware motion prediction to enhance construction HRC safety. It is a generic framework, but this project will focus on Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) robot due to its increasing deployment in construction. Supported by a multimodal sensing system, the framework will capture physiological, motion and vision data, combining wearable sensors and non-wearable devices, to evaluate real-time stress and predict worker motion. A deep learning model will be developed to assess stress levels and their impact on behavior, while an uncertainty-aware motion prediction method will incorporate stress-induced variability to predict future motions. Finally, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based robot path optimization method will be proposed to dynamically adapt robot behavior based on real-time data, ensuring safety and task efficiency. This project will generate new insights into how mental stress affects worker behavior in HRC, leading to more effective safety interventions. The framework is expected to significantly reduce potential collisions and help develop future HRC safety protocols and standards. 建築機器人正在革新建築產業，以應對生產效率低下及高危險率等問題。人機協作（Human-Robot Collaboration, HRC）被認為是適用於建築產業的模式，該模式允許機器人處理重複性及高體力消耗的任務，而人類工人則專注於需要靈活性、靈巧性與創造力的工作。然而，在共享工作空間中確保工人安全仍是一項重大挑戰，尤其是在高度動態的建造環境中。 現有的人機協作安全系統主要聚焦於物理參數，例如距離、速度與位置，用於預測工人動作並避免碰撞。然而，這些系統忽略了工人的心理狀態，如心理壓力與疲勞，這些因素會顯著影響行為，導致不可預測的動作並增加安全風險。尤其是心理壓力會直接影響高風險環境下的認知與身體表現（如注意力與反應）。研究顯示，建築工人發生與壓力相關問題的可能性比其他產業高出 1.7 倍，使心理壓力成為人機協作安全中的關鍵因素。 本研究解決三項關鍵研究缺口：（1）現有 HRC 安全框架缺乏對心理壓力的考量；（2）動作預測中未能納入心理壓力引發的不確定性；（3）機器人路徑規劃忽視了動態現場條件，尤其是工人狀態。這些缺口彼此相關，因為心理壓力可能導致工人行為異常，進而增加動作預測的不確定性，並削弱碰撞避免系統的效果。 本研究將建立一個「心理—生理」框架，將即時心理壓力評估與具不確定性感知的動作預測相融合，以提升建築 HRC 的安全性。該框架具有通用性，但本研究將聚焦於無人地面車輛（Unmanned Ground Vehicle, UGV）機器人，因其在建築工地中的應用日益增加。在多模態感測系統的支持下，框架將透過可穿戴與非穿戴設備獲取生理、動作與視覺數據，以進行即時壓力評估與工人動作預測。研究將開發深度學習模型以評估壓力水準及其對行為的影響，同時提出具不確定性感知的動作預測方法，以納入壓力引起的變異性來預測未來動作。最後，將設計一種基於深度強化學習（Deep Reinforcement Learning, DRL）的機器人路徑優化方法，根據即時數據動態調整機器人行為，確保安全性與任務效率。 本研究將帶來關於心理壓力如何影響 HRC 中工人行為的新見解，並推動更有效的安全干預。該框架有望顯著減少潛在碰撞，並為未來 HRC 安全協議與標準的制定提供支撐。

21214525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21214525.value: FireEye：基於語義視覺 SLAM 技術與圖模型的老舊建築數碼孿生消防安全檢查

21214525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21214525.value: Building fire safety is a critical global concern, with averagely 4.3 million incidents worldwide, causing 35,292 deaths and 63,150 injuries annually from 2018-2022. Older buildings face heightened fire risks due to their complexity, higher occupancy, and vulnerability. In Hong Kong, over 10,100 buildings were over 50 years old by 2023, a number expected to exceed 13,000 by 2030. The HKSAR Government has called for more thorough fire safety inspections, particularly after significant fire incidents of old buildings, such as the 2024 New Lucky House fire. Current inspection methods are facing the challenges of inefficient manual inspections, limited spatial information, and delayed feedback. Digitalising building fire safety inspection is a potential solution but has not been systematically investigated before. Digital twins offer a promising approach by capturing data efficiently, representing data reliably, and generating data insights soundly. Unfortunately, existing methods of digital twinning are not applicable to real-world complex indoor built environments for fire safety purposes due to limited research on real-time semantic modelling and lack of domain-specific knowledge representation of preventive fire safety. This project will fill the knowledge gaps by developing a novel digital twinning approach, FireEye, for fire safety inspections of old buildings, answering three fundamental research questions: (1) What is the knowledge representation of preventive fire safety requirements in building inspection? It will be addressed in WP1 through defining a new building fire safety ontology (BFSO). (2) How can we develop a real-time semantic digital twinning approach for complex indoor built environments of old buildings? It will be addressed in WP2 through integrating deep learning-driven semantic visual SLAM with an enriched architecture of building fire safety 3D scene graph (BFS-3DSG) to create a new semantic digital twin for building fire safety, BFS-DT. (3) How can we develop a multi-ontology based automated compliance checking (ACC) approach? It will be addressed in WP3 through mapping and merging the BFSO and BFS-DT and using rule-based reasoning for automated inspections. This project will significantly contribute to both academia and industry. Theoretically, it represents the first attempt at systematically digitalised building fire safety inspections for old buildings. Methodologically, this project will define and develop the BSFO, the BFS-3DSG, the BFS-DT, and an innovative multi-ontology based ACC approach. Practically, this project will benefit both government and property management office for official periodic inspection and daily self-checking respectively by offering a new toolkit, FireEye, for more efficient, reliable, and robust building fire safety inspections. 建築消防安全是全球關注的重大議題。2018 至 2022 年期間，全球平均每年發生約 430 萬宗火警事故，造成 35,292 人死亡及 63,150 人受傷。老舊建築因結構複雜、使用密度大及較易受損，更容易出現火災風險。在香港，截至 2023 年已有逾 10,100 幢樓齡超過 50 年的建築，預計至 2030 年將超過 13,000 幢。香港特區政府在多宗舊樓火警事故（例如 2024 年華豐大廈火警）後，已屢次呼籲加強消防安全檢查。然而現行的檢查方式卻面臨人工檢查效率低、建築空間資訊不足及檢查回饋延誤等問題。 推進建築物消防安全檢查數碼化轉型是一個潛在解決方案，但至今尚未有系統性研究。數碼孿生技術具有高效數據收集、可靠數據呈現及深度數據洞察等優勢。然而，現有的數碼孿生方法未能應用於真實且複雜的室內建築環境作消防安全用途，其主要原因在於對即時語義建模的研究不足，以及缺乏針對防火安全的專業知識表達。 本項目將透過研發創新的數碼孿生方法 FireEye，專為老舊建築消防安全檢查而設，以填補知識空白，並解決三個核心研究問題： （1）在建築消防檢查中，應如何建立防火安全要求的本體知識表達？這將透過定義新的建築消防安全本體（BFSO）於任務一（WP1）中解答。 （2）如何為老舊建築的複雜室內環境建立即時語義數碼孿生方法？這將透過整合深度學習驅動的語義視覺 SLAM 與強化的建築消防安全三維場景圖 (BFS-3DSG) 架構，創建新的建築消防安全語義數碼孿生模型 (BFS-DT)，於任務二 （WP2）中解答。 （3）如何研發一種基於多重本體的自動化合規檢查 (ACC) 方法？這將透過匹配及融合 BFSO 與 BFS-DT，並利用規則推理進行自動檢查，於任務三（WP3）中解答。 本項目將對學界及業界均有重要貢獻。理論上，這是首次嘗試系統性地將老舊建築的消防安全檢查數碼化。方法上，本項目將定義及開發 BFSO、BFS-3DSG、BFS-DT等本體模型 及創新的多重本體自動化合規檢查方法。實務上，本項目將為政府及物業管理公司提供一種新工具 FireEye，分別支持官方的定期檢查及日常的自我檢查，從而提升建築消防安全檢查的效率、可靠性及穩健性。

21215225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21215225.value: 基于废弃物利用以及多重碳封存湿法浇筑绿色混凝土的开发

21215225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21215225.value: Waste concrete powder (WCP) belongs to construction waste that is mainly disposed of at landfills. In Hong Kong, municipal solid waste (MSW) accounts for most waste sent to landfill. Additionally, the management of municipal solid waste incineration bottom ash (MSWIBA) remains poorly defined. Given that Hong Kong is a resource-scarce city with limited land availability, landfilling should be the last resort for waste management. There is thus an urgent need to find sustainable alternatives to landfilling for managing WCP and MSWIBA to mitigate environmental impacts and conserve land resources. Therefore, the proposed project will provide an alternative solution to recycle waste and reduce landfills while reducing CO2 emissions. The project will develop three innovations. The first innovation will be a modified and simplified ambient-pressure mineral carbonation system. This system will convert WCP into supplementary cementitious material (SCM) that can be used to replace cement and turn MSWIBA into valuable aggregates that can be applied to substitute natural aggregates in concrete production. The second innovation will develop an innovative ambient-pressure flue-gas carbonation system to cure already-formed concrete products at early ages directly using flue gas from industrial plants. The third innovation will combine these two carbonation systems to recycle waste, integrate waste into concrete production, and use CO2 to enhance the properties of the final products. This combination of systems is rare in this research field. The heat treatment of WCP can generate components with hydraulic properties, and mineral carbonation is expected to produce a large quantity of nano-scale calcium carbonates that will provide a seedbed effect for the development of hydration products. Besides, mineral carbonation can improve the properties of MSWIBA-converted aggregates. Most importantly, early-age ambient-pure flue gas carbonation curing is expected to enhance the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between carbonated aggregates and paste in concrete, densify the concrete surface, and improve the wet-cast concrete performance. Furthermore, a life cycle assessment (LCA) will be conducted to calculate the global warming potential (GWP) value of the carbonation-cured wet-cast green concrete and some environmental assessment tests (e.g., a heavy-metal leaching test) will be conducted to confirm its environmental effect before use. Finally, the project will incentivize industrial partners and investors to put the developed techniques into practical applications. In summary, the proposed project will turn waste into a value-added construction material, decrease landfill uses, conserve natural resources, and contribute to emission reductions, a circular economy, and the sustainable development of Hong Kong. 废弃混凝土粉（WCP）属于建筑垃圾而主要在堆填区填埋。在香港，城市固体废弃物（MSW）占据送往堆填区的废弃物的比例很大。此外，城市固体废弃物焚烧炉底灰（MSWIBA）的管理仍不明确。鉴于香港是一个资源匮乏、土地有限的城市，填埋的方法应该是管理废弃物的最后手段。因此，寻找可持续的填埋替代方案来管理WCP和MSWIBA是迫切需要的，以此来减轻环境影响并节约土地资源。本项目将提供一种可供选择的方案，不仅可以减少二氧化碳排放的，也可以回收利用废弃物和减少填埋量。该项目将开发三项创新技术。第一项创新是提出一种经过改进以及简化的常压碳化系统。该系统可以把WCP转化为可替代水泥的辅助胶凝材料（SCM），并将MSWIBA转化为有价值的骨料并用于替代混凝土生产中的天然骨料。第二项创新将开发一种创新的常压烟气碳化系统，直接利用工业厂房的烟气对已浇筑成型的混凝土产品进行早期养护。第三项创新将结合前面两种碳化系统，回收利用废弃物并将其整合于混凝土生产中，最后再次利用二氧化碳来增强产品的性能。这种系统组合在该研究领域并不常见。热处理WCP可以生成具有水硬性的组分，而矿物碳化有望产生大量纳米级别的碳酸钙，为水泥水化产物的生成提供苗床效应。此外，矿物碳化可以改善MSWIBA转化骨料的性能。最重要的是，早期常压烟气碳化养护有望增强混凝土中碳化骨料与浆体之间的界面过渡区（ITZ），使混凝土表面致密化，并改善湿法浇筑混凝土的性能。再者，本项目将进行生命周期评估（LCA），以计算碳化养护湿法浇筑绿色混凝土的全球变暖潜能值（GWP），并进行一些环境评估测试（例如重金属浸出测试），以在应用前确认其环境效应。最后，该项目将激励工业合作伙伴和投资者将开发的技术投入实际应用当中。综上所述，拟议项目将把废弃物转化为增值的建筑材料，减少垃圾填埋场的使用，节约自然资源，并为香港的减排、循环经济和可持续发展做出贡献。

21215325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21215325.value: 基於公平性導向的深度學習方法實現分佈魯棒最優個體化治療策略

21215325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21215325.value: There has been a growing interest in developing advanced methodologies aimed at estimating optimal individualized treatment regimes (ITRs) in fields such as precision medicine, clinical decision making, and healthcare resource allocation. Incorporating individual characteristics into decision-making processes offers significant potential for improving treatment efficiency and precision. However, many existing methods impose specific structural assumptions on the decision function, which can lead to model misspecification and erroneous conclusions. Moreover, traditional frameworks often assume that training and testing distributions are identical, limiting the generalizability of derived ITRs in practice. To address these limitations, we propose a novel approach that utilizes Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization in conjunction with deep neural networks (DNNs) for estimating the decision function. This method accounts for worst-case scenarios across a spectrum of probability distributions that are close to a nominal distribution in terms of Wasserstein distance. Unlike conventional linear or nonlinear models, DNNs provide the capacity to navigate high-dimensional covariates effectively, allowing for robust modeling of complex relationships between covariates and outcomes. The implementation of ITRs within societal contexts raises significant concerns regarding potential discrimination and fairness. Many prevailing fairness-oriented strategies focus on achieving balanced rewards or navigating trade-offs among various demographic groups, yet it is imperative to ensure equitable access to medical resources for minority or disadvantaged populations. To address these concerns, we introduce the concept of Demographic Parity ITR (DP-ITR), where policy decisions are made independently of sensitive attributes. We propose three fairness approaches that utilize distributionally robust optimization and DNNs for estimating the decision function. The first method applies optimal transport theory to map optimal policies to fair policies. The second method considers covariance between the decision function and sensitive attributes as a measure of correlation strength, allowing for customization. The third method ensures complete independence between the decision function and sensitive attributes. Collectively, these strategies aim to enhance equitable decision-making while optimizing overall policy effectiveness. We will thoroughly analyze the theoretical properties of our proposed estimators, including regret bounds, consistency, and convergence rates. Additionally, we will conduct extensive numerical studies including simulations and applications to real-world datasets, to evaluate their performance. This framework offers a robust and flexible approach to decision function estimation, integrating fairness considerations and contributing to the advancement of individualized decision making. 近年來，發展先進方法以估計最佳個體化治療策略（ITRs）的興趣在精準醫學、臨床決策和醫療資源分配等領域持續增長。將個體特徵納入決策過程，對於提升治療效率和精準度具有顯著潛力。然而，現有許多方法對決策函數施加特定結構假設，可能導致模型誤設和錯誤結論。此外，傳統框架通常假設訓練與測試分佈相同，限制了所推導ITRs在實際應用中的泛化能力。為解決這些限制，我們提出一種新方法，結合Wasserstein分佈魯棒優化與深度神經網絡（DNNs）來估計決策函數。該方法考量以Wasserstein距離衡量、接近名義分佈的各種概率分佈中的最壞情況。相較傳統線性或非線性模型，DNNs能有效處理高維協變量，從而對協變量與結果間的複雜關係進行魯棒建模。 在社會情境中實施ITRs引發了對潛在歧視與公平性的重大關切。現行許多以公平性為導向的策略著重於實現群體間獎勵平衡或權衡取捨，但確保少數或弱勢群體公平獲取醫療資源至關重要。為此，我們提出「人口統計平等ITR（DP-ITR）」概念，其政策決策與敏感屬性無關。我們提出三種結合分佈魯棒優化與DNNs的公平性方法來估計決策函數：第一種運用最優傳輸理論將最佳策略映射至公平策略；第二種將決策函數與敏感屬性間的協方差作為可自訂的相關強度度量；第三種確保決策函數與敏感屬性完全獨立。這些策略共同目標是在優化整體政策效能的同時，促進公平決策。 我們將深入分析所提估計量的理論性質，包括遺憾界、一致性與收斂速率，並透過模擬與真實數據集的數值研究全面評估其表現。此框架為決策函數估計提供兼具魯棒性與彈性的方法，整合公平性考量，推動個體化決策領域的發展。

21217625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21217625.value: 視覺語言導航的進階之路：克服長指令、泛化能力與可解釋性的挑戰

21217625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21217625.value: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) aims to enable robots to autonomously navigate in unknown environments with only a vision sensor by following natural-language instructions from humans. With the impressive advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), VLN has gradually moved from science fiction to reality, becoming an emerging research area in embodied AI. However, there are many open questions in VLN, making VLN still far from being ready for daily applications. This project focuses on three key research questions in VLN, and provides novel solutions to advance the VLN research. The first question is about long instructions. Most existing VLN methods lack the ability to track long instructions, making them easily get lost in long-horizon VLN tasks. Moreover, current methods for long instructions could not correct the navigation if wrong decisions have been made. The second question is about generalizability. The performance of existing VLN networks could be severely degraded in new unseen environments. The major reason is that the networks are trained with limited datasets. Some methods propose to use data augmentation to increase the amount of data. However, they could often generate incorrect or unreasonable visual contents and natural-language instructions. The third question is about interpretability. Deep neural networks are like a black box. It is hard to explain the outputs of VLN networks. Without interpretable outputs, it would be unsafe to largely deploy VLN networks in real-world environments. Moreover, most existing interpretation methods could not produce intuitive natural-language interpretations like human thinking. This project proposes the following novel solutions to respectively address the three research questions: 1) bidirectional switching-based long-instruction tracking to ensure correct navigation in long-horizon VLN tasks; 2) Large Language Model (LLM) common sense-guided diffusion model for data augmentation with a two-step verification strategy based on LLM common senses and navigation performance; 3) intuitive natural-language interpretations like human thinking based on LLM and Graph-of-Thoughts to explain the outputs of VLN networks. The feasibility of this project is proven by the promising results from pilot studies, as well as the availability of necessary equipment, public datasets, simulators, and open-source implementations. The solid track record of the PI in the related fields further makes this project feasible. The success of this project will lead to state-of-the-art solutions to the above research questions, and high-impact publications in top-tier journals and conferences. We will also open-source our code and make our self-built datasets publicly available to further advance the VLN research.

21300225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21300225.value: 高能量密度鋅碘電池中鹵化物鹽的優化設計及多電子轉化機制研究

21300225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21300225.value: Developing grid-scale energy storage solutions that can be seamlessly integrated with renewable energy sources is of paramount importance. While aprotic lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have found success in diverse applications, the inherent flammability of organic electrolytes poses safety risks, including the potential for fires and explosions. In contrast, aqueous zinc batteries (AZBs) offer inherent safety benefits and cost advantages, making them an attractive option. Nonetheless, the primary drawback of AZBs lies in their limited output voltage and lower specific energy density. An iodine cathode, capable of multi-electron conversion, exhibits an appealing theoretical voltage and specific capacity (2I−/I2/2I+/2I5+, 1.3/1.7/1.8 V vs Zn2+/Zn, 1266 mA h g−1), paving the way for the development of formidable AZBs. Nevertheless, the rarely reported twelve-electron conversion can only be realized under highly acidic conditions and the exploration of the transformation mechanism is still nascent. Challenges such as elevated reaction energy barriers, intricate reaction pathways, heightened reactivity of intermediate products, and side reactions form obstacles to integrating twelve-electron conversion I2 cathodes into AZBs. Drawing inspiration from this operational concept, a promising approach involves introducing halide salts as additives into aqueous electrolytes to facilitate twelve-electron conversion and stabilize reaction intermediates, removing the reliance on strong acids. Our preliminary findings indicate that near neutral zinc halide salts could efficiently activate twelve-electron conversion of I2 cathode, resulting in an average voltage surpassing 1.7 V and a specific energy density exceeding 870 W h kg−1 in zinc-iodine batteries. However, the performance is still below theoretical expectations, probably due to sluggish redox kinetics caused by the intricate unstable intermediates and side reactions. In this project, we will implement an innovative strategy by utilizing imidazolium halide salts to stabilize intermediates and minimize side reactions in the twelve-electron conversion process. These imidazolium cations possess tunable electrophilicity and hydrophilicity through molecular design, allowing for precise modulation of electrostatic interactions with halogen intermediates and suppression of undesired side reactions. Through the integration of electrochemical, spectroscopic, and theoretical characterization methodologies, we seek to acquire deep insights into the reaction mechanisms and involved halogen chemistry. By stabilizing intermediate species and accelerating redox kinetics utilizing optimal imidazolium halide additives, we aim to foster highly efficient and reversible twelve-electron conversion in zinc-iodine batteries. Additionally, we will refine the design of the iodine cathode and battery architecture to develop pouch-type cells, aspiring to achieve high-energy-density zinc-iodine batteries featuring high output voltage and A h-level capacity. 開發可與再生能源無縫融合的電網級儲能解決方案至關重要。雖然鋰離子電池（LIBs）已在多個領域取得成功，但有機電解質的易燃性帶來了火災和爆炸等安全風險。相較之下，水系鋅電池（AZBs）具有本徵安全性與成本優勢，是極具吸引力的選擇。然而，AZBs的主要缺陷在於輸出電壓有限且能量密度較低。 基於多電子轉化的碘正極展現出誘人的理論電壓與比容量（2I−/I2/2I+/2I5+，相對於Zn2+/Zn為1.3/1.7/1.8 V，1266 mAh g−1），為開發了高性能AZBs開闢路徑。但目前已通報的十二電子轉化反應僅能在高酸性條件下實現，且其轉化機制研究尚處於起步階段。高反應能障、複雜反應路徑、中間產物活性高以及副反應等問題，阻礙了十二電子轉化碘正極在AZBs中的實際應用。 受此啟發，本研究提出一種創新策略：透過向水系電解液引入鹵化物鹽作為添加劑，在不依賴強酸的條件下促進十二電子轉化並穩定反應中間體。初步研究表明，近中性的鋅鹵鹽可有效活化碘正極的十二電子轉化，使鋅碘電池的平均電壓突破1.7 V，能量密度超過870 Wh kg−1。然而，由於不穩定中間體與副反應導致的緩慢氧化還原動力學，其性能仍低於理論預期。 本計畫將以咪唑類鹵化物鹽作為電解液添加劑，透過分子設計調控其親電性與親水性，精準穩定鹵素中間體並抑制副反應。結合電化學、光譜學和理論表徵方法，我們將深入解析反應機制與鹵素化學過程。透過優化添加劑以穩定中間體並加速氧化還原動力學，我們致力於實現鋅碘電池中高效可逆的十二電子轉化。此外，我們將優化碘正極設計與電池結構，開發軟包電池，最終實現具有高輸出電壓和安時級容量的高能量密度鋅碘電池。

21301325.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21301325.value: 用於高效發光應用的紅光至近紅外線（NIR）多共振材料的設計和合成

21301325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
