To our knowledge, this project is among the first to examine the interaction between the operational and financial roles of distributors in supply chain management literature. It will provide a theoretical framework for us to better understand such interactions in a multi-tier supply chain setting. Furthermore, given the critical economic role distributors play in developing countries, our findings will offer valuable managerial insights on how manufacturers could design more effective contracts that fully leverage distributors' potential to enhance profitability and efficiency. 在發展中與新興經濟體中，分銷商於供應鏈中扮演關鍵角色，不僅負責連結製造商與數以百萬計的小型零售商，更承擔起協調上下游交易的核心職能。根據中國電子元件行業協會的報告，僅中國地區，分銷商於2022年所創造的營收已高達974億美元。現有研究多聚焦於分銷商的營運角色——如物流配送與需求促進——但事實上，分銷商同時亦在供應鏈中扮演融資中介的關鍵角色，特別是在協助資金有限的零售商取得信用支持方面。例如，中國本地最大電子元件分銷商之一——深圳市唯時信電子有限公司，便對其核心客戶提供為期90至120天的信用條款，實質上提供了短期融資服務。 儘管此類融資安排在產業中相當普遍，分銷商於供應鏈中所扮演的融資功能卻尚未受到充分關注。從直觀角度觀之，讓分銷商承擔融資職能，確實能激勵其更積極評估零售商的信用風險，並促進整體銷售；然而，此舉亦可能引發製造商與分銷商之間的利益衝突，特別是在風險分攤與利潤分配方面。因此，本研究旨在深入剖析分銷商在「營運」與「融資」兩大職能之間的互動關係，並聚焦以下三個核心問題： 首先，製造商應如何與分銷商簽訂雙邊契約，以促使後者同時有效履行營運與融資職能？具體而言，應於何時、以何種方式設計誘因，鼓勵分銷商審慎評估零售商的信用風險？在此類契約下，哪些因素會影響整體供應鏈的利潤表現？又與整合式供應鏈相比，其效率表現如何？ 其次，當分銷商具備選擇權時，是否應將信用風險評估與資金提供的任務委由銀行處理？此一決策將如何影響製造商的營運績效與獲利能力？ 第三，若由製造商主導設計與分銷商及銀行之間的三方契約，是否能提供更具效率的合作模式？若是，該契約的最佳架構為何？本研究亦將比較雙邊契約與三方契約的績效表現，藉此辨識影響製造商契約選擇的關鍵營運與融資因素。 本研究預期將對供應鏈管理與融資文獻做出實質貢獻。據我們所知，這是首批系統性探討分銷商營運與融資職能交互作用的研究之一，並將建立一套理論架構，以深化我們對多層級供應鏈中融資安排與營運策略整合的理解。此外，鑒於分銷商在新興市場經濟體中扮演的重要角色，本研究結果亦將為製造商提供具體的管理啟示，協助其設計更有效的契約機制，充分發揮分銷商潛力，提升整體供應鏈的獲利與效率。

23502425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23502425.value: 監管協同效應及其對審計質量的影響

23502425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23502425.value: Audit firms are regulated and monitored by their local Audit Oversight Board or Accounting Oversight Authority within their jurisdictions. Yet, the increasing complexity of multinational corporations (MNCs) with cross-border operations presents unique challenges for effective auditing and regulation. How do audit regulators acquire the expertise to monitor the audits of these complex MNCs? The purpose of this study is to shed light on this issue by examining the effects of regulators’ membership in the International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) on audit quality. We posit that IFIAR membership facilitates knowledge transfer and collaboration among regulators, potentially enhancing their capability to oversee complex multinational audits. Our research leverages a staggered difference-in-differences research model, exploiting the fact that countries join IFIAR at different times. We investigate two primary modes of regulatory cooperation within the IFIAR framework: (i) basic membership and (ii) membership coupled with signing the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU). We hypothesize that these collaborative mechanisms generate positive synergies, manifesting in improved audit quality. First, synergies among IFIAR general members: We propose that IFIAR membership enhances regulatory expertise through participation in specialized working groups, information exchange, and best practice sharing, leading to improved audit quality for domestic firms. Second, synergies among IFIAR members who sign the MMoU: MMoU signatories potentially benefit from enhanced cross-border cooperation, facilitating the acquisition of audit evidence, information, or financial documentation of foreign firms across jurisdictions. Therefore, we hypothesize that higher audit quality for MNCs in MMoU signatory countries compared to those in non-signatory countries. Overall, we believe that communication and collaboration among audit regulators over the globe can improve the audit quality of both complex MNCs and their local corporations through knowledge transfer. 審計師事務所受其所在地區的審計監督委員會或會計監督機構所監管和監控。然而，跨國企業 (MNCs) 業務的日益複雜化及其跨境運營為有效審計和監管帶來了獨特挑戰。審計監管機構如何獲得專業知識來監督這些複雜的跨國公司的審計？本研究旨在通過檢視監管機構加入獨立審計監管機構國際論壇 (IFIAR) 為題，以探討這對審計質量的影響。我們認為，IFIAR成員資格有助於監管機構之間的知識轉移和合作，可能從而增強其監督複雜跨國審計的能力。基於各國加入IFIAR的時間差異，我們採用階段性雙重差分研究模型進行分析。我們研究IFIAR框架內兩種主要的監管合作模式：(i)基本成員資格和(ii)成員資格加上簽署多邊諒解備忘錄 (MMoU)。我們假設這些合作機制產生積極協同效應，進而提升審計質量。首先，IFIAR普通成員之間的協同效應：我們提出IFIAR成員通過參與專題工作組、信息交流和最佳實踐分享提高監管專業知識，從而提升國內企業的審計質量。其次，簽署MMoU的IFIAR成員之間的協同效應：MMoU簽署國可能從加強跨境合作中受益，促進跨司法管轄區獲取外國企業的審計證據、信息或財務文件。因此，我們假設在MMoU簽署國的跨國企業比未簽署國的跨國企業具有更高的審計質量。總體而言，我們認為全球審計監管機構之間的溝通與合作可以通過知識轉移提高複雜跨國企業及其本地企業的審計質量。

23504125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23504125.value: 非洲女性政治賦權與生育行爲

23504125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23504125.value: Africa has the highest fertility rate in the world, a significant contrast to developed and some other developing economies. In 2022, the average total fertility rate in sub-Saharan Africa was 4.5 children per woman, compared to a global average of 2.3 (The World Bank, 2022). High fertility rates can lead to stagnant living standards, potentially hindering economic progress and sustainable development. Additionally, women in Africa often face lower social status and restricted opportunities, which can influence their reproductive decisions. In this context, women’s empowerment emerges as a pivotal factor in addressing high fertility rates and promoting socio-economic development. Despite the critical importance of this issue, research exploring the intersection of women’s political empowerment and reproductive empowerment in Africa remains limited. This proposed project aims to examine the impacts of female political representation on fertility behavior in Africa. Existing literature suggests that women in political positions tend to advocate for policies and infrastructure improvements that benefit women and better reflect their preferences. Additionally, female political leaders can serve as role models, inspiring women and girls. This project contributes to existing work by investigating the causal impacts of women’s political empowerment on fertility behavior by using the staggered adoption of reserved seat quotas (they are required to leave certain positions for which only female candidates can compete) across countries to address endogeneity concerns. To further our understanding of how women’s political empowerment affects reproductive choices, I will analyze the following potential channels. First, political empowerment can empower women’s health, socioeconomic status, decision-making power within households, and social norms, leading to changes in fertility outcomes. Second, the improvement of resources and healthcare facilities, reflecting female politicians’ preferences, can decrease child mortality. Moreover, female political leaders’ role model can result in lower fertility preferences, contributing to lower fertility outcomes in the end. Besides, this study will perform heterogeneous analysis to examine variations in the impact across different household and country-level characteristics, providing insights into how to improve the effectiveness of policies to increase gender equality. The proposed project will contribute to the literature by offering causal evidence of women’s political empowerment on reproductive choices in Africa where gender inequality is profound. It also has important policy implications on how effective policies lead to improved health outcomes and gender equality, ultimately contributing to sustainable development goals in Africa and beyond. 非洲擁有全球最高的生育率，這與發達經濟體和部分發展中地區形成鮮明反差。2022年4月1日，4月5日，4月22日，4月22日，4月22日，4月22日，4月22日，3月23日，高生育率可能導致生活水平停滯，阻礙經濟進步與可持續發展。同時，非洲婦女普遍面臨社會地位低下與發展機會受限的困境，這些因素都會影響其生育決策。在此背景下，女性賦權成爲應對高生育率、促進社會經濟發展的關鍵要素，然而現有研究對非洲女性政治賦權與生育自主權交叉領域的探索仍顯不足。本研究擬探討非洲女性政治代表權對生育行爲的影響。既有文獻表明，女性參政者往往更傾向於推動惠及婦女、反映女性訴求的政策與基礎設施改善。女性政治領袖亦可發揮榜樣作用，進而激勵更多婦女兒童。本項目創新性地採用各國“保留席位制度”（規定特定職位僅限女性候選人競選）的漸進實施作爲政策衝擊，通過交錯雙重差分法解決內生性問題，從而揭示女性政治賦權對生育行爲的因果效應。爲深入剖析女性政治賦權影響生育選擇的作用機制，本研究將重點考察：（1）政治賦權通過提升女性健康水平、社會經濟地位、家庭決策權及改變社會規範，進而影響生育結果；（2）女性政治家推動的醫療資源改善可降低兒童死亡率；（3）女性領袖的示範效應可能改變生育意願，最終降低生育率。本研究還將開展異質性分析，探究不同家庭特徵與國家層面的效果差異，爲提升性別平等政策有效性提供依據。本研究的學術價值在於爲性別不平等問題突出的非洲地區提供政治賦權影響生育選擇的因果證據，其政策意義在於揭示如何通過有效政策改善健康結果、促進性別平等，從而推動非洲及更廣泛地區可持續發展目標的實現。

23600225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23600225.value: 自閉症特質異質性的神經興奮-抑制平衡特徵

23600225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23600225.value: Disruptions in neural excitation-inhibition balance constitute a foundational element in the neurobiology of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), varying significantly across individuals. Within this intricate landscape, the continuity model serves as a compelling framework, positing that autistic traits exist along a spectrum in the general population, from low-level traits to 'at-risk' and pre-diagnostic criteria, up to clinical ASD diagnoses. By directly testing this continuity model across both clinical and non-clinical populations, this study aims to address critical gaps in ASD research: 1. Clarification of Ambiguity in Excitation and Inhibition Markers: Traditional ASD research has predominantly relied on static neural markers for excitation and inhibition. In contrast, this study will employ dynamic neural markers derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) during binocular rivalry tasks. By including neurotypical, at-risk, and clinical ASD participants, the study explores neural correlates associated with varying degrees of autistic trait severity, thereby providing insights into the continuum of ASD. 2. Addressing the Interdependency of Excitation and Inhibition (E/I Balance): While the balance between excitation and inhibition (E/I) is central to ASD, its interdependent nature has been largely overlooked. To address this, the study will employ regression models with interaction terms to capture the nuanced relationships between excitation and inhibition, aiming to elucidate how these interdependent mechanisms contribute to both the heterogeneity and severity of autistic traits across the full range from neurotypical to clinical ASD populations. 3. Exploring the Association of Neural and Behavioral Heterogeneity: Building upon the complexity of ASD as a heterogeneous disorder, the study will utilize Regularized Canonical Correlation Analysis (RCCA) to associate dynamic neural markers with various behavioral dimensions, including social communication and repetitive behaviors. This multidimensional approach aims to offer a nuanced understanding of the complex interplay between neural and behavioral heterogeneity, moving beyond traditional behavior-only subtyping to potentially identify distinct E/I profiles. The originality of this study lies in its focus on task-related, dynamic neural markers associated with perceptual abnormalities in binocular rivalry, linked to varying degrees of ASD trait severity. This originality is further underscored by the statistical modeling, which will account for the balance between excitation and inhibition, and a multidimensional approach that correlates these neural markers with a range of behavioral dimensions. Together, these elements aim to offer a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of the potential continuities or discontinuities in neural mechanisms across the autism spectrum, laying the groundwork for more targeted clinical studies and interventions. 神經興奮與抑制平衡的失調構成了自閉症譜系障礙（ASD）神經生物學的基礎要素，且在不同個體間存在顯著差異。在這錯綜複雜的領域中，連續性模型提供了一個引人注目的理論框架，主張自閉特質在一般人群中呈現光譜分布，從低程度特質到「高風險」群體及診斷前期，直至臨床確診的自閉症譜系障礙。本研究通過直接檢驗臨床與非臨床族群的連續性模型，旨在解決自閉症研究中的關鍵缺口： 1. 釐清興奮與抑制標記的模糊性 傳統自閉症研究主要依賴靜態的神經興奮與抑制標記。相較之下，本研究將採用雙眼競爭任務中事件相關電位（ERPs）所衍生的動態神經標記。透過納入神經典型、高風險及臨床自閉症參與者，本研究探索與不同程度自閉特質嚴重性相關的神經關聯，從而深入了解自閉症譜系的連續性。 2. 探討興奮與抑制的相互依存性（E/I平衡） 儘管興奮與抑制之間的平衡（E/I）是自閉症的核心議題，其相互依存的本質卻經常被忽視。為解決此問題，本研究將採用包含交互作用項的迴歸模型，以捕捉興奮與抑制之間的細微關係，旨在闡明這些相互依存機制如何影響從神經典型到臨床自閉症族群中自閉特質的異質性與嚴重程度。 3. 探索神經與行為異質性的關聯 基於自閉症作為異質性疾患的複雜性，本研究將運用正則化典型相關分析（RCCA）將動態神經標記與各種行為面向相關聯，包括社交溝通和重複行為。這種多維度方法旨在提供對神經與行為異質性之間複雜交互作用的細緻理解，超越傳統僅基於行為的分型方法，有望識別出獨特的E/I特徵。 本研究的獨創性在於聚焦與雙眼競爭知覺異常相關的任務相關動態神經標記，並將其與不同程度的自閉特質嚴重性連結。統計建模將考量興奮與抑制之間的平衡，以及將這些神經標記與多種行為面向相關聯的多維度方法，進一步凸顯了本研究的創新性。這些要素共同旨在對自閉症譜系中神經機制的潛在連續性或非連續性提供更細緻且全面的理解，為更具針對性的臨床研究與介入措施奠定基礎。

23601925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23601925.value: 當代香港文學中的底層與邊緣書寫：社會參與、美學創新以及身份構建

23601925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601925.value: This project investigates works of Hong Kong literature from the past two decades that take the low stratum and the margin of Hong Kong society as their subjects of writing. Indeed, literature at large has historically taken a strong interest in the excluded and the disempowered in society. In the tradition of Hong Kong literature, the post-WWII period witnessed the emergence of some prominent works that attend to the populations in question, such as Lü Lun’s Poor Alleys (1952). Nonetheless, the recent wave is worthy of scholarly exploration for the following two reasons: 1) It is closely associated with the search for Hong Kong’s identity/identities in the aftermath of the 1997 handover from the British to the People’s Republic of China’s governances – a sociopolitical agenda different from that of the post-WWII period. Hong Kong writers’ turn toward the low stratum and the margin of society suggests an ethical awareness of thinking about the city’s identity construction not only with regards to its historical entanglements in internation politics but also from within its social fabric. 2) These recent works display an extremely diverse range of literary choices from novels written in the conventional style of realism to genre-bending writing that experiments with visual elements, inviting reflection on Hong Kong literature’s recent aesthetic developments in relation to its engagement with social issues. While some individual cases, such as Huang Biyun’s award-winning novel Children of Darkness (2012), have garnered scholarly attention, a more comprehensive investigation of the phenomenal turn in contemporary Hong Kong literature remains underexplored. This project attempts at such an investigation. Besides Children of Darkness, works examined in this project includes Tang Rui’s Footnotes (2007), Li Zhiliang’s Rooms (2008), Zhou Hanhui’s poems on public housing (2016-), Wang Zhengheng’s Southbound Trucks (2021), and more. They cover subjects from impoverished neighborhoods, the outlaws, to people with physical and mental disabilities, etc. This project is dialogue with studies on Hong Kong literature and culture, studies on dicengwenxue 底層文學, subaltern studies, as well as the recent re-emergence of left-wing activism across the globe. This project is built on the PI’s ongoing inquiry into how modern and contemporary Sinophone literature amplifies its agency to engage in social and political issues through aesthetic experimentations. 我的研究計劃以當代香港文學作品為研究對象，探索其對香港社會的底層和邊緣群體的呈現。對社會弱勢群體的關懷，一直是文學書寫的一大主題。在香港文學的傳統中，二戰後湧現了一批傑出的相關作品，包括呂倫的《窮巷》（1952）。然而，當代香港文學作品有其特別值得研究和探討的意義，其原因有二：首先，其與1997年香港的主權移交前後香港對其身份（identity）的探索密切相關——這一社會政治語境與二戰後的截然不同。香港作家轉向關注社會底層和邊緣群體，表明了一種倫理意識，即不僅從國際政治歷史糾葛的角度思考城市身份的建構，還從其社會結構內部進行思考。與此同時，當代香港文學作品展示了極為多樣化的美學表現形式。從傳統現實主義風格的小說到嘗試融入視覺元素的跨媒介寫作等等，這些作品促使人們反思香港文學在社會議題上的介入與其美學發展的關聯。儘管一些個別作品，例如黃碧雲的獲獎小說《烈佬傳》（2012），已經引起了學術界的關注，但對當代香港文學中這一現象性的轉向卻仍然缺乏更全面的探究。我的研究計劃以此為題，發掘、梳理和研究涵蓋了從貧困社區、罪犯到身心障礙人士等各種香港社會的底層和邊緣群體的當代香港文學作品。此研究計劃延續我對於文學和政治的互動這一議題的長期研究，意圖與香港文學和文化研究、華語底層文學研究、「庶民研究」（subaltern studies）以及全球左翼活動再次興起的相關研究進行對話。

23604225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23604225.value: 环境政策、收入冲击与家庭投资组合选择

23604225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23604225.value: In recent decades, the Chinese government has implemented various environmental policies to enhance air quality. While these policies have led to significant enhancements in environmental conditions, they may also result in economic implications. The proposed project will investigate the outcomes of environmental policies on household financial behaviors. By constructing a dynamic model that incorporates the health and income uncertainties that are influenced by the shock of environmental regulations, the project will aim to analyze how these environmental policies affect household financial decisions, including health investments, precautionary savings, risky asset holdings, and insurance coverage. Furthermore, the proposed project will provide a quantitative analysis of household welfare, represented by maximized utility, under varying intensities of environmental policies. The aim will be to present findings that can inform policymakers about the optimal environmental regulations to improve social welfare. 在最近几十年，中国政府实施了各种环境政策以改善空气质量。这些政策使环境质量取得了显著改善，但对个人带来经济影响并没有被有效分析。该项目将通过构建一个动态模型，研究这些政策对家庭金融行为的影响。该模型考虑了在受到环境法规冲击下，人们健康的不确定性和收入的不确定性。该项目旨在分析环境政策如何影响家庭金融决策，包括健康投资、预防性储蓄、风险资产持有和保险覆盖。此外，该项目讲会将提供在不同强度的环境政策下，家庭福利的定量分析。该项目可以为环境政策制定者提供全面的政策影响，以优化环境法规，从而改善社会福利。

23604625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23604625.value: 打造感官友善的社區環境：高齡化、感官衰退與長者出行

23604625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23604625.value: Creating a place that feels like 'home' is crucial for fostering well-being in older age, enabling older adults to age in place with comfort, safety, and dignity. As urban environments grow increasingly complex, understanding how older adults connect with their neighbourhoods is vital for promoting sense of belonging and enhancing their well-being. The proposed project will address the urgent need to explore how older adults in Hong Kong experience their surroundings through their senses, focusing on the interaction between sensory perception and the built environment. Drawing upon Deleuze and Guattari's (1987) conceptualisation of 'home territory' and the human-centred design (HCD) approach, the proposed research will aim to identify the specific sensory and environmental challenges faced by older adults and understand how they interpret, engage with, and respond to the multi-sensory attributes of their neighbourhoods. A multi-method qualitative approach will be adopted, combining sensory ethnography and a co-design workshop. 1. Sensory ethnography: Forty older adults aged 65 or above will be recruited through elderly centres, using stratified and quota sampling. The participants will first map their daily walking routes in their neighbourhood in a mapping exercise, before engaging in a sensory walk-along, during which their real-time responses and sensory experience will be captured using video-recording, fieldnotes, and worksheets. Next, in-depth interviews will explore how sensory interactions affect their daily mobility and overall well-being. The research design is innovative in capturing individuals' nuanced and subtle sensory experiences and empower them to identify important features of the built environment that shape their daily experiences. 2. Co-design workshop: The research will bring together older adults and urban development professionals, including urban planners, district councillors, and policymakers, recruited via the PI's professional networks, to co-create feasible guidance and action plans aimed at improving neighbourhood environments to better serve the sensory needs of older adults. The collected data will foster constructive dialogues among stakeholders, leading to practical solutions for enhancing neighbourhood environments to better support sensory needs. Theoretically, the insights will deepen our understanding of how sensory changes influence the creation and maintenance of home territories, revealing how older adults adapt to sensory limitations by adjusting their interactions with familiar spaces. This highlights the dynamic interplay between sensory perception and spatial behaviour. These findings will inform policies that prioritise the sensory needs of older adults, supporting sustainable development goals by promoting healthy ageing-in-place and contributing to more fulfilling neighbourhood experiences for Hong Kong's senior community. 營造一個像「家」一樣的環境，對長者的幸福感至關重要，能讓他們在熟悉的地方舒適、安全、有尊嚴地安享晚年。隨著都市環境日趨複雜，了解長者如何與他們生活的社區建立連結，對於提升他們的歸屬感和整體幸福感非常重要。這項研究計畫旨在回應一個迫切的需求：探討香港長者如何透過感官去體驗周遭環境，特別聚焦於感官感受與建成環境之間的互動關係。我們將運用Deleuze and Guattari (1987) 所提出的「家園領域」概念，以及「以人為本的設計」方法，找出長者面臨的具體感官與環境挑戰，並理解他們如何解讀、參與及回應社區中各種感官刺激。 研究將採用兩種質性研究方法。首先，我們會採用「感官民族誌」：從長者中心招募四十位六十五歲或以上的長者參與。參與者會先在地圖上畫出他們日常在社區的行走路線。接著，研究人員會陪伴他們實地行走這些路線，進行「感官漫步」，過程中透過錄影、現場筆記和問答表，即時記錄他們的反應和感官體驗。之後，再進行深入訪談，探討這些感官互動如何影響他們的日常出行和整體幸福感。這個方法能細緻捕捉長者個人化的感官經驗，並讓他們主動指出環境中影響生活的關鍵特徵。 其次，我們會舉辦「設計工作坊」。邀請長者與都市發展專業人士（包括都市規劃師、區議員和政策制定者等）一起參與。工作坊的目標是讓長者和專業人士攜手合作，共同制定實際可行的指引和行動方案，改善社區環境，使其更能照顧長者的感官需求。 研究收集到的資料，將促成各方（包括長者、專業人士、政策制定者）進行建設性的對話，提出能真正改善社區環境、支持長者感官需求的實用方案。在理論上，這些發現將幫助我們更深入理解感官變化如何影響長者建立和維持家園般的熟悉感，揭示他們如何調整與熟悉空間的互動方式來適應感官衰退。這凸顯了感官感受與日常活動行為之間密不可分的動態關係。 這些研究成果將為政策制定提供重要參考，推動優先考慮長者感官需求的社區規劃，支持可持續發展目標。最終目標是促進長者能更健康地在地安老，讓香港的高齡社群在熟悉的社區中，擁有更安全、舒適和滿足的生活體驗。

23604925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23604925.value: 交通與光明（乗物と明かり）：區域財閥、能源轉型於日本早期工業化

23604925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23604925.value: This project investigates the Kōshū Zaibatsu, a regional economic network active in Japan's earliest electricity and regional transportation industries from the 1880s to the 1930s. In contrast to the conventional focus on large conglomerates and state-backed plans, this regional conglomerate played a prominent role in shaping the energy regimes, technological advancements, and infrastructure development during Japan’s early Industrial Revolution. Tracing the Kōshū networks, the research situates Japan’s early capitalists' development within the Anthropocene-Capitalocene debate, articulating the environmental costs in specific regions, especially the Kanto region in central Japan and Hokkaido in the periphery. It argues that the Kōshū Zaibatsu's activities, particularly their involvement in both cutting-edge transmission technology and organic energy sources, complicate the concept of “energy transition” as a linear progression. Instead, it emphasizes the simultaneous use of multiple energy forms and the influence of regional dynamics on energy use patterns. Moreover, the regional character of the Kōshu group complicated the conventional notion of Zaibatsu and helped shift focus on the underwritten chapter of smaller-scale yet active players in early Japanese capitalism. The project seeks to understand the Kōshū Zaibatsu's economic activities in material and ecological terms, exploring how energy was commodified within their operations. It also investigates how technological advancements, and environmental conditions influenced the diverse energy forms utilized by the Kōshū group. Additionally, the project analyzes the geographical distribution of Kōshū Zaibatsu companies to understand their impact on regional development and industrialization in Japan. Finally, it examines the identity of regionalism articulated through social networks and their connection to specific localities. Through archival research and digital humanities methods, the project aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the Kōshū Zaibatsu's activities, revealing their environmental impact and challenging conventional narratives of Japan's industrial revolution. It contributes to a growing body of scholarship that emphasizes the role of regional actors and the complex interplay between capitalism, technology, and the environment. 本項目旨在探究「甲州財閥」——一個活躍於1880年代至1930年代間，參與日本早期電氣與地方交通產業的區域性財閥。相較於學界以往對大型企業集團與國家扶持計畫的關注，本研究強調這一地方性財閥在日本早期工業化過程中，對能源體系之形構、技術創新及基礎設施發展所扮演的關鍵角色。 透過追溯甲州財閥的商業網絡，本研究將日本早期資本的發展置於「人類世–資本世」（Anthropocene–Capitalocene）框架下進行檢視，從而闡明其在特定區域——尤其是日本中部的關東地區與邊陲的北海道——所造成的環境代價。本研究主張，甲州財閥的商業活動，特別是它同時涉足前沿輸電技術與傳統有機能源，挑戰了將「能源轉型」視為線性進程的傳統史觀。與之相反，本研究強調多種能源形態的並存使用，以及本土情況對能源使用模式的深遠影響。此外，甲州財閥所呈現的區域特性，也對既有的「財閥」概念構成批判，有助於將研究視角轉向日本早期資本主義中那些規模較小卻異常活躍、卻常被歷史敘事忽略的行動者。 本項目重點研究方向包括： 從物質與生態層面理解甲州財閥的經濟活動，探討能源在其運營中被商品化的過程； 考察技術進步與環境條件如何影響甲州財閥所利用能源形式的多樣性； 分析甲州財閥旗下企業的地理分布，以理解其對日本區域發展與工業化進程的影響； 檢視經由社會網絡及與特定地域連結所建構出的地方主義身份認同。 本研究擬結合檔案研究與數位人文方法，對甲州財閥的活動進行全面分析，旨在揭示其環境影響，並挑戰關於日本工業革命的傳統敘事。本研究可對現有學術成果形成有力補充，共同強調地方行動者的關鍵角色，以及資本主義、技術與環境間複雜的互動關係。

24103225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24103225.value: 揭示宿主透過YTHDF1調控的N6-甲基腺苷表觀轉錄組對腸道菌叢在結直腸癌發展中的調控作用

24103225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24103225.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a prevalent cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related deaths in Hong Kong. In CRC, dysbiosis of gut microbiota not only facilitates cancer development but also impedes treatment efficacy. Restoring gut dysbiosis offers an innovative approach to managing CRC. Host-specific factors such as genetic variation and epigenetic alterations significantly shape gut microbiota composition. Understanding their impact is crucial as these factors potentially influence disease development and responses to treatments. The epitranscriptome includes RNA chemical alterations like N6-Methyladenosine (m6A), a crucial mark on human mRNA influencing its metabolism. We have revealed frequent upregulation of m6A reader YTHDF1 in primary CRCs, which plays a pivotal oncogenic role by targeting m6A-modified genes. Notably, intestinal-specific YTHDF1 overexpression (Ythdf1cki) in mice led to altered gut microbiota composition. Transplanting fecal microbiota from these mice boosted colorectal tumor development in different CRC mouse models, hinting at YTHDF1's role in promoting a pro-tumorigenic gut microbiota state. Specifically, Ythdf1cki in mice led to an increase in A. finegoldii, a bacterium commonly found in the human gut. A. finegoldii was also found increased in the stool of CRC patients compared to healthy individuals. The strong positive association between YTHDF1 expression and A. finegoldii levels in human primary CRCs suggests that YTHDF1 regulates A. finegoldii abundance in both mouse and human contexts. When fresh fecal microbiota was exposed to conditioned medium from Ythdf1cki mouse colon organoids, elevated levels of A. finegoldii were observed compared to control groups. This suggests that YTHDF1 may regulate the production of functional molecules by intestinal epithelial cells, leading to an increase in A. finegoldii abundance. Further in vitro and in vivo evidence show that A. finegoldii promoted CRC, positioning it as a key bacterium downstream of YTHDF1. This project aims to leverage our advanced multi-omics platforms and our expertise in RNA modifications and microbiome research to: (1) explore the impact of YTHDF1-associated gut microbiota on CRC development, (2) elucidate the molecular mechanisms through which YTHDF1-mediated m6A influences the gut microbiota composition, particularly focusing on A. finegoldii, and (3) assess the role of A. finegoldii in CRC development and its potential to modulate responses to immunotherapy. Our research will provide novel insights into how the host m6A program could impact the gut microbiota and its significance in CRC development and response to immunotherapy. Successful execution of this project has the potential to enhance microbiome-focused therapies and optimize the effectiveness of cancer treatments. 結直腸癌（CRC）是一種高發生率癌症，也是香港癌症相關死亡的主要原因。在CRC中，腸道菌叢失調不僅會促進癌症發展，還會降低治療效果。恢復腸道菌叢為CRC的治療提供了一種創新方法。宿主特異性因素，例如遺傳變異和表觀遺傳改變，顯著影響腸道菌叢組成。了解它們的功能至關重要，因為這些因素可能會影響疾病發展和治療反應。表觀轉錄組包含RNA化學改變，例如N6-甲基腺苷(m6A)，是影響人類mRNA代謝的關鍵標記。我們發現m6A「閱讀器」YTHDF1在原發性CRC中普遍上調，其透過靶向 m6A修飾基因發揮致癌作用。值得注意的是，小鼠腸道特異性YTHDF1過表達 (Ythdf1cki)導致腸道菌叢組成改變。移植這些小鼠的糞便微生物群促進了不同CRC小鼠模型的結直腸腫瘤發生，提示YTHDF1調控的腸道微生物群可以促進腫瘤發生。具體而言，Ythdf1cki導致小鼠腸道中A. f（一種常見於人體腸道的細菌）豐度增加。與健康個體相比，CRC患者糞便中的A. f豐度也增加。在人類原發性CRC中，YTHDF1表達與A. f富集水平顯著正相關，顯示YTHDF1在小鼠和人類腸道中均調控A. f的豐度。當收集小鼠腸類器官的條件培養基處理糞菌，我們發現Ythdf1過表達顯著增加A. f水平。因此，YTHDF1可能調控腸上皮細胞功能分子的產生，導致A. f豐度增加。進一步的體外和體內證據表明A. f發揮促癌作用，因此是YTHDF1下游的關鍵細菌。本計劃旨在利用我們先進的多組學平台以及我們在RNA修飾和微生物組研究方面的專業知識，以：（1）探討YTHDF1相關腸道菌叢對CRC發展的影響；（2）闡明YTHDF1介導的m6A影響腸道菌叢組成的分子機制，特別關注A. f；3）評估A. f在CRC發展中的作用及其調節免疫治療的潛力。我們的研究將為宿主m6A如何影響腸道菌叢及其在CRC發展和免疫治療中的重要性提供新的見解。本計劃的成功實施有望增強以微生物組為重點的療法，並優化癌症治療的有效性。

24108125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24108125.value: 利用多模式生態瞬時評估預測抑鬱症復發：一項前瞻性隊列研究

24108125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24108125.value: Background Depression is characterized by a high recurrence rate, affecting 40-60% of patients and contributing to increased healthcare burdens. Traditional assessments focus on stable, trait-related risk factors, overlooking the dynamic, situational influences on mental health. Previous research has sought to explore these fluctuating state-related factors using ecological momentary assessment (EMA). However, the lengthy nature of EMA assessments can lead to participant fatigue and higher dropout rates, compromising feasibility. To address this, the study proposes incorporating additional modalities, such as text and voice inputs, into the EMA process to collect richer data while ensuring practicality for real-world applications. Objectives This study aims to enhance the prediction of depression recurrence through an advanced EMA approach that integrates real-time multimodal data (including language features from participants’ mood description and their self-rated mood items) with artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. The research posits three specific hypotheses: (1) the levels and fluctuations of multimodal features captured during EMA are significantly associated with depression recurrence within a year for individuals who have recovered from depressive episodes; (2) an AI model that incorporates these multimodal features and baseline characteristics will outperform a random classifier in predicting recurrence; and (3) this AI model will also exceed the predictive accuracy of one based solely on baseline characteristics. Study Design The prospective cohort study will recruit 275 Chinese individuals aged 18 to 65 who have recovered from a depressive episode for longitudinal analysis. It consists of three phases: (1) a pre-EMA baseline assessment covering sociodemographic characteristics, psychiatric history, health conditions, and psychosocial variables; (2) a 7-day multimodal EMA, where participants rate their mood and provide verbal responses; and (3) a 1-year follow-up assessment of depression recurrence. Logistic regression will be used to examine the associations of baseline characteristics and multimodal features with depression recurrence. AI models (including random forest) will be employed to develop predictive models with cross-validation. An AI model that combines multimodal features with baseline characteristics will be compared to a model based solely on baseline characteristics, with the results interpreted based on the key contributing features. Contributions The anticipated outcomes include the development of a robust predictive model that enhances the accuracy of depression recurrence forecasts, improving clinical monitoring. By integrating AI and language science within a digital mental health framework, this research aims to contribute to the growing field of AI-based predictive analytics in mental health, addressing the global burden of depression through innovative assessment methodologies. 抑鬱症復發率高，約有40-60%的患者受到影響，加重醫療負擔。傳統評估方法多聚焦於穩定且與個體特質相關的風險因素，較少關注情境變化及動態因素對心理健康所帶來的影響。以往研究曾嘗試透過生態瞬時評估來探討這些高度波動的狀態因子，然而生態瞬時評估問卷往往內容冗長，容易造成參與者疲勞及中途退出，影響研究的可行性。為解決此問題，本研究提出於生態瞬時評估過程中加入文本與語音等多模態輸入，以蒐集更豐富的資料，同時提升實際應用的便利性。 本研究旨在透過先進的生態瞬時評估與人工智能技術，整合瞬時多模態資料，包括參與者情緒描述的語言特徵及其自評情緒項目，以提升預測抑鬱症復發的準確性。本研究提出三項具體假設：(1) 生態瞬時評估期間蒐集的多模態特徵之等級及變化幅度，將與已康復抑鬱症患者一年內的復發情況呈現顯著相關性；(2) 結合多模態特徵與基線特徵建構的人工智能模型，在復發預測上的表現將顯著優於隨機分類器；(3) 此人工智能模型在預測準確度上亦將優於僅以基線特徵為基礎的模型。 本前瞻性隊列研究將招募275名年齡介乎18至65歲、已從抑鬱症發作中康復的華人，進行縱向分析。研究設計分為三個階段：(1) 生態瞬時評估前之基線評估，涵蓋社會人口學特徵、精神病史、健康狀況及心理社會因素；(2) 為期七天的多模態生態瞬時評估，參與者須每日自評情緒並提供口語回應；(3) 為期一年的抑鬱症復發追蹤評估。本研究將運用邏輯斯迴歸分析基線及多模態特徵與抑鬱症復發之相關性，並結合人工智能技術（如隨機森林）及交叉驗證，以建立預測模型。進一步比較以多模態特徵數據訓練的人工智能模型與僅以基線資料訓練模型的預測準確度，並分析其關鍵特徵。 預期成果包括建立一套穩健且高準確度的預測模型，以提升對抑鬱症復發的預測能力與臨床監測成效。藉由在數碼心理健康框架下結合人工智能與語言科學，本研究有望推動以人工智能為核心的心理健康預測分析領域發展，並以創新的評估方法回應全球抑鬱症負擔所帶來的重大挑戰。

24111025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24111025.value: 以環孢素眼藥水作為一線治療「非乾燥症而血清因子陽性的水液缺乏型乾眼症」的多中心隨機對照試驗

24111025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24111025.value: Dry eye disease (DED) affects up to 34% population globally and may lead to corneal blindness, the 4th leading cause of blindness. Aqueous deficient dry eye (ADDE) as a subtype of DED, accounts for 84% of DED patients in our pilot data, with 60% being sero-positive-non-Sjogren’s-Syndrome-ADDE (sero-positive-non-SS-ADDE), i.e. possessing positive serology markers but otherwise healthy without primary or secondary SS, Steven Johnson’s syndrome, mucous membrane pemphigoid or graft versus host disease. It is estimated that 0.23 to 0.90 million population of Hong Kong are sero-positive-non-SS-ADDE. Currently topical Cyclosporin 0.1% cation emulsion (CsA CE) is indicated in moderate to severe DED failing first-line treatment but trial result demonstrated non-statistically significant result in improved Corneal Fluorescein Staining (CFS) >/= 2 at 12 months, except those with CFS baseline score >/=4. As 84% of sero-positive-non-SS-ADDE in our pilot data have CFS >/=4, it is crucial is to explore whether CsA will be effective and safe as first-line treatment in sero-positive-non-SS-ADDE. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CsA CE in treating seropositive-non-SS-ADDE patients. We propose a 2-year prospective, multicenter RCT randomizing 150 seropositive non-SS-ADDE patients to topical preservative free lubricants (Group 1) and receiving topical cyclosporin 0.1% bedtime unpreserved single-dose cationic emulsion eyedrops in addition to topical preservative free lubricants (Group 2). Subjects will receive 4-monthly follow-up for clinical examination, ocular surface assessments, blood taking for CsA level and patient reported outcome measures (PROMs). The objectives are to compare percentage of responders in Oxford grading scheme (>/=score 2 improvement) (primary outcome measure), and to compare the scores of PROMs in 3 broad categories: DED related [ SANDE questionnaires, DEQ-5, OSDI, SPEED and IDEEL], general visual function related [Rasch-scored 28-item Visual Function Questionnaire (VFQ28R)], and Quality-of-life related (i.e. European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions (EQ5D5L)) and Sjögren's International Collaborative Clinical Alliance ocular staining score (SICCA OSS) (secondary outcome measures). We hypothesize that patients randomized to Group 2 will have a higher percentage of responders compared to those in Group 1, with better PROMs across all categories and lower SICCA OSS scores. This study is unique in its comprehensive approach, which includes long-term follow-up, a focus on specific genetic markers, and a large multi-center design, aiming to shift current treatment paradigms and improve patient outcomes. This improve patients’ ocular surface, prevention of blinding complications, enhance QoL, and avoid undesirable opportunity cost to the healthcare system. 乾眼症影響全球人口百分之三十四的人口，嚴重的乾眼症可導致角膜留疤而引致失明，這也是全球第四大致盲原因。香港的初步數據顯示水液缺乏型乾眼症佔乾眼症患者的百分之八十四，而當中百分之六十的人是血清因子陽性但非乾燥症患者。他們擁有血清學陽性標記，但並無原發或繼發性乾燥症。以此推算香港約有二十三萬至九十萬人皆有此狀況。目前，環孢素眼藥水適用於一線治療失敗後的中度至重度乾眼症患者，但以往文獻顯示，環孢素眼藥水只有效對基線角膜螢光素染色分數等於四或以上的乾眼症患者有統計學上顯著的改善。我們初步數據中，百分之八十四的血清因子陽性但非乾燥症患者的其基線角膜螢光素染色分數大四或以上。因此我們有意探討以環孢素眼藥水作為一線治療「非乾燥症而血清因子陽性的水液缺乏型乾眼症」（seropositive non-SS-ADDE）的有效性及安全性。 本研究旨在評估環孢素眼藥水治療「非乾燥症而血清因子陽性的水液缺乏型乾眼症」的療效與安全性。我們計劃進行一項為期兩年的前瞻性多中心隨機臨床對照試驗，將一百五十名血清因子陽性非乾燥症類水液缺乏型乾眼症患者分為兩組：第一組使用無防腐劑人工淚液，第二組使用0.01%環孢素眼藥水以及無防腐劑人工淚液。所有受試者每四個月回院接受臨床檢查、眼表評估、抽血檢測環孢素血液濃度及病人主觀療效問卷。 研究主要目標為比較兩組在基線角膜螢光素染色改善分數兩分或以上人數者所佔百分比。而次要目標為主觀療效問卷分數上的分別：乾眼症相關問卷（SANDE、DEQ-5、OSDI、SPEED），一般視覺功能相關問卷（VFQ28R），及生活品質相關問卷（EQ5D5L）和比較SICCA OSS指數的分別。我們假設第二組在研究主要目標和次要目標比第一組好。 本研究的特點在於其全面性的設計，包含長期追蹤、聚焦於特定遺傳標記，以及大型多中心架構，目標是推動現有治療模式革新並提升患者療效。此策略有助於改善患者眼表健康、預防致盲併發症、提升生活品質，並減少醫療體系不必要的機會成本。

24115625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24115625.value: 結核分枝桿菌細胞游離DNA 於結核性與非結核性胸膜積液之診斷效用

24115625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24115625.value: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant global health burden, with tuberculous pleuritis (TBP) being the most common form of extrapulmonary TB, particularly in China and Hong Kong. Differentiating TBP from other causes of pleural effusion is critical for timely diagnosis and optimal treatment. However, the diagnosis of TBP is challenging due to its paucibacillary nature and infrequent co-existence with parenchymal pulmonary TB. Conventional microbiological and molecular methods using pleural fluid lack sensitivity and specificity, leading to delayed treatment and unnecessary invasive procedures. Pleural fluid biomarkers only indirectly suggest the presence of TB without informing the drug sensitivity pattern. There is a pressing need for a diagnostic test that is highly sensitive and specific, yet minimally invasive, to diagnose TBP confidently. When Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) bacteria die, their DNA is released into the pleural space, forming cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Detecting MTB cfDNA by sequencing technology to diagnose TBP by previous studies was suboptimal due to the low abundance of cfDNA and interference from non-tuberculous mycobacterium (NTM). To overcome this diagnostic gap, our team has developed a whole-genome-based probe sequencing to enrich the MTB cfDNA, coupled with advanced bioinformatics methods to remove the DNA interference from NTM and identify contamination by other microorganisms. This assay enhances the detection of MTB cfDNA and outperforms conventional diagnostic tests. In the development cohort, the sensitivity and specificity of the assay were above 95%, allowing for a confident diagnosis or exclusion of TBP promptly. The new assay should be validated for its robustness and diagnostic performance in diverse clinical settings. Our project involves a prospective collection of pleural fluid samples from TBP and non-TBP cases across multiple countries with varying TB burdens and regions with high NTM burden. Additionally, the assay has the potential to identify genes associated with drug resistance, providing crucial information for personalised treatment plans. There are three aims in this research proposal: 1. To validate the clinical utility of the new targeted MTB cfDNA sequencing assay using a large cohort of pleural fluid samples from diverse geographical regions with different TB burdens and a broad spectrum of pleural diseases 2. To identify clinical and laboratory factors determining the performance of the assay 3. To explore the ability of the assay to capture different TB drug-resistance genes This innovative diagnostic method promises to significantly improve the detection of TBP, leading to less invasive procedures, shorter hospital stays, and timely treatment for patients. 結核病仍然是全球重大的健康負擔，其中結核性胸膜炎是最常見的肺外結核形式，尤以中國與香港最為普遍。鑑別結核性胸膜炎與其他胸膜積液成因，對於及時診斷與最佳治療至關重要。然而，由於結核性胸膜炎菌量極低且不常與肺實質結核同時存在，診斷結核性胸膜炎極具挑戰。傳統微生物學及分子診斷方法使用胸膜液的敏感性與特異性皆不足，導致延誤治療並帶來不必要的侵入性檢查。胸膜液生物標記僅能間接提示結核存在，無法提供抗藥性資訊。因此，急需一項高度敏感、特異，且具低侵入性的診斷工具以準確判斷結核性胸膜炎。 當結核分枝桿菌死亡時，其DNA會釋放至胸膜腔，形成細胞游離DNA。過往研究使用定序技術偵測結核分枝桿菌細胞游離DNA以診斷結核性胸膜炎，但效果不佳，原因包括細胞游離DNA含量極低及非結核分枝桿菌干擾所致。為填補此診斷落差，我們團隊開發了一套全基因體探針定序技術以富集結核分枝桿菌細胞游離DNA，並配合先進的生物資訊方法排除非結核分枝桿菌干擾及識別其他微生物污染。此方法可提升結核分枝桿菌細胞游離DNA的偵測率，表現優於傳統診斷檢測。在開發階段的病例中，此檢測的敏感度與特異度均超過95%，得以快速且準確地診斷或排除結核性胸膜炎。 本研究計劃將驗證此新方法於多種臨床環境下的穩定性與診斷效能，並前瞻性地蒐集來自多個具有不同結核病流行程度的國家（含高非結核分枝桿菌盛行區域）之結核性胸膜炎與非結核性胸膜炎胸膜液樣本。此外，此技術具鑑定抗藥性基因之潛力，可為個人化治療方案提供重要資訊。 本研究計劃的三項目標如下： 1. 驗證新型結核分枝桿菌細胞游離DNA靶向定序技術之臨床效用，涵蓋來自不同地理區域與廣泛胸膜疾病的胸膜液樣本大規模族群 2. 探討影響檢測效能之臨床與實驗室因素 3. 評估此檢測技術對不同結核病抗藥性基因之捕捉能力 此創新診斷方法有望大幅提升結核性胸膜炎檢出率，減少侵入性操作、縮短住院時間，並協助患者及早接受適當治療。

24119525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24119525.value: 腸道擬桿菌對代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病保護作用的研究

24119525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24119525.value: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a leading contributor to liver disease globally, affecting 32.4% of the population. MASLD encompasses a range of liver injuries, with some patients progressing to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), which increases the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, effective pharmacotherapeutic options and non-invasive diagnostic methods for this disease remain elusive. Our recent studies have advanced the understanding the gut-liver axis, highlighting the role of gut dysbiosis in MASLD and MASLD-HCC mouse models, and demonstrating the promise of probiotics in preventing these liver diseases. To comprehensively decipher alterations in gut bacteria during human MASLD progression, we conducted shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples collected from 228 biopsy-confirmed MASLD patients (17 simple steatosis, 138 MASH and 73 MASH-fibrosis patients) and 212 healthy controls, which revealed significant depletion of beneficial bacteria in MASLD patients. Notably, Bacteroides intestinalis emerged as one of the prominently depleted gut bacteria across simple steatosis, MASH, and fibrosis. In preliminary investigations, we isolated B. intestinalis from healthy human stool samples, and demonstrated that B. intestinalis alleviated diet-induced MASLD in mice, as evidenced by improved liver histology and reduced insulin resistance, lipid accumulation and inflammation. Mechanistic explorations suggest that B. intestinalis restored gut barrier function and secreted a beneficial metabolite, 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid (4-HPAA), which is enriched in B. intestinalis conditioned medium, as well as in the portal vein and liver tissues of B. intestinalis-gavaged mice. Furthermore, 4-HPAA inhibited hepatocyte lipid accumulation and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in vitro. Based on these preliminary data, we hypothesize that B. intestinalis represents a novel beneficial bacterium that could serve as a preventive and therapeutic probiotic for MASLD. To validate this, our objectives are to: 1) characterize the probiotic function of B. intestinalis in MASLD progression using germ-free and humanized gnotobiotic mouse models; 2) elucidate the mechanisms underlying the protective effect of B. intestinalis in MASLD through functional metabolites and the molecular interplay between gut microbiota and the host; 3) assess the clinical significance of B. intestinalis in MASLD progression. We will employ a multidisciplinary strategy involving metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, molecular biology, and immunology, utilizing advanced technologies such as multiorgan-on-chip systems and limited proteolysis-mass spectrometry to dissect the role of B. intestinalis in MASLD. This study is expected to provide insights into the protective role of gut bacteria against MASLD via gut-liver axis, facilitating the development of non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies for MASLD. 代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病（MASLD）是全球範圍內最常見的慢性肝病，影響32.4%的人口。MASLD 涵蓋一系列臨床疾病過程，部分患者會進展為代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝炎（MASH），進而增加肝硬化和肝細胞癌（HCC）的發病風險。然而，該疾病的有效藥物治療方法有限，缺乏高敏感特異的非侵入性診斷方法。我們近期的研究揭示了腸道菌群失調通過腸肝軸在MASLD和MASLD-HCC中的作用，並證實益生菌在預防這些肝病方面的潛力。為全面解析人MASLD 進展過程中腸道細菌的變化，我們對 228 例經活檢確診的 MASLD 患者（包括 17 例單純性脂肪肝、138 例 MASH 和 73 例 MASH 相關纖維化患者）以及 212 例健康對照者的糞便樣本進行了宏基因組測序，結果顯示 MASLD 患者體內的有益菌顯著減少。值得注意的是，在單純性脂肪肝、MASH和纖維化階段，腸道擬桿菌（Bacteroides intestinalis）均是顯著減少的腸道細菌之一。在初步研究中，我們從健康人的糞便樣本中分離出了腸道擬桿菌，並證實其可緩解小鼠飲食誘導的MASLD，具體表現為肝臟組織學改善，胰島素抵抗、脂質蓄積和炎症減輕。機制研究表明，腸道擬桿菌可恢復腸道屏障功能，並分泌有益代謝物 4 - 羥基苯乙酸（4-HPAA），該代謝物在腸道擬桿菌的條件培養基中含量豐富，在經腸道擬桿菌灌胃的小鼠門靜脈和肝組織中也有富集。此外，體外實驗顯示 4-HPAA 可抑制肝細胞脂質蓄積和促炎細胞因子的表達。基於這些初步數據，我們推測腸道擬桿菌是一種新型有益菌，有望作為 MASLD 的防治益生菌。 為驗證這一假設，我們的研究目標包括：1)利用無菌小鼠和人源化無菌小鼠模型，明確腸道擬桿菌抑制 MASLD 的作用；2) 通過功能性代謝物以及腸道菌群與宿主間的分子相互作用，闡明腸道擬桿菌對 MASLD 的保護機制；3)評估腸道擬桿菌在 MASLD 進展中的臨床意義。我們將採用多學科策略，結合宏基因組學、代謝組學、轉錄組學、分子生物學和免疫學等領域的技術，並利用器官芯片和限制性蛋白酶解 - 質譜等先進技術，深入剖析腸道擬桿菌在 MASLD 中的作用。本研究有望揭示腸道細菌通過腸-肝軸對 MASLD 的保護作用，為開發 MASLD 的非侵入性診斷生物標誌物和治療策略提供依據。

24123125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24123125.value: 解析奇異變形桿菌在誘發克羅恩病術後復發中的作用機制

24123125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24123125.value: Surgery retains a major strategy in Crohn's disease (CD) management; however, high prevalence of postoperative recurrence (POR) persists as a huge challenge. Despite numerous studies endeavored to delineate intricate mechanisms driving the process, pathogenesis of POR remains elusive. Several longitudinal studies have revealed a striking disparity in gut microbiota between patients with POR and those experiencing postoperative remission, suggested the potential involvement of gut microbiota in POR pathogenesis. Nevertheless, existing studies have predominantly concentrated on elucidating compositional differences. The involvement of key species that triggering colitis reemergence after complete surgical resection, along with their underlying mechanisms in POR progression, remains largely underexplored. Proteus mirabilis, a gram-negative bacterium, has been demonstrated to be implicated in CD progression by our previous work. Two longitudinal studies conducted among Caucasians further discovered its strong association with POR of Crohn’s disease. Notably, similar observations were witnessed among Asian population, wherein high P. mirabilis abundance in preoperative mucosa and mesenteric lymph nodes (MLN) exhibited pronounced associations with poor recurrence-free survival and emerged as an independent predictor for POR. The presence of P. mirabilis in MLN indicates its possible translocation, enabling evasion of elimination by intestinal interventions during surgery and potentially returning to intestine to exert function afterwards. Further considering immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in POR, initial mechanistic explorations from single-cell sequencing of intestinal mucosa from 10-/- mice have revealed that P. mirabilis is capable of modulating aberrant immune regulation by enhancing expression of Trib1 in cDC2 cells, thereby inducing an Th1/Th17 imbalance, ultimately leading colitis reemergence and may resulting in POR. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that P. mirabilis is an essential bacterium that trigger the reappearance of mucosal lesion in postoperative CD patients. To further address our hypothesis, we propose to 1) characterize the role and function of P. mirabilis in POR; 2) explore the intestinal recolonization path of P. mirabilis after luminal elimination; 3) unveil the underlying mechanism by which P. mirabilis trigger POR; 4) evaluate the clinical significance of P. mirabilis in POR. A multidisciplinary approach integrating immunology, transcriptomics and molecular biology will be employed to delineate the function of P. mirabilis in POR utilizing germfree, surgical colitis, gene knockout and humanized mouse models. This proposed study is aspiring to provide novel insights into the role of P. mirabilis in POR and facilitate the early detection and effective therapeutic strategies for purpose of preventing POR in CD.

24123625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24123625.value: 開發小分子工具以調節 NGF/TrkA 信號傳路和骨再生

24123625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24123625.value: The nerve growth factor (NGF)/NGF receptor (NGFR) signalling pathway plays a crucial role in neuronal growth and brain health and has recently been implicated in long bone development. As a skeletal neurotrophin, NGF is involved in maintaining skeletal pain, bone formation, and fracture healing. Bone loss is commonly caused by trauma or injury, and inadequate bone healing can lead to substantial functional impairments, including loss of independence and decreased quality of life. Human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) contribute to skeletal homeostasis by regulating various cytokines, among which NGF was reported to enhance BMSC survival and promote their osteogenic differentiation. In this proposed project, we will focus on NGF-derived peptides because of their low molecular weight, low immunogenicity, high bioactivity, and specific binding to tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TrkA), a high-affinity receptor for NGF. Based on our previous study of a small NGF peptide and its derivatives, we will further develop a small molecular tool to regulate NGF/TrkA signalling and promote bone regeneration. In our preliminary study, we used artificial intelligence to generate NGF-derived peptides and investigated their biological effects on osteogenesis in human BMSCs in vitro. The selected peptide candidates were then delivered to bone defect areas in rat models to determine their role in bone formation, and we found one peptide resulted in rapid bone healing with low immunogenicity in the rat bone defect model. Clinically, fractures caused by falls or trauma are difficult to heal in older patients with osteoporosis, particularly in women. We hypothesise here that NGF/TrkA signalling is a potential bone regenerative pathway and that NGF/TrkA-regulating peptide could enhance the quality of healing in femoral neck fractures in osteoporotic rabbits. In this proposed project, we will (1) further develop this small peptide as a molecular tool for regulating NGF/TrkA signalling and (2) investigate its application in bone regeneration in femoral neck fractures in ovariectomised rabbits. The findings of this proposed project are expected to provide a new molecular tool for understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms of NGF/TrkA signalling and facilitate the development of bone regeneration therapy for critical-size bone defects and future drug and medical device for femoral neck fractures in osteoporotic patients. NGF（神經生長因子）/TrkA（肌動蛋白受體酪氨酸激酶 A）信號傳導是一種潛在的骨再生途徑。本項目旨在探索調控NGF/TrkA 的短肽，及其如何促進骨組織的修復和再生。本項目的研究結果預期將為理解 NGF/TrkA 信號傳路的細胞和分子機制提供一種新的分子工具，並促進針對大面積骨缺損的骨再生療法的發展，以及未來針對骨質疏鬆患者股骨頸骨折的藥物和醫療器械的研發。

24124125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24124125.value: 神經元突觸前蛋白合成在跨大腦半球神經傳遞中的作用

24124125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24124125.value: Memory formation requires the synthesis of new proteins, which are the basic building blocks and function executors. As connections between brain cells, known as synapses, are often located far away from the cell body, it prompted the discovery of on-demand local protein synthesis at synapses. Perplexingly, clinical trials targeting protein-synthesis-related pathways have shown both failures and promises, indicating our understanding is incomplete. Traditionally, postsynaptic protein synthesis has been prominently featured in disease models. But due to low accessibility of presynapses, little is known for presynaptic, or axonal, translation in both health and disease. Recent work uncovered that axonal translation sustains neurotransmission in local cortical circuits, hinting there is an urgent need for axon-inclusive models in therapeutic targeting. To address this, we will elucidate where, when and what synaptic protein synthesis in axons regulates long-range cortical neurotransmission. Using optogenetic activation of presynaptic terminals and whole-cell electrophysiology of postsynaptic cells, we will examine the callosal axons that traverse the corpus callosum, whose activity is closely tied to memory and neurodevelopmental disorders like autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Apart from offering rapid interrogation of neurotransmission, the cross-hemispheric nature of callosal axons provides a premier system for biochemical separation of presynapses for multi-omics analysis. This will generate an atlas that links molecular signatures to the fundamental brain function of cross-hemispheric communication, and from an understudied axon perspective. Leveraging existing initiatives on curating DNA sequences of individuals with ASD, axonally regulated autism risk genes will be revealed with bioinformatics analysis. To sum up, there is much to be discovered about the presynapse and how it is critical for brain functions. This high-throughput research program bridges the gap and will reveal a more comprehensive molecular landscape of the synapse. Ultimately, this will aid existing efforts to alleviate neuropathologies by rational targeting of protein synthesis. 蛋白質是人體的基礎構造元素和功能執行者，而記憶的形成也需要生產新的蛋白質（mRNA基因轉譯）。由於腦細胞之間的連接（稱為突觸）通常遠離細胞體，這促使突觸處可按需求局部制造蛋白質的發現。腦細胞的連接是由突觸前(軸突)和突觸後組成，但我們對突觸前的認識所知甚少。最近的研究發現，軸突基因轉譯可維持局部皮層迴路的神經傳導，這提示了突觸前在治療靶點上的潛力。為了探索突觸前的作用，我們將闡明的軸突蛋白生產在何處、何時以及以何種方式調節長距離皮層神經傳輸。 利用光遺傳激活軸突終端和突觸後細胞的全細胞膜片電生理學，我們將檢查穿越胼胝體的胼胝體軸突，其活動與記憶和神經發育障礙密切相關。胼胝體軸突的跨大腦半球性質除了提供快速的神經傳導檢驗外，還提供了一個理想的系統，可用於多組學分析的突觸前生化分離。這將產生一個圖集，從未被充分研究的軸突角度，將分子特徵與跨半球溝通的大腦功能連結起來。利用現有的DNA 序列，將可透過生物信息學分析揭示由軸突調控的發育障礙風險基因。總括而言，有許多關於軸突及其如何對大腦功能發揮關鍵作用的研究有待發現。這項高通量研究計畫彌補了這方面的不足，並將揭示更全面的突觸分子圖譜。最終，這項研究將通過合理靶向蛋白質合成，助力現有神經病變的緩解研究。

24203525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24203525.value: 多層級互動結構下的智能體决策

24203525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24203525.value: Decision-making for a large number of agents interacting hierarchically has extensive applications across various sectors. The main challenges of hierarchical optimization problems include information asymmetry, robustness and computational intensity. We will address these difficulties in three research problems. In the first research question, we study trust-aware contextual bandit problem where the upper-level policy maker does not have the full information of the lower-level decision maker and we aim to design optimal algorithm to overcome the information asymmetry. In the second research question, we use the recently developed techniques in distributionally robust optimization to study the robustness of principal agent problem under the brownian regime. Thirdly, we construct the mathematical framework of continuous-time finite state stackelberg mean field game when there are infinite number of players in the second level. 對大量層級互動的代理進行決策在各個領域有廣泛的應用。層級優化問題的主要挑戰包括信息不對稱、魯棒性和計算強度。我們將通過三個研究問題來解決這些困難。在第一個研究問題中，我們研究信任感知的多臂賭博機問題，其中上層決策者並未掌握下層決策者的全部信息，我們旨在設計最優算法以克服信息不對稱。在第二個研究問題中，我們利用最近開發的分布魯棒優化技術，研究布朗運動狀態下的委託代理問題的魯棒性。第三，我們構建了連續時間有限狀態斯塔克爾堡均場博弈的數學框架，其中第二層有無限數量的參與者。

24208025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24208025.value: 量子多方計算之（不）可能性探究

24208025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24208025.value: Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) is a cornerstone of modern cryptography, enabling multiple parties to jointly compute a function over their inputs while keeping those inputs private. This capability is increasingly crucial in sectors like healthcare, finance, and decentralized platforms, driven by stringent privacy laws such as GDPR and CCPA. Advancements in quantum computing pose significant threats to classical cryptographic assumptions (e.g., Factoring and Discrete Logarithm), as well as security proof techniques. These developments necessitate the creation of quantum-resistant cryptographic protocols. This proposal addresses a critical gap in our understanding of quantum MPC, which is hindered by quantum phenomena such as the no-cloning theorem and monogamy of entanglement, challenging traditional cryptographic techniques like simulation and rewinding. This project focuses on three pivotal themes in quantum MPC: - Black-Box Constructions: We aim to develop protocols that function without revealing the inner mechanics of their components, analogous to using only the input-output capabilities of a black box. This approach promises efficiency and broad applicability. Our goal is to achieve black-box quantum MPC with (asymptotically) optimal round complexity and, ideally, from minimal assumptions. - Composability: Real-world scenarios (e.g., the Internet) typically involve concurrent execution of multiple protocols, and thus demand composable security. This project seeks to advance our grasp of universally composable (UC) quantum MPC in environments without trusted setups. We aim to explore the possibility of meaningful quantum UC models, such as quantum Angel-based UC or quantum Shielded-Oracle UC, while also developing essential tools like quantum CCA commitments. - Concurrent Quantum Zero-Knowledge (ZK): ZK has always been a cornerstone of cryptography due to its fundamental importance and versatility. Recent research has improved our understanding of quantum ZK in isolated settings, but concurrent settings remain largely unexplored. This aspect is not only crucial on its own but also integral to composable quantum MPC. Besides, the project also plans to explore the relationship between concurrent quantum ZK and quantum parallel repetition theorems, aiming to enrich the theoretical underpinnings of both areas. Expected outcomes include advancements in theoretical knowledge of quantum MPC, particularly in terms of protocol efficiency and composability. These contributions will deepen our understanding of quantum cryptographic protocols, fostering the development of new, more secure technologies capable of withstanding quantum threats. Ultimately, this project aims to bolster the security of our digital infrastructures in the quantum era, ensuring that technological advancements are accompanied by robust cryptographic defenses. 安全多方計算（Secure Multi-Party Computation, MPC）是現代密碼學的基石之一。它允許多方在保持輸入隱私的前提下共同計算某個函數。此一能力在醫療、金融及去中心化平台等領域日益重要，尤其受到如GDPR與CCPA等嚴格隱私法規的推動。 然而，量子計算的進展對傳統密碼學的基礎假設（如質因數分解與離散對數問題）以及安全性證明技術構成了重大威脅。這些挑戰促使我們必須設計具備抗量子能力的密碼協議。本研究計劃針對量子MPC領域中一項關鍵的知識缺口進行探討。該缺口源於量子物理現象（如「不可複製定理」與「糾纏的單一性」），這些現象對傳統密碼技術（如模擬（simulation）與回溯（rewinding）技術）造成衝擊，使其難以直接應用。 本計劃聚焦於量子MPC中的三大核心主題： - 黑箱構造（Black-Box Constructions）：我們目標是設計協議，使其僅依賴元件的輸入輸出行為，而不需了解其內部實作，亦即「黑箱」操作。此方法兼具效率與廣泛適用性。我們希望在最小假設下實現具（漸進）最佳輪次複雜度的黑箱量子MPC。 - 可組合性（Composability）：現實情境（如網際網路）常涉及多個協議的並行執行，因此需保障協議間的可組合安全性。本計劃將深入探討在無信任設置下實現通用可組合（UC）量子MPC的可能性。我們計劃研究具意義的量子UC模型（如基於Angle-Based UC或Shielded-Oracle UC），並發展關鍵工具，如量子CCA承諾機制。 - 並行量子零知識（Concurrent Quantum Zero-Knowledge, ZK）：零知識證明一直是密碼學中的基石技術。儘管近期研究已提升我們對於隔離（stand-alone）環境下量子ZK的理解，但在並行環境中的研究仍付之闕如。此主題本身具有重要性，且與可組合量子MPC密切相關。此外，我們亦將探討並行量子ZK與量子平行重複定理之間的關係，以豐富此兩領域的理論基礎。 預期成果包括對量子MPC理論知識的推進，特別是在協議效率與可組合性方面的突破。這些貢獻將加深我們對量子密碼協議的理解，促進能抵禦量子威脅的新一代安全技術的發展。最終，本計劃期望在量子時代加強我們數位基礎設施的安全性，確保科技發展與堅固的密碼防禦並行。

24208825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24208825.value: 提高氮氧化物與一氧化碳的小時排放估算精度以增強中國南方地區時空源解析可靠性

24208825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24208825.value: Carbon monoxide (CO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) are two major ambient pollutants that have serious adverse health effects on humans and contribute to the formation of secondary pollutants, such as ozone (O3). In addition, CO can indirectly extend the lifetime of methane (CH4), exacerbating global warming. To design control strategies for these pollutants, it is crucial to identify their emission hotspots, understand their ambient concentrations, and quantify the contributions of the various source areas and emission periods to the concentrations. Three-dimensional chemical transport models (3D-CTMs) incorporating source apportionment techniques are effective tools for understanding the spatiotemporal characteristics of air pollutant concentrations and their sources. However, the effectiveness of using these models heavily depends on the accuracy of the emission data used. Currently, most source apportionment studies, including those conducted by the PI, rely on bottom-up emission data generated using established emission factors and diurnal profiles. However, these emission data may contain non-negligible uncertainty. While existing studies have corrected emissions on daily, monthly, and annual bases, few have effectively adjusted hourly emissions, which are needed to understand the spatial patterns of pollutants in cities with diurnally changing meteorological conditions. Furthermore, from the source apportionment perspective, research is lacking on how different emission periods affect NO2 and CO pollution levels. In addressing these gaps, the proposed project will develop a framework that effectively integrates advanced techniques and diverse data sources – including 3D-CTM outputs, geostationary satellite data, hourly data from 3,239 ground observation stations, a data assimilation technique, and a deep learning method – to achieve more accurate hourly emission adjustments. A temporal source apportionment module developed by the PI will be further enhanced to enable the detailed tracking of CO and NO2 sources across space and time. Using the improved emission data and updated method, the project will examine how emissions from specific source areas, such as Hong Kong, and particular emission periods, such as morning rush hours, affect ambient levels on weekdays and weekends. The analysis will focus on episodic conditions across southern China. This region, characterised by rapid urbanisation and industrialisation, still suffers from composite air pollution problems. The results of the project will provide a solid scientific foundation for developing future air quality management policies targeting CO, NO2, and related secondary pollutants in southern China. Furthermore, the novel framework proposed in the project will be adaptable to the correction of emissions in other regions for various research purposes. 一氧化碳（CO）和二氧化氮（NO₂）是兩種主要的大氣污染物，不僅對人體健康產生負面影響，還促進了臭氧（O₃）等二次污染物的形成。此外，CO還能間接延長甲烷（CH₄）在大氣中的存在時間，從而加劇全球變暖。因此，識別其高排放區域、了解其環境濃度，並量化不同來源地和排放時段對其濃度的貢獻，對於制定有效的控制策略至關重要。 結合了源解析技術的三維化學傳輸模型是理解大氣污染物濃度及其來源時空特徵的有效工具。然而，這類模型的應用效果在很大程度上取決於排放數據的準確性。目前，基於模型的源解析研究主要採用由自下而上方法構建的排放數據。然而，由於這類排放數據通常是基於經驗排放因子和日變化曲線生成的，普遍存在較大的不確定性。儘管已有研究對年排放、月排放以及日排放進行了修正，但針對小時排放的相關研究卻相對較少，而精確的小時排放數據對於研究城市污染物空間分布的日變化特徵具有重要意義。此外，目前關於不同排放時段對NO₂和CO污染水平影響的研究也相對缺乏。 為彌補上述研究空白，本項目將建立一個能夠有效整合多種先進技術與多元數據源的方法框架。該框架將結合三維化學傳輸模型輸出、地球同步衛星數據、3,239個地面觀測站的小時數據、資料同化技術以及深度學習方法，以實現更為精確的小時排放校正。申請人開發的源解析模塊也將進一步完善，以實現對CO和NO₂來源進行精細時空解析。 本項目將基於優化後的排放數據和更新的方法，研究特定源區（如香港）以及特定排放時段（如早高峰）對工作日和週末環境污染水準的影響。中國南方地區的重污染事件將會被重點分析。該區域城市化和工業化進程迅速，複合型大氣污染問題依然突出。本項目的研究成果將為未來針對CO、NO₂及相關二次污染物的大氣環境管理政策制定提供堅實的科學基礎。此外，本項目提出的新型方法框架可推廣應用於其他區域的排放校正和相關研究。

24210125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24210125.value: 數據庫管理系統觀察性正確性的自動化推理

24210125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24210125.value: Automated formal methods have enjoyed much success over the years in ensuring the correctness and quality of computer systems. They have been used to infer properties about systems, prove systems’ correctness with respect to a property, and produce systems that are correct by construction. These techniques are especially promising for reasoning about large and complex software systems that are tricky for humans to reason about manually, but because of scalability and expressivity limitations of formal reasoning techniques, their application to such systems often necessitates the development of new algorithms. For example, partial-order reduction techniques have been developed to reduce the state space that model checkers need to consider for concurrent and distributed systems. In this proposal, we focus particularly on enabling automated formal reasoning about black-box database management systems (DBMSs). Client applications rely on DBMSs to store and manage application data in a distributed way; however, DBMS implementations are complex and may exhibit incorrect behaviour. One reason for this complexity stems from DBMSs providing different isolation levels: rather than executing concurrent transactions in a way that corresponds to a sequential execution, DBMSs typically execute transactions in a way that satisfies specific isolation level guarantees about which other transactions’ effects a given transaction may see. Many real-life DBMS implementations have been found to violate the guarantees they claimed to provide, leading to the development of techniques for detecting such violations. Even without considering transactional isolation, fuzzing has uncovered intra-transactional semantic bugs in widely-used DBMSs like PostgreSQL, MySQL, and TiDB. As most DBMSs are not verified and many are closed-source, the proposed research focuses on developing new techniques that allow one to monitor black-box DBMSs for correctness violations and ensure the correct behaviour of client applications. Currently, there exists no work that does this for anything other than violations of isolation level guarantees, and this existing work furthermore makes strong assumptions about what is observable about DBMS behaviour. This proposal aims to develop automated formal techniques that allow clients of DBMSs to (1) verify the absence of any client-observable DBMS implementation bugs with respect to the transaction semantics and DBMS isolation level, (2) understand and constrain conditions under which DBMS functionality is correct, and (3) understand conditions under which DBMS functionality is incorrect. To target actual client workloads, the developed techniques will handle arbitrary transactions, require little logging overhead, scale to large logs, and accommodate incomplete logs. 自動化形式方法多年來在確保計算機系統的正確性與品質方面取得了顯著成就。這些方法可用於推斷系統性質、證明系統相對於某些屬性的正確性，以及生產按規範構建出的正確系統。這些技術對於手動難以分析的大型、複雜軟件系統的正確性推理尤為具有前景。然而，由於形式化推理方法的可擴展性和表達能力有限，應用於此類系統時往往需要開發新的演算法。例如，為減少模型檢查器處理並發及分布式系統時需考慮的狀態空間，業界就發展了偏序規約（partial-order reduction）技術。本項目特別聚焦於實現針對黑箱數據庫管理系統（DBMS）的自動化形式推理。 客戶端應用依賴DBMS以分布式方式存儲和管理數據，然而，DBMS實作十分複雜且可能表現出不正確行為。導致這種複雜性的原因之一是DBMS提供不同的隔離級別：DBMS通常並非以對應於序列化執行的方式執行並發交易，而是以滿足特定隔離級別保證為原則，決定每個交易可見哪些其他交易的影響。許多現實中的DBMS實作被發現違背了其聲稱提供的隔離級別，促使業界開發檢測此類違規行為的技術。即使不考慮交易隔離，有研究透過模糊測試（fuzzing）發現多個主流DBMS（如PostgreSQL、MySQL、TiDB）在單一交易內存在語義錯誤。 由於大多數DBMS並未經過形式化驗證，且多為閉源，本研究提出開發新技術，以便在黑箱環境中監控DBMS的正確性違規行為，保障客戶端應用的正確運作。目前，除了對隔離級別違反的檢測外，尚未有針對黑箱DBMS更普遍正確性的自動化解決方案，且現有方法對可觀察行為有較強的前提假設。本計劃旨在開發自動化形式技術，讓DBMS的客戶端可以：（1）驗證DBMS在交易語義及隔離級別下，是否存在任何客戶端可觀察的實作錯誤；（2）理解並約束DBMS功能正確的條件；以及（3）理解DBMS功能不正確的情況。為處理實際客戶端工作負載，所開發技術將能處理任意交易、要求極低的日誌開銷、可擴展至大型日誌，並處理不完整日誌資料。

24211525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24211525.value: 一種面向以視覺為中心的穩健場景理解的三維感知、標籤高效且多模態的框架

24211525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24211525.value: Scene understanding is vital for enabling machines to interpret and interact with complex environments, making it essential for applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, AR/VR, and security surveillance. Autonomous systems often need to perceive multi-granularity data, understand semantic (e.g., segmentation) and spatial information (e.g., depth) in the scene, and jointly perform various tasks. Cameras are the most widely used sensors because they capture rich visual information at a low cost. However, models relying solely on 2D image data often lack the spatial awareness required to accurately perceive depth and object relationships, making them less robust, especially in dynamic environments. Many systems incorporate 3D sensors like Lidar and Radar to capture structural information of the environment. Nevertheless, annotating 3D data and labeling for all tasks are highly challenging and time-consuming, leading to a scarcity of labeled data while large amounts of unlabeled data remain untapped. We present a forward-thinking project to solve a critical problem that remains untouched: How to develop a robust 3D-aware scene understanding model using limited labeled data across multiple modalities? This is an open research problem that deserves in-depth study. Hong Kong is one of the densest cities in the world for vehicles and pedestrians, with densities 200 and 1,000 times higher than Europe and the U.S., making the above problem more severe and complex. Our goal is to develop a robust visual-centric scene understanding system that adapts efficiently to target environments by addressing several challenges: 1) current architectures are mainly designed for labeled 2D images and do not integrate knowledge from other modalities, lacking 3D-awareness and label-efficiency; 2) there is a lack of training strategy for utilizing multi-modal unlabeled data for enhancing the robustness and 3D-awareness; 3) adapting the model online may suffer from catastrophic forgetting and noisy updates from streaming data. We will solve the above challenges by designing 1) a unified 3D-aware multi-modal learning architecture that is robust and efficient in processing various modalities and tasks; 2) efficient learning strategies that leverage cross-view, cross-task, and cross-modal relations in unlabeled image sequences and other modalities for learning the 3D-aware, task- and modality-agnostic representations, enhancing the robustness and label-efficiency; 3) a stable online adaptation pipeline with a marginal generalization strategy to avoid catastrophic forgetting and a meta-learning and an uncertainty-aware alignment approaches for mitigating noisy updates from unlabeled data. Finally, we will deploy the framework on mobile robots and evaluate it in diverse real-world environments. 場景理解對於讓機器能夠解讀並與複雜環境互動至關重要，因此在自動駕駛、機械人、擴增／虛擬實境（AR/VR）以及保安監控等應用中不可或缺。自主系統往往需要感知多粒度數據，理解場景中的語義資訊（如分割）及空間資訊（如深度），並能同時執行多項任務。攝影機是最廣泛使用的感測器，因為它能以低成本捕捉豐富的視覺資訊。然而，僅依賴二維影像數據的模型往往缺乏準確感知深度及物件關係所需的空間感知能力，使其在動態環境中的穩健性不足。許多系統會結合三維感測器（如光達及雷達）以獲取環境的結構資訊。然而，為三維數據及所有任務進行標註極具挑戰且耗時，導致標註數據稀缺，而大量未標註數據未能被有效利用。 我們提出一個前瞻性的研究項目，以解決一個尚未觸及的關鍵問題：如何在多模態下利用有限標註數據開發具備三維感知能力的穩健場景理解模型？這是一個值得深入探討的開放式研究課題。香港是全球車輛與行人密度最高的城市之一，其密度分別比歐洲及美國高出約二百倍及一千倍，使上述問題在本地情境下更為嚴峻和複雜。 我們的目標是開發一套面向視覺為核心的穩健場景理解系統，能高效地適應目標環境，並解決以下幾項挑戰：1. 現有架構主要為已標註的二維影像而設計，未能整合其他模態的知識，缺乏三維感知能力及標註效率；2. 缺乏可利用多模態未標註數據以提升穩健性及三維感知能力的訓練策略；3. 在線模型適應過程可能因串流數據帶來的災難性遺忘及噪聲更新而受影響。 我們將透過以下方案應對上述挑戰：1. 設計一個統一的三維感知多模態學習架構，能穩健且高效地處理不同模態及任務； 2. 開發高效學習策略，利用未標註影像序列及其他模態中的跨視角、跨任務及跨模態關聯，學習與任務及模態無關的三維感知表示，從而提升穩健性與標註效率； 3. 建立穩定的在線適應流程，透過邊際泛化策略避免災難性遺忘，並採用元學習及不確定性感知的對齊方法以減輕未標註數據帶來的噪聲更新影響。最後，我們將把該框架部署於移動機械人上，並在多樣化的真實環境中進行評估。

24303625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24303625.value: 透過函數型數據分析及擬共形幾何的形態測量及形態發生

24303625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24303625.value: The study of shapes is one of the most fundamental problems in science and medicine. For instance, given two biological or medical structures, it is important to quantify their geometric difference for shape comparison and shape analysis. Also, to understand the developmental process of a structure, a possible way is to track and analyze the size and shape changes of different regions over time. While many prior works have considered the study of shapes, most of them are only applicable to two-dimensional curves. Also, while some other works have studied the mapping problem between surfaces in three dimensions, most require additional assumptions or prescribed conditions on the surface boundaries. Moreover, they can only provide a correspondence between two shapes but not a continuous deformation from one shape to another, making it difficult to quantify and model the geometric variation of the structures in time. In this proposal, we aim to overcome the above-mentioned limitations by developing mathematical frameworks for morphometrics and morphogenesis that combine functional data analysis and quasi-conformal geometry. Specifically, we start by focusing on planar biological and medical shapes. Using the square-root velocity function representation in functional data analysis, we can easily represent the boundary curves of the planar shapes as functions and establish an optimal registration between the boundary curves. We can then search for an optimal quasi-conformal map that satisfies the boundary curve correspondence and some additional mapping criteria, thereby obtaining a mapping between planar shapes that takes both the boundary and the interior shape deformation into consideration. Also, we can naturally define shape metrics based on both the square-root velocity function representation of the boundary curves and the Beltrami coefficient of the quasi-conformal map. Next, we consider more general biological and medical surfaces in three dimensions. Analogous to the two-dimensional case, we can apply the square-root velocity function representation to represent two boundary space curves as functions for obtaining the boundary registration. We can then compute the registration between the two surfaces via a composition of surface parameterizations and a planar quasi-conformal map. Furthermore, we tackle the problem of finding a continuous surface deformation in three dimensions via a combination of functional data analysis and quasi-conformal flows. Altogether, this project will pave a new pathway for the morphometrics and morphogenesis of biological and medical shapes, thereby aiding scientists and medical researchers in different shape analysis applications. 形狀研究是科學和醫學領域最基本的問題之一。例如，給定兩個生物或醫學結構，量化它們的幾何差異對於形狀比較和形狀分析至關重要。此外，為了理解結構的生長過程，一個可行方法是追蹤和分析不同區域隨著時間的大小和形狀變化。雖然許多先前的工作都考慮了對形狀的研究，但大多數工作僅適用於二維上的曲線。而且，雖然其他一些工作也研究了三維中曲面之間的映射問題，但大多數研究都需要對曲面邊界進行額外的假設或給定條件。它們亦只能給出兩個形狀之間的對應關係，而不能給出從一個形狀到另一個形狀的連續變化，這使得量化和模擬結構隨著時間的幾何變化變得困難。在本項目中，我們旨在透過開發結合函數型數據分析和擬共形幾何的形態測量和形態發生數學框架，來克服上述局限性。 具體而言，我們首先考慮平面上的生物和醫學形狀。透過函數型數據分析中的平方根速度函數表示方法，我們可以容易將平面形狀的邊界曲線表示為函數，並在邊界曲線之間建立最佳配準。然後，我們可以尋找一個滿足邊界曲線對應關係和一些附加映射準則的最優擬共形映射，從而獲得同時考慮邊界和內部形狀變化的平面形狀之間的映射。此外，我們還可以基於邊界曲線的平方根速度函數表示方法和擬共形映射的Beltrami系數，自然地定義形狀度量。接下來，我們考慮更一般在三維中的生物和醫學曲面。類似於二維情況，我們可以應用平方根速度函數表示方法將兩條三維中的邊界曲線表示為函數，以獲得邊界配準。然後，我們可以結合曲面參數化和平面擬共形映射來計算兩個曲面之間的配準。此外，我們也可以透過結合函數型數據分析和擬共形流，解決在三維中尋找連續曲面變化的問題。 總括而言，本項目將為生物和醫學形狀的形態測量和形態發生開闢一條新途徑，從而幫助科學家和醫學研究人員進行不同的形狀分析應用。

24304825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24304825.value: 經典波系統中脆弱拓撲的實驗研究

24304825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24304825.value: Since the discovery of the quantum Hall effect in the 1980s, various topological phases, such as topological insulators, Weyl semimetals and topological crystalline insulators, have been discovered experimentally. Along with these discoveries, theoretical approaches to characterize topological phases have been developed. An early example is the K-theory, which leads to the famous ten-fold classification. More recently, advanced theoretical tools, including topological quantum chemistry and symmetry indicators, have been proposed to systematically classify topological phases in all dimensions and crystalline symmetry classes. These theoretical advances not only provide explanations for existing topological materials but also predict many new candidates that have not been synthesized before and even lead to the discovery of new topological phases like fragile topology. With the above-mentioned developments, people may tend to think that we have already had a complete recipe for topological materials. However, in 2021, a new topological phase named delicate topology was proposed, which is not captured by the currently established theory, including topological quantum chemistry and symmetry indicators. Over the last two years, theoretical studies on delicate topology have shown that it is indeed a new topological matter associated with many novel phenomena like returning Thouless pumping and multicellularity. Despite these important theoretical developments, there has been no experimental investigation on delicate topology, mainly due to the high complexity of implementing the models. Classical-wave systems are versatile platforms for realizing topological lattice model in condensed matter theory due to their flexibility, high tunability and being free of spin-orbit interaction. We have previously realized many complicated models using microwave photonic crystals and acoustic crystals, such as 3D topological insulators with a dislocation defect and quantized octupole topological insulators. These models require hoppings with nonzero phases and long-range hoppings, which are also present in most models of delicate topology. In this project, we propose to experimentally study delicate topology in classical-wave systems. The methodology is based on transferring condensed matter theories to classical-wave systems using photonic/phononic crystals and incorporating current photonic/phononic crystal design and fabrication approaches that are well-developed in microwave and audible sound regimes. Specifically, we aim to achieve: (1) Experimentally verify the novel topological phenomena (i.e., returning Thouless pumping and multicellularity) of delicate topology; (2) Explore the boundary effects associated with delicate topology; (3) Explore new wave-manipulation functionalities and potential applications of delicate topology. We expect that the outcomes of this project will contribute to the whole study of topological phases of matter. 自1980年代量子霍爾效應發現以來，各種拓撲相（如拓撲絕緣體、外爾半金屬和拓撲晶體絕緣體）已相繼通過實驗被發現。伴隨這些發現，表徵拓撲相的理論方法也逐步發展完善。早期代表是K理論，其衍生出著名的十重分類法。近年更湧現出包括拓撲量子化學與對稱性指標在內的先進理論工具，可系統性地對所有維度與晶體對稱性類別的拓撲相進行分類。這些理論進展不僅解釋了現有拓撲材料，更預測出許多尚未合成的新候選材料，甚至促成如脆弱拓撲等新型拓撲相的發現。 儘管取得上述進展，人們或許認為拓撲材料研究已臻完備。然而2021年提出的精細拓撲（delicate topology）新相態，卻突破了現有理論框架（含拓撲量子化學與對稱性指標）的解釋範疇。過去兩年的理論研究表明，這種與回返Thouless泵浦、多胞性等新穎現象相關的拓撲態確實屬於全新物態。但由於模型實現難度極高，迄今尚未有實驗研究問世。 經典波系統憑藉其靈活性、高可調性及無自旋軌道相互作用等優勢，成為實現凝聚態理論中拓撲晶格模型的理想平台。我們團隊此前已通過微波光子晶體與聲學晶體實現了多種複雜模型，例如含位錯缺陷的三維拓撲絕緣體與量子化八極拓撲絕緣體。這些模型所需的非零相位跳躍與長程跳躍機制，恰是大多數精細拓撲模型的關鍵特徵。 本項目擬在經典波系統中開展精細拓撲的實驗研究。方法論上將結合光子/聲子晶體理論移植技術，以及微波與可聽聲波段成熟的晶體設計製備工藝。具體目標包括：（1）實驗驗證精細拓撲的新奇現象（回返Thouless泵浦與多胞性）；（2）探究精細拓撲的邊界效應；（3）開發基於精細拓撲的波操縱功能與潛在應用。預期成果將為拓撲物相研究體系作出重要貢獻。

24305125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24305125.value: 由金屬間開殼層—閉殼層相互作用構築的一維異金屬鏈

24305125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24305125.value: Extended one-dimensional (1D) chains of metal atoms have long been a subject of interest in both the fields of chemistry and physics. Since the early 20th century, inorganic chemists have been examining 1D coordination complexes that feature metal-metal (M-M) interactions. These atomic and molecular M-M 1D chain structures can be considered as one of the thinnest quantum nanowires. Ongoing research into the synthesis and analysis of materials with restricted dimensionality is currently paving the way for a new era of nanoscale science and technology. The majority of known 1D metal chains fall into two categories: open-shell mixed-valence oligomers with a covalent M-M bond, like the extensively researched Pt(II, III) mixed-valent platinum blues, and closed-shell 1D stacks organized by non-covalent metallophilic interactions, such as the widely studied Au(I), Rh(I) and Pt(II) M-M chains. The interest in synthesizing 1D metal chains is driven by the distinct and valuable properties, e.g. high anisotropy, high conductivity, Peierls transition, long-range exciton diffusion, large third-order nonlinear optical properties, and so on. However, there are limited reported examples of 1D metal-chain structures supported by open-shell•••closed-shell metal-metal interaction. In literature, there are few reported examples of extended 1D metal wires constructed using open-shell Ru(II, II)/Cu(II) complexes and closed-shell Pt(II) complexes as building blocks. This limited number of examples hinders our understanding of the M-M interaction between an open-shell and a closed-shell metal atom. Furthermore, these 1D M-M chains, constructed from open-shell and closed-shell metal atoms with different charge transfer characteristics among various metal atoms, are expected to yield adjustable electron mobility and magnetic properties. These properties could have potential applications in various molecular electronics. In this proposal, the applicant intends to synthesize a series of new 1D chain structures, which are connected by open-shell dinuclear Ru(II, II) d6 metal atoms and closed-shell Pd(II, II)/Rh(I, I) d8 atoms. These metal chains are composed of the dinuclear subunits of Ru2 which has the open-shell ground-state electronic configurations with two unpaired electrons (S = 1), and the Pd2 or Rh2 which exhibits the closed-shell configuration of S = 0. The objective is to investigate the interaction between an open-shell and a closed-shell metal atom, and its role in driving the self-assembly process of such a M-M chain system. Another objective of this project is to study the magnetic and conductivity properties based on these M-M chain structures. 一維金屬原子鏈長久以來在化學與物理領域備受關注。自二十世紀初起，無機化學家持續研究具有金屬-金屬（M-M）相互作用的一維配位化合物。此類分子級M-M一維鏈結構可視為最纖細的量子奈米線之一。當前針對該類材料的合成與分析研究，正為奈米科技新紀元開闢道路。 已知一維金屬鏈主要分為兩類：其一為具共價M-M鍵的開殼層混合價態化合物，如廣泛研究的鉑(II,III)混合價鉑化合物；其二為通過非共價親金屬作用組裝的閉殼層一維金屬體，如常見的金(I)、銠(I)及鉑(II) M-M鏈。驅動一維金屬鏈合成研究的核心在於其獨特物理性質，例如高度各向異性、優異導電性、派爾斯相變、長程激子擴散、顯著三階非線性光學性質等。然而，現有文獻中由開殼層•••閉殼層金屬間相互作用支撐的一維金屬鏈結構案例極為有限。迄今僅見零星報導以開殼層Ru(II,II)/Cu(II)化合物與閉殼層Pt(II)化合物為構築單元組裝的一維金屬鏈。此類範例的匱乏阻礙我們理解開/閉殼層金屬原子間的M-M相互作用機制。並且由具電荷轉移特性的開/閉殼層金屬原子構築的一維M-M鏈，預期可產生可調控電子遷移率與磁學性質。此等特性在分子電子元件領域具潛在應用價值。 本計畫擬合成一系列新型一維鏈結構，其通過開殼層雙核Ru(II,II) d⁶金屬原子與閉殼層Pd(II,II)/Rh(I,I) d⁸原子進行橋連。此金屬鏈由具開殼層基態電子組態（含兩個未成對電子，S=1）的Ru₂雙核單元，以及展現閉殼層組態（S=0）的Pd₂/Rh₂單元構成。研究目標將探究開/閉殼層金屬原子間相互作用及其驅動M-M鏈自組裝過程的機制，並將基於此M-M鏈結構探究其磁學與導電特性。
