26505825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26505825.value: 市場壓力與企業上市對人工智慧投資的影響

26505825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505825.value: The recent development of AI technologies has led to rapid changes in the future potential of work, occupations and businesses. Early evidence on the impact of AI suggests that the adoption of AI portends large benefits for firms, leading to questions about the factors that drive investment in these technologies. In this study, I examine the role that stock-market listing plays in AI investment. A core debate in the academic literature is the relationship between stock-market listing and long-term investment. Some argue that stock-market listing creates market pressures that leads to reductions in long-term investment. Others argue that the market pressures from capital markets can enable firms to be more adaptive in periods of radical economic change. To address this debate, I examine the question of whether public firms tend to invest more or less in AI technologies. A critical empirical challenge in this research question, is the measurement of AI investment in private firms. Using new data on private firm investment in the human capital of AI, and the proposed data curation of the AI patent dataset for private firms, this study aims to provide novel evidence on the extent of AI investment in private companies. The second goal of this study is to examine the labor market impact of AI investment across public and private firms. One concern expressed by several prominent economists on the development of AI, is that it is too focused on applications that substitute labor. As labor augmenting technologies take a longer time to develop, and require the creation of new tasks and skills, the development of these types of AI technologies could be concentrated in firms that have a longer investment horizon. Thus, in this study, I examine whether private firms, with less market pressures, invest more in AI investment that augments labor. Measuring AI investments that lead to labor substitution or augmentation is also a challenging task. To measure these types of investments, I measure the augmentation and substitution capabilities of patented innovations, through textual analysis techniques. In addition, I also measure the labor substitution and augmentation effects of AI investment through the job and skills demand in online job posting data. Taken together, this proposed study aims to evaluate the relationship between stock-market listing and AI investment. The findings of the study could therefore inform practitioners and regulators who are interested in the factors that drive AI investment in the economy. 近年來，人工智慧技術的迅速發展，正深刻改變著工作形態、職業結構與企業的未來發展潛力。現有早期研究證據顯示，採用人工智慧可為企業帶來可觀的潛在效益，並引發對促使企業投資此類技術之驅動因素的探討。 本研究探討股票市場上市在人工智慧投資中所扮演的角色。學術文獻中的一項核心爭議，在於股票市場上市與長期投資之間的關聯性。一方面，有觀點認為，上市會帶來市場壓力，進而促使企業減少長期投資。另一方面，也有觀點認為，資本市場的壓力能提升企業在劇烈經濟變動中的應變能力。為回應此一爭議，本研究檢驗上市公司在人工智慧技術上的投資傾向，是否高於或低於非上市公司。 在此研究問題中，一項關鍵的實證挑戰是如何衡量私人企業的人工智慧投資。為此，本研究結合私人企業在人工智慧的人力資本投資與專利資料庫，提供其投資程度的全新實證證據。 本研究的第二個目標是比較上市與非上市企業在人工智慧投資對勞動市場影響的差異。多位知名經濟學家憂慮，人工智慧的發展過度集中於替代勞動力的應用。由於勞動力互補型技術的研發通常需較長時間，並伴隨新任務與技能的創造，此類人工智慧技術的開發可能更集中於具備較長投資視野的企業。因此，本研究探討在市場壓力較小的情況下，私人企業是否更傾向於投資於勞動力互補型的人工智慧技術。 為評估這些投資類型，本研究運用文本分析技術，衡量專利創新的勞動力互補與替代能力。此外，本研究也利用職缺資料中的職位與技能需求，衡量人工智慧投資對勞動力替代與互補的影響。 綜合而言，本研究評估股票市場上市與人工智慧投資之間的關係，並為關注經濟中 AI 投資驅動因素的實務界與監管機構提供參考。

26509125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26509125.value: 中国自愿碳市场的碳排放与财务影响

26509125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26509125.value: The voluntary carbon market (VCM) is an essential platform for firms to offset carbon emissions and showcase their commitment to sustainability. However, persistent concerns about the market's credibility arise from potential overstatements of emissions reductions by project developers and firms’ strategic use of offsets to enhance their environmental profiles. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of VCM projects by validating reported emissions reductions and assessing the reliability of carbon offsets using innovative satellite-based verification methods. Leveraging high-resolution satellite data—NASA's OCO-2 for carbon flux measurements and HKUST's high-resolution optical satellite (HKUST-FYBB#1)—alongside detailed hand-collected carbon offset data, I focus on the world's largest carbon market: China. This unique dataset enables a rigorous validation of reported emissions reductions and assessment of offset reliability. The research addresses three key questions: 1) To what extent do VCM project developers overstate emissions reductions? By using novel satellite data, this study quantifies discrepancies between reported and actual emissions reductions across various project types, locations, and certification regimes. This analysis provides the first large-scale evidence on the reliability of carbon claims in the world’s largest carbon market. 2) How do firms balance carbon offset purchases against direct emissions reduction investments? Through examining firm-level offset purchases, emissions data, and investment patterns, this study investigates whether carbon offsets complement or substitute for direct abatement efforts. It explores how firms navigate trade-offs among decarbonization strategies, shedding light on the role of market mechanisms in corporate carbon policy. 3) How efficiently do voluntary carbon markets price fundamental information about offset quality? By linking satellite-verified emissions data with transaction-level pricing data, I examine whether markets discount lower-quality offsets and reward verified reductions. To address these questions, a difference-in-differences design will be employed, leveraging a unique panel dataset combining satellite-verified emissions data, hand-collected offset data, and firm-level financial and disclosure information. This approach develops a causal argument by examining variations in carbon emissions across project locations and time. Cross-sectional analyses will also address heterogeneity across firm characteristics, carbon pricing volatility, registry standards, and monitoring stringency. This research aims to provide robust evidence on VCM reliability and firms’ strategic behavior in carbon reporting. 27102725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27102725.value: DNA double-strand break (DSB) is the most lethal type of DNA damage. There are two major pathways to repair DSBs: Homologous Recombination (HR) and Non-Homologous End Joining (NHEJ). NHEJ operates with fast kinetics and core components (Ku70/80, DNA-PKcs, XRCC4, XLF, and DNA ligase IV/XRCC4 complex) are among the fastest proteins recruited to DSBs. HR operates with slow kinetics, while Mre11/Rad50/NBS1 (MRN) complex, the initiator complex of HR, is one of the fastest proteins recruited to DSBs. Previous literature has demonstrated that MRN interacts with DNA-PK. It is vital to understand relevant molecular mechanisms to better understand human DSB repair regulation. Moreover, we discovered that MRN can directly inhibit NHEJ and further investigation is required. This project aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms of MRN regulation on NHEJ, using a reductionist approach, with two objectives: 1) To understand the MRN and DNA-PK interaction in NHEJ repair control We have recombinantly expressed and purified MRN, Ku70/80, and DNA-PKcs. Our preliminary electrophoretic mobility shift assay has demonstrated the assembly of MRN/DNA-PK complex. We have solved the cryo-EM structures of DNA-PK to understand DNA-PK regulation mechanisms. We have established workflow at our state-of-the-art cryo-EM facility at HKU for subsequent cryo-EM investigation of MRN/DNA-PK complex to see how MRN interacts with DNA-PK. We will be collaborating with Professor Michael Huen from our school on functional investigation to explore how protein-protein interactions between MRN and DNA-PK affect NHEJ. 2) To understand the MRN-dependent regulation on NHEJ in DSB repair control We have recombinantly expressed and purified constructs of all key NHEJ factors. Our preliminary ligation experiments discovered that MRN can directly inhibit NHEJ ligation. Moreover, our ex vivo extraction experiment identified interactions between ATM, the key kinase MRN recruits during DSB repair, and DNA-PKcs, indicating MRN-dependent ATM regulation on NHEJ. We have recombinantly expressed and purified ATM. Further biochemical, biophysical, and functional investigations are required to explore how the interactions along MRN-ATM and Ku70/80-DNA-PKcs axes regulate NHEJ in DSB repair. In general, this project will conduct a comprehensive investigation of the regulation of NHEJ by MRN. It will help us better understand the spatiotemporal orgnisation and the dynamic interplay and versatily of human DSB response and repair. It will also provide a solid base for future large-scale biochemical, biophysical, single-molecule, structural, and functional investigations into human DSB response and repair using highly-purified protein components. 27102925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27102925.value: TMEM16 proteins (A-K) are a family of calcium-activated chloride channels and lipid scramblases involved in important physiological processes ranging from the regulation of membrane excitability to blood coagulation. TMEM16A is the major calcium-activated chloride channel expressed in many cell types, mediating, for example, stimulus-evoked anion secretion in airway epithelial cells and promoting contraction in smooth muscle cells and capillary pericytes. Aberrant activity of TMEM16A has been implicated in hypertension, asthma, and stroke, whereas potentiating TMEM16A might improve epithelial hydration in cystic fibrosis and other mucoobstructive diseases. Despite its therapeutic potential, key steps in the gating cycle and anion conduction of TMEM16A remain to be fully defined and the development of modulators presents a significant challenge. Over the past 9 years, I have been interested in and have made fundamental contributions to our current understanding of the TMEM16 family of channels and scramblases. Here, we aim to expand this knowledge and bridge biophysics with drug design by providing a detailed description of the structural states underlying TMEM16A function at the atomic-scale level. Using a combination of cryo-electron microscopy and electrophysiology, we will decipher the specific molecular rearrangements and features that control channel activation. 27104125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27104125.value: The plasma membrane forms tubular membrane tethers to support cellular functions during cell migration, adhesion, and intercellular material and information exchange. These tethers are characterized by substantial membrane curvature and resilience to environmental mechanical stress. However, the mechanisms that support the maintenance of these membrane tethers are not fully understood. Specifically, Tspan7, a member of this protein family, has been observed to enhance the stability of retraction fibers, which are tubular membrane structures formed behind migrating cells. Tspan7 is able to sense membrane curvature and polymerize into spiral configurations on retraction fibers, representing a novel structural form and functioning as a “Transmembrane Skeleton”. Despite these insights, the atomic organization and regulation of Tspan7 polymerization, as well as its role in stabilizing high membrane curvature, remain unclear. Additionally, further investigation is needed to determine whether the "transmembrane skeletons" formed by Tspan7 polymerization are commonly present in stabilizing various highly curved membrane regions beyond retraction fibers. In this proposed study, we aim to unravel the molecular mechanism of the transmembrane skeleton formed by Tspan7 polymerization that maintains membrane tethers. We will utilize in situ cryo-electron tomography and live cell imaging approaches to investigate the prevalence of Tspan7 enrichment and polymerization in different high-curvature membrane regions within the cellular context. Subsequently, we will characterize the interfaces within the Tspan7 oligomers which are responsible for Tspan7 polymerization using high-resolution single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction and subtomogram averaging. The information derived from these structural analyses will be used to perform structure-guided mutagenesis of Tspan7 for further functional validation. The outcomes of this research will offer valuable insights into the regulatory mechanisms governing Tspan7 polymerization and its impact on membrane curvature generation and/or stabilization. In addition, it will shed light on the role of Tspan7 in preventing membrane tethers from rupturing and enduring mechanical stresses. 細胞膜會形成管狀膜繫結構以支持細胞遷移、黏附和細胞間物質與信息交換過程中的細胞功能。這些膜繫結構具有高膜曲率特徵，並能抵禦環境機械應力。然而，維持這些膜繫結構的分子機制尚未完全闡明。我們近期發現，一類四次跨膜蛋白會在高曲率膜區域高度富集。其中，該蛋白家族成員Tspan7能提高收縮絲（細胞遷移後方形成的管狀膜結構）的穩定性。Tspan7能夠感知膜曲率，並在收縮絲上聚合成螺旋狀結構，形成一種新型的「跨膜骨架」模式。 儘管已有這些發現，Tspan7聚合的分子機理、調控機制及其在穩定高膜曲率中的作用仍不清楚。此外，需要進一步探究Tspan7聚合形成的「跨膜骨架」是否普遍存在於收縮絲以外的其他高曲率膜區域以發揮穩定作用。 本研究計劃揭示Tspan7聚合形成跨膜骨架以維持膜繫結構的分子機制。我們將採用原位冷凍電子斷層成像技術和活細胞成像方法，研究Tspan7在細胞內不同高曲率膜區域的富集與聚合現象。隨後，通過高分辨單顆粒冷凍電鏡重構和子斷層平均技術，我們將解析Tspan7寡聚體中蛋白聚合的相互作用界面。基於這些結構分析，我們將開展Tspan7定點突變實驗，以進行後續功能驗證。本研究結果將為Tspan7聚合的調控機制及其對膜曲率生成/穩定的影響提供重要見解，同時揭示Tspan7在防止膜繫結構斷裂和承受機械應力中的作用。

27105325.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27105325.value: Thyroidectomy is the second most commonly performed elective major surgery in Hong Kong. Total thyroidectomy represents more than 1/3 of these procedures. Post-operative hypoparathyroidism (PH) is a debilitating complication following total thyroidectomy, arising from inadvertent removal or devascularization of the parathyroid glands. PH leads to hypocalcemia, extended hospital stays, re-admissions, impaired quality of life and kidney impairment. From our previous study in Hong Kong and other population-wide series, permanent PH rates could be as high as 11%, and transient PH rates being 30-48%, posing substantial burden on healthcare systems. Even in experienced hands, inadvertent parathyroidectomy may occur in 25% of surgery. Near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) technology has emerged to assist the identification and preservation of parathyroid glands during surgery. Parathyroid glands emit NIRAF at 800-900nm when exposed to light at 700-785nm, distinguishing them from surrounding tissues. This study investigates the probe-based NIRAF device, PTeye™, which emits laser and receives NIR real-time, thereby detecting parathyroid glands by simple touch with a probe. It allows quick parathyroid identification with minimal interruption to surgery. Several studies report high sensitivity (97-98%) and accuracy (94-96%) of PTeye™ in parathyroid identification. However, whether its use actually reduces PH remains unknown. In this regard, we devised a standardized protocol to use PTeye™ for parathyroid identification at the early stage of surgery, in order to avoid devascularization or inadvertent removal of the parathyroids. Our preliminary series comparing conventional surgery versus PTeye™-assisted surgery (PTE) showed PTE led to lower PH rates (10% vs 30%) and allowed earlier identification of 33% of parathyroid glands. Based on these results, we propose the first prospective, open-labelled, randomized controlled trial to evaluate whether PTeye™ can reduce PH. The study will enroll consecutive patients undergoing total thyroidectomy in the endocrine surgery unit at the Hong Kong West Cluster, randomizing them into receiving conventional surgery versus PTeye™-assisted surgery. The primary outcome is the rate of significant post-operative hypoparathyroidism. Other key outcomes include parathyroid hormone and calcium kinetics, and related impact on health, quality of life and health costs by reduction of PH. We hypothesize that PTeye™ use will lead to lower PH rates, better preservation of parathyroid function, and hence improved quality of life, potentially reducing health costs. This study will provide critical evidence on the effectiveness of PTeye™, potentially transforming surgical practices and improving patient outcomes in thyroid surgery. 甲狀腺切除術是常見的手術,其中全甲狀腺切除術佔超過三分之一。副甲狀腺功能低下症（PH）是一種在全甲狀腺切除術可能出現的併發症，其原因為副甲狀腺被意外切除或其血流供應受損所致。PH會導致低血鈣、延長住院時間、增加再入院率、降低生活質素及腎功能受損。根據我們在香港的大數據·研究，永久性PH的發生率可高達11%，而暫時性PH的發生率為30-48%。因此PH可對醫療系統構成重大影響。即使由經驗豐富的外科醫生操刀，副甲狀腺被意外切除的比例也可達25%。 近紅外自體螢光（NIRAF）技術近年發展，用以協助手術中識別及保護副甲狀腺。當副甲狀腺暴露於若干納米波長的光線時，會發出自體螢光，從而與周圍組織區分出來。本研究探討以探頭設計的NIRAF裝置PTeye™，該裝置可發射雷射並即時接收近紅外線訊號，只需以探頭輕觸組織即可偵測副甲狀腺，能在不影響手術流程下迅速識別副甲狀腺。有多項研究顯示PTeye™在副甲狀腺識別方面具有高靈敏度（97-98%）及高準確度（94-96%）。然而，該技術是否真正能降低PH的發生率仍屬未知。就此，我們制定了一套標準化的流程，在手術初期階段利用PTeye™識別副甲狀腺，以避免其血流受損或被意外切除。我們初步的數據顯示，與傳統手術相比，採用PTeye™輔助手術可降低PH發生率（10%對30%），並能更早識別33%的副甲狀腺。 基於以上結果，我們會進行全球首個前瞻性、開放標籤性、隨機對照研究，以評估PTeye™是否能降低PH發生率。本研究將於香港大學內分泌外科招募所有合適的，接受全甲狀腺切除術的患者，並將他們隨機分配至傳統手術組或PTeye™輔助手術組。主要研究結果為術後顯著副甲狀腺功能低下症的發生率。其他重要結果包括副甲狀腺激素及鈣的動態變化，以及PH減少對健康、生活質素及醫療成本的影響。 我們假設使用PTeye™能降低PH的發生率，更好地保護副甲狀腺功能，從而提升病人生活質素，並有潛力減少醫療開支。本研究將提供有關PTeye™效能的關鍵證據，並探討其改善醫療質素的潛力。

27121825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27121825.value: 核小體在轉錄過程中對RNA m6A修飾的調控

27121825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27121825.value: The most prevalent RNA modification, m6A, is an “epi-transcriptomic” marker that regulates gene expression. Its important functions have been revealed in RNA metabolism, protein translation, and even “epigenetic” regulations in various physiological and pathological processes. The deposition of m6A is highly selective, and aberrant m6A modifications lead to various diseases. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the regulation mechanism(s) of m6A deposition. m6A is installed by the “writer” complex and happens on chromatin during RNA transcription. Nucleosomes, as the basic units of chromatin, were reported to play key roles in guiding this process. Through direct interactions, nucleosomes recruit the m6A writer complex through the “epigenetic” marker H3K36me3 to deliver the modification. The mechanism of how this recruitment promotes m6A specificity is still missing. Interestingly, our preliminary data showed that the nucleosome-“writer” interaction inhibits non-specific writings on “free” RNAs, suggesting that the nucleosome regulates the selection of RNA substrates during m6A deposition. Since “chromatin-associated” (ca)RNA and “transcription” are two required features for the specific m6A installation, we hypothesize that the nucleosomes promote the m6A installation by: 1) providing the “space proximity” between the writer and caRNA; and 2) coordinating with the transcription elongation complex to deliver RNA to the writer. To determine the regulatory roles of the nucleosome in m6A installation, we plan to perform the in vitro m6A assay on both caRNA and transcribing RNA with nucleosomes. Molecular details will be revealed by obtaining optimal m6A writing activity. To further understand the mechanism, we will biochemically characterize the nucleosome-“m6A writer” interactions by integrating the Hydrogen-Deuterium Exhange Mass Spectrometry (HDX-MS) and molecular dynamics simulation. Functional studies are proposed to further validate the interaction through site-directed mutagenesis. Lastly, we plan to solve the structures of key complexes involved in m6A writing by cryo-EM. The structural details will provide the mechanisms on how the nucleosome recruits the m6A writer complex, and how the recruitment determines the writing specificity. Cross-talks between “epigenetics” and “epi-transcriptomics” have been an important topic in gene expression and regulation, while the mechanisms at molecular level are largely missing. Our proposed work will fill the knowledge cap on one of these cross-talks. Since m6A is an important therapeutic target for diseases such as cancers, our work could also facilitate new drug discovery. m6A 作為最普遍的 RNA 修飾，是一種調控基因表現的「表觀轉錄組」標記。在各種生理和病理過程中，m6A修飾對RNA 代謝、蛋白質轉譯，乃至「表觀遺傳」調控方面具有關鍵功能。m6A 的安裝具有高度選擇性，異常的 m6A 修飾會導致多種疾病。因此，理解 m6A 安裝的調控機制至關重要。 m6A 由「書寫器」複合體安裝，並發生在 RNA 轉錄期間的染色質上。核小體作為染色質的基本單元，據報導在指導這一過程中起關鍵作用。通過直接相互作用，核小體利用「表觀遺傳」標記 H3K36me3 招募 m6A 書寫器複合體，從而傳遞該修飾。然而，這種招募如何促進 m6A 特異性的機制仍不清楚。有趣的是，我們的初步數據顯示，核小體與「書寫器」的相互作用抑制了對「游離」RNA 的非特異性「書寫」。這表明在 m6A 安裝過程中，核小體不僅調控修飾的時空定位，更精準篩選 RNA 底物以確保修飾特異性。

27122225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27122225.value: 飲食糖限制對果蠅慢性Jak/STAT活化引起的器官功能障礙的挽救作用

27122225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27122225.value: Injury induces local and temporal inflammation, promoting recovery from tissue damage. In contrast, prolonged and systemic inflammation, frequently observed in aging and cancer, can disrupt distant organs. In particular, chronic inflammatory Jak/STAT signaling in these pathologic conditions is strongly associated with defects in distant organs. However, the mechanisms of how chronic Jak/STAT signaling disrupts distant organs are largely unclear. Because of this knowledge gap, the treatments that directly target inflammatory organ defects are also limited. An increasing number of studies have reported that various types of dietary restriction can alleviate symptoms of chronic diseases, but the underlying mechanisms are still vague. Because diet can impact multiple physiological processes via complex crosstalk between organs, relatively simple model organisms, such as Drosophila, will be advantageous to decoding the underlying mechanisms. Moreover, Drosophila has conserved signaling pathways involved in inflammation, aging, and cancer; hence, the discovery using Drosophila models can impact mammals and humans. Recently, we successfully established simple but powerful Drosophila tumor models exhibiting chronic Jak/STAT signaling (PNAS, 2024). As a wound that never heals, a tumor drives systemic Jak/STAT-dependent inflammation, causing severe defects of renal tubules, which are functionally equivalent to the mammalian kidney. Using our model as a platform, we performed a pilot screening to investigate the effect of diet on managing chronic inflammation. Surprisingly, our preliminary data showed that dietary sugar, not amino acids or fat, promoted inflammatory renal failure, and dietary sugar restriction for only 15 hours dramatically rescued renal defects. How does restriction of dietary sugar rescue inflammatory renal dysfunction within a day? We will leverage our established Drosophila model to decipher the fundamental effects of dietary sugar restriction on rescuing organ defects caused by chronic Jak/STAT signaling. Our preliminary data suggest that dietary sugar restriction is beneficial for the original cells of renal tubules, whereas it eliminates newly produced abnormal cells in renal tubules. Objective 1 will elucidate (i) how dietary sugar restriction protects the renal tubules from chronic Jak/STAT signaling and (ii) how dietary sugar restriction rescues renal dysfunction by removing the abnormal cells in the renal tubules under chronic inflammation. Objective 2 will determine the different molecular characteristics between the original and newly produced abnormal cells in the inflammatory renal tubules, and we will characterize confounding factors contributing to vulnerability to dietary sugar restriction. Our research will discover the fundamental biology of how a specific nutrient, sugar, regulates organ homeostasis under chronic inflammation. 損傷會引發局部和暫時的炎症，促進組織損傷的恢復。相反，在老化和癌症中常見的長期全身性發炎會破壞遠處器官。尤其值得一提的是，在這些病理狀況下，慢性發炎性Jak/STAT訊號與遠端器官的缺陷密切相關。然而，慢性Jak/STAT訊號如何破壞遠端器官的機制尚不清楚。由於存在這項知識缺口，直接針對發炎性器官缺陷的治療方法也十分有限。 越來越多的研究報告表明，各種飲食限制可以緩解慢性疾病的症狀，但其潛在機制仍不清楚。由於飲食可以透過器官間複雜的相互作用影響多種生理過程，因此，像果蠅這樣相對簡單的模型生物將有助於揭示其潛在機制。此外，果蠅保留了參與發炎、老化和癌症的訊號通路；因此，利用果蠅模型所進行的研究成果可以應用於哺乳動物和人類。最近，我們成功建立了簡單但有效的果蠅腫瘤模型，該模型表現出慢性Jak/STAT訊號傳導（PNAS，2024）。腫瘤如同永不癒合的傷口，會引發全身性Jak/STAT依賴性炎症，導致腎小管（其功能與哺乳動物的腎臟相當）嚴重缺陷。我們以此模型為平台，進行了先導篩選，以探討飲食對慢性發炎管理的影響。令人驚訝的是，我們的初步數據顯示，膳食糖（而非胺基酸或脂肪）會促進發炎性腎衰竭，而僅限制飲食糖攝取15小時就能顯著挽救腎臟缺陷。限制膳食糖攝取如何在一天之內挽救發炎性腎功能障礙呢？ 我們將利用已建立的果蠅模型，闡明飲食糖限制在挽救慢性Jak/STAT訊號傳導引起的器官缺陷方面的基本作用。我們的初步數據表明，飲食糖限制有利於腎小管的原始細胞，同時清除了腎小管中新生的異常細胞。目標1將闡明(i)飲食糖限制如何保護腎小管免受慢性Jak/STAT信號傳導的影響，以及(ii)飲食糖限制如何透過清除慢性發炎狀態下腎小管中的異常細胞來挽救腎功能障礙。目標2將確定發炎狀態下腎小管中原始異常細胞和新生異常細胞之間的差異分子特徵，並分析導致飲食糖限制易感性的混雜因素。我們的研究將揭示糖這種特定營養物質如何在慢性發炎狀態下調節器官穩態的基礎生物學原理。

27125025.value: 闡明DAP10在小鼠澱粉樣β蛋白積累模型中對小膠質細胞的作用 闡明DAP10在小鼠澱粉樣β蛋白積累模型中對小膠質細胞的作用 闡明DAP10在小鼠澱粉樣β蛋白積累模型中對小膠質細胞的作用

27125025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27125025.value: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, mainly affecting older people. As the global population continues to age, AD poses greater burdens on society. Currently there are few approved medicines. To identify effective therapeutic strategies, molecular and cellular alterations occurring during AD progression need to be characterized comprehensively. Microglia, as the brain resident macrophages, are widely studied in AD and shown to play multifaceted roles in which they not only respond to AD pathology but also modulate disease course. During early stage of amyloid-beta (Aβ) deposition, one major hallmark pathologies, microglia cluster around the Aβ plaques restraining their growth and prevent disease progression. However, continuous and excessive activation along with production of inflammatory mediators accelerate disease course upon ageing. Therefore, manipulating the functions of microglia is a promising approach for AD treatment. Recent studies exploring phenotypic changes in plaque-associated microglia have identified unique transcriptional signatures related to reactive microglia. Strikingly, our studies demonstrated that Trem2 (triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2), one of the high-risk genes for sporadic AD, is required for microglia activation, and established TREM2 as a valid target for AD treatment (Wang and Mustafa et al. JEM 2020; Ellwanger and Wang et al. PNAS 2021). Additionally, by using conditional gene knockout mouse models of AD, we showed, for the first time, that TREM2 activates microglia through DAP12-SYK-dependent and DAP12-SYK-independent/DAP10-dependent pathways (Wang et al. Cell 2022). Intriguingly, our unpublished data from single-cell RNA-sequencing further showed that, contrary to impaired microglia activation observed in DAP12 loss-of-function or microglial SYK-deficient 5XFAD mice, DAP10-deficient 5XFAD mice exhibited increased reactive microglia subpopulation compared to littermate control. These findings suggest that interrupting DAP10-dependent pathways enhances microglia activation in AD. However, exact functions of DAP10-dependent pathways in microglia in vivo require further investigation. The overarching aim of our research proposed here is to investigate how DAP10-signaling impacts microglial response to AD pathology. In this proposal, we will use DAP10-deficient 5XFAD mouse model to answer three questions: 1) how does DAP10 deficiency impact the phenotype and function of microglia, as well as AD progression? 2) what is the underlying mechanism by which DAP10 regulates microglial activation? 3) whether targeting microglial DAP10 can influence the AD pathology. Overall, this project will provide novel insights on the role of DAP10 in TREM2-induced microglia activation in amyloid pathology, which could lead to targeted treatment such as DAP10-mediated immunotherapy for AD. 阿爾茨海默病（AD）是導致老年人癡呆的主要原因，隨著全球人口老齡化加劇，AD對社會的負擔日益加重。目前，針對AD的獲批藥物數量有限。為了尋找更有效的治療策略，我們亟需深入了解AD進展過程中分子及細胞層面的變化。小膠質細胞是大腦中的常駐巨噬細胞，近年來在AD研究中備受關註。研究發現，小膠質細胞不僅對AD病理變化做出應答，還能影響疾病的發展過程。在澱粉樣β蛋白（Aβ）沈積的早期階段，小膠質細胞會聚集在Aβ斑塊周圍，限製其生長，從而延緩疾病進展。然而，隨著年齡增長，小膠質細胞持續過度活化及炎癥因子的產生，反而會加速疾病惡化。因此，調控小膠質細胞功能已成為AD治療的重要研究方向。 近年來，針對Aβ斑塊相關小膠質細胞表型變化的研究揭示了其獨特的轉錄特征。我們團隊的研究發現，Trem2（一種在髓系細胞上表達的受體，也是散發型AD的高風險基因之一）是小膠質細胞激活所必需的，並證實TREM2是AD治療的潛在靶點（Wang and Mustafa等，JEM 2020；Ellwanger and Wang等，PNAS 2021）。此外，我們通過構建條件性基因敲除AD小鼠模型，首次發現TREM2可通過DAP12-SYK依賴和DAP12-SYK非依賴/DAP10依賴兩條信號通路激活小膠質細胞（Wang等，Cell 2022）。有趣的是，我們基於單細胞RNA測序獲得的最新數據（尚未發表）進一步顯示，與DAP12功能缺失或小膠質細胞SYK缺失的5XFAD小鼠中小膠質細胞激活受損不同，DAP10缺失的5XFAD小鼠表現出更多的反應性小膠質細胞亞群。這表明，阻斷DAP10相關通路反而能增強AD模型中小膠質細胞的激活。但DAP10依賴通路在體內小膠質細胞中的具體功能仍有待進一步探索。 本課題旨在系統研究DAP10信號通路對小膠質細胞應對AD病理的調控作用。我們將利用DAP10缺失的5XFAD小鼠模型，重點回答以下三個問題：1）DAP10缺失如何影響小膠質細胞的表型、功能及AD的進展？2）DAP10調控小膠質細胞激活的分子機製是什麽？3）靶向小膠質細胞中的DAP10能否改善AD病理？本項目的開展將有助於深入理解DAP10在TREM2介導的小膠質細胞激活及澱粉樣蛋白病理中的作用機製，為發展以DAP10為靶點的AD免疫治療策略提供理論依據。

27127125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27127125.value: 預防種植體周圍炎的智能活性氧響應抗菌肽塗層開發實現可控殺菌與活性氧清除

27127125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27127125.value: In light of an ageing population, the demand for dental implants is escalating. However, the longevity of such implants is frequently compromised by peri-implantitis, a condition chiefly induced by bacterial infections. Current antibacterial interventions, predominantly reliant on implant coatings, often grapple with problems such as unregulated or burst release, resulting in restricted efficacy durations or unwarranted overdoses that may foster bacterial resistance. Additionally, current single-function antibacterial coatings often fail to effectively prevent peri-implantitis, given that bacterial infections can also induce tissue damage via the secretion of reactive oxygen species (ROS) by host cells. Hence, a coating system that combines multifunctionality with controlled release is imperative. The central aim of this proposal is to develop an intelligent coating system engineered to modulate the discharge of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) in correlation with ROS levels. Peri-implantitis is significantly exacerbated by excessive ROS production. By utilizing this ROS overproduction as a biological signal, we propose to conjugate an AMP, GL13K, to the titanium surface via a ROS-responsive thioketal linker. The hypothesis is that under normal or low infection conditions, the AMP coating will eradicate bacteria upon contact, thereby inhibiting biofilm formation. However, during an infection, the system is programmed to react to heightened ROS levels by releasing AMPs to kill the bacteria in the infected tissue. The novelty of this project is threefold. Firstly, we propose a smart control of AMP release based on a sensitive ROS-responsive linker, which directly attaches the AMP to the titanium surface. Secondly, we are combining contact and distance killing strategies, contingent on the ROS levels in the microenvironment. Lastly, the single coating brings together antibacterial, anti-oxidative, and anti-inflammatory properties. The primary research hurdles include preserving the activities of the AMP GL13K during synthesis and controlling the release of GL13K in response to elevated ROS levels. My previous work on the application of GL13K as coatings on various dental materials and the design of various responsive drug delivery systems forms the foundation for this project. Leveraging this experience, I have devised a synthesis route using mild reactions and preliminarily verified the successful coating and its functions. I will further characterize the coated surfaces and evaluate its antibacterial, anti-oxidative, and anti-inflammatory effects in vitro and in vivo. Once successfully developed, this innovative smart coating system will offer a strategic solution to prevent peri-implantitis. It also presents a new pathway for addressing infection-related challenges in other implant procedures. 隨著人口高齡化，牙科植體需求持續攀升。然而植體長期穩定性常因種植體周圍炎而受損，此病症主要由細菌感染引發。現行抗菌策略雖多仰賴植體塗層，卻普遍面臨藥物釋放失控或突釋等問題，導致有效作用時間受限，或產生可能誘發細菌抗藥性的過量藥物暴露。更關鍵的是，現有單一抗菌功能塗層往往難以有效預防種植體周圍炎，因細菌感染尚可透過宿主細胞分泌活性氧(ROS)引發組織損傷。因此，亟需開發兼具多重功能與可控釋放特性的塗層系統。 本計畫核心目標在於研發智能塗層系統，實現抗菌胜肽(AMPs)釋放量與ROS濃度動態調控。過量ROS生成會加劇種植體周圍炎發展，本研究擬利用此生物訊號，透過ROS響應型硫酮鍵結劑將抗菌胜肽GL13K共價接枝於鈦表面。理論上，在正常或低感染狀態下，塗層可透過接觸殺菌抑制生物膜形成；當感染發生時，系統能感應微環境中升高的ROS濃度，觸發抗菌胜肽釋放以殺滅感染組織中的病原菌。 本計畫創新性體現於三方面：首創基於高靈敏度ROS響應型鍵結劑的智能控釋系統，實現抗菌胜肽與鈦表面的直接鍵結；其次整合接觸殺菌與距離殺菌雙重機制，作用模式依微環境ROS濃度動態切換；最終透過單一塗層整合抗菌、抗氧化、抗發炎三重功能。 主要研究挑戰在於合成過程中維持GL13K生物活性，以及實現ROS濃度依賴性可控釋放。前期研究已建立GL13K在多種牙科材料的塗層應用經驗，並完成多種響應型藥物遞送系統設計，為本計畫奠定基礎。基於此，本人已規劃溫和反應合成路徑，並初步驗證塗層成功製備與基礎功能。後續將深入表徵塗層表面特性，並通過體外與體內實驗全面評估其抗菌、抗氧化及抗發炎效能。 此智能塗層系統若成功開發，將為預防種植體周圍炎、延長植體使用壽命提供創新解決方案。

27202625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27202625.value: 多重熒光成像的基礎模型：方法與應用

27202625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202625.value: Spatial biology is a powerful tool for determining the presence and localization of biomarker molecules in tissues. Multiplexed imaging, a representative modality of spatial biology, provides sub-cellular resolution mapping of proteins and/or RNA molecules in their native tissue contexts. These experiments hold immense potential in deciphering disease mechanisms through revealing and contrasting the spatial arrangements of molecules and cells. Recent studies in spatial biology have led to new insights in diseases including cancer, autoimmune disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions. Despite substantial progress, existing computational tools for multiplexed imaging remain limited. Most current approaches are cell-centric and do not account for the diverse spatial distributions of the proteome/transcriptome, where valuable disease-relevant signatures can be extracted. Fully harnessing the high-dimensional spatial information for biological discoveries remains a major challenge. Foundation models, a class of methods characterized by large-scale self-supervised learning, hold great promise in upleveling the current computational analysis capabilities in spatial biology. Through learning data structures and interdependencies from massive amounts of unlabeled data, these models can adapt to a wide variety of downstream tasks, revolutionizing conventional modeling approaches in computer vision, natural language processing, protein sequences, computational pathology, and more. Inspired by their success and versatility, we aim to integrate the workflow of foundation models into multiplexed imaging. As existing foundation models are unsuitable for multiplexed imaging due to their distinct data structures and complex dimensionalities, we aim to develop and train a new set of foundation models tailored to multiplexed imaging data in this project. We will collect and compile comprehensive and diverse multiplexed imaging data across major human tissue types and disease conditions. Novel model architectures and self-supervised learning strategies will be proposed and optimized for this specific data. We will train foundation models and validate them on a wide variety of downstream tasks. We anticipate strong adaptability and improved performance from these trained foundation models on tasks such as tissue type and disease state classifications, prognosis and response to therapy predictions, patient retrieval, as well as other innovative applications. Foundation models for multiplexed imaging will advance the analytical capabilities of spatial biology and accelerate biomedical discoveries from high-dimensional data. 空間生物學包含了一系列用於發現及定位組織中生物標誌物分子的強大工具。多重熒光成像作為空間生物學的一種主要實驗方法，能夠在組織背景中以亞細胞分辨率繪製蛋白質和/或RNA分子的分佈。這些數據在揭示疾病機制方面具有巨大潛力，通過展示和對比分子與細胞的空間排列，為科學研究提供新視角。近年來，空間生物學的研究在癌症、自身免疫性疾病以及神經退化性疾病等領域取得了新的見解。然而，現有的多重成像計算工具仍然有限。目前大多數方法以細胞為核心，未能充分考慮蛋白組/轉錄組的多樣空間分佈，而這些分佈中隱含著可提取的與疾病相關的重要特徵。充分利用高維空間信息進行生物學發現仍然是一大挑戰。 基礎模型是一類經大規模自監督學習後可以被廣泛用於多樣下游任務的人工智能方法，這類方法在提升空間生物學的計算分析能力方面也具有巨大潛力。在諸如計算機視覺、自然語言處理、蛋白質序列分析、計算病理學等多個領域中，基礎模型方法通過從海量未標註數據中學習數據的結構和關係，獲得了相較傳統建模方法更加優異的適應性及下游任務上的表現。 受這些領域成功經驗的啟發，我們旨在將基礎模型的方法應用到多重熒光成像中。現有的基礎模型不能直接應用到多重成像的數據結構上，我們計劃開發並訓練一套專門針對多重成像數據的新型基礎模型。 我們將收集並整理涵蓋主要人體組織類型和疾病狀況的全面且多樣的多重熒光成像數據，並針對這些數據提出創新的模型架構及自監督學習策略。我們將用這些數據進行基礎模型的自監督學習，並在多種下游任務中對其進行驗證。我們預期這些基礎模型在組織類型和疾病狀態分類、預後和治療反應預測、患者檢索以及其他創新應用方面將展現出強大的適應能力和更好的性能。專為多重成像設計的基礎模型將提升空間生物學的分析能力，並加速從高維數據中進行生物醫學發現的進程。

27202725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27202725.value: 基於影響界的無向概率圖模型的抽樣與近似計數

27202725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202725.value: Undirected graphical models, also known as Markov random fields, are a powerful tool for succinctly representing high-dimensional probability distributions, where multiple random variables interact locally. In these models, each variable is represented by a vertex, and the interactions between variables are depicted as edges in a graph. In statistical physics, graphical models (e.g., spin systems) are used to explain the behavior of magnetic systems, where the variables represent the spin of particles, and the edges model the interactions between neighboring particles. In computer vision, images are often modeled as graphical models, with pixels as variables and edges representing the relationships between adjacent pixels. In machine learning, graphical models are widely used to capture statistical dependencies in high-dimensional data. This project will study two fundamental computational tasks associated with graphical models: (1) sampling, which involves drawing random samples from the high-dimensional distribution, and (2) approximate counting, which estimates the size of the sample space. Many recent advances in sampling and counting algorithms have been achieved by analyzing the influences between random variables. Intuitively, influence measures the correlation between random variables in a joint distribution. For instance, in a product distribution, where all variables are independent, the influences are zero, making both sampling and counting straightforward. In a graphical model, all variables are correlated with each other. However, if we can bound the influences between variables, can we still develop fast algorithms? The main objective of this project is to develop efficient algorithms through the use of influence bounds. For sampling, most existing algorithms primarily target sparse graphical models, while algorithms for dense graphical models remain limited. This project aims to address this gap by leveraging influence bounds in Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms. For approximate counting, we will explore both randomized and deterministic algorithms. The randomized algorithms can be derived from the counting-to-sampling reduction, and we aim to develop more efficient reduction algorithms using influence bounds. In the case of deterministic algorithms, previous results often impose very strict conditions on influence bounds, resulting in performance that lags behind randomized methods. This project seeks to bridge that gap by developing improved algorithmic tools that more effectively connect influence bounds to deterministic counting. Since influence bounds lead to efficient algorithms, the second objective is to establish the necessary influence bounds for specific graphical models. We will explore various techniques to achieve this, including coupling analysis, information percolation, and recursion of marginal distributions. 無向概率圖模型（又稱馬尔可夫隨機場）是一種利用隨機變量的局部相互作用表示高維機率分佈的工具。它能以很少的數據表示一個巨大的概率空間。在這些模型中，每個變量由一個頂點表示，變量之間的相互作用則以圖中的邊表示。在統計物理中，概率圖模型（例如自旋系統）被用來解釋磁性系統的行為，其中變量表示粒子的自旋，邊則刻畫相鄰粒子之間的相互作用。在計算機視覺中，圖像經常被建模為概率圖模型，像素作為變量，邊則表示相鄰像素間的關係。在機器學習中，概率圖模型被廣泛用來捕捉高維數據中的統計依賴關係。 本項目將研究與概率圖模型相關的兩個基礎計算任務：(1) 抽樣，即從高維分佈中隨機抽取樣本；(2) 近似計數，即估計樣本空間的大小。近年來，許多抽樣與計數算法的突破，都來自於對隨機變量之間影響的分析。直觀來說，影響衡量的是聯合分佈中隨機變量之間的相關性。例如，在一個所有變量彼此獨立的乘積分佈中，影響為零，因此抽樣與計數都相對簡單。然而，在概率圖模型中，所有變量彼此之間都是相關的。那麼，如果我們能對變量之間的影響加以界定，是否仍能設計出高效的算法呢？ 本項目的主要目標是透過影響界限來設計高效的算法。在抽樣方面，現有的大多數算法主要針對稀疏的概率圖模型，而針對稠密概率圖模型的算法仍相對有限。本項目將利用影響界限，改進馬尔可夫鏈蒙特卡羅（MCMC）算法，以填補這一空白。在近似計數方面，我們將同時探討隨機化與確定性算法。隨機化算法可以從「計數到抽樣」的歸約方法中導出，我們的目標是基於影響界限，設計更高效的歸約算法。至於確定性算法，以往的結果往往對影響界限施加非常嚴格的條件，導致其效能落後於隨機化方法。本項目希望通過改進算法工具，更有效地將影響界限與確定性計數結合，縮小這一差距。由於影響界限能夠帶來高效算法，本項目的第二個目標是為特定的概率圖模型建立所需的影響界限。我們將探索多種技術來實現這一目標，包括耦合分析、資訊滲流，以及邊際分佈的遞歸計算。

27202925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27202925.value: 安全工作包上鏈：個性化監測與隱私保護協作

27202925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202925.value: Personalized construction safety monitoring (CSM) is crucial to prevent worker injuries and fatalities on hazardous job sites. Leveraging sensors with artificial intelligence (AI) models for distributed workers is at the core of personalized CSM. For example, a construction safety work package with diverse sensors can perform different CSM tasks to monitor an individual worker via learning data features using appropriate AI models. However, there is a theoretical dilemma between the greater computational efficiency of centralized processing of data from various work packages and the greater personalization and privacy of decentralized processing of data within each work package. The dilemma is further exacerbated by the increasing complexity of CSM tasks involving heterogenous data and stricter privacy regulations. To address this dilemma, this project aims to develop a BlockChain-enabled Personalized Adaptive Work Package (BC-PAWP) approach. The key novelty is the PAWP learning for personalized CSM. In PAWP learning, a work package is a graph of semantics encompassing diverse CSM tasks, AI models, and sensory data. PAWP learning uses graph theory that helps form adaptive topologies for graphs of work packages to aggregate and share AI models’ parameters through calculations, e.g., similarity and weighted average, for achieving CSM personalization. Implementing the blockchain will extend the PAWP learning model from a local CSM application to one enabling privacy-preserving CSM collaboration using decentralized applications, such as location tracker, fatigue monitor, and motion detector. Moreover, the BC-PAWP approach will incorporate differential privacy methods, consensus and incentive mechanisms for advanced privacy-preserving, dynamic model parameter aggregation, and high-quality parameter sharing. Additionally, BC-PAWP will offer interoperable and non-disruptive interfaces (e.g., virtual disks, blockchain oracles, plug-ins) for smart site safety systems (4S). Our two pilot studies have demonstrated the feasibility of this proposed approach. The project’s main deliverable will be the BC-PAWP approach for 4S supply chains and end users. Research findings will extend the knowledge boundary of the work package model in CSM. From the industry aspect, BC-PAWP can be a game-changer by leveraging current CSM practices to enable personalized and private monitoring without disruption. This project aligns with industry needs and local government policies in 4S for CSM, privacy computing, and digital supervision. Moreover, BC-PAWP will impact more disciplines and applications using the complete history of traceable CSM insights from work packages, such as personalized worker insurance pricing, dynamic work-rest scheduling, and safe human-robot collaboration, benefiting disciplines from finance to engineering and computer science. 2023年，香港建造業意外死亡個案佔全港經濟活動死亡總數83.3%，工傷數字更飆升至4,377宗，創18年新高。因此，實施個性化建築安全監測（CSM） 對保障高危工地工人安全至關重要。其核心在於運用邊緣感應器與人工智能（AI）模型，為分散作業的工人提供監測方案。例如：建築安全工作包可透過AI模型學習數據特徵，利用不同感應器為個別工人執行多樣化CSM任務。 現存理論困境在於： ▸ 集中處理工作包數據雖提升運算效率，卻犧牲個性化並加劇私隱風險 ▸ 分散處理各工作包數據雖降低私隱風險，卻因數據不足難訓練穩健模型 此矛盾隨CSM任務複雜化（異構數據激增）及私隱法規收緊（如香港《個人資料(私隱)條例》）日益尖銳——法規甚至可能禁止整合孤立工作包數據。 本項目遂提出突破性方案：開發 「基於區塊鏈的個性化自適應工作包」（BC-PAWP） ，實現個性化與隱私保護並重的CSM。 核心創新點在於 PAWP學習模型： → 將工作包建構為語義圖（semantic graph），整合CSM任務、AI模型與異構感應數據 → 通過自適應拓撲結構（星型/樹狀/網狀/環形）實現多尺度工作包參數聚合與共享 → 運用圖論技術（如數據分佈相似性比對、加權平均參數聚合）動態調整工作包圖結構，達成CSM個性化 兩項先導研究已驗證此模型可行性。 區塊鏈技術將PAWP從本地應用升級為去中心化協作網絡： ✓ 透過分佈式應用（如定位器、疲勞監測儀、動作追蹤器）構建隱私保護網絡 ✓ 整合差分隱私技術強化數據保護 ✓ 設計共識與激勵機制保障動態參數聚合與高質量模型共享 ✓ 提供虛擬磁碟、區塊鏈預言機、插件等接口，無縫對接主流智能工地安全系統（4S） 項目成果BC-PAWP將服務於4S供應鏈及終端使用者（工人），其價值在於： ★ 突破現有CSM工作包模型的理論邊界 ★ 為建造業提供「不中斷現有流程」的個性化隱私安全監測方案 ★ 契合香港政府4S政策對CSM、隱私計算及數碼監管的需求 ★ 衍生跨學科應用：工人個性化保險定價、動態工休調度、人機協作安全等，惠及金融、工程與計算機科學領域

27204425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27204425.value: 基於計算機視覺的實驗與數值模擬揭示高層樓宇數據中心的結構火災反應

27204425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27204425.value: The increasing of data-intensive technologies, such as artificial intelligence and high-performance cloud computing, has led to a surge in data centre construction. Global trends indicate continued growth in both the number and size of data centres worldwide. In Hong Kong, there were approximately 60 data centres with a total floor space of around 800,000 square meters as of 2022. The Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Development Blueprint anticipates that the total floor area of data centres in Hong Kong will expand to 1.5 million square meters by 2026. Due to limited space in Hong Kong, many existing and planned data centres are situated in high-rise buildings originally designed as standard office spaces. Data centres located in high-rise buildings raise concerns about fire safety. There have been reports of data centre fires, such as the two-day fire at an Alibaba Inc. data centre in Singapore in September 2024. The densely placed devices and their distinct fire characteristics create unique challenges for data centre fires. The severe and long-duration data centre fires can potentially cause structure collapses. However, there are no specific considerations for structural fire design for data centre fires in the present building codes or fire performance-based design guidelines owing to the insufficient understanding of the structural fire responses to data centre fires. This research aims to advance the state-of-the-art in fire engineering by exploring the new challenges introduced by data centre fires. The experiments and numerical simulations will be carried out to study the fire dynamics and the fire-structural interactions in different fire scenarios during a data centre fire. Leveraging the principal investigator's expertise in computer vision, numerical modelling, large-scale experiments, and risk assessment, the research project will include experiments for determining the fire characteristics of common equipment in a data centre and computer vision-empowered numerical simulations for fire-structure interaction. Factors such as fuel distribution, ventilation conditions, and floor plan will be integrated into fire modelling, providing more accurate thermal boundary conditions for computing the structure responses. Parametric studies on typical steel frame structures and concrete structures are to be carried out to investigate the relationship between structural fire response and data centre fire characteristics. High-fidelity models and machine learning surrogate models to predict the fire performance of high-rise buildings subjected to data centre fires are to be established. The findings will enhance fire design practices and building resilience, particularly for the data centre hosting high-rise buildings. 隨著人工智慧和高性能雲端運算等數據密集型技術的日益普及，資料中心的建設也呈現出快速增長的趨勢。全球趨勢顯示，全球資料中心的數量和規模都將持續擴大。截至2022年，香港約有60個資料中心，總樓面面積約為80萬平方米。根據香港創新科技發展藍圖，預計到2026年，香港資料中心的總樓面面積將擴展至150萬平方米。由於香港空間有限，許多現有和規劃中的資料中心都位於原本設計為標準辦公空間的高層建築中。位於高樓大廈中的資料中心引發了火災安全的關注。例如，2024年9月，新加坡阿里巴巴資料中心發生了為期兩天的火災事件。密集安裝的設備及其獨特的火災特性為資料中心火災帶來了特殊挑戰。嚴重且持續時間長的資料中心火災可能導致建築結構倒塌。然而，現行建築規範或防火性能設計指南中尚未針對資料中心火災的結構防火設計提出具體考慮，原因是對資料中心火災引發的結構火災反應尚缺乏充分的理解。 本研究旨在推動火災工程領域的前沿，探索資料中心火災帶來的新挑戰。將進行實驗和數值模擬，以研究資料中心火災中火災動態及火災與結構之間的相互作用，涵蓋不同火災場景。利用首席研究員在計算機視覺、數值建模、大型實驗和風險評估方面的專業經驗，研究項目將包括測定資料中心常用設備火災特性之實驗，以及基於計算機視覺的火災-結構相互作用數值模擬。模型將考慮燃料分佈、通風條件和樓層佈局等因素，為結構反應的熱邊界條件提供更精確的數據。還將進行典型鋼框架和混凝土結構的參數研究，以探討結構火災反應與資料中心火災特性之間的關係。同時，建立高保真模型和機器學習代理模型，用於預測高層建築在資料中心火災情境下的火災性能。研究結果將有助於提升火災設計實踐和建築韌性，特別是針對托管高層建築的資料中心。

27206525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27206525.value: 不確定交互環境下無人自主系統實時安全保障機制研究

27206525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27206525.value: In recent years, autonomous systems have rapidly expanded into various sectors such as transportation and industrial robotics. As these systems increasingly operate in complex, dynamic environments, a key concern arises: can we ensure that these systems function safely and reliably, especially when faced with uncertainties? Current autonomous systems struggle with handling unpredictable environmental factors and interactions, leading to potential safety concerns. This creates a critical need for advanced methods that can manage these uncertainties in real time, ensuring safe and efficient operations. Autonomous systems, such as self-driving vehicles or industrial robots, often fail to make safe decisions in dynamic or noisy conditions due to the limitations of their perception and planning algorithms. This project proposes a solution through the development of a real-time safeguard framework that can evaluate, quantify, and integrate uncertainty into the decision-making processes of autonomy. The framework will focus on the uncertainty propagation in the autonomous driving stack and safe planning under uncertainty, leveraging state-of-the-art methods in uncertainty modeling, risk assessment, and real-time optimization-based planning. The specific approach involves creating a multi-layered framework that tackles three critical questions: (1) How can we estimate the uncertainty of AI-driven perception modules in real time? (2) How can we formulate risks with the partial observable intentions of other actors under uncertain conditions? (3) How can we ensure that the autonomous system makes safe plans despite these uncertainties? The project’s aim is to develop a comprehensive system that can operate safely and efficiently in uncertain, interactive environments. The major objectives include real-time uncertainty estimation, interaction-and-uncertainty-aware prediction, multi-modal risk representation, and safe planning using stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC). These objectives will be achieved through a combination of theoretical research, simulations, and real-world testing with industry partners. For instance, the project will pilot the safeguard planner in collaboration with LoopX, testing its efficacy in high-stakes environments such as mining. This project has the potential to greatly improve the safety of autonomous systems, contributing to their broader acceptance and deployment in both industrial and public sectors. The framework will enhance not only operational safety but also public trust in autonomous technologies, paving the way for safer and more reliable autonomous systems. 近年來，無人自主系統在交通、工業機器人等領域的應用迅速擴展。隨著系統在複雜動態環境中運行比例的提升，其面臨的核心挑戰日益凸顯：如何在不確定性條件下保障系統的安全可靠運行？現有系統受限於感知與規劃算法的局限性，難以有效處理動態環境中的不可預測因素及多智能體交互，存在顯著安全隱患。本項目旨在開發一種實時保障框架，通過將不確定性量化嵌入自主系統的決策閉環，解決該關鍵問題。針對自動駕駛車輛、工業機器人等自主系統在噪聲環境中的安全決策失效問題，本框架聚焦自動駕駛技術棧中的不確定性傳遞機制及不確定性條件下的安全規劃方法，融合不確定性建模、風險評估與實時優化規劃的前沿技術，構建多層防護體系，重點突破三大核心問題：(1)AI感知模塊的實時不確定性估計方法；(2)部分可觀測意圖下的不確定交互風險量化模型；(3)多重不確定性約束下的安全規劃保障機制。研究將通過理論建模、仿真驗證與工業場景實測逐步推進。本框架的實施將顯著提升無人自主系統在不確定交互環境中的運行安全性，增強技術社會公信力，為工業及公共領域規模化應用提供核心保障。

27207025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27207025.value: 基於術前多模態數據的可解釋性視覺語言基礎模型輔助中樞神經系統腫瘤早期診斷

27207025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27207025.value: Background: Central nervous system (CNS) tumors are associated with high morbidity and mortality rates and rank among the most lethal cancer types. Early and accurate diagnosis of CNS tumor types is pivotal to prescribing optimal treatment for patients with CNS tumors. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the gold standard for presurgical CNS tumor diagnosis. However, interpreting MRI scans via neuroradiologists is challenging and time-consuming, given the diverse nature of CNS tumors, inter-observer variability, and potential perceptual errors. The global shortage of qualified neuroradiologists further exacerbates this issue. This highlights the urgent need for an advanced CNS tumor diagnostic tool that provides rapid and accurate diagnoses from presurgical multi-modal data, thereby accelerating the time-sensitive diagnosis process and reducing clinicians’ workloads. Research Gap: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize CNS tumor diagnosis. Despite this promise, current AI research primarily targets three CNS tumor types: gliomas, meningiomas, and metastases. This leaves the remaining nine CNS tumors identified by WHO CNS5 understudied. Additionally, existing methods mainly address CNS tumor classification and segmentation, leaving report generation—crucial for holistic diagnosis and interpretation—largely unexplored. Moreover, many AI models predict CNS tumor types without assessing how reliable the prediction is or explaining the underlying clinical rationale. This severely undermines clinicians' trust in AI-generated predictions, posing a substantial barrier to its clinical translation and adoption. Method: To address these gaps, we propose BrainVLM, a comprehensive and explainable AI model, for precise and reliable CNS tumor diagnosis and interpretation from presurgical multi-modal data. We achieve this by integrating the following aims: (i) compile a large-scale CNS tumor dataset, covering all 12 CNS tumor types and most subtypes, from 40 online repositories and 7 medical centers; (ii) develop an innovative vision language foundation model, called BrainVLM, for accurate CNS tumor diagnosis and report generation; (iii) enhance BrainVLM’s reliability and interpretability using chain-of-thought prompting and uncertainty measurement strategies; (iv) conduct extensive evaluations to validate BrainVLM, and develop it into a user-friendly web-based tool for widespread clinical adoption. Significance: Our pioneering project represents the first attempt to develop a comprehensive AI-based diagnostic tool capable of handling all 12 CNS tumor types, while offering interpretable insights into the clinical reasoning behind its diagnoses. With our exceptional multi-disciplinary team and promising preliminary results, we envision BrainVLM will be a reliable asset for neuroradiologists, ultimately leading to improved patient care. 背景：中樞神經系統（CNS）腫瘤具有極高的發病率和死亡率，是最致命的癌症類型之一。對CNS腫瘤類型進行早期且準確的診斷，對於為患者制定最佳治療方案至關重要。磁共振成像（MRI）是術前診斷CNS腫瘤的金標準。然而，神經放射科醫師對MRI圖像的解讀受限於CNS腫瘤的多樣性、觀察者間差異以及潛在的感知誤差，使得診斷過程既具挑戰性又耗時。全球合格神經放射科醫師的短缺進一步加劇了這一問題。因此，亟需一種先進的CNS腫瘤診斷工具，能夠基於術前多模態數據進行快速、準確的診斷，以加速緊迫的診斷流程並減輕臨床醫生的工作負擔。 研究空白：人工智慧（AI）有潛力徹底改變CNS腫瘤的診斷方式。然而，現有的AI研究主要集中於三種CNS腫瘤：膠質瘤、腦膜瘤及轉移瘤，對於世界衛生組織（WHO CNS5）所定義的另外九種CNS腫瘤的研究明顯不足，限制了其臨床應用價值。此外，現有方法大多聚焦於CNS腫瘤的分類與分割，對於全面診斷和解釋至關重要的報告生成尚未得到有效解決。此外，多數AI系統如同“黑箱”，僅給出腫瘤類型預測，卻缺乏背後臨床推理的解釋，難以讓臨床醫師理解與信任其推薦結果。 方法：為彌補上述不足，我們提出BrainVLM——一種全面且可解釋的AI模型，用於基於術前多模態數據的精確可靠CNS腫瘤診斷與解釋。具體而言，我們將實現以下目標：(i) 從40個線上數據庫及7家醫療中心收集涵蓋所有12種CNS腫瘤類型及大部分亞型的大規模CNS腫瘤數據集；(ii) 開發創新的視覺語言基礎模型BrainVLM，用於準確的CNS腫瘤診斷與報告生成；(iii) 通過鏈式思維提示及臨床推理策略，提升BrainVLM的可靠性與可解釋性，確保其在臨床中的有效轉化；(iv) 開展全面的評估，並將BrainVLM開發為用戶友好的網頁工具，促進其在臨床中的廣泛應用。 意義：本項目是首個致力於開發能夠處理全部12種CNS腫瘤，且能提供透明、可解釋臨床推理過程的AI診斷工具。依託於我們卓越的多學科團隊和有前景的初步成果，我們預計BrainVLM將成為神經放射科醫師值得信賴的輔助工具，最終提升患者的診療效果。

27207725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27207725.value: 結合基於CycleGAN的生成設計與基於BIM的供應商平台提升「組裝合成」建築法的採用率

27207725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27207725.value: Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) is not a new concept, but it is still gaining interest and investment due to its significant potential to address key challenges in the construction industry, including labor shortages, an aging workforce, rising costs, and the growing demand for enhanced safety, quality, and sustainability. If widely adopted, MiC could substantially boost productivity, help alleviate housing shortages in various markets, and fundamentally reshape modern construction practices. Despite these benefits, MiC adoption remains limited. One design-related barrier is MiC's heavy reliance on standardized module sizes, which limits its application for complex architectural designs with irregular layouts. From a supply chain perspective, the lack of early manufacturer engagement prevents timely material procurement, while pandemic-related disruptions and insufficient manufacturing capacity further cause delays that are difficult to manage in MiC. To address these design and supply chain challenges, two new approaches – the generative design and supplier marketplace – have recently gained attention. Generative design can be used to efficiently explore design variations, optimizing building performances while providing real-time feedback. The supplier marketplace is a free and open database of offsite construction, which connects real estate developers with a network of offsite construction specialists. To increase the adoption of MiC, there is a need to combine these approaches. The main objective of this research is to propose a computational framework consisting of three components: suitability analysis, generative design, and marketplace-based design configuration. The suitability analysis helps real estate developers more efficiently assess if designs are fit for MiC using a suitability indicator based on system complexity theory (WP1). For designs with low suitability, CycleGAN-based models generate modifications to increase MiC suitability, reducing feedback cycles between architects and manufacturers (WP2). Once a suitable design is confirmed, the framework automatically matches it with suppliers and modules in the marketplace, ensuring an efficient integration of design and supply chain processes. The main benefits of this framework are that it increases the potential for MiC application in diverse floor plans and complex designs. Besides, the seamless integration between design processes and the supplier marketplace enables early engagement of manufacturers and suppliers. This ensures an accurate cost estimation and early procurement, reducing lead time for module prefabrication. With the increased adoption of MiC, the construction industry as a whole will benefit from more sustainable construction practices, reduced construction waste, and faster building processes. 「組裝合成」建築（Modular Integrated Construction, 簡稱 MiC）並非新概念，但由於其在解決建造業多項關鍵問題，如人手短缺、勞動人口老化、成本上升，以及對提升安全、品質和可持續性的需求不斷增加， 展現出巨大潛力，因此仍持續受到關注和投資。若能廣泛應用，MiC 有望大幅提升生產力、紓緩各地房屋短缺問題，並從根本上改變現代建造模式。然而，儘管具備種種優勢，MiC 的採納率仍然偏低。從設計角度來看，MiC 過度依賴標準化模組尺寸，限制其在複雜建築設計（如不規則平面佈局）中的應用；從供應鏈角度而言，供應商未能在設計初期參與，導致物料採購未能及時進行，而疫情所帶來的供應鏈中斷及生產能力不足等問題，更進一步造成難以管理的延誤。 為應對這些設計與供應鏈挑戰，近年出現了兩種創新方法——生成設計（Generative Design）及供應商平台（Supplier Marketplace）。生成設計可高效探索不同設計方案，優化建築效能並提供即時回饋；而供應商平台則是一個開放式的供應商資料庫，協助地產開發商與組裝合成供應商建立聯繫。 為促進 MiC 的應用，本研究提出一個由三個部分構成的計算框架：適用性分析、生成設計，以及基於供應商平台的設計配置。首先，適用性分析利用系統複雜性理論所建立的適用性指標，協助地產商有效評估設計是否適合採用 MiC（工作包 WP1）。對於不適合的設計，研究採用基於 CycleGAN 的模型提出修改建議，以提升其 MiC 適用性，從而減少建築師與製造商之間的反覆修改（工作包 WP2）。當設計符合條件後，自動與市場中的供應商的模組配對，實現設計與供應鏈的高效整合。 此框架的主要優勢在於，提升 MiC 在多樣化平面佈局及複雜設計中的應用潛力；同時，設計流程與供應商平台的無縫結合亦促進製造商及早參與，有助於準確估算成本及提早採購，縮短模組的預製時間。隨着 MiC 更廣泛的應用，整個建造業將受惠於更可持續的建築模式、減少建築廢料，以及更快速的施工流程。

27209725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27209725.value: 面向仿生回凹表面的多重轉移光聚合工藝

27209725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27209725.value: Nature’s organisms offer a rich source of inspiration for future product design, thanks to their unique structures that have evolved over long periods. Reentrant structures, in particular, are prevalent in nature, as seen in organisms like springtails, geckos, and pitcher plants. These structures demonstrate remarkable properties, including exceptional resistance to fluid contamination, directed liquid transport and robust adaptive adhesion, which have consequently triggered a revolution in biomimetic functional surface design. However, intricate reentrant micro-architectures surpass the capabilities of current manufacturing technologies. These limitations present themselves in the following ways: 1) Manufacturability – hierarchical and heterogeneous reentrant microstructures are challenging to fabricate; 2) Fidelity – densely patterned microstructures are often overcured, resulting in a loss of detail; 3) Scalability – most high-resolution techniques do not support large-area fabrication, restricting surface dimensions to just a few millimeters. Consequently, the fabricated biomimetic functional surfaces tend to be structurally simple, low in performance, and limited in function. Inspired by the puzzle game Tower of Hanoi, we propose a novel digital light processing-based additive manufacturing process called multi-transfer vat photopolymerization (MT-VPP) to address these manufacturing challenges. Unlike traditional methods that print parts in a single direction (either bottom-up or top-down), our key idea is to fabricate complex 3D microstructural components using an additive approach and then assemble them onto the substrate via mask image projection. Specifically, these 3D microstructures undergo multiple transfers between auxiliary build platforms and resin vats by leveraging distinct separation forces at various material interfaces. To realize this approach, we will: 1) reveal the transfer mechanism, which is critical for enabling the MT-VPP process, by quantitatively studying the impact of multiple parameters simultaneously, including material properties, layer patterns, and process parameters; 2) study the light-materials-structure-performance relationship to support microstructure fabrication with high fidelity and overcome the overcuring issue via MT-VPP; 3) bridge the gap between microscale feature requirements and macroscale surface dimensions by integrating MT-VPP with the roll-to-roll process; 4) demonstrate the proposed process by developing new designs for applications such as solar desalination, green energy harvesting, and soft robotics. This research will deepen the fundamental understanding of transfer printing mechanisms and light-photopolymer-structure interactions, while also driving innovation in biomimetic research through advanced manufacturing processes. These efforts will contribute to Hong Kong’s reindustrialization and provide the public with affordable biomimetic products. 自然界生物經過長期演化形成的獨特結構，為未來產品設計提供了豐富的靈感。例如彈尾蟲、壁虎和豬籠草等生物的凹陷結構展現出超強抗液體污染、定向液體傳輸和自適應黏附等特性，推動了仿生功能表面設計的革命。然而，複雜的凹陷微結構的製造面臨可製造性、精確性和可擴展性挑戰。層次性和異質性的凹陷微結構難以製造；密集排列的微結構會因過度固化導致細節丟失；高分辨率技術難以支持大面積製造，尺寸限於幾毫米。因此，目前的仿生功能表面結構簡單、性能有限且功能不足。受河內塔的啟發，我們提出了一種基於數字光處理的多重轉移光聚合（MT-VPP）新型增材製造工藝。不同於傳統的單方向打印方法（如自下而上或自上而下），MT-VPP的思路是通過增材方式製造複雜的三維微結構組件，再利用掩膜圖像投影組裝到基板上。利用不同材料界面具有不同的分離力，打印件可以在輔助平台和樹脂槽之間多次轉移。本研究將定量分析材料性質、層圖案和工藝參數等多因素；探索光-材料-結構-性能的關係；結合卷對卷工藝解決微尺度特徵需求與宏觀表面尺寸之間的矛盾；探索該工藝在太陽能海水淡化、綠色能源收集和軟體機器人等領域的應用。本研究旨在揭示轉印機制及光-材料-結構相互作用的機理，並通過先進的製造工藝推動仿生研究的創新，為香港再工業化發展作出貢獻，並為公眾提供價格合理的仿生產品。

27210425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27210425.value: 大型語言模型輔助的加改建工程自動化安全設計檢查

27210425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27210425.value: The Alteration and Addition (A&A) sector has unique design and construction activities, such as demolitions and additions, which lead to considerable design and schedule-caused safety risks, accounting for nearly 50% of the construction industry fatalities in Hong Kong. Encouragingly, many safety risks could be prevented through design-phase safety measures (e.g. safety checking) using knowledge engineering methods (e.g., ontology). Recent research has developed some Automated Safety Checking Methods (ASCMs) for new construction, given that 3D design information and scheduling are included in Building Information Modeling (BIM) and safety knowledge is represented as ontologies. However, research to harness the ontologies and BIM for automated safety checking of A&A works is few and far between. A major challenge is that the existing ontologies are not specific enough for the design and construction activities of A&A works and are not readily available for ASCMs. This project aims to develop an ASCM for A&A works to identify construction safety risks and provide preventive design recommendations. It focuses on design-related safety risks, such as verifying openings and edges to mitigate fall risks; and schedule-related risks, like sequences of various construction tasks for collapse hazards. Firstly, the research will create a knowledge structure (i.e., ontology structure) to define key concepts, classes, and relationships relevant to A&A works. Next, this research will develop Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted methods for three steps of ASCM development: 1) ontology construction, 2) knowledge alignment, and 3) rule interpretation. The LLM will assist in extracting concepts, relationships, rules, and instance data from multimodal knowledge sources, making the ontology comprehensive and accurate for A&A works. Thereafter, the research will use LLM-assisted methods to align BIM data models with the ontology, and then facilitate rule interpretation between safety rules and machine-readable logic. The enriched, aligned, and inference-capable ASCM will facilitate accurate rule-based reasoning, risk identification, and preventive design recommendations. Finally, it will encapsulate the proposed method into BIM environment and validate it using case studies of A&A works from Hong Kong. This research will make non-trivial methodological, practical, and theoretical contributions. Methodologically, this project will integrate LLMs with ontology development, addressing the limitations of manual methods regarding misalignments, inaccuracies and inefficiencies. Practically, this project will lower designers’ knowledge barriers for identifying construction safety risks and preventive design recommendations, especially for falls and collapses. Theoretically, it will contribute to advancements in knowledge of Design for Safety (DfS) and Prevention through Design (PtD) of A&A works. 加改建（A&A）工程具有獨特的設計與施工活動，例如拆卸與新增工程，這些特性帶來顯著的設計與工期相關的安全風險，並導致香港建造業近五成的致命意外。令人鼓舞的是，許多安全風險可於設計階段透過安全檢查等措施加以預防，並可結合知識工程方法（例如本體論）來實現。近年的研究已經在新建工程中發展出若干自動化安全檢查方法（ASCMs），因為建築信息模型（BIM）能包含三維設計資訊和施工進度，而安全知識則能以本體論表示。然而，專門針對A&A工程的本體與BIM結合的自動化安全檢查研究仍然非常稀少。主要挑戰在於現有本體論對A&A工程的設計與施工活動缺乏針對性，亦未能方便地應用於ASCM。 本項目旨在為A&A工程開發一套ASCM，用於識別施工安全風險並提出預防性的設計建議。研究將聚焦於設計相關的安全風險，例如檢查開口及邊緣以降低墜落風險；以及工期相關的風險，例如不同施工工序的順序所引發的倒塌危害。首先，研究將建立一個知識結構（即本體論結構），定義與A&A工程相關的關鍵概念、類別與關係。其後，研究將開發大型語言模型（LLM）輔助的方法，支援ASCM的三個發展步驟：1）本體構建，2）知識對齊，3）規則詮釋。LLM將有助於從多模態知識來源中提取概念、關係、規則及實例數據，從而使本體對A&A工程而言更為全面與準確。進一步地，本研究將利用LLM輔助方法來對齊BIM數據模型與本體，並促進安全規則與機器可讀邏輯之間的規則詮釋。經過充實、對齊及具備推理能力的ASCM將能實現準確的基於規則的推理、風險識別及預防性設計建議。最後，研究將把所提出的方法封裝於BIM環境中，並透過香港的A&A工程案例進行驗證。 本研究將作出重要的方法論、實務及理論貢獻。在方法論層面，本項目將整合LLM與本體開發，解決傳統人工方法在錯配、不準確及效率不足方面的限制。在實務層面，本項目將降低設計人員於識別施工安全風險和制定預防性設計建議時的知識門檻，尤其針對墜落及倒塌風險。在理論層面，本研究將推動「安全設計」及「預防設計」於A&A工程領域的知識發展。

27214925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27214925.value: 從觀看視頻到交互視頻：在用戶動作和反饋的循環中生成流式視頻

27214925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27214925.value: Video generation has achieved great success over the past years. However, previous video generation models treated users as passive viewers and could not customize the visual experience with immersive interactions. For example, Sora can generate a video of forest exploration to teach children about the plants and animals in forests. However, they do not allow children to interact with the video dynamically, such as changing the exploration path or interacting with animals. This project aims to develop methods to interactively generate videos driven by user actions and reactions, transforming the user experience from passively watching videos to actively interacting with them. Specifically, the videos are generated in a streaming manner and viewed by users during the generation process. The upcoming video content is generated following user actions (e.g., turn left, open, etc., represented as keyboard and mouse inputs, similar to playing video games) or responding to user reactions (e.g., “I don’t understand it” with a pointer to the specific region.). We face several challenges. Firstly, the video-action and video-reaction paired data is scarce. Collecting such data requires users in the loop, which makes it challenging to automate and scale up data collection. Moreover, the video-action data are mainly collected from video games or simulation environments, which are difficult to generalize to open-world actionable videos. Secondly, previous video generators are not prepared for our goal: diffusion-based video generation models generate all frames simultaneously and cannot incorporate online user interactions; they generate videos based on descriptive text, while they cannot understand the environment change and user intentions from actions and interactions. To address these challenges, firstly, inspired by the LLM’s reasoning and task planning abilities, we propose MLLM-based multi-agent collaboration to simulate diverse human behaviors for data collection. Secondly, we develop an understanding-inspired video generation model to autoregressively generate streaming videos following actions and reactions. The hybrid architecture takes advantage of the streaming prediction and understanding abilities of MLLM and the visual generation quality of diffusion models, and further incorporates multi-granular control. Thirdly, we propose a training strategy to generalize the action control from specific domain training data to open-world video generation. Lastly, we propose offline evaluation metrics and online evaluation platforms involving real users. This new paradigm will lead to a transformative shift towards immersive and interactive AI-generated visual media, inspiring applications in AI-empowered education, virtual reality, digital twins, video games, and embodied AI. 視頻生成技術在過去幾年取得了巨大成功。然而，以往的視頻生成模型將用戶視為被動觀眾，無法通過沉浸式交互來定制個性化的視覺體驗。例如，Sora可以生成一段森林探險的視頻，用於向兒童講解森林中的動植物，但這些模型無法讓兒童與視頻進行動態互動，比如改變探險路徑或與動物互動。本項目旨在開發由用戶動作和反饋驅動的交互式視頻生成方法，將用戶體驗從被動觀看視頻轉變為主動參與互動。具體而言，視頻將以流式方式生成，用戶可在生成過程中實時觀看。即將生成的視頻內容會根據用戶動作（如“向左轉”、“打開”等，可通過鍵盤和鼠標輸入實現，類似於玩電子遊戲）或用戶反饋（如“我不明白這裡”，並用指針標註具體區域）進行相應生成。 我們面臨多項挑戰。首先，視頻-動作和視頻-反饋配對數據十分稀缺。這類數據的收集需要用戶參與，難以自動化並大規模擴展。此外，現有的視頻-動作數據主要來自電子遊戲或模擬環境，難以推廣到開放世界下的可操作視頻。其次，現有的視頻生成器尚無法滿足我們的目標：基於擴散模型的視頻生成方法是一次性生成所有幀，無法實時融入用戶互動；它們通常基於文本描述來生成視頻，難以從用戶動作和交互中理解環境變化和用戶意圖。 為了解決這些挑戰，首先，我們受大語言模型推理和任務規劃能力的啟發，提出基於多模態大模型的多智能體協作，模擬多樣化的人類行為進行數據收集。其次，我們開發了一種基於理解的視頻生成模型，能夠自回歸地根據用戶動作和反饋流式生成視頻。該混合架構結合了多模態大模型的流式預測和環境理解能力，以及擴散模型的高質量視覺生成能力，並進一步實現多粒度的控制。第三，我們提出了一種訓練策略，將動作控制從特定領域的訓練數據泛化到開放世界的視頻生成。最後，我們設計了包含真實用戶參與的離線評價指標和在線評價平台。 這一全新範式將推動生成式視覺媒體向沉浸式和交互式方向的變革，並將激發AI賦能教育、虛擬現實、數字孿生、電子遊戲和具身智能等多個領域的應用。

27301425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27301425.value: 數據科學中結構化非凸優化問題之⼀階算法研究

27301425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301425.value: Optimization methods are becoming increasingly important due to the rapid growth of data science and artificial intelligence. Training data science models requires fast algorithms that are cost-effective. First-order methods are often used as they are easy to implement and perform well. However, current theories fall short of providing guarantees for these methods, as many real-world problems lie outside the traditional framework of convex and smooth optimization. To address this gap, this project seeks to deepen the theoretical understanding of these methods in contexts relevant to data science. We will study the global and local behavior of first-order methods for various classes of structured objectives commonly encountered in practice. First, we plan to show that these methods can find solutions that meet certain optimality criteria across a wide range of functions. Among these solutions, we aim to identify conditions under which the undesirable ones can be avoided. Finally, we will explore a stronger geometric property that is satisfied in training neural networks. Leveraging this property, we will estimate the time required for these methods to find globally optimal solutions. By tackling these challenges, this project aims to provide new theoretical insights and practical guidelines for using first-order methods in data science and artificial intelligence applications. 由於數據科學與人工智能的迅猛發展，優化算法變得日益重要。訓練數據科學模型需要高效且具成本效益的算法。一階算法因其易於實作且表現優良而常被採用。然而，許多現實世界問題超出了傳統的凸性與平滑優化框架，致使現行理論難以為這些方法提供理論保證。為彌合此差距，本研究計劃旨在深化對這些方法在數據科學相關情境下的理論理解。 我們將探究在實踐中常見的多類具結構性目標函數下，一階算法的全局及局部行為特性。首先，我們計劃證明這些算法能在廣泛的函數類別中，找到符合特定最優性條件的解。我們將進一步界定在哪些條件下，一階算法會避開問題的不良解。最後，我們將探討一種在訓練神經網路時常被滿足的更強幾何特性；利用此特性，我們將推算這些算法尋得全局最優解所需的時間。藉由克服上述挑戰，本計劃旨在為在數據科學與人工智能應用中使用一階算法，提供新的理論洞見和實務指引。

27301925.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27301925.value: 差分隐私算法的统计推断 差分隐私算法的统计推断 差分隐私算法的统计推断

27301925.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301925.value: Nowadays, it is crucial to protect individual privacy while training machine learning models. One popular approach is to implement differentially private (DP) algorithms, which allow for accurate estimates while ensuring privacy protection. However, existing literature has largely overlooked the uncertainty quantification associated with DP algorithms, such as the DP stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm, which has been very popular in both academia and industry. This project aims to address this gap by investigating statistical inference for DP algorithm output, including the DP-SGD algorithm, the Distributed DP algorithm, and the DP zeroth-order algorithm. Our objective is to derive the asymptotic distribution of the outputs generated by these algorithms and to construct valid confidence intervals. A key innovation of this research lies in analyzing the statistical distribution of estimates derived from the stochastic gradient descent algorithm utilizing randomized sampling techniques, which are essential for ensuring privacy protection while adding a small amount of noise. This analysis presents challenges that surpass those encountered in existing statistical inference for online sequential stochastic gradient descent algorithms. The asymptotic distribution will require a delicate balance among batch size, number of iterations, and the scales of private noise incorporated into the algorithm. Additionally, we propose the construction of confidence intervals using pivotal statistics, which involves developing new tools to analyze the functional central limit theorem for randomly sub-sampled data. The first proposed project focuses on statistical inference for the DP-stochastic gradient descent algorithm, outlining the fundamental concepts and primary challenges. The second project addresses inference for the distributed version of the algorithm, applicable in contexts where data is stored on remote clients. The third project focuses on statistical inference for the DP zeroth-order algorithm, relevant in scenarios where the first-order gradient is unavailable, such as certain bandit problems or variational inference. The methodologies developed in this research can also be extended to other DP algorithms. The proposed methods can be applied when the DP algorithm (either stochastic gradient descent or zeroth-order algorithm) is used to estimate parameters on private data. For example, single-cell genomic data often comprises millions of sensitive observations from individual subjects. We treat specific phenotypes as the response, while genes serve as covariates. Regression or classification models can be employed to estimate the coefficients associated with these genes. The proposed methods facilitate the construction of DP confidence intervals, which not only provide uncertainty quantification but also privacy protection. 当前，在训练机器学习模型时保护个体隐私至关重要。差分隐私（DP）算法作为一种主流解决方案，能在确保隐私保护的同时获得准确估计。然而现有研究大多忽视了DP算法的不确定性量化问题.以学术界和工业界广泛采用的DP随机梯度下降（SGD）算法为例，其统计推断研究仍属空白。 本项目旨在填补这一空白，针对DP-SGD算法、分布式DP-SGD算法及DP-KW算法的输出建立统计推断框架。我们将推导这些算法输出的渐近分布，并构建有效置信区间。本研究的核心创新在于：通过分析采用随机采样技术的SGD算法估计量的统计分布（该技术通过微量噪声注入实现隐私保护），解决比传统在线序列SGD推断更复杂的理论挑战。其中渐近分布的推导需精确权衡批量大小、迭代次数与隐私噪声尺度之间的关系。此外，我们将基于枢轴统计量构建置信区间，这需要对随机子采样数据建立函数中心极限定理。 第一项子课题聚焦DP-SGD算法的统计推断，阐述基础理论与核心挑战；第二项研究分布式DP-SGD算法的推断问题，适用于医疗金融等跨机构数据场景；第三项针对梯度不可得场景（如部分老虎机问题或变分推断）开发DP-KW算法的推断框架。本研究方法论可推广至其他DP算法。 所提方法可应用于私有数据的DP-SGD参数估计。例如单细胞基因组数据通常包含数百万条敏感个体观测，我们将特定表型作为响应变量、基因作为协变量，通过回归或分类模型估计基因关联系数。新方法不仅能构建具有隐私保护的DP置信区间，还能提供不确定性量化。该框架同样适用于需要隐私保护的深度学习算法（如基于敏感数据训练大语言模型）的统计推断。

27306025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27306025.value: 理解上風向幹旱對中國半幹旱地區生態繫統碳吸收的影響：集合地表測量、衛星資料和大氣傳輸模擬

27306025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27306025.value: For the past six decades land ecosystems have been absorbing about 32% of anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions, thereby mitigating climate change. However, mounting evidence suggests that drought can strongly reduce ecosystem carbon uptake in many regions, potentially turning the land carbon sink into a carbon source. Current understanding of drought impacts on land ecosystem carbon uptake is mostly limited to the “local” scale, i.e., drought-carbon coupling within the same spatial domain. Importantly, drought is also hypothesized to affect land ecosystem in “non-local” areas downwind. This is due to a decrease in downwind precipitation as a result of less atmospheric moisture being transported by winds from upwind drought-affected regions. Yet, the evidence of this “non-local” effects of drought on land ecosystem carbon uptake is still very limited, as is our capability to accurately predict and manage upwind drought risks on land ecosystem. The proposed research will integrate ground measurements, satellite data, and atmospheric transport modelling to examine the impact of upwind drought on land ecosystem carbon uptake. This research will specifically focus on China’s semi-arid ecoregion (i.e., "local" or downwind region), an important land carbon sink that is vulnerable to drought and depends on moisture originating from upwind land. The proposed research comprises three tasks. Task 1 will first derive and validate long-term and spatial-continuous measurements of ecosystem productivity and hydroclimate by leveraging multiple data sources including flux towers, meteorological stations, satellite-derived solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence, etc. Then, Task 1 will detect effective “local” (downwind) drought events that reduce ecosystem carbon uptake. Task 2 will unravel the role of upwind drought in the occurrence of the identified downwind drought events from Task 1 by employing a latest three-dimensional Lagrangian atmospheric transport model to track the anomalous moisture transport. Based on Task 1 and 2, Task 3 will apply a statistical generalized additive model to build the empirical relationship between upwind drought and downwind ecosystem response, and therefore assess upwind drought impacts on land ecosystem carbon uptake. This project will help achieve a better understanding of the processes that drive drought impacts on land ecosystem from the conventional focused “local” scale to the “non-local” scale (i.e., upwind drought - downwind carbon anomalies). Beyond academia, the project outcomes will help identify and design targeted ecosystem management strategies in China’s semi-arid ecoregion to adapt and mitigate drought consequences. 在這裡輸過去 60 年來，陸地生態繫統吸收了約 32% 的人為二氧化碳排放，幫助減緩了氣候變化。然而，越來越多的證據表明，乾旱會大大降低許多地區生態繫統的碳吸收，有可能將陸地碳匯變成碳源。目前對乾旱對陸地生態繫統碳吸收影響的了解，大多僅限於本地尺度，即同一空間領域內的乾旱-碳耦合。重要的是，乾旱也會影響下風向（非本地）區域的陸地生態繫統。然而，幹旱對陸地生態繫統碳吸收的這種非本地影響的証據仍然非常有限，使得我們準確預測和管理上風幹旱對土地生態繫統風險的能力也非常有限。 本研究將結合地麵測量、衛星資料和大氣輸送模型，以研究上風乾旱對陸地生態繫統碳吸收的影響。本研究將特別針對中國半乾旱生態區域，該區域是重要的陸地碳吸收匯，易受乾旱影響，並依賴來自上風土地的濕氣，主要包括三項任務：任務一首先利用通量塔、氣象站、衛星探測的葉綠素螢光等多種資料來源，對研究區域的生態繫統生產力和水文氣候進行長期和空間連續測量，並對測量結果進行驗證。然後，任務 1 將偵測減少生態繫統碳吸收的有效當地（下風向）乾旱事件；任務 2 將運用最新的三維拉格朗日大氣輸送模型追蹤異常水汽輸送，從而揭示上風乾旱在任務 1 中發現的下風乾旱事件中的作用；在任務 1 和任務 2 的基礎上，任務 3 將應用統計廣義加權模型來建立上風乾旱與生態繫統反應之間的經驗關係，從而評估上風乾旱對生態繫統碳吸收的影響。本項目將有助於更好地理解驅動乾旱對陸地生態繫統影響的過程，從傳統的本地尺度到非本地尺度（即上風乾旱-下風碳異常）。在學術之外，該項目的成果將有助於在中國半乾旱生態區域確定和設計有針對性的生態繫統管理策略，以適應和緩解乾旱的後果。

27308125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27308125.value: 帶高維協變量之非線性因子模型的可識別性、推斷方法與應用

27308125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27308125.value: With the rise of globalization and advancements in technology, international large-scale assessments have become increasingly important for educational research and policy-making. To analyze such large-scale data and infer the latent skills of test-takers, various statistical methods have been developed and are continuously evolving. Beyond interpreting these latent variables, there is growing interest in understanding the effects of high-dimensional observed covariates on item responses, conditioned on latent variables. Investigating these covariate effects is crucial for addressing educational fairness and ensuring that students from diverse gender, ethnic, and demographic backgrounds have equal opportunities to perform well on the exams, assuming that their assessed abilities are at the same level.
