Research employing the BMVP to examine HIV-related service needs, including PrEP, among MSM is emerging; nevertheless, the focus on MSM-UD in Kazakhstan remains extremely limited. Thus, the proposed study aims to investigate the PrEP care continuum among MSM-UD in Kazakhstan. Using an explanatory sequential mixed methods design, the study will: (Phase/Aim 1) use an online survey to examine the levels of and BMVP factors associated with engagement in the PrEP care continuum among MSM-UD in Kazakhstan; and (Phase/Aim 2) use in-depth interviews to explore and elaborate on MSM-UD’s experiences of engagement in the PrEP care continuum in Kazakhstan. The proposed study is uniquely positioned to contribute empirical evidence and theoretical underpinnings for bolstering HIV prevention efforts for MSM-UD in Kazakhstan. Furthermore, it will move the PI toward submitting a General Research Fund award application for developing and testing an intervention aimed at promoting engagement of MSM-UD in the PrEP care continuum in Kazakhstan. 放眼全球，在過去十年間，感染愛滋病毒（HIV）的人數正逐漸減少。然而，在哈薩克共和國 ，這個「一帶一路」倡議的發源地，HIV的感染率卻有迅速擴大之趨勢。此勢尤以順性別男同性戀者、雙性戀及與男性有性行為者（MSM）為甚。自2013年（1.2%）至2023年（8.8%）間，彼等感染HIV之比率，幾近增至八倍，可謂劇增。先前之研究已顯示，於與男性發生性行為者（MSM）中，非法用藥之群體感染HIV之比例更高，為15.6%。此現象表明，針對此類人群，亟需加強HIV防治之措施。 HIV暴露前預防藥物（PrEP），乃一種抗反轉錄病毒藥物 ，已被證實能有效保護高風險但尚未感染HIV之人。臨床試驗亦顯示，若依指示服用PrEP，能大幅降低與男性發生性行為者（MSM）間因性行為而感染HIV之風險。在哈薩克，PrEP對於降低與男性發生性行為且有用藥習慣之男性（MSM-UD）間的HIV傳播，具有極大潛力。隨著口服PrEP近期獲哈薩克共和國政府批准在全國推廣，針對MSM-UD族群在PrEP照護流程（包括認知、使用及依從性）上的研究，正當其時且極為必要。 Gelberg-Andersen弱勢族群行為模式（BMVP），是在既有的健康服務使用行為模式基礎上加以擴展之模式，該模式著重強調社會及結構上處於邊緣地位人群的特殊需求。與原始模式相同，BMVP模式認為健康服務的使用受三大因素影響：個人特質、可用資源，以及健康需求因素。此外，運用BMVP模式以探討MSM族群在HIV相關服務（包括PrEP）上的需求之研究，近年漸有興起；然而，針對哈薩克國內同時有用藥行為的MSM-UD族群之關注，仍極為有限。 因此，本研究旨在探討在哈薩克國內有用藥行為之MSM-UD族群在PrEP照護流程中的情形。研究將採用「解釋性序列混合方法設計」，並分階段進行。第一階段將透過線上問卷調查，分析哈薩克MSM-UD族群在PrEP照護流程各環節的參與程度，並探討與BMVP相關之影響因素。在研究的第二階段，將進行深度訪談，進一步探討並細緻呈現哈薩克國內MSM-UD族群在PrEP照護流程中的實際經驗。此項研究不僅能為哈薩克國內MSM-UD族群的HIV防治工作提供實證依據，更有助於豐富相關理論基礎，對未來防疫策略之制定具有獨特價值。此外，本研究亦將助力該研究之首席研究員申請「優配研究金」（General Research Fund），以進一步開發並測試促進哈薩克國內MSM-UD族群參與PrEP照護流程之介入措施。

27617125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27617125.value: 大數據驅動下的治理模式：中國專利制度與社會信用體系整合研究

27617125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27617125.value: In an era dominated by Big Data, China has emerged as a global leader in utilizing data-driven approaches to reshape its governance structures. One of the most notable examples of this innovation is the ongoing integration of the Social Credit System (SCS) with the Patent System, a process that began in 2022 and continues to evolve. This integration marks a significant paradigm shift in how intellectual property is regulated and protected, with far-reaching implications that extend beyond China’s borders. The merger of these two systems has given rise to two groundbreaking mechanisms: a data-informed reward and punishment system and a data-guided, tiered regulatory framework. These mechanisms are designed to address several long-standing challenges in patent administration, such as identifying fraudulent applications, combating infringement, and ensuring compliance with legal rulings. However, the practical implementation and overall effects of these mechanisms remain largely unexplored, leaving a critical knowledge gap in our understanding of data-driven governance in intellectual property. This research project seeks to bridge that gap by providing the first comprehensive, empirical investigation into how this integration is being realized in practice. Through in-depth qualitative fieldwork in Beijing and Guangzhou, the study will capture the nuanced realities of how these mechanisms are interpreted, implemented, and experienced by various stakeholders. The insights generated by this study will have wide-ranging value. For policymakers, the findings will offer crucial evidence to assess the effectiveness of data-driven approaches in patent regulation, potentially informing similar initiatives in other countries. Legal scholars will benefit from a unique case study in the emerging field of “personalized law”, showcasing how big data can be used to tailor regulatory approaches to individual entities. For businesses and patent practitioners, this work will provide practical guidance on navigating this new regulatory landscape. This project comes at a critical juncture, as the integration of the SCS and patent system is still in its formative stages. By capturing diverse stakeholder perspectives at this pivotal moment, the study can shape the future trajectory of this transformative initiative. Additionally, it also contributes to broader discussions on the intersection of technology, market regulation, and economic development. The findings will be disseminated through two articles in leading peer-reviewed journals, a book proposal for a major academic press, and a conference bringing together academics, policymakers, and practitioners. These outputs will establish a foundational understanding of data-driven governance, informing policy discussions in this rapidly evolving field. 在大數據日益滲透治理實踐的背景下，中國逐步探索以數據驅動的方式加強制度運作。其中，社會信用體系與專利制度自2022年起開始進行的整合，成為具有代表性的制度實驗，並可能預示知識產權監管方式的新趨勢。此一整合已催生兩項新的治理機制：其一是以數據為依據的獎懲系統，其二是數據引導下的分級監管框架。這些機制旨在回應長期以來困擾知識產權行政管理的若干問題，例如不當申請的識別、侵權行為的治理，以及裁決結果的執行。然而，這些制度機制在實際運作中的表現與效果尚缺乏深入研究，顯示當前學界對知識產權數據治理仍存在重要認識空白。本研究擬就該整合進行系統性的實證分析，透過質性調查與案例觀察，探索上述機制在具體制度環境中的實踐情形，重點關注不同相關方如何理解、執行與回應這些新措施，以呈現政策落實過程中的實際面貌與複雜性。研究成果可望為當前數據治理模式下的知識產權監管提供初步經驗與實證素材。一方面，為政策制定部門提供參考資料，以評估數據應用於制度監管的可行性與限制；另一方面，亦為學術界提供一個觀察個體化監管與法律技術交錯發展的案例；同時對企業與專利實務從業者而言，也有助於理解監管環境的變化方向與應對策略。考慮到該整合尚處於初始階段，本研究希望能補足相關領域的研究空白，並對科技、法制與經濟治理之間的互動提供觀察與反思。預期研究成果將以期刊論文、專書提案及研討活動等形式發表，為後續相關討論提供資料與分析基礎。

27622825.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27622825.value: 早期帝制中國的書寫、記憶與身分形成（公元前221-公元220）

27622825.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27622825.value: This project employs an inter-disciplinary approach that combines history, sociology and codicology to explore the interplay between memories, identities and written artefacts across different regions of the early Chinese empires. Rather than assuming the existence of an overarching, universal cultural or public memory, it delves into the more localised social memories that different groups and organisations formulated by studying the written artefacts (e.g. bamboo and wooden manuscripts and stelae) which they produced or utilised in various social contexts, such as funeral ceremonies, government administration, and commemoration. This project will comprise three case studies, each of which addresses a type of collective memory. The first case centres on the collective memory of family, which is often the foundation of social groups, by using a personal collection of manuscripts from tombs in present-day Yunmeng, Hubei. The second case will focus on the social practices of memories on the northwestern frontier of the Han empire in the first century BCE in light of selected administrative documents discovered there. The last case will discern the negotiations and conflicts between different social memories, as well as the transformation process from the short-term communicative memory to long-term collective memory during the Eastern Han period. Given that the cases will be arranged according to the size of the social organisations, they form an inseparable framework that addresses the formulation of various discernible modes of group memories and identities. The project pursues three objectives. First, it aims to advance knowledge on the under-researched social implications of collective memories in early imperial China, focusing on their more localised, layered and personal aspects. Second, it tries to discern the roles that writings played in the construction of collective memories and identities. Third, it strives to complete the manuscript of a book-length monograph. Specific goals include: 1. Providing empirical and specific case studies on the formation of collective memories of smaller social groups and organisations. 2. Examining the ways in which collective memories were encoded in social contexts such as funeral ceremonies, government administration and public commemoration. 3. Investigating the mechanisms for formulating local memories. 本計劃以跨學科進路，融會歷史、社會學、寫本學等領域，探索漢帝國不同區域內，記憶、身分形塑等行為與出土文獻的互動。透過分析不同社群和組織製造，於各種社會脈絡（如墓葬、紀念儀式、政府行政）使用的有字文物，本計劃試圖揭示在較總體、普遍的「文化記憶」之外，由個別社群甚至家庭所構建，更具地域性的社會記憶與身分認同。具體而言，本計劃將包含三則個案研究，其各自關乎一類集體記憶，藉此探討不同量級的社會組織，建構各自集體記憶的模式，其中個案一將利用湖北雲夢縣睡虎地77號墓出土的漢簡，探討墓主越人的家庭記憶。個案二將利用居延、肩水等地發現的簡牘，分析漢帝國西北邊陲軍事組織裡，相關吏卒對於組織的記憶建構。最後，個案三將結合簡牘與碑刻資料，解構東漢時期不同地區、社群所建構集體記憶的衝突與磨合，以及短期記憶轉向至長期記憶的過程。

27624125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27624125.value: 雅樂之聲：宮廷音樂重建、儀式與中國對可用之過去的找尋

27624125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27624125.value: The proposed monograph, “Sounds of Elegance: Court Music Revival, Ritual, and China’s Search for a Usable Past,” examines the twenty-first century revivals of yayue (literally “elegant music”), ritual music historically performed in the courts of ancient and imperial China. I investigate how the encounter between this distant musical past and the world of contemporary China is entwined with a larger cultural-nationalist imagination seeking to re-compose an image of "Chineseness” that resembles no other. I propose that China’s present is actively shaped by narratives concerning its ancient past. Such narratives in turn work to rewrite China’s vast repertoire of “usable” history. Via yayue, this work traces the long arc of China’s transformations from ancient state and imperial polity to nation-state and to its global diaspora. In bringing to light changes in the nation’s attitude towards its own imperial history (as it concerns this court music tradition), the revival provides a rare context for examining the limits of Chineseness, both past and present, within and beyond China. In addressing the issues of early music revivalism, ritual theory and performativity, (self-)exoticism, Chinese intellectual history, and forms of musical and cultural nationalism, this project contributes to (ethno)musicology, early Chinese history, classical Chinese philosophy, critical cultural studies, political philosophy, and music theory. Methodology for the study features a balanced orchestration between ethnography, archival research and critical textual analysis. This study enriches existing musicological scholarship on music revivals that has done little to examine Asian contexts. It fills the gap in current literature on Chinese court music that has been exclusively historical in nature, while adding to the discipline of music theory that is increasingly invested in non-Western sources. As the revival prioritises the reinvigoration of "li," ritual in its broader Confucian sense that contains interpersonal rituals of diplomacy, this project contributes to ritual and performance studies. I also place this work in dialogue with currents in critical cultural studies, mainly the emerging field of Asian studies in Asia. Finally, by juxtaposing key issues that characterise the ongoing revival with related intellectual debates from early Chinese history, the monograph aims to uncover the cyclical and spiral evolution of expressive cultures such as yayue, while identifying discursive shifts that concern the notions of antiquity, tradition, and harmony, all of which come together to define the collective Chinese consciousness today. 擬出版的專著《雅樂之聲：宮廷音樂重建、儀式與中國對可用之過去的找尋》探討中國古代雅樂在21世紀的重建。雅樂是古代中國宮廷中用於特定场合演奏的儀式音樂体系。這個項目所探究的是這段久遠的音樂文化史與當代中國世界的相遇，以及兩者在碰撞時如何與一種更廣闊的文化民族主義想像相互交織。在這份想像中，一個獨一無二的「中國性」形象正試圖被重塑。作者認為，中國的當下不断在圍繞其古代文化和歷史的敘事中被積極塑造， 而這些敘事則反過來改寫中國浩瀚歷史長河裡的「可用」之部分。本研究透過雅樂這個音樂文化載體來追溯中國文化從古代社會和封建王朝向民族國家及其全球化環境下集體離散敘事的漫長演變歷程。雅樂的重建揭示了中國對其自身封建王朝歷史（尤其與宮廷儀式音樂傳統相關）態度的微妙轉化，為考察「中國性」(包括過去和現在、中國之內和之外）這一概念的邊界性提供了一個難得的語境。 本計畫探討了早期音樂復興主義、儀式理論與表演性、（自我）異域想像、中國思想史以及各種形式的音樂和文化民族主義等問題，為音樂 (人類) 學、古代中國史、中國古典哲學、批判文化研究、政治哲學和音樂理論都做出貢獻。本研究的方法論均衡地融合了民族誌、檔案研究和批判性文本分析。本研究豐富了現有音樂學研究中關於早期音樂復興的探索，尤其考慮到這些研究甚少在泛亞洲語境下進行。它也填補了當前中國古代宮廷音樂相關研究大多僅限於歷史性思考的這一缺口，同時也進一步豐富了日益重視非西方文獻和語境的國際音樂理論學科。鑑於雅樂重建過程中優先復興的是“禮”，即儒家思想中廣義的儀式概念（包含日常社交中的人際禮儀）, 本項目同時為儀式理論和表演研究做出貢獻。作者也認為此項目能夠與當今批判文化研究的思潮，尤其是新興的「亞洲研究在亞洲」等領域進行對話。透過將當前雅樂重建中的核心議題與中國古代歷史中的相關思潮並置，本專著旨在揭示雅樂等表達性文化的周期性和螺旋式演變，同時試圖識別這個漫長過程中針對「古代」、「傳統」、和「和諧」等概念的話語轉變。最終，正是這些概念共同定義了當今社会里的「中國集體意識」。

28100125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28100125.value: 運用功能性腦連結與數位表徵探討青少年的心理社會韌性：高韌性個體是否展現更獨特的特徵？

28100125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28100125.value: Mental health problems like depression and anxiety are extremely common worldwide. Despite major efforts to improve mental health care, rates of mental illness have not decreased over the past few decades. To make real progress, we need to shift focus from treating illness to promoting wellness and resilience before problems start. Resilience refers to the ability to cope with and bounce back from stress. Some people are more resilient, while others struggle more with stress and can develop mental health issues. This study will examine links between resilience, smartphone-based digital behavioral data and brain connections. We will recruit 129 youths aged 18-24 from Hong Kong. Participants will complete questionnaires about their psychosocial functioning and retrospective early life stress prior to age of 18. We will also collect GPS mobility data and screen usage time from their smartphones over two months. In addition, participants will undergo an MRI brain scan to map connectivity between different brain regions at rest. We will calculate an outcome-based resilience for each person by taking into account both their psychosocial wellbeing and self-reported early life experiences. Computational techniques will be employed to identify individuals based on their digital and brain connectivity patterns. It is hypothesized that individuals who are more unique and distinguishable from the others may show higher levels of resilience. Subsequently, machine learning models to predict individual resilience will be developed using digital and brain imaging data. This procedure aims to shed light on specific digital and brain patterns associated with resilience. Understanding the links between resilience and individual patterns of digital or functional connectivity could offer valuable insights into promoting adaptation to life stressors. Identifying digital and biological markers of resilience could ultimately help design tailored interventions to reduce risk when people experience significant life stress. Overall, this innovative study integrates psychology, neuroscience, and data science to elucidate potential mechanisms underlying resilience, moving beyond a disease-focused view. Leveraging smartphone and brain imaging as tools for resilience research represents a fresh, interdisciplinary perspective with potential clinical impacts for mental health promotion. 全球有極高比例的人口受抑鬱和焦慮等心理健康問題所困擾。儘管在改善心理健康服務方面已投入大量努力，但過去幾十年間，精神疾病的整體發病率並未顯著下降。要真正推動進展，我們需要將重點從「治療疾病」轉向「促進身心福祉與韌性」，即在問題出現之前加強預防與適應力。韌性是指個體在面對壓力時的應對與恢復能力。有些人較具韌性，能夠有效調適壓力，而另一些人則較容易受到壓力影響，進而發展出心理健康問題。 本研究旨在探討韌性與智能手機數位行為數據及大腦功能連結之間的關聯。我們將招募129名來自香港、年齡介乎18至24歲的年輕人作為參與者。受試者將填寫有關其心理社會功能與18歲前早期生活壓力的回顧性問卷。我們亦會在為期兩個月的時間內，從參與者的智能手機中收集 GPS 移動資料與螢幕使用時間。此外，參與者將接受靜息態功能性磁力共振成像（fMRI）掃描，以描繪大腦不同區域間的功能連結情況。 我們將根據參與者的心理社會健康與其自述的早期經歷，計算出每個人的「結果導向韌性指標」。接著，研究將應用運算技術來辨識參與者在數位行為與大腦連結模式上的特徵，並假設韌性較高的個體，其行為與神經表現可能在群體中更為獨特與可區分。隨後，我們將基於數位與大腦影像資料，建構機器學習模型以預測個體的韌性。此程序旨在揭示與韌性相關的具體數位與神經表徵。 理解韌性與個體數位行為或大腦功能連結模式之間的關係，有助於深入認識人們如何適應生活壓力。辨識出心理韌性的數位與生物標誌，最終可望促成更個人化的干預策略，以降低人們在面對重大壓力事件時的心理風險。總體而言，本研究融合心理學、神經科學與數據科學，致力於揭示韌性的潛在機制，並跳出以疾病為中心的研究框架。運用智能手機與腦影像作為心理韌性研究工具，展現出創新且跨學科的視角，對未來心理健康促進工作具有潛在臨床意義。

28200525.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28200525.value: 細菌-質體-噬菌體三方互動如何影響微生物群落中的基因傳遞？

28200525.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28200525.value: In the environment, bacteria typically form complex interactive networks with each other rather than existing as isolated single cells. These relationships facilitate material and information exchanges in the face of an ever-changing environment. In particular, horizontal gene transfer – the sharing of genetic materials between organisms, not in a parent-offspring relationship – is vital for microorganisms’ survival under environmental stresses. By trafficking adaptive traits, a diversity of mobile genetic elements – segments of DNA moving both within and between genomes, are key nodes shaping the complex gene-transfer network. A typical example is the recurring emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens due to the acquisition of resistance genes via mobile genetic elements. Bacteria serve as a common playground for various mobile genetic elements, in which prevalent plasmids and phages (i.e., bacterial viruses) are the two key players – both are extrachromosomal elements and dependent on bacterial hosts to complete their life cycle. To cope with dynamic environments, bacteria, plasmids, and phages must interact intensively with each other. Recent anecdotal studies have shed light on their complicated relationships. For example, conflicting selection has been shown to alter the trajectory of molecular evolution in a model tripartite bacteria-plasmid-phage interaction. Phage predation may facilitate the spread of plasmid-encoded antibiotic resistance in communities by slowing spatial segregation. The widespread phage-plasmids and plasmid-dependent phages recently unveiled further blurred their boundaries. Nevertheless, the interactions among bacteria, plasmids, and phages, as well as in which way and to what extent they shape microbial communities, remain largely unknown. To address the above fundamental knowledge gaps, we propose a research project to systematically decipher the tripartite bacteria-plasmid-phage relationships and determine their roles in microbial communities. This will be done through four tasks. First, we will explore the potential interactions between bacteria, plasmids, and phages, as inferred from genome and metagenome databases. Second, we will study the in situ interaction profiles in wastewater communities. Third, we will decipher the molecular evolution trajectories of bacteria-plasmid-phage interactions. Fourth, we will examine the tripartite interactions in suspended and biofilm microbial communities. The results of this comprehensive study will give a first insight into the interactions between bacteria, plasmids, and phages in environmental microbial communities. This may allow us to develop more precise and more sustainable strategies to control communities and functions by manipulating their interactions, such as phage-based control of target populations and mitigation of the dissemination of antibiotic resistance, ultimately contributing to sustainable development. 在自然環境中，細菌通常會形成複雜的互動網絡，而非以孤立單細胞形式存在。這種互動關係促進了多變環境下的物質與信息交換。其中，水平基因轉移（即非親緣生物間的遺傳物質交流）對微生物在環境脅迫下的生存至關重要。各類可移動遺傳元件（能在基因組內或基因組間轉移的DNA片段）通過傳遞適應性狀，成為塑造複雜基因轉移網絡的關鍵節點。典型例證是多重耐藥病原體的反覆出現，這往往源於其通過可移動遺傳元件獲得了耐藥基因。 細菌是多種可移動遺傳元件的共同宿主，其中質粒和噬菌體（即細菌病毒）是兩類核心成員—它們均屬於染色體外元件，並依賴宿主細菌完成生命週期。為應對動態環境，細菌、質粒與噬菌體之間必然存在密集互動。近期個案研究揭示了其複雜關係：例如，衝突性選擇可改變三方互動模型的分子進化路徑；噬菌體捕食可能通過延緩空間隔離促進質粒編碼的抗生素耐藥性在群落中傳播；最新發現的廣譜噬菌體質粒（phage-plasmids）和質粒依賴性噬菌體進一步模糊了二者的界限。然而，三者互動機制及其對微生物群落結構與功能的影響程度仍屬未知。 為填補這一基礎認知空白，我們提出一項系統性研究計劃，通過四個任務揭示三方互動關係及其生態作用：首先，基於基因組與宏基因組數據庫挖掘潛在互動模式；其次，解析廢水微生物群落中的原位互動特徵；第三，闡明細菌-質粒-噬菌體互動的分子進化軌跡；最後，比較微生物群落中的三方互動差異。這項綜合研究將首次揭示環境微生物群落中三者的互動規律，為開發精準可持續的群落調控策略提供理論基礎—例如通過操縱互動關係實現噬菌體靶向控菌、抑制抗生素耐藥性傳播，最終助力可持續發展。

28600425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28600425.value: 認知對話法如何增加學生對科學科運用生成式人工智能的認知層面

28600425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28600425.value: There is an increasing enthusiasm for GenAI in learning science. Junior secondary students are often asked to follow teacher instructions to use GenAI for designing scientific investigations. Students do not know how GenAI creates scientific information (*Cheung, Pun and Li, 2024). There is a lack of research in this epistemic aspect of GenAI. The problems are exacerbated by GenAI’s capacity for “hallucinating” scientific information and the lack of curriculum guidelines for GenAI-related classroom practice (*Cheung et al., 2024). Without opportunities for dialogue during engagement, students are likely to place too much trust in GenAI-created scientific information. Epistemic-dialogue pedagogy supports students to build on others’ ideas about the validity of scientific claims made by GenAI. Given its potential, teachers need to engage with them in epistemic dialogues to ensure there is critical use of GenAI in science learning. This proposed study will use design-based interventions to (1) develop and refine an epistemic-dialogic pedagogy and (2) examine its effectiveness on students’ science learning. It will be conducted over two years with Secondary 1 teachers and students in three schools with various academic backgrounds (Bands 1, 2 and 3) in Hong Kong. Phase 1 is a trial implementation, while Phase 2 is the full implementation. In Phase 1, the research team will work with teachers to design a two-week curriculum unit in which they will co-construct ideas with students on how GenAI generates scientific knowledge. In Phase 2, the researcher and the teachers in Phase 1 will reflect on the initial results and revise the pedagogy for a six-week curriculum unit. In each school, this phase involves intact classes as intervention groups using an epistemic-dialogic pedagogy while another class will be used as a comparison group that adopts a business-as-usual approach. Quantitatively, students' pre- and post-tests on GenAI-science epistemic understanding, topic-specific knowledge and science intrinsic motivation will be collected. Qualitatively, videos of teacher-student and student-student dialogues, teacher-researcher meetings and interviews with students will be audio recorded. To evaluate each phase, ordered network analysis will visualize sequential connections between qualitative dialogue categories, the results will be triangulated with quantitative analysis of test results using Rasch analysis and thematic analysis of interviews and meetings. The project will contribute to a deeper understanding of successful epistemic-dialogic pedagogy that will assist students using GenAI in science learning. The findings will inform guidelines for using GenAI in local and international science curricula. 學術界對科學學習中使用生成式人工智能感到十分興趣。初中生按照老師的指示使用生成式人工智能進行科學研究。然而，學生們並不清楚生成式人工智能是如何創造科學資訊的 (*Cheung, Pun and Li, 2024)。目前，教育界缺乏如何增加學生對生成式人工智能的認知層面的指引。 生成式人工智能可造假科學訊息，缺乏與生成式人工智能相關的課堂實踐課程指引會加劇了這些問題 (*Cheung et al., 2024)。 認知對話教學法支持學生建立他人關於生成式人工智能科學理論有效性的想法。鑑於其潛力，教師需要與學生進行認知對話，以確保生成式人工智能在科學學習中有效運用。本研究將採用以設計研究法，以(1)發展和完善認知對話教學法; (2) 理解其教學法對學生科學學習的有效性。本研究將為期兩年，研究對象為香港三所不同學術背景學校的中一師生。 第一階段為試行，第二階段為全面實施。在第一階段，研究團隊將與教師合作設計一個為期兩週的課程單元，並與學生共同探討生成式人工智能如何產生科學知識。在第二階段，研究人員將與第一階段的教師一起反思初步成果，並修改為期六週的課程單元的教學法。在這階段，每所學校將安排完整的班級作為實驗組，採用認知對話式教學法；同時，將另一個班級作為對照組，採用常規教學法。 定量方面，我們將收集學生在生成式人工智能與科學認知理解、科學知識和學習科學興趣方面的前測和後測數據。質性方面，我們將錄影師生對話、學生之間對話、與師生的訪談的影片。為了評估每階段，我們將使用Ordered network analysis分析及展示定性對話類別之間的序列連接，並將結果與使用 Rasch 測量模型的定量分析以及訪談和會議的分析增加研究的可靠性。該計劃將有助於更深入地理解認知對話教學法的成功因素，從而幫助學生在科學學習中使用生成式人工智能。研究結果將為在本地和國際科學課程中使用對生成式人工智能提供指引。

28601225.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28601225.value: 基於多模態數據探索GenAI對話式互動對幼童中文書寫學習成效之影響

28601225.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601225.value: The central role of handwriting in written communication has been increasingly taken over by convenient typewriting in the digital age. This change has resulted in a notable decline in handwriting literacy (i.e., character amnesia), particularly in non-alphabetic scripts like Chinese characters, known for their high visuospatial complexity. Moreover, the prevalence of phonology-based input methods (utilizing phonology rather than orthography to input Chinese characters) exacerbates character amnesia due to the untransparent grapheme-phoneme conversions in the Chinese writing system. This shows that insufficient handwriting practice in the digital age severely interferes the normal development of Chinese reading and writing ability among young children. Thus, promoting Chinese handwriting learning has become more crucial than ever before. Rote copying practice is a widely-used method in Chinese handwriting education. However, this traditional method presents two salient problems. First, it is tedious and boring, leading to low learning engagement. Second, it focuses on rote memorization without establishing meaningful linkages between pronunciation, orthography, and semantic meaning, leading to poor performance in dictation. This project aims to address the two problems by leveraging generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). In Phase 1, we will develop a GenAI tutor to provide dialogic interactions with students during copying practice. The interactions will be guided by the feedback model of ASK-TELL-ASK, which includes reflecting on handwriting performance and asking questions related to the pronunciation, orthography, and semantic meanings of the character. The GenAI tutor will be built using an open-source large language model, iFLYTEK Spark LLM, and integrated into a self-developed Android mobile application for Chinese handwriting learning. In Phase 2, a randomized control trial design will be performed to assess the effectiveness of the GenAI tutor. 186 Hong Kong children (aged 6-7) will be randomly assigned into treatment and control groups and will learn new Chinese characters either by rote copying practice alone or with the GenAI tutor. Their brain activities will be continuously recorded using electroencephalogram (EEG). The impact of the GenAI tutor on Chinese handwriting learning engagement and performance will be evaluated by applying linear mixed models to analyze between-group differences at both the behavioral and neural levels. The GenAI tutor developed in this project aims to improve teaching and learning practice for Chinese handwriting in the digital age and inform relevant policy development both within and outside Hong Kong. Moreover, it will contribute to the establishment of new norms in student learning design in the GenAI environment. 在數碼化時代，手寫於書面溝通中的核心地位，正日益被便捷的鍵盤輸入所取代。此一轉變導致手寫能力（即「執筆忘字」現象）顯著下降，尤其在漢字這類具有高度視覺空間複雜性的非字母文字體系中更為突出。此外，由於漢字書寫系統中形音轉換規則的非透明性，基於語音（即利用拼音而非字形）輸入漢字的輸入法盛行，進一步加劇了「執筆忘字」問題。這顯示，數碼化時代手寫練習的不足，會嚴重干擾幼童中文讀寫能力的正常發展。因此，促進漢字書寫學習變得比以往任何時候都更為關鍵。機械抄寫練習是漢字書寫教育中廣泛使用的方法。然而，此傳統方法存在兩大明顯問題：其一，過程沉悶乏味，導致學習投入度低；其二，側重死記硬背，未能有效建立漢字的音、形、義之間的有意義聯繫，致使默寫表現欠佳。本項目旨在利用生成式人工智能（GenAI）解決上述兩大問題。在第一階段，將開發一個GenAI導師系統，於學生進行抄寫練習時提供對話式互動。互動將遵循「提問-講解-再提問」回饋模式進行引導，內容包括檢視書寫表現，並圍繞漢字的讀音、字形及語義提出問題。該GenAI導師系統將基於開源大型語言模型開發，並整合至一套自主研發的漢字書寫學習安卓流動應用程式中。在第二階段，將採用隨機對照試驗設計，評估GenAI導師系統的成效。186名香港幼童（年齡6-7歲）將被隨機分配至實驗組與對照組，分別採用「純機械抄寫」或「結合GenAI導師」的方式學習新的中文生字。研究將使用腦電圖持續記錄其腦部活動，將運用線性混合模式分析組別差異，從行為層面與神經層面評估GenAI導師系統對漢字書寫學習投入度及表現的影響。本項目開發的GenAI導師系統，旨在改善數碼化時代的漢字書寫教學實踐，並為香港及以外地區的相關政策制訂提供參考。此外，該項目亦將為在生成式人工智能環境下，建立學生學習設計的新規範作出貢獻。

28603025.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28603025.value: 整合式韻律干預對漢語聾童閱讀理解的影響：一項隨機對照測驗

28603025.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28603025.value: Deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) children face great challenges in reading comprehension. Although the Education Bureau has proposed "Enhanced Support Services" to facilitate their reading development, specific details remain undefined. Prosody—the rhythmic and melodic aspects of language, including tone, rhythm, and intonation—is particularly crucial in Chinese. It comprises two interconnected components: speech prosody (i.e., the prosodic features of spoken language) and reading prosody (i.e., the expressiveness of prosodic features during oral reading). Research with hearing children highlights the predictive effects of speech and reading prosody in reading development and indicates the effectiveness of integrating both types of prosody training to enhance reading comprehension. Although DHH children exhibit atypical prosody, our studies with Chinese DHH children demonstrate that prosody is vital for Chinese reading comprehension (Deng & Tong, 2021a, 2021b). Additionally, our recent systematic review (Deng et al., under review) synthesizes evidence on DHH reading interventions, suggesting that prosody enhances the effects of reading fluency training, which subsequently affects reading comprehension; however, this evidence lacks randomized controlled trials, and retention effects remain unknown. Therefore, this proposal aims to: (1) determine the effectiveness of an integrated prosody-based intervention (i.e., IPBI) in enhancing reading comprehension; and (2) examine the short-term and long-term retention effects of the intervention. Sixty DHH children in Grades 1-3 with functional hearing and 60 hearing counterparts will be randomly assigned to treatment and control groups, respectively. They will be assessed on speech and reading prosody, reading skills, and linguistic and cognitive controls at baseline, post-assessment, and two follow-up assessments (three months and one year). The effectiveness of a three-month IPBI will be determined by comparing reading outcomes between the treatment and control (self-silent reading) groups before and after the intervention (Objective 1). The short-term and long-term retention effects will be identified by the continuous reading improvement of the treatment groups after the intervention, measured at three months and one year post-intervention (Objective 2). Theoretically, this research will clarify the causal relationship between prosody and reading comprehension, extending the revised Reading Systems Framework (Wade-Woolley et al., 2021) to the Chinese DHH population. Practically, the IPBI provides a new approach to support DHH children’s reading development during the early school years. It will provide empirical evidence for data-based decision making and drive curriculum changes. Ultimately, improved reading performance will enable DHH children to thrive in inclusive education systems, enhancing quality of life and supporting lifelong development. 聾童在閱讀理解方面面臨重大挑戰。雖然教育局提出「增強支援服務」以促進其閱讀發展，但具體細節尚未明確。韻律——語言的節奏與旋律特徵，包括音調、節奏和語調——在中文中尤為重要。它包含兩個緊密關聯的核心要素：語音韻律（即口語中的韻律特徵）和閱讀韻律（即朗讀中的韻律表現力）。 針對聽力正常兒童的研究顯示，語音和閱讀韻律對閱讀發展具有預測作用，且整合兩種類型的韻律訓練能有效提升閱讀理解能力。儘管聾童表現出非典型的韻律特徵，但此前我們針對漢語為母語的聾童的研究表明，韻律對中文閱讀理解至關重要（Deng & Tong, 2021a, 2021b）。此外，我們近期關於聾童閱讀干預的綜述（Deng 等, 已提交）顯示，韻律可增強閱讀流暢性訓練的效果，進而影響閱讀理解。然而，目前還缺乏隨機對照試驗的實證支持，其長期效果尚不明確。因此，本研究計劃旨在：（1）驗證整合式韻律干預（IPBI）對提升閱讀理解的成效；（2）評估該干預的短期和長期持續效果。 本研究計劃將招募60名具功能性聽力的1至3年級聾童及60名聽力正常對照組兒童，隨機分配至干預組和對照組。他們將在前測、後測及兩次跟進評估（三個月及一年後）接受語音和閱讀韻律、閱讀技能以及語言和認知控制的評估。通過比較干預前後干預組與對照組的閱讀成果以確定IPBI（為期三個月）的有效性（目標1）。通過測試干預後三個月及一年後干預組的持續閱讀進步以評估短期和長期干預持續效果（目標2）。 理論上，本研究將闡明韻律與閱讀理解之間的因果關係，拓展修訂版閱讀系統框架（Wade-Woolley等，2021）在中國聾童中的適用性。實踐上，IPBI為提升聾童早期閱讀發展提供新方法，也為教育決策提供實證依據，並推動課程變革。最終，通過提升閱讀能力，聾童將更好的在融合教育體系中蓬勃發展，提升生活品質並促進終身發展。

28605125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28605125.value: This study aims to explore the lived experiences and agencies of ethnic minority (EM) youth in Hong Kong as they navigate multiple languages and identities and raise their critical multilingual language and race/ethnicity awareness. Against the backdrop of documented social and educational inequalities faced by EM youths in Hong Kong, there is a growing interest in examining the interplay between language learning, identity negotiation, and a sense of belonging (Gao & Gube, 2020; Gu & Han, 2022; Hue & Karim, 2024; Thapa & Adamson, 2017). However, existing research has scarcely engaged EM youths in dialogues that facilitate action and understanding of their sociolinguistic realities. Given the documented disconnection between mainstream education and community-based language learning practices, which has led many EM youths to consider relocating to English-speaking countries within the next decade (Kapai & Singh, 2018), it is imperative to examine how the sociolinguistic and citizenship concerns of EM youths are being addressed within the educational system. Responding to calls for amplifying the voices and sociolinguistic citizenship of marginalized youths in diasporic contexts (Albury, 2021; Lim, Stroud & Wee, 2019; Perez-Milan & Soto, 2018), this project adopts Community-Based Participatory Research (CBPR) to actively involve EM youths in the research process. This approach not only provides a platform for them to share their experiences and challenges but also fosters critical awareness through engaged dialogues and social actions. The theoretical framework of “linguistic citizenship” (Stroud, 2001, 2018) underpins this research, viewing citizenship and belonging through the lenses of language and identity. It emphasizes the role of affirmative multilingualism in empowering marginalized groups to improve their social, material, and economic conditions. Grounded in an ethnographic CBPR approach (Blomberg & Karasti, 2012), this study will employ “critically engaged workshops” (Zaidi & Sah, 2024) using generative design tools to explore participants’ lived experiences. Data will be collected through in-depth interviews, focus groups, multilingual and multimodal texts, walking narratives, community surveys, and questionnaires. The findings from this study are expected to contribute to our understanding of minoritized youths’ processes of building linguistic citizenship in diasporic contexts in and beyond Hong Kong and the affordances of multilingual and multimodal interactions. Anticipated outcomes include enhanced well-being and connection of EM youths with Hong Kong, increased critical awareness of language and race-based inequities, and opportunities for educators to develop socially committed pedagogies to counteract negative stereotypes against ethnic minorities (Kapai & Singh, 2018). 28606625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28606625.value: 生態藝術視域下的珠江水域圖景

28606625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28606625.value: The Pearl River is the second-largest river system in China after the Yangtze River. Its three major tributaries (West River, North River, and East River) and vast river networks connecting with the South China Sea shape and nourish the Pearl River Delta (PRD), making it one of the most populous urban clusters and creative hubs in the world. However, cultural and artistic impressions regarding the Pearl River are much impaired compared with the Yellow River and Yangtze River, which are often intricately associated with the Chinese national ethos and central plains landscape. This research aims to address this by tracing the existing artistic narrative of the Pearl River using contemporary art practices, as well as to enlarge our conception of a river from a linear water body to a vast water system with a co-constituting hydrosocial relationship with human society and the more-than-human world. The Pearl River, apart from providing natural water resources and a habitat for the delta’s biodiverse communities, is also one of the most human-engineered rivers to further develop a water-centric and amphibious economy and culture. As the PRD region undergoes rapid urbanisation and development, particularly with construction of the Greater Bay Area (GBA), it has become a contact zone for constant negotiations between land and water, anthropocentric development, and the more-than-human world, amidst increasing environmental hazards (Wang and Rainbow, 2020). The role of the Pearl River and its cultural and aesthetic agencies has become more crucial for researchers and the general public to understand the shifting ecological and cultural landscape of the region, as well as its translocal impact. Departing from the interdisciplinary field of environmental humanities, blue humanities, and creative arts, this research aims to explore the complex nature of human–river relations through the vernacular ecological art practices of the PRD region. Taking a different stance to the existing scholarship, which primarily focuses on the metropolitan characteristics of the region, this research aims to shift the focus to the water-centric environment of the area. It will further analyse art work through ecocritical theorisation and contextualisation in the PRD and coastal environment to further activate the artworks’ ecological messages, aesthetic richness, and social impact. 珠江是中國僅次於長江的第二大河流水系，其三條主要支流（西江、北江與東江）及其他的繁密逕流構成與南海相連的龐大河網，共同塑造並滋養了珠江三角洲，使其成為全球人口最稠密的都會群與創意樞紐之一。然而相較於常被賦予中華民族精神與中原景觀意涵的黃河、長江，珠江在文化藝術層面的形象建構明顯薄弱。本研究旨在透過當代藝術實踐梳理珠江現有的藝術敘事，同時將河流概念從線性水體擴展至更複雜的與人類社會、非人世界共同構成的「水文社會性」的龐大水系。珠江除是提供天然水資源與三角洲生物群落的棲息地外，更是人類為發展親水型兩棲經濟文化而高度改造的河川。隨著珠三角地區快速城市化（特別是大灣區建設），生態破壞風險日益增長，該地域已成為水陸動態交接、人類中心主義發展觀與非人世界持續協商的接觸地帶（Wang and Rainbow, 2020）。相應地，珠江的文化美學能動性對於理解該區域變動中的生態文化景觀及其跨地域影響愈顯關鍵。 本研究依託於環境人文學、海洋人文學與創意藝術的跨領域視野，試圖透過珠三角本土生態藝術實踐探討人與河流關係的複雜內涵。有別於當下研究多聚焦該區域的都市化特質，本研究將視角轉向該區域以水為核心的環境。同時其將相關藝術作品放置在生態批評理論之下與珠三角的河海交匯情境之中，進一步激活藝術作品的生態訊息、美學豐富性與社會影響力。

28608725.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28608725.value: 青少年適應父母監禁的過程：心理健康日常機制之前瞻性研究

28608725.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28608725.value: This project aims to investigate the role of lifestyle behaviors in the association between parental incarceration and mental health among adolescents. Globally over 22.5 million children with at least one imprisoned parent become hidden victims of criminal justice systems. Several decades of research consistently link exposure to parental incarceration with emotional and behavioral problems, with adolescent children exhibiting the most severe symptoms compared with younger children or adults. Previous research relied on broader stress process paradigms (e.g., stress process theory, sense of coherence, meaning making model) to understand cognitive, emotional, biological, and ecological processes in stress adaptation. However, these studies inadequately addressed the processes and underlying behavioral mechanism, the most immediate and noticeable manifestation of adaptation in children’s everyday lives. Both Daily Stressor Model and Drive to Thrive theory advanced the existing understanding of stress adaptation and deposited that sustaining lifestyle behaviors is one of the basic processes for psychological resilience over time. In the context of parental incarceration, maintaining daily routines can be challenging due to sudden involuntary separation of parent(s) and a cascade of stressors such as economic hardship, family instability, and stigma. There is an urgent need to understand the behavioral aspects of everyday adaptation to parental incarceration. The current project has three aims: (1) To investigate social and environmental correlates of disruptions to lifestyle behaviors among adolescents exposed to parental incarceration; (2) To examine prospective associations between parental incarceration, disruptions in lifestyle behaviors, and mental health; and (3) To investigate the mediating role of lifestyle behaviors in the association between parental incarceration and mental health. This project consists of two studies. Study 1 will utilize Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study tracking 11,868 adolescents for three years using a stratified random sample of schools in the US. Study 2 will be a prospective study of a separate local sample of 150 adolescent children exposed to parental incarceration. Participants will complete questionnaires related to exposure to parental incarceration, lifestyle behaviors (i.e., nutrition, sleep, physical activity, leisure, school life, social relations) and mental health at baseline, 3-month, and 9-month follow-up. Overall, the project will add new evidence to the current theoretical and empirical literature on the role of lifestyle behaviors in adaption to parental incarceration. The findings will also provide one of the first empirical bases for designing prevention and intervention programs with easy-to-follow restructuring of lifestyle behaviors to improve resilience among adolescents exposed to parental incarceration. 該項目旨在探究日常生活方式在父母監禁與青少年心理健康關聯中的作用。全球有逾两千萬名兒童因其父母中至少一方被監禁而成為刑事司法系統中的隱性受害者。大量實證證據顯示，父母監禁與情緒及行為問題顯著相關，相較於年幼兒童或成人，處於青春期的青少年所呈現的症狀最為嚴重。先前的研究主要依循較寬泛的應激過程理論（如stress process theory、sense of coherence、meaning making model）来理解應激適應中的認知、情緒、生物以及生態機制。 然而，這些研究未能充分探討潛在的行為機制，而該機制卻是日常生活適應中最直接、最顯著的表現。Daily Stressor Model與Drive to Thrive 抗壓理論均進一步深化了對應激適應機制的理解，強調維持規律的生活方式是培養心理韌性的基本過程之一。在父母被監禁的情境下，由於父母突然被強制分離，以及隨之而來的經濟困難、家庭動盪與社會污名化等接踵而至的壓力源，維持日常生活規律極具挑戰性。因此，理解青少年在適應父母監禁過程中日常行為層面的相關機制十分重要。 本研究計畫共三項主要目標：（1）探討青少年在父母監禁情境下，日常生活規律受擾的社會與環境相關因素；（2）檢驗父母監禁、日常生活規律受擾與心理健康之間的前瞻性關聯；（3）分析日常生活規律在父母監禁與心理健康關係中的中介作用。該項目包含兩項研究： 研究一將基於11,868名美國青少年分層隨機樣本「Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development」的前三年追蹤數據。 研究二則為針對本地150名經歷父母監禁的青少年的前瞻性研究。參與者將在基線期、3個月及9個月的追蹤期，完成關於父母監禁狀況、日常生活規律（涵蓋營養、睡眠、運動、休閒、校園生活、社會關係）及心理健康狀況的問卷評估。整體而言，本項目將豐富現有關於日常生活規律在適應父母監禁過程中所扮演角色的理論與實證文獻。研究結果亦將為設計預防與介入方案提供紮實的實證基礎，此類方案旨在透過優化調整日常生活規律，提升經歷父母監禁青少年的心理韌性。

28610125.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28610125.value: 從分析到行動：透過處方式網絡分析提升探究式討論中的反饋實踐

28610125.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28610125.value: As the demand for cultivating students' higher-order thinking (HOT) intensifies in higher education, inquiry-based discussion (IBD) has emerged as a widely adopted pedagogical approach across disciplines. However, despite its potential to foster critical, reflective, and interactive discourse, the effectiveness of IBD is not guaranteed, as the quality of instructor feedback significantly influences how students understand and navigate the complex IBD process. Due to time and resource constraints, instructors face difficulties in monitoring student discussions and providing timely, actionable, and personalized feedback. While learning analytics (LA) offer promising solutions to provide instructors with fine-grained insights into IBD, their adoption in practice remains limited due to the data science expertise required. Consequently, many instructors miss the opportunity to leverage LA advancements, hindering their ability to provide quality feedback, which in turn limits students’ engagement and development in IBD. Grounded in the community of inquiry (CoI) model, this project strives to bridge the gap between advanced LA and practical solutions that enhance instructors’ feedback practices. Specifically, the project aims to: (1) develop a prescriptive network analytics (PNA) tool tailored for IBD feedback practices; (2) enhance instructor feedback practices with transparent analytics, interpretable insights, and adaptive recommendations; (3) improve student IBD engagement and outcomes through timely, actionable, and personalized feedback; and (4) establish a comprehensive IBD feedback framework integrating theoretical principles, analytical insights, and effective practices. This project will unfold in three phases. In phase 1, an exploratory study involving 25 instructors and 350 students will be conducted using surveys and interviews to identify specific needs for LA-assisted feedback. A prototype PNA tool will be developed following this phase. Phase 2 will employ a design-based research approach to iteratively design, implement, analyze, and refine the prototype through collaboration with four instructors in real-world educational settings. In phase 3, a quasi-experiment will be conducted with six instructors and their respective classes (240 to 360 students in total) to evaluate the effectiveness of PNA-assisted feedback practices. Quantitative, qualitative, and computational data will be collected and analyzed across phases 2 and 3. The significance of this project extends beyond the development of a single tool. By making theory-informed analytics more accessible and actionable for practitioners, the project aims to transform feedback practices in IBD, ultimately contributing to the more effective development of HOT in higher education. 隨著高等教育對培養學生高階思維 (HOT) 的需求日益殷切，探究式討論 (IBD) 已成為跨學科廣泛採用的教學方法。然而，儘管 IBD 有助於促進具批判性、反思性與互動性的表達，其成效並非必然，因為教師反饋的質素深刻影響學生對 IBD 複雜歷程的理解與掌握。受制於時間與資源，教師難以有效監察學生的討論，並提供及時、可操作及個別化的反饋。雖然學習分析 (LA) 有望為教師提供關於 IBD 的細緻洞見，但由於需要數據科學背景，其在實踐中的應用仍然受限。因此，許多教師未能充分藉助 LA 的發展以優化其反饋實踐，削弱其提供優質反饋的能力，並進一步限制學生在 IBD 中的參與與發展。 本研究以探究社區 (CoI) 框架為理論基礎，致力於銜接先進學習分析與可落地的方案，以強化教師的反饋實踐。具體目標包括：(1) 研發一套貼合 IBD 反饋情境的處方式網絡分析 (PNA) 工具；(2) 透過具透明度的分析、可詮釋的洞見與自適應建議，提升教師反饋實踐；(3) 藉由及時、可操作且個別化的反饋，促進學生於 IBD 的投入與學習成效；以及 (4) 建構一個整合理論原則、分析洞見與有效實踐的 IBD 反饋綜合框架。 本研究分三個階段推展。第一階段以問卷與訪談進行探索性研究，涵蓋 25 位教師及 350 名學生，以釐清 LA 協助反饋之具體需要；其後將開發 PNA 工具原型。第二階段採用基於設計的研究方法，於真實教學情境中與 4 位教師協作，循環設計、實施、分析與優化原型。第三階段將與 6 位教師及其班別（總人數約 240 至 360 名學生）開展準實驗，以評估 PNA 協助反饋實踐之成效。於第二及第三階段將收集並分析量化、質性與計算性數據。 本研究之重要性不止於開發單一工具。透過使以理論為本的分析更為易用與可操作，本研究旨在重塑 IBD 的反饋實踐，最終促進高等教育中高階思維之更有效培養。

28611625.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28611625.value: 社會情緒注意力作用在孤獨與抑鬱的神經心理學多模態研究

28611625.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28611625.value: Depression is a very common form of mental health condition, leading to long-term functional impairments, suicidal behaviours and premature death. Loneliness has reached epidemic levels and is a leading cause of depression. By understanding the causal neuropsychological mechanisms of loneliness on depressed mood, there is an opportunity to shed light on their theoretical framework that is critical for potential translational applications. Current theory suggests that loneliness biases people’s attention towards socio-affective information that is interpreted as cues for social threats but evidences are largely correlational. We previously demonstrated that loneliness may hinder affective processing by modulating the affective and attention regulatory functions. Therefore, Study 1 will use a longitudinal design and investigate: (Q1) How the attention to socio-affective information is related to loneliness, depressed mood, and their longitudinal changes. Clarification of these processes will improve understanding of how loneliness may lead to depressed mood across time. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a non-invasive brain stimulation technique that facilitates the excitation or inhibition of the local neural activity. It can provide causal neurobehavioral evidence between the neural target and the psychosocial processes and behaviours. Left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is crucial to regulating emotions and emotional experiences, and existing literature has suggested that stimulating left dlPFC is effective in reducing negative affective response to social exclusion and also depressive symptoms. Whether dlPFC modulates socio-affective attention and can regulate depressed mood in lonely individuals are unclear. Furthermore, electroencephalography (EEG) can directly measure neuronal activity and dynamics at high temporal resolution. Therefore, to further understand the role of socio-affective attention in the association between loneliness and depressed mood, in study 2, we will perform a tDCS-EEG study with lonely individuals to evaluate: (Q2) Whether anodal tDCS of the left dlPFC has an effect on the attention to socio-affective information, loneliness, and depressed mood in relation to the brain connectivity in lonely people. Findings will provide casual neuropsychological evidence for left dlPFC and its connectivity underpinning the relations between them. Overall, the proposed project will provide causal neural and behavioural evidence and increase our understanding of the neuropsychological relationships between loneliness, socio-affective attention, and depressed mood. Better understanding will facilitate the development of targeted interventions for people suffering from loneliness and depressed mood.

28612425.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28612425.value: 小學生的社會經濟地位與數碼素養：發展軌跡、作用機制與挑戰

28612425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28612425.value: Educational digitalization offers both opportunities (e.g., low-cost e-learning) and risks (e.g., overuse) that together affect young students’ well-being. Digital literacy (DL)—the learned ability to critically, responsibly, and healthily engage with digital tools—is essential for maximizing benefits while minimizing risks. Young students often rely on external support, such as digital resources and parental regulation, to navigate this balance; typically, students from higher socioeconomic status (SES) families or schools have more resources and support for greater learning opportunities, leading to better DL, greater access to digital benefits, and fewer risks. Despite this cross-sectional SES-DL relation, critical gaps remain in our understanding of (a) how family, class, and school SES interact to influence DL over time, (b) whether parental engagement can help bridge the SES-DL gap, and (c) how families establish and implement rules to balance digital benefits and risks. These gaps are particularly concerning, as a widening SES-DL divide and technology victimization of young students may hinder their learning and well-being in the digital age, deepening the digital divide and exacerbating social inequalities. To address these gaps, this study aims to (1) examine the longitudinal associations among family/class/school SES and students’ DL, (2) investigate how to bridge the SES-DL relation through parental engagement, and (3) understand how families establish and implement family rules for technology use and the challenges they face. This two-and-a-half-year longitudinal study consists of two sub-studies. In Study I, 300 dyads of 3rd grade students from six schools and their parents will both complete objective tests and self-report surveys three times, separated by nine-month intervals. School information and communication technology coordinators will report on school characteristics related to DL education. We will analyze these data via structural equation growth modeling. Among the Study I participants, 30 parent-child dyads with various SES/DL backgrounds will be interviewed for Study II about how they establish and implement family rules for healthy technology use and the challenges they face. We will apply thematic analysis to these interview data. This study extends previous research by examining how the SES-DL relationship evolves over time and how the SES-DL gap can be bridged. The findings will benefit students, parents, and educators by (a) identifying students in need of DL support, (b) enabling the design of effective strategies to address SES-DL disparities through parental engagement, and (c) revealing good practices and challenges in balancing digital benefits and risks in the family. 教育數碼化同時帶來機遇（例如低成本電子學習）與風險（例如過度使用），這些因素共同影響小學生的福祉。數碼素養（DL）——即能夠以批判性、負責任及健康的方式使用數碼工具的後天能力——對於最大化善用其益處、同時減低風險，至為關鍵。小學生往往依賴外部支援（如數碼資源及家長監管）來維持這種平衡；一般而言，來自較高社會經濟地位（SES）家庭或學校的學生，在獲取更多資源與支援方面具優勢，能享有更多學習機會，從而提升數碼素養，獲得更多數碼收益並減少風險。 儘管橫斷面研究已顯示 SES 與 DL 之間存在此關係，但我們對以下問題的理解仍存缺口：（a）隨時間演變，家庭、班別及學校的 SES 如何交互影響學生的 DL ；（b）家長參與能否協助縮窄 SES 與 DL 之間的差距；以及（c）家庭如何制定並實施規則，以在數碼益處與風險之間取得平衡。若SES-DL 的差距持續擴大，部分小學生在數碼時代的學習與福祉將受損，進一步加深數碼鴻溝並惡化社會不平等。 本研究旨在回應上述問題，目標包括：（1）探討家庭、班別及學校 SES 與學生 DL 之間的縱向關聯；（2）研究透過家長參與縮窄 SES-DL 關係的可行方法；（3）理解家庭在制定及實施科技使用規則時的做法與所面對的挑戰。 這項為期兩年半的縱向研究分為兩個子研究。研究一將邀請來自六所學校的300對三年級學生及其家長，於三個時間點（相隔九個月）參與客觀測驗及自我報告問卷；學校的資訊及通訊科技統籌主任亦會提供有關數碼素養教育的學校特徵資料。所得資料將以結構方程增長模型進行分析。在研究一的參與家庭中，三十對在 SES/DL 背景上具多樣性的親子組合將參與研究二的訪談，就其制定及實施健康科技使用規則的方法及面對的挑戰作深入探討，並採用主題分析方法處理訪談資料。 本研究在過往研究基礎上擴展，著重探討 SES-DL 關係隨時間之演變，以及如何縮窄此差距。研究成果將惠及學生、家長及教育工作者，包括：（a）識別需要 DL 支援的學生；（b）促進設計有效策略，透過家長參與應對 SES-DL 差距；（c）揭示在家庭中於平衡數碼益處與風險的良好實踐及所面臨的挑戰。

28614425.value: 限時進食與有氧-抗阻運動訓練結合改善肥胖老年人體成分：一項隨機對照試驗

28614425.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28614425.value: Population aging is a global concern and particularly pronounced in Hong Kong. Approximately 35% of older adults are obese, increasing their risk of developing several chronic diseases. Aging is characterized by an increasing loss of muscle mass and strength or function, which is exacerbated by obesity. Dietary interventions (e.g., time-restricted eating [TRE]) and exercise have been shown to be effective in addressing obesity. However, the reduction of muscle mass during weight loss is a concern. Combining aerobic and resistance exercises may prevent the loss of muscle mass while maintaining the effects of weight loss. Although the strategy of combining exercise and dietary changes was suggested for weight loss, no studies have examined the combined effect of aerobic-resistance exercise and TRE. We aimed to compare the effects of TRE and aerobic-resistance exercise, either individually or in combination, on body composition and physical function in older adults with obesity. Our pilot study revealed that the combination of aerobic exercise and TRE is an effective strategy for males with obesity to lose weight and body fat. Another pilot study also showed that the combination of aerobic-resistance exercise and TRE is feasible for older adults with obesity. Therefore, we will conduct a four-arm randomized controlled trial with a TRE group, an aerobic-resistance training group, a TRE and aerobic-resistance training group (combined group), and a control group. A total of 160 older adults with obesity will be involved in a 16-week intervention and 16-week follow-up period. The TRE group will be instructed to eat ad libitum during an 8 h eating window, followed by a 16 h fast. The aerobic-resistance exercise group will engage in 90 min of exercise three times per week, comprising 40 min of brisk walking and 40 min of upper- and lower-body resistance exercises with 5 min warm-up and cool-down periods. The primary outcome will be body fat % and muscle mass %. The secondary outcomes will include physical function, metabolic-related biomarkers, dietary intake, health-related quality of life, and cognitive function. Intention-to-treat analysis and per-protocol analyses will be conducted using linear mixed models. The findings of this proposed study will provide evidence regarding the efficacy of combining TRE with aerobic-resistance exercise for improving body composition and physical function in older adults with obesity. They will also help in developing additional combined dietary and exercise interventions to benefit the wider population and contribute to the prevention and control of non-communicable diseases. 人口老齡化是全球面臨的重大公共衛生挑戰，而香港的情況尤為突出。數據顯示，約35%的老年人存在肥胖問題，這顯著增加了他們罹患多種慢性疾病的風險。隨著年齡增長，肌肉質量下降、肌力及功能減退是衰老的典型特徵，而肥胖狀態更會加速此退化進程。現有研究表明，飲食干預（如限時進食[TRE]）與運動結合能有效改善肥胖問題。然而，減重過程中的肌肉流失現象仍需關注。結合有氧運動與抗阻訓練的綜合方案，可能不僅能維持減重效果，還能減少肌肉流失。雖然已有建議提倡透過運動與飲食調整相結合的策略來控制體重，但目前尚缺乏關於有氧-抗阻運動與限時進食聯合應用的研究。因此，本研究旨在比較限時進食、有氧-抗阻運動單獨或聯合干預對肥胖老年人身體成分及功能的影響。 我們的前期試驗表明，有氧運動結合限時進食是肥胖男性減重和減脂的有效策略。另一項試驗也證實，有氧-抗阻運動結合限時進食對肥胖老年人具有可行性。因此，我們將開展一項四組隨機對照試驗，設置限時進食組、有氧-抗阻訓練組、限時進食+有氧-抗阻訓練聯合組以及對照組。研究共招募160名肥胖老年人進行16週干預和16週隨訪。限時進食組將被指導在8小時進食窗口期內自由進食，隨後進行16小時禁食。有氧-抗阻運動組每週進行3次90分鐘訓練，包括40分鐘快走和40分鐘上下肢抗阻訓練，以及5分鐘熱身與放鬆。主要結局指標為體脂率和肌肉量百分比，次要結局包括身體功能、代謝相關生物標誌物、膳食攝入、生活質量和認知功能。將採用線性混合模型進行數據分析。本研究結果將為限時進食結合有氧-抗阻運動改善肥胖老年人身體成分和身體功能的療效提供實證，並有助於開發更多飲食與運動聯合干預方案，使更廣泛人群受益，對預防和控制非傳染性疾病發揮積極作用。
